When such restrictions are defined, the tokens must all fit within those restrictions; other values are non-conforming. If no such restrictions are specified, then all values are conforming.

#### 2.3.9 References

A valid hash-name reference to an element of type type is a string consisting of a U+0023 NUMBER SIGN character (#) followed by a string which exactly matches the value of the `name` attribute of an element with type type in the same [tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).

The rules for parsing a hash-name reference to an element of type type, given a context node scope, are as follows:
1. If the string being parsed does not contain a U+0023 NUMBER SIGN character, or if the first such character in the string is the last character in the string, then return null.
2. Let s be the string from the character immediately after the first U+0023 NUMBER SIGN character in the string being parsed up to the end of that string.
3. Return the first element of type type in scope's [tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), that has an [`id`](#326-global-attributes) or `name` attribute whose value is s, or null if there is no such element.

   > [!note]
   > Although [`id`](#326-global-attributes) attributes are accounted for when parsing, they are not used in determining whether a value is a [*valid* hash-name reference](#239-references). That is, a hash-name reference that refers to an element based on [`id`](#326-global-attributes) is a conformance error (unless that element also has a `name` attribute with the same value).

#### 2.3.10 Media queries

A string is a valid media query list if it matches the `<media-query-list>` production of Media Queries. [\[MQ\]](#references)

A string matches the environment of the user if it is the empty string, a string consisting of only [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), or is a media query list that matches the user's environment according to the definitions given in Media Queries. [\[MQ\]](#references)

#### 2.3.11 Unique internal values

A unique internal value is a value that is serializable, comparable by value, and never exposed to script.

To create a new unique internal value, return a [unique internal value](#2311-unique-internal-values) that has never previously been returned by this algorithm.

### 2.4 URLs

#### 2.4.1 Terminology

A string is a valid non-empty URL if it is a [valid URL string](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-url-string) but it is not the empty string.

A string is a valid URL potentially surrounded by spaces if, after [stripping leading and trailing ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) from it, it is a [valid URL string](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-url-string).

A string is a valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces if, after [stripping leading and trailing ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) from it, it is a [valid non-empty URL](#241-terminology).

---

This specification defines the URL `about:legacy-compat` as a reserved, though unresolvable, [`about:`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6694#section-2) URL, for use in [DOCTYPE](#1311-the-doctype)s in [HTML documents](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) when needed for compatibility with XML tools. [\[ABOUT\]](#references)

This specification defines the URL `about:html-kind` as a reserved, though unresolvable, [`about:`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6694#section-2) URL, that is used as an identifier for kinds of media tracks. [\[ABOUT\]](#references)

This specification defines the URL `about:srcdoc` as a reserved, though unresolvable, [`about:`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6694#section-2) URL, that is used as the [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) of [`iframe` `srcdoc` documents](#485-the-iframe-element). [\[ABOUT\]](#references)

---

A [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) matches `about:blank` if its [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) is "`about`", its [path](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-path) contains a single string "`blank`", its [username](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-username) and [password](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-password) are the empty string, and its [host](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-host) is null.

> [!note]
> Such a URL's [query](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-query) and [fragment](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment) can be non-null. For example, the [URL record](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) created by [parsing](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser) "`about:blank?foo#bar`" [matches `about:blank`](#241-terminology).

A [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) matches `about:srcdoc` if its [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) is "`about`", its [path](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-path) contains a single string "`srcdoc`", its [query](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-query) is null, its [username](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-username) and [password](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-password) are the empty string, and its [host](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-host) is null.

> [!note]
> The reason that [matches `about:srcdoc`](#241-terminology) ensures that the [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url)'s [query](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-query) is null is because it is not possible to create [an `iframe` `srcdoc` document](#485-the-iframe-element) whose [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) has a non-null [query](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-query), unlike [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)s whose [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) [matches `about:blank`](#241-terminology). In other words, the set of all [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url)s that [match `about:srcdoc`](#241-terminology) only vary in their [fragment](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment).

#### 2.4.2 Parsing URLs

Parsing a URL is the process of taking a string and obtaining the [URL record](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) that it represents. While this process is defined in URL, the HTML standard defines several wrappers to abstract base URLs and encodings. [\[URL\]](#references)

> [!note]
> Most new APIs are to use [parse a URL](#242-parsing-urls). Older APIs and HTML elements might have reason to use [encoding-parse a URL](#242-parsing-urls). When a custom base URL is needed or no base URL is desired, the [URL parser](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser) can of course be used directly as well.

To parse a URL, given a string url, relative to a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object or [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) environment, run these steps. They return failure or a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url).
1. Let baseURL be environment's [base URL](#243-document-base-urls), if environment is a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object; otherwise environment's [API base URL](#8132-environment-settings-objects).
2. Return the result of applying the [URL parser](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser) to url, with baseURL.

To encoding-parse a URL, given a string url, relative to a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object or [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) environment, run these steps. They return failure or a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url).
1. Let encoding be [UTF-8](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8).
2. If environment is a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object, then set encoding to environment's [character encoding](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).
3. Otherwise, if environment's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) is a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object, set encoding to environment's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [character encoding](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).
4. Let baseURL be environment's [base URL](#243-document-base-urls), if environment is a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object; otherwise environment's [API base URL](#8132-environment-settings-objects).
5. Return the result of applying the [URL parser](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser) to url, with baseURL and encoding.

To encoding-parse-and-serialize a URL, given a string url, relative to a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object or [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) environment, run these steps. They return failure or a string.
1. Let url be the result of [encoding-parsing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given url, relative to environment.
2. If url is failure, then return failure.
3. Return the result of applying the [URL serializer](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer) to url.

#### 2.4.3 Document base URLs

The document base URL of a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document is the [URL record](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) obtained by running these steps:
1. If document has no [descendant](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) [`base`](#423-the-base-element) element that has an [`href`](#423-the-base-element) attribute, then return document's [fallback base URL](#243-document-base-urls).
2. Otherwise, return the [frozen base URL](#423-the-base-element) of the first [`base`](#423-the-base-element) element in document that has an [`href`](#423-the-base-element) attribute, in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).

The fallback base URL of a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object document is the [URL record](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) obtained by running these steps:
1. If document is [an `iframe` `srcdoc` document](#485-the-iframe-element):
   1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): document's [about base URL](#311-the-document-object) is non-null.
   2. Return document's [about base URL](#311-the-document-object).
2. If document's [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) [matches `about:blank`](#241-terminology) and document's [about base URL](#311-the-document-object) is non-null, then return document's [about base URL](#311-the-document-object).
3. Return document's [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

---

To set the URL for a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document to a [URL record](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) url:
1. Set document's [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) to url.
2. [Respond to base URL changes](#243-document-base-urls) given document.

To respond to base URL changes for a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document:
1. The user agent should update any user interface elements which are displaying affected URLs, or data derived from such URLs, to the user. Examples of such user interface elements would be a status bar that displays a [hyperlink](#461-introduction)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements), or some user interface which displays the URL specified by a [`q`](#457-the-q-element), [`blockquote`](#444-the-blockquote-element), [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element), or [`del`](#472-the-del-element) element's `cite` attribute.
2. Ensure that the CSS [`:link`](#4163-pseudo-classes)/[`:visited`](#4163-pseudo-classes)/etc. [pseudo-classes](https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#pseudo-class) are updated appropriately.
3. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) descendant of document's [shadow-including descendants](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot):
   1. If descendant is a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element whose [result](#41211-processing-model) is a [speculation rules parse result](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results):
      1. Let oldResult be element's [result](#41211-processing-model).
      2. Let newResult be the result of [creating a speculation rules parse result](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results) given element's [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) and element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
      3. [Update speculation rules](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results) given element's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant), oldResult, and newResult.
4. [Consider speculative loads](#7613-processing-model) given document.

> [!example]
> This means that changing the base URL doesn't affect, for example, the image displayed by [`img`](#483-the-img-element) elements. Thus, subsequent accesses of the [`src`](#483-the-img-element) IDL attribute from script will return a new [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute) that might no longer correspond to the image being shown.

### 2.5 Fetching resources

#### 2.5.1 Terminology

A [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) whose [type](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-type) is "`basic`", "`cors`", or "`default`" is CORS-same-origin. [\[FETCH\]](#references)

A [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) whose [type](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-type) is "`opaque`" or "`opaqueredirect`" is CORS-cross-origin.

A [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response)'s unsafe response is its [internal response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-internal-response) if it has one, and the [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) itself otherwise.

To create a potential-CORS request, given a url, destination, corsAttributeState, and an optional *same-origin fallback flag*, run these steps:
1. Let mode be "`no-cors`" if corsAttributeState is [No CORS](#254-cors-settings-attributes), and "`cors`" otherwise.
2. If *same-origin fallback flag* is set and mode is "`no-cors`", set mode to "`same-origin`".
3. Let credentialsMode be "`include`".
4. If corsAttributeState is [Anonymous](#254-cors-settings-attributes), set credentialsMode to "`same-origin`".
5. Return a new [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) whose [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url) is url, [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) is destination, [mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-mode) is mode, [credentials mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode) is credentialsMode, and whose [use-URL-credentials flag](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-use-url-credentials-flag) is set.

#### 2.5.2 Determining the type of a resource

The Content-Type metadata of a resource must be obtained and interpreted in a manner consistent with the requirements of MIME Sniffing. [\[MIMESNIFF\]](#references)

The [computed MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#computed-mime-type) of a resource must be found in a manner consistent with the requirements given in MIME Sniffing. [\[MIMESNIFF\]](#references)

The [rules for sniffing images specifically](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#rules-for-sniffing-images-specifically), the [rules for distinguishing if a resource is text or binary](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#rules-for-text-or-binary), and the [rules for sniffing audio and video specifically](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#rules-for-sniffing-audio-and-video-specifically) are also defined in MIME Sniffing. These rules return a [MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type) as their result. [\[MIMESNIFF\]](#references)

> [!warning]
> It is imperative that the rules in MIME Sniffing be followed exactly. When a user agent uses different heuristics for content type detection than the server expects, security problems can occur. For more details, see MIME Sniffing. [\[MIMESNIFF\]](#references)

#### 2.5.3 Extracting character encodings from [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) elements

The algorithm for extracting a character encoding from a `meta` element, given a string s, is as follows. It returns either a character encoding or nothing.
1. Let position be a pointer into s, initially pointing at the start of the string.
2. *Loop*: Find the first seven characters in s after position that are an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the word "`charset`". If no such match is found, return nothing.
3. Skip any [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) that immediately follow the word "`charset`" (there might not be any).
4. If the next character is not a U+003D EQUALS SIGN (=), then move position to point just before that next character, and jump back to the step labeled *loop*.
5. Skip any [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) that immediately follow the equals sign (there might not be any).
6. Process the next character as follows:

   If it is a U+0022 QUOTATION MARK character (") and there is a later U+0022 QUOTATION MARK character (") in s

   If it is a U+0027 APOSTROPHE character (') and there is a later U+0027 APOSTROPHE character (') in s

   Return the result of [getting an encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-encoding-get) from the substring that is between this character and the next earliest occurrence of this character.

   If it is an unmatched U+0022 QUOTATION MARK character (")

   If it is an unmatched U+0027 APOSTROPHE character (')

   If there is no next character

   Return nothing.

   Otherwise

   Return the result of [getting an encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-encoding-get) from the substring that consists of this character up to but not including the first [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) or U+003B SEMICOLON character (;), or the end of s, whichever comes first.

> [!note]
> This algorithm is distinct from those in the HTTP specifications (for example, HTTP doesn't allow the use of single quotes and requires supporting a backslash-escape mechanism that is not supported by this algorithm). While the algorithm is used in contexts that, historically, were related to HTTP, the syntax as supported by implementations diverged some time ago. [\[HTTP\]](#references)

#### 2.5.4 CORS settings attributes

A CORS settings attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `anonymous` | Anonymous | [Requests](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) for the element will have their [mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-mode) set to "`cors`" and their [credentials mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode) set to "`same-origin`". |
| `use-credentials` | Use Credentials | [Requests](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) for the element will have their [mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-mode) set to "`cors`" and their [credentials mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode) set to "`include`". |

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* is the No CORS state, and its *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[empty value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the [Anonymous](#254-cors-settings-attributes) state.

The majority of fetches governed by [CORS settings attributes](#254-cors-settings-attributes) will be done via the [create a potential-CORS request](#251-terminology) algorithm.

For more modern features, where the request's [mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-mode) is always "`cors`", certain [CORS settings attributes](#254-cors-settings-attributes) have been repurposed to have a slightly different meaning, wherein they only impact the [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request)'s [credentials mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode). To perform this translation, we define the CORS settings attribute credentials mode for a given [CORS settings attribute](#254-cors-settings-attributes) to be determined by switching on the attribute's state:

[No CORS](#254-cors-settings-attributes)

[Anonymous](#254-cors-settings-attributes)

"`same-origin`"

[Use Credentials](#254-cors-settings-attributes)

"`include`"

#### 2.5.5 Referrer policy attributes

A referrer policy attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes). Each [referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy), including the empty string, is a keyword for this attribute, mapping to a state of the same name.

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the empty string state.

The impact of these states on the processing model of various [fetches](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) is defined in more detail throughout this specification, in Fetch, and in Referrer Policy. [\[FETCH\]](#references) [\[REFERRERPOLICY\]](#references)

> [!note]
> Several signals can contribute to which processing model is used for a given [fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch); a [referrer policy attribute](#255-referrer-policy-attributes) is only one of them. In general, the order in which these signals are processed are:
> 1. First, the presence of a [`noreferrer`](#46815-link-type-noreferrer) link type;
> 2. Then, the value of a [referrer policy attribute](#255-referrer-policy-attributes);
> 3. Then, the presence of any [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element with [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute set to [`referrer`](#4251-standard-metadata-names).
> 4. Finally, the \`[`Referrer-Policy`](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy-header-dfn)\` HTTP header.

#### 2.5.6 Nonce attributes

A `nonce` content attribute represents a cryptographic nonce ("number used once") which can be used by Content Security Policy to determine whether or not a given fetch will be allowed to proceed. The value is text. [\[CSP\]](#references)

Elements that have a [`nonce`](#256-nonce-attributes) content attribute ensure that the cryptographic nonce is only exposed to script (and not to side-channels like CSS attribute selectors) by taking the value from the content attribute, moving it into an internal slot named \[\[CryptographicNonce\]\], exposing it to script via the [`HTMLOrSVGOrMathMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom) interface mixin, and setting the content attribute to the empty string. Unless otherwise specified, the slot's value is the empty string.

`element.nonce`

Returns the value set for element's cryptographic nonce. If the setter was not used, this will be the value originally found in the [`nonce`](#256-nonce-attributes) content attribute.

`element.nonce = value`

Updates element's cryptographic nonce value.

The `nonce` IDL attribute must, on getting, return the value of this element's [\[\[CryptographicNonce\]\]](#256-nonce-attributes); and on setting, set this element's [\[\[CryptographicNonce\]\]](#256-nonce-attributes) to the given value.

> [!note]
> Note how the setter for the [`nonce`](#256-nonce-attributes) IDL attribute does not update the corresponding content attribute. This, as well as the below setting of the [`nonce`](#256-nonce-attributes) content attribute to the empty string when an element [becomes browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees), is meant to prevent exfiltration of the nonce value through mechanisms that can easily read content attributes, such as selectors. Learn more in [issue #2369](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/2369), where this behavior was introduced.

The following [attribute change steps](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) are used for the [`nonce`](#256-nonce-attributes) content attribute:
1. If element does not [include](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#include) [`HTMLOrSVGOrMathMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom), then return.
2. If localName is not [`nonce`](#256-nonce-attributes) or namespace is not null, then return.
3. If value is null, then set element's [\[\[CryptographicNonce\]\]](#256-nonce-attributes) to the empty string.
4. Otherwise, set element's [\[\[CryptographicNonce\]\]](#256-nonce-attributes) to value.

Whenever an element [including](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#include) [`HTMLOrSVGOrMathMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom) [becomes browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees), the user agent must execute the following steps on the element:
1. Let CSP list be element's [shadow-including root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot)'s [policy container](#311-the-document-object)'s [CSP list](#717-policy-containers).
2. If CSP list [contains a header-delivered Content Security Policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#contains-a-header-delivered-content-security-policy), and element has a [`nonce`](#256-nonce-attributes) content attribute whose value is not the empty string:
   1. Let nonce be element's [\[\[CryptographicNonce\]\]](#256-nonce-attributes).
   2. [Set an attribute value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) for element using "[`nonce`](#256-nonce-attributes)" and the empty string.
   3. Set element's [\[\[CryptographicNonce\]\]](#256-nonce-attributes) to nonce.

   > [!note]
   > If element's [\[\[CryptographicNonce\]\]](#256-nonce-attributes) were not restored it would be the empty string at this point.

The [cloning steps](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) for elements that [include](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#include) [`HTMLOrSVGOrMathMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom) given node, copy, and subtree are to set copy's [\[\[CryptographicNonce\]\]](#256-nonce-attributes) to node's [\[\[CryptographicNonce\]\]](#256-nonce-attributes).

#### 2.5.7 Lazy loading attributes

A lazy loading attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lazy` | Lazy | Used to defer fetching a resource until some conditions are met. |
| `eager` | Eager | Used to fetch a resource immediately; the default state. |

The attribute directs the user agent to fetch a resource immediately or to defer fetching until some conditions associated with the element are met, according to the attribute's current state.

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the [Eager](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) state.

---

The will lazy load element steps, given an element element, are as follows:
1. If [scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting) for element, then return false.

   > [!note]
   > This is an anti-tracking measure, because if a user agent supported lazy loading when scripting is disabled, it would still be possible for a site to track a user's approximate scroll position throughout a session, by strategically placing images in a page's markup such that a server can track how many images are requested and when.

2. If element's [lazy loading attribute](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) is in the [Lazy](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) state, then return true.
3. Return false.

Each [`img`](#483-the-img-element), [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element), [`video`](#488-the-video-element), and [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) element has associated lazy load resumption steps, initially null.

Each [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element also has associated poster lazy load resumption steps, initially null.

> [!note]
> For [`img`](#483-the-img-element), [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element), [`video`](#488-the-video-element), and [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) elements that [will lazy load](#257-lazy-loading-attributes), these steps are run from the [lazy load intersection observer](#257-lazy-loading-attributes)'s callback or when their [lazy loading attribute](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) is set to the [Eager](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) state. This causes the element to continue loading. For [`video`](#488-the-video-element) elements, [poster lazy load resumption steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) are also run at the same time.

Each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a lazy load intersection observer, initially set to null but can be set to an [`IntersectionObserver`](https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#intersectionobserver) instance.

To start intersection-observing a lazy loading element element, run these steps:
1. Let doc be element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
2. If doc's [lazy load intersection observer](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) is null, set it to a new [`IntersectionObserver`](https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#intersectionobserver) instance, initialized as follows:

   > [!warning]
   > The intention is to use the original value of the [`IntersectionObserver`](https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#intersectionobserver) constructor. However, we're forced to use the JavaScript-exposed constructor in this specification, until Intersection Observer exposes low-level hooks for use in specifications. See bug [w3c/IntersectionObserver#464](https://github.com/w3c/IntersectionObserver/issues/464) which tracks this. [\[INTERSECTIONOBSERVER\]](#references)
   - The callback is these steps, with arguments entries and observer:
     1. For each entry in entries using a method of iteration which does not trigger developer-modifiable array accessors or iteration hooks:
        1. Let resumptionSteps be null.
        2. If entry.[`isIntersecting`](https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dom-intersectionobserverentry-isintersecting) is true, then set resumptionSteps to entry.[`target`](https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dom-intersectionobserverentry-target)'s [lazy load resumption steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes).
        3. Let posterResumptionSteps be null.
        4. If entry.[`isIntersecting`](https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dom-intersectionobserverentry-isintersecting) is true and entry.[`target`](https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dom-intersectionobserverentry-target) is a [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element, then set posterResumptionSteps to the [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element's [poster lazy load resumption steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes).
        5. If resumptionSteps is null and posterResumptionSteps is null, then continue.
        6. [Stop intersection-observing a lazy loading element](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) for entry.[`target`](https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dom-intersectionobserverentry-target).
        7. If resumptionSteps is not null:
           1. Set entry.[`target`](https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dom-intersectionobserverentry-target)'s [lazy load resumption steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) to null.
           2. Invoke resumptionSteps.
        8. If posterResumptionSteps is not null:
           1. Set the [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element's [poster lazy load resumption steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) to null.
           2. Invoke posterResumptionSteps.

        > [!warning]
        > The intention is to use the original value of the [`isIntersecting`](https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dom-intersectionobserverentry-isintersecting) and [`target`](https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dom-intersectionobserverentry-target) getters. See [w3c/IntersectionObserver#464](https://github.com/w3c/IntersectionObserver/issues/464). [\[INTERSECTIONOBSERVER\]](#references)

   - The options is an [`IntersectionObserverInit`](https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dictdef-intersectionobserverinit) dictionary with the following dictionary members: «\[ "`scrollMargin`" → [lazy load scroll margin](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) \]»

     > [!note]
     > This allows for fetching the image during scrolling, when it does not yet — but is about to — intersect the viewport.

     > [!warning]
     > The [lazy load scroll margin](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) suggestions imply dynamic changes to the value, but the [`IntersectionObserver`](https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#intersectionobserver) API does not support changing the scroll margin. See issue [w3c/IntersectionObserver#428](https://github.com/w3c/IntersectionObserver/issues/428).

3. Call doc's [lazy load intersection observer](#257-lazy-loading-attributes)'s [`observe`](https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dom-intersectionobserver-observe) method with element as the argument.

   > [!warning]
   > The intention is to use the original value of the [`observe`](https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dom-intersectionobserver-observe) method. See [w3c/IntersectionObserver#464](https://github.com/w3c/IntersectionObserver/issues/464). [\[INTERSECTIONOBSERVER\]](#references)

To stop intersection-observing a lazy loading element element, run these steps:
1. Let doc be element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
2. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): doc's [lazy load intersection observer](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) is not null.
3. Call doc's [lazy load intersection observer](#257-lazy-loading-attributes)'s [`unobserve`](https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dom-intersectionobserver-unobserve) method with element as the argument.

   > [!warning]
   > The intention is to use the original value of the [`unobserve`](https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#dom-intersectionobserver-unobserve) method. See [w3c/IntersectionObserver#464](https://github.com/w3c/IntersectionObserver/issues/464). [\[INTERSECTIONOBSERVER\]](#references)

[![(This is a tracking vector.)](https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg)](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#24-privacy-concerns) The lazy load scroll margin is an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) value, but with the following suggestions to consider:
- Set a minimum value that most often results in the resources being loaded before they intersect the viewport under normal usage patterns for the given device.
- The typical scrolling speed: increase the value for devices with faster typical scrolling speeds.
- The current scrolling speed or momentum: the UA can attempt to predict where the scrolling will likely stop, and adjust the value accordingly.
- The network quality: increase the value for slow or high-latency connections.
- User preferences can influence the value.

> [!note]
> It is important [for privacy](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#24-privacy-concerns) that the [lazy load scroll margin](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) not leak additional information. For example, the typical scrolling speed on the current device could be imprecise so as to not introduce a new fingerprinting vector.

#### 2.5.8 Blocking attributes

A blocking attribute explicitly indicates that certain operations should be blocked on the fetching of an external resource. The operations that can be blocked are represented by possible blocking tokens, which are strings listed by the following table:

| Possible blocking token | Description |
| --- | --- |
| "`render`" | The element is [potentially render-blocking](#258-blocking-attributes). |

> [!note]
> In the future, there might be more [possible blocking tokens](#258-blocking-attributes).

A [blocking attribute](#258-blocking-attributes) must have a value that is an [unordered set of unique space-separated tokens](#237-space-separated-tokens), each of which are [possible blocking tokens](#258-blocking-attributes). The [supported tokens](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#71-interface-domtokenlist) of a [blocking attribute](#258-blocking-attributes) are the [possible blocking tokens](#258-blocking-attributes). Any element can have at most one [blocking attribute](#258-blocking-attributes).

The blocking tokens set for an element el are the result of the following steps:
1. Let value be the value of el's [blocking attribute](#258-blocking-attributes), or the empty string if no such attribute exists.
2. Set value to value, [converted to ASCII lowercase](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).
3. Let rawTokens be the result of [splitting value on ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).
4. Return a set containing the elements of rawTokens that are [possible blocking tokens](#258-blocking-attributes).

An element is potentially render-blocking if its [blocking tokens set](#258-blocking-attributes) contains "[`render`](#258-blocking-attributes)", or if it is implicitly potentially render-blocking, which will be defined at the individual elements. By default, an element is not [implicitly potentially render-blocking](#258-blocking-attributes).

#### 2.5.9 Fetch priority attributes

A fetch priority attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `high` | High | Signals a high-priority [fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) relative to other resources with the same [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination). |
| `low` | Low | Signals a low-priority [fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) relative to other resources with the same [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination). |
| `auto` | Auto | Signals automatic determination of [fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) priority relative to other resources with the same [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination). |

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the [Auto](#259-fetch-priority-attributes) state.

### 2.6 Common DOM interfaces

#### 2.6.1 Reflecting content attributes in IDL attributes

The building blocks for reflecting are as follows:
- A reflected target is an element or [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) object. It is typically clear from context and typically identical to the interface of the [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes). It is always identical to that interface when it is an [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) object.
- A reflected IDL attribute is an attribute interface member.
- A reflected content attribute name is a string. When the [reflected target](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) is an element, it represents the local name of a content attribute whose namespace is null. When the [reflected target](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) is an [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) object, it represents a key of the [reflected target](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes)'s [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface)'s [internal content attribute map](#41374-accessibility-semantics).

A [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) can be defined to reflect a [reflected content attribute name](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) of a [reflected target](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes). In general this means that the IDL attribute getter returns the current value of the content attribute, and the setter changes the value of the content attribute to the given value.

[Reflected targets](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) have these associated algorithms:
- get the element: takes no arguments; returns an element.
- get the content attribute: takes no arguments; returns null or a string.
- set the content attribute: takes a string value; returns nothing.
- delete the content attribute: takes no arguments; returns nothing.

For a [reflected target](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) that is an element element, these are defined as follows:

[get the element](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes)
1. Return element.

[get the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes)
1. Let attribute be the result of [getting an attribute by namespace and local name](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) given null, the [reflected content attribute name](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), and element.
2. If attribute is null, then return null.
3. Return attribute's [value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#492-interface-attr).

[set the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) with a string value
1. [Set an attribute value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) given element, the [reflected content attribute name](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), and value.

[delete the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes)
1. [Remove an attribute by namespace and local name](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) given null, the [reflected content attribute name](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), and element.

For a [reflected target](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) that is an [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) object elementInternals, they are defined as follows:

[get the element](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes)
1. Return elementInternals's [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface).

[get the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes)
1. If elementInternals's [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface)'s [internal content attribute map](#41374-accessibility-semantics)\[the [reflected content attribute name](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes)\] [does not exist](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then return null.
2. Return elementInternals's [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface)'s [internal content attribute map](#41374-accessibility-semantics)\[the [reflected content attribute name](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes)\].

[set the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) with a string value
1. [Set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) elementInternals's [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface)'s [internal content attribute map](#41374-accessibility-semantics)\[the [reflected content attribute name](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes)\] to value.

[delete the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes)
1. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) elementInternals's [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface)'s [internal content attribute map](#41374-accessibility-semantics)\[the [reflected content attribute name](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes)\].

> [!note]
> This results in somewhat redundant data structures for [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) objects as their [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface)'s [internal content attribute map](#41374-accessibility-semantics) cannot be directly manipulated and as such reflection is only happening in a single direction. This approach was nevertheless chosen to make it less error-prone to define IDL attributes that are shared between [reflected targets](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) and benefit from common API semantics.

---

IDL attributes of type [`DOMString`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-DOMString) or `DOMString?` that [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) [enumerated](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) content attributes can be limited to only known values. Per the processing models below, those will cause the getters for such IDL attributes to only return keywords for those enumerated attributes, or the empty string or null.

If a [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) has the type [`DOMString`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-DOMString):
- The getter steps are:
  1. Let element be the result of running [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [get the element](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
  2. Let contentAttributeValue be the result of running [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [get the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
  3. Let attributeDefinition be the attribute definition of element's content attribute whose namespace is null and local name is the [reflected content attribute name](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
  4. If attributeDefinition indicates it is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) and the [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) is defined to be [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes):
     1. If contentAttributeValue does not correspond to any state of attributeDefinition (e.g., it is null and there is no *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)*), or if it is in a state of attributeDefinition with no associated keyword value, then return the empty string.
     2. Return the [canonical keyword](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) for the state of attributeDefinition that contentAttributeValue corresponds to.
  5. If contentAttributeValue is null, then return the empty string.
  6. Return contentAttributeValue.
- The setter steps are to run [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [set the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) with the given value.

If a [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) has the type `DOMString?`:
- The getter steps are:
  1. Let element be the result of running [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [get the element](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
  2. Let contentAttributeValue be the result of running [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [get the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
  3. Let attributeDefinition be the attribute definition of element's content attribute whose namespace is null and local name is the [reflected content attribute name](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
  4. If attributeDefinition indicates it is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes):
     1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): the [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) is [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
     2. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): contentAttributeValue corresponds to a state of attributeDefinition.
     3. If contentAttributeValue corresponds to a state of attributeDefinition with no associated keyword value, then return null.
     4. Return the [canonical keyword](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) for the state of attributeDefinition that contentAttributeValue corresponds to.
  5. Return contentAttributeValue.
- The setter steps are:
  1. If the given value is null, then run [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [delete the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
  2. Otherwise, run [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [set the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) with the given value.

If a [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) has the type [`USVString`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-USVString), optionally treated as a URL:
- The getter steps are:
  1. Let element be the result of running [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [get the element](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
  2. Let contentAttributeValue be the result of running [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [get the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
  3. If the [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) is [treated as a URL](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes):
     1. If contentAttributeValue is null, then return the empty string.
     2. Let urlString be the result of [encoding-parsing-and-serializing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given contentAttributeValue, relative to element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
     3. If urlString is not failure, then return urlString.
  4. Return contentAttributeValue, [converted to a scalar value string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).
- The setter steps are to run [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [set the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) with the given value.

If a [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) has the type [`boolean`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-boolean):
- The getter steps are:
  1. Let contentAttributeValue be the result of running [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [get the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
  2. If contentAttributeValue is null, then return false.
  3. Return true.
- The setter steps are:
  1. If the given value is false, then run [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [delete the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
  2. If the given value is true, then run [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [set the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) with the empty string.

> [!note]
> This corresponds to the rules for [boolean content attributes](#232-boolean-attributes).

If a [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) has the type [`long`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-long), optionally limited to only non-negative numbers and optionally with a default value defaultValue:
- The getter steps are:
  1. Let contentAttributeValue be the result of running [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [get the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
  2. If contentAttributeValue is not null:
     1. Let parsedValue be the result of [integer parsing](#2341-signed-integers) contentAttributeValue if the [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) is not [limited to only non-negative numbers](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes); otherwise the result of [non-negative integer parsing](#2342-non-negative-integers) contentAttributeValue.
     2. If parsedValue is not an error and is within the [`long`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-long) range, then return parsedValue.
  3. If the [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) has a [default value](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), then return defaultValue.
  4. If the [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) is [limited to only non-negative numbers](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), then return −1.
  5. Return 0.
- The setter steps are:
  1. If the [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) is [limited to only non-negative numbers](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) and the given value is negative, then throw an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
  2. Run [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [set the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) with the given value converted to the shortest possible string representing the number as a [valid integer](#2341-signed-integers).

If a [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) has the type [`unsigned long`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-unsigned-long), optionally limited to only positive numbers, limited to only positive numbers with fallback, or clamped to the range \[clampedMin, clampedMax\], and optionally with a [default value](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) defaultValue:
- The getter steps are:
  1. Let contentAttributeValue be the result of running [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [get the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
  2. Let minimum be 0.
  3. If the [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) is [limited to only positive numbers](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) or [limited to only positive numbers with fallback](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), then set minimum to 1.
  4. If the [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) is [clamped to the range](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), then set minimum to clampedMin.
  5. Let maximum be 2147483647 if the [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) is not [clamped to the range](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes); otherwise clampedMax.
  6. If contentAttributeValue is not null:
     1. Let parsedValue be the result of [non-negative integer parsing](#2342-non-negative-integers) contentAttributeValue.
     2. If parsedValue is not an error and is in the range minimum to maximum, inclusive, then return parsedValue.
     3. If parsedValue is not an error and the [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) is [clamped to the range](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes):
        1. If parsedValue is less than minimum, then return minimum.
        2. Return maximum.
  7. If the [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) has a [default value](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), then return defaultValue.
  8. Return minimum.
- The setter steps are:
  1. If the [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) is [limited to only positive numbers](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) and the given value is 0, then throw an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
  2. Let minimum be 0.
  3. If the [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) is [limited to only positive numbers](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) or [limited to only positive numbers with fallback](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), then set minimum to 1.
  4. Let newValue be minimum.
  5. If the [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) has a [default value](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), then set newValue to defaultValue.
  6. If the given value is in the range minimum to 2147483647, inclusive, then set newValue to it.
  7. Run [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [set the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) with newValue converted to the shortest possible string representing the number as a [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers).

  > [!note]
  > [Clamped to the range](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) has no effect on the setter steps.

If a [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) has the type [`double`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-double), optionally [limited to only positive numbers](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) and optionally with a [default value](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) defaultValue:
- The getter steps are:
  1. Let contentAttributeValue be the result of running [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [get the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
  2. If contentAttributeValue is not null:
     1. Let parsedValue be the result of [floating-point number parsing](#2343-floating-point-numbers) contentAttributeValue.
     2. If parsedValue is not an error and is greater than 0, then return parsedValue.
     3. If parsedValue is not an error and the [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) is not [limited to only positive numbers](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), then return parsedValue.
  3. If the [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) has a [default value](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), then return defaultValue.
  4. Return 0.
- The setter steps are:
  1. If the [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) is [limited to only positive numbers](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) and the given value is not greater than 0, then return.
  2. Run [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [set the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) with the given value, converted to the [best representation of the number as a floating-point number](#2343-floating-point-numbers).

> [!note]
> The values Infinity and Not-a-Number (NaN) values throw an exception on setting, as defined in Web IDL. [\[WEBIDL\]](#references)

If a [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) has the type [`DOMTokenList`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#71-interface-domtokenlist), then its getter steps are to return a [`DOMTokenList`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#71-interface-domtokenlist) object whose associated element is [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) and associated attribute's local name is the [reflected content attribute name](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes). Specification authors cannot reflect IDL attributes of this type on [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface).

If a [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) has the type `T?`, where T is either [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) or an interface that inherits from [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), then with attr being the [reflected content attribute name](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes):
- Its [reflected target](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) has an explicitly set attr-element, which is a weak reference to an element or null. It is initially null.
- Its [reflected target](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) reflectedTarget has a get the attr-associated element algorithm, that runs these steps:
  1. Let element be the result of running reflectedTarget's [get the element](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
  2. Let contentAttributeValue be the result of running reflectedTarget's [get the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
  3. If reflectedTarget's [explicitly set attr-element](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) is not null:
     1. If reflectedTarget's [explicitly set attr-element](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) is a [descendant](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) of any of element's [shadow-including ancestors](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot), then return reflectedTarget's [explicitly set attr-element](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
     2. Return null.
  4. Otherwise, if contentAttributeValue is not null, return the first element candidate, in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), that meets the following criteria:
     - candidate's [root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) is the same as element's [root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees);
     - candidate's [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) is contentAttributeValue; and
     - candidate [implements](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#implements) T.

     If no such element exists, then return null.

  5. Return null.

- The getter steps are to return the result of running [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [get the attr-associated element](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
- The setter steps are:
  1. If the given value is null:
     1. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [explicitly set attr-element](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) to null.
     2. Run [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [delete the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
     3. Return.
  2. Run [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [set the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) with the empty string.
  3. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [explicitly set attr-element](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) to a weak reference to the given value.
- For element [reflected targets](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) only: the following [attribute change steps](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), given element, localName, oldValue, value, and namespace, are used to synchronize between the content attribute and the IDL attribute:
  1. If localName is not attr or namespace is not null, then return.
  2. Set element's [explicitly set attr-element](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) to null.

> [!note]
> [Reflected IDL attributes](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) of this type are strongly encouraged to have their identifier end in "`Element`" for consistency.

If a [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) has the type `FrozenArray<T>?`, where T is either [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) or an interface that inherits from [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), then with attr being the [reflected content attribute name](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes):
- Its [reflected target](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) has an explicitly set attr-elements, which is either a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of weak references to elements or null. It is initially null.
- Its [reflected target](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) has a cached attr-associated elements, which is a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of elements. It is initially « ».
- Its [reflected target](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) has a cached attr-associated elements object, which is a `FrozenArray<T>?`. It is initially null.
- Its [reflected target](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) reflectedTarget has a get the attr-associated elements algorithm, which runs these steps:
  1. Let elements be an empty [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).
  2. Let element be the result of running reflectedTarget's [get the element](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
  3. If reflectedTarget's [explicitly set attr-elements](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) is not null:
     1. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) attrElement in reflectedTarget's [explicitly set attr-elements](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes):
        1. If attrElement is not a [descendant](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) of any of element's [shadow-including ancestors](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot), then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
        2. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) attrElement to elements.
  4. Otherwise:
     1. Let contentAttributeValue be the result of running reflectedTarget's [get the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
     2. If contentAttributeValue is null, then return null.
     3. Let tokens be contentAttributeValue, [split on ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).
     4. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) id of tokens:
        1. Let candidate be the first element, in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), that meets the following criteria:
           - candidate's [root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) is the same as element's [root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees);
           - candidate's [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) is id; and
           - candidate [implements](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#implements) T.

           If no such element exists, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).

        2. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) candidate to elements.

  5. Return elements.

- The getter steps are:
  1. Let elements be the result of running [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [get the attr-associated elements](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
  2. If the contents of elements is equal to the contents of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [cached attr-associated elements](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), then return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [cached attr-associated elements object](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
  3. Let elementsAsFrozenArray be elements, [converted](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-type-mapping) to a `FrozenArray<T>?`.
  4. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [cached attr-associated elements](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) to elements.
  5. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [cached attr-associated elements object](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) to elementsAsFrozenArray.
  6. Return elementsAsFrozenArray.

  > [!note]
  > This extra caching layer is necessary to preserve the invariant that `element.reflectedElements === element.reflectedElements`.

- The setter steps are:
  1. If the given value is null:
     1. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [explicitly set attr-elements](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) to null.
     2. Run [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [delete the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
     3. Return.
  2. Run [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [set the content attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) with the empty string.
  3. Let elements be an empty [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).
  4. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) element in the given value:
     1. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) a weak reference to element to elements.
  5. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [explicitly set attr-elements](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) to elements.
- For element [reflected targets](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) only: the following [attribute change steps](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), given element, localName, oldValue, value, and namespace, are used to synchronize between the content attribute and the IDL attribute:
  1. If localName is not attr or namespace is not null, then return.
  2. Set element's [explicitly set attr-elements](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) to null.

> [!note]
> [Reflected IDL attributes](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) of this type are strongly encouraged to have their identifier end in "`Elements`" for consistency.

#### 2.6.2 Using reflect via IDL extended attributes

[Reflection](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) can be used from IDL through [extended attributes](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-extended-attribute). `[Reflect]`, `[ReflectSetter]`, `[ReflectURL]`, `[ReflectNonNegative]`, `[ReflectPositive]`, and `[ReflectPositiveWithFallback]` all trigger [reflection](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes). These must either take no arguments, or take a string; they must not appear on anything other than an interface member attribute; and only one of these can be used at a time.

For one of these primary reflection [extended attributes](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-extended-attribute), its [reflected content attribute name](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) is the string value it takes, if one is provided; otherwise it is the IDL attribute name [converted to ASCII lowercase](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).

IDL attributes with the [`[Reflect]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes) [extended attribute](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-extended-attribute) must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) [`[Reflect]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes)'s [reflected content attribute name](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

IDL attributes with the [`[ReflectSetter]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes) [extended attribute](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-extended-attribute) on setting must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) [`[ReflectSetter]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes)'s [reflected content attribute name](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

The [`[ReflectURL]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes) [extended attribute](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-extended-attribute) must only appear on attributes with a type of [`USVString`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-USVString).

IDL attributes with the [`[ReflectURL]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes) [extended attribute](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-extended-attribute) must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), [as a URL](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), [`[ReflectURL]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes)'s [reflected content attribute name](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

The [`[ReflectNonNegative]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes) [extended attribute](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-extended-attribute) must only appear on attributes with a type of [`long`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-long).

IDL attributes with the [`[ReflectNonNegative]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes) [extended attribute](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-extended-attribute) must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), [limited to only non-negative numbers](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), [`[ReflectNonNegative]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes)'s [reflected content attribute name](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

The [`[ReflectPositive]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes) and [`[ReflectPositiveWithFallback]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes) [extended attributes](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-extended-attribute) must only appear on attributes with a type of [`double`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-double) or [`unsigned
  long`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-unsigned-long).

IDL attributes with the [`[ReflectPositive]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes) [extended attribute](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-extended-attribute) must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), [limited to only positive numbers](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), [`[ReflectPositive]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes)'s [reflected content attribute name](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

IDL attributes with the [`[ReflectPositiveWithFallback]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes) [extended attribute](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-extended-attribute) must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), [limited to only positive numbers with fallback](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), [`[ReflectPositiveWithFallback]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes)'s [reflected content attribute name](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

---

To supplement the above [extended attributes](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-extended-attribute) we also introduce `[ReflectRange]`, and `[ReflectDefault]`. These augment how [reflection](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) works and also must only appear on interface member attributes.

The [`[ReflectRange]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes) [extended attribute](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-extended-attribute) must take an integer list limited to two values. It must only be used on attributes with a type of [`unsigned long`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-unsigned-long). Additionally, it must also only appear alongside [`[Reflect]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes).

IDL attributes with the [`[ReflectRange]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes) [extended attribute](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-extended-attribute) are [clamped to the range](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) \[clampedMin, clampedMax\] where clampedMin is the first, and clampedMax is the second argument to the list provided to [`[ReflectRange]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes).

The [`[ReflectDefault]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes) [extended attribute](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-extended-attribute) must only be used on attributes with a type of [`double`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-double), [`long`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-long), or [`unsigned long`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-unsigned-long). When used on an attribute of type [`double`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-double), it must take a decimal; otherwise it must take an integer. Additionally, it must also only appear alongside [`[Reflect]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes), [`[ReflectNonNegative]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes), [`[ReflectPositive]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes), or [`[ReflectPositiveWithFallback]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes).

IDL attributes with the [`[ReflectDefault]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes) [extended attribute](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-extended-attribute) have a [default value](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) provided by the argument provided to [`[ReflectDefault]`](#262-using-reflect-via-idl-extended-attributes).

#### 2.6.3 Using reflect in specifications

[Reflection](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) is primarily about improving web developer ergonomics by giving them typed access to content attributes through [reflected IDL attributes](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes). The ultimate source of truth, which the web platform builds upon, is the content attributes themselves. That is, specification authors must not use the [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) getter or setter steps, but instead must use the content attribute presence and value. (Or an abstraction on top, such as the state of an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes).)

Two important exceptions to this are [reflected IDL attributes](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) whose type is one of the following:
- `T?`, where T is either [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) or an interface that inherits from [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element)
- `FrozenArray<T>?`, where T is either [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) or an interface that inherits from [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element)

For those, specification authors must use the [reflected target](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes)'s [get the attr-associated element](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) and [get the attr-associated elements](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), respectively. The content attribute presence and value must not be used as they cannot be fully synchronized with the [reflected IDL attribute](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

A [reflected target](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes)'s [explicitly set attr-element](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), [explicitly set attr-elements](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), [cached attr-associated elements](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes), and [cached attr-associated elements object](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) are to be treated as internal implementation details and not to be built upon.

#### 2.6.4 Collections

The [`HTMLFormControlsCollection`](#2642-the-htmlformcontrolscollection-interface) and [`HTMLOptionsCollection`](#2643-the-htmloptionscollection-interface) interfaces are [collections](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4210-old-style-collections-nodelist-and-htmlcollection) derived from the [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) interface. The [`HTMLAllCollection`](#2641-the-htmlallcollection-interface) interface is a [collection](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4210-old-style-collections-nodelist-and-htmlcollection), but is not so derived.

##### 2.6.4.1 The [`HTMLAllCollection`](#2641-the-htmlallcollection-interface) interface

The [`HTMLAllCollection`](#2641-the-htmlallcollection-interface) interface is used for the legacy [`document.all`](#1633-other-elements-attributes-and-apis) attribute. It operates similarly to [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection); the main differences are that it allows a staggering variety of different (ab)uses of its methods to all end up returning something, and that it can be called as a function as an alternative to property access.

> [!note]
> All [`HTMLAllCollection`](#2641-the-htmlallcollection-interface) objects are rooted at a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) and have a filter that matches all elements, so the elements [represented by the collection](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4210-old-style-collections-nodelist-and-htmlcollection) of an [`HTMLAllCollection`](#2641-the-htmlallcollection-interface) object consist of all the descendant elements of the root [`Document`](#311-the-document-object).

Objects that implement the [`HTMLAllCollection`](#2641-the-htmlallcollection-interface) interface are [legacy platform objects](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-legacy-platform-object) with an additional \[\[Call\]\] internal method described in the [section below](#26411-call--thisargument-argumentslist-). They also have an [\[\[IsHTMLDDA\]\]](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-IsHTMLDDA-internal-slot) internal slot.

> [!note]
> Objects that implement the [`HTMLAllCollection`](#2641-the-htmlallcollection-interface) interface have several unusual behaviors, due of the fact that they have an [\[\[IsHTMLDDA\]\]](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-IsHTMLDDA-internal-slot) internal slot:
