It is initially set when the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object is created, and can change during the lifetime of the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) only upon setting [`document.domain`](#7112-relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction). A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) can differ from the [origin](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-origin) of its [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document); for example when a [child navigable](#7313-child-navigables) is [created](#7313-child-navigables), its [active document](#731-navigables)'s [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is inherited from its [parent](#731-navigables)'s [active document](#731-navigables)'s [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), even though its [active document](#731-navigables)'s [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is [`about:blank`](#219-dependencies). [\[DOM\]](#references)

When a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is created by a [script](#8141-scripts) using the [`createDocument()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#451-interface-domimplementation) or [`createHTMLDocument()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#451-interface-domimplementation) methods, the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is [ready for post-load tasks](#1327-the-end) immediately.

The document's referrer is a string (representing a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url)) that can be set when the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is created. If it is not explicitly set, then its value is the empty string.

#### 3.1.1 The [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object

DOM defines a [`Document`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) interface, which this specification extends significantly.

```webidl
enum DocumentReadyState { "loading", "interactive", "complete" };
enum DocumentVisibilityState { "visible", "hidden" };
typedef (HTMLScriptElement or SVGScriptElement) HTMLOrSVGScriptElement;

[LegacyOverrideBuiltIns]
partial interface Document {
  static Document parseHTMLUnsafe((TrustedHTML or DOMString) html, optional (ParseHTMLUnsafeOptions or TrustedHTMLParserOptions) options = {});
  static Document parseHTML(DOMString html, optional SetHTMLOptions options = {});

  // resource metadata management
  [PutForwards=href, LegacyUnforgeable] readonly attribute Location? location;
  attribute USVString domain;
  readonly attribute USVString referrer;
  attribute USVString cookie;
  readonly attribute DOMString lastModified;
  readonly attribute DocumentReadyState readyState;

  // DOM tree accessors
  getter object (DOMString name);
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString title;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString dir;
  [CEReactions] attribute HTMLElement? body;
  readonly attribute HTMLHeadElement? head;
  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection images;
  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection embeds;
  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection plugins;
  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection links;
  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection forms;
  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection scripts;
  NodeList getElementsByName(DOMString elementName);
  readonly attribute HTMLOrSVGScriptElement? currentScript; // classic scripts in a document tree only

  // dynamic markup insertion
  [CEReactions] Document open(optional DOMString unused1, optional DOMString unused2); // both arguments are ignored
  WindowProxy? open(USVString url, DOMString name, DOMString features);
  [CEReactions] undefined close();
  [CEReactions] undefined write((TrustedHTML or DOMString)... text);
  [CEReactions] undefined writeln((TrustedHTML or DOMString)... text);

  // user interaction
  readonly attribute WindowProxy? defaultView;
  boolean hasFocus();
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString designMode;
  [CEReactions] boolean execCommand(DOMString commandId, optional boolean showUI = false, optional DOMString value = "");
  boolean queryCommandEnabled(DOMString commandId);
  boolean queryCommandIndeterm(DOMString commandId);
  boolean queryCommandState(DOMString commandId);
  boolean queryCommandSupported(DOMString commandId);
  DOMString queryCommandValue(DOMString commandId);
  readonly attribute boolean hidden;
  readonly attribute DocumentVisibilityState visibilityState;

  // special event handler IDL attributes that only apply to Document objects
  [LegacyLenientThis] attribute EventHandler onreadystatechange;
  attribute EventHandler onvisibilitychange;

  // also has obsolete members
};
Document includes GlobalEventHandlers;
```

Each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a policy container (a [policy container](#717-policy-containers)), initially a new policy container, which contains policies which apply to the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object).

Each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a permissions policy, which is a [permissions policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-feature-policy/#permissions-policy), which is initially empty.

Each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a module map, which is a [module map](#8167-module-related-host-hooks), initially empty.

Each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has an opener policy, which is an [opener policy](#713-cross-origin-opener-policies), initially a new opener policy.

Each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has an is initial `about:blank`, which is a boolean, initially false.

Each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a during-loading navigation ID for WebDriver BiDi, which is a [navigation ID](#7421-supporting-concepts) or null, initially null.

> [!note]
> As the name indicates, this is used for interfacing with the WebDriver BiDi specification, which needs to be informed about certain occurrences during the early parts of the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s lifecycle, in a way that ties them to the original [navigation ID](#7421-supporting-concepts) used when the navigation that created this [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) was the [ongoing navigation](#7425-aborting-navigation). This eventually gets set back to null, after WebDriver BiDi considers the loading process to be finished. [\[BIDI\]](#references)

Each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has an about base URL, which is a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) or null, initially null.

> [!note]
> This is only populated for "`about:`"-schemed [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)s.

Each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a bfcache blocking details, which is a [set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) of [not restored reason details](#728-the-notrestoredreasons-interface), initially empty.

Each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has an open dialogs list, which is a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) elements, initially empty.

#### 3.1.2 The [`DocumentOrShadowRoot`](#312-the-documentorshadowroot-interface) interface

DOM defines the [`DocumentOrShadowRoot`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#425-mixin-documentorshadowroot) mixin, which this specification extends.

```webidl
partial interface mixin DocumentOrShadowRoot {
  readonly attribute Element? activeElement;
};
```

#### 3.1.3 Ancestor origins

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object has an associated internal ancestor origin objects list, initially null.

The internal ancestor origin objects list creation steps given a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object document and a [referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy) referrerPolicy are:
1. Let output be « ».
2. Let parentDoc be document's [container document](#7313-child-navigables).
3. If parentDoc is null, then return output.
4. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): parentDoc is [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents).
5. Let ancestorOrigins be parentDoc's [internal ancestor origin objects list](#313-ancestor-origins).
6. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): ancestorOrigins is not null.
7. Let masked be false.
8. If referrerPolicy is "`no-referrer`", then set masked to true.
9. Otherwise, if referrerPolicy is "`same-origin`" and parentDoc's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is not [same origin](#711-origins) with document's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), then set masked to true.

   > [!note]
   > Since [mixed content](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-mixed-content/#mixed-content) checks prevent [non-secure context](#8135-secure-contexts) [environments](#8131-environments) in [secure context](#8135-secure-contexts) [environments](#8131-environments), there's no need to check for [secure contexts](#8135-secure-contexts) for "`strict-origin`", "`strict-origin-when-cross-origin`", and "`no-referrer-when-downgrade`". The "`origin`" and "`origin-when-cross-origin`" values also don't need special treatment since we're at most exposing an [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) here.

10. If masked is true, then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) a new [opaque origin](#711-origins) to output.
11. Otherwise, [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) parentDoc's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) to output.
12. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) ancestorOrigin of ancestorOrigins:
    1. If masked is true and ancestorOrigin is [same origin](#711-origins) with parentDoc's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) a new [opaque origin](#711-origins) to output and [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
    2. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) ancestorOrigin to output and set masked to false.

       > [!note]
       > Setting masked to false here doesn't imply that all further ancestors' origins are necessarily exposed. They might have been previously masked when an ancestor document ran these steps, and the resulting list is used as a starting point when a child document is created (see step 5 above).

13. Return output.

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object has an associated ancestor origins list, initially null.

The ancestor origins list creation steps given a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object document are:
1. Let ancestorOrigins be document's [internal ancestor origin objects list](#313-ancestor-origins).
2. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): ancestorOrigins is not null.
3. Let output be « ».
4. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) origin of ancestorOrigins:
   1. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) the [serialization](#711-origins) of origin to output.
5. Return a new [`DOMStringList`](#265-the-domstringlist-interface) object whose associated list is output.

> [!example]
> Consider a [top-level browsing context](#7322-related-browsing-contexts) document with the URL `https://a.example/top`:
> 
> ```html
> <!doctype html>
> <title>top</title>
> <iframe referrerpolicy="no-referrer" src="https://a.example/child"></iframe>
> ```
> 
> The child document:
> 
> ```html
> <!doctype html>
> <title>child</title>
> <iframe src="https://b.example/grandchild"></iframe>
> <script>
>  console.log([...location.ancestorOrigins]);
> </script>
> ```
> 
> The grandchild document:
> 
> ```html
> <!doctype html>
> <title>grandchild</title>
> <script>
>  console.log([...location.ancestorOrigins]);
> </script>
> ```
> 
> When the child's [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object is created, its parent's origin is masked because the [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) element's [`referrerpolicy`](#485-the-iframe-element) attribute's value is "`no-referrer`", even though the documents are [same origin](#711-origins). The value logged is « "`null`" ».
> 
> When the grandchild's [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object is created, the child's [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object's [internal ancestor origin objects list](#313-ancestor-origins) (which contains a single [opaque origin](#711-origins)) is used as a starting point, and the child's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is added to the list. The value logged is thus « "`https://a.example`", "`null`" ».

> [!example]
> If we consider the previous example but the [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) element in the top document has no [`referrerpolicy`](#485-the-iframe-element) attribute, and instead the [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) element in the child document has `referrerpolicy="no-referrer"`.
> 
> In this case, the top document's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is added to the child's [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object's [internal ancestor origin objects list](#313-ancestor-origins). The value logged is « "`https://a.example`" ».
> 
> For the grandchild, the child's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is masked as an [opaque origin](#711-origins). Since the top document's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is [same origin](#711-origins) with the child document's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), it is also masked. The value logged is thus « "`null`", "`null`" ».

> [!example]
> In this example, we show that the top-level document's origin is not masked even though there's a descendant same-origin document whose origin *is* masked, since there's a cross-origin document in between.
> - Top-level with URL `https://a.example/top`
> 
>   ```html
>   <iframe src="https://b.example/child"></iframe>
>   ```
> 
>   The [ancestor origins list](#313-ancestor-origins) associated list is « ».
> 
> - Child with URL `https://b.example/child`
> 
>   ```html
>   <iframe src="https://a.example/grandchild"></iframe>
>   ```
> 
>   The [ancestor origins list](#313-ancestor-origins) associated list is « "`https://a.example`" ».
> 
> - Grandchild with URL `https://a.example/grandchild`
> 
>   ```html
>   <iframe src="https://c.example/great-grandchild"
>           referrerpolicy="no-referrer"></iframe>
>   ```
> 
>   The [ancestor origins list](#313-ancestor-origins) associated list is « "`https://b.example`", "`https://a.example`" ».
> 
> - Great-grandchild with URL `https://c.example/great-grandchild`
> 
>   The [ancestor origins list](#313-ancestor-origins) associated list is « "`null`", "`https://b.example`", "`https://a.example`" ». The top-level origin is not masked.

> [!example]
> If we consider the previous example but the top-level document's [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) also has `referrerpolicy="no-referrer"`, then the resulting [ancestor origins list](#313-ancestor-origins) associated list for each document would be:
> - Top-level: « »
> - Child: « "`null`" »
> - Grandchild: « "`https://b.example`", "`null`" »
> - Great-grandchild: « "`null`", "`https://b.example`", "`null`" ». The top-level origin is masked because it was masked when the child document ran the [internal ancestor origin objects list creation steps](#313-ancestor-origins), and that result is passed on to the grandchild document's [internal ancestor origin objects list creation steps](#313-ancestor-origins), and so on.

#### 3.1.4 Resource metadata management

`document.referrer`

Returns the [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) of the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) from which the user navigated to this one, unless it was blocked or there was no such document, in which case it returns the empty string.

The [`noreferrer`](#46815-link-type-noreferrer) link type can be used to block the referrer.

The `referrer` attribute must return [the document's referrer](#31-documents).

---

`document.cookie [ = value ]`

Returns the HTTP cookies that apply to the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object). If there are no cookies or cookies can't be applied to this resource, the empty string will be returned.

Can be set, to add a new cookie to the element's set of HTTP cookies.

If the contents are [sandboxed into an opaque origin](#715-sandboxing) (e.g., in an [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) with the [`sandbox`](#485-the-iframe-element) attribute), a ["`SecurityError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) will be thrown on getting and setting.

The `cookie` attribute represents the cookies of the resource identified by the document's [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

> [!note]
> Using the synchronous [`document.cookie`](#314-resource-metadata-management) API can be a source of performance issues. The Cookie Store API can be used instead, as it provides an asynchronous way to handle cookies to avoid performance issues. See the [Cookie Store API introduction](https://cookiestore.spec.whatwg.org/#intro) for more information. [\[COOKIESTORE\]](#references)

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object that falls into one of the following conditions is a cookie-averse `Document` object:
- A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object whose [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) is null.
- A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) whose [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document)'s [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) is not an [HTTP(S) scheme](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#http-scheme).

[![(This is a tracking vector.)](https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg)](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#24-privacy-concerns) On getting, if the document is a [cookie-averse `Document` object](#314-resource-metadata-management), then the user agent must return the empty string. Otherwise, if the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is an [opaque origin](#711-origins), the user agent must throw a ["`SecurityError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException). Otherwise, the user agent must return the [cookie-string](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc6265.html#sane-cookie-syntax) for the document's [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) for a "non-HTTP" API, decoded using [UTF-8 decode without BOM](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8-decode-without-bom). [\[COOKIES\]](#references)

On setting, if the document is a [cookie-averse `Document` object](#314-resource-metadata-management), then the user agent must do nothing. Otherwise, if the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is an [opaque origin](#711-origins), the user agent must throw a ["`SecurityError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException). Otherwise, the user agent must act as it would when [receiving a set-cookie-string](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc6265.html#storage-model) for the document's [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) via a "non-HTTP" API, consisting of the new value [encoded as UTF-8](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8-encode). [\[COOKIES\]](#references) [\[ENCODING\]](#references)

> [!note]
> Since the [`cookie`](#314-resource-metadata-management) attribute is accessible across frames, the path restrictions on cookies are only a tool to help manage which cookies are sent to which parts of the site, and are not in any way a security feature.

> [!warning]
> The [`cookie`](#314-resource-metadata-management) attribute's getter and setter synchronously access shared state. Since there is no locking mechanism, other browsing contexts in a multiprocess user agent can modify cookies while scripts are running. A site could, for instance, try to read a cookie, increment its value, then write it back out, using the new value of the cookie as a unique identifier for the session; if the site does this twice in two different browser windows at the same time, it might end up using the same "unique" identifier for both sessions, with potentially disastrous effects.

---

`document.lastModified`

Returns the date of the last modification to the document, as reported by the server, in the form "`MM/DD/YYYY hh:mm:ss`", in the user's local time zone.

If the last modification date is not known, the current time is returned instead.

The `lastModified` attribute, on getting, must return the date and time of the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s source file's last modification, in the user's local time zone, in the following format:
1. The month component of the date.
2. A U+002F SOLIDUS character (/).
3. The day component of the date.
4. A U+002F SOLIDUS character (/).
5. The year component of the date.
6. A U+0020 SPACE character.
7. The hours component of the time.
8. A U+003A COLON character (:).
9. The minutes component of the time.
10. A U+003A COLON character (:).
11. The seconds component of the time.

All the numeric components above, other than the year, must be given as two [ASCII digits](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) representing the number in base ten, zero-padded if necessary. The year must be given as the shortest possible string of four or more [ASCII digits](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) representing the number in base ten, zero-padded if necessary.

The [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s source file's last modification date and time must be derived from relevant features of the networking protocols used, e.g. from the value of the HTTP \`[`Last-Modified`](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc7232.html#header.last-modified)\` header of the document, or from metadata in the file system for local files. If the last modification date and time are not known, the attribute must return the current date and time in the above format.

#### 3.1.5 Reporting document loading status

`document.readyState`

Returns "`loading`" while the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is loading, "`interactive`" once it is finished parsing but still loading subresources, and "`complete`" once it has loaded.

The [`readystatechange`](#events) event fires on the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object when this value changes.

The [`DOMContentLoaded`](#events) event fires after the transition to "`interactive`" but before the transition to "`complete`", at the point where all subresources apart from [`async`](#4121-the-script-element) [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements have loaded.

Each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a current document readiness, a string, initially "`complete`".

> [!note]
> For [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) objects created via the [create and initialize a `Document` object](#751-shared-document-creation-infrastructure) algorithm, this will be immediately reset to "`loading`" before any script can observe the value of [`document.readyState`](#315-reporting-document-loading-status). This default applies to other cases such as [initial `about:blank`](#311-the-document-object) [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)s or [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)s without a [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts).

The `readyState` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [current document readiness](#315-reporting-document-loading-status).

To update the current document readiness for [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document to readinessValue:
1. If document's [current document readiness](#315-reporting-document-loading-status) equals readinessValue, then return.
2. Set document's [current document readiness](#315-reporting-document-loading-status) to readinessValue.
3. If document is associated with an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents):
   1. Let now be the [current high resolution time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time) given document's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant).
   2. If readinessValue is "`complete`", and document's [load timing info](#315-reporting-document-loading-status)'s [DOM complete time](#315-reporting-document-loading-status) is 0, then set document's [load timing info](#315-reporting-document-loading-status)'s [DOM complete time](#315-reporting-document-loading-status) to now.
   3. Otherwise, if readinessValue is "`interactive`", and document's [load timing info](#315-reporting-document-loading-status)'s [DOM interactive time](#315-reporting-document-loading-status) is 0, then set document's [load timing info](#315-reporting-document-loading-status)'s [DOM interactive time](#315-reporting-document-loading-status) to now.
4. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`readystatechange`](#events) at document.

---

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is said to have an active parser if it is associated with an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) or an [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents) that has not yet been [stopped](#1327-the-end) or [aborted](#1327-the-end).

---

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a [document load timing info](#315-reporting-document-loading-status) load timing info.

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a [document unload timing info](#315-reporting-document-loading-status) previous document unload timing.

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a boolean was created via cross-origin redirects, initially false.

The document load timing info [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) has the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):

navigation start time (default 0)

A number

DOM interactive time (default 0)

DOM content loaded event start time (default 0)

DOM content loaded event end time (default 0)

DOM complete time (default 0)

load event start time (default 0)

load event end time (default 0)

[`DOMHighResTimeStamp`](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dom-domhighrestimestamp) values

The document unload timing info [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) has the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):

unload event start time (default 0)

unload event end time (default 0)

[`DOMHighResTimeStamp`](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dom-domhighrestimestamp) values

#### 3.1.6 Render-blocking mechanism

Each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a render-blocking element set, a [set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) of elements, initially the empty set.

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document allows adding render-blocking elements if document's [content type](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is "[`text/html`](#171-texthtml)" and [the body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors) of document is null.

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document is render-blocked if both of the following are true:
- document's [render-blocking element set](#316-render-blocking-mechanism) is non-empty, or document [allows adding render-blocking elements](#316-render-blocking-mechanism).
- The [current high resolution time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time) given document's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) has not exceeded an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) timeout value.

An element el is render-blocking if el's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) document is [render-blocked](#316-render-blocking-mechanism), and el is in document's [render-blocking element set](#316-render-blocking-mechanism).

To block rendering on an element el:
1. Let document be el's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
2. If document [allows adding render-blocking elements](#316-render-blocking-mechanism), then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) el to document's [render-blocking element set](#316-render-blocking-mechanism).

To unblock rendering on an element el:
1. Let document be el's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
2. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) el from document's [render-blocking element set](#316-render-blocking-mechanism).

Whenever a [render-blocking](#316-render-blocking-mechanism) element el [becomes browsing-context disconnected](#214-dom-trees), or el's [blocking attribute](#258-blocking-attributes)'s value is changed so that el is no longer [potentially render-blocking](#258-blocking-attributes), then [unblock rendering](#316-render-blocking-mechanism) on el.

#### 3.1.7 DOM tree accessors

The `html` element of a document is its [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree), if it's an [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element, and null otherwise.

---

`document.head`

Returns [the `head` element](#317-dom-tree-accessors).

The `head` element of a document is the first [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element that is a child of [the `html` element](#317-dom-tree-accessors), if there is one, or null otherwise.

The `head` attribute, on getting, must return [the `head` element](#317-dom-tree-accessors) of the document (a [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element or null).

---

`document.title [ = value ]`

Returns the document's title, as given by [the `title` element](#317-dom-tree-accessors) for HTML and as given by the [SVG `title`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/struct.html#elementdef-title) element for SVG.

Can be set, to update the document's title. If there is no appropriate element to update, the new value is ignored.

The `title` element of a document is the first [`title`](#422-the-title-element) element in the document (in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees)), if there is one, or null otherwise.

The `title` attribute must, on getting, run the following algorithm:
1. If the [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) is an [SVG `svg`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/struct.html#elementdef-svg) element, then let value be the [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) of the first [SVG `title`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/struct.html#elementdef-title) element that is a child of the [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree).
2. Otherwise, let value be the [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) of [the `title` element](#317-dom-tree-accessors), or the empty string if [the `title` element](#317-dom-tree-accessors) is null.
3. [Strip and collapse ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) in value.
4. Return value.

On setting, the steps corresponding to the first matching condition in the following list must be run:

If the [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) is an [SVG `svg`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/struct.html#elementdef-svg) element
1. If there is an [SVG `title`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/struct.html#elementdef-title) element that is a child of the [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree), let element be the first such element.
2. Otherwise:
   1. Let element be the result of [creating an element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) given the [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), "`title`", and the [SVG namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces).
   2. Insert element as the [first child](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) of the [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree).
3. [String replace all](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) with the given value within element.

If the [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) is in the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces)
1. If [the `title` element](#317-dom-tree-accessors) is null and [the `head` element](#317-dom-tree-accessors) is null, then return.
2. If [the `title` element](#317-dom-tree-accessors) is non-null, let element be [the `title` element](#317-dom-tree-accessors).
3. Otherwise:
   1. Let element be the result of [creating an element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) given the [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), "`title`", and the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces).
   2. [Append](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) element to [the `head` element](#317-dom-tree-accessors).
4. [String replace all](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) with the given value within element.

Otherwise

Do nothing.

---

`document.body [ = value ]`

Returns [the body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors).

Can be set, to replace [the body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors).

If the new value is not a [`body`](#431-the-body-element) or [`frameset`](#1632-frames) element, this will throw a ["`HierarchyRequestError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#hierarchyrequesterror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

The body element of a document is the first of [the `html` element](#317-dom-tree-accessors)'s children that is either a [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element or a [`frameset`](#1632-frames) element, or null if there is no such element.

The `body` attribute, on getting, must return [the body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors) of the document (either a [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element, a [`frameset`](#1632-frames) element, or null). On setting, the following algorithm must be run:
1. If the new value is not a [`body`](#431-the-body-element) or [`frameset`](#1632-frames) element, then throw a ["`HierarchyRequestError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#hierarchyrequesterror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Otherwise, if the new value is the same as [the body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors), return.
3. Otherwise, if [the body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors) is not null, then [replace](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) [the body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors) with the new value within [the body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors)'s parent and return.
4. Otherwise, if there is no [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree), throw a ["`HierarchyRequestError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#hierarchyrequesterror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
5. Otherwise, [the body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors) is null, but there's a [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree). [Append](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) the new value to the [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree).

> [!note]
> The value returned by the [`body`](#317-dom-tree-accessors) getter is not always the one passed to the setter.

> [!example]
> In this example, the setter successfully inserts a [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element (though this is non-conforming since SVG does not allow a [`body`](#431-the-body-element) as child of [SVG `svg`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/struct.html#elementdef-svg)). However the getter will return null because the document element is not [`html`](#411-the-html-element).
> 
> ```html
> <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
>  <script>
>   document.body = document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml", "body");
>   console.assert(document.body === null);
>  </script>
> </svg>
> ```

---

`document.images`

Returns an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) of the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) elements in the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object).

`document.embeds`

`document.plugins`

Returns an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) of the [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element) elements in the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object).

`document.links`

Returns an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) of the [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements in the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) that have [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attributes.

`document.forms`

Returns an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) of the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements in the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object).

`document.scripts`

Returns an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) of the [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements in the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object).

The `images` attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) rooted at the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) node, whose filter matches only [`img`](#483-the-img-element) elements.

The `embeds` attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) rooted at the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) node, whose filter matches only [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element) elements.

The `plugins` attribute must return the same object as that returned by the [`embeds`](#317-dom-tree-accessors) attribute.

The `links` attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) rooted at the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) node, whose filter matches only [`a`](#451-the-a-element) elements with [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attributes and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements with [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attributes.

The `forms` attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) rooted at the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) node, whose filter matches only [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements.

The `scripts` attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) rooted at the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) node, whose filter matches only [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements.

---

`collection = document.getElementsByName(name)`

Returns a [`NodeList`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42101-interface-nodelist) of elements in the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) that have a `name` attribute with the value name.

The `getElementsByName(elementName)` method steps are to return a [live](#215-scripting) [`NodeList`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42101-interface-nodelist) containing all the [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) in that document that have a `name` attribute whose value is [identical to](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) the elementName argument, in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees). When the method is invoked on a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object again with the same argument, the user agent may return the same as the object returned by the earlier call. In other cases, a new [`NodeList`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42101-interface-nodelist) object must be returned.

---

`document.currentScript`

Returns the [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element, or the [SVG `script`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/interact.html#elementdef-script) element, that is currently executing, as long as the element represents a [classic script](#8141-scripts). In the case of reentrant script execution, returns the one that most recently started executing amongst those that have not yet finished executing.

Returns null if the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is not currently executing a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) or [SVG `script`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/interact.html#elementdef-script) element (e.g., because the running script is an event handler, or a timeout), or if the currently executing [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) or [SVG `script`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/interact.html#elementdef-script) element represents a [module script](#8141-scripts).

The `currentScript` attribute, on getting, must return the value to which it was most recently set. When the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is created, the [`currentScript`](#317-dom-tree-accessors) must be initialized to null.

> [!note]
> This API has fallen out of favor in the implementer and standards community, as it globally exposes [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) or [SVG `script`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/interact.html#elementdef-script) elements. As such, it is not available in newer contexts, such as when running [module scripts](#8141-scripts) or when running scripts in a [shadow tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree). We are looking into creating a new solution for identifying the running script in such contexts, which does not make it globally available: see [issue #1013](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/1013).

---

The [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) interface [supports named properties](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-support-named-properties). The [supported property names](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-supported-property-names) of a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object document at any moment consist of the following, for each element element [in a document tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) with document as its [root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), ignoring later duplicates:
- the value of element's [`id`](#326-global-attributes) content attribute, if element is a [named element](#317-dom-tree-accessors) with that value as its name; and then
- the value of element's `name` content attribute, if element is a [named element](#317-dom-tree-accessors) with that value as its name.

To [determine the value of a named property](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-determine-the-value-of-a-named-property) name for a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), the user agent must return the value obtained using the following steps:
1. Let elements be the list of [named elements](#317-dom-tree-accessors) with the name name that are [in a document tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) with the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) as their [root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).

   > [!note]
   > There will be at least one such element, since the algorithm would otherwise not have been [invoked by Web IDL](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#LegacyPlatformObjectGetOwnProperty).

2. If elements has only one element, and that element is an [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) element, and that [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) element's [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables) is not null, then return the [active `WindowProxy`](#731-navigables) of the element's [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables).
3. Otherwise, if elements has only one element, return that element.
4. Otherwise, return an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) rooted at the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) node, whose filter matches only [named elements](#317-dom-tree-accessors) with the name name.

An element is a named element with the name name if name is not the empty string and any of the following are true:
- it is an [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element), [`form`](#4103-the-form-element), [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element), [`img`](#483-the-img-element), or [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element whose `name` content attribute's value is name;
- it is an [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element whose [`id`](#326-global-attributes) content attribute's value is name; or
- it is an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element whose [`id`](#326-global-attributes) content attribute's value is name, and that has a non-empty `name` content attribute present also.

---

> [!note]
> The [`dir`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) attribute on the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) interface is defined along with the [`dir`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) content attribute.

### 3.2 Elements

#### 3.2.1 Semantics

Elements, attributes, and attribute values in HTML are defined (by this specification) to have certain meanings (semantics). For example, the [`ol`](#445-the-ol-element) element represents an ordered list, and the [`lang`](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes) attribute represents the language of the content.

These definitions allow HTML processors, such as web browsers or search engines, to present and use documents and applications in a wide variety of contexts that the author might not have considered.

> [!example]
> As a simple example, consider a web page written by an author who only considered desktop computer web browsers:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <html lang="en">
>  <head>
>   <title>My Page</title>
>  </head>
>  <body>
>   <h1>Welcome to my page</h1>
>   <p>I like cars and lorries and have a big Jeep!</p>
>   <h2>Where I live</h2>
>   <p>I live in a small hut on a mountain!</p>
>  </body>
> </html>
> ```
> 
> Because HTML conveys *meaning*, rather than presentation, the same page can also be used by a small browser on a mobile phone, without any change to the page. Instead of headings being in large letters as on the desktop, for example, the browser on the mobile phone might use the same size text for the whole page, but with the headings in bold.
> 
> But it goes further than just differences in screen size: the same page could equally be used by a blind user using a browser based around speech synthesis, which instead of displaying the page on a screen, reads the page to the user, e.g. using headphones. Instead of large text for the headings, the speech browser might use a different volume or a slower voice.
> 
> That's not all, either. Since the browsers know which parts of the page are the headings, they can create a document outline that the user can use to quickly navigate around the document, using keys for "jump to next heading" or "jump to previous heading". Such features are especially common with speech browsers, where users would otherwise find quickly navigating a page quite difficult.
> 
> Even beyond browsers, software can make use of this information. Search engines can use the headings to more effectively index a page, or to provide quick links to subsections of the page from their results. Tools can use the headings to create a table of contents (that is in fact how this very specification's table of contents is generated).
> 
> This example has focused on headings, but the same principle applies to all of the semantics in HTML.

Authors must not use elements, attributes, or attribute values for purposes other than their appropriate intended semantic purpose, as doing so prevents software from correctly processing the page.

> [!example]
> For example, the following snippet, intended to represent the heading of a corporate site, is non-conforming because the second line is not intended to be a heading of a subsection, but merely a subheading or subtitle (a subordinate heading for the same section).
> 
> ```html
> <body>
>  <h1>ACME Corporation</h1>
>  <h2>The leaders in arbitrary fast delivery since 1920</h2>
>  ...
> ```
> 
> The [`hgroup`](#437-the-hgroup-element) element can be used for these kinds of situations:
> 
> ```html
> <body>
>  <hgroup>
>   <h1>ACME Corporation</h1>
>   <p>The leaders in arbitrary fast delivery since 1920</p>
>  </hgroup>
>  ...
> ```

> [!example]
> The document in this next example is similarly non-conforming, despite being syntactically correct, because the data placed in the cells is clearly not tabular data, and the [`cite`](#456-the-cite-element) element mis-used:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <html lang="en-GB">
>  <head> <title> Demonstration </title> </head>
>  <body>
>   <table>
>    <tr> <td> My favourite animal is the cat. </td> </tr>
>    <tr>
>     <td>
>      —<a href="https://example.org/~ernest/"><cite>Ernest</cite></a>,
>      in an essay from 1992
>     </td>
>    </tr>
>   </table>
>  </body>
> </html>
> ```
> 
> This would make software that relies on these semantics fail: for example, a speech browser that allowed a blind user to navigate tables in the document would report the quote above as a table, confusing the user; similarly, a tool that extracted titles of works from pages would extract "Ernest" as the title of a work, even though it's actually a person's name, not a title.
> 
> A corrected version of this document might be:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <html lang="en-GB">
>  <head> <title> Demonstration </title> </head>
>  <body>
>   <blockquote>
>    <p> My favourite animal is the cat. </p>
>   </blockquote>
>   <p>
>    —<a href="https://example.org/~ernest/">Ernest</a>,
>    in an essay from 1992
>   </p>
>  </body>
> </html>
> ```

Authors must not use elements, attributes, or attribute values that are not permitted by this specification or [other applicable specifications](#2110-extensibility), as doing so makes it significantly harder for the language to be extended in the future.

> [!example]
> In the next example, there is a non-conforming attribute value ("carpet") and a non-conforming attribute ("texture"), which is not permitted by this specification:
> 
> ```html
> <label>Carpet: <input type="carpet" name="c" texture="deep pile"></label>
> ```
> 
> Here would be an alternative and correct way to mark this up:
> 
> ```html
> <label>Carpet: <input type="text" class="carpet" name="c" data-texture="deep pile"></label>
> ```

DOM nodes whose [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) is null are exempt from all document conformance requirements other than the [HTML syntax](#131-writing-html-documents) requirements and [XML syntax](#141-writing-documents-in-the-xml-syntax) requirements.

> [!example]
> In particular, the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element's [template contents](#4123-the-template-element)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) is null. For example, the [content model](#324-element-definitions) requirements and attribute value microsyntax requirements do not apply to a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element's [template contents](#4123-the-template-element). In this example an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element has attribute values that are placeholders that would be invalid outside a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element.
> 
> ```html
> <template>
>  <article>
>   <img src="{{src}}" alt="{{alt}}">
>   <h1></h1>
>  </article>
> </template>
> ```
> 
> However, if the above markup were to omit the `</h1>` end tag, that would be a violation of the [HTML syntax](#131-writing-html-documents), and would thus be flagged as an error by conformance checkers.

Through scripting and using other mechanisms, the values of attributes, text, and indeed the entire structure of the document may change dynamically while a user agent is processing it. The semantics of a document at an instant in time are those represented by the state of the document at that instant in time, and the semantics of a document can therefore change over time. User agents must update their presentation of the document as this occurs.

> [!example]
> HTML has a [`progress`](#41013-the-progress-element) element that describes a progress bar. If its "value" attribute is dynamically updated by a script, the UA would update the rendering to show the progress changing.

#### 3.2.2 Elements in the DOM

The nodes representing [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) in the DOM must implement, and expose to scripts, the interfaces listed for them in the relevant sections of this specification. This includes [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) in [XML documents](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), even when those documents are in another context (e.g. inside an XSLT transform).

Elements in the DOM represent things; that is, they have intrinsic *meaning*, also known as semantics.

> [!example]
> For example, an [`ol`](#445-the-ol-element) element represents an ordered list.

Elements can be referenced (referred to) in some way, either explicitly or implicitly. One way that an element in the DOM can be explicitly referenced is by giving an [`id`](#326-global-attributes) attribute to the element, and then creating a [hyperlink](#461-introduction) with that [`id`](#326-global-attributes) attribute's value as the [fragment](#74233-fragment-navigations) for the [hyperlink](#461-introduction)'s [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute value. Hyperlinks are not necessary for a reference, however; any manner of referring to the element in question will suffice.

> [!example]
> Consider the following [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element) element, which is given an [`id`](#326-global-attributes) attribute:
> 
> ```html
> <figure id="module-script-graph">
>   <img src="module-script-graph.svg"
>        alt="Module A depends on module B, which depends
>             on modules C and D.">
>   <figcaption>Figure 27: a simple module graph</figcaption>
> </figure>
> ```
> 
> A [hyperlink](#461-introduction)-based [reference](#322-elements-in-the-dom) could be created using the [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element, like so:
> 
> ```html
> As we can see in <a href="#module-script-graph">figure 27</a>, ...
> ```
> 
> However, there are many other ways of [referencing](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element) element, such as:
> - "As depicted in the figure of modules A, B, C, and D..."
> - "In Figure 27..." (without a hyperlink)
> - "From the contents of the 'simple module graph' figure..."
> - "In the figure below..." (but [this is discouraged](#4412-the-figure-element))

The basic interface, from which all the [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility)' interfaces inherit, and which must be used by elements that have no additional requirements, is the [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom) interface.

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLElement : Element {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  // metadata attributes
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString title;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString lang;
  [CEReactions] attribute boolean translate;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString dir;

  // user interaction
  [CEReactions] attribute (boolean or unrestricted double or DOMString)? hidden;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean inert;
  undefined click();
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString accessKey;
  readonly attribute DOMString accessKeyLabel;
  [CEReactions] attribute boolean draggable;
  [CEReactions] attribute boolean spellcheck;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute DOMString writingSuggestions;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute DOMString autocapitalize;
  [CEReactions] attribute boolean autocorrect;

  [CEReactions] attribute [LegacyNullToEmptyString] DOMString innerText;
  [CEReactions] attribute [LegacyNullToEmptyString] DOMString outerText;

  ElementInternals attachInternals();

  // The popover API
  undefined showPopover(optional ShowPopoverOptions options = {});
  undefined hidePopover();
  boolean togglePopover(optional (TogglePopoverOptions or boolean) options = {});
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString? popover;

  [CEReactions, Reflect, ReflectRange=(0, 8)] attribute unsigned long headingOffset;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean headingReset;
};

dictionary ShowPopoverOptions {
  HTMLElement source;
};

dictionary TogglePopoverOptions : ShowPopoverOptions {
  boolean force;
};

HTMLElement includes GlobalEventHandlers;
HTMLElement includes ElementContentEditable;
HTMLElement includes HTMLOrSVGOrMathMLElement;

[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLUnknownElement : HTMLElement {
  // Note: intentionally no [HTMLConstructor]
};
```

The [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom) interface holds methods and attributes related to a number of disparate features, and the members of this interface are therefore described in various different sections of this specification.

---

The [element interface](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) for an element with name name in the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) is determined as follows:
1. If name is [`applet`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`bgsound`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`blink`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`isindex`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`keygen`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`multicol`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`nextid`](#162-non-conforming-features), or [`spacer`](#162-non-conforming-features), then return [`HTMLUnknownElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom).
2. If name is [`acronym`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`basefont`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`big`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`center`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`nobr`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`noembed`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`noframes`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`plaintext`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`rb`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`rtc`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`strike`](#162-non-conforming-features), or [`tt`](#162-non-conforming-features), then return [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom).
3. If name is [`listing`](#162-non-conforming-features) or [`xmp`](#162-non-conforming-features), then return [`HTMLPreElement`](#443-the-pre-element).
4. Otherwise, if this specification defines an interface appropriate for the [element type](#213-xml-compatibility) corresponding to the local name name, then return that interface.
5. If [other applicable specifications](#2110-extensibility) define an appropriate interface for name, then return the interface they define.
6. If name is a [valid custom element name](#4133-core-concepts), then return [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom).
7. Return [`HTMLUnknownElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom).

> [!note]
> The use of [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom) instead of [`HTMLUnknownElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom) in the case of [valid custom element names](#4133-core-concepts) is done to ensure that any potential future [upgrades](#4135-upgrades) only cause a linear transition of the element's prototype chain, from [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom) to a subclass, instead of a lateral one, from [`HTMLUnknownElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom) to an unrelated subclass.

Features shared between HTML, SVG and MathML elements use the [`HTMLOrSVGOrMathMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom) interface mixin: [\[SVG\]](#references) [\[MATHML\]](#references)

```webidl
interface mixin HTMLOrSVGOrMathMLElement {
  [SameObject] readonly attribute DOMStringMap dataset;
  attribute DOMString nonce; // intentionally no [CEReactions]

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean autofocus;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute long tabIndex;
  undefined focus(optional FocusOptions options = {});
  undefined blur();
};
```

> [!example]
> An example of an element that is neither an HTML nor SVG nor MathML element is one created as follows:
> 
> ```html
> const el = document.createElementNS("some namespace", "example");
> console.assert(el.constructor === Element);
> ```

#### 3.2.3 HTML element constructors

To support the [custom elements](#413-custom-elements) feature, all HTML elements have special constructor behavior. This is indicated via the `[HTMLConstructor]` IDL [extended attribute](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-extended-attribute). It indicates that the interface object for the given interface will have a specific behavior when called, as defined in detail below.

The [`[HTMLConstructor]`](#323-html-element-constructors) extended attribute must take no arguments, and must only appear on [constructor operations](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-constructors). It must appear only once on a constructor operation, and the interface must contain only the single, annotated constructor operation, and no others. The annotated constructor operation must be declared to take no arguments.

Interfaces declared with constructor operations that are annotated with the [`[HTMLConstructor]`](#323-html-element-constructors) extended attribute have the following [overridden constructor steps](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#overridden-constructor-steps):
1. If [NewTarget](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-built-in-function-objects) is equal to the [active function object](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#active-function-object), then throw a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror).

   > [!example]
   > This can occur when a custom element is defined using an [element interface](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) as its constructor:
   > 
   > ```javascript
   > customElements.define("bad-1", HTMLButtonElement);
   > new HTMLButtonElement();          // (1)
   > document.createElement("bad-1");  // (2)
   > ```
   > 
   > In this case, during the execution of [`HTMLButtonElement`](#4106-the-button-element) (either explicitly, as in (1), or implicitly, as in (2)), both the [active function object](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#active-function-object) and [NewTarget](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-built-in-function-objects) are [`HTMLButtonElement`](#4106-the-button-element). If this check was not present, it would be possible to create an instance of [`HTMLButtonElement`](#4106-the-button-element) whose local name was `bad-1`.

2. Let registry be null.
3. If the [surrounding agent](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#surrounding-agent)'s [active custom element constructor map](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface)\[[NewTarget](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-built-in-function-objects)\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then set registry to the [surrounding agent](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#surrounding-agent)'s [active custom element constructor map](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface)\[[NewTarget](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-built-in-function-objects)\].
4. Otherwise, set registry to the [current global object](#81333-current)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).
5. Let definition be the item in registry's [custom element definition set](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) with [constructor](#4133-core-concepts) equal to [NewTarget](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-built-in-function-objects). If there is no such item, then throw a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror).

   > [!note]
   > Since there can be no item in registry's [custom element definition set](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) with a [constructor](#4133-core-concepts) of undefined, this step also prevents HTML element constructors from being called as functions (since in that case [NewTarget](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-built-in-function-objects) will be undefined).

6. Let isValue be null.
7. If definition's [local name](#4133-core-concepts) is equal to definition's [name](#4133-core-concepts) (i.e., definition is for an [autonomous custom element](#4133-core-concepts)):
   1. If the [active function object](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#active-function-object) is not [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom), then throw a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror).

      > [!example]
      > This can occur when a custom element is defined to not extend any local names, but inherits from a non-[`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom) class:
      > 
      > ```javascript
      > customElements.define("bad-2", class Bad2 extends HTMLParagraphElement {});
      > ```
      > 
      > In this case, during the (implicit) `super()` call that occurs when constructing an instance of `Bad2`, the [active function object](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#active-function-object) is [`HTMLParagraphElement`](#441-the-p-element), not [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom).

8. Otherwise (i.e., if definition is for a [customized built-in element](#4133-core-concepts)):
   1. Let valid local names be the list of local names for elements defined in this specification or in [other applicable specifications](#2110-extensibility) that use the [active function object](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#active-function-object) as their [element interface](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).
   2. If valid local names does not contain definition's [local name](#4133-core-concepts), then throw a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror).

      > [!example]
      > This can occur when a custom element is defined to extend a given local name but inherits from the wrong class:
      > 
      > ```javascript
      > customElements.define("bad-3", class Bad3 extends HTMLQuoteElement {}, { extends: "p" });
      > ```
      > 
      > In this case, during the (implicit) `super()` call that occurs when constructing an instance of `Bad3`, valid local names is the list containing [`q`](#457-the-q-element) and [`blockquote`](#444-the-blockquote-element), but definition's [local name](#4133-core-concepts) is [`p`](#441-the-p-element), which is not in that list.

   3. Set isValue to definition's [name](#4133-core-concepts).

9. If definition's [construction stack](#4133-core-concepts) is empty:
   1. Let element be the result of [internally creating a new object implementing the interface](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#internally-create-a-new-object-implementing-the-interface) to which the [active function object](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#active-function-object) corresponds, given the [current realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#current-realm) and [NewTarget](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-built-in-function-objects).
   2. Set element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) to the [current global object](#81333-current)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object).
   3. Set element's [namespace](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) to the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces).
   4. Set element's [namespace prefix](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) to null.
   5. Set element's [local name](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) to definition's [local name](#4133-core-concepts).
   6. Set element's [custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) to registry.
   7. Set element's [custom element state](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) to "`custom`".
   8. Set element's [custom element definition](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) to definition.
   9. Set element's [`is` value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) to isValue.
   10. Return element.

   > [!note]
   > This occurs when author script constructs a new custom element directly, e.g., via `new MyCustomElement()`.

10. Let prototype be ? [Get](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-get-o-p)([NewTarget](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-built-in-function-objects), "prototype").
11. If prototype [is not an Object](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-object-type):
    1. Let realm be ? [GetFunctionRealm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-getfunctionrealm)([NewTarget](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-built-in-function-objects)).
    2. Set prototype to the [interface prototype object](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-interface-prototype-object) of realm whose interface is the same as the interface of the [active function object](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#active-function-object).

    > [!note]
    > The realm of the [active function object](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#active-function-object) might not be realm, so we are using the more general concept of "the same interface" across realms; we are not looking for equality of [interface objects](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-interface-object). This fallback behavior, including using the realm of [NewTarget](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-built-in-function-objects) and looking up the appropriate prototype there, is designed to match analogous behavior for the JavaScript built-ins and Web IDL's [internally create a new object implementing the interface](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#internally-create-a-new-object-implementing-the-interface) algorithm.

12. Let element be the last entry in definition's [construction stack](#4133-core-concepts).
13. If element is an [*already constructed* marker](#4133-core-concepts), then throw a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror).

    > [!example]
    > This can occur when the author code inside the [custom element constructor](#4133-core-concepts) [non-conformantly](#4132-requirements-for-custom-element-constructors-and-reactions) creates another instance of the class being constructed, before calling `super()`:
    > 
    > ```javascript
    > let doSillyThing = true;
    > 
    > class DontDoThis extends HTMLElement {
    >   constructor() {
    >     if (doSillyThing) {
    >       doSillyThing = false;
    >       new DontDoThis();
    >       // Now the construction stack will contain an already constructed marker.
    >     }
    > 
    >     // This will then fail with a TypeError:
    >     super();
    >   }
    > }
    > ```

    > [!example]
    > This can also occur when author code inside the [custom element constructor](#4133-core-concepts) [non-conformantly](#4132-requirements-for-custom-element-constructors-and-reactions) calls `super()` twice, since per the JavaScript specification, this actually executes the superclass constructor (i.e. this algorithm) twice, before throwing an error:
    > 
    > ```javascript
    > class DontDoThisEither extends HTMLElement {
    >   constructor() {
    >     super();
    > 
    >     // This will throw, but not until it has already called into the HTMLElement constructor
    >     super();
    >   }
    > }
    > ```

14. Perform ? element.\[\[SetPrototypeOf\]\](prototype).
15. Replace the last entry in definition's [construction stack](#4133-core-concepts) with an [*already constructed* marker](#4133-core-concepts).
16. Return element.

    > [!note]
    > This step is normally reached when [upgrading](#4135-upgrades) a custom element; the existing element is returned, so that the `super()` call inside the [custom element constructor](#4133-core-concepts) assigns that existing element to **this**.

---

In addition to the constructor behavior implied by [`[HTMLConstructor]`](#323-html-element-constructors), some elements also have [named constructors](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-named-constructor) (which are really factory functions with a modified `prototype` property).

> [!example]
> Named constructors for HTML elements can also be used in an [`extends`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) clause when defining a [custom element constructor](#4133-core-concepts):
> 
> ```javascript
> class AutoEmbiggenedImage extends Image {
>   constructor(width, height) {
>     super(width * 10, height * 10);
>   }
> }
> 
> customElements.define("auto-embiggened", AutoEmbiggenedImage, { extends: "img" });
> 
> const image = new AutoEmbiggenedImage(15, 20);
> console.assert(image.width === 150);
> console.assert(image.height === 200);
> ```

#### 3.2.4 Element definitions

Each element in this specification has a definition that includes the following information:

Categories

A list of [categories](#3252-kinds-of-content) to which the element belongs. These are used when defining the [content models](#325-content-models) for each element.

Contexts in which this element can be used

A *non-normative* description of where the element can be used. This information is redundant with the content models of elements that allow this one as a child, and is provided only as a convenience.

> [!note]
> For simplicity, only the most specific expectations are listed.
> 
> For example, all [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is [flow content](#32522-flow-content). Thus, elements that are [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) will only be listed as "where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected", since this is the more-specific expectation. Anywhere that expects [flow content](#32522-flow-content) also expects [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content), and thus also meets this expectation.

Content model

A normative description of what content must be included as children and descendants of the element.

Tag omission in text/html

A *non-normative* description of whether, in the [`text/html`](#171-texthtml) syntax, the [start](#13121-start-tags) and [end](#13122-end-tags) tags can be omitted. This information is redundant with the normative requirements given in the [optional tags](#13124-optional-tags) section, and is provided in the element definitions only as a convenience.

Content attributes

A normative list of attributes that may be specified on the element (except where otherwise disallowed), along with non-normative descriptions of those attributes. (The content to the left of the dash is normative, the content to the right of the dash is not.)

Accessibility considerations

For authors: Conformance requirements for use of ARIA [`role`](#219-dependencies) and [`aria-*`](#219-dependencies) attributes are defined in ARIA in HTML. [\[ARIA\]](#references) [\[ARIAHTML\]](#references)

For implementers: User agent requirements for implementing accessibility API semantics are defined in HTML Accessibility API Mappings. [\[HTMLAAM\]](#references)

Sanitization

The [Sanitization](#324-element-definitions) information for each element defines its [sanitization category](#865-sanitization-constants), which affects how the element is processed during sanitization. It can also define one or more of the element's attributes as [navigating URL attributes](#865-sanitization-constants).

DOM interface

A normative definition of a DOM interface that such elements must implement.

This is then followed by a description of what the element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom), along with any additional normative conformance criteria that may apply to authors and implementations. Examples are sometimes also included.

##### 3.2.4.1 Attributes

An attribute value is a string. Except where otherwise specified, attribute values on [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) may be any string value, including the empty string, and there is no restriction on what text can be specified in such attribute values.

#### 3.2.5 Content models

Each element defined in this specification has a content model: a description of the element's expected [contents](#325-content-models). An [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) must have contents that match the requirements described in the element's content model. The contents of an element are its children in the DOM.

[ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) is always allowed between elements. User agents represent these characters between elements in the source markup as [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) nodes in the DOM. Empty [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) nodes and [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) nodes consisting of just sequences of those characters are considered inter-element whitespace.

[Inter-element whitespace](#325-content-models), comment nodes, and processing instruction nodes must be ignored when establishing whether an element's contents match the element's content model or not, and must be ignored when following algorithms that define document and element semantics.

> [!note]
> Thus, an element A is said to be *preceded or followed* by a second element B if A and B have the same parent node and there are no other element nodes or [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) nodes (other than [inter-element whitespace](#325-content-models)) between them. Similarly, a node is the *only child* of an element if that element contains no other nodes other than [inter-element whitespace](#325-content-models), comment nodes, and processing instruction nodes.

Authors must not use [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) anywhere except where they are explicitly allowed, as defined for each element, or as explicitly required by other specifications. For XML compound documents, these contexts could be inside elements from other namespaces, if those elements are defined as providing the relevant contexts.

> [!example]
> The Atom Syndication Format defines a `content` element. When its `type` attribute has the value `xhtml`, The Atom Syndication Format requires that it contain a single HTML [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element. Thus, a [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element is allowed in that context, even though this is not explicitly normatively stated by this specification. [\[ATOM\]](#references)

In addition, [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) may be orphan nodes (i.e. without a parent node).

> [!example]
> For example, creating a [`td`](#499-the-td-element) element and storing it in a global variable in a script is conforming, even though [`td`](#499-the-td-element) elements are otherwise only supposed to be used inside [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) elements.
> 
> ```javascript
> var data = {
>   name: "Banana",
>   cell: document.createElement('td'),
> };
> ```

##### 3.2.5.1 The "nothing" content model

When an element's content model is nothing, the element must contain no [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) nodes (other than [inter-element whitespace](#325-content-models)) and no element nodes.

> [!note]
> Most HTML elements whose content model is "nothing" are also, for convenience, [void elements](#1312-elements) (elements that have no [end tag](#13122-end-tags) in the [HTML syntax](#13-the-html-syntax)). However, these are entirely separate concepts.

##### 3.2.5.2 Kinds of content

Each element in HTML falls into zero or more categories that group elements with similar characteristics together. The following broad categories are used in this specification:
- [Metadata content](#32521-metadata-content)
- [Flow content](#32522-flow-content)
- [Sectioning content](#32523-sectioning-content)
- [Heading content](#32524-heading-content)
- [Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content)
- [Embedded content](#32526-embedded-content)
- [Interactive content](#32527-interactive-content)

> [!note]
> Some elements also fall into other categories, which are defined in other parts of this specification.

These categories are related as follows:

Sectioning content, heading content, phrasing content, embedded content, and interactive content are all types of flow content. Metadata is sometimes flow content. Metadata and interactive content are sometimes phrasing content. Embedded content is also a type of phrasing content, and sometimes is interactive content.

Other categories are also used for specific purposes, e.g. form controls are specified using a number of categories to define common requirements. Some elements have unique requirements and do not fit into any particular category.

###### 3.2.5.2.1 Metadata content

Metadata content is content that sets up the presentation or behavior of the rest of the content, or that sets up the relationship of the document with other documents, or that conveys other "out of band" information.
- [`base`](#423-the-base-element)
- [`link`](#424-the-link-element)
- [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element)
- [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element)
- [`script`](#4121-the-script-element)
- [`style`](#426-the-style-element)
- [`template`](#4123-the-template-element)
- [`title`](#422-the-title-element)

Elements from other namespaces whose semantics are primarily metadata-related (e.g. RDF) are also [metadata content](#32521-metadata-content).

> [!example]
> Thus, in the XML serialization, one can use RDF, like this:
> 
> ```html
> <html xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml"
>       xmlns:r="http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#" xml:lang="en">
>  <head>
>   <title>Hedral's Home Page</title>
>   <r:RDF>
>    <Person xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/10/swap/pim/contact#"
>            r:about="https://hedral.example.com/#">
>     <fullName>Cat Hedral</fullName>
