>     <mailbox r:resource="mailto:hedral@damowmow.com"/>
>     <personalTitle>Sir</personalTitle>
>    </Person>
>   </r:RDF>
>  </head>
>  <body>
>   <h1>My home page</h1>
>   <p>I like playing with string, I guess. Sister says squirrels are fun
>   too so sometimes I follow her to play with them.</p>
>  </body>
> </html>
> ```
> 
> This isn't possible in the HTML serialization, however.

###### 3.2.5.2.3 Sectioning content

Sectioning content is content that defines the scope of [`header`](#438-the-header-element) and [`footer`](#439-the-footer-element) elements.

- [`aside`](#435-the-aside-element)
- [`nav`](#434-the-nav-element)
- [`section`](#433-the-section-element)

###### 3.2.5.2.4 Heading content

Heading content defines the heading of a section (whether explicitly marked up using [sectioning content](#32523-sectioning-content) elements, or implied by the heading content itself).
- [`h1`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements)
- [`h2`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements)
- [`h3`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements)
- [`h4`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements)
- [`h5`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements)
- [`h6`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements)
- [`hgroup`](#437-the-hgroup-element) (if it has a descendant [`h1`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements) to [`h6`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements) element)

###### 3.2.5.2.5 Phrasing content

Phrasing content is the text of the document, as well as elements that mark up that text at the intra-paragraph level. Runs of [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) form [paragraphs](#3254-paragraphs).
- [`a`](#451-the-a-element)
- [`abbr`](#459-the-abbr-element)
- [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) (if it is a descendant of a [`map`](#4812-the-map-element) element)
- [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element)
- [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
- [`bdi`](#4524-the-bdi-element)
- [`bdo`](#4525-the-bdo-element)
- [`br`](#4527-the-br-element)
- [`button`](#4106-the-button-element)
- [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element)
- [`cite`](#456-the-cite-element)
- [`code`](#4515-the-code-element)
- [`data`](#4513-the-data-element)
- [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element)
- [`del`](#472-the-del-element)
- [`dfn`](#458-the-dfn-element)
- [`em`](#452-the-em-element)
- [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element)
- [`i`](#4520-the-i-element)
- [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element)
- [`img`](#483-the-img-element)
- [`input`](#4105-the-input-element)
- [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element)
- [`kbd`](#4518-the-kbd-element)
- [`label`](#4104-the-label-element)
- [`link`](#424-the-link-element) (if it is [allowed in the body](#424-the-link-element))
- [`map`](#4812-the-map-element)
- [`mark`](#4523-the-mark-element)
- [MathML `math`](https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#the-top-level-math-element)
- [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) (if the [`itemprop`](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute is present)
- [`meter`](#41014-the-meter-element)
- [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element)
- [`object`](#487-the-object-element)
- [`output`](#41012-the-output-element)
- [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element)
- [`progress`](#41013-the-progress-element)
- [`q`](#457-the-q-element)
- [`ruby`](#4510-the-ruby-element)
- [`s`](#455-the-s-element)
- [`samp`](#4517-the-samp-element)
- [`script`](#4121-the-script-element)
- [`select`](#4107-the-select-element)
- [`selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) (if it is a descendant of a [`button`](#4106-the-button-element) in a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element))
- [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element)
- [`small`](#454-the-small-element)
- [`span`](#4526-the-span-element)
- [`strong`](#453-the-strong-element)
- [`sub`](#4519-the-sub-and-sup-elements)
- [`sup`](#4519-the-sub-and-sup-elements)
- [SVG `svg`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/struct.html#elementdef-svg)
- [`template`](#4123-the-template-element)
- [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element)
- [`time`](#4514-the-time-element)
- [`u`](#4522-the-u-element)
- [`var`](#4516-the-var-element)
- [`video`](#488-the-video-element)
- [`wbr`](#4528-the-wbr-element)
- [autonomous custom elements](#4133-core-concepts)
- [text](#32525-phrasing-content)

> [!note]
> Most elements that are categorized as phrasing content can only contain elements that are themselves categorized as phrasing content, not any flow content.

Text, in the context of content models, means either nothing, or [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) nodes. [Text](#32525-phrasing-content) is sometimes used as a content model on its own, but is also [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content), and can be [inter-element whitespace](#325-content-models) (if the [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) nodes are empty or contain just [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points)).

[`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) nodes and attribute values must consist of [scalar values](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), excluding [noncharacters](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), and [controls](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) other than [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points). This specification includes extra constraints on the exact value of [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) nodes and attribute values depending on their precise context.

###### 3.2.5.2.6 Embedded content

Embedded content is content that imports another resource into the document, or content from another vocabulary that is inserted into the document.
- [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element)
- [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element)
- [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element)
- [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element)
- [`img`](#483-the-img-element)
- [MathML `math`](https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#the-top-level-math-element)
- [`object`](#487-the-object-element)
- [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element)
- [SVG `svg`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/struct.html#elementdef-svg)
- [`video`](#488-the-video-element)

Elements that are from namespaces other than the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) and that convey content but not metadata, are [embedded content](#32526-embedded-content) for the purposes of the content models defined in this specification. (For example, MathML or SVG.)

Some embedded content elements can have fallback content: content that is to be used when the external resource cannot be used (e.g. because it is of an unsupported format). The element definitions state what the fallback is, if any.

###### 3.2.5.2.7 Interactive content

Interactive content is content that is specifically intended for user interaction.
- [`a`](#451-the-a-element) (if the [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute is present)
- [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) (if the [`controls`](#481113-user-interface) attribute is present)
- [`button`](#4106-the-button-element)
- [`details`](#4111-the-details-element)
- [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element)
- [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element)
- [`img`](#483-the-img-element) (if the [`usemap`](#48141-authoring) or [`controls`](#483-the-img-element) attribute is present)
- [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) (if the [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is *not* in the [Hidden](#410511-hidden-state-typehidden) state)
- [`label`](#4104-the-label-element)
- [`select`](#4107-the-select-element)
- [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element)
- [`video`](#488-the-video-element) (if the [`controls`](#481113-user-interface) attribute is present)

###### 3.2.5.2.8 Palpable content

As a general rule, elements whose content model allows any [flow content](#32522-flow-content) or [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) should have at least one node in its [contents](#325-content-models) that is palpable content and that does not have the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute specified.

> [!note]
> [Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content) makes an element non-empty by providing either some descendant non-empty [text](#32525-phrasing-content), or else something users can hear ([`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) elements) or view ([`video`](#488-the-video-element), [`img`](#483-the-img-element), or [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) elements) or otherwise interact with (for example, interactive form controls).

This requirement is not a hard requirement, however, as there are many cases where an element can be empty legitimately, for example when it is used as a placeholder which will later be filled in by a script, or when the element is part of a template and would on most pages be filled in but on some pages is not relevant.

Conformance checkers are encouraged to provide a mechanism for authors to find elements that fail to fulfill this requirement, as an authoring aid.

The following elements are palpable content:
- [`a`](#451-the-a-element)
- [`abbr`](#459-the-abbr-element)

###### 3.2.5.2.9 Script-supporting elements

Script-supporting elements are those that do not [represent](#322-elements-in-the-dom) anything themselves (i.e. they are not rendered), but are used to support scripts, e.g. to provide functionality for the user.

The following elements are script-supporting elements:
- [`script`](#4121-the-script-element)
- [`template`](#4123-the-template-element)

##### 3.2.5.3 Transparent content models

Some elements are described as transparent; they have "transparent" in the description of their content model. The content model of a [transparent](#3253-transparent-content-models) element is derived from the content model of its parent element: the elements required in the part of the content model that is "transparent" are the same elements as required in the part of the content model of the parent of the transparent element in which the transparent element finds itself.

> [!example]
> For instance, an [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element) element inside a [`ruby`](#4510-the-ruby-element) element cannot contain an [`rt`](#4511-the-rt-element) element, because the part of the [`ruby`](#4510-the-ruby-element) element's content model that allows [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element) elements is the part that allows [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content), and the [`rt`](#4511-the-rt-element) element is not [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

> [!note]
> In some cases, where transparent elements are nested in each other, the process has to be applied iteratively.

> [!example]
> Consider the following markup fragment:
> 
> ```html
> <p><object><ins><map><a href="/">Apples</a></map></ins></object></p>
> ```
> 
> To check whether "Apples" is allowed inside the [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element, the content models are examined. The [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element's content model is transparent, as is the [`map`](#4812-the-map-element) element's, as is the [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element) element's, as is the [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element's. The [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element is found in the [`p`](#441-the-p-element) element, whose content model is [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content). Thus, "Apples" is allowed, as text is phrasing content.

When a transparent element has no parent, then the part of its content model that is "transparent" must instead be treated as accepting any [flow content](#32522-flow-content).

##### 3.2.5.4 Paragraphs

> [!note]
> The term [paragraph](#3254-paragraphs) as defined in this section is used for more than just the definition of the [`p`](#441-the-p-element) element. The [paragraph](#3254-paragraphs) concept defined here is used to describe how to interpret documents. The [`p`](#441-the-p-element) element is merely one of several ways of marking up a [paragraph](#3254-paragraphs).

A paragraph is typically a run of [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) that forms a block of text with one or more sentences that discuss a particular topic, as in typography, but can also be used for more general thematic grouping. For instance, an address is also a paragraph, as is a part of a form, a byline, or a stanza in a poem.

> [!example]
> In the following example, there are two paragraphs in a section. There is also a heading, which contains phrasing content that is not a paragraph. Note how the comments and [inter-element whitespace](#325-content-models) do not form paragraphs.
> 
> ```html
> <section>
>   <h2>Example of paragraphs</h2>
>   This is the <em>first</em> paragraph in this example.
>   <p>This is the second.</p>
>   <!-- This is not a paragraph. -->
> </section>
> ```

Paragraphs in [flow content](#32522-flow-content) are defined relative to what the document looks like without the [`a`](#451-the-a-element), [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element), [`del`](#472-the-del-element), and [`map`](#4812-the-map-element) elements complicating matters, since those elements, with their hybrid content models, can straddle paragraph boundaries, as shown in the first two examples below.

> [!note]
> Generally, having elements straddle paragraph boundaries is best avoided. Maintaining such markup can be difficult.

> [!example]
> The following example takes the markup from the earlier example and puts [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element) and [`del`](#472-the-del-element) elements around some of the markup to show that the text was changed (though in this case, the changes admittedly don't make much sense). Notice how this example has exactly the same paragraphs as the previous one, despite the [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element) and [`del`](#472-the-del-element) elements — the [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element) element straddles the heading and the first paragraph, and the [`del`](#472-the-del-element) element straddles the boundary between the two paragraphs.
> 
> ```html
> <section>
>   <ins><h2>Example of paragraphs</h2>
>   This is the <em>first</em> paragraph in</ins> this example<del>.
>   <p>This is the second.</p></del>
>   <!-- This is not a paragraph. -->
> </section>
> ```

Let view be a view of the DOM that replaces all [`a`](#451-the-a-element), [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element), [`del`](#472-the-del-element), and [`map`](#4812-the-map-element) elements in the document with their [contents](#325-content-models). Then, in view, for each run of sibling [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) nodes uninterrupted by other types of content, in an element that accepts content other than [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) as well as [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content), let first be the first node of the run, and let last be the last node of the run. For each such run that consists of at least one node that is neither [embedded content](#32526-embedded-content) nor [inter-element whitespace](#325-content-models), a paragraph exists in the original DOM from immediately before first to immediately after last. (Paragraphs can thus span across [`a`](#451-the-a-element), [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element), [`del`](#472-the-del-element), and [`map`](#4812-the-map-element) elements.)

Conformance checkers may warn authors of cases where they have paragraphs that overlap each other (this can happen with [`object`](#487-the-object-element), [`video`](#488-the-video-element), [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element), and [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) elements, and indirectly through elements in other namespaces that allow HTML to be further embedded therein, like [SVG `svg`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/struct.html#elementdef-svg) or [MathML `math`](https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#the-top-level-math-element)).

A [paragraph](#3254-paragraphs) is also formed explicitly by [`p`](#441-the-p-element) elements.

> [!note]
> The [`p`](#441-the-p-element) element can be used to wrap individual paragraphs when there would otherwise not be any content other than phrasing content to separate the paragraphs from each other.

> [!example]
> In the following example, the link spans half of the first paragraph, all of the heading separating the two paragraphs, and half of the second paragraph. It straddles the paragraphs and the heading.
> 
> ```html
> <header>
>  Welcome!
>  <a href="about.html">
>   This is home of...
>   <h1>The Falcons!</h1>
>   The Lockheed Martin multirole jet fighter aircraft!
>  </a>
>  This page discusses the F-16 Fighting Falcon's innermost secrets.
> </header>
> ```
> 
> Here is another way of marking this up, this time showing the paragraphs explicitly, and splitting the one link element into three:
> 
> ```html
> <header>
>  <p>Welcome! <a href="about.html">This is home of...</a></p>
>  <h1><a href="about.html">The Falcons!</a></h1>
>  <p><a href="about.html">The Lockheed Martin multirole jet
>  fighter aircraft!</a> This page discusses the F-16 Fighting
>  Falcon's innermost secrets.</p>
> </header>
> ```

> [!example]
> It is possible for paragraphs to overlap when using certain elements that define fallback content. For example, in the following section:
> 
> ```html
> <section>
>  <h2>My Cats</h2>
>  You can play with my cat simulator.
>  <object data="cats.sim">
>   To see the cat simulator, use one of the following links:
>   <ul>
>    <li><a href="cats.sim">Download simulator file</a>
>    <li><a href="https://sims.example.com/watch?v=LYds5xY4INU">Use online simulator</a>
>   </ul>
>   Alternatively, upgrade to the Mellblom Browser.
>  </object>
>  I'm quite proud of it.
> </section>
> ```
> 
> There are five paragraphs:
> 1. The paragraph that says "You can play with my cat simulator. *object* I'm quite proud of it.", where *object* is the [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element.
> 2. The paragraph that says "To see the cat simulator, use one of the following links:".
> 3. The paragraph that says "Download simulator file".
> 4. The paragraph that says "Use online simulator".
> 5. The paragraph that says "Alternatively, upgrade to the Mellblom Browser.".
> 
> The first paragraph is overlapped by the other four. A user agent that supports the "cats.sim" resource will only show the first one, but a user agent that shows the fallback will confusingly show the first sentence of the first paragraph as if it was in the same paragraph as the second one, and will show the last paragraph as if it was at the start of the second sentence of the first paragraph.
> 
> To avoid this confusion, explicit [`p`](#441-the-p-element) elements can be used. For example:
> 
> ```html
> <section>
>  <h2>My Cats</h2>
>  <p>You can play with my cat simulator.</p>
>  <object data="cats.sim">
>   <p>To see the cat simulator, use one of the following links:</p>
>   <ul>
>    <li><a href="cats.sim">Download simulator file</a>
>    <li><a href="https://sims.example.com/watch?v=LYds5xY4INU">Use online simulator</a>
>   </ul>
>   <p>Alternatively, upgrade to the Mellblom Browser.</p>
>  </object>
>  <p>I'm quite proud of it.</p>
> </section>
> ```

These attributes are only defined by this specification as attributes for [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility). When this specification refers to elements having these attributes, elements from namespaces that are not defined as having these attributes must not be considered as being elements with these attributes.

> [!example]
> For example, in the following XML fragment, the "`bogus`" element does not have a [`dir`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) attribute as defined in this specification, despite having an attribute with the literal name "`dir`". Thus, [the directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute) of the inner-most [`span`](#4526-the-span-element) element is '[rtl](#3264-the-dir-attribute)', inherited from the [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element indirectly through the "`bogus`" element.
> 
> ```html
> <div xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" dir="rtl">
>  <bogus xmlns="https://example.net/ns" dir="ltr">
>   <span xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml">
>   </span>
>  </bogus>
> </div>
> ```

---

DOM defines the user agent requirements for the `class`, `id`, and `slot` attributes for any element in any namespace. [\[DOM\]](#references)

The [`class`](#326-global-attributes), [`id`](#326-global-attributes), and [`slot`](#326-global-attributes) attributes may be specified on all [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility).

When specified on [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility), the [`class`](#326-global-attributes) attribute must have a value that is a [set of space-separated tokens](#237-space-separated-tokens) representing the various classes that the element belongs to.

> [!note]
> Assigning classes to an element affects class matching in selectors in CSS, the [`getElementsByClassName()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) method in the DOM, and other such features.
> 
> There are no additional restrictions on the tokens authors can use in the [`class`](#326-global-attributes) attribute, but authors are encouraged to use values that describe the nature of the content, rather than values that describe the desired presentation of the content.

When specified on [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility), the [`id`](#326-global-attributes) attribute value must be unique amongst all the [IDs](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) in the element's [tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) and must contain at least one character. The value must not contain any [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).

> [!note]
> The [`id`](#326-global-attributes) attribute specifies its element's [unique identifier (ID)](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element).
> 
> There are no other restrictions on what form an ID can take; in particular, IDs can consist of just digits, start with a digit, start with an underscore, consist of just punctuation, etc.
> 
> An element's [unique identifier](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) can be used for a variety of purposes, most notably as a way to link to specific parts of a document using [fragments](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment), as a way to target an element when scripting, and as a way to style a specific element from CSS.

Identifiers are opaque strings. Particular meanings should not be derived from the value of the [`id`](#326-global-attributes) attribute.

There are no conformance requirements for the [`slot`](#326-global-attributes) attribute specific to [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility).

> [!note]
> The [`slot`](#326-global-attributes) attribute is used to [assign a slot](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4224-assigning-slottables-and-slots) to an element: an element with a [`slot`](#326-global-attributes) attribute is [assigned](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4224-assigning-slottables-and-slots) to the [slot](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4221-slots) created by the [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element) element whose [name](#4124-the-slot-element) attribute's value matches that [`slot`](#326-global-attributes) attribute's value — but only if that [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element) element finds itself in the [shadow tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree) whose [root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees)'s [host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) has the corresponding [`slot`](#326-global-attributes) attribute value.

---

To enable assistive technology products to expose a more fine-grained interface than is otherwise possible with HTML elements and attributes, a set of [annotations for assistive technology products](#329-requirements-related-to-aria-and-to-platform-accessibility-apis) can be specified (the ARIA [`role`](#219-dependencies) and [`aria-*`](#219-dependencies) attributes). [\[ARIA\]](#references)

In [HTML documents](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), elements in the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) may have an `xmlns` attribute specified, if, and only if, it has the exact value "`http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml`". This does not apply to [XML documents](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

> [!note]
> In HTML, the `xmlns` attribute has absolutely no effect. It is basically a talisman. It is allowed merely to make migration to and from XML mildly easier. When parsed by an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents), the attribute ends up in no namespace. In XML, the attribute is part of the namespace declaration mechanism and always ends up in the "`http://www.w3.org/2000/xmlns/`" namespace.

---

XML also allows the use of the [`xml:space`](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-white-space) attribute in the [XML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) on any element in an [XML document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document). This attribute has no effect on [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility), as the default behavior in HTML is to preserve whitespace. [\[XML\]](#references)

> [!note]
> There is no way to serialize the [`xml:space`](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-white-space) attribute on [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) in the [`text/html`](#171-texthtml) syntax.

##### 3.2.6.1 The [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute

The `title` attribute [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) advisory information for the element, such as would be appropriate for a tooltip. On a link, this could be the title or a description of the target resource; on an image, it could be the image credit or a description of the image; on a paragraph, it could be a footnote or commentary on the text; on a citation, it could be further information about the source; on [interactive content](#32527-interactive-content), it could be a label for, or instructions for, use of the element; and so forth. The value is text.

> [!note]
> Relying on the [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute is currently discouraged as many user agents do not expose the attribute in an accessible manner as required by this specification (e.g., requiring a pointing device such as a mouse to cause a tooltip to appear, which excludes keyboard-only users and touch-only users, such as anyone with a modern phone or tablet).

If this attribute is omitted from an element, then it implies that the [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute of the nearest ancestor [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) with a [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute set is also relevant to this element. Setting the attribute overrides this, explicitly stating that the advisory information of any ancestors is not relevant to this element. Setting the attribute to the empty string indicates that the element has no advisory information.

If the [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute's value contains U+000A LINE FEED (LF) characters, the content is split into multiple lines. Each U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character represents a line break.

> [!example]
> Caution is advised with respect to the use of newlines in [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attributes.
> 
> For instance, the following snippet actually defines an abbreviation's expansion *with a line break in it*:
> 
> ```html
> <p>My logs show that there was some interest in <abbr title="Hypertext
> Transport Protocol">HTTP</abbr> today.</p>
> ```

Some elements, such as [`link`](#424-the-link-element), [`abbr`](#459-the-abbr-element), and [`input`](#4105-the-input-element), define additional semantics for the [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute beyond the semantics described above.

The advisory information of an element is the value that the following algorithm returns, with the algorithm being aborted once a value is returned. When the algorithm returns the empty string, then there is no advisory information.
1. If the element has a [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute, then return the result of running [normalize newlines](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) on its value.
2. If the element has a parent element, then return the parent element's [advisory information](#3261-the-title-attribute).
3. Return the empty string.

User agents should inform the user when elements have [advisory information](#3261-the-title-attribute), otherwise the information would not be discoverable.

---

##### 3.2.6.2 The [`lang`](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes) and [`xml:lang`](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-lang-tag) attributes

The `lang` attribute (in no namespace) specifies the primary language for the element's contents and for any of the element's attributes that contain text. Its value must be a valid BCP 47 language tag, or the empty string. Setting the attribute to the empty string indicates that the primary language is unknown. [\[BCP47\]](#references)

The [`lang`](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-lang-tag) attribute in the [XML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) is defined in XML. [\[XML\]](#references)

If these attributes are omitted from an element, then the language of this element is the same as the language of its parent element, if any (except for [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element) elements in a [shadow tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree)).

The [`lang`](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes) attribute in no namespace may be used on any [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility).

The [`lang` attribute in the XML namespace](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-lang-tag) may be used on [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) in [XML documents](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), as well as elements in other namespaces if the relevant specifications allow it (in particular, MathML and SVG allow [`lang` attributes in the XML namespace](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-lang-tag) to be specified on their elements). If both the [`lang`](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes) attribute in no namespace and the [`lang` attribute in the XML namespace](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-lang-tag) are specified on the same element, they must have exactly the same value when compared in an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) manner.

Authors must not use the [`lang` attribute in the XML namespace](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-lang-tag) on [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) in [HTML documents](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document). To ease migration to and from XML, authors may specify an attribute in no namespace with no prefix and with the literal localname "`xml:lang`" on [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) in [HTML documents](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), but such attributes must only be specified if a [`lang`](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes) attribute in no namespace is also specified, and both attributes must have the same value when compared in an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) manner.

> [!note]
> The attribute in no namespace with no prefix and with the literal localname "`xml:lang`" has no effect on language processing.

---

To determine the language of a node, user agents must use the first appropriate step in the following list:

If the node is an element that has a [`lang` attribute in the XML namespace](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-lang-tag) set

Use the value of that attribute.

If the node is an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) or an element in the [SVG namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces), and it has a [`lang`](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes) in no namespace attribute set

Use the value of that attribute.

If the node's parent is a [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot)

Use the [language](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes) of that [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot)'s [host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment).

If the node's [parent element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) is not null

Use the [language](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes) of that [parent element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element).

Otherwise

If there is a [pragma-set default language](#4253-pragma-directives) set, then that is the language of the node. If there is no [pragma-set default language](#4253-pragma-directives) set, then language information from a higher-level protocol (such as HTTP), if any, must be used as the final fallback language instead. In the absence of any such language information, and in cases where the higher-level protocol reports multiple languages, the language of the node is unknown, and the corresponding language tag is the empty string.

If the resulting value is not a recognized language tag, then it must be treated as an unknown language having the given language tag, distinct from all other languages. For the purposes of roundtripping or communicating with other services that expect language tags, user agents should pass unknown language tags through unmodified, and tagged as being BCP 47 language tags, so that subsequent services do not interpret the data as another type of language description. [\[BCP47\]](#references)

> [!example]
> Thus, for instance, an element with `lang="xyzzy"` would be matched by the selector `:lang(xyzzy)` (e.g. in CSS), but it would not be matched by `:lang(abcde)`, even though both are equally invalid. Similarly, if a web browser and screen reader working in unison communicated about the language of the element, the browser would tell the screen reader that the language was "xyzzy", even if it knew it was invalid, just in case the screen reader actually supported a language with that tag after all. Even if the screen reader supported both BCP 47 and another syntax for encoding language names, and in that other syntax the string "xyzzy" was a way to denote the Belarusian language, it would be *incorrect* for the screen reader to then start treating text as Belarusian, because "xyzzy" is not how Belarusian is described in BCP 47 codes (BCP 47 uses the code "be" for Belarusian).

If the resulting value is the empty string, then it must be interpreted as meaning that the language of the node is explicitly unknown.

---

User agents may use the element's language to determine proper processing or rendering (e.g. in the selection of appropriate fonts or pronunciations, for dictionary selection, or for the user interfaces of form controls such as date pickers).

##### 3.2.6.3 The [`translate`](#3263-the-translate-attribute) attribute

The `translate` attribute is used to specify whether an element's attribute values and the values of its [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node children are to be translated when the page is localized, or whether to leave them unchanged. It is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `yes` | Yes | Sets [translation mode](#3263-the-translate-attribute) to [translate-enabled](#3263-the-translate-attribute). |
| `no` | No | Sets [translation mode](#3263-the-translate-attribute) to [no-translate](#3263-the-translate-attribute). |

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the Inherit state, and its *[empty value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* is the [Yes](#3263-the-translate-attribute) state.

Each element (even non-HTML elements) has a translation mode, which is in either the [translate-enabled](#3263-the-translate-attribute) state or the [no-translate](#3263-the-translate-attribute) state. If an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility)'s [`translate`](#3263-the-translate-attribute) attribute is in the [Yes](#3263-the-translate-attribute) state, then the element's [translation mode](#3263-the-translate-attribute) is in the [translate-enabled](#3263-the-translate-attribute) state; otherwise, if the element's [`translate`](#3263-the-translate-attribute) attribute is in the [No](#3263-the-translate-attribute) state, then the element's [translation mode](#3263-the-translate-attribute) is in the [no-translate](#3263-the-translate-attribute) state. Otherwise, either the element's [`translate`](#3263-the-translate-attribute) attribute is in the [Inherit](#3263-the-translate-attribute) state, or the element is not an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) and thus does not have a [`translate`](#3263-the-translate-attribute) attribute; in either case, the element's [translation mode](#3263-the-translate-attribute) is in the same state as its [parent element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element)'s, if any, or in the [translate-enabled](#3263-the-translate-attribute) state, if the element's [parent element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) is null.

When an element is in the translate-enabled state, the element's [translatable attributes](#3263-the-translate-attribute) and the values of its [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node children are to be translated when the page is localized.

When an element is in the no-translate state, the element's attribute values and the values of its [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node children are to be left as-is when the page is localized, e.g. because the element contains a person's name or a name of a computer program.

The following attributes are translatable attributes:
- [`abbr`](#4910-the-th-element) on [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) elements
- `alt` on [`area`](#4813-the-area-element), [`img`](#483-the-img-element), and [`input`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) elements
- [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) on [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) elements, if the [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute specifies a metadata name whose value is known to be translatable
- [`download`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) on [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements
- `label` on [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element), [`option`](#41010-the-option-element), and [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) elements
- [`lang`](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes) on [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility); must be "translated" to match the language used in the translation
- `placeholder` on [`input`](#4105310-the-placeholder-attribute) and [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements
- [`srcdoc`](#485-the-iframe-element) on [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) elements; must be parsed and recursively processed
- [`style`](#3265-the-style-attribute) on [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility); must be parsed and recursively processed (e.g. for the values of ['content'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#content%E2%91%A0) properties)
- [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) on all [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility)
- [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) on [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements with a [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute in the [Button](#4105121-button-state-typebutton) state or the [Reset Button](#4105120-reset-button-state-typereset) state

Other specifications may define other attributes that are also [translatable attributes](#3263-the-translate-attribute). For example, ARIA would define the [`aria-label`](https://w3c.github.io/aria/#aria-label) attribute as translatable.

---

The `translate` IDL attribute must, on getting, return true if the element's [translation mode](#3263-the-translate-attribute) is [translate-enabled](#3263-the-translate-attribute), and false otherwise. On setting, it must set the content attribute's value to "`yes`" if the new value is true, and set the content attribute's value to "`no`" otherwise.

> [!example]
> In this example, everything in the document is to be translated when the page is localized, except the sample keyboard input and sample program output:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <html lang=en> <!-- default on the document element is translate=yes -->
>  <head>
>   <title>The Bee Game</title> <!-- implied translate=yes inherited from ancestors -->
>  </head>
>  <body>
>   <p>The Bee Game is a text adventure game in English.</p>
>   <p>When the game launches, the first thing you should do is type
>   <kbd translate=no>eat honey</kbd>. The game will respond with:</p>
>   <pre><samp translate=no>Yum yum! That was some good honey!</samp></pre>
>  </body>
> </html>
> ```

##### 3.2.6.4 The [`dir`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) attribute

The `dir` attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ltr` | LTR | The contents of the element are explicitly directionally isolated left-to-right text. |
| `rtl` | RTL | The contents of the element are explicitly directionally isolated right-to-left text. |
| `auto` | Auto | The contents of the element are explicitly directionally isolated text, but the direction is to be determined programmatically using the contents of the element (as described below). |

> [!note]
> The heuristic used by the [Auto](#3264-the-dir-attribute) state is very crude (it just looks at the first character with a strong directionality, in a manner analogous to the Paragraph Level determination in the bidirectional algorithm). Authors are urged to only use this value as a last resort when the direction of the text is truly unknown and no better server-side heuristic can be applied. [\[BIDI\]](#references)
> 
> For [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) and [`pre`](#443-the-pre-element) elements, the heuristic is applied on a per-paragraph level.

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the Undefined state.

---

The directionality of an element (any element, not just an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility)) is either 'ltr' or 'rtl'. To compute the [directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute) given an element element, switch on element's [`dir`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) attribute state:

[LTR](#3264-the-dir-attribute)

Return '[ltr](#3264-the-dir-attribute)'.

[RTL](#3264-the-dir-attribute)

Return '[rtl](#3264-the-dir-attribute)'.

[Auto](#3264-the-dir-attribute)
1. Let result be the [auto directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute) of element.
2. If result is null, then return '[ltr](#3264-the-dir-attribute)'.
3. Return result.

[Undefined](#3264-the-dir-attribute)

If element is a [`bdi`](#4524-the-bdi-element) element
1. Let result be the [auto directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute) of element.
2. If result is null, then return '[ltr](#3264-the-dir-attribute)'.
3. Return result.

If element is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Telephone](#410513-telephone-state-typetel) state

Return '[ltr](#3264-the-dir-attribute)'.

Otherwise

Return the [parent directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute) of element.

> [!note]
> Since the [`dir`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) attribute is only defined for [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility), it cannot be present on elements from other namespaces. Thus, elements from other namespaces always end up using the [parent directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute).

The auto-directionality form-associated elements are:
- [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Hidden](#410511-hidden-state-typehidden), [Text](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch), [Search](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch), [Telephone](#410513-telephone-state-typetel), [URL](#410514-url-state-typeurl), [Email](#410515-email-state-typeemail), [Password](#410516-password-state-typepassword), [Submit Button](#4105118-submit-button-state-typesubmit), [Reset Button](#4105120-reset-button-state-typereset), or [Button](#4105121-button-state-typebutton) state, and
- [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements.

To compute the auto directionality given an element element:
1. If element is an [auto-directionality form-associated element](#3264-the-dir-attribute):
   1. If element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) contains a character of bidirectional character type AL or R, and there is no character of bidirectional character type L anywhere before it in the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value), then return '[rtl](#3264-the-dir-attribute)'. [\[BIDI\]](#references)
   2. If element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is not the empty string, then return '[ltr](#3264-the-dir-attribute)'.
   3. Return null.
2. If element is a [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element) element whose [root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) is a [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) and element's [assigned nodes](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4221-slots) are not empty:
   1. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) node child of element's [assigned nodes](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4221-slots):
      1. Let childDirection be null.
      2. If child is a [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node, then set childDirection to the [text node directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute) of child.
      3. Otherwise:
         1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): child is an [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) node.
         2. Set childDirection to the [contained text auto directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute) of child with *[canExcludeRoot](#3264-the-dir-attribute)* set to true.
      4. If childDirection is not null, then return childDirection.
   2. Return null.
3. Return the [contained text auto directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute) of element with *[canExcludeRoot](#3264-the-dir-attribute)* set to false.

To compute the contained text auto directionality of an element element with a boolean canExcludeRoot:
1. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) node descendant of element's [descendants](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees):
   1. If any of
      - descendant
      - any ancestor element of descendant that is a descendant of element
      - if canExcludeRoot is true, element

      is one of
      - a [`bdi`](#4524-the-bdi-element) element
      - a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element
      - a [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element
      - a [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element
      - an element whose [`dir`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) attribute is not in the [Undefined](#3264-the-dir-attribute) state

      then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).

   2. If descendant is a [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element) element whose [root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) is a [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot), then return the [directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute) of that [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot)'s [host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment).
   3. If descendant is not a [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   4. Let result be the [text node directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute) of descendant.
   5. If result is not null, then return result.

2. Return null.

To compute the text node directionality given a [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node text:
1. If text's [data](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#410-interface-characterdata) does not contain a code point whose bidirectional character type is L, AL, or R, then return null. [\[BIDI\]](#references)
2. Let codePoint be the first code point in text's [data](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#410-interface-characterdata) whose bidirectional character type is L, AL, or R.
3. If codePoint is of bidirectional character type AL or R, then return '[rtl](#3264-the-dir-attribute)'.
4. If codePoint is of bidirectional character type L, then return '[ltr](#3264-the-dir-attribute)'.

To compute the parent directionality given an element element:
1. Let parentNode be element's parent node.
2. If parentNode is a [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot), then return the [directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute) of parentNode's [host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment).
3. If parentNode is an element, then return the [directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute) of parentNode.
4. Return '[ltr](#3264-the-dir-attribute)'.

> [!note]
> This attribute [has rendering requirements involving the bidirectional algorithm](#3282-user-agent-conformance-criteria).

---

The directionality of an attribute of an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility), which is used when the text of that attribute is to be included in the rendering in some manner, is determined as per the first appropriate set of steps from the following list:

If the attribute is a [directionality-capable attribute](#3264-the-dir-attribute) and the element's [`dir`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) attribute is in the [Auto](#3264-the-dir-attribute) state

Find the first character (in logical order) of the attribute's value that is of bidirectional character type L, AL, or R. [\[BIDI\]](#references)

If such a character is found and it is of bidirectional character type AL or R, the [directionality of the attribute](#3264-the-dir-attribute) is '[rtl](#3264-the-dir-attribute)'.

Otherwise, the [directionality of the attribute](#3264-the-dir-attribute) is '[ltr](#3264-the-dir-attribute)'.

Otherwise

The [directionality of the attribute](#3264-the-dir-attribute) is the same as [the element's directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute).

The following attributes are directionality-capable attributes:
- [`abbr`](#4910-the-th-element) on [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) elements
- `alt` on [`area`](#4813-the-area-element), [`img`](#483-the-img-element), and [`input`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) elements
- [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) on [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) elements, if the [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute specifies a metadata name whose value is primarily intended to be human-readable rather than machine-readable
- `label` on [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element), [`option`](#41010-the-option-element), and [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) elements
- `placeholder` on [`input`](#4105310-the-placeholder-attribute) and [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements
- [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) on all [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility)

---

`document.dir [ = value ]`

Returns [the `html` element](#317-dom-tree-accessors)'s [`dir`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) attribute's value, if any.

Can be set, to either "`ltr`", "`rtl`", or "`auto`" to replace [the `html` element](#317-dom-tree-accessors)'s [`dir`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) attribute's value.

If there is no [`html` element](#317-dom-tree-accessors), returns the empty string and ignores new values.

The `dir` IDL attribute on an element must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`dir`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) content attribute of that element, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

The `dir` IDL attribute on [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) objects must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`dir`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) content attribute of [the `html` element](#317-dom-tree-accessors), if any, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes). If there is no such element, then the attribute must return the empty string and do nothing on setting.

> [!note]
> Authors are strongly encouraged to use the [`dir`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) attribute to indicate text direction rather than using CSS, since that way their documents will continue to render correctly even in the absence of CSS (e.g. as interpreted by search engines).

> [!example]
> This markup fragment is of an IM conversation.
> 
> ```html
> <p dir=auto class="u1"><b><bdi>Student</bdi>:</b> How do you write "What's your name?" in Arabic?</p>
> <p dir=auto class="u2"><b><bdi>Teacher</bdi>:</b> ما اسمك؟</p>
> <p dir=auto class="u1"><b><bdi>Student</bdi>:</b> Thanks.</p>
> <p dir=auto class="u2"><b><bdi>Teacher</bdi>:</b> That's written "شكرًا".</p>
> <p dir=auto class="u2"><b><bdi>Teacher</bdi>:</b> Do you know how to write "Please"?</p>
> <p dir=auto class="u1"><b><bdi>Student</bdi>:</b> "من فضلك", right?</p>
> ```
> 
> Given a suitable style sheet and the default alignment styles for the [`p`](#441-the-p-element) element, namely to align the text to the *start edge* of the paragraph, the resulting rendering could be as follows:
> 
> ![Each paragraph rendered as a separate block, with the paragraphs left-aligned except the second paragraph and the last one, which would be right aligned, with the usernames ('Student' and 'Teacher' in this example) flush right, with a colon to their left, and the text first to the left of that.](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/im.png)
> 
> As noted earlier, the [`auto`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) value is not a panacea. The final paragraph in this example is misinterpreted as being right-to-left text, since it begins with an Arabic character, which causes the "right?" to be to the left of the Arabic text.

##### 3.2.6.5 The [`style`](#3265-the-style-attribute) attribute

All [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) may have the `style` content attribute set. This is a [style attribute](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-style-attr/#style-attribute) as defined by CSS Style Attributes. [\[CSSATTR\]](#references)

In user agents that support CSS, the attribute's value must be parsed when the attribute is added or has its value changed, according to the rules given for [style attributes](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-style-attr/#style-attribute). [\[CSSATTR\]](#references)

However, if the [Should element's inline behavior be blocked by Content Security Policy?](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#should-block-inline) algorithm returns "`Blocked`" when executed upon the attribute's [element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), "`style attribute`", and the attribute's value, then the style rules defined in the attribute's value must not be applied to the [element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element). [\[CSP\]](#references)

Documents that use [`style`](#3265-the-style-attribute) attributes on any of their elements must still be comprehensible and usable if those attributes were removed.

> [!note]
> In particular, using the [`style`](#3265-the-style-attribute) attribute to hide and show content, or to convey meaning that is otherwise not included in the document, is non-conforming. (To hide and show content, use the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute.)

---

`element.style`

Returns a [`CSSStyleDeclaration`](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#the-cssstyledeclaration-interface) object for the element's [`style`](#3265-the-style-attribute) attribute.

The [`style`](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#dom-elementcssinlinestyle-style) IDL attribute is defined in CSS Object Model. [\[CSSOM\]](#references)

> [!example]
> In the following example, the words that refer to colors are marked up using the [`span`](#4526-the-span-element) element and the [`style`](#3265-the-style-attribute) attribute to make those words show up in the relevant colors in visual media.
> 
> ```html
> <p>My sweat suit is <span style="color: green; background:
> transparent">green</span> and my eyes are <span style="color: blue;
> background: transparent">blue</span>.</p>
> ```

##### 3.2.6.6 Embedding custom non-visible data with the [`data-*`](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes) attributes

A custom data attribute is an attribute in no namespace whose name starts with the string "`data-`", has at least one character after the hyphen, is a [valid attribute local name](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#14-name-validation), and contains no [ASCII upper alphas](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).

> [!note]
> All attribute names on [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) in [HTML documents](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) get ASCII-lowercased automatically, so the restriction on ASCII uppercase letters doesn't affect such documents.

[Custom data attributes](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes) are intended to store custom data, state, annotations, and similar, private to the page or application, for which there are no more appropriate attributes or elements.

These attributes are not intended for use by software that is not known to the administrators of the site that uses the attributes. For generic extensions that are to be used by multiple independent tools, either this specification should be extended to provide the feature explicitly, or a technology like [microdata](#5-microdata) should be used (with a standardized vocabulary).

> [!example]
> For instance, a site about music could annotate list items representing tracks in an album with custom data attributes containing the length of each track. This information could then be used by the site itself to allow the user to sort the list by track length, or to filter the list for tracks of certain lengths.
> 
> ```html
> <ol>
>  <li data-length="2m11s">Beyond The Sea</li>
>  ...
> </ol>
> ```
> 
> It would be inappropriate, however, for the user to use generic software not associated with that music site to search for tracks of a certain length by looking at this data.
> 
> This is because these attributes are intended for use by the site's own scripts, and are not a generic extension mechanism for publicly-usable metadata.

> [!example]
> Similarly, a page author could write markup that provides information for a translation tool that they are intending to use:
> 
> ```html
> <p>The third <span data-mytrans-de="Anspruch">claim</span> covers the case of <span
> translate="no">HTML</span> markup.</p>
> ```
> 
> In this example, the "`data-mytrans-de`" attribute gives specific text for the MyTrans product to use when translating the phrase "claim" to German. However, the standard [`translate`](#3263-the-translate-attribute) attribute is used to tell it that in all languages, "HTML" is to remain unchanged. When a standard attribute is available, there is no need for a [custom data attribute](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes) to be used.

> [!example]
> In this example, custom data attributes are used to store the result of a feature detection for [`PaymentRequest`](https://w3c.github.io/payment-request/#dom-paymentrequest), which could be used in CSS to style a checkout page differently.
> 
> ```html
> <script>
>  if ('PaymentRequest' in window) {
>    document.documentElement.dataset.hasPaymentRequest = '';
>  }
> </script>
> ```
> 
> Here, the `data-has-payment-request` attribute is effectively being used as a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes); it is enough to check the presence of the attribute. However, if the author so wishes, it could later be populated with some value, maybe to indicate limited functionality of the feature.

Every [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) may have any number of [custom data attributes](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes) specified, with any value.

Authors should carefully design such extensions so that when the attributes are ignored and any associated CSS dropped, the page is still usable.

User agents must not derive any implementation behavior from these attributes or values. Specifications intended for user agents must not define these attributes to have any meaningful values.

JavaScript libraries may use the [custom data attributes](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes), as they are considered to be part of the page on which they are used. Authors of libraries that are reused by many authors are encouraged to include their name in the attribute names, to reduce the risk of clashes. Where it makes sense, library authors are also encouraged to make the exact name used in the attribute names customizable, so that libraries whose authors unknowingly picked the same name can be used on the same page, and so that multiple versions of a particular library can be used on the same page even when those versions are not mutually compatible.

> [!example]
> For example, a library called "DoQuery" could use attribute names like `data-doquery-range`, and a library called "jJo" could use attributes names like `data-jjo-range`. The jJo library could also provide an API to set which prefix to use (e.g. `J.setDataPrefix('j2')`, making the attributes have names like `data-j2-range`).

---

`element.dataset`

Returns a [`DOMStringMap`](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes) object for the element's [`data-*`](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes) attributes.

Hyphenated names become camel-cased. For example, `data-foo-bar=""` becomes `element.dataset.fooBar`.

The `dataset` IDL attribute provides convenient accessors for all the [`data-*`](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes) attributes on an element. On getting, the [`dataset`](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes) IDL attribute must return a [`DOMStringMap`](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes) whose associated element is this element.

The [`DOMStringMap`](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes) interface is used for the [`dataset`](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes) attribute. Each [`DOMStringMap`](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes) has an associated element.

```webidl
[Exposed=Window,
 LegacyOverrideBuiltIns]
interface DOMStringMap {
  getter DOMString (DOMString name);
  [CEReactions] setter undefined (DOMString name, DOMString value);
  [CEReactions] deleter undefined (DOMString name);
};
```

To get a `DOMStringMap`'s name-value pairs, run the following algorithm:
1. Let list be an empty list of name-value pairs.
2. For each content attribute on the [`DOMStringMap`](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes)'s [associated element](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes) whose first five characters are the string "`data-`" and whose remaining characters (if any) do not include any [ASCII upper alphas](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), in the order that those attributes are listed in the element's [attribute list](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), add a name-value pair to list whose name is the attribute's name with the first five characters removed and whose value is the attribute's value.
3. For each name in list, for each U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS character (-) in the name that is followed by an [ASCII lower alpha](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), remove the U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS character (-) and replace the character that followed it by the same character [converted to ASCII uppercase](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).
4. Return list.

The [supported property names](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-supported-property-names) on a [`DOMStringMap`](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes) object at any instant are the names of each pair returned from [getting the `DOMStringMap`'s name-value pairs](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes) at that instant, in the order returned.

To [determine the value of a named property](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-determine-the-value-of-a-named-property) name for a [`DOMStringMap`](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes), return the value component of the name-value pair whose name component is name in the list returned from [getting the `DOMStringMap`'s name-value pairs](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes).

To [set the value of a new named property](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-set-the-value-of-a-new-named-property) or [set the value of an existing named property](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-set-the-value-of-an-existing-named-property) for a [`DOMStringMap`](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes), given a property name name and a new value value, run the following steps:
1. If name contains a U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS character (-) followed by an [ASCII lower alpha](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), then throw a ["`SyntaxError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. For each [ASCII upper alpha](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) in name, insert a U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS character (-) before the character and replace the character with the same character [converted to ASCII lowercase](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).
3. Insert the string `data-` at the front of name.
4. If name is not a [valid attribute local name](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#14-name-validation), then throw an ["`InvalidCharacterError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidcharactererror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
5. [Set an attribute value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) for the [`DOMStringMap`](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes)'s [associated element](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes) using name and value.

To [delete an existing named property](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-delete-an-existing-named-property) name for a [`DOMStringMap`](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes), run the following steps:
1. For each [ASCII upper alpha](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) in name, insert a U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS character (-) before the character and replace the character with the same character [converted to ASCII lowercase](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).
2. Insert the string `data-` at the front of name.
3. [Remove an attribute by name](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) given name and the [`DOMStringMap`](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes)'s [associated element](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes).

> [!note]
> This algorithm will only get invoked by Web IDL for names that are given by the earlier algorithm for [getting the `DOMStringMap`'s name-value pairs](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes). [\[WEBIDL\]](#references)

> [!example]
> If a web page wanted an element to represent a space ship, e.g. as part of a game, it would have to use the [`class`](#326-global-attributes) attribute along with [`data-*`](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes) attributes:
> 
> ```html
> <div class="spaceship" data-ship-id="92432"
>      data-weapons="laser 2" data-shields="50%"
>      data-x="30" data-y="10" data-z="90">
>  <button class="fire"
>          onclick="spaceships[this.parentNode.dataset.shipId].fire()">
>   Fire
>  </button>
> </div>
> ```
> 
> Notice how the hyphenated attribute name becomes camel-cased in the API.

> [!example]
> Given the following fragment and elements with similar constructions:
> 
> ```html
> <img class="tower" id="tower5" data-x="12" data-y="5"
>      data-ai="robotarget" data-hp="46" data-ability="flames"
>      src="towers/rocket.png" alt="Rocket Tower">
> ```
> 
> ...one could imagine a function `splashDamage()` that takes some arguments, the first of which is the element to process:
> 
> ```javascript
> function splashDamage(node, x, y, damage) {
>   if (node.classList.contains('tower') && // checking the 'class' attribute
>       node.dataset.x == x && // reading the 'data-x' attribute
>       node.dataset.y == y) { // reading the 'data-y' attribute
>     var hp = parseInt(node.dataset.hp); // reading the 'data-hp' attribute
>     hp = hp - damage;
>     if (hp < 0) {
>       hp = 0;
>       node.dataset.ai = 'dead'; // setting the 'data-ai' attribute
>       delete node.dataset.ability; // removing the 'data-ability' attribute
>     }
>     node.dataset.hp = hp; // setting the 'data-hp' attribute
>   }
> }
> ```

#### 3.2.7 The [`innerText`](#327-the-innertext-and-outertext-properties) and [`outerText`](#327-the-innertext-and-outertext-properties) properties

`element.innerText [ = value ]`

Returns the element's text content "as rendered".

Can be set, to replace the element's children with the given value, but with line breaks converted to [`br`](#4527-the-br-element) elements.

`element.outerText [ = value ]`

Returns the element's text content "as rendered".

Can be set, to replace the element with the given value, but with line breaks converted to [`br`](#4527-the-br-element) elements.

The get the text steps, given an [HTMLElement](#322-elements-in-the-dom) element, are:
1. If element is not [being rendered](#151-introduction) or if the user agent is a non-CSS user agent, then return element's [descendant text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text).

   > [!note]
   > This step can produce surprising results, as when the [`innerText`](#327-the-innertext-and-outertext-properties) getter is invoked on an element not [being rendered](#151-introduction), its text contents are returned, but when accessed on an element that is [being rendered](#151-introduction), all of its children that are not [being rendered](#151-introduction) have their text contents ignored.

2. Let results be a new empty [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).
3. For each child node node of element:
   1. Let current be the [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) resulting from running the [rendered text collection steps](#327-the-innertext-and-outertext-properties) with node. Each item in results will either be a [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) or a positive integer (a *required line break count*).

      > [!note]
      > Intuitively, a *required line break count* item means that a certain number of line breaks appear at that point, but they can be collapsed with the line breaks induced by adjacent *required line break count* items, reminiscent to CSS margin-collapsing.

   2. For each item item in current, append item to results.

4. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) any items from results that are the empty string.
5. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) any runs of consecutive *required line break count* items at the start or end of results.
6. [Replace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) each remaining run of consecutive *required line break count* items with a string consisting of as many U+000A LF code points as the maximum of the values in the *required line break count* items.
7. Return the concatenation of the string items in results.

The `innerText` and `outerText` getter steps are to return the result of running [get the text steps](#327-the-innertext-and-outertext-properties) with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).

The rendered text collection steps, given a [node](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) node, are as follows:
1. Let items be the result of running the [rendered text collection steps](#327-the-innertext-and-outertext-properties) with each child node of node in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), and then concatenating the results to a single [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).
2. If node's [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of ['visibility'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#propdef-visibility) is not 'visible', then return items.
3. If node is not [being rendered](#151-introduction), then return items. For the purpose of this step, the following elements must act as described if the [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of the ['display'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop) property is not 'none':
   - [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) elements have an associated non-replaced inline [CSS box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#css-box) whose child boxes include only those of [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) and [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element descendant nodes;
   - [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) elements have an associated non-replaced block-level [CSS box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#css-box) whose child boxes include only those of [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element descendant nodes; and
   - [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements have an associated non-replaced block-level [CSS box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#css-box) whose child boxes are as normal for non-replaced block-level [CSS boxes](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#css-box).

   > [!note]
   > items can be non-empty due to 'display:contents'.

4. If node is a [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node, then for each CSS text box produced by node, in content order, compute the text of the box after application of the CSS ['white-space'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#white-space-property) processing rules and ['text-transform'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#text-transform-property) rules, set items to the [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of the resulting strings, and return items. The CSS ['white-space'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#white-space-property) processing rules are slightly modified: collapsible spaces at the end of lines are always collapsed, but they are only removed if the line is the last line of the block, or it ends with a [`br`](#4527-the-br-element) element. Soft hyphens should be preserved. [\[CSSTEXT\]](#references)
5. If node is a [`br`](#4527-the-br-element) element, then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) a string containing a single U+000A LF code point to items.
6. If node's [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of ['display'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop) is ['table-cell'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables/#table-cell), and node's [CSS box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#css-box) is not the last ['table-cell'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables/#table-cell) box of its enclosing ['table-row'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables/#table-row) box, then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) a string containing a single U+0009 TAB code point to items.
7. If node's [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of ['display'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop) is ['table-row'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables/#table-row), and node's [CSS box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#css-box) is not the last ['table-row'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables/#table-row) box of the nearest ancestor ['table'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables/#table) box, then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) a string containing a single U+000A LF code point to items.
8. If node is a [`p`](#441-the-p-element) element, then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) 2 (a *required line break count*) at the beginning and end of items.
9. If node's [used value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#used-value) of ['display'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop) is [block-level](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#block-level) or ['table-caption'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables/#table-caption), then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) 1 (a *required line break count*) at the beginning and end of items. [\[CSSDISPLAY\]](#references)

   > [!note]
   > Floats and absolutely-positioned elements fall into this category.

10. Return items.

> [!note]
> Note that descendant nodes of most replaced elements (e.g., [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element), [`input`](#4105-the-input-element), and [`video`](#488-the-video-element) — but not [`button`](#4106-the-button-element)) are not rendered by CSS, strictly speaking, and therefore have no [CSS boxes](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#css-box) for the purposes of this algorithm.

> [!warning]
> This algorithm is amenable to being generalized to work on [ranges](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-interface-abstractrange). Then we can use it as the basis for [`Selection`](https://w3c.github.io/selection-api/#selection-interface)'s stringifier and maybe expose it directly on [ranges](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-interface-abstractrange). See [Bugzilla bug 10583](https://www.w3.org/Bugs/Public/show_bug.cgi?id=10583).

---

The set the inner text steps, given an [HTMLElement](#322-elements-in-the-dom) element, and a string value are:
1. Let fragment be the [rendered text fragment](#327-the-innertext-and-outertext-properties) for value given element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
2. [Replace all](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) with fragment within element.

The [`innerText`](#327-the-innertext-and-outertext-properties) setter steps are to run [set the inner text steps](#327-the-innertext-and-outertext-properties) with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) and the given value.

The [`outerText`](#327-the-innertext-and-outertext-properties) setter steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s parent is null, then throw a ["`NoModificationAllowedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#nomodificationallowederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Let next be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [next sibling](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
3. Let previous be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [previous sibling](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
4. Let fragment be the [rendered text fragment](#327-the-innertext-and-outertext-properties) for the given value given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
5. If fragment has no [children](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), then [append](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) a new [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node whose [data](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#410-interface-characterdata) is the empty string and [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) is [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) to fragment.
6. [Replace](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) with fragment within [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s parent.
7. If next is non-null and next's [previous sibling](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) is a [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node, then [merge with the next text node](#327-the-innertext-and-outertext-properties) given next's [previous sibling](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
8. If previous is a [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node, then [merge with the next text node](#327-the-innertext-and-outertext-properties) given previous.

The rendered text fragment for a string input given a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document is the result of running the following steps:
1. Let fragment be the result of [creating a document fragment](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) given document.
2. Let position be a [position variable](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) for input, initially pointing at the start of input.
3. Let text be the empty string.
4. While position is not past the end of input:
   1. [Collect a sequence of code points](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) that are not U+000A LF or U+000D CR from input given position, and set text to the result.
   2. If text is not the empty string, then [append](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) a new [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node whose [data](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#410-interface-characterdata) is text and [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) is document to fragment.
   3. While position is not past the end of input, and the code point at position is either U+000A LF or U+000D CR:
