      1. If the code point at position is U+000D CR and the next code point is U+000A LF, then advance position to the next code point in input.
      2. Advance position to the next code point in input.
      3. [Append](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) the result of [creating an element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) given document, "`br`", and the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) to fragment.
5. Return fragment.

To merge with the next text node given a [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node node:
1. Let next be node's [next sibling](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
2. If next is not a [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node, then return.
3. [Replace data](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#410-interface-characterdata) with node, node's [data](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#410-interface-characterdata)'s [length](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings), 0, and next's [data](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#410-interface-characterdata).
4. [Remove](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) next.

#### 3.2.8 Requirements relating to the bidirectional algorithm

##### 3.2.8.1 Authoring conformance criteria for bidirectional-algorithm formatting characters

[Text content](#32525-phrasing-content) in [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) with [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) nodes in their [contents](#325-content-models), and text in attributes of [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) that allow free-form text, may contain characters in the ranges U+202A to U+202E and U+2066 to U+2069 (the bidirectional-algorithm formatting characters). [\[BIDI\]](#references)

> [!note]
> Authors are encouraged to use the [`dir`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) attribute, the [`bdo`](#4525-the-bdo-element) element, and the [`bdi`](#4524-the-bdi-element) element, rather than maintaining the bidirectional-algorithm formatting characters manually. The bidirectional-algorithm formatting characters interact poorly with CSS.

##### 3.2.8.2 User agent conformance criteria

User agents must implement the Unicode bidirectional algorithm to determine the proper ordering of characters when rendering documents and parts of documents. [\[BIDI\]](#references)

The mapping of HTML to the Unicode bidirectional algorithm must be done in one of three ways. Either the user agent must implement CSS, including in particular the CSS ['unicode-bidi'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#unicode-bidi), ['direction'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#direction), and ['content'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#content%E2%91%A0) properties, and must have, in its user agent style sheet, the rules using those properties given in this specification's [rendering](#15-rendering) section, or, alternatively, the user agent must act as if it implemented just the aforementioned properties and had a user agent style sheet that included all the aforementioned rules, but without letting style sheets specified in documents override them, or, alternatively, the user agent must implement another styling language with equivalent semantics. [\[CSSGC\]](#references)

The following elements and attributes have requirements defined by the [rendering](#15-rendering) section that, due to the requirements in this section, are requirements on all user agents (not just those that [support the suggested default rendering](#218-conformance-classes)):
- [`dir`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) attribute
- [`bdi`](#4524-the-bdi-element) element
- [`bdo`](#4525-the-bdo-element) element
- [`br`](#4527-the-br-element) element
- [`pre`](#443-the-pre-element) element
- [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element
- [`wbr`](#4528-the-wbr-element) element

#### 3.2.9 Requirements related to ARIA and to platform accessibility APIs

User agent requirements for implementing Accessibility API semantics on [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) are defined in HTML Accessibility API Mappings. In addition to the rules there, for a [custom element](#4133-core-concepts) element, the default ARIA role semantics are determined as follows: [\[HTMLAAM\]](#references)
1. Let map be element's [internal content attribute map](#41374-accessibility-semantics).
2. If map\["`role`"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then return it.
3. Return no role.

Similarly, for a [custom element](#4133-core-concepts) element, the default ARIA state and property semantics, for a state or property named stateOrProperty, are determined as follows:
1. If element's [attached internals](#4137-element-internals) is non-null:
   1. If element's [attached internals](#4137-element-internals)'s [get the stateOrProperty-associated element](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) exists, then return the result of running it.
   2. If element's [attached internals](#4137-element-internals)'s [get the stateOrProperty-associated elements](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) exists, then return the result of running it.
2. If element's [internal content attribute map](#41374-accessibility-semantics)\[stateOrProperty\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then return it.
3. Return the default value for stateOrProperty.

> [!note]
> The "default semantics" referred to here are sometimes also called "native", "implicit", or "host language" semantics in ARIA. [\[ARIA\]](#references)

> [!note]
> One implication of these definitions is that the default semantics can change over time. This allows custom elements the same expressivity as built-in elements; e.g., compare to how the default ARIA role semantics of an [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element change as the [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute is added or removed.

For an example of this in action, see [the custom elements section](#41313-creating-a-custom-element-with-default-accessible-roles-states-and-properties).

---

Conformance checker requirements for checking use of ARIA [`role`](#219-dependencies) and [`aria-*`](#219-dependencies) attributes on [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) are defined in ARIA in HTML. [\[ARIAHTML\]](#references)

## 4 The elements of HTML

### 4.1 The document element

#### 4.1.1 The `html` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

As document's [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree).

Wherever a subdocument fragment is allowed in a compound document.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

A [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element followed by a [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element.

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

An [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element's [start tag](#13121-start-tags) can be omitted if the first thing inside the [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element is not a [comment](#1316-comments).

An [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) can be omitted if the [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element is not immediately followed by a [comment](#1316-comments).

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-html).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-html).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLHtmlElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the root of an HTML document.

Authors are encouraged to specify a [`lang`](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes) attribute on the root [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element, giving the document's language. This aids speech synthesis tools to determine what pronunciations to use, translation tools to determine what rules to use, and so forth.

> [!example]
> The [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element in the following example declares that the document's language is English.
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE html>
> <html lang="en">
> <head>
> <title>Swapping Songs</title>
> </head>
> <body>
> <h1>Swapping Songs</h1>
> <p>Tonight I swapped some of the songs I wrote with some friends, who
> gave me some of the songs they wrote. I love sharing my music.</p>
> </body>
> </html>
> ```

### 4.2 Document metadata

#### 4.2.1 The `head` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

As the first element in an [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

If the document is [an `iframe` `srcdoc` document](#485-the-iframe-element) or if title information is available from a higher-level protocol: Zero or more elements of [metadata content](#32521-metadata-content), of which no more than one is a [`title`](#422-the-title-element) element and no more than one is a [`base`](#423-the-base-element) element.

Otherwise: One or more elements of [metadata content](#32521-metadata-content), of which exactly one is a [`title`](#422-the-title-element) element and no more than one is a [`base`](#423-the-base-element) element.

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

A [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element's [start tag](#13121-start-tags) can be omitted if the element is empty, or if the first thing inside the [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element is an element.

A [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) can be omitted if the [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element is not immediately followed by [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) or a [comment](#1316-comments).

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-head).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-head).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLHeadElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();
};
```

The [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a collection of metadata for the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object).

> [!example]
> The collection of metadata in a [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element can be large or small. Here is an example of a very short one:
> 
> ```html
> <!doctype html>
> <html lang=en>
>  <head>
>   <title>A document with a short head</title>
>  </head>
>  <body>
>  ...
> ```
> 
> Here is an example of a longer one:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <HTML LANG="EN">
>  <HEAD>
>   <META CHARSET="UTF-8">
>   <BASE HREF="https://www.example.com/">
>   <TITLE>An application with a long head</TITLE>
>   <LINK REL="STYLESHEET" HREF="default.css">
>   <LINK REL="STYLESHEET ALTERNATE" HREF="big.css" TITLE="Big Text">
>   <SCRIPT SRC="support.js"></SCRIPT>
>   <META NAME="APPLICATION-NAME" CONTENT="Long headed application">
>  </HEAD>
>  <BODY>
>  ...
> ```

> [!note]
> The [`title`](#422-the-title-element) element is a required child in most situations, but when a higher-level protocol provides title information, e.g., in the subject line of an email when HTML is used as an email authoring format, the [`title`](#422-the-title-element) element can be omitted.

#### 4.2.2 The `title` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Metadata content](#32521-metadata-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

In a [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element containing no other [`title`](#422-the-title-element) elements.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Text](#32525-phrasing-content) that is not [inter-element whitespace](#325-content-models).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-title).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-title).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLTitleElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString text;
};
```

The [`title`](#422-the-title-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the document's title or name. Authors should use titles that identify their documents even when they are used out of context, for example in a user's history or bookmarks, or in search results. The document's title is often different from its first heading, since the first heading does not have to stand alone when taken out of context.

There must be no more than one [`title`](#422-the-title-element) element per document.

> [!note]
> If it's reasonable for the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) to have no title, then the [`title`](#422-the-title-element) element is probably not required. See the [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element's content model for a description of when the element is required.

`title.text [ = value ]`

Returns the [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) of the element.

Can be set, to replace the element's children with the given value.

The `text` attribute's getter must return this [`title`](#422-the-title-element) element's [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text).

The [`text`](#422-the-title-element) attribute's setter must [string replace all](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) with the given value within this [`title`](#422-the-title-element) element.

> [!example]
> Here are some examples of appropriate titles, contrasted with the top-level headings that might be used on those same pages.
> 
> ```html
>   <title>Introduction to The Mating Rituals of Bees</title>
>     ...
>   <h1>Introduction</h1>
>   <p>This companion guide to the highly successful
>   <cite>Introduction to Medieval Bee-Keeping</cite> book is...
> ```
> 
> The next page might be a part of the same site. Note how the title describes the subject matter unambiguously, while the first heading assumes the reader knows what the context is and therefore won't wonder if the dances are Salsa or Waltz:
> 
> ```html
>   <title>Dances used during bee mating rituals</title>
>     ...
>   <h1>The Dances</h1>
> ```

The string to use as the document's title is given by the [`document.title`](#317-dom-tree-accessors) IDL attribute.

User agents should use the document's title when referring to the document in their user interface. When the contents of a [`title`](#422-the-title-element) element are used in this way, [the directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute) of that [`title`](#422-the-title-element) element should be used to set the directionality of the document's title in the user interface.

#### 4.2.3 The `base` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Metadata content](#32521-metadata-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

In a [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element containing no other [`base`](#423-the-base-element) elements.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Nothing](#3251-the-nothing-content-model).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

No [end tag](#13122-end-tags).

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`href`](#423-the-base-element) — [Document base URL](#243-document-base-urls)

[`target`](#423-the-base-element) — Default [navigable](#731-navigables) for [hyperlink](#461-introduction) [navigation](#7422-beginning-navigation) and [form submission](#41022-form-submission)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-base).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-base).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Unsafe](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLBaseElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute USVString href;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString target;
};
```

The [`base`](#423-the-base-element) element allows authors to specify the [document base URL](#243-document-base-urls) for the purposes of parsing [URLs](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url), and the name of the default [navigable](#731-navigables) for the purposes of [following hyperlinks](#465-following-hyperlinks). The element does not [represent](#322-elements-in-the-dom) any content beyond this information.

There must be no more than one [`base`](#423-the-base-element) element per document.

A [`base`](#423-the-base-element) element must have either an [`href`](#423-the-base-element) attribute, a [`target`](#423-the-base-element) attribute, or both.

The `href` content attribute, if specified, must contain a [valid URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#241-terminology).

A [`base`](#423-the-base-element) element, if it has an [`href`](#423-the-base-element) attribute, must come before any other elements in the tree that have attributes defined as taking [URLs](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url).

> [!note]
> If there are multiple [`base`](#423-the-base-element) elements with [`href`](#423-the-base-element) attributes, all but the first are ignored.

The `target` attribute, if specified, must contain a [valid navigable target name or keyword](#7317-navigable-target-names), which specifies which [navigable](#731-navigables) is to be used as the default when [hyperlinks](#461-introduction) and [forms](#4103-the-form-element) in the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) cause [navigation](#7422-beginning-navigation).

A [`base`](#423-the-base-element) element, if it has a [`target`](#423-the-base-element) attribute, must come before any elements in the tree that represent [hyperlinks](#461-introduction).

> [!note]
> If there are multiple [`base`](#423-the-base-element) elements with [`target`](#423-the-base-element) attributes, all but the first are ignored.

To get an element's target, given an [`a`](#451-the-a-element), [`area`](#4813-the-area-element), or [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element element, and an optional string-or-null target (default null), run these steps:
1. If target is null:
   1. If element has a `target` attribute, then set target to that attribute's value.
   2. Otherwise, if element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) contains a [`base`](#423-the-base-element) element with a [`target`](#423-the-base-element) attribute, set target to the value of the [`target`](#423-the-base-element) attribute of the first such [`base`](#423-the-base-element) element.
2. If target is not null, and contains an [ASCII tab or newline](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) and a U+003C (<), then set target to "`_blank`".
3. Return target.

---

A [`base`](#423-the-base-element) element that is the first [`base`](#423-the-base-element) element with an [`href`](#423-the-base-element) content attribute [in a document tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) has a frozen base URL. The [frozen base URL](#423-the-base-element) must be [immediately](#211-parallelism) [set](#423-the-base-element) for an element whenever any of the following situations occur:
- The [`base`](#423-the-base-element) element becomes the first [`base`](#423-the-base-element) element in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) with an [`href`](#423-the-base-element) content attribute in its [`Document`](#311-the-document-object).
- The [`base`](#423-the-base-element) element is the first [`base`](#423-the-base-element) element in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) with an [`href`](#423-the-base-element) content attribute in its [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), and its [`href`](#423-the-base-element) content attribute is changed.

To set the frozen base URL for an element element:
1. Let document be element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
2. Let urlRecord be the result of [parsing](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser) the value of element's [`href`](#423-the-base-element) content attribute with document's [fallback base URL](#243-document-base-urls), and document's [character encoding](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document). (Thus, the [`base`](#423-the-base-element) element isn't affected by itself.)
3. If any of the following are true:
   - urlRecord is failure;
   - urlRecord's [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) is "`data`" or "`javascript`"; or
   - running [Is base allowed for Document?](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#allow-base-for-document) on urlRecord and document returns "`Blocked`",

   then set element's [frozen base URL](#423-the-base-element) to document's [fallback base URL](#243-document-base-urls) and return.

4. Set element's [frozen base URL](#423-the-base-element) to urlRecord.
5. [Respond to base URL changes](#243-document-base-urls) given document.

The `href` IDL attribute, on getting, must return the result of running the following algorithm:
1. Let document be element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
2. Let url be the value of the [`href`](#423-the-base-element) attribute of this element, if it has one, and the empty string otherwise.
3. Let urlRecord be the result of [parsing](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser) url with document's [fallback base URL](#243-document-base-urls), and document's [character encoding](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document). (Thus, the [`base`](#423-the-base-element) element isn't affected by other [`base`](#423-the-base-element) elements or itself.)
4. If urlRecord is failure, return url.
5. Return the [serialization](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer) of urlRecord.

> [!example]
> In this example, a [`base`](#423-the-base-element) element is used to set the [document base URL](#243-document-base-urls):
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE html>
> <html lang="en">
>     <head>
>         <title>This is an example for the &lt;base&gt; element</title>
>         <base href="https://www.example.com/news/index.html">
>     </head>
>     <body>
>         <p>Visit the <a href="archives.html">archives</a>.</p>
>     </body>
> </html>
> ```
> 
> The link in the above example would be a link to "`https://www.example.com/news/archives.html`".

#### 4.2.4 The `link` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Metadata content](#32521-metadata-content).

If the element is [allowed in the body](#424-the-link-element): [flow content](#32522-flow-content).

If the element is [allowed in the body](#424-the-link-element): [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [metadata content](#32521-metadata-content) is expected.

In a [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element that is a child of a [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element.

If the element is [allowed in the body](#424-the-link-element): where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Nothing](#3251-the-nothing-content-model).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

No [end tag](#13122-end-tags).

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`href`](#424-the-link-element) — Address of the [hyperlink](#461-introduction)

[`crossorigin`](#424-the-link-element) — How the element handles crossorigin requests

[`rel`](#424-the-link-element) — Relationship between the document containing the [hyperlink](#461-introduction) and the destination resource

[`media`](#424-the-link-element) — Applicable media

[`integrity`](#424-the-link-element) — Integrity metadata used in Subresource Integrity checks [\[SRI\]](#references)

[`hreflang`](#424-the-link-element) — Language of the linked resource

[`type`](#424-the-link-element) — Hint for the type of the referenced resource

[`referrerpolicy`](#424-the-link-element) — [Referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy) for [fetches](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) initiated by the element

[`sizes`](#424-the-link-element) — Sizes of the icons (for [`rel`](#424-the-link-element)="[`icon`](#4689-link-type-icon)")

[`imagesrcset`](#424-the-link-element) — Images to use in different situations, e.g., high-resolution displays, small monitors, etc. (for [`rel`](#424-the-link-element)="[`preload`](#46820-link-type-preload)")

[`imagesizes`](#424-the-link-element) — Image sizes for different page layouts (for [`rel`](#424-the-link-element)="[`preload`](#46820-link-type-preload)")

[`as`](#424-the-link-element) — Destination for a preload request (for [`rel`](#424-the-link-element)="[`preload`](#46820-link-type-preload)" and [`rel`](#424-the-link-element)="[`modulepreload`](#46812-link-type-modulepreload)")

[`blocking`](#424-the-link-element) — Whether the element is [potentially render-blocking](#258-blocking-attributes)

[`color`](#424-the-link-element) — Color to use when customizing a site's icon (for [`rel`](#424-the-link-element)="`mask-icon`")

[`disabled`](#424-the-link-element) — Whether the link is disabled

[`fetchpriority`](#424-the-link-element) — Sets the [priority](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-priority) for [fetches](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) initiated by the element

Also, the [`title`](#424-the-link-element) attribute [has special semantics](#424-the-link-element) on this element: Title of the link; [CSS style sheet set name](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#css-style-sheet-set-name)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-link).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-link).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLLinkElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, ReflectURL] attribute USVString href;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString? crossOrigin;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString rel;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString as;
  [SameObject, PutForwards=value, Reflect="rel"] readonly attribute DOMTokenList relList;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString media;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString integrity;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString hreflang;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString type;
  [SameObject, PutForwards=value, Reflect] readonly attribute DOMTokenList sizes;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute USVString imageSrcset;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString imageSizes;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString referrerPolicy;
  [SameObject, PutForwards=value, Reflect] readonly attribute DOMTokenList blocking;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean disabled;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString fetchPriority;

  // also has obsolete members
};
HTMLLinkElement includes LinkStyle;
```

The [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element allows authors to link their document to other resources.

The address of the link(s) is given by the `href` attribute. If the [`href`](#424-the-link-element) attribute is present, then its value must be a [valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#241-terminology). One or both of the [`href`](#424-the-link-element) or [`imagesrcset`](#424-the-link-element) attributes must be present.

If both the [`href`](#424-the-link-element) and [`imagesrcset`](#424-the-link-element) attributes are absent, then the element does not define a link.

The types of link indicated (the relationships) are given by the value of the `rel` attribute, which, if present, must have a value that is a [unordered set of unique space-separated tokens](#237-space-separated-tokens). The [allowed keywords and their meanings](#468-link-types) are defined in a later section. If the [`rel`](#424-the-link-element) attribute is absent, has no keywords, or if none of the keywords used are allowed according to the definitions in this specification, then the element does not create any links.

[`rel`](#424-the-link-element)'s [supported tokens](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#71-interface-domtokenlist) are the keywords defined in [HTML link types](#468-link-types) which are allowed on [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements, impact the processing model, and are supported by the user agent. The possible [supported tokens](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#71-interface-domtokenlist) are [`alternate`](#4681-link-type-alternate), [`dns-prefetch`](#4685-link-type-dns-prefetch), [`expect`](#4686-link-type-expect), [`icon`](#4689-link-type-icon), [`manifest`](#46811-link-type-manifest), [`modulepreload`](#46812-link-type-modulepreload), [`next`](#468261-link-type-next), [`pingback`](#46817-link-type-pingback), [`preconnect`](#46818-link-type-preconnect), [`prefetch`](#46819-link-type-prefetch), [`preload`](#46820-link-type-preload), [`search`](#46822-link-type-search), and [`stylesheet`](#46823-link-type-stylesheet). [`rel`](#424-the-link-element)'s [supported tokens](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#71-interface-domtokenlist) must only include the tokens from this list that the user agent implements the processing model for.

> [!note]
> Theoretically a user agent could support the processing model for the [`canonical`](#4684-link-type-canonical) keyword — if it were a search engine that executed JavaScript. But in practice that's quite unlikely. So in most cases, [`canonical`](#4684-link-type-canonical) ought not be included in [`rel`](#424-the-link-element)'s [supported tokens](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#71-interface-domtokenlist).

A [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element must have either a [`rel`](#424-the-link-element) attribute or an [`itemprop`](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute, but not both.

If a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element has an [`itemprop`](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute, or has a [`rel`](#424-the-link-element) attribute that contains only keywords that are [body-ok](#468-link-types), then the element is said to be allowed in the body. This means that the element can be used where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

> [!note]
> If the [`rel`](#424-the-link-element) attribute is used, the element can only sometimes be used in the [`body`](#431-the-body-element) of the page. When used with the [`itemprop`](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute, the element can be used both in the [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element and in the [`body`](#431-the-body-element) of the page, subject to the constraints of the microdata model.

---

Two categories of links can be created using the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element: [links to external resources](#461-introduction) and [hyperlinks](#461-introduction). The [link types section](#468-link-types) defines whether a particular link type is an external resource or a hyperlink. One [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element can create multiple links (of which some might be [external resource links](#461-introduction) and some might be [hyperlinks](#461-introduction)); exactly which and how many links are created depends on the keywords given in the [`rel`](#424-the-link-element) attribute. User agents must process the links on a per-link basis, not a per-element basis.

> [!note]
> Each link created for a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element is handled separately. For instance, if there are two [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements with `rel="stylesheet"`, they each count as a separate external resource, and each is affected by its own attributes independently. Similarly, if a single [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element has a [`rel`](#424-the-link-element) attribute with the value `next stylesheet`, it creates both a [hyperlink](#461-introduction) (for the [`next`](#468261-link-type-next) keyword) and an [external resource link](#461-introduction) (for the [`stylesheet`](#46823-link-type-stylesheet) keyword), and they are affected by other attributes (such as [`media`](#424-the-link-element) or [`title`](#424-the-link-element)) differently.

> [!example]
> For example, the following [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element creates two [hyperlinks](#461-introduction) (to the same page):
> 
> ```html
> <link rel="author license" href="/about">
> ```
> 
> The two links created by this element are one whose semantic is that the target page has information about the current page's author, and one whose semantic is that the target page has information regarding the license under which the current page is provided.

[Hyperlinks](#461-introduction) created with the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element and its [`rel`](#424-the-link-element) attribute apply to the whole document. This contrasts with the [`rel`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute of [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements, which indicates the type of a link whose context is given by the link's location within the document.

Unlike those created by [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements, [hyperlinks](#461-introduction) created by [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements are not displayed as part of the document by default, in user agents that [support the suggested default rendering](#218-conformance-classes). And even if they are force-displayed using CSS, they have no [activation behavior](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget). Instead, they primarily provide semantic information which might be used by the page or by other software that consumes the page's contents. Additionally, the user agent can [provide its own UI for following such hyperlinks](#4246-providing-users-with-a-means-to-follow-hyperlinks-created-using-the-link-element).

The exact behavior for [links to external resources](#461-introduction) depends on the exact relationship, as defined for the relevant [link type](#468-link-types).

---

The `crossorigin` attribute is a [CORS settings attribute](#254-cors-settings-attributes). It is intended for use with [external resource links](#461-introduction).

The `media` attribute says which media the resource applies to. The value must be a [valid media query list](#2310-media-queries).

The `integrity` attribute represents the [integrity metadata](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-integrity-metadata) for requests which this element is responsible for. The value is text. The attribute must only be specified on [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements that have a [`rel`](#424-the-link-element) attribute that contains the [`stylesheet`](#46823-link-type-stylesheet), [`preload`](#46820-link-type-preload), or [`modulepreload`](#46812-link-type-modulepreload) keyword. [\[SRI\]](#references)

The `hreflang` attribute on the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element has the same semantics as the [`hreflang` attribute on the `a` element](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).

The `type` attribute gives the [MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type) of the linked resource. It is purely advisory. The value must be a [valid MIME type string](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-mime-type).

For [external resource links](#461-introduction), the [`type`](#424-the-link-element) attribute is used as a hint to user agents so that they can avoid fetching resources they do not support.

The `referrerpolicy` attribute is a [referrer policy attribute](#255-referrer-policy-attributes). It is intended for use with [external resource links](#461-introduction), where it helps set the [referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy) used when [fetching and processing the linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element). [\[REFERRERPOLICY\]](#references)

The `title` attribute gives the title of the link. With one exception, it is purely advisory. The value is text. The exception is for style sheet links that are [in a document tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree), for which the [`title`](#424-the-link-element) attribute defines [CSS style sheet sets](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#css-style-sheet-set).

> [!note]
> The [`title`](#424-the-link-element) attribute on [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements differs from the global [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute of most other elements in that a link without a title does not inherit the title of the parent element: it merely has no title.

---

The `imagesrcset` attribute may be present, and is a [srcset attribute](#48421-srcset-attributes).

The [`imagesrcset`](#424-the-link-element) and [`href`](#424-the-link-element) attributes (if [width descriptors](#48421-srcset-attributes) are not used) together contribute the [image sources](#4843-processing-model) to the [source set](#4843-processing-model).

If the [`imagesrcset`](#424-the-link-element) attribute is present and has any [image candidate strings](#48421-srcset-attributes) using a [width descriptor](#48421-srcset-attributes), the `imagesizes` attribute must also be present, and is a [sizes attribute](#48422-sizes-attributes). The [`imagesizes`](#424-the-link-element) attribute contributes the [source size](#4843-processing-model) to the [source set](#4843-processing-model).

The [`imagesrcset`](#424-the-link-element) and [`imagesizes`](#424-the-link-element) attributes must only be specified on [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements that have both a [`rel`](#424-the-link-element) attribute that specifies the [`preload`](#46820-link-type-preload) keyword, as well as an [`as`](#424-the-link-element) attribute in the "`image`" state.

> [!example]
> These attributes allow preloading the appropriate resource that is later used by an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element that has the corresponding values for its [`srcset`](#483-the-img-element) and [`sizes`](#483-the-img-element) attributes:
> 
> ```html
> <link rel="preload" as="image"
>       imagesrcset="wolf_400px.jpg 400w, wolf_800px.jpg 800w, wolf_1600px.jpg 1600w"
>       imagesizes="50vw">
> 
> <!-- ... later, or perhaps inserted dynamically ... -->
> <img src="wolf.jpg" alt="A rad wolf"
>      srcset="wolf_400px.jpg 400w, wolf_800px.jpg 800w, wolf_1600px.jpg 1600w"
>      sizes="50vw">
> ```
> 
> Note how we omit the [`href`](#424-the-link-element) attribute, as it would only be relevant for browsers that do not support [`imagesrcset`](#424-the-link-element), and in those cases it would likely cause the incorrect image to be preloaded.

> [!example]
> The [`imagesrcset`](#424-the-link-element) attribute can be combined with the [`media`](#424-the-link-element) attribute to preload the appropriate resource selected from a [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element's sources, for [art direction](#4841-introduction):
> 
> ```html
> <link rel="preload" as="image"
>       imagesrcset="dog-cropped-1x.jpg, dog-cropped-2x.jpg 2x"
>       media="(max-width: 800px)">
> <link rel="preload" as="image"
>       imagesrcset="dog-wide-1x.jpg, dog-wide-2x.jpg 2x"
>       media="(min-width: 801px)">
> 
> <!-- ... later, or perhaps inserted dynamically ... -->
> <picture>
>   <source srcset="dog-cropped-1x.jpg, dog-cropped-2x.jpg 2x"
>           media="(max-width: 800px)">
>   <img src="dog-wide-1x.jpg" srcset="dog-wide-2x.jpg 2x"
>        alt="An awesome dog">
> </picture>
> ```

---

The `sizes` attribute gives the sizes of icons for visual media. Its value, if present, is merely advisory. User agents may use the value to decide which icon(s) to use if multiple icons are available. If specified, the attribute must have a value that is an [unordered set of unique space-separated tokens](#237-space-separated-tokens) which are [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings). Each value must be either an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "[`any`](#4689-link-type-icon)", or a value that consists of two [valid non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers) that do not have a leading U+0030 DIGIT ZERO (0) character and that are separated by a single U+0078 LATIN SMALL LETTER X or U+0058 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER X character. The attribute must only be specified on [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements that have a [`rel`](#424-the-link-element) attribute that specifies the [`icon`](#4689-link-type-icon) keyword or the `apple-touch-icon` keyword.

> [!note]
> The `apple-touch-icon` keyword is a registered [extension to the predefined set of link types](#46827-other-link-types), but user agents are not required to support it in any way.

---

The `as` attribute specifies either a [preload destination](#46820-link-type-preload) or a [module preload destination](#46812-link-type-modulepreload) for a preload request for the resource given by the [`href`](#424-the-link-element) attribute. It is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes). Each of the union of [preload destinations](#46820-link-type-preload) and [module preload destinations](#46812-link-type-modulepreload) is a keyword for this attribute, mapping to a state of the same name. The attribute must be specified on [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements that have a [`rel`](#424-the-link-element) attribute that contains the [`preload`](#46820-link-type-preload) keyword; in such cases it must have a value which is a [preload destination](#46820-link-type-preload). It may be specified on [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements that have a [`rel`](#424-the-link-element) attribute that contains the [`modulepreload`](#46812-link-type-modulepreload) keyword; in such cases it must have a value which is a [module preload destination](#46812-link-type-modulepreload). For other [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements, it must not be specified.

The processing model for how the [`as`](#424-the-link-element) attribute is used is given in an individual link type's [fetch and process the linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) algorithm.

> [!note]
> The attribute does not have a *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* or *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)*, meaning that invalid or missing values for the attribute map to no state. This is accounted for in the processing model. For [`preload`](#46820-link-type-preload) links, both conditions are an error; for [`modulepreload`](#46812-link-type-modulepreload) links, a missing value will be treated as "`script`".

---

The `blocking` attribute is a [blocking attribute](#258-blocking-attributes). It is used by link types [`stylesheet`](#46823-link-type-stylesheet) and [`expect`](#4686-link-type-expect), and it must only be specified on link elements that have a [`rel`](#424-the-link-element) attribute containing those keywords.

---

The `color` attribute is used with the `mask-icon` link type. The attribute must only be specified on [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements that have a [`rel`](#424-the-link-element) attribute that contains the `mask-icon` keyword. The value must be a string that matches the CSS [<color>](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#typedef-color) production, defining a suggested color that user agents can use to customize the display of the icon that the user sees when they pin your site.

> [!note]
> This specification does not have any user agent requirements for the [`color`](#424-the-link-element) attribute.

> [!note]
> The `mask-icon` keyword is a registered [extension to the predefined set of link types](#46827-other-link-types), but user agents are not required to support it in any way.

---

[`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements have an associated explicitly enabled boolean. It is initially false.

The `disabled` attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes) that is used with the [`stylesheet`](#46823-link-type-stylesheet) link type. The attribute must only be specified on [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements that have a [`rel`](#424-the-link-element) attribute that contains the [`stylesheet`](#46823-link-type-stylesheet) keyword.

Whenever the [`disabled`](#424-the-link-element) attribute is removed, set the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element's [explicitly enabled](#424-the-link-element) attribute to true.

> [!example]
> Removing the [`disabled`](#424-the-link-element) attribute dynamically, e.g., using `document.querySelector("link").removeAttribute("disabled")`, will fetch and apply the style sheet:
> 
> ```html
> <link disabled rel="alternate stylesheet" href="css/pooh">
> ```

The `fetchpriority` attribute is a [fetch priority attribute](#259-fetch-priority-attributes) that is intended for use with [external resource links](#461-introduction), where it is used to set the [priority](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-priority) used when [fetching and processing the linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element).

---

> [!note]
> There is no reflecting IDL attribute for the [`color`](#424-the-link-element) attribute, but this might be added later.

The `as` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`as`](#424-the-link-element) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

The `crossOrigin` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`crossorigin`](#424-the-link-element) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

The `referrerPolicy` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`referrerpolicy`](#424-the-link-element) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

The `fetchPriority` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`fetchpriority`](#424-the-link-element) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

> [!note]
> The [`relList`](#424-the-link-element) attribute can be used for feature detection, by calling its [`supports()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#71-interface-domtokenlist) method to check which [types of links](#468-link-types) are supported.

##### 4.2.4.1 Processing the [`media`](#424-the-link-element) attribute

If the link is a [hyperlink](#461-introduction) then the [`media`](#424-the-link-element) attribute is purely advisory, and describes for which media the document in question was designed.

However, if the link is an [external resource link](#461-introduction), then the [`media`](#424-the-link-element) attribute is prescriptive. The user agent must apply the external resource when the [`media`](#424-the-link-element) attribute's value [matches the environment](#2310-media-queries) and the other relevant conditions apply, and must not apply it otherwise.

The default, if the [`media`](#424-the-link-element) attribute is omitted, is "`all`", meaning that by default links apply to all media.

> [!note]
> The external resource might have further restrictions defined within that limit its applicability. For example, a CSS style sheet might have some `@media` blocks. This specification does not override such further restrictions or requirements.

##### 4.2.4.2 Processing the [`type`](#424-the-link-element) attribute

If the [`type`](#424-the-link-element) attribute is present, then the user agent must assume that the resource is of the given type (even if that is not a [valid MIME type string](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-mime-type), e.g. the empty string). If the attribute is omitted, but the [external resource link](#461-introduction) type has a default type defined, then the user agent must assume that the resource is of that type. If the UA does not support the given [MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type) for the given link relationship, then the UA should not [fetch and process the linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element); if the UA does support the given [MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type) for the given link relationship, then the UA should [fetch and process the linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) at the appropriate time as specified for the [external resource link](#461-introduction)'s particular type. If the attribute is omitted, and the [external resource link](#461-introduction) type does not have a default type defined, but the user agent would [fetch and process the linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) if the type was known and supported, then the user agent should [fetch and process the linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) under the assumption that it will be supported.

User agents must not consider the [`type`](#424-the-link-element) attribute authoritative — upon fetching the resource, user agents must not use the [`type`](#424-the-link-element) attribute to determine its actual type. Only the actual type (as defined in the next paragraph) is used to determine whether to *apply* the resource, not the aforementioned assumed type.

If the [external resource link](#461-introduction) type defines rules for processing the resource's [Content-Type metadata](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource), then those rules apply. Otherwise, if the resource is expected to be an image, user agents may apply the [image sniffing rules](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#rules-for-sniffing-images-specifically), with the official type being the type determined from the resource's [Content-Type metadata](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource), and use the resulting [computed type of the resource](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#computed-mime-type) as if it was the actual type. Otherwise, if neither of these conditions apply or if the user agent opts not to apply the image sniffing rules, then the user agent must use the resource's [Content-Type metadata](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource) to determine the type of the resource. If there is no type metadata, but the [external resource link](#461-introduction) type has a default type defined, then the user agent must assume that the resource is of that type.

> [!note]
> The [`stylesheet`](#46823-link-type-stylesheet) link type defines rules for processing the resource's [Content-Type metadata](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource).

Once the user agent has established the type of the resource, the user agent must apply the resource if it is of a supported type and the other relevant conditions apply, and must ignore the resource otherwise.

> [!example]
> If a document contains style sheet links labeled as follows:
> 
> ```html
> <link rel="stylesheet" href="A" type="text/plain">
> <link rel="stylesheet" href="B" type="text/css">
> <link rel="stylesheet" href="C">
> ```
> 
> ...then a compliant UA that supported only CSS style sheets would fetch the B and C files, and skip the A file (since [`text/plain`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.1.3) is not the [MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type) for CSS style sheets).
> 
> For files B and C, it would then check the actual types returned by the server. For those that are sent as [`text/css`](#mime-types), it would apply the styles, but for those labeled as [`text/plain`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.1.3), or any other type, it would not.
> 
> If one of the two files was returned without a [Content-Type](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource) metadata, or with a syntactically incorrect type like `Content-Type: "null"`, then the default type for [`stylesheet`](#46823-link-type-stylesheet) links would kick in. Since that default type is [`text/css`](#mime-types), the style sheet *would* nonetheless be applied.

##### 4.2.4.3 Fetching and processing a resource from a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element

All [external resource links](#461-introduction) have a fetch and process the linked resource algorithm, which takes a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element el. They also have linked resource fetch setup steps which take a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element el and [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) request. Individual link types may provide their own [fetch and process the linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) algorithm, but unless explicitly stated, they use the [default fetch and process the linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) algorithm. Similarly, individual link types may provide their own [linked resource fetch setup steps](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element), but unless explicitly stated, these steps just return true.

The default fetch and process the linked resource, given a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element el, is as follows:
1. Let options be the result of [creating link options](#4244-processing-link-headers) from el.
2. Let request be the result of [creating a link request](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) given options.
3. If request is null, then return.
4. Run the [linked resource fetch setup steps](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element), given el and request. If the result is false, then return.
5. Set request's [initiator type](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-initiator-type) to "`css`" if el's [`rel`](#424-the-link-element) attribute contains the keyword [`stylesheet`](#46823-link-type-stylesheet); "`link`" otherwise.
6. [Fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request with *[processResponseConsumeBody](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#process-response-end-of-body)* set to the following steps given [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response and null, failure, or a [byte sequence](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-byte-sequences) bodyBytes:
   1. Let success be true.
   2. If any of the following are true:
      - bodyBytes is null or failure; or
      - response's [status](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-status) is not an [ok status](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#ok-status),

      then set success to false.

      > [!note]
      > Note that content-specific errors, e.g., CSS parse errors or PNG decoding errors, do not affect success.

   3. Otherwise, wait for the [link resource](#461-introduction)'s [critical subresources](#212-resources) to finish loading.

      > [!warning]
      > The specification that defines a link type's [critical subresources](#212-resources) (e.g., CSS) is expected to describe how these subresources are fetched and processed. However, since this is not currently explicit, this specification describes waiting for a [link resource](#461-introduction)'s [critical subresources](#212-resources) to be fetched and processed, with the expectation that this will be done correctly.

   4. [Process the linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) given el, success, response, and bodyBytes.

To create a link request given a [link processing options](#4244-processing-link-headers) options:
1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): options's [href](#4244-processing-link-headers) is not the empty string.
2. Let url be the result of [encoding-parsing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given options's [href](#4244-processing-link-headers), relative to options's [base URL](#4244-processing-link-headers).

   > [!warning]
   > Passing the base URL instead of a document or environment is tracked by [issue #9715](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9715).

3. If url is failure, then return null.
4. Let request be the result of [creating a potential-CORS request](#251-terminology) given url, options's [destination](#4244-processing-link-headers), and options's [crossorigin](#4244-processing-link-headers).
5. Set request's [policy container](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-policy-container) to options's [policy container](#4244-processing-link-headers).
6. Set request's [integrity metadata](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-integrity-metadata) to options's [integrity](#4244-processing-link-headers).
7. Set request's [cryptographic nonce metadata](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-nonce-metadata) to options's [cryptographic nonce metadata](#4244-processing-link-headers).
8. Set request's [referrer policy](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-referrer-policy) to options's [referrer policy](#4244-processing-link-headers).
9. Set request's [client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client) to options's [environment](#4244-processing-link-headers).
10. Set request's [priority](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-priority) to options's [fetch priority](#4244-processing-link-headers).
11. Return request.

User agents may opt to only try to [fetch and process](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) such resources when they are needed, instead of pro-actively fetching all the [external resources](#461-introduction) that are not applied.

Similar to the [fetch and process the linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) algorithm, all [external resource links](#461-introduction) have a process the linked resource algorithm which takes a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element el, boolean success, a [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response, and a [byte sequence](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-byte-sequences) bodyBytes. Individual link types may provide their own [process the linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) algorithm, but unless explicitly stated, that algorithm does nothing.

Unless otherwise specified for a given [`rel`](#424-the-link-element) keyword, the element must [delay the load event](#1327-the-end) of the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) until all the attempts to [fetch and process the linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) and its [critical subresources](#212-resources) are complete. (Resources that the user agent has not yet attempted to fetch and process, e.g., because it is waiting for the resource to be needed, do not [delay the load event](#1327-the-end).)

##### 4.2.4.4 Processing \`[`Link`](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8288.html#header)\` headers

All link types that can be [external resource links](#461-introduction) define a process a link header algorithm, which takes a [link processing options](#4244-processing-link-headers). This algorithm defines whether and how they react to appearing in an HTTP \`[`Link`](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8288.html#header)\` response header.

> [!note]
> For most link types, this algorithm does nothing. The [summary table](#468-link-types) is a good reference to quickly know whether a link type has defined [process a link header](#4244-processing-link-headers) steps.

A link processing options is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs). It has the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):

href (default the empty string)

initiator (default "`link`")

integrity (default the empty string)

type (default the empty string)

cryptographic nonce metadata (default the empty string)

A string

destination (default the empty string)

A [destination type](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#destination-type).

crossorigin (default [No CORS](#254-cors-settings-attributes))

A [CORS settings attribute](#254-cors-settings-attributes) state

referrer policy (default the empty string)

A [referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy)

source set (default null)

Null or a [source set](#4843-processing-model)

base URL

A [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url)

origin

An [origin](#711-origins)

environment

An [environment](#8131-environments)

policy container

A [policy container](#717-policy-containers)

document (default null)

Null or a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)

on document ready (default null)

Null or an algorithm accepting a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)

fetch priority (default [`Auto`](#259-fetch-priority-attributes))

A [fetch priority attribute](#259-fetch-priority-attributes) state

> [!note]
> A [link processing options](#4244-processing-link-headers) has a [base URL](#4244-processing-link-headers) and an [href](#4244-processing-link-headers) rather than a parsed URL because the URL could be a result of the options's [source set](#4244-processing-link-headers).

To create link options from element given a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element el:
1. Let document be el's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
2. Let options be a new [link processing options](#4244-processing-link-headers) with

   [crossorigin](#4244-processing-link-headers)

   the state of el's [`crossorigin`](#424-the-link-element) content attribute

   [referrer policy](#4244-processing-link-headers)

   the state of el's [`referrerpolicy`](#424-the-link-element) content attribute

   [source set](#4244-processing-link-headers)

   el's [source set](#4843-processing-model)

   [base URL](#4244-processing-link-headers)

   document's [document base URL](#243-document-base-urls)

   [origin](#4244-processing-link-headers)

   document's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document)

   [environment](#4244-processing-link-headers)

   document's [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant)

   [policy container](#4244-processing-link-headers)

   document's [policy container](#311-the-document-object)

   [document](#4244-processing-link-headers)

   document

   [cryptographic nonce metadata](#4244-processing-link-headers)

   the current value of el's [\[\[CryptographicNonce\]\]](#256-nonce-attributes) internal slot

   [fetch priority](#4244-processing-link-headers)

   the state of el's [`fetchpriority`](#424-the-link-element) content attribute

3. If el has an [`href`](#424-the-link-element) attribute, then set options's [href](#4244-processing-link-headers) to the value of el's [`href`](#424-the-link-element) attribute.
4. If el has an [`integrity`](#424-the-link-element) attribute, then set options's [integrity](#4244-processing-link-headers) to the value of el's [`integrity`](#424-the-link-element) content attribute.
5. If el has a [`type`](#424-the-link-element) attribute, then set options's [type](#4244-processing-link-headers) to the value of el's [`type`](#424-the-link-element) attribute.
6. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): options's [href](#4244-processing-link-headers) is not the empty string, or options's [source set](#4244-processing-link-headers) is not null.

   A [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element with neither an [`href`](#424-the-link-element) or an [`imagesrcset`](#424-the-link-element) does not represent a link.

7. Return options.

To extract links from headers given a [header list](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-header-list) headers:
1. Let links be a new [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).
2. Let rawLinkHeaders be the result of [getting, decoding, and splitting](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-header-list-get-decode-split) \`[`Link`](#424-the-link-element)\` from headers.
3. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) linkHeader of rawLinkHeaders:
   1. Let linkObject be the result of [parsing](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8288.html#parse-fv) linkHeader. [\[WEBLINK\]](#references)
   2. If linkObject\["`target_uri`"\] does not [exist](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   3. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) linkObject to links.
4. Return links.

To process link headers given a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) doc, a [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response, and a "`pre-media`" or "`media`" phase:
1. Let links be the result of [extracting links](#4244-processing-link-headers) from response's [header list](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-header-list).
2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) linkObject in links:
   1. Let rel be linkObject\["`relation_type`"\].
   2. Let attribs be linkObject\["`target_attributes`"\].
   3. Let expectedPhase be "`media`" if either "[`srcset`](#483-the-img-element)", "[`imagesrcset`](#424-the-link-element)", or "[`media`](#424-the-link-element)" [exist](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) in attribs; otherwise "`pre-media`".
   4. If expectedPhase is not phase, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   5. If attribs\["[`media`](#424-the-link-element)"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) and attribs\["[`media`](#424-the-link-element)"\] does not [match the environment](#2310-media-queries), then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   6. Let options be a new [link processing options](#4244-processing-link-headers) with

      [href](#4244-processing-link-headers)

      linkObject\["`target_uri`"\]

      [base URL](#4244-processing-link-headers)

      doc's [document base URL](#243-document-base-urls)

      [origin](#4244-processing-link-headers)

      doc's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document)

      [environment](#4244-processing-link-headers)

      doc's [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant)

      [policy container](#4244-processing-link-headers)

      doc's [policy container](#311-the-document-object)

      [document](#4244-processing-link-headers)

      doc

   7. [Apply link options from parsed header attributes](#4244-processing-link-headers) to options given attribs and rel. If that returned false, then return.
   8. If attribs\["[`imagesrcset`](#424-the-link-element)"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) and attribs\["[`imagesizes`](#424-the-link-element)"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then set options's [source set](#4244-processing-link-headers) to the result of [creating a source set](#48438-creating-a-source-set-from-attributes) given linkObject\["`target_uri`"\], attribs\["[`imagesrcset`](#424-the-link-element)"\], attribs\["[`imagesizes`](#424-the-link-element)"\], and null.
   9. Run the [process a link header](#4244-processing-link-headers) steps for rel given options.

To apply link options from parsed header attributes to a [link processing options](#4244-processing-link-headers) options given attribs and a string rel:
1. If rel is "[`preload`](#46820-link-type-preload)":
   1. If attribs\["[`as`](#424-the-link-element)"\] does not [exist](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then return false.
   2. Let destination be the result of [translating](#46820-link-type-preload) attribs\["[`as`](#424-the-link-element)"\].
   3. If destination is null, then return false.
   4. Set options's [destination](#4244-processing-link-headers) to destination.
2. If attribs\["[`crossorigin`](#424-the-link-element)"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) and is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for one of the [CORS settings attribute](#254-cors-settings-attributes) [keywords](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes), then set options's [crossorigin](#4244-processing-link-headers) to the [CORS settings attribute](#254-cors-settings-attributes) state corresponding to that keyword.
3. If attribs\["[`integrity`](#424-the-link-element)"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then set options's [integrity](#4244-processing-link-headers) to attribs\["[`integrity`](#424-the-link-element)"\].
4. If attribs\["[`referrerpolicy`](#424-the-link-element)"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) and is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for some [referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy), then set options's [referrer policy](#4244-processing-link-headers) to that [referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy).
5. If attribs\["[`nonce`](#256-nonce-attributes)"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then set options's [nonce](#4244-processing-link-headers) to attribs\["[`nonce`](#256-nonce-attributes)"\].
6. If attribs\["[`type`](#424-the-link-element)"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then set options's [type](#4244-processing-link-headers) to attribs\["[`type`](#424-the-link-element)"\].
7. If attribs\["[`fetchpriority`](#424-the-link-element)"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) and is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for a [fetch priority attribute](#259-fetch-priority-attributes) keyword, then set options's [fetch priority](#4244-processing-link-headers) to that [fetch priority attribute](#259-fetch-priority-attributes) keyword.
8. Return true.

##### 4.2.4.5 Early hints

Early hints allow user-agents to perform some operations, such as to speculatively load resources that are likely to be used by the document, before the navigation request is fully handled by the server and a response code is served. Servers can indicate early hints by serving a [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) with a 103 status code before serving the final [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response).[\[RFC8297\]](#references)

> [!note]
> For compatibility reasons [early hints are typically delivered over HTTP/2 or above](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8297.html#security-considerations), but for readability we use HTTP/1.1-style notation below.

> [!example]
> For example, given the following sequence of responses:
> 
> ```
> 103 Early Hint
> Link: </image.png>; rel=preload; as=image
> ```
> 
> ```
> 200 OK
> Content-Type: text/html
> 
> <!DOCTYPE html>
> ...
> <img src="/image.png">
> ```
> 
> the image will start loading before the HTML content arrives.

> [!note]
> Only the first early hint response served during the navigation is handled, and it is discarded if it is succeeded by a cross-origin redirect.

In addition to the \`[`Link`](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8288.html#header)\` headers, it is possible that the 103 response contains a [Content Security Policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#content-security-policy-object) header, which is enforced when processing the early hint.

> [!example]
> For example, given the following sequence of responses:
> 
> ```
> 103 Early Hint
> Content-Security-Policy: style-src: self;
> Link: </style.css>; rel=preload; as=style
> ```
> 
> ```
> 103 Early Hint
> Link: </image.png>; rel=preload; as=image
> ```
> 
> ```
> 302 Redirect
> Location: /alternate.html
> ```
> 
> ```
> 200 OK
> Content-Security-Policy: style-src: none;
> Link: </font.ttf>; rel=preload; as=font
> ```
> 
> The font and style would be loaded, and the image will be discarded, as only the first early hint response in the final redirect chain is respected. The late [Content Security Policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#content-security-policy-object) header comes after the request to fetch the style has already been performed, but the style will not be accessible to the document.

To process early hint headers given a [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response and an [environment](#8131-environments) reservedEnvironment:

> [!note]
> Early-hint \`[`Link`](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8288.html#header)\` headers are always processed before \`[`Link`](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8288.html#header)\` headers from the final [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response), followed by [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements. This is equivalent to prepending the contents of the early and final \`[`Link`](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8288.html#header)\` headers to the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element, in respective order.
1. Let earlyPolicyContainer be the result of [creating a policy container from a fetch response](#717-policy-containers) given response and reservedEnvironment.

   > [!note]
   > This allows the early hint [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) to include a [Content Security Policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#content-security-policy-object) which would be [enforced](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#enforced) when fetching the early hint [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request).

2. Let links be the result of [extracting links](#4244-processing-link-headers) from response's [header list](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-header-list).
3. Let earlyHints be an empty [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).
4. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) linkObject in links:

   > [!note]
   > The moment we receive the early hint link header, we begin [fetching](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) earlyRequest. If it comes back before the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is created, we set earlyResponse to the [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) of that [fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) and once the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is created we commit it (by making it available in the [map of preloaded resources](#46820-link-type-preload) as if it was a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element). If the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is created first, the [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) is committed as soon as it becomes available.
   1. Let rel be linkObject\["`relation_type`"\].
   2. Let options be a new [link processing options](#4244-processing-link-headers) with

      [href](#4244-processing-link-headers)

      linkObject\["`target_uri`"\]

      [initiator](#4244-processing-link-headers)

      "`early-hint`"

      [base URL](#4244-processing-link-headers)

      response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url)

      [origin](#4244-processing-link-headers)

      response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url)'s [origin](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-origin)

      [environment](#4244-processing-link-headers)

      reservedEnvironment

      [policy container](#4244-processing-link-headers)

      earlyPolicyContainer

   3. Let attribs be linkObject\["`target_attributes`"\].

      > [!note]
      > Only the [`as`](#424-the-link-element), [`crossorigin`](#424-the-link-element), [`integrity`](#424-the-link-element), and [`type`](#424-the-link-element) attributes are handled as part of early hint processing. The other ones, in particular [`blocking`](#424-the-link-element), [`imagesrcset`](#424-the-link-element), [`imagesizes`](#424-the-link-element), and [`media`](#424-the-link-element) are only applicable once a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is created.

   4. [Apply link options from parsed header attributes](#4244-processing-link-headers) to options given attribs and rel. If that returned false, then return.
   5. Run the [process a link header](#4244-processing-link-headers) steps for rel given options.
   6. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) options to earlyHints.

5. Return the following substeps given [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) doc: [for each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) options in earlyHints:
   1. If options's [on document ready](#4244-processing-link-headers) is null, then set options's [document](#4244-processing-link-headers) to doc.
   2. Otherwise, call options's [on document ready](#4244-processing-link-headers) with doc.

##### 4.2.4.6 Providing users with a means to follow hyperlinks created using the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element

Interactive user agents may provide users with a means to [follow the hyperlinks](#465-following-hyperlinks) created using the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element, somewhere within their user interface. Such invocations of the [follow the hyperlink](#465-following-hyperlinks) algorithm must set the *[userInvolvement](#465-following-hyperlinks)* argument to "[`browser UI`](#7421-supporting-concepts)". The exact interface is not defined by this specification, but it could include the following information (obtained from the element's attributes, again as defined below), in some form or another (possibly simplified), for each [hyperlink](#461-introduction) created with each [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element in the document:
- The relationship between this document and the resource (given by the [`rel`](#424-the-link-element) attribute)
- The title of the resource (given by the [`title`](#424-the-link-element) attribute).
- The address of the resource (given by the [`href`](#424-the-link-element) attribute).
- The language of the resource (given by the [`hreflang`](#424-the-link-element) attribute).
- The optimum media for the resource (given by the [`media`](#424-the-link-element) attribute).

User agents could also include other information, such as the type of the resource (as given by the [`type`](#424-the-link-element) attribute).

#### 4.2.5 The `meta` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Metadata content](#32521-metadata-content).

If the [`itemprop`](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute is present: [flow content](#32522-flow-content).

If the [`itemprop`](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute is present: [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

If the [`charset`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute is present, or if the element's [`http-equiv`](#4253-pragma-directives) attribute is in the [Encoding declaration state](#4253-pragma-directives): in a [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element.

If the [`http-equiv`](#4253-pragma-directives) attribute is present but not in the [Encoding declaration state](#4253-pragma-directives): in a [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element.

If the [`http-equiv`](#4253-pragma-directives) attribute is present but not in the [Encoding declaration state](#4253-pragma-directives): in a [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element that is a child of a [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element.

If the [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute is present: where [metadata content](#32521-metadata-content) is expected.

If the [`itemprop`](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute is present: where [metadata content](#32521-metadata-content) is expected.

If the [`itemprop`](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute is present: where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Nothing](#3251-the-nothing-content-model).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

No [end tag](#13122-end-tags).

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`name`](#425-the-meta-element) — Metadata name

[`http-equiv`](#4253-pragma-directives) — Pragma directive

[`content`](#425-the-meta-element) — Value of the element
