[`charset`](#425-the-meta-element) — [Character encoding declaration](#4254-specifying-the-documents-character-encoding)

[`media`](#425-the-meta-element) — Applicable media

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-meta).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-meta).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLMetaElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString name;
  [CEReactions, Reflect="http-equiv"] attribute DOMString httpEquiv;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString content;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString media;

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) various kinds of metadata that cannot be expressed using the [`title`](#422-the-title-element), [`base`](#423-the-base-element), [`link`](#424-the-link-element), [`style`](#426-the-style-element), and [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements.

The [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element can represent document-level metadata with the [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute, pragma directives with the [`http-equiv`](#4253-pragma-directives) attribute, and the file's [character encoding declaration](#4254-specifying-the-documents-character-encoding) when an HTML document is serialized to string form (e.g. for transmission over the network or for disk storage) with the [`charset`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute.

Exactly one of the [`name`](#425-the-meta-element), [`http-equiv`](#4253-pragma-directives), [`charset`](#425-the-meta-element), and [`itemprop`](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute) attributes must be specified.

If either [`name`](#425-the-meta-element), [`http-equiv`](#4253-pragma-directives), or [`itemprop`](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute) is specified, then the [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute must also be specified. Otherwise, it must be omitted.

The `charset` attribute specifies the [character encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#encoding) used by the document. This is a [character encoding declaration](#4254-specifying-the-documents-character-encoding). If the attribute is present, its value must be an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`utf-8`".

> [!note]
> The [`charset`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute on the [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element has no effect in XML documents, but is allowed in XML documents in order to facilitate migration to and from XML.

There must not be more than one [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element with a [`charset`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute per document.

The `content` attribute gives the value of the document metadata or pragma directive when the element is used for those purposes. The allowed values depend on the exact context, as described in subsequent sections of this specification.

If a [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element has a `name` attribute, it sets document metadata. Document metadata is expressed in terms of name-value pairs, the [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute on the [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element giving the name, and the [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute on the same element giving the value. The name specifies what aspect of metadata is being set; valid names and the meaning of their values are described in the following sections. If a [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element has no [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute, then the value part of the metadata name-value pair is the empty string.

The `media` attribute says which media the metadata applies to. The value must be a [valid media query list](#2310-media-queries). Unless the [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) is [`theme-color`](#4251-standard-metadata-names), the [`media`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute has no effect on the processing model and must not be used by authors.

##### 4.2.5.1 Standard metadata names

This specification defines a few names for the [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute of the [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element.

Names are case-insensitive, and must be compared in an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) manner.

`application-name`

The value must be a short free-form string giving the name of the web application that the page represents. If the page is not a web application, the [`application-name`](#4251-standard-metadata-names) metadata name must not be used. Translations of the web application's name may be given, using the [`lang`](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes) attribute to specify the language of each name.

There must not be more than one [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element with a given [language](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes) and where the [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for [`application-name`](#4251-standard-metadata-names) per document.

User agents may use the application name in UI in preference to the page's [`title`](#422-the-title-element), since the title might include status messages and the like relevant to the status of the page at a particular moment in time instead of just being the name of the application.

To find the application name to use given an ordered list of languages (e.g. British English, American English, and English), user agents must run the following steps:
1. Let languages be the list of languages.
2. Let default language be the [language](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes) of the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree), if any, and if that language is not unknown.
3. If there is a default language, and if it is not the same language as any of the languages in languages, append it to languages.
4. Let winning language be the first language in languages for which there is a [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element in the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) where the [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for [`application-name`](#4251-standard-metadata-names) and whose [language](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes) is the language in question.

   If none of the languages have such a [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element, then return; there's no given application name.

5. Return the value of the [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute of the first [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element in the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) where the [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for [`application-name`](#4251-standard-metadata-names) and whose [language](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes) is winning language.

> [!note]
> This algorithm would be used by a browser when it needs a name for the page, for instance, to label a bookmark. The languages it would provide to the algorithm would be the user's preferred languages.

`author`

The value must be a free-form string giving the name of one of the page's authors.

`description`

The value must be a free-form string that describes the page. The value must be appropriate for use in a directory of pages, e.g. in a search engine. There must not be more than one [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element where the [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for [`description`](#4251-standard-metadata-names) per document.

`generator`

The value must be a free-form string that identifies one of the software packages used to generate the document. This value must not be used on pages whose markup is not generated by software, e.g. pages whose markup was written by a user in a text editor.

> [!example]
> Here is what a tool called "Frontweaver" could include in its output, in the page's [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element, to identify itself as the tool used to generate the page:
> 
> ```html
> <meta name=generator content="Frontweaver 8.2">
> ```

`keywords`

The value must be a [set of comma-separated tokens](#238-comma-separated-tokens), each of which is a keyword relevant to the page.

> [!example]
> This page about typefaces on British motorways uses a [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element to specify some keywords that users might use to look for the page:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <html lang="en-GB">
>  <head>
>   <title>Typefaces on UK motorways</title>
>   <meta name="keywords" content="british,type face,font,fonts,highway,highways">
>  </head>
>  <body>
>   ...
> ```

> [!note]
> Many search engines do not consider such keywords, because this feature has historically been used unreliably and even misleadingly as a way to spam search engine results in a way that is not helpful for users.

To obtain the list of keywords that the author has specified as applicable to the page, the user agent must run the following steps:
1. Let keywords be an empty list.
2. For each [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element with a [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute and a [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute and where the [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for [`keywords`](#4251-standard-metadata-names):
   1. [Split the value of the element's `content` attribute on commas](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).
   2. Add the resulting tokens, if any, to keywords.
3. Remove any duplicates from keywords.
4. Return keywords. This is the list of keywords that the author has specified as applicable to the page.

User agents should not use this information when there is insufficient confidence in the reliability of the value.

> [!example]
> For instance, it would be reasonable for a content management system to use the keyword information of pages within the system to populate the index of a site-specific search engine, but a large-scale content aggregator that used this information would likely find that certain users would try to game its ranking mechanism through the use of inappropriate keywords.

`referrer`

The value must be a [referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy), which defines the default [referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy) for the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object). [\[REFERRERPOLICY\]](#references)

If any [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element element is [inserted into the document](#214-dom-trees), or has its [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) or [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attributes changed, user agents must run the following algorithm:
1. If element is not [in a document tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree), then return.
2. If element does not have a [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute whose value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for "[`referrer`](#4251-standard-metadata-names)", then return.
3. If element does not have a [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute, or that attribute's value is the empty string, then return.
4. Let value be the value of element's [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute, [converted to ASCII lowercase](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).
5. If value is one of the values given in the first column of the following table, then set value to the value given in the second column:

   | Legacy value | Referrer policy |
   | --- | --- |
   | `never` | [`no-referrer`](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy-no-referrer) |
   | `default` | the [default referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#default-referrer-policy) |
   | `always` | [`unsafe-url`](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy-unsafe-url) |
   | `origin-when-crossorigin` | [`origin-when-cross-origin`](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy-origin-when-cross-origin) |

6. If value is a [referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy), then set element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [policy container](#311-the-document-object)'s [referrer policy](#717-policy-containers) to policy.

> [!note]
> For historical reasons, unlike other standard metadata names, the processing model for [`referrer`](#4251-standard-metadata-names) is not responsive to element removals, and does not use [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees). Only the most-recently-inserted or most-recently-modified [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element in this state has an effect.

`theme-color`

The value must be a string that matches the CSS [<color>](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#typedef-color) production, defining a suggested color that user agents should use to customize the display of the page or of the surrounding user interface. For example, a browser might color the page's title bar with the specified value, or use it as a color highlight in a tab bar or task switcher.

Within an HTML document, the [`media`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute value must be unique amongst all the [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) elements with their [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute value set to an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for [`theme-color`](#4251-standard-metadata-names).

> [!example]
> This standard itself uses "WHATWG green" as its theme color:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <title>HTML Standard</title>
> <meta name="theme-color" content="#3c790a">
> ...
> ```

The [`media`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute may be used to describe the context in which the provided color should be used.

> [!example]
> If we only wanted to use "WHATWG green" as this standard's theme color in dark mode, we could use the `prefers-color-scheme` media feature:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <title>HTML Standard</title>
> <meta name="theme-color" content="#3c790a" media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)">
> ...
> ```

To obtain a page's theme color, user agents must run the following steps:
1. Let candidate elements be the list of all [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) elements that meet the following criteria, in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees):
   - the element is [in a document tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree);
   - the element has a [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute, whose value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for [`theme-color`](#4251-standard-metadata-names); and
   - the element has a [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute.
2. For each element in candidate elements:
   1. If element has a [`media`](#424-the-link-element) attribute and the value of element's [`media`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute does not [match the environment](#2310-media-queries), then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   2. Let value be the result of [stripping leading and trailing ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) from the value of element's [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute.
   3. Let color be the result of [parsing](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#parse-a-css-color-value) value.
   4. If color is not failure, then return color.
3. Return nothing (the page has no theme color).

If any [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) elements are [inserted into the document](#214-dom-trees) or [removed from the document](#214-dom-trees), or existing [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) elements have their [`name`](#425-the-meta-element), [`content`](#425-the-meta-element), or [`media`](#424-the-link-element) attributes changed, or if the environment changes such that any [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element's [`media`](#424-the-link-element) attribute's value may now or may no longer [match the environment](#2310-media-queries), user agents must re-run the above algorithm and apply the result to any affected UI.

When using the theme color in UI, user agents may adjust it in implementation-specific ways to make it more suitable for the UI in question. For example, if a user agent intends to use the theme color as a background and display white text over it, it might use a darker variant of the theme color in that part of the UI, to ensure adequate contrast.

`color-scheme`

To aid user agents in rendering the page background with the desired color scheme immediately (rather than waiting for all CSS in the page to load), a ['color-scheme'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-adjust/#color-scheme-prop) value can be provided in a [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element.

The value must be a string that matches the syntax for the CSS ['color-scheme'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-adjust/#color-scheme-prop) property value. It determines the [page's supported color-schemes](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-adjust/#pages-supported-color-schemes).

There must not be more than one [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element with its [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute value set to an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for [`color-scheme`](#4251-standard-metadata-names) per document.

> [!example]
> The following declaration indicates that the page is aware of and can handle a color scheme with dark background colors and light foreground colors:
> 
> ```html
> <meta name="color-scheme" content="dark">
> ```

To obtain a [page's supported color-schemes](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-adjust/#pages-supported-color-schemes), user agents must run the following steps:
1. Let candidate elements be the list of all [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) elements that meet the following criteria, in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees):
   - the element is [in a document tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree);
   - the element has a [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute, whose value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for [`color-scheme`](#4251-standard-metadata-names); and
   - the element has a [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute.
2. For each element in candidate elements:
   1. Let parsed be the result of [parsing a list of component values](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#parse-a-list-of-component-values) given the value of element's [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute.
   2. If parsed is a valid CSS ['color-scheme'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-adjust/#color-scheme-prop) property value, then return parsed.
3. Return null.

If any [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) elements are [inserted into the document](#214-dom-trees) or [removed from the document](#214-dom-trees), or existing [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) elements have their [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) or [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attributes changed, user agents must re-run the above algorithm.

> [!note]
> Because these rules check successive elements until they find a match, an author can provide multiple such values to handle fallback for legacy user agents. Opposite to how CSS fallback works for properties, the multiple meta elements needs to be arranged with the legacy values after the newer values.

##### 4.2.5.2 Other metadata names

Anyone can create and use their own extensions to the predefined set of metadata names. There is no requirement to register such extensions.

However, a new metadata name should not be created in any of the following cases:
- If either the name is a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url), or the value of its accompanying [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute is a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url); in those cases, registering it as an [extension to the predefined set of link types](#46827-other-link-types) is encouraged (rather than creating a new metadata name).
- If the name is for something expected to have processing requirements in user agents; in that case it ought to be standardized.

Also, before creating and using a new metadata name, consulting the [WHATWG Wiki MetaExtensions page](https://wiki.whatwg.org/wiki/MetaExtensions) is encouraged — to avoid choosing a metadata name that's already in use, and to avoid duplicating the purpose of any metadata names that are already in use, and to avoid new standardized names clashing with your chosen name. [\[WHATWGWIKI\]](#references)

Anyone is free to edit the WHATWG Wiki MetaExtensions page at any time to add a metadata name. New metadata names can be specified with the following information:

Keyword

The actual name being defined. The name should not be confusingly similar to any other defined name (e.g. differing only in case).

Brief description

A short non-normative description of what the metadata name's meaning is, including the format the value is required to be in.

Specification

A link to a more detailed description of the metadata name's semantics and requirements. It could be another page on the wiki, or a link to an external page.

Synonyms

A list of other names that have exactly the same processing requirements. Authors should not use the names defined to be synonyms (they are only intended to allow user agents to support legacy content). Anyone may remove synonyms that are not used in practice; only names that need to be processed as synonyms for compatibility with legacy content are to be registered in this way.

Status

One of the following:

Proposed

The name has not received wide peer review and approval. Someone has proposed it and is, or soon will be, using it.

Ratified

The name has received wide peer review and approval. It has a specification that unambiguously defines how to handle pages that use the name, including when they use it in incorrect ways.

Discontinued

The metadata name has received wide peer review and it has been found wanting. Existing pages are using this metadata name, but new pages should avoid it. The "brief description" and "specification" entries will give details of what authors should use instead, if anything.

If a metadata name is found to be redundant with existing values, it should be removed and listed as a synonym for the existing value.

If a metadata name is added in the "proposed" state for a period of a month or more without being used or specified, then it may be removed from the WHATWG Wiki MetaExtensions page.

If a metadata name is added with the "proposed" status and found to be redundant with existing values, it should be removed and listed as a synonym for the existing value. If a metadata name is added with the "proposed" status and found to be harmful, then it should be changed to "discontinued" status.

Anyone can change the status at any time, but should only do so in accordance with the definitions above.

##### 4.2.5.3 Pragma directives

When the `http-equiv` attribute is specified on a [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element, the element is a pragma directive.

> [!warning]
> Despite the name [`http-equiv`](#4253-pragma-directives), pragma directives are almost entirely unrelated to HTTP headers. Implementers and web developers are best off thinking of them as entirely separate, and the name as being a historical accident.
> 
> In more detail, although the [`refresh`](#4253-pragma-directives) keyword has the same processing model as the corresponding \`[`Refresh`](#78-the-refresh-header)\` header, every other standardized pragma directive has at least slightly different behavior than the similarly-named header. (And usually dramatically-different behavior.)
> 
> Implementers or specification writers contemplating adding new document-level pragmas or HTTP header-controlled switches should be cautious about this mismatch, and avoid perpetuating the existing confusion by adding the same or similar behavior to both an HTTP header and an [`http-equiv`](#4253-pragma-directives) pragma. Instead, consider providing only an HTTP header, or if an in-document pragma is needed, consider adding a new attribute to [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) similar to the model used by the [`charset`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute. (Note that avoiding in-document pragmas is often the better choice, since the DOM is mutable. Thus, even in the simple case where the developer does not add, remove, or mutate [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) elements, the policy will go from un-applied to applied during parsing, which can have complex implications.)

The [`http-equiv`](#4253-pragma-directives) attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | Conforming | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `content-language` | No | [Content language](#4253-pragma-directives) | Sets the [pragma-set default language](#4253-pragma-directives). |
| `content-type` |  | [Encoding declaration](#4253-pragma-directives) | An alternative form of setting the [`charset`](#425-the-meta-element). |
| `default-style` |  | [Default style](#4253-pragma-directives) | Sets the [name](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#css-style-sheet-set-name) of the default [CSS style sheet set](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#css-style-sheet-set). |
| `refresh` |  | [Refresh](#4253-pragma-directives) | Acts as a timed redirect. |
| `set-cookie` | No | [Set-Cookie](#4253-pragma-directives) | Has no effect. |
| `x-ua-compatible` |  | [X-UA-Compatible](#4253-pragma-directives) | In practice, encourages Internet Explorer to more closely follow the specifications. |
| `content-security-policy` |  | [Content security policy](#4253-pragma-directives) | [Enforces](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#enforced) a [Content Security Policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#content-security-policy-object) on a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object). |

When a [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element is [inserted into the document](#214-dom-trees), if its [`http-equiv`](#4253-pragma-directives) attribute is present and represents one of the above states, then the user agent must run the algorithm appropriate for that state, as described in the following list:

Content language state (`` http-equiv="`content-language`" ``)

> [!note]
> This feature is non-conforming. Authors are encouraged to use the [`lang`](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes) attribute instead.

This pragma sets the pragma-set default language. Until such a pragma is successfully processed, there is no [pragma-set default language](#4253-pragma-directives).
1. If the [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element has no [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute, then return.
2. If the element's [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute contains a U+002C COMMA character (,), then return.
3. Let input be the value of the element's [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute.
4. Let position point at the first character of input.
5. [Skip ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) within input given position.
6. [Collect a sequence of code points](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) that are not [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) from input given position.
7. Let candidate be the string that resulted from the previous step.
8. If candidate is the empty string, return.
9. Set the [pragma-set default language](#4253-pragma-directives) to candidate.

   > [!note]
   > If the value consists of multiple space-separated tokens, tokens after the first are ignored.

> [!note]
> This pragma is almost, but not quite, entirely unlike the HTTP \`[`Content-Language`](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc7231.html#header.content-language)\` header of the same name. [\[HTTP\]](#references)

Encoding declaration state (`` http-equiv="`content-type`" ``)

The [Encoding declaration state](#4253-pragma-directives) is just an alternative form of setting the [`charset`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute: it is a [character encoding declaration](#4254-specifying-the-documents-character-encoding). This state's user agent requirements are all handled by the parsing section of the specification.

For [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) elements with an [`http-equiv`](#4253-pragma-directives) attribute in the [Encoding declaration state](#4253-pragma-directives), the [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute must have a value that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for a string that consists of: "`text/html;`", optionally followed by any number of [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), followed by "`charset=utf-8`".

A document must not contain both a [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element with an [`http-equiv`](#4253-pragma-directives) attribute in the [Encoding declaration state](#4253-pragma-directives) and a [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element with the [`charset`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute present.

The [Encoding declaration state](#4253-pragma-directives) may be used in [HTML documents](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), but elements with an [`http-equiv`](#4253-pragma-directives) attribute in that state must not be used in [XML documents](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

Default style state (`` http-equiv="`default-style`" ``)

This pragma sets the [name](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#css-style-sheet-set-name) of the default [CSS style sheet set](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#css-style-sheet-set).
1. If the [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element has no [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute, or if that attribute's value is the empty string, then return.
2. [Change the preferred CSS style sheet set name](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#change-the-preferred-css-style-sheet-set-name) with the name being the value of the element's [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute. [\[CSSOM\]](#references)

Refresh state (`` http-equiv="`refresh`" ``)

This pragma acts as a timed redirect.

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object has an associated will declaratively refresh (a boolean). It is initially false.
1. If the [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element has no [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute, or if that attribute's value is the empty string, then return.
2. Let input be the value of the element's [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute.
3. Run the [shared declarative refresh steps](#4253-pragma-directives) with the [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), input, and the [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element.

The shared declarative refresh steps, given a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object document, string input, and optionally a [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element meta, are as follows:
1. If document's [will declaratively refresh](#4253-pragma-directives) is true, then return.
2. Let position point at the first [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) of input.
3. [Skip ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) within input given position.
4. Let time be 0.
5. [Collect a sequence of code points](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) that are [ASCII digits](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) from input given position, and let timeString be the result.
6. If timeString is the empty string:
   1. If the [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) in input pointed to by position is not U+002E (.), then return.
7. Otherwise, set time to the result of parsing timeString using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers).
8. [Collect a sequence of code points](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) that are [ASCII digits](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) and U+002E FULL STOP characters (.) from input given position. Ignore any collected characters.
9. Let urlRecord be document's [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).
10. If position is not past the end of input:
    1. If the [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) in input pointed to by position is not U+003B (;), U+002C (,), or [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), then return.
    2. [Skip ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) within input given position.
    3. If the [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) in input pointed to by position is U+003B (;) or U+002C (,), then advance position to the next [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).
    4. [Skip ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) within input given position.
11. If position is not past the end of input:
    1. Let urlString be the substring of input from the [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) at position to the end of the string.
    2. If the [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) in input pointed to by position is U+0055 (U) or U+0075 (u), then advance position to the next [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points). Otherwise, jump to the step labeled *skip quotes*.
    3. If the [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) in input pointed to by position is U+0052 (R) or U+0072 (r), then advance position to the next [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points). Otherwise, jump to the step labeled *parse*.
    4. If the [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) in input pointed to by position is U+004C (L) or U+006C (l), then advance position to the next [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points). Otherwise, jump to the step labeled *parse*.
    5. [Skip ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) within input given position.
    6. If the [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) in input pointed to by position is U+003D (=), then advance position to the next [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points). Otherwise, jump to the step labeled *parse*.
    7. [Skip ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) within input given position.
    8. *Skip quotes*: If the [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) in input pointed to by position is U+0027 (') or U+0022 ("), then let quote be that [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), and advance position to the next [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points). Otherwise, let quote be the empty string.
    9. Set urlString to the substring of input from the [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) at position to the end of the string.
    10. If quote is not the empty string, and there is a [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) in urlString equal to quote, then truncate urlString at that [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), so that it and all subsequent [code points](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) are removed.
    11. *Parse*: Set urlRecord to the result of [encoding-parsing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given urlString, relative to document.
    12. If urlRecord is failure, then return.
    13. If urlRecord's [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) is "[`javascript`](#74232-the-javascript-url-special-case)", then return.
12. Set document's [will declaratively refresh](#4253-pragma-directives) to true.
13. Perform one or more of the following steps:
    - After the refresh has come due (as defined below), if the user has not canceled the redirect and, if meta is given, document's [active sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing) does not have the [sandboxed automatic features browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing) set, then [navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation) document's [node navigable](#731-navigables) to urlRecord using document, with *[historyHandling](#7422-beginning-navigation)* set to "[`replace`](#7421-supporting-concepts)".

      For the purposes of the previous paragraph, a refresh is said to have come due as soon as the *later* of the following two conditions occurs:
      - At least time seconds have elapsed since document's [completely loaded time](#758-finishing-the-loading-process), adjusted to take into account user or user agent preferences.
      - If meta is given, at least time seconds have elapsed since meta was [inserted into the document](#214-dom-trees) document, adjusted to take into account user or user agent preferences.

      > [!note]
      > It is important to use document here, and not meta's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), as that might have changed between the initial set of steps and the refresh coming due and meta is not always given (in case of the HTTP \`[`Refresh`](#78-the-refresh-header)\` header).

    - Provide the user with an interface that, when selected, [navigates](#7422-beginning-navigation) document's [node navigable](#731-navigables) to urlRecord using document.
    - Do nothing.

    In addition, the user agent may, as with anything, inform the user of any and all aspects of its operation, including the state of any timers, the destinations of any timed redirects, and so forth.

For [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) elements with an [`http-equiv`](#4253-pragma-directives) attribute in the [Refresh state](#4253-pragma-directives), the [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute must have a value consisting either of:
- just a [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers), or
- a [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers), followed by a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;), followed by one or more [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), followed by a substring that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`URL`", followed by a U+003D EQUALS SIGN character (=), followed by a [valid URL string](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-url-string) that does not start with a literal U+0027 APOSTROPHE (') or U+0022 QUOTATION MARK (") character.

In the former case, the integer represents a number of seconds before the page is to be reloaded; in the latter case the integer represents a number of seconds before the page is to be replaced by the page at the given [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url).

> [!example]
> A news organization's front page could include the following markup in the page's [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element, to ensure that the page automatically reloads from the server every five minutes:
> 
> ```html
> <meta http-equiv="Refresh" content="300">
> ```

> [!example]
> A sequence of pages could be used as an automated slide show by making each page refresh to the next page in the sequence, using markup such as the following:
> 
> ```html
> <meta http-equiv="Refresh" content="20; URL=page4.html">
> ```

Set-Cookie state (`` http-equiv="`set-cookie`" ``)

This pragma is non-conforming and has no effect.

User agents are required to ignore this pragma.

X-UA-Compatible state (`` http-equiv="`x-ua-compatible`" ``)

In practice, this pragma encourages Internet Explorer to more closely follow the specifications.

For [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) elements with an [`http-equiv`](#4253-pragma-directives) attribute in the [X-UA-Compatible state](#4253-pragma-directives), the [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute must have a value that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`IE=edge`".

User agents are required to ignore this pragma.

Content security policy state (`` http-equiv="`content-security-policy`" ``)

This pragma [enforces](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#enforced) a [Content Security Policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#content-security-policy-object) on a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object). [\[CSP\]](#references)
1. If the [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element is not a child of a [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element, return.
2. If the [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element has no [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute, or if that attribute's value is the empty string, then return.
3. Let policy be the result of executing Content Security Policy's [parse a serialized Content Security Policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#parse-serialized-policy) algorithm on the [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element's [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute's value, with a source of "meta", and a disposition of "enforce".
4. Remove all occurrences of the [`report-uri`](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#report-uri), [`frame-ancestors`](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#frame-ancestors), and [`sandbox`](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#sandbox) [directives](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#directives) from policy.
5. [Enforce the policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#enforced) policy.

For [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) elements with an [`http-equiv`](#4253-pragma-directives) attribute in the [Content security policy state](#4253-pragma-directives), the [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute must have a value consisting of a [valid Content Security Policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#grammardef-serialized-policy), but must not contain any [`report-uri`](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#report-uri), [`frame-ancestors`](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#frame-ancestors), or [`sandbox`](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#sandbox) [directives](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#directives). The [Content Security Policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#content-security-policy-object) given in the [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute will be [enforced](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#enforced) upon the current document. [\[CSP\]](#references)

> [!note]
> At the time of inserting the [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element to the document, it is possible that some resources have already been fetched. For example, images might be stored in the [list of available images](#48433-the-list-of-available-images) prior to dynamically inserting a [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element with an [`http-equiv`](#4253-pragma-directives) attribute in the [Content security policy state](#4253-pragma-directives). Resources that have already been fetched are not guaranteed to be blocked by a [Content Security Policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#content-security-policy-object) that's [enforced](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#enforced) late.

> [!example]
> A page might choose to mitigate the risk of cross-site scripting attacks by preventing the execution of inline JavaScript, as well as blocking all plugin content, using a policy such as the following:
> 
> ```html
> <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'">
> ```

There must not be more than one [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element with any particular state in the document at a time.

##### 4.2.5.4 Specifying the document's character encoding

A character encoding declaration is a mechanism by which the [character encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#encoding) used to store or transmit a document is specified.

The Encoding standard requires use of the [UTF-8](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8) [character encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#encoding) and requires use of the "`utf-8`" [encoding label](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#label) to identify it. Those requirements necessitate that the document's [character encoding declaration](#4254-specifying-the-documents-character-encoding), if it exists, specifies an [encoding label](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#label) using an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for "`utf-8`". Regardless of whether a [character encoding declaration](#4254-specifying-the-documents-character-encoding) is present or not, the actual [character encoding](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) used to encode the document must be [UTF-8](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8). [\[ENCODING\]](#references)

To enforce the above rules, authoring tools must default to using [UTF-8](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8) for newly-created documents.

The following restrictions also apply:
- The character encoding declaration must be serialized without the use of [character references](#1314-character-references) or character escapes of any kind.
- The element containing the character encoding declaration must be serialized completely within the first 1024 bytes of the document.

In addition, due to a number of restrictions on [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) elements, there can only be one [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element)-based character encoding declaration per document.

If an [HTML document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) does not start with a BOM, and its [encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#encoding) is not explicitly given by [Content-Type metadata](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource), and the document is not [an `iframe` `srcdoc` document](#485-the-iframe-element), then the encoding must be specified using a [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element with a [`charset`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute or a [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element with an [`http-equiv`](#4253-pragma-directives) attribute in the [Encoding declaration state](#4253-pragma-directives).

> [!note]
> A character encoding declaration is required (either in the [Content-Type metadata](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource) or explicitly in the file) even when all characters are in the ASCII range, because a character encoding is needed to process non-ASCII characters entered by the user in forms, in URLs generated by scripts, and so forth.
> 
> Using non-UTF-8 encodings can have unexpected results on form submission and URL encodings, which use the [document's character encoding](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) by default.

If the document is [an `iframe` `srcdoc` document](#485-the-iframe-element), the document must not have a [character encoding declaration](#4254-specifying-the-documents-character-encoding). (In this case, the source is already decoded, since it is part of the document that contained the [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element).)

In XML, the XML declaration should be used for inline character encoding information, if necessary.

> [!example]
> In HTML, to declare that the character encoding is [UTF-8](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8), the author could include the following markup near the top of the document (in the [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element):
> 
> ```html
> <meta charset="utf-8">
> ```
> 
> In XML, the XML declaration would be used instead, at the very top of the markup:
> 
> ```html
> <?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
> ```

#### 4.2.6 The `style` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Metadata content](#32521-metadata-content).

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [metadata content](#32521-metadata-content) is expected.

In a [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element that is a child of a [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element.

Where [flow content](#32522-flow-content) is expected, as the first child of its parent.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Text](#32525-phrasing-content) that gives a [conformant style sheet](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#w3c-conformance-classes).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`media`](#426-the-style-element) — Applicable media

[`blocking`](#426-the-style-element) — Whether the element is [potentially render-blocking](#258-blocking-attributes)

Also, the [`title`](#426-the-style-element) attribute [has special semantics](#426-the-style-element) on this element: [CSS style sheet set name](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#css-style-sheet-set-name)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-style).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-style).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLStyleElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  attribute boolean disabled;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString media;
  [SameObject, PutForwards=value, Reflect] readonly attribute DOMTokenList blocking;

  // also has obsolete members
};
HTMLStyleElement includes LinkStyle;
```

The [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element allows authors to embed CSS style sheets in their documents. The [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element is one of several inputs to the styling processing model. The element does not [represent](#322-elements-in-the-dom) content for the user.

The `disabled` getter steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) does not have an [associated CSS style sheet](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#associated-css-style-sheet), return false.
2. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [associated CSS style sheet](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#associated-css-style-sheet)'s [disabled flag](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-disabled-flag) is set, return true.
3. Return false.

The [`disabled`](#426-the-style-element) setter steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) does not have an [associated CSS style sheet](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#associated-css-style-sheet), return.
2. If the given value is true, set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [associated CSS style sheet](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#associated-css-style-sheet)'s [disabled flag](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-disabled-flag). Otherwise, unset [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [associated CSS style sheet](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#associated-css-style-sheet)'s [disabled flag](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-disabled-flag).

> [!example]
> Importantly, [`disabled`](#426-the-style-element) attribute assignments only take effect when the [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element has an [associated CSS style sheet](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#associated-css-style-sheet):
> 
> ```javascript
> const style = document.createElement('style');
> style.disabled = true;
> style.textContent = 'body { background-color: red; }';
> document.body.append(style);
> console.log(style.disabled); // false
> ```

The `media` attribute says which media the styles apply to. The value must be a [valid media query list](#2310-media-queries). The user agent must apply the styles when the [`media`](#426-the-style-element) attribute's value [matches the environment](#2310-media-queries) and the other relevant conditions apply, and must not apply them otherwise.

> [!note]
> The styles might be further limited in scope, e.g. in CSS with the use of `@media` blocks. This specification does not override such further restrictions or requirements.

The default, if the [`media`](#426-the-style-element) attribute is omitted, is "`all`", meaning that by default styles apply to all media.

The `blocking` attribute is a [blocking attribute](#258-blocking-attributes).

The `title` attribute on [`style`](#426-the-style-element) elements defines [CSS style sheet sets](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#css-style-sheet-set). If the [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element has no [`title`](#426-the-style-element) attribute, then it has no title; the [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute of ancestors does not apply to the [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element. If the [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element is not [in a document tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree), then the [`title`](#426-the-style-element) attribute is ignored. [\[CSSOM\]](#references)

> [!note]
> The [`title`](#426-the-style-element) attribute on [`style`](#426-the-style-element) elements, like the [`title`](#424-the-link-element) attribute on [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements, differs from the global [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute in that a [`style`](#426-the-style-element) block without a title does not inherit the title of the parent element: it merely has no title.

The [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) of a [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element must be that of a [conformant style sheet](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#w3c-conformance-classes).

If a [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element is a descendant of a [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element, then the style sheet given by its [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) must not contain any `@import` rules, and each [style rule](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#style-rule) and each [`@scope`](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade-6/#at-ruledef-scope) rule with a [<scope-start>](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade-6/#typedef-scope-start) in it, other than those inside an `@mixin` or `@supports-condition` rule, must be inside an [`@scope`](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade-6/#at-ruledef-scope) rule without a [<scope-start>](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade-6/#typedef-scope-start), e.g., "`@scope { ... }`" or "`@scope to (.x) { ... }`".

> [!note]
> The [scoping root](https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#scoping-root) of such an [`@scope`](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade-6/#at-ruledef-scope) rule is the [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element's parent, so its style rules can only style the parent and the parent's descendants. Since the [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element has to be the first child of its parent, those descendants come after the [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element. This prevents a [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element in the [`body`](#431-the-body-element) from restyling content that the user agent might already have rendered, other than its parent.

> [!note]
> At-rules like `@font-face`, `@keyframes`, and `@property` define names for the whole document. Using such names only within the [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element's parent, and picking names that aren't used elsewhere, avoids restyling content that the user agent might already have rendered.

> [!example]
> In the following fragment, the [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element only styles its parent [`article`](#432-the-article-element) element and that element's descendants:
> 
> ```html
> <article>
>  <style>
>   @scope {
>     :scope { border: 1px solid; }
>     img { max-width: 100%; }
>   }
>  </style>
>  <h2>Kittens</h2>
>  <img src="kittens.jpg" alt="Three kittens asleep in a basket.">
> </article>
> ```
> 
> Adding `h2 { margin: 0; }` outside the [`@scope`](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade-6/#at-ruledef-scope) rule would make the style sheet non-conforming, even though the only [`h2`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements) element comes after the [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element.

A [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element is [implicitly potentially render-blocking](#258-blocking-attributes) if the element was created by its [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s parser.

---

The user agent must run the [update a `style` block](#426-the-style-element) algorithm whenever any of the following conditions occur:
- The element is popped off the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) of an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) or [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents).
- The element is not on the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) of an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) or [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents), and it [becomes connected](#214-dom-trees) or [disconnected](#214-dom-trees).
- The element is not on the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) of an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) or [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents), and its [children changed steps](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) run.

The update a `style` block algorithm is as follows:
1. Let element be the [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element.
2. If element has an [associated CSS style sheet](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#associated-css-style-sheet), [remove the CSS style sheet](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#remove-a-css-style-sheet) in question.
3. If element is not [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree), then return.
4. If element's [`type`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute is present and its value is neither the empty string nor an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for "[`text/css`](#mime-types)", then return.

   > [!note]
   > In particular, a [`type`](#162-non-conforming-features) value with parameters, such as "`text/css; charset=utf-8`", will cause this algorithm to return early.

5. If the [Should element's inline behavior be blocked by Content Security Policy?](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#should-block-inline) algorithm returns "`Blocked`" when executed upon element, "`style`", and element's [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text), then return. [\[CSP\]](#references)
6. [Create a CSS style sheet](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#create-a-css-style-sheet) with the following properties:

   [type](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-type)

   [`text/css`](#mime-types)

   [owner node](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-owner-node)

   element

   [media](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-media)

   The [`media`](#426-the-style-element) attribute of element.

   > [!note]
   > This is a reference to the (possibly absent at this time) attribute, rather than a copy of the attribute's current value. CSSOM defines what happens when the attribute is dynamically set, changed, or removed.

   [title](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-title)

   The [`title`](#426-the-style-element) attribute of element, if element is [in a document tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree), or the empty string otherwise.

   > [!note]
   > Again, this is a *reference* to the attribute.

   [alternate flag](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-alternate-flag)

   Unset.

   [origin-clean flag](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-origin-clean-flag)

   Set.

   [location](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-location)

   [parent CSS style sheet](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-parent-css-style-sheet)

   [owner CSS rule](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-owner-css-rule)

   null

   [disabled flag](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-disabled-flag)

   Left at its default value.

   [CSS rules](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-css-rules)

   Left uninitialized.

   > [!warning]
   > This doesn't seem right. Presumably we should be using the element's [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text)? Tracked as [issue #2997](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/2997).

7. If element [contributes a script-blocking style sheet](#427-interactions-of-styling-and-scripting), [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) element to its [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [script-blocking style sheet set](#427-interactions-of-styling-and-scripting).
8. If element's [`media`](#426-the-style-element) attribute's value [matches the environment](#2310-media-queries) and element is [potentially render-blocking](#258-blocking-attributes), then [block rendering](#316-render-blocking-mechanism) on element.

Once the attempts to obtain the style sheet's [critical subresources](#212-resources), if any, are complete, or, if the style sheet has no [critical subresources](#212-resources), once the style sheet has been parsed and processed, the user agent must run these steps:

> [!warning]
> Fetching the [critical subresources](#212-resources) is not well-defined; probably [issue #968](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/968) is the best resolution for that. In the meantime, any [critical subresource](#212-resources) [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) should have its [render-blocking](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-render-blocking) set to whether or not the [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element is currently [render-blocking](#316-render-blocking-mechanism).
1. Let element be the [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element associated with the style sheet in question.
2. Let success be true.
3. If the attempts to obtain any of the style sheet's [critical subresources](#212-resources) failed for any reason (e.g., DNS error, HTTP 404 response, a connection being prematurely closed, unsupported Content-Type), set success to false.

   > [!note]
   > Note that content-specific errors, e.g., CSS parse errors or PNG decoding errors, do not affect success.

4. [Queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given element and the following steps:
   1. If success is true, [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`load`](#events) at element.
   2. Otherwise, [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) at element.
   3. If element [contributes a script-blocking style sheet](#427-interactions-of-styling-and-scripting):
      1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [script-blocking style sheet set](#427-interactions-of-styling-and-scripting) [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) element.
      2. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) element from its [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [script-blocking style sheet set](#427-interactions-of-styling-and-scripting).
   4. [Unblock rendering](#316-render-blocking-mechanism) on element.

The element must [delay the load event](#1327-the-end) of the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) until all the attempts to obtain the style sheet's [critical subresources](#212-resources), if any, are complete.

> [!note]
> This specification does not specify a style system, but CSS is expected to be supported by most web browsers. [\[CSS\]](#references)

The [`LinkStyle`](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#the-linkstyle-interface) interface is also implemented by this element. [\[CSSOM\]](#references)

> [!example]
> The following document has its stress emphasis styled as bright red text rather than italics text, while leaving titles of works and Latin words in their default italics. It shows how using appropriate elements enables easier restyling of documents.
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE html>
> <html lang="en-US">
>  <head>
>   <title>My favorite book</title>
>   <style>
>    body { color: black; background: white; }
>    em { font-style: normal; color: red; }
>   </style>
>  </head>
>  <body>
>   <p>My <em>favorite</em> book of all time has <em>got</em> to be
>   <cite>A Cat's Life</cite>. It is a book by P. Rahmel that talks
>   about the <i lang="la">Felis catus</i> in modern human society.</p>
>  </body>
> </html>
> ```

#### 4.2.7 Interactions of styling and scripting

If the style sheet referenced no other resources (e.g., it was an internal style sheet given by a [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element with no `@import` rules), then the style rules must be [immediately](#211-parallelism) made available to script; otherwise, the style rules must only be made available to script once the [event loop](#8171-definitions) reaches its [update the rendering](#8173-processing-model) step.

An element el in the context of a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) of an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) or [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents) contributes a script-blocking style sheet if all of the following are true:
- el was created by that [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s parser.
- el is either a [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element or a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element that was an [external resource link that contributes to the styling processing model](#46823-link-type-stylesheet) when the el was created by the parser.
- el's `media` attribute's value [matches the environment](#2310-media-queries).
- el's style sheet was enabled when the element was created by the parser.
- The last time the [event loop](#8171-definitions) reached [step 1](#8173-processing-model), el's [root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) was that [`Document`](#311-the-document-object).
- The user agent hasn't given up on loading that particular style sheet yet. A user agent may give up on loading a style sheet at any time.

  > [!note]
  > Giving up on a style sheet before the style sheet loads, if the style sheet eventually does still load, means that the script might end up operating with incorrect information. For example, if a style sheet sets the color of an element to green, but a script that inspects the resulting style is executed before the sheet is loaded, the script will find that the element is black (or whatever the default color is), and might thus make poor choices (e.g., deciding to use black as the color elsewhere on the page, instead of green). Implementers have to balance the likelihood of a script using incorrect information with the performance impact of doing nothing while waiting for a slow network request to finish.

> [!warning]
> It is expected that counterparts to the above rules also apply to [`<?xml-stylesheet?>`](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml-stylesheet/#the-xml-stylesheet-processing-instruction) PIs. However, this has not yet been thoroughly investigated.

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a script-blocking style sheet set, which is an [ordered set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets), initially empty.

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document has a style sheet that is blocking scripts if the following steps return true:
1. If document's [script-blocking style sheet set](#427-interactions-of-styling-and-scripting) is not [empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists), then return true.
2. If document's [node navigable](#731-navigables) is null, then return false.
3. Let containerDocument be document's [node navigable](#731-navigables)'s [container document](#7313-child-navigables).
4. If containerDocument is non-null and containerDocument's [script-blocking style sheet set](#427-interactions-of-styling-and-scripting) is not [empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists), then return true.
5. Return false.

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has no style sheet that is blocking scripts if it does not [have a style sheet that is blocking scripts](#427-interactions-of-styling-and-scripting).

### 4.3 Sections

#### 4.3.1 The `body` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

As the second element in an [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

A [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element's [start tag](#13121-start-tags) can be omitted if the element is empty, or if the first thing inside the [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element is not [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) or a [comment](#1316-comments), except if the first thing inside the [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element is a [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element), [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element), [`link`](#424-the-link-element), [`script`](#4121-the-script-element), [`style`](#426-the-style-element), or [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element.

A [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) can be omitted if the [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element is not immediately followed by a [comment](#1316-comments).

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`onafterprint`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects)

[`onbeforeprint`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects)

[`onbeforeunload`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects)

[`onhashchange`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects)

[`onlanguagechange`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects)

[`onmessage`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects)

[`onmessageerror`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects)

[`onoffline`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects)

[`ononline`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects)

[`onpageswap`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects)

[`onpagehide`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects)

[`onpagereveal`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects)

[`onpageshow`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects)

[`onpopstate`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects)

[`onrejectionhandled`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects)

[`onstorage`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects)

[`onunhandledrejection`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects)

[`onunload`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-body).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-body).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLBodyElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  // also has obsolete members
};

HTMLBodyElement includes WindowEventHandlers;
```

The [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the contents of the document.

In conforming documents, there is only one [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element. The [`document.body`](#317-dom-tree-accessors) IDL attribute provides scripts with easy access to a document's [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element.

> [!note]
> Some DOM operations (for example, parts of the [drag and drop](#611-drag-and-drop) model) are defined in terms of "[the body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors)". This refers to a particular element in the DOM, as per the definition of the term, and not any arbitrary [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element.

The [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element exposes as [event handler content attributes](#8181-event-handlers) a number of the [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers) of the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object. It also mirrors their [event handler IDL attributes](#8181-event-handlers).

The [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers) of the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object named by the [`Window`-reflecting body element event handler set](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects), exposed on the [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element, replace the generic [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers) with the same names normally supported by [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility).

> [!example]
> Thus, for example, a bubbling [`error`](#events) event dispatched on a child of [the body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors) of a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) would first trigger the [`onerror`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects) [event handler content attributes](#8181-event-handlers) of that element, then that of the root [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element, and only *then* would it trigger the [`onerror`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects) [event handler content attribute](#8181-event-handlers) on the [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element. This is because the event would bubble from the target, to the [`body`](#431-the-body-element), to the [`html`](#411-the-html-element), to the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), to the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object), and the [event handler](#8181-event-handlers) on the [`body`](#431-the-body-element) is watching the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) not the [`body`](#431-the-body-element). A regular event listener attached to the [`body`](#431-the-body-element) using `addEventListener()`, however, would be run when the event bubbled through the [`body`](#431-the-body-element) and not when it reaches the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object.

> [!example]
> This page updates an indicator to show whether or not the user is online:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <html lang="en">
>  <head>
>   <title>Online or offline?</title>
>   <script>
>    function update(online) {
>      document.getElementById('status').textContent =
>        online ? 'Online' : 'Offline';
>    }
>   </script>
>  </head>
>  <body ononline="update(true)"
>        onoffline="update(false)"
>        onload="update(navigator.onLine)">
>   <p>You are: <span id="status">(Unknown)</span></p>
>  </body>
> </html>
> ```

#### 4.3.2 The `article` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Sectioning content](#32523-sectioning-content).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [sectioning content](#32523-sectioning-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-article).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-article).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom).

The [`article`](#432-the-article-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a complete, or self-contained, composition in a document, page, application, or site and that is, in principle, independently distributable or reusable, e.g. in syndication. This could be a forum post, a magazine or newspaper article, a blog entry, a user-submitted comment, an interactive widget or gadget, or any other independent item of content.

When [`article`](#432-the-article-element) elements are nested, the inner [`article`](#432-the-article-element) elements represent articles that are in principle related to the contents of the outer article. For instance, a blog entry on a site that accepts user-submitted comments could represent the comments as [`article`](#432-the-article-element) elements nested within the [`article`](#432-the-article-element) element for the blog entry.

Author information associated with an [`article`](#432-the-article-element) element (q.v. the [`address`](#4310-the-address-element) element) does not apply to nested [`article`](#432-the-article-element) elements.

> [!note]
> When used specifically with content to be redistributed in syndication, the [`article`](#432-the-article-element) element is similar in purpose to the `entry` element in Atom. [\[ATOM\]](#references)

> [!note]
> The schema.org microdata vocabulary can be used to provide the publication date for an [`article`](#432-the-article-element) element, using one of the CreativeWork subtypes.

When the main content of the page (i.e. excluding footers, headers, navigation blocks, and sidebars) is all one single self-contained composition, that content may be marked with an [`article`](#432-the-article-element), but it is technically redundant in that case (since it's self-evident that the page is a single composition, as it is a single document).

> [!example]
> This example shows a blog post using the [`article`](#432-the-article-element) element, with some schema.org annotations:
> 
> ```html
> <article itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/BlogPosting">
>  <header>
>   <h2 itemprop="headline">The Very First Rule of Life</h2>
>   <p><time itemprop="datePublished" datetime="2009-10-09">3 days ago</time></p>
>   <link itemprop="url" href="?comments=0">
>  </header>
>  <p>If there's a microphone anywhere near you, assume it's hot and
>  sending whatever you're saying to the world. Seriously.</p>
>  <p>...</p>
>  <footer>
>   <a itemprop="discussionUrl" href="?comments=1">Show comments...</a>
>  </footer>
> </article>
> ```
> 
> Here is that same blog post, but showing some of the comments:
> 
> ```html
> <article itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/BlogPosting">
>  <header>
>   <h2 itemprop="headline">The Very First Rule of Life</h2>
>   <p><time itemprop="datePublished" datetime="2009-10-09">3 days ago</time></p>
>   <link itemprop="url" href="?comments=0">
>  </header>
>  <p>If there's a microphone anywhere near you, assume it's hot and
>  sending whatever you're saying to the world. Seriously.</p>
>  <p>...</p>
>  <section>
>   <h1>Comments</h1>
>   <article itemprop="comment" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Comment" id="c1">
>    <link itemprop="url" href="#c1">
>    <footer>
>     <p>Posted by: <span itemprop="creator" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person">
>      <span itemprop="name">George Washington</span>
>     </span></p>
>     <p><time itemprop="dateCreated" datetime="2009-10-10">15 minutes ago</time></p>
>    </footer>
>    <p>Yeah! Especially when talking about your lobbyist friends!</p>
>   </article>
>   <article itemprop="comment" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Comment" id="c2">
>    <link itemprop="url" href="#c2">
>    <footer>
>     <p>Posted by: <span itemprop="creator" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person">
>      <span itemprop="name">George Hammond</span>
>     </span></p>
>     <p><time itemprop="dateCreated" datetime="2009-10-10">5 minutes ago</time></p>
>    </footer>
>    <p>Hey, you have the same first name as me.</p>
>   </article>
>  </section>
> </article>
> ```
> 
> Notice the use of [`footer`](#439-the-footer-element) to give the information for each comment (such as who wrote it and when): the [`footer`](#439-the-footer-element) element *can* appear at the start of its section when appropriate, such as in this case. (Using [`header`](#438-the-header-element) in this case wouldn't be wrong either; it's mostly a matter of authoring preference.)

> [!example]
> In this example, [`article`](#432-the-article-element) elements are used to host widgets on a portal page. The widgets are implemented as [customized built-in elements](#4133-core-concepts) in order to get specific styling and scripted behavior.
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <html lang=en>
> <title>eHome Portal</title>
> <script src="/scripts/widgets.js"></script>
> <link rel=stylesheet href="/styles/main.css">
> <article is="stock-widget">
>  <h2>Stocks</h2>
>  <table>
>   <thead> <tr> <th> Stock <th> Value <th> Delta
>   <tbody> <template> <tr> <td> <td> <td> </template>
>  </table>
>  <p> <input type=button value="Refresh" onclick="this.parentElement.refresh()">
