> I first lived there):</p>
> <ol>
>  <li>United Kingdom
>  <li>Switzerland
>  <li>United States
>  <li>Norway
> </ol>
> ```

#### 4.4.6 The `ul` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

If the element's children include at least one [`li`](#448-the-li-element) element: [Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [flow content](#32522-flow-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

Zero or more [`li`](#448-the-li-element) and [script-supporting](#32529-script-supporting-elements) elements.

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-ul).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-ul).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLUListElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`ul`](#446-the-ul-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a list of items, where the order of the items is not important — that is, where changing the order would not materially change the meaning of the document.

The items of the list are the [`li`](#448-the-li-element) element child nodes of the [`ul`](#446-the-ul-element) element.

> [!example]
> The following markup shows a list where the order does not matter, and where the [`ul`](#446-the-ul-element) element is therefore appropriate. Compare this list to the equivalent list in the [`ol`](#445-the-ol-element) section to see an example of the same items using the [`ol`](#445-the-ol-element) element.
> 
> ```html
> <p>I have lived in the following countries:</p>
> <ul>
>  <li>Norway
>  <li>Switzerland
>  <li>United Kingdom
>  <li>United States
> </ul>
> ```
> 
> Note that changing the order of the list does not change the meaning of the document. The items in the snippet above are given in alphabetical order, but in the snippet below they are given in order of the size of their current account balance in 2007, without changing the meaning of the document whatsoever:
> 
> ```html
> <p>I have lived in the following countries:</p>
> <ul>
>  <li>Switzerland
>  <li>Norway
>  <li>United Kingdom
>  <li>United States
> </ul>
> ```

#### 4.4.7 The `menu` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

If the element's children include at least one [`li`](#448-the-li-element) element: [Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [flow content](#32522-flow-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

Zero or more [`li`](#448-the-li-element) and [script-supporting](#32529-script-supporting-elements) elements.

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-menu).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-menu).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLMenuElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`menu`](#447-the-menu-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a toolbar consisting of its contents, in the form of an unordered list of items (represented by [`li`](#448-the-li-element) elements), each of which represents a command that the user can perform or activate.

> [!note]
> The [`menu`](#447-the-menu-element) element is simply a semantic alternative to [`ul`](#446-the-ul-element) to express an unordered list of commands (a "toolbar").

> [!example]
> In this example, a text-editing application uses a [`menu`](#447-the-menu-element) element to provide a series of editing commands:
> 
> ```html
> <menu>
>  <li><button onclick="copy()"><img src="copy.svg" alt="Copy"></button></li>
>  <li><button onclick="cut()"><img src="cut.svg" alt="Cut"></button></li>
>  <li><button onclick="paste()"><img src="paste.svg" alt="Paste"></button></li>
> </menu>
> ```
> 
> Note that the styling to make this look like a conventional toolbar menu is up to the application.

#### 4.4.8 The `li` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Inside [`ol`](#445-the-ol-element) elements.

Inside [`ul`](#446-the-ul-element) elements.

Inside [`menu`](#447-the-menu-element) elements.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

An [`li`](#448-the-li-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) can be omitted if the [`li`](#448-the-li-element) element is immediately followed by another [`li`](#448-the-li-element) element or if there is no more content in the parent element.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

If the element is not a child of an [`ul`](#446-the-ul-element) or [`menu`](#447-the-menu-element) element: [`value`](#448-the-li-element) — [Ordinal value](#448-the-li-element) of the list item

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-li).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-li).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants) with attributes [`value`](#448-the-li-element).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLLIElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute long value;

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`li`](#448-the-li-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a list item. If its parent element is an [`ol`](#445-the-ol-element), [`ul`](#446-the-ul-element), or [`menu`](#447-the-menu-element) element, then the element is an item of the parent element's list, as defined for those elements. Otherwise, the list item has no defined list-related relationship to any other [`li`](#448-the-li-element) element.

The `value` attribute, if present, must be a [valid integer](#2341-signed-integers). It is used to determine the [ordinal value](#448-the-li-element) of the list item, when the [`li`](#448-the-li-element)'s [list owner](#448-the-li-element) is an [`ol`](#445-the-ol-element) element.

---

Any element whose [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of ['display'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop) is 'list-item' has a list owner, which is determined as follows:
1. If the element is not [being rendered](#151-introduction), return null; the element has no [list owner](#448-the-li-element).
2. Let ancestor be the element's parent.
3. If the element has an [`ol`](#445-the-ol-element), [`ul`](#446-the-ul-element), or [`menu`](#447-the-menu-element) ancestor, set ancestor to the closest such ancestor element.
4. Return the closest inclusive ancestor of ancestor that produces a [CSS box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#css-box).

   > [!note]
   > Such an element will always exist, as at the very least the [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) will always produce a [CSS box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#css-box).

To determine the ordinal value of each element owned by a given [list owner](#448-the-li-element) owner, perform the following steps:
1. Let i be 1.
2. If owner is an [`ol`](#445-the-ol-element) element, let numbering be owner's [starting value](#445-the-ol-element). Otherwise, let numbering be 1.
3. *Loop*: If i is greater than the number of [list items that owner owns](#448-the-li-element), then return; all of owner's [owned list items](#448-the-li-element) have been assigned [ordinal values](#448-the-li-element).
4. Let item be the ith of owner's [owned list items](#448-the-li-element), in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
5. If item is an [`li`](#448-the-li-element) element that has a [`value`](#448-the-li-element) attribute:
   1. Let parsed be the result of [parsing the value of the attribute as an integer](#2341-signed-integers).
   2. If parsed is not an error, then set numbering to parsed.
6. The [ordinal value](#448-the-li-element) of item is numbering.
7. If owner is an [`ol`](#445-the-ol-element) element, and owner has a [`reversed`](#445-the-ol-element) attribute, decrement numbering by 1; otherwise, increment numbering by 1.
8. Increment i by 1.
9. Go to the step labeled *loop*.

---

> [!example]
> The element's [`value`](#448-the-li-element) IDL attribute does not directly correspond to its [ordinal value](#448-the-li-element); it simply [reflects](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the content attribute. For example, given this list:
> 
> ```html
> <ol>
>  <li>Item 1
>  <li value="3">Item 3
>  <li>Item 4
> </ol>
> ```
> 
> The [ordinal values](#448-the-li-element) are 1, 3, and 4, whereas the [`value`](#448-the-li-element) IDL attributes return 0, 3, 0 on getting.

> [!example]
> The following example, the top ten movies are listed (in reverse order). Note the way the list is given a title by using a [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element) element and its [`figcaption`](#4413-the-figcaption-element) element.
> 
> ```html
> <figure>
>  <figcaption>The top 10 movies of all time</figcaption>
>  <ol>
>   <li value="10"><cite>Josie and the Pussycats</cite>, 2001</li>
>   <li value="9"><cite lang="sh">Црна мачка, бели мачор</cite>, 1998</li>
>   <li value="8"><cite>A Bug's Life</cite>, 1998</li>
>   <li value="7"><cite>Toy Story</cite>, 1995</li>
>   <li value="6"><cite>Monsters, Inc</cite>, 2001</li>
>   <li value="5"><cite>Cars</cite>, 2006</li>
>   <li value="4"><cite>Toy Story 2</cite>, 1999</li>
>   <li value="3"><cite>Finding Nemo</cite>, 2003</li>
>   <li value="2"><cite>The Incredibles</cite>, 2004</li>
>   <li value="1"><cite>Ratatouille</cite>, 2007</li>
>  </ol>
> </figure>
> ```
> 
> The markup could also be written as follows, using the [`reversed`](#445-the-ol-element) attribute on the [`ol`](#445-the-ol-element) element:
> 
> ```html
> <figure>
>  <figcaption>The top 10 movies of all time</figcaption>
>  <ol reversed>
>   <li><cite>Josie and the Pussycats</cite>, 2001</li>
>   <li><cite lang="sh">Црна мачка, бели мачор</cite>, 1998</li>
>   <li><cite>A Bug's Life</cite>, 1998</li>
>   <li><cite>Toy Story</cite>, 1995</li>
>   <li><cite>Monsters, Inc</cite>, 2001</li>
>   <li><cite>Cars</cite>, 2006</li>
>   <li><cite>Toy Story 2</cite>, 1999</li>
>   <li><cite>Finding Nemo</cite>, 2003</li>
>   <li><cite>The Incredibles</cite>, 2004</li>
>   <li><cite>Ratatouille</cite>, 2007</li>
>  </ol>
> </figure>
> ```

> [!note]
> While it is conforming to include heading elements (e.g. [`h1`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements)) inside [`li`](#448-the-li-element) elements, it likely does not convey the semantics that the author intended. A heading starts a new section, so a heading in a list implicitly splits the list into spanning multiple sections.

#### 4.4.9 The `dl` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

If the element's children include at least one name-value group: [Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [flow content](#32522-flow-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

Either: Zero or more groups each consisting of one or more [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) elements followed by one or more [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) elements, optionally intermixed with [script-supporting elements](#32529-script-supporting-elements).

Or: One or more [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) elements, optionally intermixed with [script-supporting elements](#32529-script-supporting-elements).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-dl).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-dl).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLDListElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`dl`](#449-the-dl-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) an association list consisting of zero or more name-value groups (a description list). A name-value group consists of one or more names ([`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) elements, possibly as children of a [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element child) followed by one or more values ([`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) elements, possibly as children of a [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element child), ignoring any nodes other than [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) and [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) element children, and [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) and [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) elements that are children of [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element children. Within a single [`dl`](#449-the-dl-element) element, there should not be more than one [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) element for each name.

Name-value groups may be terms and definitions, metadata topics and values, questions and answers, or any other groups of name-value data.

The values within a group are alternatives; multiple paragraphs forming part of the same value must all be given within the same [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) element.

The order of the list of groups, and of the names and values within each group, may be significant.

In order to annotate groups with [microdata](#5-microdata) attributes, or other [global attributes](#326-global-attributes) that apply to whole groups, or just for styling purposes, each group in a [`dl`](#449-the-dl-element) element can be wrapped in a [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element. This does not change the semantics of the [`dl`](#449-the-dl-element) element.

The name-value groups of a [`dl`](#449-the-dl-element) element dl are determined using the following algorithm. A name-value group has a name (a list of [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) elements, initially empty) and a value (a list of [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) elements, initially empty).
1. Let groups be an empty list of name-value groups.
2. Let current be a new name-value group.
3. Let seenDd be false.
4. Let child be dl's [first child](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
5. Let grandchild be null.
6. While child is not null:
   1. If child is a [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element:
      1. Let grandchild be child's [first child](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
      2. While grandchild is not null:
         1. [Process `dt` or `dd`](#449-the-dl-element) for grandchild.
         2. Set grandchild to grandchild's [next sibling](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
   2. Otherwise, [process `dt` or `dd`](#449-the-dl-element) for child.
   3. Set child to child's [next sibling](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
7. If current is not empty, then append current to groups.
8. Return groups.

To process `dt` or `dd` for a node node means to follow these steps:
1. Let groups, current, and seenDd be the same variables as those of the same name in the algorithm that invoked these steps.
2. If node is a [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) element:
   1. If seenDd is true, then append current to groups, set current to a new name-value group, and set seenDd to false.
   2. Append node to current's name.
3. Otherwise, if node is a [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) element, then append node to current's value and set seenDd to true.

> [!note]
> When a name-value group has an empty list as name or value, it is often due to accidentally using [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) elements in the place of [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) elements and vice versa. Conformance checkers can spot such mistakes and might be able to advise authors how to correctly use the markup.

> [!example]
> In the following example, one entry ("Authors") is linked to two values ("John" and "Luke").
> 
> ```html
> <dl>
>  <dt> Authors
>  <dd> John
>  <dd> Luke
>  <dt> Editor
>  <dd> Frank
> </dl>
> ```

> [!example]
> In the following example, one definition is linked to two terms.
> 
> ```html
> <dl>
>  <dt lang="en-US"> <dfn>color</dfn> </dt>
>  <dt lang="en-GB"> <dfn>colour</dfn> </dt>
>  <dd> A sensation which (in humans) derives from the ability of
>  the fine structure of the eye to distinguish three differently
>  filtered analyses of a view. </dd>
> </dl>
> ```

> [!example]
> The following example illustrates the use of the [`dl`](#449-the-dl-element) element to mark up metadata of sorts. At the end of the example, one group has two metadata labels ("Authors" and "Editors") and two values ("Robert Rothman" and "Daniel Jackson"). This example also uses the [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element around the groups of [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) and [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) element, to aid with styling.
> 
> ```html
> <dl>
>  <div>
>   <dt> Last modified time </dt>
>   <dd> 2004-12-23T23:33Z </dd>
>  </div>
>  <div>
>   <dt> Recommended update interval </dt>
>   <dd> 60s </dd>
>  </div>
>  <div>
>   <dt> Authors </dt>
>   <dt> Editors </dt>
>   <dd> Robert Rothman </dd>
>   <dd> Daniel Jackson </dd>
>  </div>
> </dl>
> ```

> [!example]
> The following example shows the [`dl`](#449-the-dl-element) element used to give a set of instructions. The order of the instructions here is important (in the other examples, the order of the blocks was not important).
> 
> ```html
> <p>Determine the victory points as follows (use the
> first matching case):</p>
> <dl>
>  <dt> If you have exactly five gold coins </dt>
>  <dd> You get five victory points </dd>
>  <dt> If you have one or more gold coins, and you have one or more silver coins </dt>
>  <dd> You get two victory points </dd>
>  <dt> If you have one or more silver coins </dt>
>  <dd> You get one victory point </dd>
>  <dt> Otherwise </dt>
>  <dd> You get no victory points </dd>
> </dl>
> ```

> [!example]
> The following snippet shows a [`dl`](#449-the-dl-element) element being used as a glossary. Note the use of [`dfn`](#458-the-dfn-element) to indicate the word being defined.
> 
> ```html
> <dl>
>  <dt><dfn>Apartment</dfn>, n.</dt>
>  <dd>An execution context grouping one or more threads with one or
>  more COM objects.</dd>
>  <dt><dfn>Flat</dfn>, n.</dt>
>  <dd>A deflated tire.</dd>
>  <dt><dfn>Home</dfn>, n.</dt>
>  <dd>The user's login directory.</dd>
> </dl>
> ```

> [!example]
> This example uses [microdata](#5-microdata) attributes in a [`dl`](#449-the-dl-element) element, together with the [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element, to annotate the ice cream desserts at a French restaurant.
> 
> ```html
> <dl>
>  <div itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Product">
>   <dt itemprop="name">Café ou Chocolat Liégeois
>   <dd itemprop="offers" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Offer">
>    <span itemprop="price">3.50</span>
>    <data itemprop="priceCurrency" value="EUR">€</data>
>   <dd itemprop="description">
>    2 boules Café ou Chocolat, 1 boule Vanille, sauce café ou chocolat, chantilly
>  </div>
> 
>  <div itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Product">
>   <dt itemprop="name">Américaine
>   <dd itemprop="offers" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Offer">
>    <span itemprop="price">3.50</span>
>    <data itemprop="priceCurrency" value="EUR">€</data>
>   <dd itemprop="description">
>    1 boule Crème brûlée, 1 boule Vanille, 1 boule Caramel, chantilly
>  </div>
> </dl>
> ```
> 
> Without the [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element the markup would need to use the [`itemref`](#522-items) attribute to link the data in the [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) elements with the item, as follows.
> 
> ```html
> <dl>
>  <dt itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Product" itemref="1-offer 1-description">
>   <span itemprop="name">Café ou Chocolat Liégeois</span>
>  <dd id="1-offer" itemprop="offers" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Offer">
>   <span itemprop="price">3.50</span>
>   <data itemprop="priceCurrency" value="EUR">€</data>
>  <dd id="1-description" itemprop="description">
>   2 boules Café ou Chocolat, 1 boule Vanille, sauce café ou chocolat, chantilly
> 
>  <dt itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Product" itemref="2-offer 2-description">
>   <span itemprop="name">Américaine</span>
>  <dd id="2-offer" itemprop="offers" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Offer">
>   <span itemprop="price">3.50</span>
>   <data itemprop="priceCurrency" value="EUR">€</data>
>  <dd id="2-description" itemprop="description">
>   1 boule Crème brûlée, 1 boule Vanille, 1 boule Caramel, chantilly
> </dl>
> ```

> [!note]
> The [`dl`](#449-the-dl-element) element is inappropriate for marking up dialogue. See some [examples of how to mark up dialogue](#4143-conversations).

#### 4.4.10 The `dt` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Before [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) or [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) elements inside [`dl`](#449-the-dl-element) elements.

Before [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) or [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) elements inside [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) elements that are children of a [`dl`](#449-the-dl-element) element.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content), but with no [`header`](#438-the-header-element), [`footer`](#439-the-footer-element), [sectioning content](#32523-sectioning-content), or [heading content](#32524-heading-content) descendants.

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

A [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) can be omitted if the [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) element is immediately followed by another [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) element or a [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) element.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-dt).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-dt).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom).

The [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the term, or name, part of a term-description group in a description list ([`dl`](#449-the-dl-element) element).

> [!note]
> The [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) element itself, when used in a [`dl`](#449-the-dl-element) element, does not indicate that its contents are a term being defined, but this can be indicated using the [`dfn`](#458-the-dfn-element) element.

> [!example]
> This example shows a list of frequently asked questions (a FAQ) marked up using the [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) element for questions and the [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) element for answers.
> 
> ```html
> <article>
>  <h1>FAQ</h1>
>  <dl>
>   <dt>What do we want?</dt>
>   <dd>Our data.</dd>
>   <dt>When do we want it?</dt>
>   <dd>Now.</dd>
>   <dt>Where is it?</dt>
>   <dd>We are not sure.</dd>
>  </dl>
> </article>
> ```

#### 4.4.11 The `dd` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

After [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) or [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) elements inside [`dl`](#449-the-dl-element) elements.

After [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) or [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) elements inside [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) elements that are children of a [`dl`](#449-the-dl-element) element.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

A [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) can be omitted if the [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) element is immediately followed by another [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) element or a [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-dd).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-dd).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom).

The [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the description, definition, or value, part of a term-description group in a description list ([`dl`](#449-the-dl-element) element).

> [!example]
> A [`dl`](#449-the-dl-element) can be used to define a vocabulary list, like in a dictionary. In the following example, each entry, given by a [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) with a [`dfn`](#458-the-dfn-element), has several [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element)s, showing the various parts of the definition.
> 
> ```html
> <dl>
>  <dt><dfn>happiness</dfn></dt>
>  <dd class="pronunciation">/ˈhæpinəs/</dd>
>  <dd class="part-of-speech"><i><abbr>n.</abbr></i></dd>
>  <dd>The state of being happy.</dd>
>  <dd>Good fortune; success. <q>Oh <b>happiness</b>! It worked!</q></dd>
>  <dt><dfn>rejoice</dfn></dt>
>  <dd class="pronunciation">/rɪˈdʒɔɪs/</dd>
>  <dd><i class="part-of-speech"><abbr>v.intr.</abbr></i> To be delighted oneself.</dd>
>  <dd><i class="part-of-speech"><abbr>v.tr.</abbr></i> To cause one to be delighted.</dd>
> </dl>
> ```

#### 4.4.12 The `figure` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [flow content](#32522-flow-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

Either: one [`figcaption`](#4413-the-figcaption-element) element followed by [flow content](#32522-flow-content).

Or: [flow content](#32522-flow-content) followed by one [`figcaption`](#4413-the-figcaption-element) element.

Or: [flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-figure).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-figure).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom).

The [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) some [flow content](#32522-flow-content), optionally with a caption, that is self-contained (like a complete sentence) and is typically [referenced](#322-elements-in-the-dom) as a single unit from the main flow of the document.

> [!note]
> "Self-contained" in this context does not necessarily mean independent. For example, each sentence in a paragraph is self-contained; an image that is part of a sentence would be inappropriate for [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element), but an entire sentence made of images would be fitting.

The element can thus be used to annotate illustrations, diagrams, photos, code listings, etc.

> [!note]
> When a [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element) is referred to from the main content of the document by identifying it by its caption (e.g., by figure number), it enables such content to be easily moved away from that primary content, e.g., to the side of the page, to dedicated pages, or to an appendix, without affecting the flow of the document.
> 
> If a [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element) element is [referenced](#322-elements-in-the-dom) by its relative position, e.g., "in the photograph above" or "as the next figure shows", then moving the figure would disrupt the page's meaning. Authors are encouraged to consider using labels to refer to figures, rather than using such relative references, so that the page can easily be restyled without affecting the page's meaning.

The first [`figcaption`](#4413-the-figcaption-element) element child of the element, if any, represents the caption of the [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element) element's contents. If there is no child [`figcaption`](#4413-the-figcaption-element) element, then there is no caption.

A [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element) element's contents are part of the surrounding flow. If the purpose of the page is to display the figure, for example a photograph on an image sharing site, the [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element) and [`figcaption`](#4413-the-figcaption-element) elements can be used to explicitly provide a caption for that figure. For content that is only tangentially related, or that serves a separate purpose than the surrounding flow, the [`aside`](#435-the-aside-element) element should be used (and can itself wrap a [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element)). For example, a pull quote that repeats content from an [`article`](#432-the-article-element) would be more appropriate in an [`aside`](#435-the-aside-element) than in a [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element), because it isn't part of the content, it's a repetition of the content for the purposes of enticing readers or highlighting key topics.

> [!example]
> This example shows the [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element) element to mark up a code listing.
> 
> ```html
> <p>In <a href="#l4">listing 4</a> we see the primary core interface
> API declaration.</p>
> <figure id="l4">
>  <figcaption>Listing 4. The primary core interface API declaration.</figcaption>
>  <pre><code>interface PrimaryCore {
>  boolean verifyDataLine();
>  undefined sendData(sequence&lt;byte> data);
>  undefined initSelfDestruct();
> }</code></pre>
> </figure>
> <p>The API is designed to use UTF-8.</p>
> ```

> [!example]
> Here we see a [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element) element to mark up a photo that is the main content of the page (as in a gallery).
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <html lang="en">
> <title>Bubbles at work — My Gallery™</title>
> <figure>
>  <img src="bubbles-work.jpeg"
>       alt="Bubbles, sitting in his office chair, works on his
>            latest project intently.">
>  <figcaption>Bubbles at work</figcaption>
> </figure>
> <nav><a href="19414.html">Prev</a> — <a href="19416.html">Next</a></nav>
> ```

> [!example]
> In this example, we see an image that is *not* a figure, as well as an image and a video that are. The first image is literally part of the example's second sentence, so it's not a self-contained unit, and thus [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element) would be inappropriate.
> 
> ```html
> <h2>Malinko's comics</h2>
> 
> <p>This case centered on some sort of "intellectual property"
> infringement related to a comic (see Exhibit A). The suit started
> after a trailer ending with these words:
> 
> <blockquote>
>  <img src="promblem-packed-action.png" alt="ROUGH COPY! Promblem-Packed Action!">
> </blockquote>
> 
> <p>...was aired. A lawyer, armed with a Bigger Notebook, launched a
> preemptive strike using snowballs. A complete copy of the trailer is
> included with Exhibit B.
> 
> <figure>
>  <img src="ex-a.png" alt="Two squiggles on a dirty piece of paper.">
>  <figcaption>Exhibit A. The alleged <cite>rough copy</cite> comic.</figcaption>
> </figure>
> 
> <figure>
>  <video src="ex-b.mov"></video>
>  <figcaption>Exhibit B. The <cite>Rough Copy</cite> trailer.</figcaption>
> </figure>
> 
> <p>The case was resolved out of court.
> ```

> [!example]
> Here, a part of a poem is marked up using [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element).
> 
> ```html
> <figure>
>  <p>'Twas brillig, and the slithy toves<br>
>  Did gyre and gimble in the wabe;<br>
>  All mimsy were the borogoves,<br>
>  And the mome raths outgrabe.</p>
>  <figcaption><cite>Jabberwocky</cite> (first verse). Lewis Carroll, 1832-98</figcaption>
> </figure>
> ```

> [!example]
> In this example, which could be part of a much larger work discussing a castle, nested [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element) elements are used to provide both a group caption and individual captions for each figure in the group:
> 
> ```html
> <figure>
>  <figcaption>The castle through the ages: 1423, 1858, and 1999 respectively.</figcaption>
>  <figure>
>   <figcaption>Etching. Anonymous, ca. 1423.</figcaption>
>   <img src="castle1423.jpeg" alt="The castle has one tower, and a tall wall around it.">
>  </figure>
>  <figure>
>   <figcaption>Oil-based paint on canvas. Maria Towle, 1858.</figcaption>
>   <img src="castle1858.jpeg" alt="The castle now has two towers and two walls.">
>  </figure>
>  <figure>
>   <figcaption>Film photograph. Peter Jankle, 1999.</figcaption>
>   <img src="castle1999.jpeg" alt="The castle lies in ruins, the original tower all that remains in one piece.">
>  </figure>
> </figure>
> ```

> [!example]
> The previous example could also be more succinctly written as follows (using [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attributes in place of the nested [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element)/[`figcaption`](#4413-the-figcaption-element) pairs):
> 
> ```html
> <figure>
>  <img src="castle1423.jpeg" title="Etching. Anonymous, ca. 1423."
>       alt="The castle has one tower, and a tall wall around it.">
>  <img src="castle1858.jpeg" title="Oil-based paint on canvas. Maria Towle, 1858."
>       alt="The castle now has two towers and two walls.">
>  <img src="castle1999.jpeg" title="Film photograph. Peter Jankle, 1999."
>       alt="The castle lies in ruins, the original tower all that remains in one piece.">
>  <figcaption>The castle through the ages: 1423, 1858, and 1999 respectively.</figcaption>
> </figure>
> ```

> [!example]
> The figure is sometimes [referenced](#322-elements-in-the-dom) only implicitly from the content:
> 
> ```html
> <article>
>  <h1>Fiscal negotiations stumble in Congress as deadline nears</h1>
>  <figure>
>   <img src="obama-reid.jpeg" alt="Obama and Reid sit together smiling in the Oval Office.">
>   <figcaption>Barack Obama and Harry Reid. White House press photograph.</figcaption>
>  </figure>
>  <p>Negotiations in Congress to end the fiscal impasse sputtered on Tuesday, leaving both chambers
>  grasping for a way to reopen the government and raise the country's borrowing authority with a
>  Thursday deadline drawing near.</p>
>  ...
> </article>
> ```

#### 4.4.13 The `figcaption` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

As the first or last child of a [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element) element.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-figcaption).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-figcaption).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom).

The [`figcaption`](#4413-the-figcaption-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a caption or legend for the rest of the contents of the [`figcaption`](#4413-the-figcaption-element) element's parent [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element) element, if any.

> [!example]
> The element can contain additional information about the source:
> 
> ```html
> <figcaption>
>  <p>A duck.</p>
>  <p><small>Photograph courtesy of 🌟 News.</small></p>
> </figcaption>
> ```
> 
> ```html
> <figcaption>
>  <p>Average rent for 3-room apartments, excluding non-profit apartments</p>
>  <p>Zürich’s Statistics Office — <time datetime=2017-11-14>14 November 2017</time></p>
> </figcaption>
> ```

#### 4.4.14 The `main` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [flow content](#32522-flow-content) is expected, but only if it is a [hierarchically correct `main` element](#4414-the-main-element).

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-main).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-main).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom).

The [`main`](#4414-the-main-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the dominant contents of the document.

A document must not have more than one [`main`](#4414-the-main-element) element that does not have the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute specified.

A hierarchically correct `main` element is one whose ancestor elements are limited to [`html`](#411-the-html-element), [`body`](#431-the-body-element), [`div`](#4416-the-div-element), [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) without an [accessible name](https://w3c.github.io/accname/#dfn-accessible-name), and [autonomous custom elements](#4133-core-concepts). Each [`main`](#4414-the-main-element) element must be a [hierarchically correct `main` element](#4414-the-main-element).

> [!example]
> In this example, the author has used a presentation where each component of the page is rendered in a box. To wrap the main content of the page (as opposed to the header, the footer, the navigation bar, and a sidebar), the [`main`](#4414-the-main-element) element is used.
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE html>
> <html lang="en">
> <title>RPG System 17</title>
> <style>
>  header, nav, aside, main, footer {
>    margin: 0.5em; border: thin solid; padding: 0.5em;
>    background: #EFF; color: black; box-shadow: 0 0 0.25em #033;
>  }
>  h1, h2, p { margin: 0; }
>  nav, main { float: left; }
>  aside { float: right; }
>  footer { clear: both; }
> </style>
> <header>
>  <h1>System Eighteen</h1>
> </header>
> <nav>
>  <a href="../16/">← System 17</a>
>  <a href="../18/">RPXIX →</a>
> </nav>
> <aside>
>  <p>This system has no HP mechanic, so there's no healing.
> </aside>
> <main>
>  <h2>Character creation</h2>
>  <p>Attributes (magic, strength, agility) are purchased at the cost of one point per level.</p>
>  <h2>Rolls</h2>
>  <p>Each encounter, roll the dice for all your skills. If you roll more than the opponent, you win.</p>
> </main>
> <footer>
>  <p>Copyright © 2013
> </footer>
> </html>
> ```
> 
> In the following example, multiple [`main`](#4414-the-main-element) elements are used and script is used to make navigation work without a server roundtrip and to set the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute on those that are not current:
> 
> ```html
> <!doctype html>
> <html lang=en-CA>
> <meta charset=utf-8>
> <title> … </title>
> <link rel=stylesheet href=spa.css>
> <script src=spa.js async></script>
> <nav>
>  <a href=/>Home</a>
>  <a href=/about>About</a>
>  <a href=/contact>Contact</a>
> </nav>
> <main>
>  <h1>Home</h1>
>  …
> </main>
> <main hidden>
>  <h1>About</h1>
>  …
> </main>
> <main hidden>
>  <h1>Contact</h1>
>  …
> </main>
> <footer>Made with ❤️ by <a href=https://example.com/>Example 👻</a>.</footer>
> ```

#### 4.4.15 The `search` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [flow content](#32522-flow-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-search).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-search).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom).

The [`search`](#4415-the-search-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a part of a document or application that contains a set of form controls or other content related to performing a search or filtering operation. This could be a search of the web site or application; a way of searching or filtering search results on the current web page; or a global or Internet-wide search function.

> [!note]
> It's not appropriate to use the [`search`](#4415-the-search-element) element just for presenting search results, though suggestions and links as part of "quick search" results can be included as part of a search feature. Rather, a returned web page of search results would instead be expected to be presented as part of the main content of that web page.

> [!example]
> In the following example, the author is including a search form within the [`header`](#438-the-header-element) of the web page:
> 
> ```html
> <header>
>   <h1><a href="/">My fancy blog</a></h1>
>   ...
>   <search>
>     <form action="search.php">
>       <label for="query">Find an article</label>
>       <input id="query" name="q" type="search">
>       <button type="submit">Go!</button>
>     </form>
>   </search>
> </header>
> ```

> [!example]
> In this example, the author has implemented their web application's search functionality entirely with JavaScript. There is no use of the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element to perform server-side submission, but the containing [`search`](#4415-the-search-element) element semantically identifies the purpose of the descendant content as representing search capabilities.
> 
> ```html
> <search>
>   <label>
>     Find and filter your query
>     <input type="search" id="query">
>   </label>
>   <label>
>     <input type="checkbox" id="exact-only">
>     Exact matches only
>   </label>
> 
>   <section>
>     <h3>Results found:</h3>
>     <ul id="results">
>       <li>
>         <p><a href="services/consulting">Consulting services</a></p>
>         <p>
>           Find out how can we help you improve your business with our integrated consultants, Bob and Bob.
>         </p>
>       </li>
>       ...
>     </ul>
>     <!--
>       when a query returns or filters out all results
>       render the no results message here
>     -->
>     <output id="no-results"></output>
>   </section>
> </search>
> ```

> [!example]
> In the following example, the page has two search features. The first is located in the web page's [`header`](#438-the-header-element) and serves as a global mechanism to search the web site's content. Its purpose is indicated by its specified [`title`](#422-the-title-element) attribute. The second is included as part of the main content of the page, as it represents a mechanism to search and filter the content of the current page. It contains a heading to indicate its purpose.
> 
> ```html
> <body>
>   <header>
>     ...
>     <search title="Website">
>       ...
>     </search>
>   </header>
>   <main>
>     <h1>Hotels near your location</h1>
>      <search>
>        <h2>Filter results</h2>
>        ...
>      </search>
>      <article>
>       <!-- search result content -->
>     </article>
>   </main>
> </body>
> ```

#### 4.4.16 The `div` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [flow content](#32522-flow-content) is expected.

As a child of a [`dl`](#449-the-dl-element) element.

As a descendant of an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element, an [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element, or a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

If the element is a child of a [`dl`](#449-the-dl-element) element: One or more [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) elements followed by one or more [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) elements, optionally intermixed with [script-supporting elements](#32529-script-supporting-elements).

Otherwise, if the element is a descendant of an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element, an [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element, or a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element: [transparent](#3253-transparent-content-models).

Otherwise: [flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-div).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-div).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLDivElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element has no special meaning at all. It [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) its children. It can be used with the [`class`](#326-global-attributes), [`lang`](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes), and [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attributes to mark up semantics common to a group of consecutive elements. It can also be used in a [`dl`](#449-the-dl-element) element, wrapping groups of [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) and [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) elements.

> [!note]
> Authors are strongly encouraged to view the [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element as an element of last resort, for when no other element is suitable. Use of more appropriate elements instead of the [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element leads to better accessibility for readers and easier maintainability for authors.

> [!example]
> For example, a blog post would be marked up using [`article`](#432-the-article-element), a chapter using [`section`](#433-the-section-element), a page's navigation aids using [`nav`](#434-the-nav-element), and a group of form controls using [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element).
> 
> On the other hand, [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) elements can be useful for stylistic purposes or to wrap multiple paragraphs within a section that are all to be annotated in a similar way. In the following example, we see [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) elements used as a way to set the language of two paragraphs at once, instead of setting the language on the two paragraph elements separately:
> 
> ```html
> <article lang="en-US">
>  <h1>My use of language and my cats</h1>
>  <p>My cat's behavior hasn't changed much since her absence, except
>  that she plays her new physique to the neighbors regularly, in an
>  attempt to get pets.</p>
>  <div lang="en-GB">
>   <p>My other cat, coloured black and white, is a sweetie. He followed
>   us to the pool today, walking down the pavement with us. Yesterday
>   he apparently visited our neighbours. I wonder if he recognises that
>   their flat is a mirror image of ours.</p>
>   <p>Hm, I just noticed that in the last paragraph I used British
>   English. But I'm supposed to write in American English. So I
>   shouldn't say "pavement" or "flat" or "colour"...</p>
>  </div>
>  <p>I should say "sidewalk" and "apartment" and "color"!</p>
> </article>
> ```

### 4.5 Text-level semantics

#### 4.5.1 The `a` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

If the element has an [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute: [Interactive content](#32527-interactive-content).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Transparent](#3253-transparent-content-models), but there must be no [interactive content](#32527-interactive-content) descendant, [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element descendant, or descendant with the [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attribute specified.

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) — Address of the [hyperlink](#461-introduction)

[`target`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) — [Navigable](#731-navigables) for [hyperlink](#461-introduction) [navigation](#7422-beginning-navigation)

[`download`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) — Whether to download the resource instead of navigating to it, and its filename if so

[`ping`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) — [URLs](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) to ping

[`rel`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) — Relationship between the location in the document containing the [hyperlink](#461-introduction) and the destination resource

[`hreflang`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) — Language of the linked resource

[`type`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) — Hint for the type of the referenced resource

[`referrerpolicy`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) — [Referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy) for [fetches](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) initiated by the element

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

If the element has an [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute: [for authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-a); [for implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-a).

Otherwise: [for authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-a-no-href); [for implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-a-no-href).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants) with attributes [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements), [`hreflang`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements), and [`type`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements), and [navigating URL attributes](#865-sanitization-constants) [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLAnchorElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString download;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute USVString ping;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString rel;
  [SameObject, PutForwards=value, Reflect="rel"] readonly attribute DOMTokenList relList;

  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString text;

  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString referrerPolicy;

  // also has obsolete members
};
HTMLAnchorElement includes HyperlinkElementUtils;
HTMLAnchorElement includes HTMLHyperlinkElementUtils;
```

If the [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element has an [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute, then it [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a [hyperlink](#461-introduction) (a hypertext anchor) labeled by its contents.

If the [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element has no [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute, then the element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a placeholder for where a link might otherwise have been placed, if it had been relevant, consisting of just the element's contents.

The [`target`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements), [`download`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements), [`ping`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements), [`rel`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements), [`hreflang`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements), [`type`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements), and [`referrerpolicy`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attributes must be omitted if the [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute is not present.

If the [`itemprop`](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute is specified on an [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element, then the [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute must also be specified.

> [!example]
> If a site uses a consistent navigation toolbar on every page, then the link that would normally link to the page itself could be marked up using an [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element:
> 
> ```html
> <nav>
>  <ul>
>   <li> <a href="/">Home</a> </li>
>   <li> <a href="/news">News</a> </li>
>   <li> <a>Examples</a> </li>
>   <li> <a href="/legal">Legal</a> </li>
>  </ul>
> </nav>
> ```

The [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements), [`target`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements), [`download`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements), [`ping`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements), and [`referrerpolicy`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attributes affect what happens when users [follow hyperlinks](#465-following-hyperlinks) or [download hyperlinks](#466-downloading-resources) created using the [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element. The [`rel`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements), [`hreflang`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements), and [`type`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) attributes may be used to indicate to the user the likely nature of the target resource before the user follows the link.

`a.text`

Same as [`textContent`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).

The IDL attribute `referrerPolicy` must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`referrerpolicy`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

The `text` attribute's getter must return this element's [descendant text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text).

The [`text`](#451-the-a-element) attribute's setter must [string replace all](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) with the given value within this element.

> [!example]
> The [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element can be wrapped around entire paragraphs, lists, tables, and so forth, even entire sections, so long as there is no interactive content within (e.g., buttons or other links). This example shows how this can be used to make an entire advertising block into a link:
> 
> ```html
> <aside class="advertising">
>  <h1>Advertising</h1>
>  <a href="https://ad.example.com/?adid=1929&amp;pubid=1422">
>   <section>
>    <h1>Mellblomatic 9000!</h1>
>    <p>Turn all your widgets into mellbloms!</p>
>    <p>Only $9.99 plus shipping and handling.</p>
>   </section>
>  </a>
>  <a href="https://ad.example.com/?adid=375&amp;pubid=1422">
>   <section>
>    <h1>The Mellblom Browser</h1>
>    <p>Web browsing at the speed of light.</p>
>    <p>No other browser goes faster!</p>
>   </section>
>  </a>
> </aside>
> ```

> [!example]
> The following example shows how a bit of script can be used to effectively make an entire row in a job listing table a hyperlink:
> 
> ```html
> <table>
>  <tr>
>   <th>Position
>   <th>Team
>   <th>Location
>  <tr>
>   <td><a href="/jobs/manager">Manager</a>
>   <td>Remotees
>   <td>Remote
>  <tr>
>   <td><a href="/jobs/director">Director</a>
>   <td>Remotees
>   <td>Remote
>  <tr>
>   <td><a href="/jobs/astronaut">Astronaut</a>
>   <td>Architecture
>   <td>Remote
> </table>
> <script>
> document.querySelector("table").onclick = ({ target }) => {
>   if (target.parentElement.localName === "tr") {
>     const link = target.parentElement.querySelector("a");
>     if (link) {
>       link.click();
>     }
>   }
> }
> </script>
> ```

#### 4.5.2 The `em` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-em).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-em).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom).

The [`em`](#452-the-em-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) stress emphasis of its contents.

The level of stress that a particular piece of content has is given by its number of ancestor [`em`](#452-the-em-element) elements.

The placement of stress emphasis changes the meaning of the sentence. The element thus forms an integral part of the content. The precise way in which stress is used in this way depends on the language.

> [!example]
> These examples show how changing the stress emphasis changes the meaning. First, a general statement of fact, with no stress:
> 
> ```html
> <p>Cats are cute animals.</p>
> ```
> 
> By emphasizing the first word, the statement implies that the kind of animal under discussion is in question (maybe someone is asserting that dogs are cute):
> 
> ```html
> <p><em>Cats</em> are cute animals.</p>
> ```
> 
> Moving the stress to the verb, one highlights that the truth of the entire sentence is in question (maybe someone is saying cats are not cute):
> 
> ```html
> <p>Cats <em>are</em> cute animals.</p>
> ```
> 
> By moving it to the adjective, the exact nature of the cats is reasserted (maybe someone suggested cats were *mean* animals):
> 
> ```html
> <p>Cats are <em>cute</em> animals.</p>
> ```
> 
> Similarly, if someone asserted that cats were vegetables, someone correcting this might emphasize the last word:
> 
> ```html
> <p>Cats are cute <em>animals</em>.</p>
> ```
> 
> By emphasizing the entire sentence, it becomes clear that the speaker is fighting hard to get the point across. This kind of stress emphasis also typically affects the punctuation, hence the exclamation mark here.
> 
> ```html
> <p><em>Cats are cute animals!</em></p>
> ```
> 
> Anger mixed with emphasizing the cuteness could lead to markup such as:
> 
> ```html
> <p><em>Cats are <em>cute</em> animals!</em></p>
> ```

> [!note]
> The [`em`](#452-the-em-element) element isn't a generic "italics" element. Sometimes, text is intended to stand out from the rest of the paragraph, as if it was in a different mood or voice. For this, the [`i`](#4520-the-i-element) element is more appropriate.
> 
> The [`em`](#452-the-em-element) element also isn't intended to convey importance; for that purpose, the [`strong`](#453-the-strong-element) element is more appropriate.

#### 4.5.3 The `strong` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-strong).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-strong).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom).

The [`strong`](#453-the-strong-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) strong importance, seriousness, or urgency for its contents.

**Importance**: the [`strong`](#453-the-strong-element) element can be used in a heading, caption, or paragraph to distinguish the part that really matters from other parts that might be more detailed, more jovial, or merely boilerplate. (This is distinct from marking up subheadings, for which the [`hgroup`](#437-the-hgroup-element) element is appropriate.)

> [!example]
> For example, the first word of the previous paragraph is marked up with [`strong`](#453-the-strong-element) to distinguish it from the more detailed text in the rest of the paragraph.

**Seriousness**: the [`strong`](#453-the-strong-element) element can be used to mark up a warning or caution notice.

**Urgency**: the [`strong`](#453-the-strong-element) element can be used to denote contents that the user needs to see sooner than other parts of the document.

The relative level of importance of a piece of content is given by its number of ancestor [`strong`](#453-the-strong-element) elements; each [`strong`](#453-the-strong-element) element increases the importance of its contents.

Changing the importance of a piece of text with the [`strong`](#453-the-strong-element) element does not change the meaning of the sentence.

> [!example]
> Here, the word "chapter" and the actual chapter number are mere boilerplate, and the actual name of the chapter is marked up with [`strong`](#453-the-strong-element):
> 
> ```html
> <h1>Chapter 1: <strong>The Praxis</strong></h1>
> ```
> 
> In the following example, the name of the diagram in the caption is marked up with [`strong`](#453-the-strong-element), to distinguish it from boilerplate text (before) and the description (after):
> 
> ```html
> <figcaption>Figure 1. <strong>Ant colony dynamics</strong>. The ants in this colony are
> affected by the heat source (upper left) and the food source (lower right).</figcaption>
> ```
> 
> In this example, the heading is really "Flowers, Bees, and Honey", but the author has added a light-hearted addition to the heading. The [`strong`](#453-the-strong-element) element is thus used to mark up the first part to distinguish it from the latter part.
> 
> ```html
> <h1><strong>Flowers, Bees, and Honey</strong> and other things I don't understand</h1>
> ```

> [!example]
> Here is an example of a warning notice in a game, with the various parts marked up according to how important they are:
> 
> ```html
> <p><strong>Warning.</strong> This dungeon is dangerous.
> <strong>Avoid the ducks.</strong> Take any gold you find.
> <strong><strong>Do not take any of the diamonds</strong>,
> they are explosive and <strong>will destroy anything within
> ten meters.</strong></strong> You have been warned.</p>
> ```

> [!example]
> In this example, the [`strong`](#453-the-strong-element) element is used to denote the part of the text that the user is intended to read first.
> 
> ```html
> <p>Welcome to Remy, the reminder system.</p>
> <p>Your tasks for today:</p>
> <ul>
>  <li><p><strong>Turn off the oven.</strong></p></li>
>  <li><p>Put out the trash.</p></li>
>  <li><p>Do the laundry.</p></li>
> </ul>
> ```

#### 4.5.4 The `small` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-small).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-small).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom).

The [`small`](#454-the-small-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) side comments such as small print.

> [!note]
> Small print typically features disclaimers, caveats, legal restrictions, or copyrights. Small print is also sometimes used for attribution, or for satisfying licensing requirements.

> [!note]
> The [`small`](#454-the-small-element) element does not "de-emphasize" or lower the importance of text emphasized by the [`em`](#452-the-em-element) element or marked as important with the [`strong`](#453-the-strong-element) element. To mark text as not emphasized or important, simply do not mark it up with the [`em`](#452-the-em-element) or [`strong`](#453-the-strong-element) elements respectively.

The [`small`](#454-the-small-element) element should not be used for extended spans of text, such as multiple paragraphs, lists, or sections of text. It is only intended for short runs of text. The text of a page listing terms of use, for instance, would not be a suitable candidate for the [`small`](#454-the-small-element) element: in such a case, the text is not a side comment, it is the main content of the page.

The [`small`](#454-the-small-element) element must not be used for subheadings; for that purpose, use the [`hgroup`](#437-the-hgroup-element) element.

> [!example]
> In this example, the [`small`](#454-the-small-element) element is used to indicate that value-added tax is not included in a price of a hotel room:
> 
> ```html
> <dl>
>  <dt>Single room
>  <dd>199 € <small>breakfast included, VAT not included</small>
>  <dt>Double room
>  <dd>239 € <small>breakfast included, VAT not included</small>
> </dl>
> ```

> [!example]
> In this second example, the [`small`](#454-the-small-element) element is used for a side comment in an article.
> 
> ```html
> <p>Example Corp today announced record profits for the
> second quarter <small>(Full Disclosure: Foo News is a subsidiary of
> Example Corp)</small>, leading to speculation about a third quarter
> merger with Demo Group.</p>
> ```
> 
> This is distinct from a sidebar, which might be multiple paragraphs long and is removed from the main flow of text. In the following example, we see a sidebar from the same article. This sidebar also has small print, indicating the source of the information in the sidebar.
> 
> ```html
> <aside>
>  <h1>Example Corp</h1>
>  <p>This company mostly creates small software and Web
>  sites.</p>
>  <p>The Example Corp company mission is "To provide entertainment
>  and news on a sample basis".</p>
>  <p><small>Information obtained from <a
>  href="https://example.com/about.html">example.com</a> home
>  page.</small></p>
> </aside>
> ```

> [!example]
> In this last example, the [`small`](#454-the-small-element) element is marked as being *important* small print.
> 
> ```html
> <p><strong><small>Continued use of this service will result in a kiss.</small></strong></p>
> ```

#### 4.5.5 The `s` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-s).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-s).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom).

The [`s`](#455-the-s-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) contents that are no longer accurate or no longer relevant.

> [!note]
> The [`s`](#455-the-s-element) element is not appropriate when indicating document edits; to mark a span of text as having been removed from a document, use the [`del`](#472-the-del-element) element.

> [!example]
> In this example a recommended retail price has been marked as no longer relevant as the product in question has a new sale price.
> 
> ```html
> <p>Buy our Iced Tea and Lemonade!</p>
> <p><s>Recommended retail price: $3.99 per bottle</s></p>
> <p><strong>Now selling for just $2.99 a bottle!</strong></p>
> ```

#### 4.5.6 The `cite` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-cite).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-cite).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom).

The [`cite`](#456-the-cite-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the title of a work (e.g. a book, a paper, an essay, a poem, a score, a song, a script, a film, a TV show, a game, a sculpture, a painting, a theatre production, a play, an opera, a musical, an exhibition, a legal case report, a computer program, etc.). This can be a work that is being quoted or [referenced](#322-elements-in-the-dom) in detail (i.e., a citation), or it can just be a work that is mentioned in passing.

A person's name is not the title of a work — even if people call that person a piece of work — and the element must therefore not be used to mark up people's names. (In some cases, the [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) element might be appropriate for names; e.g. in a gossip article where the names of famous people are keywords rendered with a different style to draw attention to them. In other cases, if an element is *really* needed, the [`span`](#4526-the-span-element) element can be used.)

> [!example]
> This next example shows a typical use of the [`cite`](#456-the-cite-element) element:
> 
> ```html
> <p>My favorite book is <cite>The Reality Dysfunction</cite> by
> Peter F. Hamilton. My favorite comic is <cite>Pearls Before
> Swine</cite> by Stephan Pastis. My favorite track is <cite>Jive
> Samba</cite> by the Cannonball Adderley Sextet.</p>
> ```

> [!example]
> This is correct usage:
> 
> ```html
> <p>According to the Wikipedia article <cite>HTML</cite>, as it
> stood in mid-February 2008, leaving attribute values unquoted is
> unsafe. This is obviously an over-simplification.</p>
> ```
> 
> The following, however, is incorrect usage, as the [`cite`](#456-the-cite-element) element here is containing far more than the title of the work:
> 
> ```html
> <!-- do not copy this example, it is an example of bad usage! -->
> <p>According to <cite>the Wikipedia article on HTML</cite>, as it
> stood in mid-February 2008, leaving attribute values unquoted is
> unsafe. This is obviously an over-simplification.</p>
> ```

> [!example]
> The [`cite`](#456-the-cite-element) element is a key part of any citation in a bibliography, but it is only used to mark the title:
> 
> ```html
> <p><cite>Universal Declaration of Human Rights</cite>, United Nations,
> December 1948. Adopted by General Assembly resolution 217 A (III).</p>
> ```

> [!note]
> A *citation* is not a *quote* (for which the [`q`](#457-the-q-element) element is appropriate).

> [!example]
> This is incorrect usage, because [`cite`](#456-the-cite-element) is not for quotes:
> 
> ```html
> <p><cite>This is wrong!</cite>, said Ian.</p>
> ```
> 
> This is also incorrect usage, because a person is not a work:
> 
> ```html
> <p><q>This is still wrong!</q>, said <cite>Ian</cite>.</p>
> ```
> 
> The correct usage does not use a [`cite`](#456-the-cite-element) element:
> 
> ```html
> <p><q>This is correct</q>, said Ian.</p>
> ```
> 
> As mentioned above, the [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) element might be relevant for marking names as being keywords in certain kinds of documents:
> 
> ```html
> <p>And then <b>Ian</b> said <q>this might be right, in a
> gossip column, maybe!</q>.</p>
> ```

> [!note]
> Where the title of a work is conventionally set off with punctuation — for example, the quotation marks used around article titles in English, or the corner brackets (『』) used around book titles in Japanese — that punctuation is not part of the title, and belongs outside the [`cite`](#456-the-cite-element) element.

> [!example]
> This is correct usage:
> 
> ```html
> <p>My review of 『<cite lang="ja">阪急電車</cite>』 was titled “<cite>A cute series of short stories</cite>”.</p>
> ```

#### 4.5.7 The `q` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`cite`](#457-the-q-element) — Link to the source of the quotation or more information about the edit

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-q).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-q).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

Uses [`HTMLQuoteElement`](#444-the-blockquote-element).

The [`q`](#457-the-q-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) some [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) quoted from another source.

Quotation punctuation (such as quotation marks) that is quoting the contents of the element must not appear immediately before, after, or inside [`q`](#457-the-q-element) elements; they will be inserted into the rendering by the user agent.

Content inside a [`q`](#457-the-q-element) element must be quoted from another source, whose address, if it has one, may be cited in the `cite` attribute. The source may be fictional, as when quoting characters in a novel or screenplay.

If the [`cite`](#457-the-q-element) attribute is present, it must be a [valid URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#241-terminology). To obtain the corresponding citation link, the value of the attribute must be [parsed](#242-parsing-urls) relative to the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node). User agents may allow users to follow such citation links, but they are primarily intended for private use (e.g., by server-side scripts collecting statistics about a site's use of quotations), not for readers.

The [`q`](#457-the-q-element) element must not be used in place of quotation marks that do not represent quotes; for example, it is inappropriate to use the [`q`](#457-the-q-element) element for marking up sarcastic statements.

The use of [`q`](#457-the-q-element) elements to mark up quotations is entirely optional; using explicit quotation punctuation without [`q`](#457-the-q-element) elements is just as correct.

> [!example]
> Here is a simple example of the use of the [`q`](#457-the-q-element) element:
> 
> ```html
> <p>The man said <q>Things that are impossible just take
> longer</q>. I disagreed with him.</p>
> ```

> [!example]
> Here is an example with both an explicit citation link in the [`q`](#457-the-q-element) element, and an explicit citation outside:
> 
> ```html
> <p>The W3C page <cite>About W3C</cite> says the W3C's
> mission is <q cite="https://www.w3.org/Consortium/">To lead the
> World Wide Web to its full potential by developing protocols and
> guidelines that ensure long-term growth for the Web</q>. I
> disagree with this mission.</p>
> ```

> [!example]
> In the following example, the quotation itself contains a quotation:
> 
> ```html
> <p>In <cite>Example One</cite>, he writes <q>The man
> said <q>Things that are impossible just take longer</q>. I
> disagreed with him</q>. Well, I disagree even more!</p>
> ```

> [!example]
> In the following example, quotation marks are used instead of the [`q`](#457-the-q-element) element:
> 
> ```html
> <p>His best argument was ❝I disagree❞, which
> I thought was laughable.</p>
> ```

> [!example]
> In the following example, there is no quote — the quotation marks are used to name a word. Use of the [`q`](#457-the-q-element) element in this case would be inappropriate.
> 
> ```html
> <p>The word "ineffable" could have been used to describe the disaster
> resulting from the campaign's mismanagement.</p>
> ```

#### 4.5.8 The `dfn` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content), but there must be no [`dfn`](#458-the-dfn-element) element descendants.

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

Also, the [`title`](#458-the-dfn-element) attribute [has special semantics](#458-the-dfn-element) on this element: Full term or expansion of abbreviation

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-dfn).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-dfn).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom).
