The [`bdo`](#4525-the-bdo-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) explicit text directionality formatting control for its children. It allows authors to override the Unicode bidirectional algorithm by explicitly specifying a direction override. [\[BIDI\]](#references)

Authors must specify the [`dir`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) attribute on this element, with the value [`ltr`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) to specify a left-to-right override and with the value [`rtl`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) to specify a right-to-left override. The [`auto`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) value must not be specified.

> [!note]
> This element [has rendering requirements involving the bidirectional algorithm](#3282-user-agent-conformance-criteria).

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-span).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLSpanElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();
};
```

The [`span`](#4526-the-span-element) element doesn't mean anything on its own, but can be useful when used together with the [global attributes](#326-global-attributes), e.g. [`class`](#326-global-attributes), [`lang`](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes), or [`dir`](#3264-the-dir-attribute). It [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) its children.

> [!example]
> In this example, a code fragment is marked up using [`span`](#4526-the-span-element) elements and [`class`](#326-global-attributes) attributes so that its keywords and identifiers can be color-coded from CSS:
> 
> ```html
> <pre><code class="lang-c"><span class="keyword">for</span> (<span class="ident">j</span> = 0; <span class="ident">j</span> &lt; 256; <span class="ident">j</span>++) {
>   <span class="ident">i_t3</span> = (<span class="ident">i_t3</span> & 0x1ffff) | (<span class="ident">j</span> &lt;&lt; 17);
>   <span class="ident">i_t6</span> = (((((((<span class="ident">i_t3</span> >> 3) ^ <span class="ident">i_t3</span>) >> 1) ^ <span class="ident">i_t3</span>) >> 8) ^ <span class="ident">i_t3</span>) >> 5) & 0xff;
>   <span class="keyword">if</span> (<span class="ident">i_t6</span> == <span class="ident">i_t1</span>)
>     <span class="keyword">break</span>;
> }</code></pre>
> ```

#### 4.5.27 The `br` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Nothing](#3251-the-nothing-content-model).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

No [end tag](#13122-end-tags).

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-br).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-br).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLBRElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`br`](#4527-the-br-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a line break.

> [!note]
> While line breaks are usually represented in visual media by physically moving subsequent text to a new line, a style sheet or user agent would be equally justified in causing line breaks to be rendered in a different manner, for instance as green dots, or as extra spacing.

[`br`](#4527-the-br-element) elements must be used only for line breaks that are actually part of the content, as in poems or addresses.

> [!example]
> The following example is correct usage of the [`br`](#4527-the-br-element) element:
> 
> ```html
> <p>P. Sherman<br>
> 42 Wallaby Way<br>
> Sydney</p>
> ```

[`br`](#4527-the-br-element) elements must not be used for separating thematic groups in a paragraph.

> [!example]
> The following examples are non-conforming, as they abuse the [`br`](#4527-the-br-element) element:
> 
> ```html
> <p><a ...>34 comments.</a><br>
> <a ...>Add a comment.</a></p>
> ```
> 
> ```html
> <p><label>Name: <input name="name"></label><br>
> <label>Address: <input name="address"></label></p>
> ```
> 
> Here are alternatives to the above, which are correct:
> 
> ```html
> <p><a ...>34 comments.</a></p>
> <p><a ...>Add a comment.</a></p>
> ```
> 
> ```html
> <p><label>Name: <input name="name"></label></p>
> <p><label>Address: <input name="address"></label></p>
> ```

If a [paragraph](#3254-paragraphs) consists of nothing but a single [`br`](#4527-the-br-element) element, it represents a placeholder blank line (e.g. as in a template). Such blank lines must not be used for presentation purposes.

Any content inside [`br`](#4527-the-br-element) elements must not be considered part of the surrounding text.

> [!note]
> This element [has rendering requirements involving the bidirectional algorithm](#3282-user-agent-conformance-criteria).

#### 4.5.28 The `wbr` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Nothing](#3251-the-nothing-content-model).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

No [end tag](#13122-end-tags).

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-wbr).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-wbr).

The [`wbr`](#4528-the-wbr-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a line break opportunity.

> [!example]
> In the following example, someone is quoted as saying something which, for effect, is written as one long word. However, to ensure that the text can be wrapped in a readable fashion, the individual words in the quote are separated using a [`wbr`](#4528-the-wbr-element) element.
> 
> ```html
> <p>So then she pointed at the tiger and screamed
> "there<wbr>is<wbr>no<wbr>way<wbr>you<wbr>are<wbr>ever<wbr>going<wbr>to<wbr>catch<wbr>me"!</p>
> ```

Any content inside [`wbr`](#4528-the-wbr-element) elements must not be considered part of the surrounding text.

```javascript
var wbr = document.createElement("wbr");
wbr.textContent = "This is wrong";
document.body.appendChild(wbr);
```

> [!note]
> This element [has rendering requirements involving the bidirectional algorithm](#3282-user-agent-conformance-criteria).

### 4.6 Links

#### 4.6.1 Introduction

Links are a conceptual construct, created by [`a`](#451-the-a-element), [`area`](#4813-the-area-element), [`form`](#4103-the-form-element), and [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements, that [represent](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a connection between two resources, one of which is the current [`Document`](#311-the-document-object). There are three kinds of links in HTML:

Links to external resources

These are links to resources that are to be used to augment the current document, generally automatically processed by the user agent. All [external resource links](#461-introduction) have a [fetch and process the linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) algorithm which describes how the resource is obtained.

Hyperlinks

These are links to other resources that are generally exposed to the user by the user agent so that the user can cause the user agent to [navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation) to those resources, e.g. to visit them in a browser or download them.

Internal resource links

These are links to resources within the current document, used to give those resources special meaning or behavior.

For [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements with an [`href`](#424-the-link-element) attribute and a [`rel`](#424-the-link-element) attribute, links must be created for the keywords of the [`rel`](#424-the-link-element) attribute, as defined for those keywords in the [link types](#468-link-types) section.

Similarly, for [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements with an [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute and a [`rel`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute, links must be created for the keywords of the [`rel`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute as defined for those keywords in the [link types](#468-link-types) section. Unlike [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements, however, [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements with an [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute that either do not have a [`rel`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute, or whose [`rel`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute has no keywords that are defined as specifying [hyperlinks](#461-introduction), must also create a [hyperlink](#461-introduction). This implied hyperlink has no special meaning (it has no [link type](#468-link-types)) beyond linking the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) to the resource given by the element's [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute.

Similarly, for [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements with a [`rel`](#4103-the-form-element) attribute, links must be created for the keywords of the [`rel`](#4103-the-form-element) attribute as defined for those keywords in the [link types](#468-link-types) section. [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements that do not have a [`rel`](#4103-the-form-element) attribute, or whose [`rel`](#4103-the-form-element) attribute has no keywords that are defined as specifying [hyperlinks](#461-introduction), must also create a [hyperlink](#461-introduction).

A [hyperlink](#461-introduction) can have one or more hyperlink annotations that modify the processing semantics of that hyperlink.

#### 4.6.2 Links created by [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements

The `href` attribute on [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements must have a value that is a [valid URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#241-terminology).

> [!note]
> The [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute on [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements is not required; when those elements do not have [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attributes they do not create hyperlinks.

The `target` attribute, if present, must be a [valid navigable target name or keyword](#7317-navigable-target-names). It gives the name of the [navigable](#731-navigables) that will be used. User agents use this name when [following hyperlinks](#465-following-hyperlinks).

The `download` attribute, if present, indicates that the author intends the hyperlink to be used for [downloading a resource](#466-downloading-resources). The attribute may have a value; the value, if any, specifies the default filename that the author recommends for use in labeling the resource in a local file system. There are no restrictions on allowed values, but authors are cautioned that most file systems have limitations with regard to what punctuation is supported in filenames, and user agents are likely to adjust filenames accordingly.

The `ping` attribute, if present, gives the URLs of the resources that are interested in being notified if the user follows the hyperlink. The value must be a [set of space-separated tokens](#237-space-separated-tokens), each of which must be a [valid non-empty URL](#241-terminology) whose [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) is an [HTTP(S) scheme](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#http-scheme). The value is used by the user agent for [hyperlink auditing](#467-hyperlink-auditing).

The `rel` attribute on [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements controls what kinds of links the elements create. The attribute's value must be an [unordered set of unique space-separated tokens](#237-space-separated-tokens). The [allowed keywords and their meanings](#468-link-types) are defined below.

[`rel`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements)'s [supported tokens](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#71-interface-domtokenlist) are the keywords defined in [HTML link types](#468-link-types) which are allowed on [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements, impact the processing model, and are supported by the user agent. The possible [supported tokens](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#71-interface-domtokenlist) are [`noreferrer`](#46815-link-type-noreferrer), [`noopener`](#46814-link-type-noopener), and [`opener`](#46816-link-type-opener). [`rel`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements)'s [supported tokens](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#71-interface-domtokenlist) must only include the tokens from this list that the user agent implements the processing model for.

The [`rel`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute has no default value. If the attribute is omitted or if none of the values in the attribute are recognized by the user agent, then the document has no particular relationship with the destination resource other than there being a hyperlink between the two.

The `referrerpolicy` attribute is a [referrer policy attribute](#255-referrer-policy-attributes). Its purpose is to set the [referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy) used when [following hyperlinks](#465-following-hyperlinks). [\[REFERRERPOLICY\]](#references)

---

When an [`a`](#451-the-a-element) or [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element's [activation behavior](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) is invoked, the user agent may allow the user to indicate a preference regarding whether the hyperlink is to be used for [navigation](#7422-beginning-navigation) or whether the resource it specifies is to be downloaded.

In the absence of a user preference, the default should be navigation if the element has no [`download`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute, and should be to download the specified resource if it does.

The [activation behavior](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) of an [`a`](#451-the-a-element) or [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element element given an event event is:
1. If element has no [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute, then return.
2. Let hyperlinkSuffix be null.
3. If element is an [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element, and event's [target](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) is an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) with an [`ismap`](#483-the-img-element) attribute specified:
   1. Let x and y be 0.
   2. If event's [`isTrusted`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute is initialized to true, then set x to the distance in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) from the left edge of the image to the location of the click, and set y to the distance in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) from the top edge of the image to the location of the click.
   3. If x is negative, set x to 0.
   4. If y is negative, set y to 0.
   5. Set hyperlinkSuffix to the concatenation of U+003F (?), the value of x expressed as a base-ten integer using [ASCII digits](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), U+002C (,), and the value of y expressed as a base-ten integer using [ASCII digits](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).
4. Let userInvolvement be event's [user navigation involvement](#7421-supporting-concepts).
5. If the user has expressed a preference to download the hyperlink, then set userInvolvement to "[`browser UI`](#7421-supporting-concepts)".

   > [!note]
   > That is, if the user has expressed a specific preference for downloading, this no longer counts as merely "[`activation`](#7421-supporting-concepts)".

6. If element has a [`download`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute, or if the user has expressed a preference to download the hyperlink, then [download the hyperlink](#466-downloading-resources) created by element with *[hyperlinkSuffix](#466-downloading-resources)* set to hyperlinkSuffix and *[userInvolvement](#466-downloading-resources)* set to userInvolvement.
7. Otherwise, [follow the hyperlink](#465-following-hyperlinks) created by element with *[hyperlinkSuffix](#465-following-hyperlinks)* set to hyperlinkSuffix and *[userInvolvement](#465-following-hyperlinks)* set to userInvolvement.

#### 4.6.3 API for hyperlink elements

```webidl
interface mixin HyperlinkElementUtils {
  readonly attribute USVString origin;
  [CEReactions] attribute USVString protocol;
  [CEReactions] attribute USVString username;
  [CEReactions] attribute USVString password;
  [CEReactions] attribute USVString host;
  [CEReactions] attribute USVString hostname;
  [CEReactions] attribute USVString port;
  [CEReactions] attribute USVString pathname;
  [CEReactions] attribute USVString search;
  [CEReactions] attribute USVString hash;

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString hreflang;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString type;
};
```

`hyperlink.origin`

Returns the hyperlink's URL's origin.

`hyperlink.protocol`

Returns the hyperlink's URL's scheme.

Can be set, to change the URL's scheme.

`hyperlink.username`

Returns the hyperlink's URL's username.

Can be set, to change the URL's username.

`hyperlink.password`

Returns the hyperlink's URL's password.

Can be set, to change the URL's password.

`hyperlink.host`

Returns the hyperlink's URL's host and port (if different from the default port for the scheme).

Can be set, to change the URL's host and port.

`hyperlink.hostname`

Returns the hyperlink's URL's host.

Can be set, to change the URL's host.

`hyperlink.port`

Returns the hyperlink's URL's port.

Can be set, to change the URL's port.

`hyperlink.pathname`

Returns the hyperlink's URL's path.

Can be set, to change the URL's path.

`hyperlink.search`

Returns the hyperlink's URL's query (includes leading "`?`" if non-empty).

Can be set, to change the URL's query (ignores leading "`?`").

`hyperlink.hash`

Returns the hyperlink's URL's fragment (includes leading "`#`" if non-empty).

Can be set, to change the URL's fragment (ignores leading "`#`").

An element implementing the [`HyperlinkElementUtils`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) mixin is a hyperlink element.

A [hyperlink element](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) has an associated url (null or a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url)). It is initially null.

A [hyperlink element](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) has the following [extract an origin](#7113-the-origin-interface) steps:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) is null, then return null.
2. Return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements)'s [origin](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-origin).

A [hyperlink element](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) must have an associated set the url algorithm.

When [hyperlink elements](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) are created, the user agent must [set the url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).

A [hyperlink element](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) has an associated reinitialize url algorithm, which runs these steps:
1. If the element's [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) is non-null, its [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) is "`blob`", and it has an [opaque path](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-opaque-path), then terminate these steps.
2. [Set the url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).

A [hyperlink element](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) must have an associated update `href` algorithm.

The `hreflang` attribute on [hyperlink elements](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) that create [hyperlinks](#461-introduction), if present, gives the language of the linked resource. It is purely advisory. The value must be a valid BCP 47 language tag. [\[BCP47\]](#references) User agents must not consider this attribute authoritative — upon fetching the resource, user agents must use only language information associated with the resource to determine its language, not metadata included in the link to the resource.

The `type` attribute on [hyperlink elements](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements), if present, gives the [MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type) of the linked resource. It is purely advisory. The value must be a [valid MIME type string](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-mime-type). User agents must not consider the [`type`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) attribute authoritative — upon fetching the resource, user agents must not use metadata included in the link to the resource to determine its type.

---

The `origin` getter steps are:
1. [Reinitialize url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
2. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) is null, return the empty string.
3. Return the [serialization](#711-origins) of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements)'s [origin](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-origin).

The `protocol` getter steps are:
1. [Reinitialize url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
2. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) is null, return "`:`".
3. Return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements)'s [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme), followed by "`:`".

The [`protocol`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) setter steps are:
1. [Reinitialize url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
2. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) is null, then return.
3. [Basic URL parse](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-basic-url-parser) the given value, followed by "`:`", with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) as [*url*](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#basic-url-parser-url) and [scheme start state](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#scheme-start-state) as [*state override*](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#basic-url-parser-state-override).

   > [!note]
   > Because the URL parser ignores multiple consecutive colons, providing a value of "`https:`" (or even "`https::::`") is the same as providing a value of "`https`".

4. [Update `href`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).

The `username` getter steps are:
1. [Reinitialize url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
2. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) is null, return the empty string.
3. Return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements)'s [username](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-username).

The [`username`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) setter steps are:
1. [Reinitialize url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
2. Let url be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
3. If url is null or url [cannot have a username/password/port](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#cannot-have-a-username-password-port), then return.
4. [Set the username](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#set-the-username), given url and the given value.
5. [Update `href`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).

The `password` getter steps are:
1. [Reinitialize url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
2. Let url be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
3. If url is null, then return the empty string.
4. Return url's [password](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-password).

The [`password`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) setter steps are:
1. [Reinitialize url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
2. Let url be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
3. If url is null or url [cannot have a username/password/port](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#cannot-have-a-username-password-port), then return.
4. [Set the password](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#set-the-password), given url and the given value.
5. [Update `href`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).

The `host` getter steps are:
1. [Reinitialize url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
2. Let url be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
3. If url or url's [host](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-host) is null, return the empty string.
4. If url's [port](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-port) is null, return url's [host](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-host), [serialized](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-host-serializer).
5. Return url's [host](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-host), [serialized](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-host-serializer), followed by "`:`" and url's [port](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-port), [serialized](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#serialize-an-integer).

The [`host`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) setter steps are:
1. [Reinitialize url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
2. Let url be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
3. If url is null or url has an [opaque path](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-opaque-path), then return.
4. [Basic URL parse](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-basic-url-parser) the given value, with url as [*url*](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#basic-url-parser-url) and [host state](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#host-state) as [*state override*](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#basic-url-parser-state-override).
5. [Update `href`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).

The `hostname` getter steps are:
1. [Reinitialize url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
2. Let url be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
3. If url or url's [host](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-host) is null, return the empty string.
4. Return url's [host](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-host), [serialized](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-host-serializer).

The [`hostname`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) setter steps are:
1. [Reinitialize url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
2. Let url be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
3. If url is null or url has an [opaque path](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-opaque-path), then return.
4. [Basic URL parse](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-basic-url-parser) the given value, with url as [*url*](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#basic-url-parser-url) and [hostname state](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#hostname-state) as [*state override*](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#basic-url-parser-state-override).
5. [Update `href`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).

The `port` getter steps are:
1. [Reinitialize url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
2. Let url be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
3. If url or url's [port](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-port) is null, return the empty string.
4. Return url's [port](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-port), [serialized](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#serialize-an-integer).

The [`port`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) setter steps are:
1. [Reinitialize url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
2. Let url be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
3. If url is null or url [cannot have a username/password/port](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#cannot-have-a-username-password-port), then return.
4. If the given value is the empty string, then set url's [port](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-port) to null.
5. Otherwise, [basic URL parse](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-basic-url-parser) the given value, with url as [*url*](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#basic-url-parser-url) and [port state](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#port-state) as [*state override*](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#basic-url-parser-state-override).
6. [Update `href`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).

The `pathname` getter steps are:
1. [Reinitialize url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
2. Let url be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
3. If url is null, then return the empty string.
4. Return the result of [URL path serializing](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-path-serializer) url.

The [`pathname`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) setter steps are:
1. [Reinitialize url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
2. Let url be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
3. If url is null or url has an [opaque path](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-opaque-path), then return.
4. Set url's [path](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-path) to the empty list.
5. [Basic URL parse](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-basic-url-parser) the given value, with url as [*url*](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#basic-url-parser-url) and [path start state](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#path-start-state) as [*state override*](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#basic-url-parser-state-override).
6. [Update `href`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).

The `search` getter steps are:
1. [Reinitialize url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
2. Let url be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
3. If url is null, or url's [query](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-query) is either null or the empty string, return the empty string.
4. Return "`?`", followed by url's [query](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-query).

The [`search`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) setter steps are:
1. [Reinitialize url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
2. Let url be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
3. If url is null, terminate these steps.
4. If the given value is the empty string, set url's [query](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-query) to null.
5. Otherwise:
   1. Let input be the given value with a single leading "`?`" removed, if any.
   2. Set url's [query](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-query) to the empty string.
   3. [Basic URL parse](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-basic-url-parser) input, with url as [*url*](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#basic-url-parser-url) and [query state](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#query-state) as [*state override*](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#basic-url-parser-state-override).
6. [Update `href`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).

The `hash` getter steps are:
1. [Reinitialize url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
2. Let url be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
3. If url is null, or url's [fragment](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment) is either null or the empty string, return the empty string.
4. Return "`#`", followed by url's [fragment](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment).

The [`hash`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) setter steps are:
1. [Reinitialize url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
2. Let url be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
3. If url is null, then return.
4. If the given value is the empty string, set url's [fragment](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment) to null.
5. Otherwise:
   1. Let input be the given value with a single leading "`#`" removed, if any.
   2. Set url's [fragment](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment) to the empty string.
   3. [Basic URL parse](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-basic-url-parser) input, with url as [*url*](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#basic-url-parser-url) and [fragment state](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#fragment-state) as [*state override*](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#basic-url-parser-state-override).
6. [Update `href`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).

#### 4.6.4 API for [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements

```webidl
interface mixin HTMLHyperlinkElementUtils {
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] stringifier attribute USVString href;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString target;
};
```

`hyperlink.toString()`

`hyperlink.href`

Returns the hyperlink's URL.

Can be set, to change the URL.

The `href` getter steps are:
1. [Reinitialize url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
2. Let url be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements).
3. If url is null and [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) has no [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) content attribute, return the empty string.
4. Otherwise, if url is null, return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) content attribute's value.
5. Return url, [serialized](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer).

The [HTML element insertion steps](#214-dom-trees) for [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements, given insertedNode, are:
1. If insertedNode is not [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree), then return.
2. [Consider speculative loads](#7613-processing-model) given insertedNode's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).

The [HTML element removing steps](#214-dom-trees) for [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements, given removedNode, isSubtreeRoot, and oldAncestor are:
1. If oldAncestor is not [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree), then return.
2. [Consider speculative loads](#7613-processing-model) given oldAncestor's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).

The [HTML element moving steps](#214-dom-trees) for [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements, given movedNode, are:
1. [Consider speculative loads](#7613-processing-model) given movedNode's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).

The following [attribute change steps](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), given element, localName, oldValue, value, and namespace, are used for all [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements:
1. If namespace is not null, then return.
2. If oldValue equals value, then return.
3. If localName is [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements), then [set the url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) given element.

   > [!note]
   > This is only observable for [`blob:`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#blob-url) URLs as [parsing](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser) them involves a [Blob URL Store](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#BlobURLStore) lookup.

4. If localName is [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements), [`referrerpolicy`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements), or [`rel`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements), then [consider speculative loads](#7613-processing-model) given element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).

To [update `href`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) for an [`HTMLAnchorElement`](#451-the-a-element) or [`HTMLAreaElement`](#4813-the-area-element) element, set the element's [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) content attribute's value to the element's [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements), [serialized](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer).

The [set the url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) algorithm for [`HTMLAnchorElement`](#451-the-a-element) and [`HTMLAreaElement`](#4813-the-area-element) elements is as follows:
1. Set this element's [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) to null.
2. If this element's [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) content attribute is absent, then return.
3. Let url be the result of [encoding-parsing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given this element's [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) content attribute's value, relative to this element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
4. If url is not failure, then set this element's [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) to url.

#### 4.6.5 Following hyperlinks

An element element cannot navigate if any of the following are true:
- element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents); or
- element is not an [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element and is not [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree).

> [!note]
> This is also used by [form submission](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) for the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element. The exception for [`a`](#451-the-a-element) elements is for compatibility with web content.

To get an element's noopener, given an [`a`](#451-the-a-element), [`area`](#4813-the-area-element), or [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element element, a [URL record](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) url, and a string target, perform the following steps. They return a boolean.
1. If element's [link types](#468-link-types) include the [`noopener`](#46814-link-type-noopener) or [`noreferrer`](#46815-link-type-noreferrer) keyword, then return true.
2. If element's [link types](#468-link-types) do not include the [`opener`](#46816-link-type-opener) keyword and target is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for "`_blank`", then return true.
3. If url's [blob URL entry](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-blob-entry) is not null:
   1. Let blobOrigin be url's [blob URL entry](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-blob-entry)'s [environment](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#blob-url-entry-environment)'s [origin](#8132-environment-settings-objects).
   2. Let topLevelOrigin be element's [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant)'s [top-level origin](#8131-environments).
   3. If blobOrigin is not [same site](#7111-sites) with topLevelOrigin, then return true.
4. Return false.

To follow the hyperlink created by an element subject, given an optional hyperlinkSuffix (default null) and an optional userInvolvement (default "[`none`](#7421-supporting-concepts)"):
1. If subject [cannot navigate](#465-following-hyperlinks), then return.
2. Let targetAttributeValue be the empty string.
3. If subject is an [`a`](#451-the-a-element) or [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element, then set targetAttributeValue to the result of [getting an element's target](#423-the-base-element) given subject.
4. Let urlRecord be the result of [encoding-parsing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given subject's [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute value, relative to subject's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
5. If urlRecord is failure, then return.
6. Let noopener be the result of [getting an element's noopener](#465-following-hyperlinks) with subject, urlRecord, and targetAttributeValue.
7. Let targetNavigable be the first return value of applying [the rules for choosing a navigable](#7317-navigable-target-names) given targetAttributeValue, subject's [node navigable](#731-navigables), and noopener.
8. If targetNavigable is null, then return.
9. Let urlString be the result of applying the [URL serializer](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer) to urlRecord.
10. If hyperlinkSuffix is non-null, then append it to urlString.
11. [Navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation) targetNavigable to urlString using subject's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), with *[referrerPolicy](#7422-beginning-navigation)* set to subject's [hyperlink referrer policy](#465-following-hyperlinks), *[userInvolvement](#7422-beginning-navigation)* set to userInvolvement, and *[sourceElement](#7422-beginning-navigation)* set to subject.

    > [!note]
    > Unlike many other types of navigations, following hyperlinks does not have special "[`replace`](#7421-supporting-concepts)" behavior for when documents are not [completely loaded](#758-finishing-the-loading-process). This is true for both user-initiated instances of following hyperlinks, as well as script-triggered ones via, e.g., `aElement.click()`.

The hyperlink referrer policy for an element subject is the value returned by the following steps:
1. If subject's [link types](#468-link-types) includes the [`noreferrer`](#46815-link-type-noreferrer) keyword, then return "`no-referrer`".
2. Return the current state of subject's [`referrerpolicy`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) content attribute.

#### 4.6.6 Downloading resources

In some cases, resources are intended for later use rather than immediate viewing. To indicate that a resource is intended to be downloaded for use later, rather than immediately used, the [`download`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute can be specified on the [`a`](#451-the-a-element) or [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element that creates the [hyperlink](#461-introduction) to that resource.

The attribute can furthermore be given a value, to specify the filename that user agents are to use when storing the resource in a file system. This value can be overridden by the \`[`Content-Disposition`](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc6266.html)\` HTTP header's filename parameters. [\[RFC6266\]](#references)

In cross-origin situations, the [`download`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute has to be combined with the \`[`Content-Disposition`](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc6266.html)\` HTTP header, specifically with the `attachment` disposition type, to avoid the user being warned of possibly nefarious activity. (This is to protect users from being made to download sensitive personal or confidential information without their full understanding.)

---

To download the hyperlink created by an element subject, given an optional hyperlinkSuffix (default null) and an optional userInvolvement (default "[`none`](#7421-supporting-concepts)"):
1. If subject [cannot navigate](#465-following-hyperlinks), then return.
2. If subject's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [active sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing) has the [sandboxed downloads browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing) set, then return.
3. Let urlString be the result of [encoding-parsing-and-serializing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given subject's [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute value, relative to subject's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
4. If urlString is failure, then return.
5. If hyperlinkSuffix is non-null, then append it to urlString.
6. If userInvolvement is not "[`browser UI`](#7421-supporting-concepts)":
   1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): subject has a [`download`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute.
   2. Let navigation be subject's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant)'s [navigation API](#7262-the-navigation-interface).
   3. Let filename be the value of subject's [`download`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute.
   4. Let continue be the result of [firing a download request `navigate` event](#726104-firing-the-event) at navigation with *[destinationURL](#726104-firing-the-event)* set to urlString, *[userInvolvement](#726104-firing-the-event)* set to userInvolvement, *[sourceElement](#726104-firing-the-event)* set to subject, and *[filename](#726104-firing-the-event)* set to filename.
   5. If continue is false, then return.
   6. [Inform the navigation API about aborting navigation](#7268-ongoing-navigation-tracking) given subject's [node navigable](#731-navigables).
7. Optionally, the user agent may return, if it believes doing so would safeguard the user from a potentially hostile download.
8. Let request be a new [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) whose [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url) is urlString, [client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client) is [entry settings object](#81331-entry), [initiator](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-initiator) is "`download`", [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) is the empty string, and whose [use-URL-credentials flag](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-use-url-credentials-flag) is set.
9. [Fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request, with *[processResponse](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#process-response)* set to the following steps given [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response:
   1. [Handle as a download](#466-downloading-resources) response with subject's [node navigable](#731-navigables) and null.

To handle as a download a [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response with a [navigable](#731-navigables) navigable and a [navigation ID](#7421-supporting-concepts) or null navigationId:
1. Let suggestedFilename be the result of [getting the suggested filename](#466-downloading-resources) for response.
2. Let download behavior be the result of [WebDriver BiDi download will begin](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-download-will-begin) with navigable and a new [WebDriver BiDi navigation status](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-navigation-status) whose [id](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-id) is navigationId, [status](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-status) is "[`pending`](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-pending)", [url](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-url) is response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url), [suggestedFilename](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-suggested-filename) is suggestedFilename, and [downloadResponse](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) is response.
3. If download behavior is not null and download behavior's [allowed](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#download-behavior-struct-allowed) is false:
   1. Invoke [WebDriver BiDi download end](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-download-end) with navigable and a new [WebDriver BiDi navigation status](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-navigation-status) whose [id](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-id) is navigationId, [status](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-status) is "[`canceled`](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-canceled)", [url](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-url) is response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url), and [downloadResponse](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) is response.
   2. Return.
4. If download behavior is not null, let destinationFolder be download behavior's [destinationFolder](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#download-behavior-struct-destination-folder).
5. Run these steps [in parallel](#211-parallelism):
   1. Run [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) steps to save response for later use. If destinationFolder is not null, the user agent should save the file to that path. If the user agent needs a filename, the user agent should use the suggestedFilename.
   2. If any of the following are true:
      - the download is canceled by the user;
      - the download is canceled by the user agent;
      - an error occurs (for example, a network error, not enough storage, an unavailable destination folder);

      then:
      1. Invoke [WebDriver BiDi download end](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-download-end) with navigable and a new [WebDriver BiDi navigation status](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-navigation-status) whose [id](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-id) is navigationId, [status](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-status) is "[`canceled`](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-canceled)", [url](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-url) is response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url).
      2. Return.

   3. When the download completes successfully, invoke [WebDriver BiDi download end](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-download-end) with navigable and a new [WebDriver BiDi navigation status](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-navigation-status) whose [id](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-id) is navigationId, [status](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-status) is "[`complete`](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-complete)", [downloadedFilepath](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-downloaded-filepath) is an absolute path of the downloaded file if available, otherwise null, [url](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-url) is response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url), and [downloadResponse](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) is response.

To get the suggested filename for a [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response:

> [!warning]
> This algorithm is intended to mitigate security dangers involved in downloading files from untrusted sites, and user agents are strongly urged to follow it.
1. Let filename be the undefined value.
2. If response has a \`[`Content-Disposition`](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc6266.html)\` header, that header specifies the `attachment` disposition type, and the header includes filename information, then let filename have the value specified by the header, and jump to the step labeled *sanitize* below. [\[RFC6266\]](#references)
3. Let interface origin be the [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) of the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) in which the [download](#466-downloading-resources) or [navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation) action resulting in the download was initiated, if any.
4. Let response origin be the [origin](#711-origins) of the URL of response, unless that URL's [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) component is `data`, in which case let response origin be the same as the interface origin, if any.
5. If there is no interface origin, then let trusted operation be true. Otherwise, let trusted operation be true if response origin is the [same origin](#711-origins) as interface origin, and false otherwise.
6. If trusted operation is true and response has a \`[`Content-Disposition`](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc6266.html)\` header and that header includes filename information, then let filename have the value specified by the header, and jump to the step labeled *sanitize* below. [\[RFC6266\]](#references)
7. If the download was not initiated from a [hyperlink](#461-introduction) created by an [`a`](#451-the-a-element) or [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element, or if the element of the [hyperlink](#461-introduction) from which it was initiated did not have a [`download`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute when the download was initiated, or if there was such an attribute but its value when the download was initiated was the empty string, then jump to the step labeled *no proposed filename*.
8. Let proposed filename have the value of the [`download`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute of the element of the [hyperlink](#461-introduction) that initiated the download at the time the download was initiated.
9. If trusted operation is true, let filename have the value of proposed filename, and jump to the step labeled *sanitize* below.
10. If response has a \`[`Content-Disposition`](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc6266.html)\` header and that header specifies the `attachment` disposition type, let filename have the value of proposed filename, and jump to the step labeled *sanitize* below. [\[RFC6266\]](#references)
11. *No proposed filename*: If trusted operation is true, or if the user indicated a preference for having the response in question downloaded, let filename have a value derived from the [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) of response in an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) manner, and jump to the step labeled *sanitize* below.
12. Let filename be set to the user's preferred filename or to a filename selected by the user agent, and jump to the step labeled *sanitize* below.

    > [!warning]
    > If the algorithm reaches this step, then a download was begun from a different origin than response, and the origin did not mark the file as suitable for downloading, and the download was not initiated by the user. This could be because a [`download`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute was used to trigger the download, or because response is not of a type that the user agent supports.
    > 
    > This could be dangerous, because, for instance, a hostile server could be trying to get a user to unknowingly download private information and then re-upload it to the hostile server, by tricking the user into thinking the data is from the hostile server.
    > 
    > Thus, it is in the user's interests that the user be somehow notified that response comes from quite a different source, and to prevent confusion, any suggested filename from the potentially hostile interface origin should be ignored.

13. *Sanitize*: Optionally, allow the user to influence filename. For example, a user agent could prompt the user for a filename, potentially providing the value of filename as determined above as a default value.
14. Adjust filename to be suitable for the local file system.

    > [!example]
    > For example, this could involve removing characters that are not legal in filenames, or trimming leading and trailing whitespace.

15. If the platform conventions do not in any way use [extensions](#466-downloading-resources) to determine the types of file on the file system, then return filename as the filename.
16. Let claimed type be the type given by response's [Content-Type metadata](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource), if any is known. Let named type be the type given by filename's [extension](#466-downloading-resources), if any is known. For the purposes of this step, a *type* is a mapping of a [MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type) to an [extension](#466-downloading-resources).
17. If named type is consistent with the user's preferences (e.g., because the value of filename was determined by prompting the user), then return filename as the filename.
18. If claimed type and named type are the same type (i.e., the type given by response's [Content-Type metadata](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource) is consistent with the type given by filename's [extension](#466-downloading-resources)), then return filename as the filename.
19. If the claimed type is known, then alter filename to add an [extension](#466-downloading-resources) corresponding to claimed type.

    Otherwise, if named type is known to be potentially dangerous (e.g. it will be treated by the platform conventions as a native executable, shell script, HTML application, or executable-macro-capable document), then optionally alter filename to add a known-safe [extension](#466-downloading-resources) (e.g. "`.txt`").

    > [!note]
    > This last step would make it impossible to download executables, which might not be desirable. As always, implementers are forced to balance security and usability in this matter.

20. Return filename as the filename.

For the purposes of this algorithm, a file extension consists of any part of the filename that platform conventions dictate will be used for identifying the type of the file. For example, many operating systems use the part of the filename following the last dot ("`.`") in the filename to determine the type of the file, and from that the manner in which the file is to be opened or executed.

User agents should ignore any directory or path information provided by the response itself, its [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url), and any [`download`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute, in deciding where to store the resulting file in the user's file system.

#### 4.6.7 Hyperlink auditing

If a [hyperlink](#461-introduction) created by an [`a`](#451-the-a-element) or [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element has a [`ping`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute, and the user follows the hyperlink, and the value of the element's [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute can be [parsed](#242-parsing-urls), relative to the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), without failure, then the user agent must take the [`ping`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute's value, [split that string on ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings), [parse](#242-parsing-urls) each resulting token, relative to the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), and then run these steps for each resulting [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) ping URL, ignoring when parsing returns failure:
1. If ping URL's [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) is not an [HTTP(S) scheme](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#http-scheme), then return.
2. Optionally, return. (For example, the user agent might wish to ignore any or all ping URLs in accordance with the user's expressed preferences.)
3. Let settingsObject be the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant).
4. Let request be a new [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) whose [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url) is ping URL, [method](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-method) is \``POST`\`, [header list](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-header-list) is « (\`[`Content-Type`](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource)\`, \`[`text/ping`](#174-textping)\`) », [body](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-body) is \``PING`\`, [client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client) is settingsObject, [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) is the empty string, [credentials mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode) is "`include`", [referrer](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-referrer) is "`no-referrer`", and whose [use-URL-credentials flag](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-use-url-credentials-flag) is set, and whose [initiator type](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-initiator-type) is "`ping`".
5. Let target URL be the result of [encoding-parsing-and-serializing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given the element's [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute's value, relative to the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), and then:

   If the [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) of the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object containing the hyperlink being audited and ping URL have the [same origin](#711-origins)

   If the origins are different, but the [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) of the [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) of the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) containing the hyperlink being audited is not "`https`"

   request must include a \`[`Ping-From`](#4671-the-ping-from-and-ping-to-headers)\` header with, as its value, the [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) of the document containing the hyperlink, and a \`[`Ping-To`](#4671-the-ping-from-and-ping-to-headers)\` HTTP header with, as its value, the target URL.

   Otherwise

   request must include a \`[`Ping-To`](#4671-the-ping-from-and-ping-to-headers)\` HTTP header with, as its value, target URL. request does not include a \`[`Ping-From`](#4671-the-ping-from-and-ping-to-headers)\` header.

6. [Fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request.

This may be done [in parallel](#211-parallelism) with the primary fetch, and is independent of the result of that fetch.

User agents should allow the user to adjust this behavior, for example in conjunction with a setting that disables the sending of HTTP \`[`Referer`](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc7231.html#header.referer)\` (sic) headers. Based on the user's preferences, UAs may either [ignore](#214-dom-trees) the [`ping`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute altogether, or selectively ignore URLs in the list (e.g. ignoring any third-party URLs); this is explicitly accounted for in the steps above.

User agents must ignore any entity bodies returned in the responses. User agents may close the connection prematurely once they start receiving a response body.

[![(This is a tracking vector.)](https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg)](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#24-privacy-concerns) An [`a`](#451-the-a-element) or [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element that creates a [hyperlink](#461-introduction) and has the [`ping`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute is present, user agents may indicate to the user that following the hyperlink will also cause secondary requests to be sent in the background, possibly including listing the actual target URLs.

> [!example]
> For example, a visual user agent could include the hostnames of the target ping URLs along with the hyperlink's actual URL in a status bar or tooltip.

> [!note]
> The [`ping`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute is redundant with pre-existing technologies like HTTP redirects and JavaScript in allowing web pages to track which off-site links are most popular or allowing advertisers to track click-through rates.
> 
> However, the [`ping`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute provides these advantages to the user over those alternatives:
> - It allows the user to see the final target URL unobscured.
> - It allows the UA to inform the user about the out-of-band notifications.
> - It allows the UA to optimize the use of available network bandwidth so that the target page loads faster.

##### 4.6.7.1 The \`[`Ping-From`](#4671-the-ping-from-and-ping-to-headers)\` and \`[`Ping-To`](#4671-the-ping-from-and-ping-to-headers)\` headers

The \``Ping-From`\` and \``Ping-To`\` HTTP request headers are included in [hyperlink auditing](#467-hyperlink-auditing) requests. Their value is a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url), [serialized](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer).

#### 4.6.8 Link types

The following table summarizes the link types that are defined by this specification, by their corresponding keywords. This table is non-normative; the actual definitions for the link types are given in the next few sections.

In this section, the term *referenced document* refers to the resource identified by the element representing the link, and the term *current document* refers to the resource within which the element representing the link finds itself.

To determine which link types apply to a [`link`](#424-the-link-element), [`a`](#451-the-a-element), [`area`](#4813-the-area-element), or [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element, the element's `rel` attribute must be [split on ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings). The resulting tokens are the keywords for the link types that apply to that element.

Except where otherwise specified, a keyword must not be specified more than once per [`rel`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute.

Some of the sections that follow the table below list synonyms for certain keywords. The indicated synonyms are to be handled as specified by user agents, but must not be used in documents (for example, the keyword "`copyright`").

Keywords are always [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings), and must be compared as such.

> [!example]
> Thus, `rel="next"` is the same as `rel="NEXT"`.

Keywords that are body-ok affect whether [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements are [allowed in the body](#424-the-link-element). The [body-ok](#468-link-types) keywords are [`dns-prefetch`](#4685-link-type-dns-prefetch), [`modulepreload`](#46812-link-type-modulepreload), [`pingback`](#46817-link-type-pingback), [`preconnect`](#46818-link-type-preconnect), [`prefetch`](#46819-link-type-prefetch), [`preload`](#46820-link-type-preload), and [`stylesheet`](#46823-link-type-stylesheet).

New link types that are to be implemented by web browsers are to be added to this standard. The remainder can be [registered as extensions](#46827-other-link-types).

| Link type | Effect on... | [body-ok](#468-link-types) | Has \`[`Link`](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8288.html#header)\` processing | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`link`](#424-the-link-element) | [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) | [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) |
| [`alternate`](#4681-link-type-alternate) | [Hyperlink](#461-introduction) | *not allowed* | · | · | Gives alternate representations of the current document. |
| [`canonical`](#4684-link-type-canonical) | [Hyperlink](#461-introduction) | *not allowed* | · | · | Gives the preferred URL for the current document. |
| [`author`](#4682-link-type-author) | [Hyperlink](#461-introduction) | *not allowed* | · | · | Gives a link to the author of the current document or article. |
| [`bookmark`](#4683-link-type-bookmark) | *not allowed* | [Hyperlink](#461-introduction) | *not allowed* | · | · | Gives the permalink for the nearest ancestor section. |
| [`dns-prefetch`](#4685-link-type-dns-prefetch) | [External Resource](#461-introduction) | *not allowed* | Yes | · | Specifies that the user agent should preemptively perform DNS resolution for the target resource's [origin](#711-origins). |
| [`expect`](#4686-link-type-expect) | [Internal Resource](#461-introduction) | *not allowed* | · | · | Expect an element with the target ID to appear in the current document. |
| [`external`](#4687-link-type-external) | *not allowed* | [Annotation](#461-introduction) | · | · | Indicates that the referenced document is not part of the same site as the current document. |
| [`help`](#4688-link-type-help) | [Hyperlink](#461-introduction) | · | · | Provides a link to context-sensitive help. |
| [`icon`](#4689-link-type-icon) | [External Resource](#461-introduction) | *not allowed* | · | · | Imports an icon to represent the current document. |
| [`manifest`](#46811-link-type-manifest) | [External Resource](#461-introduction) | *not allowed* | · | · | Imports or links to an [application manifest](https://w3c.github.io/manifest/#dfn-manifest). [\[MANIFEST\]](#references) |
| [`modulepreload`](#46812-link-type-modulepreload) | [External Resource](#461-introduction) | *not allowed* | Yes | · | Specifies that the user agent must preemptively [fetch the module script](#8142-fetching-scripts) and store it in the document's [module map](#311-the-document-object) for later evaluation. Optionally, the module's dependencies can be fetched as well. |
| [`license`](#46810-link-type-license) | [Hyperlink](#461-introduction) | · | · | Indicates that the main content of the current document is covered by the copyright license described by the referenced document. |
| [`next`](#468261-link-type-next) | [Hyperlink](#461-introduction) | · | · | Indicates that the current document is a part of a series, and that the next document in the series is the referenced document. |
| [`nofollow`](#46813-link-type-nofollow) | *not allowed* | [Annotation](#461-introduction) | · | · | Indicates that the current document's original author or publisher does not endorse the referenced document. |
| [`noopener`](#46814-link-type-noopener) | *not allowed* | [Annotation](#461-introduction) | · | · | Creates a [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables) with a non-[auxiliary browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) if the hyperlink would otherwise create one that was auxiliary (i.e., has an appropriate [`target`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute value). |
| [`noreferrer`](#46815-link-type-noreferrer) | *not allowed* | [Annotation](#461-introduction) | · | · | No \`[`Referer`](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc7231.html#header.referer)\` (sic) header will be included. Additionally, has the same effect as [`noopener`](#46814-link-type-noopener). |
| [`opener`](#46816-link-type-opener) | *not allowed* | [Annotation](#461-introduction) | · | · | Creates an [auxiliary browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) if the hyperlink would otherwise create a [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables) with a non-[auxiliary browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) (i.e., has "`_blank`" as [`target`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute value). |
| [`pingback`](#46817-link-type-pingback) | [External Resource](#461-introduction) | *not allowed* | Yes | · | Gives the address of the pingback server that handles pingbacks to the current document. |
| [`preconnect`](#46818-link-type-preconnect) | [External Resource](#461-introduction) | *not allowed* | Yes | Yes | Specifies that the user agent should preemptively connect to the target resource's [origin](#711-origins). |
| [`prefetch`](#46819-link-type-prefetch) | [External Resource](#461-introduction) | *not allowed* | Yes | · | Specifies that the user agent should preemptively [fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) and cache the target resource as it is likely to be required for a followup [navigation](#7422-beginning-navigation). |
| [`preload`](#46820-link-type-preload) | [External Resource](#461-introduction) | *not allowed* | Yes | Yes | Specifies that the user agent must preemptively [fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) and cache the target resource for current [navigation](#7422-beginning-navigation) according to the [preload destination](#46820-link-type-preload) given by the [`as`](#424-the-link-element) attribute (and the [priority](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-priority) associated with the [corresponding](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-potential-destination-translate) [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination)). |
| [`prev`](#468262-link-type-prev) | [Hyperlink](#461-introduction) | · | · | Indicates that the current document is a part of a series, and that the previous document in the series is the referenced document. |
| [`privacy-policy`](#46821-link-type-privacy-policy) | [Hyperlink](#461-introduction) | *not allowed* | · | · | Gives a link to information about the data collection and usage practices that apply to the current document. |
| [`search`](#46822-link-type-search) | [Hyperlink](#461-introduction) | · | · | Gives a link to a resource that can be used to search through the current document and its related pages. |
| [`stylesheet`](#46823-link-type-stylesheet) | [External Resource](#461-introduction) | *not allowed* | Yes | · | Imports a style sheet. |
| [`tag`](#46824-link-type-tag) | *not allowed* | [Hyperlink](#461-introduction) | *not allowed* | · | · | Gives a tag (identified by the given address) that applies to the current document. |
| [`terms-of-service`](#46825-link-type-terms-of-service) | [Hyperlink](#461-introduction) | *not allowed* | · | · | Gives a link to information about the agreements between the current document's provider and users who wish to use the current document. |

##### 4.6.8.1 Link type "`alternate`"

The [`alternate`](#4681-link-type-alternate) keyword may be used with [`link`](#424-the-link-element), [`a`](#451-the-a-element), and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements.

The meaning of this keyword depends on the values of the other attributes.

If the element is a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element and the [`rel`](#424-the-link-element) attribute also contains the keyword [`stylesheet`](#46823-link-type-stylesheet)

The [`alternate`](#4681-link-type-alternate) keyword modifies the meaning of the [`stylesheet`](#46823-link-type-stylesheet) keyword in the way described for that keyword. The [`alternate`](#4681-link-type-alternate) keyword does not create a link of its own.

> [!example]
> Here, a set of [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements provide some style sheets:
> 
> ```html
> <!-- a persistent style sheet -->
> <link rel="stylesheet" href="default.css">
> 
> <!-- the preferred alternate style sheet -->
> <link rel="stylesheet" href="green.css" title="Green styles">
> 
> <!-- some alternate style sheets -->
> <link rel="alternate stylesheet" href="contrast.css" title="High contrast">
> <link rel="alternate stylesheet" href="big.css" title="Big fonts">
> <link rel="alternate stylesheet" href="wide.css" title="Wide screen">
> ```

If the [`alternate`](#4681-link-type-alternate) keyword is used with the [`type`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) attribute set to the value `application/rss+xml` or the value `application/atom+xml`

The keyword creates a [hyperlink](#461-introduction) referencing a syndication feed (though not necessarily syndicating exactly the same content as the current page).

For the purposes of feed autodiscovery, user agents should consider all [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements in the document with the [`alternate`](#4681-link-type-alternate) keyword used and with their [`type`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) attribute set to the value `application/rss+xml` or the value `application/atom+xml`. If the user agent has the concept of a default syndication feed, the first such element (in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees)) should be used as the default.

> [!example]
> The following [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements give syndication feeds for a blog:
> 
> ```html
> <link rel="alternate" type="application/atom+xml" href="posts.xml" title="Cool Stuff Blog">
> <link rel="alternate" type="application/atom+xml" href="posts.xml?category=robots" title="Cool Stuff Blog: robots category">
> <link rel="alternate" type="application/atom+xml" href="comments.xml" title="Cool Stuff Blog: Comments">
> ```
> 
> Such [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements would be used by user agents engaged in feed autodiscovery, with the first being the default (where applicable).
> 
> The following example offers various different syndication feeds to the user, using [`a`](#451-the-a-element) elements:
> 
> ```html
> <p>You can access the planets database using Atom feeds:</p>
> <ul>
>  <li><a href="recently-visited-planets.xml" rel="alternate" type="application/atom+xml">Recently Visited Planets</a></li>
>  <li><a href="known-bad-planets.xml" rel="alternate" type="application/atom+xml">Known Bad Planets</a></li>
>  <li><a href="unexplored-planets.xml" rel="alternate" type="application/atom+xml">Unexplored Planets</a></li>
> </ul>
> ```
> 
> These links would not be used in feed autodiscovery.

Otherwise

The keyword creates a [hyperlink](#461-introduction) referencing an alternate representation of the current document.

The nature of the referenced document is given by the [`hreflang`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements), and [`type`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) attributes.

If the [`alternate`](#4681-link-type-alternate) keyword is used with the [`hreflang`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) attribute, and that attribute's value differs from the [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree)'s [language](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes), it indicates that the referenced document is a translation.

If the [`alternate`](#4681-link-type-alternate) keyword is used with the [`type`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) attribute, it indicates that the referenced document is a reformulation of the current document in the specified format.

The [`hreflang`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) and [`type`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) attributes can be combined when specified with the [`alternate`](#4681-link-type-alternate) keyword.

> [!example]
> The following example shows how you can specify versions of the page that use alternative formats, are aimed at other languages, and that are intended for other media:
> 
> ```html
> <link rel=alternate href="/en/html" hreflang=en type=text/html title="English HTML">
> <link rel=alternate href="/fr/html" hreflang=fr type=text/html title="French HTML">
> <link rel=alternate href="/en/html/print" hreflang=en type=text/html media=print title="English HTML (for printing)">
> <link rel=alternate href="/fr/html/print" hreflang=fr type=text/html media=print title="French HTML (for printing)">
> <link rel=alternate href="/en/pdf" hreflang=en type=application/pdf title="English PDF">
> <link rel=alternate href="/fr/pdf" hreflang=fr type=application/pdf title="French PDF">
> ```

This relationship is transitive — that is, if a document links to two other documents with the link type "[`alternate`](#4681-link-type-alternate)", then, in addition to implying that those documents are alternative representations of the first document, it is also implying that those two documents are alternative representations of each other.

##### 4.6.8.2 Link type "`author`"

The [`author`](#4682-link-type-author) keyword may be used with [`link`](#424-the-link-element), [`a`](#451-the-a-element), and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements. This keyword creates a [hyperlink](#461-introduction).

For [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements, the [`author`](#4682-link-type-author) keyword indicates that the referenced document provides further information about the author of the nearest [`article`](#432-the-article-element) element ancestor of the element defining the hyperlink, if there is one, or of the page as a whole, otherwise.

For [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements, the [`author`](#4682-link-type-author) keyword indicates that the referenced document provides further information about the author for the page as a whole.

> [!note]
> The "referenced document" can be, and often is, a [`mailto:`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6068#section-2) URL giving the email address of the author. [\[MAILTO\]](#references)

**Synonyms**: For historical reasons, user agents must also treat [`link`](#424-the-link-element), [`a`](#451-the-a-element), and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements that have a `rev` attribute with the value "`made`" as having the [`author`](#4682-link-type-author) keyword specified as a link relationship.

##### 4.6.8.3 Link type "`bookmark`"

The [`bookmark`](#4683-link-type-bookmark) keyword may be used with [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements. This keyword creates a [hyperlink](#461-introduction).

The [`bookmark`](#4683-link-type-bookmark) keyword gives a permalink for the nearest ancestor [`article`](#432-the-article-element) element of the linking element in question, or of the section the linking element is most closely associated with, if there are no ancestor [`article`](#432-the-article-element) elements.

> [!example]
> The following snippet has three permalinks. A user agent could determine which permalink applies to which part of the spec by looking at where the permalinks are given.
>
