> ```html
>  ...
>  <body>
>   <h1>Example of permalinks</h1>
>   <div id="a">
>    <h2>First example</h2>
>    <p><a href="a.html" rel="bookmark">This permalink applies to
>    only the content from the first H2 to the second H2</a>. The DIV isn't
>    exactly that section, but it roughly corresponds to it.</p>
>   </div>
>   <h2>Second example</h2>
>   <article id="b">
>    <p><a href="b.html" rel="bookmark">This permalink applies to
>    the outer ARTICLE element</a> (which could be, e.g., a blog post).</p>
>    <article id="c">
>     <p><a href="c.html" rel="bookmark">This permalink applies to
>     the inner ARTICLE element</a> (which could be, e.g., a blog comment).</p>
>    </article>
>   </article>
>  </body>
>  ...
> ```

##### 4.6.8.4 Link type "`canonical`"

The [`canonical`](#4684-link-type-canonical) keyword may be used with [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element. This keyword creates a [hyperlink](#461-introduction).

The [`canonical`](#4684-link-type-canonical) keyword indicates that URL given by the [`href`](#424-the-link-element) attribute is the preferred URL for the current document. That helps search engines reduce duplicate content, as described in more detail in The Canonical Link Relation. [\[RFC6596\]](#references)

##### 4.6.8.5 Link type "`dns-prefetch`"

The [`dns-prefetch`](#4685-link-type-dns-prefetch) keyword may be used with [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements. This keyword creates an [external resource link](#461-introduction). This keyword is [body-ok](#468-link-types).

The [`dns-prefetch`](#4685-link-type-dns-prefetch) keyword indicates that preemptively performing DNS resolution for the [origin](#711-origins) of the specified resource is likely to be beneficial, as it is highly likely that the user will require resources located at that [origin](#711-origins), and the user experience would be improved by preempting the latency costs associated with DNS resolution.

There is no default type for resources given by the [`dns-prefetch`](#4685-link-type-dns-prefetch) keyword.

The appropriate times to [fetch and process](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) this type of link are:
- When the [external resource link](#461-introduction) is created on a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees).
- When the [external resource link](#461-introduction)'s [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element [becomes browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees).
- When the [`href`](#424-the-link-element) attribute of the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element of an [external resource link](#461-introduction) that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees) is changed.

The [fetch and process the linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) steps for this type of linked resource, given a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element el, are:
1. Let url be the result of [encoding-parsing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given el's [`href`](#424-the-link-element) attribute's value, relative to el's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
2. If url is failure, then return.
3. Let partitionKey be the result of [determining the network partition key](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#determine-the-network-partition-key) given el's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant).
4. The user agent should [resolve an origin](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#resolve-an-origin) given partitionKey and url's [origin](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-origin).

   > [!note]
   > As the results of this algorithm can be cached, future fetches could be faster.

##### 4.6.8.6 Link type "`expect`"

The [`expect`](#4686-link-type-expect) keyword may be used with [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements. This keyword creates an [internal resource link](#461-introduction).

An [internal resource link](#461-introduction) created by the [`expect`](#4686-link-type-expect) keyword can be used to [block rendering](#316-render-blocking-mechanism) until the element that it [indicates](#7464-scrolling-to-a-fragment) is connected to the document and fully parsed.

There is no default type for resources given by the [`expect`](#4686-link-type-expect) keyword.

Whenever any of the following conditions occur for a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element el:
- the [`expect`](#4686-link-type-expect) [internal resource link](#461-introduction) is created on el that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees);
- an [`expect`](#4686-link-type-expect) [internal resource link](#461-introduction) has been created on el and el becomes [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees);
- an [`expect`](#4686-link-type-expect) [internal resource link](#461-introduction) has been created on el, el is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees), and el's [`href`](#424-the-link-element) attribute is set, changed, or removed; or
- an [`expect`](#4686-link-type-expect) [internal resource link](#461-introduction) has been created on el, el is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees), and el's [`media`](#424-the-link-element) attribute is set, changed, or removed,

then [process](#4686-link-type-expect) el.

To process internal resource link given a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element el, run these steps:
1. Let doc be el's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
2. Let url be the result of [encoding-parsing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given el's [`href`](#424-the-link-element) attribute's value, relative to doc.
3. If this fails, or if url does not [equal](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-equals) doc's [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) with *[exclude fragments](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-equals-exclude-fragments)* set to true, then [unblock rendering](#316-render-blocking-mechanism) on el and return.
4. Let indicatedElement be the result of [selecting the indicated part](#7464-scrolling-to-a-fragment) given doc and url.
5. If all of the following are true:
   - doc's [current document readiness](#315-reporting-document-loading-status) is "`loading`";
   - el creates an [internal resource link](#461-introduction);
   - el is [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees);
   - el's [`rel`](#424-the-link-element) attribute contains [`expect`](#4686-link-type-expect);
   - el is [potentially render-blocking](#258-blocking-attributes);
   - el's [`media`](#424-the-link-element) attribute [matches the environment](#2310-media-queries); and
   - indicatedElement is not an element, or is on a [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) of an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) whose associated [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is doc,

   then [block rendering](#316-render-blocking-mechanism) on el.

6. Otherwise, [unblock rendering](#316-render-blocking-mechanism) on el.

To process internal resource links given a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) doc:
1. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) [`expect`](#4686-link-type-expect) [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element link in doc's [render-blocking element set](#316-render-blocking-mechanism), [process](#4686-link-type-expect) link.

The following [attribute change steps](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), given element, localName, oldValue, value, and namespace, are used to ensure [`expect`](#4686-link-type-expect) [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements respond to dynamic [`id`](#326-global-attributes) and [`name`](#162-non-conforming-features) changes:
1. If namespace is not null, then return.
2. If element is in a [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) of an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents), then return.
3. If any of the following is true:
   - localName is [`id`](#326-global-attributes); or
   - localName is [`name`](#162-non-conforming-features) and element is an [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element,

   then [process internal resource links](#4686-link-type-expect) given element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).

##### 4.6.8.7 Link type "`external`"

The [`external`](#4687-link-type-external) keyword may be used with [`a`](#451-the-a-element), [`area`](#4813-the-area-element), and [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements. This keyword does not create a [hyperlink](#461-introduction), but [annotates](#461-introduction) any other hyperlinks created by the element (the implied hyperlink, if no other keywords create one).

The [`external`](#4687-link-type-external) keyword indicates that the link is leading to a document that is not part of the site that the current document forms a part of.

##### 4.6.8.8 Link type "`help`"

The [`help`](#4688-link-type-help) keyword may be used with [`link`](#424-the-link-element), [`a`](#451-the-a-element), [`area`](#4813-the-area-element), and [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements. This keyword creates a [hyperlink](#461-introduction).

For [`a`](#451-the-a-element), [`area`](#4813-the-area-element), and [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements, the [`help`](#4688-link-type-help) keyword indicates that the referenced document provides further help information for the parent of the element defining the hyperlink, and its children.

> [!example]
> In the following example, the form control has associated context-sensitive help. The user agent could use this information, for example, displaying the referenced document if the user presses the "Help" or "F1" key.
> 
> ```html
>  <p><label> Topic: <input name=topic> <a href="help/topic.html" rel="help">(Help)</a></label></p>
> ```

For [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements, the [`help`](#4688-link-type-help) keyword indicates that the referenced document provides help for the page as a whole.

For [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements, on some browsers, the [`help`](#4688-link-type-help) keyword causes the link to use a different cursor.

##### 4.6.8.9 Link type "`icon`"

The [`icon`](#4689-link-type-icon) keyword may be used with [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements. This keyword creates an [external resource link](#461-introduction).

The specified resource is an icon representing the page or site, and should be used by the user agent when representing the page in the user interface.

Icons could be auditory icons, visual icons, or other kinds of icons. If multiple icons are provided, the user agent must select the most appropriate icon according to the [`type`](#424-the-link-element), [`media`](#424-the-link-element), and [`sizes`](#424-the-link-element) attributes. If there are multiple equally appropriate icons, user agents must use the last one declared in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) at the time that the user agent collected the list of icons. If the user agent tries to use an icon but that icon is determined, upon closer examination, to in fact be inappropriate (e.g. because it uses an unsupported format), then the user agent must try the next-most-appropriate icon as determined by the attributes.

> [!note]
> User agents are not required to update icons when the list of icons changes, but are encouraged to do so.

There is no default type for resources given by the [`icon`](#4689-link-type-icon) keyword. However, for the purposes of [determining the type of the resource](#4242-processing-the-type-attribute), user agents must expect the resource to be an image.

The [`sizes`](#424-the-link-element) keywords represent icon sizes in raw pixels (as opposed to [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px)).

> [!note]
> An icon that is 50 [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) wide intended for displays with a device pixel density of two device pixels per [CSS pixel](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) (2x, 192dpi) would have a width of 100 raw pixels. This feature does not support indicating that a different resource is to be used for small high-resolution icons vs large low-resolution icons (e.g. 50×50 2x vs 100×100 1x).

To parse and process the attribute's value, the user agent must first [split the attribute's value on ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings), and must then parse each resulting keyword to determine what it represents.

The `any` keyword represents that the resource contains a scalable icon, e.g. as provided by an SVG image.

Other keywords must be further parsed as follows to determine what they represent:
1. If the keyword doesn't contain exactly one U+0078 LATIN SMALL LETTER X or U+0058 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER X character, then this keyword doesn't represent anything. Return for that keyword.
2. Let width string be the string before the "`x`" or "`X`".
3. Let height string be the string after the "`x`" or "`X`".
4. If either width string or height string start with a U+0030 DIGIT ZERO (0) character or contain any characters other than [ASCII digits](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), then this keyword doesn't represent anything. Return for that keyword.
5. Apply the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers) to width string to obtain width.
6. Apply the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers) to height string to obtain height.
7. The keyword represents that the resource contains a bitmap icon with a width of width device pixels and a height of height device pixels.

The keywords specified on the [`sizes`](#424-the-link-element) attribute must not represent icon sizes that are not actually available in the linked resource.

The [linked resource fetch setup steps](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) for this type of linked resource, given a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element el and [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) request, are:
1. Set request's [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) to "`image`".
2. Return true.

The [process a link header](#4244-processing-link-headers) steps for this type of linked resource are to do nothing.

In the absence of a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) with the [`icon`](#4689-link-type-icon) keyword, for [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) objects whose [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document)'s [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) is an [HTTP(S) scheme](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#http-scheme), user agents may instead run these steps:
1. Let request be a new [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) whose [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url) is the [URL record](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) obtained by resolving the [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) "`/favicon.ico`" against the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object's [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), [client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client) is the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object's [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant), [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) is "`image`", [credentials mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode) is "`include`", and whose [use-URL-credentials flag](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-use-url-credentials-flag) is set.
2. [Fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request, with *[processResponse](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#process-response)* set to the following steps given [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response:
   1. Use response's [unsafe response](#251-terminology) as an icon as if it had been declared using the [`icon`](#4689-link-type-icon) keyword.

> [!example]
> The following snippet shows the top part of an application with several icons.
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <html lang="en">
>  <head>
>   <title>lsForums — Inbox</title>
>   <link rel=icon href=favicon.png sizes="16x16" type="image/png">
>   <link rel=icon href=windows.ico sizes="32x32 48x48" type="image/vnd.microsoft.icon">
>   <link rel=icon href=mac.icns sizes="128x128 512x512 8192x8192 32768x32768">
>   <link rel=icon href=iphone.png sizes="57x57" type="image/png">
>   <link rel=icon href=gnome.svg sizes="any" type="image/svg+xml">
>   <link rel=stylesheet href=lsforums.css>
>   <script src=lsforums.js></script>
>   <meta name=application-name content="lsForums">
>  </head>
>  <body>
>   ...
> ```

For historical reasons, the [`icon`](#4689-link-type-icon) keyword may be preceded by the keyword "`shortcut`". If the "`shortcut`" keyword is present, the [`rel`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute's entire value must be an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`shortcut icon`" (with a single U+0020 SPACE character between the tokens and no other [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points)).

##### 4.6.8.10 Link type "`license`"

The [`license`](#46810-link-type-license) keyword may be used with [`link`](#424-the-link-element), [`a`](#451-the-a-element), [`area`](#4813-the-area-element), and [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements. This keyword creates a [hyperlink](#461-introduction).

The [`license`](#46810-link-type-license) keyword indicates that the referenced document provides the copyright license terms under which the main content of the current document is provided.

This specification does not specify how to distinguish between the main content of a document and content that is not deemed to be part of that main content. The distinction should be made clear to the user.

> [!example]
> Consider a photo sharing site. A page on that site might describe and show a photograph, and the page might be marked up as follows:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <html lang="en">
>  <head>
>   <title>Exampl Pictures: Kissat</title>
>   <link rel="stylesheet" href="/style/default">
>  </head>
>  <body>
>   <h1>Kissat</h1>
>   <nav>
>    <a href="../">Return to photo index</a>
>   </nav>
>   <figure>
>    <img src="/pix/39627052_fd8dcd98b5.jpg">
>    <figcaption>Kissat</figcaption>
>   </figure>
>   <p>One of them has six toes!</p>
>   <p><small><a rel="license" href="http://www.opensource.org/licenses/mit-license.php">MIT Licensed</a></small></p>
>   <footer>
>    <a href="/">Home</a> | <a href="../">Photo index</a>
>    <p><small>© copyright 2009 Exampl Pictures. All Rights Reserved.</small></p>
>   </footer>
>  </body>
> </html>
> ```
> 
> In this case the [`license`](#46810-link-type-license) applies to just the photo (the main content of the document), not the whole document. In particular not the design of the page itself, which is covered by the copyright given at the bottom of the document. This could be made clearer in the styling (e.g. making the license link prominently positioned near the photograph, while having the page copyright in light small text at the foot of the page).

**Synonyms**: For historical reasons, user agents must also treat the keyword "`copyright`" like the [`license`](#46810-link-type-license) keyword.

##### 4.6.8.11 Link type "`manifest`"

The [`manifest`](#46811-link-type-manifest) keyword may be used with [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements. This keyword creates an [external resource link](#461-introduction).

The [`manifest`](#46811-link-type-manifest) keyword indicates the manifest file that provides metadata associated with the current document.

There is no default type for resources given by the [`manifest`](#46811-link-type-manifest) keyword.

When a web application is not [installed](https://w3c.github.io/manifest/#dfn-installed-web-application), the appropriate time to [fetch and process the linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) for this link type is when the user agent deems it necessary. For example, when the user chooses to [install the web application](https://w3c.github.io/manifest/#dfn-installed-web-application).

For an [installed web application](https://w3c.github.io/manifest/#dfn-installed-web-application), the appropriate times to [fetch and process the linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) for this link type are:
- When the [external resource link](#461-introduction) is created on a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees).
- When the [external resource link](#461-introduction)'s [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element [becomes browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees).
- When the [`href`](#424-the-link-element) attribute of the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element of an [external resource link](#461-introduction) that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees) is changed.

In any case, only the first [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) whose [`rel`](#424-the-link-element) attribute contains the token [`manifest`](#46811-link-type-manifest) may be used.

A user agent must not [delay the load event](#1327-the-end) for this link type.

The [linked resource fetch setup steps](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) for this type of linked resource, given a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element el and [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) request, are:
1. Let navigable be el's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [node navigable](#731-navigables).
2. If navigable is null, then return false.
3. If navigable is not a [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables), then return false.
4. Set request's [initiator](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-initiator) to "`manifest`".
5. Set request's [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) to "`manifest`".
6. Set request's [mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-mode) to "`cors`".
7. Set request's [credentials mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode) to the [CORS settings attribute credentials mode](#254-cors-settings-attributes) for el's [`crossorigin`](#424-the-link-element) content attribute.
8. Return true.

To [process this type of linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) given a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element el, boolean success, [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response, and [byte sequence](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-byte-sequences) bodyBytes:
1. If response's [Content-Type metadata](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource) is not a [JSON MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#json-mime-type), then set success to false.
2. If success is true:
   1. Let document URL be el's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).
   2. Let manifest URL be response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url).
   3. Let client be el's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant).
   4. [Process the manifest](https://w3c.github.io/manifest/#dfn-processing-a-manifest) given document URL, manifest URL, bodyBytes, and client. [\[MANIFEST\]](#references)

The [process a link header](#4244-processing-link-headers) steps for this type of linked resource are to do nothing.

##### 4.6.8.12 Link type "`modulepreload`"

The [`modulepreload`](#46812-link-type-modulepreload) keyword may be used with [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements. This keyword creates an [external resource link](#461-introduction). This keyword is [body-ok](#468-link-types).

The [`modulepreload`](#46812-link-type-modulepreload) keyword is a specialized alternative to the [`preload`](#46820-link-type-preload) keyword, with a processing model geared toward preloading [module scripts](#8141-scripts). In particular, it uses the specific fetch behavior for module scripts (including, e.g., a different interpretation of the [`crossorigin`](#424-the-link-element) attribute), and places the result into the appropriate [module map](#311-the-document-object) for later evaluation. In contrast, a similar [external resource link](#461-introduction) using the [`preload`](#46820-link-type-preload) keyword would place the result in the preload cache, without affecting the document's [module map](#311-the-document-object).

Additionally, implementations can take advantage of the fact that [module scripts](#8141-scripts) declare their dependencies in order to fetch the specified module's dependency as well. This is intended as an optimization opportunity, since the user agent knows that, in all likelihood, those dependencies will also be needed later. It will not generally be observable without using technology such as service workers, or monitoring on the server side. Notably, the appropriate [`load`](#events) or [`error`](#events) events will occur after the specified module is fetched, and will not wait for any dependencies.

A user agent must not [delay the load event](#1327-the-end) for this link type.

A module preload destination is "`json`", "`style`", "`text`", or a [script-like destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-destination-script-like).

The appropriate times to [fetch and process the linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) for such a link are:
- When the [external resource link](#461-introduction) is created on a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees).
- When the [external resource link](#461-introduction)'s [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element [becomes browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees).
- When the [`href`](#424-the-link-element) attribute of the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element of an [external resource link](#461-introduction) that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees) is changed.

> [!note]
> Unlike some other link relations, changing the relevant attributes (such as [`as`](#424-the-link-element), [`crossorigin`](#424-the-link-element), and [`referrerpolicy`](#424-the-link-element)) of such a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) does not trigger a new fetch. This is because the document's [module map](#311-the-document-object) has already been populated by a previous fetch, and so re-fetching would be pointless.

The [fetch and process the linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) algorithm for [`modulepreload`](#46812-link-type-modulepreload) links, given a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element el, is as follows:
1. If el's [`href`](#424-the-link-element) attribute's value is the empty string, then return.
2. Let destination be the current state of el's [`as`](#424-the-link-element) attribute (a [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination)), or "`script`" if it is in no state.
3. If destination is not a [module preload destination](#46812-link-type-modulepreload), then [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given el to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) at el, and return.
4. Let url be the result of [encoding-parsing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given el's [`href`](#424-the-link-element) attribute's value, relative to el's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
5. If url is failure, then return.
6. Let settings object be el's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant).
7. Let credentials mode be the [CORS settings attribute credentials mode](#254-cors-settings-attributes) for el's [`crossorigin`](#424-the-link-element) attribute.
8. Let cryptographic nonce be el.[\[\[CryptographicNonce\]\]](#256-nonce-attributes).
9. Let integrity metadata be the value of el's [`integrity`](#424-the-link-element) attribute, if it is specified, or the empty string otherwise.
10. If el does not have an [`integrity`](#424-the-link-element) attribute, then set integrity metadata to the result of [resolving a module integrity metadata](#8142-fetching-scripts) with url and settings object.
11. Let referrer policy be the current state of el's [`referrerpolicy`](#424-the-link-element) attribute.
12. Let fetch priority be the current state of el's [`fetchpriority`](#424-the-link-element) attribute.
13. Let options be a [script fetch options](#8142-fetching-scripts) whose [cryptographic nonce](#8142-fetching-scripts) is cryptographic nonce, [integrity metadata](#8142-fetching-scripts) is integrity metadata, [parser metadata](#8142-fetching-scripts) is "`not-parser-inserted`", [credentials mode](#8142-fetching-scripts) is credentials mode, [referrer policy](#8142-fetching-scripts) is referrer policy, and [fetch priority](#8142-fetching-scripts) is fetch priority.
14. [Fetch a modulepreload module script graph](#8142-fetching-scripts) given url, destination, settings object, options, and with the following steps given result:
    1. If result is null, then [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) at el, and return.
    2. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`load`](#events) at el.

The [process a link header](#4244-processing-link-headers) steps for this type of linked resource are to do nothing.

> [!example]
> The following snippet shows the top part of an application with several modules preloaded:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE html>
> <html lang="en">
> <title>IRCFog</title>
> 
> <link rel="modulepreload" href="app.mjs">
> <link rel="modulepreload" href="helpers.mjs">
> <link rel="modulepreload" href="irc.mjs">
> <link rel="modulepreload" href="fog-machine.mjs">
> 
> <script type="module" src="app.mjs">
> ...
> ```
> 
> Assume that the module graph for the application is as follows:
> 
> ![The module graph is rooted at app.mjs, which depends on irc.mjs and fog-machine.mjs. In turn, irc.mjs depends on helpers.mjs.](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/ircfog-modules.svg)
> 
> Here we see the application developer has used [`modulepreload`](#46812-link-type-modulepreload) to declare all of the modules in their module graph, ensuring that the user agent initiates fetches for them all. Without such preloading, the user agent might need to go through multiple network roundtrips before discovering `helpers.mjs`, if technologies such as HTTP/2 Server Push are not in play. In this way, [`modulepreload`](#46812-link-type-modulepreload) [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements can be used as a sort of "manifest" of the application's modules.

> [!example]
> The following code shows how [`modulepreload`](#46812-link-type-modulepreload) links can be used in conjunction with [`import()`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-import-calls) to ensure network fetching is done ahead of time, so that when [`import()`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-import-calls) is called, the module is already ready (but not evaluated) in the [module map](#8167-module-related-host-hooks):
> 
> ```html
> <link rel="modulepreload" href="awesome-viewer.mjs">
> 
> <button onclick="import('./awesome-viewer.mjs').then(m => m.view())">
>   View awesome thing
> </button>
> ```

##### 4.6.8.13 Link type "`nofollow`"

The [`nofollow`](#46813-link-type-nofollow) keyword may be used with [`a`](#451-the-a-element), [`area`](#4813-the-area-element), and [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements. This keyword does not create a [hyperlink](#461-introduction), but [annotates](#461-introduction) any other hyperlinks created by the element (the implied hyperlink, if no other keywords create one).

The [`nofollow`](#46813-link-type-nofollow) keyword indicates that the link is not endorsed by the original author or publisher of the page, or that the link to the referenced document was included primarily because of a commercial relationship between people affiliated with the two pages.

##### 4.6.8.14 Link type "`noopener`"

The [`noopener`](#46814-link-type-noopener) keyword may be used with [`a`](#451-the-a-element), [`area`](#4813-the-area-element), and [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements. This keyword does not create a [hyperlink](#461-introduction), but [annotates](#461-introduction) any other hyperlinks created by the element (the implied hyperlink, if no other keywords create one).

The keyword indicates that any newly created [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables) which results from following the [hyperlink](#461-introduction) will not contain an [auxiliary browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts). E.g., the resulting [`Window`](#722-the-window-object)'s [`opener`](#7224-accessing-related-windows) getter will return null.

> [!note]
> See also the [processing model](#7317-navigable-target-names).

> [!example]
> This typically creates a [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables) with an [auxiliary browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) (assuming there is no existing [navigable](#731-navigables) whose [target name](#731-navigables) is "`example`"):
> 
> ```html
> <a href=help.html target=example>Help!</a>
> ```
> 
> This creates a [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables) with a non-[auxiliary browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) (assuming the same thing):
> 
> ```html
> <a href=help.html target=example rel=noopener>Help!</a>
> ```
> 
> These are equivalent and only navigate the [parent navigable](#731-navigables):
> 
> ```html
> <a href=index.html target=_parent>Home</a>
> ```
> 
> ```html
> <a href=index.html target=_parent rel=noopener>Home</a>
> ```

##### 4.6.8.15 Link type "`noreferrer`"

The [`noreferrer`](#46815-link-type-noreferrer) keyword may be used with [`a`](#451-the-a-element), [`area`](#4813-the-area-element), and [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements. This keyword does not create a [hyperlink](#461-introduction), but [annotates](#461-introduction) any other hyperlinks created by the element (the implied hyperlink, if no other keywords create one).

It indicates that no referrer information is to be leaked when following the link and also implies the [`noopener`](#46814-link-type-noopener) keyword behavior under the same conditions.

> [!note]
> See also the [processing model](#465-following-hyperlinks) where referrer is directly manipulated.

> [!example]
> `<a href="..." rel="noreferrer" target="_blank">` has the same behavior as `<a href="..." rel="noreferrer noopener" target="_blank">`.

##### 4.6.8.16 Link type "`opener`"

The [`opener`](#46816-link-type-opener) keyword may be used with [`a`](#451-the-a-element), [`area`](#4813-the-area-element), and [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements. This keyword does not create a [hyperlink](#461-introduction), but [annotates](#461-introduction) any other hyperlinks created by the element (the implied hyperlink, if no other keywords create one).

The keyword indicates that any newly created [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables) which results from following the [hyperlink](#461-introduction) will contain an [auxiliary browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts).

> [!note]
> See also the [processing model](#465-following-hyperlinks).

> [!example]
> In the following example the [`opener`](#46816-link-type-opener) is used to allow the help page popup to navigate its opener, e.g., in case what the user is looking for can be found elsewhere. An alternative might be to use a named target, rather than `_blank`, but this has the potential to clash with existing names.
> 
> ```html
> <a href="..." rel=opener target=_blank>Help!</a>
> ```

##### 4.6.8.17 Link type "`pingback`"

The [`pingback`](#46817-link-type-pingback) keyword may be used with [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements. This keyword creates an [external resource link](#461-introduction). This keyword is [body-ok](#468-link-types).

For the semantics of the [`pingback`](#46817-link-type-pingback) keyword, see Pingback 1.0. [\[PINGBACK\]](#references)

##### 4.6.8.18 Link type "`preconnect`"

The [`preconnect`](#46818-link-type-preconnect) keyword may be used with [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements. This keyword creates an [external resource link](#461-introduction). This keyword is [body-ok](#468-link-types).

The [`preconnect`](#46818-link-type-preconnect) keyword indicates that preemptively initiating a connection to the [origin](#711-origins) of the specified resource is likely to be beneficial, as it is highly likely that the user will require resources located at that [origin](#711-origins), and the user experience would be improved by preempting the latency costs associated with establishing the connection.

There is no default type for resources given by the [`preconnect`](#46818-link-type-preconnect) keyword.

A user agent must not [delay the load event](#1327-the-end) for this link type.

The appropriate times to [fetch and process](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) this type of link are:
- When the [external resource link](#461-introduction) is created on a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees).
- When the [external resource link](#461-introduction)'s [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element [becomes browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees).
- When the [`href`](#424-the-link-element) attribute of the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element of an [external resource link](#461-introduction) that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees) is changed.
- When the [`crossorigin`](#424-the-link-element) attribute of the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element of an [external resource link](#461-introduction) that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees) is set, changed, or removed.

The [fetch and process the linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) steps for this type of linked resource, given a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element el, are to [create link options](#4244-processing-link-headers) from el and to [preconnect](#46818-link-type-preconnect) given the result.

The [process a link header](#4244-processing-link-headers) step for this type of linked resource given a [link processing options](#4244-processing-link-headers) options are to [preconnect](#46818-link-type-preconnect) given options.

To preconnect given a [link processing options](#4244-processing-link-headers) options:
1. If options's [href](#4244-processing-link-headers) is an empty string, return.
2. Let url be the result of [encoding-parsing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given options's [href](#4244-processing-link-headers), relative to options's [base URL](#4244-processing-link-headers).

   > [!warning]
   > Passing the base URL instead of a document or environment is tracked by [issue #9715](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9715).

3. If url is failure, then return.
4. If url's [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) is not an [HTTP(S) scheme](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#http-scheme), then return.
5. Let partitionKey be the result of [determining the network partition key](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#determine-the-network-partition-key) given options's [environment](#4244-processing-link-headers).
6. Let useCredentials be true.
7. If options's [crossorigin](#4244-processing-link-headers) is [Anonymous](#254-cors-settings-attributes) and options's [origin](#4244-processing-link-headers) does not have the [same origin](#711-origins) as url's [origin](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-origin), then set useCredentials to false.
8. The user agent should [obtain a connection](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-connection-obtain) given partitionKey, url's [origin](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-origin), and useCredentials.

   > [!note]
   > This connection is obtained but not used directly. It will remain in the [connection pool](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-connection-pool) for subsequent use.

   The user agent should attempt to initiate a preconnect and perform the full connection handshake (DNS+TCP for HTTP, and DNS+TCP+TLS for HTTPS origins) whenever possible, but is allowed to elect to perform a partial handshake (DNS only for HTTP, and DNS or DNS+TCP for HTTPS origins), or skip it entirely, due to resource constraints or other reasons.

   The optimal number of connections per origin is dependent on the negotiated protocol, users current connectivity profile, available device resources, global connection limits, and other context specific variables. As a result, the decision for how many connections should be opened is deferred to the user agent.

##### 4.6.8.19 Link type "`prefetch`"

The [`prefetch`](#46819-link-type-prefetch) keyword may be used with [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements. This keyword creates an [external resource link](#461-introduction). This keyword is [body-ok](#468-link-types).

The [`prefetch`](#46819-link-type-prefetch) keyword indicates that preemptively [fetching](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) and caching the specified resource or same-site document is likely to be beneficial, as it is highly likely that the user will require this resource for future navigations.

There is no default type for resources given by the [`prefetch`](#46819-link-type-prefetch) keyword.

The appropriate times to [fetch and process](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) this type of link are:
- When the [external resource link](#461-introduction) is created on a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees).
- When the [external resource link](#461-introduction)'s [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element [becomes browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees).
- When the [`href`](#424-the-link-element) attribute of the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element of an [external resource link](#461-introduction) that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees) is changed.
- When the [`crossorigin`](#424-the-link-element) attribute of the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element of an [external resource link](#461-introduction) that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees) is set, changed, or removed.

The [fetch and process the linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) algorithm for [`prefetch`](#46819-link-type-prefetch) links, given a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element el, is as follows:
1. If el's [`href`](#424-the-link-element) attribute's value is the empty string, then return.
2. Let options be the result of [creating link options](#4244-processing-link-headers) from el.
3. Let request be the result of [creating a link request](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) given options.
4. If request is null, then return.
5. Set request's [initiator](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-initiator) to "`prefetch`".
6. Let processPrefetchResponse be the following steps given a [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response and null, failure, or a [byte sequence](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-byte-sequences) bytesOrNull:
   1. If response is a [network error](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-network-error), [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) at el.
   2. Otherwise, [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`load`](#events) at el.
7. The user agent should [fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request, with *[processResponseConsumeBody](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#process-response-end-of-body)* set to processPrefetchResponse. User agents may delay the fetching of request to prioritize other requests that are necessary for the current document.

The [process a link header](#4244-processing-link-headers) steps for this type of linked resource are to do nothing.

##### 4.6.8.20 Link type "`preload`"

The [`preload`](#46820-link-type-preload) keyword may be used with [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements. This keyword creates an [external resource link](#461-introduction). This keyword is [body-ok](#468-link-types).

The [`preload`](#46820-link-type-preload) keyword indicates that the user agent will preemptively [fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) and cache the specified resource according to the [preload destination](#46820-link-type-preload) given by the [`as`](#424-the-link-element) attribute, and the [priority](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-priority) given by the [`fetchpriority`](#424-the-link-element) attribute, as it is highly likely that the user will require this resource for the current navigation.

> [!note]
> User-agents might perform additional operations when a resource is loaded, such as preemptively [decoding images](#483-the-img-element) or [creating style sheets](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#create-a-css-style-sheet). However, these additional operations cannot have observable effects.

There is no default type for resources given by the [`preload`](#46820-link-type-preload) keyword.

A user agent must not [delay the load event](#1327-the-end) for this link type.

The appropriate times to [fetch and process the linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) for such a link are:
- When the [external resource link](#461-introduction) is created on a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees).
- When the [external resource link](#461-introduction)'s [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element [becomes browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees).
- When the [`href`](#424-the-link-element) attribute of the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element of an [external resource link](#461-introduction) that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees) is changed.
- When the [`as`](#424-the-link-element) attribute of the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element of an [external resource link](#461-introduction) that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees) is changed.
- When the [`type`](#424-the-link-element) attribute of the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element of an [external resource link](#461-introduction) that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees), but was previously not obtained due to the [`type`](#424-the-link-element) attribute specifying an unsupported type for the request [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination), is set, removed, or changed.
- When the [`media`](#424-the-link-element) attribute of the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element of an [external resource link](#461-introduction) that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees), but was previously not obtained due to the [`media`](#424-the-link-element) attribute not [matching the environment](#2310-media-queries), is changed or removed.

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a map of preloaded resources, which is an [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), initially empty.

A preload key is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs). It has the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):

URL

A [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url)

destination

A [preload destination](#46820-link-type-preload)

mode

A [request mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-mode), either "`same-origin`", "`cors`", or "`no-cors`"

credentials mode

A [credentials mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode)

A [preload key](#46820-link-type-preload)'s [equality](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#311-identity-and-equality) is [itemwise equality](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs).

A preload entry is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs). It has the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):

integrity metadata

A string

response

Null or a [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response)

on response available

Null, or an algorithm accepting a [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) or null

To consume a preloaded resource for [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) window, given a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) url, a string destination, a string mode, a string credentialsMode, a string integrityMetadata, and onResponseAvailable, which is an algorithm accepting a [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response):
1. Let key be a [preload key](#46820-link-type-preload) whose [URL](#46820-link-type-preload) is url, [destination](#46820-link-type-preload) is destination, [mode](#46820-link-type-preload) is mode, and [credentials mode](#46820-link-type-preload) is credentialsMode.
2. Let preloads be window's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [map of preloaded resources](#46820-link-type-preload).
3. If key does not [exist](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) in preloads, then return false.
4. Let entry be preloads\[key\].
5. Let consumerIntegrityMetadata be the result of [parsing](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-subresource-integrity/#parse-metadata) integrityMetadata.
6. Let preloadIntegrityMetadata be the result of [parsing](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-subresource-integrity/#parse-metadata) entry's [integrity metadata](#46820-link-type-preload).
7. If none of the following conditions apply:
   - consumerIntegrityMetadata is `no metadata`;
   - consumerIntegrityMetadata is equal to preloadIntegrityMetadata; or

     > [!warning]
     > This comparison would ignore unknown integrity options. See [issue #116.](https://github.com/w3c/webappsec-subresource-integrity/issues/116)

   then return false.

   > [!note]
   > A mismatch in integrity metadata between the preload and the consumer, even if both match the data, would lead to an additional fetch from the network.

   > [!note]
   > It is important that [network errors](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-network-error) are added to the preload cache so that if a preload request results in an error, the erroneous response isn't re-requested from the network later. This also has security implications; consider the case where a developer specifies subresource integrity metadata on a preload request, but not the following resource request. If the preload request fails subresource integrity verification and is discarded, the resource request will fetch and consume a potentially-malicious response from the network without verifying its integrity. [\[SRI\]](#references)

8. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) preloads\[key\].
9. If entry's [response](#46820-link-type-preload) is null, then set entry's [on response available](#46820-link-type-preload) to onResponseAvailable.
10. Otherwise, call onResponseAvailable with entry's [response](#46820-link-type-preload).
11. Return true.

For the purposes of this section, a string type matches a [preload destination](#46820-link-type-preload) destination if the following algorithm returns true:
1. If type is an empty string, then return true.
2. If destination is "`fetch`", then return true.
3. Let mimeTypeRecord be the result of [parsing](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#parse-a-mime-type) type.
4. If mimeTypeRecord is failure, then return false.
5. If mimeTypeRecord is not [supported by the user agent](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#supported-by-the-user-agent), then return false.
6. If any of the following are true:
   - destination is "`script`" and mimeTypeRecord is a [JavaScript MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type);
   - destination is "`image`" and mimeTypeRecord is an [image MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#image-mime-type);
   - destination is "`font`" and mimeTypeRecord is a [font MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#font-mime-type);
   - destination is "`style`" and mimeTypeRecord's [essence](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type-essence) is [`text/css`](#mime-types); or
   - destination is "`track`" and mimeTypeRecord's [essence](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type-essence) is [`text/vtt`](#mime-types),

   then return true.

7. Return false.

To create a preload key for a [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) request, return a new [preload key](#46820-link-type-preload) whose [URL](#46820-link-type-preload) is request's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url), [destination](#46820-link-type-preload) is request's [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination), [mode](#46820-link-type-preload) is request's [mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-mode), and [credentials mode](#46820-link-type-preload) is request's [credentials mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode).

A preload destination is "`fetch`", "`font`", "`image`", "`script`", "`style`", or "`track`".

To translate a preload destination given a string destination:
1. If destination is not a [preload destination](#46820-link-type-preload), then return null.
2. Return the result of [translating](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-potential-destination-translate) destination.

To preload given a [link processing options](#4244-processing-link-headers) options and an optional processResponse, which is an algorithm accepting a [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response):
1. If options's [type](#4244-processing-link-headers) doesn't [match](#46820-link-type-preload) options's [destination](#4244-processing-link-headers), then return.
2. If options's [destination](#4244-processing-link-headers) is "`image`" and options's [source set](#4244-processing-link-headers) is not null, then set options's [href](#4244-processing-link-headers) to the result of [selecting an image source](#48437-selecting-an-image-source) from options's [source set](#4244-processing-link-headers).
3. Let request be the result of [creating a link request](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) given options.
4. If request is null, then return.
5. Let unsafeEndTime be 0.
6. Let entry be a new [preload entry](#46820-link-type-preload) whose [integrity metadata](#46820-link-type-preload) is options's [integrity](#4244-processing-link-headers).
7. Let key be the result of [creating a preload key](#46820-link-type-preload) given request.
8. If options's [document](#4244-processing-link-headers) is null, then set request's [initiator type](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-initiator-type) to "`early hint`".
9. Let controller be null.
10. Let reportTiming given a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document be to [report timing](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#finalize-and-report-timing) for controller given document's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant).
11. Set controller to the result of [fetching](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request, with *[processResponseConsumeBody](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#process-response-end-of-body)* set to the following steps given a [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response and null, failure, or a [byte sequence](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-byte-sequences) bodyBytes:
    1. If bodyBytes is a [byte sequence](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-byte-sequences), then set response's [body](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-body) to bodyBytes [as a body](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#byte-sequence-as-a-body).

       > [!note]
       > By using *[processResponseConsumeBody](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#process-response-end-of-body)*, we have [extracted](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#bodyinit-safely-extract) the entire [body](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-body). This is necessary to ensure the preloader loads the entire body from the network, regardless of whether the preload will be consumed (which is uncertain at this point). This step then resets the request's body to a new body containing the same bytes, so that other specifications can read from it at the time of actual consumption, despite us having already done so once.

    2. Otherwise, set response to a [network error](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-network-error).
    3. Set unsafeEndTime to the [unsafe shared current time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-unsafe-shared-current-time).
    4. If options's [document](#4244-processing-link-headers) is not null, then call reportTiming given options's [document](#4244-processing-link-headers).
    5. If entry's [on response available](#46820-link-type-preload) is null, then set entry's [response](#46820-link-type-preload) to response; otherwise call entry's [on response available](#46820-link-type-preload) given response.
    6. If processResponse is given, then call processResponse with response.

12. Let commit be the following steps given a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document:
    1. If entry's [response](#46820-link-type-preload) is not null, then call reportTiming given document.
    2. Set document's [map of preloaded resources](#46820-link-type-preload)\[key\] to entry.
13. If options's [document](#4244-processing-link-headers) is null, then set options's [on document ready](#4244-processing-link-headers) to commit. Otherwise, call commit with options's [document](#4244-processing-link-headers).

The [fetch and process the linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) steps for this type of linked resource, given a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element el, are:
1. [Update the source set](#48439-updating-the-source-set) for el.
2. Let options be the result of [creating link options](#4244-processing-link-headers) from el.
3. Let destination be the result of [translating](#46820-link-type-preload) the keyword representing the state of el's [`as`](#424-the-link-element) attribute.
4. If destination is null, then return.
5. Set options's [destination](#4244-processing-link-headers) to destination.
6. [Preload](#46820-link-type-preload) options, with the following steps given a [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response:
   1. If response is a [network error](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-network-error), [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) at el. Otherwise, [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`load`](#events) at el.

      > [!warning]
      > The actual browsers' behavior is different from the spec here, and the feasibility of changing the behavior has not yet been investigated. See [issue #1142](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/1142).

The [process a link header](#4244-processing-link-headers) step for this type of link given a [link processing options](#4244-processing-link-headers) options is to [preload](#46820-link-type-preload) options.

##### 4.6.8.21 Link type "`privacy-policy`"

The [`privacy-policy`](#46821-link-type-privacy-policy) keyword may be used with [`link`](#424-the-link-element), [`a`](#451-the-a-element), and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements. This keyword creates a [hyperlink](#461-introduction).

The [`privacy-policy`](#46821-link-type-privacy-policy) keyword indicates that the referenced document contains information about the data collection and usage practices that apply to the current document, as described in more detail in Additional Link Relation Types. The referenced document may be a standalone privacy policy, or a specific section of some more general document. [\[RFC6903\]](#references)

##### 4.6.8.22 Link type "`search`"

The [`search`](#46822-link-type-search) keyword may be used with [`link`](#424-the-link-element), [`a`](#451-the-a-element), [`area`](#4813-the-area-element), and [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements. This keyword creates a [hyperlink](#461-introduction).

The [`search`](#46822-link-type-search) keyword indicates that the referenced document provides an interface specifically for searching the document and its related resources.

> [!note]
> OpenSearch description documents can be used with [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements and the [`search`](#46822-link-type-search) link type to enable user agents to autodiscover search interfaces. [\[OPENSEARCH\]](#references)

##### 4.6.8.23 Link type "`stylesheet`"

The [`stylesheet`](#46823-link-type-stylesheet) keyword may be used with [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements. This keyword creates an [external resource link](#461-introduction) that contributes to the styling processing model. This keyword is [body-ok](#468-link-types).

The specified resource is a [CSS style sheet](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#css-style-sheet) that describes how to present the document.

If the [`alternate`](#4681-link-type-alternate) keyword is also specified on the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element, then the link is an alternative style sheet; in this case, the [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute must be specified on the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element, with a non-empty value.

The default type for resources given by the [`stylesheet`](#46823-link-type-stylesheet) keyword is [`text/css`](#mime-types).

A [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element of this type is [implicitly potentially render-blocking](#258-blocking-attributes) if the element was created by its [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s parser.

When the [`disabled`](#424-the-link-element) attribute of a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element with a [`stylesheet`](#46823-link-type-stylesheet) keyword is set, [disable](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#disable-a-css-style-sheet) the [associated CSS style sheet](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#associated-css-style-sheet).

The appropriate times to [fetch and process](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) this type of link are:
- When the [external resource link](#461-introduction) is created on a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees).
- When the [external resource link](#461-introduction)'s [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element [becomes browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees).
- When the [`href`](#424-the-link-element) attribute of the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element of an [external resource link](#461-introduction) that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees) is changed.
- When the [`disabled`](#424-the-link-element) attribute of the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element of an [external resource link](#461-introduction) that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees) is set, changed, or removed.
- When the [`crossorigin`](#424-the-link-element) attribute of the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element of an [external resource link](#461-introduction) that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees) is set, changed, or removed.
- When the [`type`](#424-the-link-element) attribute of the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element of an [external resource link](#461-introduction) that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees) is set or changed to a value that does not or no longer matches the [Content-Type metadata](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource) of the previous obtained external resource, if any.
- When the [`type`](#424-the-link-element) attribute of the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element of an [external resource link](#461-introduction) that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees), but was previously not obtained due to the [`type`](#424-the-link-element) attribute specifying an unsupported type, is removed or changed.
- When the [external resource link](#461-introduction) that is already [browsing-context connected](#214-dom-trees) changes from being [an alternative style sheet](#46823-link-type-stylesheet) to not being one, or vice versa.

**Quirk**: If the document has been set to [quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), has the [same origin](#711-origins) as the [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) of the external resource, and the [Content-Type metadata](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource) of the external resource is not a supported style sheet type, the user agent must instead assume it to be [`text/css`](#mime-types).

The [linked resource fetch setup steps](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) for this type of linked resource, given a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element el and [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) request, are:
1. If el's [`disabled`](#424-the-link-element) attribute is set, then return false.
2. If el [contributes a script-blocking style sheet](#427-interactions-of-styling-and-scripting), [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) el to its [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [script-blocking style sheet set](#427-interactions-of-styling-and-scripting).
3. If el's [`media`](#424-the-link-element) attribute's value [matches the environment](#2310-media-queries) and el is [potentially render-blocking](#258-blocking-attributes), then [block rendering](#316-render-blocking-mechanism) on el.
4. If el is currently [render-blocking](#316-render-blocking-mechanism), then set request's [render-blocking](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-render-blocking) to true.
5. Return true.

> [!warning]
> See [issue #968](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/968) for plans to use the CSSOM [fetch a CSS style sheet](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#fetching-css-style-sheets) algorithm instead of the [default fetch and process the linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) algorithm. In the meantime, any [critical subresource](#212-resources) [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) should have its [render-blocking](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-render-blocking) set to whether or not the [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element is currently [render-blocking](#316-render-blocking-mechanism).

To [process this type of linked resource](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) given a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element el, boolean success, [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response, and [byte sequence](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-byte-sequences) bodyBytes:
1. If the resource's [Content-Type metadata](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource) is not [`text/css`](#mime-types), then set success to false.
2. If el no longer creates an [external resource link](#461-introduction) that contributes to the styling processing model, or if, since the resource in question was [fetched](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element), it has become appropriate to [fetch](#4243-fetching-and-processing-a-resource-from-a-link-element) it again:
   1. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) el from el's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [script-blocking style sheet set](#427-interactions-of-styling-and-scripting).
   2. Return.
3. If el has an [associated CSS style sheet](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#associated-css-style-sheet), [remove the CSS style sheet](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#remove-a-css-style-sheet).
4. If success is true:
   1. [Create a CSS style sheet](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#create-a-css-style-sheet) with the following properties:

      [type](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-type)

      [`text/css`](#mime-types)

      [location](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-location)

      response's [URL list](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url-list)\[0\]

      > [!warning]
      > We provide a URL here on the assumption that [w3c/csswg-drafts issue #9316](https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/9316) will be fixed.

      [owner node](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-owner-node)

      el

      [media](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-media)

      The [`media`](#424-the-link-element) attribute of el.

      > [!note]
      > This is a reference to the (possibly absent at this time) attribute, rather than a copy of the attribute's current value. CSSOM defines what happens when the attribute is dynamically set, changed, or removed.

      [title](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-title)

      The [`title`](#424-the-link-element) attribute of el, if el is [in a document tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree), or the empty string otherwise.

      > [!note]
      > This is similarly a reference to the attribute, rather than a copy of the attribute's current value.

      [alternate flag](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-alternate-flag)

      Set if [the link is an alternative style sheet](#46823-link-type-stylesheet) and el's [explicitly enabled](#424-the-link-element) is false; unset otherwise.

      [origin-clean flag](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-origin-clean-flag)

      Set if the resource is [CORS-same-origin](#251-terminology); unset otherwise.

      [parent CSS style sheet](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-parent-css-style-sheet)

      [owner CSS rule](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-owner-css-rule)

      null

      [disabled flag](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-disabled-flag)

      Left at its default value.

      [CSS rules](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#concept-css-style-sheet-css-rules)

      Left uninitialized.

      > [!warning]
      > This doesn't seem right. Presumably we should be using bodyBytes? Tracked as [issue #2997](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/2997).

      The CSS [environment encoding](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#environment-encoding) is the result of running the following steps: [\[CSSSYNTAX\]](#references)
      1. If el has a [`charset`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute, [get an encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-encoding-get) from that attribute's value. If that succeeds, return the resulting encoding. [\[ENCODING\]](#references)
      2. Otherwise, return the [document's character encoding](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document). [\[DOM\]](#references)

   2. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`load`](#events) at el.

5. Otherwise, [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) at el.
6. If el [contributes a script-blocking style sheet](#427-interactions-of-styling-and-scripting):
   1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): el's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [script-blocking style sheet set](#427-interactions-of-styling-and-scripting) [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) el.
   2. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) el from its [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [script-blocking style sheet set](#427-interactions-of-styling-and-scripting).
7. [Unblock rendering](#316-render-blocking-mechanism) on el.

The [process a link header](#4244-processing-link-headers) steps for this type of linked resource are to do nothing.

##### 4.6.8.24 Link type "`tag`"

The [`tag`](#46824-link-type-tag) keyword may be used with [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements. This keyword creates a [hyperlink](#461-introduction).

The [`tag`](#46824-link-type-tag) keyword indicates that the *tag* that the referenced document represents applies to the current document.

> [!note]
> Since it indicates that the tag *applies to the current document*, it would be inappropriate to use this keyword in the markup of a [tag cloud](#4142-tag-clouds), which lists the popular tags across a set of pages.

> [!example]
> This document is about some gems, and so it is *tagged* with "`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gemstone`" to unambiguously categorize it as applying to the "jewel" kind of gems, and not to, say, the towns in the US, the Ruby package format, or the Swiss locomotive class:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <html lang="en">
>  <head>
>   <title>My Precious</title>
>  </head>
>  <body>
>   <header><h1>My precious</h1> <p>Summer 2012</p></header>
>   <p>Recently I managed to dispose of a red gem that had been
>   bothering me. I now have a much nicer blue sapphire.</p>
>   <p>The red gem had been found in a bauxite stone while I was digging
>   out the office level, but nobody was willing to haul it away. The
>   same red gem stayed there for literally years.</p>
>   <footer>
>    Tags: <a rel=tag href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gemstone">Gemstone</a>
>   </footer>
>  </body>
> </html>
> ```

> [!example]
> In *this* document, there are two articles. The "[`tag`](#46824-link-type-tag)" link, however, applies to the whole page (and would do so wherever it was placed, including if it was within the [`article`](#432-the-article-element) elements).
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <html lang="en">
>  <head>
>   <title>Gem 4/4</title>
>  </head>
>  <body>
>   <article>
>    <h1>801: Steinbock</h1>
>    <p>The number 801 Gem 4/4 electro-diesel has an ibex and was rebuilt in 2002.</p>
>   </article>
>   <article>
>    <h1>802: Murmeltier</h1>
>    <figure>
>     <img src="https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b0/Trains_de_la_Bernina_en_hiver_2.jpg"
>          alt="The 802 was red with pantographs and tall vents on the side.">
>     <figcaption>The 802 in the 1980s, above Lago Bianco.</figcaption>
>    </figure>
>    <p>The number 802 Gem 4/4 electro-diesel has a marmot and was rebuilt in 2003.</p>
>   </article>
>   <p class="topic"><a rel=tag href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhaetian_Railway_Gem_4/4">Gem 4/4</a></p>
>  </body>
> </html>
> ```

##### 4.6.8.25 Link Type "`terms-of-service`"

The [`terms-of-service`](#46825-link-type-terms-of-service) keyword may be used with [`link`](#424-the-link-element), [`a`](#451-the-a-element), and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements. This keyword creates a [hyperlink](#461-introduction).

The [`terms-of-service`](#46825-link-type-terms-of-service) keyword indicates that the referenced document contains information about the agreements between the current document's provider and users who wish to use the current document, as described in more detail in Additional Link Relation Types. [\[RFC6903\]](#references)

##### 4.6.8.26 Sequential link types

Some documents form part of a sequence of documents.

A sequence of documents is one where each document can have a *previous sibling* and a *next sibling*. A document with no previous sibling is the start of its sequence, a document with no next sibling is the end of its sequence.

A document may be part of multiple sequences.

###### 4.6.8.26.1 Link type "`next`"

The [`next`](#468261-link-type-next) keyword may be used with [`link`](#424-the-link-element), [`a`](#451-the-a-element), [`area`](#4813-the-area-element), and [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements. This keyword creates a [hyperlink](#461-introduction).

The [`next`](#468261-link-type-next) keyword indicates that the document is part of a sequence, and that the link is leading to the document that is the next logical document in the sequence.

When the [`next`](#468261-link-type-next) keyword is used with a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element, user agents should process such links as if they were using one of the [`dns-prefetch`](#4685-link-type-dns-prefetch), [`preconnect`](#46818-link-type-preconnect), or [`prefetch`](#46819-link-type-prefetch) keywords. Which keyword the user agent wishes to use is implementation-dependent; for example, a user agent may wish to use the less-costly [`preconnect`](#46818-link-type-preconnect) processing model when trying to conserve data, battery power, or processing power, or may wish to pick a keyword depending on heuristic analysis of past user behavior in similar scenarios.

###### 4.6.8.26.2 Link type "`prev`"

The [`prev`](#468262-link-type-prev) keyword may be used with [`link`](#424-the-link-element), [`a`](#451-the-a-element), [`area`](#4813-the-area-element), and [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements. This keyword creates a [hyperlink](#461-introduction).

The [`prev`](#468262-link-type-prev) keyword indicates that the document is part of a sequence, and that the link is leading to the document that is the previous logical document in the sequence.

**Synonyms**: For historical reasons, user agents must also treat the keyword "`previous`" like the [`prev`](#468262-link-type-prev) keyword.

##### 4.6.8.27 Other link types

Extensions to the predefined set of link types may be registered on the [microformats page for existing rel values](https://microformats.org/wiki/existing-rel-values#HTML5_link_type_extensions). [\[MFREL\]](#references)

Anyone is free to edit the microformats page for existing rel values at any time to add a type. Extension types must be specified with the following information:

Keyword

The actual value being defined. The value should not be confusingly similar to any other defined value (e.g. differing only in case).

If the value contains a U+003A COLON character (:), it must also be an [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute).

Effect on... [`link`](#424-the-link-element)

One of the following:

Not allowed

The keyword must not be specified on [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements.

Hyperlink

The keyword may be specified on a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element; it creates a [hyperlink](#461-introduction).

External Resource

The keyword may be specified on a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element; it creates an [external resource link](#461-introduction).

Effect on... [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element)

One of the following:

Not allowed

The keyword must not be specified on [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements.

Hyperlink

The keyword may be specified on [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements; it creates a [hyperlink](#461-introduction).

External Resource

The keyword may be specified on [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements; it creates an [external resource link](#461-introduction).

Hyperlink Annotation

The keyword may be specified on [`a`](#451-the-a-element) and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements; it [annotates](#461-introduction) other [hyperlinks](#461-introduction) created by the element.

Effect on... [`form`](#4103-the-form-element)

One of the following:

Not allowed

The keyword must not be specified on [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements.

Hyperlink

The keyword may be specified on [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements; it creates a [hyperlink](#461-introduction).

External Resource

The keyword may be specified on [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements; it creates an [external resource link](#461-introduction).

Hyperlink Annotation

The keyword may be specified on [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements; it [annotates](#461-introduction) other [hyperlinks](#461-introduction) created by the element.

Brief description

A short non-normative description of what the keyword's meaning is.

Specification

A link to a more detailed description of the keyword's semantics and requirements. It could be another page on the wiki, or a link to an external page.

Synonyms

A list of other keyword values that have exactly the same processing requirements. Authors should not use the values defined to be synonyms, they are only intended to allow user agents to support legacy content.
