Anyone may remove synonyms that are not used in practice; only names that need to be processed as synonyms for compatibility with legacy content are to be registered in this way.

Status

One of the following:

Proposed

The keyword has not received wide peer review and approval. Someone has proposed it and is, or soon will be, using it.

Ratified

The keyword has received wide peer review and approval. It has a specification that unambiguously defines how to handle pages that use the keyword, including when they use it in incorrect ways.

Discontinued

The keyword has received wide peer review and it has been found wanting. Existing pages are using this keyword, but new pages should avoid it. The "brief description" and "specification" entries will give details of what authors should use instead, if anything.

If a keyword is found to be redundant with existing values, it should be removed and listed as a synonym for the existing value.

If a keyword is registered in the "proposed" state for a period of a month or more without being used or specified, then it may be removed from the registry.

If a keyword is added with the "proposed" status and found to be redundant with existing values, it should be removed and listed as a synonym for the existing value. If a keyword is added with the "proposed" status and found to be harmful, then it should be changed to "discontinued" status.

Anyone can change the status at any time, but should only do so in accordance with the definitions above.

Conformance checkers must use the information given on the microformats page for existing rel values to establish if a value is allowed or not: values defined in this specification or marked as "proposed" or "ratified" must be accepted when used on the elements for which they apply as described in the "Effect on..." field, whereas values marked as "discontinued" or not listed in either this specification or on the aforementioned page must be rejected as invalid. Conformance checkers may cache this information (e.g. for performance reasons or to avoid the use of unreliable network connectivity).

When an author uses a new type not defined by either this specification or the wiki page, conformance checkers should offer to add the value to the wiki, with the details described above, with the "proposed" status.

Types defined as extensions in the [microformats page for existing rel values](https://microformats.org/wiki/existing-rel-values#HTML5_link_type_extensions) with the status "proposed" or "ratified" may be used with the `rel` attribute on [`link`](#424-the-link-element), [`a`](#451-the-a-element), and [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements in accordance to the "Effect on..." field. [\[MFREL\]](#references)

### 4.7 Edits

The [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element) and [`del`](#472-the-del-element) elements represent edits to the document.

#### 4.7.1 The `ins` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Transparent](#3253-transparent-content-models).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`cite`](#473-attributes-common-to-ins-and-del-elements) — Link to the source of the quotation or more information about the edit

[`datetime`](#473-attributes-common-to-ins-and-del-elements) — Date and (optionally) time of the change

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-ins).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-ins).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants) with attributes [`cite`](#473-attributes-common-to-ins-and-del-elements), [`datetime`](#473-attributes-common-to-ins-and-del-elements).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

Uses [`HTMLModElement`](#473-attributes-common-to-ins-and-del-elements).

The [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) an addition to the document.

> [!example]
> The following represents the addition of a single paragraph:
> 
> ```html
> <aside>
>  <ins>
>   <p> I like fruit. </p>
>  </ins>
> </aside>
> ```
> 
> As does the following, because everything in the [`aside`](#435-the-aside-element) element here counts as [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) and therefore there is just one [paragraph](#3254-paragraphs):
> 
> ```html
> <aside>
>  <ins>
>   Apples are <em>tasty</em>.
>  </ins>
>  <ins>
>   So are pears.
>  </ins>
> </aside>
> ```

[`ins`](#471-the-ins-element) elements should not cross [implied paragraph](#3254-paragraphs) boundaries.

> [!example]
> The following example represents the addition of two paragraphs, the second of which was inserted in two parts. The first [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element) element in this example thus crosses a paragraph boundary, which is considered poor form.
> 
> ```html
> <aside>
>  <!-- don't do this -->
>  <ins datetime="2005-03-16 00:00Z">
>   <p> I like fruit. </p>
>   Apples are <em>tasty</em>.
>  </ins>
>  <ins datetime="2007-12-19 00:00Z">
>   So are pears.
>  </ins>
> </aside>
> ```
> 
> Here is a better way of marking this up. It uses more elements, but none of the elements cross implied paragraph boundaries.
> 
> ```html
> <aside>
>  <ins datetime="2005-03-16 00:00Z">
>   <p> I like fruit. </p>
>  </ins>
>  <ins datetime="2005-03-16 00:00Z">
>   Apples are <em>tasty</em>.
>  </ins>
>  <ins datetime="2007-12-19 00:00Z">
>   So are pears.
>  </ins>
> </aside>
> ```

#### 4.7.2 The `del` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Transparent](#3253-transparent-content-models).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`cite`](#473-attributes-common-to-ins-and-del-elements) — Link to the source of the quotation or more information about the edit

[`datetime`](#473-attributes-common-to-ins-and-del-elements) — Date and (optionally) time of the change

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-del).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-del).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants) with attributes [`cite`](#473-attributes-common-to-ins-and-del-elements), [`datetime`](#473-attributes-common-to-ins-and-del-elements).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

Uses [`HTMLModElement`](#473-attributes-common-to-ins-and-del-elements).

The [`del`](#472-the-del-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a removal from the document.

[`del`](#472-the-del-element) elements should not cross [implied paragraph](#3254-paragraphs) boundaries.

> [!example]
> The following shows a "to do" list where items that have been done are crossed-off with the date and time of their completion.
> 
> ```html
> <h1>To Do</h1>
> <ul>
>  <li>Empty the dishwasher</li>
>  <li><del datetime="2009-10-11T01:25-07:00">Watch Walter Lewin's lectures</del></li>
>  <li><del datetime="2009-10-10T23:38-07:00">Download more tracks</del></li>
>  <li>Buy a printer</li>
> </ul>
> ```

#### 4.7.3 Attributes common to [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element) and [`del`](#472-the-del-element) elements

The `cite` attribute may be used to specify the [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) of a document that explains the change. When that document is long, for instance the minutes of a meeting, authors are encouraged to include a [fragment](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment) pointing to the specific part of that document that discusses the change.

If the [`cite`](#473-attributes-common-to-ins-and-del-elements) attribute is present, it must be a [valid URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#241-terminology) that explains the change. To obtain the corresponding citation link, the value of the attribute must be [parsed](#242-parsing-urls) relative to the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node). User agents may allow users to follow such citation links, but they are primarily intended for private use (e.g., by server-side scripts collecting statistics about a site's edits), not for readers.

The `datetime` attribute may be used to specify the time and date of the change.

If present, the [`datetime`](#473-attributes-common-to-ins-and-del-elements) attribute's value must be a [valid date string with optional time](#23510-vaguer-moments-in-time).

User agents must parse the [`datetime`](#473-attributes-common-to-ins-and-del-elements) attribute according to the [parse a date or time string](#23510-vaguer-moments-in-time) algorithm. If that doesn't return a [date](#2352-dates) or a [global date and time](#2357-global-dates-and-times), then the modification has no associated timestamp (the value is non-conforming; it is not a [valid date string with optional time](#23510-vaguer-moments-in-time)). Otherwise, the modification is marked as having been made at the given [date](#2352-dates) or [global date and time](#2357-global-dates-and-times). If the given value is a [global date and time](#2357-global-dates-and-times), then user agents should use the associated time-zone offset information to determine which time zone to present the given datetime in.

This value may be shown to the user, but it is primarily intended for private use.

The [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element) and [`del`](#472-the-del-element) elements must implement the [`HTMLModElement`](#473-attributes-common-to-ins-and-del-elements) interface:

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLModElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, ReflectURL] attribute USVString cite;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString dateTime;
};
```

#### 4.7.4 Edits and paragraphs

*This section is non-normative.*

Since the [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element) and [`del`](#472-the-del-element) elements do not affect [paragraphing](#3254-paragraphs), it is possible, in some cases where paragraphs are [implied](#3254-paragraphs) (without explicit [`p`](#441-the-p-element) elements), for an [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element) or [`del`](#472-the-del-element) element to span both an entire paragraph or other non-[phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) elements and part of another paragraph. For example:

```html
<section>
 <ins>
  <p>
   This is a paragraph that was inserted.
  </p>
  This is another paragraph whose first sentence was inserted
  at the same time as the paragraph above.
 </ins>
 This is a second sentence, which was there all along.
</section>
```

By only wrapping some paragraphs in [`p`](#441-the-p-element) elements, one can even get the end of one paragraph, a whole second paragraph, and the start of a third paragraph to be covered by the same [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element) or [`del`](#472-the-del-element) element (though this is very confusing, and not considered good practice):

```html
<section>
 This is the first paragraph. <ins>This sentence was
 inserted.
 <p>This second paragraph was inserted.</p>
 This sentence was inserted too.</ins> This is the
 third paragraph in this example.
 <!-- (don't do this) -->
</section>
```

However, due to the way [implied paragraphs](#3254-paragraphs) are defined, it is not possible to mark up the end of one paragraph and the start of the very next one using the same [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element) or [`del`](#472-the-del-element) element. You instead have to use one (or two) [`p`](#441-the-p-element) element(s) and two [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element) or [`del`](#472-the-del-element) elements, as for example:

```html
<section>
 <p>This is the first paragraph. <del>This sentence was
 deleted.</del></p>
 <p><del>This sentence was deleted too.</del> That
 sentence needed a separate &lt;del&gt; element.</p>
</section>
```

Partly because of the confusion described above, authors are strongly encouraged to always mark up all paragraphs with the [`p`](#441-the-p-element) element, instead of having [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element) or [`del`](#472-the-del-element) elements that cross [implied paragraphs](#3254-paragraphs) boundaries.

#### 4.7.5 Edits and lists

*This section is non-normative.*

The content models of the [`ol`](#445-the-ol-element) and [`ul`](#446-the-ul-element) elements do not allow [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element) and [`del`](#472-the-del-element) elements as children. Lists always represent all their items, including items that would otherwise have been marked as deleted.

To indicate that an item is inserted or deleted, an [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element) or [`del`](#472-the-del-element) element can be wrapped around the contents of the [`li`](#448-the-li-element) element. To indicate that an item has been replaced by another, a single [`li`](#448-the-li-element) element can have one or more [`del`](#472-the-del-element) elements followed by one or more [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element) elements.

> [!example]
> In the following example, a list that started empty had items added and removed from it over time. The bits in the example that have been emphasized show the parts that are the "current" state of the list. The list item numbers don't take into account the edits, though.
> 
> ```html
> <h1>Stop-ship bugs</h1>
> <ol>
>  <li><ins datetime="2008-02-12T15:20Z">Bug 225:
>  Rain detector doesn't work in snow</ins></li>
>  <li><del datetime="2008-03-01T20:22Z"><ins datetime="2008-02-14T12:02Z">Bug 228:
>  Water buffer overflows in April</ins></del></li>
>  <li><ins datetime="2008-02-16T13:50Z">Bug 230:
>  Water heater doesn't use renewable fuels</ins></li>
>  <li><del datetime="2008-02-20T21:15Z"><ins datetime="2008-02-16T14:25Z">Bug 232:
>  Carbon dioxide emissions detected after startup</ins></del></li>
> </ol>
> ```

> [!example]
> In the following example, a list that started with just fruit was replaced by a list with just colors.
> 
> ```html
> <h1>List of <del>fruits</del><ins>colors</ins></h1>
> <ul>
>  <li><del>Lime</del><ins>Green</ins></li>
>  <li><del>Apple</del></li>
>  <li>Orange</li>
>  <li><del>Pear</del></li>
>  <li><ins>Teal</ins></li>
>  <li><del>Lemon</del><ins>Yellow</ins></li>
>  <li>Olive</li>
>  <li><ins>Purple</ins></li>
> </ul>
> ```

#### 4.7.6 Edits and tables

*This section is non-normative.*

The elements that form part of the table model have complicated content model requirements that do not allow for the [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element) and [`del`](#472-the-del-element) elements, so indicating edits to a table can be difficult.

To indicate that an entire row or an entire column has been added or removed, the entire contents of each cell in that row or column can be wrapped in [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element) or [`del`](#472-the-del-element) elements (respectively).

> [!example]
> Here, a table's row has been added:
> 
> ```html
> <table>
>  <thead>
>   <tr> <th> Game name           <th> Game publisher   <th> Verdict
>  <tbody>
>   <tr> <td> Diablo 2            <td> Blizzard         <td> 8/10
>   <tr> <td> Portal              <td> Valve            <td> 10/10
>   <tr> <td> <ins>Portal 2</ins> <td> <ins>Valve</ins> <td> <ins>10/10</ins>
> </table>
> ```
> 
> Here, a column has been removed (the time at which it was removed is given also, as is a link to the page explaining why):
> 
> ```html
> <table>
>  <thead>
>   <tr> <th> Game name           <th> Game publisher   <th> <del cite="/edits/r192" datetime="2011-05-02 14:23Z">Verdict</del>
>  <tbody>
>   <tr> <td> Diablo 2            <td> Blizzard         <td> <del cite="/edits/r192" datetime="2011-05-02 14:23Z">8/10</del>
>   <tr> <td> Portal              <td> Valve            <td> <del cite="/edits/r192" datetime="2011-05-02 14:23Z">10/10</del>
>   <tr> <td> Portal 2            <td> Valve            <td> <del cite="/edits/r192" datetime="2011-05-02 14:23Z">10/10</del>
> </table>
> ```

Generally speaking, there is no good way to indicate more complicated edits (e.g. that a cell was removed, moving all subsequent cells up or to the left).

### 4.8 Embedded content

#### 4.8.1 The `picture` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Embedded content](#32526-embedded-content).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [embedded content](#32526-embedded-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

Zero or more [`source`](#482-the-source-element) elements, followed by one [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element, optionally intermixed with [script-supporting elements](#32529-script-supporting-elements).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-picture).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-picture).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLPictureElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();
};
```

The [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element is a container which provides multiple sources to its contained [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element to allow authors to declaratively control or give hints to the user agent about which image resource to use, based on the screen pixel density, [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) size, image format, and other factors. It [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) its children.

> [!note]
> The [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element is somewhat different from the similar-looking [`video`](#488-the-video-element) and [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) elements. While all of them contain [`source`](#482-the-source-element) elements, the [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element's [`src`](#482-the-source-element) attribute has no meaning when the element is nested within a [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element, and the resource selection algorithm is different. Also, the [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element itself does not display anything; it merely provides a context for its contained [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element that enables it to choose from multiple [URLs](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url).

#### 4.8.2 The `source` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

As a child of a [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element, before the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element.

As a child of a [media element](#4811-media-elements), before any [flow content](#32522-flow-content) or [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) elements.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Nothing](#3251-the-nothing-content-model).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

No [end tag](#13122-end-tags).

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`type`](#482-the-source-element) — Type of embedded resource

[`media`](#482-the-source-element) — Applicable media

[`src`](#482-the-source-element) (in [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) or [`video`](#488-the-video-element)) — Address of the resource

[`srcset`](#482-the-source-element) (in [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element)) — Images to use in different situations, e.g., high-resolution displays, small monitors, etc.

[`sizes`](#482-the-source-element) (in [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element)) — Image sizes for different page layouts

[`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes) (in [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element)) — Horizontal dimension

[`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes) (in [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element)) — Vertical dimension

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-source).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-source).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLSourceElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, ReflectURL] attribute USVString src;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString type;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute USVString srcset;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString sizes;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString media;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute unsigned long width;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute unsigned long height;
};
```

The [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element allows authors to specify multiple alternative [source sets](#4843-processing-model) for [`img`](#483-the-img-element) elements or multiple alternative [media resources](#4811-media-elements) for [media elements](#4811-media-elements). It does not [represent](#322-elements-in-the-dom) anything on its own.

The `type` attribute may be present. If present, the value must be a [valid MIME type string](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-mime-type).

The `media` attribute may also be present. If present, the value must contain a [valid media query list](#2310-media-queries). The user agent will skip to the next [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element if the value does not [match the environment](#2310-media-queries).

> [!note]
> The [`media`](#482-the-source-element) attribute is only evaluated once during the [resource selection algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) for [media elements](#4811-media-elements). In contrast, when using the [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element, the user agent will [react to changes in the environment](#484313-reacting-to-environment-changes).

The remainder of the requirements depend on whether the parent is a [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element or a [media element](#4811-media-elements):

The [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element's parent is a [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element

The `srcset` attribute must be present, and is a [srcset attribute](#48421-srcset-attributes).

The [`srcset`](#482-the-source-element) attribute contributes the [image sources](#4843-processing-model) to the [source set](#4843-processing-model), if the [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element is selected.

If the [`srcset`](#482-the-source-element) attribute has any [image candidate strings](#48421-srcset-attributes) using a [width descriptor](#48421-srcset-attributes), the [`sizes`](#482-the-source-element) attribute may also be present. If, additionally, the following sibling [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element does not [allow auto-sizes](#483-the-img-element), the [`sizes`](#482-the-source-element) attribute must be present. The `sizes` attribute is a [sizes attribute](#48422-sizes-attributes), which contributes the [source size](#4843-processing-model) to the [source set](#4843-processing-model), if the [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element is selected.

> [!note]
> If the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element [allows auto-sizes](#483-the-img-element), then the [`sizes`](#482-the-source-element) attribute can be omitted on previous sibling [`source`](#482-the-source-element) elements. In such cases, it is equivalent to specifying [`auto`](#48422-sizes-attributes).

The [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element supports [dimension attributes](#4817-dimension-attributes). The [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element can use the [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes) and [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes) attributes of a [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element, instead of those on the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element itself, to determine its rendered dimensions and aspect-ratio, [as defined in the Rendering section](#1543-attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images).

The [`type`](#482-the-source-element) attribute gives the type of the images in the [source set](#4843-processing-model), to allow the user agent to skip to the next [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element if it does not support the given type.

> [!note]
> If the [`type`](#482-the-source-element) attribute is *not* specified, the user agent will not select a different [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element if it finds that it does not support the image format after fetching it.

When a [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element has a following sibling [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element or [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element with a [`srcset`](#483-the-img-element) attribute specified, it must have at least one of the following:
- A [`media`](#482-the-source-element) attribute specified with a value that, after [stripping leading and trailing ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings), is not the empty string and is not an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`all`".
- A [`type`](#482-the-source-element) attribute specified.

The [`src`](#482-the-source-element) attribute must not be present.

The [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element's parent is a [media element](#4811-media-elements)

The `src` attribute gives the [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements). The value must be a [valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#241-terminology). This attribute must be present.

The [`type`](#482-the-source-element) attribute gives the type of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements), to help the user agent determine if it can play this [media resource](#4811-media-elements) before fetching it. The `codecs` parameter, which certain MIME types define, might be necessary to specify exactly how the resource is encoded. [\[RFC6381\]](#references)

> [!note]
> Dynamically modifying a [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element's [`src`](#482-the-source-element) or [`type`](#482-the-source-element) attribute when the element is already inserted in a [`video`](#488-the-video-element) or [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) element will have no effect. To change what is playing, just use the [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) attribute on the [media element](#4811-media-elements) directly, possibly making use of the [`canPlayType()`](#48113-mime-types) method to pick from amongst available resources. Generally, manipulating [`source`](#482-the-source-element) elements manually after the document has been parsed is an unnecessarily complicated approach.

> [!example]
> The following list shows some examples of how to use the `codecs=` MIME parameter in the [`type`](#482-the-source-element) attribute.
> 
> H.264 Constrained baseline profile video (main and extended video compatible) level 3 and Low-Complexity AAC audio in MP4 container
> 
> ```html
> <source src='video.mp4' type='video/mp4; codecs="avc1.42E01E, mp4a.40.2"'>
> ```
> 
> H.264 Extended profile video (baseline-compatible) level 3 and Low-Complexity AAC audio in MP4 container
> 
> ```html
> <source src='video.mp4' type='video/mp4; codecs="avc1.58A01E, mp4a.40.2"'>
> ```
> 
> H.264 Main profile video level 3 and Low-Complexity AAC audio in MP4 container
> 
> ```html
> <source src='video.mp4' type='video/mp4; codecs="avc1.4D401E, mp4a.40.2"'>
> ```
> 
> H.264 'High' profile video (incompatible with main, baseline, or extended profiles) level 3 and Low-Complexity AAC audio in MP4 container
> 
> ```html
> <source src='video.mp4' type='video/mp4; codecs="avc1.64001E, mp4a.40.2"'>
> ```
> 
> MPEG-4 Visual Simple Profile Level 0 video and Low-Complexity AAC audio in MP4 container
> 
> ```html
> <source src='video.mp4' type='video/mp4; codecs="mp4v.20.8, mp4a.40.2"'>
> ```
> 
> MPEG-4 Advanced Simple Profile Level 0 video and Low-Complexity AAC audio in MP4 container
> 
> ```html
> <source src='video.mp4' type='video/mp4; codecs="mp4v.20.240, mp4a.40.2"'>
> ```
> 
> MPEG-4 Visual Simple Profile Level 0 video and AMR audio in 3GPP container
> 
> ```html
> <source src='video.3gp' type='video/3gpp; codecs="mp4v.20.8, samr"'>
> ```
> 
> Theora video and Vorbis audio in Ogg container
> 
> ```html
> <source src='video.ogv' type='video/ogg; codecs="theora, vorbis"'>
> ```
> 
> Theora video and Speex audio in Ogg container
> 
> ```html
> <source src='video.ogv' type='video/ogg; codecs="theora, speex"'>
> ```
> 
> Vorbis audio alone in Ogg container
> 
> ```html
> <source src='audio.ogg' type='audio/ogg; codecs=vorbis'>
> ```
> 
> Speex audio alone in Ogg container
> 
> ```html
> <source src='audio.spx' type='audio/ogg; codecs=speex'>
> ```
> 
> FLAC audio alone in Ogg container
> 
> ```html
> <source src='audio.oga' type='audio/ogg; codecs=flac'>
> ```
> 
> Dirac video and Vorbis audio in Ogg container
> 
> ```html
> <source src='video.ogv' type='video/ogg; codecs="dirac, vorbis"'>
> ```

The [`srcset`](#482-the-source-element) and [`sizes`](#482-the-source-element) attributes must not be present.

The [`source`](#482-the-source-element) [HTML element insertion steps](#214-dom-trees), given insertedNode, are:
1. Let parent be insertedNode's [parent](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
2. If parent is a [media element](#4811-media-elements) that has no [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) attribute and whose [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) has the value [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#48114-network-states), then invoke that [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [resource selection algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource).
3. If parent is a [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element, then [for each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) child of parent's [children](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), if child is an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element, then count this as a [relevant mutation](#48432-reacting-to-dom-mutations) for child.

The [`source`](#482-the-source-element) [HTML element moving steps](#214-dom-trees), given movedNode, isSubtreeRoot, and oldAncestor are:
1. If movedNode's [parent](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) is a [media element](#4811-media-elements) that has no [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) attribute and whose [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) has the value [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#48114-network-states), then invoke that [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [resource selection algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource).
2. If isSubtreeRoot is true and oldAncestor is a [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element, then [for each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) child of oldAncestor's [children](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees): if child is an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element, then count this as a [relevant mutation](#48432-reacting-to-dom-mutations) for child.

The [`source`](#482-the-source-element) [HTML element removing steps](#214-dom-trees), given removedNode, isSubtreeRoot, and oldAncestor are:
1. If isSubtreeRoot is true and oldAncestor is a [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element, then [for each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) child of oldAncestor's [children](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees): if child is an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element, then count this as a [relevant mutation](#48432-reacting-to-dom-mutations) for child.

> [!example]
> If the author isn't sure if user agents will all be able to render the media resources provided, the author can listen to the [`error`](#events) event on the last [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element and trigger fallback behavior:
> 
> ```html
> <script>
>  function fallback(video) {
>    // replace <video> with its contents
>    while (video.hasChildNodes()) {
>      if (video.firstChild instanceof HTMLSourceElement)
>        video.removeChild(video.firstChild);
>      else
>        video.parentNode.insertBefore(video.firstChild, video);
>    }
>    video.parentNode.removeChild(video);
>  }
> </script>
> <video controls autoplay>
>  <source src='video.mp4' type='video/mp4; codecs="avc1.42E01E, mp4a.40.2"'>
>  <source src='video.ogv' type='video/ogg; codecs="theora, vorbis"'
>          onerror="fallback(parentNode)">
>  ...
> </video>
> ```

#### 4.8.3 The `img` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Embedded content](#32526-embedded-content).

[Form-associated element](#4102-categories).

If the element has a [`usemap`](#48141-authoring) or [`controls`](#483-the-img-element) attribute: [Interactive content](#32527-interactive-content).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [embedded content](#32526-embedded-content) is expected.

As a child of a [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element, after all [`source`](#482-the-source-element) elements.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Nothing](#3251-the-nothing-content-model).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

No [end tag](#13122-end-tags).

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`alt`](#483-the-img-element) — Replacement text for use when images are not available

[`src`](#483-the-img-element) — Address of the resource

[`srcset`](#483-the-img-element) — Images to use in different situations, e.g., high-resolution displays, small monitors, etc.

[`sizes`](#483-the-img-element) — Image sizes for different page layouts

[`crossorigin`](#483-the-img-element) — How the element handles crossorigin requests

[`usemap`](#48141-authoring) — Name of [image map](#48141-authoring) to use

[`ismap`](#483-the-img-element) — Whether the image is a server-side image map

[`controls`](#483-the-img-element) — Show user agent controls

[`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes) — Horizontal dimension

[`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes) — Vertical dimension

[`referrerpolicy`](#483-the-img-element) — [Referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy) for [fetches](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) initiated by the element

[`decoding`](#483-the-img-element) — Decoding hint to use when processing this image for presentation

[`loading`](#483-the-img-element) — Used when determining loading deferral

[`fetchpriority`](#483-the-img-element) — Sets the [priority](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-priority) for [fetches](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) initiated by the element

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

If the element has a non-empty [`alt`](#483-the-img-element) attribute: [for authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-img); [for implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-img).

Otherwise: [for authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-img-empty-alt); [for implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-img-empty-alt).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window,
 LegacyFactoryFunction=Image(optional unsigned long width, optional unsigned long height)]
interface HTMLImageElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString alt;
  [CEReactions, ReflectURL] attribute USVString src;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute USVString srcset;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString sizes;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString? crossOrigin;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString useMap;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean isMap;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean controls;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute unsigned long width;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute unsigned long height;
  readonly attribute unsigned long naturalWidth;
  readonly attribute unsigned long naturalHeight;
  readonly attribute boolean complete;
  readonly attribute USVString currentSrc;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString referrerPolicy;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString decoding;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString loading;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString fetchPriority;

  Promise<undefined> decode();

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

An [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element represents an image.

An [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element has a dimension attribute source, initially set to the element itself.

The image given by the `src` and `srcset` attributes, and any previous sibling [`source`](#482-the-source-element) elements' [`srcset`](#482-the-source-element) attributes if the parent is a [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element, is the embedded content; the value of the `alt` attribute provides equivalent content for those who cannot process images or who have image loading disabled (i.e., it is the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [fallback content](#32526-embedded-content)).

The requirements on the [`alt`](#483-the-img-element) attribute's value are described [in a separate section](#4844-requirements-for-providing-text-to-act-as-an-alternative-for-images).

At least one of the [`src`](#483-the-img-element) and [`srcset`](#483-the-img-element) attributes must be present.

If the [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute is present, it must contain a [valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#241-terminology) referencing a non-interactive, optionally animated, image resource that is neither paged nor scripted.

> [!note]
> The requirements above imply that images can be static bitmaps (e.g. PNGs, GIFs, JPEGs), single-page vector documents (single-page PDFs, XML files with an SVG document element), animated bitmaps (APNGs, animated GIFs), animated vector graphics (XML files with an SVG [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) that use declarative SMIL animation), and so forth. However, these definitions preclude SVG files with script, multipage PDF files, interactive MNG files, HTML documents, plain text documents, and the like. [\[PNG\]](#references) [\[GIF\]](#references) [\[JPEG\]](#references) [\[PDF\]](#references) [\[XML\]](#references) [\[APNG\]](#references) [\[SVG\]](#references) [\[MNG\]](#references)

The [`srcset`](#483-the-img-element) attribute is a [srcset attribute](#48421-srcset-attributes).

The [`srcset`](#483-the-img-element) attribute and the [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute (if [width descriptors](#48421-srcset-attributes) are not used) contribute the [image sources](#4843-processing-model) to the [source set](#4843-processing-model) (if no [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element was selected).

If the [`srcset`](#483-the-img-element) attribute is present and has any [image candidate strings](#48421-srcset-attributes) using a [width descriptor](#48421-srcset-attributes), the [`sizes`](#483-the-img-element) attribute must also be present. If the [`srcset`](#483-the-img-element) attribute is *not* specified, and the [`loading`](#483-the-img-element) attribute is in the [Lazy](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) state, the [`sizes`](#483-the-img-element) attribute may be specified with the value "`auto`" ([ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings)). The `sizes` attribute is a [sizes attribute](#48422-sizes-attributes), which contributes the [source size](#4843-processing-model) to the [source set](#4843-processing-model) (if no [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element was selected).

An [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element allows auto-sizes if:
- its [`loading`](#483-the-img-element) attribute is in the [Lazy](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) state, and
- its [`sizes`](#483-the-img-element) attribute's value is "`auto`" ([ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings)), or starts with "`auto,`" ([ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings)).

The `crossorigin` attribute is a [CORS settings attribute](#254-cors-settings-attributes). Its purpose is to allow images from third-party sites that allow cross-origin access to be used with [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element).

The `referrerpolicy` attribute is a [referrer policy attribute](#255-referrer-policy-attributes). Its purpose is to set the [referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy) used when [fetching](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) the image. [\[REFERRERPOLICY\]](#references)

The `decoding` attribute indicates the preferred method to [decode](#48434-decoding-images) this image. The attribute, if present, must be an [image decoding hint](#48434-decoding-images). This attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the [Auto](#48434-decoding-images) state.

The `fetchpriority` attribute is a [fetch priority attribute](#259-fetch-priority-attributes). Its purpose is to set the [priority](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-priority) used when [fetching](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) the image.

The `loading` attribute is a [lazy loading attribute](#257-lazy-loading-attributes). Its purpose is to indicate the policy for loading images that are outside the viewport.

When the [`loading`](#483-the-img-element) attribute's state is changed to the [Eager](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) state, the user agent must run these steps:
1. Let resumptionSteps be the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [lazy load resumption steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes).
2. If resumptionSteps is null, then return.
3. Set the [`img`](#483-the-img-element)'s [lazy load resumption steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) to null.
4. Invoke resumptionSteps.

> [!example]
> ```html
> <img src="1.jpeg" alt="1">
> <img src="2.jpeg" loading=eager alt="2">
> <img src="3.jpeg" loading=lazy alt="3">
> <div id=very-large></div> <!-- Everything after this div is below the viewport -->
> <img src="4.jpeg" alt="4">
> <img src="5.jpeg" loading=lazy alt="5">
> ```
> 
> In the example above, the images load as follows:
> 
> `1.jpeg`, `2.jpeg`, `4.jpeg`
> 
> The images load eagerly and delay the window's load event.
> 
> `3.jpeg`
> 
> The image loads when layout is known, due to being in the viewport, however it does not delay the window's load event.
> 
> `5.jpeg`
> 
> The image loads only once scrolled into the viewport, and does not delay the window's load event.
> 
> > [!note]
> > Developers are encouraged to specify a preferred aspect ratio via [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes) and [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes) attributes on lazy loaded images, even if CSS sets the image's width and height properties, to prevent the page layout from shifting around after the image loads.

The [`img`](#483-the-img-element) [HTML element insertion steps](#214-dom-trees), given insertedNode, are:
1. If insertedNode's parent is a [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element, then, count this as a [relevant mutation](#48432-reacting-to-dom-mutations) for insertedNode.

The [`img`](#483-the-img-element) [HTML element moving steps](#214-dom-trees), given movedNode, isSubtreeRoot, and oldAncestor are:
1. If isSubtreeRoot is true and oldAncestor is a [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element, then count this as a [relevant mutation](#48432-reacting-to-dom-mutations) for movedNode.

The [`img`](#483-the-img-element) [HTML element removing steps](#214-dom-trees), given removedNode, isSubtreeRoot, and oldAncestor are:
1. If isSubtreeRoot is true and oldAncestor is a [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element, then count this as a [relevant mutation](#48432-reacting-to-dom-mutations) for removedNode.
2. Set removedNode's [last auto-sizes width](#4843-processing-model) to null.

---

The [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element must not be used as a layout tool. In particular, [`img`](#483-the-img-element) elements should not be used to display transparent images, as such images rarely convey meaning and rarely add anything useful to the document.

---

What an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element represents depends on the [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute and the [`alt`](#483-the-img-element) attribute.

If the [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute is set and the [`alt`](#483-the-img-element) attribute is set to the empty string

The image is either decorative or supplemental to the rest of the content, redundant with some other information in the document.

If the image is [available](#4843-processing-model) and the user agent is configured to display that image, then the element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the element's image data.

Otherwise, the element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) nothing, and may be omitted completely from the rendering. User agents may provide the user with a notification that an image is present but has been omitted from the rendering.

If the [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute is set and the [`alt`](#483-the-img-element) attribute is set to a value that isn't empty

The image is a key part of the content; the [`alt`](#483-the-img-element) attribute gives a textual equivalent or replacement for the image.

If the image is [available](#4843-processing-model) and the user agent is configured to display that image, then the element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the element's image data.

Otherwise, the element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the text given by the [`alt`](#483-the-img-element) attribute. User agents may provide the user with a notification that an image is present but has been omitted from the rendering.

If the [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute is set and the [`alt`](#483-the-img-element) attribute is not

The image might be a key part of the content, and there is no textual equivalent of the image available.

> [!note]
> In a conforming document, the absence of the [`alt`](#483-the-img-element) attribute indicates that the image is a key part of the content but that a textual replacement for the image was not available when the image was generated.

If the image is [available](#4843-processing-model) and the user agent is configured to display that image, then the element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the element's image data.

If the image has a [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute whose value is the empty string, then the element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) nothing.

Otherwise, the user agent should display some sort of indicator that there is an image that is not being rendered, and may, if requested by the user, or if so configured, or when required to provide contextual information in response to navigation, provide caption information for the image, derived as follows:
1. If the image has a [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute whose value is not the empty string, then return the value of that attribute.
2. If the image is a descendant of a [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element) element that has a child [`figcaption`](#4413-the-figcaption-element) element, and, ignoring the [`figcaption`](#4413-the-figcaption-element) element and its descendants, the [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element) element has no [flow content](#32522-flow-content) descendants other than [inter-element whitespace](#325-content-models) and the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element, then return the contents of the first such [`figcaption`](#4413-the-figcaption-element) element.
3. Return nothing. (There is no caption information.)

If the [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute is not set and either the [`alt`](#483-the-img-element) attribute is set to the empty string or the [`alt`](#483-the-img-element) attribute is not set at all

The element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) nothing.

Otherwise

The element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the text given by the [`alt`](#483-the-img-element) attribute.

The [`alt`](#483-the-img-element) attribute does not represent advisory information. User agents must not present the contents of the [`alt`](#483-the-img-element) attribute in the same way as content of the [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute.

User agents may always provide the user with the option to display any image, or to prevent any image from being displayed. User agents may also apply heuristics to help the user make use of the image when the user is unable to see it, e.g. due to a visual disability or because they are using a text terminal with no graphics capabilities. Such heuristics could include, for instance, optical character recognition (OCR) of text found within the image.

> [!warning]
> While user agents are encouraged to repair cases of missing [`alt`](#483-the-img-element) attributes, authors must not rely on such behavior. [Requirements for providing text to act as an alternative for images](#4844-requirements-for-providing-text-to-act-as-an-alternative-for-images) are described in detail below.

The *contents* of [`img`](#483-the-img-element) elements, if any, are ignored for the purposes of rendering.

---

The [`usemap`](#48141-authoring) attribute, if present, can indicate that the image has an associated [image map](#48141-authoring).

The `ismap` attribute, when used on an element that is a descendant of an [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element with an [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute, indicates by its presence that the element provides access to a server-side image map. This affects how events are handled on the corresponding [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element.

The [`ismap`](#483-the-img-element) attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes). The attribute must not be specified on an element that does not have an ancestor [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element with an [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute.

> [!note]
> The [`usemap`](#48141-authoring) and [`ismap`](#483-the-img-element) attributes can result in confusing behavior when used together with [`source`](#482-the-source-element) elements with the [`media`](#482-the-source-element) attribute specified in a [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element.

The `controls` attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes). If present, it indicates that the user agent may expose a user interface to the user. The attribute must not be specified on an element that does not have an [`alt`](#483-the-img-element) attribute, or whose [`alt`](#483-the-img-element) attribute's value is the empty string.

If the [`controls`](#483-the-img-element) attribute is present, the user agent may expose controls over the image (e.g., a control for fullscreen viewing). The specific controls provided are [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology), and can be platform-specific or based on the user's preferences.

If the user agent exposes a user interface by displaying controls over the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element, then the user agent should suppress any user interaction events while the user agent is interacting with this interface.

> [!warning]
> [Issue #12318](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/12318) tracks the interaction between image controls and animated images. User agents should not expose animation controls for images before that issue is resolved.

---

The [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element supports [dimension attributes](#4817-dimension-attributes).

The `crossOrigin` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`crossorigin`](#483-the-img-element) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

The `referrerPolicy` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`referrerpolicy`](#483-the-img-element) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

The `decoding` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`decoding`](#483-the-img-element) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

The `loading` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`loading`](#483-the-img-element) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

The `fetchPriority` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`fetchpriority`](#483-the-img-element) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

`image.width [ = value ]`

`image.height [ = value ]`

These attributes return the rendered dimensions of the image. When the image is not being rendered, they return the [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes) and [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes) content attributes' values, defaulting to [`naturalWidth`](#483-the-img-element) and [`naturalHeight`](#483-the-img-element).

They can be set, to change the corresponding content attributes.

`image.naturalWidth`

`image.naturalHeight`

These attributes return the [density-corrected natural width and height](#4843-processing-model) of the image, or 0 if the image is not *[available](#4843-processing-model)*.

`image.complete`

Returns true if the image has been completely downloaded or if no image is specified; otherwise, returns false.

`image.currentSrc`

Returns the image's [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute).

`image.decode()`

This method causes the user agent to [decode](#48434-decoding-images) the image [in parallel](#211-parallelism), returning a promise that fulfills when decoding is complete.

The promise will be rejected with an ["`EncodingError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#encodingerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the image cannot be decoded.

`image = new Image([ width [, height ] ])`

Returns a new [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element, with the [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes) and [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes) attributes set to the values passed in the relevant arguments, if applicable.

To determine the dimensions of an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element image:
1. Let naturalDimensions be null.
2. If image is *[available](#4843-processing-model)*, then set naturalDimensions to image's [density-corrected natural width and height](#4843-processing-model).
3. Return the result of [determining the dimensions](#4817-dimension-attributes) of image given naturalDimensions.

The `width` getter steps are to return the width of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [dimensions](#483-the-img-element).

The `height` getter steps are to return the height of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [dimensions](#483-the-img-element).

The `naturalWidth` and `naturalHeight` getter steps are:
1. If the image is not *[available](#4843-processing-model)*, then return 0.
2. Return the respective component of the image's [density-corrected natural width and height](#4843-processing-model), in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px). [\[CSS\]](#references)

> [!note]
> Since the [density-corrected natural width and height](#4843-processing-model) of an image take into account any orientation specified in its metadata, [`naturalWidth`](#483-the-img-element) and [`naturalHeight`](#483-the-img-element) reflect the dimensions after applying any rotation needed to correctly orient the image, regardless of the value of the ['image-orientation'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images-3/#the-image-orientation) property.

The `complete` getter steps are:
1. If any of the following are true:
   - both the [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute and the [`srcset`](#483-the-img-element) attribute are omitted;
   - the [`srcset`](#483-the-img-element) attribute is omitted and the [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute's value is the empty string;
   - the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [state](#4843-processing-model) is [completely available](#4843-processing-model) and its [pending request](#4843-processing-model) is null; or
   - the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [state](#4843-processing-model) is [broken](#4843-processing-model) and its [pending request](#4843-processing-model) is null,

   then return true.

2. Return false.

The `currentSrc` IDL attribute must return the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [current URL](#4843-processing-model).

The `decode()` method, when invoked, must perform the following steps:
1. Let promise be a new promise.
2. [Queue a microtask](#8172-queuing-tasks) to perform the following steps:

   > [!note]
   > This is done because [updating the image data](#48435-updating-the-image-data) takes place in a microtask as well. Thus, to make code such as
   > 
   > ```javascript
   > img.src = "stars.jpg";
   > img.decode();
   > ```
   > 
   > properly decode `stars.jpg`, we need to delay any processing by one microtask.
   1. Let global be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant).
   2. If any of the following are true:
      - [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents); or
      - [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [state](#4843-processing-model) is [broken](#4843-processing-model),

      then reject promise with an ["`EncodingError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#encodingerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

   3. Otherwise, [in parallel](#211-parallelism), wait for one of the following cases to occur, and perform the corresponding actions:

      This [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) stops being [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents)

      This [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [current request](#4843-processing-model) changes or is mutated

      This [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [state](#4843-processing-model) becomes [broken](#4843-processing-model)

      [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) with global to reject promise with an ["`EncodingError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#encodingerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

      This [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [state](#4843-processing-model) becomes [completely available](#4843-processing-model)

      [Decode](#48434-decoding-images) the image.

      If decoding does not need to be performed for this image (for example because it is a vector graphic) or the decoding process completes successfully, then [queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) with global to resolve promise with undefined.

      If decoding fails (for example due to invalid image data), then [queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) with global to reject promise with an ["`EncodingError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#encodingerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

      User agents should ensure that the decoded media data stays readily available until at least the end of the next successful [update the rendering](#8173-processing-model) step in the [event loop](#8171-definitions). This is an important part of the API contract, and should not be broken if at all possible. (Typically, this would only be violated in low-memory situations that require evicting decoded image data, or when the image is too large to keep in decoded form for this period of time.)

      > [!note]
      > Animated images will become [completely available](#4843-processing-model) only after all their frames are loaded. Thus, even though an implementation could decode the first frame before that point, the above steps will not do so, instead waiting until all frames are available.

3. Return promise.

> [!example]
> Without the [`decode()`](#483-the-img-element) method, the process of loading an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element and then displaying it might look like the following:
> 
> ```javascript
> const img = new Image();
> img.src = "nebula.jpg";
> img.onload = () => {
>     document.body.appendChild(img);
> };
> img.onerror = () => {
>     document.body.appendChild(new Text("Could not load the nebula :("));
> };
> ```
> 
> However, this can cause notable dropped frames, as the paint that occurs after inserting the image into the DOM causes a synchronous decode on the main thread.
> 
> This can instead be rewritten using the [`decode()`](#483-the-img-element) method:
> 
> ```javascript
> const img = new Image();
> img.src = "nebula.jpg";
> img.decode().then(() => {
>     document.body.appendChild(img);
> }).catch(() => {
>     document.body.appendChild(new Text("Could not load the nebula :("));
> });
> ```
> 
> This latter form avoids the dropped frames of the original, by allowing the user agent to decode the image [in parallel](#211-parallelism), and only inserting it into the DOM (and thus causing it to be painted) once the decoding process is complete.

> [!example]
> Because the [`decode()`](#483-the-img-element) method attempts to ensure that the decoded image data is available for at least one frame, it can be combined with the [`requestAnimationFrame()`](#812-animation-frames) API. This means it can be used with coding styles or frameworks that ensure that all DOM modifications are batched together as [animation frame callbacks](#812-animation-frames):
> 
> ```javascript
> const container = document.querySelector("#container");
> 
> const { containerWidth, containerHeight } = computeDesiredSize();
> requestAnimationFrame(() => {
>  container.style.width = containerWidth;
>  container.style.height = containerHeight;
> });
> 
> // ...
> 
> const img = new Image();
> img.src = "supernova.jpg";
> img.decode().then(() => {
>     requestAnimationFrame(() => container.appendChild(img));
> });
> ```

A legacy factory function is provided for creating [`HTMLImageElement`](#483-the-img-element) objects (in addition to the factory methods from DOM such as [`createElement()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document)): `Image(width, height)`. When invoked, the legacy factory function must perform the following steps:
1. Let document be the [current global object](#81333-current)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object).
2. Let img be the result of [creating an element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) given document, "`img`", and the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces).
3. If width is given, then [set an attribute value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) for img using "[`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes)" and width.
4. If height is given, then [set an attribute value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) for img using "[`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes)" and height.
5. Return img.

> [!example]
> A single image can have different appropriate alternative text depending on the context.
> 
> In each of the following cases, the same image is used, yet the [`alt`](#483-the-img-element) text is different each time. The image is the coat of arms of the Carouge municipality in the canton Geneva in Switzerland.
> 
> Here it is used as a supplementary icon:
> 
> ```html
> <p>I lived in <img src="carouge.svg" alt=""> Carouge.</p>
> ```
> 
> Here it is used as an icon representing the town:
> 
> ```html
> <p>Home town: <img src="carouge.svg" alt="Carouge"></p>
> ```
> 
> Here it is used as part of a text on the town:
> 
> ```html
> <p>Carouge has a coat of arms.</p>
> <p><img src="carouge.svg" alt="The coat of arms depicts a lion, sitting in front of a tree."></p>
> <p>It is used as decoration all over the town.</p>
> ```
> 
> Here it is used as a way to support a similar text where the description is given as well as, instead of as an alternative to, the image:
> 
> ```html
> <p>Carouge has a coat of arms.</p>
> <p><img src="carouge.svg" alt=""></p>
> <p>The coat of arms depicts a lion, sitting in front of a tree.
> It is used as decoration all over the town.</p>
> ```
> 
> Here it is used as part of a story:
> 
> ```html
> <p>She picked up the folder and a piece of paper fell out.</p>
> <p><img src="carouge.svg" alt="Shaped like a shield, the paper had a
> red background, a green tree, and a yellow lion with its tongue
> hanging out and whose tail was shaped like an S."></p>
> <p>She stared at the folder. S! The answer she had been looking for all
> this time was simply the letter S! How had she not seen that before? It all
> came together now. The phone call where Hector had referred to a lion's tail,
> the time Maria had stuck her tongue out...</p>
> ```
> 
> Here it is not known at the time of publication what the image will be, only that it will be a coat of arms of some kind, and thus no replacement text can be provided, and instead only a brief caption for the image is provided, in the [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute:
> 
> ```html
> <p>The last user to have uploaded a coat of arms uploaded this one:</p>
> <p><img src="last-uploaded-coat-of-arms.cgi" title="User-uploaded coat of arms."></p>
> ```
> 
> Ideally, the author would find a way to provide real replacement text even in this case, e.g. by asking the previous user. Not providing replacement text makes the document more difficult to use for people who are unable to view images, e.g. blind users, or users or very low-bandwidth connections or who pay by the byte, or users who are forced to use a text-only web browser.

> [!example]
> Here are some more examples showing the same picture used in different contexts, with different appropriate alternate texts each time.
> 
> ```html
> <article>
>  <h1>My cats</h1>
>  <h2>Fluffy</h2>
>  <p>Fluffy is my favorite.</p>
>  <img src="fluffy.jpg" alt="She likes playing with a ball of yarn.">
>  <p>She's just too cute.</p>
>  <h2>Miles</h2>
>  <p>My other cat, Miles just eats and sleeps.</p>
> </article>
> ```
> 
> ```html
> <article>
>  <h1>Photography</h1>
>  <h2>Shooting moving targets indoors</h2>
>  <p>The trick here is to know how to anticipate; to know at what speed and
>  what distance the subject will pass by.</p>
>  <img src="fluffy.jpg" alt="A cat flying by, chasing a ball of yarn, can be
>  photographed quite nicely using this technique.">
>  <h2>Nature by night</h2>
>  <p>To achieve this, you'll need either an extremely sensitive film, or
>  immense flash lights.</p>
> </article>
> ```
> 
> ```html
> <article>
>  <h1>About me</h1>
>  <h2>My pets</h2>
>  <p>I've got a cat named Fluffy and a dog named Miles.</p>
>  <img src="fluffy.jpg" alt="Fluffy, my cat, tends to keep itself busy.">
>  <p>My dog Miles and I like go on long walks together.</p>
>  <h2>music</h2>
>  <p>After our walks, having emptied my mind, I like listening to Bach.</p>
> </article>
> ```
> 
> ```html
> <article>
>  <h1>Fluffy and the Yarn</h1>
>  <p>Fluffy was a cat who liked to play with yarn. She also liked to jump.</p>
>  <aside><img src="fluffy.jpg" alt="" title="Fluffy"></aside>
>  <p>She would play in the morning, she would play in the evening.</p>
> </article>
> ```

#### 4.8.4 Images

##### 4.8.4.1 Introduction

*This section is non-normative.*

To embed an image in HTML, when there is only a single image resource, use the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element and its [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute.

> [!example]
> ```html
> <h2>From today's featured article</h2>
> <img src="/uploads/100-marie-lloyd.jpg" alt="" width="100" height="150">
> <p><b><a href="/wiki/Marie_Lloyd">Marie Lloyd</a></b> (1870–1922)
> was an English <a href="/wiki/Music_hall">music hall</a> singer, ...
> ```

However, there are a number of situations for which the author might wish to use multiple image resources that the user agent can choose from:
- Different users might have different environmental characteristics:
  - The users' physical screen size might be different from one another.

    > [!example]
    > A mobile phone's screen might be 4 inches diagonally, while a laptop's screen might be 14 inches diagonally.

    > [!note]
    > This is only relevant when an image's rendered size depends on the [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) size.

  - The users' screen pixel density might be different from one another.

    > [!example]
    > A mobile phone's screen might have three times as many physical pixels per inch compared to another mobile phone's screen, regardless of their physical screen size.

  - The users' zoom level might be different from one another, or might change for a single user over time.

    > [!example]
    > A user might zoom in to a particular image to be able to get a more detailed look.

    The zoom level and the screen pixel density (the previous point) can both affect the number of physical screen pixels per [CSS pixel](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px). This ratio is usually referred to as device-pixel-ratio.

  - The users' screen orientation might be different from one another, or might change for a single user over time.

    > [!example]
    > A tablet can be held upright or rotated 90 degrees, so that the screen is either "portrait" or "landscape".

  - The users' network speed, network latency and bandwidth cost might be different from one another, or might change for a single user over time.

    > [!example]
    > A user might be on a fast, low-latency and constant-cost connection while at work, on a slow, low-latency and constant-cost connection while at home, and on a variable-speed, high-latency and variable-cost connection anywhere else.

- Authors might want to show the same image content but with different rendered size depending on, usually, the width of the [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport). This is usually referred to as viewport-based selection.

  > [!example]
  > A web page might have a banner at the top that always spans the entire [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) width. In this case, the rendered size of the image depends on the physical size of the screen (assuming a maximised browser window).

  > [!example]
  > Another web page might have images in columns, with a single column for screens with a small physical size, two columns for screens with medium physical size, and three columns for screens with big physical size, with the images varying in rendered size in each case to fill up the [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport). In this case, the rendered size of an image might be *bigger* in the one-column layout compared to the two-column layout, despite the screen being smaller.

- Authors might want to show different image content depending on the rendered size of the image. This is usually referred to as art direction.

  > [!example]
  > When a web page is viewed on a screen with a large physical size (assuming a maximised browser window), the author might wish to include some less relevant parts surrounding the critical part of the image. When the same web page is viewed on a screen with a small physical size, the author might wish to show only the critical part of the image.

- Authors might want to show the same image content but using different image formats, depending on which image formats the user agent supports. This is usually referred to as image format-based selection.

  > [!example]
  > A web page might have some images in the JPEG, WebP and JPEG XR image formats, with the latter two having better compression abilities compared to JPEG. Since different user agents can support different image formats, with some formats offering better compression ratios, the author would like to serve the better formats to user agents that support them, while providing JPEG fallback for user agents that don't.

The above situations are not mutually exclusive. For example, it is reasonable to combine different resources for different [device-pixel-ratio](#4841-introduction) with different resources for [art direction](#4841-introduction).

While it is possible to solve these problems using scripting, doing so introduces some other problems:
- Some user agents aggressively download images specified in the HTML markup, before scripts have had a chance to run, so that web pages complete loading sooner. If a script changes which image to download, the user agent will potentially start two separate downloads, which can instead cause worse page loading performance.
- If the author avoids specifying any image in the HTML markup and instead instantiates a single download from script, that avoids the double download problem above but then no image will be downloaded at all for users with scripting disabled and the aggressive image downloading optimization will also be disabled.

With this in mind, this specification introduces a number of features to address the above problems in a declarative manner.

[Device-pixel-ratio](#4841-introduction)-based selection when the rendered size of the image is fixed

The [`src`](#483-the-img-element) and [`srcset`](#483-the-img-element) attributes on the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element can be used, using the `x` descriptor, to provide multiple images that only vary in their size (the smaller image is a scaled-down version of the bigger image).

> [!note]
> The `x` descriptor is not appropriate when the rendered size of the image depends on the [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) width ([viewport-based selection](#4841-introduction)), but can be used together with [art direction](#4841-introduction).

> [!example]
> ```html
> <h2>From today's featured article</h2>
> <img src="/uploads/100-marie-lloyd.jpg"
>      srcset="/uploads/150-marie-lloyd.jpg 1.5x, /uploads/200-marie-lloyd.jpg 2x"
>      alt="" width="100" height="150">
> <p><b><a href="/wiki/Marie_Lloyd">Marie Lloyd</a></b> (1870–1922)
> was an English <a href="/wiki/Music_hall">music hall</a> singer, ...
> ```
> 
> The user agent can choose any of the given resources depending on the user's screen's pixel density, zoom level, and possibly other factors such as the user's network conditions.
> 
> For backwards compatibility with older user agents that don't yet understand the [`srcset`](#483-the-img-element) attribute, one of the URLs is specified in the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute. This will result in something useful (though perhaps lower-resolution than the user would like) being displayed even in older user agents. For new user agents, the [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute participates in the resource selection, as if it was specified in [`srcset`](#483-the-img-element) with a `1x` descriptor.
> 
> The image's rendered size is given in the [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes) and [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes) attributes, which allows the user agent to allocate space for the image before it is downloaded.

[Viewport-based selection](#4841-introduction)

The [`srcset`](#483-the-img-element) and [`sizes`](#483-the-img-element) attributes can be used, using the `w` descriptor, to provide multiple images that only vary in their size (the smaller image is a scaled-down version of the bigger image).

> [!example]
> In this example, a banner image takes up the entire [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) width (using appropriate CSS).
> 
> ```html
> <h1><img sizes="100vw" srcset="wolf-400.jpg 400w, wolf-800.jpg 800w, wolf-1600.jpg 1600w"
>      src="wolf-400.jpg" alt="The rad wolf"></h1>
> ```
> 
> The user agent will calculate the effective pixel density of each image from the specified `w` descriptors and the specified rendered size in the [`sizes`](#483-the-img-element) attribute. It can then choose any of the given resources depending on the user's screen's pixel density, zoom level, and possibly other factors such as the user's network conditions.
> 
> If the user's screen is 320 [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) wide, this is equivalent to specifying `wolf-400.jpg 1.25x, wolf-800.jpg 2.5x, wolf-1600.jpg 5x`. On the other hand, if the user's screen is 1200 [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) wide, this is equivalent to specifying `wolf-400.jpg 0.33x, wolf-800.jpg 0.67x, wolf-1600.jpg 1.33x`. By using the `w` descriptors and the [`sizes`](#483-the-img-element) attribute, the user agent can choose the correct image source to download regardless of how large the user's device is.
> 
> For backwards compatibility, one of the URLs is specified in the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute. In new user agents, the [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute is ignored when the [`srcset`](#483-the-img-element) attribute uses `w` descriptors.

> [!example]
> In this example, the web page has three layouts depending on the width of the [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport). The narrow layout has one column of images (the width of each image is about 100%), the middle layout has two columns of images (the width of each image is about 50%), and the widest layout has three columns of images, and some page margin (the width of each image is about 33%). It breaks between these layouts when the [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) is `30em` wide and `50em` wide, respectively.
> 
> ```html
> <img sizes="(max-width: 30em) 100vw, (max-width: 50em) 50vw, calc(33vw - 100px)"
>      srcset="swing-200.jpg 200w, swing-400.jpg 400w, swing-800.jpg 800w, swing-1600.jpg 1600w"
>      src="swing-400.jpg" alt="Kettlebell Swing">
> ```
> 
> The [`sizes`](#483-the-img-element) attribute sets up the layout breakpoints at `30em` and `50em`, and declares the image sizes between these breakpoints to be `100vw`, `50vw`, or `calc(33vw - 100px)`. These sizes do not necessarily have to match up exactly with the actual image width as specified in the CSS.
> 
> The user agent will pick a width from the [`sizes`](#483-the-img-element) attribute, using the first item with a [<media-condition>](https://drafts.csswg.org/mediaqueries/#typedef-media-condition) (the part in parentheses) that evaluates to true, or using the last item (`calc(33vw -
>      100px)`) if they all evaluate to false.
> 
> For example, if the [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) width is `29em`, then `(max-width: 30em)` evaluates to true and `100vw` is used, so the image size, for the purpose of resource selection, is `29em`.
