If the [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) width is instead `32em`, then `(max-width: 30em)` evaluates to false, but `(max-width: 50em)` evaluates to true and `50vw` is used, so the image size, for the purpose of resource selection, is `16em` (half the [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) width). Notice that the slightly wider [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) results in a smaller image because of the different layout.
> 
> The user agent can then calculate the effective pixel density and choose an appropriate resource similarly to the previous example.

> [!example]
> This example is the same as the previous example, but the image is [lazy-loaded](#257-lazy-loading-attributes). In this case, the [`sizes`](#483-the-img-element) attribute can use the [`auto`](#48422-sizes-attributes) keyword, and the user agent will use the [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes) attribute (or the width specified in CSS) for the [source size](#4843-processing-model).
> 
> ```html
> <img loading="lazy" width="200" height="200" sizes="auto"
>      srcset="swing-200.jpg 200w, swing-400.jpg 400w, swing-800.jpg 800w, swing-1600.jpg 1600w"
>      src="swing-400.jpg" alt="Kettlebell Swing">
> ```
> 
> For better backwards-compatibility with legacy user agents that don't support the [`auto`](#48422-sizes-attributes) keyword, fallback sizes can be specified if desired.
> 
> ```html
> <img loading="lazy" width="200" height="200"
>      sizes="auto, (max-width: 30em) 100vw, (max-width: 50em) 50vw, calc(33vw - 100px)"
>      srcset="swing-200.jpg 200w, swing-400.jpg 400w, swing-800.jpg 800w, swing-1600.jpg 1600w"
>      src="swing-400.jpg" alt="Kettlebell Swing">
> ```

[Art direction](#4841-introduction)-based selection

The [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element and the [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element, together with the [`media`](#482-the-source-element) attribute, can be used to provide multiple images that vary the image content (for instance the smaller image might be a cropped version of the bigger image).

> [!example]
> ```html
> <picture>
>   <source media="(min-width: 45em)" srcset="large.jpg">
>   <source media="(min-width: 32em)" srcset="med.jpg">
>   <img src="small.jpg" alt="The wolf runs through the snow.">
> </picture>
> ```
> 
> The user agent will choose the first [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element for which the media query in the [`media`](#482-the-source-element) attribute matches, and then choose an appropriate URL from its [`srcset`](#482-the-source-element) attribute.
> 
> The rendered size of the image varies depending on which resource is chosen. To specify dimensions that the user agent can use before having downloaded the image, CSS can be used.
> 
> ```css
> img { width: 300px; height: 300px }
> @media (min-width: 32em) { img { width: 500px; height:300px } }
> @media (min-width: 45em) { img { width: 700px; height:400px } }
> ```

> [!example]
> This example combines [art direction](#4841-introduction)- and [device-pixel-ratio](#4841-introduction)-based selection. A banner that takes half the [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) is provided in two versions, one for wide screens and one for narrow screens.
> 
> ```html
> <h1>
>  <picture>
>   <source media="(max-width: 500px)" srcset="banner-phone.jpeg, banner-phone-HD.jpeg 2x">
>   <img src="banner.jpeg" srcset="banner-HD.jpeg 2x" alt="The Breakfast Combo">
>  </picture>
> </h1>
> ```

[Image format-based selection](#4841-introduction)

The [`type`](#482-the-source-element) attribute on the [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element can be used to provide multiple images in different formats.

> [!example]
> ```html
> <h2>From today's featured article</h2>
> <picture>
>  <source srcset="/uploads/100-marie-lloyd.webp" type="image/webp">
>  <source srcset="/uploads/100-marie-lloyd.jxr" type="image/vnd.ms-photo">
>  <img src="/uploads/100-marie-lloyd.jpg" alt="" width="100" height="150">
> </picture>
> <p><b><a href="/wiki/Marie_Lloyd">Marie Lloyd</a></b> (1870–1922)
> was an English <a href="/wiki/Music_hall">music hall</a> singer, ...
> ```
> 
> In this example, the user agent will choose the first source that has a [`type`](#482-the-source-element) attribute with a supported MIME type. If the user agent supports WebP images, the first [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element will be chosen. If not, but the user agent does support JPEG XR images, the second [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element will be chosen. If neither of those formats are supported, the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element will be chosen.

###### 4.8.4.1.1 Adaptive images

*This section is non-normative.*

CSS and media queries can be used to construct graphical page layouts that adapt dynamically to the user's environment, in particular to different [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) dimensions and pixel densities. For content, however, CSS does not help; instead, we have the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [`srcset`](#483-the-img-element) attribute and the [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element. This section walks through a sample case showing how to use these features.

Consider a situation where on wide screens (wider than 600 [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px)) a 300×150 image named `a-rectangle.png` is to be used, but on smaller screens (600 [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) and less), a smaller 100×100 image called `a-square.png` is to be used. The markup for this would look like this:

```html
<figure>
 <picture>
  <source srcset="a-square.png" media="(max-width: 600px)">
  <img src="a-rectangle.png" alt="Barney Frank wears a suit and glasses.">
 </picture>
 <figcaption>Barney Frank, 2011</figcaption>
</figure>
```

> [!note]
> For details on what to put in the [`alt`](#483-the-img-element) attribute, see the [Requirements for providing text to act as an alternative for images](#4844-requirements-for-providing-text-to-act-as-an-alternative-for-images) section.

The problem with this is that the user agent does not necessarily know what dimensions to use for the image when the image is loading. To avoid the layout having to be reflowed multiple times as the page is loading, CSS and CSS media queries can be used to provide the dimensions:

```html
<style>
 #a { width: 300px; height: 150px; }
 @media (max-width: 600px) { #a { width: 100px; height: 100px; } }
</style>
<figure>
 <picture>
  <source srcset="a-square.png" media="(max-width: 600px)">
  <img src="a-rectangle.png" alt="Barney Frank wears a suit and glasses." id="a">
 </picture>
 <figcaption>Barney Frank, 2011</figcaption>
</figure>
```

Alternatively, the [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes) and [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes) attributes can be used on the [`source`](#482-the-source-element) and [`img`](#483-the-img-element) elements to provide the width and height:

```html
<figure>
 <picture>
  <source srcset="a-square.png" media="(max-width: 600px)" width="100" height="100">
  <img src="a-rectangle.png" width="300" height="150"
  alt="Barney Frank wears a suit and glasses.">
 </picture>
 <figcaption>Barney Frank, 2011</figcaption>
</figure>

```

---

The [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element is used with the [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute, which gives the URL of the image to use for legacy user agents that do not support the [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element. This leads to a question of which image to provide in the [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute.

If the author wants the biggest image in legacy user agents, the markup could be as follows:

```html
<picture>
 <source srcset="pear-mobile.jpeg" media="(max-width: 720px)">
 <source srcset="pear-tablet.jpeg" media="(max-width: 1280px)">
 <img src="pear-desktop.jpeg" alt="The pear is juicy.">
</picture>
```

However, if legacy mobile user agents are more important, one can list all three images in the [`source`](#482-the-source-element) elements, overriding the [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute entirely.

```html
<picture>
 <source srcset="pear-mobile.jpeg" media="(max-width: 720px)">
 <source srcset="pear-tablet.jpeg" media="(max-width: 1280px)">
 <source srcset="pear-desktop.jpeg">
 <img src="pear-mobile.jpeg" alt="The pear is juicy.">
</picture>
```

Since at this point the [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute is actually being ignored entirely by [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element)-supporting user agents, the [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute can default to any image, including one that is neither the smallest nor biggest:

```html
<picture>
 <source srcset="pear-mobile.jpeg" media="(max-width: 720px)">
 <source srcset="pear-tablet.jpeg" media="(max-width: 1280px)">
 <source srcset="pear-desktop.jpeg">
 <img src="pear-tablet.jpeg" alt="The pear is juicy.">
</picture>
```

---

Above the `max-width` media feature is used, giving the maximum ([viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport)) dimensions that an image is intended for. It is also possible to use `min-width` instead.

```html
<picture>
 <source srcset="pear-desktop.jpeg" media="(min-width: 1281px)">
 <source srcset="pear-tablet.jpeg" media="(min-width: 721px)">
 <img src="pear-mobile.jpeg" alt="The pear is juicy.">
</picture>
```

##### 4.8.4.2 Attributes common to [`source`](#482-the-source-element), [`img`](#483-the-img-element), and [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements

###### 4.8.4.2.1 Srcset attributes

A srcset attribute is an attribute with requirements defined in this section.

If present, its value must consist of one or more [image candidate strings](#48421-srcset-attributes), each separated from the next by a U+002C COMMA character (,). If an [image candidate string](#48421-srcset-attributes) contains no descriptors and no [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) after the URL, the following [image candidate string](#48421-srcset-attributes), if there is one, must begin with one or more [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).

An image candidate string consists of the following components, in order, with the further restrictions described below this list:
1. Zero or more [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).
2. A [valid non-empty URL](#241-terminology) that does not start or end with a U+002C COMMA character (,), referencing a non-interactive, optionally animated, image resource that is neither paged nor scripted.
3. Zero or more [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).
4. Zero or one of the following:
   - A width descriptor, consisting of: [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), a [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers) giving a number greater than zero representing the width descriptor value, and a U+0077 LATIN SMALL LETTER W character.
   - A pixel density descriptor, consisting of: [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), a [valid floating-point number](#2343-floating-point-numbers) giving a number greater than zero representing the pixel density descriptor value, and a U+0078 LATIN SMALL LETTER X character.
5. Zero or more [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).

There must not be an [image candidate string](#48421-srcset-attributes) for an element that has the same [width descriptor value](#48421-srcset-attributes) as another [image candidate string](#48421-srcset-attributes)'s [width descriptor value](#48421-srcset-attributes) for the same element.

There must not be an [image candidate string](#48421-srcset-attributes) for an element that has the same [pixel density descriptor value](#48421-srcset-attributes) as another [image candidate string](#48421-srcset-attributes)'s [pixel density descriptor value](#48421-srcset-attributes) for the same element. For the purpose of this requirement, an [image candidate string](#48421-srcset-attributes) with no descriptors is equivalent to an [image candidate string](#48421-srcset-attributes) with a `1x` descriptor.

If an [image candidate string](#48421-srcset-attributes) for an element has the [width descriptor](#48421-srcset-attributes) specified, all other [image candidate strings](#48421-srcset-attributes) for that element must also have the [width descriptor](#48421-srcset-attributes) specified.

The specified width in an [image candidate string](#48421-srcset-attributes)'s [width descriptor](#48421-srcset-attributes) must match the [natural width](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-width) in the resource given by the [image candidate string](#48421-srcset-attributes)'s URL, if it has a [natural width](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-width).

If an element has a [sizes attribute](#48422-sizes-attributes) present, all [image candidate strings](#48421-srcset-attributes) for that element must have the [width descriptor](#48421-srcset-attributes) specified.

###### 4.8.4.2.2 Sizes attributes

A sizes attribute is an attribute with requirements defined in this section.

If present, the value must be a [valid source size list](#48422-sizes-attributes).

A valid source size list is a string that matches the following grammar: [\[CSSVALUES\]](#references) [\[MQ\]](#references)

```html
<source-size-list> = <source-size>#? , <source-size-value>
<source-size> = <media-condition> <source-size-value> | auto
<source-size-value> = <length> | auto
```

A [<source-size-value>](#48422-sizes-attributes) that is a [<length>](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#lengths) must not be negative, and must not use CSS functions other than the [math functions](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#math-function).

The keyword `auto` is a width that is computed in [parse a sizes attribute](#484311-parsing-a-sizes-attribute). If present, it must be the first entry and the entire [<source-size-list>](#48422-sizes-attributes) value must either be the string "`auto`" ([ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings)) or start with the string "`auto,`" ([ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings)).

> [!note]
> If the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element that initiated the image loading (with the [update the image data](#48435-updating-the-image-data) or [react to environment changes](#484313-reacting-to-environment-changes) algorithms) [allows auto-sizes](#483-the-img-element) and is [being rendered](#151-introduction), then [`auto`](#48422-sizes-attributes) is the [concrete object size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#concrete-object-size) width. If it [allows auto-sizes](#483-the-img-element) and is not [being rendered](#151-introduction), but its [last auto-sizes width](#4843-processing-model) is not null, then [`auto`](#48422-sizes-attributes) is that width. Otherwise, the [`auto`](#48422-sizes-attributes) value is ignored and the next [source size](#4843-processing-model) is used instead, if any.

The [`auto`](#48422-sizes-attributes) keyword may be specified in the [`sizes`](#482-the-source-element) attribute of [`source`](#482-the-source-element) elements and [`sizes`](#483-the-img-element) attribute of [`img`](#483-the-img-element) elements, if the following conditions are met. Otherwise, [`auto`](#48422-sizes-attributes) must not be specified.
- The element is a [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element with a following sibling [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element.
- The element is an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element.
- The [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element referenced in either condition above [allows auto-sizes](#483-the-img-element).

> [!note]
> In addition, it is strongly encouraged to specify dimensions using the [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes) and [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes) attributes or with CSS. Without specified dimensions, the image will likely render with 300x150 dimensions because `sizes="auto"` implies `contain-intrinsic-size: 300px
>   150px` in [the Rendering section](#1542-images).

The [<source-size-value>](#48422-sizes-attributes) gives the intended layout width of the image. The author can specify different widths for different environments with [<media-condition>](https://drafts.csswg.org/mediaqueries/#typedef-media-condition)s.

> [!note]
> Percentages are not allowed in a [<source-size-value>](#48422-sizes-attributes), to avoid confusion about what it would be relative to. The ['vw'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#vw) unit can be used for sizes relative to the [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) width.

##### 4.8.4.3 Processing model

---

An [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element has a current request and a pending request. The [current request](#4843-processing-model) is initially set to a new [image request](#4843-processing-model). The [pending request](#4843-processing-model) is initially set to null.

An image request has a state, current URL, and image data.

An [image request](#4843-processing-model)'s [state](#4843-processing-model) is one of the following:

Unavailable

The user agent hasn't obtained any image data, or has obtained some or all of the image data but hasn't yet decoded enough of the image to get the image dimensions.

Partially available

The user agent has obtained some of the image data and at least the image dimensions are available.

Completely available

The user agent has obtained all of the image data and at least the image dimensions are available.

Broken

The user agent has obtained all of the image data that it can, but it cannot even decode the image enough to get the image dimensions (e.g. the image is corrupted, or the format is not supported, or no data could be obtained).

An [image request](#4843-processing-model)'s [current URL](#4843-processing-model) is initially the empty string.

An [image request](#4843-processing-model)'s [image data](#4843-processing-model) is the decoded image data.

When an [image request](#4843-processing-model)'s [state](#4843-processing-model) is either [partially available](#4843-processing-model) or [completely available](#4843-processing-model), the [image request](#4843-processing-model) is said to be available.

When an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [state](#4843-processing-model) is [completely available](#4843-processing-model) and the user agent can decode the media data without errors, then the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element is said to be fully decodable.

An [image request](#4843-processing-model)'s [state](#4843-processing-model) is initially [unavailable](#4843-processing-model).

When an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [current request](#4843-processing-model) is [available](#4843-processing-model), the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element provides a [paint source](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images-4/#paint-source) whose width is the image's [density-corrected natural width](#4843-processing-model) (if any), whose height is the image's [density-corrected natural height](#4843-processing-model) (if any), and whose appearance is the natural appearance of the image.

---

An [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element is said to use `srcset` or `picture` if it has a [`srcset`](#483-the-img-element) attribute specified or if it has a parent that is a [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element.

---

Each [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element has a last selected source, which must initially be null.

Each [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element has a last auto-sizes width, which is a length in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) or null, initially null.

Each [image request](#4843-processing-model) has a current pixel density, which must initially be 1.

Each [image request](#4843-processing-model) has preferred density-corrected dimensions, which is either a struct consisting of a width and a height or is null. It must initially be null.

To determine the density-corrected natural width and height of an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element img:
1. Let density be img's [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [current pixel density](#4843-processing-model).
2. Let dimensions be img's [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [preferred density-corrected dimensions](#4843-processing-model).

   > [!note]
   > The [preferred density-corrected dimensions](#4843-processing-model) are set in the [prepare an image for presentation](#48436-preparing-an-image-for-presentation) algorithm based on meta information in the image.

3. If dimensions is not null, then set dimensions's width to dimensions's width divided by density, set dimensions's height to dimensions's height divided by density, and return dimensions.
4. Let intrinsicWidth, intrinsicHeight, and intrinsicRatio be img's [intrinsic width, intrinsic height, and intrinsic aspect ratio](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions), if any, respectively.
5. If intrinsicWidth is not absent, then set intrinsicWidth to intrinsicWidth divided by density.
6. If intrinsicHeight is not absent, then set intrinsicHeight to intrinsicHeight divided by density.
7. Return the result of applying the [default sizing algorithm](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#default-sizing) with intrinsicWidth, intrinsicHeight, and intrinsicRatio, using a [default object size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#default-object-size) of 300 by 150.

> [!example]
> For example, if the [current pixel density](#4843-processing-model) is 3.125, that means that there are 300 device pixels per [CSS inch](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#in), and thus if the image data is 300x600, it has [density-corrected natural width and height](#4843-processing-model) of 96 [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) by 192 [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px).

All [`img`](#483-the-img-element) and [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements are associated with a [source set](#4843-processing-model).

A source set is an ordered set of zero or more [image sources](#4843-processing-model) and a [source size](#4843-processing-model).

An image source is a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url), and optionally either a [pixel density descriptor](#48421-srcset-attributes), or a [width descriptor](#48421-srcset-attributes).

A source size is a [<source-size-value>](#48422-sizes-attributes). When a [source size](#4843-processing-model) has a unit relative to the [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport), it must be interpreted relative to the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport). Other units must be interpreted the same as in Media Queries. [\[MQ\]](#references)

---

A parse error for algorithms in this section indicates a non-fatal mismatch between input and requirements. User agents are encouraged to expose [parse error](#4843-processing-model)s somehow.

---

Whether the image is fetched successfully or not (e.g. whether the response status was an [ok status](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#ok-status)) must be ignored when determining the image's type and whether it is a valid image.

> [!note]
> This allows servers to return images with error responses, and have them displayed.

The user agent should apply the [image sniffing rules](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#rules-for-sniffing-images-specifically) to determine the type of the image, with the image's [associated Content-Type headers](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource) giving the official type. If these rules are not applied, then the type of the image must be the type given by the image's [associated Content-Type headers](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource).

User agents must not support non-image resources with the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element (e.g. XML files whose [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) is an HTML element). User agents must not run executable code (e.g. scripts) embedded in the image resource. User agents must only display the first page of a multipage resource (e.g. a PDF file). User agents must not allow the resource to act in an interactive fashion, but should honour any animation in the resource.

This specification does not specify which image types are to be supported.

###### 4.8.4.3.1 When to obtain images

By default, images are obtained immediately. User agents may provide users with the option to instead obtain them on-demand. (The on-demand option might be used by bandwidth-constrained users, for example.)

When obtaining images immediately, the user agent must synchronously [update the image data](#48435-updating-the-image-data) of the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element, with the *restart animation* flag set if so stated, whenever that element is created or has experienced [relevant mutations](#48432-reacting-to-dom-mutations).

When obtaining images on demand, the user agent must [update the image data](#48435-updating-the-image-data) of an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element whenever it needs the image data (i.e., on demand), but only if the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [state](#4843-processing-model) is [unavailable](#4843-processing-model). When an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element has experienced [relevant mutations](#48432-reacting-to-dom-mutations), if the user agent only obtains images on demand, the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [state](#4843-processing-model) must return to [unavailable](#4843-processing-model).

###### 4.8.4.3.2 Reacting to DOM mutations

The relevant mutations for an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element are as follows:
- The element's [`src`](#483-the-img-element), [`srcset`](#483-the-img-element), or [`sizes`](#483-the-img-element) attributes are set, changed, or removed.
- The element's [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute is set to the same value as the previous value. This must set the *restart animation* flag for the [update the image data](#48435-updating-the-image-data) algorithm.
- The element's [`crossorigin`](#483-the-img-element) attribute's state is changed.
- The element's [`referrerpolicy`](#483-the-img-element) attribute's state is changed.
- The [`img`](#483-the-img-element) or [`source`](#482-the-source-element) [HTML element insertion steps](#214-dom-trees), [HTML element removing steps](#214-dom-trees), and [HTML element moving steps](#214-dom-trees) count the mutation as a [relevant mutation](#48432-reacting-to-dom-mutations).
- The element's parent is a [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element and a [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element that is a previous sibling has its [`srcset`](#482-the-source-element), [`sizes`](#482-the-source-element), [`media`](#482-the-source-element), [`type`](#482-the-source-element), [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes) or [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes) attributes set, changed, or removed.
- The element's [adopting steps](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) are run.
- If the element [allows auto-sizes](#483-the-img-element): the element starts [being rendered](#151-introduction), or its [concrete object size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#concrete-object-size) width changes. This must set the *maybe omit events* flag for the [update the image data](#48435-updating-the-image-data) algorithm.

###### 4.8.4.3.3 The list of available images

Each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object must have a list of available images. Each image in this list is identified by a tuple consisting of an [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute), a [CORS settings attribute](#254-cors-settings-attributes) mode, and, if the mode is not [No CORS](#254-cors-settings-attributes), an [origin](#711-origins). Each image furthermore has an ignore higher-layer caching flag. User agents may copy entries from one [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object's [list of available images](#48433-the-list-of-available-images) to another at any time (e.g. when the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is created, user agents can add to it all the images that are loaded in other [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)s), but must not change the keys of entries copied in this way when doing so, and must unset the [ignore higher-layer caching](#48433-the-list-of-available-images) flag for the copied entry. User agents may also remove images from such lists at any time (e.g. to save memory). User agents must remove entries in the [list of available images](#48433-the-list-of-available-images) as appropriate given higher-layer caching semantics for the resource (e.g. the HTTP \`[`Cache-Control`](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc7234.html#header.cache-control)\` response header) when the [ignore higher-layer caching](#48433-the-list-of-available-images) flag is unset.

> [!note]
> The [list of available images](#48433-the-list-of-available-images) is intended to enable synchronous switching when changing the [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute to a URL that has previously been loaded, and to avoid re-downloading images in the same document even when they don't allow caching per HTTP. It is not used to avoid re-downloading the same image while the previous image is still loading.

> [!note]
> The user agent can also store the image data separately from the [list of available images](#48433-the-list-of-available-images).

> [!example]
> For example, if a resource has the HTTP response header \``Cache-Control: must-revalidate`\`, and its [ignore higher-layer caching](#48433-the-list-of-available-images) flag is unset, the user agent would remove it from the [list of available images](#48433-the-list-of-available-images) but could keep the image data separately, and use that if the server responds with a `304 Not Modified` status.

###### 4.8.4.3.4 Decoding images

Image data is usually encoded in order to reduce file size. This means that in order for the user agent to present the image to the screen, the data needs to be decoded. Decoding is the process which converts an image's media data into a bitmap form, suitable for presentation to the screen. Note that this process can be slow relative to other processes involved in presenting content. Thus, the user agent can choose when to perform decoding, in order to create the best user experience.

Image decoding is said to be synchronous if it prevents presentation of other content until it is finished. Typically, this has an effect of atomically presenting the image and any other content at the same time. However, this presentation is delayed by the amount of time it takes to perform the decode.

Image decoding is said to be asynchronous if it does not prevent presentation of other content. This has an effect of presenting non-image content faster. However, the image content is missing on screen until the decode finishes. Once the decode is finished, the screen is updated with the image.

In both synchronous and asynchronous decoding modes, the final content is presented to screen after the same amount of time has elapsed. The main difference is whether the user agent presents non-image content ahead of presenting the final content.

In order to aid the user agent in deciding whether to perform synchronous or asynchronous decode, the [`decoding`](#483-the-img-element) attribute can be set on [`img`](#483-the-img-element) elements. The possible values of the [`decoding`](#483-the-img-element) attribute are the following image decoding hint keywords:

| Keyword | State | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sync` | Sync | Indicates a preference to [decode](#48434-decoding-images) this image synchronously for atomic presentation with other content. |
| `async` | Async | Indicates a preference to [decode](#48434-decoding-images) this image asynchronously to avoid delaying presentation of other content. |
| `auto` | Auto | Indicates no preference in decoding mode (the default). |

When [decoding](#48434-decoding-images) an image, the user agent should respect the preference indicated by the [`decoding`](#483-the-img-element) attribute's state. If the state indicated is [Auto](#48434-decoding-images), then the user agent is free to choose any decoding behavior.

> [!note]
> It is also possible to control the decoding behavior using the [`decode()`](#483-the-img-element) method. Since the [`decode()`](#483-the-img-element) method performs [decoding](#48434-decoding-images) independently from the process responsible for presenting content to screen, it is unaffected by the [`decoding`](#483-the-img-element) attribute.

###### 4.8.4.3.5 Updating the image data

> [!note]
> This algorithm cannot be called from steps running [in parallel](#211-parallelism). If a user agent needs to call this algorithm from steps running [in parallel](#211-parallelism), it needs to [queue](#8172-queuing-tasks) a task to do so.

When the user agent is to update the image data of an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element element, optionally with the *restart animation* flag set, optionally with the *maybe omit events* flag set, it must run the following steps:
1. If element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents):
   1. Continue running this algorithm [in parallel](#211-parallelism).
   2. Wait until element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) is [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents).
   3. If another instance of this algorithm for element was started after this instance (even if it aborted and is no longer running), then return.
   4. [Queue a microtask](#8172-queuing-tasks) to continue this algorithm.
2. If the user agent cannot support images, or its support for images has been disabled, then [abort the image request](#48435-updating-the-image-data) for the [current request](#4843-processing-model) and the [pending request](#4843-processing-model), set the [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [state](#4843-processing-model) to [unavailable](#4843-processing-model), set the [pending request](#4843-processing-model) to null, and return.
3. Let previousURL be the [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [current URL](#4843-processing-model).
4. Let selected source be null and selected pixel density be undefined.
5. If element does not [use `srcset` or `picture`](#4843-processing-model) and it has a [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute specified whose value is not the empty string, then set selected source to the value of element's [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute and set selected pixel density to 1.0.
6. Set element's [last selected source](#4843-processing-model) to selected source.
7. If selected source is not null:
   1. Let urlString be the result of [encoding-parsing-and-serializing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given selected source, relative to element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
   2. If urlString is failure, then abort this inner set of steps.
   3. Let key be a tuple consisting of urlString, element's [`crossorigin`](#483-the-img-element) attribute's mode, and, if that mode is not [No CORS](#254-cors-settings-attributes), element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).
   4. If the [list of available images](#48433-the-list-of-available-images) contains an entry for key:
      1. Set the [ignore higher-layer caching](#48433-the-list-of-available-images) flag for that entry.
      2. [Abort the image request](#48435-updating-the-image-data) for the [current request](#4843-processing-model) and the [pending request](#4843-processing-model).
      3. Set the [pending request](#4843-processing-model) to null.
      4. Set the [current request](#4843-processing-model) to a new [image request](#4843-processing-model) whose [image data](#4843-processing-model) is that of the entry and whose [state](#4843-processing-model) is [completely available](#4843-processing-model).
      5. [Prepare the current request for presentation](#48436-preparing-an-image-for-presentation) given element.
      6. Set the [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [current pixel density](#4843-processing-model) to selected pixel density.
      7. [Queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given element and the following steps:
         1. If *restart animation* is set, then [restart the animation](#1542-images).
         2. Set the [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [current URL](#4843-processing-model) to urlString.
         3. If *maybe omit events* is not set or previousURL is not equal to urlString, then [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`load`](#events) at element.
      8. Abort the [update the image data](#48435-updating-the-image-data) algorithm.
8. [Queue a microtask](#8172-queuing-tasks) to perform the rest of this algorithm, allowing the [task](#8171-definitions) that invoked this algorithm to continue.
9. If another instance of this algorithm for element was started after this instance (even if it aborted and is no longer running), then return.

   > [!note]
   > Only the last instance takes effect, to avoid multiple requests when, for example, the [`src`](#483-the-img-element), [`srcset`](#483-the-img-element), and [`crossorigin`](#483-the-img-element) attributes are all set in succession.

10. Let selected source and selected pixel density be the URL and pixel density that results from [selecting an image source](#48437-selecting-an-image-source), respectively.
11. If selected source is null:
    1. Set the [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [state](#4843-processing-model) to [broken](#4843-processing-model), [abort the image request](#48435-updating-the-image-data) for the [current request](#4843-processing-model) and the [pending request](#4843-processing-model), and set the [pending request](#4843-processing-model) to null.
    2. [Queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given element and the following steps:
       1. Change the [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [current URL](#4843-processing-model) to the empty string.
       2. If all of the following are true:
          - element has a [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute or it [uses `srcset` or `picture`](#4843-processing-model); and
          - *maybe omit events* is not set or previousURL is not the empty string,

          then [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) at element.

    3. Return.

12. Let urlString be the result of [encoding-parsing-and-serializing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given selected source, relative to element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
13. If urlString is failure:
    1. [Abort the image request](#48435-updating-the-image-data) for the [current request](#4843-processing-model) and the [pending request](#4843-processing-model).
    2. Set the [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [state](#4843-processing-model) to [broken](#4843-processing-model).
    3. Set the [pending request](#4843-processing-model) to null.
    4. [Queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given element and the following steps:
       1. Change the [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [current URL](#4843-processing-model) to selected source.
       2. If *maybe omit events* is not set or previousURL is not equal to selected source, then [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) at element.
    5. Return.
14. If the [pending request](#4843-processing-model) is not null and urlString is the same as the [pending request](#4843-processing-model)'s [current URL](#4843-processing-model), then return.
15. If urlString is the same as the [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [current URL](#4843-processing-model) and the [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [state](#4843-processing-model) is [partially available](#4843-processing-model):
    1. [Abort the image request](#48435-updating-the-image-data) for the [pending request](#4843-processing-model).
    2. If *restart animation* is set, then [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given element to [restart the animation](#1542-images).
    3. Return.
16. [Abort the image request](#48435-updating-the-image-data) for the [pending request](#4843-processing-model).
17. Set image request to a new [image request](#4843-processing-model) whose [current URL](#4843-processing-model) is urlString.
18. If the [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [state](#4843-processing-model) is [unavailable](#4843-processing-model) or [broken](#4843-processing-model), then set the [current request](#4843-processing-model) to image request. Otherwise, set the [pending request](#4843-processing-model) to image request.
19. Let request be the result of [creating a potential-CORS request](#251-terminology) given urlString, "`image`", and the current state of element's [`crossorigin`](#483-the-img-element) content attribute.
20. Set request's [client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client) to element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant).
21. If element [uses `srcset` or `picture`](#4843-processing-model), set request's [initiator](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-initiator) to "`imageset`".
22. Set request's [referrer policy](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-referrer-policy) to the current state of element's [`referrerpolicy`](#483-the-img-element) attribute.
23. Set request's [priority](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-priority) to the current state of element's [`fetchpriority`](#483-the-img-element) attribute.
24. Let delay load event be true if the [`img`](#483-the-img-element)'s [lazy loading attribute](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) is in the [Eager](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) state, or if [scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting) for the [`img`](#483-the-img-element), and false otherwise.
25. If the [will lazy load element steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) given the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) return true:
    1. Set the [`img`](#483-the-img-element)'s [lazy load resumption steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) to the rest of this algorithm starting with the step labeled *fetch the image*.
    2. [Start intersection-observing a lazy loading element](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) for element.
    3. Return.
26. *Fetch the image*: [Fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request. Return from this algorithm, and run the remaining steps as part of the fetch's *[processResponse](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#process-response)* for the [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response.

    The resource obtained in this fashion, if any, is image request's [image data](#4843-processing-model). It can be either [CORS-same-origin](#251-terminology) or [CORS-cross-origin](#251-terminology); this affects the image's interaction with other APIs (e.g., when used on a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element)).

    When delay load event is true, fetching the image must [delay the load event](#1327-the-end) of element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) until the [task](#8171-definitions) that is [queued](#8172-queuing-tasks) by the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) once the resource has been fetched ([defined below](#48435-updating-the-image-data)) has been run.

    > [!warning]
    > This, unfortunately, can be used to perform a rudimentary port scan of the user's local network (especially in conjunction with scripting, though scripting isn't actually necessary to carry out such an attack). User agents may implement [cross-origin](#711-origins) access control policies that are stricter than those described above to mitigate this attack, but unfortunately such policies are typically not compatible with existing web content.

27. As soon as possible, jump to the first applicable entry from the following list:

    If the resource type is [`multipart/x-mixed-replace`](#172-multipartx-mixed-replace)

    The next [task](#8171-definitions) that is [queued](#8172-queuing-tasks) by the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) while the image is being fetched must run the following steps:
    1. If image request is the [pending request](#4843-processing-model) and at least one body part has been completely decoded, [abort the image request](#48435-updating-the-image-data) for the [current request](#4843-processing-model), and [upgrade the pending request to the current request](#48435-updating-the-image-data).
    2. Otherwise, if image request is the [pending request](#4843-processing-model) and the user agent is able to determine that image request's image is corrupted in some fatal way such that the image dimensions cannot be obtained, [abort the image request](#48435-updating-the-image-data) for the [current request](#4843-processing-model), [upgrade the pending request to the current request](#48435-updating-the-image-data), and set the [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [state](#4843-processing-model) to [broken](#4843-processing-model).
    3. Otherwise, if image request is the [current request](#4843-processing-model), its [state](#4843-processing-model) is [unavailable](#4843-processing-model), and the user agent is able to determine image request's image's width and height, set the [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [state](#4843-processing-model) to [partially available](#4843-processing-model).
    4. Otherwise, if image request is the [current request](#4843-processing-model), its [state](#4843-processing-model) is [unavailable](#4843-processing-model), and the user agent is able to determine that image request's image is corrupted in some fatal way such that the image dimensions cannot be obtained, set the [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [state](#4843-processing-model) to [broken](#4843-processing-model).

    Each [task](#8171-definitions) that is [queued](#8172-queuing-tasks) by the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) while the image is being fetched must update the presentation of the image, but as each new body part comes in, if the user agent is able to determine the image's width and height, it must [prepare element's current request for presentation](#48436-preparing-an-image-for-presentation) given element and replace the previous image. Once one body part has been completely decoded, perform the following steps:
    1. Set element's [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [state](#4843-processing-model) to [completely available](#4843-processing-model).
    2. If *maybe omit events* is not set or previousURL is not equal to urlString, then [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given element to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`load`](#events) at element.

    If the resource type and data corresponds to a supported image format, [as described below](#4843-processing-model)

    The next [task](#8171-definitions) that is [queued](#8172-queuing-tasks) by the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) while the image is being fetched must run the following steps:
    1. If the user agent is able to determine image request's image's width and height, and image request is the [pending request](#4843-processing-model), set image request's [state](#4843-processing-model) to [partially available](#4843-processing-model).
    2. Otherwise, if the user agent is able to determine image request's image's width and height, and image request is the [current request](#4843-processing-model), [prepare image request for presentation](#48436-preparing-an-image-for-presentation) given element and set image request's [state](#4843-processing-model) to [partially available](#4843-processing-model).
    3. Otherwise, if the user agent is able to determine that image request's image is corrupted in some fatal way such that the image dimensions cannot be obtained, and image request is the [pending request](#4843-processing-model):
       1. [Abort the image request](#48435-updating-the-image-data) for the [current request](#4843-processing-model) and the [pending request](#4843-processing-model).
       2. [Upgrade the pending request to the current request](#48435-updating-the-image-data).
       3. Set the [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [state](#4843-processing-model) to [broken](#4843-processing-model).
       4. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) at element.
    4. Otherwise, if the user agent is able to determine that image request's image is corrupted in some fatal way such that the image dimensions cannot be obtained, and image request is the [current request](#4843-processing-model):
       1. [Abort the image request](#48435-updating-the-image-data) for image request.
       2. If *maybe omit events* is not set or previousURL is not equal to urlString, then [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) at element.

    That [task](#8171-definitions), and each subsequent [task](#8171-definitions) that is [queued](#8172-queuing-tasks) by the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) while the image is being fetched, must, if image request is the [current request](#4843-processing-model), update the presentation of the image appropriately (e.g., if the image is a progressive JPEG, each packet can improve the resolution of the image).

    Furthermore, the last [task](#8171-definitions) that is [queued](#8172-queuing-tasks) by the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) once the resource has been fetched must additionally run these steps:
    1. If image request is the [pending request](#4843-processing-model), [abort the image request](#48435-updating-the-image-data) for the [current request](#4843-processing-model), [upgrade the pending request to the current request](#48435-updating-the-image-data), and [prepare image request for presentation](#48436-preparing-an-image-for-presentation) given element.
    2. Set image request to the [completely available](#4843-processing-model) state.
    3. Add the image to the [list of available images](#48433-the-list-of-available-images) using the key key, with the [ignore higher-layer caching](#48433-the-list-of-available-images) flag set.
    4. If *maybe omit events* is not set or previousURL is not equal to urlString, then [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`load`](#events) at element.

    Otherwise

    The image data is not in a supported file format; the user agent must set image request's [state](#4843-processing-model) to [broken](#4843-processing-model), [abort the image request](#48435-updating-the-image-data) for the [current request](#4843-processing-model) and the [pending request](#4843-processing-model), [upgrade the pending request to the current request](#48435-updating-the-image-data) if image request is the [pending request](#4843-processing-model), and then, if *maybe omit events* is not set or previousURL is not equal to urlString, [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given element to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) at element.

While a user agent is running the above algorithm for an element x, there must be a strong reference from the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) to the element x, even if that element is not [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree).

To abort the image request for an [image request](#4843-processing-model) or null image request means to run the following steps:
1. If image request is null, then return.
2. Forget image request's [image data](#4843-processing-model), if any.
3. Abort any instance of the [fetching](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) algorithm for image request, discarding any pending tasks generated by that algorithm.

To upgrade the pending request to the current request for an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element means to run the following steps:
1. Set the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [current request](#4843-processing-model) to the [pending request](#4843-processing-model).
2. Set the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [pending request](#4843-processing-model) to null.

###### 4.8.4.3.6 Preparing an image for presentation

To prepare an image for presentation for an [image request](#4843-processing-model) req given image element img:
1. Let exifTagMap be the EXIF tags obtained from req's [image data](#4843-processing-model), as defined by the relevant codec. [\[EXIF\]](#references)
2. Let physicalWidth and physicalHeight be the width and height obtained from req's [image data](#4843-processing-model), as defined by the relevant codec.
3. Let dimX be the value of exifTagMap's tag `0xA002` (`PixelXDimension`).
4. Let dimY be the value of exifTagMap's tag `0xA003` (`PixelYDimension`).
5. Let resX be the value of exifTagMap's tag `0x011A` (`XResolution`).
6. Let resY be the value of exifTagMap's tag `0x011B` (`YResolution`).
7. Let resUnit be the value of exifTagMap's tag `0x0128` (`ResolutionUnit`).
8. If all the following are true:
   - dimX is a positive integer;
   - dimY is a positive integer;
   - resX is a positive floating-point number;
   - resY is a positive floating-point number;
   - physicalWidth × 72 / resX is dimX;
   - physicalHeight × 72 / resY is dimY;
   - resUnit is `2` (`Inch`),

   then:
   1. If req's [image data](#4843-processing-model) is [CORS-cross-origin](#251-terminology), then set img's [natural dimensions](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions) to dimX and dimY, and scale img's pixel data accordingly.
   2. Otherwise, set req's [preferred density-corrected dimensions](#4843-processing-model) to a struct with its width set to dimX and its height set to dimY.

9. Update req's [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's presentation appropriately.

> [!note]
> Resolution in EXIF is equivalent to [CSS points per inch](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#pt), therefore 72 is the base for computing size from resolution.

> [!warning]
> It is not yet specified what would be the case if EXIF arrives after the image is already presented. See [issue #4929](https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/4929).

###### 4.8.4.3.7 Selecting an image source

To select an image source given an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element el:
1. [Update the source set](#48439-updating-the-source-set) for el.
2. If el's [source set](#4843-processing-model) is empty, return null as the URL and undefined as the pixel density.
3. Return the result of [selecting an image](#48437-selecting-an-image-source) from el's [source set](#4843-processing-model).

To select an image source from a source set given a [source set](#4843-processing-model) sourceSet:
1. If an entry b in sourceSet has the same associated [pixel density descriptor](#48421-srcset-attributes) as an earlier entry a in sourceSet, then remove entry b. Repeat this step until none of the entries in sourceSet have the same associated [pixel density descriptor](#48421-srcset-attributes) as an earlier entry.
2. In an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) manner, choose one [image source](#4843-processing-model) from sourceSet. Let selectedSource be this choice.
3. Return selectedSource and its associated pixel density.

###### 4.8.4.3.8 Creating a source set from attributes

When asked to create a source set given a string default source, a string srcset, a string sizes, and an element or null img:
1. Let source set be an empty [source set](#4843-processing-model).
2. If srcset is not an empty string, then set source set to the result of [parsing](#484310-parsing-a-srcset-attribute) srcset.
3. Set source set's [source size](#4843-processing-model) to the result of [parsing](#484311-parsing-a-sizes-attribute) sizes with img.
4. If default source is not the empty string and source set does not contain an [image source](#4843-processing-model) with a [pixel density descriptor](#48421-srcset-attributes) value of 1, and no [image source](#4843-processing-model) with a [width descriptor](#48421-srcset-attributes), append default source to source set.
5. [Normalize the source densities](#484312-normalizing-the-source-densities) of source set.
6. Return source set.

###### 4.8.4.3.9 Updating the source set

When asked to update the source set for a given [`img`](#483-the-img-element) or [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element el, user agents must do the following:
1. Set el's [source set](#4843-processing-model) to an empty [source set](#4843-processing-model).
2. Let elements be « el ».
3. If el is an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element whose parent node is a [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element, then [replace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) the contents of elements with el's parent node's child elements, retaining relative order.
4. Let img be el if el is an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element, otherwise null.
5. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) child in elements:
   1. If child is el:
      1. Let default source be the empty string.
      2. Let srcset be the empty string.
      3. Let sizes be the empty string.
      4. If el is an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element that has a [`srcset`](#483-the-img-element) attribute, then set srcset to that attribute's value.
      5. Otherwise, if el is a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element that has an [`imagesrcset`](#424-the-link-element) attribute, then set srcset to that attribute's value.
      6. If el is an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element that has a [`sizes`](#483-the-img-element) attribute, then set sizes to that attribute's value.
      7. Otherwise, if el is a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element that has an [`imagesizes`](#424-the-link-element) attribute, then set sizes to that attribute's value.
      8. If el is an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element that has a [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute, then set default source to that attribute's value.
      9. Otherwise, if el is a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element that has an [`href`](#424-the-link-element) attribute, then set default source to that attribute's value.
      10. Set el's [source set](#4843-processing-model) to the result of [creating a source set](#48438-creating-a-source-set-from-attributes) given default source, srcset, sizes, and img.
      11. Return.

          > [!note]
          > If el is a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element, then elements contains only el, so this step will be reached immediately and the rest of the algorithm will not run.

   2. If child is not a [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   3. If child does not have a [`srcset`](#482-the-source-element) attribute, [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration) to the next child.
   4. [Parse child's srcset attribute](#484310-parsing-a-srcset-attribute) and let source set be the returned [source set](#4843-processing-model).
   5. If source set has zero [image sources](#4843-processing-model), [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration) to the next child.
   6. If child has a [`media`](#482-the-source-element) attribute, and its value does not [match the environment](#2310-media-queries), [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration) to the next child.
   7. [Parse child's sizes attribute](#484311-parsing-a-sizes-attribute) with img, and let source set's [source size](#4843-processing-model) be the returned value.
   8. If child has a [`type`](#482-the-source-element) attribute, and its value is an unknown or unsupported [MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type), [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration) to the next child.
   9. If child has [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes) or [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes) attributes, set el's [dimension attribute source](#483-the-img-element) to child. Otherwise, set el's [dimension attribute source](#483-the-img-element) to el.
   10. [Normalize the source densities](#484312-normalizing-the-source-densities) of source set.
   11. Set el's [source set](#4843-processing-model) to source set.
   12. Return.

> [!note]
> Each [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element independently considers its previous sibling [`source`](#482-the-source-element) elements plus the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element itself for selecting an [image source](#4843-processing-model), ignoring any other (invalid) elements, including other [`img`](#483-the-img-element) elements in the same [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element, or [`source`](#482-the-source-element) elements that are following siblings of the relevant [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element.

###### 4.8.4.3.10 Parsing a srcset attribute

When asked to parse a srcset attribute from an element, parse the value of the element's [srcset attribute](#48421-srcset-attributes) as follows:
1. Let input be the value passed to this algorithm.
2. Let position be a pointer into input, initially pointing at the start of the string.
3. Let candidates be an initially empty [source set](#4843-processing-model).
4. *Splitting loop*: [Collect a sequence of code points](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) that are [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) or U+002C COMMA characters from input given position. If any U+002C COMMA characters were collected, that is a [parse error](#4843-processing-model).
5. If position is past the end of input, return candidates.
6. [Collect a sequence of code points](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) that are not [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) from input given position, and let url be the result.
7. Let descriptors be a new empty list.
8. If url ends with U+002C (,):
   1. Remove all trailing U+002C COMMA characters from url. If this removed more than one character, that is a [parse error](#4843-processing-model).

   Otherwise:
   1. *Descriptor tokenizer*: [Skip ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) within input given position.
   2. Let current descriptor be the empty string.
   3. Let state be *in descriptor*.
   4. Let c be the character at position. Do the following depending on the value of state. For the purpose of this step, "EOF" is a special character representing that position is past the end of input.

      *In descriptor*

      Do the following, depending on the value of c:

      [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points)

      If current descriptor is not empty, append current descriptor to descriptors and let current descriptor be the empty string. Set state to *after descriptor*.

      U+002C COMMA (,)

      Advance position to the next character in input. If current descriptor is not empty, append current descriptor to descriptors. Jump to the step labeled *descriptor parser*.

      U+0028 LEFT PARENTHESIS (()

      Append c to current descriptor. Set state to *in parens*.

      EOF

      If current descriptor is not empty, append current descriptor to descriptors. Jump to the step labeled *descriptor parser*.

      Anything else

      Append c to current descriptor.

      *In parens*

      Do the following, depending on the value of c:

      U+0029 RIGHT PARENTHESIS ())

      Append c to current descriptor. Set state to *in descriptor*.

      EOF

      Append current descriptor to descriptors. Jump to the step labeled *descriptor parser*.

      Anything else

      Append c to current descriptor.

      *After descriptor*

      Do the following, depending on the value of c:

      [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points)

      Stay in this state.

      EOF

      Jump to the step labeled *descriptor parser*.

      Anything else

      Set state to *in descriptor*. Set position to the *previous* character in input.

      Advance position to the next character in input. Repeat this step.

      > [!note]
      > In order to be compatible with future additions, this algorithm supports multiple descriptors and descriptors with parens.

9. *Descriptor parser*: Let error be *no*.
10. Let width be *absent*.
11. Let density be *absent*.
12. Let future-compat-h be *absent*.
13. For each descriptor in descriptors, run the appropriate set of steps from the following list:

    If the descriptor consists of a [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers) followed by a U+0077 LATIN SMALL LETTER W character
    1. If the user agent does not support the [`sizes`](#483-the-img-element) attribute, let error be *yes*.

       > [!note]
       > A conforming user agent will support the [`sizes`](#483-the-img-element) attribute. However, user agents typically implement and ship features in an incremental manner in practice.

    2. If width and density are not both *absent*, then let error be *yes*.
    3. Apply the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers) to the descriptor. If the result is 0, let error be *yes*. Otherwise, let width be the result.

    If the descriptor consists of a [valid floating-point number](#2343-floating-point-numbers) followed by a U+0078 LATIN SMALL LETTER X character
    1. If width, density and future-compat-h are not all *absent*, then let error be *yes*.
    2. Apply the [rules for parsing floating-point number values](#2343-floating-point-numbers) to the descriptor. If the result is less than 0, let error be *yes*. Otherwise, let density be the result.

       > [!note]
       > If density is 0, the [natural dimensions](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions) will be infinite. User agents are [expected to have limits](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#32-avoid-limits-on-algorithm-inputs) in how big images can be rendered.

    If the descriptor consists of a [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers) followed by a U+0068 LATIN SMALL LETTER H character

    This is a [parse error](#4843-processing-model).
    1. If future-compat-h and density are not both *absent*, then let error be *yes*.
    2. Apply the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers) to the descriptor. If the result is 0, let error be *yes*. Otherwise, let future-compat-h be the result.

    Anything else

    Let error be *yes*.

14. If future-compat-h is not *absent* and width is *absent*, let error be *yes*.
15. If error is still *no*, then append a new [image source](#4843-processing-model) to candidates whose URL is url, associated with a width width if not *absent* and a pixel density density if not *absent*. Otherwise, there is a [parse error](#4843-processing-model).
16. Return to the step labeled *splitting loop*.

###### 4.8.4.3.11 Parsing a sizes attribute

When asked to parse a sizes attribute from an element element, with an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element or null img:
1. Let unparsed sizes list be the result of [parsing a comma-separated list of component values](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#parse-a-comma-separated-list-of-component-values) from the value of element's [sizes attribute](#48422-sizes-attributes) (or the empty string, if the attribute is absent). [\[CSSSYNTAX\]](#references)
2. Let size be null.
3. For each unparsed size in unparsed sizes list:
   1. Remove all consecutive [<whitespace-token>](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#typedef-whitespace-token)s from the end of unparsed size. If unparsed size is now empty, then that is a [parse error](#4843-processing-model); [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   2. If the last [component value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#component-value) in unparsed size is a valid non-negative [<source-size-value>](#48422-sizes-attributes), then set size to its value and remove the [component value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#component-value) from unparsed size. Any CSS function other than the [math functions](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#math-function) is invalid. Otherwise, there is a [parse error](#4843-processing-model); [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   3. If size is [`auto`](#48422-sizes-attributes), and img is not null, and img [allows auto-sizes](#483-the-img-element):
      1. If img is [being rendered](#151-introduction), then set size to the [concrete object size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#concrete-object-size) width of img, in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px), and set img's [last auto-sizes width](#4843-processing-model) to size.
      2. Otherwise, if img's [last auto-sizes width](#4843-processing-model) is not null, then set size to img's [last auto-sizes width](#4843-processing-model).

      > [!note]
      > If size is still [`auto`](#48422-sizes-attributes), then it will be ignored.

   4. Remove all consecutive [<whitespace-token>](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#typedef-whitespace-token)s from the end of unparsed size. If unparsed size is now empty:
      1. If this was not the last item in unparsed sizes list, that is a [parse error](#4843-processing-model).
      2. If size is not [`auto`](#48422-sizes-attributes), then return size. Otherwise, continue.
   5. Parse the remaining [component values](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#component-value) in unparsed size as a [<media-condition>](https://drafts.csswg.org/mediaqueries/#typedef-media-condition). If it does not parse correctly, or it does parse correctly but the [<media-condition>](https://drafts.csswg.org/mediaqueries/#typedef-media-condition) evaluates to false, [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration). [\[MQ\]](#references)
   6. If size is not [`auto`](#48422-sizes-attributes), then return size. Otherwise, continue.

4. Return `100vw`.

> [!note]
> It is invalid to use a bare [<source-size-value>](#48422-sizes-attributes) that is a [<length>](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#lengths) (without an accompanying [<media-condition>](https://drafts.csswg.org/mediaqueries/#typedef-media-condition)) as an entry in the [<source-size-list>](#48422-sizes-attributes) that is not the last entry. However, the parsing algorithm allows it at any point in the [<source-size-list>](#48422-sizes-attributes), and will accept it immediately as the size if the preceding entries in the list weren't used. This is to enable future extensions, and protect against simple author errors such as a final trailing comma. A bare [`auto`](#48422-sizes-attributes) keyword is allowed to have other entries following it to provide a fallback for legacy user agents.

###### 4.8.4.3.12 Normalizing the source densities

An [image source](#4843-processing-model) can have a [pixel density descriptor](#48421-srcset-attributes), a [width descriptor](#48421-srcset-attributes), or no descriptor at all accompanying its URL. Normalizing a [source set](#4843-processing-model) gives every [image source](#4843-processing-model) a [pixel density descriptor](#48421-srcset-attributes).

When asked to normalize the source densities of a [source set](#4843-processing-model) source set, the user agent must do the following:
1. Let source size be source set's [source size](#4843-processing-model).
2. For each [image source](#4843-processing-model) in source set:
   1. If the [image source](#4843-processing-model) has a [pixel density descriptor](#48421-srcset-attributes), [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration) to the next [image source](#4843-processing-model).
   2. Otherwise, if the [image source](#4843-processing-model) has a [width descriptor](#48421-srcset-attributes), replace the [width descriptor](#48421-srcset-attributes) with a [pixel density descriptor](#48421-srcset-attributes) with a [value](#48421-srcset-attributes) of the [width descriptor value](#48421-srcset-attributes) divided by source size and a unit of `x`.

      > [!note]
      > If the [source size](#4843-processing-model) is 0, then the density would be infinity, which results in the [natural dimensions](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions) being 0 by 0.

   3. Otherwise, give the [image source](#4843-processing-model) a [pixel density descriptor](#48421-srcset-attributes) of `1x`.

###### 4.8.4.3.13 Reacting to environment changes

The user agent may at any time run the following algorithm to update an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's image in order to react to changes in the environment. (User agents are *not required* to ever run this algorithm; for example, if the user is not looking at the page any more, the user agent might want to wait until the user has returned to the page before determining which image to use, in case the environment changes again in the meantime.)

> [!note]
> User agents are encouraged to run this algorithm in particular when the user changes the [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport)'s size (e.g. by resizing the window or changing the page zoom), and when an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element is [inserted into a document](#214-dom-trees), so that the [density-corrected natural width and height](#4843-processing-model) match the new [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport), and so that the correct image is chosen when [art direction](#4841-introduction) is involved.
1. [Await a stable state](#8173-processing-model). The [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model) consists of all the remaining steps of this algorithm until the algorithm says the [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model) has ended. (Steps in [synchronous sections](#8173-processing-model) are marked with ⌛.)
2. ⌛ If the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element does not [use `srcset` or `picture`](#4843-processing-model), its [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents), it has image data whose resource type is [`multipart/x-mixed-replace`](#172-multipartx-mixed-replace), or its [pending request](#4843-processing-model) is not null, then return.
3. ⌛ Let selected source and selected pixel density be the URL and pixel density that results from [selecting an image source](#48437-selecting-an-image-source), respectively.
4. ⌛ If selected source is null, then return.
5. ⌛ If selected source and selected pixel density are the same as the element's [last selected source](#4843-processing-model) and [current pixel density](#4843-processing-model), then return.
6. ⌛ Let urlString be the result of [encoding-parsing-and-serializing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given selected source, relative to the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
7. ⌛ If urlString is failure, then return.
8. ⌛ Let corsAttributeState be the state of the element's [`crossorigin`](#483-the-img-element) content attribute.
9. ⌛ Let origin be the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).
10. ⌛ Let client be the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant).
11. ⌛ Let key be a tuple consisting of urlString, corsAttributeState, and, if corsAttributeState is not [No CORS](#254-cors-settings-attributes), origin.
12. ⌛ Let image request be a new [image request](#4843-processing-model) whose [current URL](#4843-processing-model) is urlString.
13. ⌛ Set the element's [pending request](#4843-processing-model) to image request.
14. End the [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model), continuing the remaining steps [in parallel](#211-parallelism).
15. Let finishUpdate be the following steps:
    1. If the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element has experienced [relevant mutations](#48432-reacting-to-dom-mutations) since this algorithm started, then set the [pending request](#4843-processing-model) to null and abort these steps.
    2. Set the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [last selected source](#4843-processing-model) to selected source and the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [current pixel density](#4843-processing-model) to selected pixel density.
    3. Set the image request's [state](#4843-processing-model) to [completely available](#4843-processing-model).
    4. Add the image to the [list of available images](#48433-the-list-of-available-images) using the key key, with the [ignore higher-layer caching](#48433-the-list-of-available-images) flag set.
    5. [Upgrade the pending request to the current request](#48435-updating-the-image-data).
    6. [Prepare image request for presentation](#48436-preparing-an-image-for-presentation) given the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element.
    7. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`load`](#events) at the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element.
16. If the [list of available images](#48433-the-list-of-available-images) contains an entry for key:
    1. Set image request's [image data](#4843-processing-model) to that of the entry.
    2. [Queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element and finishUpdate.
17. Otherwise:
    1. Let request be the result of [creating a potential-CORS request](#251-terminology) given urlString, "`image`", and corsAttributeState.
    2. Set request's [client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client) to client and set request's [initiator](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-initiator) to "`imageset`".
    3. Set request's [referrer policy](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-referrer-policy) to the current state of the element's [`referrerpolicy`](#483-the-img-element) attribute.
    4. Set request's [priority](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-priority) to the current state of the element's [`fetchpriority`](#483-the-img-element) attribute.
    5. [Fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request, with *[processResponse](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#process-response)* set to the following steps given [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response:
       1. If response's [unsafe response](#251-terminology) is a [network error](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-network-error) or if the image format is unsupported (as determined by applying the [image sniffing rules](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#rules-for-sniffing-images-specifically), again as mentioned earlier), or if the user agent is able to determine that image request's image is corrupted in some fatal way such that the image dimensions cannot be obtained, or if the resource type is [`multipart/x-mixed-replace`](#172-multipartx-mixed-replace), then set the [pending request](#4843-processing-model) to null and return.
       2. Otherwise, response's [unsafe response](#251-terminology) is image request's [image data](#4843-processing-model). It can be either [CORS-same-origin](#251-terminology) or [CORS-cross-origin](#251-terminology); this affects the image's interaction with other APIs (e.g., when used on a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element)).
