The `referrerPolicy` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`referrerpolicy`](#485-the-iframe-element) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

The `loading` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`loading`](#485-the-iframe-element) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

The `contentDocument` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [content document](#7313-child-navigables).

The `contentWindow` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [content window](#7313-child-navigables).

> [!example]
> Here is an example of a page using an [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) to include advertising from an advertising broker:
> 
> ```html
> <iframe src="https://ads.example.com/?customerid=923513721&amp;format=banner"
>         width="468" height="60"></iframe>
> ```

#### 4.8.6 The `embed` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Embedded content](#32526-embedded-content).

[Interactive content](#32527-interactive-content).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [embedded content](#32526-embedded-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Nothing](#3251-the-nothing-content-model).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

No [end tag](#13122-end-tags).

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`src`](#486-the-embed-element) — Address of the resource

[`type`](#486-the-embed-element) — Type of embedded resource

[`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes) — Horizontal dimension

[`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes) — Vertical dimension

Any other attribute that has no namespace (see prose).

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-embed).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-embed).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Unsafe](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLEmbedElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, ReflectURL] attribute USVString src;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString type;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString width;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString height;
  Document? getSVGDocument();

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element) element provides an integration point for an external application or interactive content.

The `src` attribute gives the [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) of the resource being embedded. The attribute, if present, must contain a [valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#241-terminology).

If the [`itemprop`](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute is specified on an [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element) element, then the [`src`](#486-the-embed-element) attribute must also be specified.

The `type` attribute, if present, gives the [MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type) by which the plugin to instantiate is selected. The value must be a [valid MIME type string](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-mime-type). If both the [`type`](#486-the-embed-element) attribute and the [`src`](#486-the-embed-element) attribute are present, then the [`type`](#486-the-embed-element) attribute must specify the same type as the explicit [Content-Type metadata](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource) of the resource given by the [`src`](#486-the-embed-element) attribute.

While any of the following conditions are occurring, any [plugin](#216-plugins) instantiated for the element must be removed, and the [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) nothing:
- The element has neither a [`src`](#486-the-embed-element) attribute nor a [`type`](#486-the-embed-element) attribute.
- The element has a [media element](#4811-media-elements) ancestor.
- The element has an ancestor [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element that is *not* showing its [fallback content](#32526-embedded-content).

An [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element) element is said to be potentially active when the following conditions are all met simultaneously:
- The element is [in a document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) or was [in a document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) the last time the [event loop](#8171-definitions) reached [step 1](#8173-processing-model).
- The element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) is [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents).
- The element has either a [`src`](#486-the-embed-element) attribute set or a [`type`](#486-the-embed-element) attribute set (or both).
- The element's [`src`](#486-the-embed-element) attribute is either absent or its value is not the empty string.
- The element is not a descendant of a [media element](#4811-media-elements).
- The element is not a descendant of an [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element that is not showing its [fallback content](#32526-embedded-content).
- The element is [being rendered](#151-introduction), or was [being rendered](#151-introduction) the last time the [event loop](#8171-definitions) reached [step 1](#8173-processing-model).

Whenever an [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element) element that was not [potentially active](#486-the-embed-element) becomes [potentially active](#486-the-embed-element), and whenever a [potentially active](#486-the-embed-element) [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element) element that is remaining [potentially active](#486-the-embed-element) has its [`src`](#486-the-embed-element) attribute set, changed, or removed or its [`type`](#486-the-embed-element) attribute set, changed, or removed, the user agent must [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the embed task source given the element to run [the `embed` element setup steps](#486-the-embed-element) for that element.

The `embed` element setup steps for a given [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element) element element are as follows:
1. If another [task](#8171-definitions) has since been queued to run [the `embed` element setup steps](#486-the-embed-element) for element, then return.
2. If element has a [`src`](#486-the-embed-element) attribute set:
   1. Let url be the result of [encoding-parsing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given element's [`src`](#486-the-embed-element) attribute's value, relative to element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
   2. If url is failure, then return.
   3. Let request be a new [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) whose [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url) is url, [client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client) is element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant), [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) is "`embed`", [credentials mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode) is "`include`", [mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-mode) is "`navigate`", [initiator type](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-initiator-type) is "`embed`", and whose [use-URL-credentials flag](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-use-url-credentials-flag) is set.
   4. [Fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request, with *[processResponse](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#process-response)* set to the following steps given [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response:
      1. If another [task](#8171-definitions) has since been queued to run [the `embed` element setup steps](#486-the-embed-element) for element, then return.
      2. If response is a [network error](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-network-error), then [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`load`](#events) at element, and return.
      3. Let type be the result of determining the [type of content](#486-the-embed-element) given element and response.
      4. Switch on type:

         null
         1. [Display no plugin](#486-the-embed-element) for element.

         Otherwise
         1. If element's [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables) is null, then [create a new child navigable](#7313-child-navigables) for element.
         2. [Navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation) element's [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables) to response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url) using element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), with *[response](#7422-beginning-navigation)* set to response, and *[historyHandling](#7422-beginning-navigation)* set to "[`replace`](#7421-supporting-concepts)".

            > [!note]
            > element's [`src`](#486-the-embed-element) attribute does not get updated if the [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables) gets further navigated to other locations.

         3. element now [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) its [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables).

      Fetching the resource must [delay the load event](#1327-the-end) of element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).

3. Otherwise, [display no plugin](#486-the-embed-element) for element.

To determine the type of the content given an [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element) element element and a [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response, run the following steps:
1. If element has a [`type`](#486-the-embed-element) attribute, and that attribute's value is a type that a [plugin](#216-plugins) supports, then return the value of the [`type`](#486-the-embed-element) attribute.
2. If the [path](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-path) component of response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url) matches a pattern that a [plugin](#216-plugins) supports, then return the type that that plugin can handle.

   > [!example]
   > For example, a plugin might say that it can handle URLs with [path](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-path) components that end with the four character string "`.swf`".

3. If response has explicit [Content-Type metadata](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource), and that value is a type that a [plugin](#216-plugins) supports, then return that value.
4. Return null.

> [!note]
> It is intentional that the above algorithm allows response to have a non-[ok status](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#ok-status). This allows servers to return data for plugins even with error responses (e.g., HTTP 500 Internal Server Error codes can still contain plugin data).

To display no plugin for an [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element) element element:
1. [Destroy a child navigable](#7316-navigable-destruction) given element.
2. Display an indication that no [plugin](#216-plugins) could be found for element, as the contents of element.
3. element now [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) nothing.

> [!note]
> The [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element) element has no [fallback content](#32526-embedded-content); its descendants are ignored.

Whenever an [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element) element that was [potentially active](#486-the-embed-element) stops being [potentially active](#486-the-embed-element), any [plugin](#216-plugins) that had been instantiated for that element must be unloaded.

The [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element) element [potentially delays the load event](#485-the-iframe-element).

The [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element) element supports [dimension attributes](#4817-dimension-attributes).

#### 4.8.7 The `object` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Embedded content](#32526-embedded-content).

[Listed](#4102-categories) [form-associated element](#4102-categories).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [embedded content](#32526-embedded-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Transparent](#3253-transparent-content-models).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`data`](#487-the-object-element) — Address of the resource

[`type`](#487-the-object-element) — Type of embedded resource

[`name`](#487-the-object-element) — Name of [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables)

[`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) — Associates the element with a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element

[`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes) — Horizontal dimension

[`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes) — Vertical dimension

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-object).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-object).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Unsafe](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLObjectElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, ReflectURL] attribute USVString data;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString type;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString name;
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString width;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString height;
  readonly attribute Document? contentDocument;
  readonly attribute WindowProxy? contentWindow;
  Document? getSVGDocument();

  readonly attribute boolean willValidate;
  readonly attribute ValidityState validity;
  readonly attribute DOMString validationMessage;
  boolean checkValidity();
  boolean reportValidity();
  undefined setCustomValidity(DOMString error);

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

Depending on the type of content instantiated by the [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element, the node also supports other interfaces.

The [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element can represent an external resource, which, depending on the type of the resource, will either be treated as an image or as a [child navigable](#7313-child-navigables).

The `data` attribute specifies the [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) of the resource. It must be present, and must contain a [valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#241-terminology).

The `type` attribute, if present, specifies the type of the resource. If present, the attribute must be a [valid MIME type string](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-mime-type).

The `name` attribute, if present, must be a [valid navigable target name](#7317-navigable-target-names). The given value is used to name the element's [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables), if applicable, and if present when the element's [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables) is [created](#7313-child-navigables).

Whenever one of the following conditions occur:
- the element is created,
- the element is popped off the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) of an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) or [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents),
- the element is not on the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) of an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) or [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents), and it is either [inserted into a document](#214-dom-trees) or [removed from a document](#214-dom-trees),
- the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) changes whether it is [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents),
- one of the element's ancestor [`object`](#487-the-object-element) elements changes to or from showing its [fallback content](#32526-embedded-content),
- the element's [`classid`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute is set, changed, or removed,
- the element's [`classid`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute is not present, and its [`data`](#487-the-object-element) attribute is set, changed, or removed,
- neither the element's [`classid`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute nor its [`data`](#487-the-object-element) attribute are present, and its [`type`](#487-the-object-element) attribute is set, changed, or removed,
- the element changes from [being rendered](#151-introduction) to not being rendered, or vice versa,

...the user agent must [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given the [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element to run the following steps to (re)determine what the [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element represents. This [task](#8171-definitions) being [queued](#8172-queuing-tasks) or actively running must [delay the load event](#1327-the-end) of the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
1. If the user has indicated a preference that this [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element's [fallback content](#32526-embedded-content) be shown instead of the element's usual behavior, then jump to the step below labeled *fallback*.

   > [!note]
   > For example, a user could ask for the element's [fallback content](#32526-embedded-content) to be shown because that content uses a format that the user finds more accessible.

2. If the element has an ancestor [media element](#4811-media-elements), or has an ancestor [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element that is *not* showing its [fallback content](#32526-embedded-content), or if the element is not [in a document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) whose [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) is non-null, or if the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents), or if the element is still in the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) of an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) or [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents), or if the element is not [being rendered](#151-introduction), then jump to the step below labeled *fallback*.
3. If the [`data`](#487-the-object-element) attribute is present and its value is not the empty string:
   1. If the [`type`](#487-the-object-element) attribute is present and its value is not a type that the user agent supports, then the user agent may jump to the step below labeled *fallback* without fetching the content to examine its real type.
   2. Let url be the result of [encoding-parsing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given the [`data`](#487-the-object-element) attribute's value, relative to the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
   3. If url is failure, then [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) at the element and jump to the step below labeled *fallback*.
   4. Let request be a new [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) whose [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url) is url, [client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client) is the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant), [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) is "`object`", [credentials mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode) is "`include`", [mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-mode) is "`navigate`", [initiator type](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-initiator-type) is "`object`", and whose [use-URL-credentials flag](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-use-url-credentials-flag) is set.
   5. [Fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request.

      Fetching the resource must [delay the load event](#1327-the-end) of the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) until the [task](#8171-definitions) that is [queued](#8172-queuing-tasks) by the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) once the resource has been fetched (defined next) has been run.

   6. If the resource is not yet available (e.g. because the resource was not available in the cache, so that loading the resource required making a request over the network), then jump to the step below labeled *fallback*. The [task](#8171-definitions) that is [queued](#8172-queuing-tasks) by the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) once the resource is available must restart this algorithm from this step. Resources can load incrementally; user agents may opt to consider a resource "available" whenever enough data has been obtained to begin processing the resource.
   7. If the load failed (e.g. there was an HTTP 404 error, there was a DNS error), [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) at the element, then jump to the step below labeled *fallback*.
   8. Determine the resource type, as follows:
      1. Let the resource type be unknown.
      2. If the user agent is configured to strictly obey Content-Type headers for this resource, and the resource has associated [Content-Type metadata](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource), then let the resource type be the type specified in the resource's [Content-Type metadata](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource), and jump to the step below labeled *handler*.

         > [!warning]
         > This can introduce a vulnerability, wherein a site is trying to embed a resource that uses a particular type, but the remote site overrides that and instead furnishes the user agent with a resource that triggers a different type of content with different security characteristics.

      3. Run the appropriate set of steps from the following list:

         If the resource has associated [Content-Type metadata](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource)
         1. Let binary be false.
         2. If the type specified in the resource's [Content-Type metadata](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource) is "[`text/plain`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.1.3)", and the result of applying the [rules for distinguishing if a resource is text or binary](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#rules-for-text-or-binary) to the resource is that the resource is not [`text/plain`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.1.3), then set binary to true.
         3. If the type specified in the resource's [Content-Type metadata](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource) is "[`application/octet-stream`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.5.1)", then set binary to true.
         4. If binary is false, then let the resource type be the type specified in the resource's [Content-Type metadata](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource), and jump to the step below labeled *handler*.
         5. If there is a [`type`](#487-the-object-element) attribute present on the [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element, and its value is not [`application/octet-stream`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.5.1), then run the following steps:
            1. If the attribute's value is a type that starts with "`image/`" that is not also an [XML MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#xml-mime-type), then let the resource type be the type specified in that [`type`](#487-the-object-element) attribute.
            2. Jump to the step below labeled *handler*.

         Otherwise, if the resource does not have associated [Content-Type metadata](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource)
         1. If there is a [`type`](#487-the-object-element) attribute present on the [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element, then let the tentative type be the type specified in that [`type`](#487-the-object-element) attribute.

            Otherwise, let tentative type be the [computed type of the resource](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#computed-mime-type).

         2. If tentative type is *not* [`application/octet-stream`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.5.1), then let resource type be tentative type and jump to the step below labeled *handler*.

      4. If applying the [URL parser](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser) algorithm to the [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) of the specified resource (after any redirects) results in a [URL record](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) whose [path](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-path) component matches a pattern that a [plugin](#216-plugins) supports, then let resource type be the type that that plugin can handle.

         > [!example]
         > For example, a plugin might say that it can handle resources with [path](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-path) components that end with the four character string "`.swf`".

      > [!note]
      > It is possible for this step to finish, or for one of the substeps above to jump straight to the next step, with resource type still being unknown. In both cases, the next step will trigger fallback.

   9. *Handler*: Handle the content as given by the first of the following cases that matches:

      If the resource type is an [XML MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#xml-mime-type), or if the resource type does not start with "`image/`"

      If the [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element's [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables) is null, then [create a new child navigable](#7313-child-navigables) for the element.

      Let response be the [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) from [fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch).

      If response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url) does not [match `about:blank`](#241-terminology), then [navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation) the element's [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables) to response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url) using the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), with *[historyHandling](#7422-beginning-navigation)* set to "[`replace`](#7421-supporting-concepts)".

      > [!note]
      > The [`data`](#487-the-object-element) attribute of the [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element doesn't get updated if the [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables) gets further [navigated](#7422-beginning-navigation) to other locations.

      The [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) its [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables).

      If the resource type starts with "`image/`", and support for images has not been disabled

      [Destroy a child navigable](#7316-navigable-destruction) given the [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element.

      Apply the [image sniffing](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#rules-for-sniffing-images-specifically) rules to determine the type of the image.

      The [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the specified image.

      If the image cannot be rendered, e.g. because it is malformed or in an unsupported format, jump to the step below labeled *fallback*.

      Otherwise

      The given resource type is not supported. Jump to the step below labeled *fallback*.

      > [!note]
      > If the previous step ended with the resource type being unknown, this is the case that is triggered.

   10. The element's contents are not part of what the [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element represents.
   11. If the [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element does not represent its [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables), then once the resource is completely loaded, [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given the [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`load`](#events) at the element.

       > [!note]
       > If the element *does* represent its [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables), then an analogous task will be queued when the created [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is [completely finished loading](#758-finishing-the-loading-process).

   12. Return.

4. *Fallback*: The [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the element's children. This is the element's [fallback content](#32526-embedded-content). [Destroy a child navigable](#7316-navigable-destruction) given the element.

Due to the algorithm above, the contents of [`object`](#487-the-object-element) elements act as [fallback content](#32526-embedded-content), used only when referenced resources can't be shown (e.g. because it returned a 404 error). This allows multiple [`object`](#487-the-object-element) elements to be nested inside each other, targeting multiple user agents with different capabilities, with the user agent picking the first one it supports.

The [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element [potentially delays the load event](#485-the-iframe-element).

The [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) attribute is used to explicitly associate the [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element with its [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms).

The [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element supports [dimension attributes](#4817-dimension-attributes).

The `contentDocument` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [content document](#7313-child-navigables).

The `contentWindow` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [content window](#7313-child-navigables).

The [`willValidate`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), [`validity`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), and [`validationMessage`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) attributes, and the [`checkValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), [`reportValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), and [`setCustomValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) methods, are part of the [constraint validation API](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api). The [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) IDL attribute is part of the element's forms API.

> [!example]
> In this example, an HTML page is embedded in another using the [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element.
> 
> ```html
> <figure>
>  <object data="clock.html"></object>
>  <figcaption>My HTML Clock</figcaption>
> </figure>
> ```

#### 4.8.8 The `video` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Embedded content](#32526-embedded-content).

If the element has a [`controls`](#481113-user-interface) attribute: [Interactive content](#32527-interactive-content).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [embedded content](#32526-embedded-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

If the element has a [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) attribute: zero or more [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) elements, then [transparent](#3253-transparent-content-models), but with no [media element](#4811-media-elements) descendants.

If the element does not have a [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) attribute: zero or more [`source`](#482-the-source-element) elements, then zero or more [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) elements, then [transparent](#3253-transparent-content-models), but with no [media element](#4811-media-elements) descendants.

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) — Address of the resource

[`crossorigin`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) — How the element handles crossorigin requests

[`poster`](#488-the-video-element) — Poster frame to show prior to video playback

[`preload`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) — Hints how much buffering the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) will likely need

[`autoplay`](#48117-ready-states) — Hint that the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) can be started automatically when the page is loaded

[`playsinline`](#488-the-video-element) — Encourage the user agent to display video content within the element's playback area

[`loop`](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) — Whether to loop the [media resource](#4811-media-elements)

[`muted`](#481113-user-interface) — Whether to mute the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) by default

[`controls`](#481113-user-interface) — Show user agent controls

[`loading`](#4811-media-elements) — Used when determining loading deferral

[`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes) — Horizontal dimension

[`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes) — Vertical dimension

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-video).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-video).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLVideoElement : HTMLMediaElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute unsigned long width;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute unsigned long height;
  readonly attribute unsigned long videoWidth;
  readonly attribute unsigned long videoHeight;
  [CEReactions, ReflectURL] attribute USVString poster;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean playsInline;

};
```

A [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element is used for playing videos or movies, and audio files with captions.

Content may be provided inside the [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element. User agents should not show this content to the user; it is intended for older web browsers which do not support [`video`](#488-the-video-element), so that text can be shown to the users of these older browsers informing them of how to access the video contents.

> [!note]
> In particular, this content is not intended to address accessibility concerns. To make video content accessible to the partially sighted, the blind, the hard-of-hearing, the deaf, and those with other physical or cognitive disabilities, a variety of features are available. Captions can be provided, either embedded in the video stream or as external files using the [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element. Sign-language tracks can be embedded in the video stream. Audio descriptions can be embedded in the video stream or in text form using a [WebVTT file](https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#webvtt-file) referenced using the [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element and synthesized into speech by the user agent. WebVTT can also be used to provide chapter titles. For users who would rather not use a media element at all, transcripts or other textual alternatives can be provided by simply linking to them in the prose near the [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element. [\[WEBVTT\]](#references)

The [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element is a [media element](#4811-media-elements) whose [media data](#4811-media-elements) is ostensibly video data, possibly with associated audio data.

The [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element has an internal [shadow tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree) with no [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element) elements.

The [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource), [`crossorigin`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource), [`preload`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource), [`autoplay`](#48117-ready-states), [`loop`](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), [`muted`](#481113-user-interface), and [`controls`](#481113-user-interface) attributes are [the attributes common to all media elements](#4811-media-elements).

The `poster` attribute gives the [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) of an image file that the user agent can show while no video data is available. The attribute, if present, must contain a [valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#241-terminology).

If the specified resource is to be used, then, when the element is created or when the [`poster`](#488-the-video-element) attribute is set, changed, or removed, the user agent must run the following steps to determine the element's poster frame (regardless of the value of the element's [show poster flag](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource)):
1. If there is an existing instance of this algorithm running for this [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element, abort that instance of this algorithm without changing the [poster frame](#488-the-video-element).
2. If the [`poster`](#488-the-video-element) attribute's value is the empty string or if the attribute is absent:
   1. Set the [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element's [poster lazy load resumption steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) to null.
   2. There is no [poster frame](#488-the-video-element); return.
3. Let url be the result of [encoding-parsing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given the [`poster`](#488-the-video-element) attribute's value, relative to the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
4. If url is failure, then return. There is no [poster frame](#488-the-video-element).
5. Let request be a new [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) whose [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url) is url, [client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client) is the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant), [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) is "`image`", [initiator type](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-initiator-type) is "`video`", [credentials mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode) is "`include`", and whose [use-URL-credentials flag](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-use-url-credentials-flag) is set.
6. If the [will lazy load element steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) given the [`video`](#488-the-video-element) return true:
   1. Let posterResumptionSteps be the rest of this algorithm starting with the step labeled *Fetch*.
   2. Set the [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element's [poster lazy load resumption steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) to posterResumptionSteps.
   3. Return.
7. [Fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request. This must [delay the load event](#1327-the-end) of the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
8. If an image is thus obtained, the [poster frame](#488-the-video-element) is that image. Otherwise, there is no [poster frame](#488-the-video-element).

> [!note]
> The image given by the [`poster`](#488-the-video-element) attribute, the *[poster frame](#488-the-video-element)*, is intended to be a representative frame of the video (typically one of the first non-blank frames) that gives the user an idea of what the video is like.

The `playsinline` attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes). If present, it serves as a hint to the user agent that the video ought to be displayed "inline" in the document by default, constrained to the element's playback area, instead of being displayed fullscreen or in an independent resizable window.

> [!note]
> The absence of the [`playsinline`](#488-the-video-element) attribute does not imply that the video will display fullscreen by default. Indeed, most user agents have chosen to play all videos inline by default, and in such user agents the [`playsinline`](#488-the-video-element) attribute has no effect.

If the [`poster`](#488-the-video-element) attribute is present and the [`loading`](#4811-media-elements) attribute is in the [Lazy](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) state, the user agent must defer loading the poster image source data until the element's [lazy load resumption steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) are invoked.

> [!example]
> ```html
> <video src="1.mp4" poster="1.jpg" type="video/mp4">
> <video src="2.mp4" type="video/mp4" loading="eager">
> <video src="3.mp4" type="video/mp4" loading="lazy">
> <video src="4.mp4" type="video/mp4" loading="lazy" autoplay>
> <div id="very-large"></div> <!-- Everything after this div is below the viewport -->
> <video src="5.mp4" type="video/mp4">
> <video src="6.mp4" type="video/mp4" loading="lazy">
> <video src="7.mp4" type="video/mp4" autoplay loading="lazy">
> <video src="8.mp4" type="video/mp4" poster="8.jpg" loading="lazy">
> <video src="9.mp4" type="video/mp4" preload="none" poster="9.jpg" loading="lazy">
> <video src="10.mp4" type="video/mp4" preload="metadata" loading="lazy">
> <video src="11.mp4" type="video/mp4" poster="11.jpg" preload="none" loading="eager">
> ```
> 
> In the example above, the videos load as follows:
> 
> `1.mp4`
> 
> The video and poster image load eagerly and delay the window's load event.
> 
> `2.mp4`, `5.mp4`
> 
> The videos load eagerly and delay the window's load event.
> 
> `3.mp4`
> 
> The video loads when layout is known, due to being in the viewport, however it does not delay the window's load event.
> 
> `4.mp4`
> 
> The video loads and autoplay playback begins when layout is known, due to being in the viewport, however it does not delay the window's load event.
> 
> `6.mp4`
> 
> The video loads only once scrolled into the viewport, and does not delay the window's load event.
> 
> `7.mp4`
> 
> The video loads and autoplay playback begins only once scrolled into the viewport, and does not delay the window's load event.
> 
> `8.mp4`
> 
> The video and poster image load only once scrolled into the viewport, and does not delay the window's load event.
> 
> `9.mp4`
> 
> The video does not load until played. The poster image loads only once scrolled into the viewport, and does not delay the window's load event.
> 
> `10.mp4`
> 
> The video's metadata loads only once scrolled into the viewport, and does not delay the window's load event.
> 
> `11.mp4`
> 
> The video does not load until played. The poster image loads eagerly and delays the window's load event.

---

A [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element represents what is given for the first matching condition in the list below:

When no video data is available (the element's [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) attribute is either [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#48117-ready-states), or [`HAVE_METADATA`](#48117-ready-states) but no video data has yet been obtained at all, or the element's [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) attribute is any subsequent value but the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) does not have a video channel)

The [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) its [poster frame](#488-the-video-element), if any, or else [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black) with no [natural dimensions](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions).

When the [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element is [paused](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) is the first frame of video, and the element's [show poster flag](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) is set

The [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) its [poster frame](#488-the-video-element), if any, or else the first frame of the video.

When the [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element is [paused](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), and the frame of video corresponding to the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) is not available (e.g. because the video is seeking or buffering)

When the [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element is neither [potentially playing](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) nor [paused](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) (e.g. when seeking or stalled)

The [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the last frame of the video to have been rendered.

When the [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element is [paused](#48118-playing-the-media-resource)

The [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the frame of video corresponding to the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource).

Otherwise (the [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element has a video channel and is [potentially playing](#48118-playing-the-media-resource))

The [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the frame of video at the continuously increasing ["current" position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource). When the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) changes such that the last frame rendered is no longer the frame corresponding to the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) in the video, the new frame must be rendered.

Frames of video must be obtained from the video track that was [selected](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) when the [event loop](#8171-definitions) last reached [step 1](#8173-processing-model).

> [!note]
> Which frame in a video stream corresponds to a particular playback position is defined by the video stream's format.

The [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element also [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) any [text track cues](#4811111-text-track-model) whose [text track cue active flag](#4811111-text-track-model) is set and whose [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) is in the [showing](#4811111-text-track-model) mode, and any audio from the [media resource](#4811-media-elements), at the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource).

Any audio associated with the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) must, if played, be played synchronized with the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), at the element's [effective media volume](#481113-user-interface). The user agent must play the audio from audio tracks that were [enabled](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) when the [event loop](#8171-definitions) last reached step 1.

In addition to the above, the user agent may provide messages to the user (such as "buffering", "no video loaded", "error", or more detailed information) by overlaying text or icons on the video or other areas of the element's playback area, or in another appropriate manner.

User agents that cannot render the video may instead make the element [represent](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a link to an external video playback utility or to the video data itself.

When a [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element's [media resource](#4811-media-elements) has a video channel, the element provides a [paint source](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images-4/#paint-source) whose width is the [media resource](#4811-media-elements)'s [natural width](#488-the-video-element), whose height is the [media resource](#4811-media-elements)'s [natural height](#488-the-video-element), and whose appearance is the frame of video corresponding to the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), if that is available, or else (e.g. when the video is seeking or buffering) its previous appearance, if any, or else (e.g. because the video is still loading the first frame) blackness.

---

`video.videoWidth`

`video.videoHeight`

These attributes return the natural dimensions of the video, or 0 if the dimensions are not known.

The natural width and natural height of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) are the dimensions of the resource in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) after taking into account the resource's dimensions, aspect ratio, clean aperture, resolution, and so forth, as defined for the format used by the resource. If an anamorphic format does not define how to apply the aspect ratio to the video data's dimensions to obtain the "correct" dimensions, then the user agent must apply the ratio by increasing one dimension and leaving the other unchanged.

The `videoWidth` getter steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) attribute is [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#48117-ready-states), then return 0.
2. Return the [natural width](#488-the-video-element) of the video in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px).

The `videoHeight` getter steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) attribute is [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#48117-ready-states), then return 0.
2. Return the [natural height](#488-the-video-element) of the video in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px).

Whenever the [natural width](#488-the-video-element) or [natural height](#488-the-video-element) of the video changes (including, for example, because the [selected video track](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) was changed), if the element's [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) attribute is not [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#48117-ready-states), the user agent must [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`resize`](#481116-events-summary) at the [media element](#4811-media-elements).

The [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element supports [dimension attributes](#4817-dimension-attributes).

In the absence of style rules to the contrary, video content should be rendered inside the element's playback area such that the video content is shown centered in the playback area at the largest possible size that fits completely within it, with the video content's aspect ratio being preserved. Thus, if the aspect ratio of the playback area does not match the aspect ratio of the video, the video will be shown letterboxed or pillarboxed. Areas of the element's playback area that do not contain the video represent nothing.

> [!note]
> In user agents that implement CSS, the above requirement can be implemented by using the [style rule suggested in the Rendering section](#1541-embedded-content).

The [natural width](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-width) of a [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element's playback area is the [natural width](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-width) of the [poster frame](#488-the-video-element), if that is available and the element currently [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) its poster frame; otherwise, it is the [natural width](#488-the-video-element) of the video resource, if that is available; otherwise the [natural width](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-width) is missing.

The [natural height](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-height) of a [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element's playback area is the [natural height](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-height) of the [poster frame](#488-the-video-element), if that is available and the element currently [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) its poster frame; otherwise it is the [natural height](#488-the-video-element) of the video resource, if that is available; otherwise the [natural height](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-height) is missing.

The [default object size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#default-object-size) is a width of 300 [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) and a height of 150 [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px). [\[CSSIMAGES\]](#references)

---

User agents should provide controls to enable or disable the display of closed captions, audio description tracks, and other additional data associated with the video stream, though such features should, again, not interfere with the page's normal rendering.

User agents may allow users to view the video content in manners more suitable to the user, such as fullscreen or in an independent resizable window. User agents may even trigger such a viewing mode by default upon playing a video, although they should not do so when the [`playsinline`](#488-the-video-element) attribute is specified. As with the other user interface features, controls to enable this should not interfere with the page's normal rendering unless the user agent is [exposing a user interface](#481113-user-interface). In such an independent viewing mode, however, user agents may make full user interfaces visible, even if the [`controls`](#481113-user-interface) attribute is absent.

User agents may allow video playback to affect system features that could interfere with the user's experience; for example, user agents could disable screensavers while video playback is in progress.

---

> [!example]
> This example shows how to detect when a video has failed to play correctly:
> 
> ```html
> <script>
>  function failed(e) {
>    // video playback failed - show a message saying why
>    switch (e.target.error.code) {
>      case e.target.error.MEDIA_ERR_ABORTED:
>        alert('You aborted the video playback.');
>        break;
>      case e.target.error.MEDIA_ERR_NETWORK:
>        alert('A network error caused the video download to fail part-way.');
>        break;
>      case e.target.error.MEDIA_ERR_DECODE:
>        alert('The video playback was aborted due to a corruption problem or because the video used features your browser did not support.');
>        break;
>      case e.target.error.MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED:
>        alert('The video could not be loaded, either because the server or network failed or because the format is not supported.');
>        break;
>      default:
>        alert('An unknown error occurred.');
>        break;
>    }
>  }
> </script>
> <p><video src="tgif.vid" autoplay controls onerror="failed(event)"></video></p>
> <p><a href="tgif.vid">Download the video file</a>.</p>
> ```

#### 4.8.9 The `audio` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Embedded content](#32526-embedded-content).

If the element has a [`controls`](#481113-user-interface) attribute: [Interactive content](#32527-interactive-content).

If the element has a [`controls`](#481113-user-interface) attribute: [Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [embedded content](#32526-embedded-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

If the element has a [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) attribute: zero or more [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) elements, then [transparent](#3253-transparent-content-models), but with no [media element](#4811-media-elements) descendants.

If the element does not have a [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) attribute: zero or more [`source`](#482-the-source-element) elements, then zero or more [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) elements, then [transparent](#3253-transparent-content-models), but with no [media element](#4811-media-elements) descendants.

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) — Address of the resource

[`crossorigin`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) — How the element handles crossorigin requests

[`preload`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) — Hints how much buffering the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) will likely need

[`autoplay`](#48117-ready-states) — Hint that the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) can be started automatically when the page is loaded

[`loop`](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) — Whether to loop the [media resource](#4811-media-elements)

[`muted`](#481113-user-interface) — Whether to mute the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) by default

[`controls`](#481113-user-interface) — Show user agent controls

[`loading`](#4811-media-elements) — Used when determining loading deferral

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-audio).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-audio).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window,
 LegacyFactoryFunction=Audio(optional DOMString src)]
interface HTMLAudioElement : HTMLMediaElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();
};
```

An [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a sound or audio stream.

Content may be provided inside the [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) element. User agents should not show this content to the user; it is intended for older web browsers which do not support [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element), so that text can be shown to the users of these older browsers informing them of how to access the audio contents.

> [!note]
> In particular, this content is not intended to address accessibility concerns. To make audio content accessible to the deaf or to those with other physical or cognitive disabilities, a variety of features are available. If captions or a sign language video are available, the [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element can be used instead of the [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) element to play the audio, allowing users to enable the visual alternatives. Chapter titles can be provided to aid navigation, using the [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element and a [WebVTT file](https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#webvtt-file). And, naturally, transcripts or other textual alternatives can be provided by simply linking to them in the prose near the [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) element. [\[WEBVTT\]](#references)

The [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) element is a [media element](#4811-media-elements) whose [media data](#4811-media-elements) is ostensibly audio data.

The [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) element has an internal [shadow tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree) with no [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element) elements.

The [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource), [`crossorigin`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource), [`preload`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource), [`autoplay`](#48117-ready-states), [`loop`](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), [`muted`](#481113-user-interface), [`controls`](#481113-user-interface), and [`loading`](#4811-media-elements) attributes are [the attributes common to all media elements](#4811-media-elements).

> [!note]
> [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) elements without a [`controls`](#481113-user-interface) attribute will not be displayed by the user agent, preventing them from lazy loading.

> [!example]
> ```html
> <audio src="1.mp3" type="audio/mpeg" controls>
> <audio src="2.mp3" type="audio/mpeg" controls loading="eager">
> <audio src="3.mp3" type="audio/mpeg" controls loading="lazy">
> <audio src="4.mp3" type="audio/mpeg" controls loading="lazy" autoplay>
> <div id="very-large"></div> <!-- Everything after this div is below the viewport -->
> <audio src="5.mp3" type="audio/mpeg" controls>
> <audio src="6.mp3" type="audio/mpeg" controls loading="lazy">
> <audio src="7.mp3" type="audio/mpeg" controls autoplay loading="lazy">
> <audio src="8.mp3" type="audio/mpeg" controls preload="metadata" loading="lazy">
> ```
> 
> In the example above, the audio files load as follows:
> 
> `1.mp3`, `2.mp3`, `5.mp3`
> 
> The audio file loads eagerly and delays the window's load event.
> 
> `3.mp3`
> 
> The audio loads when layout is known, due to being in the viewport, however it does not delay the window's load event.
> 
> `4.mp3`
> 
> The audio loads and autoplay playback begins when layout is known, due to being in the viewport, however it does not delay the window's load event.
> 
> `6.mp3`
> 
> The audio loads only once scrolled into the viewport, and does not delay the window's load event.
> 
> `7.mp3`
> 
> The audio loads and autoplay playback begins only once scrolled into the viewport, and does not delay the window's load event.
> 
> `8.mp3`
> 
> The audio's metadata loads only once scrolled into the viewport, and does not delay the window's load event.

`audio = new Audio([ url ])`

Returns a new [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) element, with the [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) attribute set to the value passed in the argument, if applicable.

A legacy factory function is provided for creating [`HTMLAudioElement`](#489-the-audio-element) objects (in addition to the factory methods from DOM such as [`createElement()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document)): `Audio(src)`. When invoked, the legacy factory function must perform the following steps:
1. Let document be the [current global object](#81333-current)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object).
2. Let audio be the result of [creating an element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) given document, "`audio`", and the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces).
3. [Set an attribute value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) for audio using "[`preload`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource)" and "[`auto`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource)".
4. If src is given, then [set an attribute value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) for audio using "[`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource)" and src. (This will [cause the user agent to invoke](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) the object's [resource selection algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) before returning.)
5. Return audio.

#### 4.8.10 The `track` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

As a child of a [media element](#4811-media-elements), before any [flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Nothing](#3251-the-nothing-content-model).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

No [end tag](#13122-end-tags).

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`kind`](#4810-the-track-element) — The type of text track

[`src`](#4810-the-track-element) — Address of the resource

[`srclang`](#4810-the-track-element) — Language of the text track

[`label`](#4810-the-track-element) — User-visible label

[`default`](#4810-the-track-element) — Enable the track if no other [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) is more suitable

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-track).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-track).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLTrackElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString kind;
  [CEReactions, ReflectURL] attribute USVString src;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString srclang;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString label;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean default;

  const unsigned short NONE = 0;
  const unsigned short LOADING = 1;
  const unsigned short LOADED = 2;
  const unsigned short ERROR = 3;
  readonly attribute unsigned short readyState;

  readonly attribute TextTrack track;
};
```

The [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element allows authors to specify explicit external timed [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) for [media elements](#4811-media-elements). It does not [represent](#322-elements-in-the-dom) anything on its own.

The `kind` attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `subtitles` | Subtitles | Transcription or translation of the dialogue, suitable for when the sound is available but not understood (e.g. because the user does not understand the language of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements)'s audio track). Overlaid on the video. |
| `captions` | Captions | Transcription or translation of the dialogue, sound effects, relevant musical cues, and other relevant audio information, suitable for when sound is unavailable or not clearly audible (e.g. because it is muted, drowned-out by ambient noise, or because the user is deaf). Overlaid on the video; labeled as appropriate for the hard-of-hearing. |
| `descriptions` | Descriptions | Textual descriptions of the video component of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements), intended for audio synthesis when the visual component is obscured, unavailable, or not usable (e.g. because the user is interacting with the application without a screen while driving, or because the user is blind). Synthesized as audio. |
| `chapters` | Chapters metadata | Tracks intended for use from script. Not displayed by the user agent. |
| `metadata` | Metadata |

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* is the [subtitles](#4810-the-track-element) state, and its *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* is the [metadata](#4810-the-track-element) state.

The `src` attribute gives the [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) of the text track data. The value must be a [valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#241-terminology). This attribute must be present.

The element has an associated track URL (a string), initially the empty string.

When the element's [`src`](#4810-the-track-element) attribute is set, run these steps:
1. Let trackURL be failure.
2. Let value be the element's [`src`](#4810-the-track-element) attribute value.
3. If value is not the empty string, then set trackURL to the result of [encoding-parsing-and-serializing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given value, relative to the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
4. Set the element's [track URL](#4810-the-track-element) to trackURL if it is not failure; otherwise to the empty string.

If the element's [track URL](#4810-the-track-element) identifies a WebVTT resource, and the element's [`kind`](#4810-the-track-element) attribute is not in the [chapters metadata](#4810-the-track-element) or [metadata](#4810-the-track-element) state, then the WebVTT file must be a [WebVTT file using caption or subtitle cue text](https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#webvtt-file-using-caption-or-subtitle-cue-text). [\[WEBVTT\]](#references)

The `srclang` attribute gives the language of the text track data. The value must be a valid BCP 47 language tag. This attribute must be present if the element's [`kind`](#4810-the-track-element) attribute is in the [subtitles](#4810-the-track-element) state. [\[BCP47\]](#references)

If the element has a [`srclang`](#4810-the-track-element) attribute whose value is not the empty string, then the element's track language is the value of the attribute. Otherwise, the element has no [track language](#4810-the-track-element).

The `label` attribute gives a user-readable title for the track. This title is used by user agents when listing [subtitle](#4810-the-track-element), [caption](#4810-the-track-element), and [audio description](#4810-the-track-element) tracks in their user interface.

The value of the [`label`](#4810-the-track-element) attribute, if the attribute is present, must not be the empty string. Furthermore, there must not be two [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element children of the same [media element](#4811-media-elements) whose [`kind`](#4810-the-track-element) attributes are in the same state, whose [`srclang`](#4810-the-track-element) attributes are both missing or have values that represent the same language, and whose [`label`](#4810-the-track-element) attributes are again both missing or both have the same value.

If the element has a [`label`](#4810-the-track-element) attribute whose value is not the empty string, then the element's track label is the value of the attribute. Otherwise, the element's [track label](#4810-the-track-element) is an empty string.

The `default` attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes), which, if specified, indicates that the track is to be enabled if the user's preferences do not indicate that another track would be more appropriate.

Each [media element](#4811-media-elements) must have no more than one [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element child whose [`kind`](#4810-the-track-element) attribute is in the [subtitles](#4810-the-track-element) or [captions](#4810-the-track-element) state and whose [`default`](#4810-the-track-element) attribute is specified.

Each [media element](#4811-media-elements) must have no more than one [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element child whose [`kind`](#4810-the-track-element) attribute is in the [description](#4810-the-track-element) state and whose [`default`](#4810-the-track-element) attribute is specified.

Each [media element](#4811-media-elements) must have no more than one [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element child whose [`kind`](#4810-the-track-element) attribute is in the [chapters metadata](#4810-the-track-element) state and whose [`default`](#4810-the-track-element) attribute is specified.

> [!note]
> There is no limit on the number of [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) elements whose [`kind`](#4810-the-track-element) attribute is in the [metadata](#4810-the-track-element) state and whose [`default`](#4810-the-track-element) attribute is specified.

`track.readyState`

Returns the [text track readiness state](#4811111-text-track-model), represented by a number from the following list:

`track.NONE (0)`

The [text track not loaded](#4811111-text-track-model) state.

`track.LOADING (1)`

The [text track loading](#4811111-text-track-model) state.

`track.LOADED (2)`

The [text track loaded](#4811111-text-track-model) state.

`track.ERROR (3)`

The [text track failed to load](#4811111-text-track-model) state.

`track.track`

Returns the [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element's [text track](#4811111-text-track-model).

The `readyState` attribute must return the numeric value corresponding to the [text track readiness state](#4811111-text-track-model) of the [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element's [text track](#4811111-text-track-model), as defined by the following list:

`NONE` (numeric value 0)

The [text track not loaded](#4811111-text-track-model) state.

`LOADING` (numeric value 1)

The [text track loading](#4811111-text-track-model) state.

`LOADED` (numeric value 2)

The [text track loaded](#4811111-text-track-model) state.

`ERROR` (numeric value 3)

The [text track failed to load](#4811111-text-track-model) state.

The `track` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [text track](#4811111-text-track-model).

The `kind` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the content attribute of the same name, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

> [!example]
> This video has subtitles in several languages:
> 
> ```html
> <video src="brave.webm">
>  <track kind=subtitles src=brave.en.vtt srclang=en label="English">
>  <track kind=captions src=brave.en.hoh.vtt srclang=en label="English for the Hard of Hearing">
>  <track kind=subtitles src=brave.fr.vtt srclang=fr lang=fr label="Français">
>  <track kind=subtitles src=brave.de.vtt srclang=de lang=de label="Deutsch">
> </video>
> ```
> 
> (The [`lang`](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes) attributes on the last two describe the language of the [`label`](#4810-the-track-element) attribute, not the language of the subtitles themselves. The language of the subtitles is given by the [`srclang`](#4810-the-track-element) attribute.)

#### 4.8.11 Media elements

[HTMLMediaElement](#4811-media-elements) objects ([`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) and [`video`](#488-the-video-element), in this specification) are simply known as media elements.

```webidl
enum CanPlayTypeResult { "" /* empty string */, "maybe", "probably" };
typedef (MediaStream or MediaSource or Blob) MediaProvider;

[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLMediaElement : HTMLElement {

  // error state
  readonly attribute MediaError? error;

  // network state
  [CEReactions, ReflectURL] attribute USVString src;
  attribute MediaProvider? srcObject;
  readonly attribute USVString currentSrc;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString? crossOrigin;
  const unsigned short NETWORK_EMPTY = 0;
  const unsigned short NETWORK_IDLE = 1;
  const unsigned short NETWORK_LOADING = 2;
  const unsigned short NETWORK_NO_SOURCE = 3;
  readonly attribute unsigned short networkState;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString preload;
  readonly attribute TimeRanges buffered;
  undefined load();
  CanPlayTypeResult canPlayType(DOMString type);

  // ready state
  const unsigned short HAVE_NOTHING = 0;
  const unsigned short HAVE_METADATA = 1;
  const unsigned short HAVE_CURRENT_DATA = 2;
  const unsigned short HAVE_FUTURE_DATA = 3;
  const unsigned short HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA = 4;
  readonly attribute unsigned short readyState;
  readonly attribute boolean seeking;

  // playback state
  attribute double currentTime;
  undefined fastSeek(double time);
  readonly attribute unrestricted double duration;
  object getStartDate();
  readonly attribute boolean paused;
  attribute double defaultPlaybackRate;
  attribute double playbackRate;
  attribute boolean preservesPitch;
  readonly attribute TimeRanges played;
  readonly attribute TimeRanges seekable;
  readonly attribute boolean ended;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean autoplay;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean loop;
  Promise<undefined> play();
  undefined pause();

  // controls
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean controls;
  attribute double volume;
  attribute boolean muted;
  [CEReactions, Reflect="muted"] attribute boolean defaultMuted;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString loading;

  // tracks
  [SameObject] readonly attribute AudioTrackList audioTracks;
  [SameObject] readonly attribute VideoTrackList videoTracks;
  [SameObject] readonly attribute TextTrackList textTracks;
  TextTrack addTextTrack(TextTrackKind kind, optional DOMString label = "", optional DOMString language = "");
};
```

The media element attributes, [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource), [`crossorigin`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource), [`preload`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource), [`autoplay`](#48117-ready-states), [`loop`](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), [`muted`](#481113-user-interface), [`controls`](#481113-user-interface), and [`loading`](#4811-media-elements), apply to all [media elements](#4811-media-elements). They are defined in this section.

The `loading` attribute is a [lazy loading attribute](#257-lazy-loading-attributes). Its purpose is to indicate the policy for loading media resources that are outside the viewport.

When the [`loading`](#4811-media-elements) attribute's state is changed to the [Eager](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) state, the user agent must run these steps:
1. Let resumptionSteps be the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [lazy load resumption steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes).
2. Let posterResumptionSteps be null.
3. If the [media element](#4811-media-elements) is a [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element, then set posterResumptionSteps to the [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element's [poster lazy load resumption steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes).
4. If resumptionSteps is null and posterResumptionSteps is null, then return.
5. If resumptionSteps is not null:
   1. Set the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [lazy load resumption steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) to null.
   2. Invoke resumptionSteps.
6. If posterResumptionSteps is not null:
   1. Set the [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element's [poster lazy load resumption steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) to null.
   2. Invoke posterResumptionSteps.

The `loading` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`loading`](#4811-media-elements) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

When the [`loading`](#4811-media-elements) attribute is in the [Lazy](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) state, it takes precedence over the [`preload`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) attribute by deferring data fetching.

If the [`autoplay`](#48117-ready-states) attribute is present and the [`loading`](#4811-media-elements) attribute is in the [Lazy](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) state, the user agent must also defer starting playback (and any associated network requests autoplay can introduce) until the element's [lazy load resumption steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) are invoked.

[Media elements](#4811-media-elements) are used to present audio data, or video and audio data, to the user. This is referred to as media data in this section, since this section applies equally to [media elements](#4811-media-elements) for audio or for video. The term media resource is used to refer to the complete set of media data, e.g. the complete video file, or complete audio file.

A [media resource](#4811-media-elements) has an associated origin, which is either "`none`", "`multiple`", "`rewritten`", or an [origin](#711-origins). It is initially set to "`none`".

A [media resource](#4811-media-elements) can have multiple audio and video tracks. For the purposes of a [media element](#4811-media-elements), the video data of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) is only that of the currently selected track (if any) as given by the element's [`videoTracks`](#481110-media-resources-with-multiple-media-tracks) attribute when the [event loop](#8171-definitions) last reached [step 1](#8173-processing-model), and the audio data of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) is the result of mixing all the currently enabled tracks (if any) given by the element's [`audioTracks`](#481110-media-resources-with-multiple-media-tracks) attribute when the [event loop](#8171-definitions) last reached [step 1](#8173-processing-model).

> [!note]
> Both [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) and [`video`](#488-the-video-element) elements can be used for both audio and video. The main difference between the two is simply that the [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) element has no playback area for visual content (such as video or captions), whereas the [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element does.

Each [media element](#4811-media-elements) has a unique media element event task source.

To queue a media element task with a [media element](#4811-media-elements) element and a series of steps steps, [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [media element event task source](#4811-media-elements) given element and steps.

##### 4.8.11.1 Error codes

`media.error`

Returns a [`MediaError`](#48111-error-codes) object representing the current error state of the element.

Returns null if there is no error.
