All [media elements](#4811-media-elements) have an associated error status, which records the last error the element encountered since its [resource selection algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) was last invoked. The `error` attribute, on getting, must return the [`MediaError`](#48111-error-codes) object created for this last error, or null if there has not been an error.

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface MediaError {
  const unsigned short MEDIA_ERR_ABORTED = 1;
  const unsigned short MEDIA_ERR_NETWORK = 2;
  const unsigned short MEDIA_ERR_DECODE = 3;
  const unsigned short MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED = 4;

  readonly attribute unsigned short code;
  readonly attribute DOMString message;
};
```

`media.error.code`

Returns the current error's error code, from the list below.

`media.error.message`

Returns a specific informative diagnostic message about the error condition encountered. The message and message format are not generally uniform across different user agents. If no such message is available, then the empty string is returned.

Every [`MediaError`](#48111-error-codes) object has a message, which is a string, and a code, which is one of the following:

`MEDIA_ERR_ABORTED` (numeric value 1)

The fetching process for the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) was aborted by the user agent at the user's request.

`MEDIA_ERR_NETWORK` (numeric value 2)

A network error of some description caused the user agent to stop fetching the [media resource](#4811-media-elements), after the resource was established to be usable.

`MEDIA_ERR_DECODE` (numeric value 3)

An error of some description occurred while decoding the [media resource](#4811-media-elements), after the resource was established to be usable.

`MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED` (numeric value 4)

The [media resource](#4811-media-elements) indicated by the [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) attribute or [assigned media provider object](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) was not suitable.

To create a `MediaError`, given an error code which is one of the above values, return a new [`MediaError`](#48111-error-codes) object whose [code](#48111-error-codes) is the given error code and whose [message](#48111-error-codes) is a string containing any details the user agent is able to supply about the cause of the error condition, or the empty string if the user agent is unable to supply such details. This message string must not contain only the information already available via the supplied error code; for example, it must not simply be a translation of the code into a string format. If no additional information is available beyond that provided by the error code, the [message](#48111-error-codes) must be set to the empty string.

The `code` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [code](#48111-error-codes).

The `message` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [message](#48111-error-codes).

##### 4.8.11.2 Location of the media resource

The `src` content attribute on [media elements](#4811-media-elements) gives the [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) of the media resource (video, audio) to show. The attribute, if present, must contain a [valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#241-terminology).

If the [`itemprop`](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute is specified on the [media element](#4811-media-elements), then the [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) attribute must also be specified.

The `crossorigin` content attribute on [media elements](#4811-media-elements) is a [CORS settings attribute](#254-cors-settings-attributes).

If a [media element](#4811-media-elements) is created with a [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) attribute, the user agent must [immediately](#211-parallelism) invoke the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [resource selection algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource).

If a [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) attribute of a [media element](#4811-media-elements) is set or changed, the user agent must invoke the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [media element load algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource). (*Removing* the [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) attribute does not do this, even if there are [`source`](#482-the-source-element) elements present.)

The `crossOrigin` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`crossorigin`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

A media provider object is an object that can represent a [media resource](#4811-media-elements), separate from a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url). [`MediaStream`](https://w3c.github.io/mediacapture-main/getusermedia.html#idl-def-mediastream) objects, [`MediaSource`](https://w3c.github.io/media-source/#idl-def-mediasource) objects, and [`Blob`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-Blob) objects are all [media provider objects](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource).

Each [media element](#4811-media-elements) has an assigned media provider object, which is a [media provider object](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) or null, initially null.

`media.srcObject [ = source ]`

Allows the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to be assigned a [media provider object](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource).

`media.currentSrc`

Returns the [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) of the current [media resource](#4811-media-elements), if any.

Returns the empty string when there is no [media resource](#4811-media-elements), or it doesn't have a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url).

The `currentSrc` IDL attribute must initially be set to the empty string. Its value is changed by the [resource selection algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) defined below.

The `srcObject` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [assigned media provider object](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource).

The [`srcObject`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) setter steps are:
1. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [assigned media provider object](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) to the given value.
2. Invoke [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [media element load algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource).

> [!note]
> There are three ways to specify a [media resource](#4811-media-elements): the [`srcObject`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) IDL attribute, the [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) content attribute, and [`source`](#482-the-source-element) elements. The IDL attribute takes priority, followed by the content attribute, followed by the elements.

##### 4.8.11.3 MIME types

A [media resource](#4811-media-elements) can be described in terms of its *type*, specifically a [MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type), in some cases with a `codecs` parameter. (Whether the `codecs` parameter is allowed or not depends on the MIME type.) [\[RFC6381\]](#references)

Types are usually somewhat incomplete descriptions; for example "`video/mpeg`" doesn't say anything except what the container type is, and even a type like "`video/mp4; codecs="avc1.42E01E, mp4a.40.2"`" doesn't include information like the actual bitrate (only the maximum bitrate). Thus, given a type, a user agent can often only know whether it *might* be able to play media of that type (with varying levels of confidence), or whether it definitely *cannot* play media of that type.

A type that the user agent knows it cannot render is one that describes a resource that the user agent definitely does not support, for example because it doesn't recognize the container type, or it doesn't support the listed codecs.

The [MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type) "[`application/octet-stream`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.5.1)" with no parameters is never [a type that the user agent knows it cannot render](#48113-mime-types). User agents must treat that type as equivalent to the lack of any explicit [Content-Type metadata](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource) when it is used to label a potential [media resource](#4811-media-elements).

> [!note]
> Only the [MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type) "[`application/octet-stream`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.5.1)" with no parameters is special-cased here; if any parameter appears with it, it will be treated just like any other [MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type). This is a deviation from the rule that unknown [MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type) parameters should be ignored.

`media.canPlayType(type)`

Returns the empty string (a negative response), "maybe", or "probably" based on how confident the user agent is that it can play media resources of the given type.

The `canPlayType(type)` method must return the empty string if type is [a type that the user agent knows it cannot render](#48113-mime-types) or is the type "[`application/octet-stream`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.5.1)"; it must return "`probably`" if the user agent is confident that the type represents a [media resource](#4811-media-elements) that it can render if used with this [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) or [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element; and it must return "`maybe`" otherwise. Implementers are encouraged to return "[`maybe`](#48113-mime-types)" unless the type can be confidently established as being supported or not. Generally, a user agent should never return "[`probably`](#48113-mime-types)" for a type that allows the `codecs` parameter if that parameter is not present.

> [!example]
> This script tests to see if the user agent supports a (fictional) new format to dynamically decide whether to use a [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element:
> 
> ```html
> <section id="video">
>  <p><a href="playing-cats.nfv">Download video</a></p>
> </section>
> <script>
>  const videoSection = document.getElementById('video');
>  const videoElement = document.createElement('video');
>  const support = videoElement.canPlayType('video/x-new-fictional-format;codecs="kittens,bunnies"');
>  if (support === "probably") {
>    videoElement.setAttribute("src", "playing-cats.nfv");
>    videoSection.replaceChildren(videoElement);
>  }
> </script>
> ```

> [!note]
> The [`type`](#482-the-source-element) attribute of the [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element allows the user agent to avoid downloading resources that use formats it cannot render.

##### 4.8.11.4 Network states

`media.networkState`

Returns the current state of network activity for the element, from the codes in the list below.

As [media elements](#4811-media-elements) interact with the network, their current network activity is represented by the `networkState` attribute. On getting, it must return the current network state of the element, which must be one of the following values:

`NETWORK_EMPTY` (numeric value 0)

The element has not yet been initialized. All attributes are in their initial states.

`NETWORK_IDLE` (numeric value 1)

The element's [resource selection algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) is active and has selected a [resource](#4811-media-elements), but it is not actually using the network at this time.

`NETWORK_LOADING` (numeric value 2)

The user agent is actively trying to download data.

`NETWORK_NO_SOURCE` (numeric value 3)

The element's [resource selection algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) is active, but it has not yet found a [resource](#4811-media-elements) to use.

The [resource selection algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) defined below describes exactly when the [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) attribute changes value and what events fire to indicate changes in this state.

##### 4.8.11.5 Loading the media resource

`media.load()`

Causes the element to reset and start selecting and loading a new [media resource](#4811-media-elements) from scratch.

All [media elements](#4811-media-elements) have a can autoplay flag, which must begin in the true state, and a delaying-the-load-event flag, which must begin in the false state. While the [delaying-the-load-event flag](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) is true, the element must [delay the load event](#1327-the-end) of its document.

When the `load()` method on a [media element](#4811-media-elements) is invoked, the user agent must run the following steps:
1. Let resumptionSteps be the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [lazy load resumption steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes).
2. If resumptionSteps is not null:
   1. Set the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [lazy load resumption steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) to null.
   2. Invoke resumptionSteps.
3. Run the [media element load algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource).

A [media element](#4811-media-elements) has an associated boolean is currently stalled, which is initially false.

The media element load algorithm consists of the following steps:
1. Set this element's [is currently stalled](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) to false.
2. Abort any already-running instance of the [resource selection algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) for this element.
3. Let pending tasks be a list of all [tasks](#8171-definitions) from the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [media element event task source](#4811-media-elements) in one of the [task queues](#8171-definitions).
4. For each task in pending tasks that would [resolve pending play promises](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) or [reject pending play promises](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), immediately resolve or reject those promises in the order the corresponding tasks were queued.
5. Remove each [task](#8171-definitions) in pending tasks from its [task queue](#8171-definitions).

   > [!note]
   > Basically, pending events and callbacks are discarded and promises in-flight to be resolved/rejected are resolved/rejected immediately when the media element starts loading a new resource.

6. If the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) is set to [`NETWORK_LOADING`](#48114-network-states) or [`NETWORK_IDLE`](#48114-network-states), [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`abort`](#481116-events-summary) at the [media element](#4811-media-elements).
7. If the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) is not set to [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#48114-network-states):
   1. [Queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`emptied`](#481116-events-summary) at the [media element](#4811-media-elements).
   2. If a fetching process is in progress for the [media element](#4811-media-elements), the user agent should stop it.
   3. If the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [assigned media provider object](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) is a [`MediaSource`](https://w3c.github.io/media-source/#idl-def-mediasource) object, then [detach](https://w3c.github.io/media-source/#mediasource-detach) it.
   4. [Forget the media element's media-resource-specific tracks](#48115-loading-the-media-resource).
   5. If [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) is not set to [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#48117-ready-states), then set it to that state.
   6. If the [`paused`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) attribute is false:
      1. Set the [`paused`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) attribute to true.
      2. [Take pending play promises](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) and [reject pending play promises](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) with the result and an ["`AbortError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#aborterror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
   7. If [`seeking`](#48119-seeking) is true, set it to false.
   8. Set the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) to 0.

      Set the [official playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) to 0.

      If this changed the [official playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), then [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`timeupdate`](#481116-events-summary) at the [media element](#4811-media-elements).

   9. Set the [timeline offset](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) to Not-a-Number (NaN).
   10. Update the [`duration`](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) attribute to Not-a-Number (NaN).

       > [!note]
       > The user agent [will not](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) fire a [`durationchange`](#481116-events-summary) event for this particular change of the duration.

8. Set the [`playbackRate`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) attribute to the value of the [`defaultPlaybackRate`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) attribute.
9. Set the [`error`](#48111-error-codes) attribute to null and the [can autoplay flag](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) to true.
10. Invoke the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [resource selection algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource).
11. > [!note]
    > Playback of any previously playing [media resource](#4811-media-elements) for this element stops.

The resource selection algorithm for a [media element](#4811-media-elements) is as follows. This algorithm is always invoked as part of a [task](#8171-definitions), but one of the first steps in the algorithm is to return and continue running the remaining steps [in parallel](#211-parallelism). In addition, this algorithm interacts closely with the [event loop](#8171-definitions) mechanism; in particular, it has [synchronous sections](#8173-processing-model) (which are triggered as part of the [event loop](#8171-definitions) algorithm). Steps in such sections are marked with ⌛.
1. Set the element's [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) attribute to the [`NETWORK_NO_SOURCE`](#48114-network-states) value.
2. Set the element's [show poster flag](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) to true.
3. [Await a stable state](#8173-processing-model), allowing the [task](#8171-definitions) that invoked this algorithm to continue. The [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model) consists of all the remaining steps of this algorithm until the algorithm says the [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model) has ended. (Steps in [synchronous sections](#8173-processing-model) are marked with ⌛.)
4. ⌛ If the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [lazy loading attribute](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) is in the [Eager](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) state or [scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting), then set the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [delaying-the-load-event flag](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) to true (this [delays the load event](#1327-the-end)).
5. ⌛ If the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [blocked-on-parser](#4811111-text-track-model) flag is false, then [populate the list of pending text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model).
6. ⌛ Let mode be null.
7. ⌛ Let candidate be null.
8. ⌛ If the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [assigned media provider object](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) is not null, then set mode to *object*.
9. ⌛ Otherwise, if the [media element](#4811-media-elements) has a [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) attribute, then set mode to *attribute*.
10. ⌛ Otherwise, if the [media element](#4811-media-elements) has a [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element child, then set mode to *children* and set candidate to the first [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element child in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
11. ⌛ Otherwise:
    1. ⌛ Set the [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) to [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#48114-network-states).
    2. ⌛ Set the element's [delaying-the-load-event flag](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) to false. This stops [delaying the load event](#1327-the-end).
    3. End the [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model) and return.
12. ⌛ Set the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) to [`NETWORK_LOADING`](#48114-network-states).
13. ⌛ [Queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`loadstart`](#481116-events-summary) at the [media element](#4811-media-elements).
14. Run the appropriate steps from the following list:

    If mode is *object*
    1. ⌛ Set the [`currentSrc`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) attribute to the empty string.
    2. End the [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model), continuing the remaining steps [in parallel](#211-parallelism).
    3. Run the [resource fetch algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) with the [assigned media provider object](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource). If that algorithm returns without aborting *this* one, then the load failed.
    4. *Failed with media provider*: Reaching this step indicates that the media resource failed to load. [Take pending play promises](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) and [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to run the [dedicated media source failure steps](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) with the result.
    5. Wait for the [task](#8171-definitions) queued by the previous step to have executed.
    6. Return. The element won't attempt to load another resource until this algorithm is triggered again.

    If mode is *attribute*
    1. ⌛ If the [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) attribute's value is the empty string, then end the [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model), and jump down to the *failed with attribute* step below.
    2. ⌛ Let urlRecord be the result of [encoding-parsing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given the [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) attribute's value, relative to the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) when the [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) attribute was last changed.
    3. ⌛ If urlRecord is not failure, then set the [`currentSrc`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) attribute to the result of applying the [URL serializer](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer) to urlRecord.
    4. End the [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model), continuing the remaining steps [in parallel](#211-parallelism).
    5. If urlRecord is not failure, then run the [resource fetch algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) with urlRecord. If that algorithm returns without aborting *this* one, then the load failed.
    6. *Failed with attribute*: Reaching this step indicates that the media resource failed to load or that urlRecord is failure. [Take pending play promises](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) and [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to run the [dedicated media source failure steps](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) with the result.
    7. Wait for the [task](#8171-definitions) queued by the previous step to have executed.
    8. Return. The element won't attempt to load another resource until this algorithm is triggered again.

    Otherwise (mode is *children*)
    1. ⌛ Let pointer be a position defined by two adjacent nodes in the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s child list, treating the start of the list (before the first child in the list, if any) and end of the list (after the last child in the list, if any) as nodes in their own right. One node is the node before pointer, and the other node is the node after pointer. Initially, let pointer be the position between the candidate node and the next node, if there are any, or the end of the list, if it is the last node.

       As nodes are [inserted](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms), [removed](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms), and [moved](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) into the [media element](#4811-media-elements), pointer must be updated as follows:

       If a new node is [inserted](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) or [moved](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) between the two nodes that define pointer

       Let pointer be the point between the node before pointer and the new node. In other words, insertions at pointer go after pointer.

       If the node before pointer is removed

       Let pointer be the point between the node after pointer and the node before the node after pointer. In other words, pointer doesn't move relative to the remaining nodes.

       If the node after pointer is removed

       Let pointer be the point between the node before pointer and the node after the node before pointer. Just as with the previous case, pointer doesn't move relative to the remaining nodes.

       Other changes don't affect pointer.

    2. ⌛ *Process candidate*: If candidate does not have a [`src`](#482-the-source-element) attribute, or if its [`src`](#482-the-source-element) attribute's value is the empty string, then end the [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model), and jump down to the *failed with elements* step below.
    3. ⌛ If candidate has a [`media`](#482-the-source-element) attribute whose value does not [match the environment](#2310-media-queries), then end the [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model), and jump down to the *failed with elements* step below.
    4. ⌛ Let urlRecord be the result of [encoding-parsing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given candidate's [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) attribute's value, relative to candidate's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) when the [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) attribute was last changed.
    5. ⌛ If urlRecord is failure, then end the [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model), and jump down to the *failed with elements* step below.
    6. ⌛ If candidate has a [`type`](#482-the-source-element) attribute whose value, when parsed as a [MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type) (including any codecs described by the `codecs` parameter, for types that define that parameter), represents [a type that the user agent knows it cannot render](#48113-mime-types), then end the [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model), and jump down to the *failed with elements* step below.
    7. ⌛ Set the [`currentSrc`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) attribute to the result of applying the [URL serializer](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer) to urlRecord.
    8. End the [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model), continuing the remaining steps [in parallel](#211-parallelism).
    9. Run the [resource fetch algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) with urlRecord. If that algorithm returns without aborting *this* one, then the load failed.
    10. *Failed with elements*: [Queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#481116-events-summary) at candidate.
    11. [Await a stable state](#8173-processing-model). The [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model) consists of all the remaining steps of this algorithm until the algorithm says the [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model) has ended. (Steps in [synchronous sections](#8173-processing-model) are marked with ⌛.)
    12. ⌛ [Forget the media element's media-resource-specific tracks](#48115-loading-the-media-resource).
    13. ⌛ *Find next candidate*: Let candidate be null.
    14. ⌛ *Search loop*: If the node after pointer is the end of the list, then jump to the *waiting* step below.
    15. ⌛ If the node after pointer is a [`source`](#482-the-source-element) element, let candidate be that element.
    16. ⌛ Advance pointer so that the node before pointer is now the node that was after pointer, and the node after pointer is the node after the node that used to be after pointer, if any.
    17. ⌛ If candidate is null, jump back to the *search loop* step. Otherwise, jump back to the *process candidate* step.
    18. ⌛ *Waiting*: Set the element's [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) attribute to the [`NETWORK_NO_SOURCE`](#48114-network-states) value.
    19. ⌛ Set the element's [show poster flag](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) to true.
    20. ⌛ [Queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to set the element's [delaying-the-load-event flag](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) to false. This stops [delaying the load event](#1327-the-end).
    21. End the [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model), continuing the remaining steps [in parallel](#211-parallelism).
    22. Wait until the node after pointer is a node other than the end of the list. (This step might wait forever.)
    23. [Await a stable state](#8173-processing-model). The [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model) consists of all the remaining steps of this algorithm until the algorithm says the [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model) has ended. (Steps in [synchronous sections](#8173-processing-model) are marked with ⌛.)
    24. ⌛ If the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [lazy loading attribute](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) is in the [Eager](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) state or [scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting), then set the element's [delaying-the-load-event flag](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) back to true (this [delays the load event](#1327-the-end) again, in case it hasn't been fired yet).
    25. ⌛ Set the [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) back to [`NETWORK_LOADING`](#48114-network-states).
    26. ⌛ Jump back to the *find next candidate* step above.

    The dedicated media source failure steps with a list of promises promises are the following steps:
    1. Set the [`error`](#48111-error-codes) attribute to the result of [creating a `MediaError`](#48111-error-codes) with [`MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED`](#48111-error-codes).
    2. [Forget the media element's media-resource-specific tracks](#48115-loading-the-media-resource).
    3. Set the element's [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) attribute to the [`NETWORK_NO_SOURCE`](#48114-network-states) value.
    4. Set the element's [show poster flag](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) to true.
    5. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#481116-events-summary) at the [media element](#4811-media-elements).
    6. [Reject pending play promises](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) with promises and a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
    7. Set the element's [delaying-the-load-event flag](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) to false. This stops [delaying the load event](#1327-the-end).

To verify a media response given a [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response, a [media resource](#4811-media-elements) resource, and "`entire resource`" or a (number, number or "`until end`") tuple byteRange:
1. If response is a [network error](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-network-error), then return false.
2. If byteRange is "`entire resource`", then return true.
3. Let internalResponse be response's [unsafe response](#251-terminology).
4. If internalResponse's [status](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-status) is 200, then return true.
5. If internalResponse's [status](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-status) is not 206, then return false.
6. If the result of [extracting content-range values](https://wicg.github.io/background-fetch/#extract-content-range-values) from internalResponse is failure, then return false.

   > [!note]
   > Note that the extracted values are not used, and in particular are not compared to byteRange. So this step serves as syntactic validation of the \`[`Content-Range`](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc7233.html#header.content-range)\` header, but if the \`[`Content-Range`](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc7233.html#header.content-range)\` values on the response mismatch the \`[`Range`](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc7233.html#header.range)\` values on the request, that is not considered a failure.

7. Let origin be "`rewritten`" if internalResponse's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url) is null; otherwise internalResponse's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url)'s [origin](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-origin).
8. Let previousOrigin be resource's [origin](#4811-media-elements).
9. If any of the following are true:
   - previousOrigin is "`none`";
   - origin and previousOrigin are "`rewritten`"; or
   - origin and previousOrigin are [origins](#711-origins), and origin is [same origin](#711-origins) with previousOrigin,

   then set resource's [origin](#4811-media-elements) to origin.

   Otherwise, if response is [CORS-cross-origin](#251-terminology), then return false.

   Otherwise, set resource's [origin](#4811-media-elements) to "`multiple`".

   > [!note]
   > This ensures that opaque responses with range headers do not leak information by being patched together with other responses from different origins.

10. Return true.

The resource fetch algorithm for a [media element](#4811-media-elements) and a given [URL record](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) or [media provider object](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) is as follows:
1. If the [will lazy load element steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) return true:
   1. Let resumptionSteps be the rest of this algorithm starting with the step labeled *Let mode be remote*.
   2. Set the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [lazy load resumption steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) to resumptionSteps.
   3. [Start intersection-observing a lazy loading element](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) for the [media element](#4811-media-elements).
   4. Return.
2. Let mode be *remote*.
3. If the algorithm was invoked with [media provider object](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource), then set mode to *local*.

   Otherwise:
   1. Let isTopLevelSelfFetch be false.
   2. Let settingsObject be the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant).
   3. Let global be the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant).
   4. If all of the following conditions are true:
      - global is a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object;
      - global's [navigable](#722-the-window-object) is not null;
      - global's [navigable](#722-the-window-object)'s [parent](#731-navigables) is null; and
      - settingsObject's [creation URL](#8131-environments) [equals](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-equals) the [URL record](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url),

      then set isTopLevelSelfFetch to true.

   5. Let stringOrEnvironment be "`top-level-self-fetch`" if isTopLevelSelfFetch is true; otherwise settingsObject.
   6. Let object be the result of [obtaining a blob object](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#blob-url-obtain-object) using the [URL record](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url)'s [blob URL entry](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-blob-entry) and stringOrEnvironment.
   7. If object is a [media provider object](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource), then set mode to *local*.

4. If mode is *remote*, then let the current media resource be the resource given by the [URL record](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) passed to this algorithm; otherwise, let the current media resource be the resource given by the [media provider object](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource). Either way, the current media resource is now the element's [media resource](#4811-media-elements).
5. Remove all [media-resource-specific text tracks](#4811112-sourcing-in-band-text-tracks) from the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of pending text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model), if any.
6. Run the appropriate steps from the following list:

   If mode is remote
   1. Optionally, run the following substeps. This is the expected behavior if the user agent intends to not attempt to fetch the resource until the user requests it explicitly (e.g. as a way to implement the [`preload`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) attribute's [`none`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) keyword).
      1. Set the [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) to [`NETWORK_IDLE`](#48114-network-states).
      2. [Queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`suspend`](#481116-events-summary) at the element.
      3. [Queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to set the element's [delaying-the-load-event flag](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) to false. This stops [delaying the load event](#1327-the-end).
      4. Wait for the task to be run.
      5. Wait for an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) event (e.g., the user requesting that the media element begin playback).
      6. Set the element's [delaying-the-load-event flag](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) back to true (this [delays the load event](#1327-the-end) again, in case it hasn't been fired yet).
      7. Set the [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) to [`NETWORK_LOADING`](#48114-network-states).
   2. Let destination be "`audio`" if the [media element](#4811-media-elements) is an [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) element, or "`video`" otherwise.
   3. Let request be the result of [creating a potential-CORS request](#251-terminology) given current media resource's [URL record](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url), destination, and the current state of the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`crossorigin`](#4121-the-script-element) content attribute.
   4. Set request's [client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client) to the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant).
   5. Set request's [initiator type](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-initiator-type) to destination.
   6. Let byteRange, which is "`entire resource`" or a (number, number or "`until end`") tuple, be the byte range required to satisfy missing data in [media data](#4811-media-elements). This value is [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) and may rely on codec, network conditions or other heuristics. The user-agent may determine to fetch the resource in full, in which case byteRange would be "`entire resource`", to fetch from a byte offset until the end, in which case byteRange would be (number, "`until end`"), or to fetch a range between two byte offsets, in which case byteRange would be a (number, number) tuple representing the two offsets.
   7. If byteRange is not "`entire resource`":
      1. If byteRange\[1\] is "`until end`", then [add a range header](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-add-range-header) to request given byteRange\[0\].
      2. Otherwise, [add a range header](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-add-range-header) to request given byteRange\[0\] and byteRange\[1\].
   8. [Fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request, with *[processResponse](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#process-response)* set to the following steps given [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response:
      1. Let global be the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant).
      2. Let updateMedia be to [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to run the first appropriate steps from the [media data processing steps list](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) below. (A new task is used for this so that the work described below occurs relative to the appropriate [media element event task source](#4811-media-elements) rather than using the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources).)
      3. Let processEndOfMedia be the following step: If the fetching process has completed without errors, including decoding the media data, and if all of the data is available to the user agent without network access, then, the user agent must move on to the *final step* below. This might never happen, e.g. when streaming an infinite resource such as web radio, or if the resource is longer than the user agent's ability to cache data.
      4. If the result of [verifying](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) response given the current media resource and byteRange is false, then abort these steps.
      5. Otherwise, [incrementally read](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#body-incrementally-read) response's [body](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-body) given updateMedia, processEndOfMedia, an empty algorithm, and global.
      6. Update the [media data](#4811-media-elements) with the contents of response's [unsafe response](#251-terminology) obtained in this fashion. response can be [CORS-same-origin](#251-terminology) or [CORS-cross-origin](#251-terminology); this affects whether subtitles referenced in the [media data](#4811-media-elements) are exposed in the API and, for [`video`](#488-the-video-element) elements, whether a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) gets tainted when the video is drawn on it.

      The media element stall timeout is an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) length of time, which should be about three seconds. When a [media element](#4811-media-elements) that is actively attempting to obtain [media data](#4811-media-elements) has failed to receive any data for a duration equal to the [media element stall timeout](#48115-loading-the-media-resource), the user agent must [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to:
      1. Set the element's [is currently stalled](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) to true.
      2. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`stalled`](#481116-events-summary) at the element.

      User agents may allow users to selectively block or slow [media data](#4811-media-elements) downloads. When a [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s download has been blocked altogether, the user agent must act as if it was stalled (as opposed to acting as if the connection was closed). The rate of the download may also be throttled automatically by the user agent, e.g. to balance the download with other connections sharing the same bandwidth.

      User agents may decide to not download more content at any time, e.g. after buffering five minutes of a one hour media resource, while waiting for the user to decide whether to play the resource or not, while waiting for user input in an interactive resource, or when the user navigates away from the page. When a [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s download has been suspended, the user agent must [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to set the [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) to [`NETWORK_IDLE`](#48114-network-states) and [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`suspend`](#481116-events-summary) at the element. If and when downloading of the resource resumes, the user agent must [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to set the [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) to [`NETWORK_LOADING`](#48114-network-states). Between the queuing of these tasks, the load is suspended (so [`progress`](#481116-events-summary) events don't fire, as described above).

      > [!note]
      > The [`preload`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) attribute provides a hint regarding how much buffering the author thinks is advisable, even in the absence of the [`autoplay`](#48117-ready-states) attribute.

      When a user agent decides to completely suspend a download, e.g., if it is waiting until the user starts playback before downloading any further content, the user agent must [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to set the element's [delaying-the-load-event flag](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) to false. This stops [delaying the load event](#1327-the-end).

      Although the above steps give an algorithm for issuing requests, the user agent may use other means besides those exact ones, especially in the face of error conditions. For example, the user agent may reconnect to the server or switch to a streaming protocol. The user agent must only consider the resource erroneous, and proceed into the error branches of the above steps, if the user agent has given up trying to fetch the resource.

      To determine the format of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements), the user agent must use the [rules for sniffing audio and video specifically](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#rules-for-sniffing-audio-and-video-specifically).

      While the load is not suspended (see below), every 350ms (±200ms) or for every byte received, whichever is *least* frequent, [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to:
      1. Set the element's [is currently stalled](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) to false.
      2. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`progress`](#481116-events-summary) at the element.

      While the user agent might still need network access to obtain parts of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements), the user agent must remain on this step.

      > [!example]
      > For example, if the user agent has discarded the first half of a video, the user agent will remain at this step even once the [playback has ended](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), because there is always the chance the user will seek back to the start. In fact, in this situation, once [playback has ended](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), the user agent will end up firing a [`suspend`](#481116-events-summary) event, as described earlier.

   Otherwise (mode is *local*)

   The resource described by the current media resource, if any, contains the [media data](#4811-media-elements). It is [CORS-same-origin](#251-terminology).

   If the current media resource is a raw data stream (e.g. from a [`File`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file) object), then to determine the format of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements), the user agent must use the [rules for sniffing audio and video specifically](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#rules-for-sniffing-audio-and-video-specifically). Otherwise, if the data stream is pre-decoded, then the format is the format given by the relevant specification.

   Whenever new data for the current media resource becomes available, [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to run the first appropriate steps from the [media data processing steps list](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) below.

   When the current media resource is permanently exhausted (e.g. all the bytes of a [`Blob`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-Blob) have been processed), if there were no decoding errors, then the user agent must move on to the *final step* below. This might never happen, e.g. if the current media resource is a [`MediaStream`](https://w3c.github.io/mediacapture-main/getusermedia.html#idl-def-mediastream).

   The media data processing steps list is as follows:

   If the [media data](#4811-media-elements) cannot be fetched at all, due to network errors, causing the user agent to give up trying to fetch the resource

   If the [media data](#4811-media-elements) can be fetched but is found by inspection to be in an unsupported format, or can otherwise not be rendered at all

   DNS errors, HTTP 4xx and 5xx errors (and equivalents in other protocols), and other fatal network errors that occur before the user agent has established whether the current media resource is usable, as well as the file using an unsupported container format, or using unsupported codecs for all the data, must cause the user agent to execute the following steps:
   1. The user agent should cancel the fetching process.
   2. Abort this subalgorithm, returning to the [resource selection algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource).

   If the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) is found to have an audio track
   1. Create an [`AudioTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object to represent the audio track.
   2. Update the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`audioTracks`](#481110-media-resources-with-multiple-media-tracks) attribute's [`AudioTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object with the new [`AudioTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object.
   3. Let enable be *unknown*.
   4. If either the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) or the [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) of the current media resource indicate a particular set of audio tracks to enable, or if the user agent has information that would facilitate the selection of specific audio tracks to improve the user's experience: if this audio track is one of the ones to enable, then set enable to *true*, otherwise, set enable to *false*.

      > [!example]
      > This could be triggered by [media fragment syntax](https://www.w3.org/TR/media-frags/#media-fragment-syntax), but it could also be triggered e.g. by the user agent selecting a 5.1 surround sound audio track over a stereo audio track.

   5. If enable is still *unknown*, then, if the [media element](#4811-media-elements) does not yet have an [enabled](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) audio track, then set enable to *true*, otherwise, set enable to *false*.
   6. If enable is *true*, then enable this audio track, otherwise, do not enable this audio track.
   7. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`addtrack`](#481116-events-summary) at this [`AudioTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object, using [`TrackEvent`](#481115-the-trackevent-interface), with the [`track`](#481115-the-trackevent-interface) attribute initialized to the new [`AudioTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object.

   If the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) is found to have a video track
   1. Create a [`VideoTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object to represent the video track.
   2. Update the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`videoTracks`](#481110-media-resources-with-multiple-media-tracks) attribute's [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object with the new [`VideoTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object.
   3. Let enable be *unknown*.
   4. If either the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) or the [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) of the current media resource indicate a particular set of video tracks to enable, or if the user agent has information that would facilitate the selection of specific video tracks to improve the user's experience: if this video track is the first such video track, then set enable to *true*, otherwise, set enable to *false*.

      > [!example]
      > This could again be triggered by [media fragment syntax](https://www.w3.org/TR/media-frags/#media-fragment-syntax).

   5. If enable is still *unknown*, then, if the [media element](#4811-media-elements) does not yet have a [selected](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) video track, then set enable to *true*, otherwise, set enable to *false*.
   6. If enable is *true*, then select this track and unselect any previously selected video tracks, otherwise, do not select this video track. If other tracks are unselected, then [a `change` event will be fired](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects).
   7. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`addtrack`](#481116-events-summary) at this [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object, using [`TrackEvent`](#481115-the-trackevent-interface), with the [`track`](#481115-the-trackevent-interface) attribute initialized to the new [`VideoTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object.

   Once enough of the [media data](#4811-media-elements) has been fetched to determine the duration of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements), its dimensions, and other metadata

   This indicates that the resource is usable. The user agent must follow these substeps:
   1. [Establish the media timeline](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) for the purposes of the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) and the [earliest possible position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), based on the [media data](#4811-media-elements).
   2. Update the [timeline offset](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) to the date and time that corresponds to the zero time in the [media timeline](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) established in the previous step, if any. If no explicit time and date is given by the [media resource](#4811-media-elements), the [timeline offset](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) must be set to Not-a-Number (NaN).
   3. Set the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) and the [official playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) to the [earliest possible position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource).
   4. Update the [`duration`](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) attribute with the time of the last frame of the resource, if known, on the [media timeline](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) established above. If it is not known (e.g. a stream that is in principle infinite), update the [`duration`](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) attribute to the value positive Infinity.

      > [!note]
      > The user agent [will](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`durationchange`](#481116-events-summary) at the element at this point.

   5. For [`video`](#488-the-video-element) elements, set the [`videoWidth`](#488-the-video-element) and [`videoHeight`](#488-the-video-element) attributes, and [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`resize`](#481116-events-summary) at the [media element](#4811-media-elements).

      > [!note]
      > Further [`resize`](#481116-events-summary) events will be fired if the dimensions subsequently change.

   6. Set the [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) attribute to [`HAVE_METADATA`](#48117-ready-states).

      > [!note]
      > A [`loadedmetadata`](#481116-events-summary) DOM event [will be fired](#48117-ready-states) as part of setting the [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) attribute to a new value.

   7. Let jumped be false.
   8. If the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [default playback start position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) is greater than zero, then [seek](#48119-seeking) to that time, and let jumped be true.
   9. Set the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [default playback start position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) to zero.
   10. Let the initial playback position be 0.
   11. If either the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) or the [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) of the current media resource indicate a particular start time, then set the initial playback position to that time and, if jumped is still false, [seek](#48119-seeking) to that time.

       > [!example]
       > For example, with media formats that support [media fragment syntax](https://www.w3.org/TR/media-frags/#media-fragment-syntax), the [fragment](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment) can be used to indicate a start position.

   12. If there is no [enabled](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) audio track, then enable an audio track. This [will cause a `change` event to be fired](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects).
   13. If there is no [selected](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) video track, then select a video track. This [will cause a `change` event to be fired](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects).

   Once the [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) attribute reaches [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#48117-ready-states), [after the `loadeddata` event has been fired](#48117-ready-states), set the element's [delaying-the-load-event flag](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) to false. This stops [delaying the load event](#1327-the-end).

   > [!note]
   > A user agent that is attempting to reduce network usage while still fetching the metadata for each [media resource](#4811-media-elements) would also stop buffering at this point, following [the rules described previously](#48115-loading-the-media-resource), which involve the [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) attribute switching to the [`NETWORK_IDLE`](#48114-network-states) value and a [`suspend`](#481116-events-summary) event firing.

   > [!note]
   > The user agent is *required* to determine the duration of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) and go through this step before playing.

   Once the entire [media resource](#4811-media-elements) has been fetched (but potentially before any of it has been decoded)

   [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`progress`](#481116-events-summary) at the [media element](#4811-media-elements).

   Set the [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) to [`NETWORK_IDLE`](#48114-network-states) and [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`suspend`](#481116-events-summary) at the [media element](#4811-media-elements).

   If the user agent ever discards any [media data](#4811-media-elements) and then needs to resume the network activity to obtain it again, then it must [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to set the [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) to [`NETWORK_LOADING`](#48114-network-states).

   > [!note]
   > If the user agent can keep the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) loaded, then the algorithm will continue to its *final step* below, which aborts the algorithm.

   If the connection is interrupted after some [media data](#4811-media-elements) has been received, causing the user agent to give up trying to fetch the resource

   Fatal network errors that occur after the user agent has established whether the current media resource is usable (i.e. once the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) attribute is no longer [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#48117-ready-states)) must cause the user agent to execute the following steps:
   1. The user agent should cancel the fetching process.
   2. Set the [`error`](#48111-error-codes) attribute to the result of [creating a `MediaError`](#48111-error-codes) with [`MEDIA_ERR_NETWORK`](#48111-error-codes).
   3. Set the element's [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) attribute to the [`NETWORK_IDLE`](#48114-network-states) value.
   4. Set the element's [delaying-the-load-event flag](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) to false. This stops [delaying the load event](#1327-the-end).
   5. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#481116-events-summary) at the [media element](#4811-media-elements).
   6. Abort the overall [resource selection algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource).

   If the [media data](#4811-media-elements) is corrupted

   Fatal errors in decoding the [media data](#4811-media-elements) that occur after the user agent has established whether the current media resource is usable (i.e. once the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) attribute is no longer [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#48117-ready-states)) must cause the user agent to execute the following steps:
   1. The user agent should cancel the fetching process.
   2. Set the [`error`](#48111-error-codes) attribute to the result of [creating a `MediaError`](#48111-error-codes) with [`MEDIA_ERR_DECODE`](#48111-error-codes).
   3. Set the element's [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) attribute to the [`NETWORK_IDLE`](#48114-network-states) value.
   4. Set the element's [delaying-the-load-event flag](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) to false. This stops [delaying the load event](#1327-the-end).
   5. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#481116-events-summary) at the [media element](#4811-media-elements).
   6. Abort the overall [resource selection algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource).

   If the [media data](#4811-media-elements) fetching process is aborted by the user

   The fetching process is aborted by the user, e.g. because the user pressed a "stop" button, the user agent must execute the following steps. These steps are not followed if the [`load()`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) method itself is invoked while these steps are running, as the steps above handle that particular kind of abort.
   1. The user agent should cancel the fetching process.
   2. Set the [`error`](#48111-error-codes) attribute to the result of [creating a `MediaError`](#48111-error-codes) with [`MEDIA_ERR_ABORTED`](#48111-error-codes).
   3. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`abort`](#481116-events-summary) at the [media element](#4811-media-elements).
   4. If the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) attribute has a value equal to [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#48117-ready-states), set the element's [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) attribute to the [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#48114-network-states) value, set the element's [show poster flag](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) to true, and [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`emptied`](#481116-events-summary) at the element.

      Otherwise, set the element's [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) attribute to the [`NETWORK_IDLE`](#48114-network-states) value.

   5. Set the element's [delaying-the-load-event flag](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) to false. This stops [delaying the load event](#1327-the-end).
   6. Abort the overall [resource selection algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource).

   If the [media data](#4811-media-elements) can be fetched but has non-fatal errors or uses, in part, codecs that are unsupported, preventing the user agent from rendering the content completely correctly but not preventing playback altogether

   The server returning data that is partially usable but cannot be optimally rendered must cause the user agent to render just the bits it can handle, and ignore the rest.

   If the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) is found to declare a [media-resource-specific text track](#4811112-sourcing-in-band-text-tracks) that the user agent supports

   If the [media data](#4811-media-elements) is [CORS-same-origin](#251-terminology), run the [steps to expose a media-resource-specific text track](#4811112-sourcing-in-band-text-tracks) with the relevant data.

   > [!note]
   > Cross-origin videos do not expose their subtitles, since that would allow attacks such as hostile sites reading subtitles from confidential videos on a user's intranet.

7. *Final step*: If the user agent ever reaches this step (which can only happen if the entire resource gets loaded and kept available): abort the overall [resource selection algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource).

When a [media element](#4811-media-elements) is to forget the media element's media-resource-specific tracks, the user agent must remove from the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) all the [media-resource-specific text tracks](#4811112-sourcing-in-band-text-tracks), then empty the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`audioTracks`](#481110-media-resources-with-multiple-media-tracks) attribute's [`AudioTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object, then empty the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`videoTracks`](#481110-media-resources-with-multiple-media-tracks) attribute's [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object. No events (in particular, no [`removetrack`](#481116-events-summary) events) are fired as part of this; the [`error`](#481116-events-summary) and [`emptied`](#481116-events-summary) events, fired by the algorithms that invoke this one, can be used instead.

---

The `preload` attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auto` | Automatic | Hints to the user agent that the user agent can put the user's needs first without risk to the server, up to and including optimistically downloading the entire resource. |
| `none` | None | Hints to the user agent that either the author does not expect the user to need the media resource, or that the server wants to minimize unnecessary traffic. This state does not provide a hint regarding how aggressively to actually download the media resource if buffering starts anyway (e.g. once the user hits "play"). |
| `metadata` | Metadata | Hints to the user agent that the author does not expect the user to need the media resource, but that fetching the resource metadata (dimensions, track list, duration, etc.), and maybe even the first few frames, is reasonable. If the user agent precisely fetches no more than the metadata, then the [media element](#4811-media-elements) will end up with its [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) attribute set to [`HAVE_METADATA`](#48117-ready-states); typically though, some frames will be obtained as well and it will probably be [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#48117-ready-states) or [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#48117-ready-states). When the media resource is playing, hints to the user agent that bandwidth is to be considered scarce, e.g. suggesting throttling the download so that the media data is obtained at the slowest possible rate that still maintains consistent playback. |

The attribute's *[empty value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* is the [Automatic](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) state.

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology), though the [Metadata](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) state is suggested as a compromise between reducing server load and providing an optimal user experience.

The attribute can be changed even once the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) is being buffered or played; the descriptions in the table above are to be interpreted with that in mind.

> [!note]
> Authors might switch the attribute from "[`none`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource)" or "[`metadata`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource)" to "[`auto`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource)" dynamically once the user begins playback. For example, on a page with many videos this might be used to indicate that the many videos are not to be downloaded unless requested, but that once one *is* requested it is to be downloaded aggressively.

The [`preload`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) attribute is intended to provide a hint to the user agent about what the author thinks will lead to the best user experience. The attribute may be ignored altogether, for example based on explicit user preferences or based on the available connectivity.

The `preload` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the content attribute of the same name, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

> [!note]
> The [`autoplay`](#48117-ready-states) attribute can override the [`preload`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) attribute (since if the media plays, it naturally has to buffer first, regardless of the hint given by the [`preload`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) attribute). Including both is not an error, however.

> [!note]
> In [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) and [`video`](#488-the-video-element) elements, if [scripting is enabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting), the [`loading`](#4811-media-elements) attribute can defer the [`preload`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) attribute's hinted behavior until the element's [lazy load resumption steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) are run.

---

`media.buffered`

Returns a [`TimeRanges`](#481114-time-ranges) object that represents the ranges of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) that the user agent has buffered.

The `buffered` getter steps are to return a new [normalized `TimeRanges` object](#481114-time-ranges) that represents the ranges of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [media resource](#4811-media-elements), if any, that the user agent has buffered. User agents must accurately determine the ranges available, even for media streams where this can only be determined by tedious inspection.

> [!note]
> Typically this will be a single range anchored at the zero point, but if, e.g. the user agent uses HTTP range requests in response to seeking, then there could be multiple ranges.

User agents may discard previously buffered data.

> [!note]
> Thus, a time position included within a range of the objects return by the [`buffered`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) attribute at one time can end up being not included in the range(s) of objects returned by the same attribute at later times.

> [!warning]
> Returning a new object each time is a bad pattern for attribute getters and is only enshrined here as it would be costly to change it. It is not to be copied to new APIs.

##### 4.8.11.6 Offsets into the media resource

`media.duration`

Returns the length of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements), in seconds, assuming that the start of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) is at time zero.

Returns NaN if the duration isn't available.

Returns Infinity for unbounded streams.

`media.currentTime [ = value ]`

Returns the [official playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), in seconds.

Can be set, to seek to the given time.

A [media resource](#4811-media-elements) has a media timeline that maps times (in seconds) to positions in the [media resource](#4811-media-elements). The origin of a timeline is its earliest defined position. The duration of a timeline is its last defined position.

Establishing the media timeline: if the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) somehow specifies an explicit timeline whose origin is not negative (i.e. gives each frame a specific time offset and gives the first frame a zero or positive offset), then the [media timeline](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) should be that timeline. (Whether the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) can specify a timeline or not depends on the [media resource](#4811-media-elements)'s format.) If the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) specifies an explicit start time *and date*, then that time and date should be considered the zero point in the [media timeline](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource); the [timeline offset](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) will be the time and date, exposed using the [`getStartDate()`](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) method.

If the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) has a discontinuous timeline, the user agent must extend the timeline used at the start of the resource across the entire resource, so that the [media timeline](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) increases linearly starting from the [earliest possible position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) (as defined below), even if the underlying [media data](#4811-media-elements) has out-of-order or even overlapping time codes.

> [!example]
> For example, if two clips have been concatenated into one video file, but the video format exposes the original times for the two clips, the video data might expose a timeline that goes, say, 00:15..00:29 and then 00:05..00:38. However, the user agent would not expose those times; it would instead expose the times as 00:15..00:29 and 00:29..01:02, as a single video.

[![(This is a tracking vector.)](https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg)](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#24-privacy-concerns) In the rare case of a [media resource](#4811-media-elements) that does not have an explicit timeline, the zero time on the [media timeline](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) should correspond to the first frame of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements). In the even rarer case of a [media resource](#4811-media-elements) with no explicit timings of any kind, not even frame durations, the user agent must itself determine the time for each frame in an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) manner.

> [!note]
> An example of a file format with no explicit timeline but with explicit frame durations is the Animated GIF format. An example of a file format with no explicit timings at all is the JPEG-push format ([`multipart/x-mixed-replace`](#172-multipartx-mixed-replace) with JPEG frames, often used as the format for MJPEG streams).

If, in the case of a resource with no timing information, the user agent will nonetheless be able to seek to an earlier point than the first frame originally provided by the server, then the zero time should correspond to the earliest seekable time of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements); otherwise, it should correspond to the first frame received from the server (the point in the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) at which the user agent began receiving the stream).

> [!note]
> At the time of writing, there is no known format that lacks explicit frame time offsets yet still supports seeking to a frame before the first frame sent by the server.

> [!example]
> Consider a stream from a TV broadcaster, which begins streaming on a sunny Friday afternoon in October, and always sends connecting user agents the media data on the same media timeline, with its zero time set to the start of this stream. Months later, user agents connecting to this stream will find that the first frame they receive has a time with millions of seconds. The [`getStartDate()`](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) method would always return the date that the broadcast started; this would allow controllers to display real times in their scrubber (e.g. "2:30pm") rather than a time relative to when the broadcast began ("8 months, 4 hours, 12 minutes, and 23 seconds").
> 
> Consider a stream that carries a video with several concatenated fragments, broadcast by a server that does not allow user agents to request specific times but instead just streams the video data in a predetermined order, with the first frame delivered always being identified as the frame with time zero. If a user agent connects to this stream and receives fragments defined as covering timestamps 2010-03-20 23:15:00 UTC to 2010-03-21 00:05:00 UTC and 2010-02-12 14:25:00 UTC to 2010-02-12 14:35:00 UTC, it would expose this with a [media timeline](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) starting at 0s and extending to 3,600s (one hour). Assuming the streaming server disconnected at the end of the second clip, the [`duration`](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) attribute would then return 3,600. The [`getStartDate()`](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) method would return a [`Date`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-date-objects) object with a time corresponding to 2010-03-20 23:15:00 UTC. However, if a different user agent connected five minutes later, *it* would (presumably) receive fragments covering timestamps 2010-03-20 23:20:00 UTC to 2010-03-21 00:05:00 UTC and 2010-02-12 14:25:00 UTC to 2010-02-12 14:35:00 UTC, and would expose this with a [media timeline](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) starting at 0s and extending to 3,300s (fifty five minutes). In this case, the [`getStartDate()`](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) method would return a [`Date`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-date-objects) object with a time corresponding to 2010-03-20 23:20:00 UTC.
> 
> In both of these examples, the [`seekable`](#48119-seeking) attribute would give the ranges that the controller would want to actually display in its UI; typically, if the servers don't support seeking to arbitrary times, this would be the range of time from the moment the user agent connected to the stream up to the latest frame that the user agent has obtained; however, if the user agent starts discarding earlier information, the actual range might be shorter.

In any case, the user agent must ensure that the [earliest possible position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) (as defined below) using the established [media timeline](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), is greater than or equal to zero.

The [media timeline](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) also has an associated clock. Which clock is used is user-agent defined, and may be [media resource](#4811-media-elements)-dependent, but it should approximate the user's wall clock.

[Media elements](#4811-media-elements) have a current playback position, which must initially (i.e. in the absence of [media data](#4811-media-elements)) be zero seconds. The [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) is a time on the [media timeline](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource).

[Media elements](#4811-media-elements) also have an official playback position, which must initially be set to zero seconds. The [official playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) is an approximation of the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) that is kept stable while scripts are running.

[Media elements](#4811-media-elements) also have a default playback start position, which must initially be set to zero seconds. This time is used to allow the element to be seeked even before the media is loaded.

Each [media element](#4811-media-elements) has a show poster flag. When a [media element](#4811-media-elements) is created, this flag must be set to true.
