This flag is used to control when the user agent is to show a poster frame for a [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element instead of showing the video contents.

The `currentTime` attribute must, on getting, return the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [default playback start position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), unless that is zero, in which case it must return the element's [official playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource). The returned value must be expressed in seconds. On setting, if the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) is [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#48117-ready-states), then it must set the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [default playback start position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) to the new value; otherwise, it must set the [official playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) to the new value and then [seek](#48119-seeking) to the new value. The new value must be interpreted as being in seconds.

If the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) is a streaming resource, then the user agent might be unable to obtain certain parts of the resource after it has expired from its buffer. Similarly, some [media resources](#4811-media-elements) might have a [media timeline](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) that doesn't start at zero. The earliest possible position is the earliest position in the stream or resource that the user agent can ever obtain again. It is also a time on the [media timeline](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource).

> [!note]
> The [earliest possible position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) is not explicitly exposed in the API; it corresponds to the start time of the first range in the [`seekable`](#48119-seeking) attribute's [`TimeRanges`](#481114-time-ranges) object, if any, or the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) otherwise.

When the [earliest possible position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) changes: if the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) is before the [earliest possible position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), the user agent must [seek](#48119-seeking) to the [earliest possible position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource); otherwise, if the user agent has not fired a [`timeupdate`](#481116-events-summary) event at the element in the past 15 to 250ms and is not still running event handlers for such an event, then the user agent must [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`timeupdate`](#481116-events-summary) at the element.

> [!note]
> Because of the above requirement and the requirement in the [resource fetch algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) that kicks in [when the metadata of the clip becomes known](#48115-loading-the-media-resource), the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) can never be less than the [earliest possible position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource).

If at any time the user agent learns that an audio or video track has ended and all [media data](#4811-media-elements) relating to that track corresponds to parts of the [media timeline](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) that are *before* the [earliest possible position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), the user agent may [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to run these steps:
1. Remove the track from the [`audioTracks`](#481110-media-resources-with-multiple-media-tracks) attribute's [`AudioTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object or the [`videoTracks`](#481110-media-resources-with-multiple-media-tracks) attribute's [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object as appropriate.
2. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`removetrack`](#481116-events-summary) at the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s aforementioned [`AudioTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) or [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object, using [`TrackEvent`](#481115-the-trackevent-interface), with the [`track`](#481115-the-trackevent-interface) attribute initialized to the [`AudioTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) or [`VideoTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object representing the track.

The `duration` attribute must return the time of the end of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements), in seconds, on the [media timeline](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource). If no [media data](#4811-media-elements) is available, then the attributes must return the Not-a-Number (NaN) value. If the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) is not known to be bounded (e.g. streaming radio, or a live event with no announced end time), then the attribute must return the positive Infinity value.

The user agent must determine the duration of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) before playing any part of the [media data](#4811-media-elements) and before setting [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) to a value greater than or equal to [`HAVE_METADATA`](#48117-ready-states), even if doing so requires fetching multiple parts of the resource.

When the length of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) changes to a known value (e.g. from being unknown to known, or from a previously established length to a new length), the user agent must [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`durationchange`](#481116-events-summary) at the [media element](#4811-media-elements). (The event is not fired when the duration is reset as part of loading a new media resource.) If the duration is changed such that the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) ends up being greater than the time of the end of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements), then the user agent must also [seek](#48119-seeking) to the time of the end of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements).

> [!example]
> If an "infinite" stream ends for some reason, then the duration would change from positive Infinity to the time of the last frame or sample in the stream, and the [`durationchange`](#481116-events-summary) event would be fired. Similarly, if the user agent initially estimated the [media resource](#4811-media-elements)'s duration instead of determining it precisely, and later revises the estimate based on new information, then the duration would change and the [`durationchange`](#481116-events-summary) event would be fired.

Some video files also have an explicit date and time corresponding to the zero time in the [media timeline](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), known as the timeline offset. Initially, the [timeline offset](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) must be set to Not-a-Number (NaN).

The `getStartDate()` method must return [a new `Date` object](#219-dependencies) representing the current [timeline offset](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource).

---

The `loop` attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes) that, if specified, indicates that the [media element](#4811-media-elements) is to seek back to the start of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) upon reaching the end.

##### 4.8.11.7 Ready states

`media.readyState`

Returns a value that expresses the current state of the element with respect to rendering the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), from the codes in the list below.

[Media elements](#4811-media-elements) have a *ready state*, which describes to what degree they are ready to be rendered at the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource). The possible values are as follows; the ready state of a media element at any particular time is the greatest value describing the state of the element:

`HAVE_NOTHING` (numeric value 0)

No information regarding the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) is available. No data for the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) is available. [Media elements](#4811-media-elements) whose [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) attribute are set to [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#48114-network-states) are always in the [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#48117-ready-states) state.

`HAVE_METADATA` (numeric value 1)

Enough of the resource has been obtained that the duration of the resource is available. In the case of a [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element, the dimensions of the video are also available. No [media data](#4811-media-elements) is available for the immediate [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource).

`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA` (numeric value 2)

Data for the immediate [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) is available, but either not enough data is available that the user agent could successfully advance the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) in the [direction of playback](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) at all without immediately reverting to the [`HAVE_METADATA`](#48117-ready-states) state, or there is no more data to obtain in the [direction of playback](#48118-playing-the-media-resource). For example, in video this corresponds to the user agent having data from the current frame, but not the next frame, when the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) is at the end of the current frame; and to when [playback has ended](#48118-playing-the-media-resource).

`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA` (numeric value 3)

Data for the immediate [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) is available, as well as enough data for the user agent to advance the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) in the [direction of playback](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) at least a little without immediately reverting to the [`HAVE_METADATA`](#48117-ready-states) state, and [the text tracks are ready](#4811111-text-track-model). For example, in video this corresponds to the user agent having data for at least the current frame and the next frame when the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) is at the instant in time between the two frames, or to the user agent having the video data for the current frame and audio data to keep playing at least a little when the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) is in the middle of a frame. The user agent cannot be in this state if [playback has ended](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), as the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) can never advance in this case.

`HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA` (numeric value 4)

All the conditions described for the [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#48117-ready-states) state are met, and, in addition, either of the following conditions is also true:
- The user agent estimates that data is being fetched at a rate where the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), if it were to advance at the element's [`playbackRate`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), would not overtake the available data before playback reaches the end of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements).
- The user agent has entered a state where waiting longer will not result in further data being obtained, and therefore nothing would be gained by delaying playback any further. (For example, the buffer might be full.)

> [!note]
> In practice, the difference between [`HAVE_METADATA`](#48117-ready-states) and [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#48117-ready-states) is negligible. Really the only time the difference is relevant is when painting a [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element onto a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element), where it distinguishes the case where something will be drawn ([`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#48117-ready-states) or greater) from the case where nothing is drawn ([`HAVE_METADATA`](#48117-ready-states) or less). Similarly, the difference between [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#48117-ready-states) (only the current frame) and [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#48117-ready-states) (at least this frame and the next) can be negligible (in the extreme, only one frame). The only time that distinction really matters is when a page provides an interface for "frame-by-frame" navigation.

When the ready state of a [media element](#4811-media-elements) whose [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) is not [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#48114-network-states) changes, the user agent must follow the steps given below:
1. Apply the first applicable set of substeps from the following list:

   If the previous ready state was [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#48117-ready-states), and the new ready state is [`HAVE_METADATA`](#48117-ready-states)

   [Queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`loadedmetadata`](#481116-events-summary) at the element.

   > [!note]
   > Before this task is run, as part of the [event loop](#8171-definitions) mechanism, the rendering will have been updated to resize the [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element if appropriate.

   If the previous ready state was [`HAVE_METADATA`](#48117-ready-states) and the new ready state is [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#48117-ready-states) or greater

   If this is the first time this occurs for this [media element](#4811-media-elements) since the [`load()`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) algorithm was last invoked, the user agent must [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`loadeddata`](#481116-events-summary) at the element.

   If the new ready state is [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#48117-ready-states) or [`HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA`](#48117-ready-states), then the relevant steps below must then be run also.

   If the previous ready state was [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#48117-ready-states) or more, and the new ready state is [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#48117-ready-states) or less

   If the [media element](#4811-media-elements) was [potentially playing](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) before its [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) attribute changed to a value lower than [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#48117-ready-states), and the element has not [ended playback](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), and playback has not [stopped due to errors](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), [paused for user interaction](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), or [paused for in-band content](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), the user agent must [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`timeupdate`](#481116-events-summary) at the element, and [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`waiting`](#481116-events-summary) at the element.

   If the previous ready state was [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#48117-ready-states) or less, and the new ready state is [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#48117-ready-states)

   The user agent must [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`canplay`](#481116-events-summary) at the element.

   If the element's [`paused`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) attribute is false, the user agent must [notify about playing](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) for the element.

   If the new ready state is [`HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA`](#48117-ready-states)

   If the previous ready state was [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#48117-ready-states) or less, the user agent must [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`canplay`](#481116-events-summary) at the element, and, if the element's [`paused`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) attribute is false, [notify about playing](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) for the element.

   The user agent must [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`canplaythrough`](#481116-events-summary) at the element.

   If the element is not [eligible for autoplay](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), then the user agent must abort these substeps.

   The user agent may run the following substeps:
   1. Set the [`paused`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) attribute to false.
   2. If the element's [show poster flag](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) is true, set it to false and run the *[time marches on](#48118-playing-the-media-resource)* steps.
   3. [Queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the element to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`play`](#481116-events-summary) at the element.
   4. [Notify about playing](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) for the element.

   Alternatively, if the element is a [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element, the user agent may start observing whether the element [intersects the viewport](#151-introduction). When the element starts [intersecting the viewport](#151-introduction), if the element is still [eligible for autoplay](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), run the substeps above. Optionally, when the element stops [intersecting the viewport](#151-introduction), if the [can autoplay flag](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) is still true and the [`autoplay`](#48117-ready-states) attribute is still specified, run the following substeps:
   1. Run the [internal pause steps](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) and set the [can autoplay flag](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) to true.
   2. [Queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the element to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`pause`](#481116-events-summary) at the element.

   > [!note]
   > The substeps for playing and pausing can run multiple times as the element starts or stops [intersecting the viewport](#151-introduction), as long as the [can autoplay flag](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) is true.

   > [!note]
   > User agents do not need to support autoplay, and it is suggested that user agents honor user preferences on the matter. Authors are urged to use the [`autoplay`](#48117-ready-states) attribute rather than using script to force the video to play, so as to allow the user to override the behavior if so desired.

> [!note]
> It is possible for the ready state of a media element to jump between these states discontinuously. For example, the state of a media element can jump straight from [`HAVE_METADATA`](#48117-ready-states) to [`HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA`](#48117-ready-states) without passing through the [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#48117-ready-states) and [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#48117-ready-states) states.

The `readyState` IDL attribute must, on getting, return the value described above that describes the current ready state of the [media element](#4811-media-elements).

The `autoplay` attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes). When present, the user agent (as described in the algorithm described herein) will automatically begin playback of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) as soon as it can do so without stopping.

> [!note]
> Authors are urged to use the [`autoplay`](#48117-ready-states) attribute rather than using script to trigger automatic playback, as this allows the user to override the automatic playback when it is not desired, e.g. when using a screen reader. Authors are also encouraged to consider not using the automatic playback behavior at all, and instead to let the user agent wait for the user to start playback explicitly.

##### 4.8.11.8 Playing the media resource

`media.paused`

Returns true if playback is paused; false otherwise.

`media.ended`

Returns true if playback has reached the end of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements).

`media.defaultPlaybackRate [ = value ]`

Returns the default rate of playback, for when the user is not fast-forwarding or reversing through the [media resource](#4811-media-elements).

Can be set, to change the default rate of playback.

The default rate has no direct effect on playback, but if the user switches to a fast-forward mode, when they return to the normal playback mode, it is expected that the rate of playback will be returned to the default rate of playback.

`media.playbackRate [ = value ]`

Returns the current rate playback, where 1.0 is normal speed.

Can be set, to change the rate of playback.

`media.preservesPitch`

Returns true if pitch-preserving algorithms are used when the [`playbackRate`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) is not 1.0. The default value is true.

Can be set to false to have the [media resource](#4811-media-elements)'s audio pitch change up or down depending on the [`playbackRate`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource). This is useful for aesthetic and performance reasons.

`media.played`

Returns a [`TimeRanges`](#481114-time-ranges) object that represents the ranges of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) that the user agent has played.

`media.play()`

Sets the [`paused`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) attribute to false, loading the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) and beginning playback if necessary. If the playback had ended, will restart it from the start.

`media.pause()`

Sets the [`paused`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) attribute to true, loading the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) if necessary.

The `paused` attribute represents whether the [media element](#4811-media-elements) is paused or not. The attribute must initially be true.

A [media element](#4811-media-elements) is a blocked media element if its [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) attribute is in the [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#48117-ready-states) state, the [`HAVE_METADATA`](#48117-ready-states) state, or the [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#48117-ready-states) state, or if the element has [paused for user interaction](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) or [paused for in-band content](#48118-playing-the-media-resource).

A [media element](#4811-media-elements) is said to be potentially playing when its [`paused`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) attribute is false, the element has not [ended playback](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), playback has not [stopped due to errors](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), and the element is not a [blocked media element](#48118-playing-the-media-resource).

> [!note]
> A [`waiting`](#481116-events-summary) DOM event [can be fired](#48117-ready-states) as a result of an element that is [potentially playing](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) stopping playback due to its [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) attribute changing to a value lower than [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#48117-ready-states).

A [media element](#4811-media-elements) is said to be eligible for autoplay when all of the following are true:
- its [can autoplay flag](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) is true;
- its [`paused`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) attribute is true;
- it has an [`autoplay`](#48117-ready-states) attribute specified;
- if it is an [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) or [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element and its [lazy loading attribute](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) is either in the [Eager](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) state or has started loading while in the [Lazy](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) state, or [scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting) for the element;
- its [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [active sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing) does not have the [sandboxed automatic features browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing) set; and
- its [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) is [allowed to use](#485-the-iframe-element) the "[`autoplay`](#22-policy-controlled-features)" feature.

A [media element](#4811-media-elements) is said to be allowed to play if the user agent and the system allow media playback in the current context.

> [!example]
> For example, a user agent could allow playback only when the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object has [transient activation](#641-data-model), but an exception could be made to allow playback while [muted](#481113-user-interface).

A [media element](#4811-media-elements) is said to have ended playback when:
- The element's [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) attribute is [`HAVE_METADATA`](#48117-ready-states) or greater, and
- Either:
  - The [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) is the end of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements), and
  - The [direction of playback](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) is forwards, and
  - The [media element](#4811-media-elements) does not have a [`loop`](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) attribute specified.

  Or:
  - The [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) is the [earliest possible position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), and
  - The [direction of playback](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) is backwards.

The `ended` attribute must return true if, the last time the [event loop](#8171-definitions) reached [step 1](#8173-processing-model), the [media element](#4811-media-elements) had [ended playback](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) and the [direction of playback](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) was forwards, and false otherwise.

A [media element](#4811-media-elements) is said to have stopped due to errors when the element's [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) attribute is [`HAVE_METADATA`](#48117-ready-states) or greater, and the user agent [encounters a non-fatal error](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) during the processing of the [media data](#4811-media-elements), and due to that error, is not able to play the content at the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource).

A [media element](#4811-media-elements) is said to have paused for user interaction when its [`paused`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) attribute is false, the [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) attribute is either [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#48117-ready-states) or [`HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA`](#48117-ready-states), and the user agent has reached a point in the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) where the user has to make a selection for the resource to continue.

It is possible for a [media element](#4811-media-elements) to have both [ended playback](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) and [paused for user interaction](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) at the same time.

When a [media element](#4811-media-elements) that is [potentially playing](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) stops playing because it has [paused for user interaction](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), the user agent must [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`timeupdate`](#481116-events-summary) at the element.

A [media element](#4811-media-elements) is said to have paused for in-band content when its [`paused`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) attribute is false, the [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) attribute is either [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#48117-ready-states) or [`HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA`](#48117-ready-states), and the user agent has suspended playback of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) in order to play content that is temporally anchored to the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) and has a nonzero length, or to play content that is temporally anchored to a segment of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) but has a length longer than that segment.

> [!example]
> One example of when a [media element](#4811-media-elements) would be [paused for in-band content](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) is when the user agent is playing [audio descriptions](#4810-the-track-element) from an external WebVTT file, and the synthesized speech generated for a cue is longer than the time between the [text track cue start time](#4811111-text-track-model) and the [text track cue end time](#4811111-text-track-model).

---

When the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) reaches the end of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) when the [direction of playback](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) is forwards, then the user agent must follow these steps:
1. If the [media element](#4811-media-elements) has a [`loop`](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) attribute specified, then [seek](#48119-seeking) to the [earliest possible position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) and return.
2. As defined above, the [`ended`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) IDL attribute starts returning true once the [event loop](#8171-definitions) returns to [step 1](#8173-processing-model).
3. [Queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) and the following steps:
   1. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`timeupdate`](#481116-events-summary) at the [media element](#4811-media-elements).
   2. If the [media element](#4811-media-elements) has [ended playback](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), the [direction of playback](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) is forwards, and [paused](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) is false:
      1. Set the [`paused`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) attribute to true.
      2. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`pause`](#481116-events-summary) at the [media element](#4811-media-elements).
      3. [Take pending play promises](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) and [reject pending play promises](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) with the result and an ["`AbortError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#aborterror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
   3. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`ended`](#481116-events-summary) at the [media element](#4811-media-elements).

When the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) reaches the [earliest possible position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) when the [direction of playback](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) is backwards, then the user agent must only [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`timeupdate`](#481116-events-summary) at the element.

> [!note]
> The word "reaches" here does not imply that the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) needs to have changed during normal playback; it could be via [seeking](#48119-seeking), for instance.

---

The `defaultPlaybackRate` attribute gives the desired speed at which the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) is to play, as a multiple of its intrinsic speed. The attribute is mutable: on getting it must return the last value it was set to, or 1.0 if it hasn't yet been set; on setting the attribute must be set to the new value.

> [!note]
> The [`defaultPlaybackRate`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) is used by the user agent when it [exposes a user interface to the user](#481113-user-interface).

The `playbackRate` attribute gives the effective playback rate, which is the speed at which the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) plays, as a multiple of its intrinsic speed. If it is not equal to the [`defaultPlaybackRate`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), then the implication is that the user is using a feature such as fast forward or slow motion playback. The attribute is mutable: on getting it must return the last value it was set to, or 1.0 if it hasn't yet been set; on setting, the user agent must follow these steps:
1. If the given value is not supported by the user agent, then throw a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Set [`playbackRate`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) to the new value, and if the element is [potentially playing](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), change the playback speed.

When the [`defaultPlaybackRate`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) or [`playbackRate`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) attributes change value (either by being set by script or by being changed directly by the user agent, e.g. in response to user control), the user agent must [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`ratechange`](#481116-events-summary) at the [media element](#4811-media-elements). The user agent must process attribute changes smoothly and must not introduce any perceivable gaps or muting of playback in response.

The `preservesPitch` getter steps are to return true if a pitch-preserving algorithm is in effect during playback. The setter steps are to correspondingly switch the pitch-preserving algorithm on or off, without any perceivable gaps or muting of playback. By default, such a pitch-preserving algorithm must be in effect (i.e., the getter will initially return true).

---

The `played` getter steps are to return a new [normalized `TimeRanges` object](#481114-time-ranges) that represents the ranges of points on the [media timeline](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [media resource](#4811-media-elements) reached through the usual monotonic increase of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) during normal playback, if any.

> [!warning]
> Returning a new object each time is a bad pattern for attribute getters and is only enshrined here as it would be costly to change it. It is not to be copied to new APIs.

---

Each [media element](#4811-media-elements) has a list of pending play promises, which must initially be empty.

To take pending play promises for a [media element](#4811-media-elements), the user agent must run the following steps:
1. Let promises be an empty list of promises.
2. Copy the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of pending play promises](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) to promises.
3. Clear the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of pending play promises](#48118-playing-the-media-resource).
4. Return promises.

To resolve pending play promises for a [media element](#4811-media-elements) with a list of promises promises, the user agent must resolve each promise in promises with undefined.

To reject pending play promises for a [media element](#4811-media-elements) with a list of promises promises and an exception name error, the user agent must reject each promise in promises with error.

To notify about playing for a [media element](#4811-media-elements), the user agent must run the following steps:
1. [Take pending play promises](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) and let promises be the result.
2. [Queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the element and the following steps:
   1. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`playing`](#481116-events-summary) at the element.
   2. [Resolve pending play promises](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) with promises.

When the `play()` method on a [media element](#4811-media-elements) is invoked, the user agent must run the following steps:
1. If the [media element](#4811-media-elements) is not [allowed to play](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), then return [a promise rejected with](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#a-promise-rejected-with) a ["`NotAllowedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notallowederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. If the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`error`](#48111-error-codes) attribute is not null and its [code](#48111-error-codes) is [`MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED`](#48111-error-codes), then return [a promise rejected with](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#a-promise-rejected-with) a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

   > [!note]
   > This means that the [dedicated media source failure steps](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) have run. Playback is not possible until the [media element load algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) clears the [`error`](#48111-error-codes) attribute.

3. Let resumptionSteps be the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [lazy load resumption steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes).
4. If resumptionSteps is not null:
   1. Set the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [lazy load resumption steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) to null.
   2. Invoke resumptionSteps.
5. Let promise be a new promise and append promise to the [list of pending play promises](#48118-playing-the-media-resource).
6. Run the [internal play steps](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) for the [media element](#4811-media-elements).
7. Return promise.

The internal play steps for a [media element](#4811-media-elements) are as follows:
1. If the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) attribute has the value [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#48114-network-states), invoke the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [resource selection algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource).
2. If the [playback has ended](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) and the [direction of playback](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) is forwards, [seek](#48119-seeking) to the [earliest possible position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements).

   > [!note]
   > This [will cause](#48119-seeking) the user agent to [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`timeupdate`](#481116-events-summary) at the [media element](#4811-media-elements).

3. If the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`paused`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) attribute is true:
   1. Change the value of [`paused`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) to false.
   2. If the [show poster flag](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) is true, set the element's [show poster flag](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) to false and run the *[time marches on](#48118-playing-the-media-resource)* steps.
   3. [Queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`play`](#481116-events-summary) at the element.
   4. If the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) attribute has the value [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#48117-ready-states), [`HAVE_METADATA`](#48117-ready-states), or [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#48117-ready-states), [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`waiting`](#481116-events-summary) at the element.

      Otherwise, the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) attribute has the value [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#48117-ready-states) or [`HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA`](#48117-ready-states): [notify about playing](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) for the element.

4. Otherwise, if the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) attribute has the value [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#48117-ready-states) or [`HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA`](#48117-ready-states), [take pending play promises](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) and [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [resolve pending play promises](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) with the result.

   > [!note]
   > The media element is already playing. However, it's possible that promise will be [rejected](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) before the queued task is run.

5. Set the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [can autoplay flag](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) to false.

---

When the `pause()` method is invoked, and when the user agent is required to pause the [media element](#4811-media-elements), the user agent must run the following steps:
1. If the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) attribute has the value [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#48114-network-states), invoke the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [resource selection algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource).
2. Run the [internal pause steps](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) for the [media element](#4811-media-elements).

The internal pause steps for a [media element](#4811-media-elements) are as follows:
1. Set the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [can autoplay flag](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) to false.
2. If the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`paused`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) attribute is false, run the following steps:
   1. Change the value of [`paused`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) to true.
   2. [Take pending play promises](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) and let promises be the result.
   3. [Queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) and the following steps:
      1. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`timeupdate`](#481116-events-summary) at the element.
      2. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`pause`](#481116-events-summary) at the element.
      3. [Reject pending play promises](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) with promises and an ["`AbortError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#aborterror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
   4. Set the [official playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) to the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource).

---

If the element's [`playbackRate`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) is positive or zero, then the direction of playback is forwards. Otherwise, it is backwards.

When a [media element](#4811-media-elements) is [potentially playing](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) and its [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is a [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents) [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), its [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) must increase monotonically at the element's [`playbackRate`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) units of media time per unit time of the [media timeline](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource)'s clock. (This specification always refers to this as an *increase*, but that increase could actually be a *de*crease if the element's [`playbackRate`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) is negative.)

> [!note]
> The element's [`playbackRate`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) can be 0.0, in which case the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) doesn't move, despite playback not being paused ([`paused`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) doesn't become true, and the [`pause`](#481116-events-summary) event doesn't fire).

> [!note]
> This specification doesn't define how the user agent achieves the appropriate playback rate — depending on the protocol and media available, it is plausible that the user agent could negotiate with the server to have the server provide the media data at the appropriate rate, so that (except for the period between when the rate is changed and when the server updates the stream's playback rate) the client doesn't actually have to drop or interpolate any frames.

Any time the user agent [provides a stable state](#8173-processing-model), the [official playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) must be set to the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource).

If the element's [`playbackRate`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) is not 1.0 and [`preservesPitch`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) is true, the user agent must apply pitch adjustment to preserve the original pitch of the audio. Otherwise, the user agent must speed up or slow down the audio without any pitch adjustment.

When a [media element](#4811-media-elements) is [potentially playing](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), its audio data played must be synchronized with the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), at the element's [effective media volume](#481113-user-interface). The user agent must play the audio from audio tracks that were enabled when the [event loop](#8171-definitions) last reached [step 1](#8173-processing-model).

When a [media element](#4811-media-elements) is not [potentially playing](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), audio must not play for the element.

[Media elements](#4811-media-elements) that are [potentially playing](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) while not [in a document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) must not play any video, but should play any audio component. Media elements must not stop playing just because all references to them have been removed; only once a media element is in a state where no further audio could ever be played by that element may the element be garbage collected.

> [!note]
> It is possible for an element to which no explicit references exist to play audio, even if such an element is not still actively playing: for instance, it could be unpaused but stalled waiting for content to buffer, or it could be still buffering, but with a [`suspend`](#481116-events-summary) event listener that begins playback. Even a media element whose [media resource](#4811-media-elements) has no audio tracks could eventually play audio again if it had an event listener that changes the [media resource](#4811-media-elements).

---

Each [media element](#4811-media-elements) has a list of newly introduced cues, which must be initially empty. Whenever a [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) is added to the [list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model) of a [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) that is in the [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) for a [media element](#4811-media-elements), that [cue](#4811111-text-track-model) must be added to the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of newly introduced cues](#48118-playing-the-media-resource). Whenever a [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) is added to the [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) for a [media element](#4811-media-elements), all of the [cues](#4811111-text-track-model) in that [text track](#4811111-text-track-model)'s [list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model) must be added to the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of newly introduced cues](#48118-playing-the-media-resource). When a [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of newly introduced cues](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) has new cues added while the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [show poster flag](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) is not set, then the user agent must run the *[time marches on](#48118-playing-the-media-resource)* steps.

When a [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) is removed from the [list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model) of a [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) that is in the [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) for a [media element](#4811-media-elements), and whenever a [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) is removed from the [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) of a [media element](#4811-media-elements), if the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [show poster flag](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) is not set, then the user agent must run the *[time marches on](#48118-playing-the-media-resource)* steps.

When the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) of a [media element](#4811-media-elements) changes (e.g. due to playback or seeking), the user agent must run the *[time marches on](#48118-playing-the-media-resource)* steps. To support use cases that depend on the timing accuracy of cue event firing, such as synchronizing captions with shot changes in a video, user agents should fire cue events as close as possible to their position on the media timeline, and ideally within 20 milliseconds. If the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) changes while the steps are running, then the user agent must wait for the steps to complete, and then must immediately rerun the steps. These steps are thus run as often as possible or needed.

> [!note]
> If one iteration takes a long time, this can cause short duration [cues](#4811111-text-track-model) to be skipped over as the user agent rushes ahead to "catch up", so these cues will not appear in the [`activeCues`](#4811115-text-track-api) list.

The *time marches on* steps are as follows:
1. Let current cues be a list of [cues](#4811111-text-track-model), initialized to contain all the [cues](#4811111-text-track-model) of all the [hidden](#4811111-text-track-model) or [showing](#4811111-text-track-model) [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) of the [media element](#4811-media-elements) (not the [disabled](#4811111-text-track-model) ones) whose [start times](#4811111-text-track-model) are less than or equal to the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) and whose [end times](#4811111-text-track-model) are greater than the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource).
2. Let other cues be a list of [cues](#4811111-text-track-model), initialized to contain all the [cues](#4811111-text-track-model) of [hidden](#4811111-text-track-model) and [showing](#4811111-text-track-model) [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) of the [media element](#4811-media-elements) that are not present in current cues.
3. Let last time be the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) at the time this algorithm was last run for this [media element](#4811-media-elements), if this is not the first time it has run.
4. If the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) has, since the last time this algorithm was run, only changed through its usual monotonic increase during normal playback, then let missed cues be the list of [cues](#4811111-text-track-model) in other cues whose [start times](#4811111-text-track-model) are greater than or equal to last time and whose [end times](#4811111-text-track-model) are less than or equal to the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource). Otherwise, let missed cues be an empty list.
5. Remove all the [cues](#4811111-text-track-model) in missed cues that are also in the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of newly introduced cues](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), and then empty the element's [list of newly introduced cues](#48118-playing-the-media-resource).
6. If the time was reached through the usual monotonic increase of the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) during normal playback, and if the user agent has not fired a [`timeupdate`](#481116-events-summary) event at the element in the past 15 to 250ms and is not still running event handlers for such an event, then the user agent must [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`timeupdate`](#481116-events-summary) at the element. (In the other cases, such as explicit seeks, relevant events get fired as part of the overall process of changing the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource).)

   > [!note]
   > The event thus is not to be fired faster than about 66Hz or slower than 4Hz (assuming the event handlers don't take longer than 250ms to run). User agents are encouraged to vary the frequency of the event based on the system load and the average cost of processing the event each time, so that the UI updates are not any more frequent than the user agent can comfortably handle while decoding the video.

7. If all of the [cues](#4811111-text-track-model) in current cues have their [text track cue active flag](#4811111-text-track-model) set, none of the [cues](#4811111-text-track-model) in other cues have their [text track cue active flag](#4811111-text-track-model) set, and missed cues is empty, then return.
8. If the time was reached through the usual monotonic increase of the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) during normal playback, and there are [cues](#4811111-text-track-model) in other cues that have their [text track cue pause-on-exit flag](#4811111-text-track-model) set and that either have their [text track cue active flag](#4811111-text-track-model) set or are also in missed cues, then [immediately](#211-parallelism) [pause](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) the [media element](#4811-media-elements).

   > [!note]
   > In the other cases, such as explicit seeks, playback is not paused by going past the end time of a [cue](#4811111-text-track-model), even if that [cue](#4811111-text-track-model) has its [text track cue pause-on-exit flag](#4811111-text-track-model) set.

9. Let events be a list of [tasks](#8171-definitions), initially empty. Each [task](#8171-definitions) in this list will be associated with a [text track](#4811111-text-track-model), a [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model), and a time, which are used to sort the list before the [tasks](#8171-definitions) are queued.

   Let affected tracks be a list of [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model), initially empty.

   When the steps below say to prepare an event named event for a [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) target with a time time, the user agent must run these steps:
   1. Let track be the [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) with which the [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) target is associated.
   2. Create a [task](#8171-definitions) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named event at target.
   3. Add the newly created [task](#8171-definitions) to events, associated with the time time, the [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) track, and the [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) target.
   4. Add track to affected tracks.

10. For each [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) in missed cues, [prepare an event](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) named [`enter`](#481116-events-summary) for the [`TextTrackCue`](#4811115-text-track-api) object with the [text track cue start time](#4811111-text-track-model).
11. For each [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) in other cues that either has its [text track cue active flag](#4811111-text-track-model) set or is in missed cues, [prepare an event](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) named [`exit`](#481116-events-summary) for the [`TextTrackCue`](#4811115-text-track-api) object with the later of the [text track cue end time](#4811111-text-track-model) and the [text track cue start time](#4811111-text-track-model).
12. For each [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) in current cues that does not have its [text track cue active flag](#4811111-text-track-model) set, [prepare an event](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) named [`enter`](#481116-events-summary) for the [`TextTrackCue`](#4811115-text-track-api) object with the [text track cue start time](#4811111-text-track-model).
13. Sort the [tasks](#8171-definitions) in events in ascending time order ([tasks](#8171-definitions) with earlier times first).

    Further sort [tasks](#8171-definitions) in events that have the same time by the relative [text track cue order](#4811111-text-track-model) of the [text track cues](#4811111-text-track-model) associated with these [tasks](#8171-definitions).

    Finally, sort [tasks](#8171-definitions) in events that have the same time and same [text track cue order](#4811111-text-track-model) by placing [tasks](#8171-definitions) that fire [`enter`](#481116-events-summary) events before those that fire [`exit`](#481116-events-summary) events.

14. [Queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) for each [task](#8171-definitions) in events, in list order.
15. Sort affected tracks in the same order as the [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) appear in the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model), and remove duplicates.
16. For each [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) in affected tracks, in the list order, [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`cuechange`](#481116-events-summary) at the [`TextTrack`](#4811115-text-track-api) object, and, if the [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) has a corresponding [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element, to then [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`cuechange`](#481116-events-summary) at the [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element as well.
17. Set the [text track cue active flag](#4811111-text-track-model) of all the [cues](#4811111-text-track-model) in the current cues, and unset the [text track cue active flag](#4811111-text-track-model) of all the [cues](#4811111-text-track-model) in the other cues.
18. Run the [rules for updating the text track rendering](#4811111-text-track-model) of each of the [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) in affected tracks that are [showing](#4811111-text-track-model), providing the [text track](#4811111-text-track-model)'s [text track language](#4811111-text-track-model) as the fallback language if it is not the empty string. For example, for [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) based on WebVTT, the [rules for updating the display of WebVTT text tracks](https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#rules-for-updating-the-display-of-webvtt-text-tracks). [\[WEBVTT\]](#references)

For the purposes of the algorithm above, a [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) is considered to be part of a [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) only if it is listed in the [text track list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model), not merely if it is associated with the [text track](#4811111-text-track-model).

> [!note]
> If the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) stops being a [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents) document, then the playback will [stop](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) until the document is active again.

When a [media element](#4811-media-elements) is [removed from a `Document`](#214-dom-trees), the user agent must run the following steps:
1. [Await a stable state](#8173-processing-model), allowing the [task](#8171-definitions) that removed the [media element](#4811-media-elements) from the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) to continue. The [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model) consists of all the remaining steps of this algorithm. (Steps in the [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model) are marked with ⌛.)
2. ⌛ If the [media element](#4811-media-elements) is [in a document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree), return.
3. ⌛ Run the [internal pause steps](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) for the [media element](#4811-media-elements).

##### 4.8.11.9 Seeking

`media.seeking`

Returns true if the user agent is currently seeking.

`media.seekable`

Returns a [`TimeRanges`](#481114-time-ranges) object that represents the ranges of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) to which it is possible for the user agent to seek.

`media.fastSeek(time)`

Seeks to near the given time as fast as possible, trading precision for speed. (To seek to a precise time, use the [`currentTime`](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) attribute.)

This does nothing if the media resource has not been loaded.

The `seeking` attribute must initially have the value false.

The `fastSeek(time)` method must [seek](#48119-seeking) to the time given by time, with the *approximate-for-speed* flag set.

When the user agent is required to seek to a particular new playback position in the [media resource](#4811-media-elements), optionally with the *approximate-for-speed* flag set, it means that the user agent must run the following steps. This algorithm interacts closely with the [event loop](#8171-definitions) mechanism; in particular, it has a [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model) (which is triggered as part of the [event loop](#8171-definitions) algorithm). Steps in that section are marked with ⌛.
1. Set the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [show poster flag](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) to false.
2. If the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) is [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#48117-ready-states), return.
3. If the element's [`seeking`](#48119-seeking) IDL attribute is true, then another instance of this algorithm is already running. Abort that other instance of the algorithm without waiting for the step that it is running to complete.
4. Set the [`seeking`](#48119-seeking) IDL attribute to true.
5. If the seek was in response to a DOM method call or setting of an IDL attribute, then continue the script. The remainder of these steps must be run [in parallel](#211-parallelism). With the exception of the steps marked with ⌛, they could be aborted at any time by another instance of this algorithm being invoked.
6. If the new playback position is later than the end of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements), then let it be the end of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) instead.
7. If the new playback position is less than the [earliest possible position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), let it be that position instead.
8. If the (possibly now changed) new playback position is not in one of the ranges given in the [`seekable`](#48119-seeking) attribute, then let it be the position in one of the ranges given in the [`seekable`](#48119-seeking) attribute that is the nearest to the new playback position. If two positions both satisfy that constraint (i.e. the new playback position is exactly in the middle between two ranges in the [`seekable`](#48119-seeking) attribute), then use the position that is closest to the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource). If there are no ranges given in the [`seekable`](#48119-seeking) attribute, then set the [`seeking`](#48119-seeking) IDL attribute to false and return.
9. If the *approximate-for-speed* flag is set, adjust the new playback position to a value that will allow for playback to resume promptly. If new playback position before this step is before [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), then the adjusted new playback position must also be before the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource). Similarly, if the new playback position before this step is after [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), then the adjusted new playback position must also be after the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource).

   > [!example]
   > For example, the user agent could snap to a nearby key frame, so that it doesn't have to spend time decoding then discarding intermediate frames before resuming playback.

10. [Queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`seeking`](#481116-events-summary) at the element.
11. Set the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) to the new playback position.

    > [!note]
    > If the [media element](#4811-media-elements) was [potentially playing](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) immediately before it started seeking, but seeking caused its [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) attribute to change to a value lower than [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#48117-ready-states), then a [`waiting`](#481116-events-summary) event [will be fired](#48117-ready-states) at the element.

    > [!note]
    > This step sets the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), and thus can immediately trigger other conditions, such as the rules regarding when playback "[reaches the end of the media resource](#48118-playing-the-media-resource)" (part of the logic that handles looping), even before the user agent is actually able to render the media data for that position (as determined in the next step).

    > [!note]
    > The [`currentTime`](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) attribute returns the [official playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), not the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), and therefore gets updated before script execution, separate from this algorithm.

12. Wait until the user agent has established whether or not the [media data](#4811-media-elements) for the new playback position is available, and, if it is, until it has decoded enough data to play back that position.
13. [Await a stable state](#8173-processing-model). The [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model) consists of all the remaining steps of this algorithm. (Steps in the [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model) are marked with ⌛.)
14. ⌛ Set the [`seeking`](#48119-seeking) IDL attribute to false.
15. ⌛ Run the [time marches on](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) steps.
16. ⌛ [Queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`timeupdate`](#481116-events-summary) at the element.
17. ⌛ [Queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`seeked`](#481116-events-summary) at the element.

---

The `seekable` getter steps are to return a new [normalized `TimeRanges` object](#481114-time-ranges) that represents the ranges of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [media resource](#4811-media-elements), if any, that the user agent is able to seek to.

> [!note]
> If the user agent can seek to anywhere in the [media resource](#4811-media-elements), e.g. because it is a simple movie file and the user agent and the server support HTTP Range requests, then the attribute would return an object with one range, whose start is the time of the first frame (the [earliest possible position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), typically zero), and whose end is the same as the time of the first frame plus the [`duration`](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) attribute's value (which would equal the time of the last frame, and might be positive Infinity).

> [!note]
> The range might be continuously changing, e.g. if the user agent is buffering a sliding window on an infinite stream. This is the behavior seen with DVRs viewing live TV, for instance.

> [!warning]
> Returning a new object each time is a bad pattern for attribute getters and is only enshrined here as it would be costly to change it. It is not to be copied to new APIs.

User agents should adopt a very liberal and optimistic view of what is seekable. User agents should also buffer recent content where possible to enable seeking to be fast.

> [!example]
> For instance, consider a large video file served on an HTTP server without support for HTTP Range requests. A browser *could* implement this by only buffering the current frame and data obtained for subsequent frames, never allow seeking, except for seeking to the very start by restarting the playback. However, this would be a poor implementation. A high quality implementation would buffer the last few minutes of content (or more, if sufficient storage space is available), allowing the user to jump back and rewatch something surprising without any latency, and would in addition allow arbitrary seeking by reloading the file from the start if necessary, which would be slower but still more convenient than having to literally restart the video and watch it all the way through just to get to an earlier unbuffered spot.

[Media resources](#4811-media-elements) might be internally scripted or interactive. Thus, a [media element](#4811-media-elements) could play in a non-linear fashion. If this happens, the user agent must act as if the algorithm for [seeking](#48119-seeking) was used whenever the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) changes in a discontinuous fashion (so that the relevant events fire).

##### 4.8.11.10 Media resources with multiple media tracks

A [media resource](#4811-media-elements) can have multiple embedded audio and video tracks. For example, in addition to the primary video and audio tracks, a [media resource](#4811-media-elements) could have foreign-language dubbed dialogues, director's commentaries, audio descriptions, alternative angles, or sign-language overlays.

`media.audioTracks`

Returns an [`AudioTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object representing the audio tracks available in the [media resource](#4811-media-elements).

`media.videoTracks`

Returns a [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object representing the video tracks available in the [media resource](#4811-media-elements).

The `audioTracks` attribute of a [media element](#4811-media-elements) must return a [live](#215-scripting) [`AudioTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object representing the audio tracks available in the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [media resource](#4811-media-elements).

The `videoTracks` attribute of a [media element](#4811-media-elements) must return a [live](#215-scripting) [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object representing the video tracks available in the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [media resource](#4811-media-elements).

> [!note]
> There are only ever one [`AudioTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object and one [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object per [media element](#4811-media-elements), even if another [media resource](#4811-media-elements) is loaded into the element: the objects are reused. (The [`AudioTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) and [`VideoTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) objects are not, though.)

###### 4.8.11.10.1 [`AudioTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) and [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) objects

The [`AudioTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) and [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) interfaces are used by attributes defined in the previous section.

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface AudioTrackList : EventTarget {
  readonly attribute unsigned long length;
  getter AudioTrack (unsigned long index);
  AudioTrack? getTrackById(DOMString id);

  attribute EventHandler onchange;
  attribute EventHandler onaddtrack;
  attribute EventHandler onremovetrack;
};

[Exposed=Window]
interface AudioTrack {
  readonly attribute DOMString id;
  readonly attribute DOMString kind;
  readonly attribute DOMString label;
  readonly attribute DOMString language;
  attribute boolean enabled;
};

[Exposed=Window]
interface VideoTrackList : EventTarget {
  readonly attribute unsigned long length;
  getter VideoTrack (unsigned long index);
  VideoTrack? getTrackById(DOMString id);
  readonly attribute long selectedIndex;

  attribute EventHandler onchange;
  attribute EventHandler onaddtrack;
  attribute EventHandler onremovetrack;
};

[Exposed=Window]
interface VideoTrack {
  readonly attribute DOMString id;
  readonly attribute DOMString kind;
  readonly attribute DOMString label;
  readonly attribute DOMString language;
  attribute boolean selected;
};
```

`media.audioTracks.length`

`media.videoTracks.length`

Returns the number of tracks in the list.

`audioTrack = media.audioTracks[index]`

`videoTrack = media.videoTracks[index]`

Returns the specified [`AudioTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) or [`VideoTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object.

`audioTrack = media.audioTracks.getTrackById(id)`

`videoTrack = media.videoTracks.getTrackById(id)`

Returns the [`AudioTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) or [`VideoTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object with the given identifier, or null if no track has that identifier.

`audioTrack.id`

`videoTrack.id`

Returns the ID of the given track. This is the ID that can be used with a [fragment](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment) if the format supports [media fragment syntax](https://www.w3.org/TR/media-frags/#media-fragment-syntax), and that can be used with the `getTrackById()` method.

`audioTrack.kind`

`videoTrack.kind`

Returns the category the given track falls into. The [possible track categories](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) are given below.

`audioTrack.label`

`videoTrack.label`

Returns the label of the given track, if known, or the empty string otherwise.

`audioTrack.language`

`videoTrack.language`

Returns the language of the given track, if known, or the empty string otherwise.

`audioTrack.enabled [ = value ]`

Returns true if the given track is active, and false otherwise.

Can be set, to change whether the track is enabled or not. If multiple audio tracks are enabled simultaneously, they are mixed.

`media.videoTracks.selectedIndex`

Returns the index of the currently selected track, if any, or −1 otherwise.

`videoTrack.selected [ = value ]`

Returns true if the given track is active, and false otherwise.

Can be set, to change whether the track is selected or not. Either zero or one video track is selected; selecting a new track while a previous one is selected will unselect the previous one.

An [`AudioTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object represents a dynamic list of zero or more audio tracks, of which zero or more can be enabled at a time. Each audio track is represented by an [`AudioTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object.

A [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object represents a dynamic list of zero or more video tracks, of which zero or one can be selected at a time. Each video track is represented by a [`VideoTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object.

Tracks in [`AudioTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) and [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) objects must be consistently ordered. If the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) is in a format that defines an order, then that order must be used; otherwise, the order must be the relative order in which the tracks are declared in the [media resource](#4811-media-elements). The order used is called the *natural order* of the list.

> [!note]
> Each track in one of these objects thus has an index; the first has the index 0, and each subsequent track is numbered one higher than the previous one. If a [media resource](#4811-media-elements) dynamically adds or removes audio or video tracks, then the indices of the tracks will change dynamically. If the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) changes entirely, then all the previous tracks will be removed and replaced with new tracks.

The [`AudioTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) `length` and [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) `length` attribute getters must return the number of tracks represented by their objects at the time of getting.

The [supported property indices](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-supported-property-indices) of [`AudioTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) and [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) objects at any instant are the numbers from zero to the number of tracks represented by the respective object minus one, if any tracks are represented. If an [`AudioTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) or [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object represents no tracks, it has no [supported property indices](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-supported-property-indices).

To [determine the value of an indexed property](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-determine-the-value-of-an-indexed-property) for a given index index in an [`AudioTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) or [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object list, the user agent must return the [`AudioTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) or [`VideoTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object that represents the indexth track in list.

The [`AudioTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) `getTrackById(id)` and [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) `getTrackById(id)` methods must return the first [`AudioTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) or [`VideoTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object (respectively) in the [`AudioTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) or [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object (respectively) whose identifier is equal to the value of the id argument (in the natural order of the list, as defined above). When no tracks match the given argument, the methods must return null.

The [`AudioTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) and [`VideoTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) objects represent specific tracks of a [media resource](#4811-media-elements). Each track can have an identifier, category, label, and language. These aspects of a track are permanent for the lifetime of the track; even if a track is removed from a [media resource](#4811-media-elements)'s [`AudioTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) or [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) objects, those aspects do not change.

In addition, [`AudioTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) objects can each be enabled or disabled; this is the audio track's *enabled state*. When an [`AudioTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) is created, its *enabled state* must be set to false (disabled).
