The [resource fetch algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) can override this.

Similarly, a single [`VideoTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object per [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object can be selected, this is the video track's *selection state*. When a [`VideoTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) is created, its *selection state* must be set to false (not selected). The [resource fetch algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) can override this.

The [`AudioTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) `id` and [`VideoTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) `id` attributes must return the identifier of the track, if it has one, or the empty string otherwise. If the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) is in a format that supports [media fragment syntax](https://www.w3.org/TR/media-frags/#media-fragment-syntax), the identifier returned for a particular track must be the same identifier that would enable the track if used as the name of a track in the track dimension of such a [fragment](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment). [\[INBAND\]](#references)

> [!example]
> For example, in Ogg files, this would be the Name header field of the track. [\[OGGSKELETONHEADERS\]](#references)

The [`AudioTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) `kind` and [`VideoTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) `kind` attributes must return the category of the track, if it has one, or the empty string otherwise.

The category of a track is the string given in the first column of the table below that is the most appropriate for the track based on the definitions in the table's second and third columns, as determined by the metadata included in the track in the [media resource](#4811-media-elements). The cell in the third column of a row says what the category given in the cell in the first column of that row applies to; a category is only appropriate for an audio track if it applies to audio tracks, and a category is only appropriate for video tracks if it applies to video tracks. Categories must only be returned for [`AudioTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) objects if they are appropriate for audio, and must only be returned for [`VideoTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) objects if they are appropriate for video.

For Ogg files, the Role header field of the track gives the relevant metadata. For DASH media resources, the `Role` element conveys the information. For WebM, only the `FlagDefault` element currently maps to a value. Sourcing In-band Media Resource Tracks from Media Containers into HTML has further details. [\[OGGSKELETONHEADERS\]](#references) [\[DASH\]](#references) [\[WEBMCG\]](#references) [\[INBAND\]](#references)

Return values for [`AudioTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects)'s [`kind`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) and [`VideoTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects)'s [`kind`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects)

| Category | Definition | Applies to... | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| "`alternative`" | A possible alternative to the main track, e.g. a different take of a song (audio), or a different angle (video). | Audio and video. | Ogg: "audio/alternate" or "video/alternate"; DASH: "alternate" without "main" and "commentary" roles, and, for audio, without the "dub" role (other roles ignored). |
| "`captions`" | A version of the main video track with captions burnt in. (For legacy content; new content would use text tracks.) | Video only. | DASH: "caption" and "main" roles together (other roles ignored). |
| "`descriptions`" | An audio description of a video track. | Audio only. | Ogg: "audio/audiodesc". |
| "`main`" | The primary audio or video track. | Audio and video. | Ogg: "audio/main" or "video/main"; WebM: the "FlagDefault" element is set; DASH: "main" role without "caption", "subtitle", and "dub" roles (other roles ignored). |
| "`main-desc`" | The primary audio track, mixed with audio descriptions. | Audio only. | AC3 audio in MPEG-2 TS: bsmod=2 and full\_svc=1. |
| "`sign`" | A sign-language interpretation of an audio track. | Video only. | Ogg: "video/sign". |
| "`subtitles`" | A version of the main video track with subtitles burnt in. (For legacy content; new content would use text tracks.) | Video only. | DASH: "subtitle" and "main" roles together (other roles ignored). |
| "`translation`" | A translated version of the main audio track. | Audio only. | Ogg: "audio/dub". DASH: "dub" and "main" roles together (other roles ignored). |
| "`commentary`" | Commentary on the primary audio or video track, e.g. a director's commentary. | Audio and video. | DASH: "commentary" role without "main" role (other roles ignored). |
| "" (empty string) | No explicit kind, or the kind given by the track's metadata is not recognized by the user agent. | Audio and video. |  |

The [`AudioTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) `label` and [`VideoTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) `label` attributes must return the label of the track, if it has one, or the empty string otherwise. [\[INBAND\]](#references)

The [`AudioTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) `language` and [`VideoTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) `language` attributes must return the BCP 47 language tag of the language of the track, if it has one, or the empty string otherwise. If the user agent is not able to express that language as a BCP 47 language tag (for example because the language information in the [media resource](#4811-media-elements)'s format is a free-form string without a defined interpretation), then the method must return the empty string, as if the track had no language. [\[INBAND\]](#references)

The [`AudioTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) `enabled` attribute, on getting, must return true if the track is currently enabled, and false otherwise. On setting, it must enable the track if the new value is true, and disable it otherwise. (If the track is no longer in an [`AudioTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object, then the track being enabled or disabled has no effect beyond changing the value of the attribute on the [`AudioTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object.)

Whenever an audio track in an [`AudioTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) that was disabled is enabled, and whenever one that was enabled is disabled, the user agent must [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`change`](#481116-events-summary) at the [`AudioTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object.

An audio track that has no data for a particular position on the [media timeline](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), or that does not exist at that position, must be interpreted as being silent at that point on the timeline.

The [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) `selectedIndex` attribute must return the index of the currently selected track, if any. If the [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object does not currently represent any tracks, or if none of the tracks are selected, it must instead return −1.

The [`VideoTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) `selected` attribute, on getting, must return true if the track is currently selected, and false otherwise. On setting, it must select the track if the new value is true, and unselect it otherwise. If the track is in a [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects), then all the other [`VideoTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) objects in that list must be unselected. (If the track is no longer in a [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object, then the track being selected or unselected has no effect beyond changing the value of the attribute on the [`VideoTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object.)

Whenever a track in a [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) that was previously not selected is selected, and whenever the selected track in a [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) is unselected without a new track being selected in its stead, the user agent must [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`change`](#481116-events-summary) at the [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) object. This [task](#8171-definitions) must be [queued](#8172-queuing-tasks) before the [task](#8171-definitions) that fires the [`resize`](#481116-events-summary) event, if any.

A video track that has no data for a particular position on the [media timeline](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) must be interpreted as being [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black) at that point on the timeline, with the same dimensions as the last frame before that position, or, if the position is before all the data for that track, the same dimensions as the first frame for that track. A track that does not exist at all at the current position must be treated as if it existed but had no data.

> [!example]
> For instance, if a video has a track that is only introduced after one hour of playback, and the user selects that track then goes back to the start, then the user agent will act as if that track started at the start of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) but was simply transparent until one hour in.

---

The following are the [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers) (and their corresponding [event handler event types](#8181-event-handlers)) that must be supported, as [event handler IDL attributes](#8181-event-handlers), by all objects implementing the [`AudioTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) and [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) interfaces:

| [Event handler](#8181-event-handlers) | [Event handler event type](#8181-event-handlers) |
| --- | --- |
| `onchange` | [`change`](#481116-events-summary) |
| `onaddtrack` | [`addtrack`](#481116-events-summary) |
| `onremovetrack` | [`removetrack`](#481116-events-summary) |

###### 4.8.11.10.2 Selecting specific audio and video tracks declaratively

The [`audioTracks`](#481110-media-resources-with-multiple-media-tracks) and [`videoTracks`](#481110-media-resources-with-multiple-media-tracks) attributes allow scripts to select which track should play, but it is also possible to select specific tracks declaratively, by specifying particular tracks in the [fragment](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment) of the [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements). The format of the [fragment](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment) depends on the [MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type) of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements). [\[RFC2046\]](#references) [\[URL\]](#references)

> [!example]
> In this example, a video that uses a format that supports [media fragment syntax](https://www.w3.org/TR/media-frags/#media-fragment-syntax) is embedded in such a way that the alternative angles labeled "Alternative" are enabled instead of the default video track.
> 
> ```html
> <video src="myvideo#track=Alternative"></video>
> ```

##### 4.8.11.11 Timed text tracks

###### 4.8.11.11.1 Text track model

A [media element](#4811-media-elements) can have a group of associated text tracks, known as the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s list of text tracks. The [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) are sorted as follows:
1. The [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) corresponding to [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element children of the [media element](#4811-media-elements), in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
2. Any [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) added using the [`addTextTrack()`](#4811115-text-track-api) method, in the order they were added, oldest first.
3. Any [media-resource-specific text tracks](#4811112-sourcing-in-band-text-tracks) ([text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) corresponding to data in the [media resource](#4811-media-elements)), in the order defined by the [media resource](#4811-media-elements)'s format specification.

A [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) is a [`TextTrack`](#4811115-text-track-api) object and consists of:

The kind of text track

This decides how the track is handled by the user agent. The kind is represented by a string. The possible strings are:
- `subtitles`
- `captions`
- `descriptions`
- `chapters`
- `metadata`

The [kind of track](#4811111-text-track-model) can change dynamically, in the case of a [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) corresponding to a [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element.

A label

This is a human-readable string intended to identify the track for the user.

The [label of a track](#4811111-text-track-model) can change dynamically, in the case of a [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) corresponding to a [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element.

When a [text track label](#4811111-text-track-model) is the empty string, the user agent should automatically generate an appropriate label from the text track's other properties (e.g. the kind of text track and the text track's language) for use in its user interface. This automatically-generated label is not exposed in the API.

An in-band metadata track dispatch type

This is a string extracted from the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) specifically for in-band metadata tracks to enable such tracks to be dispatched to different scripts in the document.

> [!example]
> For example, a traditional TV station broadcast streamed on the web and augmented with web-specific interactive features could include text tracks with metadata for ad targeting, trivia game data during game shows, player states during sports games, recipe information during food programs, and so forth. As each program starts and ends, new tracks might be added or removed from the stream, and as each one is added, the user agent could bind them to dedicated script modules using the value of this attribute.

Other than for in-band metadata text tracks, the [in-band metadata track dispatch type](#4811111-text-track-model) is the empty string. How this value is populated for different media formats is described in [steps to expose a media-resource-specific text track](#4811112-sourcing-in-band-text-tracks).

A language

This is a string (a BCP 47 language tag) representing the language of the text track's cues. [\[BCP47\]](#references)

The [language of a text track](#4811111-text-track-model) can change dynamically, in the case of a [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) corresponding to a [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element.

An identifier

A string.

A readiness state

One of the following:

Not loaded

Indicates that the text track's cues have not been obtained.

Loading

Indicates that the text track is loading and there have been no fatal errors encountered so far. Further cues might still be added to the track by the parser.

Loaded

Indicates that the text track has been loaded with no fatal errors.

Failed to load

Indicates that the text track was enabled, but when the user agent attempted to obtain it, this failed in some way (e.g., [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) could not be [parsed](#242-parsing-urls), network error, unknown text track format). Some or all of the cues are likely missing and will not be obtained.

The [readiness state](#4811111-text-track-model) of a [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) changes dynamically as the track is obtained.

A mode

One of the following:

Disabled

Indicates that the text track is not active. Other than for the purposes of exposing the track in the DOM, the user agent is ignoring the text track. No cues are active, no events are fired, and the user agent will not attempt to obtain the track's cues.

Hidden

Indicates that the text track is active, but that the user agent is not actively displaying the cues. If no attempt has yet been made to obtain the track's cues, the user agent will perform such an attempt momentarily. The user agent is maintaining a list of which cues are active, and events are being fired accordingly.

Showing

Indicates that the text track is active. If no attempt has yet been made to obtain the track's cues, the user agent will perform such an attempt momentarily. The user agent is maintaining a list of which cues are active, and events are being fired accordingly. In addition, for text tracks whose [kind](#4811111-text-track-model) is [`subtitles`](#4811111-text-track-model) or [`captions`](#4811111-text-track-model), the cues are being overlaid on the video as appropriate; for text tracks whose [kind](#4811111-text-track-model) is [`descriptions`](#4811111-text-track-model), the user agent is making the cues available to the user in a non-visual fashion; and for text tracks whose [kind](#4811111-text-track-model) is [`chapters`](#4811111-text-track-model), the user agent is making available to the user a mechanism by which the user can navigate to any point in the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) by selecting a cue.

A list of zero or more cues

A list of [text track cues](#4811111-text-track-model), along with rules for updating the text track rendering. For example, for WebVTT, the [rules for updating the display of WebVTT text tracks](https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#rules-for-updating-the-display-of-webvtt-text-tracks). [\[WEBVTT\]](#references)

The [list of cues of a text track](#4811111-text-track-model) can change dynamically, either because the [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) has [not yet been loaded](#4811111-text-track-model) or is still [loading](#4811111-text-track-model), or due to DOM manipulation.

---

Each [media element](#4811-media-elements) has a list of pending text tracks, which must initially be empty, a blocked-on-parser flag, which must initially be false, and a did-perform-automatic-track-selection flag, which must also initially be false.

When the user agent is required to populate the list of pending text tracks of a [media element](#4811-media-elements), the user agent must add to the element's [list of pending text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) each [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) in the element's [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) whose [text track mode](#4811111-text-track-model) is not [disabled](#4811111-text-track-model) and whose [text track readiness state](#4811111-text-track-model) is [loading](#4811111-text-track-model).

Whenever a [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element's parent node changes, the user agent must remove the corresponding [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) from any [list of pending text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) that it is in.

Whenever a [text track](#4811111-text-track-model)'s [text track readiness state](#4811111-text-track-model) changes to either [loaded](#4811111-text-track-model) or [failed to load](#4811111-text-track-model), the user agent must remove it from any [list of pending text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) that it is in.

When a [media element](#4811-media-elements) is created by an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) or [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents), the user agent must set the element's [blocked-on-parser](#4811111-text-track-model) flag to true. When a [media element](#4811-media-elements) is popped off the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) of an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) or [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents), the user agent must [honor user preferences for automatic text track selection](#4811113-sourcing-out-of-band-text-tracks), [populate the list of pending text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model), and set the element's [blocked-on-parser](#4811111-text-track-model) flag to false.

The [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) of a [media element](#4811-media-elements) are ready when both the element's [list of pending text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) is empty and the element's [blocked-on-parser](#4811111-text-track-model) flag is false.

Each [media element](#4811-media-elements) has a pending text track change notification flag, which must initially be unset.

Whenever a [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) that is in a [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) has its [text track mode](#4811111-text-track-model) change value, the user agent must run the following steps for the [media element](#4811-media-elements):
1. If the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [pending text track change notification flag](#4811111-text-track-model) is set, return.
2. Set the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [pending text track change notification flag](#4811111-text-track-model).
3. [Queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to run these steps:
   1. Unset the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [pending text track change notification flag](#4811111-text-track-model).
   2. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`change`](#481116-events-summary) at the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`textTracks`](#4811115-text-track-api) attribute's [`TextTrackList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object.
4. If the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [show poster flag](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) is not set, run the *[time marches on](#48118-playing-the-media-resource)* steps.

The [task source](#8171-definitions) for the [tasks](#8171-definitions) listed in this section is the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources).

---

A text track cue is the unit of time-sensitive data in a [text track](#4811111-text-track-model), corresponding for instance for subtitles and captions to the text that appears at a particular time and disappears at another time.

Each [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) consists of:

An identifier

An arbitrary string.

A start time

The time, in seconds and fractions of a second, that describes the beginning of the range of the [media data](#4811-media-elements) to which the cue applies.

An end time

The time, in seconds and fractions of a second, that describes the end of the range of the [media data](#4811-media-elements) to which the cue applies, or positive Infinity for an [unbounded text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model).

A pause-on-exit flag

A boolean indicating whether playback of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) is to pause when the end of the range to which the cue applies is reached.

Some additional format-specific data

Additional fields, as needed for the format, including the actual data of the cue. For example, WebVTT has a [text track cue writing direction](https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#webvtt-cue-writing-direction) and so forth. [\[WEBVTT\]](#references)

An unbounded text track cue is a text track cue with a [text track cue end time](#4811111-text-track-model) set to positive Infinity. An active [unbounded text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) cannot become inactive through the usual monotonic increase of the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) during normal playback (e.g. a metadata cue for a chapter in a live event with no announced end time.)

> [!note]
> The [text track cue start time](#4811111-text-track-model) and [text track cue end time](#4811111-text-track-model) can be negative. (The [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) can never be negative, though, so cues entirely before time zero cannot be active.)

Each [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) has a corresponding [`TextTrackCue`](#4811115-text-track-api) object (or more specifically, an object that inherits from [`TextTrackCue`](#4811115-text-track-api) — for example, WebVTT cues use the [`VTTCue`](https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#vttcue) interface). A [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model)'s in-memory representation can be dynamically changed through this [`TextTrackCue`](#4811115-text-track-api) API. [\[WEBVTT\]](#references)

A [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) is associated with [rules for updating the text track rendering](#4811111-text-track-model), as defined by the specification for the specific kind of [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model). These rules are used specifically when the object representing the cue is added to a [`TextTrack`](#4811115-text-track-api) object using the [`addCue()`](#4811115-text-track-api) method.

In addition, each [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) has two pieces of dynamic information:

The active flag

This flag must be initially unset. The flag is used to ensure events are fired appropriately when the cue becomes active or inactive, and to make sure the right cues are rendered.

The user agent must synchronously unset this flag whenever the [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) is removed from its [text track](#4811111-text-track-model)'s [text track list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model); whenever the [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) itself is removed from its [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) or has its [text track mode](#4811111-text-track-model) changed to [disabled](#4811111-text-track-model); and whenever the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) is changed back to [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#48117-ready-states). When the flag is unset in this way for one or more cues in [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) that were [showing](#4811111-text-track-model) prior to the relevant incident, the user agent must, after having unset the flag for all the affected cues, apply the [rules for updating the text track rendering](#4811111-text-track-model) of those [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model). For example, for [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) based on WebVTT, the [rules for updating the display of WebVTT text tracks](https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#rules-for-updating-the-display-of-webvtt-text-tracks). [\[WEBVTT\]](#references)

The display state

This is used as part of the rendering model, to keep cues in a consistent position. It must initially be empty. Whenever the [text track cue active flag](#4811111-text-track-model) is unset, the user agent must empty the [text track cue display state](#4811111-text-track-model).

The [text track cues](#4811111-text-track-model) of a [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) are ordered relative to each other in the text track cue order, which is determined as follows: first group the [cues](#4811111-text-track-model) by their [text track](#4811111-text-track-model), with the groups being sorted in the same order as their [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) appear in the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model); then, within each group, [cues](#4811111-text-track-model) must be sorted by their [start time](#4811111-text-track-model), earliest first; then, any [cues](#4811111-text-track-model) with the same [start time](#4811111-text-track-model) must be sorted by their [end time](#4811111-text-track-model), latest first; and finally, any [cues](#4811111-text-track-model) with identical [end times](#4811111-text-track-model) must be sorted in the order they were last added to their respective [text track list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model), oldest first (so e.g. for cues from a WebVTT file, that would initially be the order in which the cues were listed in the file). [\[WEBVTT\]](#references)

###### 4.8.11.11.2 Sourcing in-band text tracks

A media-resource-specific text track is a [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) that corresponds to data found in the [media resource](#4811-media-elements).

Rules for processing and rendering such data are defined by the relevant specifications, e.g. the specification of the video format if the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) is a video. Details for some legacy formats can be found in Sourcing In-band Media Resource Tracks from Media Containers into HTML. [\[INBAND\]](#references)

When a [media resource](#4811-media-elements) contains data that the user agent recognizes and supports as being equivalent to a [text track](#4811111-text-track-model), the user agent [runs](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) the steps to expose a media-resource-specific text track with the relevant data, as follows.
1. Associate the relevant data with a new [text track](#4811111-text-track-model). The [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) is a [media-resource-specific text track](#4811112-sourcing-in-band-text-tracks).
2. Set the new [text track](#4811111-text-track-model)'s [kind](#4811111-text-track-model), [label](#4811111-text-track-model), [language](#4811111-text-track-model), and [identifier](#4811111-text-track-model) based on the semantics of the relevant data, as defined by the relevant specification. If there is no label in that data, then the [label](#4811111-text-track-model) must be set to the empty string.

   If the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) is in a format that supports [media fragment syntax](https://www.w3.org/TR/media-frags/#media-fragment-syntax), then the [identifier](#4811111-text-track-model) must be the same identifier that would enable the track if used as the name of a track in the track dimension of such a [fragment](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment).

3. Associate the [text track list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model) with the [rules for updating the text track rendering](#4811111-text-track-model) appropriate for the format in question.
4. If the new [text track](#4811111-text-track-model)'s [kind](#4811111-text-track-model) is [`chapters`](#4811111-text-track-model) or [`metadata`](#4811111-text-track-model), then set the [text track in-band metadata track dispatch type](#4811111-text-track-model) as follows, based on the type of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements):

   If the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) is an Ogg file

   The [text track in-band metadata track dispatch type](#4811111-text-track-model) must be set to the value of the Name header field. [\[OGGSKELETONHEADERS\]](#references)

   If the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) is a WebM file

   The [text track in-band metadata track dispatch type](#4811111-text-track-model) must be set to the value of the `CodecID` element. [\[WEBMCG\]](#references)

   If the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) is an MPEG-2 file

   Let stream type be the value of the "stream\_type" field describing the text track's type in the file's program map section, interpreted as an 8-bit unsigned integer. Let length be the value of the "ES\_info\_length" field for the track in the same part of the program map section, interpreted as an integer as defined by Generic coding of moving pictures and associated audio information. Let descriptor bytes be the length bytes following the "ES\_info\_length" field. The [text track in-band metadata track dispatch type](#4811111-text-track-model) must be set to the concatenation of the stream type byte and the zero or more descriptor bytes bytes, expressed in hexadecimal using [ASCII upper hex digits](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points). [\[MPEG2\]](#references)

   If the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) is an MPEG-4 file

   Let stsd box be the first `stsd` box of the first `stbl` box of the first `minf` box of the first `mdia` box of the [text track](#4811111-text-track-model)'s `trak` box in the first `moov` box of the file, or null if no such `stsd` box exists. If stsd box is null, or if stsd box has neither a `mett` box nor a `metx` box, then the [text track in-band metadata track dispatch type](#4811111-text-track-model) must be set to the empty string. Otherwise, if stsd box has a `mett` box, then the [text track in-band metadata track dispatch type](#4811111-text-track-model) must be set to either the concatenation of the string "`mett`", a U+0020 SPACE character, and the value of the first `mime_format` field of the first `mett` box of stsd box, or the empty string if that field is absent in that box. Otherwise, if stsd box has no `mett` box but has a `metx` box, then the [text track in-band metadata track dispatch type](#4811111-text-track-model) must be set to either the concatenation of the string "`metx`", a U+0020 SPACE character, and the value of the first `namespace` field of the first `metx` box of stsd box, or the empty string if that field is absent in that box. [\[MPEG4\]](#references)

5. Populate the new [text track](#4811111-text-track-model)'s [list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model) with the cues parsed so far, following the [guidelines for exposing cues](#4811114-guidelines-for-exposing-cues-in-various-formats-as-text-track-cues), and begin updating it dynamically as necessary.
6. Set the new [text track](#4811111-text-track-model)'s [readiness state](#4811111-text-track-model) to [loaded](#4811111-text-track-model).
7. Set the new [text track](#4811111-text-track-model)'s [mode](#4811111-text-track-model) to the mode consistent with the user's preferences and the requirements of the relevant specification for the data.

   > [!note]
   > For instance, if there are no other active subtitles, and this is a forced subtitle track (a subtitle track giving subtitles in the audio track's primary language, but only for audio that is actually in another language), then those subtitles might be activated here.

8. Add the new [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) to the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model).
9. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`addtrack`](#481116-events-summary) at the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`textTracks`](#4811115-text-track-api) attribute's [`TextTrackList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object, using [`TrackEvent`](#481115-the-trackevent-interface), with the [`track`](#481115-the-trackevent-interface) attribute initialized to the [text track](#4811111-text-track-model).

###### 4.8.11.11.3 Sourcing out-of-band text tracks

When a [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element is created, it must be associated with a new [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) (with its value set as defined below).

The [text track kind](#4811111-text-track-model) is determined from the state of the element's [`kind`](#4810-the-track-element) attribute according to the following table; for a state given in a cell of the first column, the [kind](#4811111-text-track-model) is the string given in the second column:

| State | String |
| --- | --- |
| [Subtitles](#4810-the-track-element) | [`subtitles`](#4811111-text-track-model) |
| [Captions](#4810-the-track-element) | [`captions`](#4811111-text-track-model) |
| [Descriptions](#4810-the-track-element) | [`descriptions`](#4811111-text-track-model) |
| [Chapters metadata](#4810-the-track-element) | [`chapters`](#4811111-text-track-model) |
| [Metadata](#4810-the-track-element) | [`metadata`](#4811111-text-track-model) |

The [text track label](#4811111-text-track-model) is the element's [track label](#4810-the-track-element).

The [text track language](#4811111-text-track-model) is the element's [track language](#4810-the-track-element), if any; otherwise the empty string.

The [text track identifier](#4811111-text-track-model) is the element's [`id`](#326-global-attributes) attribute value, if any; otherwise the empty string.

As the [`kind`](#4810-the-track-element), [`label`](#4810-the-track-element), [`srclang`](#4810-the-track-element), and [`id`](#326-global-attributes) attributes are set, changed, or removed, the [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) must update accordingly, as per the definitions above.

> [!note]
> Changes to the [track URL](#4810-the-track-element) are handled in the algorithm below.

The [text track readiness state](#4811111-text-track-model) is initially [not loaded](#4811111-text-track-model), and the [text track mode](#4811111-text-track-model) is initially [disabled](#4811111-text-track-model).

The [text track list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model) is initially empty. It is dynamically modified when the referenced file is parsed. Associated with the list are the [rules for updating the text track rendering](#4811111-text-track-model) appropriate for the format in question; for WebVTT, this is the [rules for updating the display of WebVTT text tracks](https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#rules-for-updating-the-display-of-webvtt-text-tracks). [\[WEBVTT\]](#references)

When a [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element's parent element changes and the new parent is a [media element](#4811-media-elements), then the user agent must add the [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element's corresponding [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) to the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model), and then [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`addtrack`](#481116-events-summary) at the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`textTracks`](#4811115-text-track-api) attribute's [`TextTrackList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object, using [`TrackEvent`](#481115-the-trackevent-interface), with the [`track`](#481115-the-trackevent-interface) attribute initialized to the [text track](#4811111-text-track-model).

When a [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element's parent element changes and the old parent was a [media element](#4811-media-elements), then the user agent must remove the [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element's corresponding [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) from the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model), and then [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`removetrack`](#481116-events-summary) at the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`textTracks`](#4811115-text-track-api) attribute's [`TextTrackList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object, using [`TrackEvent`](#481115-the-trackevent-interface), with the [`track`](#481115-the-trackevent-interface) attribute initialized to the [text track](#4811111-text-track-model).

---

When a [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) corresponding to a [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element is added to a [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model), the user agent must [queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to run the following steps for the [media element](#4811-media-elements):
1. If the element's [blocked-on-parser](#4811111-text-track-model) flag is true, then return.
2. If the element's [did-perform-automatic-track-selection](#4811111-text-track-model) flag is true, then return.
3. [Honor user preferences for automatic text track selection](#4811113-sourcing-out-of-band-text-tracks) for this element.

When the user agent is required to honor user preferences for automatic text track selection for a [media element](#4811-media-elements), the user agent must run the following steps:
1. [Perform automatic text track selection](#4811113-sourcing-out-of-band-text-tracks) for [`subtitles`](#4811111-text-track-model) and [`captions`](#4811111-text-track-model).
2. [Perform automatic text track selection](#4811113-sourcing-out-of-band-text-tracks) for [`descriptions`](#4811111-text-track-model).
3. If there are any [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) in the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) whose [text track kind](#4811111-text-track-model) is [`chapters`](#4811111-text-track-model) or [`metadata`](#4811111-text-track-model) that correspond to [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) elements with a [`default`](#4810-the-track-element) attribute set whose [text track mode](#4811111-text-track-model) is set to [disabled](#4811111-text-track-model), then set the [text track mode](#4811111-text-track-model) of all such tracks to [hidden](#4811111-text-track-model).
4. Set the element's [did-perform-automatic-track-selection](#4811111-text-track-model) flag to true.

When the steps above say to perform automatic text track selection for one or more [text track kinds](#4811111-text-track-model), it means to run the following steps:
1. Let candidates be a list consisting of the [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) in the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) whose [text track kind](#4811111-text-track-model) is one of the kinds that were passed to the algorithm, if any, in the order given in the [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model).
2. If candidates is empty, then return.
3. If any of the [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) in candidates have a [text track mode](#4811111-text-track-model) set to [showing](#4811111-text-track-model), return.
4. If the user has expressed an interest in having a track from candidates enabled based on its [text track kind](#4811111-text-track-model), [text track language](#4811111-text-track-model), and [text track label](#4811111-text-track-model), then set its [text track mode](#4811111-text-track-model) to [showing](#4811111-text-track-model).

   > [!note]
   > For example, the user could have set a browser preference to the effect of "I want French captions whenever possible", or "If there is a subtitle track with 'Commentary' in the title, enable it", or "If there are audio description tracks available, enable one, ideally in Swiss German, but failing that in Standard Swiss German or Standard German".

   Otherwise, if there are any [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) in candidates that correspond to [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) elements with a [`default`](#4810-the-track-element) attribute set whose [text track mode](#4811111-text-track-model) is set to [disabled](#4811111-text-track-model), then set the [text track mode](#4811111-text-track-model) of the first such track to [showing](#4811111-text-track-model).

When a [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) corresponding to a [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element experiences any of the following circumstances, the user agent must [start the `track` processing model](#4811113-sourcing-out-of-band-text-tracks) for that [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) and its [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element:
- The [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element is created.
- The [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) has its [text track mode](#4811111-text-track-model) changed.
- The [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element's parent element changes and the new parent is a [media element](#4811-media-elements).

When a user agent is to start the `track` processing model for a [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) and its [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element, it must run the following algorithm. This algorithm interacts closely with the [event loop](#8171-definitions) mechanism; in particular, it has a [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model) (which is triggered as part of the [event loop](#8171-definitions) algorithm). The steps in that section are marked with ⌛.
1. If another occurrence of this algorithm is already running for this [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) and its [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element, return, letting that other algorithm take care of this element.
2. If the [text track](#4811111-text-track-model)'s [text track mode](#4811111-text-track-model) is not set to one of [hidden](#4811111-text-track-model) or [showing](#4811111-text-track-model), then return.
3. If the [text track](#4811111-text-track-model)'s [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element does not have a [media element](#4811-media-elements) as a parent, return.
4. Run the remainder of these steps [in parallel](#211-parallelism), allowing whatever caused these steps to run to continue.
5. *Top*: [Await a stable state](#8173-processing-model). The [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model) consists of the following steps. (The steps in the [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model) are marked with ⌛.)
6. ⌛ Set the [text track readiness state](#4811111-text-track-model) to [loading](#4811111-text-track-model).
7. ⌛ Let URL be the [track URL](#4810-the-track-element) of the [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element.
8. ⌛ If the [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element's parent is a [media element](#4811-media-elements), then let corsAttributeState be the state of the parent [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`crossorigin`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) content attribute. Otherwise, let corsAttributeState be [No CORS](#254-cors-settings-attributes).
9. End the [synchronous section](#8173-processing-model), continuing the remaining steps [in parallel](#211-parallelism).
10. If URL is not the empty string:
    1. Let request be the result of [creating a potential-CORS request](#251-terminology) given URL, "`track`", and corsAttributeState, and with the *same-origin fallback flag* set.
    2. Set request's [client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client) to the [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant).
    3. Set request's [initiator type](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-initiator-type) to "`track`".
    4. [Fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request.

    The [tasks](#8171-definitions) [queued](#8172-queuing-tasks) by the fetching algorithm on the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) to process the data as it is being fetched must determine the type of the resource. If the type of the resource is not a supported text track format, the load will fail, as described below. Otherwise, the resource's data must be passed to the appropriate parser (e.g., the [WebVTT parser](https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#webvtt-parser)) as it is received, with the [text track list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model) being used for that parser's output. [\[WEBVTT\]](#references)

    > [!note]
    > The appropriate parser will incrementally update the [text track list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model) during these [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) [tasks](#8171-definitions), as each such task is run with whatever data has been received from the network).

    > [!danger]
    > This specification does not currently say whether or how to check the MIME types of text tracks, or whether or how to perform file type sniffing using the actual file data. Implementers differ in their intentions on this matter and it is therefore unclear what the right solution is. In the absence of any requirement here, the HTTP specifications' strict requirement to follow the Content-Type header prevails ("Content-Type specifies the media type of the underlying data." ... "If and only if the media type is not given by a Content-Type field, the recipient MAY attempt to guess the media type via inspection of its content and/or the name extension(s) of the URI used to identify the resource.").

    If fetching fails for any reason (network error, the server returns an error code, CORS fails, etc.), or if URL is the empty string, then [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to first change the [text track readiness state](#4811111-text-track-model) to [failed to load](#4811111-text-track-model) and then [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#481116-events-summary) at the [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element.

    If fetching does not fail, but the type of the resource is not a supported text track format, or the file was not successfully processed (e.g., the format in question is an XML format and the file contained a well-formedness error that XML requires be detected and reported to the application), then the [task](#8171-definitions) that is [queued](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) in which the aforementioned problem is found must change the [text track readiness state](#4811111-text-track-model) to [failed to load](#4811111-text-track-model) and [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#481116-events-summary) at the [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element.

    If fetching does not fail, and the file was successfully processed, then the final [task](#8171-definitions) that is [queued](#8172-queuing-tasks) by the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources), after it has finished parsing the data, must change the [text track readiness state](#4811111-text-track-model) to [loaded](#4811111-text-track-model), and [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`load`](#481116-events-summary) at the [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element.

    If, while fetching is ongoing, either:
    - the [track URL](#4810-the-track-element) changes so that it is no longer equal to URL, while the [text track mode](#4811111-text-track-model) is set to [hidden](#4811111-text-track-model) or [showing](#4811111-text-track-model); or
    - the [text track mode](#4811111-text-track-model) changes to [hidden](#4811111-text-track-model) or [showing](#4811111-text-track-model), while the [track URL](#4810-the-track-element) is not equal to URL,

    ...then the user agent must abort [fetching](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch), discarding any pending [tasks](#8171-definitions) generated by that algorithm (and in particular, not adding any cues to the [text track list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model) after the moment the URL changed), and then [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given the [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element that first changes the [text track readiness state](#4811111-text-track-model) to [failed to load](#4811111-text-track-model) and then [fires an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#481116-events-summary) at the [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element.

11. Wait until the [text track readiness state](#4811111-text-track-model) is no longer set to [loading](#4811111-text-track-model).
12. Wait until the [track URL](#4810-the-track-element) is no longer equal to URL, at the same time as the [text track mode](#4811111-text-track-model) is set to [hidden](#4811111-text-track-model) or [showing](#4811111-text-track-model).
13. Jump to the step labeled *top*.

Whenever a [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element has its [`src`](#4810-the-track-element) attribute set, changed, or removed, the user agent must [immediately](#211-parallelism) empty the element's [text track](#4811111-text-track-model)'s [text track list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model). (This also causes the algorithm above to stop adding cues from the resource being obtained using the previously given URL, if any.)

###### 4.8.11.11.4 Guidelines for exposing cues in various formats as [text track cues](#4811111-text-track-model)

How a specific format's text track cues are to be interpreted for the purposes of processing by an HTML user agent is defined by that format. In the absence of such a specification, this section provides some constraints within which implementations can attempt to consistently expose such formats.

To support the [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) model of HTML, each unit of timed data is converted to a [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model). Where the mapping of the format's features to the aspects of a [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) as defined in this specification are not defined, implementations must ensure that the mapping is consistent with the definitions of the aspects of a [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) as defined above, as well as with the following constraints:

The [text track cue identifier](#4811111-text-track-model)

Should be set to the empty string if the format has no obvious analogue to a per-cue identifier.

The [text track cue pause-on-exit flag](#4811111-text-track-model)

Should be set to false.

###### 4.8.11.11.5 Text track API

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface TextTrackList : EventTarget {
  readonly attribute unsigned long length;
  getter TextTrack (unsigned long index);
  TextTrack? getTrackById(DOMString id);

  attribute EventHandler onchange;
  attribute EventHandler onaddtrack;
  attribute EventHandler onremovetrack;
};
```

`media.textTracks.length`

Returns the number of [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) associated with the [media element](#4811-media-elements) (e.g. from [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) elements). This is the number of [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) in the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model).

`media.textTracks[ n ]`

Returns the nth [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) in the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model).

`textTrack = media.textTracks.getTrackById(id)`

Returns the [`TextTrack`](#4811115-text-track-api) object with the given identifier, or null if no track has that identifier.

A [`TextTrackList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object represents a dynamically updating list of [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) in a given order.

The `textTracks` attribute of [media elements](#4811-media-elements) must return a [`TextTrackList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object representing the [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) in the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model), in the same order as in the [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model).

The `length` attribute of a [`TextTrackList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object must return the number of [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) in the list represented by the [`TextTrackList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object.

The [supported property indices](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-supported-property-indices) of a [`TextTrackList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object at any instant are the numbers from zero to the number of [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) in the list represented by the [`TextTrackList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object minus one, if any. If there are no [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) in the list, there are no [supported property indices](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-supported-property-indices).

To [determine the value of an indexed property](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-determine-the-value-of-an-indexed-property) of a [`TextTrackList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object for a given index index, the user agent must return the indexth [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) in the list represented by the [`TextTrackList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object.

The `getTrackById(id)` method must return the first [`TextTrack`](#4811115-text-track-api) in the [`TextTrackList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object whose [`id`](#4811115-text-track-api) IDL attribute would return a value equal to the value of the id argument. When no tracks match the given argument, the method must return null.

---

```webidl
enum TextTrackMode { "disabled",  "hidden",  "showing" };
enum TextTrackKind { "subtitles",  "captions",  "descriptions",  "chapters",  "metadata" };

[Exposed=Window]
interface TextTrack : EventTarget {
  readonly attribute TextTrackKind kind;
  readonly attribute DOMString label;
  readonly attribute DOMString language;

  readonly attribute DOMString id;
  readonly attribute DOMString inBandMetadataTrackDispatchType;

  attribute TextTrackMode mode;

  readonly attribute TextTrackCueList? cues;
  readonly attribute TextTrackCueList? activeCues;

  undefined addCue(TextTrackCue cue);
  undefined removeCue(TextTrackCue cue);

  attribute EventHandler oncuechange;
};
```

`textTrack = media.addTextTrack(kind [, label [, language ] ])`

Creates and returns a new [`TextTrack`](#4811115-text-track-api) object, which is also added to the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model).

`textTrack.kind`

Returns the [text track kind](#4811111-text-track-model) string.

`textTrack.label`

Returns the [text track label](#4811111-text-track-model), if there is one, or the empty string otherwise (indicating that a custom label probably needs to be generated from the other attributes of the object if the object is exposed to the user).

`textTrack.language`

Returns the [text track language](#4811111-text-track-model) string.

`textTrack.id`

Returns the ID of the given track.

For in-band tracks, this is the ID that can be used with a [fragment](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment) if the format supports [media fragment syntax](https://www.w3.org/TR/media-frags/#media-fragment-syntax), and that can be used with the [`getTrackById()`](#4811115-text-track-api) method.

For [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) corresponding to [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) elements, this is the ID of the [`track`](#4810-the-track-element) element.

`textTrack.inBandMetadataTrackDispatchType`

Returns the [text track in-band metadata track dispatch type](#4811111-text-track-model) string.

`textTrack.mode [ = value ]`

Returns the [text track mode](#4811111-text-track-model), represented by a string from the following list:

"[`disabled`](#4811115-text-track-api)"

The [text track disabled](#4811111-text-track-model) mode.

"[`hidden`](#4811115-text-track-api)"

The [text track hidden](#4811111-text-track-model) mode.

"[`showing`](#4811115-text-track-api)"

The [text track showing](#4811111-text-track-model) mode.

Can be set, to change the mode.

`textTrack.cues`

Returns the [text track list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model), as a [`TextTrackCueList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object.

`textTrack.activeCues`

Returns the [text track cues](#4811111-text-track-model) from the [text track list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model) that are currently active (i.e. that start before the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) and end after it), as a [`TextTrackCueList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object.

`textTrack.addCue(cue)`

Adds the given cue to textTrack's [text track list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model).

`textTrack.removeCue(cue)`

Removes the given cue from textTrack's [text track list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model).

The `addTextTrack(kind, label,
  language)` method of [media elements](#4811-media-elements), when invoked, must run the following steps:
1. Create a new [text track](#4811111-text-track-model), and set its [text track kind](#4811111-text-track-model) to kind, its [text track label](#4811111-text-track-model) to label, its [text track language](#4811111-text-track-model) to language, its [text track readiness state](#4811111-text-track-model) to the [text track loaded](#4811111-text-track-model) state, its [text track mode](#4811111-text-track-model) to the [text track hidden](#4811111-text-track-model) mode, and its [text track list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model) to an empty list.

   Initially, the [text track list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model) is not associated with any [rules for updating the text track rendering](#4811111-text-track-model). When a [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) is added to it, the [text track list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model) has its rules permanently set accordingly.

2. Add the new [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) to the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model).
3. [Queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given the [media element](#4811-media-elements) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`addtrack`](#481116-events-summary) at the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [`textTracks`](#4811115-text-track-api) attribute's [`TextTrackList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object, using [`TrackEvent`](#481115-the-trackevent-interface), with the [`track`](#481115-the-trackevent-interface) attribute initialized to the new [text track](#4811111-text-track-model).
4. Return the new [text track](#4811111-text-track-model).

---

The `kind` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [kind](#4811111-text-track-model).

The `label` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [label](#4811111-text-track-model).

The `language` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [language](#4811111-text-track-model).

The `id` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [identifier](#4811111-text-track-model).

The `inBandMetadataTrackDispatchType` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [in-band metadata track dispatch type](#4811111-text-track-model).

The `mode` getter steps are to return the string switching on [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [mode](#4811111-text-track-model):

The [text track disabled](#4811111-text-track-model) mode

"`disabled`"

The [text track hidden](#4811111-text-track-model) mode

"`hidden`"

The [text track showing](#4811111-text-track-model) mode

"`showing`"

The [`mode`](#4811115-text-track-api) setter steps are to set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [mode](#4811111-text-track-model) to the mode switching on the given value:

"[`disabled`](#4811115-text-track-api)"

The [text track disabled](#4811111-text-track-model) mode.

"[`hidden`](#4811115-text-track-api)"

The [text track hidden](#4811111-text-track-model) mode.

"[`showing`](#4811115-text-track-api)"

The [text track showing](#4811111-text-track-model) mode.

The `cues` getter steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [mode](#4811111-text-track-model) is the [text track disabled](#4811111-text-track-model) mode, then return null.
2. Return a [live](#215-scripting) [`TextTrackCueList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object that represents the subset of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [text track list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model) whose [end times](#4811111-text-track-model) occur at or after the [earliest possible position when the script started](#4811115-text-track-api), in [text track cue order](#4811111-text-track-model).

For each [`TextTrack`](#4811115-text-track-api) object, when an object is returned, the same [`TextTrackCueList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object must be returned each time.

The earliest possible position when the script started is whatever the [earliest possible position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) was the last time the [event loop](#8171-definitions) reached step 1.

The `activeCues` getter steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [mode](#4811111-text-track-model) is the [text track disabled](#4811111-text-track-model) mode, then return null.
2. Return a [live](#215-scripting) [`TextTrackCueList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object that represents the subset of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [text track list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model) whose [active flag was set when the script started](#4811115-text-track-api), in [text track cue order](#4811111-text-track-model).

For each [`TextTrack`](#4811115-text-track-api) object, when an object is returned, the same [`TextTrackCueList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object must be returned each time.

A [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model)'s active flag was set when the script started if its [text track cue active flag](#4811111-text-track-model) was set the last time the [event loop](#8171-definitions) reached [step 1](#8173-processing-model).

---

The `addCue(cue)` method steps are:
1. Let list be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [text track list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model).
2. If list does not yet have any associated [rules for updating the text track rendering](#4811111-text-track-model), then associate list with the [rules for updating the text track rendering](#4811111-text-track-model) appropriate to cue.
3. If list's associated [rules for updating the text track rendering](#4811111-text-track-model) are not the same [rules for updating the text track rendering](#4811111-text-track-model) as appropriate for cue, then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
4. If the given cue is in a [text track list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model), then remove cue from that [text track list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model).
5. Add cue to list.

The `removeCue(cue)` method steps are:
1. If the given cue is not in [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [text track list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model), then throw a ["`NotFoundError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notfounderror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Remove cue from [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [text track list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model).

> [!example]
> In this example, an [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) element is used to play a specific sound-effect from a sound file containing many sound effects. A cue is used to pause the audio, so that it ends exactly at the end of the clip, even if the browser is busy running some script. If the page had relied on script to pause the audio, then the start of the next clip might be heard if the browser was not able to run the script at the exact time specified.
> 
> ```javascript
> var sfx = new Audio('sfx.wav');
> var sounds = sfx.addTextTrack('metadata');
> 
> // add sounds we care about
> function addFX(start, end, name) {
>   var cue = new VTTCue(start, end, '');
>   cue.id = name;
>   cue.pauseOnExit = true;
>   sounds.addCue(cue);
> }
> addFX(12.783, 13.612, 'dog bark');
> addFX(13.612, 15.091, 'kitten mew');
> 
> function playSound(id) {
>   sfx.currentTime = sounds.getCueById(id).startTime;
>   sfx.play();
> }
> 
> // play a bark as soon as we can
> sfx.oncanplaythrough = function () {
>   playSound('dog bark');
> }
> // meow when the user tries to leave,
> // and have the browser ask them to stay
> window.onbeforeunload = function (e) {
>   playSound('kitten mew');
>   e.preventDefault();
> }
> ```

---

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface TextTrackCueList {
  readonly attribute unsigned long length;
  getter TextTrackCue (unsigned long index);
  TextTrackCue? getCueById(DOMString id);
};
```

`cuelist.length`

Returns the number of [cues](#4811111-text-track-model) in the list.

`cuelist[index]`

Returns the [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) with index index in the list. The cues are sorted in [text track cue order](#4811111-text-track-model).

`cuelist.getCueById(id)`

Returns the first [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) (in [text track cue order](#4811111-text-track-model)) with [text track cue identifier](#4811111-text-track-model) id.

Returns null if none of the cues have the given identifier or if the argument is the empty string.

A [`TextTrackCueList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object represents a dynamically updating list of [text track cues](#4811111-text-track-model) in a given order.

The `length` attribute must return the number of [cues](#4811111-text-track-model) in the list represented by the [`TextTrackCueList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object.

The [supported property indices](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-supported-property-indices) of a [`TextTrackCueList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object at any instant are the numbers from zero to the number of [cues](#4811111-text-track-model) in the list represented by the [`TextTrackCueList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object minus one, if any. If there are no [cues](#4811111-text-track-model) in the list, there are no [supported property indices](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-supported-property-indices).

To [determine the value of an indexed property](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-determine-the-value-of-an-indexed-property) for a given index index, the user agent must return the indexth [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) in the list represented by the [`TextTrackCueList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object.

The `getCueById(id)` method, when called with an argument other than the empty string, must return the first [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) in the list represented by the [`TextTrackCueList`](#4811115-text-track-api) object whose [text track cue identifier](#4811111-text-track-model) is id, if any, or null otherwise. If the argument is the empty string, then the method must return null.

---

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface TextTrackCue : EventTarget {
  readonly attribute TextTrack? track;

  attribute DOMString id;
  attribute double startTime;
  attribute unrestricted double endTime;
  attribute boolean pauseOnExit;

  attribute EventHandler onenter;
  attribute EventHandler onexit;
};
```

`cue.track`

Returns the [`TextTrack`](#4811115-text-track-api) object to which this [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) belongs, if any, or null otherwise.

`cue.id [ = value ]`

Returns the [text track cue identifier](#4811111-text-track-model).

Can be set.

`cue.startTime [ = value ]`

Returns the [text track cue start time](#4811111-text-track-model), in seconds.

Can be set.

`cue.endTime [ = value ]`

Returns the [text track cue end time](#4811111-text-track-model), in seconds.

Returns positive Infinity for an [unbounded text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model).

Can be set.

`cue.pauseOnExit [ = value ]`

Returns true if the [text track cue pause-on-exit flag](#4811111-text-track-model) is set, false otherwise.

Can be set.

The `track` getter steps are to return the [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) in whose [list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model) [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) finds itself, if any; or null otherwise.

The `id` attribute, on getting, must return the [text track cue identifier](#4811111-text-track-model) of the [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) that the [`TextTrackCue`](#4811115-text-track-api) object represents. On setting, the [text track cue identifier](#4811111-text-track-model) must be set to the new value.

The `startTime` attribute, on getting, must return the [text track cue start time](#4811111-text-track-model) of the [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) that the [`TextTrackCue`](#4811115-text-track-api) object represents, in seconds. On setting, the [text track cue start time](#4811111-text-track-model) must be set to the new value, interpreted in seconds; then, if the [`TextTrackCue`](#4811115-text-track-api) object's [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) is in a [text track](#4811111-text-track-model)'s [list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model), and that [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) is in a [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model), and the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [show poster flag](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) is not set, then run the *[time marches on](#48118-playing-the-media-resource)* steps for that [media element](#4811-media-elements).

The `endTime` attribute, on getting, must return the [text track cue end time](#4811111-text-track-model) of the [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) that the [`TextTrackCue`](#4811115-text-track-api) object represents, in seconds or positive Infinity. On setting, if the new value is negative Infinity or a Not-a-Number (NaN) value, then throw a [TypeError ](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) exception. Otherwise, the [text track cue end time](#4811111-text-track-model) must be set to the new value. Then, if the [`TextTrackCue`](#4811115-text-track-api) object's [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) is in a [text track](#4811111-text-track-model)'s [list of cues](#4811111-text-track-model), and that [text track](#4811111-text-track-model) is in a [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model), and the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [show poster flag](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) is not set, then run the *[time marches on](#48118-playing-the-media-resource)* steps for that [media element](#4811-media-elements).

The `pauseOnExit` attribute, on getting, must return true if the [text track cue pause-on-exit flag](#4811111-text-track-model) of the [text track cue](#4811111-text-track-model) that the [`TextTrackCue`](#4811115-text-track-api) object represents is set; or false otherwise. On setting, the [text track cue pause-on-exit flag](#4811111-text-track-model) must be set if the new value is true, and must be unset otherwise.

###### 4.8.11.11.6 Event handlers for objects of the text track APIs

The following are the [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers) that (and their corresponding [event handler event types](#8181-event-handlers)) that must be supported, as [event handler IDL attributes](#8181-event-handlers), by all objects implementing the [`TextTrackList`](#4811115-text-track-api) interface:

| [Event handler](#8181-event-handlers) | [Event handler event type](#8181-event-handlers) |
| --- | --- |
| `onchange` | [`change`](#481116-events-summary) |
| `onaddtrack` | [`addtrack`](#481116-events-summary) |
| `onremovetrack` | [`removetrack`](#481116-events-summary) |

The following are the [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers) that (and their corresponding [event handler event types](#8181-event-handlers)) that must be supported, as [event handler IDL attributes](#8181-event-handlers), by all objects implementing the [`TextTrack`](#4811115-text-track-api) interface:

| [Event handler](#8181-event-handlers) | [Event handler event type](#8181-event-handlers) |
| --- | --- |
| `oncuechange` | [`cuechange`](#481116-events-summary) |

The following are the [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers) (and their corresponding [event handler event types](#8181-event-handlers)) that must be supported, as [event handler IDL attributes](#8181-event-handlers), by all objects implementing the [`TextTrackCue`](#4811115-text-track-api) interface:

| [Event handler](#8181-event-handlers) | [Event handler event type](#8181-event-handlers) |
| --- | --- |
| `onenter` | [`enter`](#481116-events-summary) |
| `onexit` | [`exit`](#481116-events-summary) |

###### 4.8.11.11.7 Best practices for metadata text tracks

*This section is non-normative.*

Text tracks can be used for storing data relating to the media data, for interactive or augmented views.

For example, a page showing a sports broadcast could include information about the current score. Suppose a robotics competition was being streamed live. The image could be overlaid with the scores, as follows:

In order to make the score display render correctly whenever the user seeks to an arbitrary point in the video, the metadata text track cues need to be as long as is appropriate for the score. For example, in the frame above, there would be maybe one cue that lasts the length of the match that gives the match number, one cue that lasts until the blue alliance's score changes, and one cue that lasts until the red alliance's score changes. If the video is just a stream of the live event, the time in the bottom right would presumably be automatically derived from the current video time, rather than based on a cue. However, if the video was just the highlights, then that might be given in cues also.

The following shows what fragments of this could look like in a WebVTT file:

```
WEBVTT

...

05:10:00.000 --> 05:12:15.000
matchtype:qual
matchnumber:37

...

05:11:02.251 --> 05:11:17.198
red:78

05:11:03.672 --> 05:11:54.198
blue:66

05:11:17.198 --> 05:11:25.912
red:80

05:11:25.912 --> 05:11:26.522
red:83

05:11:26.522 --> 05:11:26.982
red:86

05:11:26.982 --> 05:11:27.499
red:89

...
```

The key here is to notice that the information is given in cues that span the length of time to which the relevant event applies. If, instead, the scores were given as zero-length (or very brief, nearly zero-length) cues when the score changes, for example saying "red+2" at 05:11:17.198, "red+3" at 05:11:25.912, etc, problems arise: primarily, seeking is much harder to implement, as the script has to walk the entire list of cues to make sure that no notifications have been missed; but also, if the cues are short it's possible the script will never see that they are active unless it listens to them specifically.

When using cues in this manner, authors are encouraged to use the [`cuechange`](#481116-events-summary) event to update the current annotations. (In particular, using the [`timeupdate`](#481116-events-summary) event would be less appropriate as it would require doing work even when the cues haven't changed, and, more importantly, would introduce a higher latency between when the metadata cues become active and when the display is updated, since [`timeupdate`](#481116-events-summary) events are rate-limited.)

##### 4.8.11.12 Identifying a track kind through a URL

Other specifications or formats that need a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) to identify the return values of the [`AudioTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) [`kind`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) or [`VideoTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) [`kind`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects) IDL attributes, or identify the [kind of text track](#4811111-text-track-model), must use the [`about:html-kind`](#241-terminology) [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url).

##### 4.8.11.13 User interface

The `controls` attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes). If present, it indicates that the author has not provided a scripted controller and would like the user agent to provide its own set of controls.

If the attribute is present, or if [scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting) for the [media element](#4811-media-elements), then the user agent should expose a user interface to the user. This user interface should include features to begin playback, pause playback, seek to an arbitrary position in the content (if the content supports arbitrary seeking), change the volume, change the display of closed captions or embedded sign-language tracks, select different audio tracks or turn on audio descriptions, and show the media content in manners more suitable to the user (e.g. fullscreen video or in an independent resizable window).
