Other controls may also be made available.

Even when the attribute is absent, however, user agents may provide controls to affect playback of the media resource (e.g. play, pause, seeking, track selection, and volume controls), but such features should not interfere with the page's normal rendering. For example, such features could be exposed in the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s context menu, platform media keys, or a remote control. The user agent may implement this simply by [exposing a user interface to the user](#481113-user-interface) as described above (as if the [`controls`](#481113-user-interface) attribute was present).

If the user agent [exposes a user interface to the user](#481113-user-interface) by displaying controls over the [media element](#4811-media-elements), then the user agent should suppress any user interaction events while the user agent is interacting with this interface. (For example, if the user clicks on a video's playback control, [`mousedown`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#mousedown) events and so forth would not simultaneously be fired at elements on the page.)

Where possible (specifically, for starting, stopping, pausing, and unpausing playback, for seeking, for changing the rate of playback, for fast-forwarding or rewinding, for listing, enabling, and disabling text tracks, and for muting or changing the volume of the audio), user interface features exposed by the user agent must be implemented in terms of the DOM API described above, so that, e.g., all the same events fire.

Features such as fast-forward or rewind must be implemented by only changing the `playbackRate` attribute (and not the `defaultPlaybackRate` attribute).

Seeking must be implemented in terms of [seeking](#48119-seeking) to the requested position in the [media element](#4811-media-elements)'s [media timeline](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource). For media resources where seeking to an arbitrary position would be slow, user agents are encouraged to use the *approximate-for-speed* flag when seeking in response to the user manipulating an approximate position interface such as a seek bar.

---

`media.volume [ = value ]`

Returns the current playback volume, as a number in the range 0.0 to 1.0, where 0.0 is the quietest and 1.0 the loudest.

Can be set, to change the volume.

Throws an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the new value is not in the range 0.0 .. 1.0.

`media.muted [ = value ]`

Returns true if audio is muted, overriding the [`volume`](#481113-user-interface) attribute, and false if the [`volume`](#481113-user-interface) attribute is being honored.

Can be set, to change whether the audio is muted or not.

A [media element](#4811-media-elements) has a playback volume, which is a fraction in the range 0.0 (silent) to 1.0 (loudest). Initially, the volume should be 1.0, but user agents may remember the last set value across sessions, on a per-site basis or otherwise, so the volume may start at other values.

To set the playback volume of a [media element](#4811-media-elements) element to a number value:
1. If element's [playback volume](#481113-user-interface) equals value, then return.
2. Set element's [playback volume](#481113-user-interface) to value.
3. If element is not [allowed to play](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), then run the [internal pause steps](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) for element.
4. [Queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given element to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`volumechange`](#481116-events-summary) at element.

The `volume` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [playback volume](#481113-user-interface).

The [`volume`](#481113-user-interface) setter steps are:
1. If the given value is not in the range 0.0 to 1.0 inclusive, then throw an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. [Set the playback volume](#481113-user-interface) of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) to the given value.

A [media element](#4811-media-elements) is muted if any of the following are true:
- Its [muted state](#481113-user-interface) is true.
- Its [muted state](#481113-user-interface) is "`default`" and it has a [`muted`](#481113-user-interface) content attribute.
- The [direction of playback](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) is backwards.
- Its [`playbackRate`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) is so low or so high that the user agent cannot play audio usefully.

Each [media element](#4811-media-elements) has a muted state, which is either true, false, or "`default`"; it is initially "`default`". User agents may [set the muted state](#481113-user-interface) of a [media element](#4811-media-elements) to true or false (e.g., remembering the last set value across sessions, on a per-site basis or otherwise).

To set the muted state of a [media element](#4811-media-elements) element to a boolean value:
1. If element's [muted state](#481113-user-interface) equals value, then return.
2. Set element's [muted state](#481113-user-interface) to value.
3. If element is not [allowed to play](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), then run the [internal pause steps](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) for element.
4. [Queue a media element task](#4811-media-elements) given element to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`volumechange`](#481116-events-summary) at element.

The `muted` getter steps are to return true if [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) is [muted](#481113-user-interface); otherwise false.

The [`muted`](#481113-user-interface) setter steps are to [set the muted state](#481113-user-interface) of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) to the given value.

A user agent has an associated volume locked (a boolean). Its value is [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) and determines whether the [playback volume](#481113-user-interface) takes effect.

An element's effective media volume is determined as follows:
1. If the user has indicated that the user agent is to override the volume of the element, then return the volume desired by the user.
2. If the user agent's [volume locked](#481113-user-interface) is true, then return the system volume.
3. If the element is [muted](#481113-user-interface), then return 0.
4. Let volume be the [playback volume](#481113-user-interface) of the audio portions of the [media element](#4811-media-elements), in range 0.0 (silent) to 1.0 (loudest).
5. Return volume, interpreted relative to the range 0.0 to 1.0, with 0.0 being silent, and 1.0 being the loudest setting, values in between increasing in loudness. The range need not be linear. The loudest setting may be lower than the system's loudest possible setting; for example the user could have set a maximum volume.

The `muted` content attribute on [media elements](#4811-media-elements) is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes) that gives the default value for muting.

> [!note]
> This attribute has no further effect once the [`muted`](#481113-user-interface) setter has been invoked or the user indicated a preference.

> [!example]
> This video (an advertisement) autoplays, but to avoid annoying users, it does so without sound, and allows the user to turn the sound on. The user agent can pause the video if it's unmuted without a user interaction.
> 
> ```html
> <video src="adverts.cgi?kind=video" controls autoplay loop muted></video>
> ```

##### 4.8.11.14 Time ranges

Objects implementing the [`TimeRanges`](#481114-time-ranges) interface represent a list of ranges (periods) of time.

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface TimeRanges {
  readonly attribute unsigned long length;
  double start(unsigned long index);
  double end(unsigned long index);
};
```

`media.length`

Returns the number of ranges in the object.

`time = media.start(index)`

Returns the time for the start of the range with the given index.

Throws an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the index is out of range.

`time = media.end(index)`

Returns the time for the end of the range with the given index.

Throws an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the index is out of range.

A [`TimeRanges`](#481114-time-ranges) object has ranges, a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of zero or more [time ranges](#481114-time-ranges).

A time range is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) with the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):
- A start, a number, in seconds.
- An end, a number, in seconds.

The `length` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [ranges](#481114-time-ranges)'s [size](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).

The `start(index)` method steps are:
1. If index is greater than or equal to [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [ranges](#481114-time-ranges)'s [size](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists), then throw an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [ranges](#481114-time-ranges)\[index\]'s [start](#481114-time-ranges).

The `end(index)` method steps are:
1. If index is greater than or equal to [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [ranges](#481114-time-ranges)'s [size](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists), then throw an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [ranges](#481114-time-ranges)\[index\]'s [end](#481114-time-ranges).

A [`TimeRanges`](#481114-time-ranges) object is a normalized `TimeRanges` object if the following are true for each [time range](#481114-time-ranges) in its [ranges](#481114-time-ranges):
- Its [start](#481114-time-ranges) is greater than the [end](#481114-time-ranges) of all earlier [time ranges](#481114-time-ranges).
- Its [start](#481114-time-ranges) is less than or equal to its [end](#481114-time-ranges).

In other words, the [time ranges](#481114-time-ranges) in such an object are ordered, don't overlap, and don't touch (adjacent ones are folded into one bigger [time range](#481114-time-ranges)). A [time range](#481114-time-ranges) can be empty (referencing just a single moment in time), e.g., to indicate that only one frame is currently buffered in the case that the user agent has discarded the entire [media resource](#4811-media-elements) except for the current frame, when a [media element](#4811-media-elements) is paused.

A [time range](#481114-time-ranges)'s [start](#481114-time-ranges) and [end](#481114-time-ranges) are inclusive.

> [!example]
> Thus, the [end](#481114-time-ranges) of a [time range](#481114-time-ranges) would be equal to the [start](#481114-time-ranges) of a following adjacent (touching but not overlapping) [time range](#481114-time-ranges). Similarly, a [time range](#481114-time-ranges) covering a whole timeline anchored at zero would have a [start](#481114-time-ranges) equal to zero and an [end](#481114-time-ranges) equal to the duration of the timeline.

The timelines used by the objects returned by the [`buffered`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource), [`seekable`](#48119-seeking), and [`played`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) IDL attributes of [media elements](#4811-media-elements) must be that element's [media timeline](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource).

##### 4.8.11.15 The [`TrackEvent`](#481115-the-trackevent-interface) interface

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface TrackEvent : Event {
  constructor(DOMString type, optional TrackEventInit eventInitDict = {});

  readonly attribute (VideoTrack or AudioTrack or TextTrack)? track;
};

dictionary TrackEventInit : EventInit {
  (VideoTrack or AudioTrack or TextTrack)? track = null;
};
```

`event.track`

Returns the track object ([`TextTrack`](#4811115-text-track-api), [`AudioTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects), or [`VideoTrack`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects)) to which the event relates.

The `track` attribute must return the value it was initialized to. It represents the context information for the event.

##### 4.8.11.16 Events summary

*This section is non-normative.*

The following events fire on [media elements](#4811-media-elements) as part of the processing model described above:

| Event name | Interface | Fired when... | Preconditions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `loadstart` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | The user agent begins looking for [media data](#4811-media-elements), as part of the [resource selection algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource). | [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) equals [`NETWORK_LOADING`](#48114-network-states) |
| `progress` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | The user agent is fetching [media data](#4811-media-elements). | [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) equals [`NETWORK_LOADING`](#48114-network-states) |
| `suspend` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | The user agent is intentionally not currently fetching [media data](#4811-media-elements). | [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) equals [`NETWORK_IDLE`](#48114-network-states) |
| `abort` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | The user agent stops fetching the [media data](#4811-media-elements) before it is completely downloaded, but not due to an error. | [`error`](#48111-error-codes) is an object with the code [`MEDIA_ERR_ABORTED`](#48111-error-codes). [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) equals either [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#48114-network-states) or [`NETWORK_IDLE`](#48114-network-states), depending on when the download was aborted. |
| `error` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | An error occurs while fetching the [media data](#4811-media-elements) or the type of the resource is not a supported media format. | [`error`](#48111-error-codes) is an object with the code [`MEDIA_ERR_NETWORK`](#48111-error-codes) or higher. [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) equals either [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#48114-network-states) or [`NETWORK_IDLE`](#48114-network-states), depending on when the download was aborted. |
| `emptied` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | A [media element](#4811-media-elements) whose [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) was previously not in the [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#48114-network-states) state has just switched to that state (either because of a fatal error during load that's about to be reported, or because the [`load()`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) method was invoked while the [resource selection algorithm](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) was already running). | [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) is [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#48114-network-states); all the IDL attributes are in their initial states. |
| `stalled` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | The user agent is trying to fetch [media data](#4811-media-elements), but data is unexpectedly not forthcoming. | [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) is [`NETWORK_LOADING`](#48114-network-states). |
| `loadedmetadata` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | The user agent has just determined the duration and dimensions of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) and [the text tracks are ready](#4811111-text-track-model). | [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) is newly equal to [`HAVE_METADATA`](#48117-ready-states) or greater for the first time. |
| `loadeddata` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | The user agent can render the [media data](#4811-media-elements) at the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) for the first time. | [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) newly increased to [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#48117-ready-states) or greater for the first time. |
| `canplay` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | The user agent can resume playback of the [media data](#4811-media-elements), but estimates that if playback were to be started now, the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) could not be rendered at the current playback rate up to its end without having to stop for further buffering of content. | [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) newly increased to [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#48117-ready-states) or greater. |
| `canplaythrough` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | The user agent estimates that if playback were to be started now, the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) could be rendered at the current playback rate all the way to its end without having to stop for further buffering. | [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) is newly equal to [`HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA`](#48117-ready-states). |
| `playing` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | Playback is ready to start after having been paused or delayed due to lack of [media data](#4811-media-elements). | [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) is newly greater than or equal to [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#48117-ready-states) and [`paused`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) is false, or [`paused`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) is newly false and [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) is greater than or equal to [`HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`](#48117-ready-states). Even if this event fires, the element might still not be [potentially playing](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), e.g. if the element is [paused for user interaction](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) or [paused for in-band content](#48118-playing-the-media-resource). |
| `waiting` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | Playback has stopped because the next frame is not available, but the user agent expects that frame to become available in due course. | [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) is less than or equal to [`HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`](#48117-ready-states), and [`paused`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) is false. Either [`seeking`](#48119-seeking) is true, or the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) is not contained in any of the ranges in [`buffered`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource). It is possible for playback to stop for other reasons without [`paused`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) being false, but those reasons do not fire this event (and when those situations resolve, a separate [`playing`](#481116-events-summary) event is not fired either): e.g., [playback has ended](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), or playback [stopped due to errors](#48118-playing-the-media-resource), or the element has [paused for user interaction](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) or [paused for in-band content](#48118-playing-the-media-resource). |
| `seeking` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | The [`seeking`](#48119-seeking) IDL attribute changed to true, and the user agent has started seeking to a new position. |  |
| `seeked` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | The [`seeking`](#48119-seeking) IDL attribute changed to false after the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) was changed. |  |
| `ended` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | Playback has stopped because the end of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) was reached. | [`currentTime`](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) equals the end of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements); [`ended`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) is true. |
| `durationchange` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | The [`duration`](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) attribute has just been updated. |  |
| `timeupdate` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | The [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) changed as part of normal playback or in an especially interesting way, for example discontinuously. |  |
| `play` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | The element is no longer paused. Fired after the [`play()`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) method has returned, or when the [`autoplay`](#48117-ready-states) attribute has caused playback to begin. | [`paused`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) is newly false. |
| `pause` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | The element has been paused. Fired after the [`pause()`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) method has returned. | [`paused`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) is newly true. |
| `ratechange` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | Either the [`defaultPlaybackRate`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) or the [`playbackRate`](#48118-playing-the-media-resource) attribute has just been updated. |  |
| `resize` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | One or both of the [`videoWidth`](#488-the-video-element) and [`videoHeight`](#488-the-video-element) attributes have just been updated. | [Media element](#4811-media-elements) is a [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element; [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) is not [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#48117-ready-states) |
| `volumechange` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | Either the [`volume`](#481113-user-interface) attribute or the [`muted`](#481113-user-interface) attribute has changed. Fired after the relevant attribute's setter has returned. |  |

The following event fires on [`source`](#482-the-source-element) elements:

The following events fire on [`AudioTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects), [`VideoTrackList`](#4811101-audiotracklist-and-videotracklist-objects), and [`TextTrackList`](#4811115-text-track-api) objects:

| `removetrack` | [`TrackEvent`](#481115-the-trackevent-interface) | A track has been removed from the track list. |

##### 4.8.11.17 Security and privacy considerations

The main security and privacy implications of the [`video`](#488-the-video-element) and [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) elements come from the ability to embed media cross-origin. There are two directions that threats can flow: from hostile content to a victim page, and from a hostile page to victim content.

---

If a victim page embeds hostile content, the threat is that the content might contain scripted code that attempts to interact with the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) that embeds the content. To avoid this, user agents must ensure that there is no access from the content to the embedding page. In the case of media content that uses DOM concepts, the embedded content must be treated as if it was in its own unrelated [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables).

> [!example]
> For instance, if an SVG animation was embedded in a [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element, the user agent would not give it access to the DOM of the outer page. From the perspective of scripts in the SVG resource, the SVG file would appear to be in a lone top-level traversable with no parent.

---

If a hostile page embeds victim content, the threat is that the embedding page could obtain information from the content that it would not otherwise have access to. The API does expose some information: the existence of the media, its type, its duration, its size, and the performance characteristics of its host. Such information is already potentially problematic, but in practice the same information can more or less be obtained using the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element, and so it has been deemed acceptable.

However, significantly more sensitive information could be obtained if the user agent further exposes metadata within the content, such as subtitles. That information is therefore only exposed if the video resource uses CORS. The [`crossorigin`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) attribute allows authors to enable CORS. [\[FETCH\]](#references)

> [!example]
> Without this restriction, an attacker could trick a user running within a corporate network into visiting a site that attempts to load a video from a previously leaked location on the corporation's intranet. If such a video included confidential plans for a new product, then being able to read the subtitles would present a serious confidentiality breach.

##### 4.8.11.18 Best practices for authors using media elements

*This section is non-normative.*

Playing audio and video resources on small devices such as set-top boxes or mobile phones is often constrained by limited hardware resources in the device. For example, a device might only support three simultaneous videos. For this reason, it is a good practice to release resources held by [media elements](#4811-media-elements) when they are done playing, either by being very careful about removing all references to the element and allowing it to be garbage collected, or, even better, by setting the element's [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) attribute to an empty string. In cases where [`srcObject`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) was set, instead set the [`srcObject`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) to null.

Similarly, when the playback rate is not exactly 1.0, hardware, software, or format limitations can cause video frames to be dropped and audio to be choppy or muted.

##### 4.8.11.19 Best practices for implementers of media elements

*This section is non-normative.*

How accurately various aspects of the [media element](#4811-media-elements) API are implemented is considered a quality-of-implementation issue.

For example, when implementing the [`buffered`](#48115-loading-the-media-resource) attribute, how precise an implementation reports the ranges that have been buffered depends on how carefully the user agent inspects the data. Since the API reports ranges as times, but the data is obtained in byte streams, a user agent receiving a variable-bitrate stream might only be able to determine precise times by actually decoding all of the data. User agents aren't required to do this, however; they can instead return estimates (e.g. based on the average bitrate seen so far) which get revised as more information becomes available.

As a general rule, user agents are urged to be conservative rather than optimistic. For example, it would be bad to report that everything had been buffered when it had not.

Another quality-of-implementation issue would be playing a video backwards when the codec is designed only for forward playback (e.g. there aren't many key frames, and they are far apart, and the intervening frames only have deltas from the previous frame). User agents could do a poor job, e.g. only showing key frames; however, better implementations would do more work and thus do a better job, e.g. actually decoding parts of the video forwards, storing the complete frames, and then playing the frames backwards.

Similarly, while implementations are allowed to drop buffered data at any time (there is no requirement that a user agent keep all the media data obtained for the lifetime of the media element), it is again a quality of implementation issue: user agents with sufficient resources to keep all the data around are encouraged to do so, as this allows for a better user experience. For example, if the user is watching a live stream, a user agent could allow the user only to view the live video; however, a better user agent would buffer everything and allow the user to seek through the earlier material, pause it, play it forwards and backwards, etc.

---

When a [media element](#4811-media-elements) that is paused is [removed from a document](#214-dom-trees) and not reinserted before the next time the [event loop](#8171-definitions) reaches [step 1](#8173-processing-model), implementations that are resource constrained are encouraged to take that opportunity to release all hardware resources (like video planes, networking resources, and data buffers) used by the [media element](#4811-media-elements). (User agents still have to keep track of the playback position and so forth, though, in case playback is later restarted.)

#### 4.8.12 The `map` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Transparent](#3253-transparent-content-models).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`name`](#4812-the-map-element) — Name of [image map](#48141-authoring) to [reference](#322-elements-in-the-dom) from the [`usemap`](#48141-authoring) attribute

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-map).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-map).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLMapElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString name;
  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection areas;
};
```

The [`map`](#4812-the-map-element) element, in conjunction with an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element and any [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element descendants, defines an [image map](#48141-authoring). The element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) its children.

The `name` attribute gives the map a name so that it can be [referenced](#322-elements-in-the-dom). The attribute must be present and must have a non-empty value with no [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points). The value of the [`name`](#4812-the-map-element) attribute must not be equal to the value of the [`name`](#4812-the-map-element) attribute of another [`map`](#4812-the-map-element) element in the same [tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees). If the [`id`](#326-global-attributes) attribute is also specified, both attributes must have the same value.

`map.areas`

Returns an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) of the [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements in the [`map`](#4812-the-map-element).

The `areas` attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) rooted at the [`map`](#4812-the-map-element) element, whose filter matches only [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements.

> [!example]
> Image maps can be defined in conjunction with other content on the page, to ease maintenance. This example is of a page with an image map at the top of the page and a corresponding set of text links at the bottom.
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <HTML LANG="EN">
> <TITLE>Babies™: Toys</TITLE>
> <HEADER>
>  <H1>Toys</H1>
>  <IMG SRC="/images/menu.gif"
>       ALT="Babies™ navigation menu. Select a department to go to its page."
>       USEMAP="#NAV">
> </HEADER>
>  ...
> <FOOTER>
>  <MAP NAME="NAV">
>   <P>
>    <A HREF="/clothes/">Clothes</A>
>    <AREA ALT="Clothes" COORDS="0,0,100,50" HREF="/clothes/"> |
>    <A HREF="/toys/">Toys</A>
>    <AREA ALT="Toys" COORDS="100,0,200,50" HREF="/toys/"> |
>    <A HREF="/food/">Food</A>
>    <AREA ALT="Food" COORDS="200,0,300,50" HREF="/food/"> |
>    <A HREF="/books/">Books</A>
>    <AREA ALT="Books" COORDS="300,0,400,50" HREF="/books/">
>   </P>
>  </MAP>
> </FOOTER>
> ```

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLAreaElement : HTMLElement {

  // also has obsolete members
};
HTMLAreaElement includes HyperlinkElementUtils;
HTMLAreaElement includes HTMLHyperlinkElementUtils;
```

The [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) either a hyperlink with some text and a corresponding area on an [image map](#48141-authoring), or a dead area on an image map.

An [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element with a parent node must have a [`map`](#4812-the-map-element) element ancestor.

If the [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element has an [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute, then the [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element represents a [hyperlink](#461-introduction). In this case, the `alt` attribute must be present. It specifies the text of the hyperlink. Its value must be text that, when presented with the texts specified for the other hyperlinks of the [image map](#48141-authoring), and with the alternative text of the image, but without the image itself, provides the user with the same kind of choice as the hyperlink would when used without its text but with its shape applied to the image. The [`alt`](#4813-the-area-element) attribute may be left blank if there is another [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element in the same [image map](#48141-authoring) that points to the same resource and has a non-blank [`alt`](#4813-the-area-element) attribute.

If the [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element has no [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute, then the area represented by the element cannot be selected, and the [`alt`](#4813-the-area-element) attribute must be omitted.

In both cases, the [`shape`](#4813-the-area-element) and [`coords`](#4813-the-area-element) attributes specify the area.

The `shape` attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | Conforming | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `circle` |  | [Circle state](#4813-the-area-element) | Designates a circle, using exactly three integers in the [`coords`](#4813-the-area-element) attribute. |
| `circ` | No |
| `default` |  | [Default state](#4813-the-area-element) | This area is the whole image. (The [`coords`](#4813-the-area-element) attribute is not used.) |
| `poly` |  | [Polygon state](#4813-the-area-element) | Designates a polygon, using at-least six integers in the [`coords`](#4813-the-area-element) attribute. |
| `polygon` | No |
| `rect` |  | [Rectangle state](#4813-the-area-element) | Designates a rectangle, using exactly four integers in the [`coords`](#4813-the-area-element) attribute. |
| `rectangle` | No |

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the [rectangle](#4813-the-area-element) state.

The `coords` attribute must, if specified, contain a [valid list of floating-point numbers](#2346-lists-of-floating-point-numbers). This attribute gives the coordinates for the shape described by the [`shape`](#4813-the-area-element) attribute. The processing for this attribute is described as part of the [image map](#48141-authoring) processing model.

In the circle state, [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements must have a [`coords`](#4813-the-area-element) attribute present, with three integers, the last of which must be non-negative. The first integer must be the distance in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) from the left edge of the image to the center of the circle, the second integer must be the distance in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) from the top edge of the image to the center of the circle, and the third integer must be the radius of the circle, again in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px).

In the default state, [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements must not have a [`coords`](#4813-the-area-element) attribute. (The area is the whole image.)

In the polygon state, [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements must have a [`coords`](#4813-the-area-element) attribute with at least six integers, and the number of integers must be even. Each pair of integers must represent a coordinate given as the distances from the left and the top of the image in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) respectively, and all the coordinates together must represent the points of the polygon, in order.

In the rectangle state, [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements must have a [`coords`](#4813-the-area-element) attribute with exactly four integers, the first of which must be less than the third, and the second of which must be less than the fourth. The four points must represent, respectively, the distance from the left edge of the image to the left side of the rectangle, the distance from the top edge to the top side, the distance from the left edge to the right side, and the distance from the top edge to the bottom side, all in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px).

When user agents allow users to [follow hyperlinks](#465-following-hyperlinks) or [download hyperlinks](#466-downloading-resources) created using the [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element, the [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements), [`target`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements), [`download`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements), and [`ping`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attributes decide how the link is followed. The [`rel`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute may be used to indicate to the user the likely nature of the target resource before the user follows the link.

The [`target`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements), [`download`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements), [`ping`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements), [`rel`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements), [`referrerpolicy`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements), [`hreflang`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements), and [`type`](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) attributes must be omitted if the [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute is not present.

If the [`itemprop`](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute is specified on an [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element, then the [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute must also be specified.

The IDL attribute `referrerPolicy` must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`referrerpolicy`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

#### 4.8.14 Image maps

##### 4.8.14.1 Authoring

An image map allows geometric areas on an image to be associated with [hyperlinks](#461-introduction).

An image, in the form of an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element, may be associated with an image map (in the form of a [`map`](#4812-the-map-element) element) by specifying a `usemap` attribute on the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element. The [`usemap`](#48141-authoring) attribute, if specified, must be a [valid hash-name reference](#239-references) to a [`map`](#4812-the-map-element) element.

> [!example]
> Consider an image that looks as follows:
> 
> ![A line with four shapes in it, equally spaced: a red hollow box, a green circle, a blue triangle, and a yellow four-pointed star.](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/sample-usemap.png)
> 
> If we wanted just the colored areas to be clickable, we could do it as follows:
> 
> ```html
> <p>
>  Please select a shape:
>  <img src="shapes.png" usemap="#shapes"
>       alt="Four shapes are available: a red hollow box, a green circle, a blue triangle, and a yellow four-pointed star.">
>  <map name="shapes">
>   <area shape=rect coords="50,50,100,100"> <!-- the hole in the red box -->
>   <area shape=rect coords="25,25,125,125" href="red.html" alt="Red box.">
>   <area shape=circle coords="200,75,50" href="green.html" alt="Green circle.">
>   <area shape=poly coords="325,25,262,125,388,125" href="blue.html" alt="Blue triangle.">
>   <area shape=poly coords="450,25,435,60,400,75,435,90,450,125,465,90,500,75,465,60"
>         href="yellow.html" alt="Yellow star.">
>  </map>
> </p>
> ```

##### 4.8.14.2 Processing model

If an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element has a [`usemap`](#48141-authoring) attribute specified, user agents must process it as follows:
1. Parse the attribute's value using the [rules for parsing a hash-name reference](#239-references) to a [`map`](#4812-the-map-element) element, with the element as the context node. This will return either an element (the map) or null.
2. If that returned null, then return. The image is not associated with an image map after all.
3. Otherwise, the user agent must collect all the [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements that are descendants of the map. Let areas be that list.

Having obtained the list of [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements that form the image map (the areas), interactive user agents must process the list in one of two ways.

If the user agent intends to show the text that the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element represents, then it must use the following steps:
1. Remove all the [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements in areas that have no [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute.
2. Remove all the [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements in areas that have no [`alt`](#4813-the-area-element) attribute, or whose [`alt`](#4813-the-area-element) attribute's value is the empty string, *if* there is another [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element in areas with the same value in the [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute and with a non-empty [`alt`](#4813-the-area-element) attribute.
3. Each remaining [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element in areas represents a [hyperlink](#461-introduction). Those hyperlinks should all be made available to the user in a manner associated with the text of the [`img`](#483-the-img-element).

   In this context, user agents may represent [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) and [`img`](#483-the-img-element) elements with no specified `alt` attributes, or whose `alt` attributes are the empty string or some other non-visible text, in an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) fashion intended to indicate the lack of suitable author-provided text.

If the user agent intends to show the image and allow interaction with the image to select hyperlinks, then the image must be associated with a set of layered shapes, taken from the [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements in areas, in reverse [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) (so the last specified [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element in the map is the bottom-most shape, and the first element in the map, in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), is the top-most shape).

Each [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element in areas must be processed as follows to obtain a shape to layer onto the image:
1. Find the state that the element's [`shape`](#4813-the-area-element) attribute represents.
2. Use the [rules for parsing a list of floating-point numbers](#2346-lists-of-floating-point-numbers) to parse the element's [`coords`](#4813-the-area-element) attribute, if it is present, and let the coords list be the result. If the attribute is absent, let the coords list be the empty list.
3. If the number of items in the coords list is less than the minimum number given for the [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element's current state, as per the following table, then the shape is empty; return.

   | State | Minimum number of items |
   | --- | --- |
   | [Circle state](#4813-the-area-element) | 3 |
   | [Default state](#4813-the-area-element) | 0 |
   | [Polygon state](#4813-the-area-element) | 6 |
   | [Rectangle state](#4813-the-area-element) | 4 |

4. Check for excess items in the coords list as per the entry in the following list corresponding to the [`shape`](#4813-the-area-element) attribute's state:

   [Circle state](#4813-the-area-element)

   Drop any items in the list beyond the third.

   [Default state](#4813-the-area-element)

   Drop all items in the list.

   [Polygon state](#4813-the-area-element)

   Drop the last item if there's an odd number of items.

   [Rectangle state](#4813-the-area-element)

   Drop any items in the list beyond the fourth.

5. If the [`shape`](#4813-the-area-element) attribute represents the [rectangle state](#4813-the-area-element), and the first number in the list is numerically greater than the third number in the list, then swap those two numbers around.
6. If the [`shape`](#4813-the-area-element) attribute represents the [rectangle state](#4813-the-area-element), and the second number in the list is numerically greater than the fourth number in the list, then swap those two numbers around.
7. If the [`shape`](#4813-the-area-element) attribute represents the [circle state](#4813-the-area-element), and the third number in the list is less than or equal to zero, then the shape is empty; return.
8. Now, the shape represented by the element is the one described for the entry in the list below corresponding to the state of the [`shape`](#4813-the-area-element) attribute:

   [Circle state](#4813-the-area-element)

   Let x be the first number in coords, y be the second number, and r be the third number.

   The shape is a circle whose center is x [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) from the left edge of the image and y [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) from the top edge of the image, and whose radius is r [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px).

   [Default state](#4813-the-area-element)

   The shape is a rectangle that exactly covers the entire image.

   [Polygon state](#4813-the-area-element)

   Let xi be the (2i)th entry in coords, and yi be the (2i+1)th entry in coords (the first entry in coords being the one with index 0).

   Let the coordinates be (xi, yi), interpreted in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) measured from the top left of the image, for all integer values of i from 0 to (N/2)-1, where N is the number of items in coords.

   The shape is a polygon whose vertices are given by the coordinates, and whose interior is established using the even-odd rule. [\[GRAPHICS\]](#references)

   [Rectangle state](#4813-the-area-element)

   Let x1 be the first number in coords, y1 be the second number, x2 be the third number, and y2 be the fourth number.

   The shape is a rectangle whose top-left corner is given by the coordinate (x1, y1) and whose bottom right corner is given by the coordinate (x2, y2), those coordinates being interpreted as [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) from the top left corner of the image.

   For historical reasons, the coordinates must be interpreted relative to the *displayed* image after any stretching caused by the CSS ['width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-width-property) and ['height'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-height-property) properties (or, for non-CSS browsers, the image element's `width` and `height` attributes — CSS browsers map those attributes to the aforementioned CSS properties).

   > [!note]
   > Browser zoom features and transforms applied using CSS or SVG do not affect the coordinates.

Pointing device interaction with an image associated with a set of layered shapes per the above algorithm must result in the relevant user interaction events being first fired to the top-most shape covering the point that the pointing device indicated, if any, or to the image element itself, if there is no shape covering that point. User agents may also allow individual [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements representing [hyperlinks](#461-introduction) to be selected and activated (e.g. using a keyboard).

> [!note]
> Because a [`map`](#4812-the-map-element) element (and its [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements) can be associated with multiple [`img`](#483-the-img-element) elements, it is possible for an [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element to correspond to multiple *[focusable areas](#662-data-model)* of the document.

Image maps are [live](#215-scripting); if the DOM is mutated, then the user agent must act as if it had rerun the algorithms for image maps.

#### 4.8.15 MathML

The [MathML `math`](https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#the-top-level-math-element) element falls into the [embedded content](#32526-embedded-content), [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content), [flow content](#32522-flow-content), and [palpable content](#32528-palpable-content) categories for the purposes of the content models in this specification.

When the [MathML `annotation-xml`](https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#dfn-annotation-xml) element contains elements from the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces), such elements must all be [flow content](#32522-flow-content).

When the MathML token elements ([`mi`](https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#the-mi-element), [`mo`](https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#operator-fence-separator-or-accent-mo), [`mn`](https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#number-mn), [`ms`](https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#string-literal-ms), and [`mtext`](https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#text-mtext)) are descendants of HTML elements, they may contain [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) elements from the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces).

User agents must handle text other than [inter-element whitespace](#325-content-models) found in MathML elements whose content models do not allow straight text by pretending for the purposes of MathML content models, layout, and rendering that the text is actually wrapped in a [MathML `mtext`](https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#text-mtext) element. (Such text is not, however, conforming.)

User agents must act as if any MathML element whose contents does not match the element's content model was replaced, for the purposes of MathML layout and rendering, by a [MathML `merror`](https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#error-message-merror) element containing some appropriate error message.

The semantics of MathML elements are defined by MathML and [other applicable specifications](#2110-extensibility). [\[MATHML\]](#references)

> [!example]
> Here is an example of the use of MathML in an HTML document:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE html>
> <html lang="en">
>  <head>
>   <title>The quadratic formula</title>
>  </head>
>  <body>
>   <h1>The quadratic formula</h1>
>   <p>
>    <math>
>     <mi>x</mi>
>     <mo>=</mo>
>     <mfrac>
>      <mrow>
>       <mo form="prefix">−</mo> <mi>b</mi>
>       <mo>±</mo>
>       <msqrt>
>        <msup> <mi>b</mi> <mn>2</mn> </msup>
>        <mo>−</mo>
>        <mn>4</mn> <mo>⁢</mo> <mi>a</mi> <mo>⁢</mo> <mi>c</mi>
>       </msqrt>
>      </mrow>
>      <mrow>
>       <mn>2</mn> <mo>⁢</mo> <mi>a</mi>
>      </mrow>
>     </mfrac>
>    </math>
>   </p>
>  </body>
> </html>
> ```

#### 4.8.16 SVG

The [SVG `svg`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/struct.html#elementdef-svg) element falls into the [embedded content](#32526-embedded-content), [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content), [flow content](#32522-flow-content), and [palpable content](#32528-palpable-content) categories for the purposes of the content models in this specification.

When the [SVG `foreignObject`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/embedded.html#elementdef-foreignObject) element contains elements from the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces), such elements must all be [flow content](#32522-flow-content).

The content model for the [SVG `title`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/struct.html#elementdef-title) element inside [HTML documents](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content). (This further constrains the requirements given in SVG 2.)

The semantics of SVG elements are defined by SVG 2 and [other applicable specifications](#2110-extensibility). [\[SVG\]](#references)

---

`doc = iframe.getSVGDocument()`

`doc = embed.getSVGDocument()`

`doc = object.getSVGDocument()`

Returns the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object, in the case of [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element), [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element), or [`object`](#487-the-object-element) elements being used to embed SVG.

The `getSVGDocument()` method steps are:
1. Let document be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [content document](#7313-child-navigables).
2. If document is non-null and was created by the [page load processing model for XML files](#753-loading-xml-documents) section because the [computed type of the resource](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#computed-mime-type) in the [navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation) algorithm was [`image/svg+xml`](#mime-types), then return document.
3. Return null.

#### 4.8.17 Dimension attributes

**Author requirements**: The `width` and `height` attributes on [`img`](#483-the-img-element), [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element), [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element), [`object`](#487-the-object-element), [`video`](#488-the-video-element), [`source`](#482-the-source-element) when the parent is a [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element and, when their [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Image Button](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) state, [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements may be specified to give the dimensions of the visual content of the element (the width and height respectively, relative to the nominal direction of the output medium), in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px). The attributes, if specified, must have values that are [valid non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers).

The specified dimensions given may differ from the dimensions specified in the resource itself, since the resource may have a resolution that differs from the CSS pixel resolution. (On screens, [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) have a resolution of 96ppi, but in general the CSS pixel resolution depends on the reading distance.) If both attributes are specified, then one of the following statements must be true:
- specified width - 0.5 ≤ specified height \* target ratio ≤ specified width + 0.5
- specified height - 0.5 ≤ specified width / target ratio ≤ specified height + 0.5
- specified height = specified width = 0

The target ratio is the ratio of the [natural width](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-width) to the [natural height](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-height) in the resource. The specified width and specified height are the values of the [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes) and [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes) attributes respectively.

The two attributes must be omitted if the resource in question does not have both a [natural width](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-width) and a [natural height](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-height).

If the two attributes are both 0, it indicates that the element is not intended for the user (e.g. it might be a part of a service to count page views).

> [!note]
> The dimension attributes are not intended to be used to stretch the image.

**User agent requirements**: User agents are expected to use these attributes [as hints for the rendering](#1543-attributes-for-embedded-content-and-images).

> [!note]
> For [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element), [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element) and [`object`](#487-the-object-element) the IDL attributes are [`DOMString`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-DOMString); for [`video`](#488-the-video-element) and [`source`](#482-the-source-element) the IDL attributes are [`unsigned
>   long`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-unsigned-long).

> [!note]
> The corresponding IDL attributes for [`img`](#483-the-img-element) and [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements are defined in those respective elements' sections, as they are slightly more specific to those elements' other behaviors. Both are defined in terms of the algorithm below.

To determine the dimensions of an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) or [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element element given a struct consisting of a width and a height, or null, naturalDimensions:
1. If element is [being rendered](#151-introduction), then return the width and height of element's [content box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#content-box), in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px). [\[CSS\]](#references)
2. Let width and height be 0.
3. If naturalDimensions is not null, then set width to naturalDimensions's width and height to naturalDimensions's height.
4. If element has a [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes) attribute:
   1. Let attributeWidth be the result of [parsing that attribute's value](#2342-non-negative-integers).
   2. If attributeWidth is not an error, then set width to attributeWidth.
5. If element has a [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes) attribute:
   1. Let attributeHeight be the result of [parsing that attribute's value](#2342-non-negative-integers).
   2. If attributeHeight is not an error, then set height to attributeHeight.
6. Return a width of width and a height of height, in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px).

### 4.9 Tabular data

#### 4.9.1 The `table` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [flow content](#32522-flow-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

In this order: optionally a [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element) element, followed by zero or more [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) elements, followed optionally by a [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) element, followed by either zero or more [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) elements or one or more [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) elements, followed optionally by a [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element, optionally intermixed with one or more [script-supporting elements](#32529-script-supporting-elements).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-table).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-table).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLTableElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions] attribute HTMLTableCaptionElement? caption;
  HTMLTableCaptionElement createCaption();
  [CEReactions] undefined deleteCaption();

  [CEReactions] attribute HTMLTableSectionElement? tHead;
  HTMLTableSectionElement createTHead();
  [CEReactions] undefined deleteTHead();

  [CEReactions] attribute HTMLTableSectionElement? tFoot;
  HTMLTableSectionElement createTFoot();
  [CEReactions] undefined deleteTFoot();

  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection tBodies;
  HTMLTableSectionElement createTBody();

  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection rows;
  HTMLTableRowElement insertRow(optional long index = -1);
  [CEReactions] undefined deleteRow(long index);

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) data with more than one dimension, in the form of a [table](#4912-processing-model).

The [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element takes part in the [table model](#4912-processing-model). Tables have rows, columns, and cells given by their descendants. The rows and columns form a grid; a table's cells must completely cover that grid without overlap.

> [!note]
> Precise rules for determining whether this conformance requirement is met are described in the description of the [table model](#4912-processing-model).

Authors are encouraged to provide information describing how to interpret complex tables. Guidance on how to [provide such information](#4911-techniques-for-describing-tables) is given below.

Tables must not be used as layout aids. Historically, some web authors have misused tables in HTML as a way to control their page layout. This usage is non-conforming, because tools attempting to extract tabular data from such documents would obtain very confusing results. In particular, users of accessibility tools like screen readers are likely to find it very difficult to navigate pages with tables used for layout.

> [!note]
> There are a variety of alternatives to using HTML tables for layout, such as CSS grid layout, CSS flexible box layout ("flexbox"), CSS multi-column layout, CSS positioning, and the CSS table model. [\[CSS\]](#references)

---

Tables can be complicated to understand and navigate. To help users with this, user agents should clearly delineate cells in a table from each other, unless the user agent has classified the table as a (non-conforming) layout table.

> [!note]
> Authors and implementers are encouraged to consider using some of the [table design techniques](#4912-techniques-for-table-design) described below to make tables easier to navigate for users.

User agents, especially those that do table analysis on arbitrary content, are encouraged to find heuristics to determine which tables actually contain data and which are merely being used for layout. This specification does not define a precise heuristic, but the following are suggested as possible indicators:

| Feature | Indication |
| --- | --- |
| The use of the [`role`](#219-dependencies) attribute with the value [`presentation`](https://w3c.github.io/aria/#presentation) | Probably a layout table |
| The use of the non-conforming [`border`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute with the non-conforming value 0 | Probably a layout table |
| The use of the non-conforming [`cellspacing`](#162-non-conforming-features) and [`cellpadding`](#162-non-conforming-features) attributes with the value 0 | Probably a layout table |
| The use of [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element), [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element), or [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) elements | Probably a non-layout table |
| The use of the [`headers`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements) and [`scope`](#4910-the-th-element) attributes | Probably a non-layout table |
| The use of the non-conforming [`border`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute with a value other than 0 | Probably a non-layout table |
| Explicit visible borders set using CSS | Probably a non-layout table |
| The use of the [`summary`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute | Not a good indicator (both layout and non-layout tables have historically been given this attribute) |

> [!note]
> It is quite possible that the above suggestions are wrong. Implementers are urged to provide feedback elaborating on their experiences with trying to create a layout table detection heuristic.

If a [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element has a (non-conforming) [`summary`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute, and the user agent has not classified the table as a layout table, the user agent may report the contents of that attribute to the user.

---

`table.caption [ = value ]`

Returns the table's [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element) element.

Can be set, to replace the [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element) element.

`caption = table.createCaption()`

Ensures the table has a [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element) element, and returns it.

`table.deleteCaption()`

Ensures the table does not have a [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element) element.

`table.tHead [ = value ]`

Returns the table's [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) element.

Can be set, to replace the [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) element. If the new value is not a [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) element, throws a ["`HierarchyRequestError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#hierarchyrequesterror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

`thead = table.createTHead()`

Ensures the table has a [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) element, and returns it.

`table.deleteTHead()`

Ensures the table does not have a [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) element.

`table.tFoot [ = value ]`

Returns the table's [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element.

Can be set, to replace the [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element. If the new value is not a [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element, throws a ["`HierarchyRequestError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#hierarchyrequesterror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

`tfoot = table.createTFoot()`

Ensures the table has a [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element, and returns it.

`table.deleteTFoot()`

Ensures the table does not have a [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element.

`table.tBodies`

Returns an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) of the [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) elements of the table.

`tbody = table.createTBody()`

Creates a [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) element, inserts it into the table, and returns it.

`table.rows`

Returns an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) of the [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) elements of the table.

`tr = table.insertRow([ index ])`

Creates a [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element, along with a [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) if required, inserts them into the table at the position given by the argument, and returns the [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element).

The position is relative to the rows in the table. The index −1, which is the default if the argument is omitted, is equivalent to inserting at the end of the table.

If the given position is less than −1 or greater than the number of rows, throws an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

`table.deleteRow(index)`

Removes the [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element with the given position in the table.

The position is relative to the rows in the table. The index −1 is equivalent to deleting the last row of the table.

If the given position is less than −1 or greater than the index of the last row, or if there are no rows, throws an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

To create a table element given a [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element tableElement and a string localName, return the result of [creating an element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) given tableElement's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), localName, and the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces).

The `caption` getter steps are to return the first [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element) element child of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), if any; otherwise null.

The [`caption`](#491-the-table-element) setter steps are:
1. Remove the first [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element) element child of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), if any.
2. If the given value is not null, then insert it as the first node of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).

The `createCaption()` method steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) has a [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element) element child, then return the first such element.
2. Let caption be the result of [creating a table element](#491-the-table-element) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) and "`caption`".
3. Insert caption as the first node of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
4. Return caption.

The `deleteCaption()` method steps are to remove the first [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element) element child of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), if any.

The `tHead` getter steps are to return the first [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) element child of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), if any; otherwise null.

The [`tHead`](#491-the-table-element) setter steps are:
1. If the given value is neither null nor a [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) element, then throw a ["`HierarchyRequestError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#hierarchyrequesterror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Remove the first [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) element child of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), if any.
3. If the given value is not null, then insert it immediately before the first element child of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) that is neither a [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element) element nor a [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element, if any; otherwise insert it at the end of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).

The `createTHead()` method steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) has a [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) element child, then return the first such element.
2. Let thead be the result of [creating a table element](#491-the-table-element) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) and "`thead`".
3. Insert thead immediately before the first element child of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) that is neither a [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element) element nor a [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element, if any; otherwise insert thead at the end of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
4. Return thead.

The `deleteTHead()` method steps are to remove the first [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) element child of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), if any.

The `tFoot` getter steps are to return the first [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element child of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), if any; otherwise null.

The [`tFoot`](#491-the-table-element) setter steps are:
1. If the given value is neither null nor a [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element, then throw a ["`HierarchyRequestError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#hierarchyrequesterror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Remove the first [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element child of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), if any.
3. If the given value is not null, then insert it at the end of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).

The `createTFoot()` method steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) has a [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element child, then return the first such element.
2. Let tfoot be the result of [creating a table element](#491-the-table-element) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) and "`tfoot`".
3. Insert tfoot at the end of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
4. Return tfoot.

The `deleteTFoot()` method steps are to remove the first [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element child of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), if any.

The `tBodies` getter steps are to return an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) rooted at [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), whose filter matches only [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) elements that are children of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).

The `createTBody()` method steps are:
1. Let tbody be the result of [creating a table element](#491-the-table-element) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) and "`tbody`".
2. Insert tbody immediately after the last [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) element child of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), if any; otherwise insert tbody at the end of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
3. Return tbody.

The `rows` getter steps are to return an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) rooted at [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), whose filter matches only [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) elements that are either children of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), or children of [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element), [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element), or [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) elements that are themselves children of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this). The elements in the collection must be ordered such that those elements whose parent is a [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) are included first, in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), followed by those elements whose parent is either [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) or a [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) element, again in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), followed finally by those elements whose parent is a [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element, still in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).

The `insertRow(index)` method steps are:
1. If index is less than −1 or greater than the number of elements in the [`rows`](#491-the-table-element) collection, then throw an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Let tr be the result of [creating a table element](#491-the-table-element) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) and "`tr`".
3. If the [`rows`](#491-the-table-element) collection has zero elements in it, and [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) has no [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) elements in it:
   1. Let tbody be the result of [creating a table element](#491-the-table-element) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) and "`tbody`".
   2. Append tr to tbody.
   3. Append tbody to [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
4. Otherwise, if the [`rows`](#491-the-table-element) collection has zero elements in it, then append tr to the last [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) element in [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
5. Otherwise, if index is −1 or equal to the number of items in the [`rows`](#491-the-table-element) collection, then append tr to the parent of the last [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element in the [`rows`](#491-the-table-element) collection.
6. Otherwise, insert tr immediately before the indexth [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element in the [`rows`](#491-the-table-element) collection, in the same parent.
7. Return tr.

The `deleteRow(index)` method steps are:
1. If index is less than −1 or greater than or equal to the number of elements in the [`rows`](#491-the-table-element) collection, then throw an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. If index is −1, then [remove](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) the last element in the [`rows`](#491-the-table-element) collection from its parent, or do nothing if the [`rows`](#491-the-table-element) collection is empty.
3. Otherwise, [remove](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) the indexth element in the [`rows`](#491-the-table-element) collection from its parent.

> [!example]
> Here is an example of a table being used to mark up a Sudoku puzzle. Observe the lack of headers, which are not necessary in such a table.
> 
> ```html
> <style>
>  #sudoku { border-collapse: collapse; border: solid thick; }
>  #sudoku colgroup, table#sudoku tbody { border: solid medium; }
>  #sudoku td { border: solid thin; height: 1.4em; width: 1.4em; text-align: center; padding: 0; }
> </style>
> <h1>Today's Sudoku</h1>
> <table id="sudoku">
>  <colgroup><col><col><col>
>  <colgroup><col><col><col>
>  <colgroup><col><col><col>
>  <tbody>
>   <tr> <td> 1 <td>   <td> 3 <td> 6 <td>   <td> 4 <td> 7 <td>   <td> 9
>   <tr> <td>   <td> 2 <td>   <td>   <td> 9 <td>   <td>   <td> 1 <td>
>   <tr> <td> 7 <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td> 6
>  <tbody>
>   <tr> <td> 2 <td>   <td> 4 <td>   <td> 3 <td>   <td> 9 <td>   <td> 8
>   <tr> <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>
>   <tr> <td> 5 <td>   <td>   <td> 9 <td>   <td> 7 <td>   <td>   <td> 1
>  <tbody>
>   <tr> <td> 6 <td>   <td>   <td>   <td> 5 <td>   <td>   <td>   <td> 2
>   <tr> <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>   <td> 7 <td>   <td>   <td>   <td>
>   <tr> <td> 9 <td>   <td>   <td> 8 <td>   <td> 2 <td>   <td>   <td> 5
> </table>
> ```

##### 4.9.1.1 Techniques for describing tables

For tables that consist of more than just a grid of cells with headers in the first row and headers in the first column, and for any table in general where the reader might have difficulty understanding the content, authors should include explanatory information introducing the table. This information is useful for all users, but is especially useful for users who cannot see the table, e.g. users of screen readers.

Such explanatory information should introduce the purpose of the table, outline its basic cell structure, highlight any trends or patterns, and generally teach the user how to use the table.

For instance, the following table:

Characteristics with positive and negative sides

| Negative | Characteristic | Positive |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sad | Mood | Happy |
| Failing | Grade | Passing |

...might benefit from a description explaining the way the table is laid out, something like "Characteristics are given in the second column, with the negative side in the left column and the positive side in the right column".

There are a variety of ways to include this information, such as:

In prose, surrounding the table

> [!example]
> ```html
> <p>In the following table, characteristics are given in the second
> column, with the negative side in the left column and the positive
> side in the right column.</p>
> <table>
>  <caption>Characteristics with positive and negative sides</caption>
>  <thead>
>   <tr>
>    <th id="n"> Negative
>    <th> Characteristic
>    <th> Positive
>  <tbody>
>   <tr>
>    <td headers="n r1"> Sad
>    <th id="r1"> Mood
>    <td> Happy
>   <tr>
>    <td headers="n r2"> Failing
>    <th id="r2"> Grade
>    <td> Passing
> </table>
> ```

In the table's [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element)

> [!example]
> ```html
> <table>
>  <caption>
>   <strong>Characteristics with positive and negative sides.</strong>
>   <p>Characteristics are given in the second column, with the
>   negative side in the left column and the positive side in the right
>   column.</p>
>  </caption>
>  <thead>
>   <tr>
>    <th id="n"> Negative
>    <th> Characteristic
>    <th> Positive
>  <tbody>
>   <tr>
>    <td headers="n r1"> Sad
>    <th id="r1"> Mood
>    <td> Happy
>   <tr>
>    <td headers="n r2"> Failing
>    <th id="r2"> Grade
>    <td> Passing
> </table>
> ```

In the table's [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element), in a [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element

> [!example]
> ```html
> <table>
>  <caption>
>   <strong>Characteristics with positive and negative sides.</strong>
>   <details>
>    <summary>Help</summary>
>    <p>Characteristics are given in the second column, with the
>    negative side in the left column and the positive side in the right
>    column.</p>
>   </details>
>  </caption>
>  <thead>
>   <tr>
>    <th id="n"> Negative
>    <th> Characteristic
>    <th> Positive
>  <tbody>
>   <tr>
>    <td headers="n r1"> Sad
>    <th id="r1"> Mood
>    <td> Happy
>   <tr>
>    <td headers="n r2"> Failing
>    <th id="r2"> Grade
>    <td> Passing
> </table>
> ```

Next to the table, in the same [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element)

> [!example]
> ```html
> <figure>
>  <figcaption>Characteristics with positive and negative sides</figcaption>
>  <p>Characteristics are given in the second column, with the
