>  negative side in the left column and the positive side in the right
>  column.</p>
>  <table>
>   <thead>
>    <tr>
>     <th id="n"> Negative
>     <th> Characteristic
>     <th> Positive
>   <tbody>
>    <tr>
>     <td headers="n r1"> Sad
>     <th id="r1"> Mood
>     <td> Happy
>    <tr>
>     <td headers="n r2"> Failing
>     <th id="r2"> Grade
>     <td> Passing
>  </table>
> </figure>
> ```

Next to the table, in a [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element)'s [`figcaption`](#4413-the-figcaption-element)

> [!example]
> ```html
> <figure>
>  <figcaption>
>   <strong>Characteristics with positive and negative sides</strong>
>   <p>Characteristics are given in the second column, with the
>   negative side in the left column and the positive side in the right
>   column.</p>
>  </figcaption>
>  <table>
>   <thead>
>    <tr>
>     <th id="n"> Negative
>     <th> Characteristic
>     <th> Positive
>   <tbody>
>    <tr>
>     <td headers="n r1"> Sad
>     <th id="r1"> Mood
>     <td> Happy
>    <tr>
>     <td headers="n r2"> Failing
>     <th id="r2"> Grade
>     <td> Passing
>  </table>
> </figure>
> ```

Authors may also use other techniques, or combinations of the above techniques, as appropriate.

The best option, of course, rather than writing a description explaining the way the table is laid out, is to adjust the table such that no explanation is needed.

> [!example]
> In the case of the table used in the examples above, a simple rearrangement of the table so that the headers are on the top and left sides removes the need for an explanation as well as removing the need for the use of [`headers`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements) attributes:
> 
> ```html
> <table>
>  <caption>Characteristics with positive and negative sides</caption>
>  <thead>
>   <tr>
>    <th> Characteristic
>    <th> Negative
>    <th> Positive
>  <tbody>
>   <tr>
>    <th> Mood
>    <td> Sad
>    <td> Happy
>   <tr>
>    <th> Grade
>    <td> Failing
>    <td> Passing
> </table>
> ```

##### 4.9.1.2 Techniques for table design

Good table design is key to making tables more readable and usable.

In visual media, providing column and row borders and alternating row backgrounds can be very effective to make complicated tables more readable.

For tables with large volumes of numeric content, using monospaced fonts can help users see patterns, especially in situations where a user agent does not render the borders. (Unfortunately, for historical reasons, not rendering borders on tables is a common default.)

In speech media, table cells can be distinguished by reporting the corresponding headers before reading the cell's contents, and by allowing users to navigate the table in a grid fashion, rather than serializing the entire contents of the table in source order.

Authors are encouraged to use CSS to achieve these effects.

User agents are encouraged to render tables using these techniques whenever the page does not use CSS and the table is not classified as a layout table.

#### 4.9.2 The `caption` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

As the first element child of a [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content), but with no descendant [`table`](#491-the-table-element) elements.

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

A [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) can be omitted if the [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element) element is not immediately followed by [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) or a [comment](#1316-comments).

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-caption).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-caption).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLTableCaptionElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the title of the [`table`](#491-the-table-element) that is its parent, if it has a parent and that is a [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element.

The [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element) element takes part in the [table model](#4912-processing-model).

When a [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element is the only content in a [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element) element other than the [`figcaption`](#4413-the-figcaption-element), the [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element) element should be omitted in favor of the [`figcaption`](#4413-the-figcaption-element).

A caption can introduce context for a table, making it significantly easier to understand.

> [!example]
> Consider, for instance, the following table:
> 
> |  | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
> | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 |
> | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 |
> | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 |
> | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 | 11 |
> | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 | 11 | 12 |
> 
> In the abstract, this table is not clear. However, with a caption giving the table's number (for [reference](#322-elements-in-the-dom) in the main prose) and explaining its use, it makes more sense:
> 
> ```html
> <caption>
> <p>Table 1.
> <p>This table shows the total score obtained from rolling two
> six-sided dice. The first row represents the value of the first die,
> the first column the value of the second die. The total is given in
> the cell that corresponds to the values of the two dice.
> </caption>
> ```
> 
> This provides the user with more context:
> 
> Table 1.
> 
> This table shows the total score obtained from rolling two six-sided dice. The first row represents the value of the first die, the first column the value of the second die. The total is given in the cell that corresponds to the values of the two dice.
> 
> |  | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
> | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 |
> | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 |
> | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 |
> | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 | 11 |
> | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 | 11 | 12 |

#### 4.9.3 The `colgroup` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

As a child of a [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element, after any [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element) elements and before any [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element), [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element), [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element), and [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) elements.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

If the [`span`](#493-the-colgroup-element) attribute is present: [Nothing](#3251-the-nothing-content-model).

If the [`span`](#493-the-colgroup-element) attribute is absent: Zero or more [`col`](#494-the-col-element) and [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) elements.

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

A [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element's [start tag](#13121-start-tags) can be omitted if the first thing inside the [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element is a [`col`](#494-the-col-element) element, and if the element is not immediately preceded by another [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element whose [end tag](#13122-end-tags) has been omitted. (It can't be omitted if the element is empty.)

A [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) can be omitted if the [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element is not immediately followed by [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) or a [comment](#1316-comments).

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`span`](#493-the-colgroup-element) — Number of columns spanned by the element

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-colgroup).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-colgroup).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants) with attributes [`span`](#493-the-colgroup-element).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLTableColElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect, ReflectDefault=1, ReflectRange=(1, 1000)] attribute unsigned long span;

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a [group](#4912-processing-model) of one or more [columns](#4912-processing-model) in the [`table`](#491-the-table-element) that is its parent, if it has a parent and that is a [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element.

If the [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element contains no [`col`](#494-the-col-element) elements, then the element may have a `span` content attribute specified, whose value must be a [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers) greater than zero and less than or equal to 1000.

The [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element and its [`span`](#493-the-colgroup-element) attribute take part in the [table model](#4912-processing-model).

#### 4.9.4 The `col` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

As a child of a [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element that doesn't have a [`span`](#494-the-col-element) attribute.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Nothing](#3251-the-nothing-content-model).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

No [end tag](#13122-end-tags).

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`span`](#494-the-col-element) — Number of columns spanned by the element

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-col).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-col).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants) with attributes [`span`](#494-the-col-element).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

Uses [`HTMLTableColElement`](#493-the-colgroup-element), as defined for [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) elements.

If a [`col`](#494-the-col-element) element has a parent and that is a [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element that itself has a parent that is a [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element, then the [`col`](#494-the-col-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) one or more [columns](#4912-processing-model) in the [column group](#4912-processing-model) represented by that [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element).

The element may have a `span` content attribute specified, whose value must be a [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers) greater than zero and less than or equal to 1000.

The [`col`](#494-the-col-element) element and its [`span`](#494-the-col-element) attribute take part in the [table model](#4912-processing-model).

#### 4.9.5 The `tbody` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

As a child of a [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element, after any [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element), [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element), and [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) elements, but only if there are no [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) elements that are children of the [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

Zero or more [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) and [script-supporting](#32529-script-supporting-elements) elements.

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

A [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) element's [start tag](#13121-start-tags) can be omitted if the first thing inside the [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) element is a [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element, and if the element is not immediately preceded by a [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element), [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element), or [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element whose [end tag](#13122-end-tags) has been omitted. (It can't be omitted if the element is empty.)

A [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) can be omitted if the [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) element is immediately followed by a [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) or [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-tbody).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-tbody).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLTableSectionElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection rows;
  HTMLTableRowElement insertRow(optional long index = -1);
  [CEReactions] undefined deleteRow(long index);

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`HTMLTableSectionElement`](#495-the-tbody-element) interface is also used for [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) and [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) elements.

The [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a [block](#4912-processing-model) of [rows](#4912-processing-model) that consist of a body of data for the parent [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element, if the [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) element has a parent and it is a [`table`](#491-the-table-element).

The [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) element takes part in the [table model](#4912-processing-model).

`tbody.rows`

Returns an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) of the [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) elements of the table section.

`tr = tbody.insertRow([ index ])`

Creates a [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element, inserts it into the table section at the position given by the argument, and returns the [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element).

The position is relative to the rows in the table section. The index −1, which is the default if the argument is omitted, is equivalent to inserting at the end of the table section.

If the given position is less than −1 or greater than the number of rows, throws an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

`tbody.deleteRow(index)`

Removes the [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element with the given position in the table section.

The position is relative to the rows in the table section. The index −1 is equivalent to deleting the last row of the table section.

If the given position is less than −1 or greater than the index of the last row, or if there are no rows, throws an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

The `rows` attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) rooted at this element, whose filter matches only [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) elements that are children of this element.

The `insertRow(index)` method must act as follows:
1. If index is less than −1 or greater than the number of elements in the [`rows`](#495-the-tbody-element) collection, throw an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Let table row be the result of [creating an element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) given this element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), "`tr`", and the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces).
3. If index is −1 or equal to the number of items in the [`rows`](#495-the-tbody-element) collection, then [append](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) table row to this element.
4. Otherwise, [insert](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) table row as a child of this element, immediately before the indexth [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element in the [`rows`](#495-the-tbody-element) collection.
5. Return table row.

The `deleteRow(index)` method must, when invoked, act as follows:
1. If index is less than −1 or greater than or equal to the number of elements in the [`rows`](#495-the-tbody-element) collection, then throw an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. If index is −1, then [remove](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) the last element in the [`rows`](#495-the-tbody-element) collection from this element, or do nothing if the [`rows`](#495-the-tbody-element) collection is empty.
3. Otherwise, [remove](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) the indexth element in the [`rows`](#495-the-tbody-element) collection from this element.

#### 4.9.6 The `thead` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

As a child of a [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element, after any [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element), and [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) elements and before any [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element), [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element), and [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) elements, but only if there are no other [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) elements that are children of the [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

Zero or more [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) and [script-supporting](#32529-script-supporting-elements) elements.

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

A [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) can be omitted if the [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) element is immediately followed by a [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) or [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-thead).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-thead).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

Uses [`HTMLTableSectionElement`](#495-the-tbody-element), as defined for [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) elements.

The [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the [block](#4912-processing-model) of [rows](#4912-processing-model) that consist of the column labels (headers) and any ancillary non-header cells for the parent [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element, if the [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) element has a parent and it is a [`table`](#491-the-table-element).

The [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) element takes part in the [table model](#4912-processing-model).

> [!example]
> This example shows a [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) element being used. Notice the use of both [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) and [`td`](#499-the-td-element) elements in the [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) element: the first row is the headers, and the second row is an explanation of how to fill in the table.
> 
> ```html
> <table>
>  <caption> School auction sign-up sheet </caption>
>  <thead>
>   <tr>
>    <th><label for=e1>Name</label>
>    <th><label for=e2>Product</label>
>    <th><label for=e3>Picture</label>
>    <th><label for=e4>Price</label>
>   <tr>
>    <td>Your name here
>    <td>What are you selling?
>    <td>Link to a picture
>    <td>Your reserve price
>  <tbody>
>   <tr>
>    <td>Ms Danus
>    <td>Doughnuts
>    <td><img src="https://example.com/mydoughnuts.png" title="Doughnuts from Ms Danus">
>    <td>$45
>   <tr>
>    <td><input id=e1 type=text name=who required form=f>
>    <td><input id=e2 type=text name=what required form=f>
>    <td><input id=e3 type=url name=pic form=f>
>    <td><input id=e4 type=number step=0.01 min=0 value=0 required form=f>
> </table>
> <form id=f action="/auction.cgi">
>  <input type=button name=add value="Submit">
> </form>
> ```

#### 4.9.7 The `tfoot` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

As a child of a [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element, after any [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element), [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element), [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element), [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element), and [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) elements, but only if there are no other [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) elements that are children of the [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

Zero or more [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) and [script-supporting](#32529-script-supporting-elements) elements.

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

A [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) can be omitted if there is no more content in the parent element.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-tfoot).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-tfoot).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

Uses [`HTMLTableSectionElement`](#495-the-tbody-element), as defined for [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) elements.

The [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the [block](#4912-processing-model) of [rows](#4912-processing-model) that consist of the column summaries (footers) for the parent [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element, if the [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element has a parent and it is a [`table`](#491-the-table-element).

The [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element takes part in the [table model](#4912-processing-model).

#### 4.9.8 The `tr` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

As a child of a [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) element.

As a child of a [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) element.

As a child of a [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element.

As a child of a [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element, after any [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element), [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element), and [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) elements, but only if there are no [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) elements that are children of the [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

Zero or more [`td`](#499-the-td-element), [`th`](#4910-the-th-element), and [script-supporting](#32529-script-supporting-elements) elements.

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

A [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) can be omitted if the [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element is immediately followed by another [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-tr).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-tr).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLTableRowElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  readonly attribute long rowIndex;
  readonly attribute long sectionRowIndex;
  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection cells;
  HTMLTableCellElement insertCell(optional long index = -1);
  [CEReactions] undefined deleteCell(long index);

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a [row](#4912-processing-model) of [cells](#4912-processing-model) in a [table](#4912-processing-model).

The [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element takes part in the [table model](#4912-processing-model).

`tr.rowIndex`

Returns the position of the row in the table's [`rows`](#491-the-table-element) list.

Returns −1 if the element isn't in a table.

`tr.sectionRowIndex`

Returns the position of the row in the table section's [`rows`](#495-the-tbody-element) list.

Returns −1 if the element isn't in a table section.

`tr.cells`

Returns an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) of the [`td`](#499-the-td-element) and [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) elements of the row.

`cell = tr.insertCell([ index ])`

Creates a [`td`](#499-the-td-element) element, inserts it into the table row at the position given by the argument, and returns the [`td`](#499-the-td-element).

The position is relative to the cells in the row. The index −1, which is the default if the argument is omitted, is equivalent to inserting at the end of the row.

If the given position is less than −1 or greater than the number of cells, throws an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

`tr.deleteCell(index)`

Removes the [`td`](#499-the-td-element) or [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element with the given position in the row.

The position is relative to the cells in the row. The index −1 is equivalent to deleting the last cell of the row.

If the given position is less than −1 or greater than the index of the last cell, or if there are no cells, throws an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

The `rowIndex` attribute must, if this element has a parent [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element, or a parent [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element), [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element), or [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element and a *grandparent* [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element, return the index of this [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element in that [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element's [`rows`](#491-the-table-element) collection. If there is no such [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element, then the attribute must return −1.

The `sectionRowIndex` attribute must, if this element has a parent [`table`](#491-the-table-element), [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element), [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element), or [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element, return the index of the [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element in the parent element's `rows` collection (for tables, that's [`HTMLTableElement`](#491-the-table-element)'s [`rows`](#491-the-table-element) collection; for table sections, that's [`HTMLTableSectionElement`](#495-the-tbody-element)'s [`rows`](#495-the-tbody-element) collection). If there is no such parent element, then the attribute must return −1.

The `cells` attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) rooted at this [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element, whose filter matches only [`td`](#499-the-td-element) and [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) elements that are children of the [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element.

The `insertCell(index)` method must act as follows:
1. If index is less than −1 or greater than the number of elements in the [`cells`](#498-the-tr-element) collection, then throw an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Let table cell be the result of [creating an element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) given this [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), "`td`", and the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces).
3. If index is equal to −1 or equal to the number of items in [`cells`](#498-the-tr-element) collection, then [append](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) table cell to this [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element.
4. Otherwise, [insert](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) table cell as a child of this [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element, immediately before the indexth [`td`](#499-the-td-element) or [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element in the [`cells`](#498-the-tr-element) collection.
5. Return table cell.

The `deleteCell(index)` method must act as follows:
1. If index is less than −1 or greater than or equal to the number of elements in the [`cells`](#498-the-tr-element) collection, then throw an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. If index is −1, then [remove](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) the last element in the [`cells`](#498-the-tr-element) collection from its parent, or do nothing if the [`cells`](#498-the-tr-element) collection is empty.
3. Otherwise, [remove](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) the indexth element in the [`cells`](#498-the-tr-element) collection from its parent.

#### 4.9.9 The `td` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

As a child of a [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

A [`td`](#499-the-td-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) can be omitted if the [`td`](#499-the-td-element) element is immediately followed by a [`td`](#499-the-td-element) or [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`colspan`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements) — Number of columns that the cell is to span

[`rowspan`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements) — Number of rows that the cell is to span

[`headers`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements) — The header cells for this cell

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-td).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-td).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants) with attributes [`colspan`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements), [`headers`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements), [`rowspan`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLTableCellElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect, ReflectDefault=1, ReflectRange=(1, 1000)] attribute unsigned long colSpan;
  [CEReactions, Reflect, ReflectDefault=1, ReflectRange=(0, 65534)] attribute unsigned long rowSpan;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString headers;
  readonly attribute long cellIndex;

  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString scope; // only conforming for th elements
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString abbr;  // only conforming for th elements

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`HTMLTableCellElement`](#499-the-td-element) interface is also used for [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) elements.

The [`td`](#499-the-td-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a data [cell](#4912-processing-model) in a table.

The [`td`](#499-the-td-element) element and its [`colspan`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements), [`rowspan`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements), and [`headers`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements) attributes take part in the [table model](#4912-processing-model).

User agents, especially in non-visual environments or where displaying the table as a 2D grid is impractical, may give the user context for the cell when rendering the contents of a cell; for instance, giving its position in the [table model](#4912-processing-model), or listing the cell's header cells (as determined by the [algorithm for assigning header cells](#49122-forming-relationships-between-data-cells-and-header-cells)). When a cell's header cells are being listed, user agents may use the value of [`abbr`](#4910-the-th-element) attributes on those header cells, if any, instead of the contents of the header cells themselves.

> [!example]
> In this example, we see a snippet of a web application consisting of a grid of editable cells (essentially a simple spreadsheet). One of the cells has been configured to show the sum of the cells above it. Three have been marked as headings, which use [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) elements instead of [`td`](#499-the-td-element) elements. A script would attach event handlers to these elements to maintain the total.
> 
> ```html
> <table>
>  <tr>
>   <th><input value="Name">
>   <th><input value="Paid ($)">
>  <tr>
>   <td><input value="Jeff">
>   <td><input value="14">
>  <tr>
>   <td><input value="Britta">
>   <td><input value="9">
>  <tr>
>   <td><input value="Abed">
>   <td><input value="25">
>  <tr>
>   <td><input value="Shirley">
>   <td><input value="2">
>  <tr>
>   <td><input value="Annie">
>   <td><input value="5">
>  <tr>
>   <td><input value="Troy">
>   <td><input value="5">
>  <tr>
>   <td><input value="Pierce">
>   <td><input value="1000">
>  <tr>
>   <th><input value="Total">
>   <td><output value="1060">
> </table>
> ```

#### 4.9.10 The `th` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

As a child of a [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content), but with no [`header`](#438-the-header-element), [`footer`](#439-the-footer-element), [sectioning content](#32523-sectioning-content), or [heading content](#32524-heading-content) descendants.

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

A [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) can be omitted if the [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element is immediately followed by a [`td`](#499-the-td-element) or [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`colspan`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements) — Number of columns that the cell is to span

[`rowspan`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements) — Number of rows that the cell is to span

[`headers`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements) — The header cells for this cell

[`scope`](#4910-the-th-element) — Specifies which cells the header cell applies to

[`abbr`](#4910-the-th-element) — Alternative label to use for the header cell when referencing the cell in other contexts

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-th).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-th).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Default](#865-sanitization-constants) with attributes [`abbr`](#4910-the-th-element), [`colspan`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements), [`headers`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements), [`rowspan`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements), [`scope`](#4910-the-th-element).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

Uses [`HTMLTableCellElement`](#499-the-td-element), as defined for [`td`](#499-the-td-element) elements.

The [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a header [cell](#4912-processing-model) in a table.

The [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element may have a `scope` content attribute specified.

The [`scope`](#4910-the-th-element) attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `row` | Row | The header cell applies to some of the subsequent cells in the same row(s). |
| `col` | Column | The header cell applies to some of the subsequent cells in the same column(s). |
| `rowgroup` | Row Group | The header cell applies to all the remaining cells in the row group. |
| `colgroup` | Column Group | The header cell applies to all the remaining cells in the column group. |

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the Auto state. (In this state the header cell applies to a set of cells selected based on context.)

A [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element's [`scope`](#4910-the-th-element) attribute must not be in the [Row Group](#4910-the-th-element) state if the element is not anchored in a [row group](#4912-processing-model), nor in the [Column Group](#4910-the-th-element) state if the element is not anchored in a [column group](#4912-processing-model).

The [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element may have an `abbr` content attribute specified. Its value must be an alternative label for the header cell, to be used when referencing the cell in other contexts (e.g. when describing the header cells that apply to a data cell). It is typically an abbreviated form of the full header cell, but can also be an expansion, or merely a different phrasing.

The [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element and its [`colspan`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements), [`rowspan`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements), [`headers`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements), and [`scope`](#4910-the-th-element) attributes take part in the [table model](#4912-processing-model).

> [!example]
> The following example shows how the [`scope`](#4910-the-th-element) attribute's [`rowgroup`](#4910-the-th-element) value affects which data cells a header cell applies to.
> 
> Here is a markup fragment showing a table:
> 
> ```html
> <table>
>  <thead>
>   <tr> <th> ID <th> Measurement <th> Average <th> Maximum
>  <tbody>
>   <tr> <td> <th scope=rowgroup> Cats <td> <td>
>   <tr> <td> 93 <th> Legs <td> 3.5 <td> 4
>   <tr> <td> 10 <th> Tails <td> 1 <td> 1
>  <tbody>
>   <tr> <td> <th scope=rowgroup> English speakers <td> <td>
>   <tr> <td> 32 <th> Legs <td> 2.67 <td> 4
>   <tr> <td> 35 <th> Tails <td> 0.33 <td> 1
> </table>
> ```
> 
> This would result in the following table:
> 
> | ID | Measurement | Average | Maximum |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> |  | Cats |  |  |
> | 93 | Legs | 3.5 | 4 |
> | 10 | Tails | 1 | 1 |
> |  | English speakers |  |  |
> | 32 | Legs | 2.67 | 4 |
> | 35 | Tails | 0.33 | 1 |
> 
> The headers in the first row all apply directly down to the rows in their column.
> 
> The headers with a [`scope`](#4910-the-th-element) attribute in the [Row Group](#4910-the-th-element) state apply to all the cells in their row group other than the cells in the first column.
> 
> The remaining headers apply just to the cells to the right of them.
> 
> ![](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/table-scope-diagram.png)

#### 4.9.11 Attributes common to [`td`](#499-the-td-element) and [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) elements

The [`td`](#499-the-td-element) and [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) elements may have a `colspan` content attribute specified, whose value must be a [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers) greater than zero and less than or equal to 1000.

The [`td`](#499-the-td-element) and [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) elements may also have a `rowspan` content attribute specified, whose value must be a [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers) less than or equal to 65534. For this attribute, the value zero means that the cell is to span all the remaining rows in the row group.

These attributes give the number of columns and rows respectively that the cell is to span. These attributes must not be used to overlap cells, as described in the description of the [table model](#4912-processing-model).

---

The [`td`](#499-the-td-element) and [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element may have a `headers` content attribute specified. The [`headers`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements) attribute, if specified, must contain a string consisting of an [unordered set of unique space-separated tokens](#237-space-separated-tokens), none of which are [identical to](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) another token and each of which must have the value of an [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) of a [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element taking part in the same [table](#4912-processing-model) as the [`td`](#499-the-td-element) or [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element (as defined by the [table model](#4912-processing-model)).

A [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element with [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) id is said to be *directly targeted* by all [`td`](#499-the-td-element) and [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) elements in the same [table](#4912-processing-model) that have [`headers`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements) attributes whose values include as one of their tokens the [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) id. A [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element A is said to be *targeted* by a [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) or [`td`](#499-the-td-element) element B if either A is *directly targeted* by B or if there exists an element C that is itself *targeted* by the element B and A is *directly targeted* by C.

A [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element must not be *targeted* by itself.

The [`colspan`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements), [`rowspan`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements), and [`headers`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements) attributes take part in the [table model](#4912-processing-model).

---

`cell.cellIndex`

Returns the position of the cell in the row's [`cells`](#498-the-tr-element) list. This does not necessarily correspond to the x-position of the cell in the table, since earlier cells might cover multiple rows or columns.

Returns −1 if the element isn't in a row.

The `cellIndex` IDL attribute must, if the element has a parent [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element, return the index of the cell's element in the parent element's [`cells`](#498-the-tr-element) collection. If there is no such parent element, then the attribute must return −1.

The `scope` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the content attribute of the same name, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

#### 4.9.12 Processing model

The various table elements and their content attributes together define the table model.

A table consists of cells aligned on a two-dimensional grid of slots with coordinates (x, y). The grid is finite, and is either empty or has one or more slots. If the grid has one or more slots, then the x coordinates are always in the range 0 ≤ x < xwidth, and the y coordinates are always in the range 0 ≤ y < yheight. If one or both of xwidth and yheight are zero, then the table is empty (has no slots). Tables correspond to [`table`](#491-the-table-element) elements.

A cell is a set of slots anchored at a slot (cellx, celly), and with a particular width and height such that the cell covers all the slots with coordinates (x, y) where cellx ≤ x < cellx+width and celly ≤ y < celly+height. Cells can either be *data cells* or *header cells*. Data cells correspond to [`td`](#499-the-td-element) elements, and header cells correspond to [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) elements. Cells of both types can have zero or more associated header cells.

It is possible, in certain error cases, for two cells to occupy the same slot.

A row is a complete set of slots from x=0 to x=xwidth-1, for a particular value of y. Rows usually correspond to [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) elements, though a [row group](#4912-processing-model) can have some implied [rows](#4912-processing-model) at the end in some cases involving [cells](#4912-processing-model) spanning multiple rows.

A column is a complete set of slots from y=0 to y=yheight-1, for a particular value of x. Columns can correspond to [`col`](#494-the-col-element) elements. In the absence of [`col`](#494-the-col-element) elements, columns are implied.

A row group is a set of [rows](#4912-processing-model) anchored at a slot (0, groupy) with a particular height such that the row group covers all the slots with coordinates (x, y) where 0 ≤ x < xwidth and groupy ≤ y < groupy+height. Row groups correspond to [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element), [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element), and [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) elements. Not every row is necessarily in a row group.

A column group is a set of [columns](#4912-processing-model) anchored at a slot (groupx, 0) with a particular width such that the column group covers all the slots with coordinates (x, y) where groupx ≤ x < groupx+width and 0 ≤ y < yheight. Column groups correspond to [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) elements. Not every column is necessarily in a column group.

[Row groups](#4912-processing-model) cannot overlap each other. Similarly, [column groups](#4912-processing-model) cannot overlap each other.

A [cell](#4912-processing-model) cannot cover slots that are from two or more [row groups](#4912-processing-model). It is, however, possible for a cell to be in multiple [column groups](#4912-processing-model). All the slots that form part of one cell are part of zero or one [row groups](#4912-processing-model) and zero or more [column groups](#4912-processing-model).

In addition to [cells](#4912-processing-model), [columns](#4912-processing-model), [rows](#4912-processing-model), [row groups](#4912-processing-model), and [column groups](#4912-processing-model), [tables](#4912-processing-model) can have a [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element) element associated with them. This gives the table a heading, or legend.

A table model error is an error with the data represented by [`table`](#491-the-table-element) elements and their descendants. Documents must not have table model errors.

##### 4.9.12.1 Forming a table

To determine which elements correspond to which slots in a [table](#4912-processing-model) associated with a [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element, to determine the dimensions of the table (xwidth and yheight), and to determine if there are any [table model errors](#4912-processing-model), user agents must use the following algorithm:
1. Let xwidth be 0.
2. Let yheight be 0.
3. Let pending [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) elements be a list of [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) elements, initially empty.
4. Let the table be the [table](#4912-processing-model) represented by the [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element. The xwidth and yheight variables give the table's dimensions. The table is initially empty.
5. If the [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element has no children elements, then return the table (which will be empty).
6. Associate the first [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element) element child of the [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element with the table. If there are no such children, then it has no associated [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element) element.
7. Let the current element be the first element child of the [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element.

   If a step in this algorithm ever requires the current element to be advanced to the next child of the `table` when there is no such next child, then the user agent must jump to the step labeled *end*, near the end of this algorithm.

8. While the current element is not one of the following elements, [advance](#49121-forming-a-table) the current element to the next child of the [`table`](#491-the-table-element):
   - [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element)
   - [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element)
   - [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element)
   - [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element)
   - [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element)
9. If the current element is a [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element), follow these substeps:
   1. *Column groups*: Process the current element according to the appropriate case below:

      If the current element has any [`col`](#494-the-col-element) element children

      Follow these steps:
      1. Let xstart have the value of xwidth.
      2. Let the current column be the first [`col`](#494-the-col-element) element child of the [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element.
      3. *Columns*: If the current column [`col`](#494-the-col-element) element has a [`span`](#494-the-col-element) attribute, then parse its value using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers).

         If the result of parsing the value is not an error or zero, then let span be that value.

         Otherwise, if the [`col`](#494-the-col-element) element has no [`span`](#494-the-col-element) attribute, or if trying to parse the attribute's value resulted in an error or zero, then let span be 1.

         If span is greater than 1000, let it be 1000 instead.

      4. Increase xwidth by span.
      5. Let the last span [columns](#4912-processing-model) in the table correspond to the current column [`col`](#494-the-col-element) element.
      6. If current column is not the last [`col`](#494-the-col-element) element child of the [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element, then let the current column be the next [`col`](#494-the-col-element) element child of the [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element, and return to the step labeled *columns*.
      7. Let all the last [columns](#4912-processing-model) in the table from x=xstart to x=xwidth-1 form a new [column group](#4912-processing-model), anchored at the slot (xstart, 0), with width xwidth-xstart, corresponding to the [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element.

      If the current element has no [`col`](#494-the-col-element) element children
      1. If the [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element has a [`span`](#493-the-colgroup-element) attribute, then parse its value using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers).

         If the result of parsing the value is not an error or zero, then let span be that value.

         Otherwise, if the [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element has no [`span`](#493-the-colgroup-element) attribute, or if trying to parse the attribute's value resulted in an error or zero, then let span be 1.

         If span is greater than 1000, let it be 1000 instead.

      2. Increase xwidth by span.
      3. Let the last span [columns](#4912-processing-model) in the table form a new [column group](#4912-processing-model), anchored at the slot (xwidth-span, 0), with width span, corresponding to the [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element.

   2. [Advance](#49121-forming-a-table) the current element to the next child of the [`table`](#491-the-table-element).
   3. While the current element is not one of the following elements, [advance](#49121-forming-a-table) the current element to the next child of the [`table`](#491-the-table-element):
      - [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element)
      - [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element)
      - [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element)
      - [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element)
      - [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element)
   4. If the current element is a [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element, jump to the step labeled *column groups* above.

10. Let ycurrent be 0.
11. Let the list of downward-growing cells be an empty list.
12. *Rows*: While the current element is not one of the following elements, [advance](#49121-forming-a-table) the current element to the next child of the [`table`](#491-the-table-element):
    - [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element)
    - [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element)
    - [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element)
    - [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element)
13. If the current element is a [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element), then run the [algorithm for processing rows](#49121-forming-a-table), [advance](#49121-forming-a-table) the current element to the next child of the [`table`](#491-the-table-element), and return to the step labeled *rows*.
14. Run the [algorithm for ending a row group](#49121-forming-a-table).
15. If the current element is a [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element), then add that element to the list of pending [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) elements, [advance](#49121-forming-a-table) the current element to the next child of the [`table`](#491-the-table-element), and return to the step labeled *rows*.
16. The current element is either a [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) or a [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element).

    Run the [algorithm for processing row groups](#49121-forming-a-table).

17. [Advance](#49121-forming-a-table) the current element to the next child of the [`table`](#491-the-table-element).
18. Return to the step labeled *rows*.
19. *End*: For each [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element in the list of pending [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) elements, in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), run the [algorithm for processing row groups](#49121-forming-a-table).
20. If there exists a [row](#4912-processing-model) or [column](#4912-processing-model) in the table containing only [slots](#4912-processing-model) that do not have a [cell](#4912-processing-model) anchored to them, then this is a [table model error](#4912-processing-model).
21. Return the table.

The algorithm for processing row groups, which is invoked by the set of steps above for processing [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element), [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element), and [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) elements, is:
1. Let ystart have the value of yheight.
2. For each [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element that is a child of the element being processed, in tree order, run the [algorithm for processing rows](#49121-forming-a-table).
3. If yheight > ystart, then let all the last [rows](#4912-processing-model) in the table from y=ystart to y=yheight-1 form a new [row group](#4912-processing-model), anchored at the slot with coordinate (0, ystart), with height yheight-ystart, corresponding to the element being processed.
4. Run the [algorithm for ending a row group](#49121-forming-a-table).

The algorithm for ending a row group, which is invoked by the set of steps above when starting and ending a block of rows, is:
1. While ycurrent is less than yheight, follow these steps:
   1. Run the [algorithm for growing downward-growing cells](#49121-forming-a-table).
   2. Increase ycurrent by 1.
2. Empty the list of downward-growing cells.

The algorithm for processing rows, which is invoked by the set of steps above for processing [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) elements, is:
1. If yheight is equal to ycurrent, then increase yheight by 1. (ycurrent is never *greater* than yheight.)
2. Let xcurrent be 0.
3. Run the [algorithm for growing downward-growing cells](#49121-forming-a-table).
4. If the [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element being processed has no [`td`](#499-the-td-element) or [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element children, then increase ycurrent by 1, abort this set of steps, and return to the algorithm above.
5. Let current cell be the first [`td`](#499-the-td-element) or [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element child in the [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element being processed.
6. *Cells*: While xcurrent is less than xwidth and the slot with coordinate (xcurrent, ycurrent) already has a cell assigned to it, increase xcurrent by 1.
7. If xcurrent is equal to xwidth, increase xwidth by 1. (xcurrent is never *greater* than xwidth.)
8. If the current cell has a [`colspan`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements) attribute, then [parse that attribute's value](#2342-non-negative-integers), and let colspan be the result.

   If parsing that value failed, or returned zero, or if the attribute is absent, then let colspan be 1, instead.

   If colspan is greater than 1000, let it be 1000 instead.

9. If the current cell has a [`rowspan`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements) attribute, then [parse that attribute's value](#2342-non-negative-integers), and let rowspan be the result.

   If parsing that value failed or if the attribute is absent, then let rowspan be 1, instead.

   If rowspan is greater than 65534, let it be 65534 instead.

10. Let cell grows downward be false.
11. If rowspan is zero, then set cell grows downward to true and set rowspan to 1.
12. If xwidth < xcurrent+colspan, then let xwidth be xcurrent+colspan.
13. If yheight < ycurrent+rowspan, then let yheight be ycurrent+rowspan.
14. Let the slots with coordinates (x, y) such that xcurrent ≤ x < xcurrent+colspan and ycurrent ≤ y < ycurrent+rowspan be covered by a new [cell](#4912-processing-model) c, anchored at (xcurrent, ycurrent), which has width colspan and height rowspan, corresponding to the current cell element.

    If the current cell element is a [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element, let this new cell c be a header cell; otherwise, let it be a data cell.

    To establish which header cells apply to the current cell element, use the [algorithm for assigning header cells](#49122-forming-relationships-between-data-cells-and-header-cells) described in the next section.

    If any of the slots involved already had a [cell](#4912-processing-model) covering them, then this is a [table model error](#4912-processing-model). Those slots now have two cells overlapping.

15. If cell grows downward is true, then add the tuple {c, xcurrent, colspan} to the list of downward-growing cells.
16. Increase xcurrent by colspan.
17. If current cell is the last [`td`](#499-the-td-element) or [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element child in the [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element being processed, then increase ycurrent by 1, abort this set of steps, and return to the algorithm above.
18. Let current cell be the next [`td`](#499-the-td-element) or [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element child in the [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element being processed.
19. Return to the step labeled *cells*.

When the algorithms above require the user agent to run the algorithm for growing downward-growing cells, the user agent must, for each {cell, cellx, width} tuple in the list of downward-growing cells, if any, extend the [cell](#4912-processing-model) cell so that it also covers the slots with coordinates (x, ycurrent), where cellx ≤ x < cellx+width.

##### 4.9.12.2 Forming relationships between data cells and header cells

Each cell can be assigned zero or more header cells. The algorithm for assigning header cells to a cell principal cell is as follows.
1. Let header list be an empty list of cells.
2. Let (principalx, principaly) be the coordinate of the slot to which the principal cell is anchored.
3. If the principal cell has a [`headers`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements) attribute specified
   1. Take the value of the principal cell's [`headers`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements) attribute and [split it on ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings), letting id list be the list of tokens obtained.
   2. For each token in the id list, if the first element in the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) with an [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) equal to the token is a cell in the same [table](#4912-processing-model), and that cell is not the principal cell, then add that cell to header list.

   If principal cell does not have a [`headers`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements) attribute specified
   1. Let principalwidth be the width of the principal cell.
   2. Let principalheight be the height of the principal cell.
   3. For each value of y from principaly to principaly+principalheight-1, run the [internal algorithm for scanning and assigning header cells](#49122-forming-relationships-between-data-cells-and-header-cells), with the principal cell, the header list, the initial coordinate (principalx, y), and the increments Δx=−1 and Δy=0.
   4. For each value of x from principalx to principalx+principalwidth-1, run the [internal algorithm for scanning and assigning header cells](#49122-forming-relationships-between-data-cells-and-header-cells), with the principal cell, the header list, the initial coordinate (x, principaly), and the increments Δx=0 and Δy=−1.
   5. If the principal cell is anchored in a [row group](#4912-processing-model), then add all header cells that are [row group headers](#49122-forming-relationships-between-data-cells-and-header-cells) and are anchored in the same row group with an x-coordinate less than or equal to principalx+principalwidth-1 and a y-coordinate less than or equal to principaly+principalheight-1 to header list.
   6. If the principal cell is anchored in a [column group](#4912-processing-model), then add all header cells that are [column group headers](#49122-forming-relationships-between-data-cells-and-header-cells) and are anchored in the same column group with an x-coordinate less than or equal to principalx+principalwidth-1 and a y-coordinate less than or equal to principaly+principalheight-1 to header list.

4. Remove all the [empty cells](#49122-forming-relationships-between-data-cells-and-header-cells) from the header list.
5. Remove any duplicates from the header list.
6. Remove principal cell from the header list if it is there.
7. Assign the headers in the header list to the principal cell.

The internal algorithm for scanning and assigning header cells, given a principal cell, a header list, an initial coordinate (initialx, initialy), and Δx and Δy increments, is as follows:
1. Let x equal initialx.
2. Let y equal initialy.
3. Let opaque headers be an empty list of cells.
4. If principal cell is a header cell

   Let in header block be true, and let headers from current header block be a list of cells containing just the principal cell.

   Otherwise

   Let in header block be false and let headers from current header block be an empty list of cells.

5. *Loop*: Increment x by Δx; increment y by Δy.

   > [!note]
   > For each invocation of this algorithm, one of Δx and Δy will be −1, and the other will be 0.

6. If either x or y are less than 0, then abort this internal algorithm.
7. If there is no cell covering slot (x, y), or if there is more than one cell covering slot (x, y), return to the substep labeled *loop*.
8. Let current cell be the cell covering slot (x, y).
9. If current cell is a header cell
   1. Set in header block to true.
   2. Add current cell to headers from current header block.
   3. Let blocked be false.
   4. If Δx is 0

      If there are any cells in the opaque headers list anchored with the same x-coordinate as the current cell, and with the same width as current cell, then let blocked be true.

      If the current cell is not a [column header](#49122-forming-relationships-between-data-cells-and-header-cells), then let blocked be true.

      If Δy is 0

      If there are any cells in the opaque headers list anchored with the same y-coordinate as the current cell, and with the same height as current cell, then let blocked be true.

      If the current cell is not a [row header](#49122-forming-relationships-between-data-cells-and-header-cells), then let blocked be true.

   5. If blocked is false, then add the current cell to the header list.

   If current cell is a data cell and in header block is true

   Set in header block to false. Add all the cells in headers from current header block to the opaque headers list, and empty the headers from current header block list.

10. Return to the step labeled *loop*.

A header cell anchored at the slot with coordinate (x, y) with width width and height height is said to be a column header if any of the following are true:
- the cell's [`scope`](#4910-the-th-element) attribute is in the [Column](#4910-the-th-element) state; or
- the cell's [`scope`](#4910-the-th-element) attribute is in the [Auto](#4910-the-th-element) state, and there are no data cells in any of the cells covering slots with y-coordinates y .. y+height-1.

A header cell anchored at the slot with coordinate (x, y) with width width and height height is said to be a row header if any of the following are true:
- the cell's [`scope`](#4910-the-th-element) attribute is in the [Row](#4910-the-th-element) state; or
- the cell's [`scope`](#4910-the-th-element) attribute is in the [Auto](#4910-the-th-element) state, the cell is not a [column header](#49122-forming-relationships-between-data-cells-and-header-cells), and there are no data cells in any of the cells covering slots with x-coordinates x .. x+width-1.

A header cell is said to be a column group header if its [`scope`](#4910-the-th-element) attribute is in the [Column Group](#4910-the-th-element) state.

A header cell is said to be a row group header if its [`scope`](#4910-the-th-element) attribute is in the [Row Group](#4910-the-th-element) state.

A cell is said to be an empty cell if it contains no elements and its [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text), if any, consists only of [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).
