Some states of the [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute define a value sanitization algorithm.

Each [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element has a [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value), which is exposed by the [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute. Some states define an algorithm to convert a string to a number, an algorithm to convert a number to a string, an algorithm to convert a string to a `Date` object, and an algorithm to convert a `Date` object to a string, which are used by [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute), [`valueAsDate`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`valueAsNumber`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`stepUp()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis).

An [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [dirty value flag](#410181-a-form-controls-value) must be set to true whenever the user interacts with the control in a way that changes the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value). (It is also set to true when the value is programmatically changed, as described in the definition of the [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute.)

The `value` content attribute gives the default [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element. When the [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) content attribute is added, set, or removed, if the control's [dirty value flag](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is false, the user agent must set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element to the value of the [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) content attribute, if there is one, or the empty string otherwise, and then run the current [value sanitization algorithm](#4105-the-input-element), if one is defined.

Each [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element has a [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value), which is exposed by the [`checked`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute.

Each [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element has a boolean dirty checkedness flag. When it is true, the element is said to have a *dirty checkedness*. The [dirty checkedness flag](#4105-the-input-element) must be initially set to false when the element is created, and must be set to true whenever the user interacts with the control in a way that changes the [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

The `checked` content attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes) that gives the default [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element. When the [`checked`](#4105-the-input-element) content attribute is added, if the control does not have *[dirty checkedness](#4105-the-input-element)*, the user agent must set the [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element to true; when the [`checked`](#4105-the-input-element) content attribute is removed, if the control does not have *[dirty checkedness](#4105-the-input-element)*, the user agent must set the [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element to false.

The [reset algorithm](#41023-resetting-a-form) for [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements is to set its [user validity](#410181-a-form-controls-value), [dirty value flag](#410181-a-form-controls-value), and [dirty checkedness flag](#4105-the-input-element) back to false, set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element to the value of the [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) content attribute, if there is one, or the empty string otherwise, set the [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element to true if the element has a [`checked`](#4105-the-input-element) content attribute and false if it does not, empty the list of [selected files](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile), and then invoke the [value sanitization algorithm](#4105-the-input-element), if the [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute's current state defines one.

Each [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element can be [mutable](#410182-mutability). Except where otherwise specified, an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element is always [mutable](#410182-mutability). Similarly, except where otherwise specified, the user agent should not allow the user to modify the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) or [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element is [disabled](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute), it is not [mutable](#410182-mutability).

> [!note]
> The [`readonly`](#410533-the-readonly-attribute) attribute can also in some cases (e.g. for the [Date](#410517-date-state-typedate) state, but not the [Checkbox](#4105115-checkbox-state-typecheckbox) state) stop an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element from being [mutable](#410182-mutability).

The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element can support a picker. A picker is a user interface element that allows the end user to choose a value. Whether an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element supports a picker depends on the [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute state and [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) behavior. An [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element must support a picker when its [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [File Upload](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) state.

> [!note]
> As of the time of this writing, typical browser implementations show such picker UI for:
> - [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attributes are in the [Date](#410517-date-state-typedate), [Month](#410518-month-state-typemonth), [Week](#410519-week-state-typeweek), [Time](#4105110-time-state-typetime), [Local Date and Time](#4105111-local-date-and-time-state-typedatetime-local), and [Color](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) states;
> - [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements in various states that have a [suggestions source element](#410539-the-list-attribute);
> - [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [File Upload](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) state; and
> - [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) elements.

The [cloning steps](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) for [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements given node, copy, and subtree are to propagate the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value), [dirty value flag](#410181-a-form-controls-value), [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value), [dirty checkedness flag](#4105-the-input-element), and [indeterminateness](#4105-the-input-element) from node to copy.

The [activation behavior](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) for [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements element, given event, are these steps:
1. If element is not [mutable](#410182-mutability), and element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is neither in the [Checkbox](#4105115-checkbox-state-typecheckbox) nor in the [Radio](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio) state, then return.
2. Run element's input activation behavior, if any, and do nothing otherwise.
3. If element has a [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) and element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is not in the [Button](#4105121-button-state-typebutton) state, then return.
4. Run the [popover target attribute activation behavior](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes) given element and event's [target](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event).

> [!note]
> Recall that an element's [activation behavior](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) runs for both user-initiated activations and for synthetic activations (e.g., via `el.click()`). User agents might also have behaviors for a given control — not specified here — that are triggered only by true user-initiated activations. A common choice is to [show the picker, if applicable](#41054-common-input-element-apis), for the control. In contrast, the [input activation behavior](#4105-the-input-element) only shows pickers for the special historical cases of the [File Upload](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) and [Color](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) states.

The [legacy-pre-activation behavior](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) for [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements are these steps:
1. If this element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Checkbox state](#4105115-checkbox-state-typecheckbox), then set this element's [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to its opposite value (i.e. true if it is false, false if it is true) and set this element's [indeterminateness](#4105-the-input-element) to false.
2. If this element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Radio Button state](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio), then get a reference to the element in this element's [radio button group](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio) that has its [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) set to true, if any, and then set this element's [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to true.

The [legacy-canceled-activation behavior](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) for [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements are these steps:
1. If the element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Checkbox state](#4105115-checkbox-state-typecheckbox), then set the element's [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) and the element's [indeterminateness](#4105-the-input-element) back to the values they had before the [legacy-pre-activation behavior](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) was run.
2. If this element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Radio Button state](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio), then if the element to which a reference was obtained in the [legacy-pre-activation behavior](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget), if any, is still in what is now this element's [radio button group](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio), if it still has one, and if so, set that element's [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to true; or else, if there was no such element, or that element is no longer in this element's [radio button group](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio), or if this element no longer has a [radio button group](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio), set this element's [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to false.

---

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element is first created, the element's rendering and behavior must be set to the rendering and behavior defined for the [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute's state, and the [value sanitization algorithm](#4105-the-input-element), if one is defined for the [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute's state, must be invoked.

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute changes state, the user agent must run the following steps:
1. If the previous state of the element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute put the [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute in the *[value](#41054-common-input-element-apis)* mode, and the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is not the empty string, and the new state of the element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute puts the [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute in either the *[default](#41054-common-input-element-apis)* mode or the *[default/on](#41054-common-input-element-apis)* mode, then set the element's [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) content attribute to the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value).
2. Otherwise, if the previous state of the element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute put the [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute in any mode other than the *[value](#41054-common-input-element-apis)* mode, and the new state of the element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute puts the [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute in the *[value](#41054-common-input-element-apis)* mode, then set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element to the value of the [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) content attribute, if there is one, or the empty string otherwise, and then set the control's [dirty value flag](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to false.
3. Otherwise, if the previous state of the element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute put the [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute in any mode other than the *[filename](#41054-common-input-element-apis)* mode, and the new state of the element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute puts the [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute in the *[filename](#41054-common-input-element-apis)* mode, then set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element to the empty string.
4. Update the element's rendering and behavior to the new state's.
5. Signal a type change for the element. (The [Radio Button](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio) state uses this, in particular.)
6. Invoke the [value sanitization algorithm](#4105-the-input-element), if one is defined for the [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute's new state.
7. Let previouslySelectable be true if [`setRangeText()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) previously [applied](#4105-the-input-element) to the element, and false otherwise.
8. Let nowSelectable be true if [`setRangeText()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) now [applies](#4105-the-input-element) to the element, and false otherwise.
9. If previouslySelectable is false and nowSelectable is true, set the element's [text entry cursor position](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) to the beginning of the text control, and [set its selection direction](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) to "`none`".

---

The [`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) attribute represents the element's name. The [`dirname`](#410192-submitting-element-directionality-the-dirname-attribute) attribute controls how the element's [directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute) is submitted. The [`disabled`](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute) attribute is used to make the control non-interactive and to prevent its value from being submitted. The [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) attribute is used to explicitly associate the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element with its [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms). The [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) attribute controls how the user agent provides autofill behavior.

Each [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element has an indeterminateness, a boolean which is initially false. It only has an effect on [checkbox](#4105115-checkbox-state-typecheckbox) controls, including their rendering and accessibility semantics. An [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's indeterminateness is independent of its [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

The `indeterminate` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [indeterminateness](#4105-the-input-element).

The [`indeterminate`](#4105-the-input-element) setter steps are to set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [indeterminateness](#4105-the-input-element) to the given value.

The `colorSpace` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`colorspace`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes). The `type` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the respective content attribute of the same name, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

The `width` and `height` getter steps are to return the respective component of the result of determining the [dimensions](#4105-the-input-element) of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).

To determine the dimensions of an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element input:
1. If input's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is not in the [Image Button](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) state, then return a width of 0 and a height of 0. (In that case no image is *[available](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage)*.)
2. Let naturalDimensions be null.
3. If an image is *[available](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage)*, then set naturalDimensions to the result of applying the [default sizing algorithm](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#default-sizing) with that image's [natural width, natural height, and natural aspect ratio](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions), if any, using a [default object size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#default-object-size) of 300 by 150.
4. Return the result of [determining the dimensions](#4817-dimension-attributes) of input given naturalDimensions.

The [`willValidate`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), [`validity`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), and [`validationMessage`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) IDL attributes, and the [`checkValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), [`reportValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), and [`setCustomValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) methods, are part of the [constraint validation API](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api). The [`labels`](#4104-the-label-element) IDL attribute provides a list of the element's [`label`](#4104-the-label-element)s. The [`select()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionDirection`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`setRangeText()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), and [`setSelectionRange()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) methods and IDL attributes expose the element's text selection. The [`disabled`](#4105-the-input-element), [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms), and [`name`](#4105-the-input-element) IDL attributes are part of the element's forms API.

##### 4.10.5.1 States of the [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute

###### 4.10.5.1.1 Hidden state (`type=hidden`)

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Hidden](#410511-hidden-state-typehidden) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a value that is not intended to be examined or manipulated by the user.

**Constraint validation**: If an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Hidden](#410511-hidden-state-typehidden) state, it is [barred from constraint validation](#410211-definitions).

If the [`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) attribute is present and has a value that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for "[`_charset_`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute)", then the element's [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute must be omitted.

The [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) and [`dirname`](#410192-submitting-element-directionality-the-dirname-attribute) content attributes [apply](#4105-the-input-element) to this element.

The [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute [applies](#4105-the-input-element) to this element and is in mode [default](#41054-common-input-element-apis).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`accept`](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile), [`alpha`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`alt`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`checked`](#4105-the-input-element), [`colorspace`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes), [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute), [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`maxlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`minlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute), [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute), [`placeholder`](#4105310-the-placeholder-attribute), [`popovertarget`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`popovertargetaction`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`readonly`](#410533-the-readonly-attribute), [`required`](#410534-the-required-attribute), [`size`](#410532-the-size-attribute), [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute), and [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes).

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`checked`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`files`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`list`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionDirection`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`valueAsDate`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`valueAsNumber`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`setRangeText()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`setSelectionRange()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`stepDown()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`stepUp()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) methods.

The [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) and [`change`](#events) events [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element).

###### 4.10.5.1.2 Text (`type=text`) state and Search state (`type=search`)

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Text](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch) state or the [Search](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a one line plain text edit control for the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

> [!note]
> The difference between the [Text](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch) state and the [Search](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch) state is primarily stylistic: on platforms where search controls are distinguished from regular text controls, the [Search](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch) state might result in an appearance consistent with the platform's search controls rather than appearing like a regular text control.

If the element is [mutable](#410182-mutability), its [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) should be editable by the user. User agents must not allow users to insert U+000A LINE FEED (LF) or U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) characters into the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

If the element is [mutable](#410182-mutability), the user agent should allow the user to change the writing direction of the element, setting it either to a left-to-right writing direction or a right-to-left writing direction. If the user does so, the user agent must then run the following steps:
1. Set the element's [`dir`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) attribute to "[`ltr`](#3264-the-dir-attribute)" if the user selected a left-to-right writing direction, and "[`rtl`](#3264-the-dir-attribute)" if the user selected a right-to-left writing direction.
2. [Queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [user interaction task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given the element to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) at the element, with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) and [`composed`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attributes initialized to true.

The [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute, if specified, must have a value that contains no U+000A LINE FEED (LF) or U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) characters.

**The [value sanitization algorithm](#4105-the-input-element) is as follows**: [Strip newlines](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) from the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

The following common [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element content attributes, IDL attributes, and methods [apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute), [`dirname`](#410192-submitting-element-directionality-the-dirname-attribute), [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute), [`maxlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`minlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute), [`placeholder`](#4105310-the-placeholder-attribute), [`readonly`](#410533-the-readonly-attribute), [`required`](#410534-the-required-attribute), and [`size`](#410532-the-size-attribute) content attributes; [`list`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionDirection`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), and [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`setRangeText()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), and [`setSelectionRange()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) methods.

The [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute is in mode [value](#41054-common-input-element-apis).

The [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) and [`change`](#events) events [apply](#4105-the-input-element).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`accept`](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile), [`alpha`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`alt`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`checked`](#4105-the-input-element), [`colorspace`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes), [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute), [`popovertarget`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`popovertargetaction`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute), and [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes).

###### 4.10.5.1.3 Telephone state (`type=tel`)

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Telephone](#410513-telephone-state-typetel) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a control for editing a telephone number given in the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

If the element is [mutable](#410182-mutability), its [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) should be editable by the user. User agents may change the spacing and, with care, the punctuation of [values](#410181-a-form-controls-value) that the user enters. User agents must not allow users to insert U+000A LINE FEED (LF) or U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) characters into the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

The [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute, if specified, must have a value that contains no U+000A LINE FEED (LF) or U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) characters.

**The [value sanitization algorithm](#4105-the-input-element) is as follows**: [Strip newlines](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) from the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

> [!note]
> Unlike the [URL](#410514-url-state-typeurl) and [Email](#410515-email-state-typeemail) types, the [Telephone](#410513-telephone-state-typetel) type does not enforce a particular syntax. This is intentional; in practice, telephone number fields tend to be free-form fields, because there are a wide variety of valid phone numbers. Systems that need to enforce a particular format are encouraged to use the [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute) attribute or the [`setCustomValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) method to hook into the client-side validation mechanism.

The following common [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element content attributes, IDL attributes, and methods [apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute), [`dirname`](#410192-submitting-element-directionality-the-dirname-attribute), [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute), [`maxlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`minlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute), [`placeholder`](#4105310-the-placeholder-attribute), [`readonly`](#410533-the-readonly-attribute), [`required`](#410534-the-required-attribute), and [`size`](#410532-the-size-attribute) content attributes; [`list`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionDirection`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), and [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`setRangeText()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), and [`setSelectionRange()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) methods.

The [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute is in mode [value](#41054-common-input-element-apis).

The [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) and [`change`](#events) events [apply](#4105-the-input-element).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`accept`](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile), [`alpha`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`alt`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`checked`](#4105-the-input-element), [`colorspace`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes), [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute), [`popovertarget`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`popovertargetaction`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute), and [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes).

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`checked`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`files`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`valueAsDate`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`valueAsNumber`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`stepDown()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) and [`stepUp()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) methods.

###### 4.10.5.1.4 URL state (`type=url`)

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [URL](#410514-url-state-typeurl) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a control for editing a single [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute) given in the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

If the element is [mutable](#410182-mutability), the user agent should allow the user to change the URL represented by its [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value). User agents may allow the user to set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to a string that is not a [valid](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-url-string) [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute), but may also or instead automatically escape characters entered by the user so that the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is always a [valid](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-url-string) [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute) (even if that isn't the actual value seen and edited by the user in the interface). User agents should allow the user to set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to the empty string. User agents must not allow users to insert U+000A LINE FEED (LF) or U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) characters into the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

The [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute, if specified and not empty, must have a value that is a [valid URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#241-terminology) that is also an [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute).

**The [value sanitization algorithm](#4105-the-input-element) is as follows**: [Strip newlines](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) from the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value), then [strip leading and trailing ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) from the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

**Constraint validation**: While the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element is neither the empty string nor a [valid](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-url-string) [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute), the element is [suffering from a type mismatch](#410211-definitions).

The following common [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element content attributes, IDL attributes, and methods [apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute), [`dirname`](#410192-submitting-element-directionality-the-dirname-attribute), [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute), [`maxlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`minlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute), [`placeholder`](#4105310-the-placeholder-attribute), [`readonly`](#410533-the-readonly-attribute), [`required`](#410534-the-required-attribute), and [`size`](#410532-the-size-attribute) content attributes; [`list`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionDirection`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), and [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`setRangeText()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), and [`setSelectionRange()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) methods.

The [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute is in mode [value](#41054-common-input-element-apis).

The [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) and [`change`](#events) events [apply](#4105-the-input-element).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`accept`](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile), [`alpha`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`alt`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`checked`](#4105-the-input-element), [`colorspace`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes), [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute), [`popovertarget`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`popovertargetaction`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute), and [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes).

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`checked`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`files`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`valueAsDate`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`valueAsNumber`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`stepDown()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) and [`stepUp()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) methods.

> [!example]
> If a document contained the following markup:
> 
> ```html
> <input type="url" name="location" list="urls">
> <datalist id="urls">
>  <option label="MIME: Format of Internet Message Bodies" value="https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2045">
>  <option label="HTML" value="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/">
>  <option label="DOM" value="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/">
>  <option label="Fullscreen" value="https://fullscreen.spec.whatwg.org/">
>  <option label="Media Session" value="https://mediasession.spec.whatwg.org/">
>  <option label="The Single UNIX Specification, Version 3" value="http://www.unix.org/version3/">
> </datalist>
> ```
> 
> ...and the user had typed "spec.w", and the user agent had also found that the user had visited `https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-parsing` and `https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/` in the recent past, then the rendering might look like this:
> 
> ![A text box with an icon on the left followed by the text "spec.w" and a cursor, with a drop down button on the right hand side; with, below, a drop down box containing a list of six URLs on the left, with the first four having grayed out labels on the right; and a scrollbar to the right of the drop down box, indicating further values are available.](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/sample-url.svg)
> 
> The first four URLs in this sample consist of the four URLs in the author-specified list that match the text the user has entered, sorted in some [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) manner (maybe by how frequently the user refers to those URLs). Note how the UA is using the knowledge that the values are URLs to allow the user to omit the scheme part and perform intelligent matching on the domain name.
> 
> The last two URLs (and probably many more, given the scrollbar's indications of more values being available) are the matches from the user agent's session history data. This data is not made available to the page DOM. In this particular case, the UA has no titles to provide for those values.

###### 4.10.5.1.5 Email state (`type=email`)

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Email](#410515-email-state-typeemail) state, the rules in this section apply.

How the [Email](#410515-email-state-typeemail) state operates depends on whether the [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute) attribute is specified or not.

When the [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute) attribute is not specified on the element

The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a control for editing an email address given in the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

If the element is [mutable](#410182-mutability), the user agent should allow the user to change the email address represented by its [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value). User agents may allow the user to set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to a string that is not a [valid email address](#410515-email-state-typeemail). The user agent should act in a manner consistent with expecting the user to provide a single email address. User agents should allow the user to set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to the empty string. User agents must not allow users to insert U+000A LINE FEED (LF) or U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) characters into the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value). User agents may transform the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) for display and editing; in particular, user agents should convert punycode in the domain labels of the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to IDN in the display and vice versa.

**Constraint validation**: While the user interface is representing input that the user agent cannot convert to punycode, the control is [suffering from bad input](#410211-definitions).

The [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute, if specified and not empty, must have a value that is a single [valid email address](#410515-email-state-typeemail).

**The [value sanitization algorithm](#4105-the-input-element) is as follows**: [Strip newlines](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) from the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value), then [strip leading and trailing ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) from the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

**Constraint validation**: While the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element is neither the empty string nor a single [valid email address](#410515-email-state-typeemail), the element is [suffering from a type mismatch](#410211-definitions).

When the [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute) attribute *is* specified on the element

The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a control for adding, removing, and editing the email addresses given in the element's [value*s*](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

If the element is [mutable](#410182-mutability), the user agent should allow the user to add, remove, and edit the email addresses represented by its [values](#410181-a-form-controls-value). User agents may allow the user to set any individual value in the list of [value*s*](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to a string that is not a [valid email address](#410515-email-state-typeemail), but must not allow users to set any individual value to a string containing U+002C COMMA (,), U+000A LINE FEED (LF), or U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) characters. User agents should allow the user to remove all the addresses in the element's [values](#410181-a-form-controls-value). User agents may transform the [values](#410181-a-form-controls-value) for display and editing; in particular, user agents should convert punycode in the domain labels of the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to IDN in the display and vice versa.

**Constraint validation**: While the user interface describes a situation where an individual value contains a U+002C COMMA (,) or is representing input that the user agent cannot convert to punycode, the control is [suffering from bad input](#410211-definitions).

Whenever the user changes the element's [value*s*](#410181-a-form-controls-value), the user agent must run the following steps:
1. Let latest values be a copy of the element's [value*s*](#410181-a-form-controls-value).
2. [Strip leading and trailing ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) from each value in latest values.
3. Set the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to the result of concatenating all the values in latest values, separating each value from the next by a single U+002C COMMA character (,), maintaining the list's order.

The [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid email address list](#410515-email-state-typeemail).

**The [value sanitization algorithm](#4105-the-input-element) is as follows**:
1. [Split on commas](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value), [strip leading and trailing ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) from each resulting token, if any, and let the element's [values](#410181-a-form-controls-value) be the (possibly empty) resulting list of (possibly empty) tokens, maintaining the original order.
2. Set the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to the result of concatenating the element's [values](#410181-a-form-controls-value), separating each value from the next by a single U+002C COMMA character (,), maintaining the list's order.

**Constraint validation**: While the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element is not a [valid email address list](#410515-email-state-typeemail), the element is [suffering from a type mismatch](#410211-definitions).

When the [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute) attribute is set or removed, the user agent must run the [value sanitization algorithm](#4105-the-input-element).

A valid email address is a string that matches the `email` production of the following ABNF, the character set for which is Unicode. This ABNF implements the extensions described in RFC 1123. [\[ABNF\]](#references) [\[RFC5322\]](#references) [\[RFC1034\]](#references) [\[RFC1123\]](#references)

```abnf
email         = 1*( atext / "." ) "@" label *( "." label )
label         = let-dig [ [ ldh-str ] let-dig ]  ; limited to a length of 63 characters by RFC 1034 section 3.5
atext         = < as defined in RFC 5322 section 3.2.3 >
let-dig       = < as defined in RFC 1034 section 3.5 >
ldh-str       = < as defined in RFC 1034 section 3.5 >
```

> [!note]
> This requirement is a [willful violation](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-compliance-with-other-specifications) of RFC 5322, which defines a syntax for email addresses that is simultaneously too strict (before the "@" character), too vague (after the "@" character), and too lax (allowing comments, whitespace characters, and quoted strings in manners unfamiliar to most users) to be of practical use here.

> [!note]
> The following JavaScript- and Perl-compatible regular expression is an implementation of the above definition.
> 
> ```
> /^[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+\/=?^_`{|}~-]+@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?(?:\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*$/
> ```

A valid email address list is a [set of comma-separated tokens](#238-comma-separated-tokens), where each token is itself a [valid email address](#410515-email-state-typeemail). To obtain the list of tokens from a [valid email address list](#410515-email-state-typeemail), an implementation must [split the string on commas](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).

The following common [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element content attributes, IDL attributes, and methods [apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute), [`dirname`](#410192-submitting-element-directionality-the-dirname-attribute), [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute), [`maxlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`minlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute), [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute), [`placeholder`](#4105310-the-placeholder-attribute), [`readonly`](#410533-the-readonly-attribute), [`required`](#410534-the-required-attribute), and [`size`](#410532-the-size-attribute) content attributes; [`list`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) and [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) method.

The [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute is in mode [value](#41054-common-input-element-apis).

The [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) and [`change`](#events) events [apply](#4105-the-input-element).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`accept`](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile), [`alpha`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`alt`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`checked`](#4105-the-input-element), [`colorspace`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes), [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`popovertarget`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`popovertargetaction`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute), and [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes).

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`checked`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`files`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionDirection`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`valueAsDate`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`valueAsNumber`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`setRangeText()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`setSelectionRange()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`stepDown()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) and [`stepUp()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) methods.

###### 4.10.5.1.6 Password state (`type=password`)

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Password](#410516-password-state-typepassword) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a one line plain text edit control for the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value). The user agent should obscure the value so that people other than the user cannot see it.

If the element is [mutable](#410182-mutability), its [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) should be editable by the user. User agents must not allow users to insert U+000A LINE FEED (LF) or U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) characters into the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

The [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute, if specified, must have a value that contains no U+000A LINE FEED (LF) or U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) characters.

**The [value sanitization algorithm](#4105-the-input-element) is as follows**: [Strip newlines](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) from the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

###### 4.10.5.1.7 Date state (`type=date`)

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Date](#410517-date-state-typedate) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a control for setting the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to a string representing a specific [date](#2352-dates).

If the element is [mutable](#410182-mutability), the user agent should allow the user to change the [date](#2352-dates) represented by its [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value), as obtained by [parsing a date](#2352-dates) from it. User agents must not allow the user to set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to a non-empty string that is not a [valid date string](#2352-dates). If the user agent provides a user interface for selecting a [date](#2352-dates), then the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) must be set to a [valid date string](#2352-dates) representing the user's selection. User agents should allow the user to set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to the empty string.

**Constraint validation**: While the user interface describes input that the user agent cannot convert to a [valid date string](#2352-dates), the control is [suffering from bad input](#410211-definitions).

> [!note]
> See the [introduction section](#41018-date-time-and-number-formats) for a discussion of the difference between the input format and submission format for date, time, and number form controls, and the [implementation notes](#41052-implementation-notes-regarding-localization-of-form-controls) regarding localization of form controls.

The [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute, if specified and not empty, must have a value that is a [valid date string](#2352-dates).

**The [value sanitization algorithm](#4105-the-input-element) is as follows**: If the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element is not a [valid date string](#2352-dates), then set it to the empty string instead.

The [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid date string](#2352-dates). The [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid date string](#2352-dates).

The [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute) attribute is expressed in days. The [step scale factor](#410538-the-step-attribute) is 86,400,000 (which converts the days to milliseconds, as used in the other algorithms). The [default step](#410538-the-step-attribute) is 1 day.

When the element is [suffering from a step mismatch](#410211-definitions), the user agent may round the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to the nearest [date](#2352-dates) for which the element would not [suffer from a step mismatch](#410211-definitions).

**The [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#4105-the-input-element), given a string input, is as follows**: If [parsing a date](#2352-dates) from input results in an error, then return an error; otherwise, return the number of milliseconds elapsed from midnight UTC on the morning of 1970-01-01 (the time represented by the value "`1970-01-01T00:00:00.0Z`") to midnight UTC on the morning of the parsed [date](#2352-dates), ignoring leap seconds.

**The [algorithm to convert a number to a string](#4105-the-input-element), given a number input, is as follows**: Return a [valid date string](#2352-dates) that represents the [date](#2352-dates) that, in UTC, is current input milliseconds after midnight UTC on the morning of 1970-01-01 (the time represented by the value "`1970-01-01T00:00:00.0Z`").

**The [algorithm to convert a string to a `Date` object](#4105-the-input-element), given a string input, is as follows**: If [parsing a date](#2352-dates) from input results in an error, then return an error; otherwise, return [a new `Date` object](#219-dependencies) representing midnight UTC on the morning of the parsed [date](#2352-dates).

**The [algorithm to convert a `Date` object to a string](#4105-the-input-element), given a [`Date`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-date-objects) object input, is as follows**: Return a [valid date string](#2352-dates) that represents the [date](#2352-dates) current at the time represented by input in the UTC time zone.

> [!note]
> The [Date](#410517-date-state-typedate) state (and other date- and time-related states described in subsequent sections) is not intended for the entry of values for which a precise date and time relative to the contemporary calendar cannot be established. For example, it would be inappropriate for the entry of times like "one millisecond after the big bang", "the early part of the Jurassic period", or "a winter around 250 BCE".
> 
> For the input of dates before the introduction of the Gregorian calendar, authors are encouraged to not use the [Date](#410517-date-state-typedate) state (and the other date- and time-related states described in subsequent sections), as user agents are not required to support converting dates and times from earlier periods to the Gregorian calendar, and asking users to do so manually puts an undue burden on users. (This is complicated by the manner in which the Gregorian calendar was phased in, which occurred at different times in different countries, ranging from partway through the 16th century all the way to early in the 20th.) Instead, authors are encouraged to provide fine-grained input controls using the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element and [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements with the [Number](#4105112-number-state-typenumber) state.

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Month](#410518-month-state-typemonth) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a control for setting the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to a string representing a specific [month](#2351-months).

User agents must not allow the user to set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to a non-empty string that is not a [valid month string](#2351-months). If the user agent provides a user interface for selecting a [month](#2351-months), then the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) must be set to a [valid month string](#2351-months) representing the user's selection. User agents should allow the user to set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to the empty string.

**Constraint validation**: While the user interface describes input that the user agent cannot convert to a [valid month string](#2351-months), the control is [suffering from bad input](#410211-definitions).

> [!note]
> See the [introduction section](#41018-date-time-and-number-formats) for a discussion of the difference between the input format and submission format for date, time, and number form controls, and the [implementation notes](#41052-implementation-notes-regarding-localization-of-form-controls) regarding localization of form controls.

The [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute, if specified and not empty, must have a value that is a [valid month string](#2351-months).

**The [value sanitization algorithm](#4105-the-input-element) is as follows**: If the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element is not a [valid month string](#2351-months), then set it to the empty string instead.

The [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid month string](#2351-months). The [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid month string](#2351-months).

The [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute) attribute is expressed in months. The [step scale factor](#410538-the-step-attribute) is 1 (there is no conversion needed as the algorithms use months). The [default step](#410538-the-step-attribute) is 1 month.

When the element is [suffering from a step mismatch](#410211-definitions), the user agent may round the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to the nearest [month](#2351-months) for which the element would not [suffer from a step mismatch](#410211-definitions).

**The [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#4105-the-input-element), given a string input, is as follows**: If [parsing a month](#2351-months) from input results in an error, then return an error; otherwise, return the number of months between January 1970 and the parsed [month](#2351-months).

**The [algorithm to convert a number to a string](#4105-the-input-element), given a number input, is as follows**: Return a [valid month string](#2351-months) that represents the [month](#2351-months) that has input months between it and January 1970.

**The [algorithm to convert a string to a `Date` object](#4105-the-input-element), given a string input, is as follows**: If [parsing a month](#2351-months) from input results in an error, then return an error; otherwise, return [a new `Date` object](#219-dependencies) representing midnight UTC on the morning of the first day of the parsed [month](#2351-months).

**The [algorithm to convert a `Date` object to a string](#4105-the-input-element), given a [`Date`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-date-objects) object input, is as follows**: Return a [valid month string](#2351-months) that represents the [month](#2351-months) current at the time represented by input in the UTC time zone.

The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a control for setting the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to a string representing a specific [week](#2358-weeks).

If the element is [mutable](#410182-mutability), the user agent should allow the user to change the [week](#2358-weeks) represented by its [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value), as obtained by [parsing a week](#2358-weeks) from it. User agents must not allow the user to set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to a non-empty string that is not a [valid week string](#2358-weeks). If the user agent provides a user interface for selecting a [week](#2358-weeks), then the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) must be set to a [valid week string](#2358-weeks) representing the user's selection. User agents should allow the user to set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to the empty string.

> [!note]

The [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid week string](#2358-weeks). The [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid week string](#2358-weeks).

The [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute) attribute is expressed in weeks. **The [algorithm to convert a number to a string](#4105-the-input-element), given a number input, is as follows**: Return a [valid week string](#2358-weeks) that represents the [week](#2358-weeks) that, in UTC, is current input milliseconds after midnight UTC on the morning of 1970-01-01 (the time represented by the value "`1970-01-01T00:00:00.0Z`").

**The [algorithm to convert a string to a `Date` object](#4105-the-input-element), given a string input, is as follows**: If [parsing a week](#2358-weeks) from input results in an error, then return an error; otherwise, return [a new `Date` object](#219-dependencies) representing midnight UTC on the morning of the Monday of the parsed [week](#2358-weeks).

> [!note]
> See the [introduction section](#41018-date-time-and-number-formats) for a discussion of the difference between the input format and submission format for date, time, and number form controls, and the [implementation notes](#41052-implementation-notes-regarding-localization-of-form-controls) regarding localization of form controls.

The [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute, if specified and not empty, must have a value that is a [valid time string](#2354-times).

**The [value sanitization algorithm](#4105-the-input-element) is as follows**: If the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element is not a [valid time string](#2354-times), then set it to the empty string instead.

The form control [has a periodic domain](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes).

The [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid time string](#2354-times). The [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid time string](#2354-times).

The [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute) attribute is expressed in seconds. The [step scale factor](#410538-the-step-attribute) is 1000 (which converts the seconds to milliseconds, as used in the other algorithms). The [default step](#410538-the-step-attribute) is 60 seconds.

When the element is [suffering from a step mismatch](#410211-definitions), the user agent may round the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to the nearest [time](#2354-times) for which the element would not [suffer from a step mismatch](#410211-definitions).

**The [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#4105-the-input-element), given a string input, is as follows**: If [parsing a time](#2354-times) from input results in an error, then return an error; otherwise, return the number of milliseconds elapsed from midnight to the parsed [time](#2354-times) on a day with no time changes.

**The [algorithm to convert a number to a string](#4105-the-input-element), given a number input, is as follows**: Return a [valid time string](#2354-times) that represents the [time](#2354-times) that is input milliseconds after midnight on a day with no time changes.

**The [algorithm to convert a string to a `Date` object](#4105-the-input-element), given a string input, is as follows**: If [parsing a time](#2354-times) from input results in an error, then return an error; otherwise, return [a new `Date` object](#219-dependencies) representing the parsed [time](#2354-times) in UTC on 1970-01-01.

**The [algorithm to convert a `Date` object to a string](#4105-the-input-element), given a [`Date`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-date-objects) object input, is as follows**: Return a [valid time string](#2354-times) that represents the UTC [time](#2354-times) component that is represented by input.

The following common [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element content attributes, IDL attributes, and methods [apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute), [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute), [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`readonly`](#410533-the-readonly-attribute), [`required`](#410534-the-required-attribute), and [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute) content attributes; [`list`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`valueAsDate`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`valueAsNumber`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`stepDown()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`stepUp()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) methods.

The [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute is in mode [value](#41054-common-input-element-apis).

The [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) and [`change`](#events) events [apply](#4105-the-input-element).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`accept`](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile), [`alpha`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`alt`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`checked`](#4105-the-input-element), [`colorspace`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`dirname`](#410192-submitting-element-directionality-the-dirname-attribute), [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes), [`maxlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`minlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute), [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute), [`placeholder`](#4105310-the-placeholder-attribute), [`popovertarget`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`popovertargetaction`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`size`](#410532-the-size-attribute), [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), and [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes).

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`checked`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`files`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), and [`selectionDirection`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) IDL attributes; [`setRangeText()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), and [`setSelectionRange()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) methods.

###### 4.10.5.1.11 Local Date and Time state (`type=datetime-local`)

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Local Date and Time](#4105111-local-date-and-time-state-typedatetime-local) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a control for setting the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to a string representing a [local date and time](#2355-local-dates-and-times), with no time-zone offset information.

If the element is [mutable](#410182-mutability), the user agent should allow the user to change the [date and time](#2355-local-dates-and-times) represented by its [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value), as obtained by [parsing a date and time](#2355-local-dates-and-times) from it. User agents must not allow the user to set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to a non-empty string that is not a [valid normalized local date and time string](#2355-local-dates-and-times). If the user agent provides a user interface for selecting a [local date and time](#2355-local-dates-and-times), then the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) must be set to a [valid normalized local date and time string](#2355-local-dates-and-times) representing the user's selection. User agents should allow the user to set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to the empty string.

**Constraint validation**: While the user interface describes input that the user agent cannot convert to a [valid normalized local date and time string](#2355-local-dates-and-times), the control is [suffering from bad input](#410211-definitions).

> [!note]
> See the [introduction section](#41018-date-time-and-number-formats) for a discussion of the difference between the input format and submission format for date, time, and number form controls, and the [implementation notes](#41052-implementation-notes-regarding-localization-of-form-controls) regarding localization of form controls.

The [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute, if specified and not empty, must have a value that is a [valid local date and time string](#2355-local-dates-and-times).

**The [value sanitization algorithm](#4105-the-input-element) is as follows**: If the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element is a [valid local date and time string](#2355-local-dates-and-times), then set it to a [valid normalized local date and time string](#2355-local-dates-and-times) representing the same date and time; otherwise, set it to the empty string instead.

The [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid local date and time string](#2355-local-dates-and-times). The [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid local date and time string](#2355-local-dates-and-times).

The [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute) attribute is expressed in seconds. The [step scale factor](#410538-the-step-attribute) is 1000 (which converts the seconds to milliseconds, as used in the other algorithms). The [default step](#410538-the-step-attribute) is 60 seconds.

When the element is [suffering from a step mismatch](#410211-definitions), the user agent may round the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to the nearest [local date and time](#2355-local-dates-and-times) for which the element would not [suffer from a step mismatch](#410211-definitions).

**The [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#4105-the-input-element), given a string input, is as follows**: If [parsing a date and time](#2355-local-dates-and-times) from input results in an error, then return an error; otherwise, return the number of milliseconds elapsed from midnight on the morning of 1970-01-01 (the time represented by the value "`1970-01-01T00:00:00.0`") to the parsed [local date and time](#2355-local-dates-and-times), ignoring leap seconds.

**The [algorithm to convert a number to a string](#4105-the-input-element), given a number input, is as follows**: Return a [valid normalized local date and time string](#2355-local-dates-and-times) that represents the date and time that is input milliseconds after midnight on the morning of 1970-01-01 (the time represented by the value "`1970-01-01T00:00:00.0`").

> [!note]
> See [the note on historical dates](#410517-date-state-typedate) in the [Date](#410517-date-state-typedate) state section.

The following common [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element content attributes, IDL attributes, and methods [apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute), [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute), [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`readonly`](#410533-the-readonly-attribute), [`required`](#410534-the-required-attribute), and [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute) content attributes; [`list`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`valueAsNumber`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`stepDown()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`stepUp()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) methods.

The [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute is in mode [value](#41054-common-input-element-apis).

The [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) and [`change`](#events) events [apply](#4105-the-input-element).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`accept`](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile), [`alpha`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`alt`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`checked`](#4105-the-input-element), [`colorspace`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`dirname`](#410192-submitting-element-directionality-the-dirname-attribute), [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes), [`maxlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`minlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute), [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute), [`placeholder`](#4105310-the-placeholder-attribute), [`popovertarget`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`popovertargetaction`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`size`](#410532-the-size-attribute), [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), and [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes).

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`checked`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`files`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionDirection`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), and [`valueAsDate`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`setRangeText()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), and [`setSelectionRange()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) methods.

> [!example]
> The following example shows part of a flight booking application. The application uses an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element with its [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute set to [`datetime-local`](#4105111-local-date-and-time-state-typedatetime-local), and it then interprets the given date and time in the time zone of the selected airport.
> 
> ```html
> <fieldset>
>  <legend>Destination</legend>
>  <p><label>Airport: <input type=text name=to list=airports></label></p>
>  <p><label>Departure time: <input type=datetime-local name=totime step=3600></label></p>
> </fieldset>
> <datalist id=airports>
>  <option value=ATL label="Atlanta">
>  <option value=MEM label="Memphis">
>  <option value=LHR label="London Heathrow">
>  <option value=LAX label="Los Angeles">
>  <option value=FRA label="Frankfurt">
> </datalist>
> ```

###### 4.10.5.1.12 Number state (`type=number`)

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Number](#4105112-number-state-typenumber) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a control for setting the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to a string representing a number.

If the element is [mutable](#410182-mutability), the user agent should allow the user to change the number represented by its [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value), as obtained from applying the [rules for parsing floating-point number values](#2343-floating-point-numbers) to it. User agents must not allow the user to set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to a non-empty string that is not a [valid floating-point number](#2343-floating-point-numbers). If the user agent provides a user interface for selecting a number, then the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) must be set to the [best representation of the number representing the user's selection as a floating-point number](#2343-floating-point-numbers). User agents should allow the user to set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to the empty string.

**Constraint validation**: While the user interface describes input that the user agent cannot convert to a [valid floating-point number](#2343-floating-point-numbers), the control is [suffering from bad input](#410211-definitions).

> [!note]
> This specification does not define what user interface user agents are to use; user agent vendors are encouraged to consider what would best serve their users' needs. For example, a user agent in Persian or Arabic markets might support Persian and Arabic numeric input (converting it to the format required for submission as described above). Similarly, a user agent designed for Romans might display the value in Roman numerals rather than in decimal; or (more realistically) a user agent designed for the French market might display the value with apostrophes between thousands and commas before the decimals, and allow the user to enter a value in that manner, internally converting it to the submission format described above.

The [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute, if specified and not empty, must have a value that is a [valid floating-point number](#2343-floating-point-numbers).

**The [value sanitization algorithm](#4105-the-input-element) is as follows**: If the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element is not a [valid floating-point number](#2343-floating-point-numbers), then set it to the empty string instead.

The [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid floating-point number](#2343-floating-point-numbers). The [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid floating-point number](#2343-floating-point-numbers).
