The [step scale factor](#410538-the-step-attribute) is 1. The [default step](#410538-the-step-attribute) is 1 (allowing only integers to be selected by the user, unless the [step base](#410538-the-step-attribute) has a non-integer value).

When the element is [suffering from a step mismatch](#410211-definitions), the user agent may round the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to the nearest number for which the element would not [suffer from a step mismatch](#410211-definitions). If there are two such numbers, user agents are encouraged to pick the one nearest positive infinity.

**The [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#4105-the-input-element), given a string input, is as follows**: If applying the [rules for parsing floating-point number values](#2343-floating-point-numbers) to input results in an error, then return an error; otherwise, return the resulting number.

**The [algorithm to convert a number to a string](#4105-the-input-element), given a number input, is as follows**: Return a [valid floating-point number](#2343-floating-point-numbers) that represents input.

The following common [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element content attributes, IDL attributes, and methods [apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute), [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute), [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`placeholder`](#4105310-the-placeholder-attribute), [`readonly`](#410533-the-readonly-attribute), [`required`](#410534-the-required-attribute), and [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute) content attributes; [`list`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`valueAsNumber`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`stepDown()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`stepUp()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) methods.

The [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute is in mode [value](#41054-common-input-element-apis).

The [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) and [`change`](#events) events [apply](#4105-the-input-element).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`accept`](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile), [`alpha`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`alt`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`checked`](#4105-the-input-element), [`colorspace`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`dirname`](#410192-submitting-element-directionality-the-dirname-attribute), [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes), [`maxlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`minlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute), [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute), [`popovertarget`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`popovertargetaction`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`size`](#410532-the-size-attribute), [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), and [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes).

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`checked`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`files`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionDirection`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), and [`valueAsDate`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`setRangeText()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), and [`setSelectionRange()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) methods.

> [!example]
> Here is an example of using a numeric input control:
> 
> ```html
> <label>How much do you want to charge? $<input type=number min=0 step=0.01 name=price></label>
> ```
> 
> As described above, a user agent might support numeric input in the user's local format, converting it to the format required for submission as described above. This might include handling grouping separators (as in "872,000,000,000") and various decimal separators (such as "3,99" vs "3.99") or using local digits (such as those in Arabic, Devanagari, Persian, and Thai).

> [!note]
> The `type=number` state is not appropriate for input that happens to only consist of numbers but isn't strictly speaking a number. For example, it would be inappropriate for credit card numbers or US postal codes. A simple way of determining whether to use `type=number` is to consider whether it would make sense for the input control to have a spinbox interface (e.g. with "up" and "down" arrows). Getting a credit card number wrong by 1 in the last digit isn't a minor mistake, it's as wrong as getting every digit incorrect. So it would not make sense for the user to select a credit card number using "up" and "down" buttons. When a spinbox interface is not appropriate, `type=text` is probably the right choice (possibly with an [`inputmode`](#689-input-modalities-the-inputmode-attribute) or [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute) attribute).

###### 4.10.5.1.13 Range state (`type=range`)

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Range](#4105113-range-state-typerange) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a control for setting the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to a string representing a number, but with the caveat that the exact value is not important, letting UAs provide a simpler interface than they do for the [Number](#4105112-number-state-typenumber) state.

If the element is [mutable](#410182-mutability), the user agent should allow the user to change the number represented by its [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value), as obtained from applying the [rules for parsing floating-point number values](#2343-floating-point-numbers) to it. User agents must not allow the user to set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to a string that is not a [valid floating-point number](#2343-floating-point-numbers). If the user agent provides a user interface for selecting a number, then the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) must be set to a [best representation of the number representing the user's selection as a floating-point number](#2343-floating-point-numbers). User agents must not allow the user to set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to the empty string.

**Constraint validation**: While the user interface describes input that the user agent cannot convert to a [valid floating-point number](#2343-floating-point-numbers), the control is [suffering from bad input](#410211-definitions).

The [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid floating-point number](#2343-floating-point-numbers).

**The [value sanitization algorithm](#4105-the-input-element) is as follows**: If the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element is not a [valid floating-point number](#2343-floating-point-numbers), then set it to the [best representation, as a floating-point number](#2343-floating-point-numbers), of the [default value](#4105113-range-state-typerange).

The default value is the [minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) plus half the difference between the [minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) and the [maximum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), unless the [maximum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) is less than the [minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), in which case the [default value](#4105113-range-state-typerange) is the [minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes).

When the element is [suffering from an underflow](#410211-definitions), the user agent must set the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to the [best representation, as a floating-point number](#2343-floating-point-numbers), of the [minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes).

When the element is [suffering from an overflow](#410211-definitions), if the [maximum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) is not less than the [minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), the user agent must set the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to a [valid floating-point number](#2343-floating-point-numbers) that represents the [maximum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes).

When the element is [suffering from a step mismatch](#410211-definitions), the user agent must round the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to the nearest number for which the element would not [suffer from a step mismatch](#410211-definitions), and which is greater than or equal to the [minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), and, if the [maximum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) is not less than the [minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), which is less than or equal to the [maximum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), if there is a number that matches these constraints. If two numbers match these constraints, then user agents must use the one nearest to positive infinity.

> [!example]
> For example, the markup `<input type="range" min=0 max=100 step=20 value=50>` results in a range control whose initial value is 60.

> [!example]
> Here is an example of a range control using an autocomplete list with the [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute) attribute. This could be useful if there are values along the full range of the control that are especially important, such as preconfigured light levels or typical speed limits in a range control used as a speed control. The following markup fragment:
> 
> ```html
> <input type="range" min="-100" max="100" value="0" step="10" name="power" list="powers">
> <datalist id="powers">
> <option value="0">
> <option value="-30">
> <option value="30">
>  <option value="++50">
> </datalist>
> ```
> 
> ...with the following style sheet applied:
> 
> ```css
> input { writing-mode: vertical-lr; height: 75px; width: 49px; background: #D5CCBB; color: black; }
> ```
> 
> ...might render as:
> 
> ![A vertical slider control whose primary color is black and whose background color is beige, with the slider having five tick marks, one long one at each extremity, and three short ones clustered around the midpoint.](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/sample-range.png)
> 
> Note how the UA determined the orientation of the control from the ratio of the style-sheet-specified height and width properties. The colors were similarly derived from the style sheet. The tick marks, however, were derived from the markup. In particular, the [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute) attribute has not affected the placement of tick marks, the UA deciding to only use the author-specified completion values and then adding longer tick marks at the extremes.
> 
> Note also how the invalid value `++50` was ignored.

> [!example]
> For another example, consider the following markup fragment:
> 
> ```html
> <input name=x type=range min=100 max=700 step=9.09090909 value=509.090909>
> ```
> 
> A user agent could display in a variety of ways, for instance:
> 
> ![As a dial.](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/sample-range-2a.png)
> 
> Or, alternatively, for instance:
> 
> ![As a long horizontal slider with tick marks.](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/sample-range-2b.png)
> 
> The user agent could pick which one to display based on the dimensions given in the style sheet. This would allow it to maintain the same resolution for the tick marks, despite the differences in width.

> [!example]
> Finally, here is an example of a range control with two labeled values:
> 
> ```html
> <input type="range" name="a" list="a-values">
> <datalist id="a-values">
> <option value="10" label="Low">
> <option value="90" label="High">
> </datalist>
> ```
> 
> With styles that make the control draw vertically, it might look as follows:
> 
> ![A vertical slider control with two tick marks, one near the top labeled 'High', and one near the bottom labeled 'Low'.](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/sample-range-labels.png)

> [!note]
> In this state, the range and step constraints are enforced even during user input, and there is no way to set the value to the empty string.

The [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid floating-point number](#2343-floating-point-numbers). The [default minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) is 0. The [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid floating-point number](#2343-floating-point-numbers). The [default maximum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) is 100.

The [step scale factor](#410538-the-step-attribute) is 1. The [default step](#410538-the-step-attribute) is 1 (allowing only integers, unless the [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attribute has a non-integer value).

**The [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#4105-the-input-element), given a string input, is as follows**: If applying the [rules for parsing floating-point number values](#2343-floating-point-numbers) to input results in an error, then return an error; otherwise, return the resulting number.

**The [algorithm to convert a number to a string](#4105-the-input-element), given a number input, is as follows**: Return the [best representation, as a floating-point number](#2343-floating-point-numbers), of input.

The following common [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element content attributes, IDL attributes, and methods [apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute), [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute), [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), and [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute) content attributes; [`list`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`valueAsNumber`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`stepDown()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) and [`stepUp()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) methods.

The [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute is in mode [value](#41054-common-input-element-apis).

The [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) and [`change`](#events) events [apply](#4105-the-input-element).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`accept`](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile), [`alpha`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`alt`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`checked`](#4105-the-input-element), [`colorspace`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`dirname`](#410192-submitting-element-directionality-the-dirname-attribute), [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes), [`maxlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`minlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute), [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute), [`placeholder`](#4105310-the-placeholder-attribute), [`popovertarget`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`popovertargetaction`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`readonly`](#410533-the-readonly-attribute), [`required`](#410534-the-required-attribute), [`size`](#410532-the-size-attribute), [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), and [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes).

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`checked`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`files`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionDirection`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), and [`valueAsDate`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`setRangeText()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), and [`setSelectionRange()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) methods.

###### 4.10.5.1.14 Color state (`type=color`)

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Color](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a color well control, for setting the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to a string representing the serialization of a CSS color.

> [!note]
> In this state, there is always a CSS color picked, and there is no way for the end user to set the value to the empty string.

The `alpha` attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes). If present, it indicates the CSS color's alpha component can be manipulated by the end user and does not have to be fully opaque.

The `colorspace` attribute indicates the color space of the serialized CSS color. It also hints at the desired user interface for selecting a CSS color. It is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `limited-srgb` | Limited sRGB | The CSS color is converted to the ['srgb'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#valdef-color-srgb) color space and limited to 8-bits per component, e.g., "`#123456`" or "`color(srgb 0 1 0 / 0.5)`". |
| `display-p3` | Display P3 | The CSS color is converted to the ['display-p3'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#valdef-color-display-p3) color space, e.g., "`color(display-p3 1.84 -0.19 0.72 / 0.6)`". |

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the [Limited sRGB](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) state.

Whenever the element's [`alpha`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) or [`colorspace`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) attributes are changed, the user agent must run [update a color well control color](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) given the element.

If the element is [mutable](#410182-mutability), the user agent should allow the user to change the color represented by its [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value), as obtained from [parsing](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#parse-a-css-color-value) it. User agents must not allow the user to set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to a string that running [update a color well control color](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) for the element would not set it to. If the user agent provides a user interface for selecting a CSS color, then the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) must be set to the result of [serializing a color well control color](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) given the element and the end user's selection.

The [input activation behavior](#4105-the-input-element) for such an element element is to [show the picker, if applicable](#41054-common-input-element-apis), for element.

**Constraint validation**: While the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is not the empty string and [parsing](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#parse-a-css-color-value) it returns failure, the control is [suffering from bad input](#410211-definitions).

The [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute, if specified and not the empty string, must have a value that is a CSS color.

**The [value sanitization algorithm](#4105-the-input-element) is as follows**: Run [update a color well control color](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) for the element.

To update a color well control color, given an element element:
1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): element is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Color](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) state.
2. Let value be the result of running these steps:
   1. If element's [dirty value flag](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is false, then return the result of [getting an attribute by namespace and local name](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) given null, "`value`", and element.
   2. Return element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value).
3. Let color be the result of [parsing](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#parse-a-css-color-value) value.
4. If color is failure, then set color to [opaque black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#opaque-black).
5. Set element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to the result of [serializing a color well control color](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) given element and color.

To serialize a color well control color, given an element element and a CSS color color:
1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): element is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Color](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) state.
2. Let htmlCompatible be false.
3. If element's [`alpha`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) attribute is not specified, then set color's alpha component to be fully opaque.
4. If element's [`colorspace`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) attribute is in the [Limited sRGB](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) state:
   1. Set color to color [converted](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#color-conversion) to the ['srgb'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#valdef-color-srgb) color space.
   2. Round each of color's components so they are in the range 0 to 255, inclusive. Components are to be [rounded towards +∞](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-4/#combine-integers).
   3. If element's [`alpha`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) attribute is not specified, then set htmlCompatible to true.

      > [!note]
      > This intentionally uses a different serialization path for compatibility with an earlier version of the color well control.

   4. Otherwise, set color to color converted using the ['color()'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#color-function) function.

5. Otherwise:
   1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): element's [`colorspace`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) attribute is in the [Display P3](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) state.
   2. Set color to color [converted](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#color-conversion) to the ['display-p3'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#valdef-color-display-p3) color space.
6. Return the result of [serializing](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#serializing-color-values) color. If htmlCompatible is true, then do so with [HTML-compatible serialization requested](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#color-serialization-html-compatible-serialization-is-requested).

The following common [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element content attributes and IDL attributes [apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`alpha`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute), [`colorspace`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), and [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute) content attributes; [`list`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) and [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) method.

The [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute is in mode [value](#41054-common-input-element-apis).

The [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) and [`change`](#events) events [apply](#4105-the-input-element).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`accept`](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile), [`alt`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`checked`](#4105-the-input-element), [`dirname`](#410192-submitting-element-directionality-the-dirname-attribute), [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes), [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`maxlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`minlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute), [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute), [`placeholder`](#4105310-the-placeholder-attribute), [`popovertarget`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`popovertargetaction`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`readonly`](#410533-the-readonly-attribute), [`required`](#410534-the-required-attribute), [`size`](#410532-the-size-attribute), [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute), and [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes).

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`checked`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`files`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionDirection`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`valueAsDate`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) and, [`valueAsNumber`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`setRangeText()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`setSelectionRange()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`stepDown()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`stepUp()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) methods.

###### 4.10.5.1.15 Checkbox state (`type=checkbox`)

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Checkbox](#4105115-checkbox-state-typecheckbox) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a two-state control that represents the element's [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) state. If the element's [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) state is true, the control represents a positive selection, and if it is false, a negative selection. If the element's [indeterminateness](#4105-the-input-element) is true, then the control's selection should be obscured.

The [input activation behavior](#4105-the-input-element) is to run the following steps:
1. If the element is not [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree), then return.
2. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) at the element with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) and [`composed`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attributes initialized to true.
3. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`change`](#events) at the element with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true.

**Constraint validation**: If the element is *[required](#410534-the-required-attribute)* and its [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is false, then the element is [suffering from being missing](#410211-definitions).

`input.indeterminate [ = value ]`

When set, overrides the rendering of [checkbox](#4105115-checkbox-state-typecheckbox) controls so that the current value is not visible.

The following common [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element content attributes and IDL attributes [apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`checked`](#4105-the-input-element), and [`required`](#410534-the-required-attribute) content attributes; [`checked`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) and [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes.

The [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute is in mode [default/on](#41054-common-input-element-apis).

The [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) and [`change`](#events) events [apply](#4105-the-input-element).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`accept`](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile), [`alpha`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`alt`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute), [`colorspace`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`dirname`](#410192-submitting-element-directionality-the-dirname-attribute), [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes), [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute), [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`maxlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`minlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute), [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute), [`placeholder`](#4105310-the-placeholder-attribute), [`popovertarget`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`popovertargetaction`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`readonly`](#410533-the-readonly-attribute), [`size`](#410532-the-size-attribute), [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute), and [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes).

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`files`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`list`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionDirection`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`valueAsDate`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`valueAsNumber`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`setRangeText()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`setSelectionRange()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`stepDown()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`stepUp()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) methods.

###### 4.10.5.1.16 Radio Button state (`type=radio`)

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Radio Button](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a control that, when used in conjunction with other [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements, forms a *[radio button group](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio)* in which only one control can have its [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) state set to true. If the element's [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) state is true, the control represents the selected control in the group, and if it is false, it indicates a control in the group that is not selected.

The *radio button group* that contains an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element a also contains all the other [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements b that fulfill all of the following conditions:
- The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element b's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Radio Button](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio) state.
- Either a and b have the same [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms), or they both have no [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms).
- Both a and b are in the same [tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
- They both have a [`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) attribute, their [`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) attributes are not empty, and the value of a's [`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) attribute equals the value of b's [`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) attribute.

A [tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) must not contain an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose *[radio button group](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio)* contains only that element.

When any of the following phenomena occur, if the element's [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) state is true after the occurrence, the [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) state of all the other elements in the same *[radio button group](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio)* must be set to false:
- The element's [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) state is set to true (for whatever reason).
- The element's [`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) attribute is set, changed, or removed.
- The element's [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) changes.
- [A type change is signalled](#4105-the-input-element) for the element.
- The element [becomes connected](#214-dom-trees).

The [input activation behavior](#4105-the-input-element) is to run the following steps:
1. If the element is not [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree), then return.
2. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) at the element with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) and [`composed`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attributes initialized to true.
3. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`change`](#events) at the element with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true.

**Constraint validation**: If an element in the *[radio button group](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio)* is *[required](#410534-the-required-attribute)*, and all of the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements in the *[radio button group](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio)* have a [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) that is false, then the element is [suffering from being missing](#410211-definitions).

> [!example]
> The following example, for some reason, has specified that puppers are both [required](#410534-the-required-attribute) and [disabled](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute):
> 
> ```html
> <form>
>  <p><label><input type="radio" name="dog-type" value="pupper" required disabled> Pupper</label>
>  <p><label><input type="radio" name="dog-type" value="doggo"> Doggo</label>
>  <p><button>Make your choice</button>
> </form>
> ```
> 
> If the user tries to submit this form without first selecting "Doggo", then *both* [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements will be [suffering from being missing](#410211-definitions), since an element in the [radio button group](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio) is [required](#410534-the-required-attribute) (viz. the first element), and both of the elements in the radio button group have a false [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value).
> 
> On the other hand, if the user selects "Doggo" and then submits the form, then neither [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element will be [suffering from being missing](#410211-definitions), since while one of them is [required](#410534-the-required-attribute), not all of them have a false [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

> [!note]
> If none of the radio buttons in a [radio button group](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio) are checked, then they will all be initially unchecked in the interface, until such time as one of them is checked (either by the user or by script).

The following common [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element content attributes and IDL attributes [apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`checked`](#4105-the-input-element) and [`required`](#410534-the-required-attribute) content attributes; [`checked`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) and [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes.

The [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute is in mode [default/on](#41054-common-input-element-apis).

The [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) and [`change`](#events) events [apply](#4105-the-input-element).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`accept`](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile), [`alpha`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`alt`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute), [`colorspace`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`dirname`](#410192-submitting-element-directionality-the-dirname-attribute), [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes), [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute), [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`maxlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`minlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute), [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute), [`placeholder`](#4105310-the-placeholder-attribute), [`popovertarget`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`popovertargetaction`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`readonly`](#410533-the-readonly-attribute), [`size`](#410532-the-size-attribute), [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute), and [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes).

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`files`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`list`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionDirection`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`valueAsDate`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`valueAsNumber`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`setRangeText()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`setSelectionRange()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`stepDown()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`stepUp()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) methods.

###### 4.10.5.1.17 File Upload state (`type=file`)

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [File Upload](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a list of selected files, each file consisting of a filename, a file type, and a file body (the contents of the file).

Filenames must not contain [path components](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile), even in the case that a user has selected an entire directory hierarchy or multiple files with the same name from different directories. Path components, for the purposes of the [File Upload](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) state, are those parts of filenames that are separated by U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\) characters.

Unless the [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute) attribute is set, there must be no more than one file in the list of [selected files](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile).

The [input activation behavior](#4105-the-input-element) for such an element element is to [show the picker, if applicable](#41054-common-input-element-apis), for element.

If the element is [mutable](#410182-mutability), the user agent should allow the user to change the files on the list in other ways also, e.g., adding or removing files by drag-and-drop. When the user does so, the user agent must [update the file selection](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) for the element.

If the element is not [mutable](#410182-mutability), the user agent must not allow the user to change the element's selection.

To update the file selection for an element element:
1. [Queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [user interaction task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given element and the following steps:
   1. Update element's [selected files](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) so that it represents the user's selection.
   2. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) at the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element, with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) and [`composed`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attributes initialized to true.
   3. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`change`](#events) at the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element, with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true.

**Constraint validation**: If the element is *[required](#410534-the-required-attribute)* and the list of [selected files](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) is empty, then the element is [suffering from being missing](#410211-definitions).

---

The `accept` attribute may be specified to provide user agents with a hint of what file types will be accepted.

If specified, the attribute must consist of a [set of comma-separated tokens](#238-comma-separated-tokens), each of which must be an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for one of the following:

The string "`audio/*`"

Indicates that sound files are accepted.

The string "`video/*`"

Indicates that video files are accepted.

The string "`image/*`"

Indicates that image files are accepted.

A [valid MIME type string with no parameters](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-mime-type-with-no-parameters)

Indicates that files of the specified type are accepted.

A string whose first character is a U+002E FULL STOP character (.)

Indicates that files with the specified file extension are accepted.

The tokens must not be [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) matches for any of the other tokens (i.e. duplicates are not allowed). To obtain the list of tokens from the attribute, the user agent must [split the attribute value on commas](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).

User agents may use the value of this attribute to display a more appropriate user interface than a generic file picker. For instance, given the value `image/*`, a user agent could offer the user the option of using a local camera or selecting a photograph from their photo collection; given the value `audio/*`, a user agent could offer the user the option of recording a clip using a headset microphone.

User agents should prevent the user from selecting files that are not accepted by one (or more) of these tokens.

> [!note]
> Authors are encouraged to specify both any MIME types and any corresponding extensions when looking for data in a specific format.

> [!example]
> For example, consider an application that converts Microsoft Word documents to Open Document Format files. Since Microsoft Word documents are described with a wide variety of MIME types and extensions, the site can list several, as follows:
> 
> ```html
> <input type="file" accept=".doc,.docx,.xml,application/msword,application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document">
> ```
> 
> On platforms that only use file extensions to describe file types, the extensions listed here can be used to filter the allowed documents, while the MIME types can be used with the system's type registration table (mapping MIME types to extensions used by the system), if any, to determine any other extensions to allow. Similarly, on a system that does not have filenames or extensions but labels documents with MIME types internally, the MIME types can be used to pick the allowed files, while the extensions can be used if the system has an extension registration table that maps known extensions to MIME types used by the system.

> [!warning]
> Extensions tend to be ambiguous (e.g. there are an untold number of formats that use the "`.dat`" extension, and users can typically quite easily rename their files to have a "`.doc`" extension even if they are not Microsoft Word documents), and MIME types tend to be unreliable (e.g. many formats have no formally registered types, and many formats are in practice labeled using a number of different MIME types). Authors are reminded that, as usual, data received from a client should be treated with caution, as it may not be in an expected format even if the user is not hostile and the user agent fully obeyed the [`accept`](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) attribute's requirements.

> [!example]
> For historical reasons, the [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute prefixes the filename with the string "`C:\fakepath\`". Some legacy user agents actually included the full path (which was a security vulnerability). As a result of this, obtaining the filename from the [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute in a backwards-compatible way is non-trivial. The following function extracts the filename in a suitably compatible manner:
> 
> ```javascript
> function extractFilename(path) {
>   if (path.substr(0, 12) == "C:\\fakepath\\")
>     return path.substr(12); // modern browser
>   var x;
>   x = path.lastIndexOf('/');
>   if (x >= 0) // Unix-based path
>     return path.substr(x+1);
>   x = path.lastIndexOf('\\');
>   if (x >= 0) // Windows-based path
>     return path.substr(x+1);
>   return path; // just the filename
> }
> ```
> 
> This can be used as follows:
> 
> ```html
> <p><input type=file name=image onchange="updateFilename(this.value)"></p>
> <p>The name of the file you picked is: <span id="filename">(none)</span></p>
> <script>
>  function updateFilename(path) {
>    var name = extractFilename(path);
>    document.getElementById('filename').textContent = name;
>  }
> </script>
> ```

---

The following common [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element content attributes and IDL attributes [apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`accept`](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile), [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute), and [`required`](#410534-the-required-attribute) content attributes; [`files`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) and [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) method.

The [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute is in mode [filename](#41054-common-input-element-apis).

The [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) and [`change`](#events) events [apply](#4105-the-input-element).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`alpha`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`alt`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute), [`checked`](#4105-the-input-element), [`colorspace`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`dirname`](#410192-submitting-element-directionality-the-dirname-attribute), [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes), [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute), [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`maxlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`minlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute), [`popovertarget`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`popovertargetaction`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`placeholder`](#4105310-the-placeholder-attribute), [`readonly`](#410533-the-readonly-attribute), [`size`](#410532-the-size-attribute), [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute), and [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes).

The element's [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute must be omitted.

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`checked`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`list`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionDirection`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`valueAsDate`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`valueAsNumber`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`setRangeText()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`setSelectionRange()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`stepDown()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`stepUp()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) methods.

###### 4.10.5.1.18 Submit Button state (`type=submit`)

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Submit Button](#4105118-submit-button-state-typesubmit) state, the rules in this section apply.

[![(This is a tracking vector.)](https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg)](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#24-privacy-concerns) The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a button that, when activated, submits the form. If the element has a [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute, the button's label must be the value of that attribute; otherwise, it must be an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) string that means "Submit" or some such. The element is a [button](#4102-categories), specifically a [submit button](#4102-categories).

> [!note]
> Since the default label is [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology), and the width of the button typically depends on the button's label, the button's width can leak a few bits of fingerprintable information. These bits are likely to be strongly correlated to the identity of the user agent and the user's locale.

The element's [optional value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is the value of the element's [`value`](#4106-the-button-element) attribute, if there is one; otherwise null.

The element's [input activation behavior](#4105-the-input-element) given event is as follows:
1. If the element does not have a [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms), then return.
2. If the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents), then return.
3. [Submit](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) the element's [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) from the element with *[userInvolvement](#410223-form-submission-algorithm)* set to event's [user navigation involvement](#7421-supporting-concepts).

The [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), and [`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) attributes are [attributes for form submission](#410196-form-submission-attributes).

> [!note]
> The [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) attribute can be used to make submit buttons that do not trigger the constraint validation.

The following common [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element content attributes and IDL attributes [apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`dirname`](#410192-submitting-element-directionality-the-dirname-attribute), [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`popovertarget`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), and [`popovertargetaction`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes) content attributes; [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute.

The [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute is in mode [default](#41054-common-input-element-apis).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`accept`](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile), [`alpha`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`alt`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute), [`checked`](#4105-the-input-element), [`colorspace`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes), [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute), [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`maxlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`minlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute), [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute), [`placeholder`](#4105310-the-placeholder-attribute), [`readonly`](#410533-the-readonly-attribute), [`required`](#410534-the-required-attribute), [`size`](#410532-the-size-attribute), [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute), and [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes).

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`checked`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`files`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`list`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionDirection`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`valueAsDate`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`valueAsNumber`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`setRangeText()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`setSelectionRange()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`stepDown()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`stepUp()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) methods.

The [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) and [`change`](#events) events [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element).

###### 4.10.5.1.19 Image Button state (`type=image`)

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Image Button](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) either an image from which a user can select a coordinate and submit the form, or alternatively a button from which the user can submit the form. The element is a [button](#4102-categories), specifically a [submit button](#4102-categories).

> [!note]
> The coordinate is sent to the server [during form submission](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) by sending two entries for the element, derived from the name of the control but with "`.x`" and "`.y`" appended to the name with the x and y components of the coordinate respectively.

---

The image is given by the `src` attribute. The [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) attribute must be present, and must contain a [valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#241-terminology) referencing a non-interactive, optionally animated, image resource that is neither paged nor scripted.

When any of these events occur:
- the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is first set to the [Image Button](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) state (possibly when the element is first created), and the [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) attribute is present
- the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is changed back to the [Image Button](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) state, and the [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) attribute is present, and its value has changed since the last time the [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute was in the [Image Button](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) state
- the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Image Button](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) state, and the [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) attribute is set or changed

then unless the user agent cannot support images, or its support for images has been disabled, or the user agent only fetches images on demand, or the [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) attribute's value is the empty string, run these steps:
1. Let url be the result of [encoding-parsing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given the [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) attribute's value, relative to the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
2. If url is failure, then return.
3. Let request be a new [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) whose [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url) is url, [client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client) is the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant), [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) is "`image`", [initiator type](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-initiator-type) is "`input`", [credentials mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode) is "`include`", and whose [use-URL-credentials flag](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-use-url-credentials-flag) is set.
4. [Fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request, with *[processResponseEndOfBody](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-processresponseendofbody)* set to the following steps given [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response:
   1. If the download was successful and the image is *[available](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage)*, [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [user interaction task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`load`](#events) at the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element.
   2. Otherwise, if the fetching process fails without a response from the remote server, or completes but the image is not a valid or supported image, then [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [user interaction task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) on the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element.

Fetching the image must [delay the load event](#1327-the-end) of the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) until the [task](#8171-definitions) that is [queued](#8172-queuing-tasks) by the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) once the resource has been fetched (defined below) has been run.

If the image was successfully obtained, with no network errors, and the image's type is a supported image type, and the image is a valid image of that type, then the image is said to be *available*. If this is true before the image is completely downloaded, each [task](#8171-definitions) that is [queued](#8172-queuing-tasks) by the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) while the image is being fetched must update the presentation of the image appropriately.

The user agent should apply the [image sniffing rules](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#rules-for-sniffing-images-specifically) to determine the type of the image, with the image's [associated Content-Type headers](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource) giving the official type. If these rules are not applied, then the type of the image must be the type given by the image's [associated Content-Type headers](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource).

User agents must not support non-image resources with the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element. User agents must not run executable code embedded in the image resource. User agents must only display the first page of a multipage resource. User agents must not allow the resource to act in an interactive fashion, but should honor any animation in the resource.

---

The `alt` attribute provides the textual label for the button for users and user agents who cannot use the image. The [`alt`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) attribute must be present, and must contain a non-empty string giving the label that would be appropriate for an equivalent button if the image was unavailable.

The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element supports [dimension attributes](#4817-dimension-attributes).

---

If the [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) attribute is set, and the image is *[available](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage)* and the user agent is configured to display that image, then the element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a control for selecting a [coordinate](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) from the image specified by the [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) attribute. In that case, if the element is [mutable](#410182-mutability), the user agent should allow the user to select this [coordinate](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage).

Otherwise, the element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a submit button whose label is given by the value of the [`alt`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) attribute.

The element's [input activation behavior](#4105-the-input-element) given event is as follows:
1. If the element does not have a [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms), then return.
2. If the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents), then return.
3. If the user activated the control while explicitly selecting a coordinate, then set the element's [selected coordinate](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) to that coordinate.

   > [!note]
   > This is only possible under the conditions outlined above, when the element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a control for selecting such a coordinate. Even then, the user might activate the control without explicitly selecting a coordinate.

4. [Submit](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) the element's [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) from the element with *[userInvolvement](#410223-form-submission-algorithm)* set to event's [user navigation involvement](#7421-supporting-concepts).

The element's selected coordinate consists of an x-component and a y-component. It is initially (0, 0). The coordinates represent the position relative to the edge of the element's image, with the coordinate space having the positive x direction to the right, and the positive y direction downwards.

The x-component must be a [valid integer](#2341-signed-integers) representing a number x in the range −(borderleft+paddingleft) ≤ x ≤ width+borderright+paddingright, where width is the rendered width of the image, borderleft is the width of the border on the left of the image, paddingleft is the width of the padding on the left of the image, borderright is the width of the border on the right of the image, and paddingright is the width of the padding on the right of the image, with all dimensions given in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px).

The y-component must be a [valid integer](#2341-signed-integers) representing a number y in the range −(bordertop+paddingtop) ≤ y ≤ height+borderbottom+paddingbottom, where height is the rendered height of the image, bordertop is the width of the border above the image, paddingtop is the width of the padding above the image, borderbottom is the width of the border below the image, and paddingbottom is the width of the padding below the image, with all dimensions given in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px).

Where a border or padding is missing, its width is zero [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px).

---

The [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), and [`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) attributes are [attributes for form submission](#410196-form-submission-attributes).

`image.width [ = value ]`

`image.height [ = value ]`

These attributes return the rendered dimensions of the image. When the image is not being rendered, they return the [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes) and [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes) content attributes' values, defaulting to the image's [natural dimensions](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions), if any; otherwise 0.

They can be set, to change the corresponding content attributes.

The following common [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element content attributes and IDL attributes [apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`alt`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes), [`popovertarget`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`popovertargetaction`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes), [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), and [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes) content attributes; [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute.

The [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute is in mode [default](#41054-common-input-element-apis).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`accept`](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile), [`alpha`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute), [`checked`](#4105-the-input-element), [`colorspace`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`dirname`](#410192-submitting-element-directionality-the-dirname-attribute), [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute), [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`maxlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`minlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute), [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute), [`placeholder`](#4105310-the-placeholder-attribute), [`readonly`](#410533-the-readonly-attribute), [`required`](#410534-the-required-attribute), [`size`](#410532-the-size-attribute), and [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute).

The element's [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute must be omitted.

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`checked`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`files`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`list`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionDirection`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`valueAsDate`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`valueAsNumber`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`setRangeText()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`setSelectionRange()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`stepDown()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`stepUp()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) methods.

The [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) and [`change`](#events) events [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element).

> [!note]
> Many aspects of this state's behavior are similar to the behavior of the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element. Readers are encouraged to read that section, where many of the same requirements are described in more detail.

> [!example]
> Take the following form:
> 
> ```html
> <form action="process.cgi">
>  <input type=image src=map.png name=where alt="Show location list">
> </form>
> ```
> 
> If the user clicked on the image at coordinate (127,40) then the URL used to submit the form would be "`process.cgi?where.x=127&where.y=40`".
> 
> (In this example, it's assumed that for users who don't see the map, and who instead just see a button labeled "Show location list", clicking the button will cause the server to show a list of locations to pick from instead of the map.)

###### 4.10.5.1.20 Reset Button state (`type=reset`)

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Reset Button](#4105120-reset-button-state-typereset) state, the rules in this section apply.

[![(This is a tracking vector.)](https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg)](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#24-privacy-concerns) The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a button that, when activated, resets the form. If the element has a [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute, the button's label must be the value of that attribute; otherwise, it must be an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) string that means "Reset" or some such. The element is a [button](#4102-categories).

> [!note]
> Since the default label is [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology), and the width of the button typically depends on the button's label, the button's width can leak a few bits of fingerprintable information. These bits are likely to be strongly correlated to the identity of the user agent and the user's locale.

The element's [input activation behavior](#4105-the-input-element) is as follows:
1. If the element does not have a [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms), then return.
2. If the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents), then return.
3. [Reset](#41023-resetting-a-form) the [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) from the element.

**Constraint validation**: The element is [barred from constraint validation](#410211-definitions).

The [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute [applies](#4105-the-input-element) to this element and is in mode [default](#41054-common-input-element-apis).

The following common [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element content attributes [apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`popovertarget`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes) and [`popovertargetaction`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`accept`](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile), [`alpha`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`alt`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute), [`checked`](#4105-the-input-element), [`colorspace`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`dirname`](#410192-submitting-element-directionality-the-dirname-attribute), [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes), [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute), [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`maxlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`minlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute), [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute), [`placeholder`](#4105310-the-placeholder-attribute), [`readonly`](#410533-the-readonly-attribute), [`required`](#410534-the-required-attribute), [`size`](#410532-the-size-attribute), [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute), and [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes).

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`checked`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`files`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`list`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionDirection`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`valueAsDate`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`valueAsNumber`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`setRangeText()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`setSelectionRange()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`stepDown()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`stepUp()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) methods.

The [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) and [`change`](#events) events [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element).

###### 4.10.5.1.21 Button state (`type=button`)

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Button](#4105121-button-state-typebutton) state, the rules in this section apply.

The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a button with no default behavior. A label for the button must be provided in the [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute, though it may be the empty string. If the element has a [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute, the button's label must be the value of that attribute; otherwise, it must be the empty string. The element is a [button](#4102-categories).

The element has no [input activation behavior](#4105-the-input-element).

**Constraint validation**: The element is [barred from constraint validation](#410211-definitions).

The [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute [applies](#4105-the-input-element) to this element and is in mode [default](#41054-common-input-element-apis).

The following common [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element content attributes [apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`popovertarget`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes) and [`popovertargetaction`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes).

The following content attributes must not be specified and [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`accept`](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile), [`alpha`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`alt`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute), [`checked`](#4105-the-input-element), [`colorspace`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor), [`dirname`](#410192-submitting-element-directionality-the-dirname-attribute), [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes), [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute), [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`maxlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), [`minlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute), [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute), [`placeholder`](#4105310-the-placeholder-attribute), [`readonly`](#410533-the-readonly-attribute), [`required`](#410534-the-required-attribute), [`size`](#410532-the-size-attribute), [`src`](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage), [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute), and [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes).

The following IDL attributes and methods [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the element: [`checked`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`files`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`list`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionDirection`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`valueAsDate`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`valueAsNumber`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attributes; [`select()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`setRangeText()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`setSelectionRange()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`stepDown()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and [`stepUp()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) methods.

The [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) and [`change`](#events) events [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element).

##### 4.10.5.2 Implementation notes regarding localization of form controls

*This section is non-normative.*

The formats shown to the user in date, time, and number controls is independent of the format used for form submission.

Browsers are encouraged to use user interfaces that present dates, times, and numbers according to the conventions of either the locale implied by the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [language](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes) or the user's preferred locale. Using the page's locale will ensure consistency with page-provided data.

> [!example]
> For example, it would be confusing to users if an American English page claimed that a Cirque De Soleil show was going to be showing on 02/03, but their browser, configured to use the British English locale, only showed the date 03/02 in the ticket purchase date picker. Using the page's locale would at least ensure that the date was presented in the same format everywhere. (There's still a risk that the user would end up arriving a month late, of course, but there's only so much that can be done about such cultural differences...)

##### 4.10.5.3 Common [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element attributes
