These attributes only [apply](#4105-the-input-element) to an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element if its [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in a state whose definition declares that the attribute [applies](#4105-the-input-element). When an attribute [doesn't apply](#4105-the-input-element) to an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element, user agents must [ignore](#214-dom-trees) the attribute, regardless of the requirements and definitions below.

###### 4.10.5.3.1 The [`maxlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes) and [`minlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes) attributes

The `maxlength` attribute, when it [applies](#4105-the-input-element), is a [form control `maxlength` attribute](#410193-limiting-user-input-length-the-maxlength-attribute).

The `minlength` attribute, when it [applies](#4105-the-input-element), is a [form control `minlength` attribute](#410194-setting-minimum-input-length-requirements-the-minlength-attribute).

If the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element has a [maximum allowed value length](#410193-limiting-user-input-length-the-maxlength-attribute), then the [length](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) of the value of the element's [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute must be less than or equal to the element's [maximum allowed value length](#410193-limiting-user-input-length-the-maxlength-attribute).

> [!example]
> The following extract shows how a messaging client's text entry could be arbitrarily restricted to a fixed number of characters, thus forcing any conversation through this medium to be terse and discouraging intelligent discourse.
> 
> ```html
> <label>What are you doing? <input name=status maxlength=140></label>
> ```

> [!example]
> Here, a password is given a minimum length:
> 
> ```html
> <p><label>Username: <input name=u required></label>
> <p><label>Password: <input name=p required minlength=12></label>
> ```

###### 4.10.5.3.2 The [`size`](#410532-the-size-attribute) attribute

The `size` attribute gives the number of characters that, in a visual rendering, the user agent is to allow the user to see while editing the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

The [`size`](#410532-the-size-attribute) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers) greater than zero.

If the attribute is present, then its value must be parsed using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers), and if the result is a number greater than zero, then the user agent should ensure that at least that many characters are visible.

The [`size`](#4105-the-input-element) IDL attribute is [limited to only positive numbers](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) and has a [default value](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) of 20.

###### 4.10.5.3.3 The [`readonly`](#410533-the-readonly-attribute) attribute

The `readonly` attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes) that controls whether or not the user can edit the form control. When specified, the element is not [mutable](#410182-mutability).

**Constraint validation**: If the [`readonly`](#410533-the-readonly-attribute) attribute is specified on an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element, the element is [barred from constraint validation](#410211-definitions).

> [!note]
> The difference between [`disabled`](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute) and [`readonly`](#410533-the-readonly-attribute) is that read-only controls can still function, whereas disabled controls generally do not function as controls until they are enabled. This is spelled out in more detail elsewhere in this specification with normative requirements that refer to the [disabled](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute) concept (for example, the element's [activation behavior](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget), whether or not it is a [focusable area](#662-data-model), or when [constructing the entry list](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list)). Any other behavior related to user interaction with disabled controls, such as whether text can be selected or copied, is not defined in this standard.
> 
> Only text controls can be made read-only, since for other controls (such as checkboxes and buttons) there is no useful distinction between being read-only and being disabled, so the [`readonly`](#410533-the-readonly-attribute) attribute [does not apply](#4105-the-input-element).

> [!example]
> In the following example, the existing product identifiers cannot be modified, but they are still displayed as part of the form, for consistency with the row representing a new product (where the identifier is not yet filled in).
> 
> ```html
> <form action="products.cgi" method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data">
>  <table>
>   <tr> <th> Product ID <th> Product name <th> Price <th> Action
>   <tr>
>    <td> <input readonly="readonly" name="1.pid" value="H412">
>    <td> <input required="required" name="1.pname" value="Floor lamp Ulke">
>    <td> $<input required="required" type="number" min="0" step="0.01" name="1.pprice" value="49.99">
>    <td> <button formnovalidate="formnovalidate" name="action" value="delete:1">Delete</button>
>   <tr>
>    <td> <input readonly="readonly" name="2.pid" value="FG28">
>    <td> <input required="required" name="2.pname" value="Table lamp Ulke">
>    <td> $<input required="required" type="number" min="0" step="0.01" name="2.pprice" value="24.99">
>    <td> <button formnovalidate="formnovalidate" name="action" value="delete:2">Delete</button>
>   <tr>
>    <td> <input required="required" name="3.pid" value="" pattern="[A-Z0-9]+">
>    <td> <input required="required" name="3.pname" value="">
>    <td> $<input required="required" type="number" min="0" step="0.01" name="3.pprice" value="">
>    <td> <button formnovalidate="formnovalidate" name="action" value="delete:3">Delete</button>
>  </table>
>  <p> <button formnovalidate="formnovalidate" name="action" value="add">Add</button> </p>
>  <p> <button name="action" value="update">Save</button> </p>
> </form>
> ```

###### 4.10.5.3.4 The [`required`](#410534-the-required-attribute) attribute

The `required` attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes). When specified, the element is *required*.

**Constraint validation**: If the element is *[required](#410534-the-required-attribute)*, and its [`value`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) IDL attribute [applies](#4105-the-input-element) and is in the mode [value](#41054-common-input-element-apis), and the element is [mutable](#410182-mutability), and the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is the empty string, then the element is [suffering from being missing](#410211-definitions).

> [!example]
> The following form has two required fields, one for an email address and one for a password. It also has a third field that is only considered valid if the user types the same password in the password field and this third field.
> 
> ```html
> <h1>Create new account</h1>
> <form action="/newaccount" method=post
>       oninput="up2.setCustomValidity(up2.value != up.value ? 'Passwords do not match.' : '')">
>  <p>
>   <label for="username">Email address:</label>
>   <input id="username" type=email required name=un>
>  <p>
>   <label for="password1">Password:</label>
>   <input id="password1" type=password required name=up>
>  <p>
>   <label for="password2">Confirm password:</label>
>   <input id="password2" type=password name=up2>
>  <p>
>   <input type=submit value="Create account">
> </form>
> ```

> [!example]
> For radio buttons, the [`required`](#410534-the-required-attribute) attribute is satisfied if any of the radio buttons in the [group](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio) is selected. Thus, in the following example, any of the radio buttons can be checked, not just the one marked as required:
> 
> ```html
> <fieldset>
>  <legend>Did the movie pass the Bechdel test?</legend>
>  <p><label><input type="radio" name="bechdel" value="no-characters"> No, there are not even two female characters in the movie. </label>
>  <p><label><input type="radio" name="bechdel" value="no-names"> No, the female characters never talk to each other. </label>
>  <p><label><input type="radio" name="bechdel" value="no-topic"> No, when female characters talk to each other it's always about a male character. </label>
>  <p><label><input type="radio" name="bechdel" value="yes" required> Yes. </label>
>  <p><label><input type="radio" name="bechdel" value="unknown"> I don't know. </label>
> </fieldset>
> ```
> 
> To avoid confusion as to whether a [radio button group](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio) is required or not, authors are encouraged to specify the attribute on all the radio buttons in a group. Indeed, in general, authors are encouraged to avoid having radio button groups that do not have any initially checked controls in the first place, as this is a state that the user cannot return to, and is therefore generally considered a poor user interface.

###### 4.10.5.3.5 The [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute) attribute

The `multiple` attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes) that indicates whether the user is to be allowed to specify more than one value.

> [!example]
> The following extract shows how an email client's "To" field could accept multiple email addresses.
> 
> ```html
> <label>To: <input type=email multiple name=to></label>
> ```
> 
> If the user had, amongst many friends in their user contacts database, two friends "Spider-Man" (with address "spider@parker.example.net") and "Scarlet Witch" (with address "scarlet@avengers.example.net"), then, after the user has typed "s", the user agent might suggest these two email addresses to the user.
> 
> ![](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/sample-email-1.svg)
> 
> The page could also link in the user's contacts database from the site:
> 
> ```html
> <label>To: <input type=email multiple name=to list=contacts></label>
> ...
> <datalist id="contacts">
>  <option value="hedral@damowmow.com">
>  <option value="pillar@example.com">
>  <option value="astrophy@cute.example">
>  <option value="astronomy@science.example.org">
> </datalist>
> ```
> 
> Suppose the user had entered "bob@example.net" into this text control, and then started typing a second email address starting with "s". The user agent might show both the two friends mentioned earlier, as well as the "astrophy" and "astronomy" values given in the [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element.
> 
> ![](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/sample-email-2.svg)

> [!example]
> The following extract shows how an email client's "Attachments" field could accept multiple files for upload.
> 
> ```html
> <label>Attachments: <input type=file multiple name=att></label>
> ```

###### 4.10.5.3.6 The [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute) attribute

The `pattern` attribute specifies a regular expression against which the control's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value), or, when the [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute) attribute [applies](#4105-the-input-element) and is set, the control's [values](#410181-a-form-controls-value), are to be checked.

If specified, the attribute's value must match the JavaScript *[Pattern](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#prod-Pattern)*`[+UnicodeSetsMode, +N]` production.

The compiled pattern regular expression of an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element, if it exists, is a JavaScript [`RegExp`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-regexp-regular-expression-objects) object. It is determined as follows:
1. If the element does not have a [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute) attribute specified, then return nothing. The element has no [compiled pattern regular expression](#410536-the-pattern-attribute).
2. Let pattern be the value of the [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute) attribute of the element.
3. Let regexpCompletion be [RegExpCreate](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-regexpcreate)(pattern, "`v`").
4. If regexpCompletion is an [abrupt completion](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type), then return nothing. The element has no [compiled pattern regular expression](#410536-the-pattern-attribute).

   > [!note]
   > User agents are encouraged to log this error in a developer console, to aid debugging.

5. Let anchoredPattern be the string "`^(?:`", followed by pattern, followed by "`)$`".
6. Return ! [RegExpCreate](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-regexpcreate)(anchoredPattern, "`v`").

> [!note]
> The reasoning behind these steps, instead of just using the value of the [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute) attribute directly, is twofold. First, we want to ensure that when matched against a string, the regular expression's start is anchored to the start of the string and its end to the end of the string. Second, we want to ensure that the regular expression is valid in standalone form, instead of only becoming valid after being surrounded by the "`^(?:`" and "`)$`" anchors.

A [`RegExp`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-regexp-regular-expression-objects) object regexp matches a string input, if ! [RegExpBuiltinExec](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-regexpbuiltinexec)(regexp, input) is not null.

**Constraint validation**: If the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is not the empty string, and either the element's [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute) attribute is not specified or it [does not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element given its [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute's current state, and the element has a [compiled pattern regular expression](#410536-the-pattern-attribute) but that regular expression does not [match](#410536-the-pattern-attribute) the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value), then the element is [suffering from a pattern mismatch](#410211-definitions).

**Constraint validation**: If the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is not the empty string, and the element's [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute) attribute is specified and [applies](#4105-the-input-element) to the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element, and the element has a [compiled pattern regular expression](#410536-the-pattern-attribute) but that regular expression does not [match](#410536-the-pattern-attribute) each of the element's [values](#410181-a-form-controls-value), then the element is [suffering from a pattern mismatch](#410211-definitions).

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element has a [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute) attribute specified, authors should include a `title` attribute to give a description of the pattern. User agents may use the contents of this attribute, if it is present, when informing the user that the pattern is not matched, or at any other suitable time, such as in a tooltip or read out by assistive technology when the control [gains focus](#662-data-model).

> [!example]
> For example, the following snippet:
> 
> ```html
> <label> Part number:
>  <input pattern="[0-9][A-Z]{3}" name="part"
>         title="A part number is a digit followed by three uppercase letters."/>
> </label>
> ```
> 
> ...could cause the UA to display an alert such as:
> 
> ```
> A part number is a digit followed by three uppercase letters.
> You cannot submit this form when the field is incorrect.
> ```

When a control has a [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute) attribute, the [`title`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute) attribute, if used, must describe the pattern. Additional information could also be included, so long as it assists the user in filling in the control. Otherwise, assistive technology would be impaired.

> [!example]
> For instance, if the title attribute contained the caption of the control, assistive technology could end up saying something like The text you have entered does not match the required pattern. Birthday, which is not useful.

UAs may still show the [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) in non-error situations (for example, as a tooltip when hovering over the control), so authors should be careful not to word [`title`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute)s as if an error has necessarily occurred.

###### 4.10.5.3.7 The [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) and [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attributes

Some form controls can have explicit constraints applied limiting the allowed range of values that the user can provide. Normally, such a range would be linear and continuous. A form control can have a periodic domain, however, in which case the form control's broadest possible range is finite, and authors can specify explicit ranges within it that span the boundaries.

> [!example]
> Specifically, the broadest range of a [`type=time`](#4105110-time-state-typetime) control is midnight to midnight (24 hours), and authors can set both continuous linear ranges (such as 9pm to 11pm) and discontinuous ranges spanning midnight (such as 11pm to 1am).

The `min` and `max` attributes indicate the allowed range of values for the element.

Their syntax is defined by the section that defines the [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute's current state.

If the element has a [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attribute, and the result of applying the [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#4105-the-input-element) to the value of the [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attribute is a number, then that number is the element's minimum; otherwise, if the [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute's current state defines a default minimum, then that is the [minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes); otherwise, the element has no [minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes).

The [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attribute also defines the [step base](#410538-the-step-attribute).

If the element has a [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attribute, and the result of applying the [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#4105-the-input-element) to the value of the [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attribute is a number, then that number is the element's maximum; otherwise, if the [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute's current state defines a default maximum, then that is the [maximum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes); otherwise, the element has no [maximum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes).

If the element does not [have a periodic domain](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), the [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attribute's value (the [maximum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes)) must not be less than the [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attribute's value (its [minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes)).

> [!note]
> If an element that does not [have a periodic domain](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) has a [maximum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) that is less than its [minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), then so long as the element has a [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value), it will either be [suffering from an underflow](#410211-definitions) or [suffering from an overflow](#410211-definitions).

An element has a reversed range if it [has a periodic domain](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) and its [maximum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) is less than its [minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes).

An element has range limitations if it has a defined [minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) or a defined [maximum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes).

**Constraint validation**: When the element has a [minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) and does not [have a reversed range](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), and the result of applying the [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#4105-the-input-element) to the string given by the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is a number, and the number obtained from that algorithm is less than the [minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), the element is [suffering from an underflow](#410211-definitions).

**Constraint validation**: When the element has a [maximum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) and does not [have a reversed range](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), and the result of applying the [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#4105-the-input-element) to the string given by the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is a number, and the number obtained from that algorithm is more than the [maximum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), the element is [suffering from an overflow](#410211-definitions).

**Constraint validation**: When an element [has a reversed range](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), and the result of applying the [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#4105-the-input-element) to the string given by the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is a number, and the number obtained from that algorithm is more than the [maximum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) *and* less than the [minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), the element is simultaneously [suffering from an underflow](#410211-definitions) and [suffering from an overflow](#410211-definitions).

> [!example]
> The following date control limits input to dates that are before the 1980s:
> 
> ```html
> <input name=bday type=date max="1979-12-31">
> ```

> [!example]
> The following number control limits input to whole numbers greater than zero:
> 
> ```html
> <input name=quantity required="" type="number" min="1" value="1">
> ```

> [!example]
> The following time control limits input to those minutes that occur between 9pm and 6am, defaulting to midnight:
> 
> ```html
> <input name="sleepStart" type=time min="21:00" max="06:00" step="60" value="00:00">
> ```

###### 4.10.5.3.8 The [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute) attribute

The `step` attribute indicates the granularity that is expected (and required) of the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) or [values](#410181-a-form-controls-value), by limiting the allowed values. The section that defines the [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute's current state also defines the default step, the step scale factor, and in some cases the default step base, which are used in processing the attribute as described below.

The [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute) attribute, if specified, must either have a value that is a [valid floating-point number](#2343-floating-point-numbers) that [parses](#2343-floating-point-numbers) to a number that is greater than zero, or must have a value that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`any`".

The attribute provides the allowed value step for the element, as follows:
1. If the attribute does not [apply](#4105-the-input-element), then there is no [allowed value step](#410538-the-step-attribute).
2. Otherwise, if the attribute is absent, then the [allowed value step](#410538-the-step-attribute) is the [default step](#410538-the-step-attribute) multiplied by the [step scale factor](#410538-the-step-attribute).
3. Otherwise, if the attribute's value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`any`", then there is no [allowed value step](#410538-the-step-attribute).
4. Otherwise, if the [rules for parsing floating-point number values](#2343-floating-point-numbers), when they are applied to the attribute's value, return an error, zero, or a number less than zero, then the [allowed value step](#410538-the-step-attribute) is the [default step](#410538-the-step-attribute) multiplied by the [step scale factor](#410538-the-step-attribute).
5. Otherwise, the [allowed value step](#410538-the-step-attribute) is the number returned by the [rules for parsing floating-point number values](#2343-floating-point-numbers) when they are applied to the attribute's value, multiplied by the [step scale factor](#410538-the-step-attribute).

The step base is the value returned by the following algorithm:
1. If the element has a [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) content attribute, and the result of applying the [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#4105-the-input-element) to the value of the [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) content attribute is not an error, then return that result.
2. If the element has a [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) content attribute, and the result of applying the [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#4105-the-input-element) to the value of the [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) content attribute is not an error, then return that result.
3. If a [default step base](#410538-the-step-attribute) is defined for this element given its [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute's state, then return it.
4. Return zero.

**Constraint validation**: When the element has an [allowed value step](#410538-the-step-attribute), and the result of applying the [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#4105-the-input-element) to the string given by the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is a number, and that number subtracted from the [step base](#410538-the-step-attribute) is not an integral multiple of the [allowed value step](#410538-the-step-attribute), the element is [suffering from a step mismatch](#410211-definitions).

> [!example]
> The following range control only accepts values in the range 0..1, and allows 256 steps in that range:
> 
> ```html
> <input name=opacity type=range min=0 max=1 step=0.00392156863>
> ```

> [!example]
> The following control allows any time in the day to be selected, with any accuracy (e.g. thousandth-of-a-second accuracy or more):
> 
> ```html
> <input name=favtime type=time step=any>
> ```
> 
> Normally, time controls are limited to an accuracy of one minute.

###### 4.10.5.3.9 The [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute) attribute

The `list` attribute is used to identify an element that lists predefined options suggested to the user.

If present, its value must be the [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) of a [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element in the same [tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).

The suggestions source element is the first element in the [tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) to have an [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) equal to the value of the [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute) attribute, if that element is a [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element. If there is no [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute) attribute, or if there is no element with that [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), or if the first element with that [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) is not a [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element, then there is no [suggestions source element](#410539-the-list-attribute).

If there is a [suggestions source element](#410539-the-list-attribute), then, when the user agent is allowing the user to edit the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value), the user agent should offer the suggestions represented by the [suggestions source element](#410539-the-list-attribute) to the user in a manner suitable for the type of control used. If appropriate, the user agent should use the suggestion's [label](#41010-the-option-element) and [value](#41010-the-option-element) to identify the suggestion to the user.

User agents are encouraged to filter the suggestions represented by the [suggestions source element](#410539-the-list-attribute) when the number of suggestions is large, including only the most relevant ones (e.g. based on the user's input so far). No precise threshold is defined, but capping the list at four to seven values is reasonable. If filtering based on the user's input, user agents should search within both the [label](#41010-the-option-element) and [value](#41010-the-option-element) of the suggestions for matches. User agents should consider how input variations affect the matching process. Unicode normalization should be applied so that different underlying Unicode code point sequences, caused by different keyboard- or input-specific mechanisms, do not interfere with the matching process. Case variations should be ignored, which may require language-specific case mapping. For examples of these, see Character Model for the World Wide Web: String Matching. User agents may also provide other matching features: for illustration, a few examples include matching different forms of kana to each other (or to kanji), ignoring accents, or applying spelling correction. [\[CHARMODNORM\]](#references)

> [!example]
> This text field allows you to choose a type of JavaScript function.
> 
> ```html
> <input type="text" list="function-types">
> <datalist id="function-types">
>   <option value="function">function</option>
>   <option value="async function">async function</option>
>   <option value="function*">generator function</option>
>   <option value="=>">arrow function</option>
>   <option value="async =>">async arrow function</option>
>   <option value="async function*">async generator function</option>
> </datalist>
> ```
> 
> For user agents that follow the above suggestions, both the [label](#41010-the-option-element) and [value](#41010-the-option-element) would be shown:
> 
> ![A text box with a drop down button on the right hand side; with, below, a drop down box containing a list of the six values the left and the six labels on the right.](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/sample-datalist.svg)
> 
> Then, typing "arrow" or "=>" would filter the list to the entries with labels "arrow function" and "async arrow function". Typing "generator" or "\*" would filter the list to the entries with labels "generator function" and "async generator function".

> [!note]
> As always, user agents are free to make user interface decisions which are appropriate for their particular requirements and for the user's particular circumstances. However, this has historically been an area of confusion for implementers, web developers, and users alike, so we've given some "should" suggestions above.

How user selections of suggestions are handled depends on whether the element is a control accepting a single value only, or whether it accepts multiple values:

If the element does not have a [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute) attribute specified or if the [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute) attribute [does not apply](#4105-the-input-element)

When the user selects a suggestion, the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) must be set to the selected suggestion's [value](#41010-the-option-element), as if the user had written that value themself.

If the element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Email](#410515-email-state-typeemail) state and the element has a [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute) attribute specified

When the user selects a suggestion, the user agent must either add a new entry to the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [values](#410181-a-form-controls-value), whose value is the selected suggestion's [value](#41010-the-option-element), or change an existing entry in the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [values](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to have the value given by the selected suggestion's [value](#41010-the-option-element), as if the user had themself added an entry with that value, or edited an existing entry to be that value. Which behavior is to be applied depends on the user interface in an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) manner.

---

If the [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute) attribute [does not apply](#4105-the-input-element), there is no [suggestions source element](#410539-the-list-attribute).

> [!example]
> This URL field offers some suggestions.
> 
> ```html
> <label>Homepage: <input name=hp type=url list=hpurls></label>
> <datalist id=hpurls>
>  <option value="https://www.google.com/" label="Google">
>  <option value="https://www.reddit.com/" label="Reddit">
> </datalist>
> ```
> 
> Other URLs from the user's history might show also; this is up to the user agent.

> [!example]
> This example demonstrates how to design a form that uses the autocompletion list feature while still degrading usefully in legacy user agents.
> 
> If the autocompletion list is merely an aid, and is not important to the content, then simply using a [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element with children [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements is enough. To prevent the values from being rendered in legacy user agents, they need to be placed inside the [`value`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute instead of inline.
> 
> ```html
> <p>
>  <label>
>   Enter a breed:
>   <input type="text" name="breed" list="breeds">
>   <datalist id="breeds">
>    <option value="Abyssinian">
>    <option value="Alpaca">
>    <!-- ... -->
>   </datalist>
>  </label>
> </p>
> ```
> 
> However, if the values need to be shown in legacy UAs, then fallback content can be placed inside the [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element, as follows:
> 
> ```html
> <p>
>  <label>
>   Enter a breed:
>   <input type="text" name="breed" list="breeds">
>  </label>
>  <datalist id="breeds">
>   <label>
>    or select one from the list:
>    <select name="breed">
>     <option value=""> (none selected)
>     <option>Abyssinian
>     <option>Alpaca
>     <!-- ... -->
>    </select>
>   </label>
>  </datalist>
> </p>
> ```
> 
> The fallback content will only be shown in UAs that don't support [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element). The options, on the other hand, will be detected by all UAs, even though they are not children of the [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element.
> 
> Note that if an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element used in a [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) is [`selected`](#41010-the-option-element), it will be selected by default by legacy UAs (because it affects the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element), but it will not have any effect on the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element in UAs that support [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element).

###### 4.10.5.3.10 The [`placeholder`](#4105310-the-placeholder-attribute) attribute

The `placeholder` attribute represents a *short* hint (a word or short phrase) intended to aid the user with data entry when the control has no value. A hint could be a sample value or a brief description of the expected format. The attribute, if specified, must have a value that contains no U+000A LINE FEED (LF) or U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) characters.

The [`placeholder`](#4105310-the-placeholder-attribute) attribute should not be used as an alternative to a [`label`](#4104-the-label-element). For a longer hint or other advisory text, the [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute is more appropriate.

> [!note]
> These mechanisms are very similar but subtly different: the hint given by the control's [`label`](#4104-the-label-element) is shown at all times; the short hint given in the [`placeholder`](#4105310-the-placeholder-attribute) attribute is shown before the user enters a value; and the hint in the [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute is shown when the user requests further help.

User agents should present this hint to the user, after having [stripped newlines](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) from it, when the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is the empty string, especially if the control is not [focused](#662-data-model).

If a user agent normally doesn't show this hint to the user when the control is [focused](#662-data-model), then the user agent should nonetheless show the hint for the control if it was focused as a result of the [`autofocus`](#667-the-autofocus-attribute) attribute, since in that case the user will not have had an opportunity to examine the control before focusing it.

> [!example]
> Here is an example of a mail configuration user interface that uses the [`placeholder`](#4105310-the-placeholder-attribute) attribute:
> 
> ```html
> <fieldset>
>  <legend>Mail Account</legend>
>  <p><label>Name: <input type="text" name="fullname" placeholder="John Ratzenberger"></label></p>
>  <p><label>Address: <input type="email" name="address" placeholder="john@example.net"></label></p>
>  <p><label>Password: <input type="password" name="password"></label></p>
>  <p><label>Description: <input type="text" name="desc" placeholder="My Email Account"></label></p>
> </fieldset>
> ```

> [!example]
> In situations where the control's content has one directionality but the placeholder needs to have a different directionality, Unicode's bidirectional-algorithm formatting characters can be used in the attribute value:
> 
> ```html
> <input name=t1 type=tel placeholder="&#x202B; رقم الهاتف 1 &#x202E;">
> <input name=t2 type=tel placeholder="&#x202B; رقم الهاتف 2 &#x202E;">
> ```
> 
> For slightly more clarity, here's the same example using numeric character references instead of inline Arabic:
> 
> ```html
> <input name=t1 type=tel placeholder="&#x202B;&#1585;&#1602;&#1605; &#1575;&#1604;&#1607;&#1575;&#1578;&#1601; 1&#x202E;">
> <input name=t2 type=tel placeholder="&#x202B;&#1585;&#1602;&#1605; &#1575;&#1604;&#1607;&#1575;&#1578;&#1601; 2&#x202E;">
> ```

##### 4.10.5.4 Common [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element APIs

`input.value [ = value ]`

Returns the current [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the form control.

Can be set, to change the value.

Throws an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if it is set to any value other than the empty string when the control is a file upload control.

`input.checked [ = value ]`

Returns the current [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the form control.

Can be set, to change the [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

`input.files [ = files ]`

Returns a [`FileList`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#filelist-section) object listing the [selected files](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) of the form control.

Returns null if the control isn't a file control.

Can be set to a [`FileList`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#filelist-section) object to change the [selected files](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) of the form control. For instance, as the result of a drag-and-drop operation.

`input.valueAsDate [ = value ]`

Returns a [`Date`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-date-objects) object representing the form control's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value), if applicable; otherwise, returns null.

Can be set, to change the value.

Throws an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the control isn't date- or time-based.

`input.valueAsNumber [ = value ]`

Returns a number representing the form control's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value), if applicable; otherwise, returns NaN.

Can be set, to change the value. Setting this to NaN will set the underlying value to the empty string.

Throws an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the control is neither date- or time-based nor numeric.

`input.stepUp([ n ])`

`input.stepDown([ n ])`

Changes the form control's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) by the value given in the [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute) attribute, multiplied by n. The default value for n is 1.

Throws ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the control is neither date- or time-based nor numeric, or if the [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute) attribute's value is "`any`".

`input.list`

Returns the [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element indicated by the [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute) attribute.

`input.showPicker()`

Shows any applicable picker UI for input, so that the user can select a value.

If input does not [support a picker](#4105-the-input-element), this method does nothing.

Throws an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if input is not [mutable](#410182-mutability).

Throws a ["`NotAllowedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notallowederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if called without [transient user activation](#641-data-model).

Throws a ["`SecurityError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if input is inside a cross-origin [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element), unless input is in the [File Upload](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) or [Color](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) states.

The `value` IDL attribute allows scripts to manipulate the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element. The attribute is in one of the following modes, which define its behavior:

value

On getting, return the current [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element.

On setting:
1. Let oldValue be the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value).
2. Set the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to the new value.
3. Set the element's [dirty value flag](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to true.
4. Invoke the [value sanitization algorithm](#4105-the-input-element), if the element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute's current state defines one.
5. If the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) (after applying the [value sanitization algorithm](#4105-the-input-element)) is different from oldValue, and the element has a [text entry cursor position](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), move the [text entry cursor position](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) to the end of the text control, unselecting any selected text and [resetting the selection direction](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) to "`none`".

default

On getting, if the element has a [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) content attribute, return that attribute's value; otherwise, return the empty string.

On setting, set the value of the element's [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) content attribute to the new value.

default/on

On getting, if the element has a [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) content attribute, return that attribute's value; otherwise, return the string "`on`".

On setting, set the value of the element's [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) content attribute to the new value.

filename

On getting, return the string "`C:\fakepath\`" followed by the name of the first file in the list of [selected files](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile), if any, or the empty string if the list is empty.

On setting, if the new value is the empty string, empty the list of [selected files](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile); otherwise, throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

> [!note]
> This "fakepath" requirement is a sad accident of history. See [the example in the File Upload state section](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) for more information.

> [!note]
> Since [path components](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) are not permitted in filenames in the list of [selected files](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile), the "\\fakepath\\" cannot be mistaken for a path component.

---

The `checked` IDL attribute allows scripts to manipulate the [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element. On getting, it must return the current [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element; and on setting, it must set the element's [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to the new value and set the element's [dirty checkedness flag](#4105-the-input-element) to true.

---

The `files` IDL attribute allows scripts to access the element's [selected files](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile).

On getting, if the IDL attribute [applies](#4105-the-input-element), it must return a [`FileList`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#filelist-section) object that represents the current [selected files](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile). The same object must be returned until the list of [selected files](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) changes. If the IDL attribute [does not apply](#4105-the-input-element), then it must instead return null. [\[FILEAPI\]](#references)

On setting, it must run these steps:
1. If the IDL attribute [does not apply](#4105-the-input-element) or the given value is null, then return.
2. Replace the element's [selected files](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) with the given value.

---

The `valueAsDate` IDL attribute represents the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element, interpreted as a date.

On getting, if the [`valueAsDate`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) attribute [does not apply](#4105-the-input-element), as defined for the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute's current state, then return null. Otherwise, run the [algorithm to convert a string to a `Date` object](#4105-the-input-element) defined for that state to the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value); if the algorithm returned a [`Date`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-date-objects) object, then return it, otherwise, return null.

On setting, if the [`valueAsDate`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) attribute [does not apply](#4105-the-input-element), as defined for the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute's current state, then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException); otherwise, if the new value is not null and not a [`Date`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-date-objects) object throw a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) exception; otherwise, if the new value is null or a [`Date`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-date-objects) object representing the NaN time value, then set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element to the empty string; otherwise, run the [algorithm to convert a `Date` object to a string](#4105-the-input-element), as defined for that state, on the new value, and set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element to the resulting string.

---

The `valueAsNumber` IDL attribute represents the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element, interpreted as a number.

On getting, if the [`valueAsNumber`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) attribute [does not apply](#4105-the-input-element), as defined for the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute's current state, then return a Not-a-Number (NaN) value. Otherwise, run the [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#4105-the-input-element) defined for that state to the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value); if the algorithm returned a number, then return it, otherwise, return a Not-a-Number (NaN) value.

On setting, if the new value is infinite, then throw a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) exception. Otherwise, if the [`valueAsNumber`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) attribute [does not apply](#4105-the-input-element), as defined for the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute's current state, then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException). Otherwise, if the new value is a Not-a-Number (NaN) value, then set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element to the empty string. Otherwise, run the [algorithm to convert a number to a string](#4105-the-input-element), as defined for that state, on the new value, and set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element to the resulting string.

---

The `stepDown(n)` and `stepUp(n)` methods, when invoked, must run the following algorithm:
1. If the [`stepDown()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) and [`stepUp()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) methods [do not apply](#4105-the-input-element), as defined for the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute's current state, then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. If the element has no [allowed value step](#410538-the-step-attribute), then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
3. If the element has a [minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) and a [maximum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) and the [minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) is greater than the [maximum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), then return.
4. If the element has a [minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) and a [maximum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) and there is no value greater than or equal to the element's [minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) and less than or equal to the element's [maximum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) that, when subtracted from the [step base](#410538-the-step-attribute), is an integral multiple of the [allowed value step](#410538-the-step-attribute), then return.
5. If applying the [algorithm to convert a string to a number](#4105-the-input-element) to the string given by the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) does not result in an error, then let value be the result of that algorithm. Otherwise, let value be zero.
6. Let valueBeforeStepping be value.
7. If value subtracted from the [step base](#410538-the-step-attribute) is not an integral multiple of the [allowed value step](#410538-the-step-attribute), then set value to the nearest value that, when subtracted from the [step base](#410538-the-step-attribute), is an integral multiple of the [allowed value step](#410538-the-step-attribute), and that is less than value if the method invoked was the [`stepDown()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) method, and more than value otherwise.

   Otherwise (value subtracted from the [step base](#410538-the-step-attribute) is an integral multiple of the [allowed value step](#410538-the-step-attribute)):
   1. Let n be the argument.
   2. Let delta be the [allowed value step](#410538-the-step-attribute) multiplied by n.
   3. If the method invoked was the [`stepDown()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) method, negate delta.
   4. Let value be the result of adding delta to value.

8. If the element has a [minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), and value is less than that [minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), then set value to the smallest value that, when subtracted from the [step base](#410538-the-step-attribute), is an integral multiple of the [allowed value step](#410538-the-step-attribute), and that is more than or equal to that [minimum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes).
9. If the element has a [maximum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), and value is greater than that [maximum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes), then set value to the largest value that, when subtracted from the [step base](#410538-the-step-attribute), is an integral multiple of the [allowed value step](#410538-the-step-attribute), and that is less than or equal to that [maximum](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes).
10. If either the method invoked was the [`stepDown()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) method and value is greater than valueBeforeStepping, or the method invoked was the [`stepUp()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) method and value is less than valueBeforeStepping, then return.

    > [!example]
    > This ensures that invoking the [`stepUp()`](#41054-common-input-element-apis) method on the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element in the following example does not change the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of that element:
    > 
    > ```html
    > <input type=number value=1 max=0>
    > ```

11. Let value as string be the result of running the [algorithm to convert a number to a string](#4105-the-input-element), as defined for the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute's current state, on value.
12. Set the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the element to value as string.

---

The `list` IDL attribute must return the current [suggestions source element](#410539-the-list-attribute), if any, or null otherwise.

---

The [`HTMLInputElement`](#4105-the-input-element) `showPicker()` and [`HTMLSelectElement`](#4107-the-select-element) `showPicker()` method steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) is not [mutable](#410182-mutability), then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant)'s [origin](#8132-environment-settings-objects) is not [same origin](#711-origins) with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant)'s [top-level origin](#8131-environments), and [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) is a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element, or [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is not in the [File Upload](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) state or [Color](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) state, then throw a ["`SecurityError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

   > [!note]
   > [File](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) and [Color](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) inputs are exempted from this check for historical reason: their [input activation behavior](#4105-the-input-element) also shows their pickers, and has never been guarded by an origin check.

3. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) does not have [transient activation](#641-data-model), then throw a ["`NotAllowedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notallowederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
4. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) is a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element, and [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) is not [being rendered](#151-introduction), then throw a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
5. [Show the picker, if applicable](#41054-common-input-element-apis), for [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).

To show the picker, if applicable for an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) or [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element element:
1. If element's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) does not have [transient activation](#641-data-model), then return.
2. If element is not [mutable](#410182-mutability), then return.
3. [Consume user activation](#642-processing-model) given element's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant).
4. If element does not [support a picker](#4105-the-input-element), then return.
5. If element is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element and element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [File Upload](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) state, then run these steps [in parallel](#211-parallelism):
   1. Optionally, wait until any prior execution of this algorithm has terminated.
   2. Let dismissed be the result of [WebDriver BiDi file dialog opened](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-file-dialog-opened) with element.
   3. If dismissed is false:
      1. Display a prompt to the user requesting that the user specify some files. If the [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute) attribute is not set on element, there must be no more than one file selected; otherwise, any number may be selected. Files can be from the filesystem or created on the fly, e.g., a picture taken from a camera connected to the user's device.
      2. Wait for the user to have made their selection.
   4. If dismissed is true or if the user dismissed the prompt without changing their selection, then [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [user interaction task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given element to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`cancel`](#events) at element, with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true.
   5. Otherwise, [update the file selection](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) for element.

   > [!note]
   > As with all user interface specifications, user agents have a good deal of freedom in how they interpret these requirements. The above text implies that a user either dismisses the prompt or changes their selection; exactly one of these will be true. But the mapping of these possibilities to specific user interface elements is not mandated by the standard. For example, a user agent might interpret clicking the "Cancel" button when files were previously selected as a change of selection to select zero files, thus firing [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) and [`change`](#events). Or it might interpret such a click as a dismissal that leaves the selection unchanged, thus firing [`cancel`](#events). Similarly, it's up to the user agent whether re-selecting the same files as were previously selected counts as a dismissal, or as a change of selection.

6. Otherwise, the user agent should show the relevant user interface for selecting a value for element, in the way it normally would when the user interacts with the control.

   When showing such a user interface, it must respect the requirements stated in the relevant parts of the specification for how element behaves given its [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute state. (For example, various sections describe restrictions on the resulting [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) string.)

   This step can have side effects, such as closing other pickers that were previously shown by this algorithm. (If this closes a file selection picker, then per the above that will lead to firing either [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) and [`change`](#events) events, or a [`cancel`](#events) event.)

##### 4.10.5.5 Common event behaviors

When the [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) and [`change`](#events) events [apply](#4105-the-input-element) (which is the case for all [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) controls other than [buttons](#4102-categories) and those with the [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute in the [Hidden](#410511-hidden-state-typehidden) state), the events are fired to indicate that the user has interacted with the control. The [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) event fires whenever the user has modified the data of the control. The [`change`](#events) event fires when the value is committed, if that makes sense for the control, or else when the control [loses focus](#664-processing-model). In all cases, the [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) event comes before the corresponding [`change`](#events) event (if any).

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element has a defined [input activation behavior](#4105-the-input-element), the rules for dispatching these events, if they [apply](#4105-the-input-element), are given in the section above that defines the [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute's state. (This is the case for all [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) controls with the [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute in the [Checkbox](#4105115-checkbox-state-typecheckbox) state, the [Radio Button](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio) state, or the [File Upload](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) state.)

For [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements without a defined [input activation behavior](#4105-the-input-element), but to which these events [apply](#4105-the-input-element), and for which the user interface involves both interactive manipulation and an explicit commit action, then when the user changes the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value), the user agent must [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [user interaction task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) at the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element, with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) and [`composed`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attributes initialized to true, and any time the user commits the change, the user agent must [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [user interaction task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element to set its [user validity](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to true and [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`change`](#events) at the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element, with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true.

> [!example]
> An example of a user interface involving both interactive manipulation and a commit action would be a [Range](#4105113-range-state-typerange) controls that use a slider, when manipulated using a pointing device. While the user is dragging the control's knob, [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) events would fire whenever the position changed, whereas the [`change`](#events) event would only fire when the user let go of the knob, committing to a specific value.

For [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements without a defined [input activation behavior](#4105-the-input-element), but to which these events [apply](#4105-the-input-element), and for which the user interface involves an explicit commit action but no intermediate manipulation, then any time the user commits a change to the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value), the user agent must [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [user interaction task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element to first [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) at the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element, with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) and [`composed`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attributes initialized to true, and then [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`change`](#events) at the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element, with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true.

> [!example]
> An example of a user interface with a commit action would be a [Color](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) control that consists of a single button that brings up a color wheel: if the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) only changes when the dialog is closed, then that would be the explicit commit action. On the other hand, if manipulating the control changes the color interactively, then there might be no commit action.

> [!example]
> Another example of a user interface with a commit action would be a [Date](#410517-date-state-typedate) control that allows both text-based user input and user selection from a drop-down calendar: while text input might not have an explicit commit step, selecting a date from the drop down calendar and then dismissing the drop down would be a commit action.

For [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements without a defined [input activation behavior](#4105-the-input-element), but to which these events [apply](#4105-the-input-element), any time the user causes the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to change without an explicit commit action, the user agent must [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [user interaction task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) at the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element, with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) and [`composed`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attributes initialized to true. The corresponding [`change`](#events) event, if any, will be fired when the control [loses focus](#664-processing-model).

> [!example]
> Examples of a user changing the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) would include the user typing into a text control, pasting a new value into the control, or undoing an edit in that control. Some user interactions do not cause changes to the value, e.g., hitting the "delete" key in an empty text control, or replacing some text in the control with text from the clipboard that happens to be exactly the same text.

> [!example]
> A [Range](#4105113-range-state-typerange) control in the form of a slider that the user has [focused](#662-data-model) and is interacting with using a keyboard would be another example of the user changing the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) without a commit step.

In the case of [tasks](#8171-definitions) that just fire an [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) event, user agents may wait for a suitable break in the user's interaction before [queuing](#8172-queuing-tasks) the tasks; for example, a user agent could wait for the user to have not hit a key for 100ms, so as to only fire the event when the user pauses, instead of continuously for each keystroke.

When the user agent is to change an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) on behalf of the user (e.g. as part of a form prefilling feature), the user agent must [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [user interaction task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element to first update the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) accordingly, then [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) at the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element, with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) and [`composed`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attributes initialized to true, then [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`change`](#events) at the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element, with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true.

> [!note]
> These events are not fired in response to changes made to the values of form controls by scripts. (This is to make it easier to update the values of form controls in response to the user manipulating the controls, without having to then filter out the script's own changes to avoid an infinite loop.)

> [!note]
> These events are also not fired when the browser changes the values of form controls as part of [state restoration during navigation](#7465-persisted-history-entry-state).

#### 4.10.6 The `button` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Interactive content](#32527-interactive-content).

[Listed](#4102-categories), [labelable](#4102-categories), [submittable](#4102-categories), and [autocapitalize-and-autocorrect inheriting](#4102-categories) [form-associated element](#4102-categories).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

As the first child of a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content), but there must be no [interactive content](#32527-interactive-content) descendant and no descendant with the [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attribute specified. If the element is the first child of a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element, then it may also have one descendant [`selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) element.

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`command`](#4106-the-button-element) — Indicates to the targeted element which action to take.

[`commandfor`](#4106-the-button-element) — Targets another element to be invoked.

[`disabled`](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute) — Whether the form control is disabled

[`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) — Associates the element with a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element

[`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) — [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) to use for [form submission](#41022-form-submission)

[`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) — [Entry list](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) encoding type to use for [form submission](#41022-form-submission)

[`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) — Variant to use for [form submission](#41022-form-submission)

[`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) — Bypass form control validation for [form submission](#41022-form-submission)

[`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) — [Navigable](#731-navigables) for [form submission](#41022-form-submission)

[`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) — Name of the element to use for [form submission](#41022-form-submission) and in the [`form.elements`](#4103-the-form-element) API

[`popovertarget`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes) — Targets a popover element to toggle, show, or hide

[`popovertargetaction`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes) — Indicates whether a targeted popover element is to be toggled, shown, or hidden

[`type`](#4106-the-button-element) — Type of button

[`value`](#4106-the-button-element) — Value to be used for [form submission](#41022-form-submission)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-button).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-button).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants) with [navigating URL attributes](#865-sanitization-constants) [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLButtonElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute DOMString command;
  [CEReactions, Reflect="commandfor"] attribute Element? commandForElement;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean disabled;
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute USVString formAction;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString formEnctype;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString formMethod;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean formNoValidate;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString formTarget;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString name;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute DOMString type;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString value;

  readonly attribute boolean willValidate;
  readonly attribute ValidityState validity;
  readonly attribute DOMString validationMessage;
  boolean checkValidity();
  boolean reportValidity();
  undefined setCustomValidity(DOMString error);

  readonly attribute NodeList labels;
};
HTMLButtonElement includes PopoverTargetAttributes;
```

The [`button`](#4106-the-button-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a button labeled by its contents.

The element is a [button](#4102-categories).

The `type` attribute controls the behavior of the button when it is activated. It is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `submit` | Submit Button | Submits the form. |
| `reset` | Reset Button | Resets the form. |
| `button` | Button | Does nothing. |

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the Auto state.

A [`button`](#4106-the-button-element) element is said to be a [submit button](#4102-categories) if any of the following are true:
- the [`type`](#4106-the-button-element) attribute is in the [Auto](#4106-the-button-element) state, both the [`command`](#4106-the-button-element) and [`commandfor`](#4106-the-button-element) content attributes are not present, and the [parent](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) node is not a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element; or
- the [`type`](#4106-the-button-element) attribute is in the [Submit Button](#4106-the-button-element) state.

**Constraint validation**: If the element is not a [submit button](#4102-categories), the element is [barred from constraint validation](#410211-definitions).

If a [`button`](#4106-the-button-element) element is the first [child](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) which is an [element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) of a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element, then it is [inert](#63-inert-subtrees).

If specified, the `commandfor` attribute value must be the [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) of an element in the same [tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) as the [button](#4102-categories) with the [`commandfor`](#4106-the-button-element) attribute.

The `command` attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `toggle-popover` | Toggle Popover | Shows or hides the targeted [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) element. |
| `show-popover` | Show Popover | Shows the targeted [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) element. |
| `hide-popover` | Hide Popover | Hides the targeted [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) element. |
| `close` | Close | Closes the targeted [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) element. |
| `request-close` | Request Close | Requests to close the targeted [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) element. |
| `show-modal` | Show Modal | Opens the targeted [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) element as modal. |
| A [custom command keyword](#4106-the-button-element) | Custom | Only dispatches the [`command`](#events) event on the targeted element. |

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the Unknown state.

A custom command keyword is a string that [starts with](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) "`--`".

To determine if a command is valid for a target given a [`command`](#4106-the-button-element) attribute command and an element target:
1. If command is in the [Unknown](#4106-the-button-element) state, then return false.
2. If command is in the [Custom](#4106-the-button-element) state, then return true.
3. If target is not an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility), then return false.
4. If command is in any of the following states:
   - [Toggle Popover](#4106-the-button-element)
   - [Show Popover](#4106-the-button-element)
   - [Hide Popover](#4106-the-button-element)

   then return true.

5. If this standard does not define [is valid command steps](#4106-the-button-element) for target's [local name](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), then return false.
6. Otherwise, return the result of running target's corresponding [is valid command steps](#4106-the-button-element) given command.

> [!note]
> The intent is to avoid dispatching a command event on an element type that does not support that command.
> 
> However, element state is not considered. If an element can support a particular command, the event is dispatched, even if that element is in a state where it cannot execute that command.
> 
> This means, for example, that command events are dispatched for popover commands on all [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility), even if they do not have a [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute.

A [`button`](#4106-the-button-element) element element's [activation behavior](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) given event is:
1. If element is [disabled](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute), then return.
2. If element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents), then return.
3. If element has a [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms):
   1. If element is a [submit button](#4102-categories), then [submit](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) element's [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) from element with *[userInvolvement](#410223-form-submission-algorithm)* set to event's [user navigation involvement](#7421-supporting-concepts), and return.
   2. If element's [`type`](#4106-the-button-element) attribute is in the [Reset Button](#4106-the-button-element) state, then [reset](#41023-resetting-a-form) element's [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms), and return.
   3. If element's [`type`](#4106-the-button-element) attribute is in the [Auto](#4106-the-button-element) state, then return.
4. Let target be the result of running element's [get the `commandfor`-associated element](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
5. If target is not null:
   1. Let command be element's [`command`](#4106-the-button-element) attribute.
   2. If the result of [determining if a command is valid for a target](#4106-the-button-element) given command and target is false, then return.
   3. Let continue be the result of [firing an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`command`](#events) at target, using [`CommandEvent`](#652-the-commandevent-interface), with its [`command`](#652-the-commandevent-interface) attribute initialized to command, its [`source`](#652-the-commandevent-interface) attribute initialized to element, and its [`cancelable`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true.

      > [!warning]
      > [DOM standard issue #1328](https://github.com/whatwg/dom/issues/1328) tracks how to better standardize associated event data in a way which makes sense on Events.
