Currently an event attribute initialized to a value cannot also have a getter, and so an internal slot (or map of additional fields) is required to properly specify this.

   4. If continue is false, then return.
   5. If target is not [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree), then return.
   6. If command is in the [Custom](#4106-the-button-element) state, then return.
   7. If command is in the [Hide Popover](#4106-the-button-element) state:
      1. Let validity be the result of running [check popover validity](#612-the-popover-attribute) given target, true, and null. If this throws an exception, catch it, and let validity be false.
      2. If validity is true, then run the [hide popover algorithm](#612-the-popover-attribute) given target, true, true, false, and element.
   8. Otherwise, if command is in the [Toggle Popover](#4106-the-button-element) state:
      1. Let validity be the result of running [check popover validity](#612-the-popover-attribute) given target, false, and null. If this throws an exception, catch it, and let validity be false.
      2. If validity is true, then run the [show popover algorithm](#612-the-popover-attribute) given target, false, and element.
      3. Otherwise:
         1. Let validity be the result of running [check popover validity](#612-the-popover-attribute) given target, true, and null. If this throws an exception, catch it, and let validity be false.
         2. If validity is true, then run the [hide popover algorithm](#612-the-popover-attribute) given target, true, true, false, and element.
   9. Otherwise, if command is in the [Show Popover](#4106-the-button-element) state:
      1. Let validity be the result of running [check popover validity](#612-the-popover-attribute) given target, false, and null. If this throws an exception, catch it, and let validity be false.
      2. If validity is true, then run the [show popover algorithm](#612-the-popover-attribute) given target, false, and element.
   10. Otherwise, if this standard defines [command steps](#4106-the-button-element) for target's [local name](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), then run the corresponding [command steps](#4106-the-button-element) given target, element, and command.

6. Otherwise, run the [popover target attribute activation behavior](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes) given element and event's [target](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event).

An [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) can have specific is valid command steps and command steps defined for the element's [local name](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element).

The [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) attribute is used to explicitly associate the [`button`](#4106-the-button-element) element with its [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms). The [`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) attribute represents the element's name. The [`disabled`](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute) attribute is used to make the control non-interactive and to prevent its value from being submitted. The [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), and [`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) attributes are [attributes for form submission](#410196-form-submission-attributes).

> [!note]
> The [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) attribute can be used to make submit buttons that do not trigger the constraint validation.

The [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), and [`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) must not be specified if the element is not a [submit button](#4102-categories).

The `command` getter steps are:
1. Let command be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`command`](#4106-the-button-element) attribute.
2. If command is in the [Custom](#4106-the-button-element) state, then return command's value.
3. If command is in the [Unknown](#4106-the-button-element) state, then return the empty string.
4. Return the keyword corresponding to the value of command.

The `value` attribute gives the element's value for the purposes of form submission. The element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is the value of the element's [`value`](#4106-the-button-element) attribute, if there is one; otherwise the empty string. The element's [optional value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is the value of the element's [`value`](#4106-the-button-element) attribute, if there is one; otherwise null.

> [!note]
> A button (and its value) is only included in the form submission if the button itself was used to initiate the form submission.

---

The `type` getter steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) is a [submit button](#4102-categories), then return "`submit`".
2. Let state be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`type`](#4106-the-button-element) attribute.
3. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): state is not in the [Submit Button](#4106-the-button-element) state.
4. If state is in the [Auto](#4106-the-button-element) state, then return "`button`".
5. Return the keyword value corresponding to state.

The [`willValidate`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), [`validity`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), and [`validationMessage`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) IDL attributes, and the [`checkValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), [`reportValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), and [`setCustomValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) methods, are part of the [constraint validation API](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api). The [`labels`](#4104-the-label-element) IDL attribute provides a list of the element's [`label`](#4104-the-label-element)s. The [`disabled`](#4106-the-button-element), [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms), and [`name`](#4106-the-button-element) IDL attributes are part of the element's forms API.

> [!example]
> The following button is labeled "Show hint" and pops up a dialog box when activated:
> 
> ```html
> <button type=button
>         onclick="alert('This 15-20 minute piece was composed by George Gershwin.')">
>  Show hint
> </button>
> ```

> [!example]
> The following shows how [buttons](#4102-categories) can use [`commandfor`](#4106-the-button-element) to show and hide an element with the [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute when activated:
> 
> ```html
> <button type=button
>         commandfor="the-popover"
>         command="show-popover">
>  Show menu
> </button>
> <div popover
>      id="the-popover">
>  <button commandfor="the-popover"
>          command="hide-popover">
>   Hide menu
>  </button>
> </div>
>     
> ```

> [!example]
> The following shows how buttons can use [`commandfor`](#4106-the-button-element) with a [custom command keyword](#4106-the-button-element) on an element, demonstrating how one could use custom commands for unspecified behavior:
> 
> ```html
> <button type=button
>         commandfor="the-image"
>         command="--rotate-landscape">
>  Rotate Left
> </button>
> <button type=button
>         commandfor="the-image"
>         command="--rotate-portrait">
>  Rotate Right
> </button>
> <img id="the-image"
>      src="photo.jpg">
> <script>
>   const image = document.getElementById("the-image");
>   image.addEventListener("command", (event) => {
>    if ( event.command == "--rotate-landscape" ) {
>     event.target.style.rotate = "-90deg"
>    } else if ( event.command == "--rotate-portrait" ) {
>     event.target.style.rotate = "0deg"
>    }
>   });
> </script>
>     
> ```

#### 4.10.7 The `select` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Interactive content](#32527-interactive-content).

[Listed](#4102-categories), [labelable](#4102-categories), [submittable](#4102-categories), [resettable](#4102-categories), and [autocapitalize-and-autocorrect inheriting](#4102-categories) [form-associated element](#4102-categories).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

Zero or one [`button`](#4106-the-button-element) elements if the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) is a [drop-down box](#15516-the-select-element), followed by zero or more [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements, [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) elements, [`hr`](#442-the-hr-element) elements, [script-supporting elements](#32529-script-supporting-elements), [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) elements, or [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) elements.

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) — Hint for form autofill feature

[`disabled`](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute) — Whether the form control is disabled

[`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) — Associates the element with a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element

[`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) — Whether to allow multiple values

[`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) — Name of the element to use for [form submission](#41022-form-submission) and in the [`form.elements`](#4103-the-form-element) API

[`required`](#4107-the-select-element) — Whether the control is required for [form submission](#41022-form-submission)

[`size`](#4107-the-select-element) — Size of the control

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

If the element has a [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute or a [`size`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute with a value > 1: [for authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-select-multiple-or-size-greater-1); [for implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-select-listbox).

Otherwise: [for authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-select); [for implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-select-combobox).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLSelectElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute DOMString autocomplete;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean disabled;
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean multiple;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString name;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean required;
  [CEReactions, Reflect, ReflectDefault=0] attribute unsigned long size;
  

  readonly attribute DOMString type;

  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLOptionsCollection options;
  [CEReactions] attribute unsigned long length;
  getter HTMLOptionElement? item(unsigned long index);
  HTMLOptionElement? namedItem(DOMString name);
  [CEReactions] undefined add((HTMLOptionElement or HTMLOptGroupElement) element, optional (HTMLElement or long)? before = null);
  [CEReactions] undefined remove(); // ChildNode overload
  [CEReactions] undefined remove(long index);
  [CEReactions] setter undefined (unsigned long index, HTMLOptionElement? option);

  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection selectedOptions;
  [CEReactions] attribute long selectedIndex;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString value;

  readonly attribute boolean willValidate;
  readonly attribute ValidityState validity;
  readonly attribute DOMString validationMessage;
  boolean checkValidity();
  boolean reportValidity();
  undefined setCustomValidity(DOMString error);

  undefined showPicker();

  readonly attribute NodeList labels;
};
```

The [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element represents a control for selecting amongst a set of options.

The `multiple` attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes). If the attribute is present, then the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a control for selecting zero or more options from the [list of options](#4107-the-select-element). If the attribute is absent, then the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a control for selecting a single option from the [list of options](#4107-the-select-element).

The `size` attribute gives the number of options to show to the user. The [`size`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers) greater than zero.

The `required` attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes). When specified, the user will be required to select a value before submitting the form.

The [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) attribute is used to explicitly associate the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element with its [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms). The [`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) attribute represents the element's name. The [`disabled`](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute) attribute is used to make the control non-interactive and to prevent its value from being submitted. The [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) attribute controls how the user agent provides autofill behavior.

If a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element has a [`required`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute specified, and has a [display size](#4107-the-select-element) of 1; and if the [value](#41010-the-option-element) of the first [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element in the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element's [list of options](#4107-the-select-element) (if any) is the empty string, and that [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element does not have an [ancestor](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) in between itself and the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element, then that [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) is the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element's placeholder label option.

If a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element has a [`required`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute specified, does not have a [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute specified, and has a [display size](#4107-the-select-element) of 1, then the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element must have a [placeholder label option](#4107-the-select-element).

> [!note]
> In practice, the requirement stated in the paragraph above can only apply when a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element does not have a [`size`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute with a value greater than 1.

---

**Constraint validation**: If the element has its [`required`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute specified, and either none of the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements in the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element's [list of options](#4107-the-select-element) have their [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) set to true, or the only [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element in the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element's [list of options](#4107-the-select-element) with its [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) set to true is the [placeholder label option](#4107-the-select-element), then the element is [suffering from being missing](#410211-definitions).

The [reset algorithm](#41023-resetting-a-form) for a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element selectElement is:
1. Set selectElement's [user validity](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to false.
2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) optionElement of selectElement's [list of options](#4107-the-select-element):
   1. If optionElement has a [`selected`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute, then set optionElement's [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) to true; otherwise set it to false.
   2. Set optionElement's [dirtiness](#41010-the-option-element) to false.
3. Run the [selectedness setting algorithm](#4107-the-select-element) given selectElement.
4. [Update a `select`'s descendant `selectedcontent` elements](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) given selectElement.

A [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element that is not [disabled](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute) is [mutable](#410182-mutability).

---

The user agent should allow the user to pick an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element from a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element in its [list of options](#4107-the-select-element) (either through a click, or through unfocusing the element after changing its value, or through a [menu command](#41135-using-the-option-element-to-define-a-command), or through any other mechanism) by running the [pick an option](#4107-the-select-element) algorithm given the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element, the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element, and if the [`select`'s contents are being rendered with base appearance](#15516-the-select-element), a corresponding [`keydown`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-keydown) or [`mouseup`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#mouseup) event, otherwise null.

To pick an option given a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element select, an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element option, and an [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) or null event:
1. If select has the [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute or select is [disabled](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute), then return.
2. If event is not null and event's [canceled flag](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) is set, then return.
3. If event is a [`MouseEvent`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#dom-mouseevent) and event's [`button`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#dom-mouseevent-button) attribute is not 0, then return.
4. Set option's [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) to true.
5. Set option's [dirtiness](#41010-the-option-element) to true.
6. [Send `select` update notifications](#4107-the-select-element) given select.
7. If select is being rendered as a [drop-down box](#15516-the-select-element) with [base appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance), then run the [hide popover algorithm](#612-the-popover-attribute) given select's [select popover](#15516-the-select-element).

If the [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute is absent, whenever an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element in the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element's [list of options](#4107-the-select-element) has its [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) set to true, and whenever an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element with its [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) set to true is added to the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element's [list of options](#4107-the-select-element), the user agent must set the [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) of all the other [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements in its [list of options](#4107-the-select-element) to false.

If the [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute is absent and the element's [display size](#4107-the-select-element) is greater than 1, then the user agent should also allow the user to request that the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) whose [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) is true, if any, be unselected. Upon this request being conveyed to the user agent, and before the relevant user interaction event is queued (e.g. before the [`click`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click) event), the user agent must set the [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) of that [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element to false, set its [dirtiness](#41010-the-option-element) to true, and then [send `select` update notifications](#4107-the-select-element).

If the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) is being rendered as a [drop-down box](#15516-the-select-element) with [base appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance), then the user agent should allow the user to open the picker given a corresponding [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element select and a corresponding [`mousedown`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#mousedown) or [`keydown`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-keydown) event event:
1. If event's [canceled flag](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) is set, then return.
2. If event is a [`MouseEvent`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#dom-mouseevent) and event's [`button`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#dom-mouseevent-button) attribute is not 0, then return.
3. Run the [show popover](#612-the-popover-attribute) algorithm given select's [select popover](#15516-the-select-element), false, and select.

If the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) is being rendered with [base appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance), then the user agent should allow the user to focus another option given the new [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element to focus option and a [`keydown`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-keydown) event event:
1. If event's [canceled flag](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) is set, then return.
2. Run the [focusing steps](#664-processing-model) on option.

> [!note]
> Implementations commonly allow the user to focus the next or previous option via the arrow-up and arrow-down keys, focus the first or last option via the Home or End keys, or focus the first or last option in the viewport of the picker via the PageUp or PageDown keys.

> [!note]
> Which particular keys of the keyboard cause these actions might differ across implementations and platforms. The ARIA Authoring Practices Guide has good [recommendations](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/examples/combobox-select-only/) for this behavior.

If the [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute is present, and the element is not [disabled](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute), then the user agent should allow the user to toggle the [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) of the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements in its [list of options](#4107-the-select-element) that are themselves not [disabled](#41010-the-option-element). Upon such an element being [toggled](#4107-the-select-element) (either through a click, or through a [menu command](#41135-using-the-option-element-to-define-a-command), or any other mechanism), and before the relevant user interaction event is queued (e.g. before a related [`click`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click) event), the [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) of the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element must be changed (from true to false or false to true), the [dirtiness](#41010-the-option-element) of the element must be set to true, and the user agent must [send `select` update notifications](#4107-the-select-element).

---

The display size of a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element is the result of applying the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers) to the value of the element's [`size`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute, if it has one and parsing it is successful. If applying those rules to the attribute's value is not successful, or if the [`size`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute is absent, then the element's [display size](#4107-the-select-element) is 4 if the element's [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) content attribute is present, and 1 otherwise.

To get the list of options given a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element select:
1. Let options be « ».
2. Let node be the [first child](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) of select in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
3. [While](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration) node is not null:
   1. If node is an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element, then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) node to options.
   2. If any of the following conditions are true:
      - node is a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element;
      - node is an [`hr`](#442-the-hr-element) element;
      - node is an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element;
      - node is a [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element;
      - node is an [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element and node has an [ancestor](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) in between itself and select,

      then set node to the next [descendant](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) of select in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), excluding node's [descendants](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), if any such node exists; otherwise null.

      Otherwise, set node to the next [descendant](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) of select in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), if any such node exists; otherwise null.

4. Return options.

To ask for a reset given an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element option:
1. Let select be option's [cached nearest ancestor `select` element](#41010-the-option-element).
2. If select is null, then return.
3. Run the [selectedness setting algorithm](#4107-the-select-element) given select.
4. [Update a `select`'s descendant `selectedcontent` elements](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) given select.

To run the selectedness setting algorithm given a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element select, run these steps. They return a boolean.
1. If select has the [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute, then return false.
2. Let hasChanged be false.
3. Let firstEnabledOption be null.
4. Let lastSelectedOption be null.
5. For each option of select's [list of options](#4107-the-select-element):
   1. If option's [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) is true:
      1. If lastSelectedOption is not null:
         1. Set lastSelectedOption's [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) to false.
         2. Set hasChanged to true.
      2. Set lastSelectedOption to option.
   2. If firstEnabledOption is null and option is not [disabled](#41010-the-option-element), then set firstEnabledOption to option.
6. If lastSelectedOption is null, firstEnabledOption is not null, and select's [display size](#4107-the-select-element) is 1:
   1. Set firstEnabledOption's [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) to true.
   2. Set hasChanged to true.
7. Return hasChanged.

To reset a `select`'s selectedness, given a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element select and a boolean hasChanged:
1. If the result of running the [selectedness setting algorithm](#4107-the-select-element) given select is true, then set hasChanged to true.
2. If hasChanged is false, then return.
3. [Update a `select`'s descendant `selectedcontent` elements](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) given select.

Whenever a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element's [`size`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute is set, changed, or removed, [reset a `select`'s selectedness](#4107-the-select-element) given the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element and false.

Whenever a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element select's [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute is added or removed, run these steps:
1. If the [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute was removed, then set the [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) of all but the first [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element with its [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) set to true in select's [list of options](#4107-the-select-element) to false.
2. [Reset a `select`'s selectedness](#4107-the-select-element) given select and true.

> [!note]
> The [`selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) elements of a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element are not kept up to date while it has a [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute, which is why they are always updated here.

To send `select` update notifications for a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element element, [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [user interaction task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given element to run these steps:
1. Set element's [user validity](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to true.
2. [Update a `select`'s descendant `selectedcontent` elements](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) given element.
3. [Clone selected `option` into `select` button](#41010-the-option-element) given element.
4. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) at element, with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) and [`composed`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attributes initialized to true.
5. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`change`](#events) at element, with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true.

---

`select.type`

Returns "`select-multiple`" if the element has a [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute, and "`select-one`" otherwise.

`select.options`

Returns an [`HTMLOptionsCollection`](#2643-the-htmloptionscollection-interface) of the [list of options](#4107-the-select-element).

`select.length [ = value ]`

Returns the number of elements in the [list of options](#4107-the-select-element).

When set to a smaller number, truncates the number of [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements in the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element).

When set to a greater number, adds new blank [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements to the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element).

`element = select.item(index)`

`select[index]`

Returns the item with index index from the [list of options](#4107-the-select-element). The items are sorted in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).

`element = select.namedItem(name)`

Returns the first item with [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) or [`name`](#162-non-conforming-features) name from the [list of options](#4107-the-select-element).

Returns null if no element with that [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) could be found.

`select.add(element [, before ])`

Inserts element before the node given by before.

The before argument can be a number, in which case element is inserted before the item with that number, or an element from the [list of options](#4107-the-select-element), in which case element is inserted before that element.

If before is omitted, null, or a number out of range, then element will be added at the end of the list.

This method will throw a ["`HierarchyRequestError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#hierarchyrequesterror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if element is an ancestor of the element into which it is to be inserted.

`select.selectedOptions`

Returns an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) of the [list of options](#4107-the-select-element) that are selected.

`select.selectedIndex [ = value ]`

Returns the index of the first selected item, if any, or −1 if there is no selected item.

Can be set, to change the selection.

`select.value [ = value ]`

Returns the [value](#41010-the-option-element) of the first selected item, if any, or the empty string if there is no selected item.

Can be set, to change the selection.

`select.showPicker()`

Shows any applicable picker UI for select, so that the user can select a value.

Throws an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if select is not [mutable](#410182-mutability).

Throws a ["`NotAllowedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notallowederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if called without [transient user activation](#641-data-model).

Throws a ["`SecurityError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if select is inside a cross-origin [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element).

Throws a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if select is not [being rendered](#151-introduction).

The `type` IDL attribute, on getting, must return the string "`select-one`" if the [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute is absent, and the string "`select-multiple`" if the [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute is present.

The `options` IDL attribute must return an [`HTMLOptionsCollection`](#2643-the-htmloptionscollection-interface) rooted at the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) node, whose filter matches the elements in the [list of options](#4107-the-select-element).

The [`options`](#4107-the-select-element) collection is also mirrored on the [`HTMLSelectElement`](#4107-the-select-element) object. The [supported property indices](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-supported-property-indices) at any instant are the indices supported by the object returned by the [`options`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute at that instant.

The `length` IDL attribute must return the number of nodes [represented](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4210-old-style-collections-nodelist-and-htmlcollection) by the [`options`](#4107-the-select-element) collection. On setting, it must act like the attribute of the same name on the [`options`](#4107-the-select-element) collection.

The `item(index)` method must return the value returned by [the method of the same name](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) on the [`options`](#4107-the-select-element) collection, when invoked with the same argument.

The `namedItem(name)` method must return the value returned by [the method of the same name](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) on the [`options`](#4107-the-select-element) collection, when invoked with the same argument.

When the user agent is to [set the value of a new indexed property](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-set-the-value-of-a-new-indexed-property) or [set the value of an existing indexed property](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-set-the-value-of-an-existing-indexed-property) for a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element, it must instead run [the corresponding algorithm](#2643-the-htmloptionscollection-interface) on the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element's [`options`](#4107-the-select-element) collection.

Similarly, the `add(element, before)` method must act like its namesake method on that same [`options`](#4107-the-select-element) collection.

The `remove()` method must act like its namesake method on that same [`options`](#4107-the-select-element) collection when it has arguments, and like its namesake method on the [`ChildNode`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#428-mixin-childnode) interface implemented by the [`HTMLSelectElement`](#4107-the-select-element) ancestor interface [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) when it has no arguments.

The `selectedOptions` IDL attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) rooted at the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) node, whose filter matches the elements in the [list of options](#4107-the-select-element) that have their [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) set to true.

A [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element's selected index is the [index](#41010-the-option-element) of the first [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element in its [list of options](#4107-the-select-element) in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) that has its [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) set to true. If there isn't one, then it is −1.

To set the selected index of a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element select to a value value:
1. Let firstMatchingOption be null.
2. For each option of select's [list of options](#4107-the-select-element):
   1. Set option's [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) to false.
   2. If firstMatchingOption is null and option's [index](#41010-the-option-element) is equal to value, then set firstMatchingOption to option.
3. If firstMatchingOption is not null, then set firstMatchingOption's [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) to true and set firstMatchingOption's [dirtiness](#41010-the-option-element) to true.
4. [Update a `select`'s descendant `selectedcontent` elements](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) given select.

> [!note]
> This can result in no element having a [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) set to true even in the case of the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element having no [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute and a [display size](#4107-the-select-element) of 1.

The `selectedIndex` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [selected index](#4107-the-select-element).

The [`selectedIndex`](#4107-the-select-element) setter steps are to [set the selected index](#4107-the-select-element) of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) to the given value.

The `value` getter steps are to return the [value](#41010-the-option-element) of the first [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element in [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [list of options](#4107-the-select-element) in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) that has its [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) set to true, if any. If there isn't one, then return the empty string.

The [`value`](#4107-the-select-element) setter steps are:
1. Let firstMatchingOption be null.
2. For each option of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [list of options](#4107-the-select-element):
   1. Set option's [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) to false.
   2. If firstMatchingOption is null and option's [value](#41010-the-option-element) is equal to the given value, then set firstMatchingOption to option.
3. If firstMatchingOption is not null, then set firstMatchingOption's [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) to true and set firstMatchingOption's [dirtiness](#41010-the-option-element) to true.
4. [Update a `select`'s descendant `selectedcontent` elements](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).

> [!note]
> This can result in no element having a [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) set to true even in the case of the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element having no [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute and a [display size](#4107-the-select-element) of 1.

> [!note]
> For historical reasons, the default value of the [`size`](#4107-the-select-element) IDL attribute does not return the actual size used, which, in the absence of the [`size`](#4107-the-select-element) content attribute, is either 1 or 4 depending on the presence of the [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute.

The [`willValidate`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), [`validity`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), and [`validationMessage`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) IDL attributes, and the [`checkValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), [`reportValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), and [`setCustomValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) methods, are part of the [constraint validation API](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api). The [`labels`](#4104-the-label-element) IDL attribute provides a list of the element's [`label`](#4104-the-label-element)s. The [`disabled`](#4107-the-select-element), [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms), and [`name`](#4107-the-select-element) IDL attributes are part of the element's forms API.

---

> [!example]
> The following example shows how a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element can be used to offer the user with a set of options from which the user can select a single option. The default option is preselected.
> 
> ```html
> <p>
>  <label for="unittype">Select unit type:</label>
>  <select id="unittype" name="unittype">
>   <option value="1"> Miner </option>
>   <option value="2"> Puffer </option>
>   <option value="3" selected> Snipey </option>
>   <option value="4"> Max </option>
>   <option value="5"> Firebot </option>
>  </select>
> </p>
> ```
> 
> When there is no default option, a placeholder can be used instead:
> 
> ```html
> <select name="unittype" required>
>  <option value=""> Select unit type </option>
>  <option value="1"> Miner </option>
>  <option value="2"> Puffer </option>
>  <option value="3"> Snipey </option>
>  <option value="4"> Max </option>
>  <option value="5"> Firebot </option>
> </select>
> ```

> [!example]
> Here, the user is offered a set of options from which they can select any number. By default, all five options are selected.
> 
> ```html
> <p>
>  <label for="allowedunits">Select unit types to enable on this map:</label>
>  <select id="allowedunits" name="allowedunits" multiple>
>   <option value="1" selected> Miner </option>
>   <option value="2" selected> Puffer </option>
>   <option value="3" selected> Snipey </option>
>   <option value="4" selected> Max </option>
>   <option value="5" selected> Firebot </option>
>  </select>
> </p>
> ```

> [!example]
> Sometimes, a user has to select one or more items. This example shows such an interface.
> 
> ```html
> <label>
>  Select the songs from that you would like on your Act II Mix Tape:
>  <select multiple required name="act2">
>   <option value="s1">It Sucks to Be Me (Reprise)
>   <option value="s2">There is Life Outside Your Apartment
>   <option value="s3">The More You Ruv Someone
>   <option value="s4">Schadenfreude
>   <option value="s5">I Wish I Could Go Back to College
>   <option value="s6">The Money Song
>   <option value="s7">School for Monsters
>   <option value="s8">The Money Song (Reprise)
>   <option value="s9">There's a Fine, Fine Line (Reprise)
>   <option value="s10">What Do You Do With a B.A. in English? (Reprise)
>   <option value="s11">For Now
>  </select>
> </label>
> ```

> [!example]
> Occasionally it can be useful to have a separator:
> 
> ```html
> <label>
>  Select the song to play next:
>  <select required name="next">
>   <option value="sr">Random
>   <hr>
>   <option value="s1">It Sucks to Be Me (Reprise)
>   <option value="s2">There is Life Outside Your Apartment
>   …
> ```

> [!example]
> Here is an example which uses [`div`](#4416-the-div-element), [`legend`](#41016-the-legend-element), [`img`](#483-the-img-element), [`button`](#4106-the-button-element), and [`selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) elements:
> 
> ```html
> <select>
>   <button>
>     <selectedcontent></selectedcontent>
>   </button>
>   <div class="border">
>     <optgroup>
>       <legend>WHATWG Specifications</legend>
>       <option>
>         <img src="html.jpg" alt="">
>         HTML
>       </option>
>       <option>
>         <img src="dom.jpg" alt="">
>         DOM
>       </option>
>     </optgroup>
>   </div>
>   <div class="border">
>     <optgroup>
>       <legend>W3C Specifications</legend>
>       <option>
>         <img src="forms.jpg" alt="">
>         CSS Form Control Styling
>       </option>
>       <option>
>         <img src="pseudo.jpg" alt="">
>         CSS Pseudo-Elements
>       </option>
>     <optgroup>
>   </div>
> </select>
> ```

> [!note]
> The first child [`button`](#4106-the-button-element) element as allowed by the content model of [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) is not a submit button. It is used to replace the in-page rendering of the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element. Its form submission behavior is prevented because it is [inert](#63-inert-subtrees). A [`selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) element can be used inside this [`button`](#4106-the-button-element) element to display the contents of the currently selected [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element.

#### 4.10.8 The `datalist` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

Either: [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

Or: Zero or more [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) and [script-supporting](#32529-script-supporting-elements) elements.

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-datalist).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-datalist).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLDataListElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection options;
};
```

The [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element represents a set of [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements that represent predefined options for other controls. In the rendering, the [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) nothing and it, along with its children, should be hidden.

The [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element can be used in two ways. In the simplest case, the [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element has just [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element children.

> [!example]
> ```html
> <label>
>  Animal:
>  <input name=animal list=animals>
>  <datalist id=animals>
>   <option value="Cat">
>   <option value="Dog">
>  </datalist>
> </label>
> ```

In the more elaborate case, the [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element can be given contents that are to be displayed for down-level clients that don't support [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element). In this case, the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements are provided inside a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element inside the [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element.

> [!example]
> ```html
> <label>
>  Animal:
>  <input name=animal list=animals>
> </label>
> <datalist id=animals>
>  <label>
>   or select from the list:
>   <select name=animal>
>    <option value="">
>    <option>Cat
>    <option>Dog
>   </select>
>  </label>
> </datalist>
> ```

The [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element is hooked up to an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element using the [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute) attribute on the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element.

Each [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element that is a descendant of the [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element, that is not [disabled](#41010-the-option-element), and whose [value](#41010-the-option-element) is a string that isn't the empty string, represents a suggestion. Each suggestion has a [value](#41010-the-option-element) and a [label](#41010-the-option-element).

`datalist.options`

Returns an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) of the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements of the [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element.

The `options` IDL attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) rooted at the [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) node, whose filter matches [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements.

**Constraint validation**: If an element has a [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element ancestor, it is [barred from constraint validation](#410211-definitions).

#### 4.10.9 The `optgroup` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

As a descendant of a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

Zero or one [`legend`](#41016-the-legend-element) element followed by zero or more [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements, [script-supporting elements](#32529-script-supporting-elements), [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) elements, or [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) elements.

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

An [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) can be omitted if the [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element is immediately followed by another [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element, if it is immediately followed by an [`hr`](#442-the-hr-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`disabled`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) — Whether the form control is disabled

[`label`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) — User-visible label

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-optgroup).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-optgroup).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLOptGroupElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean disabled;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString label;
};
```

The [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a [group of `option` elements](#4109-the-optgroup-element) with a common label.

The element's group of `option` elements consists of the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements that are descendants of the [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element.

When showing [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements in [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) elements, user agents should show the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements of such groups as being related to each other and separate from other [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements.

The `disabled` attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes) and can be used to [disable](#41010-the-option-element) a [group of `option` elements](#4109-the-optgroup-element) together.

Whenever an [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element's [`disabled`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) attribute is added or removed, then:
1. Let select be the [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element's [nearest ancestor `select`](#41010-the-option-element).
2. If select is null, then return.
3. [Reset a `select`'s selectedness](#4107-the-select-element) given select and false.

The `label` attribute must be specified if the [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) has no child [`legend`](#41016-the-legend-element) element.

To get an `optgroup` element's label, given an [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) optgroup:
1. If optgroup's first element child is a [`legend`](#41016-the-legend-element) element, then return the result of [get HTML-aware text content](#41010-the-option-element) given that [`legend`](#41016-the-legend-element) element and true.
2. If optgroup has a [`label`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) attribute, then return the value of that attribute.
3. Return the empty string.

The value of the [`optgroup` label algorithm](#4109-the-optgroup-element) gives the name of the group, for the purposes of the user interface. User agents should use this attribute's value when labeling the group of [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements in a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element.

> [!note]
> There is no way to select an [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element. Only [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements can be selected. An [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element merely provides a label for a group of [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements.

> [!example]
> The following snippet shows how a set of lessons from three courses could be offered in a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) drop-down widget:
> 
> ```html
> <form action="courseselector.dll" method="get">
>  <p>Which course would you like to watch today?
>  <p><label>Course:
>   <select name="c">
>    <optgroup label="8.01 Physics I: Classical Mechanics">
>     <option value="8.01.1">Lecture 01: Powers of Ten
>     <option value="8.01.2">Lecture 02: 1D Kinematics
>     <option value="8.01.3">Lecture 03: Vectors
>    <optgroup label="8.02 Electricity and Magnetism">
>     <option value="8.02.1">Lecture 01: What holds our world together?
>     <option value="8.02.2">Lecture 02: Electric Field
>     <option value="8.02.3">Lecture 03: Electric Flux
>    <optgroup label="8.03 Physics III: Vibrations and Waves">
>     <option value="8.03.1">Lecture 01: Periodic Phenomenon
>     <option value="8.03.2">Lecture 02: Beats
>     <option value="8.03.3">Lecture 03: Forced Oscillations with Damping
>   </select>
>  </label>
>  <p><input type=submit value="▶ Play">
> </form>
> ```

#### 4.10.10 The `option` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

As a descendant of a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element.

As a descendant of a [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element.

As a descendant of an [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

If the element has a [`label`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute and a [`value`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute: [Nothing](#3251-the-nothing-content-model).

If the element has a [`label`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute but no [`value`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute: [Text](#32525-phrasing-content).

If the element has no [`label`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute and is not a descendant of a [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element: Zero or more [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) elements or [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content), but there must be no [interactive content](#32527-interactive-content) descendant, [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element descendant, [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element descendant, or descendant with the [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attribute specified

If the element has no [`label`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute and is a descendant of a [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element: [Text](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

An [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) can be omitted if the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element is immediately followed by another [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element, if it is immediately followed by an [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element, if it is immediately followed by an [`hr`](#442-the-hr-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`disabled`](#41010-the-option-element) — Whether the form control is disabled

[`label`](#41010-the-option-element) — User-visible label

[`selected`](#41010-the-option-element) — Whether the option is selected by default

[`value`](#41010-the-option-element) — Value to be used for [form submission](#41022-form-submission)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-option).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-option).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window,
 LegacyFactoryFunction=Option(optional DOMString text = "", optional DOMString value, optional boolean defaultSelected = false, optional boolean selected = false)]
interface HTMLOptionElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean disabled;
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute DOMString label;
  [CEReactions, Reflect="selected"] attribute boolean defaultSelected;
  [CEReactions] attribute boolean selected;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute DOMString value;

  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString text;
  readonly attribute long index;
};
```

The [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) an option in a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element or as part of a list of suggestions in a [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element.

In certain circumstances described in the definition of the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element, an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element can be a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element's [placeholder label option](#4107-the-select-element). A [placeholder label option](#4107-the-select-element) does not represent an actual option, but instead represents a label for the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) control.

The `disabled` attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes). An [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element option is disabled if the following steps return true:
1. If option's [`disabled`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute is present, then return true.
2. For each ancestor of option's [ancestors](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) in reverse [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees):
   1. If ancestor is a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element), [`hr`](#442-the-hr-element), [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element), or [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element, then return false.
   2. If ancestor is an [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element, then return true if ancestor's [`disabled`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) attribute is present; otherwise false.
3. Return false.

Whenever an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element's [`disabled`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute is added or removed, then:
1. Let select be the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element's [cached nearest ancestor `select` element](#41010-the-option-element).
2. If select is null, then return.
3. [Reset a `select`'s selectedness](#4107-the-select-element) given select and false.

An [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element that is [disabled](#41010-the-option-element) must prevent any [`click`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click) events that are [queued](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [user interaction task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) from being dispatched on the element.

> [!note]
> Being [disabled](#41010-the-option-element) does not prevent all modifications to the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element. For example, its [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) could be modified programmatically from JavaScript. Or, it could be indirectly modified by user action, e.g., if other non-disabled [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements in the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element were modified.

The `label` attribute provides a label for the element.

To get an `option` element's label, given an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element option and a boolean includeAltText:
1. If option has a [`label`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute whose value is not the empty string, then return that value.
2. Return the result of [get HTML-aware text content](#41010-the-option-element) given option and includeAltText.

The [`label`](#41010-the-option-element) content attribute, if specified, must not be empty.

The `value` attribute provides a value for the element. The value of an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element is the value of the [`value`](#41010-the-option-element) content attribute, if there is one, or, if there is not, the result of [get HTML-aware text content](#41010-the-option-element) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) and false.

The `selected` attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes). It represents the default [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) of the element.

The dirtiness of an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element is a boolean state, initially false. It controls whether adding or removing the [`selected`](#41010-the-option-element) content attribute has any effect.

The selectedness of an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element is a boolean state, initially false. Except where otherwise specified, when the element is created, its [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) must be set to true if the element has a [`selected`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute.

Whenever an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element option's [`selected`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute is added or removed:
1. Let hasChanged be false.
2. If option's [dirtiness](#41010-the-option-element) is false:
   1. If the [`selected`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute was added and option's [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) is false, then set option's [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) to true and set hasChanged to true.
   2. If the [`selected`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute was removed and option's [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) is true, then set option's [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) to false and set hasChanged to true.
3. Let select be option's [cached nearest ancestor `select` element](#41010-the-option-element).
4. If select is null, then return.
5. [Reset a `select`'s selectedness](#4107-the-select-element) given select and hasChanged.

> [!note]
> For example, in a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element without a [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute, adding the [`selected`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute to an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) that is not selected deselects the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) that was. The [selectedness setting algorithm](#4107-the-select-element) then has nothing left to change, so without hasChanged the [`selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) elements would not be updated.

> [!note]
> The [`Option()`](#41010-the-option-element) constructor, when called with three or fewer arguments, overrides the initial state of the [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) state to always be false even if the third argument is true (implying that a [`selected`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute is to be set). The fourth argument can be used to explicitly set the initial [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) state when using the constructor.

A [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element whose [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute is not specified must not have more than one descendant [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element with its [`selected`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute set.

An [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element's index is the number of [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements that are in the same [list of options](#4107-the-select-element) but that come before it in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees). If the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element is not in a [list of options](#4107-the-select-element), then the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element's [index](#41010-the-option-element) is zero.

Each [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element has a cached nearest ancestor `select` element, which is a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element or null, initially set to null.

To update an `option`'s nearest ancestor `select`, given an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) option, run these steps. They return a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) elements whose [descendant](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) [`selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) elements need updating.
1. Let oldSelect be option's [cached nearest ancestor `select` element](#41010-the-option-element).
2. Let newSelect be option's [nearest ancestor `select`](#41010-the-option-element).
3. Set option's [cached nearest ancestor `select` element](#41010-the-option-element) to newSelect.
4. If oldSelect is newSelect, then return « ».
5. Let result be « ».
6. For each select of « oldSelect, newSelect »:
   1. If select is null, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   2. Let hasChanged be the result of running the [selectedness setting algorithm](#4107-the-select-element) given select.
   3. If option's [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) is true or hasChanged is true, then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) select to result.
7. Return result.

The [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) [HTML element insertion steps](#214-dom-trees), given insertedOption, are to [update an `option`'s nearest ancestor `select`](#41010-the-option-element) given insertedOption.

> [!note]
> The returned [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) elements are intentionally ignored here. Any [`selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) update is instead performed by the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) [HTML element post-connection steps](#214-dom-trees), which run once the tree is in a consistent state.

The [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) [HTML element post-connection steps](#214-dom-trees), given insertedOption, are to [update descendant `selectedcontent` elements for an `option`](#41010-the-option-element) given insertedOption.

To update descendant `selectedcontent` elements for an `option`, given an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element option:
1. Let select be option's [cached nearest ancestor `select` element](#41010-the-option-element).
2. If select is null or option's [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) is false, then return.
3. [Update a `select`'s descendant `selectedcontent` elements](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) given select.

The [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) [HTML element removing steps](#214-dom-trees), given removedNode, isSubtreeRoot, and oldAncestor, are:
1. Let selects be the result of [update an `option`'s nearest ancestor `select`](#41010-the-option-element) given removedNode.
2. For each select of selects: [queue a microtask](#8172-queuing-tasks) to [update a `select`'s descendant `selectedcontent` elements](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) given select.

The [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) [HTML element moving steps](#214-dom-trees), given movedNode, isSubtreeRoot, and oldAncestor, are:
1. Let selects be the result of [update an `option`'s nearest ancestor `select`](#41010-the-option-element) given movedNode.
2. For each select of selects: [queue a microtask](#8172-queuing-tasks) to [update a `select`'s descendant `selectedcontent` elements](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) given select.

To get the nearest ancestor `select` given an [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) element, run these steps. They return a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element or null.
1. Let ancestorOptgroup be null.
2. For each ancestor of element's [ancestors](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), in reverse [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees):
   1. If ancestor is a [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element), [`hr`](#442-the-hr-element), or [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element, then return null.
   2. If ancestor is an [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element:
      1. If ancestorOptgroup is not null, then return null.
      2. Set ancestorOptgroup to ancestor.
   3. If ancestor is a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element), then return ancestor.
3. Return null.

To clone selected `option` into `select` button, given a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element select:
1. Let option be the first element of select's [option list](#4107-the-select-element) whose [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) is set to true, if such an element exists; otherwise null.
2. Let text be the empty string.
3. If option is not null, then set text to option's [label](#41010-the-option-element).
4. Set select's [select fallback button text](#15516-the-select-element) to text.

When an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element option is popped off the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) of an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) or [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents), [update descendant `selectedcontent` elements for an `option`](#41010-the-option-element) given option.

`option.selected`

Returns true if the element is selected, and false otherwise.

Can be set, to override the current state of the element.

`option.index`

Returns the index of the element in its [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element's [`options`](#4107-the-select-element) list.

`option.form`

Returns the element's [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element, if any, or null otherwise.

`option.text`

Same as [`textContent`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), except that spaces are collapsed and [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements are skipped.

`option = new Option([ text [, value [, defaultSelected [, selected ] ] ] ])`

Returns a new [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element.

The text argument sets the contents of the element.

The value argument sets the [`value`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute.

The defaultSelected argument sets the [`selected`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute.

The selected argument sets whether or not the element is selected. If it is omitted, even if the defaultSelected argument is true, the element is not selected.

The `label` getter steps are:
1. Let attribute be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`label`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute.
2. If attribute is null, then return the result of [getting an `option` element's label](#41010-the-option-element) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) and false.
3. Return attribute's [value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#492-interface-attr).

The `value` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [value](#41010-the-option-element).

The `selected` getter steps are to return true if [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) is true, and false otherwise.

The [`selected`](#41010-the-option-element) setter steps are:
1. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) to the given value.
2. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [dirtiness](#41010-the-option-element) to true.
3. [Ask for a reset](#4107-the-select-element) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).

The `index` IDL attribute must return the element's [index](#41010-the-option-element).

The `text` getter steps are to return the result of [get HTML-aware text content](#41010-the-option-element) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) and false.

The [`text`](#41010-the-option-element) setter steps are to [string replace all](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) with the given value within [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).

The `form` getter steps are:
1. Let select be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [nearest ancestor `select`](#41010-the-option-element).
2. If select is null, then return null.
3. Return select's [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms).

A legacy factory function is provided for creating [`HTMLOptionElement`](#41010-the-option-element) objects (in addition to the factory methods from DOM such as [`createElement()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document)): `Option(text, value,
  defaultSelected, selected)`. When invoked, the legacy factory function must perform the following steps:
1. Let document be the [current global object](#81333-current)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object).
2. Let option be the result of [creating an element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) given document, "`option`", and the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces).
3. If text is not the empty string, then append to option a new [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node whose data is text.
4. If value is given, then [set an attribute value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) for option using "[`value`](#41010-the-option-element)" and value.
5. If defaultSelected is true, then [set an attribute value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) for option using "[`selected`](#41010-the-option-element)" and the empty string.
6. If selected is true, then set option's [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) to true; otherwise set its [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) to false (even if defaultSelected is true).
7. Return option.

To get HTML-aware text content, given an element element and a boolean includeAltText:
1. Let text be the empty string.
2. For each [descendant](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) descendant of element in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees):
   1. If descendant is a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) or [SVG `script`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/interact.html#elementdef-script) element, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration) skipping all [descendants](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) of descendant.
   2. If descendant is a [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node, then set text to the concatenation of text and descendant's [data](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#410-interface-characterdata).
   3. If descendant is an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element with an [`alt`](#483-the-img-element) attribute and includeAltText is true, then set text to the concatenation of text and the value of descendant's [`alt`](#483-the-img-element) attribute.
   4. If descendant is an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration) skipping all [descendants](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) of descendant.
3. Return the result of [strip and collapse ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) given text.

> [!note]
> When no [`value`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute is set on the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element, its text contents are used to generate a submittable value. In the case that the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element has child elements, this can lead to unexpected results such as [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements which render differently but have the same value. In order to address this, setting the [`value`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute on [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements is recommended.

#### 4.10.11 The `textarea` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Interactive content](#32527-interactive-content).

[Listed](#4102-categories), [labelable](#4102-categories), [submittable](#4102-categories), [resettable](#4102-categories), and [autocapitalize-and-autocorrect inheriting](#4102-categories) [form-associated element](#4102-categories).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Text](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) — Hint for form autofill feature

[`cols`](#41011-the-textarea-element) — Maximum number of characters per line

[`dirname`](#410192-submitting-element-directionality-the-dirname-attribute) — Name of form control to use for sending the element's [directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute) in [form submission](#41022-form-submission)

[`disabled`](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute) — Whether the form control is disabled

[`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) — Associates the element with a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element

[`maxlength`](#41011-the-textarea-element) — Maximum [length](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) of value

[`minlength`](#41011-the-textarea-element) — Minimum [length](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) of value

[`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) — Name of the element to use for [form submission](#41022-form-submission) and in the [`form.elements`](#4103-the-form-element) API

[`placeholder`](#41011-the-textarea-element) — User-visible label to be placed within the form control

[`readonly`](#41011-the-textarea-element) — Whether to allow the value to be edited by the user

[`required`](#41011-the-textarea-element) — Whether the control is required for [form submission](#41022-form-submission)

[`rows`](#41011-the-textarea-element) — Number of lines to show

[`wrap`](#41011-the-textarea-element) — How the value of the form control is to be wrapped for [form submission](#41022-form-submission)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-textarea).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-textarea).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLTextAreaElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute DOMString autocomplete;
  [CEReactions, ReflectPositiveWithFallback, ReflectDefault=20] attribute unsigned long cols;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString dirName;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean disabled;
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
  [CEReactions, ReflectNonNegative] attribute long maxLength;
  [CEReactions, ReflectNonNegative] attribute long minLength;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString name;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString placeholder;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean readOnly;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean required;
  [CEReactions, ReflectPositiveWithFallback, ReflectDefault=2] attribute unsigned long rows;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString wrap;

  readonly attribute DOMString type;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString defaultValue;
  attribute [LegacyNullToEmptyString] DOMString value;
  readonly attribute unsigned long textLength;

  readonly attribute boolean willValidate;
  readonly attribute ValidityState validity;
  readonly attribute DOMString validationMessage;
  boolean checkValidity();
  boolean reportValidity();
  undefined setCustomValidity(DOMString error);

  readonly attribute NodeList labels;

  undefined select();
  attribute unsigned long selectionStart;
  attribute unsigned long selectionEnd;
  attribute DOMString selectionDirection;
  undefined setRangeText(DOMString replacement);
  undefined setRangeText(DOMString replacement, unsigned long start, unsigned long end, optional SelectionMode selectionMode = "preserve");
```
