```webidl
  undefined setSelectionRange(unsigned long start, unsigned long end, optional DOMString direction);
};
```

The [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a multiline plain text edit control for the element's raw value. The contents of the control represent the control's default value.

The [raw value](#41011-the-textarea-element) of a [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) control must be initially the empty string.

> [!note]
> This element [has rendering requirements involving the bidirectional algorithm](#3282-user-agent-conformance-criteria).

The `readonly` attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes) used to control whether the text can be edited by the user or not.

> [!example]
> In this example, a text control is marked read-only because it represents a read-only file:
> 
> ```html
> Filename: <code>/etc/bash.bashrc</code>
> <textarea name="buffer" readonly>
> # System-wide .bashrc file for interactive bash(1) shells.
> 
> # To enable the settings / commands in this file for login shells as well,
> # this file has to be sourced in /etc/profile.
> 
> # If not running interactively, don't do anything
> [ -z "$PS1" ] &amp;&amp; return
> 
> ...</textarea>
> ```

**Constraint validation**: If the [`readonly`](#41011-the-textarea-element) attribute is specified on a [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element, the element is [barred from constraint validation](#410211-definitions).

A [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element is [mutable](#410182-mutability) if it is neither [disabled](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute) nor has a [`readonly`](#41011-the-textarea-element) attribute specified.

When a [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) is [mutable](#410182-mutability), its [raw value](#41011-the-textarea-element) should be editable by the user: the user agent should allow the user to edit, insert, and remove text, and to insert and remove line breaks in the form of U+000A LINE FEED (LF) characters. Any time the user causes the element's [raw value](#41011-the-textarea-element) to change, the user agent must [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [user interaction task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given the [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) at the [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element, with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) and [`composed`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attributes initialized to true. User agents may wait for a suitable break in the user's interaction before queuing the task; for example, a user agent could wait for the user to have not hit a key for 100ms, so as to only fire the event when the user pauses, instead of continuously for each keystroke.

A [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element's [dirty value flag](#410181-a-form-controls-value) must be set to true whenever the user interacts with the control in a way that changes the [raw value](#41011-the-textarea-element).

The [cloning steps](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) for [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements given node, copy, and subtree are to propagate the [raw value](#41011-the-textarea-element) and [dirty value flag](#410181-a-form-controls-value) from node to copy.

The [children changed steps](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) for [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements must, if the element's [dirty value flag](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is false, set the element's [raw value](#41011-the-textarea-element) to its [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text).

The [reset algorithm](#41023-resetting-a-form) for [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements is to set the [user validity](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to false, the [dirty value flag](#410181-a-form-controls-value) back to false, and the [raw value](#41011-the-textarea-element) to its [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text).

When a [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element is popped off the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) of an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) or [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents), then the user agent must invoke the element's [reset algorithm](#41023-resetting-a-form).

If the element is [mutable](#410182-mutability), the user agent should allow the user to change the writing direction of the element, setting it either to a left-to-right writing direction or a right-to-left writing direction. If the user does so, the user agent must then run the following steps:
1. Set the element's [`dir`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) attribute to "[`ltr`](#3264-the-dir-attribute)" if the user selected a left-to-right writing direction, and "[`rtl`](#3264-the-dir-attribute)" if the user selected a right-to-left writing direction.
2. [Queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [user interaction task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given the [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) at the [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element, with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) and [`composed`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attributes initialized to true.

The `cols` attribute specifies the expected maximum number of characters per line. If the [`cols`](#41011-the-textarea-element) attribute is specified, its value must be a [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers) greater than zero. If applying the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers) to the attribute's value results in a number greater than zero, then the element's character width is that value; otherwise, it is 20.

The user agent may use the [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element's [character width](#41011-the-textarea-element) as a hint to the user as to how many characters the server prefers per line (e.g. for visual user agents by making the width of the control be that many characters). In visual renderings, the user agent should wrap the user's input in the rendering so that each line is no wider than this number of characters.

The `rows` attribute specifies the number of lines to show. If the [`rows`](#41011-the-textarea-element) attribute is specified, its value must be a [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers) greater than zero. If applying the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers) to the attribute's value results in a number greater than zero, then the element's character height is that value; otherwise, it is 2.

Visual user agents should set the height of the control to the number of lines given by [character height](#41011-the-textarea-element).

The `wrap` attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `soft` | Soft | Text is not to be wrapped when submitted (though can still be wrapped in the rendering). |
| `hard` | Hard | Text is to have newlines added by the user agent so that the text is wrapped when it is submitted. |

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the [Soft](#41011-the-textarea-element) state.

If the element's [`wrap`](#41011-the-textarea-element) attribute is in the [Hard](#41011-the-textarea-element) state, the [`cols`](#41011-the-textarea-element) attribute must be specified.

For historical reasons, the element's value is normalized in three different ways for three different purposes. The [raw value](#41011-the-textarea-element) is the value as it was originally set. It is not normalized. The [API value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is the value used in the [`value`](#41011-the-textarea-element) IDL attribute, [`textLength`](#41011-the-textarea-element) IDL attribute, and by the [`maxlength`](#410193-limiting-user-input-length-the-maxlength-attribute) and [`minlength`](#410194-setting-minimum-input-length-requirements-the-minlength-attribute) content attributes. It is normalized so that line breaks use U+000A LINE FEED (LF) characters. Finally, there is the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value), as used in form submission and other processing models in this specification. It is normalized as for the [API value](#410181-a-form-controls-value), and in addition, if necessary given the element's [`wrap`](#41011-the-textarea-element) attribute, additional line breaks are inserted to wrap the text at the given width.

The algorithm for obtaining the element's [API value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is to return the element's [raw value](#41011-the-textarea-element), with [newlines normalized](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).

The element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is defined to be the element's [API value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) with the [textarea wrapping transformation](#41011-the-textarea-element) applied. The textarea wrapping transformation is the following algorithm, as applied to a string:
1. If the element's [`wrap`](#41011-the-textarea-element) attribute is in the [Hard](#41011-the-textarea-element) state, insert U+000A LINE FEED (LF) characters into the string using an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) algorithm so that each line has no more than [character width](#41011-the-textarea-element) characters. For the purposes of this requirement, lines are delimited by the start of the string, the end of the string, and U+000A LINE FEED (LF) characters.

The `maxlength` attribute is a [form control `maxlength` attribute](#410193-limiting-user-input-length-the-maxlength-attribute).

If the [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element has a [maximum allowed value length](#410193-limiting-user-input-length-the-maxlength-attribute), then the element's children must be such that the [length](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) of the value of the element's [descendant text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) with [newlines normalized](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) is less than or equal to the element's [maximum allowed value length](#410193-limiting-user-input-length-the-maxlength-attribute).

The `minlength` attribute is a [form control `minlength` attribute](#410194-setting-minimum-input-length-requirements-the-minlength-attribute).

The `required` attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes). When specified, the user will be required to enter a value before submitting the form.

**Constraint validation**: If the element has its [`required`](#41011-the-textarea-element) attribute specified, and the element is [mutable](#410182-mutability), and the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is the empty string, then the element is [suffering from being missing](#410211-definitions).

The `placeholder` attribute represents a *short* hint (a word or short phrase) intended to aid the user with data entry when the control has no value. A hint could be a sample value or a brief description of the expected format.

The [`placeholder`](#41011-the-textarea-element) attribute should not be used as an alternative to a [`label`](#4104-the-label-element). For a longer hint or other advisory text, the [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute is more appropriate.

> [!note]
> These mechanisms are very similar but subtly different: the hint given by the control's [`label`](#4104-the-label-element) is shown at all times; the short hint given in the [`placeholder`](#41011-the-textarea-element) attribute is shown before the user enters a value; and the hint in the [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute is shown when the user requests further help.

User agents should present this hint to the user when the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is the empty string and the control is not [focused](#662-data-model) (e.g. by displaying it inside a blank unfocused control). All U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN U+000A LINE FEED character pairs (CRLF) in the hint, as well as all other U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) and U+000A LINE FEED (LF) characters in the hint, must be treated as line breaks when rendering the hint.

If a user agent normally doesn't show this hint to the user when the control is [focused](#662-data-model), then the user agent should nonetheless show the hint for the control if it was focused as a result of the [`autofocus`](#667-the-autofocus-attribute) attribute, since in that case the user will not have had an opportunity to examine the control before focusing it.

The [`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) attribute represents the element's name. The [`dirname`](#410192-submitting-element-directionality-the-dirname-attribute) attribute controls how the element's [directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute) is submitted. The [`disabled`](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute) attribute is used to make the control non-interactive and to prevent its value from being submitted. The [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) attribute is used to explicitly associate the [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element with its [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms). The [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) attribute controls how the user agent provides autofill behavior.

`textarea.type`

Returns the string "`textarea`".

`textarea.value`

Returns the current value of the element.

Can be set, to change the value.

The `type` IDL attribute must return the value "`textarea`".

The `defaultValue` attribute's getter must return the element's [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text).

The [`defaultValue`](#41011-the-textarea-element) attribute's setter must [string replace all](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) with the given value within this element.

The `value` IDL attribute must, on getting, return the element's [API value](#410181-a-form-controls-value). On setting, it must perform the following steps:
1. Let oldAPIValue be this element's [API value](#410181-a-form-controls-value).
2. Set this element's [raw value](#41011-the-textarea-element) to the new value.
3. Set this element's [dirty value flag](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to true.
4. If the new [API value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is different from oldAPIValue, then move the [text entry cursor position](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) to the end of the text control, unselecting any selected text and [resetting the selection direction](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) to "`none`".

The `textLength` IDL attribute must return the [length](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) of the element's [API value](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

The [`willValidate`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), [`validity`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), and [`validationMessage`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) IDL attributes, and the [`checkValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), [`reportValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), and [`setCustomValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) methods, are part of the [constraint validation API](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api). The [`labels`](#4104-the-label-element) IDL attribute provides a list of the element's [`label`](#4104-the-label-element)s. The [`select()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`selectionDirection`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), [`setRangeText()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), and [`setSelectionRange()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) methods and IDL attributes expose the element's text selection. The [`disabled`](#41011-the-textarea-element), [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms), and [`name`](#41011-the-textarea-element) IDL attributes are part of the element's forms API.

> [!example]
> Here is an example of a [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) being used for unrestricted free-form text input in a form:
> 
> ```html
> <p>If you have any comments, please let us know: <textarea cols=80 name=comments></textarea></p>
> ```
> 
> To specify a maximum length for the comments, one can use the [`maxlength`](#41011-the-textarea-element) attribute:
> 
> ```html
> <p>If you have any short comments, please let us know: <textarea cols=80 name=comments maxlength=200></textarea></p>
> ```
> 
> To give a default value, text can be included inside the element:
> 
> ```html
> <p>If you have any comments, please let us know: <textarea cols=80 name=comments>You rock!</textarea></p>
> ```
> 
> You can also give a minimum length. Here, a letter needs to be filled out by the user; a template (which is shorter than the minimum length) is provided, but is insufficient to submit the form:
> 
> ```html
> <textarea required minlength="500">Dear Madam Speaker,
> 
> Regarding your letter dated ...
> 
> ...
> 
> Yours Sincerely,
> 
> ...</textarea>
> ```
> 
> A placeholder can be given as well, to suggest the basic form to the user, without providing an explicit template:
> 
> ```html
> <textarea placeholder="Dear Francine,
> 
> They closed the parks this week, so we won't be able to
> meet your there. Should we just have dinner?
> 
> Love,
> Daddy"></textarea>
> ```
> 
> To have the browser submit [the directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute) of the element along with the value, the [`dirname`](#410192-submitting-element-directionality-the-dirname-attribute) attribute can be specified:
> 
> ```html
> <p>If you have any comments, please let us know (you may use either English or Hebrew for your comments):
> <textarea cols=80 name=comments dirname=comments.dir></textarea></p>
> ```

#### 4.10.12 The `output` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Listed](#4102-categories), [labelable](#4102-categories), [resettable](#4102-categories), and [autocapitalize-and-autocorrect inheriting](#4102-categories) [form-associated element](#4102-categories).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`for`](#41012-the-output-element) — Specifies controls from which the output was calculated

[`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) — Associates the element with a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element

[`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) — Name of the element to use in the [`form.elements`](#4103-the-form-element) API.

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-output).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-output).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLOutputElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [SameObject, PutForwards=value, Reflect="for"] readonly attribute DOMTokenList htmlFor;
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString name;

  readonly attribute DOMString type;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString defaultValue;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString value;

  readonly attribute boolean willValidate;
  readonly attribute ValidityState validity;
  readonly attribute DOMString validationMessage;
  boolean checkValidity();
  boolean reportValidity();
  undefined setCustomValidity(DOMString error);

  readonly attribute NodeList labels;
};
```

The [`output`](#41012-the-output-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the result of a calculation performed by the application, or the result of a user action.

> [!note]
> This element can be contrasted with the [`samp`](#4517-the-samp-element) element, which is the appropriate element for quoting the output of other programs run previously.

The `for` content attribute allows an explicit relationship to be made between the result of a calculation and the elements that represent the values that went into the calculation or that otherwise influenced the calculation. The [`for`](#41012-the-output-element) attribute, if specified, must contain a string consisting of an [unordered set of unique space-separated tokens](#237-space-separated-tokens), none of which are [identical to](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) another token and each of which must have the value of an [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) of an element in the same [tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).

The [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) attribute is used to explicitly associate the [`output`](#41012-the-output-element) element with its [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms). The [`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) attribute represents the element's name. The [`output`](#41012-the-output-element) element is associated with a form so that it can be easily [referenced](#322-elements-in-the-dom) from the event handlers of form controls; the element's value itself is not submitted when the form is submitted.

The element has a default value override (null or a string). Initially it must be null.

The element's default value is determined by the following steps:
1. If this element's [default value override](#41012-the-output-element) is non-null, then return it.
2. Return this element's [descendant text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text).

The [reset algorithm](#41023-resetting-a-form) for [`output`](#41012-the-output-element) elements is to run these steps:
1. [String replace all](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) with this element's [default value](#41012-the-output-element) within this element.
2. Set this element's [default value override](#41012-the-output-element) to null.

`output.value [ = value ]`

Returns the element's current value.

Can be set, to change the value.

`output.defaultValue [ = value ]`

Returns the element's current default value.

Can be set, to change the default value.

`output.type`

Returns the string "`output`".

The `value` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [descendant text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text).

The [`value`](#41012-the-output-element) setter steps are:
1. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [default value override](#41012-the-output-element) to its [default value](#41012-the-output-element).
2. [String replace all](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) with the given value within [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).

The `defaultValue` getter steps are to return the result of running [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [default value](#41012-the-output-element).

The [`defaultValue`](#41012-the-output-element) setter steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [default value override](#41012-the-output-element) is null, then [string replace all](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) with the given value within [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) and return.
2. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [default value override](#41012-the-output-element) to the given value.

The `type` getter steps are to return "`output`".

The [`willValidate`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), [`validity`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), and [`validationMessage`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) IDL attributes, and the [`checkValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), [`reportValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), and [`setCustomValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) methods, are part of the [constraint validation API](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api). The [`labels`](#4104-the-label-element) IDL attribute provides a list of the element's [`label`](#4104-the-label-element)s. The [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) and [`name`](#41012-the-output-element) IDL attributes are part of the element's forms API.

> [!example]
> A simple calculator could use [`output`](#41012-the-output-element) for its display of calculated results:
> 
> ```html
> <form onsubmit="return false" oninput="o.value = a.valueAsNumber + b.valueAsNumber">
>  <input id=a type=number step=any> +
>  <input id=b type=number step=any> =
>  <output id=o for="a b"></output>
> </form>
> ```

> [!example]
> In this example, an [`output`](#41012-the-output-element) element is used to report the results of a calculation performed by a remote server, as they come in:
> 
> ```html
> <output id="result"></output>
> <script>
>  var primeSource = new WebSocket('ws://primes.example.net/');
>  primeSource.onmessage = function (event) {
>    document.getElementById('result').value = event.data;
>  }
> </script>
> ```

#### 4.10.13 The `progress` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Labelable element](#4102-categories).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content), but there must be no [`progress`](#41013-the-progress-element) element descendants.

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`value`](#41013-the-progress-element) — Current value of the element

[`max`](#41013-the-progress-element) — Upper bound of range

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-progress).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-progress).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLProgressElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute double value;
  [CEReactions, ReflectPositive, ReflectDefault=1.0] attribute double max;
  readonly attribute double position;
  readonly attribute NodeList labels;
};
```

The [`progress`](#41013-the-progress-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the completion progress of a task. The progress is either indeterminate, indicating that progress is being made but that it is not clear how much more work remains to be done before the task is complete (e.g. because the task is waiting for a remote host to respond), or the progress is a number in the range zero to a maximum, giving the fraction of work that has so far been completed.

There are two attributes that determine the current task completion represented by the element. The `value` attribute specifies how much of the task has been completed, and the `max` attribute specifies how much work the task requires in total. The units are arbitrary and not specified.

> [!note]
> To make a determinate progress bar, add a [`value`](#41013-the-progress-element) attribute with the current progress (either a number from 0.0 to 1.0, or, if the [`max`](#41013-the-progress-element) attribute is specified, a number from 0 to the value of the [`max`](#41013-the-progress-element) attribute). To make an indeterminate progress bar, remove the [`value`](#41013-the-progress-element) attribute.

Authors are encouraged to also include the current value and the maximum value inline as text inside the element, so that the progress is made available to users of legacy user agents.

> [!example]
> Here is a snippet of a web application that shows the progress of some automated task:
> 
> ```html
> <section>
>  <h2>Task Progress</h2>
>  <p>Progress: <progress id=p max=100><span>0</span>%</progress></p>
>  <script>
>   var progressBar = document.getElementById('p');
>   function updateProgress(newValue) {
>     progressBar.value = newValue;
>     progressBar.getElementsByTagName('span')[0].textContent = newValue;
>   }
>  </script>
> </section>
> ```
> 
> (The `updateProgress()` method in this example would be called by some other code on the page to update the actual progress bar as the task progressed.)

The [`value`](#41013-the-progress-element) and [`max`](#41013-the-progress-element) attributes, when present, must have values that are [valid floating-point numbers](#2343-floating-point-numbers). The [`value`](#41013-the-progress-element) attribute, if present, must have a value greater than or equal to zero, and less than or equal to the value of the [`max`](#41013-the-progress-element) attribute, if present, or 1.0, otherwise. The [`max`](#41013-the-progress-element) attribute, if present, must have a value greater than zero.

> [!note]
> The [`progress`](#41013-the-progress-element) element is the wrong element to use for something that is just a gauge, as opposed to task progress. For instance, indicating disk space usage using [`progress`](#41013-the-progress-element) would be inappropriate. Instead, the [`meter`](#41014-the-meter-element) element is available for such use cases.

**User agent requirements**: If the [`value`](#41013-the-progress-element) attribute is omitted, then the progress bar is an indeterminate progress bar. Otherwise, it is a determinate progress bar.

If the progress bar is a determinate progress bar and the element has a [`max`](#41013-the-progress-element) attribute, the user agent must parse the [`max`](#41013-the-progress-element) attribute's value according to the [rules for parsing floating-point number values](#2343-floating-point-numbers). If this does not result in an error, and if the parsed value is greater than zero, then the maximum value of the progress bar is that value. Otherwise, if the element has no [`max`](#41013-the-progress-element) attribute, or if it has one but parsing it resulted in an error, or if the parsed value was less than or equal to zero, then the [maximum value](#41013-the-progress-element) of the progress bar is 1.0.

If the progress bar is a determinate progress bar, user agents must parse the [`value`](#41013-the-progress-element) attribute's value according to the [rules for parsing floating-point number values](#2343-floating-point-numbers). If this does not result in an error and the parsed value is greater than zero, then the value of the progress bar is that parsed value. Otherwise, if parsing the [`value`](#41013-the-progress-element) attribute's value resulted in an error or a number less than or equal to zero, then the [value](#41013-the-progress-element) of the progress bar is zero.

If the progress bar is a determinate progress bar, then the current value is the [maximum value](#41013-the-progress-element), if [value](#41013-the-progress-element) is greater than the [maximum value](#41013-the-progress-element), and [value](#41013-the-progress-element) otherwise.

**UA requirements for showing the progress bar**: When representing a [`progress`](#41013-the-progress-element) element to the user, the UA should indicate whether it is a determinate or indeterminate progress bar, and in the former case, should indicate the relative position of the [current value](#41013-the-progress-element) relative to the [maximum value](#41013-the-progress-element).

`progress.position`

For a determinate progress bar (one with known current and maximum values), returns the result of dividing the current value by the maximum value.

For an indeterminate progress bar, returns −1.

If the progress bar is an indeterminate progress bar, then the `position` IDL attribute must return −1. Otherwise, it must return the result of dividing the [current value](#41013-the-progress-element) by the [maximum value](#41013-the-progress-element).

The `value` getter steps are to return 0 if [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) is an indeterminate progress bar; otherwise [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [current value](#41013-the-progress-element).

> [!note]
> Setting the [`value`](#41013-the-progress-element) IDL attribute to itself when the corresponding content attribute is absent would change the progress bar from an indeterminate progress bar to a determinate progress bar with no progress.

The [`labels`](#4104-the-label-element) IDL attribute provides a list of the element's [`label`](#4104-the-label-element)s.

#### 4.10.14 The `meter` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Labelable element](#4102-categories).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content), but there must be no [`meter`](#41014-the-meter-element) element descendants.

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`value`](#41014-the-meter-element) — Current value of the element

[`min`](#41014-the-meter-element) — Lower bound of range

[`max`](#41014-the-meter-element) — Upper bound of range

[`low`](#41014-the-meter-element) — High limit of low range

[`high`](#41014-the-meter-element) — Low limit of high range

[`optimum`](#41014-the-meter-element) — Optimum value in gauge

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-meter).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-meter).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLMeterElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute double value;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute double min;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute double max;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute double low;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute double high;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute double optimum;
  readonly attribute NodeList labels;
};
```

The [`meter`](#41014-the-meter-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a scalar measurement within a known range, or a fractional value; for example disk usage, the relevance of a query result, or the fraction of a voting population to have selected a particular candidate.

This is also known as a gauge.

The [`meter`](#41014-the-meter-element) element should not be used to indicate progress (as in a progress bar). For that role, HTML provides a separate [`progress`](#41013-the-progress-element) element.

> [!note]
> The [`meter`](#41014-the-meter-element) element also does not represent a scalar value of arbitrary range — for example, it would be wrong to use this to report a weight, or height, unless there is a known maximum value.

There are six attributes that determine the semantics of the gauge represented by the element.

The `min` attribute specifies the lower bound of the range, and the `max` attribute specifies the upper bound. The `value` attribute specifies the value to have the gauge indicate as the "measured" value.

The other three attributes can be used to segment the gauge's range into "low", "medium", and "high" parts, and to indicate which part of the gauge is the "optimum" part. The `low` attribute specifies the range that is considered to be the "low" part, and the `high` attribute specifies the range that is considered to be the "high" part. The `optimum` attribute gives the position that is "optimum"; if that is higher than the "high" value then this indicates that the higher the value, the better; if it's lower than the "low" mark then it indicates that lower values are better, and naturally if it is in between then it indicates that neither high nor low values are good.

**Authoring requirements**: The [`value`](#41014-the-meter-element) attribute must be specified. The [`value`](#41014-the-meter-element), [`min`](#41014-the-meter-element), [`low`](#41014-the-meter-element), [`high`](#41014-the-meter-element), [`max`](#41014-the-meter-element), and [`optimum`](#41014-the-meter-element) attributes, when present, must have values that are [valid floating-point numbers](#2343-floating-point-numbers).

In addition, the attributes' values are further constrained:

Let value be the [`value`](#41014-the-meter-element) attribute's number.

If the [`min`](#41014-the-meter-element) attribute is specified, then let minimum be that attribute's value; otherwise, let it be 0.

If the [`max`](#41014-the-meter-element) attribute is specified, then let maximum be that attribute's value; otherwise, let it be 1.0.

The following inequalities must hold, as applicable:
- minimum ≤ value ≤ maximum
- minimum ≤ [`low`](#41014-the-meter-element) ≤ maximum (if [`low`](#41014-the-meter-element) is specified)
- minimum ≤ [`high`](#41014-the-meter-element) ≤ maximum (if [`high`](#41014-the-meter-element) is specified)
- minimum ≤ [`optimum`](#41014-the-meter-element) ≤ maximum (if [`optimum`](#41014-the-meter-element) is specified)
- [`low`](#41014-the-meter-element) ≤ [`high`](#41014-the-meter-element) (if both [`low`](#41014-the-meter-element) and [`high`](#41014-the-meter-element) are specified)

> [!note]
> If no minimum or maximum is specified, then the range is assumed to be 0..1, and the value thus has to be within that range.

Authors are encouraged to include a textual representation of the gauge's state in the element's contents, for users of user agents that do not support the [`meter`](#41014-the-meter-element) element.

When used with [microdata](#5-microdata), the [`meter`](#41014-the-meter-element) element's [`value`](#41014-the-meter-element) attribute provides the element's machine-readable value.

> [!example]
> The following examples show three gauges that would all be three-quarters full:
> 
> ```html
> Storage space usage: <meter value=6 max=8>6 blocks used (out of 8 total)</meter>
> ```
> 
> ```html
> Voter turnout: <meter value=0.75><img alt="75%" src="graph75.png"></meter>
> ```
> 
> ```html
> Tickets sold: <meter min="0" max="100" value="75"></meter>
> ```
> 
> The following example is incorrect use of the element, because it doesn't give a range (and since the default maximum is 1, both of the gauges would end up looking maxed out):
> 
> ```html
> <p>The grapefruit pie had a radius of <meter value=12>12cm</meter>
> and a height of <meter value=2>2cm</meter>.</p> <!-- BAD! -->
> ```
> 
> Instead, one would either not include the meter element, or use the meter element with a defined range to give the dimensions in context compared to other pies:
> 
> ```html
> <p>The grapefruit pie had a radius of 12cm and a height of
> 2cm.</p>
> <dl>
>  <dt>Radius: <dd> <meter min=0 max=20 value=12>12cm</meter>
>  <dt>Height: <dd> <meter min=0 max=10 value=2>2cm</meter>
> </dl>
> ```

There is no explicit way to specify units in the [`meter`](#41014-the-meter-element) element, but the units may be specified in the [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute in free-form text.

> [!example]
> The example above could be extended to mention the units:
> 
> ```html
> <dl>
>  <dt>Radius: <dd> <meter min=0 max=20 value=12 title="centimeters">12cm</meter>
>  <dt>Height: <dd> <meter min=0 max=10 value=2 title="centimeters">2cm</meter>
> </dl>
> ```

**User agent requirements**: User agents must parse the [`min`](#41014-the-meter-element), [`max`](#41014-the-meter-element), [`value`](#41014-the-meter-element), [`low`](#41014-the-meter-element), [`high`](#41014-the-meter-element), and [`optimum`](#41014-the-meter-element) attributes using the [rules for parsing floating-point number values](#2343-floating-point-numbers).

User agents must then use all these numbers to obtain values for six points on the gauge, as follows. (The order in which these are evaluated is important, as some of the values refer to earlier ones.)

The minimum value

If the [`min`](#41014-the-meter-element) attribute is specified and a value could be parsed out of it, then the minimum value is that value. Otherwise, the minimum value is zero.

The maximum value

If the [`max`](#41014-the-meter-element) attribute is specified and a value could be parsed out of it, then the candidate maximum value is that value. Otherwise, the candidate maximum value is 1.0.

If the candidate maximum value is greater than or equal to the minimum value, then the maximum value is the candidate maximum value. Otherwise, the maximum value is the same as the minimum value.

The actual value

If the [`value`](#41014-the-meter-element) attribute is specified and a value could be parsed out of it, then that value is the candidate actual value. Otherwise, the candidate actual value is zero.

If the candidate actual value is less than the minimum value, then the actual value is the minimum value.

Otherwise, if the candidate actual value is greater than the maximum value, then the actual value is the maximum value.

Otherwise, the actual value is the candidate actual value.

The low boundary

If the [`low`](#41014-the-meter-element) attribute is specified and a value could be parsed out of it, then the candidate low boundary is that value. Otherwise, the candidate low boundary is the same as the minimum value.

If the candidate low boundary is less than the minimum value, then the low boundary is the minimum value.

Otherwise, if the candidate low boundary is greater than the maximum value, then the low boundary is the maximum value.

Otherwise, the low boundary is the candidate low boundary.

The high boundary

If the [`high`](#41014-the-meter-element) attribute is specified and a value could be parsed out of it, then the candidate high boundary is that value. Otherwise, the candidate high boundary is the same as the maximum value.

If the candidate high boundary is less than the low boundary, then the high boundary is the low boundary.

Otherwise, if the candidate high boundary is greater than the maximum value, then the high boundary is the maximum value.

Otherwise, the high boundary is the candidate high boundary.

The optimum point

If the [`optimum`](#41014-the-meter-element) attribute is specified and a value could be parsed out of it, then the candidate optimum point is that value. Otherwise, the candidate optimum point is the midpoint between the minimum value and the maximum value.

If the candidate optimum point is less than the minimum value, then the optimum point is the minimum value.

Otherwise, if the candidate optimum point is greater than the maximum value, then the optimum point is the maximum value.

Otherwise, the optimum point is the candidate optimum point.

All of which will result in the following inequalities all being true:
- minimum value ≤ actual value ≤ maximum value
- minimum value ≤ low boundary ≤ high boundary ≤ maximum value
- minimum value ≤ optimum point ≤ maximum value

**UA requirements for regions of the gauge**: If the optimum point is equal to the low boundary or the high boundary, or anywhere in between them, then the region between the low and high boundaries of the gauge must be treated as the optimum region, and the low and high parts, if any, must be treated as suboptimal. Otherwise, if the optimum point is less than the low boundary, then the region between the minimum value and the low boundary must be treated as the optimum region, the region from the low boundary up to the high boundary must be treated as a suboptimal region, and the remaining region must be treated as an even less good region. Finally, if the optimum point is higher than the high boundary, then the situation is reversed; the region between the high boundary and the maximum value must be treated as the optimum region, the region from the high boundary down to the low boundary must be treated as a suboptimal region, and the remaining region must be treated as an even less good region.

**UA requirements for showing the gauge**: When representing a [`meter`](#41014-the-meter-element) element to the user, the UA should indicate the relative position of the actual value to the minimum and maximum values, and the relationship between the actual value and the three regions of the gauge.

> [!example]
> The following markup:
> 
> ```html
> <h3>Suggested groups</h3>
> <menu>
>  <li><a href="?cmd=hsg" onclick="hideSuggestedGroups()">Hide suggested groups</a></li>
> </menu>
> <ul>
>  <li>
>   <p><a href="/group/comp.infosystems.www.authoring.stylesheets/view">comp.infosystems.www.authoring.stylesheets</a> -
>      <a href="/group/comp.infosystems.www.authoring.stylesheets/subscribe">join</a></p>
>   <p>Group description: <strong>Layout/presentation on the WWW.</strong></p>
>   <p><meter value="0.5">Moderate activity,</meter> Usenet, 618 subscribers</p>
>  </li>
>  <li>
>   <p><a href="/group/netscape.public.mozilla.xpinstall/view">netscape.public.mozilla.xpinstall</a> -
>      <a href="/group/netscape.public.mozilla.xpinstall/subscribe">join</a></p>
>   <p>Group description: <strong>Mozilla XPInstall discussion.</strong></p>
>   <p><meter value="0.25">Low activity,</meter> Usenet, 22 subscribers</p>
>  </li>
>  <li>
>   <p><a href="/group/mozilla.dev.general/view">mozilla.dev.general</a> -
>      <a href="/group/mozilla.dev.general/subscribe">join</a></p>
>   <p><meter value="0.25">Low activity,</meter> Usenet, 66 subscribers</p>
>  </li>
> </ul>
> ```
> 
> Might be rendered as follows:
> 
> ![With the <meter> elements rendered as inline green bars of varying lengths.](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/sample-meter.png)

User agents may combine the value of the [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute and the other attributes to provide context-sensitive help or inline text detailing the actual values.

> [!example]
> For example, the following snippet:
> 
> ```html
> <meter min=0 max=60 value=23.2 title=seconds></meter>
> ```
> 
> ...might cause the user agent to display a gauge with a tooltip saying "Value: 23.2 out of 60." on one line and "seconds" on a second line.

The `value` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [actual value](#41014-the-meter-element).

The `min` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [minimum value](#41014-the-meter-element).

The `max` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [maximum value](#41014-the-meter-element).

The `low` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [low boundary](#41014-the-meter-element).

The `high` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [high boundary](#41014-the-meter-element).

The `optimum` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [optimum value](#41014-the-meter-element).

The [`labels`](#4104-the-label-element) IDL attribute provides a list of the element's [`label`](#4104-the-label-element)s.

> [!example]
> The following example shows how a gauge could fall back to localized or pretty-printed text.
> 
> ```html
> <p>Disk usage: <meter min=0 value=170261928 max=233257824>170 261 928 bytes used
> out of 233 257 824 bytes available</meter></p>
> ```

#### 4.10.15 The `fieldset` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Listed](#4102-categories) and [autocapitalize-and-autocorrect inheriting](#4102-categories) [form-associated element](#4102-categories).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [flow content](#32522-flow-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

Optionally, a [`legend`](#41016-the-legend-element) element, followed by [flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`disabled`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) — Whether the descendant form controls, except any inside [`legend`](#41016-the-legend-element), are disabled

[`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) — Associates the element with a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element

[`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) — Name of the element to use in the [`form.elements`](#4103-the-form-element) API.

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-fieldset).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-fieldset).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLFieldSetElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean disabled;
  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString name;

  readonly attribute DOMString type;

  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection elements;

  readonly attribute boolean willValidate;
  [SameObject] readonly attribute ValidityState validity;
  readonly attribute DOMString validationMessage;
  boolean checkValidity();
  boolean reportValidity();
  undefined setCustomValidity(DOMString error);
};
```

The [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a set of form controls (or other content) grouped together, optionally with a caption. The caption is given by the first [`legend`](#41016-the-legend-element) element that is a child of the [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element, if any. The remainder of the descendants form the group.

The `disabled` attribute, when specified, causes all the form control descendants of the [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element, excluding those that are descendants of the [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element's first [`legend`](#41016-the-legend-element) element child, if any, to be [disabled](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute).

A [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element is a disabled fieldset if it matches any of the following conditions:
- Its [`disabled`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) attribute is specified.
- It is a descendant of another [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element whose [`disabled`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) attribute is specified, and it is *not* a descendant of that [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element's first [`legend`](#41016-the-legend-element) element child, if any.

The [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) attribute is used to explicitly associate the [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element with its [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms). The [`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) attribute represents the element's name.

`fieldset.type`

Returns the string "fieldset".

`fieldset.elements`

Returns an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) of the form controls in the element.

The `type` IDL attribute must return the string "`fieldset`".

The `elements` IDL attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) rooted at the [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element, whose filter matches [listed elements](#4102-categories).

The [`willValidate`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), [`validity`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), and [`validationMessage`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) attributes, and the [`checkValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), [`reportValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), and [`setCustomValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) methods, are part of the [constraint validation API](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api). The [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) and [`name`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) IDL attributes are part of the element's forms API.

> [!example]
> This example shows a [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element being used to group a set of related controls:
> 
> ```html
> <fieldset>
>  <legend>Display</legend>
>  <p><label><input type=radio name=c value=0 checked> Black on White</label>
>  <p><label><input type=radio name=c value=1> White on Black</label>
>  <p><label><input type=checkbox name=g> Use grayscale</label>
>  <p><label>Enhance contrast <input type=range name=e list=contrast min=0 max=100 value=0 step=1></label>
>  <datalist id=contrast>
>   <option label=Normal value=0>
>   <option label=Maximum value=100>
>  </datalist>
> </fieldset>
> ```

> [!example]
> The following snippet shows a fieldset with a checkbox in the legend that controls whether or not the fieldset is enabled. The contents of the fieldset consist of two required text controls and an optional year/month control.
> 
> ```html
> <fieldset name="clubfields" disabled>
>  <legend> <label>
>   <input type=checkbox name=club onchange="form.clubfields.disabled = !checked">
>   Use Club Card
>  </label> </legend>
>  <p><label>Name on card: <input name=clubname required></label></p>
>  <p><label>Card number: <input name=clubnum required pattern="[-0-9]+"></label></p>
>  <p><label>Expiry date: <input name=clubexp type=month></label></p>
> </fieldset>
> ```

> [!example]
> You can also nest [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) elements. Here is an example expanding on the previous one that does so:
> 
> ```html
> <fieldset name="clubfields" disabled>
>  <legend> <label>
>   <input type=checkbox name=club onchange="form.clubfields.disabled = !checked">
>   Use Club Card
>  </label> </legend>
>  <p><label>Name on card: <input name=clubname required></label></p>
>  <fieldset name="numfields">
>   <legend> <label>
>    <input type=radio checked name=clubtype onchange="form.numfields.disabled = !checked">
>    My card has numbers on it
>   </label> </legend>
>   <p><label>Card number: <input name=clubnum required pattern="[-0-9]+"></label></p>
>  </fieldset>
>  <fieldset name="letfields" disabled>
>   <legend> <label>
>    <input type=radio name=clubtype onchange="form.letfields.disabled = !checked">
>    My card has letters on it
>   </label> </legend>
>   <p><label>Card code: <input name=clublet required pattern="[A-Za-z]+"></label></p>
>  </fieldset>
> </fieldset>
> ```
> 
> In this example, if the outer "Use Club Card" checkbox is not checked, everything inside the outer [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element), including the two radio buttons in the legends of the two nested [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element)s, will be disabled. However, if the checkbox is checked, then the radio buttons will both be enabled and will let you select which of the two inner [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element)s is to be enabled.

> [!example]
> This example shows a grouping of controls where the [`legend`](#41016-the-legend-element) element both labels the grouping, and the nested heading element surfaces the grouping in the document outline:
> 
> ```html
> <fieldset>
>  <legend> <h2>
>   How can we best reach you?
>  </h2> </legend>
>  <p> <label>
>  <input type=radio checked name=contact_pref>
>   Phone
>  </label> </p>
>  <p> <label>
>   <input type=radio name=contact_pref>
>   Text
>  </label> </p>
>  <p> <label>
>   <input type=radio name=contact_pref>
>   Email
>  </label> </p>
> </fieldset>
> ```

#### 4.10.16 The `legend` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

None.

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

As the [first child](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) of a [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element.

As the [first child](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) of an [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

If the element is a child of an [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element: [Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content), but there must be no [interactive content](#32527-interactive-content) and no descendant with the [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attribute.

Otherwise: [Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content), optionally intermixed with [heading content](#32524-heading-content).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-legend).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-legend).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLLegendElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;

  // also has obsolete members
};
```

The [`legend`](#41016-the-legend-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a caption for the rest of the contents of the [`legend`](#41016-the-legend-element) element's parent [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element, if any. Otherwise, if the [`legend`](#41016-the-legend-element) has a parent [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element, then the [`legend`](#41016-the-legend-element) represents the [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element)'s label.

`legend.form`

Returns the element's [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element, if any, or null otherwise.

The `form` IDL attribute's behavior depends on whether the [`legend`](#41016-the-legend-element) element is in a [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element or not. If the [`legend`](#41016-the-legend-element) has a [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element as its parent, then the [`form`](#41016-the-legend-element) IDL attribute must return the same value as the [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) IDL attribute on that [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element. Otherwise, it must return null.

#### 4.10.17 The `selectedcontent` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

As a descendant of a [`button`](#4106-the-button-element) element which is a child of a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Nothing](#3251-the-nothing-content-model).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-selectedcontent).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-selectedcontent).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLSelectedContentElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();
};
```

The [`selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) element reflects the contents of a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element's currently selected [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element. [`selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) elements can be used to declaratively show the selected [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element's contents within the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element's first child [`button`](#4106-the-button-element) element.

> [!note]
> The [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element's [`label`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute can be used to render a visible label for the option, but the [`selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) element will not reflect the content of the [`label`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute.

Every [`selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) element has a boolean disabled, which is initially false.

To update a `select`'s descendant `selectedcontent` elements given a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element select:
1. If select has the [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute, then return.
2. Let descendantSelectedcontents be a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of select's [descendants](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), that are [`selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) elements whose [disabled](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) is false.
3. For each selectedcontent of descendantSelectedcontents: [update a `selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) given select and selectedcontent.

To update a `selectedcontent` given a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element select and a [`selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) element selectedcontent:
1. If selectedcontent's [disabled](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) is true, then return.
2. Let option be the first [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) in select's [list of options](#4107-the-select-element) whose [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) is true, if any such [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) exists; otherwise null.
3. If option is null, then [clear a `selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) given selectedcontent.
4. Otherwise, [clone an option into a `selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) given option and selectedcontent.

To clone an `option` into a `selectedcontent`, given an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element option and a [`selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) element selectedcontent:
1. Let documentFragment be the result of [creating a document fragment](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) given option's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
2. For each child of option's [children](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees):
   1. Let childClone be the result of running [clone](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) given child with [subtree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) set to true.
   2. [Append](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) childClone to documentFragment.
3. [Replace all](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) with documentFragment within selectedcontent.

To clear a `selectedcontent` given a [`selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) element selectedcontent:
1. [Replace all](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) with null within selectedcontent.

The [`selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) [HTML element insertion steps](#214-dom-trees), given selectedcontent, are to [recalculate a `selectedcontent` element's disabledness](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) given selectedcontent.

The [`selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) [HTML element post-connection steps](#214-dom-trees), given selectedcontent, are:
1. Let select be the result of [recalculate a `selectedcontent` element's disabledness](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) given selectedcontent.
2. If selectedcontent's [disabled](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) is true, select is null, or select has the [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute, then return.
3. [Update a `selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) given select and selectedcontent.

The [`selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) [HTML element moving steps](#214-dom-trees), given movedNode, isSubtreeRoot, and oldAncestor, are:
1. Let select be the result of [recalculate a `selectedcontent` element's disabledness](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) given movedNode.
2. If movedNode's [disabled](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) is true, select is null, or select has the [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute, then return.
3. [Queue a microtask](#8172-queuing-tasks) to [update a `selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) given select and movedNode.

To recalculate a `selectedcontent` element's disabledness, given a [`selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) element selectedcontent, run these steps. They return a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element or null.
1. Let nearestSelectAncestor be null.
2. Set selectedcontent's [disabled](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) to false.
3. For each ancestor of selectedcontent's [ancestors](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), in reverse [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees):
   1. If ancestor is a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element:
      1. If nearestSelectAncestor is null, then set nearestSelectAncestor to ancestor and [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
      2. Set selectedcontent's [disabled](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) to true and [break](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   2. If ancestor is an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element or a [`selectedcontent`](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) element, then set selectedcontent's [disabled](#41017-the-selectedcontent-element) to true and [break](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
4. Return nearestSelectAncestor.

#### 4.10.18 Form control infrastructure

##### 4.10.18.1 A form control's value

Most form controls have a value and a checkedness. (The latter is only used by [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements.) These are used to describe how the user interacts with the control.

A control's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is its internal state. As such, it might not match the user's current input.

> [!example]
> For instance, if a user enters the word "three" into [a numeric field](#4105112-number-state-typenumber) that expects digits, the user's input would be the string "three" but the control's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) would remain unchanged. Or, if a user enters the email address "  awesome@example.com" (with leading whitespace) into [an email field](#410515-email-state-typeemail), the user's input would be the string "  awesome@example.com" but the browser's UI for email fields might translate that into a [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of "`awesome@example.com`" (without the leading whitespace).

[`input`](#4105-the-input-element) and [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements have a dirty value flag. This is used to track the interaction between the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) and default value. If it is false, [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) mirrors the default value. If it is true, the default value is ignored.

Some form controls also have an optional value. This largely mirrors the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) but doesn't normalize to an empty string. This ought to be used sparingly, you generally want [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

[`input`](#4105-the-input-element), [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element), and [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) elements have a user validity boolean. It is initially set to false.

To define the behavior of constraint validation in the face of the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute) attribute, [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements can also have separately defined value*s*.

To define the behavior of the [`maxlength`](#410193-limiting-user-input-length-the-maxlength-attribute) and [`minlength`](#410194-setting-minimum-input-length-requirements-the-minlength-attribute) attributes, as well as other APIs specific to the [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element, all form control with a [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) also have an algorithm for obtaining an API value. By default this algorithm is to simply return the control's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

The [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element does not have a [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value); the [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) of its [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements is what is used instead.

##### 4.10.18.2 Mutability

A form control can be designated as mutable.

> [!note]
> This determines (by means of definitions and requirements in this specification that rely on whether an element is so designated) whether or not the user can modify the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) or [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of a form control, or whether or not a control can be automatically prefilled.

##### 4.10.18.3 Association of controls and forms

A [form-associated element](#4102-categories) can have a relationship with a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element, which is called the element's form owner. If a [form-associated element](#4102-categories) is not associated with a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element, its [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) is said to be null.

A [form-associated element](#4102-categories) has an associated parser inserted flag.

A [form-associated element](#4102-categories) is, by default, associated with its nearest ancestor [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element (as described below), but, if it is [listed](#4102-categories), may have a `form` attribute specified to override this.

> [!note]
> This feature allows authors to work around the lack of support for nested [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements.

If a [listed](#4102-categories) [form-associated element](#4102-categories) has a [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) attribute specified, then that attribute's value must be the [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) of a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element in the element's [tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).

> [!note]
> The rules in this section are complicated by the fact that although conforming documents or [trees](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) will never contain nested [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements, it is quite possible (e.g., using a script that performs DOM manipulation) to generate [trees](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) that have such nested elements. They are also complicated by rules in the HTML parser that, for historical reasons, can result in a [form-associated element](#4102-categories) being associated with a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element that is not its ancestor.

When a [form-associated element](#4102-categories) is created, its [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) must be initialized to null (no owner).

When a [form-associated element](#4102-categories) is to be associated with a form, its [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) must be set to that form.

When a [listed](#4102-categories) [form-associated element](#4102-categories)'s [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) attribute is set, changed, or removed, then the user agent must [reset the form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) of that element.

When a [listed](#4102-categories) [form-associated element](#4102-categories) has a [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) attribute and the [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) of any of the elements in the [tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) changes, then the user agent must [reset the form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) of that [form-associated element](#4102-categories).

When a [listed](#4102-categories) [form-associated element](#4102-categories) has a [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) attribute and an element with an [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) is [inserted into](#214-dom-trees) or [removed from](#214-dom-trees) the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), or its [HTML element moving steps](#214-dom-trees) are run, then the user agent must [reset the form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) of that [form-associated element](#4102-categories).

> [!note]
> The form owner is also reset by the [HTML element insertion steps](#214-dom-trees), [HTML element removing steps](#214-dom-trees), and [HTML element moving steps](#214-dom-trees).

To reset the form owner of a [form-associated element](#4102-categories) element:
1. Unset element's [parser inserted flag](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms).
2. If all of the following are true:
   - element's [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) is not null;
   - element is not [listed](#4102-categories) or its [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) content attribute is not present; and
   - element's [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) is its nearest [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element ancestor after the change to the ancestor chain,

   then return.

3. Set element's [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) to null.
4. If element is [listed](#4102-categories), has a [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) content attribute, and is [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree):
   1. If the first element in element's [tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), to have an [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) that is [identical to](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) element's [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) content attribute's value, is a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element, then [associate](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) the element with that [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element.
5. Otherwise, if element has an ancestor [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element, then [associate](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) element with the nearest such ancestor [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element.

> [!example]
> In the following non-conforming snippet
> 
> ```html
> ...
>  <form id="a">
>   <div id="b"></div>
>  </form>
>  <script>
>   document.getElementById('b').innerHTML =
>      '<table><tr><td></form><form id="c"><input id="d"></table>' +
>      '<input id="e">';
>  </script>
> ...
> ```
> 
> the [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) of "d" would be the inner nested form "c", while the [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) of "e" would be the outer form "a".
> 
> This happens as follows: First, the "e" node gets associated with "c" in the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents). Then, the [`innerHTML`](#854-the-innerhtml-property) algorithm moves the nodes from the temporary document to the "b" element. At this point, the nodes see their ancestor chain change, and thus all the "magic" associations done by the parser are reset to normal ancestor associations.
> 
> This example is a non-conforming document, though, as it is a violation of the content models to nest [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements, and there is a [parse error](#1322-parse-errors) for the `</form>` tag.

`element.form`

Returns the element's [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms).

Returns null if there isn't one.

[Listed](#4102-categories) [form-associated elements](#4102-categories) except for [form-associated custom elements](#4133-core-concepts) have a `form` IDL attribute, which, on getting, must return the element's [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms), or null if there isn't one.

[Form-associated custom elements](#4133-core-concepts) don't have a [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) IDL attribute. Instead, their [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) object has a `form` IDL attribute. On getting, it must throw a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) is not a [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts). Otherwise, it must return the element's [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms), or null if there isn't one.

#### 4.10.19 Attributes common to form controls

##### 4.10.19.1 Naming form controls: the [`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) attribute

The `name` content attribute gives the name of the form control, as used in [form submission](#41022-form-submission) and in the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element's [`elements`](#4103-the-form-element) object. If the attribute is specified, its value must not be the empty string or `isindex`.

> [!note]
> A number of user agents historically implemented special support for first-in-form text controls with the name `isindex`, and this specification previously defined related user agent requirements for it. However, some user agents subsequently dropped that special support, and the related requirements were removed from this specification. So, to avoid problematic reinterpretations in legacy user agents, the name `isindex` is no longer allowed.

Other than `isindex`, any non-empty value for [`name`](#4103-the-form-element) is allowed. An [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the name `_charset_` is special: if used as the name of a [Hidden](#410511-hidden-state-typehidden) control with no [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute, then during submission the [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is automatically given a value consisting of the submission character encoding.

> [!note]
> DOM clobbering is a common cause of security issues. Avoid using the names of built-in form properties with the [`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) content attribute.
> 
> In this example, the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element overrides the built-in [`method`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) property:
> 
> ```javascript
> let form = document.createElement("form");
> let input = document.createElement("input");
> form.appendChild(input);
> 
> form.method;           // => "get"
> input.name = "method"; // DOM clobbering occurs here
> form.method === input; // => true
> ```
> 
> Since the input name takes precedence over built-in form properties, the JavaScript reference `form.method` will point to the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element named "method" instead of the built-in [`method`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) property.

##### 4.10.19.2 Submitting element directionality: the [`dirname`](#410192-submitting-element-directionality-the-dirname-attribute) attribute

The `dirname` attribute on a form control element enables the submission of [the directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute) of the element, and gives the name of the control that contains this value during [form submission](#41022-form-submission).
