If such an attribute is specified, its value must not be the empty string.

> [!example]
> In this example, a form contains a text control and a submission button:
> 
> ```html
> <form action="addcomment.cgi" method=post>
>  <p><label>Comment: <input type=text name="comment" dirname="comment.dir" required></label></p>
>  <p><button name="mode" type=submit value="add">Post Comment</button></p>
> </form>
> ```
> 
> When the user submits the form, the user agent includes three fields, one called "comment", one called "comment.dir", and one called "mode"; so if the user types "Hello", the submission body might be something like:
> 
> ```
> comment=Hello&comment.dir=ltr&mode=add
> ```
> 
> If the user manually switches to a right-to-left writing direction and enters "مرحبا", the submission body might be something like:
> 
> ```
> comment=%D9%85%D8%B1%D8%AD%D8%A8%D8%A7&comment.dir=rtl&mode=add
> ```

##### 4.10.19.3 Limiting user input length: the [`maxlength`](#410193-limiting-user-input-length-the-maxlength-attribute) attribute

A form control `maxlength` attribute, controlled by the [dirty value flag](#410181-a-form-controls-value), declares a limit on the number of characters a user can input. The number of characters is measured using [length](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) and, in the case of [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements, with all newlines normalized to a single character (as opposed to CRLF pairs).

If an element has its [form control `maxlength` attribute](#410193-limiting-user-input-length-the-maxlength-attribute) specified, the attribute's value must be a [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers). If the attribute is specified and applying the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers) to its value results in a number, then that number is the element's maximum allowed value length. If the attribute is omitted or parsing its value results in an error, then there is no [maximum allowed value length](#410193-limiting-user-input-length-the-maxlength-attribute).

**Constraint validation**: If an element has a [maximum allowed value length](#410193-limiting-user-input-length-the-maxlength-attribute), its [dirty value flag](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is true, its [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) was last changed by a user edit (as opposed to a change made by a script), and the [length](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) of the element's [API value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is greater than the element's [maximum allowed value length](#410193-limiting-user-input-length-the-maxlength-attribute), then the element is [suffering from being too long](#410211-definitions).

User agents may prevent the user from causing the element's [API value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to be set to a value whose [length](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) is greater than the element's [maximum allowed value length](#410193-limiting-user-input-length-the-maxlength-attribute).

> [!note]
> In the case of [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements, the [API value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) and [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) differ. In particular, [newline normalization](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) is applied before the [maximum allowed value length](#410193-limiting-user-input-length-the-maxlength-attribute) is checked (whereas the [textarea wrapping transformation](#41011-the-textarea-element) is not applied).

##### 4.10.19.4 Setting minimum input length requirements: the [`minlength`](#410194-setting-minimum-input-length-requirements-the-minlength-attribute) attribute

A form control `minlength` attribute, controlled by the [dirty value flag](#410181-a-form-controls-value), declares a lower bound on the number of characters a user can input. The "number of characters" is measured using [length](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) and, in the case of [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements, with all newlines normalized to a single character (as opposed to CRLF pairs).

> [!note]
> The [`minlength`](#410194-setting-minimum-input-length-requirements-the-minlength-attribute) attribute does not imply the `required` attribute. If the form control has no `required` attribute, then the value can still be omitted; the [`minlength`](#410194-setting-minimum-input-length-requirements-the-minlength-attribute) attribute only kicks in once the user has entered a value at all. If the empty string is not allowed, then the `required` attribute also needs to be set.

If an element has its [form control `minlength` attribute](#410194-setting-minimum-input-length-requirements-the-minlength-attribute) specified, the attribute's value must be a [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers). If the attribute is specified and applying the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers) to its value results in a number, then that number is the element's minimum allowed value length. If the attribute is omitted or parsing its value results in an error, then there is no [minimum allowed value length](#410194-setting-minimum-input-length-requirements-the-minlength-attribute).

If an element has both a [maximum allowed value length](#410193-limiting-user-input-length-the-maxlength-attribute) and a [minimum allowed value length](#410194-setting-minimum-input-length-requirements-the-minlength-attribute), the [minimum allowed value length](#410194-setting-minimum-input-length-requirements-the-minlength-attribute) must be smaller than or equal to the [maximum allowed value length](#410193-limiting-user-input-length-the-maxlength-attribute).

**Constraint validation**: If an element has a [minimum allowed value length](#410194-setting-minimum-input-length-requirements-the-minlength-attribute), its [dirty value flag](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is true, its [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) was last changed by a user edit (as opposed to a change made by a script), its [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is not the empty string, and the [length](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) of the element's [API value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is less than the element's [minimum allowed value length](#410194-setting-minimum-input-length-requirements-the-minlength-attribute), then the element is [suffering from being too short](#410211-definitions).

> [!example]
> In this example, there are four text controls. The first is required, and has to be at least 5 characters long. The other three are optional, but if the user fills one in, the user has to enter at least 10 characters.
> 
> ```html
> <form action="/events/menu.cgi" method="post">
>  <p><label>Name of Event: <input required minlength=5 maxlength=50 name=event></label></p>
>  <p><label>Describe what you would like for breakfast, if anything:
>     <textarea name="breakfast" minlength="10"></textarea></label></p>
>  <p><label>Describe what you would like for lunch, if anything:
>     <textarea name="lunch" minlength="10"></textarea></label></p>
>  <p><label>Describe what you would like for dinner, if anything:
>     <textarea name="dinner" minlength="10"></textarea></label></p>
>  <p><input type=submit value="Submit Request"></p>
> </form>
> ```

##### 4.10.19.5 Enabling and disabling form controls: the [`disabled`](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute) attribute

The `disabled` content attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes).

> [!note]
> The [`disabled`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute for [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements and the [`disabled`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) attribute for [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) elements are defined separately.

A form control is disabled if any of the following are true:
- the element is a [`button`](#4106-the-button-element), [`input`](#4105-the-input-element), [`select`](#4107-the-select-element), [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element), or [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts), and the [`disabled`](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute) attribute is specified on this element (regardless of its value); or
- the element is a descendant of a [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element whose [`disabled`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) attribute is specified, and the element is *not* a descendant of that [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element's first [`legend`](#41016-the-legend-element) element child, if any.

A form control that is [disabled](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute) must prevent any [`click`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click) events that are [queued](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [user interaction task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) from being dispatched on the element.

> [!note]
> Being [disabled](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute) does not prevent all modifications to the form control. For example, the control's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) or [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) could be modified programmatically from JavaScript. Or, they could be indirectly modified by user action, e.g., if other non-disabled elements in the control's [radio button group](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio) were modified.

**Constraint validation**: If an element is [disabled](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute), it is [barred from constraint validation](#410211-definitions).

##### 4.10.19.6 Form submission attributes

Attributes for form submission can be specified both on [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements and on [submit buttons](#4102-categories) (elements that represent buttons that submit forms, e.g. an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Submit Button](#4105118-submit-button-state-typesubmit) state).

The [attributes for form submission](#410196-form-submission-attributes) that may be specified on [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements are [`action`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`enctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`method`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`novalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), and [`target`](#410196-form-submission-attributes).

The corresponding [attributes for form submission](#410196-form-submission-attributes) that may be specified on [submit buttons](#4102-categories) are [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes), and [`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes). When omitted, they default to the values given on the corresponding attributes on the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element.

---

The `action` and `formaction` content attributes, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#241-terminology).

The action of an element is the value of the element's [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) attribute, if the element is a [submit button](#4102-categories) and has such an attribute, or the value of its [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms)'s [`action`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) attribute, if *it* has one, or else the empty string.

---

The `method` and `formmethod` content attributes are [enumerated attributes](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `get` | GET | Indicates the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) will use the HTTP GET method. |
| `post` | POST | Indicates the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) will use the HTTP POST method. |
| `dialog` | Dialog | Indicates the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) is intended to close the [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) box in which the form finds itself, if any, and otherwise not submit. |

The [`method`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the [GET](#410196-form-submission-attributes) state.

The [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) attribute has no *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)*, and its *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* is the [GET](#410196-form-submission-attributes) state.

The method of an element is one of those states. If the element is a [submit button](#4102-categories) and has a [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) attribute, then the element's [method](#410196-form-submission-attributes) is that attribute's state; otherwise, it is the [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms)'s [`method`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) attribute's state.

> [!example]
> Here the [`method`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) attribute is used to explicitly specify the default value, "[`get`](#410196-form-submission-attributes)", so that the search query is submitted in the URL:
> 
> ```html
> <form method="get" action="/search.cgi">
>  <p><label>Search terms: <input type=search name=q></label></p>
>  <p><input type=submit></p>
> </form>
> ```

> [!example]
> On the other hand, here the [`method`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) attribute is used to specify the value "[`post`](#410196-form-submission-attributes)", so that the user's message is submitted in the HTTP request's body:
> 
> ```html
> <form method="post" action="/post-message.cgi">
>  <p><label>Message: <input type=text name=m></label></p>
>  <p><input type=submit value="Submit message"></p>
> </form>
> ```

> [!example]
> In this example, a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) is used with a [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element). The [`method`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) attribute's "[`dialog`](#410196-form-submission-attributes)" keyword is used to have the dialog automatically close when the form is submitted.
> 
> ```html
> <dialog id="ship">
>  <form method=dialog>
>   <p>A ship has arrived in the harbour.</p>
>   <button type=submit value="board">Board the ship</button>
>   <button type=submit value="call">Call to the captain</button>
>  </form>
> </dialog>
> <script>
>  var ship = document.getElementById('ship');
>  ship.showModal();
>  ship.onclose = function (event) {
>    if (ship.returnValue == 'board') {
>      // ...
>    } else {
>      // ...
>    }
>  };
> </script>
> ```

---

The `enctype` and `formenctype` content attributes are [enumerated attributes](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:
- The "`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`" keyword and corresponding state.
- The "`multipart/form-data`" keyword and corresponding state.
- The "`text/plain`" keyword and corresponding state.

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) state.

The [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) attribute has no *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)*, and its *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* is the [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) state.

The enctype of an element is one of those three states. If the element is a [submit button](#4102-categories) and has a [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) attribute, then the element's [enctype](#410196-form-submission-attributes) is that attribute's state; otherwise, it is the [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms)'s [`enctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) attribute's state.

---

The `target` and `formtarget` content attributes, if specified, must have values that are [valid navigable target names or keywords](#7317-navigable-target-names).

---

The `novalidate` and `formnovalidate` content attributes are [boolean attributes](#232-boolean-attributes). If present, they indicate that the form is not to be validated during submission.

The no-validate state of an element is true if the element is a [submit button](#4102-categories) and the element's [`formnovalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) attribute is present, or if the element's [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms)'s [`novalidate`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) attribute is present, and false otherwise.

> [!example]
> This attribute is useful to include "save" buttons on forms that have validation constraints, to allow users to save their progress even though they haven't fully entered the data in the form. The following example shows a simple form that has two required fields. There are three buttons: one to submit the form, which requires both fields to be filled in; one to save the form so that the user can come back and fill it in later; and one to cancel the form altogether.
> 
> ```html
> <form action="editor.cgi" method="post">
>  <p><label>Name: <input required name=fn></label></p>
>  <p><label>Essay: <textarea required name=essay></textarea></label></p>
>  <p><input type=submit name=submit value="Submit essay"></p>
>  <p><input type=submit formnovalidate name=save value="Save essay"></p>
>  <p><input type=submit formnovalidate name=cancel value="Cancel"></p>
> </form>
> ```

---

The `action` getter steps are:
1. Let attribute be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`action`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) attribute.
2. If attribute is null or attribute's [value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#492-interface-attr) is the empty string, then return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).
3. Let urlString be the result of [encoding-parsing-and-serializing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given attribute's [value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#492-interface-attr), relative to [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
4. If urlString is not failure, then return urlString.
5. Return attribute's [value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#492-interface-attr), [converted to a scalar value string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).

The `formAction` getter steps are:
1. Let attribute be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`formaction`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) attribute.
2. If attribute is null or attribute's [value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#492-interface-attr) is the empty string, then return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).
3. Let urlString be the result of [encoding-parsing-and-serializing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given attribute's [value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#492-interface-attr), relative to [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
4. If urlString is not failure, then return urlString.
5. Return attribute's [value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#492-interface-attr), [converted to a scalar value string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).

The `method` and `enctype` IDL attributes must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the respective content attributes of the same name, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes). The `encoding` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`enctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes). The `formEnctype` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`formenctype`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes). The `formMethod` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`formmethod`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

##### 4.10.19.7 Autofill

###### 4.10.19.7.1 Autofilling form controls: the [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) attribute

User agents sometimes have features for helping users fill forms in, for example prefilling the user's address based on earlier user input. The `autocomplete` content attribute can be used to hint to the user agent how to, or indeed whether to, provide such a feature.

There are two ways this attribute is used. When wearing the autofill expectation mantle, the [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) attribute describes what input is expected from users. When wearing the autofill anchor mantle, the [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) attribute describes the meaning of the given value.

On an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Hidden](#410511-hidden-state-typehidden) state, the [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) attribute wears the [autofill anchor mantle](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute). In all other cases, it wears the [autofill expectation mantle](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute).

When wearing the [autofill expectation mantle](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute), the [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is an ordered [set of space-separated tokens](#237-space-separated-tokens) consisting of either a single token that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "[`off`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)", or a single token that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "[`on`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)", or [autofill detail tokens](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute).

When wearing the [autofill anchor mantle](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute), the [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is an ordered [set of space-separated tokens](#237-space-separated-tokens) consisting of just [autofill detail tokens](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) (i.e. the "[`on`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" and "[`off`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" keywords are not allowed).

Autofill detail tokens are the following, in the order given below:
1. Optionally, a token whose first eight characters are an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`section-`", meaning that the field belongs to the named group.

   > [!example]
   > For example, if there are two shipping addresses in the form, then they could be marked up as:
   > 
   > ```html
   > <fieldset>
   >  <legend>Ship the blue gift to...</legend>
   >  <p> <label> Address:     <textarea name=ba autocomplete="section-blue shipping street-address"></textarea> </label>
   >  <p> <label> City:        <input name=bc autocomplete="section-blue shipping address-level2"> </label>
   >  <p> <label> Postal Code: <input name=bp autocomplete="section-blue shipping postal-code"> </label>
   > </fieldset>
   > <fieldset>
   >  <legend>Ship the red gift to...</legend>
   >  <p> <label> Address:     <textarea name=ra autocomplete="section-red shipping street-address"></textarea> </label>
   >  <p> <label> City:        <input name=rc autocomplete="section-red shipping address-level2"> </label>
   >  <p> <label> Postal Code: <input name=rp autocomplete="section-red shipping postal-code"> </label>
   > </fieldset>
   > ```

2. Optionally, a token that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for one of the following strings:
   - "`shipping`", meaning the field is part of the shipping address or contact information
   - "`billing`", meaning the field is part of the billing address or contact information
3. Either of the following two options:
   - A token that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for one of the following [autofill field](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) names, excluding those that are [inappropriate for the control](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute):
     - "[`name`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`honorific-prefix`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`given-name`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`additional-name`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`family-name`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`honorific-suffix`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`nickname`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`username`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`new-password`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`current-password`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`one-time-code`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`organization-title`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`organization`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`street-address`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`address-line1`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`address-line2`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`address-line3`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`address-level4`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`address-level3`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`address-level2`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`address-level1`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`country`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`country-name`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`postal-code`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`cc-name`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`cc-given-name`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`cc-additional-name`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`cc-family-name`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`cc-number`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`cc-exp`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`cc-exp-month`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`cc-exp-year`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`cc-csc`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`cc-type`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`transaction-currency`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`transaction-amount`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`language`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`bday`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`bday-day`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`bday-month`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`bday-year`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`sex`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`url`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
     - "[`photo`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"

     (See the table below for descriptions of these values.)

   - The following, in the given order:
     1. Optionally, a token that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for one of the following strings:
        - "`home`", meaning the field is for contacting someone at their residence
        - "`work`", meaning the field is for contacting someone at their workplace
        - "`mobile`", meaning the field is for contacting someone regardless of location
        - "`fax`", meaning the field describes a fax machine's contact details
        - "`pager`", meaning the field describes a pager's or beeper's contact details
     2. A token that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for one of the following [autofill field](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) names, excluding those that are [inappropriate for the control](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute):
        - "[`tel`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
        - "[`tel-country-code`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
        - "[`tel-national`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
        - "[`tel-area-code`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
        - "[`tel-local`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
        - "[`tel-local-prefix`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
        - "[`tel-local-suffix`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
        - "[`tel-extension`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
        - "[`email`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
        - "[`impp`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"

        (See the table below for descriptions of these values.)

4. Optionally, a token that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`webauthn`", meaning the user agent should show [public key credentials](https://w3c.github.io/webauthn/#public-key-credential) available via [`conditional`](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#dom-credentialmediationrequirement-conditional) mediation when the user interacts with the form control. [`webauthn`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) is only valid for [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) and [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements.

As noted earlier, the meaning of the attribute and its keywords depends on the mantle that the attribute is wearing.

When wearing the [autofill expectation mantle](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)...

The "`off`" keyword indicates either that the control's input data is particularly sensitive (for example the activation code for a nuclear weapon); or that it is a value that will never be reused (for example a one-time-key for a bank login) and the user will therefore have to explicitly enter the data each time, instead of being able to rely on the UA to prefill the value for them; or that the document provides its own autocomplete mechanism and does not want the user agent to provide autocompletion values.

The "`on`" keyword indicates that the user agent is allowed to provide the user with autocompletion values, but does not provide any further information about what kind of data the user might be expected to enter. User agents would have to use heuristics to decide what autocompletion values to suggest.

The [autofill field](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) listed above indicates that the user agent is allowed to provide the user with autocompletion values, and specifies what kind of value is expected. The meaning of each such keyword is described in the table below.

If the [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) attribute is omitted, the default value corresponding to the state of the element's [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms)'s [`autocomplete`](#4103-the-form-element) attribute is used instead (either "[`on`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" or "[`off`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"). If there is no [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms), then the value "[`on`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" is used.

When wearing the [autofill anchor mantle](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)...

The [autofill field](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) listed above indicates that the value of the particular kind of value specified is that value provided for this element. The meaning of each such keyword is described in the table below.

> [!example]
> In this example the page has explicitly specified the currency and amount of the transaction. The form requests a credit card and other billing details. The user agent could use this information to suggest a credit card that it knows has sufficient balance and that supports the relevant currency.
> 
> ```html
> <form method=post action="step2.cgi">
>  <input type=hidden autocomplete=transaction-currency value="CHF">
>  <input type=hidden autocomplete=transaction-amount value="15.00">
>  <p><label>Credit card number: <input type=text inputmode=numeric autocomplete=cc-number></label>
>  <p><label>Expiry Date: <input type=month autocomplete=cc-exp></label>
>  <p><input type=submit value="Continue...">
> </form>
> ```

The autofill field keywords relate to each other as described in the table below. Each field name listed on a row of this table corresponds to the meaning given in the cell for that row in the column labeled "Meaning". Some fields correspond to subparts of other fields; for example, a credit card expiry date can be expressed as one field giving both the month and year of expiry ("[`cc-exp`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"), or as two fields, one giving the month ("[`cc-exp-month`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)") and one the year ("[`cc-exp-year`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"). In such cases, the names of the broader fields cover multiple rows, in which the narrower fields are defined.

> [!note]
> Generally, authors are encouraged to use the broader fields rather than the narrower fields, as the narrower fields tend to expose Western biases. For example, while it is common in some Western cultures to have a given name and a family name, in that order (and thus often referred to as a *first name* and a *surname*), many cultures put the family name first and the given name second, and many others simply have one name (a *mononym*). Having a single field is therefore more flexible.

Some fields are only appropriate for certain form controls. An [autofill field](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) name is inappropriate for a control if the control does not belong to the group listed for that [autofill field](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) in the fifth column of the first row describing that [autofill field](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) in the table below. What controls fall into each group is described below the table.

| Field name | Meaning | Canonical Format | Canonical Format Example | Control group |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| "`name`" | Full name | Free-form text, no newlines | Sir Timothy John Berners-Lee, OM, KBE, FRS, FREng, FRSA | [Text](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
|  | "`honorific-prefix`" | Prefix or title (e.g. "Mr.", "Ms.", "Dr.", "Mlle") | Free-form text, no newlines | Sir | [Text](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
| "`given-name`" | Given name (in some Western cultures, also known as the *first name*) | Free-form text, no newlines | Timothy | [Text](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
| "`additional-name`" | Additional names (in some Western cultures, also known as *middle names*, forenames other than the first name) | Free-form text, no newlines | John | [Text](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
| "`family-name`" | Family name (in some Western cultures, also known as the *last name* or *surname*) | Free-form text, no newlines | Berners-Lee | [Text](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
| "`honorific-suffix`" | Suffix (e.g. "Jr.", "B.Sc.", "MBASW", "II") | Free-form text, no newlines | OM, KBE, FRS, FREng, FRSA | [Text](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
| "`nickname`" | Nickname, screen name, handle: a typically short name used instead of the full name | Free-form text, no newlines | Tim | [Text](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
| "`organization-title`" | Job title (e.g. "Software Engineer", "Senior Vice President", "Deputy Managing Director") | Free-form text, no newlines | Professor | [Text](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
| "`username`" | A username | Free-form text, no newlines | timbl | [Username](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
| "`new-password`" | A new password (e.g. when creating an account or changing a password) | Free-form text, no newlines | GUMFXbadyrS3 | [Password](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
| "`current-password`" | The current password for the account identified by the [`username`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) field (e.g. when logging in) | Free-form text, no newlines | qwerty | [Password](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
| "`one-time-code`" | One-time code used for verifying user identity | Free-form text, no newlines | 123456 | [Password](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
| "`organization`" | Company name corresponding to the person, address, or contact information in the other fields associated with this field | Free-form text, no newlines | World Wide Web Consortium | [Text](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
| "`street-address`" | Street address (multiple lines, newlines preserved) | Free-form text | 32 Vassar Street   MIT Room 32-G524 | [Multiline](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
|  | "`address-line1`" | Street address (one line per field) | Free-form text, no newlines | 32 Vassar Street | [Text](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
| "`address-line2`" | Free-form text, no newlines | MIT Room 32-G524 | [Text](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
| "`address-line3`" | Free-form text, no newlines |  | [Text](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
| "`address-level4`" | The most fine-grained [administrative level](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute), in addresses with four administrative levels | Free-form text, no newlines |  | [Text](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
| "`address-level3`" | The [third administrative level](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute), in addresses with three or more administrative levels | Free-form text, no newlines |  | [Text](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
| "`address-level2`" | The [second administrative level](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute), in addresses with two or more administrative levels; in the countries with two administrative levels, this would typically be the city, town, village, or other locality within which the relevant street address is found | Free-form text, no newlines | Cambridge | [Text](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
| "`address-level1`" | The broadest [administrative level](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) in the address, i.e. the province within which the locality is found; for example, in the US, this would be the state; in Switzerland it would be the canton; in the UK, the post town | Free-form text, no newlines | MA | [Text](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
| "`country`" | Country code | Valid [ISO 3166-1-alpha-2 country code](https://www.iso.org/iso-3166-country-codes.html) [\[ISO3166\]](#references) | US | [Text](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
| "`country-name`" | Country name | Free-form text, no newlines; [derived from `country` in some cases](#4101972-processing-model) | US | [Text](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
| "`postal-code`" | Postal code, post code, ZIP code, CEDEX code (if CEDEX, append "CEDEX", and the *arrondissement*, if relevant, to the [`address-level2`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) field) | Free-form text, no newlines | 02139 | [Text](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |

|  | "`cc-given-name`" | Given name as given on the payment instrument (in some Western cultures, also known as the *first name*) | Free-form text, no newlines | Tim | [Text](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
| "`cc-additional-name`" | Additional names given on the payment instrument (in some Western cultures, also known as *middle names*, forenames other than the first name) | Free-form text, no newlines |  | [Text](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |
| "`cc-family-name`" | Family name given on the payment instrument (in some Western cultures, also known as the *last name* or *surname*) | Free-form text, no newlines | Berners-Lee | [Text](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |

| "`cc-exp-year`" | Year component of the expiration date of the payment instrument | [Valid integer](#2341-signed-integers) greater than zero | 2014 | [Numeric](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) |

**Address levels**: The "[`address-level1`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" – "[`address-level4`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" fields are used to describe the locality of the street address. Different locales have different numbers of levels. For example, the US uses two levels (state and town), the UK uses one or two depending on the address (the post town, and in some cases the locality), and China can use three (province, city, district). The "[`address-level1`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" field represents the widest administrative division. Different locales order the fields in different ways; for example, in the US the town (level 2) precedes the state (level 1); while in Japan the prefecture (level 1) precedes the city (level 2) which precedes the district (level 3). Authors are encouraged to provide forms that are presented in a way that matches the country's conventions (hiding, showing, and rearranging fields accordingly as the user changes the country).

###### 4.10.19.7.2 Processing model

Each [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element to which the [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) attribute [applies](#4105-the-input-element), each [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element, and each [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element, has an autofill hint set, an autofill scope, an autofill field name, a non-autofill credential type, and an IDL-exposed autofill value.

The [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model) specifies the specific kind of data expected in the field, e.g. "[`street-address`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" or "[`cc-exp`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)".

The [autofill hint set](#4101972-processing-model) identifies what address or contact information type the user agent is to look at, e.g. "[`shipping`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) [`fax`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" or "[`billing`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)".

The [non-autofill credential type](#4101972-processing-model) identifies a type of [credential](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#credential) that may be offered by the user agent when the user interacts with the field alongside other [autofill field](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) values. If this value is "`webauthn`" instead of null, selecting a credential of that type will resolve a pending [`conditional`](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#dom-credentialmediationrequirement-conditional) mediation [`navigator.credentials.get()`](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#dom-credentialscontainer-get) request, instead of autofilling the field.

> [!example]
> For example, a sign-in page could instruct the user agent to either autofill a saved password, or show a [public key credential](https://w3c.github.io/webauthn/#public-key-credential) that will resolve a pending [`navigator.credentials.get()`](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#dom-credentialscontainer-get) request. A user can select either to sign-in.
> 
> ```html
> <input name=password type=password autocomplete="current-password webauthn">
> ```

The [autofill scope](#4101972-processing-model) identifies the group of fields whose information concerns the same subject, and consists of the [autofill hint set](#4101972-processing-model) with, if applicable, the "`section-*`" prefix, e.g. "`billing`", "`section-parent shipping`", or "`section-child shipping
  home`".

These values are defined as the result of running the following algorithm:
1. If the element has no [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) attribute, then jump to the step labeled *default*.
2. Let tokens be the result of [splitting the attribute's value on ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).
3. If tokens is empty, then jump to the step labeled *default*.
4. Let index be the index of the last token in tokens.
5. Let field be the indexth token in tokens.
6. Let category be the result of [determining a field's category](#4101972-processing-model) given field.
7. If category is null, then jump to the step labeled *default*.
8. If category is Off or Automatic, and either tokens's [size](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) is greater than 1 or the element's [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) attribute is wearing the [autofill anchor mantle](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute), then jump to the step labeled *default*.
9. If category is Off, set the element's [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model) to the string "`off`", set its [autofill hint set](#4101972-processing-model) to empty, and set its [IDL-exposed autofill value](#4101972-processing-model) to the string "`off`". Then, return.
10. If category is Automatic, set the element's [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model) to the string "`on`", set its [autofill hint set](#4101972-processing-model) to empty, and set its [IDL-exposed autofill value](#4101972-processing-model) to the string "`on`". Then, return.
11. Let scope tokens be an empty list.
12. Let hint tokens be an empty set.
13. Let credential type be null.
14. Let IDL value have the same value as field.
15. If category is Credential and the indexth token in tokens is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for "[`webauthn`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)", then run the substeps that follow:
    1. Set credential type to "`webauthn`".
    2. If the indexth token in tokens is the first entry, then skip to the step labeled *done*.
    3. Decrement index by one.
    4. Set category to the result of [determining a field's category](#4101972-processing-model) given the indexth token in tokens.
    5. If category is not Normal and category is not Contact, then jump to the step labeled *default*.
    6. Set IDL value to the concatenation of the indexth token in tokens, a U+0020 SPACE character, and the previous value of IDL value.
16. If the indexth token in tokens is the first entry, then skip to the step labeled *done*.
17. Decrement index by one.
18. If category is Contact and the indexth token in tokens is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for one of the strings in the following list:
    - "[`home`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
    - "[`work`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
    - "[`mobile`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
    - "[`fax`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
    - "[`pager`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"

    then:
    1. Let contact be the matching string from the list above.
    2. Insert contact at the start of scope tokens.
    3. Add contact to hint tokens.
    4. Let IDL value be the concatenation of contact, a U+0020 SPACE character, and the previous value of IDL value.
    5. If the indexth entry in tokens is the first entry, then skip to the step labeled *done*.
    6. Decrement index by one.

19. If the indexth token in tokens is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for one of the strings in the following list:
    - "[`shipping`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"
    - "[`billing`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)"

    then:
    1. Let mode be the matching string from the list above.
    2. Insert mode at the start of scope tokens.
    3. Add mode to hint tokens.
    4. Let IDL value be the concatenation of mode, a U+0020 SPACE character, and the previous value of IDL value.
    5. If the indexth entry in tokens is the first entry, then skip to the step labeled *done*.
    6. Decrement index by one.

20. If the indexth entry in tokens is not the first entry, then jump to the step labeled *default*.
21. If the first eight characters of the indexth token in tokens are not an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "[`section-`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)", then jump to the step labeled *default*.
22. Let section be the indexth token in tokens, [converted to ASCII lowercase](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).
23. Insert section at the start of scope tokens.
24. Let IDL value be the concatenation of section, a U+0020 SPACE character, and the previous value of IDL value.
25. *Done*: Set the element's [autofill hint set](#4101972-processing-model) to hint tokens.
26. Set the element's [non-autofill credential type](#4101972-processing-model) to credential type.
27. Set the element's [autofill scope](#4101972-processing-model) to scope tokens.
28. Set the element's [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model) to field.
29. Set the element's [IDL-exposed autofill value](#4101972-processing-model) to IDL value.
30. Return.
31. *Default*: Set the element's [IDL-exposed autofill value](#4101972-processing-model) to the empty string, and its [autofill hint set](#4101972-processing-model) and [autofill scope](#4101972-processing-model) to empty.
32. If the element's [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) attribute is wearing the [autofill anchor mantle](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute), then set the element's [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model) to the empty string and return.
33. Let form be the element's [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms), if any, or null otherwise.
34. If form is not null and form's [`autocomplete`](#4103-the-form-element) attribute is in the [Off](#4103-the-form-element) state, then set the element's [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model) to "[`off`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)".

    Otherwise, set the element's [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model) to "[`on`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)".

To determine a field's category, given field:
1. If the field is not an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for one of the tokens given in the first column of the following table, then return null.

   | Token | Category |
   | --- | --- |
   | "[`off`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" | Off |
   | "[`on`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" | Automatic |
   | "[`name`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" | Normal |
   | "[`honorific-prefix`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" | Normal |
   | "[`given-name`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" | Normal |
   | "[`additional-name`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" | Normal |
   | "[`family-name`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" | Normal |
   | "[`honorific-suffix`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" | Normal |
   | "[`nickname`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" | Normal |
   | "[`organization-title`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" | Normal |
   | "[`username`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" | Normal |
   | "[`new-password`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" | Normal |
   | "[`current-password`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" | Normal |
   | "[`one-time-code`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" | Normal |

---

For the purposes of autofill, a control's data depends on the kind of control:

An [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element with its [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute in the [Email](#410515-email-state-typeemail) state and with the [`multiple`](#410535-the-multiple-attribute) attribute specified

The element's [value*s*](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

Any other [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element

A [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element

The element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

A [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element with its [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute specified

The [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements in the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element's [list of options](#4107-the-select-element) that have their [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) set to true.

Any other [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element

The [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element in the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element's [list of options](#4107-the-select-element) that has its [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) set to true.

---

How to process the [autofill hint set](#4101972-processing-model), [autofill scope](#4101972-processing-model), and [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model) depends on the mantle that the [`autocomplete`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) attribute is wearing.

When wearing the [autofill expectation mantle](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)...

When an element's [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model) is "[`off`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)", the user agent should not remember the [control's data](#4101972-processing-model), and should not offer past values to the user.

> [!note]
> In addition, when an element's [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model) is "[`off`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)", [values are reset](#7462-updating-the-document) when [reactivating a document](#7462-updating-the-document).

> [!example]
> Banks frequently do not want UAs to prefill login information:
> 
> ```html
> <p><label>Account: <input type="text" name="ac" autocomplete="off"></label></p>
> <p><label>PIN: <input type="password" name="pin" autocomplete="off"></label></p>
> ```

When an element's [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model) is *not* "[`off`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)", the user agent may store the [control's data](#4101972-processing-model), and may offer previously stored values to the user.

> [!example]
> For example, suppose a user visits a page with this control:
> 
> ```html
> <select name="country">
>  <option>Afghanistan
>  <option>Albania
>  <option>Algeria
>  <option>Andorra
>  <option>Angola
>  <option>Antigua and Barbuda
>  <option>Argentina
>  <option>Armenia
>  <!-- ... -->
>  <option>Yemen
>  <option>Zambia
>  <option>Zimbabwe
> </select>
> ```
> 
> This might render as follows:
> 
> ![A drop-down control with a long alphabetical list of countries.](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/select-country-1.png)
> 
> Suppose that on the first visit to this page, the user selects "Zambia". On the second visit, the user agent could duplicate the entry for Zambia at the top of the list, so that the interface instead looks like this:
> 
> ![The same drop-down control with the alphabetical list of countries, but with Zambia as an entry at the top.](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/select-country-2.png)

When the [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model) is "[`on`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)", the user agent should attempt to use heuristics to determine the most appropriate values to offer the user, e.g. based on the element's [`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) value, the position of the element in its [tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), what other fields exist in the form, and so forth.

When the [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model) is one of the names of the [autofill fields](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) described above, the user agent should provide suggestions that match the meaning of the field name as given in the table earlier in this section. The [autofill hint set](#4101972-processing-model) should be used to select amongst multiple possible suggestions.

> [!example]
> For example, if a user once entered one address into fields that used the "[`shipping`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" keyword, and another address into fields that used the "[`billing`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" keyword, then in subsequent forms only the first address would be suggested for form controls whose [autofill hint set](#4101972-processing-model) contains the keyword "[`shipping`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)". Both addresses might be suggested, however, for address-related form controls whose [autofill hint set](#4101972-processing-model) does not contain either keyword.

When wearing the [autofill anchor mantle](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)...

When the [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model) is not the empty string, then the user agent must act as if the user had specified the [control's data](#4101972-processing-model) for the given [autofill hint set](#4101972-processing-model), [autofill scope](#4101972-processing-model), and [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model) combination.

When the user agent autofills form controls, elements with the same [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) and the same [autofill scope](#4101972-processing-model) must use data relating to the same person, address, payment instrument, and contact details. When a user agent autofills "[`country`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" and "[`country-name`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" fields with the same [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) and [autofill scope](#4101972-processing-model), and the user agent has a value for the [`country`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" field(s), then the "[`country-name`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" field(s) must be filled using a human-readable name for the same country. When a user agent fills in multiple fields at once, all fields with the same [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model), [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms), and [autofill scope](#4101972-processing-model) must be filled with the same value.

> [!example]
> Suppose a user agent knows of two phone numbers, +1 555 123 1234 and +1 555 666 7777. It would not be conforming for the user agent to fill a field with `autocomplete="shipping tel-local-prefix"` with the value "123" and another field in the same form with `autocomplete="shipping tel-local-suffix"` with the value "7777". The only valid prefilled values given the aforementioned information would be "123" and "1234", or "666" and "7777", respectively.

> [!example]
> Similarly, if a form for some reason contained both a "[`cc-exp`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" field and a "[`cc-exp-month`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" field, and the user agent prefilled the form, then the month component of the former would have to match the latter.

> [!example]
> This requirement interacts with the [autofill anchor mantle](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) also. Consider the following markup snippet:
> 
> ```html
> <form>
>  <input type=hidden autocomplete="nickname" value="TreePlate">
>  <input type=text autocomplete="nickname">
> </form>
> ```
> 
> The only value that a conforming user agent could suggest in the text control is "TreePlate", the value given by the hidden [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element.

The "`section-*`" tokens in the [autofill scope](#4101972-processing-model) are opaque; user agents must not attempt to derive meaning from the precise values of these tokens.

> [!example]
> For example, it would not be conforming if the user agent decided that it should offer the address it knows to be the user's daughter's address for "`section-child`" and the addresses it knows to be the user's spouses' addresses for "`section-spouse`".

The autocompletion mechanism must be implemented by the user agent acting as if the user had modified the [control's data](#4101972-processing-model), and must be done at a time where the element is [mutable](#410182-mutability) (e.g. just after the element has been inserted into the document, or when the user agent [stops parsing](#1327-the-end)). User agents must only prefill controls using values that the user could have entered.

> [!example]
> For example, if a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element only has [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements with values "Steve" and "Rebecca", "Jay", and "Bob", and has an [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model) "[`given-name`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)", but the user agent's only idea for what to prefill the field with is "Evan", then the user agent cannot prefill the field. It would not be conforming to somehow set the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element to the value "Evan", since the user could not have done so themselves.

A user agent prefilling a form control must not discriminate between form controls that are [in a document tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) and those that are [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree); that is, it is not conforming to make the decision on whether or not to autofill based on whether the element's [root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) is a [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) versus a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object).

A user agent prefilling a form control's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) must not cause that control to [suffer from a type mismatch](#410211-definitions), [suffer from being too long](#410211-definitions), [suffer from being too short](#410211-definitions), [suffer from an underflow](#410211-definitions), [suffer from an overflow](#410211-definitions), or [suffer from a step mismatch](#410211-definitions). A user agent prefilling a form control's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) must not cause that control to [suffer from a pattern mismatch](#410211-definitions) either. Where possible given the control's constraints, user agents must use the format given as canonical in the aforementioned table. Where it's not possible for the canonical format to be used, user agents should use heuristics to attempt to convert values so that they can be used.

> [!example]
> For example, if the user agent knows that the user's middle name is "Ines", and attempts to prefill a form control that looks like this:
> 
> ```html
> <input name=middle-initial maxlength=1 autocomplete="additional-name">
> ```
> 
> ...then the user agent could convert "Ines" to "I" and prefill it that way.

> [!example]
> A more elaborate example would be with month values. If the user agent knows that the user's birthday is the 27th of July 2012, then it might try to prefill all of the following controls with slightly different values, all driven from this information:
> 
> ```html
> <input name=b type=month autocomplete="bday">
> ```
> 
> ```html
> <select name=c autocomplete="bday">
>  <option>Jan
>  <option>Feb
>  ...
>  <option>Jul
>  <option>Aug
>  ...
> </select>
> ```
> 
> ```html
> <input name=a type=number min=1 max=12 autocomplete="bday-month">
> ```
> 
> ```html
> <input name=a type=number min=0 max=11 autocomplete="bday-month">
> ```
> 
> ```html
> <input name=a type=number min=1 max=11 autocomplete="bday-month">
> ```
> 
> |  | 2012-07 | The day is dropped since the [Month](#410518-month-state-typemonth) state only accepts a month/year combination. (Note that this example is non-conforming, because the [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model) [`bday`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute) is not allowed with the [Month](#410518-month-state-typemonth) state.) |
> | --- | --- | --- |
> |  | July | The user agent picks the month from the listed options, either by noticing there are twelve options and picking the 7th, or by recognizing that one of the strings (three characters "Jul" followed by a newline and a space) is a close match for the name of the month (July) in one of the user agent's supported languages, or through some other similar mechanism. |
> |  | 7 | User agent converts "July" to a month number in the range 1..12, like the field. |
> |  | 6 | User agent converts "July" to a month number in the range 0..11, like the field. |
> |  |  | User agent doesn't fill in the field, since it can't make a good guess as to what the form expects. |

A user agent may allow the user to override an element's [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model), e.g. to change it from "[`off`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" to "[`on`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" to allow values to be remembered and prefilled despite the page author's objections, or to always "[`off`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)", never remembering values.

More specifically, user agents may in particular consider replacing the [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model) of form controls that match the description given in the first column of the following table, when their [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model) is either "[`on`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" or "[`off`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)", with the value given in the second cell of that row. If this table is used, the replacements must be done in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), since all but the first row references the [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model) of earlier elements. When the descriptions below refer to form controls being preceded or followed by others, they mean in the list of [listed elements](#4102-categories) that share the same [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms).

| Form control | New [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model) |
| --- | --- |
| an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Text](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch) state that is followed by an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Password](#410516-password-state-typepassword) state | "[`username`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" |
| an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Password](#410516-password-state-typepassword) state that is preceded by an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model) is "[`username`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" | "[`current-password`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" |
| an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Password](#410516-password-state-typepassword) state that is preceded by an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model) is "[`current-password`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" | "[`new-password`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" |
| an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Password](#410516-password-state-typepassword) state that is preceded by an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [autofill field name](#4101972-processing-model) is "[`new-password`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" | "[`new-password`](#4101971-autofilling-form-controls-the-autocomplete-attribute)" |

The `autocomplete` IDL attribute, on getting, must return the element's [IDL-exposed autofill value](#4101972-processing-model).

#### 4.10.20 APIs for the text control selections

The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) and [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements define several attributes and methods for handling their selection. Their shared algorithms are defined here.

`element.select()`

Selects everything in the text control.

`element.selectionStart [ = value ]`

Returns the offset to the start of the selection.

Can be set, to change the start of the selection.

`element.selectionEnd [ = value ]`

Returns the offset to the end of the selection.

Can be set, to change the end of the selection.

`element.selectionDirection [ = value ]`

Returns the current direction of the selection.

Can be set, to change the direction of the selection.

The possible values are "`forward`", "`backward`", and "`none`".

`element.setSelectionRange(start, end [, direction])`

Changes the selection to cover the given substring in the given direction. If the direction is omitted, it will be reset to be the platform default (none or forward).

`element.setRangeText(replacement [, start, end [, selectionMode ] ])`

Replaces a range of text with the new text. If the start and end arguments are not provided, the range is assumed to be the selection.

The final argument determines how the selection will be set after the text has been replaced. The possible values are:

"[`select`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections)"

Selects the newly inserted text.

"[`start`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections)"

Moves the selection to just before the inserted text.

"[`end`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections)"

Moves the selection to just after the selected text.

"[`preserve`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections)"

Attempts to preserve the selection. This is the default.

All [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements to which these APIs [apply](#4105-the-input-element), and all [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements, have either a selection or a text entry cursor position at all times (even for elements that are not [being rendered](#151-introduction)), measured in offsets into the [code units](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) of the control's [relevant value](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections). The initial state must consist of a [text entry cursor](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) at the beginning of the control.

For [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements, these APIs must operate on the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value). For [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements, these APIs must operate on the element's [API value](#410181-a-form-controls-value). In the below algorithms, we call the value string being operated on the relevant value.

> [!example]
> The use of [API value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) instead of [raw value](#41011-the-textarea-element) for [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements means that U+000D (CR) characters are normalized away. For example,
> 
> ```html
> <textarea id="demo"></textarea>
> <script>
>  demo.value = "A\r\nB";
>  demo.setRangeText("replaced", 0, 2);
>  assert(demo.value === "replacedB");
> </script>
> ```
> 
> If we had operated on the [raw value](#41011-the-textarea-element) of "`A\r\nB`", then we would have replaced the characters "`A\r`", ending up with a result of "`replaced\nB`". But since we used the [API value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of "`A\nB`", we replaced the characters "`A\n`", giving "`replacedB`".

> [!note]
> Characters with no visible rendering, such as U+200D ZERO WIDTH JOINER, still count as characters. Thus, for instance, the selection can include just an invisible character, and the text insertion cursor can be placed to one side or another of such a character.

Whenever the [relevant value](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) changes for an element to which these APIs apply, run these steps:
1. If the element has a [selection](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections):
   1. If the start of the selection is now past the end of the [relevant value](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), set it to the end of the [relevant value](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections).
   2. If the end of the selection is now past the end of the [relevant value](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), set it to the end of the [relevant value](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections).
   3. If the user agent does not support empty selection, and both the start and end of the selection are now pointing to the end of the [relevant value](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), then instead set the element's [text entry cursor position](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) to the end of the [relevant value](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), removing any selection.
2. Otherwise, the element must have a [text entry cursor position](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) position. If it is now past the end of the [relevant value](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), set it to the end of the [relevant value](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections).

> [!note]
> In some cases where the [relevant value](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) changes, other parts of the specification will also modify the [text entry cursor position](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), beyond just the clamping steps above. For example, see the [`value`](#41011-the-textarea-element) setter for [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element).

Where possible, user interface features for changing the [text selection](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) in [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) and [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements must be implemented using the [set the selection range](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) algorithm so that, e.g., all the same events fire.

The [selections](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) of [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) and [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements have a selection direction, which is either "`forward`", "`backward`", or "`none`". The exact meaning of the selection direction depends on the platform. This direction is set when the user manipulates the selection. The initial [selection direction](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) must be "`none`" if the platform supports that direction, or "`forward`" otherwise.

To set the selection direction of an element to a given direction, update the element's [selection direction](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) to the given direction, unless the direction is "`none`" and the platform does not support that direction; in that case, update the element's [selection direction](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) to "`forward`".

> [!note]
> On Windows, the direction indicates the position of the caret relative to the selection: a "`forward`" selection has the caret at the end of the selection and a "`backward`" selection has the caret at the start of the selection. Windows has no "`none`" direction.
> 
> On Mac, the direction indicates which end of the selection is affected when the user adjusts the size of the selection using the arrow keys with the Shift modifier: the "`forward`" direction means the end of the selection is modified, and the "`backward`" direction means the start of the selection is modified. The "`none`" direction is the default on Mac, it indicates that no particular direction has yet been selected. The user sets the direction implicitly when first adjusting the selection, based on which directional arrow key was used.

The `select()` method, when invoked, must run the following steps:
1. If this element is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element, and either [`select()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) [does not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to this element or the corresponding control has no selectable text, return.

   > [!example]
