   > For instance, in a user agent where [`<input type=color>`](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) is rendered as a color well with a picker, as opposed to a text control accepting a hexadecimal color code, there would be no selectable text, and thus calls to the method are ignored.

2. [Set the selection range](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) with 0 and infinity.

The `selectionStart` attribute's getter must run the following steps:
1. If this element is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element, and [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) [does not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to this element, return null.
2. If there is no [selection](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), return the [code unit](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) offset within the [relevant value](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) to the character that immediately follows the [text entry cursor](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections).
3. Return the [code unit](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) offset within the [relevant value](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) to the character that immediately follows the start of the [selection](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections).

The [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) attribute's setter must run the following steps:
1. If this element is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element, and [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) [does not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to this element, throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Let end be the value of this element's [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) attribute.
3. If end is less than the given value, set end to the given value.
4. [Set the selection range](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) with the given value, end, and the value of this element's [`selectionDirection`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) attribute.

The `selectionEnd` attribute's getter must run the following steps:
1. If this element is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element, and [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) [does not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to this element, return null.
2. If there is no [selection](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections), return the [code unit](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) offset within the [relevant value](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) to the character that immediately follows the [text entry cursor](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections).
3. Return the [code unit](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) offset within the [relevant value](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) to the character that immediately follows the end of the [selection](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections).

The [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) attribute's setter must run the following steps:
1. If this element is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element, and [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) [does not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to this element, throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. [Set the selection range](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) with the value of this element's [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) attribute, the given value, and the value of this element's [`selectionDirection`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) attribute.

The `selectionDirection` attribute's getter must run the following steps:
1. If this element is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element, and [`selectionDirection`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) [does not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to this element, return null.
2. Return this element's [selection direction](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections).

The [`selectionDirection`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) attribute's setter must run the following steps:
1. If this element is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element, and [`selectionDirection`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) [does not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to this element, throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. [Set the selection range](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) with the value of this element's [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) attribute, the value of this element's [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) attribute, and the given value.

The `setSelectionRange(start, end,
  direction)` method, when invoked, must run the following steps:
1. If this element is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element, and [`setSelectionRange()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) [does not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to this element, throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. [Set the selection range](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) with start, end, and direction.

To set the selection range with an integer or null start, an integer or null or the special value infinity end, and optionally a string direction, run the following steps:
1. If start is null, let start be 0.
2. If end is null, let end be 0.
3. Set the [selection](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) of the text control to the sequence of [code units](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) within the [relevant value](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) starting with the code unit at the startth position (in logical order) and ending with the code unit at the (end-1)th position. Arguments greater than the [length](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) of the [relevant value](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) of the text control (including the special value infinity) must be treated as pointing at the end of the text control. If end is less than or equal to start, then the start of the selection and the end of the selection must both be placed immediately before the character with offset end. In UAs where there is no concept of an empty selection, this must set the cursor to be just before the character with offset end.
4. If direction is not [identical to](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) either "`backward`" or "`forward`", or if the direction argument was not given, set direction to "`none`".
5. [Set the selection direction](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) of the text control to direction.
6. If the previous steps caused the [selection](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) of the text control to be modified (in either extent or [direction](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections)), then [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [user interaction task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given the element to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`select`](#events) at the element, with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true.

The `setRangeText(replacement, start,
  end, selectMode)` method, when invoked, must run the following steps:
1. If this element is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element, and [`setRangeText()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) [does not apply](#4105-the-input-element) to this element, throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Set this element's [dirty value flag](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to true.
3. If the method has only one argument, then let start and end have the values of the [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) attribute and the [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) attribute respectively.

   Otherwise, let start, end have the values of the second and third arguments respectively.

4. If start is greater than end, then throw an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
5. If start is greater than the [length](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) of the [relevant value](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) of the text control, then set it to the [length](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) of the [relevant value](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) of the text control.
6. If end is greater than the [length](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) of the [relevant value](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) of the text control, then set it to the [length](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) of the [relevant value](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) of the text control.
7. Let selection start be the current value of the [`selectionStart`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) attribute.
8. Let selection end be the current value of the [`selectionEnd`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) attribute.
9. If start is less than end, delete the sequence of [code units](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) within the element's [relevant value](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) starting with the code unit at the startth position and ending with the code unit at the (end-1)th position.
10. Insert the value of the first argument into the text of the [relevant value](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) of the text control, immediately before the startth [code unit](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).
11. Let new length be the [length](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) of the value of the first argument.
12. Let new end be the sum of start and new length.
13. Run the appropriate set of substeps from the following list:

    If the fourth argument's value is "`select`"

    Let selection start be start.

    Let selection end be new end.

    If the fourth argument's value is "`start`"

    Let selection start and selection end be start.

    If the fourth argument's value is "`end`"

    Let selection start and selection end be new end.

    If the fourth argument's value is "`preserve`"

    If the method has only one argument
    1. Let old length be end minus start.
    2. Let delta be new length minus old length.
    3. If selection start is greater than end, then increment it by delta. (If delta is negative, i.e. the new text is shorter than the old text, then this will *decrease* the value of selection start.)

       Otherwise: if selection start is greater than start, then set it to start. (This snaps the start of the selection to the start of the new text if it was in the middle of the text that it replaced.)

    4. If selection end is greater than end, then increment it by delta in the same way.

       Otherwise: if selection end is greater than start, then set it to new end. (This snaps the end of the selection to the end of the new text if it was in the middle of the text that it replaced.)

14. [Set the selection range](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) with selection start and selection end.

The [`setRangeText()`](#41020-apis-for-the-text-control-selections) method uses the following enumeration:

```webidl
enum SelectionMode {
  "select",
  "start",
  "end",
  "preserve" // default
};
```

---

> [!example]
> To obtain the currently selected text, the following JavaScript suffices:
> 
> ```javascript
> var selectionText = control.value.substring(control.selectionStart, control.selectionEnd);
> ```
> 
> ...where control is the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) or [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element.

> [!example]
> To add some text at the start of a text control, while maintaining the text selection, the three attributes must be preserved:
> 
> ```javascript
> var oldStart = control.selectionStart;
> var oldEnd = control.selectionEnd;
> var oldDirection = control.selectionDirection;
> var prefix = "http://";
> control.value = prefix + control.value;
> control.setSelectionRange(oldStart + prefix.length, oldEnd + prefix.length, oldDirection);
> ```
> 
> ...where control is the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) or [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element.

#### 4.10.21 Constraints

##### 4.10.21.1 Definitions

A [submittable element](#4102-categories) is a candidate for constraint validation except when a condition has barred the element from constraint validation. (For example, an element is [barred from constraint validation](#410211-definitions) if it has a [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element ancestor.)

An element can have a custom validity error message defined. Initially, an element must have its [custom validity error message](#410211-definitions) set to the empty string. When its value is not the empty string, the element is [suffering from a custom error](#410211-definitions). It can be set using the [`setCustomValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) method, except for [form-associated custom elements](#4133-core-concepts). [Form-associated custom elements](#4133-core-concepts) can have a [custom validity error message](#410211-definitions) set via their [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) object's [`setValidity()`](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements) method. The user agent should use the [custom validity error message](#410211-definitions) when alerting the user to the problem with the control.

An element can be constrained in various ways. The following is the list of validity states that a form control can be in, making the control invalid for the purposes of constraint validation. (The definitions below are non-normative; other parts of this specification define more precisely when each state applies or does not.)

Suffering from being missing

When a control has no [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) but has a `required` attribute ([`input`](#4105-the-input-element) [`required`](#410534-the-required-attribute), [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) [`required`](#41011-the-textarea-element)); or, more complicated rules for [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) elements and controls in [radio button groups](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio), as specified in their sections.

When the [`setValidity()`](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements) method sets `valueMissing` flag to true for a [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts).

Suffering from a type mismatch

When a control that allows arbitrary user input has a [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) that is not in the correct syntax ([Email](#410515-email-state-typeemail), [URL](#410514-url-state-typeurl)).

When the [`setValidity()`](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements) method sets `typeMismatch` flag to true for a [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts).

Suffering from a pattern mismatch

When a control has a [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) that doesn't satisfy the [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute) attribute.

When the [`setValidity()`](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements) method sets `patternMismatch` flag to true for a [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts).

Suffering from being too long

When a control has a [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) that is too long for the [form control `maxlength` attribute](#410193-limiting-user-input-length-the-maxlength-attribute) ([`input`](#4105-the-input-element) [`maxlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) [`maxlength`](#41011-the-textarea-element)).

When the [`setValidity()`](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements) method sets `tooLong` flag to true for a [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts).

Suffering from being too short

When a control has a [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) that is too short for the [form control `minlength` attribute](#410194-setting-minimum-input-length-requirements-the-minlength-attribute) ([`input`](#4105-the-input-element) [`minlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes), [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) [`minlength`](#41011-the-textarea-element)).

When the [`setValidity()`](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements) method sets `tooShort` flag to true for a [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts).

Suffering from an underflow

When a control has a [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) that is not the empty string and is too low for the [`min`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attribute.

When the [`setValidity()`](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements) method sets `rangeUnderflow` flag to true for a [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts).

Suffering from an overflow

When a control has a [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) that is not the empty string and is too high for the [`max`](#410537-the-min-and-max-attributes) attribute.

When the [`setValidity()`](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements) method sets `rangeOverflow` flag to true for a [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts).

Suffering from a step mismatch

When a control has a [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) that doesn't fit the rules given by the [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute) attribute.

When the [`setValidity()`](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements) method sets `stepMismatch` flag to true for a [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts).

Suffering from bad input

When a control has incomplete input and the user agent does not think the user ought to be able to submit the form in its current state.

When the [`setValidity()`](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements) method sets `badInput` flag to true for a [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts).

Suffering from a custom error

When a control's [custom validity error message](#410211-definitions) (as set by the element's [`setCustomValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) method or [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface)'s [`setValidity()`](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements) method) is not the empty string.

> [!note]
> An element can still suffer from these states even when the element is [disabled](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute); thus these states can be represented in the DOM even if validating the form during submission wouldn't indicate a problem to the user.

An element satisfies its constraints if it is not suffering from any of the above [validity states](#410211-definitions).

##### 4.10.21.2 Constraint validation

When the user agent is required to statically validate the constraints of [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element form, it must run the following steps, which return either a *positive* result (all the controls in the form are valid) or a *negative* result (there are invalid controls) along with a (possibly empty) list of elements that are invalid and for which no script has claimed responsibility:
1. Let controls be a list of all the [submittable elements](#4102-categories) whose [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) is form, in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
2. Let invalid controls be an initially empty list of elements.
3. For each element field in controls, in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees):
   1. If field is not a [candidate for constraint validation](#410211-definitions), then move on to the next element.
   2. Otherwise, if field [satisfies its constraints](#410211-definitions), then move on to the next element.
   3. Otherwise, add field to invalid controls.
4. If invalid controls is empty, then return a *positive* result.
5. Let unhandled invalid controls be an initially empty list of elements.
6. For each element field in invalid controls, if any, in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees):
   1. Let notCanceled be the result of [firing an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`invalid`](#events) at field, with the [`cancelable`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true.
   2. If notCanceled is true, then add field to unhandled invalid controls.
7. Return a *negative* result with the list of elements in the unhandled invalid controls list.

If a user agent is to interactively validate the constraints of [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element form, then the user agent must run the following steps:
1. [Statically validate the constraints](#410212-constraint-validation) of form, and let unhandled invalid controls be the list of elements returned if the result was *negative*.
2. If the result was *positive*, then return that result.
3. Report the problems with the constraints of at least one of the elements given in unhandled invalid controls to the user.
   - User agents may focus one of those elements in the process, by running the [focusing steps](#664-processing-model) for that element, and may change the scrolling position of the document, or perform some other action that brings the element to the user's attention. For elements that are [form-associated custom elements](#4133-core-concepts), user agents should use their [validation anchor](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements) instead, for the purposes of these actions.
   - User agents may report more than one constraint violation.
   - User agents may coalesce related constraint violation reports if appropriate (e.g. if multiple radio buttons in a [group](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio) are marked as required, only one error need be reported).
   - If one of the controls is not [being rendered](#151-introduction) (e.g. it has the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute set), then user agents may report a script error.
4. Return a *negative* result.

##### 4.10.21.3 The constraint validation API

`element.willValidate`

Returns true if the element will be validated when the form is submitted; false otherwise.

`element.setCustomValidity(message)`

Sets a custom error, so that the element would fail to validate. The given message is the message to be shown to the user when reporting the problem to the user.

If the argument is the empty string, clears the custom error.

`element.validity.valueMissing`

Returns true if the element has no value but is a required field; false otherwise.

`element.validity.typeMismatch`

Returns true if the element's value is not in the correct syntax; false otherwise.

`element.validity.patternMismatch`

Returns true if the element's value doesn't match the provided pattern; false otherwise.

`element.validity.tooLong`

Returns true if the element's value is longer than the provided maximum length; false otherwise.

`element.validity.tooShort`

Returns true if the element's value, if it is not the empty string, is shorter than the provided minimum length; false otherwise.

`element.validity.rangeUnderflow`

Returns true if the element's value is lower than the provided minimum; false otherwise.

`element.validity.rangeOverflow`

Returns true if the element's value is higher than the provided maximum; false otherwise.

`element.validity.stepMismatch`

Returns true if the element's value doesn't fit the rules given by the [`step`](#410538-the-step-attribute) attribute; false otherwise.

`element.validity.badInput`

Returns true if the user has provided input in the user interface that the user agent is unable to convert to a value; false otherwise.

`element.validity.customError`

Returns true if the element has a custom error; false otherwise.

`element.validity.valid`

Returns true if the element's value has no validity problems; false otherwise.

`valid = element.checkValidity()`

Returns true if the element's value has no validity problems; false otherwise. Fires an [`invalid`](#events) event at the element in the latter case.

`valid = element.reportValidity()`

Returns true if the element's value has no validity problems; otherwise, returns false, fires an [`invalid`](#events) event at the element, and (if the event isn't canceled) reports the problem to the user.

`element.validationMessage`

Returns the error message that would be shown to the user if the element was to be checked for validity.

The `willValidate` attribute's getter must return true, if this element is a [candidate for constraint validation](#410211-definitions), and false otherwise (i.e., false if any conditions are [barring it from constraint validation](#410211-definitions)).

The `willValidate` attribute of [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) interface, on getting, must throw a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) is not a [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts). Otherwise, it must return true if the [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) is a [candidate for constraint validation](#410211-definitions), and false otherwise.

The `setCustomValidity(error)` method steps are:
1. Set error to the result of [normalizing newlines](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) given error.
2. Set the [custom validity error message](#410211-definitions) to error.

> [!example]
> In the following example, a script checks the value of a form control each time it is edited, and whenever it is not a valid value, uses the [`setCustomValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) method to set an appropriate message.
> 
> ```html
> <label>Feeling: <input name=f type="text" oninput="check(this)"></label>
> <script>
>  function check(input) {
>    if (input.value == "good" ||
>        input.value == "fine" ||
>        input.value == "tired") {
>      input.setCustomValidity('"' + input.value + '" is not a feeling.');
>    } else {
>      // input is fine -- reset the error message
>      input.setCustomValidity('');
>    }
>  }
> </script>
> ```

The `validity` attribute's getter must return a [`ValidityState`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) object that represents the [validity states](#410211-definitions) of this element. This object is [live](#215-scripting).

The `validity` attribute of [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) interface, on getting, must throw a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) is not a [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts). Otherwise, it must return a [`ValidityState`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) object that represents the [validity states](#410211-definitions) of the [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface). This object is [live](#215-scripting).

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface ValidityState {
  readonly attribute boolean valueMissing;
  readonly attribute boolean typeMismatch;
  readonly attribute boolean patternMismatch;
  readonly attribute boolean tooLong;
  readonly attribute boolean tooShort;
  readonly attribute boolean rangeUnderflow;
  readonly attribute boolean rangeOverflow;
  readonly attribute boolean stepMismatch;
  readonly attribute boolean badInput;
  readonly attribute boolean customError;
  readonly attribute boolean valid;
};
```

A [`ValidityState`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) object has the following attributes. On getting, they must return true if the corresponding condition given in the following list is true, and false otherwise.

`valueMissing`

The control is [suffering from being missing](#410211-definitions).

`typeMismatch`

The control is [suffering from a type mismatch](#410211-definitions).

`patternMismatch`

The control is [suffering from a pattern mismatch](#410211-definitions).

`tooLong`

The control is [suffering from being too long](#410211-definitions).

`tooShort`

The control is [suffering from being too short](#410211-definitions).

`rangeUnderflow`

The control is [suffering from an underflow](#410211-definitions).

`rangeOverflow`

The control is [suffering from an overflow](#410211-definitions).

`stepMismatch`

The control is [suffering from a step mismatch](#410211-definitions).

`badInput`

The control is [suffering from bad input](#410211-definitions).

`customError`

The control is [suffering from a custom error](#410211-definitions).

`valid`

None of the other conditions are true.

The check validity steps for an element element are:
1. If element is a [candidate for constraint validation](#410211-definitions) and does not [satisfy its constraints](#410211-definitions):
   1. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`invalid`](#events) at element, with the [`cancelable`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true (though canceling has no effect).
   2. Return false.
2. Return true.

The `checkValidity()` method, when invoked, must run the [check validity steps](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) on this element.

The `checkValidity()` method of the [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) interface must run these steps:
1. Let element be this [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface)'s [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface).
2. If element is not a [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts), then throw a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
3. Run the [check validity steps](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) on element.

The report validity steps for an element element are:
1. If element is a [candidate for constraint validation](#410211-definitions) and does not [satisfy its constraints](#410211-definitions):
   1. Let report be the result of [firing an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`invalid`](#events) at element, with the [`cancelable`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true.
   2. If report is true, then report the problems with the constraints of this element to the user. When reporting the problem with the constraints to the user, the user agent may run the [focusing steps](#664-processing-model) for element, and may change the scrolling position of the document, or perform some other action that brings element to the user's attention. User agents may report more than one constraint violation, if element suffers from multiple problems at once.
   3. Return false.
2. Return true.

The `reportValidity()` method, when invoked, must run the [report validity steps](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) on this element.

The `reportValidity()` method of the [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) interface must run these steps:
1. Let element be this [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface)'s [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface).
2. If element is not a [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts), then throw a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
3. Run the [report validity steps](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) on element.

The `validationMessage` attribute's getter must run these steps:
1. If this element is not a [candidate for constraint validation](#410211-definitions) or if this element [satisfies its constraints](#410211-definitions), then return the empty string.
2. Return a suitably localized message that the user agent would show the user if this were the only form control with a validity constraint problem. If the user agent would not actually show a textual message in such a situation (e.g., it would show a graphical cue instead), then return a suitably localized message that expresses (one or more of) the validity constraint(s) that the control does not satisfy. If the element is a [candidate for constraint validation](#410211-definitions) and is [suffering from a custom error](#410211-definitions), then the [custom validity error message](#410211-definitions) should be present in the return value.

##### 4.10.21.4 Security

Servers should not rely on client-side validation. Client-side validation can be intentionally bypassed by hostile users, and unintentionally bypassed by users of older user agents or automated tools that do not implement these features. The constraint validation features are only intended to improve the user experience, not to provide any kind of security mechanism.

#### 4.10.22 Form submission

##### 4.10.22.1 Introduction

*This section is non-normative.*

When a form is submitted, the data in the form is converted into the structure specified by the [enctype](#410196-form-submission-attributes), and then sent to the destination specified by the [action](#410196-form-submission-attributes) using the given [method](#410196-form-submission-attributes).

For example, take the following form:

```html
<form action="/find.cgi" method=get>
 <input type=text name=t>
 <input type=search name=q>
 <input type=submit>
</form>
```

If the user types in "cats" in the first field and "fur" in the second, and then hits the submit button, then the user agent will load `/find.cgi?t=cats&q=fur`.

On the other hand, consider this form:

```html
<form action="/find.cgi" method=post enctype="multipart/form-data">
 <input type=text name=t>
 <input type=search name=q>
 <input type=submit>
</form>
```

Given the same user input, the result on submission is quite different: the user agent instead does an HTTP POST to the given URL, with as the entity body something like the following text:

```
------kYFrd4jNJEgCervE
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="t"

cats
------kYFrd4jNJEgCervE
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="q"

fur
------kYFrd4jNJEgCervE--
```

##### 4.10.22.2 Implicit submission

A [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element's default button is the first [submit button](#4102-categories) in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) whose [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) is that [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element.

If the user agent supports letting the user submit a form implicitly (for example, on some platforms hitting the "enter" key while a text control is [focused](#662-data-model) implicitly submits the form), then doing so for a form, whose [default button](#410222-implicit-submission) has [activation behavior](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) and is not [disabled](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute), must cause the user agent to [fire a `click` event](#8183-event-firing) at that [default button](#410222-implicit-submission).

> [!note]
> There are pages on the web that are only usable if there is a way to implicitly submit forms, so user agents are strongly encouraged to support this.

If the form has no [submit button](#4102-categories), then the implicit submission mechanism must perform the following steps:
1. If the form has more than one [field that blocks implicit submission](#410222-implicit-submission), then return.
2. [Submit](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element from the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element itself with *[userInvolvement](#410223-form-submission-algorithm)* set to "[`activation`](#7421-supporting-concepts)".

For the purpose of the previous paragraph, an element is a field that blocks implicit submission of a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element if it is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) is that [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element and whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in one of the following states: [Text](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch), [Search](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch), [Telephone](#410513-telephone-state-typetel), [URL](#410514-url-state-typeurl), [Email](#410515-email-state-typeemail), [Password](#410516-password-state-typepassword), [Date](#410517-date-state-typedate), [Month](#410518-month-state-typemonth), [Week](#410519-week-state-typeweek), [Time](#4105110-time-state-typetime), [Local Date and Time](#4105111-local-date-and-time-state-typedatetime-local), [Number](#4105112-number-state-typenumber)

##### 4.10.22.3 Form submission algorithm

Each [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element has a constructing entry list boolean, initially false.

Each [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element has a firing submission events boolean, initially false.

To submit a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element form from an element submitter (typically a button), given an optional boolean submitted from `submit()` method (default false) and an optional [user navigation involvement](#7421-supporting-concepts) userInvolvement (default "[`none`](#7421-supporting-concepts)"):
1. If form [cannot navigate](#465-following-hyperlinks), then return.
2. If form's [constructing entry list](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) is true, then return.
3. Let form document be form's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
4. If form document's [active sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing) has its [sandboxed forms browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing) set, then return.
5. If submitted from [`submit()`](#4103-the-form-element) method is false:
   1. If form's [firing submission events](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) is true, then return.
   2. Set form's [firing submission events](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) to true.
   3. For each element field in the list of [submittable elements](#4102-categories) whose [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) is form, set field's [user validity](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to true.
   4. If the submitter element's [no-validate state](#410196-form-submission-attributes) is false, then [interactively validate the constraints](#410212-constraint-validation) of form and examine the result. If the result is negative (i.e., the constraint validation concluded that there were invalid fields and probably informed the user of this):
      1. Set form's [firing submission events](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) to false.
      2. Return.
   5. Let submitterButton be null if submitter is form. Otherwise, let submitterButton be submitter.
   6. Let shouldContinue be the result of [firing an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`submit`](#events) at form using [`SubmitEvent`](#4102210-the-submitevent-interface), with the [`submitter`](#4102210-the-submitevent-interface) attribute initialized to submitterButton, the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true, and the [`cancelable`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true.
   7. Set form's [firing submission events](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) to false.
   8. If shouldContinue is false, then return.
   9. If form [cannot navigate](#465-following-hyperlinks), then return.

      > [!note]
      > [Cannot navigate](#465-following-hyperlinks) is run again as dispatching the [`submit`](#events) event could have changed the outcome.

6. Let encoding be the result of [picking an encoding for the form](#410225-selecting-a-form-submission-encoding).
7. Let entry list be the result of [constructing the entry list](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) with form, submitter, and encoding.
8. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): entry list is not null.
9. If form [cannot navigate](#465-following-hyperlinks), then return.

   > [!note]
   > [Cannot navigate](#465-following-hyperlinks) is run again as dispatching the [`formdata`](#events) event in [constructing the entry list](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) could have changed the outcome.

10. Let method be the submitter element's [method](#410196-form-submission-attributes).
11. If method is [dialog](#410196-form-submission-attributes):
    1. If form does not have an ancestor [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) element, then return.
    2. Let subject be form's nearest ancestor [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) element.
    3. Let result be null.
    4. If submitter is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Image Button](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) state:
       1. Let (x, y) be the [selected coordinate](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage).
       2. Set result to the concatenation of x, "`,`", and y.
    5. Otherwise, if submitter is a [submit button](#4102-categories), then set result to submitter's [optional value](#410181-a-form-controls-value).
    6. [Close the dialog](#4114-the-dialog-element) subject with result and null.
    7. Return.
12. Let action be the submitter element's [action](#410196-form-submission-attributes).
13. If action is the empty string, let action be the [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) of the form document.
14. Let parsed action be the result of [encoding-parsing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given action, relative to submitter's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
15. If parsed action is failure, then return.
16. Let scheme be the [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) of parsed action.
17. Let enctype be the submitter element's [enctype](#410196-form-submission-attributes).
18. Let formTarget be null.
19. If the submitter element is a [submit button](#4102-categories) and it has a [`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) attribute, then set formTarget to the [`formtarget`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) attribute value.
20. Let target be the result of [getting an element's target](#423-the-base-element) given submitter's [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) and formTarget.
21. Let noopener be the result of [getting an element's noopener](#465-following-hyperlinks) with form, parsed action, and target.
22. Let targetNavigable be the first return value of applying [the rules for choosing a navigable](#7317-navigable-target-names) given target, form's [node navigable](#731-navigables), and noopener.
23. If targetNavigable is null, then return.
24. Let historyHandling be "[`auto`](#7421-supporting-concepts)".
25. If form document equals targetNavigable's [active document](#731-navigables), and form document has not yet [completely loaded](#758-finishing-the-loading-process), then set historyHandling to "[`replace`](#7421-supporting-concepts)".
26. Select the appropriate row in the table below based on scheme as given by the first cell of each row. Then, select the appropriate cell on that row based on method as given in the first cell of each column. Then, jump to the steps named in that cell and defined below the table.

    |  | [GET](#410196-form-submission-attributes) | [POST](#410196-form-submission-attributes) |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | `http` | [Mutate action URL](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) | [Submit as entity body](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) |
    | `https` | [Mutate action URL](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) | [Submit as entity body](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) |
    | `ftp` | [Get action URL](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) | [Get action URL](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) |
    | `javascript` | [Get action URL](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) | [Get action URL](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) |
    | `data` | [Mutate action URL](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) | [Get action URL](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) |
    | `mailto` | [Mail with headers](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) | [Mail as body](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) |

    If scheme is not one of those listed in this table, then the behavior is not defined by this specification. User agents should, in the absence of another specification defining this, act in a manner analogous to that defined in this specification for similar schemes.

    Each [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element has a planned navigation, which is either null or a [task](#8171-definitions); when the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) is first created, its [planned navigation](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) must be set to null. In the behaviors described below, when the user agent is required to plan to navigate to a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) url given an optional [POST resource](#7412-document-state)-or-null postResource (default null), it must run the following steps:
    1. Let referrerPolicy be the empty string.
    2. If the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element's [link types](#468-link-types) include the [`noreferrer`](#46815-link-type-noreferrer) keyword, then set referrerPolicy to "`no-referrer`".
    3. If the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) has a non-null [planned navigation](#410223-form-submission-algorithm), remove it from its [task queue](#8171-definitions).
    4. [Queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element and the following steps:
       1. Set the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element)'s [planned navigation](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) to null.
       2. [Navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation) targetNavigable to url using the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), with *[historyHandling](#7422-beginning-navigation)* set to historyHandling, *[userInvolvement](#7422-beginning-navigation)* set to userInvolvement, *[sourceElement](#7422-beginning-navigation)* set to submitter, *[referrerPolicy](#7422-beginning-navigation)* set to referrerPolicy, *[documentResource](#7422-beginning-navigation)* set to postResource, and *[formDataEntryList](#7422-beginning-navigation)* set to entry list.
    5. Set the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element)'s [planned navigation](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) to the just-queued [task](#8171-definitions).

    The behaviors are as follows:

    Mutate action URL

    Let pairs be the result of [converting to a list of name-value pairs](#410226-converting-an-entry-list-to-a-list-of-name-value-pairs) with entry list.

    Let query be the result of running the [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` serializer](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-urlencoded-serializer) with pairs and encoding.

    Set parsed action's [query](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-query) component to query.

    [Plan to navigate](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) to parsed action.

    Submit as entity body

    [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): method is [POST](#410196-form-submission-attributes).

    Switch on enctype:

    [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`](#410196-form-submission-attributes)

    Let pairs be the result of [converting to a list of name-value pairs](#410226-converting-an-entry-list-to-a-list-of-name-value-pairs) with entry list.

    Let body be the result of running the [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` serializer](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-urlencoded-serializer) with pairs and encoding.

    Set body to the result of [encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8-encode) body.

    Let mimeType be \`[`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-urlencoded)\`.

    [`multipart/form-data`](#410196-form-submission-attributes)

    Let body be the result of running the [`multipart/form-data` encoding algorithm](#410228-multipart-form-data) with entry list and encoding.

    Let mimeType be the [isomorphic encoding](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) of the concatenation of "`multipart/form-data; boundary=`" and the [`multipart/form-data` boundary string](#410228-multipart-form-data) generated by the [`multipart/form-data` encoding algorithm](#410228-multipart-form-data).

    [`text/plain`](#410196-form-submission-attributes)

    Let pairs be the result of [converting to a list of name-value pairs](#410226-converting-an-entry-list-to-a-list-of-name-value-pairs) with entry list.

    Let body be the result of running the [`text/plain` encoding algorithm](#410229-plain-text-form-data) with pairs.

    Set body to the result of [encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#encode) body using encoding.

    Let mimeType be \`[`text/plain`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.1.3)\`.

    [Plan to navigate](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) to parsed action given a [POST resource](#7412-document-state) whose [request body](#7412-document-state) is body and [request content-type](#7412-document-state) is mimeType.

    Get action URL

    [Plan to navigate](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) to parsed action.

    > [!note]
    > entry list is discarded.

    Mail with headers

    Let pairs be the result of [converting to a list of name-value pairs](#410226-converting-an-entry-list-to-a-list-of-name-value-pairs) with entry list.

    Let headers be the result of running the [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` serializer](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-urlencoded-serializer) with pairs and encoding.

    Replace occurrences of U+002B PLUS SIGN characters (+) in headers with the string "`%20`".

    Set parsed action's [query](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-query) to headers.

    [Plan to navigate](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) to parsed action.

    Mail as body

    Let pairs be the result of [converting to a list of name-value pairs](#410226-converting-an-entry-list-to-a-list-of-name-value-pairs) with entry list.

    Switch on enctype:

    [`text/plain`](#410196-form-submission-attributes)

    Let body be the result of running the [`text/plain` encoding algorithm](#410229-plain-text-form-data) with pairs.

    Set body to the result of running [UTF-8 percent-encode](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#string-utf-8-percent-encode) on body using the [default encode set](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#default-encode-set). [\[URL\]](#references)

    Otherwise

    Let body be the result of running the [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` serializer](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-urlencoded-serializer) with pairs and encoding.

    If parsed action's [query](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-query) is null, then set it to the empty string.

    If parsed action's [query](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-query) is not the empty string, then append a single U+0026 AMPERSAND character (&) to it.

    Append "`body=`" to parsed action's [query](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-query).

    Append body to parsed action's [query](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-query).

    [Plan to navigate](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) to parsed action.

##### 4.10.22.4 Constructing the entry list

An entry list is a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [entries](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list), typically representing the contents of a form. An entry is a tuple consisting of a name (a [scalar value string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings)) and a value (either a [scalar value string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) or a [`File`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file) object).

To create an entry given a string name, a string or [`Blob`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-Blob) object value, and optionally a [scalar value string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) filename:
1. Set name to the result of [converting](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) name into a [scalar value string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).
2. If value is a string, then set value to the result of [converting](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) value into a [scalar value string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).
3. Otherwise:
   1. If value is not a [`File`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file) object, then set value to a new [`File`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file) object, representing the same bytes, whose [`name`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-name) attribute value is "`blob`".
   2. If filename is given, then set value to a new [`File`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file) object, representing the same bytes, whose [`name`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-name) attribute is filename.

   > [!note]
   > These operations will create a new [`File`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file) object if either filename is given or the passed [`Blob`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-Blob) is not a [`File`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file) object. In those cases, the identity of the passed [`Blob`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-Blob) object is not kept.

4. Return an [entry](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) whose [name](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) is name and whose [value](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) is value.

To construct the entry list given a form, an optional submitter (default null), and an optional encoding (default [UTF-8](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8)):
1. If form's [constructing entry list](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) is true, then return null.
2. Set form's [constructing entry list](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) to true.
3. Let controls be a list of all the [submittable elements](#4102-categories) whose [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) is form, in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
4. Let entry list be a new empty [entry list](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list).
5. For each element field in controls, in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees):
   1. If any of the following are true:
      - field has a [`datalist`](#4108-the-datalist-element) element ancestor;
      - field is [disabled](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute);
      - field is a [button](#4102-categories) but it is not submitter;
      - field is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Checkbox](#4105115-checkbox-state-typecheckbox) state and whose [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is false; or
      - field is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Radio Button](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio) state and whose [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) is false,

      then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).

   2. If the field element is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Image Button](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) state:
      1. If the field element is not submitter, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
      2. If the field element has a [`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) attribute specified and its value is not the empty string, let name be that value followed by U+002E (.). Otherwise, let name be the empty string.
      3. Let namex be the concatenation of name and U+0078 (x).
      4. Let namey be the concatenation of name and U+0079 (y).
      5. Let (x, y) be the [selected coordinate](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage).
      6. [Create an entry](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) with namex and x, and [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) it to entry list.
      7. [Create an entry](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) with namey and y, and [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) it to entry list.
      8. [Continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   3. If the field is a [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts), then perform the [entry construction algorithm](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements) given field and entry list, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   4. If either the field element does not have a [`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) attribute specified, or its [`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) attribute's value is the empty string, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   5. Let name be the value of the field element's [`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) attribute.
   6. If the field element is a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element, then for each [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element in the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element's [list of options](#4107-the-select-element) whose [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) is true and that is not [disabled](#41010-the-option-element), [create an entry](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) with name and the [value](#41010-the-option-element) of the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element, and [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) it to entry list.
   7. Otherwise, if the field element is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Checkbox](#4105115-checkbox-state-typecheckbox) state or the [Radio Button](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio) state:
      1. If the field element has a [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute specified, then let value be the value of that attribute; otherwise, let value be the string "`on`".
      2. [Create an entry](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) with name and value, and [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) it to entry list.
   8. Otherwise, if the field element is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [File Upload](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) state:
      1. If there are no [selected files](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile), then [create an entry](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) with name and a new [`File`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file) object with an empty name, [`application/octet-stream`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.5.1) as type, and an empty body, and [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) it to entry list.
      2. Otherwise, for each file in [selected files](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile), [create an entry](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) with name and a [`File`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file) object representing the file, and [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) it to entry list.
   9. Otherwise, if the field element is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Hidden](#410511-hidden-state-typehidden) state and name is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for "[`_charset_`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute)":
      1. Let charset be the [name](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#name) of encoding.
      2. [Create an entry](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) with name and charset, and [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) it to entry list.
   10. Otherwise, [create an entry](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) with name and the [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of the field element, and [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) it to entry list.
   11. If the element has a [`dirname`](#410192-submitting-element-directionality-the-dirname-attribute) attribute, that attribute's value is not the empty string, and the element is an [auto-directionality form-associated element](#3264-the-dir-attribute):
       1. Let dirname be the value of the element's [`dirname`](#410192-submitting-element-directionality-the-dirname-attribute) attribute.
       2. Let dir be the string "`ltr`" if [the directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute) of the element is '[ltr](#3264-the-dir-attribute)', and "`rtl`" otherwise (i.e., when [the directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute) of the element is '[rtl](#3264-the-dir-attribute)').
       3. [Create an entry](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) with dirname and dir, and [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) it to entry list.

6. Let form data be a new [`FormData`](https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#formdata) object associated with entry list.
7. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`formdata`](#events) at form using [`FormDataEvent`](#4102211-the-formdataevent-interface), with the [`formData`](#4102211-the-formdataevent-interface) attribute initialized to form data and the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true.
8. Set form's [constructing entry list](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) to false.
9. Return a [clone](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of entry list.

##### 4.10.22.5 Selecting a form submission encoding

If the user agent is to pick an encoding for a form, it must run the following steps:
1. Let encoding be the [document's character encoding](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).
2. If the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element has an [`accept-charset`](#4103-the-form-element) attribute, set encoding to the return value of running these substeps:
   1. Let input be the value of the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element's [`accept-charset`](#4103-the-form-element) attribute.
   2. Let candidate encoding labels be the result of [splitting input on ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).
   3. Let candidate encodings be an empty list of [character encodings](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#encoding).
   4. For each token in candidate encoding labels in turn (in the order in which they were found in input), [get an encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-encoding-get) for the token and, if this does not result in failure, append the [encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#encoding) to candidate encodings.
   5. If candidate encodings is empty, return [UTF-8](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8).
   6. Return the first encoding in candidate encodings.
3. Return the result of [getting an output encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#get-an-output-encoding) from encoding.

##### 4.10.22.6 Converting an entry list to a list of name-value pairs

The [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-urlencoded) and [`text/plain`](#410229-plain-text-form-data) encoding algorithms take a list of name-value pairs, where the values must be strings, rather than an [entry list](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) where the value can be a [`File`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file). The following algorithm performs the conversion.

To convert to a list of name-value pairs an [entry list](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) entry list, run these steps:
1. Let list be an empty [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of name-value pairs.
2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) entry of entry list:
   1. Let name be entry's [name](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list), with every occurrence of U+000D (CR) not followed by U+000A (LF), and every occurrence of U+000A (LF) not preceded by U+000D (CR), replaced by a string consisting of U+000D (CR) and U+000A (LF).
   2. If entry's [value](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) is a [`File`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file) object, then let value be entry's [value](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list)'s [`name`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-name). Otherwise, let value be entry's [value](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list).
   3. Replace every occurrence of U+000D (CR) not followed by U+000A (LF), and every occurrence of U+000A (LF) not preceded by U+000D (CR), in value, by a string consisting of U+000D (CR) and U+000A (LF).
   4. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) to list a new name-value pair whose name is name and whose value is value.
3. Return list.

##### 4.10.22.7 URL-encoded form data

See URL for details on [`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-urlencoded). [\[URL\]](#references)

##### 4.10.22.8 Multipart form data

The `multipart/form-data` encoding algorithm, given an [entry list](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) entry list and an [encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#encoding) encoding, is as follows:
1. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) entry of entry list:
   1. Replace every occurrence of U+000D (CR) not followed by U+000A (LF), and every occurrence of U+000A (LF) not preceded by U+000D (CR), in entry's [name](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list), by a string consisting of a U+000D (CR) and U+000A (LF).
   2. If entry's [value](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) is not a [`File`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file) object, then replace every occurrence of U+000D (CR) not followed by U+000A (LF), and every occurrence of U+000A (LF) not preceded by U+000D (CR), in entry's [value](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list), by a string consisting of a U+000D (CR) and U+000A (LF).
2. Return the byte sequence resulting from encoding the entry list using the rules described by RFC 7578, Returning Values from Forms: `multipart/form-data`, given the following conditions: [\[RFC7578\]](#references)
   - Each [entry](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) in entry list is a *field*, the [name](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) of the entry is the *field name* and the [value](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) of the entry is the *field value*.
   - The order of parts must be the same as the order of fields in entry list. Multiple entries with the same name must be treated as distinct fields.
   - Field names, field values for non-file fields, and filenames for file fields, in the generated [`multipart/form-data`](#mime-types) resource must be set to the result of [encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#encode) the corresponding entry's name or value with encoding, converted to a byte sequence.
   - For field names and filenames for file fields, the result of the encoding in the previous bullet point must be escaped by replacing any 0x0A (LF) bytes with the byte sequence \``%0A`\`, 0x0D (CR) with \``%0D`\` and 0x22 (") with \``%22`\`. The user agent must not perform any other escapes.
   - The parts of the generated [`multipart/form-data`](#mime-types) resource that correspond to non-file fields must not have a \`[`Content-Type`](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource)\` header specified.
   - The boundary used by the user agent in generating the return value of this algorithm is the `multipart/form-data` boundary string. (This value is used to generate the MIME type of the form submission payload generated by this algorithm.)

For details on how to interpret [`multipart/form-data`](#mime-types) payloads, see RFC 7578. [\[RFC7578\]](#references)

##### 4.10.22.9 Plain text form data

The `text/plain` encoding algorithm, given a list of name-value pairs pairs, is as follows:
1. Let result be the empty string.
2. For each pair in pairs:
   1. Append pair's name to result.
   2. Append a single U+003D EQUALS SIGN character (=) to result.
   3. Append pair's value to result.
   4. Append a U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character pair to result.
3. Return result.

Payloads using the [`text/plain`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.1.3) format are intended to be human readable. They are not reliably interpretable by computer, as the format is ambiguous (for example, there is no way to distinguish a literal newline in a value from the newline at the end of the value).

##### 4.10.22.10 The [`SubmitEvent`](#4102210-the-submitevent-interface) interface

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface SubmitEvent : Event {
  constructor(DOMString type, optional SubmitEventInit eventInitDict = {});

  readonly attribute HTMLElement? submitter;
};

dictionary SubmitEventInit : EventInit {
  HTMLElement? submitter = null;
};
```

`event.submitter`

Returns the element representing the [submit button](#4102-categories) that triggered the [form submission](#41022-form-submission), or null if the submission was not triggered by a button.

The `submitter` attribute must return the value it was initialized to.

##### 4.10.22.11 The [`FormDataEvent`](#4102211-the-formdataevent-interface) interface

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface FormDataEvent : Event {
  constructor(DOMString type, FormDataEventInit eventInitDict);

  readonly attribute FormData formData;
};

dictionary FormDataEventInit : EventInit {
  required FormData formData;
};
```

`event.formData`

Returns a [`FormData`](https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#formdata) object representing names and values of elements associated to the target [`form`](#4103-the-form-element). Operations on the [`FormData`](https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#formdata) object will affect form data to be submitted.

The `formData` attribute must return the value it was initialized to. It represents a [`FormData`](https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#formdata) object associated to the [entry list](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) that is [constructed](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) when the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) is submitted.

#### 4.10.23 Resetting a form

When a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element form is reset, run these steps:
1. Let reset be the result of [firing an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`reset`](#events) at form, with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) and [`cancelable`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attributes initialized to true.
2. If reset is true, then invoke the [reset algorithm](#41023-resetting-a-form) of each [resettable element](#4102-categories) whose [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) is form.

Each [resettable element](#4102-categories) defines its own reset algorithm. Changes made to form controls as part of these algorithms do not count as changes caused by the user (and thus, e.g., do not cause [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) events to fire).

### 4.11 Interactive elements

#### 4.11.1 The `details` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Interactive content](#32527-interactive-content).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [flow content](#32522-flow-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

One [`summary`](#4112-the-summary-element) element followed by [flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`name`](#4111-the-details-element) — Name of group of mutually-exclusive [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) elements

[`open`](#4111-the-details-element) — Whether the details are visible

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-details).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-details).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLDetailsElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString name;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean open;
};
```

The [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) a disclosure widget from which the user can obtain additional information or controls.

> [!note]
> As with all HTML elements, it is not conforming to use the [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element when attempting to represent another type of control. For example, tab widgets and menu widgets are not disclosure widgets, so abusing the [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element to implement these patterns is incorrect.

> [!note]
> The [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element is not appropriate for footnotes. Please see [the section on footnotes](#4144-footnotes) for details on how to mark up footnotes.

The first [`summary`](#4112-the-summary-element) element child of the element, if any, [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the summary or legend of the details. If there is no child [`summary`](#4112-the-summary-element) element, the user agent should provide its own legend (e.g. "Details").

The rest of the element's contents [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) the additional information or controls.

The `name` content attribute gives the name of the group of related [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) elements that the element is a member of. Opening one member of this group causes other members of the group to close. If the attribute is specified, its value must not be the empty string.

Before using this feature, authors should consider whether this grouping of related [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) elements into an exclusive accordion is helpful or harmful to users. While using an exclusive accordion can reduce the maximum amount of space that a set of content can occupy, it can also frustrate users who have to open many items to find what they want or users who want to look at the contents of multiple items at the same time.

A document must not contain more than one [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element in the same [details name group](#4111-the-details-element) that has the [`open`](#4111-the-details-element) attribute present. Authors must not use script to add [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) elements to a document in a way that would cause a [details name group](#4111-the-details-element) to have more than one [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element with the [`open`](#4111-the-details-element) attribute present.

> [!note]
> The group of elements that is created by a common [`name`](#4111-the-details-element) attribute is exclusive, meaning that at most one of the [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) elements can be open at once. While this exclusivity is enforced by user agents, the resulting enforcement immediately changes the [`open`](#4111-the-details-element) attributes in the markup. This requirement on authors forbids such misleading markup.

A document must not contain a [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element that is a descendant of another [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element in the same [details name group](#4111-the-details-element).

Documents that use the [`name`](#4111-the-details-element) attribute to group multiple related [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) elements should keep those related elements together in a containing element (such as a [`section`](#433-the-section-element) element or [`article`](#432-the-article-element) element). When it makes sense for the group to be introduced with a heading, authors should put that heading in a [heading](#4311-headings-and-outlines) element at the start of the containing element.

> [!note]
> Visually and programmatically grouping related elements together can be important for accessible user experiences. This can help users understand the relationship between such elements. When related elements are in disparate sections of a web page rather than being grouped, the elements' relationships to each other can be less discoverable or understandable.

The `open` content attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes). If present, it indicates that both the summary and the additional information is to be shown to the user. If the attribute is absent, only the summary is to be shown.

When the element is created, if the attribute is absent, the additional information should be hidden; if the attribute is present, that information should be shown. Subsequently, if the attribute is removed, then the information should be hidden; if the attribute is added, the information should be shown.

The user agent should allow the user to request that the additional information be shown or hidden. To honor a request for the details to be shown, the user agent must [set](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) the [`open`](#4111-the-details-element) attribute on the element to the empty string. To honor a request for the information to be hidden, the user agent must [remove](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) the [`open`](#4111-the-details-element) attribute from the element.

> [!note]
> This ability to request that additional information be shown or hidden may simply be the [activation behavior](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) of the appropriate [`summary`](#4112-the-summary-element) element, in the case such an element exists. However, if no such element exists, user agents can still provide this ability through some other user interface affordance.

The details name group that contains a [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element a also contains all the other [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) elements b that fulfill all of the following conditions:
- Both a and b are in the same [tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
- They both have a [`name`](#4111-the-details-element) attribute, their [`name`](#4111-the-details-element) attributes are not the empty string, and the value of a's [`name`](#4111-the-details-element) attribute equals the value of b's [`name`](#4111-the-details-element) attribute.

Every [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element has a details toggle task tracker, which is a [toggle task tracker](#651-the-toggleevent-interface) or null, initially null.

The following [attribute change steps](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), given element, localName, oldValue, value, and namespace, are used for all [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) elements:
1. If namespace is not null, then return.
2. If localName is [`name`](#4111-the-details-element), then [ensure details exclusivity by closing the given element if needed](#4111-the-details-element) given element.
3. If localName is [`open`](#4111-the-details-element):
   1. If one of oldValue or value is null and the other is not null, run the following steps, which are known as the details notification task steps, for this [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element:

      > [!note]
      > When the [`open`](#4111-the-details-element) attribute is toggled several times in succession, the resulting tasks essentially get coalesced so that only one event is fired.
      1. If oldValue is null, [queue a details toggle event task](#4111-the-details-element) given the [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element, "`closed`", and "`open`".
      2. Otherwise, [queue a details toggle event task](#4111-the-details-element) given the [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element, "`open`", and "`closed`".

   2. If oldValue is null and value is not null, then [ensure details exclusivity by closing other elements if needed](#4111-the-details-element) given element.

The [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) [HTML element insertion steps](#214-dom-trees), given insertedNode, are:
1. [Ensure details exclusivity by closing the given element if needed](#4111-the-details-element) given insertedNode.

> [!note]
> To be clear, these attribute change and insertion steps also run when an attribute or element is inserted via the parser.

To queue a details toggle event task given a [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element element, a string oldState, and a string newState:
1. If element's [details toggle task tracker](#4111-the-details-element) is not null:
