1. Let attribute be the result of [getting an attribute by namespace and local name](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) given null, [`src`](#4121-the-script-element)'s [local name](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#492-interface-attr), and [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
2. If attribute is null, then return the empty string.
3. Let urlString be the result of [encoding-parsing-and-serializing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given attribute's [value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#492-interface-attr), relative to [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
4. If urlString is not failure, then return urlString.
5. Return attribute's [value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#492-interface-attr), [converted to a scalar value string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).

The [`src`](#4121-the-script-element) setter steps are:
1. Let compliantScriptURL be the result of invoking the [get trusted type compliant string](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#get-trusted-type-compliant-string) algorithm with [`TrustedScriptURL`](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trustedscripturl), [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant), the given value, "`HTMLScriptElement src`", and "`script`".
2. [Set an attribute value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), [`src`](#4121-the-script-element)'s [local name](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#492-interface-attr), and compliantScriptURL.

The `crossOrigin` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`crossorigin`](#4121-the-script-element) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

The `referrerPolicy` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`referrerpolicy`](#4121-the-script-element) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

The `fetchPriority` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`fetchpriority`](#4121-the-script-element) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

The `async` getter steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [force async](#41211-processing-model) is true, then return true.
2. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`async`](#4121-the-script-element) content attribute is present, then return true.
3. Return false.

The [`async`](#4121-the-script-element) setter steps are:
1. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [force async](#41211-processing-model) to false.
2. If the given value is true, then set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`async`](#4121-the-script-element) content attribute to the empty string.
3. Otherwise, remove [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`async`](#4121-the-script-element) content attribute.

`script.text [ = value ]`

Returns the [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) of the element.

`script.text = value`

Replaces the element's children with the text given by value.

`` `HTMLScriptElement`.supports(type) ``

Returns true if the given type is a script type supported by the user agent. The possible script types in this specification are "`classic`", "`module`", and "`importmap`", but others might be added in the future.

> [!note]
> The [`text`](#4121-the-script-element) and [`textContent`](#4121-the-script-element) IDL attributes are the encouraged way of dynamically setting the text of a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element, as their setters check the given value against Trusted Types. [\[TRUSTED-TYPES\]](#references) Manipulating text nodes directly will instead invoke the default policy on the element's [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) when the script is prepared. (The [`innerText`](#4121-the-script-element) setter also checks the given value, but replaces line breaks with [`br`](#4527-the-br-element) elements, which are not part of the [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text).)

The `innerText` getter steps are to return the result of running [get the text steps](#327-the-innertext-and-outertext-properties) with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).

The [`innerText`](#4121-the-script-element) setter steps are:
1. Let compliantScript be the result of invoking the [get trusted type compliant string](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#get-trusted-type-compliant-string) algorithm with [`TrustedScript`](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trustedscript), [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant), the given value, "`HTMLScriptElement innerText`", and "`script`".
2. [Update script trustedness](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#update-script-trustedness) for [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) given compliantScript.
3. Run [set the inner text steps](#327-the-innertext-and-outertext-properties) with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) and compliantScript.

> [!warning]
> The [`innerText`](#4121-the-script-element) setter stores the compliant string as the [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element's Trusted Types script text, but then replaces any line breaks in it with [`br`](#4527-the-br-element) elements, so the element's [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) no longer matches. See [w3c/trusted-types#517](https://github.com/w3c/trusted-types/issues/517).

The `textContent` getter steps are to return the result of running [get text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).

The [`textContent`](#4121-the-script-element) setter steps are:
1. Let value be the given value.
2. If value is null, then set value to the empty string.
3. Let compliantScript be the result of invoking the [get trusted type compliant string](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#get-trusted-type-compliant-string) algorithm with [`TrustedScript`](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trustedscript), [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant), value, "`HTMLScriptElement textContent`", and "`script`".
4. [Update script trustedness](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#update-script-trustedness) for [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) given compliantScript.
5. Run [set text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) and compliantScript.

The `text` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text).

The [`text`](#4121-the-script-element) setter steps are:
1. Let compliantScript be the result of invoking the [get trusted type compliant string](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#get-trusted-type-compliant-string) algorithm with [`TrustedScript`](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trustedscript), [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant), the given value, "`HTMLScriptElement text`", and "`script`".
2. [Update script trustedness](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#update-script-trustedness) for [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) given compliantScript.
3. [String replace all](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) with compliantScript within [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).

The static `supports(type)` method steps are:
1. If type [is](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) "`classic`", then return true.
2. If type [is](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) "`module`", then return true.
3. If type [is](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) "`importmap`", then return true.
4. If type [is](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) "`speculationrules`", then return true.
5. Return false.

> [!note]
> The type argument has to exactly match these values; we do not perform an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match. This is different from how [`type`](#4121-the-script-element) content attribute values are treated, and how [`DOMTokenList`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#71-interface-domtokenlist)'s [`supports()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#71-interface-domtokenlist) method works, but it aligns with the [`WorkerType`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) enumeration used in the [`Worker()`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) constructor.

---

> [!example]
> In this example, two [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements are used. One embeds an external [classic script](#8141-scripts), and the other includes some data as a [data block](#4121-the-script-element).
> 
> ```html
> <script src="game-engine.js"></script>
> <script type="text/x-game-map">
> ........U.........e
> o............A....e
> .....A.....AAA....e
> .A..AAA...AAAAA...e
> </script>
> ```
> 
> The data in this case might be used by the script to generate the map of a video game. The data doesn't have to be used that way, though; maybe the map data is actually embedded in other parts of the page's markup, and the data block here is just used by the site's search engine to help users who are looking for particular features in their game maps.

> [!example]
> The following sample shows how a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element can be used to define a function that is then used by other parts of the document, as part of a [classic script](#8141-scripts). It also shows how a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element can be used to invoke script while the document is being parsed, in this case to initialize the form's output.
> 
> ```html
> <script>
>  function calculate(form) {
>    var price = 52000;
>    if (form.elements.brakes.checked)
>      price += 1000;
>    if (form.elements.radio.checked)
>      price += 2500;
>    if (form.elements.turbo.checked)
>      price += 5000;
>    if (form.elements.sticker.checked)
>      price += 250;
>    form.elements.result.value = price;
>  }
> </script>
> <form name="pricecalc" onsubmit="return false" onchange="calculate(this)">
>  <fieldset>
>   <legend>Work out the price of your car</legend>
>   <p>Base cost: £52000.</p>
>   <p>Select additional options:</p>
>   <ul>
>    <li><label><input type=checkbox name=brakes> Ceramic brakes (£1000)</label></li>
>    <li><label><input type=checkbox name=radio> Satellite radio (£2500)</label></li>
>    <li><label><input type=checkbox name=turbo> Turbo charger (£5000)</label></li>
>    <li><label><input type=checkbox name=sticker> "XZ" sticker (£250)</label></li>
>   </ul>
>   <p>Total: £<output name=result></output></p>
>  </fieldset>
>  <script>
>   calculate(document.forms.pricecalc);
>  </script>
> </form>
> ```

> [!example]
> The following sample shows how a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element can be used to include an external [JavaScript module script](#8141-scripts).
> 
> ```html
> <script type="module" src="app.mjs"></script>
> ```
> 
> This module, and all its dependencies (expressed through JavaScript `import` statements in the source file), will be fetched. Once the entire resulting module graph has been imported, and the document has finished parsing, the contents of `app.mjs` will be evaluated.
> 
> Additionally, if code from another [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element in the same [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) imports the module from `app.mjs` (e.g. via `import
>    "./app.mjs";`), then the same [JavaScript module script](#8141-scripts) created by the former [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element will be imported.

> [!example]
> This example shows how to include a [JavaScript module script](#8141-scripts) for modern user agents, and a [classic script](#8141-scripts) for older user agents:
> 
> ```html
> <script type="module" src="app.mjs"></script>
> <script nomodule defer src="classic-app-bundle.js"></script>
> ```
> 
> In modern user agents that support [JavaScript module scripts](#8141-scripts), the [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element with the [`nomodule`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute will be ignored, and the [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element with a [`type`](#4121-the-script-element) of "`module`" will be fetched and evaluated (as a [JavaScript module script](#8141-scripts)). Conversely, older user agents will ignore the [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element with a [`type`](#4121-the-script-element) of "`module`", as that is an unknown script type for them — but they will have no problem fetching and evaluating the other [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element (as a [classic script](#8141-scripts)), since they do not implement the [`nomodule`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute.

> [!example]
> The following sample shows how a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element can be used to write an inline [JavaScript module script](#8141-scripts) that performs a number of substitutions on the document's text, in order to make for a more interesting reading experience (e.g. on a news site): [\[XKCD1288\]](#references)
> 
> ```html
> <script type="module">
>  import { walkAllTextNodeDescendants } from "./dom-utils.mjs";
> 
>  const substitutions = new Map([
>    ["witnesses", "these dudes I know"]
>    ["allegedly", "kinda probably"]
>    ["new study", "Tumblr post"]
>    ["rebuild", "avenge"]
>    ["space", "spaaace"]
>    ["Google glass", "Virtual Boy"]
>    ["smartphone", "Pokédex"]
>    ["electric", "atomic"]
>    ["Senator", "Elf-Lord"]
>    ["car", "cat"]
>    ["election", "eating contest"]
>    ["Congressional leaders", "river spirits"]
>    ["homeland security", "Homestar Runner"]
>    ["could not be reached for comment", "is guilty and everyone knows it"]
>  ]);
> 
>  function substitute(textNode) {
>    for (const [before, after] of substitutions.entries()) {
>      textNode.data = textNode.data.replace(new RegExp(`\\b${before}\\b`, "ig"), after);
>    }
>  }
> 
>  walkAllTextNodeDescendants(document.body, substitute);
> </script>
> ```
> 
> Some notable features gained by using a JavaScript module script include the ability to import functions from other JavaScript modules, strict mode by default, and how top-level declarations do not introduce new properties onto the [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects). Also note that no matter where this [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element appears in the document, it will not be evaluated until both document parsing has complete and its dependency (`dom-utils.mjs`) has been fetched and evaluated.

> [!example]
> The following sample shows how a [JSON module script](#8141-scripts) can be imported from inside a [JavaScript module script](#8141-scripts):
> 
> ```html
> <script type="module">
>  import peopleInSpace from "http://api.open-notify.org/astros.json" with { type: "json" };
> 
>  const list = document.querySelector("#people-in-space");
>  for (const { craft, name } of peopleInSpace.people) {
>    const li = document.createElement("li");
>    li.textContent = `${name} / ${craft}`;
>    list.append(li);
>  }
> </script>
> ```
> 
> MIME type checking for module scripts is strict. In order for the fetch of the [JSON module script](#8141-scripts) to succeed, the HTTP response must have a [JSON MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#json-mime-type), for example `Content-Type: text/json`. On the other hand, if the `with { type: "json" }` part of the statement is omitted, it is assumed that the intent is to import a [JavaScript module script](#8141-scripts), and the fetch will fail if the HTTP response has a MIME type that is not a [JavaScript MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type).

##### 4.12.1.1 Processing model

A [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element has several associated pieces of state.

A [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element has a parser document, which is either null or a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), initially null. It is set by the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) and the [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents) on [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements they insert, and affects the processing of those elements. [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements with non-null [parser documents](#41211-processing-model) are known as parser-inserted.

A [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element has a preparation-time document, which is either null or a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), initially null. It is used to prevent scripts that move between documents during [preparation](#41211-processing-model) from [executing](#41211-processing-model).

A [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element has a force async boolean, initially true. It is set to false by the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) and the [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents) on [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements they insert, and when the element gets an [`async`](#4121-the-script-element) content attribute added.

A [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element has a from an external file boolean, initially false. It is determined when the script is [prepared](#41211-processing-model), based on the [`src`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute of the element at that time.

A [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element has a ready to be parser-executed boolean, initially false. This is used only used for elements that are also [parser-inserted](#41211-processing-model), to let the parser know when to execute the script.

A [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element has an already started boolean, initially false.

A [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element has a delaying the load event boolean, initially false.

A [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element has a type, which is either null, "`classic`", "`module`", "`importmap`", or "`speculationrules`", initially null. It is determined when the element is [prepared](#41211-processing-model), based on the [`type`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute of the element at that time.

A [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element has a result, which is either "`uninitialized`", null (representing an error), a [script](#8141-scripts), an [import map parse result](#8148-import-map-parse-results), or a [speculation rules parse result](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results). It is initially "`uninitialized`".

A [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element has steps to run when the result is ready, which are a series of steps or null, initially null. To mark as ready a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element el given a result:
1. Set el's [result](#41211-processing-model) to result.
2. If el's [steps to run when the result is ready](#41211-processing-model) are not null, then run them.
3. Set el's [steps to run when the result is ready](#41211-processing-model) to null.
4. Set el's [delaying the load event](#41211-processing-model) to false.

---

A [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element el is [implicitly potentially render-blocking](#258-blocking-attributes) if el's [type](#41211-processing-model) is "`classic`", el is [parser-inserted](#41211-processing-model), and el does not have an [`async`](#4121-the-script-element) or [`defer`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute.

The [cloning steps](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) for [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements given node, copy, and subtree are to set copy's [already started](#41211-processing-model) to node's [already started](#41211-processing-model).

When an [`async`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute is added to a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element el, the user agent must set el's [force async](#41211-processing-model) to false.

Whenever a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element el's [delaying the load event](#41211-processing-model) is true, the user agent must [delay the load event](#1327-the-end) of el's [preparation-time document](#41211-processing-model).

---

The [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) [HTML element post-connection steps](#214-dom-trees), given insertedNode, are:
1. If insertedNode is [parser-inserted](#41211-processing-model), then return.
2. [Prepare the script element](#41211-processing-model) given insertedNode.

> [!example]
> The [HTML element post-connection steps](#214-dom-trees) only run when the inserted element is still [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree), which protects against cases where an earlier-inserted [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) removes a later-inserted [`script`](#4121-the-script-element). For instance:
> 
> ```html
> <script>
> const script1 = document.createElement('script');
> script1.innerText = `
>   document.querySelector('#script2').remove();
> `;
> 
> const script2 = document.createElement('script');
> script2.id = 'script2';
> script2.textContent = `console.log('script#2 running')`;
> 
> document.body.append(script1, script2);
> </script>
> ```
> 
> Nothing is printed to the console in this example. By the time the [HTML element post-connection steps](#214-dom-trees) run for the first [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) that was atomically inserted by [`append()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md), it can observe that the second [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) is already [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree) to the DOM, and it removes it from the DOM. Because the second [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) is no longer [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree), its [HTML element post-connection steps](#214-dom-trees) do not run, and it does not get [prepared](#41211-processing-model).

The [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) [HTML element removing steps](#214-dom-trees) given removedNode are:
1. If removedNode's [result](#41211-processing-model) is a [speculation rules parse result](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results):
   1. [Unregister speculation rules](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results) given removedNode's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) and removedNode's [result](#41211-processing-model).
   2. Set removedNode's [already started](#41211-processing-model) to false.
   3. Set removedNode's [result](#41211-processing-model) to null.

The [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) [children changed steps](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) given changedNode are:
1. If the [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element is not [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree), then return.
2. Run the [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) [HTML element post-connection steps](#214-dom-trees), given changedNode.

> [!example]
> This has an interesting implication on the execution order of a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element and any newly-inserted child [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements. Consider the following snippet:
> 
> ```html
> <script id=outer-script></script>
> 
> <script>
>   const outerScript = document.querySelector('#outer-script');
> 
>   const start = new Text('console.log(1);');
>   const innerScript = document.createElement('script');
>   innerScript.textContent = `console.log('inner script executing')`;
>   const end = new Text('console.log(2);');
> 
>   outerScript.append(start, innerScript, end);
> 
>   // Logs:
>   // 1
>   // 2
>   // inner script executing
> </script>
> ```
> 
> By the time the second script block executes, the `outer-script` has already been [prepared](#41211-processing-model), but because it is empty, it did not execute and therefore is not marked as [already started](#41211-processing-model). The atomic insertion of the [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) nodes and nested [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element have the following effects:
> 1. All three child nodes get atomically inserted as children of `outer-script`; all of their [insertion steps](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) run, which have no observable consequences in this case.
> 2. The `outer-script`'s [children changed steps](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) run, which [prepares](#41211-processing-model) that script; because its body is now non-empty, this executes the contents of the two [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) nodes, in order.
> 3. The [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) [HTML element post-connection steps](#214-dom-trees) finally run for `innerScript`, causing its body to execute.

The following [attribute change steps](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), given element, localName, oldValue, value, and namespace, are used for all [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements:
1. If namespace is not null, then return.
2. If localName is [`src`](#4121-the-script-element), value is not null, and element is [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree), then run the [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) [HTML element post-connection steps](#214-dom-trees), given element.

To prepare the script element given a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element el:
1. If el's [already started](#41211-processing-model) is true, then return.
2. Let parser document be el's [parser document](#41211-processing-model).
3. Set el's [parser document](#41211-processing-model) to null.

   > [!note]
   > This is done so that if parser-inserted [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements fail to run when the parser tries to run them, e.g. because they are empty or specify an unsupported scripting language, another script can later mutate them and cause them to run again.

4. If parser document is non-null and el does not have an [`async`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute, then set el's [force async](#41211-processing-model) to true.

   > [!note]
   > This is done so that if a parser-inserted [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element fails to run when the parser tries to run it, but it is later executed after a script dynamically updates it, it will execute in an async fashion even if the [`async`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute isn't set.

5. Let source text be el's [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text).
6. If el has no [`src`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute, and source text is the empty string, then return.
7. If el is not [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree), then return.
8. If any of the following are true:
   - el has a [`type`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute whose value is the empty string;
   - el has no [`type`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute but it has a [`language`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute and *that* attribute's value is the empty string; or
   - el has neither a [`type`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute nor a [`language`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute,

   then let the script block's type string for this [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element be "`text/javascript`".

   Otherwise, if el has a [`type`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute, then let the script block's type string be the value of that attribute.

   Otherwise, el has a non-empty [`language`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute; let the script block's type string be the concatenation of "`text/`" and the value of el's [`language`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute.

   > [!note]
   > The [`language`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute is never conforming, and is always ignored if there is a [`type`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute present.

9. If the script block's type string is a [JavaScript MIME type essence match](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type-essence-match), or el has a [`type`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute whose value with [leading and trailing ASCII whitespace stripped](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) is a [JavaScript MIME type essence match](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type-essence-match), then set el's [type](#41211-processing-model) to "`classic`".
10. Otherwise, if the script block's type string is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`module`", then set el's [type](#41211-processing-model) to "`module`".
11. Otherwise, if the script block's type string is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`importmap`", then set el's [type](#41211-processing-model) to "`importmap`".
12. Otherwise, if the script block's type string is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`speculationrules`", then set el's [type](#41211-processing-model) to "`speculationrules`".
13. Otherwise, return. (No script is executed, and el's [type](#41211-processing-model) is left as null.)
14. If parser document is non-null, then set el's [parser document](#41211-processing-model) back to parser document and set el's [force async](#41211-processing-model) to false.
15. Set el's [already started](#41211-processing-model) to true.
16. Set el's [preparation-time document](#41211-processing-model) to its [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
17. If parser document is non-null, and parser document is not equal to el's [preparation-time document](#41211-processing-model), then return.
18. If [scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting) for el, then return.

    > [!note]
    > The definition of [scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting) means that, amongst others, the following scripts will not execute: scripts in [`XMLHttpRequest`](https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#xmlhttprequest)'s [`responseXML`](https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-xmlhttprequest-responsexml) documents, scripts in [`DOMParser`](#851-the-domparser-interface)-created documents, scripts in documents created by [`XSLTProcessor`](#219-dependencies)'s [`transformToDocument`](#219-dependencies) feature, and scripts that are first inserted by a script into a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) that was created using the [`createDocument()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#451-interface-domimplementation) API. [\[XHR\]](#references) [\[DOMPARSING\]](#references) [\[XSLTP\]](#references) [\[DOM\]](#references)

19. If el has a [`nomodule`](#4121-the-script-element) content attribute and its [type](#41211-processing-model) is "`classic`", then return.

    > [!note]
    > This means specifying [`nomodule`](#4121-the-script-element) on a [module script](#8141-scripts) has no effect; the algorithm continues onward.

20. Let cspType be "`script speculationrules`" if el's [type](#41211-processing-model) is "`speculationrules`"; otherwise, "`script`".
21. If el does not have a [`src`](#4121-the-script-element) content attribute, and the [Should element's inline behavior be blocked by Content Security Policy?](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#should-block-inline) algorithm returns "`Blocked`" when given el, cspType, and source text, then return. [\[CSP\]](#references)
22. If el has an [`event`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute and a [`for`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute, and el's [type](#41211-processing-model) is "`classic`":
    1. Let for be the value of el's [`for`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute.
    2. Let event be the value of el's [`event`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute.
    3. [Strip leading and trailing ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) from event and for.
    4. If for is not an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`window`", then return.
    5. If event is not an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for either the string "`onload`" or the string "`onload()`", then return.
23. If el has a [`charset`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute, then let encoding be the result of [getting an encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-encoding-get) from the value of the [`charset`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute.

    If el does not have a [`charset`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute, or if [getting an encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-encoding-get) failed, then let encoding be el's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [the encoding](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

    > [!note]
    > If el's [type](#41211-processing-model) is "`module`", this encoding will be ignored.

24. Let classic script CORS setting be the current state of el's [`crossorigin`](#4121-the-script-element) content attribute.
25. Let module script credentials mode be the [CORS settings attribute credentials mode](#254-cors-settings-attributes) for el's [`crossorigin`](#4121-the-script-element) content attribute.
26. Let cryptographic nonce be el's [\[\[CryptographicNonce\]\]](#256-nonce-attributes) internal slot's value.
27. If el has an [`integrity`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute, then let integrity metadata be that attribute's value.

    Otherwise, let integrity metadata be the empty string.

28. Let referrer policy be the current state of el's [`referrerpolicy`](#4121-the-script-element) content attribute.
29. Let fetch priority be the current state of el's [`fetchpriority`](#4121-the-script-element) content attribute.
30. Let parser metadata be "`parser-inserted`" if el is [parser-inserted](#41211-processing-model), and "`not-parser-inserted`" otherwise.
31. Let options be a [script fetch options](#8142-fetching-scripts) whose [cryptographic nonce](#8142-fetching-scripts) is cryptographic nonce, [integrity metadata](#8142-fetching-scripts) is integrity metadata, [parser metadata](#8142-fetching-scripts) is parser metadata, [credentials mode](#8142-fetching-scripts) is module script credentials mode, [referrer policy](#8142-fetching-scripts) is referrer policy, and [fetch priority](#8142-fetching-scripts) is fetch priority.
32. Let settings object be el's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant).
33. If el has a [`src`](#4121-the-script-element) content attribute:
    1. If el's [type](#41211-processing-model) is "`importmap`" or "`speculationrules`", then [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given el to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) at el, and return.

       > [!note]
       > External import maps and speculation rules are not currently supported. See [WICG/import-maps issue #235](https://github.com/WICG/import-maps/issues/235) and [WICG/nav-speculation issue #348](https://github.com/WICG/nav-speculation/issues/348) for discussions on adding support.

    2. Let src be the value of el's [`src`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute.
    3. If src is the empty string, then [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given el to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) at el, and return.
    4. Set el's [from an external file](#41211-processing-model) to true.
    5. Let url be the result of [encoding-parsing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given src, relative to el's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
    6. If url is failure, then [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given el to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) at el, and return.
    7. If el is [potentially render-blocking](#258-blocking-attributes), then [block rendering](#316-render-blocking-mechanism) on el.
    8. Set el's [delaying the load event](#41211-processing-model) to true.
    9. If el is currently [render-blocking](#316-render-blocking-mechanism), then set options's [render-blocking](#8142-fetching-scripts) to true.
    10. Let onComplete given result be the following steps:
        1. [Mark as ready](#41211-processing-model) el given result.
    11. Switch on el's [type](#41211-processing-model):

        "`classic`"

        [Fetch a classic script](#8142-fetching-scripts) given url, settings object, options, classic script CORS setting, encoding, and onComplete.

        "`module`"

        If el does not have an [`integrity`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute, then set options's [integrity metadata](#8142-fetching-scripts) to the result of [resolving a module integrity metadata](#8142-fetching-scripts) with url and settings object.

        [Fetch an external module script graph](#8142-fetching-scripts) given url, settings object, options, and onComplete.

        For performance reasons, user agents may start fetching the classic script or module graph (as defined above) as soon as the [`src`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute is set, instead, in the hope that el will become connected (and that the [`crossorigin`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute won't change value in the meantime). Either way, once el [becomes connected](#214-dom-trees), the load must have started as described in this step. If the UA performs such prefetching, but el never becomes connected, or the [`src`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute is dynamically changed, or the [`crossorigin`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute is dynamically changed, then the user agent will not execute the script so obtained, and the fetching process will have been effectively wasted.

34. If el does not have a [`src`](#4121-the-script-element) content attribute:
    1. Let base URL be el's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [document base URL](#243-document-base-urls).
    2. Switch on el's [type](#41211-processing-model):

       "`classic`"
       1. Let script be the result of [creating a classic script](#8143-creating-scripts) using source text, settings object, base URL, and options.
       2. [Mark as ready](#41211-processing-model) el given script.

       "`module`"
       1. Set el's [delaying the load event](#41211-processing-model) to true.
       2. If el is [potentially render-blocking](#258-blocking-attributes):
          1. [Block rendering](#316-render-blocking-mechanism) on el.
          2. Set options's [render-blocking](#8142-fetching-scripts) to true.
       3. [Fetch an inline module script graph](#8142-fetching-scripts), given source text, base URL, settings object, options, and with the following steps given result:
          1. [Queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given el to perform the following steps:
             1. [Mark as ready](#41211-processing-model) el given result.

             > [!note]
             > Queueing a task here means that, even if the inline module script has no dependencies or synchronously results in a parse error, we won't proceed to [execute the script element](#41211-processing-model) synchronously.

       "`importmap`"
       1. Let result be the result of [creating an import map parse result](#8148-import-map-parse-results) given source text and base URL.
       2. [Mark as ready](#41211-processing-model) el given result.

       "`speculationrules`"
       1. Let result be the result of [creating a speculation rules parse result](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results) given source text and el's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
       2. [Mark as ready](#41211-processing-model) el given result.

35. If el's [type](#41211-processing-model) is "`classic`" and el has a [`src`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute, or el's [type](#41211-processing-model) is "`module`":
    1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): el's [result](#41211-processing-model) is "`uninitialized`".
    2. If el has an [`async`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute or el's [force async](#41211-processing-model) is true:
       1. Let scripts be el's [preparation-time document](#41211-processing-model)'s [set of scripts that will execute as soon as possible](#41211-processing-model).
       2. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) el to scripts.
       3. Set el's [steps to run when the result is ready](#41211-processing-model) to the following:
          1. [Execute the script element](#41211-processing-model) el.
          2. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) el from scripts.
    3. Otherwise, if el is not [parser-inserted](#41211-processing-model):
       1. Let scripts be el's [preparation-time document](#41211-processing-model)'s [list of scripts that will execute in order as soon as possible](#41211-processing-model).
       2. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) el to scripts.
       3. Set el's [steps to run when the result is ready](#41211-processing-model) to the following:
          1. If scripts\[0\] is not el, then abort these steps.
          2. While scripts is not empty, and scripts\[0\]'s [result](#41211-processing-model) is not "`uninitialized`":
             1. [Execute the script element](#41211-processing-model) scripts\[0\].
             2. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) scripts\[0\].
    4. Otherwise, if el has a [`defer`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute or el's [type](#41211-processing-model) is "`module`":
       1. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) el to its [parser document](#41211-processing-model)'s [list of scripts that will execute when the document has finished parsing](#41211-processing-model).
       2. Set el's [steps to run when the result is ready](#41211-processing-model) to the following: set el's [ready to be parser-executed](#41211-processing-model) to true. (The parser will handle executing the script.)
    5. Otherwise:
       1. Set el's [parser document](#41211-processing-model)'s [pending parsing-blocking script](#41211-processing-model) to el.
       2. [Block rendering](#316-render-blocking-mechanism) on el.
       3. Set el's [steps to run when the result is ready](#41211-processing-model) to the following: set el's [ready to be parser-executed](#41211-processing-model) to true. (The parser will handle executing the script.)
36. Otherwise:
    1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): el's [result](#41211-processing-model) is *not* "`uninitialized`".
    2. If all of the following are true:
       - el's [type](#41211-processing-model) is "`classic`";
       - el is [parser-inserted](#41211-processing-model);
       - el's [parser document](#41211-processing-model) [has a style sheet that is blocking scripts](#427-interactions-of-styling-and-scripting); and
       - either the parser that created el is an [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents), or it's an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) whose [script nesting level](#1321-overview-of-the-parsing-model) is not greater than one,

       then:
       1. Set el's [parser document](#41211-processing-model)'s [pending parsing-blocking script](#41211-processing-model) to el.
       2. Set el's [ready to be parser-executed](#41211-processing-model) to true. (The parser will handle executing the script.)

    3. Otherwise, [immediately](#211-parallelism) [execute the script element](#41211-processing-model) el, even if other scripts are already executing.

Each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a pending parsing-blocking script, which is a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element or null, initially null.

Each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a set of scripts that will execute as soon as possible, which is a [set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) of [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements, initially empty.

Each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a list of scripts that will execute in order as soon as possible, which is a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements, initially empty.

Each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a list of scripts that will execute when the document has finished parsing, which is a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements, initially empty.

> [!note]
> If a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element that blocks a parser gets moved to another [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) before it would normally have stopped blocking that parser, it nonetheless continues blocking that parser until the condition that causes it to be blocking the parser no longer applies (e.g., if the script is a [pending parsing-blocking script](#41211-processing-model) because the original [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) [has a style sheet that is blocking scripts](#427-interactions-of-styling-and-scripting) when it was parsed, but then the script is moved to another [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) before the blocking style sheet(s) loaded, the script still blocks the parser until the style sheets are all loaded, at which time the script executes and the parser is unblocked).

To execute the script element given a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element el:
1. Let document be el's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
2. If el's [preparation-time document](#41211-processing-model) is not equal to document, then return.
3. [Unblock rendering](#316-render-blocking-mechanism) on el.
4. If el's [result](#41211-processing-model) is null, then [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) at el, and return.
5. If el's [from an external file](#41211-processing-model) is true, or el's [type](#41211-processing-model) is "`module`", then increment document's [ignore-destructive-writes counter](#843-documentwrite).
6. Switch on el's [type](#41211-processing-model):

   "`classic`"
   1. Let oldCurrentScript be the value to which document's [`currentScript`](#317-dom-tree-accessors) object was most recently set.
   2. If el's [root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) is *not* a [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot), then set document's [`currentScript`](#317-dom-tree-accessors) attribute to el. Otherwise, set it to null.

      > [!note]
      > This does not use the [in a document tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) check, as el could have been removed from the document prior to execution, and in that scenario [`currentScript`](#317-dom-tree-accessors) still needs to point to it.

   3. [Run the classic script](#8144-calling-scripts) given by el's [result](#41211-processing-model).
   4. Set document's [`currentScript`](#317-dom-tree-accessors) attribute to oldCurrentScript.

   "`module`"
   1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): document's [`currentScript`](#317-dom-tree-accessors) attribute is null.
   2. [Run the module script](#8144-calling-scripts) given by el's [result](#41211-processing-model).

   "`importmap`"
   1. [Register an import map](#8148-import-map-parse-results) given el's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) and el's [result](#41211-processing-model).

   "`speculationrules`"
   1. [Register speculation rules](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results) given el's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) and el's [result](#41211-processing-model).

7. Decrement the [ignore-destructive-writes counter](#843-documentwrite) of document, if it was incremented in the earlier step.
8. If el's [from an external file](#41211-processing-model) is true, then [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`load`](#events) at el.

##### 4.12.1.2 Scripting languages

User agents are not required to support JavaScript. This standard needs to be updated if a language other than JavaScript comes along and gets similar wide adoption by web browsers. Until such a time, implementing other languages is in conflict with this standard, given the processing model defined for the [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element.

Servers should use [`text/javascript`](#mime-types) for JavaScript resources, in accordance with Updates to ECMAScript Media Types. Servers should not use other [JavaScript MIME types](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type) for JavaScript resources, and must not use non-[JavaScript MIME types](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type). [\[RFC9239\]](#references)

For external JavaScript resources, MIME type parameters in \`[`Content-Type`](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource)\` headers are generally ignored. (In some cases the \``charset`\` parameter has an effect.) However, for the [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element's [`type`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute they are significant; it uses the [JavaScript MIME type essence match](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type-essence-match) concept.

> [!note]
> For example, scripts with their [`type`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute set to "`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`" will not be evaluated, even though that is a valid [JavaScript MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type) when parsed.

Furthermore, again for external JavaScript resources, special considerations apply around \`[`Content-Type`](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource)\` header processing as detailed in the [prepare the script element](#41211-processing-model) algorithm and Fetch. [\[FETCH\]](#references)

##### 4.12.1.3 Restrictions for contents of `script` elements

> [!note]
> The easiest and safest way to avoid the rather strange restrictions described in this section is to always escape an ASCII case-insensitive match for "`<!--`" as "`\x3C!--`", "`<script`" as "`\x3Cscript`", and "`</script`" as "`\x3C/script`" when these sequences appear in literals in scripts (e.g. in strings, regular expressions, or comments), and to avoid writing code that uses such constructs in expressions. Doing so avoids the pitfalls that the restrictions in this section are prone to triggering: namely, that, for historical reasons, parsing of [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) blocks in HTML is a strange and exotic practice that acts unintuitively in the face of these sequences.

The [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element's [descendant text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) must match the `script` production in the following ABNF, the character set for which is Unicode. [\[ABNF\]](#references)

```abnf
script        = outer *( comment-open inner comment-close outer )

outer         = < any string that doesn't contain a substring that matches not-in-outer >
not-in-outer  = comment-open
inner         = < any string that doesn't contain a substring that matches not-in-inner >
not-in-inner  = comment-close / script-open

comment-open  = "<!--"
comment-close = "-->"
script-open   = "<" s c r i p t tag-end

s             =  %x0053 ; U+0053 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER S
s             =/ %x0073 ; U+0073 LATIN SMALL LETTER S
c             =  %x0043 ; U+0043 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER C
c             =/ %x0063 ; U+0063 LATIN SMALL LETTER C
r             =  %x0052 ; U+0052 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER R
r             =/ %x0072 ; U+0072 LATIN SMALL LETTER R
i             =  %x0049 ; U+0049 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER I
i             =/ %x0069 ; U+0069 LATIN SMALL LETTER I
p             =  %x0050 ; U+0050 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER P
p             =/ %x0070 ; U+0070 LATIN SMALL LETTER P
t             =  %x0054 ; U+0054 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER T
t             =/ %x0074 ; U+0074 LATIN SMALL LETTER T

tag-end       =  %x0009 ; U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION (tab)
tag-end       =/ %x000A ; U+000A LINE FEED (LF)
tag-end       =/ %x000C ; U+000C FORM FEED (FF)
tag-end       =/ %x0020 ; U+0020 SPACE
tag-end       =/ %x002F ; U+002F SOLIDUS (/)
tag-end       =/ %x003E ; U+003E GREATER-THAN SIGN (>)
```

When a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element contains [script documentation](#41214-inline-documentation-for-external-scripts), there are further restrictions on the contents of the element, as described in the section below.

> [!example]
> The following script illustrates this issue. Suppose you have a script that contains a string, as in:
> 
> ```javascript
> const example = 'Consider this string: <!-- <script>';
> console.log(example);
> ```
> 
> If one were to put this string directly in a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) block, it would violate the restrictions above:
> 
> ```html
> <script>
>   const example = 'Consider this string: <!-- <script>';
>   console.log(example);
> </script>
> ```
> 
> The bigger problem, though, and the reason why it would violate those restrictions, is that actually the script would get parsed weirdly: *the script block above is not terminated*. That is, what looks like a "`</script>`" end tag in this snippet is actually still part of the [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) block. The script doesn't execute (since it's not terminated); if it somehow were to execute, as it might if the markup looked as follows, it would fail because the script (highlighted here) is not valid JavaScript:
> 
> ```html
> <script>
>   const example = 'Consider this string: <!-- <script>';
>   console.log(example);
> </script>
> <!-- despite appearances, this is actually part of the script still! -->
> <script>
>  ... // this is the same script block still...
> </script>
> ```
> 
> What is going on here is that for legacy reasons, "`<!--`" and "`<script`" strings in [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements in HTML need to be balanced in order for the parser to consider closing the block.
> 
> By escaping the problematic strings as mentioned at the top of this section, the problem is avoided entirely:
> 
> ```html
> <script>
>   // Note: `\x3C` is an escape sequence for `<`.
>   const example = 'Consider this string: \x3C!-- \x3Cscript>';
>   console.log(example);
> </script>
> <!-- this is just a comment between script blocks -->
> <script>
>  ... // this is a new script block
> </script>
> ```
> 
> It is possible for these sequences to naturally occur in script expressions, as in the following examples:
> 
> ```javascript
> if (x<!--y) { ... }
> if ( player<script ) { ... }
> ```
> 
> In such cases the characters cannot be escaped, but the expressions can be rewritten so that the sequences don't occur, as in:
> 
> ```javascript
> if (x < !--y) { ... }
> if (!--y > x) { ... }
> if (!(--y) > x) { ... }
> if (player < script) { ... }
> if (script > player) { ... }
> ```
> 
> Doing this also avoids a different pitfall as well: for related historical reasons, the string "<!--" in [classic scripts](#8141-scripts) is actually treated as a line comment start, just like "//".

##### 4.12.1.4 Inline documentation for external scripts

If a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element's [`src`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute is specified, then the contents of the [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element, if any, must be such that the value of the [`text`](#4121-the-script-element) IDL attribute, which is derived from the element's contents, matches the `documentation` production in the following ABNF, the character set for which is Unicode. [\[ABNF\]](#references)

```abnf
documentation = *( *( space / tab / comment ) [ line-comment ] newline )
comment       = slash star *( not-star / star not-slash ) 1*star slash
line-comment  = slash slash *not-newline

; characters
tab           = %x0009 ; U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION (tab)
newline       = %x000A ; U+000A LINE FEED (LF)
space         = %x0020 ; U+0020 SPACE
star          = %x002A ; U+002A ASTERISK (*)
slash         = %x002F ; U+002F SOLIDUS (/)
not-newline   = %x0000-0009 / %x000B-10FFFF
                ; a scalar value other than U+000A LINE FEED (LF)
not-star      = %x0000-0029 / %x002B-10FFFF
                ; a scalar value other than U+002A ASTERISK (*)
not-slash     = %x0000-002E / %x0030-10FFFF
                ; a scalar value other than U+002F SOLIDUS (/)
```

> [!note]
> This corresponds to putting the contents of the element in JavaScript comments.

> [!note]
> This requirement is in addition to the earlier restrictions on the syntax of contents of [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements.

> [!example]
> This allows authors to include documentation, such as license information or API information, inside their documents while still referring to external script files. The syntax is constrained so that authors don't accidentally include what looks like valid script while also providing a [`src`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute.
> 
> ```html
> <script src="cool-effects.js">
>  // create new instances using:
>  //    var e = new Effect();
>  // start the effect using .play, stop using .stop:
>  //    e.play();
>  //    e.stop();
> </script>
> ```

##### 4.12.1.5 Interaction of [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements and XSLT

> [!danger]
> Avoid using client-side XSLT in browsers. The browser implementations of XSLT are highly susceptible to memory safety vulnerabilities, and the web platform has evolved toward JavaScript as the safe replacement. For these reasons, this feature is in the process of being removed from the web platform. (This is a long process that takes many years.)

*This section is non-normative.*

This specification does not define how XSLT interacts with the [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element. However, in the absence of another specification actually defining this, here are some guidelines for implementers, based on existing implementations:
- When an XSLT transformation program is triggered by an `<?xml-stylesheet?>` processing instruction and the browser implements a direct-to-DOM transformation, [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements created by the XSLT processor need to have its [parser document](#41211-processing-model) set correctly, and run in document order (modulo scripts marked [`defer`](#4121-the-script-element) or [`async`](#4121-the-script-element)), [immediately](#211-parallelism), as the transformation is occurring.
- The [`XSLTProcessor`](#219-dependencies) [`transformToDocument()`](#219-dependencies) method adds elements to a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object with a null [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts), and, accordingly, any [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements they create need to have their [already started](#41211-processing-model) set to true in the [prepare the script element](#41211-processing-model) algorithm and never get executed ([scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting)). Such [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements still need to have their [parser document](#41211-processing-model) set, though, such that their [`async`](#4121-the-script-element) IDL attribute will return false in the absence of an [`async`](#4121-the-script-element) content attribute.
- The [`XSLTProcessor`](#219-dependencies) [`transformToFragment()`](#219-dependencies) method needs to create a fragment that is equivalent to one built manually by creating the elements using [`document.createElementNS()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document). For instance, it needs to create [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements with null [parser document](#41211-processing-model) and with their [already started](#41211-processing-model) set to false, so that they will execute when the fragment is inserted into a document.

The main distinction between the first two cases and the last case is that the first two operate on [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)s and the last operates on a fragment.

#### 4.12.2 The `noscript` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Metadata content](#32521-metadata-content).

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

In a [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element of an [HTML document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), if there are no ancestor [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) elements.

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected in [HTML documents](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), if there are no ancestor [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) elements.

As a descendant of a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element or an [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element, if there are no ancestor [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) elements.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

When [scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting), in a [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element: in any order, zero or more [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements, zero or more [`style`](#426-the-style-element) elements, and zero or more [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) elements.

When [scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting), not in a [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element: [transparent](#3253-transparent-content-models), but there must be no [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element descendants.

Otherwise: text that conforms to the requirements given in the prose.

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-noscript).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-noscript).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

Uses [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom).

The [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) nothing if [scripting is enabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting), and [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) its children if [scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting). It is used to present different markup to user agents that support scripting and those that don't support scripting, by affecting how the document is parsed.

When used in [HTML documents](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), the allowed content model is as follows:

In a [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element, if [scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting) for the [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element

The [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element must contain only [`link`](#424-the-link-element), [`style`](#426-the-style-element), and [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) elements.

In a [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element, if [scripting is enabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting) for the [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element

The [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element must contain only text, except that invoking the [HTML fragment parsing algorithm](#134-parsing-html-fragments) with the [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element as the [context](#134-parsing-html-fragments) element and the text contents as the input must result in a list of nodes that consists only of [`link`](#424-the-link-element), [`style`](#426-the-style-element), and [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) elements that would be conforming if they were children of the [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element, and no [parse errors](#1322-parse-errors).

Outside of [`head`](#421-the-head-element) elements, if [scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting) for the [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element

The [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element's content model is [transparent](#3253-transparent-content-models), with the additional restriction that a [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element must not have a [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element as an ancestor (that is, [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) can't be nested).

Outside of [`head`](#421-the-head-element) elements, if [scripting is enabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting) for the [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element

The [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element must contain only text, except that the text must be such that running the following algorithm results in a conforming document with no [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) elements and no [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements, and such that no step in the algorithm throws an exception or causes an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) to flag a [parse error](#1322-parse-errors):
1. Remove every [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element from the document.
2. Make a list of every [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element in the document. For every [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element in that list, perform the following steps:
   1. Let s be the [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) of the [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element.
   2. Set the [`outerHTML`](#855-the-outerhtml-property) attribute of the [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element to the value of s. (This, as a side-effect, causes the [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element to be removed from the document.)

> [!note]
> All these contortions are required because, for historical reasons, the [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element is handled differently by the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) based on whether [scripting mode](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) was [Disabled](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) when the parser was invoked.

The [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element must not be used in [XML documents](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

> [!note]
> The [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element is only effective in [the HTML syntax](#13-the-html-syntax), it has no effect in [the XML syntax](#14-the-xml-syntax). This is because the way it works is by essentially "turning off" the parser when scripts are enabled, so that the contents of the element are treated as pure text and not as real elements. XML does not define a mechanism by which to do this.

The [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element has no other requirements. In particular, children of the [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element are not exempt from [form submission](#41022-form-submission), scripting, and so forth, even when [scripting is enabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting) for the element.

> [!example]
> In the following example, a [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element is used to provide fallback for a script.
> 
> ```html
> <form action="calcSquare.php">
>  <p>
>   <label for=x>Number</label>:
>   <input id="x" name="x" type="number">
>  </p>
>  <script>
>   var x = document.getElementById('x');
>   var output = document.createElement('p');
>   output.textContent = 'Type a number; it will be squared right then!';
>   x.form.appendChild(output);
>   x.form.onsubmit = function () { return false; }
>   x.oninput = function () {
>     var v = x.valueAsNumber;
>     output.textContent = v + ' squared is ' + v * v;
>   };
>  </script>
>  <noscript>
>   <input type=submit value="Calculate Square">
>  </noscript>
> </form>
> ```
> 
> When script is disabled, a button appears to do the calculation on the server side. When script is enabled, the value is computed on-the-fly instead.
> 
> The [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element is a blunt instrument. Sometimes, scripts might be enabled, but for some reason the page's script might fail. For this reason, it's generally better to avoid using [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element), and to instead design the script to change the page from being a scriptless page to a scripted page on the fly, as in the next example:
> 
> ```html
> <form action="calcSquare.php">
>  <p>
>   <label for=x>Number</label>:
>   <input id="x" name="x" type="number">
>  </p>
>  <input id="submit" type=submit value="Calculate Square">
>  <script>
>   var x = document.getElementById('x');
>   var output = document.createElement('p');
>   output.textContent = 'Type a number; it will be squared right then!';
>   x.form.appendChild(output);
>   x.form.onsubmit = function () { return false; }
>   x.oninput = function () {
>     var v = x.valueAsNumber;
>     output.textContent = v + ' squared is ' + v * v;
>   };
>   var submit = document.getElementById('submit');
>   submit.parentNode.removeChild(submit);
>  </script>
> </form>
> ```
> 
> The above technique is also useful in [XML documents](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), since [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) is not allowed there.

#### 4.12.3 The `template` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Metadata content](#32521-metadata-content).

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Script-supporting element](#32529-script-supporting-elements).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [metadata content](#32521-metadata-content) is expected.

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

Where [script-supporting elements](#32529-script-supporting-elements) are expected.

As a child of a [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element that doesn't have a [`span`](#493-the-colgroup-element) attribute.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Nothing](#3251-the-nothing-content-model) (for clarification, [see example](#4123-the-template-element)).

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`for`](#4123-the-template-element) — Updates existing content

[`shadowrootmode`](#4123-the-template-element) — Enables streaming declarative shadow roots

[`shadowrootdelegatesfocus`](#4123-the-template-element) — Sets [delegates focus](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) on a declarative shadow root

[`shadowrootserializable`](#4123-the-template-element) — Sets [serializable](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) on a declarative shadow root

[`shadowrootslotassignment`](#4123-the-template-element) — Sets [slot assignment](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) on a declarative shadow root

[`shadowrootclonable`](#4123-the-template-element) — Sets [clonable](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) on a declarative shadow root

[`shadowrootcustomelementregistry`](#4123-the-template-element) — Enables declarative shadow roots to indicate they will use a custom element registry

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-template).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-template).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLTemplateElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  readonly attribute DocumentFragment content;
  [CEReactions, Reflect="for"] attribute DOMString htmlFor;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString shadowRootMode;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean shadowRootDelegatesFocus;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean shadowRootSerializable;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString shadowRootSlotAssignment;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean shadowRootClonable;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString shadowRootCustomElementRegistry;
};
```

The [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element is used to declare fragments of HTML that can be cloned and inserted in the document by script.

In a rendering, the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) nothing.

The `for` content attribute identifies the [`ProcessingInstruction`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#413-interface-processinginstruction) that marks the location at which to insert content (`<?marker>`) or the start of the range to replace (`<?start>`). If the attribute is specified, the attribute's value must equal the value of the `name` attribute of a `<?marker>` or `<?start>` [`ProcessingInstruction`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#413-interface-processinginstruction) in the same [tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) as the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element.

The `shadowrootmode` content attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `open` | Open | The template element represents an open declarative shadow root. |
| `closed` | Closed | The template element represents a closed declarative shadow root. |

The [`shadowrootmode`](#4123-the-template-element) attribute's *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the None state.

The `shadowrootdelegatesfocus` content attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes).

The `shadowrootserializable` content attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes).

The `shadowrootslotassignment` content attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `named` | Named | The declarative shadow root uses named slot assignment. |
| `manual` | Manual | The declarative shadow root uses manual slot assignment. |

The [`shadowrootslotassignment`](#4123-the-template-element) attribute's *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the [Named](#4123-the-template-element) state.

The `shadowrootclonable` content attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes).

The `shadowrootcustomelementregistry` content attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes).

The [template contents](#4123-the-template-element) of a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element [are not children of the element itself](#1312-elements).

> [!note]
> It is also possible, as a result of DOM manipulation, for a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element to contain [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) nodes and element nodes; however, having any is a violation of the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element's content model, since its content model is defined as [nothing](#3251-the-nothing-content-model).

> [!example]
> For example, consider the following document:
> 
> ```html
> <!doctype html>
> <html lang="en">
>  <head>
>   <title>Homework</title>
>  <body>
>   <template id="template"><p>Smile!</p></template>
>   <script>
>    let num = 3;
>    const fragment = document.getElementById('template').content.cloneNode(true);
>    while (num-- > 1) {
>      fragment.firstChild.before(fragment.firstChild.cloneNode(true));
>      fragment.firstChild.textContent += fragment.lastChild.textContent;
>    }
>    document.body.appendChild(fragment);
>   </script>
> </html>
> ```
> 
> The [`p`](#441-the-p-element) element in the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) is *not* a child of the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) in the DOM; it is a child of the [`DocumentFragment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) returned by the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element's [`content`](#4123-the-template-element) IDL attribute.
> 
> If the script were to call [`appendChild()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) on the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element, that would add a child to the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element (as for any other element); however, doing so is a violation of the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element's content model.

`template.content`

Returns the [template contents](#4123-the-template-element) (a [`DocumentFragment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment)).

Each [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element has an associated [`DocumentFragment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) object that is its template contents. The [template contents](#4123-the-template-element) have [no conformance requirements](#321-semantics). When a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element is created, the user agent must run the following steps to establish the [template contents](#4123-the-template-element):
1. Let document be the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [appropriate template contents owner document](#4123-the-template-element).
2. Create a [`DocumentFragment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) object whose [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) is document and [host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) is the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element.
3. Set the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element's [template contents](#4123-the-template-element) to the newly created [`DocumentFragment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) object.

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document's appropriate template contents owner document is the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) returned by the following algorithm:
1. If document is not a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) created by this algorithm:
   1. If document does not yet have an associated inert template document:
      1. Let newDocument be the result of [creating a document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) that implements [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), given document's [relevant realm](#81334-relevant); its [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) is null. This is "a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) created by this algorithm" for the purposes of the step above.
      2. If document is an [HTML document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), then mark newDocument as an [HTML document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) also.
      3. Set document's [associated inert template document](#4123-the-template-element) to newDocument.
   2. Set document to document's [associated inert template document](#4123-the-template-element).

   > [!note]
   > Each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) not created by this algorithm thus gets a single [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) to act as its proxy for owning the [template contents](#4123-the-template-element) of all its [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) elements, so that they aren't in a [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) and thus remain inert (e.g. scripts do not run). Meanwhile, [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) elements inside [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) objects that *are* created by this algorithm just reuse the same [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) owner for their contents.

2. Return document.

Each [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element has an associated [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element)-or-[`DocumentFragment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment)-or-null insertion target, which is initially null.

Each [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element has an associated [`ProcessingInstruction`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#413-interface-processinginstruction)-or-null insertion start marker and insertion end marker, which are initially null.

The [adopting steps](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) (with node and oldDocument as parameters) for [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) elements are the following:
1. Let document be node's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [appropriate template contents owner document](#4123-the-template-element).

   > [!note]
