   > node's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) is the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object that node was just adopted *into*.

2. [Adopt](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) node's [template contents](#4123-the-template-element) (a [`DocumentFragment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) object) into document.

The `content` getter steps are:
1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [template contents](#4123-the-template-element) is not a [`ShadowRoot`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) node.
2. Return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [template contents](#4123-the-template-element).

The `shadowRootMode` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`shadowrootmode`](#4123-the-template-element) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

The `shadowRootSlotAssignment` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`shadowrootslotassignment`](#4123-the-template-element) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

> [!note]
> The [shadowRootCustomElementRegistry](#4123-the-template-element) IDL attribute intentionally does not have a boolean type so it can be extended.

---

The [cloning steps](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) for [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) elements given node, copy, and subtree are:
1. If subtree is false, then return.
2. For each child of node's [template contents](#4123-the-template-element)'s [children](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees): [clone a node](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) given child with [*document*](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) set to copy's [template contents](#4123-the-template-element)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), [*subtree*](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) set to true, and [*parent*](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) set to copy's [template contents](#4123-the-template-element).

To prepare content patching given an [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) or [`DocumentFragment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) scope and a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element template:
1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): template's [`for`](#4123-the-template-element) attribute is specified.
2. Let markerName be template's [`for`](#4123-the-template-element) attribute's value.
3. If markerName is the empty string, then return false.
4. Let (start, end) be the result of [find markers](#4123-the-template-element) given scope and markerName.
5. If start is null, then return false.
6. Set template's [insertion target](#4123-the-template-element) to start's [parent](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
7. Set template's [insertion start marker](#4123-the-template-element) to start.
8. Set template's [insertion end marker](#4123-the-template-element) to end.
9. If start is end, then return true.
10. Let removedNodes be an empty [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).
11. Let currentNode be start's [next sibling](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
12. While currentNode is not null:
    1. If currentNode is end, then [break](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
    2. Append currentNode to removedNodes.
    3. Set currentNode to currentNode's [next sibling](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
13. For each node of removedNodes:
    1. If node's [parent](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) is not null, then [remove](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) node.

       > [!note]
       > The parent might have changed because removing a node can fire events like the [`pagehide`](#events) event, and an event handler can mutate the DOM. The parent identity is not checked; as long as the node still has a parent, it is removed.

14. Return true.

To find markers given a node scope and a string name:
1. For each descendant of scope's [descendants](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees):
   1. If descendant is not a [`ProcessingInstruction`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#413-interface-processinginstruction) node, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   2. If the result of [getting a processing instruction attribute](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#413-interface-processinginstruction) given descendant and "`name`" is not name, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   3. If descendant's [target](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#413-interface-processinginstruction) is "`marker`", then return (descendant, descendant).
   4. If descendant's [target](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#413-interface-processinginstruction) is "`start`":
      1. Let start be descendant.
      2. Let nestingLevel be 0.
      3. Let sibling be start's [next sibling](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
      4. While sibling is not null:
         1. If sibling is a [`ProcessingInstruction`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#413-interface-processinginstruction) node:
            1. If sibling's [target](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#413-interface-processinginstruction) is "`start`", then increment nestingLevel by one.
            2. If sibling's [target](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#413-interface-processinginstruction) is "`end`":
               1. If nestingLevel is 0, then return (start, sibling).
               2. Decrement nestingLevel by one.
         2. Set sibling to sibling's [next sibling](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
      5. Return (start, null).

         > [!note]
         > No matching `<?end>` was found, which is interpreted as a range from start to the end of its parent.

2. Return (null, null).

> [!example]
> In this example, a script populates a table four-column with data from a data structure, using a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) to provide the element structure instead of manually generating the structure from markup.
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE html>
> <html lang='en'>
> <title>Cat data</title>
> <script>
>  // Data is hard-coded here, but could come from the server
>  var data = [
>    { name: 'Pillar', color: 'Ticked Tabby', sex: 'Female (neutered)', legs: 3 },
>    { name: 'Hedral', color: 'Tuxedo', sex: 'Male (neutered)', legs: 4 },
>  ];
> </script>
> <table>
>  <thead>
>   <tr>
>    <th>Name <th>Color <th>Sex <th>Legs
>  <tbody>
>   <template id="row">
>    <tr><td><td><td><td>
>   </template>
> </table>
> <script>
>  var template = document.querySelector('#row');
>  for (var i = 0; i < data.length; i += 1) {
>    var cat = data[i];
>    var clone = template.content.cloneNode(true);
>    var cells = clone.querySelectorAll('td');
>    cells[0].textContent = cat.name;
>    cells[1].textContent = cat.color;
>    cells[2].textContent = cat.sex;
>    cells[3].textContent = cat.legs;
>    template.parentNode.appendChild(clone);
>  }
> </script>
> ```
> 
> This example uses [`cloneNode()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) on the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element)'s contents; it could equivalently have used [`document.importNode()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), which does the same thing. The only difference between these two APIs is when the [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) is updated: with [`cloneNode()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) it is updated when the nodes are appended with [`appendChild()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), with [`document.importNode()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) it is updated when the nodes are cloned.

> [!example]
> In this example, a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element with a [`for`](#4123-the-template-element) attribute is used to populate a list of countries in a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element, after the main content of the page has been delivered.
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE html>
> <html lang="en">
>  <head>
>   <title>Out-of-order countries</title>
>   <style>
>    #countries:empty {
>     opacity: 0;
>    }
>   </style>
>  </head>
>  <body>
>   <select id=countries><?marker name="country-options"?></select>
>   ...
>   <template for="country-options"><option>Antigua</option>...</template>
>  </body>
> </html>
> ```
> 
> The `<?marker?>` processing instruction is replaced with the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements from the later [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element. The [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element is transparent until it is populated.

> [!example]
> In this example, a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element with a [`for`](#4123-the-template-element) attribute is used to stream a document out-of-order, sending fast static content first and recommendations computed asynchronously as they become available on the server.
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE html>
> <html lang="en">
>  <head>
>   <title>Async recommendation engine</title>
>   <style>
>    aside {
>     /* position the aside where it can grow without causing layout shift or obscuring other content */
>    }
>    aside:has(.placeholder) {
>     /* style the placeholder content */
>    }
>   </style>
>  </head>
>  <body>
>   <h1>How to train your cat</h1>
>   <p>Set realistic goals and don't expect your cat to make a perfect cup of tea
>   on the first try.</p>
>   <aside>
>     <p>Recommended reading:</p>
>     <?start name="recommended">
>     <ul class="placeholder">
>       <li>...</li>
>       <li>...</li>
>       <li>...</li>
>     </ul>
>     <?end>
>   </aside>
>   <p>...</p>
>   <p>Now sit back and enjoy your tea with your cat.</p>
> 
>   <!-- The server has a potentially long delay at this point. -->
> 
>   <template for="recommended">
>     <ul>
>       <li>Cat or butler, which is right for you?</li>
>       <li>Rewarding good cat behavior</li>
>       <li>Kettles considered harmful</li>
>     </ul>
>   </template>
>  </body>
> </html>
> ```
> 
> The content between `<?start name="recommended">` and `<?end>` is replaced with the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) contents. Since the new content does not use `class="placeholder"`, the placeholder styling no longer applies.

##### 4.12.3.1 Interaction of [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) elements with XSLT and XPath

> [!danger]
> Avoid using client-side XSLT in browsers. The browser implementations of XSLT are highly susceptible to memory safety vulnerabilities, and the web platform has evolved toward JavaScript as the safe replacement. For these reasons, this feature is in the process of being removed from the web platform. (This is a long process that takes many years.)

*This section is non-normative.*

This specification does not define how XSLT and XPath interact with the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element. However, in the absence of another specification actually defining this, here are some guidelines for implementers, which are intended to be consistent with other processing described in this specification:
- An XSLT processor based on an XML parser that acts [as described in this specification](#142-parsing-xml-documents) needs to act as if [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) elements contain as descendants their [template contents](#4123-the-template-element) for the purposes of the transform.
- An XSLT processor that outputs a DOM needs to ensure that nodes that would go into a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element are instead placed into the element's [template contents](#4123-the-template-element).
- XPath evaluation using the XPath DOM API when applied to a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) parsed using the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) or the [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents) described in this specification needs to ignore [template contents](#4123-the-template-element).

#### 4.12.4 The `slot` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Transparent](#3253-transparent-content-models)

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`name`](#4124-the-slot-element) — Name of shadow tree slot

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-slot).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-slot).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLSlotElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString name;
  sequence<Node> assignedNodes(optional AssignedNodesOptions options = {});
  sequence<Element> assignedElements(optional AssignedNodesOptions options = {});
  undefined assign((Element or Text)... nodes);
};

dictionary AssignedNodesOptions {
  boolean flatten = false;
};
```

The [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element) element defines a [slot](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4221-slots). It is typically used in a [shadow tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree). A [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) its [assigned nodes](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4221-slots), if any, and its contents otherwise.

The `name` content attribute may contain any string value. It represents a [slot](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4221-slots)'s [name](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4221-slots).

> [!note]
> The [`name`](#4124-the-slot-element) attribute is used to [assign slots](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4224-assigning-slottables-and-slots) to other elements: a [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element) element with a [`name`](#4124-the-slot-element) attribute creates a named [slot](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4221-slots) to which any element is [assigned](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4224-assigning-slottables-and-slots) if that element has a [`slot`](#326-global-attributes) attribute whose value matches that [`name`](#4124-the-slot-element) attribute's value, and the [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element) element is a child of the [shadow tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree) whose [root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees)'s [host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) has that corresponding [`slot`](#326-global-attributes) attribute value.

`slot.name`

Can be used to get and set slot's [name](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4221-slots).

`slot.assignedNodes()`

Returns slot's [assigned nodes](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4221-slots).

`slot.assignedNodes({ flatten: true })`

Returns slot's [assigned nodes](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4221-slots), if any, and slot's children otherwise, and does the same for any [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element) elements encountered therein, recursively, until there are no [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element) elements left.

`slot.assignedElements()`

Returns slot's [assigned nodes](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4221-slots), limited to elements.

`slot.assignedElements({ flatten: true })`

Returns the same as [`assignedNodes({ flatten: true
   })`](#4124-the-slot-element), limited to elements.

`slot.assign(...nodes)`

Sets slot's [manually assigned nodes](#4124-the-slot-element) to the given nodes.

The [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element) element has manually assigned nodes, which is an [ordered set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) of [slottables](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4222-slottables) set by [`assign()`](#4124-the-slot-element). This set is initially empty.

> [!note]
> The [manually assigned nodes](#4124-the-slot-element) set can be implemented using weak references to the [slottables](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4222-slottables), because this set is not directly accessible from script.

The `assignedNodes(options)` method steps are:
1. If options\["[`flatten`](#4124-the-slot-element)"\] is false, then return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [assigned nodes](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4221-slots).
2. Return the result of [finding flattened slottables](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4223-finding-slots-and-slottables) with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).

The `assignedElements(options)` method steps are:
1. If options\["[`flatten`](#4124-the-slot-element)"\] is false, then return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [assigned nodes](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4221-slots), filtered to contain only [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) nodes.
2. Return the result of [finding flattened slottables](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4223-finding-slots-and-slottables) with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), filtered to contain only [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) nodes.

The `assign(...nodes)` method steps are:
1. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) node of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [manually assigned nodes](#4124-the-slot-element), set node's [manual slot assignment](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4222-slottables) to null.
2. Let nodesSet be a new [ordered set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets).
3. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) node of nodes:
   1. If node's [manual slot assignment](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4222-slottables) refers to a [slot](#4124-the-slot-element), then remove node from that [slot](#4124-the-slot-element)'s [manually assigned nodes](#4124-the-slot-element).
   2. Set node's [manual slot assignment](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4222-slottables) to [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
   3. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) node to nodesSet.
4. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [manually assigned nodes](#4124-the-slot-element) to nodesSet.
5. Run [assign slottables for a tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4224-assigning-slottables-and-slots) for [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).

#### 4.12.5 The `canvas` element

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Embedded content](#32526-embedded-content).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [embedded content](#32526-embedded-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Transparent](#3253-transparent-content-models), but with no [interactive content](#32527-interactive-content) descendants except for [`a`](#451-the-a-element) elements, [`img`](#483-the-img-element) elements with [`usemap`](#48141-authoring) attributes, [`button`](#4106-the-button-element) elements, [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute are in the [Checkbox](#4105115-checkbox-state-typecheckbox) or [Radio Button](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio) states, [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements that are [buttons](#4102-categories), and [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) elements with a [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute or a [display size](#4107-the-select-element) greater than 1.

[Tag omission in text/html](#324-element-definitions):

Neither tag is omissible.

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes)

[`width`](#4125-the-canvas-element) — Horizontal dimension

[`height`](#4125-the-canvas-element) — Vertical dimension

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

[For authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-canvas).

[For implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-canvas).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
typedef (CanvasRenderingContext2D or ImageBitmapRenderingContext or WebGLRenderingContext or WebGL2RenderingContext or GPUCanvasContext) RenderingContext;

[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLCanvasElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions] attribute unsigned long width;
  [CEReactions] attribute unsigned long height;

  RenderingContext? getContext(DOMString contextId, optional any options = null);

  USVString toDataURL(optional DOMString type = "image/png", optional any quality);
  undefined toBlob(BlobCallback _callback, optional DOMString type = "image/png", optional any quality);
  OffscreenCanvas transferControlToOffscreen();
};

callback BlobCallback = undefined (Blob? blob);
```

The [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element provides scripts with a resolution-dependent bitmap canvas, which can be used for rendering graphs, game graphics, art, or other visual images on the fly.

Authors should not use the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element in a document when a more suitable element is available. For example, it is inappropriate to use a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element to render a page heading: if the desired presentation of the heading is graphically intense, it should be marked up using appropriate elements (typically [`h1`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements)) and then styled using CSS and supporting technologies such as [shadow trees](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree).

When authors use the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element, they must also provide content that, when presented to the user, conveys essentially the same function or purpose as the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element)'s bitmap. This content may be placed as content of the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element. The contents of the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element, if any, are the element's [fallback content](#32526-embedded-content).

---

In interactive visual media, if [scripting is enabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting) for the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element, and if support for [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) elements has been enabled, then the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) [embedded content](#32526-embedded-content) consisting of a dynamically created image, the element's bitmap.

In non-interactive, static, visual media, if the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element has been previously associated with a rendering context (e.g. if the page was viewed in an interactive visual medium and is now being printed, or if some script that ran during the page layout process painted on the element), then the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) [embedded content](#32526-embedded-content) with the element's current bitmap and size. Otherwise, the element represents its [fallback content](#32526-embedded-content) instead.

In non-visual media, and in visual media if [scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting) for the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element or if support for [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) elements has been disabled, the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) its [fallback content](#32526-embedded-content) instead.

When a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) [embedded content](#32526-embedded-content), the user can still focus descendants of the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element (in the [fallback content](#32526-embedded-content)). When an element is [focused](#662-data-model), it is the target of keyboard interaction events (even though the element itself is not visible). This allows authors to make an interactive canvas keyboard-accessible: authors should have a one-to-one mapping of interactive regions to *[focusable areas](#662-data-model)* in the [fallback content](#32526-embedded-content). (Focus has no effect on mouse interaction events.) [\[UIEVENTS\]](#references)

An element whose nearest [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element ancestor is [being rendered](#151-introduction) and [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) [embedded content](#32526-embedded-content) is an element that is being used as relevant canvas fallback content.

---

The [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element has two attributes to control the size of the element's bitmap: `width` and `height`. These attributes, when specified, must have values that are [valid non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers). The [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers) must be used to obtain their numeric values. If an attribute is missing, or if parsing its value returns an error, then the default value must be used instead. The [`width`](#4125-the-canvas-element) attribute defaults to 300, and the [`height`](#4125-the-canvas-element) attribute defaults to 150.

When setting the value of the [`width`](#4125-the-canvas-element) or [`height`](#4125-the-canvas-element) attribute, if the [context mode](#4125-the-canvas-element) of the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element is set to [placeholder](#4125-the-canvas-element), the user agent must throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) and leave the attribute's value unchanged.

The [natural dimensions](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions) of the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element when it [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) [embedded content](#32526-embedded-content) are equal to the dimensions of the element's bitmap.

The user agent must use a square pixel density consisting of one pixel of image data per coordinate space unit for the bitmaps of a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) and its rendering contexts.

> [!note]
> A [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element can be sized arbitrarily by a style sheet, its bitmap is then subject to the ['object-fit'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#the-object-fit) CSS property.

---

The bitmaps of [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) elements, the bitmaps of [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) objects, as well as some of the bitmaps of rendering contexts, such as those described in the sections on the [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context), [`OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D`](#412531-the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context), and [`ImageBitmapRenderingContext`](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) objects below, have an origin-clean flag, which can be set to true or false. Initially, when the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element or [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) object is created, its bitmap's [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag must be set to true.

A [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element can have a rendering context bound to it. Initially, it does not have a bound rendering context. To keep track of whether it has a rendering context or not, and what kind of rendering context it is, a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) also has a canvas context mode, which is initially none but can be changed to either placeholder, 2d, bitmaprenderer, webgl, webgl2, or webgpu by algorithms defined in this specification.

When its [canvas context mode](#4125-the-canvas-element) is [none](#4125-the-canvas-element), a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element has no rendering context, and its bitmap must be [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black) with a [natural width](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-width) equal to [the numeric value](#4125-the-canvas-element) of the element's [`width`](#4125-the-canvas-element) attribute and a [natural height](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-height) equal to [the numeric value](#4125-the-canvas-element) of the element's [`height`](#4125-the-canvas-element) attribute, those values being interpreted in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px), and being updated as the attributes are set, changed, or removed.

When its [canvas context mode](#4125-the-canvas-element) is [placeholder](#4125-the-canvas-element), a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element has no rendering context. It serves as a placeholder for an [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object, and the content of the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element is updated by the [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object's rendering context.

When a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element represents [embedded content](#32526-embedded-content), it provides a [paint source](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images-4/#paint-source) whose width is the element's [natural width](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-width), whose height is the element's [natural height](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-height), and whose appearance is the element's bitmap.

Whenever the [`width`](#4125-the-canvas-element) and [`height`](#4125-the-canvas-element) content attributes are set, removed, changed, or redundantly set to the value they already have, then the user agent must perform the action from the row of the following table that corresponds to the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element's [context mode](#4125-the-canvas-element).

[Context Mode](#4125-the-canvas-element)

Action

[2d](#4125-the-canvas-element)

Follow the steps to [set bitmap dimensions](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) to [the numeric values](#4125-the-canvas-element) of the [`width`](#4125-the-canvas-element) and [`height`](#4125-the-canvas-element) content attributes.

[webgl](#4125-the-canvas-element) or [webgl2](#4125-the-canvas-element)

Follow the behavior defined in the WebGL specifications. [\[WEBGL\]](#references)

[webgpu](#4125-the-canvas-element)

Follow the behavior defined in WebGPU. [\[WEBGPU\]](#references)

[bitmaprenderer](#4125-the-canvas-element)

If the context's [bitmap mode](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) is set to [blank](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface), run the steps to [set an `ImageBitmapRenderingContext`'s output bitmap](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface), passing the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element's rendering context.

[placeholder](#4125-the-canvas-element)

Do nothing.

[none](#4125-the-canvas-element)

Do nothing.

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
|  |  |
|  |  |
|  |  |
|  |  |
|  |  |
|  |  |

The `width` and `height` IDL attributes must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the respective content attributes of the same name, with the same defaults.

---

`context = canvas.getContext(contextId [, options ])`

Returns an object that exposes an API for drawing on the canvas. contextId specifies the desired API: "[`2d`](#4125-the-canvas-element)", "[`bitmaprenderer`](#4125-the-canvas-element)", "[`webgl`](#4125-the-canvas-element)", "[`webgl2`](#4125-the-canvas-element)", or "[`webgpu`](#4125-the-canvas-element)". options is handled by that API.

This specification defines the "[`2d`](#4125-the-canvas-element)" and "[`bitmaprenderer`](#4125-the-canvas-element)" contexts below. The WebGL specifications define the "[`webgl`](#4125-the-canvas-element)" and "[`webgl2`](#4125-the-canvas-element)" contexts. WebGPU defines the "[`webgpu`](#4125-the-canvas-element)" context. [\[WEBGL\]](#references) [\[WEBGPU\]](#references)

Returns null if contextId is not supported, or if the canvas has already been initialized with another context type (e.g., trying to get a "[`2d`](#4125-the-canvas-element)" context after getting a "[`webgl`](#4125-the-canvas-element)" context).

The `getContext(contextId, options)` method of the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. If options is not an [object](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-object), then set options to null.
2. Set options to the result of [converting](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-type-mapping) options to a JavaScript value.
3. Run the steps in the cell of the following table whose column header matches this [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element's [canvas context mode](#4125-the-canvas-element) and whose row header matches contextId:

   •

   Let context be the result of running the [2D context creation algorithm](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) and options.

   •

   Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [context mode](#4125-the-canvas-element) to [2d](#4125-the-canvas-element).

   •

   Return context.

   •

   Let context be the result of running the [`ImageBitmapRenderingContext` creation algorithm](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) and options.

   •

   Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [context mode](#4125-the-canvas-element) to [bitmaprenderer](#4125-the-canvas-element).

   •

   Return context.

   •

   Let context be the result of following the instructions given in the WebGL specifications' *Context Creation* sections. [\[WEBGL\]](#references)

   •

   If context is null, then return null; otherwise set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [context mode](#4125-the-canvas-element) to [webgl](#4125-the-canvas-element) or [webgl2](#4125-the-canvas-element).

   •

   Return context.

   •

   Let context be the result of following the instructions given in WebGPU's [Canvas Rendering](https://gpuweb.github.io/gpuweb/#canvas-rendering) section. [\[WEBGPU\]](#references)

   •

   If context is null, then return null; otherwise set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [context mode](#4125-the-canvas-element) to [webgpu](#4125-the-canvas-element).

   •

   Return context.

   |  | [none](#4125-the-canvas-element) | [2d](#4125-the-canvas-element) | [bitmaprenderer](#4125-the-canvas-element) | [webgl](#4125-the-canvas-element) or [webgl2](#4125-the-canvas-element) | [webgpu](#4125-the-canvas-element) | [placeholder](#4125-the-canvas-element) |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | "`2d`" |  | Return the same object as was returned the last time the method was invoked with this same first argument. | Return null. | Return null. | Return null. | Throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException). |
   | "`bitmaprenderer`" |  | Return null. | Return the same object as was returned the last time the method was invoked with this same first argument. | Return null. | Return null. | Throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException). |
   | "`webgl`" or "`webgl2`", if the user agent supports the WebGL feature in its current configuration |  | Return null. | Return null. | Return the same object as was returned the last time the method was invoked with this same first argument. | Return null. | Throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException). |
   | "`webgpu`", if the user agent supports the WebGPU feature in its current configuration |  | Return null. | Return null. | Return null. | Return the same object as was returned the last time the method was invoked with this same first argument. | Throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException). |
   | An unsupported value\* | Return null. | Return null. | Return null. | Return null. | Return null. | Throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException). |

   \* For example, the "[`webgl`](#4125-the-canvas-element)" or "[`webgl2`](#4125-the-canvas-element)" value in the case of a user agent having exhausted the graphics hardware's abilities and having no software fallback implementation.

---

`url = canvas.toDataURL([ type [, quality ] ])`

Returns a [`data:` URL](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2397#section-2) for the image in the canvas.

The first argument, if provided, controls the type of the image to be returned (e.g. PNG or JPEG). The default is "[`image/png`](#mime-types)"; that type is also used if the given type isn't supported. The second argument applies if the type is an image format that supports variable quality (such as "[`image/jpeg`](#mime-types)"), and is a number in the range 0.0 to 1.0 inclusive indicating the desired quality level for the resulting image.

When trying to use types other than "[`image/png`](#mime-types)", authors can check if the image was really returned in the requested format by checking to see if the returned string starts with one of the exact strings "`data:image/png,`" or "`data:image/png;`". If it does, the image is PNG, and thus the requested type was not supported. (The one exception to this is if the canvas has either no height or no width, in which case the result might simply be "`data:,`".)

`canvas.toBlob(callback [, type [, quality ] ])`

Creates a [`Blob`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-Blob) object representing a file containing the image in the canvas, and invokes a callback with a handle to that object.

The second argument, if provided, controls the type of the image to be returned (e.g. PNG or JPEG). The default is "[`image/png`](#mime-types)"; that type is also used if the given type isn't supported. The third argument applies if the type is an image format that supports variable quality (such as "[`image/jpeg`](#mime-types)"), and is a number in the range 0.0 to 1.0 inclusive indicating the desired quality level for the resulting image.

`canvas.transferControlToOffscreen()`

Returns a newly created [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object that uses the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element as a placeholder. Once the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element has become a placeholder for an [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object, its natural size can no longer be changed, and it cannot have a rendering context. The content of the placeholder canvas is updated on the [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface)'s [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [update the rendering](#8173-processing-model) steps.

The `toDataURL(type, quality)` method, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. If this [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element's bitmap's [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag is set to false, then throw a ["`SecurityError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. If this [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element's bitmap has no pixels (i.e. either its horizontal dimension or its vertical dimension is zero), then return the string "`data:,`". (This is the shortest [`data:` URL](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2397#section-2); it represents the empty string in a `text/plain` resource.)
3. Let file be [a serialization of this `canvas` element's bitmap as a file](#41255-serializing-bitmaps-to-a-file), passing type and quality if given.
4. If file is null, then return "`data:,`".
5. Return a [`data:` URL](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2397#section-2) representing file. [\[RFC2397\]](#references)

The `toBlob(callback, type,
  quality)` method, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. If this [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element's bitmap's [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag is set to false, then throw a ["`SecurityError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Let result be null.
3. If this [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element's bitmap has pixels (i.e., neither its horizontal dimension nor its vertical dimension is zero), then set result to a copy of this [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element's bitmap.
4. Run these steps [in parallel](#211-parallelism):
   1. If result is non-null, then set result to [a serialization of result as a file](#41255-serializing-bitmaps-to-a-file) with type and quality if given.
   2. [Queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the canvas blob serialization task source given the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element to run these steps:
      1. If result is non-null, then set result to a new [`Blob`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-Blob) object, created in the [relevant realm](#81334-relevant) of this [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element, representing result. [\[FILEAPI\]](#references)
      2. [Invoke](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invoke-a-callback-function) callback with « result » and "`report`".

The `transferControlToOffscreen()` method, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. If this [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element's [context mode](#4125-the-canvas-element) is not set to [none](#4125-the-canvas-element), throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Let offscreenCanvas be a new [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object with its width and height equal to the values of the [`width`](#4125-the-canvas-element) and [`height`](#4125-the-canvas-element) content attributes of this [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element.
3. Set the offscreenCanvas's [placeholder `canvas` element](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) to a weak reference to this [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element.
4. Set this [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element's [context mode](#4125-the-canvas-element) to [placeholder](#4125-the-canvas-element).
5. Set the offscreenCanvas's [inherited language](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) to the [language](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes) of this [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element.
6. Set the offscreenCanvas's [inherited direction](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) to the [directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute) of this [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element.
7. Return offscreenCanvas.

##### 4.12.5.1 The 2D rendering context

```webidl
typedef (HTMLImageElement or
         SVGImageElement) HTMLOrSVGImageElement;

typedef (HTMLOrSVGImageElement or
         HTMLVideoElement or
         HTMLCanvasElement or
         ImageBitmap or
         OffscreenCanvas or
         VideoFrame) CanvasImageSource;

enum CanvasColorType { "unorm8", "float16" };

enum CanvasFillRule { "nonzero", "evenodd" };

dictionary CanvasRenderingContext2DSettings {
  boolean alpha = true;
  boolean desynchronized = false;
  PredefinedColorSpace colorSpace = "srgb";
  CanvasColorType colorType = "unorm8";
  boolean willReadFrequently = false;
};

enum ImageSmoothingQuality { "low", "medium", "high" };

[Exposed=Window]
interface CanvasRenderingContext2D {
  // back-reference to the canvas
  readonly attribute HTMLCanvasElement canvas;
};
CanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasSettings;
CanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasState;
CanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasTransform;
CanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasCompositing;
CanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasImageSmoothing;
CanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasFillStrokeStyles;
CanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasShadowStyles;
CanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasFilters;
CanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasRect;
CanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasDrawPath;
CanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasUserInterface;
CanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasText;
CanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasDrawImage;
CanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasImageData;
CanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasPathDrawingStyles;
CanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasTextDrawingStyles;
CanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasPath;

interface mixin CanvasSettings {
  // settings
  CanvasRenderingContext2DSettings getContextAttributes();
};

interface mixin CanvasState {
  // state
  undefined save(); // push state on state stack
  undefined restore(); // pop state stack and restore state
  undefined reset(); // reset the rendering context to its default state
  boolean isContextLost(); // return whether context is lost
};

interface mixin CanvasTransform {
  // transformations (default transform is the identity matrix)
  undefined scale(unrestricted double x, unrestricted double y);
  undefined rotate(unrestricted double angle);
  undefined translate(unrestricted double x, unrestricted double y);
  undefined transform(unrestricted double a, unrestricted double b, unrestricted double c, unrestricted double d, unrestricted double e, unrestricted double f);

  [NewObject] DOMMatrix getTransform();
  undefined setTransform(unrestricted double a, unrestricted double b, unrestricted double c, unrestricted double d, unrestricted double e, unrestricted double f);
  undefined setTransform(optional DOMMatrix2DInit transform = {});
  undefined resetTransform();

};

interface mixin CanvasCompositing {
  // compositing
  attribute unrestricted double globalAlpha; // (default 1.0)
  attribute DOMString globalCompositeOperation; // (default "source-over")
};

interface mixin CanvasImageSmoothing {
  // image smoothing
  attribute boolean imageSmoothingEnabled; // (default true)
  attribute ImageSmoothingQuality imageSmoothingQuality; // (default low)

};

interface mixin CanvasFillStrokeStyles {
  // colors and styles (see also the CanvasPathDrawingStyles and CanvasTextDrawingStyles interfaces)
  attribute (DOMString or CanvasGradient or CanvasPattern) strokeStyle; // (default black)
  attribute (DOMString or CanvasGradient or CanvasPattern) fillStyle; // (default black)
  CanvasGradient createLinearGradient(double x0, double y0, double x1, double y1);
  CanvasGradient createRadialGradient(double x0, double y0, double r0, double x1, double y1, double r1);
  CanvasGradient createConicGradient(double startAngle, double x, double y);
  CanvasPattern? createPattern(CanvasImageSource image, [LegacyNullToEmptyString] DOMString repetition);

};

interface mixin CanvasShadowStyles {
  // shadows
  attribute unrestricted double shadowOffsetX; // (default 0)
  attribute unrestricted double shadowOffsetY; // (default 0)
  attribute unrestricted double shadowBlur; // (default 0)
  attribute DOMString shadowColor; // (default transparent black)
};

interface mixin CanvasFilters {
  // filters
  attribute DOMString filter; // (default "none")
};

interface mixin CanvasRect {
  // rects
  undefined clearRect(unrestricted double x, unrestricted double y, unrestricted double w, unrestricted double h);
  undefined fillRect(unrestricted double x, unrestricted double y, unrestricted double w, unrestricted double h);
  undefined strokeRect(unrestricted double x, unrestricted double y, unrestricted double w, unrestricted double h);
};

interface mixin CanvasDrawPath {
  // path API (see also CanvasPath)
  undefined beginPath();
  undefined fill(optional CanvasFillRule fillRule = "nonzero");
  undefined fill(Path2D path, optional CanvasFillRule fillRule = "nonzero");
  undefined stroke();
  undefined stroke(Path2D path);
  undefined clip(optional CanvasFillRule fillRule = "nonzero");
  undefined clip(Path2D path, optional CanvasFillRule fillRule = "nonzero");
  boolean isPointInPath(unrestricted double x, unrestricted double y, optional CanvasFillRule fillRule = "nonzero");
  boolean isPointInPath(Path2D path, unrestricted double x, unrestricted double y, optional CanvasFillRule fillRule = "nonzero");
  boolean isPointInStroke(unrestricted double x, unrestricted double y);
  boolean isPointInStroke(Path2D path, unrestricted double x, unrestricted double y);
};

interface mixin CanvasUserInterface {
  undefined drawFocusIfNeeded(Element element);
  undefined drawFocusIfNeeded(Path2D path, Element element);
};

interface mixin CanvasText {
  // text (see also the CanvasPathDrawingStyles and CanvasTextDrawingStyles interfaces)
  undefined fillText(DOMString text, unrestricted double x, unrestricted double y, optional unrestricted double maxWidth);
  undefined strokeText(DOMString text, unrestricted double x, unrestricted double y, optional unrestricted double maxWidth);
  TextMetrics measureText(DOMString text);
};

interface mixin CanvasDrawImage {
  // drawing images
  undefined drawImage(CanvasImageSource image, unrestricted double dx, unrestricted double dy);
  undefined drawImage(CanvasImageSource image, unrestricted double dx, unrestricted double dy, unrestricted double dw, unrestricted double dh);
  undefined drawImage(CanvasImageSource image, unrestricted double sx, unrestricted double sy, unrestricted double sw, unrestricted double sh, unrestricted double dx, unrestricted double dy, unrestricted double dw, unrestricted double dh);
};

interface mixin CanvasImageData {
  // pixel manipulation
  ImageData createImageData([EnforceRange] long sw, [EnforceRange] long sh, optional ImageDataSettings settings = {});
  ImageData createImageData(ImageData imageData);
  ImageData getImageData([EnforceRange] long sx, [EnforceRange] long sy, [EnforceRange] long sw, [EnforceRange] long sh, optional ImageDataSettings settings = {});
  undefined putImageData(ImageData imageData, [EnforceRange] long dx, [EnforceRange] long dy);
  undefined putImageData(ImageData imageData, [EnforceRange] long dx, [EnforceRange] long dy, [EnforceRange] long dirtyX, [EnforceRange] long dirtyY, [EnforceRange] long dirtyWidth, [EnforceRange] long dirtyHeight);
};

enum CanvasLineCap { "butt", "round", "square" };
enum CanvasLineJoin { "round", "bevel", "miter" };
enum CanvasTextAlign { "start", "end", "left", "right", "center" };
enum CanvasTextBaseline { "top", "hanging", "middle", "alphabetic", "ideographic", "bottom" };
enum CanvasDirection { "ltr", "rtl", "inherit" };
enum CanvasFontKerning { "auto", "normal", "none" };
enum CanvasFontStretch { "ultra-condensed", "extra-condensed", "condensed", "semi-condensed", "normal", "semi-expanded", "expanded", "extra-expanded", "ultra-expanded" };
enum CanvasFontVariantCaps { "normal", "small-caps", "all-small-caps", "petite-caps", "all-petite-caps", "unicase", "titling-caps" };
enum CanvasTextRendering { "auto", "optimizeSpeed", "optimizeLegibility", "geometricPrecision" };

interface mixin CanvasPathDrawingStyles {
  // line caps/joins
  attribute unrestricted double lineWidth; // (default 1)
  attribute CanvasLineCap lineCap; // (default "butt")
  attribute CanvasLineJoin lineJoin; // (default "miter")

interface mixin CanvasTextDrawingStyles {

  attribute CanvasDirection direction; // (default: "inherit")
  attribute DOMString letterSpacing; // (default: "0px")
  attribute CanvasFontKerning fontKerning; // (default: "auto")
  attribute CanvasFontStretch fontStretch; // (default: "normal")

interface mixin CanvasPath {

  undefined bezierCurveTo(unrestricted double cp1x, unrestricted double cp1y, unrestricted double cp2x, unrestricted double cp2y, unrestricted double x, unrestricted double y);
  undefined arcTo(unrestricted double x1, unrestricted double y1, unrestricted double x2, unrestricted double y2, unrestricted double radius); 
  undefined rect(unrestricted double x, unrestricted double y, unrestricted double w, unrestricted double h);
  undefined roundRect(unrestricted double x, unrestricted double y, unrestricted double w, unrestricted double h, optional (unrestricted double or DOMPointInit or sequence<(unrestricted double or DOMPointInit)>) radii = 0);
  undefined arc(unrestricted double x, unrestricted double y, unrestricted double radius, unrestricted double startAngle, unrestricted double endAngle, optional boolean counterclockwise = false); 
  undefined ellipse(unrestricted double x, unrestricted double y, unrestricted double radiusX, unrestricted double radiusY, unrestricted double rotation, unrestricted double startAngle, unrestricted double endAngle, optional boolean counterclockwise = false);

[Exposed=(Window,Worker)]

};

[Exposed=(Window,Worker)]
interface CanvasPattern {
  // opaque object

};

[Exposed=(Window,Worker)]
interface TextMetrics {
  // x-direction
  readonly attribute double width; // advance width

  // y-direction

  readonly attribute double fontBoundingBoxDescent;
  readonly attribute double actualBoundingBoxAscent;
  readonly attribute double actualBoundingBoxDescent;

  constructor(optional (Path2D or DOMString) path);

  undefined addPath(Path2D path, optional DOMMatrix2DInit transform = {});
};
Path2D includes CanvasPath;
```

> [!note]
> To maintain compatibility with existing web content, user agents need to enumerate methods defined in [`CanvasUserInterface`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) immediately after the [`stroke()`](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) method on [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) objects.

`context = canvas.getContext('2d' [, { [ alpha: true ] [, desynchronized: false ] [, colorSpace: 'srgb'] [, willReadFrequently: false ]} ])`

Returns a [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object that is permanently bound to a particular [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element.

If the [`alpha`](#412512-the-canvas-settings) member is false, then the context is forced to always be opaque.

If the [`desynchronized`](#412512-the-canvas-settings) member is true, then the context might be [desynchronized](#412512-the-canvas-settings).

The [`colorSpace`](#412512-the-canvas-settings) member specifies the [color space](#412512-the-canvas-settings) of the rendering context.

The [`colorType`](#412512-the-canvas-settings) member specifies the [color type](#412512-the-canvas-settings) of the rendering context.

If the [`willReadFrequently`](#412512-the-canvas-settings) member is true, then the context is marked for [readback optimization](#412512-the-canvas-settings).

`context.canvas`

Returns the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element.

`attributes = context.getContextAttributes()`

Returns an object whose:
- [`alpha`](#412512-the-canvas-settings) member is true if the context has an alpha component that is not 1.0; otherwise false.
- [`desynchronized`](#412512-the-canvas-settings) member is true if the context can be [desynchronized](#412512-the-canvas-settings).
- [`colorSpace`](#412512-the-canvas-settings) member is a string indicating the context's [color space](#412512-the-canvas-settings).
- [`colorType`](#412512-the-canvas-settings) member is a string indicating the context's [color type](#412512-the-canvas-settings).
- [`willReadFrequently`](#412512-the-canvas-settings) member is true if the context is marked for [readback optimization](#412512-the-canvas-settings).

---

The [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) 2D rendering context represents a flat linear Cartesian surface whose origin (0,0) is at the top left corner, with the coordinate space having x values increasing when going right, and y values increasing when going down. The x-coordinate of the right-most edge is equal to the width of the rendering context's [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings) in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px); similarly, the y-coordinate of the bottom-most edge is equal to the height of the rendering context's [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings) in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px).

The size of the coordinate space does not necessarily represent the size of the actual bitmaps that the user agent will use internally or during rendering. On high-definition displays, for instance, the user agent may internally use bitmaps with four device pixels per unit in the coordinate space, so that the rendering remains at high quality throughout. Anti-aliasing can similarly be implemented using oversampling with bitmaps of a higher resolution than the final image on the display.

> [!example]
> Using [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) to describe the size of a rendering context's [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings) does not mean that when rendered the canvas will cover an equivalent area in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px). [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) are reused for ease of integration with CSS features, such as text layout.
> 
> In other words, the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element below's rendering context has a 200x200 [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings) (which internally uses [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) as a unit for ease of integration with CSS) and is rendered as 100x100 [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px):
> 
> ```html
> <canvas width=200 height=200 style=width:100px;height:100px>
> ```

---

The 2D context creation algorithm, which is passed a target (a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element) and options, consists of running these steps:
1. Let settings be the result of [converting](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-type-mapping) options to the dictionary type [`CanvasRenderingContext2DSettings`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context). (This can throw an exception.)
2. Let context be a new [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object.
3. Initialize context's [`canvas`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) attribute to point to target.
4. Set context's [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings) to the same bitmap as target's bitmap (so that they are shared).
5. [Set bitmap dimensions](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) to [the numeric values](#4125-the-canvas-element) of target's [`width`](#4125-the-canvas-element) and [`height`](#4125-the-canvas-element) content attributes.
6. Run the [canvas settings output bitmap initialization algorithm](#412512-the-canvas-settings), given context and settings.
7. Return context.

---

When the user agent is to set bitmap dimensions to width and height, it must run these steps:
1. [Reset the rendering context to its default state](#412513-the-canvas-state).
2. Resize the [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings) to the new width and height.
3. Let canvas be the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element to which the rendering context's [`canvas`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) attribute was initialized.
4. If [the numeric value](#4125-the-canvas-element) of canvas's [`width`](#4125-the-canvas-element) content attribute differs from width, then set canvas's [`width`](#4125-the-canvas-element) content attribute to the shortest possible string representing width as a [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers).
5. If [the numeric value](#4125-the-canvas-element) of canvas's [`height`](#4125-the-canvas-element) content attribute differs from height, then set canvas's [`height`](#4125-the-canvas-element) content attribute to the shortest possible string representing height as a [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers).

> [!example]
> Only one square appears to be drawn in the following example:
> 
> ```javascript
> // canvas is a reference to a <canvas> element
> var context = canvas.getContext('2d');
> context.fillRect(0,0,50,50);
> canvas.setAttribute('width', '300'); // clears the canvas
> context.fillRect(0,100,50,50);
> canvas.width = canvas.width; // clears the canvas
> context.fillRect(100,0,50,50); // only this square remains
> ```

---

The `canvas` attribute must return the value it was initialized to when the object was created.

---

The [`CanvasColorType`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) enumeration is used to specify the [color type](#412512-the-canvas-settings) of the canvas's backing store.

The "`unorm8`" value indicates that the type for all color components is 8-bit unsigned normalized.

The "`float16`" value indicates that the type for all color components is 16-bit floating point.

---

The [`CanvasFillRule`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) enumeration is used to select the fill rule algorithm by which to determine if a point is inside or outside a path.

The "`nonzero`" value indicates the nonzero winding rule, wherein a point is considered to be outside a shape if the number of times a half-infinite straight line drawn from that point crosses the shape's path going in one direction is equal to the number of times it crosses the path going in the other direction.

The "`evenodd`" value indicates the even-odd rule, wherein a point is considered to be outside a shape if the number of times a half-infinite straight line drawn from that point crosses the shape's path is even.

If a point is not outside a shape, it is inside the shape.

---

The [`ImageSmoothingQuality`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) enumeration is used to express a preference for the interpolation quality to use when smoothing images.

The "`low`" value indicates a preference for a low level of image interpolation quality. Low-quality image interpolation may be more computationally efficient than higher settings.

The "`medium`" value indicates a preference for a medium level of image interpolation quality.

The "`high`" value indicates a preference for a high level of image interpolation quality. High-quality image interpolation may be more computationally expensive than lower settings.

> [!note]
> Bilinear scaling is an example of a relatively fast, lower-quality image-smoothing algorithm. Bicubic or Lanczos scaling are examples of image-smoothing algorithms that produce higher-quality output. This specification does not mandate that specific interpolation algorithms be used.

###### 4.12.5.1.1 Implementation notes

*This section is non-normative.*

The [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings), when it is not directly displayed by the user agent, implementations can, instead of updating this bitmap, merely remember the sequence of drawing operations that have been applied to it until such time as the bitmap's actual data is needed (for example because of a call to [`drawImage()`](#4125115-drawing-images), or the [`createImageBitmap()`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) factory method). In many cases, this will be more memory efficient.

The bitmap of a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element is the one bitmap that's pretty much always going to be needed in practice. The [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings) of a rendering context, when it has one, is always just an alias to a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element's bitmap.

Additional bitmaps are sometimes needed, e.g. to enable fast drawing when the canvas is being painted at a different size than its [natural size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions), or to enable double buffering so that graphics updates, like page scrolling for example, can be processed concurrently while canvas draw commands are being executed.

###### 4.12.5.1.2 The canvas settings

A [`CanvasSettings`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object has an output bitmap that is initialized when the object is created.

The [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings) has an [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag, which can be set to true or false. Initially, when one of these bitmaps is created, its [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag must be set to true.

The [`CanvasSettings`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object also has an alpha boolean. When a [`CanvasSettings`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object's [alpha](#412512-the-canvas-settings) is false, then its alpha component must be fixed to 1.0 (fully opaque) for all pixels, and attempts to change the alpha component of any pixel must be silently ignored.

> [!note]
> Thus, the bitmap of such a context starts off as [opaque black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#opaque-black) instead of [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black); [`clearRect()`](#4125111-drawing-rectangles-to-the-bitmap) always results in [opaque black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#opaque-black) pixels, every fourth byte from [`getImageData()`](#4125116-pixel-manipulation) is always 255, the [`putImageData()`](#4125116-pixel-manipulation) method effectively ignores every fourth byte in its input, and so on. However, the alpha component of styles and images drawn onto the canvas are still honoured up to the point where they would impact the [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings)'s alpha component; for instance, drawing a 50% transparent white square on a freshly created [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings) with its [alpha](#412512-the-canvas-settings) set to false will result in a fully-opaque gray square.

The [`CanvasSettings`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object also has a desynchronized boolean. When a [`CanvasSettings`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object's [desynchronized](#412512-the-canvas-settings) is true, then the user agent may optimize the rendering of the canvas to reduce the latency, as measured from input events to rasterization, by desynchronizing the canvas paint cycle from the event loop, bypassing the ordinary user agent rendering algorithm, or both. Insofar as this mode involves bypassing the usual paint mechanisms, rasterization, or both, it might introduce visible tearing artifacts.

> [!note]
> The user agent usually renders on a buffer which is not being displayed, quickly swapping it and the one being scanned out for presentation; the former buffer is called back buffer and the latter *front buffer*. A popular technique for reducing latency is called front buffer rendering, also known as *single buffer* rendering, where rendering happens in parallel and racily with the scanning out process. This technique reduces the latency at the price of potentially introducing tearing artifacts and can be used to implement in total or part of the [desynchronized](#412512-the-canvas-settings) boolean. [\[MULTIPLEBUFFERING\]](#references)

> [!note]
> The [desynchronized](#412512-the-canvas-settings) boolean can be useful when implementing certain kinds of applications, such as drawing applications, where the latency between input and rasterization is critical.

The [`CanvasSettings`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object also has a will read frequently boolean. When a [`CanvasSettings`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object's [will read frequently](#412512-the-canvas-settings) is true, the user agent may optimize the canvas for readback operations.

> [!note]
> On most devices the user agent needs to decide whether to store the canvas's [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings) on the GPU (this is also called "hardware accelerated"), or on the CPU (also called "software"). Most rendering operations are more performant for accelerated canvases, with the major exception being readback with [`getImageData()`](#4125116-pixel-manipulation), [`toDataURL()`](#4125-the-canvas-element), or [`toBlob()`](#4125-the-canvas-element). [`CanvasSettings`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) objects with [will read frequently](#412512-the-canvas-settings) equal to true tell the user agent that the webpage is likely to perform many readback operations and that it is advantageous to use a software canvas.

The [`CanvasSettings`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object also has a color space setting of type [`PredefinedColorSpace`](#41254-color-spaces-and-color-space-conversion). The [`CanvasSettings`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object's [color space](#412512-the-canvas-settings) indicates the color space for the [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings).

The [`CanvasSettings`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object also has a color type setting of type [`CanvasColorType`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context). The [`CanvasSettings`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object's [color type](#412512-the-canvas-settings) indicates the data type of the color and alpha components of the pixels of the [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings).

To initialize a `CanvasSettings` output bitmap, given a [`CanvasSettings`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) context and a [`CanvasRenderingContext2DSettings`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) settings:
1. Set context's [alpha](#412512-the-canvas-settings) to settings\["`alpha`"\].
2. Set context's [desynchronized](#412512-the-canvas-settings) to settings\["`desynchronized`"\].
3. Set context's [color space](#412512-the-canvas-settings) to settings\["`colorSpace`"\].
4. Set context's [color type](#412512-the-canvas-settings) to settings\["`colorType`"\].
5. Set context's [will read frequently](#412512-the-canvas-settings) to settings\["`willReadFrequently`"\].

The `getContextAttributes()` method steps are to return «\[ "[`alpha`](#412512-the-canvas-settings)" → [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [alpha](#412512-the-canvas-settings), "[`desynchronized`](#412512-the-canvas-settings)" → [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [desynchronized](#412512-the-canvas-settings), "[`colorSpace`](#412512-the-canvas-settings)" → [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [color space](#412512-the-canvas-settings), "[`colorType`](#412512-the-canvas-settings)" → [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [color type](#412512-the-canvas-settings), "[`willReadFrequently`](#412512-the-canvas-settings)" → [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [will read frequently](#412512-the-canvas-settings) \]».

###### 4.12.5.1.3 The canvas state

Objects that implement the [`CanvasState`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface maintain a stack of drawing states. Drawing states consist of:
- The current [transformation matrix](#412518-transformations).
- The current [clipping region](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas).
- The current [letter spacing](#412515-text-styles), [word spacing](#412515-text-styles), [fill style](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles), [stroke style](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles), [filter](#4125120-filters), [global alpha](#4125117-compositing), [compositing and blending operator](#4125117-compositing), and [shadow color](#4125119-shadows).
- The current values of the following attributes: [`lineWidth`](#412514-line-styles), [`lineCap`](#412514-line-styles), [`lineJoin`](#412514-line-styles), [`miterLimit`](#412514-line-styles), [`lineDashOffset`](#412514-line-styles), [`shadowOffsetX`](#4125119-shadows), [`shadowOffsetY`](#4125119-shadows), [`shadowBlur`](#4125119-shadows), [`lang`](#412515-text-styles), [`font`](#412515-text-styles), [`textAlign`](#412515-text-styles), [`textBaseline`](#412515-text-styles), [`direction`](#412515-text-styles), [`fontKerning`](#412515-text-styles), [`fontStretch`](#412515-text-styles), [`fontVariantCaps`](#412515-text-styles), [`textRendering`](#412515-text-styles), [`imageSmoothingEnabled`](#4125118-image-smoothing), [`imageSmoothingQuality`](#4125118-image-smoothing).
- The current [dash list](#412514-line-styles).

> [!note]
> The rendering context's bitmaps are not part of the drawing state, as they depend on whether and how the rendering context is bound to a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element.

Objects that implement the [`CanvasState`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) mixin have a context lost boolean, that is initialized to false when the object is created. The [context lost](#412513-the-canvas-state) value is updated in the [context lost steps](#8173-processing-model).

`context.save()`

Pushes the current state onto the stack.

`context.restore()`

Pops the top state on the stack, restoring the context to that state.

`context.reset()`

Resets the rendering context, which includes the backing buffer, the drawing state stack, path, and styles.

`context.isContextLost()`

Returns true if the rendering context was lost. Context loss can occur due to driver crashes, running out of memory, etc. In these cases, the canvas loses its backing storage and takes steps to [reset the rendering context to its default state](#412513-the-canvas-state).

The `save()` method steps are to push a copy of the current drawing state onto the drawing state stack.

The `restore()` method steps are to pop the top entry in the drawing state stack, and reset the drawing state it describes. If there is no saved state, then the method must do nothing.

The `reset()` method steps are to [reset the rendering context to its default state](#412513-the-canvas-state).

To reset the rendering context to its default state:
1. Clear canvas's bitmap to [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black).
2. Empty the list of subpaths in the context's [current default path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas).
3. Clear the context's drawing state stack.
4. Reset everything that [drawing state](#412513-the-canvas-state) consists of to their initial values.

The `isContextLost()` method steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [context lost](#412513-the-canvas-state).

###### 4.12.5.1.4 Line styles

`context.lineWidth [ = value ]`

`styles.lineWidth [ = value ]`

Returns the current line width.

Can be set, to change the line width. Values that are not finite values greater than zero are ignored.

`context.lineCap [ = value ]`

`styles.lineCap [ = value ]`

Returns the current line cap style.

Can be set, to change the line cap style.

The possible line cap styles are "`butt`", "`round`", and "`square`". Other values are ignored.

`context.lineJoin [ = value ]`

`styles.lineJoin [ = value ]`

Returns the current line join style.

Can be set, to change the line join style.

The possible line join styles are "`bevel`", "`round`", and "`miter`". Other values are ignored.

`context.miterLimit [ = value ]`

`styles.miterLimit [ = value ]`

Returns the current miter limit ratio.

Can be set, to change the miter limit ratio. Values that are not finite values greater than zero are ignored.

`context.setLineDash(segments)`

`styles.setLineDash(segments)`

Sets the current line dash pattern (as used when stroking). The argument is a list of distances for which to alternately have the line on and the line off.

`segments = context.getLineDash()`

`segments = styles.getLineDash()`

Returns a copy of the current line dash pattern. The array returned will always have an even number of entries (i.e. the pattern is normalized).

`context.lineDashOffset`

`styles.lineDashOffset`

Returns the phase offset (in the same units as the line dash pattern).

Can be set, to change the phase offset. Values that are not finite values are ignored.

Objects that implement the [`CanvasPathDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface have attributes and methods (defined in this section) that control how lines are treated by the object.

The `lineWidth` attribute gives the width of lines, in coordinate space units. On getting, it must return the current value. On setting, zero, negative, infinite, and NaN values must be ignored, leaving the value unchanged; other values must change the current value to the new value.

When the object implementing the [`CanvasPathDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface is created, the [`lineWidth`](#412514-line-styles) attribute must initially have the value 1.0.

---

The `lineCap` attribute defines the type of endings that UAs will place on the end of lines. The three valid values are "`butt`", "`round`", and "`square`".

On getting, it must return the current value. On setting, the current value must be changed to the new value.

When the object implementing the [`CanvasPathDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface is created, the [`lineCap`](#412514-line-styles) attribute must initially have the value "`butt`".

---

The `lineJoin` attribute defines the type of corners that UAs will place where two lines meet. The three valid values are "`bevel`", "`round`", and "`miter`".

On getting, it must return the current value. On setting, the current value must be changed to the new value.

When the object implementing the [`CanvasPathDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface is created, the [`lineJoin`](#412514-line-styles) attribute must initially have the value "`miter`".

---

When the [`lineJoin`](#412514-line-styles) attribute has the value "`miter`", strokes use the miter limit ratio to decide how to render joins. The miter limit ratio can be explicitly set using the `miterLimit` attribute. On getting, it must return the current value. On setting, zero, negative, infinite, and NaN values must be ignored, leaving the value unchanged; other values must change the current value to the new value.

When the object implementing the [`CanvasPathDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface is created, the [`miterLimit`](#412514-line-styles) attribute must initially have the value 10.0.

---

Each [`CanvasPathDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object has a dash list, which is either empty or consists of an even number of non-negative numbers. Initially, the [dash list](#412514-line-styles) must be empty.

The `setLineDash(segments)` method, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. If any value in segments is not finite (e.g. an Infinity or a NaN value), or if any value is negative (less than zero), then return (without throwing an exception; user agents could show a message on a developer console, though, as that would be helpful for debugging).
2. If the number of elements in segments is odd, then let segments be the concatenation of two copies of segments.
3. Set the object's [dash list](#412514-line-styles) to segments.

When the `getLineDash()` method is invoked, it must return a sequence whose values are the values of the object's [dash list](#412514-line-styles), in the same order.

It is sometimes useful to change the "phase" of the dash pattern, e.g. to achieve a "marching ants" effect. The phase can be set using the `lineDashOffset` attribute. On getting, it must return the current value. On setting, infinite and NaN values must be ignored, leaving the value unchanged; other values must change the current value to the new value.

When the object implementing the [`CanvasPathDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface is created, the [`lineDashOffset`](#412514-line-styles) attribute must initially have the value 0.0.

---

When a user agent is to trace a path, given an object style that implements the [`CanvasPathDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface, it must run the following algorithm. This algorithm returns a new [path](#412516-building-paths).
1. Let path be a copy of the path being traced.
2. Prune all zero-length [line segments](#412516-building-paths) from path.
3. Remove from path any subpaths containing no lines (i.e. subpaths with just one point).
4. Replace each point in each subpath of path other than the first point and the last point of each subpath by a *join* that joins the line leading to that point to the line leading out of that point, such that the subpaths all consist of two points (a starting point with a line leading out of it, and an ending point with a line leading into it), one or more lines (connecting the points and the joins), and zero or more joins (each connecting one line to another), connected together such that each subpath is a series of one or more lines with a join between each one and a point on each end.
5.
