Add a straight closing line to each closed subpath in path connecting the last point and the first point of that subpath; change the last point to a join (from the previously last line to the newly added closing line), and change the first point to a join (from the newly added closing line to the first line).
6. If style's [dash list](#412514-line-styles) is empty, then jump to the step labeled *convert*.
7. Let pattern width be the concatenation of all the entries of style's [dash list](#412514-line-styles), in coordinate space units.
8. For each subpath subpath in path, run the following substeps. These substeps mutate the subpaths in path *in vivo*.
   1. Let subpath width be the length of all the lines of subpath, in coordinate space units.
   2. Let offset be the value of style's [`lineDashOffset`](#412514-line-styles), in coordinate space units.
   3. While offset is greater than pattern width, decrement it by pattern width.

      While offset is less than zero, increment it by pattern width.

   4. Define L to be a linear coordinate line defined along all lines in subpath, such that the start of the first line in the subpath is defined as coordinate 0, and the end of the last line in the subpath is defined as coordinate subpath width.
   5. Let position be 0 minus offset.
   6. Let index be 0.
   7. Let current state be *off* (the other states being *on* and *zero-on*).
   8. *Dash on*: Let segment length be the value of style's [dash list](#412514-line-styles)'s indexth entry.
   9. Increment position by segment length.
   10. If position is greater than subpath width, then end these substeps for this subpath and start them again for the next subpath; if there are no more subpaths, then jump to the step labeled *convert* instead.
   11. If segment length is nonzero, then let current state be *on*.
   12. Increment index by one.
   13. *Dash off*: Let segment length be the value of style's [dash list](#412514-line-styles)'s indexth entry.
   14. Let start be the offset position on L.
   15. Increment position by segment length.
   16. If position is less than zero, then jump to the step labeled *post-cut*.
   17. If start is less than zero, then let start be zero.
   18. If position is greater than subpath width, then let end be the offset subpath width on L. Otherwise, let end be the offset position on L.
   19. Jump to the first appropriate step:

       If segment length is zero and current state is *off*

       Do nothing, just continue to the next step.

       If current state is *off*

       Cut the line on which end finds itself short at end and place a point there, cutting in two the subpath that it was in; remove all line segments, joins, points, and subpaths that are between start and end; and finally place a single point at start with no lines connecting to it.

       The point has a *directionality* for the purposes of drawing line caps (see below). The directionality is the direction that the original line had at that point (i.e. when L was defined above).

       Otherwise

       Cut the line on which start finds itself into two at start and place a point there, cutting in two the subpath that it was in, and similarly cut the line on which end finds itself short at end and place a point there, cutting in two the subpath that *it* was in, and then remove all line segments, joins, points, and subpaths that are between start and end.

       If start and end are the same point, then this results in just the line being cut in two and two points being inserted there, with nothing being removed, unless a join also happens to be at that point, in which case the join must be removed.

   20. *Post-cut*: If position is greater than subpath width, then jump to the step labeled *convert*.
   21. Increment index by one. If it is equal to the number of entries in style's [dash list](#412514-line-styles), then let index be 0.
   22. Return to the step labeled *dash on*.

9. *Convert*: This is the step that converts the path to a new path that represents its stroke.

   Create a new [path](#412516-building-paths) that describes the edge of the areas that would be covered if a straight line of length equal to style's [`lineWidth`](#412514-line-styles) was swept along each subpath in path while being kept at an angle such that the line is orthogonal to the path being swept, replacing each point with the end cap necessary to satisfy style's [`lineCap`](#412514-line-styles) attribute as described previously and elaborated below, and replacing each join with the join necessary to satisfy style's [`lineJoin`](#412514-line-styles) type, as defined below.

   **Caps**: Each point has a flat edge perpendicular to the direction of the line coming out of it. This is then augmented according to the value of style's [`lineCap`](#412514-line-styles). The "`butt`" value means that no additional line cap is added. The "`round`" value means that a semi-circle with the diameter equal to style's [`lineWidth`](#412514-line-styles) width must additionally be placed on to the line coming out of each point. The "`square`" value means that a rectangle with the length of style's [`lineWidth`](#412514-line-styles) width and the width of half style's [`lineWidth`](#412514-line-styles) width, placed flat against the edge perpendicular to the direction of the line coming out of the point, must be added at each point.

   Points with no lines coming out of them must have two caps placed back-to-back as if it was really two points connected to each other by an infinitesimally short straight line in the direction of the point's *directionality* (as defined above).

   **Joins**: In addition to the point where a join occurs, two additional points are relevant to each join, one for each line: the two corners found half the line width away from the join point, one perpendicular to each line, each on the side furthest from the other line.

   A triangle connecting these two opposite corners with a straight line, with the third point of the triangle being the join point, must be added at all joins. The [`lineJoin`](#412514-line-styles) attribute controls whether anything else is rendered. The three aforementioned values have the following meanings:

   The "`bevel`" value means that this is all that is rendered at joins.

   The "`round`" value means that an arc connecting the two aforementioned corners of the join, abutting (and not overlapping) the aforementioned triangle, with the diameter equal to the line width and the origin at the point of the join, must be added at joins.

   The "`miter`" value means that a second triangle must (if it can given the miter length) be added at the join, with one line being the line between the two aforementioned corners, abutting the first triangle, and the other two being continuations of the outside edges of the two joining lines, as long as required to intersect without going over the miter length.

   The miter length is the distance from the point where the join occurs to the intersection of the line edges on the outside of the join. The miter limit ratio is the maximum allowed ratio of the miter length to half the line width. If the miter length would cause the miter limit ratio (as set by style's [`miterLimit`](#412514-line-styles) attribute) to be exceeded, then this second triangle must not be added.

   The subpaths in the newly created path must be oriented such that for any point, the number of times a half-infinite straight line drawn from that point crosses a subpath is even if and only if the number of times a half-infinite straight line drawn from that same point crosses a subpath going in one direction is equal to the number of times it crosses a subpath going in the other direction.

10. Return the newly created path.

###### 4.12.5.1.5 Text styles

`context.lang [ = value ]`

`styles.lang [ = value ]`

Returns the current language setting.

Can be set to a BCP 47 language tag, the empty string, or "[`inherit`](#412515-text-styles)", to change the language used when resolving fonts. "[`inherit`](#412515-text-styles)" takes the language from the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element's language, or the associated [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) when there is no [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element.

The default is "[`inherit`](#412515-text-styles)".

`context.font [ = value ]`

`styles.font [ = value ]`

Returns the current font settings.

Can be set, to change the font. The syntax is the same as for the CSS ['font'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-prop) property; values that cannot be parsed as CSS font values are ignored. The default is "10px sans-serif".

Relative keywords and lengths are computed relative to the font of the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element.

`context.textAlign [ = value ]`

`styles.textAlign [ = value ]`

Returns the current text alignment settings.

Can be set, to change the alignment. The possible values are and their meanings are given below. Other values are ignored. The default is "`start`".

`context.textBaseline [ = value ]`

`styles.textBaseline [ = value ]`

Returns the current baseline alignment settings.

Can be set, to change the baseline alignment. The possible values and their meanings are given below. Other values are ignored. The default is "[`alphabetic`](#412515-text-styles)".

`context.direction [ = value ]`

`styles.direction [ = value ]`

Returns the current directionality.

Can be set, to change the directionality. The possible values and their meanings are given below. Other values are ignored. The default is "[`inherit`](#412515-text-styles)".

`context.letterSpacing [ = value ]`

`styles.letterSpacing [ = value ]`

Returns the current spacing between characters in the text.

Can be set, to change spacing between characters. Values that cannot be parsed as a CSS [<length>](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#lengths) are ignored. The default is "`0px`".

`context.fontKerning [ = value ]`

`styles.fontKerning [ = value ]`

Returns the current font kerning settings.

Can be set, to change the font kerning. The possible values and their meanings are given below. Other values are ignored. The default is "[`auto`](#412515-text-styles)".

`context.fontStretch [ = value ]`

`styles.fontStretch [ = value ]`

Returns the current font stretch settings.

Can be set, to change the font stretch. The possible values and their meanings are given below. Other values are ignored. The default is "[`normal`](#412515-text-styles)".

`context.fontVariantCaps [ = value ]`

`styles.fontVariantCaps [ = value ]`

Returns the current font variant caps settings.

Can be set, to change the font variant caps. The possible values and their meanings are given below. Other values are ignored. The default is "[`normal`](#412515-text-styles)".

`context.textRendering [ = value ]`

`styles.textRendering [ = value ]`

Returns the current text rendering settings.

Can be set, to change the text rendering. The possible values and their meanings are given below. Other values are ignored. The default is "[`auto`](#412515-text-styles)".

`context.wordSpacing [ = value ]`

`styles.wordSpacing [ = value ]`

Returns the current spacing between words in the text.

Can be set, to change spacing between words. Values that cannot be parsed as a CSS [<length>](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#lengths) are ignored. The default is "`0px`".

Objects that implement the [`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface have attributes (defined in this section) that control how text is laid out (rasterized or outlined) by the object. Such objects can also have a font style source object. For [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) objects, this is the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element given by the value of the context's [`canvas`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) attribute. For [`OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D`](#412531-the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context) objects, this is the [associated `OffscreenCanvas` object](#412531-the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context).

Font resolution for the [font style source object](#412515-text-styles) requires a [font source](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-font-loading/#font-source). This is determined for a given object implementing [`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) by the following steps: [\[CSSFONTLOAD\]](#references)
1. If object's [font style source object](#412515-text-styles) is a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element, return the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
2. Otherwise, object's [font style source object](#412515-text-styles) is an [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object:
   1. Let global be object's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant).
   2. If global is a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object, then return global's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object).
   3. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): global implements [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface).
   4. Return global.

> [!example]
> This is an example of font resolution with a regular [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element with ID `c1`.
> 
> ```javascript
> const font = new FontFace("MyCanvasFont", "url(mycanvasfont.ttf)");
> documents.fonts.add(font);
> 
> const context = document.getElementById("c1").getContext("2d");
> document.fonts.ready.then(function() {
>   context.font = "64px MyCanvasFont";
>   context.fillText("hello", 0, 0);
> });
> ```
> 
> In this example, the canvas will display text using `mycanvasfont.ttf` as its font.

> [!example]
> This is an example of how font resolution can happen using [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface). Assuming a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element with ID `c2` which is transferred to a worker like so:
> 
> ```javascript
> const offscreenCanvas = document.getElementById("c2").transferControlToOffscreen();
> worker.postMessage(offscreenCanvas, [offscreenCanvas]);
> ```
> 
> Then, in the worker:
> 
> ```javascript
> self.onmessage = function(ev) {
>   const transferredCanvas = ev.data;
>   const context = transferredCanvas.getContext("2d");
>   const font = new FontFace("MyFont", "url(myfont.ttf)");
>   self.fonts.add(font);
>   self.fonts.ready.then(function() {
>     context.font = "64px MyFont";
>     context.fillText("hello", 0, 0);
>   });
> };
> ```
> 
> In this example, the canvas will display a text using `myfont.ttf`. Notice that the font is only loaded inside the worker, and not in the document context.

The `font` IDL attribute, on setting, must be [parsed as a CSS <'font'> value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#parse-grammar) (but without supporting property-independent style sheet syntax like 'inherit'), and the resulting font must be assigned to the context, with the ['line-height'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#propdef-line-height) component forced to 'normal', with the ['font-size'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-size-prop) component converted to [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px), and with system fonts being computed to explicit values. If the new value is syntactically incorrect (including using property-independent style sheet syntax like 'inherit' or 'initial'), then it must be ignored, without assigning a new font value. [\[CSS\]](#references)

Font family names must be interpreted in the context of the [font style source object](#412515-text-styles) when the font is to be used; any fonts embedded using `@font-face` or loaded using [`FontFace`](#219-dependencies) objects that are visible to the [font style source object](#412515-text-styles) must therefore be available once they are loaded. (Each [font style source object](#412515-text-styles) has a [font source](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-font-loading/#font-source), which determines what fonts are available.) If a font is used before it is fully loaded, or if the [font style source object](#412515-text-styles) does not have that font in scope at the time the font is to be used, then it must be treated as if it was an unknown font, falling back to another as described by the relevant CSS specifications. [\[CSSFONTS\]](#references) [\[CSSFONTLOAD\]](#references)

On getting, the [`font`](#412515-text-styles) attribute must return the [serialized form](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#serialize-a-css-value) of the current font of the context (with no ['line-height'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#propdef-line-height) component). [\[CSSOM\]](#references)

> [!example]
> For example, after the following statement:
> 
> ```javascript
> context.font = 'italic 400 12px/2 Unknown Font, sans-serif';
> ```
> 
> ...the expression `context.font` would evaluate to the string "`italic 12px "Unknown Font", sans-serif`". The "400" font-weight doesn't appear because that is the default value. The line-height doesn't appear because it is forced to "normal", the default value.

When the object implementing the [`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface is created, the font of the context must be set to 10px sans-serif. When the ['font-size'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-size-prop) component is set to lengths using percentages, ['em'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#em) or ['ex'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#ex) units, or the 'larger' or 'smaller' keywords, these must be interpreted relative to the [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of the ['font-size'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-size-prop) property of the [font style source object](#412515-text-styles) at the time that the attribute is set, if it is an element. When the ['font-weight'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-weight-prop) component is set to the relative values 'bolder' and 'lighter', these must be interpreted relative to the [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of the ['font-weight'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-weight-prop) property of the [font style source object](#412515-text-styles) at the time that the attribute is set, if it is an element. If the [computed values](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) are undefined for a particular case (e.g. because the [font style source object](#412515-text-styles) is not an element or is not [being rendered](#151-introduction)), then the relative keywords must be interpreted relative to the normal-weight 10px sans-serif default.

The `textAlign` IDL attribute, on getting, must return the current value. On setting, the current value must be changed to the new value. When the object implementing the [`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface is created, the [`textAlign`](#412515-text-styles) attribute must initially have the value [`start`](#412515-text-styles).

The `textBaseline` IDL attribute, on getting, must return the current value. On setting, the current value must be changed to the new value. When the object implementing the [`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface is created, the [`textBaseline`](#412515-text-styles) attribute must initially have the value [`alphabetic`](#412515-text-styles).

Objects that implement the [`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface have an associated language value used to localize font rendering. Valid values are a BCP 47 language tag, the empty string, or "inherit" where the language comes from the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element's language, or the associated [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) when there is no [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element. Initially, the [language](#412515-text-styles) must be "[`inherit`](#412515-text-styles)".

The `lang` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [language](#412515-text-styles).

The [`lang`](#412515-text-styles) setter steps are to set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [language](#412515-text-styles) to the given value.

The `direction` IDL attribute, on getting, must return the current value. On setting, the current value must be changed to the new value. When the object implementing the [`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface is created, the [`direction`](#412515-text-styles) attribute must initially have the value "[`inherit`](#412515-text-styles)".

Objects that implement the [`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface have attributes that control the spacing between letters and words. Such objects have associated letter spacing and word spacing values, which are CSS [<length>](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#lengths) values. Initially, both must be the result of [parsing](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#parse-grammar) "`0px`" as a CSS [<length>](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#lengths).

The `letterSpacing` getter steps are to return the [serialized form](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#serialize-a-css-value) of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [letter spacing](#412515-text-styles).

The [`letterSpacing`](#412515-text-styles) setter steps are:
1. Let parsed be the result of [parsing](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#parse-grammar) the given value as a CSS [<length>](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#lengths).
2. If parsed is failure, then return.
3. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [letter spacing](#412515-text-styles) to parsed.

The `wordSpacing` getter steps are to return the [serialized form](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#serialize-a-css-value) of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [word spacing](#412515-text-styles).

The [`wordSpacing`](#412515-text-styles) setter steps are:
1. Let parsed be the result of [parsing](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#parse-grammar) the given value as a CSS [<length>](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#lengths).
2. If parsed is failure, then return.
3. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [word spacing](#412515-text-styles) to parsed.

The `fontKerning` IDL attribute, on getting, must return the current value. On setting, the current value must be changed to the new value. When the object implementing the [`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface is created, the [`fontKerning`](#412515-text-styles) attribute must initially have the value "[`auto`](#412515-text-styles)".

The `fontStretch` IDL attribute, on getting, must return the current value. On setting, the current value must be changed to the new value. When the object implementing the [`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface is created, the [`fontStretch`](#412515-text-styles) attribute must initially have the value "[`normal`](#412515-text-styles)".

The `fontVariantCaps` IDL attribute, on getting, must return the current value. On setting, the current value must be changed to the new value. When the object implementing the [`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface is created, the [`fontVariantCaps`](#412515-text-styles) attribute must initially have the value "[`normal`](#412515-text-styles)".

The `textRendering` IDL attribute, on getting, must return the current value. On setting, the current value must be changed to the new value. When the object implementing the [`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface is created, the [`textRendering`](#412515-text-styles) attribute must initially have the value "[`auto`](#412515-text-styles)".

The [`textAlign`](#412515-text-styles) attribute's allowed keywords are as follows:

`start`

Align to the start edge of the text (left side in left-to-right text, right side in right-to-left text).

`end`

Align to the end edge of the text (right side in left-to-right text, left side in right-to-left text).

`left`

Align to the left.

`right`

Align to the right.

`center`

Align to the center.

The [`textBaseline`](#412515-text-styles) attribute's allowed keywords correspond to alignment points in the font:

![The em-over baseline is roughly at the top of the glyphs in a font, the hanging baseline is where some glyphs like आ are anchored, the middle is half-way between the em-over and em-under baselines, the alphabetic baseline is where characters like Á, ÿ, f, and Ω are anchored, the ideographic-under baseline is where glyphs like 私 and 達 are anchored, and the em-under baseline is roughly at the bottom of the glyphs in a font. The top and bottom of the bounding box can be far from these baselines, due to glyphs extending far outside em-over and em-under baselines.](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/baselines.png)

The keywords map to these alignment points as follows:

`top`

The [em-over baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#em-over-baseline)

`hanging`

The [hanging baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#hanging-baseline)

`middle`

Halfway between the [em-over baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#em-over-baseline) and the [em-under baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#em-under-baseline)

`alphabetic`

The [alphabetic baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#alphabetic-baseline)

`ideographic`

The [ideographic-under baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#ideographic-under-baseline)

`bottom`

The [em-under baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#em-under-baseline)

The [`direction`](#412515-text-styles) attribute's allowed keywords are as follows:

`ltr`

Treat input to the [text preparation algorithm](#412515-text-styles) as left-to-right text.

`rtl`

Treat input to the [text preparation algorithm](#412515-text-styles) as right-to-left text.

`inherit`

Use the process in the [text preparation algorithm](#412515-text-styles) to obtain the text direction from the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element, [placeholder `canvas` element](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface), or [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree).

The [`fontKerning`](#412515-text-styles) attribute's allowed keywords are as follows:

`auto`

Kerning is applied at the discretion of the user agent.

`normal`

Kerning is applied.

`none`

Kerning is not applied.

The [`fontStretch`](#412515-text-styles) attribute's allowed keywords are as follows:

`ultra-condensed`

Same as CSS ['font-stretch'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#propdef-font-stretch) ['ultra-condensed'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#valdef-font-stretch-ultra-condensed) setting.

`extra-condensed`

Same as CSS ['font-stretch'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#propdef-font-stretch) ['extra-condensed'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#valdef-font-stretch-extra-condensed) setting.

`condensed`

Same as CSS ['font-stretch'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#propdef-font-stretch) ['condensed'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#valdef-font-stretch-condensed) setting.

`semi-condensed`

Same as CSS ['font-stretch'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#propdef-font-stretch) ['semi-condensed'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#valdef-font-stretch-semi-condensed) setting.

`normal`

The default setting, where width of the glyphs is at 100%.

`semi-expanded`

Same as CSS ['font-stretch'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#propdef-font-stretch) ['semi-expanded'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#valdef-font-stretch-semi-expanded) setting.

`expanded`

Same as CSS ['font-stretch'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#propdef-font-stretch) ['expanded'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#valdef-font-stretch-expanded) setting.

`extra-expanded`

Same as CSS ['font-stretch'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#propdef-font-stretch) ['extra-expanded'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#valdef-font-stretch-extra-expanded) setting.

`ultra-expanded`

Same as CSS ['font-stretch'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#propdef-font-stretch) ['ultra-expanded'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#valdef-font-stretch-ultra-expanded) setting.

The [`fontVariantCaps`](#412515-text-styles) attribute's allowed keywords are as follows:

`normal`

None of the features listed below are enabled.

`small-caps`

Same as CSS ['font-variant-caps'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#propdef-font-variant-caps) ['small-caps'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#valdef-font-variant-caps-small-caps) setting.

`all-small-caps`

Same as CSS ['font-variant-caps'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#propdef-font-variant-caps) ['all-small-caps'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#valdef-font-variant-caps-all-small-caps) setting.

`petite-caps`

Same as CSS ['font-variant-caps'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#propdef-font-variant-caps) ['petite-caps'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#valdef-font-variant-caps-petite-caps) setting.

`all-petite-caps`

Same as CSS ['font-variant-caps'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#propdef-font-variant-caps) ['all-petite-caps'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#valdef-font-variant-caps-all-petite-caps) setting.

`unicase`

Same as CSS ['font-variant-caps'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#propdef-font-variant-caps) ['unicase'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#valdef-font-variant-caps-unicase) setting.

`titling-caps`

Same as CSS ['font-variant-caps'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#propdef-font-variant-caps) ['titling-caps'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#valdef-font-variant-caps-titling-caps) setting.

The [`textRendering`](#412515-text-styles) attribute's allowed keywords are as follows:

`auto`

Same as 'auto' in [SVG text-rendering](https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/painting.html#TextRendering) property.

`optimizeSpeed`

Same as 'optimizeSpeed' in [SVG text-rendering](https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/painting.html#TextRendering) property.

`optimizeLegibility`

Same as 'optimizeLegibility' in [SVG text-rendering](https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/painting.html#TextRendering) property.

`geometricPrecision`

Same as 'geometricPrecision' in [SVG text-rendering](https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/painting.html#TextRendering) property.

The text preparation algorithm is as follows. It takes as input a string text, a [`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object target, and an optional length maxWidth. It returns an array of glyph shapes, each positioned on a common coordinate space, a physical alignment whose value is one of *left*, *right*, and *center*, and an [inline box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box). (Most callers of this algorithm ignore the physical alignment and the [inline box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box).)
1. If maxWidth was provided but is less than or equal to zero or equal to NaN, then return an empty array.
2. Replace all [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) in text with U+0020 SPACE characters.
3. Let font be the current font of target, as given by that object's [`font`](#412515-text-styles) attribute.
4. Let language be the target's [language](#412515-text-styles).
5. If language is "[`inherit`](#412515-text-styles)":
   1. Let sourceObject be object's [font style source object](#412515-text-styles).
   2. If sourceObject is a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element, then set language to the sourceObject's [language](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes).
   3. Otherwise:
      1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): sourceObject is an [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object.
      2. Set language to the sourceObject's [inherited language](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface).
6. If language is the empty string, then set language to [explicitly unknown](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes).
7. Apply the appropriate step from the following list to determine the value of direction:

   If the target object's [`direction`](#412515-text-styles) attribute has the value "[`ltr`](#412515-text-styles)"

   Let direction be '[ltr](#3264-the-dir-attribute)'.

   If the target object's [`direction`](#412515-text-styles) attribute has the value "[`rtl`](#412515-text-styles)"

   Let direction be '[rtl](#3264-the-dir-attribute)'.

   If the target object's [`direction`](#412515-text-styles) attribute has the value "[`inherit`](#412515-text-styles)"
   1. Let sourceObject be object's [font style source object](#412515-text-styles).
   2. If sourceObject is a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element, then let direction be sourceObject's [directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute).
   3. Otherwise:
      1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): sourceObject is an [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object.
      2. Let direction be sourceObject's [inherited direction](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface).

8. Form a hypothetical infinitely-wide CSS [line box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#line-box) containing a single [inline box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box) containing the text text, with the CSS [content language](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text-4/#content-language) set to language, and with its CSS properties set as follows:

   | Property | Source |
   | --- | --- |
   | ['direction'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#direction) | direction |
   | ['font'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-prop) | font |
   | ['font-kerning'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#propdef-font-kerning) | target's [`fontKerning`](#412515-text-styles) |
   | ['font-stretch'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#propdef-font-stretch) | target's [`fontStretch`](#412515-text-styles) |
   | ['font-variant-caps'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#propdef-font-variant-caps) | target's [`fontVariantCaps`](#412515-text-styles) |
   | ['letter-spacing'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#letter-spacing-property) | target's [letter spacing](#412515-text-styles) |
   | [SVG text-rendering](https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/painting.html#TextRendering) | target's [`textRendering`](#412515-text-styles) |
   | ['white-space'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#white-space-property) | 'pre' |
   | ['word-spacing'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#propdef-word-spacing) | target's [word spacing](#412515-text-styles) |

   and with all other properties set to their initial values.

9. If maxWidth was provided and the hypothetical width of the [inline box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box) in the hypothetical [line box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#line-box) is greater than maxWidth [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px), then change font to have a more condensed font (if one is available or if a reasonably readable one can be synthesized by applying a horizontal scale factor to the font) or a smaller font, and return to the previous step.
10. The anchor point is a point on the [inline box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box), and the physical alignment is one of the values *left*, *right*, and *center*. These variables are determined by the [`textAlign`](#412515-text-styles) and [`textBaseline`](#412515-text-styles) values as follows:

    Horizontal position:

    If [`textAlign`](#412515-text-styles) is [`left`](#412515-text-styles)

    If [`textAlign`](#412515-text-styles) is [`start`](#412515-text-styles) and direction is 'ltr'

    If [`textAlign`](#412515-text-styles) is [`end`](#412515-text-styles) and direction is 'rtl'

    Set the anchor point's horizontal position to the left edge of the [inline box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box), and let physical alignment be *left*.

    If [`textAlign`](#412515-text-styles) is [`right`](#412515-text-styles)

    If [`textAlign`](#412515-text-styles) is [`end`](#412515-text-styles) and direction is 'ltr'

    If [`textAlign`](#412515-text-styles) is [`start`](#412515-text-styles) and direction is 'rtl'

    Set the anchor point's horizontal position to the right edge of the [inline box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box), and let physical alignment be *right*.

    If [`textAlign`](#412515-text-styles) is [`center`](#412515-text-styles)

    Set the anchor point's horizontal position to half way between the left and right edges of the [inline box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box), and let physical alignment be *center*.

    Vertical position:

    If [`textBaseline`](#412515-text-styles) is [`top`](#412515-text-styles)

    Set the anchor point's vertical position to the top of the em box of the [first available font](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#first-available-font) of the [inline box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box).

    If [`textBaseline`](#412515-text-styles) is [`hanging`](#412515-text-styles)

    Set the anchor point's vertical position to the [hanging baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#hanging-baseline) of the [first available font](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#first-available-font) of the [inline box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box).

    If [`textBaseline`](#412515-text-styles) is [`middle`](#412515-text-styles)

    Set the anchor point's vertical position to half way between the bottom and the top of the em box of the [first available font](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#first-available-font) of the [inline box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box).

    If [`textBaseline`](#412515-text-styles) is [`alphabetic`](#412515-text-styles)

    Set the anchor point's vertical position to the [alphabetic baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#alphabetic-baseline) of the [first available font](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#first-available-font) of the [inline box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box).

    If [`textBaseline`](#412515-text-styles) is [`ideographic`](#412515-text-styles)

    Set the anchor point's vertical position to the [ideographic-under baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#ideographic-under-baseline) of the [first available font](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#first-available-font) of the [inline box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box).

    If [`textBaseline`](#412515-text-styles) is [`bottom`](#412515-text-styles)

    Set the anchor point's vertical position to the bottom of the em box of the [first available font](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#first-available-font) of the [inline box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box).

11. Let result be an array constructed by iterating over each glyph in the [inline box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box) from left to right (if any), adding to the array, for each glyph, the shape of the glyph as it is in the [inline box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box), positioned on a coordinate space using [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) with its origin at the anchor point.
12. Return result, physical alignment, and the inline box.

###### 4.12.5.1.6 Building paths

Objects that implement the [`CanvasPath`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface have a [path](#412516-building-paths). A path has a list of zero or more subpaths. Each subpath consists of a list of one or more points, connected by straight or curved line segments, and a flag indicating whether the subpath is closed or not. A closed subpath is one where the last point of the subpath is connected to the first point of the subpath by a straight line. Subpaths with only one point are ignored when painting the path.

[Paths](#412516-building-paths) have a need new subpath flag. When this flag is set, certain APIs create a new subpath rather than extending the previous one. When a [path](#412516-building-paths) is created, its [need new subpath](#412516-building-paths) flag must be set.

When an object implementing the [`CanvasPath`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface is created, its [path](#412516-building-paths) must be initialized to zero subpaths.

`context.moveTo(x, y)`

`path.moveTo(x, y)`

Creates a new subpath with the given point.

`context.closePath()`

`path.closePath()`

Marks the current subpath as closed, and starts a new subpath with a point the same as the start and end of the newly closed subpath.

`context.lineTo(x, y)`

`path.lineTo(x, y)`

Adds the given point to the current subpath, connected to the previous one by a straight line.

`context.quadraticCurveTo(cpx, cpy, x, y)`

`path.quadraticCurveTo(cpx, cpy, x, y)`

Adds the given point to the current subpath, connected to the previous one by a quadratic Bézier curve with the given control point.

`context.bezierCurveTo(cp1x, cp1y, cp2x, cp2y, x, y)`

`path.bezierCurveTo(cp1x, cp1y, cp2x, cp2y, x, y)`

Adds the given point to the current subpath, connected to the previous one by a cubic Bézier curve with the given control points.

`context.arcTo(x1, y1, x2, y2, radius)`

`path.arcTo(x1, y1, x2, y2, radius)`

Adds an arc with the given control points and radius to the current subpath, connected to the previous point by a straight line.

Throws an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the given radius is negative.

![](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/arcTo1.png) ![](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/arcTo2.png) ![](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/arcTo3.png)

`context.arc(x, y, radius, startAngle, endAngle [, counterclockwise ])`

`path.arc(x, y, radius, startAngle, endAngle [, counterclockwise ])`

Adds points to the subpath such that the arc described by the circumference of the circle described by the arguments, starting at the given start angle and ending at the given end angle, going in the given direction (defaulting to clockwise), is added to the path, connected to the previous point by a straight line.

Throws an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the given radius is negative.

![](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/arc1.png)

`context.ellipse(x, y, radiusX, radiusY, rotation, startAngle, endAngle [, counterclockwise])`

`path.ellipse(x, y, radiusX, radiusY, rotation, startAngle, endAngle [, counterclockwise])`

Adds points to the subpath such that the arc described by the circumference of the ellipse described by the arguments, starting at the given start angle and ending at the given end angle, going in the given direction (defaulting to clockwise), is added to the path, connected to the previous point by a straight line.

Throws an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the given radius is negative.

`context.rect(x, y, w, h)`

`path.rect(x, y, w, h)`

Adds a new closed subpath to the path, representing the given rectangle.

`context.roundRect(x, y, w, h, radii)`

`path.roundRect(x, y, w, h, radii)`

Adds a new closed subpath to the path representing the given rounded rectangle. radii is either a list of radii or a single radius representing the corners of the rectangle in pixels. If a list is provided, the number and order of these radii function in the same way as the CSS ['border-radius'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-radius) property. A single radius behaves the same way as a list with a single element.

If w and h are both greater than or equal to 0, or if both are smaller than 0, then the path is drawn clockwise. Otherwise, it is drawn counterclockwise.

When w is negative, the rounded rectangle is flipped horizontally, which means that the radius values that normally apply to the left corners are used on the right and vice versa. Similarly, when h is negative, the rounded rect is flipped vertically.

When a value r in radii is a number, the corresponding corner(s) are drawn as circular arcs of radius r.

When a value r in radii is an object with `{ x, y
    }` properties, the corresponding corner(s) are drawn as elliptical arcs whose x and y radii are equal to r.x and r.y, respectively.

When the sum of the radii of two corners of the same edge is greater than the length of the edge, all the radii of the rounded rectangle are scaled by a factor of length / (r1 + r2). If multiple edges have this property, the scale factor of the edge with the smallest scale factor is used. This is consistent with CSS behavior.

Throws a [`RangeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-rangeerror) if radii is a list whose size is not one, two, three, or four.

Throws a [`RangeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-rangeerror) if a value in radii is a negative number, or is an `{ x, y }` object whose `x` or `y` properties are negative numbers.

The following methods allow authors to manipulate the [paths](#412516-building-paths) of objects implementing the [`CanvasPath`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface.

For objects implementing the [`CanvasDrawPath`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) and [`CanvasTransform`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interfaces, the points passed to the methods, and the resulting lines added to [current default path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) by these methods, must be transformed according to the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations) before being added to the path.

The `moveTo(x,
  y)` method, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. If either of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
2. Create a new subpath with the specified point as its first (and only) point.

When the user agent is to ensure there is a subpath for a coordinate (x, y) on a [path](#412516-building-paths), the user agent must check to see if the [path](#412516-building-paths) has its [need new subpath](#412516-building-paths) flag set. If it does, then the user agent must create a new subpath with the point (x, y) as its first (and only) point, as if the [`moveTo()`](#412516-building-paths) method had been called, and must then unset the [path](#412516-building-paths)'s [need new subpath](#412516-building-paths) flag.

The `closePath()` method, when invoked, must do nothing if the object's path has no subpaths. Otherwise, it must mark the last subpath as closed, create a new subpath whose first point is the same as the previous subpath's first point, and finally add this new subpath to the path.

> [!note]
> If the last subpath had more than one point in its list of points, then this is equivalent to adding a straight line connecting the last point back to the first point of the last subpath, thus "closing" the subpath.

---

New points and the lines connecting them are added to subpaths using the methods described below. In all cases, the methods only modify the last subpath in the object's path.

The `lineTo(x,
  y)` method, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. If either of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
2. If the object's path has no subpaths, then [ensure there is a subpath](#412516-building-paths) for (x, y).
3. Otherwise, connect the last point in the subpath to the given point (x, y) using a straight line, and then add the given point (x, y) to the subpath.

The `quadraticCurveTo(cpx, cpy,
  x, y)` method, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
2. [Ensure there is a subpath](#412516-building-paths) for (cpx, cpy).
3. Connect the last point in the subpath to the given point (x, y) using a quadratic Bézier curve with control point (cpx, cpy). [\[BEZIER\]](#references)
4. Add the given point (x, y) to the subpath.

The `bezierCurveTo(cp1x, cp1y,
  cp2x, cp2y, x, y)` method, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
2. [Ensure there is a subpath](#412516-building-paths) for (cp1x, cp1y).
3. Connect the last point in the subpath to the given point (x, y) using a cubic Bézier curve with control points (cp1x, cp1y) and (cp2x, cp2y). [\[BEZIER\]](#references)
4. Add the point (x, y) to the subpath.

---

The `arcTo(x1,
  y1, x2, y2, radius)` method, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
2. [Ensure there is a subpath](#412516-building-paths) for (x1, y1).
3. If radius is negative, then throw an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
4. Let the point (x0, y0) be the last point in the subpath, transformed by the inverse of the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations) (so that it is in the same coordinate system as the points passed to the method).
5. If the point (x0, y0) is equal to the point (x1, y1), or if the point (x1, y1) is equal to the point (x2, y2), or if radius is zero, then add the point (x1, y1) to the subpath, and connect that point to the previous point (x0, y0) by a straight line.
6. Otherwise, if the points (x0, y0), (x1, y1), and (x2, y2) all lie on a single straight line, then add the point (x1, y1) to the subpath, and connect that point to the previous point (x0, y0) by a straight line.
7. Otherwise, let The Arc be the shortest arc given by circumference of the circle that has radius radius, and that has one point tangent to the half-infinite line that crosses the point (x0, y0) and ends at the point (x1, y1), and that has a different point tangent to the half-infinite line that ends at the point (x1, y1) and crosses the point (x2, y2). The points at which this circle touches these two lines are called the start and end tangent points respectively. Connect the point (x0, y0) to the start tangent point by a straight line, adding the start tangent point to the subpath, and then connect the start tangent point to the end tangent point by The Arc, adding the end tangent point to the subpath.

---

The `arc(x,
  y, radius, startAngle, endAngle,
  counterclockwise)` method, when invoked, must run the [ellipse method steps](#412516-building-paths) with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), x, y, radius, radius, 0, startAngle, endAngle, and counterclockwise.

> [!note]
> This makes it equivalent to [`ellipse()`](#412516-building-paths) except that both radii are equal and rotation is 0.

The `ellipse(x,
  y, radiusX, radiusY, rotation, startAngle,
  endAngle, counterclockwise)` method, when invoked, must run the [ellipse method steps](#412516-building-paths) with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), x, y, radiusX, radiusY, rotation, startAngle, endAngle, and counterclockwise.

The determine the point on an ellipse steps, given ellipse, and angle, are:
1. Let eccentricCircle be the circle that shares its origin with ellipse, with a radius equal to the semi-major axis of ellipse.
2. Let outerPoint be the point on eccentricCircle's circumference at angle measured in radians clockwise from ellipse's semi-major axis.
3. Let chord be the line perpendicular to ellipse's major axis between this axis and outerPoint.
4. Return the point on chord that crosses ellipse's circumference.

The ellipse method steps, given canvasPath, x, y, radiusX, radiusY, rotation, startAngle, endAngle, and counterclockwise, are:
1. If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
2. If either radiusX or radiusY are negative, then throw an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
3. If canvasPath's path has any subpaths, then add a straight line from the last point in the subpath to the start point of the arc.
4. Add the start and end points of the arc to the subpath, and connect them with an arc. The arc and its start and end points are defined as follows:

   Consider an ellipse that has its origin at (x, y), that has a major-axis radius radiusX and a minor-axis radius radiusY, and that is rotated about its origin such that its semi-major axis is inclined rotation radians clockwise from the x-axis.

   If counterclockwise is false and endAngle − startAngle is greater than or equal to 2π, or, if counterclockwise is *true* and startAngle − endAngle is greater than or equal to 2π, then the arc is the whole circumference of this ellipse, and both the start point and the end point are the result of running the [determine the point on an ellipse steps](#412516-building-paths) given this ellipse and startAngle.

   Otherwise, the start point is the result of running the [determine the point on an ellipse steps](#412516-building-paths) given this ellipse and startAngle, the end point is the result of running the [determine the point on an ellipse steps](#412516-building-paths) given this ellipse and endAngle, and the arc is the path along the circumference of this ellipse from the start point to the end point, going counterclockwise if counterclockwise is true, and clockwise otherwise. Since the points are on the ellipse, as opposed to being simply angles from zero, the arc can never cover an angle greater than 2π radians.

   > [!note]
   > Even if the arc covers the entire circumference of the ellipse and there are no other points in the subpath, the path is not closed unless the [`closePath()`](#412516-building-paths) method is appropriately invoked.

---

The `rect(x,
  y, w, h)` method, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
2. Create a new subpath containing just the four points (x, y), (x+w, y), (x+w, y+h), (x, y+h), in that order, with those four points connected by straight lines.
3. Mark the subpath as closed.
4. Create a new subpath with the point (x, y) as the only point in the subpath.

The `roundRect(x, y, w,
  h, radii)` method steps are:
1. If any of x, y, w, or h are infinite or NaN, then return.
2. If radii is an [`unrestricted
      double`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-unrestricted-double) or [`DOMPointInit`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dictdef-dompointinit), then set radii to « radii ».
3. If radii is not a list of size one, two, three, or four, then throw a [`RangeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-rangeerror).
4. Let normalizedRadii be an empty list.
5. For each radius of radii:
   1. If radius is a [`DOMPointInit`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dictdef-dompointinit):
      1. If radius\["[`x`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x)"\] or radius\["[`y`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-y)"\] is infinite or NaN, then return.
      2. If radius\["[`x`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x)"\] or radius\["[`y`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-y)"\] is negative, then throw a [`RangeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-rangeerror).
      3. Otherwise, append radius to normalizedRadii.
   2. If radius is a [`unrestricted
            double`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-unrestricted-double):
      1. If radius is infinite or NaN, then return.
      2. If radius is negative, then throw a [`RangeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-rangeerror).
      3. Otherwise, append «\[ "[`x`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x)" → radius, "[`y`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x)" → radius \]» to normalizedRadii.
6. Let upperLeft, upperRight, lowerRight, and lowerLeft be null.
7. If normalizedRadii's size is 4, then set upperLeft to normalizedRadii\[0\], set upperRight to normalizedRadii\[1\], set lowerRight to normalizedRadii\[2\], and set lowerLeft to normalizedRadii\[3\].
8. If normalizedRadii's size is 3, then set upperLeft to normalizedRadii\[0\], set upperRight and lowerLeft to normalizedRadii\[1\], and set lowerRight to normalizedRadii\[2\].
9. If normalizedRadii's size is 2, then set upperLeft and lowerRight to normalizedRadii\[0\] and set upperRight and lowerLeft to normalizedRadii\[1\].
10. If normalizedRadii's size is 1, then set upperLeft, upperRight, lowerRight, and lowerLeft to normalizedRadii\[0\].
11. Corner curves must not overlap. Scale all radii to prevent this:
    1. Let top be upperLeft\["[`x`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x)"\] + upperRight\["[`x`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x)"\].
    2. Let right be upperRight\["[`y`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-y)"\] + lowerRight\["[`y`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-y)"\].
    3. Let bottom be lowerRight\["[`x`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x)"\] + lowerLeft\["[`x`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x)"\].
    4. Let left be upperLeft\["[`y`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-y)"\] + lowerLeft\["[`y`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-y)"\].
    5. Let scale be the minimum value of the ratios w / top, h / right, w / bottom, h / left.
    6. If scale is less than 1, then set the [`x`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x) and [`y`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-y) members of upperLeft, upperRight, lowerLeft, and lowerRight to their current values multiplied by scale.
12. Create a new subpath:
    1. Move to the point (x + upperLeft\["[`x`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x)"\], y).
    2. Draw a straight line to the point (x + w − upperRight\["[`x`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x)"\], y).
    3. Draw an arc to the point (x + w, y + upperRight\["[`y`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-y)"\]).
    4. Draw a straight line to the point (x + w, y + h − lowerRight\["[`y`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-y)"\]).
    5. Draw an arc to the point (x + w − lowerRight\["[`x`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x)"\], y + h).
    6. Draw a straight line to the point (x + lowerLeft\["[`x`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x)"\], y + h).
    7. Draw an arc to the point (x, y + h − lowerLeft\["[`y`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-y)"\]).
    8. Draw a straight line to the point (x, y + upperLeft\["[`y`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-y)"\]).
    9. Draw an arc to the point (x + upperLeft\["[`x`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dom-dompointinit-x)"\], y).
13. Mark the subpath as closed.
14. Create a new subpath with the point (x, y) as the only point in the subpath.

> [!note]
> This is designed to behave similarly to the CSS ['border-radius'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-radius) property.

###### 4.12.5.1.7 [`Path2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) objects

[`Path2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) objects can be used to declare paths that are then later used on objects implementing the [`CanvasDrawPath`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface. In addition to many of the APIs described in earlier sections, [`Path2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) objects have methods to combine paths, and to add text to paths.

`path = new Path2D()`

Creates a new empty [`Path2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object.

`path = new Path2D(path)`

When path is a [`Path2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object, returns a copy.

When path is a string, creates the path described by the argument, interpreted as SVG path data. [\[SVG\]](#references)

`path.addPath(path [, transform ])`

Adds to the path the path given by the argument.

The `Path2D(path)` constructor, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. Let output be a new [`Path2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object.
2. If path is not given, then return output.
3. If path is a [`Path2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object, then add all subpaths of path to output and return output. (In other words, it returns a copy of the argument.)
4. Let svgPath be the result of parsing and interpreting path according to SVG 2's rules for path data. [\[SVG\]](#references)

   > [!note]
   > The resulting path could be empty. SVG defines error handling rules for parsing and applying path data.

5. Let (x, y) be the last point in svgPath.
6. Add all the subpaths, if any, from svgPath to output.
7. Create a new subpath in output with (x, y) as the only point in the subpath.
8. Return output.

---

The `addPath(path,
  transform)` method, when invoked on a [`Path2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object a, must run these steps:
1. If the [`Path2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object path has no subpaths, then return.
2. Let matrix be the result of [creating a `DOMMatrix` from the 2D dictionary](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#create-a-dommatrix-from-the-2d-dictionary) transform.
3. If one or more of matrix's [m11 element](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m11-element), [m12 element](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m12-element), [m21 element](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m21-element), [m22 element](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m22-element), [m41 element](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m41-element), or [m42 element](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m42-element) are infinite or NaN, then return.
4. Create a copy of all the subpaths in path. Let c be this copy.
5. Transform all the coordinates and lines in c by the transform matrix matrix.
6. Let (x, y) be the last point in the last subpath of c.
7. Add all the subpaths in c to a.
8. Create a new subpath in a with (x, y) as the only point in the subpath.

###### 4.12.5.1.8 Transformations

Objects that implement the [`CanvasTransform`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface have a current transformation matrix, as well as methods (described in this section) to manipulate it. When an object implementing the [`CanvasTransform`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface is created, its transformation matrix must be initialized to the identity matrix.

The [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations) is applied to coordinates when creating the [current default path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas), and when painting text, shapes, and [`Path2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) objects, on objects implementing the [`CanvasTransform`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface.

The transformations must be performed in reverse order.

> [!note]
> For instance, if a scale transformation that doubles the width is applied to the canvas, followed by a rotation transformation that rotates drawing operations by a quarter turn, and a rectangle twice as wide as it is tall is then drawn on the canvas, the actual result will be a square.

`context.scale(x, y)`

Changes the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations) to apply a scaling transformation with the given characteristics.

`context.rotate(angle)`

Changes the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations) to apply a rotation transformation with the given characteristics. The angle is in radians.

`context.translate(x, y)`

Changes the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations) to apply a translation transformation with the given characteristics.

`context.transform(a, b, c, d, e, f)`

Changes the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations) to apply the matrix given by the arguments as described below.

`matrix = context.getTransform()`

Returns a copy of the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations), as a newly created [`DOMMatrix`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dommatrix) object.

`context.setTransform(a, b, c, d, e, f)`

Changes the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations) *to* the matrix given by the arguments as described below.

`context.setTransform(transform)`

Changes the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations) *to* the matrix represented by the passed [`DOMMatrix2DInit`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dictdef-dommatrix2dinit) dictionary.

`context.resetTransform()`

Changes the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations) to the identity matrix.

The `scale(x,
  y)` method, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. If either of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
2. Add the scaling transformation described by the arguments to the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations). The x argument represents the scale factor in the horizontal direction and the y argument represents the scale factor in the vertical direction. The factors are multiples.

The `rotate(angle)` method, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. If angle is infinite or NaN, then return.
2. Add the rotation transformation described by the argument to the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations). The angle argument represents a clockwise rotation angle expressed in radians.

The `translate(x, y)` method, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. If either of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
2. Add the translation transformation described by the arguments to the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations). The x argument represents the translation distance in the horizontal direction and the y argument represents the translation distance in the vertical direction. The arguments are in coordinate space units.

The `transform(a, b, c,
  d, e, f)` method, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
2. Replace the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations) with the result of [multiplying](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-multiply) the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations) with the matrix described by:

   | a | c | e |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | b | d | f |
   | 0 | 0 | 1 |

> [!note]
> The arguments a, b, c, d, e, and f are sometimes called m11, m12, m21, m22, dx, and dy or m11, m21, m12, m22, dx, and dy. Care ought to be taken in particular with the order of the second and third arguments (b and c) as their order varies from API to API and APIs sometimes use the notation m12/m21 and sometimes m21/m12 for those positions.

The `getTransform()` method, when invoked, must return a newly created [`DOMMatrix`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dommatrix) representing a copy of the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations) matrix of the context.

> [!note]
> This returned object is not live, so updating it will not affect the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations), and updating the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations) will not affect an already returned [`DOMMatrix`](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#dommatrix).

The `setTransform(a, b, c,
  d, e, f)` method, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
2. Reset the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations) to the matrix described by:

   | a | c | e |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | b | d | f |
   | 0 | 0 | 1 |

The `setTransform(transform)` method, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. Let matrix be the result of [creating a `DOMMatrix` from the 2D dictionary](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#create-a-dommatrix-from-the-2d-dictionary) transform.
2. If one or more of matrix's [m11 element](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m11-element), [m12 element](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m12-element), [m21 element](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m21-element), [m22 element](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m22-element), [m41 element](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m41-element), or [m42 element](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m42-element) are infinite or NaN, then return.
3. Reset the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations) to matrix.

The `resetTransform()` method, when invoked, must reset the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations) to the identity matrix.

> [!note]
> Given a matrix of the form created by the [`transform()`](#412518-transformations) and [`setTransform()`](#412518-transformations) methods, i.e.,
> 
> | a | c | e |
> | --- | --- | --- |
> | b | d | f |
> | 0 | 0 | 1 |
> 
> the resulting transformed coordinates after transform matrix multiplication will be
> 
> xnew = a x + c y + e  
> ynew = b x + d y + f

###### 4.12.5.1.9 Image sources for 2D rendering contexts

Some methods on the [`CanvasDrawImage`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) and [`CanvasFillStrokeStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interfaces take the union type [`CanvasImageSource`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) as an argument.

This union type allows objects implementing any of the following interfaces to be used as image sources:
- [`HTMLOrSVGImageElement`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) ([`img`](#483-the-img-element) or [SVG `image`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/embedded.html#elementdef-image) elements)
- [`HTMLVideoElement`](#488-the-video-element) ([`video`](#488-the-video-element) elements)
- [`HTMLCanvasElement`](#4125-the-canvas-element) ([`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) elements)
- [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface)
- [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface)
- [`VideoFrame`](https://w3c.github.io/webcodecs/#videoframe-interface)

> [!note]
> Although not formally specified as such, [SVG `image`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/embedded.html#elementdef-image) elements are expected to be implemented nearly identical to [`img`](#483-the-img-element) elements. That is, [SVG `image`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/embedded.html#elementdef-image) elements share the fundamental concepts and features of [`img`](#483-the-img-element) elements.

> [!note]
> The [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) interface can be created from a number of other image-representing types, including [`ImageData`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface).

To check the usability of the image argument, where image is a [`CanvasImageSource`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object, run these steps:
1. Switch on image:

   [`HTMLOrSVGImageElement`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context)

   If image's [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [state](#4843-processing-model) is [broken](#4843-processing-model), then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

   If image is not [fully decodable](#4843-processing-model), then return *bad*.

   If image has a [natural width](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-width) or [natural height](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-height) (or both) equal to zero, then return *bad*.

   [`HTMLVideoElement`](#488-the-video-element)

   If image's [`readyState`](#48117-ready-states) attribute is either [`HAVE_NOTHING`](#48117-ready-states) or [`HAVE_METADATA`](#48117-ready-states), then return *bad*.

   [`HTMLCanvasElement`](#4125-the-canvas-element)

   [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface)

   If image has either a horizontal dimension or a vertical dimension equal to zero, then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

   [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface)

   [`VideoFrame`](https://w3c.github.io/webcodecs/#videoframe-interface)

   If image's [\[\[Detached\]\]](#272-transferable-objects) internal slot value is set to true, then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

2. Return *good*.

When a [`CanvasImageSource`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object represents an [`HTMLOrSVGImageElement`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context), the element's image must be used as the source image.

Specifically, when a [`CanvasImageSource`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object represents an animated image in an [`HTMLOrSVGImageElement`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context), the user agent must use the default image of the animation (the one that the format defines is to be used when animation is not supported or is disabled), or, if there is no such image, the first frame of the animation, when rendering the image for [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) APIs.

When a [`CanvasImageSource`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object represents an [`HTMLVideoElement`](#488-the-video-element), then the frame at the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource) when the method with the argument is invoked must be used as the source image when rendering the image for [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) APIs, and the source image's dimensions must be the [natural width](#488-the-video-element) and [natural height](#488-the-video-element) of the [media resource](#4811-media-elements) (i.e., after any aspect-ratio correction has been applied).

When a [`CanvasImageSource`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object represents an [`HTMLCanvasElement`](#4125-the-canvas-element), the element's bitmap must be used as the source image.

When a [`CanvasImageSource`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object represents an element that is [being rendered](#151-introduction) and that element has been resized, the original image data of the source image must be used, not the image as it is rendered (e.g. [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes) and [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes) attributes on the source element have no effect on how the object is interpreted when rendering the image for [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) APIs).

When a [`CanvasImageSource`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object represents an [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface), the object's bitmap image data must be used as the source image.

When a [`CanvasImageSource`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object represents an [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface), the object's bitmap must be used as the source image.

When a [`CanvasImageSource`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object represents a [`VideoFrame`](https://w3c.github.io/webcodecs/#videoframe-interface), the object's pixel data must be used as the source image, and the source image's dimensions must be the object's [\[\[display width\]\]](https://w3c.github.io/webcodecs/#dom-videoframe-display-width-slot) and [\[\[display height\]\]](https://w3c.github.io/webcodecs/#dom-videoframe-display-height-slot).

An object image is not origin-clean if, switching on image's type:

[`HTMLOrSVGImageElement`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context)

image's [current request](#4843-processing-model)'s [image data](#4843-processing-model) is [CORS-cross-origin](#251-terminology).

[`HTMLVideoElement`](#488-the-video-element)

image's [media data](#4811-media-elements) is [CORS-cross-origin](#251-terminology).

[`HTMLCanvasElement`](#4125-the-canvas-element)

[`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface)

[`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface)

image's bitmap's [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag is false.

###### 4.12.5.1.10 Fill and stroke styles

`context.fillStyle [ = value ]`

Returns the current style used for filling shapes.

Can be set, to change the [fill style](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles).

The style can be either a string containing a CSS color, or a [`CanvasGradient`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) or [`CanvasPattern`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object. Invalid values are ignored.

`context.strokeStyle [ = value ]`

Returns the current style used for stroking shapes.

Can be set, to change the [stroke style.](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles)

The style can be either a string containing a CSS color, or a [`CanvasGradient`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) or [`CanvasPattern`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object. Invalid values are ignored.

Objects that implement the [`CanvasFillStrokeStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface have attributes and methods (defined in this section) that control how shapes are treated by the object.

Such objects have associated fill style and stroke style values, which are either CSS colors, [`CanvasPattern`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context)s, or [`CanvasGradient`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context)s. Initially, both must be the result of [parsing](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#parse-a-css-color-value) the string "`#000000`".

When the value is a CSS color, it must not be affected by the transformation matrix when used to draw on bitmaps.

> [!note]
> When set to a [`CanvasPattern`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) or [`CanvasGradient`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object, changes made to the object after the assignment do affect subsequent stroking or filling of shapes.

The `fillStyle` getter steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [fill style](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles) is a CSS color, then return the [serialization](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#serializing-color-values) of that color with [HTML-compatible serialization requested](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#color-serialization-html-compatible-serialization-is-requested).
2. Return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [fill style](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles).

The [`fillStyle`](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles) setter steps are:
1. If the given value is a string:
   1. Let context be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`canvas`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) attribute's value, if that is an element; otherwise null.
   2. Let parsedValue be the result of [parsing](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#parse-a-css-color-value) the given value with context if non-null.
   3. If parsedValue is failure, then return.
   4. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [fill style](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles) to parsedValue.
   5. Return.
2. If the given value is a [`CanvasPattern`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object that is marked as [not origin-clean](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles), then set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag to false.
3. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [fill style](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles) to the given value.

The `strokeStyle` getter steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [stroke style](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles) is a CSS color, then return the [serialization](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#serializing-color-values) of that color with [HTML-compatible serialization requested](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#color-serialization-html-compatible-serialization-is-requested).
2. Return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [stroke style](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles).

The [`strokeStyle`](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles) setter steps are:
1. If the given value is a string:
   1. Let context be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`canvas`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) attribute's value, if that is an element; otherwise null.
   2. Let parsedValue be the result of [parsing](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#parse-a-css-color-value) the given value with context if non-null.
   3. If parsedValue is failure, then return.
   4. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [stroke style](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles) to parsedValue.
   5. Return.
2. If the given value is a [`CanvasPattern`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object that is marked as [not origin-clean](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles), then set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag to false.
3. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [stroke style](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles) to the given value.

---
