There are three types of gradients, linear gradients, radial gradients, and conic gradients, represented by objects implementing the opaque [`CanvasGradient`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface.

Once a gradient has been created (see below), stops are placed along it to define how the colors are distributed along the gradient. The color of the gradient at each stop is the color specified for that stop, [converted](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#color-conversion) to the context's [color space](#412512-the-canvas-settings). Between each such stop, the colors and the alpha component must be linearly interpolated in the context's [color space](#412512-the-canvas-settings) without premultiplying the alpha value to find the color to use at that offset. Before the first stop, the color must be the color of the first stop. After the last stop, the color must be the color of the last stop. When there are no stops, the gradient is [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black).

`gradient.addColorStop(offset, color)`

Adds a color stop with the given color to the gradient at the given offset. 0.0 is the offset at one end of the gradient, 1.0 is the offset at the other end.

Throws an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the offset is out of range. Throws a ["`SyntaxError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the color cannot be parsed.

`gradient = context.createLinearGradient(x0, y0, x1, y1)`

Returns a [`CanvasGradient`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object that represents a linear gradient that paints along the line given by the coordinates represented by the arguments.

`gradient = context.createRadialGradient(x0, y0, r0, x1, y1, r1)`

Returns a [`CanvasGradient`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object that represents a radial gradient that paints along the cone given by the circles represented by the arguments.

If either of the radii are negative, throws an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

`gradient = context.createConicGradient(startAngle, x, y)`

Returns a [`CanvasGradient`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object that represents a conic gradient that paints clockwise along the rotation around the center represented by the arguments.

The `addColorStop(offset,
  color)` method on the [`CanvasGradient`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context), when invoked, must run these steps:
1. If the offset is less than 0 or greater than 1, then throw an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Let parsed color be the result of [parsing](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#parse-a-css-color-value) color.

   > [!note]
   > No element is passed to the parser because [`CanvasGradient`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) objects are [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element)-neutral — a [`CanvasGradient`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object created by one [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) can be used by another, and there is therefore no way to know which is the "element in question" at the time that the color is specified.

3. If parsed color is failure, throw a ["`SyntaxError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
4. Place a new stop on the gradient, at offset offset relative to the whole gradient, and with the color parsed color.

   If multiple stops are added at the same offset on a gradient, then they must be placed in the order added, with the first one closest to the start of the gradient, and each subsequent one infinitesimally further along towards the end point (in effect causing all but the first and last stop added at each point to be ignored).

The `createLinearGradient(x0, y0,
  x1, y1)` method takes four arguments that represent the start point (x0, y0) and end point (x1, y1) of the gradient. The method, when invoked, must return a linear [`CanvasGradient`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) initialized with the specified line.

Linear gradients must be rendered such that all points on a line perpendicular to the line that crosses the start and end points have the color at the point where those two lines cross (with the colors coming from the [interpolation and extrapolation](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles) described above). The points in the linear gradient must be transformed as described by the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations) when rendering.

If x0 = x1 and y0 = y1, then the linear gradient must paint nothing.

The `createRadialGradient(x0, y0,
  r0, x1, y1, r1)` method takes six arguments, the first three representing the start circle with origin (x0, y0) and radius r0, and the last three representing the end circle with origin (x1, y1) and radius r1. The values are in coordinate space units. If either of r0 or r1 are negative, then an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) must be thrown. Otherwise, the method, when invoked, must return a radial [`CanvasGradient`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) initialized with the two specified circles.

Radial gradients must be rendered by following these steps:
1. If x0 = x1 and y0 = y1 and r0 = r1, then the radial gradient must paint nothing. Return.
2. Let x(ω) = (x1-x0)ω + x0.

   Let y(ω) = (y1-y0)ω + y0.

   Let r(ω) = (r1-r0)ω + r0.

   Let the color at ω be the color at that position on the gradient (with the colors coming from the [interpolation and extrapolation](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles) described above).

3. For all values of ω where r(ω) > 0, starting with the value of ω nearest to positive infinity and ending with the value of ω nearest to negative infinity, draw the circumference of the circle with radius r(ω) at position (x(ω), y(ω)), with the color at ω, but only painting on the parts of the bitmap that have not yet been painted on by earlier circles in this step for this rendering of the gradient.

> [!note]
> This effectively creates a cone, touched by the two circles defined in the creation of the gradient, with the part of the cone before the start circle (0.0) using the color of the first offset, the part of the cone after the end circle (1.0) using the color of the last offset, and areas outside the cone untouched by the gradient ([transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black)).

The resulting radial gradient must then be transformed as described by the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations) when rendering.

The `createConicGradient(startAngle,
  x, y)` method takes three arguments, the first argument, startAngle, represents the angle in radians at which the gradient begins, and the last two arguments, (x, y), represent the center of the gradient in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px). The method, when invoked, must return a conic [`CanvasGradient`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) initialized with the specified center and angle.

It follows the same rendering rule as CSS ['conic-gradient'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images-4/#funcdef-conic-gradient) and it is equivalent to CSS 'conic-gradient(from adjustedStartAnglerad at xpx ypx, angularColorStopList)'. Here:
- adjustedStartAngle is given by startAngle + π/2;
- angularColorStopList is given by the color stops that have been added to the [`CanvasGradient`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) using [`addColorStop()`](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles), with the color stop offsets interpreted as percentages.

Gradients must be painted only where the relevant stroking or filling effects requires that they be drawn.

---

Patterns are represented by objects implementing the opaque [`CanvasPattern`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface.

`pattern = context.createPattern(image, repetition)`

Returns a [`CanvasPattern`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object that uses the given image and repeats in the direction(s) given by the repetition argument.

The allowed values for repetition are `repeat` (both directions), `repeat-x` (horizontal only), `repeat-y` (vertical only), and `no-repeat` (neither). If the repetition argument is empty, the value `repeat` is used.

If the image isn't yet fully decoded, then nothing is drawn. If the image is a canvas with no data, throws an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

`pattern.setTransform(transform)`

Sets the transformation matrix that will be used when rendering the pattern during a fill or stroke painting operation.

The `createPattern(image,
  repetition)` method, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. Let usability be the result of [checking the usability of](#412519-image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts) image.
2. If usability is *bad*, then return null.
3. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): usability is *good*.
4. If repetition is the empty string, then set it to "`repeat`".
5. If repetition is not [identical to](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) one of "`repeat`", "`repeat-x`", "`repeat-y`", or "`no-repeat`", then throw a ["`SyntaxError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
6. Let pattern be a new [`CanvasPattern`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object with the image image and the repetition behavior given by repetition.
7. If image [is not origin-clean](#412519-image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts), then mark pattern as not origin-clean.
8. Return pattern.

Modifying the image used when creating a [`CanvasPattern`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object after calling the [`createPattern()`](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles) method must not affect the pattern(s) rendered by the [`CanvasPattern`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object.

Patterns have a transformation matrix, which controls how the pattern is used when it is painted. Initially, a pattern's transformation matrix must be the identity matrix.

The `setTransform(transform)` method, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. Let matrix be the result of [creating a `DOMMatrix` from the 2D dictionary](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#create-a-dommatrix-from-the-2d-dictionary) transform.
2. If one or more of matrix's [m11 element](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m11-element), [m12 element](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m12-element), [m21 element](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m21-element), [m22 element](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m22-element), [m41 element](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m41-element), or [m42 element](https://drafts.csswg.org/geometry/#matrix-m42-element) are infinite or NaN, then return.
3. Reset the pattern's transformation matrix to matrix.

When a pattern is to be rendered within an area, the user agent must run the following steps to determine what is rendered:
1. Create an infinite [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black) bitmap.
2. Place a copy of the image on the bitmap, anchored such that its top left corner is at the origin of the coordinate space, with one coordinate space unit per [CSS pixel](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) of the image, then place repeated copies of this image horizontally to the left and right, if the repetition behavior is "`repeat-x`", or vertically up and down, if the repetition behavior is "`repeat-y`", or in all four directions all over the bitmap, if the repetition behavior is "`repeat`".

   If the original image data is a bitmap image, then the value painted at a point in the area of the repetitions is computed by filtering the original image data. When scaling up, if the [`imageSmoothingEnabled`](#4125118-image-smoothing) attribute is set to false, then the image must be rendered using nearest-neighbor interpolation. Otherwise, the user agent may use any filtering algorithm (for example bilinear interpolation or nearest-neighbor). User agents which support multiple filtering algorithms may use the value of the [`imageSmoothingQuality`](#4125118-image-smoothing) attribute to guide the choice of filtering algorithm. When such a filtering algorithm requires a pixel value from outside the original image data, it must instead use the value from wrapping the pixel's coordinates to the original image's dimensions. (That is, the filter uses 'repeat' behavior, regardless of the value of the pattern's repetition behavior.)

3. Transform the resulting bitmap according to the pattern's transformation matrix.
4. Transform the resulting bitmap again, this time according to the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations).
5. Replace any part of the image outside the area in which the pattern is to be rendered with [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black).
6. The resulting bitmap is what is to be rendered, with the same origin and same scale.

---

If a radial gradient or repeated pattern is used when the transformation matrix is singular, then the resulting style must be [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black) (otherwise the gradient or pattern would be collapsed to a point or line, leaving the other pixels undefined). Linear gradients and solid colors always define all points even with singular transformation matrices.

###### 4.12.5.1.11 Drawing rectangles to the bitmap

Objects that implement the [`CanvasRect`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface provide the following methods for immediately drawing rectangles to the bitmap. The methods each take four arguments; the first two give the x and y coordinates of the top left of the rectangle, and the second two give the width w and height h of the rectangle, respectively.

The [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations) must be applied to the following four coordinates, which form the path that must then be closed to get the specified rectangle: (x, y), (x+w, y), (x+w, y+h), (x, y+h).

Shapes are painted without affecting the [current default path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas), and are subject to the [clipping region](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas), and, with the exception of [`clearRect()`](#4125111-drawing-rectangles-to-the-bitmap), also [shadow effects](#4125119-shadows), [global alpha](#4125117-compositing), and the [current compositing and blending operator](#4125117-compositing).

`context.clearRect(x, y, w, h)`

Clears all pixels on the bitmap in the given rectangle to [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black).

`context.fillRect(x, y, w, h)`

Paints the given rectangle onto the bitmap, using the current fill style.

`context.strokeRect(x, y, w, h)`

Paints the box that outlines the given rectangle onto the bitmap, using the current stroke style.

The `clearRect(x, y, w,
  h)` method, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
2. Let pixels be the set of pixels in the specified rectangle that also intersect the current [clipping region](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas).
3. Clear the pixels in pixels to a [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black), erasing any previous image.

> [!note]
> If either height or width are zero, this method has no effect, since the set of pixels would be empty.

The `fillRect(x,
  y, w, h)` method, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
2. If either w or h are zero, then return.
3. Paint the specified rectangular area using [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [fill style](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles).

The `strokeRect(x, y, w,
  h)` method, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
2. Take the result of [tracing the path](#412514-line-styles) described below, using the [`CanvasPathDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface's line styles, and fill it with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [stroke style](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles).

If both w and h are zero, the path has a single subpath with just one point (x, y), and no lines, and this method thus has no effect (the [trace a path](#412514-line-styles) algorithm returns an empty path in that case).

If just one of either w or h is zero, then the path has a single subpath consisting of two points, with coordinates (x, y) and (x+w, y+h), in that order, connected by a single straight line.

Otherwise, the path has a single subpath consisting of four points, with coordinates (x, y), (x+w, y), (x+w, y+h), and (x, y+h), connected to each other in that order by straight lines.

###### 4.12.5.1.12 Drawing text to the bitmap

`context.fillText(text, x, y [, maxWidth ])`

`context.strokeText(text, x, y [, maxWidth ])`

Fills or strokes (respectively) the given text at the given position. If a maximum width is provided, the text will be scaled to fit that width if necessary.

`metrics = context.measureText(text)`

Returns a [`TextMetrics`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object with the metrics of the given text in the current font.

`metrics.width`

`metrics.actualBoundingBoxLeft`

`metrics.actualBoundingBoxRight`

`metrics.fontBoundingBoxAscent`

`metrics.fontBoundingBoxDescent`

`metrics.actualBoundingBoxAscent`

`metrics.actualBoundingBoxDescent`

`metrics.emHeightAscent`

`metrics.emHeightDescent`

`metrics.hangingBaseline`

`metrics.alphabeticBaseline`

`metrics.ideographicBaseline`

Returns the measurement described below.

Objects that implement the [`CanvasText`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface provide the following methods for rendering text.

The `fillText(text, x, y,
  maxWidth)` and `strokeText(text, x, y,
  maxWidth)` methods render the given text at the given (x, y) coordinates ensuring that the text isn't wider than maxWidth if specified, using the current [`font`](#412515-text-styles), [`textAlign`](#412515-text-styles), and [`textBaseline`](#412515-text-styles) values. Specifically, when the methods are invoked, the user agent must run these steps:
1. If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
2. Run the [text preparation algorithm](#412515-text-styles), passing it text, the object implementing the [`CanvasText`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface, and, if the maxWidth argument was provided, that argument. Let glyphs be the result.
3. Move all the shapes in glyphs to the right by x [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) and down by y [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px).
4. Paint the shapes given in glyphs, as transformed by the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations), with each [CSS pixel](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) in the coordinate space of glyphs mapped to one coordinate space unit.

   For [`fillText()`](#4125112-drawing-text-to-the-bitmap), [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [fill style](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles) must be applied to the shapes and [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [stroke style](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles) must be ignored. For [`strokeText()`](#4125112-drawing-text-to-the-bitmap), the reverse holds: [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [stroke style](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles) must be applied to the result of [tracing](#412514-line-styles) the shapes using the object implementing the [`CanvasText`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface for the line styles, and [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [fill style](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles) must be ignored.

   These shapes are painted without affecting the current path, and are subject to [shadow effects](#4125119-shadows), [global alpha](#4125117-compositing), the [clipping region](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas), and the [current compositing and blending operator](#4125117-compositing).

[![(This is a tracking vector.)](https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg)](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#24-privacy-concerns) The `measureText(text)` method steps are to run the [text preparation algorithm](#412515-text-styles), passing it text and the object implementing the [`CanvasText`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface, and then using the returned [inline box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box) return a new [`TextMetrics`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object with members behaving as described in the following list: [\[CSS\]](#references)

`width` attribute

The width of that [inline box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box), in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px). (The text's advance width.)

`actualBoundingBoxLeft` attribute

The distance parallel to the baseline from the alignment point given by the [`textAlign`](#412515-text-styles) attribute to the left side of the bounding rectangle of the given text, in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px); positive numbers indicating a distance going left from the given alignment point.

> [!note]
> The sum of this value and the next ([`actualBoundingBoxRight`](#4125112-drawing-text-to-the-bitmap)) can be wider than the width of the [inline box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box) ([`width`](#4125112-drawing-text-to-the-bitmap)), in particular with slanted fonts where characters overhang their advance width.

`actualBoundingBoxRight` attribute

The distance parallel to the baseline from the alignment point given by the [`textAlign`](#412515-text-styles) attribute to the right side of the bounding rectangle of the given text, in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px); positive numbers indicating a distance going right from the given alignment point.

`fontBoundingBoxAscent` attribute

The distance from the horizontal line indicated by the [`textBaseline`](#412515-text-styles) attribute to the [ascent metric](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#ascent-metric) of the [first available font](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#first-available-font), in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px); positive numbers indicating a distance going up from the given baseline.

> [!note]
> This value and the next are useful when rendering a background that have to have a consistent height even if the exact text being rendered changes. The [`actualBoundingBoxAscent`](#4125112-drawing-text-to-the-bitmap) attribute (and its corresponding attribute for the descent) are useful when drawing a bounding box around specific text.

`fontBoundingBoxDescent` attribute

The distance from the horizontal line indicated by the [`textBaseline`](#412515-text-styles) attribute to the [descent metric](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#descent-metric) of the [first available font](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#first-available-font), in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px); positive numbers indicating a distance going down from the given baseline.

`actualBoundingBoxAscent` attribute

The distance from the horizontal line indicated by the [`textBaseline`](#412515-text-styles) attribute to the top of the bounding rectangle of the given text, in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px); positive numbers indicating a distance going up from the given baseline.

> [!note]
> This number can vary greatly based on the input text, even if the first font specified covers all the characters in the input. For example, the [`actualBoundingBoxAscent`](#4125112-drawing-text-to-the-bitmap) of a lowercase "o" from an [alphabetic baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#alphabetic-baseline) would be less than that of an uppercase "F". The value can easily be negative; for example, the distance from the top of the em box ([`textBaseline`](#412515-text-styles) value "[`top`](#412515-text-styles)") to the top of the bounding rectangle when the given text is just a single comma "`,`" would likely (unless the font is quite unusual) be negative.

`actualBoundingBoxDescent` attribute

The distance from the horizontal line indicated by the [`textBaseline`](#412515-text-styles) attribute to the bottom of the bounding rectangle of the given text, in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px); positive numbers indicating a distance going down from the given baseline.

`emHeightAscent` attribute

The distance from the horizontal line indicated by the [`textBaseline`](#412515-text-styles) attribute to the [em-over baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#em-over-baseline) in the [inline box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box), in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px); positive numbers indicating that the given baseline is below the [em-over baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#em-over-baseline) (so this value will usually be positive). Zero if the given baseline is the [em-over baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#em-over-baseline); half the font size if the given baseline is halfway between the [em-over baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#em-over-baseline) and the [em-under baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#em-under-baseline).

`emHeightDescent` attribute

The distance from the horizontal line indicated by the [`textBaseline`](#412515-text-styles) attribute to the [em-under baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#em-under-baseline) in the [inline box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box), in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px); positive numbers indicating that the given baseline is above the [em-under baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#em-under-baseline). (Zero if the given baseline is the [em-under baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#em-under-baseline).)

`hangingBaseline` attribute

The distance from the horizontal line indicated by the [`textBaseline`](#412515-text-styles) attribute to the [hanging baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#hanging-baseline) of the [inline box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box), in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px); positive numbers indicating that the given baseline is below the [hanging baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#hanging-baseline). (Zero if the given baseline is the [hanging baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#hanging-baseline).)

`alphabeticBaseline` attribute

The distance from the horizontal line indicated by the [`textBaseline`](#412515-text-styles) attribute to the [alphabetic baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#alphabetic-baseline) of the [inline box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box), in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px); positive numbers indicating that the given baseline is below the [alphabetic baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#alphabetic-baseline). (Zero if the given baseline is the [alphabetic baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#alphabetic-baseline).)

`ideographicBaseline` attribute

The distance from the horizontal line indicated by the [`textBaseline`](#412515-text-styles) attribute to the [ideographic-under baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#ideographic-under-baseline) of the [inline box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#inline-box), in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px); positive numbers indicating that the given baseline is below the [ideographic-under baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#ideographic-under-baseline). (Zero if the given baseline is the [ideographic-under baseline](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-inline/#ideographic-under-baseline).)

> [!note]
> Glyphs rendered using [`fillText()`](#4125112-drawing-text-to-the-bitmap) and [`strokeText()`](#4125112-drawing-text-to-the-bitmap) can spill out of the box given by the font size and the width returned by [`measureText()`](#4125112-drawing-text-to-the-bitmap) (the text width). Authors are encouraged to use the bounding box values described above if this is an issue.

> [!note]
> A future version of the 2D context API might provide a way to render fragments of documents, rendered using CSS, straight to the canvas. This would be provided in preference to a dedicated way of doing multiline layout.

###### 4.12.5.1.13 Drawing paths to the canvas

Objects that implement the [`CanvasDrawPath`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface have a current default path. There is only one [current default path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas), it is not part of the [drawing state](#412513-the-canvas-state). The [current default path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) is a [path](#412516-building-paths), as described above.

`context.beginPath()`

Resets the [current default path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas).

`context.fill([ fillRule ])`

`context.fill(path [, fillRule ])`

Fills the subpaths of the [current default path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) or the given path with the current fill style, obeying the given fill rule.

`context.stroke()`

`context.stroke(path)`

Strokes the subpaths of the [current default path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) or the given path with the current stroke style.

`context.clip([ fillRule ])`

`context.clip(path [, fillRule ])`

Further constrains the clipping region to the [current default path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) or the given path, using the given fill rule to determine what points are in the path.

`context.isPointInPath(x, y [, fillRule ])`

`context.isPointInPath(path, x, y [, fillRule ])`

Returns true if the given point is in the [current default path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) or the given path, using the given fill rule to determine what points are in the path.

`context.isPointInStroke(x, y)`

`context.isPointInStroke(path, x, y)`

Returns true if the given point would be in the region covered by the stroke of the [current default path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) or the given path, given the current stroke style.

The `beginPath()` method steps are to empty the list of subpaths in [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [current default path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) so that it once again has zero subpaths.

Where the following method definitions use the term intended path for a [`Path2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context)-or-null path, it means path itself if it is a [`Path2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object, or the [current default path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) otherwise.

When the [intended path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) is a [`Path2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object, the coordinates and lines of its subpaths must be transformed according to the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations) on the object implementing the [`CanvasTransform`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface when used by these methods (without affecting the [`Path2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object itself). When the intended path is the [current default path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas), it is not affected by the transform. (This is because transformations already affect the [current default path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) when it is constructed, so applying it when it is painted as well would result in a double transformation.)

The `fill(fillRule)` method steps are to run the [fill steps](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), null, and fillRule.

The `fill(path, fillRule)` method steps are to run the [fill steps](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), path, and fillRule.

The fill steps, given a [`CanvasDrawPath`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) context, a [`Path2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context)-or-null path, and a [fill rule](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) fillRule, are to fill all the subpaths of the [intended path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) for path, using context's [fill style](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles), and using the [fill rule](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) indicated by fillRule. Open subpaths must be implicitly closed when being filled (without affecting the actual subpaths).

The `stroke()` method steps are to run the [stroke steps](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) and null.

The `stroke(path)` method steps are to run the [stroke steps](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) and path.

The stroke steps, given a [`CanvasDrawPath`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) context and a [`Path2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context)-or-null path, are to [trace](#412514-line-styles) the [intended path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) for path, using context's line styles as set by its [`CanvasPathDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) mixin, and then fill the resulting path using context's [stroke style](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles), using the [nonzero winding rule](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context).

> [!note]
> As a result of how the algorithm to [trace a path](#412514-line-styles) is defined, overlapping parts of the paths in one stroke operation are treated as if their union was what was painted.

> [!note]
> The stroke *style* is affected by the transformation during painting, even if the [current default path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) is used.

Paths, when filled or stroked, must be painted without affecting the [current default path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) or any [`Path2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) objects, and must be subject to [shadow effects](#4125119-shadows), [global alpha](#4125117-compositing), the [clipping region](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas), and the [current compositing and blending operator](#4125117-compositing). (The effect of transformations is described above and varies based on which path is being used.)

---

The `clip(fillRule)` method steps are to run the [clip steps](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), null, and fillRule.

The `clip(path, fillRule)` method steps are to run the [clip steps](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), path, and fillRule.

The clip steps, given a [`CanvasDrawPath`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) context, a [`Path2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context)-or-null path, and a [fill rule](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) fillRule, are to create a new clipping region by calculating the intersection of context's current clipping region and the area described by the [intended path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) for path, using the [fill rule](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) indicated by fillRule. Open subpaths must be implicitly closed when computing the clipping region, without affecting the actual subpaths. The new clipping region replaces the current clipping region.

When the context is initialized, its current clipping region must be set to the largest infinite surface (i.e. by default, no clipping occurs).

---

The `isPointInPath(x, y,
  fillRule)` method steps are to return the result of the [is point in path steps](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), null, x, y, and fillRule.

The `isPointInPath(path, x,
  y, fillRule)` method steps are to return the result of the [is point in path steps](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), path, x, y, and fillRule.

The is point in path steps, given a [`CanvasDrawPath`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) context, a [`Path2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context)-or-null path, two numbers x and y, and a [fill rule](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) fillRule, are:
1. If x or y are infinite or NaN, then return false.
2. If the point given by the x and y coordinates, when treated as coordinates in the canvas coordinate space unaffected by the current transformation, is inside the [intended path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) for path as determined by the [fill rule](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) indicated by fillRule, then return true. Open subpaths must be implicitly closed when computing the area inside the path, without affecting the actual subpaths. Points on the path itself must be considered to be inside the path.
3. Return false.

---

The `isPointInStroke(x, y)` method steps are to return the result of the [is point in stroke steps](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), null, x, and y.

The `isPointInStroke(path, x,
  y)` method steps are to return the result of the [is point in stroke steps](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), path, x, and y.

The is point in stroke steps, given a [`CanvasDrawPath`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) context, a [`Path2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context)-or-null path, and two numbers x and y, are:
1. If x or y are infinite or NaN, then return false.
2. If the point given by the x and y coordinates, when treated as coordinates in the canvas coordinate space unaffected by the current transformation, is inside the path that results from [tracing](#412514-line-styles) the [intended path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) for path, using the [nonzero winding rule](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context), and using context's line styles as set by its [`CanvasPathDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) mixin, then return true. Points on the resulting path must be considered to be inside the path.
3. Return false.

---

> [!example]
> This [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element has a couple of checkboxes. The path-related commands are highlighted:
> 
> ```html
> <canvas height=400 width=750>
>  <label><input type=checkbox id=showA> Show As</label>
>  <label><input type=checkbox id=showB> Show Bs</label>
>  <!-- ... -->
> </canvas>
> <script>
>  function drawCheckbox(context, element, x, y, paint) {
>    context.save();
>    context.font = '10px sans-serif';
>    context.textAlign = 'left';
>    context.textBaseline = 'middle';
>    var metrics = context.measureText(element.labels[0].textContent);
>    if (paint) {
>      context.beginPath();
>      context.strokeStyle = 'black';
>      context.rect(x-5, y-5, 10, 10);
>      context.stroke();
>      if (element.checked) {
>        context.fillStyle = 'black';
>        context.fill();
>      }
>      context.fillText(element.labels[0].textContent, x+5, y);
>    }
>    context.beginPath();
>    context.rect(x-7, y-7, 12 + metrics.width+2, 14);
> 
>    context.drawFocusIfNeeded(element);
>    context.restore();
>  }
>  function drawBase() { /* ... */ }
>  function drawAs() { /* ... */ }
>  function drawBs() { /* ... */ }
>  function redraw() {
>    var canvas = document.getElementsByTagName('canvas')[0];
>    var context = canvas.getContext('2d');
>    context.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
>    drawCheckbox(context, document.getElementById('showA'), 20, 40, true);
>    drawCheckbox(context, document.getElementById('showB'), 20, 60, true);
>    drawBase();
>    if (document.getElementById('showA').checked)
>      drawAs();
>    if (document.getElementById('showB').checked)
>      drawBs();
>  }
>  function processClick(event) {
>    var canvas = document.getElementsByTagName('canvas')[0];
>    var context = canvas.getContext('2d');
>    var x = event.clientX;
>    var y = event.clientY;
>    var node = event.target;
>    while (node) {
>      x -= node.offsetLeft - node.scrollLeft;
>      y -= node.offsetTop - node.scrollTop;
>      node = node.offsetParent;
>    }
>    drawCheckbox(context, document.getElementById('showA'), 20, 40, false);
>    if (context.isPointInPath(x, y))
>      document.getElementById('showA').checked = !(document.getElementById('showA').checked);
>    drawCheckbox(context, document.getElementById('showB'), 20, 60, false);
>    if (context.isPointInPath(x, y))
>      document.getElementById('showB').checked = !(document.getElementById('showB').checked);
>    redraw();
>  }
>  document.getElementsByTagName('canvas')[0].addEventListener('focus', redraw, true);
>  document.getElementsByTagName('canvas')[0].addEventListener('blur', redraw, true);
>  document.getElementsByTagName('canvas')[0].addEventListener('change', redraw, true);
>  document.getElementsByTagName('canvas')[0].addEventListener('click', processClick, false);
>  redraw();
> </script>
> ```

###### 4.12.5.1.14 Drawing focus rings

`context.drawFocusIfNeeded(element)`

If element is [focused](#662-data-model), draws a focus ring around the [current default path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas), following the platform conventions for focus rings.

`context.drawFocusIfNeeded(path, element)`

If element is [focused](#662-data-model), draws a focus ring around path, following the platform conventions for focus rings.

Objects that implement the [`CanvasUserInterface`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface provide the following methods to draw focus rings.

The `drawFocusIfNeeded(element)` method steps are to [draw focus if needed](#4125114-drawing-focus-rings) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), element, and [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [current default path](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas).

The `drawFocusIfNeeded(path,
  element)` method steps are to [draw focus if needed](#4125114-drawing-focus-rings) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), element, and path.

To draw focus if needed, given an object implementing [`CanvasUserInterface`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) context, an element element, and a [path](#412516-building-paths) path:
1. If element is not [focused](#662-data-model) or is not a descendant of context's [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element, then return.
2. Draw a focus ring of the appropriate style along path, following platform conventions.

   > [!note]
   > Some platforms only draw focus rings around elements that have been focused from the keyboard, and not those focused from the mouse. Other platforms simply don't draw focus rings around some elements at all unless relevant accessibility features are enabled. This API is intended to follow these conventions. User agents that implement distinctions based on the manner in which the element was focused are encouraged to classify focus driven by the [`focus()`](#666-focus-management-apis) method based on the kind of user interaction event from which the call was triggered (if any).

   The focus ring should not be subject to the [shadow effects](#4125119-shadows), the [global alpha](#4125117-compositing), the [current compositing and blending operator](#4125117-compositing), the [fill style](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles), the [stroke style](#4125110-fill-and-stroke-styles), or any of the members in the [`CanvasPathDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context), [`CanvasTextDrawingStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interfaces, but *should* be subject to the [clipping region](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas). (The effect of transformations is described above and varies based on which path is being used.)

3. [Inform the user](#4125114-drawing-focus-rings) that the focus is at the location given by the intended path. User agents may wait until the next time the [event loop](#8171-definitions) reaches its [update the rendering](#8173-processing-model) step to optionally inform the user.

User agents should not implicitly close open subpaths in the intended path when drawing the focus ring.

> [!note]
> This might be a moot point, however. For example, if the focus ring is drawn as an axis-aligned bounding rectangle around the points in the intended path, then whether the subpaths are closed or not has no effect. This specification intentionally does not specify precisely how focus rings are to be drawn: user agents are expected to honor their platform's native conventions.

"Inform the user", as used in this section, does not imply any persistent state change. It could mean, for instance, calling a system accessibility API to notify assistive technologies such as magnification tools so that the user's magnifier moves to the given area of the canvas. However, it does not associate the path with the element, or provide a region for tactile feedback, etc.

###### 4.12.5.1.15 Drawing images

Objects that implement the [`CanvasDrawImage`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface have the `drawImage()` method to draw images.

This method can be invoked with three different sets of arguments:
- `drawImage(image, dx, dy)`
- `drawImage(image, dx, dy, dw, dh)`
- `drawImage(image, sx, sy, sw, sh, dx, dy, dw, dh)`

`context.drawImage(image, dx, dy)`

`context.drawImage(image, dx, dy, dw, dh)`

`context.drawImage(image, sx, sy, sw, sh, dx, dy, dw, dh)`

Draws the given image onto the canvas. The arguments are interpreted as follows:

![The sx and sy parameters give the x and y coordinates of the source rectangle; the sw and sh arguments give the width and height of the source rectangle; the dx and dy give the x and y coordinates of the destination rectangle; and the dw and dh arguments give the width and height of the destination rectangle.](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/drawImage.png)

If the image isn't yet fully decoded, then nothing is drawn. If the image is a canvas with no data, throws an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

When the [`drawImage()`](#4125115-drawing-images) method is invoked, the user agent must run these steps:
1. If any of the arguments are infinite or NaN, then return.
2. Let usability be the result of [checking the usability of image](#412519-image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts).
3. If usability is *bad*, then return (without drawing anything).
4. Establish the source and destination rectangles as follows:

   If not specified, the dw and dh arguments must default to the values of sw and sh, interpreted such that one [CSS pixel](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) in the image is treated as one unit in the [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings)'s coordinate space. If the sx, sy, sw, and sh arguments are omitted, then they must default to 0, 0, the image's [natural width](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-width) in image pixels, and the image's [natural height](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-height) in image pixels, respectively. If the image has no [natural dimensions](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions), then the *concrete object size* must be used instead, as determined using the CSS "[Concrete Object Size Resolution](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#default-sizing)" algorithm, with the *specified size* having neither a definite width nor height, nor any additional constraints, the object's natural properties being those of the image argument, and the [default object size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#default-object-size) being the size of the [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings). [\[CSSIMAGES\]](#references)

   The source rectangle is the rectangle whose corners are the four points (sx, sy), (sx+sw, sy), (sx+sw, sy+sh), (sx, sy+sh).

   The destination rectangle is the rectangle whose corners are the four points (dx, dy), (dx+dw, dy), (dx+dw, dy+dh), (dx, dy+dh).

   When the source rectangle is outside the source image, the source rectangle must be clipped to the source image and the destination rectangle must be clipped in the same proportion.

   > [!note]
   > When the destination rectangle is outside the destination image (the [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings)), the pixels that land outside the [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings) are discarded, as if the destination was an infinite canvas whose rendering was clipped to the dimensions of the [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings).

5. If one of the sw or sh arguments is zero, then return. Nothing is painted.
6. Paint the region of the image argument specified by the source rectangle on the region of the rendering context's [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings) specified by the destination rectangle, after applying the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations) to the destination rectangle.

   The image data must be processed in the original direction, even if the dimensions given are negative.

   When scaling up, if the [`imageSmoothingEnabled`](#4125118-image-smoothing) attribute is set to true, the user agent should attempt to apply a smoothing algorithm to the image data when it is scaled. User agents which support multiple filtering algorithms may use the value of the [`imageSmoothingQuality`](#4125118-image-smoothing) attribute to guide the choice of filtering algorithm when the [`imageSmoothingEnabled`](#4125118-image-smoothing) attribute is set to true. Otherwise, the image must be rendered using nearest-neighbor interpolation.

   > [!note]
   > This specification does not define the precise algorithm to use when scaling an image down, or when scaling an image up when the [`imageSmoothingEnabled`](#4125118-image-smoothing) attribute is set to true.

   > [!note]
   > When a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element is drawn onto itself, the [drawing model](#4125122-drawing-model) requires the source to be copied before the image is drawn, so it is possible to copy parts of a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element onto overlapping parts of itself.

   If the original image data is a bitmap image, then the value painted at a point in the destination rectangle is computed by filtering the original image data. The user agent may use any filtering algorithm (for example bilinear interpolation or nearest-neighbor). When the filtering algorithm requires a pixel value from outside the original image data, it must instead use the value from the nearest edge pixel. (That is, the filter uses 'clamp-to-edge' behavior.) When the filtering algorithm requires a pixel value from outside the source rectangle but inside the original image data, then the value from the original image data must be used.

   > [!note]
   > Thus, scaling an image in parts or in whole will have the same effect. This does mean that when sprites coming from a single sprite sheet are to be scaled, adjacent images in the sprite sheet can interfere. This can be avoided by ensuring each sprite in the sheet is surrounded by a border of [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black), or by copying sprites to be scaled into temporary [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) elements and drawing the scaled sprites from there.

   Images are painted without affecting the current path, and are subject to [shadow effects](#4125119-shadows), [global alpha](#4125117-compositing), the [clipping region](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas), and the [current compositing and blending operator](#4125117-compositing).

7. If image [is not origin-clean](#412519-image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts), then set the [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context)'s [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag to false.

###### 4.12.5.1.16 Pixel manipulation

`imageData = context.createImageData(imageData)`

Returns an [`ImageData`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) object with the same dimensions and color space as the argument. All the pixels in the returned object are [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black).

`imageData = context.createImageData(sw, sh [, settings])`

Returns an [`ImageData`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) object with the given dimensions. The color space of the returned object is the [color space](#412512-the-canvas-settings) of context unless overridden by settings. All the pixels in the returned object are [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black).

Throws an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if either of the width or height arguments are zero.

`imageData = context.getImageData(sx, sy, sw, sh [, settings])`

Returns an [`ImageData`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) object containing the image data for the given rectangle of the bitmap. The color space of the returned object is the [color space](#412512-the-canvas-settings) of context unless overridden by settings.

Throws an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the either of the width or height arguments are zero.

`context.putImageData(imageData, dx, dy [, dirtyX, dirtyY, dirtyWidth, dirtyHeight ])`

Paints the data from the given [`ImageData`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) object onto the bitmap. If a dirty rectangle is provided, only the pixels from that rectangle are painted.

The [`globalAlpha`](#4125117-compositing) and [`globalCompositeOperation`](#4125117-compositing) properties, as well as the [shadow attributes](#4125119-shadows), are ignored for the purposes of this method call; pixels in the canvas are replaced wholesale, with no composition, alpha blending, no shadows, etc.

Throws an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the imageData object's [`data`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute value's \[\[ViewedArrayBuffer\]\] internal slot is detached.

Objects that implement the [`CanvasImageData`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface provide the following methods for reading and writing pixel data to the bitmap.

The `createImageData(sw, sh,
  settings)` method steps are:
1. If one or both of sw and sh are zero, then throw an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Let newImageData be a [new](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#new) [`ImageData`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) object.
3. [Initialize](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) newImageData given the absolute magnitude of sw, the absolute magnitude of sh, settings, and *[defaultColorSpace](#8111-the-imagedata-interface)* set to [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [color space](#412512-the-canvas-settings).
4. Initialize the image data of newImageData to [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black).
5. Return newImageData.

The `createImageData(imageData)` method steps are:
1. Let newImageData be a [new](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#new) [`ImageData`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) object.
2. Let settings be the [`ImageDataSettings`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) object «\[ "[`colorSpace`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface)" → [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [colorSpace](#8111-the-imagedata-interface), "[`pixelFormat`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface)" → [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [pixelFormat](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) \]».
3. [Initialize](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) newImageData given the value of imageData's [`width`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute, the value of imageData's [`height`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute, and settings.
4. Initialize the image data of newImageData to [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black).
5. Return newImageData.

The `getImageData(sx, sy, sw,
  sh, settings)` method steps are:
1. If either the sw or sh arguments are zero, then throw an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. If the [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context)'s [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag is set to false, then throw a ["`SecurityError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
3. Let imageData be a [new](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#new) [`ImageData`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) object.
4. [Initialize](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) imageData given sw, sh, settings, and *[defaultColorSpace](#8111-the-imagedata-interface)* set to [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [color space](#412512-the-canvas-settings).
5. Let the source rectangle be the rectangle whose corners are the four points (sx, sy), (sx+sw, sy), (sx+sw, sy+sh), (sx, sy+sh).
6. Set the pixel values of imageData to be the pixels of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings) in the area specified by the source rectangle in the bitmap's coordinate space units, converted from [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [color space](#412512-the-canvas-settings) to imageData's [`colorSpace`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) using ['relative-colorimetric'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-5/#valdef-color-profile-rendering-intent-relative-colorimetric) rendering intent.
7. Set the pixels values of imageData for areas of the source rectangle that are outside of the [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings) to [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black).
8. Return imageData.

The `putImageData(imageData,
  dx, dy)` method steps are to [put pixels from an `ImageData` onto a bitmap](#4125116-pixel-manipulation), given imageData, [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings), dx, dy, 0, 0, imageData's [`width`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface), and imageData's [`height`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface).

The `putImageData(imageData,
  dx, dy, dirtyX, dirtyY,
  dirtyWidth, dirtyHeight)` method steps are to [put pixels from an `ImageData` onto a bitmap](#4125116-pixel-manipulation), given imageData, [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings), dx, dy, dirtyX, dirtyY, dirtyWidth, and dirtyHeight.

To put pixels from an `ImageData` onto a bitmap, given an [`ImageData`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) imageData, an [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings) bitmap, and numbers dx, dy, dirtyX, dirtyY, dirtyWidth, and dirtyHeight:
1. Let buffer be imageData's [`data`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute value's \[\[ViewedArrayBuffer\]\] internal slot.
2. If [IsDetachedBuffer](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-isdetachedbuffer)(buffer) is true, then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
3. If dirtyWidth is negative, then let dirtyX be dirtyX+dirtyWidth, and let dirtyWidth be equal to the absolute magnitude of dirtyWidth.

   If dirtyHeight is negative, then let dirtyY be dirtyY+dirtyHeight, and let dirtyHeight be equal to the absolute magnitude of dirtyHeight.

4. If dirtyX is negative, then let dirtyWidth be dirtyWidth+dirtyX, and let dirtyX be 0.

   If dirtyY is negative, then let dirtyHeight be dirtyHeight+dirtyY, and let dirtyY be 0.

5. If dirtyX+dirtyWidth is greater than the [`width`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute of the imageData argument, then let dirtyWidth be the value of that [`width`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute, minus the value of dirtyX.

   If dirtyY+dirtyHeight is greater than the [`height`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute of the imageData argument, then let dirtyHeight be the value of that [`height`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute, minus the value of dirtyY.

6. If, after those changes, either dirtyWidth or dirtyHeight are negative or zero, then return without affecting any bitmaps.
7. For all integer values of x and y where dirtyX ≤ x < dirtyX+dirtyWidth and dirtyY ≤ y < dirtyY+dirtyHeight, set the pixel with coordinate (dx+x, dy+y) in bitmap to the color of the pixel at coordinate (x, y) in the imageData data structure's [bitmap](#8111-the-imagedata-interface), converted from imageData's [`colorSpace`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) to the [color space](#412512-the-canvas-settings) of bitmap using ['relative-colorimetric'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-5/#valdef-color-profile-rendering-intent-relative-colorimetric) rendering intent.

> [!note]
> Due to the lossy nature of converting between color spaces and converting to and from [premultiplied alpha](#41257-premultiplied-alpha-and-the-2d-rendering-context) color values, pixels that have just been set using [`putImageData()`](#4125116-pixel-manipulation), and are not completely opaque, might be returned to an equivalent [`getImageData()`](#4125116-pixel-manipulation) as different values.

The current path, [transformation matrix](#412518-transformations), [shadow attributes](#4125119-shadows), [global alpha](#4125117-compositing), the [clipping region](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas), and [current compositing and blending operator](#4125117-compositing) must not affect the methods described in this section.

> [!example]
> In the following example, the script generates an [`ImageData`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) object so that it can draw onto it.
> 
> ```javascript
> // canvas is a reference to a <canvas> element
> var context = canvas.getContext('2d');
> 
> // create a blank slate
> var data = context.createImageData(canvas.width, canvas.height);
> 
> // create some plasma
> FillPlasma(data, 'green'); // green plasma
> 
> // add a cloud to the plasma
> AddCloud(data, data.width/2, data.height/2); // put a cloud in the middle
> 
> // paint the plasma+cloud on the canvas
> context.putImageData(data, 0, 0);
> 
> // support methods
> function FillPlasma(data, color) { ... }
> function AddCloud(data, x, y) { ... }
> ```

> [!example]
> Here is an example of using [`getImageData()`](#4125116-pixel-manipulation) and [`putImageData()`](#4125116-pixel-manipulation) to implement an edge detection filter.
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <html lang="en">
>  <head>
>   <title>Edge detection demo</title>
>   <script>
>    var image = new Image();
>    function init() {
>      image.onload = demo;
>      image.src = "image.jpeg";
>    }
>    function demo() {
>      var canvas = document.getElementsByTagName('canvas')[0];
>      var context = canvas.getContext('2d');
> 
>      // draw the image onto the canvas
>      context.drawImage(image, 0, 0);
> 
>      // get the image data to manipulate
>      var input = context.getImageData(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
> 
>      // get an empty slate to put the data into
>      var output = context.createImageData(canvas.width, canvas.height);
> 
>      // alias some variables for convenience
>      // In this case input.width and input.height
>      // match canvas.width and canvas.height
>      // but we'll use the former to keep the code generic.
>      var w = input.width, h = input.height;
>      var inputData = input.data;
>      var outputData = output.data;
> 
>      // edge detection
>      for (var y = 1; y < h-1; y += 1) {
>        for (var x = 1; x < w-1; x += 1) {
>          for (var c = 0; c < 3; c += 1) {
>            var i = (y*w + x)*4 + c;
>            outputData[i] = 127 + -inputData[i - w*4 - 4] -   inputData[i - w*4] - inputData[i - w*4 + 4] +
>                                  -inputData[i - 4]       + 8*inputData[i]       - inputData[i + 4] +
>                                  -inputData[i + w*4 - 4] -   inputData[i + w*4] - inputData[i + w*4 + 4];
>          }
>          outputData[(y*w + x)*4 + 3] = 255; // alpha
>        }
>      }
> 
>      // put the image data back after manipulation
>      context.putImageData(output, 0, 0);
>    }
>   </script>
>  </head>
>  <body onload="init()">
>   <canvas></canvas>
>  </body>
> </html>
> ```

> [!example]
> Here is an example of color space conversion applied when drawing a solid color and reading the result back using and [`getImageData()`](#4125116-pixel-manipulation).
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <html lang="en">
> <title>Color space image data demo</title>
> 
> <canvas></canvas>
> 
> <script>
> const canvas = document.querySelector('canvas');
> const context = canvas.getContext('2d', {colorSpace:'display-p3'});
> 
> // Draw a red rectangle. Note that the hex color notation
> // specifies sRGB colors.
> context.fillStyle = "#FF0000";
> context.fillRect(0, 0, 64, 64);
> 
> // Get the image data.
> const pixels = context.getImageData(0, 0, 1, 1);
> 
> // This will print 'display-p3', reflecting the default behavior
> // of returning image data in the canvas's color space.
> console.log(pixels.colorSpace);
> 
> // This will print the values 234, 51, and 35, reflecting the
> // red fill color, converted to 'display-p3'.
> console.log(pixels.data[0]);
> console.log(pixels.data[1]);
> console.log(pixels.data[2]);
> </script>
> ```

###### 4.12.5.1.17 Compositing

`context.globalAlpha [ = value ]`

Returns the current [global alpha](#4125117-compositing) value applied to rendering operations.

Can be set, to change the [global alpha](#4125117-compositing) value. Values outside of the range 0.0 .. 1.0 are ignored.

`context.globalCompositeOperation [ = value ]`

Returns the [current compositing and blending operator](#4125117-compositing), from the values defined in Compositing and Blending. [\[COMPOSITE\]](#references)

Can be set, to change the [current compositing and blending operator](#4125117-compositing). Unknown values are ignored.

Objects that implement the [`CanvasCompositing`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface have a [global alpha](#4125117-compositing) value and a [current compositing and blending operator](#4125117-compositing) value that both affect all the drawing operations on this object.

The global alpha value gives an alpha value that is applied to shapes and images before they are composited onto the [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings). The value ranges from 0.0 (fully transparent) to 1.0 (no additional transparency). It must initially have the value 1.0.

The `globalAlpha` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [global alpha](#4125117-compositing).

The [`globalAlpha`](#4125117-compositing) setter steps are:
1. If the given value is either infinite, NaN, or not in the range 0.0 to 1.0, then return.
2. Otherwise, set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [global alpha](#4125117-compositing) to the given value.

The current compositing and blending operator value controls how shapes and images are drawn onto the [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings), once they have had the [global alpha](#4125117-compositing) and the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations) applied. Initially, it must be set to "[`source-over`](https://drafts.csswg.org/compositing/#porterduffcompositingoperators_srcover)".

The `globalCompositeOperation` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [current compositing and blending operator](#4125117-compositing).

The [`globalCompositeOperation`](#4125117-compositing) setter steps are:
1. If the given value is not [identical to](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) any of the values that the [<blend-mode>](https://drafts.csswg.org/compositing/#ltblendmodegt) or the [<composite-mode>](https://drafts.csswg.org/compositing/#compositemode) properties are defined to take, then return. [\[COMPOSITE\]](#references)
2. Otherwise, set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [current compositing and blending operator](#4125117-compositing) to the given value.

###### 4.12.5.1.18 Image smoothing

`context.imageSmoothingEnabled [ = value ]`

Returns whether pattern fills and the [`drawImage()`](#4125115-drawing-images) method will attempt to smooth images if their pixels don't line up exactly with the display, when scaling images up.

Can be set, to change whether images are smoothed (true) or not (false).

`context.imageSmoothingQuality [ = value ]`

Returns the current image-smoothing-quality preference.

Can be set, to change the preferred quality of image smoothing. The possible values are "[`low`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context)", "[`medium`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context)" and "[`high`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context)". Unknown values are ignored.

Objects that implement the [`CanvasImageSmoothing`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface have attributes that control how image smoothing is performed.

The `imageSmoothingEnabled` attribute, on getting, must return the last value it was set to. On setting, it must be set to the new value. When the object implementing the [`CanvasImageSmoothing`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface is created, the attribute must be set to true.

The `imageSmoothingQuality` attribute, on getting, must return the last value it was set to. On setting, it must be set to the new value. When the object implementing the [`CanvasImageSmoothing`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface is created, the attribute must be set to "[`low`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context)".

###### 4.12.5.1.19 Shadows

All drawing operations on an object which implements the [`CanvasShadowStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface are affected by the four global shadow attributes.

`context.shadowColor [ = value ]`

Returns the current shadow color.

Can be set, to change the shadow color. Values that cannot be parsed as CSS colors are ignored.

`context.shadowOffsetX [ = value ]`

`context.shadowOffsetY [ = value ]`

Returns the current shadow offset.

Can be set, to change the shadow offset. Values that are not finite numbers are ignored.

`context.shadowBlur [ = value ]`

Returns the current level of blur applied to shadows.

Can be set, to change the blur level. Values that are not finite numbers greater than or equal to zero are ignored.

Objects which implement the [`CanvasShadowStyles`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface have an associated shadow color, which is a CSS color. Initially, it must be [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black).

The `shadowColor` getter steps are to return the [serialization](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#serializing-color-values) of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [shadow color](#4125119-shadows) with [HTML-compatible serialization requested](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#color-serialization-html-compatible-serialization-is-requested).

The [`shadowColor`](#4125119-shadows) setter steps are:
1. Let context be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`canvas`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) attribute's value, if that is an element; otherwise null.
2. Let parsedValue be the result of [parsing](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#parse-a-css-color-value) the given value with context if non-null.
3. If parsedValue is failure, then return.
4. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [shadow color](#4125119-shadows) to parsedValue.

The `shadowOffsetX` and `shadowOffsetY` attributes specify the distance that the shadow will be offset in the positive horizontal and positive vertical distance respectively. Their values are in coordinate space units. They are not affected by the current transformation matrix.

When the context is created, the shadow offset attributes must initially have the value 0.

On getting, they must return their current value. On setting, the attribute being set must be set to the new value, except if the value is infinite or NaN, in which case the new value must be ignored.

The `shadowBlur` attribute specifies the level of the blurring effect. (The units do not map to coordinate space units, and are not affected by the current transformation matrix.)

When the context is created, the [`shadowBlur`](#4125119-shadows) attribute must initially have the value 0.

On getting, the attribute must return its current value. On setting, the attribute must be set to the new value, except if the value is negative, infinite or NaN, in which case the new value must be ignored.

Shadows are only drawn if the opacity component of the alpha component of the [shadow color](#4125119-shadows) is nonzero and either the [`shadowBlur`](#4125119-shadows) is nonzero, or the [`shadowOffsetX`](#4125119-shadows) is nonzero, or the [`shadowOffsetY`](#4125119-shadows) is nonzero.

[When shadows are drawn](#4125119-shadows), they must be rendered as follows:
1. Let A be an infinite [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black) bitmap on which the source image for which a shadow is being created has been rendered.
2. Let B be an infinite [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black) bitmap, with a coordinate space and an origin identical to A.
3. Copy the alpha component of A to B, offset by [`shadowOffsetX`](#4125119-shadows) in the positive x direction, and [`shadowOffsetY`](#4125119-shadows) in the positive y direction.
4. If [`shadowBlur`](#4125119-shadows) is greater than 0:
   1. Let σ be half the value of [`shadowBlur`](#4125119-shadows).
   2. Perform a 2D Gaussian Blur on B, using σ as the standard deviation.

   User agents may limit values of σ to an implementation-specific maximum value to avoid exceeding hardware limitations during the Gaussian blur operation.

5. Set the red, green, and blue components of every pixel in B to the red, green, and blue components (respectively) of the [shadow color](#4125119-shadows).
6. Multiply the alpha component of every pixel in B by the alpha component of the [shadow color](#4125119-shadows).
7. The shadow is in the bitmap B, and is rendered as part of the [drawing model](#4125122-drawing-model) described below.

If the [current compositing and blending operator](#4125117-compositing) is "[`copy`](https://drafts.csswg.org/compositing/#porterduffcompositingoperators_src)", then shadows effectively won't render (since the shape will overwrite the shadow).

###### 4.12.5.1.20 Filters

All drawing operations on an object which implements the [`CanvasFilters`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) interface are affected by the global `filter` attribute.

`context.filter [ = value ]`

Returns the current filter.

Can be set, to change the filter. Values can either be the string "`none`" or a string parseable as a [<filter-value-list>](https://drafts.csswg.org/filter-effects/#typedef-filter-value-list). Other values are ignored.

Such objects have an associated current filter, which is a string. Initially the [current filter](#4125120-filters) is set to the string "`none`". Whenever the value of the [current filter](#4125120-filters) is the string "`none`" filters will be disabled for the context.

The [`filter`](#4125120-filters) getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [current filter](#4125120-filters).

The [`filter`](#4125120-filters) setter steps are:
1. If the given value is "`none`", then set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [current filter](#4125120-filters) to "`none`" and return.
2. Let parsedValue be the result of [parsing](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-syntax/#parse-grammar) the given values as a [<filter-value-list>](https://drafts.csswg.org/filter-effects/#typedef-filter-value-list). If any property-independent style sheet syntax like 'inherit' or 'initial' is present, then this parsing must return failure.
3. If parsedValue is failure, then return.
4. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [current filter](#4125120-filters) to the given value.

> [!note]
> Though `` context.`filter` = "`none`" `` will disable filters for the context, `` context.`filter` = "" ``, `` context.`filter` = null ``, and `` context.`filter` =
>   undefined `` are all treated as unparseable inputs and the value of the [current filter](#4125120-filters) is left unchanged.

Coordinates used in the value of the [current filter](#4125120-filters) are interpreted such that one pixel is equivalent to one SVG user space unit and to one canvas coordinate space unit. Filter coordinates are not affected by the [current transformation matrix](#412518-transformations). The current transformation matrix affects only the input to the filter. Filters are applied in the [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings)'s coordinate space.

When the value of the [current filter](#4125120-filters) is a string parsable as a [<filter-value-list>](https://drafts.csswg.org/filter-effects/#typedef-filter-value-list) which defines lengths using percentages or using ['em'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#em) or ['ex'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#ex) units, these must be interpreted relative to the [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of the ['font-size'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-size-prop) property of the [font style source object](#412515-text-styles) at the time that the attribute is set. If the [computed values](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) are undefined for a particular case (e.g. because the [font style source object](#412515-text-styles) is not an element or is not [being rendered](#151-introduction)), then the relative keywords must be interpreted relative to the default value of the [`font`](#412515-text-styles) attribute. The 'larger' and 'smaller' keywords are not supported.

If the value of the [current filter](#4125120-filters) is a string parseable as a [<filter-value-list>](https://drafts.csswg.org/filter-effects/#typedef-filter-value-list) with a reference to an SVG filter in the same document, and this SVG filter changes, then the changed filter is used for the next draw operation.

If the value of the [current filter](#4125120-filters) is a string parseable as a [<filter-value-list>](https://drafts.csswg.org/filter-effects/#typedef-filter-value-list) with a reference to an SVG filter in an external resource document and that document is not loaded when a drawing operation is invoked, then the drawing operation must proceed with no filtering.

###### 4.12.5.1.21 Working with externally-defined SVG filters

*This section is non-normative.*

Since drawing is performed using filter value "`none`" until an externally-defined filter has finished loading, authors might wish to determine whether such a filter has finished loading before proceeding with a drawing operation. One way to accomplish this is to load the externally-defined filter elsewhere within the same page in some element that sends a `load` event (for example, an [SVG `use`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/struct.html#elementdef-use) element), and wait for the `load` event to be dispatched.

###### 4.12.5.1.22 Drawing model

When a shape or image is painted, user agents must follow these steps, in the order given (or act as if they do):
1. Render the shape or image onto an infinite [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black) bitmap, creating image A, as described in the previous sections. For shapes, the current fill, stroke, and line styles must be honored, and the stroke must itself also be subjected to the current transformation matrix.
2. Convert the image A to the context's [color space](#412512-the-canvas-settings).

   > [!note]
   > There do not exist any inputs to a 2D context for which the color space is undefined. The color space for CSS colors is defined in CSS Color.
