The color space for images that specify no color profile information is ['srgb'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#valdef-color-srgb), as specified in the [Color Spaces of Untagged Colors](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#untagged) section of CSS Color. [\[CSSCOLOR\]](#references)

3. Multiply the alpha component of every pixel in A by [`global alpha`](#4125117-compositing).
4. When the [current filter](#4125120-filters) is set to a value other than "`none`" and all the externally-defined filters it references, if any, are in documents that are currently loaded, then use image A as the input to the [current filter](#4125120-filters), creating image B. If the [current filter](#4125120-filters) is a string parseable as a [<filter-value-list>](https://drafts.csswg.org/filter-effects/#typedef-filter-value-list), then draw using the [current filter](#4125120-filters) in the same manner as SVG.

   Otherwise, let B be an alias for A.

5. [When shadows are drawn](#4125119-shadows), render the shadow from image B, using the current shadow styles, creating image C.
6. [When shadows are drawn](#4125119-shadows), composite C within the [clipping region](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) over the current [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings) using the [current compositing and blending operator](#4125117-compositing).
7. Composite B within the [clipping region](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas) over the current [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings) using the [current compositing and blending operator](#4125117-compositing).

When compositing onto the [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings), pixels that would fall outside of the [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings) must be discarded.

###### 4.12.5.1.23 Best practices

When a canvas is interactive, authors should include [focusable](#662-data-model) elements in the element's fallback content corresponding to each [focusable](#662-data-model) part of the canvas, as in the [example above](#4125113-drawing-paths-to-the-canvas).

When rendering focus rings, to ensure that focus rings have the appearance of native focus rings, authors should use the [`drawFocusIfNeeded()`](#4125114-drawing-focus-rings) method, passing it the element for which a ring is being drawn. This method only draws the focus ring if the element is [focused](#662-data-model), so that it can simply be called whenever drawing the element, without checking whether the element is focused or not first.

Authors should avoid implementing text editing controls using the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element. Doing so has a large number of disadvantages:
- Mouse placement of the caret has to be reimplemented.
- Keyboard movement of the caret has to be reimplemented (possibly across lines, for multiline text input).
- Scrolling of the text control has to be implemented (horizontally for long lines, vertically for multiline input).
- Native features such as copy-and-paste have to be reimplemented.
- Native features such as spell-checking have to be reimplemented.
- Native features such as drag-and-drop have to be reimplemented.
- Native features such as page-wide text search have to be reimplemented.
- Native features specific to the user, for example custom text services, have to be reimplemented. This is close to impossible since each user might have different services installed, and there is an unbounded set of possible such services.
- Bidirectional text editing has to be reimplemented.
- For multiline text editing, line wrapping has to be implemented for all relevant languages.
- Text selection has to be reimplemented.
- Dragging of bidirectional text selections has to be reimplemented.
- Platform-native keyboard shortcuts have to be reimplemented.
- Platform-native input method editors (IMEs) have to be reimplemented.
- Undo and redo functionality has to be reimplemented.
- Accessibility features such as magnification following the caret or selection have to be reimplemented.

This is a huge amount of work, and authors are most strongly encouraged to avoid doing any of it by instead using the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element, the [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element, or the [`contenteditable`](#681-making-document-regions-editable-the-contenteditable-content-attribute) attribute.

###### 4.12.5.1.24 Examples

*This section is non-normative.*

> [!example]
> Here is an example of a script that uses canvas to draw [pretty glowing lines](data:text/html;charset=utf-8;base64,PCFET0NUWVBFIEhUTUw%2BDQo8aHRtbCBsYW5nPSJlbiI%2BDQogPGhlYWQ%2BDQogIDx0aXRsZT5QcmV0dHkgR2xvd2luZyBMaW5lczwvdGl0bGU%2BDQogPC9oZWFkPg0KIDxib2R5Pg0KPGNhbnZhcyB3aWR0aD0iODAwIiBoZWlnaHQ9IjQ1MCI%2BPC9jYW52YXM%%2BDQogPC9ib2R5Pg0KPC9odG1sPg0K).
> 
> ```html
> <canvas width="800" height="450"></canvas>
> <script>
> 
>  var context = document.getElementsByTagName('canvas')[0].getContext('2d');
> 
>  var lastX = context.canvas.width * Math.random();
>  var lastY = context.canvas.height * Math.random();
>  var hue = 0;
>  function line() {
>    context.save();
>    context.translate(context.canvas.width/2, context.canvas.height/2);
>    context.scale(0.9, 0.9);
>    context.translate(-context.canvas.width/2, -context.canvas.height/2);
>    context.beginPath();
>    context.lineWidth = 5 + Math.random() * 10;
>    context.moveTo(lastX, lastY);
>    lastX = context.canvas.width * Math.random();
>    lastY = context.canvas.height * Math.random();
>    context.bezierCurveTo(context.canvas.width * Math.random(),
>                          context.canvas.height * Math.random(),
>                          context.canvas.width * Math.random(),
>                          context.canvas.height * Math.random(),
>                          lastX, lastY);
> 
>    hue = hue + 10 * Math.random();
>    context.strokeStyle = 'hsl(' + hue + ', 50%, 50%)';
>    context.shadowColor = 'white';
>    context.shadowBlur = 10;
>    context.stroke();
>    context.restore();
>  }
>  setInterval(line, 50);
> 
>  function blank() {
>    context.fillStyle = 'rgba(0,0,0,0.1)';
>    context.fillRect(0, 0, context.canvas.width, context.canvas.height);
>  }
>  setInterval(blank, 40);
> 
> </script>
> ```

> [!example]
> The 2D rendering context for [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) is often used for sprite-based games. The following example demonstrates this:
> 
> Here is the source for this example:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <html lang="en">
> <meta charset="utf-8">
> <title>Blue Robot Demo</title>
> <style>
>   html { overflow: hidden; min-height: 200px; min-width: 380px; }
>   body { height: 200px; position: relative; margin: 8px; }
>   .buttons { position: absolute; bottom: 0px; left: 0px; margin: 4px; }
> </style>
> <canvas width="380" height="200"></canvas>
> <script>
>  var Landscape = function (context, width, height) {
>    this.offset = 0;
>    this.width = width;
>    this.advance = function (dx) {
>      this.offset += dx;
>    };
>    this.horizon = height * 0.7;
>    // This creates the sky gradient (from a darker blue to white at the bottom)
>    this.sky = context.createLinearGradient(0, 0, 0, this.horizon);
>    this.sky.addColorStop(0.0, 'rgb(55,121,179)');
>    this.sky.addColorStop(0.7, 'rgb(121,194,245)');
>    this.sky.addColorStop(1.0, 'rgb(164,200,214)');
>    // this creates the grass gradient (from a darker green to a lighter green)
>    this.earth = context.createLinearGradient(0, this.horizon, 0, height);
>    this.earth.addColorStop(0.0, 'rgb(81,140,20)');
>    this.earth.addColorStop(1.0, 'rgb(123,177,57)');
>    this.paintBackground = function (context, width, height) {
>      // first, paint the sky and grass rectangles
>      context.fillStyle = this.sky;
>      context.fillRect(0, 0, width, this.horizon);
>      context.fillStyle = this.earth;
>      context.fillRect(0, this.horizon, width, height-this.horizon);
>      // then, draw the cloudy banner
>      // we make it cloudy by having the draw text off the top of the
>      // canvas, and just having the blurred shadow shown on the canvas
>      context.save();
>      context.translate(width-((this.offset+(this.width*3.2)) % (this.width*4.0))+0, 0);
>      context.shadowColor = 'white';
>      context.shadowOffsetY = 30+this.horizon/3; // offset down on canvas
>      context.shadowBlur = '5';
>      context.fillStyle = 'white';
>      context.textAlign = 'left';
>      context.textBaseline = 'top';
>      context.font = '20px sans-serif';
>      context.fillText('WHATWG ROCKS', 10, -30); // text up above canvas
>      context.restore();
>      // then, draw the background tree
>      context.save();
>      context.translate(width-((this.offset+(this.width*0.2)) % (this.width*1.5))+30, 0);
>      context.beginPath();
>      context.fillStyle = 'rgb(143,89,2)';
>      context.lineStyle = 'rgb(10,10,10)';
>      context.lineWidth = 2;
>      context.rect(0, this.horizon+5, 10, -50); // trunk
>      context.fill();
>      context.stroke();
>      context.beginPath();
>      context.fillStyle = 'rgb(78,154,6)';
>      context.arc(5, this.horizon-60, 30, 0, Math.PI*2); // leaves
>      context.fill();
>      context.stroke();
>      context.restore();
>    };
>    this.paintForeground = function (context, width, height) {
>      // draw the box that goes in front
>      context.save();
>      context.translate(width-((this.offset+(this.width*0.7)) % (this.width*1.1))+0, 0);
>      context.beginPath();
>      context.rect(0, this.horizon - 5, 25, 25);
>      context.fillStyle = 'rgb(220,154,94)';
>      context.lineStyle = 'rgb(10,10,10)';
>      context.lineWidth = 2;
>      context.fill();
>      context.stroke();
>      context.restore();
>    };
>  };
> </script>
> <script>
>  var BlueRobot = function () {
>    this.sprites = new Image();
>    this.sprites.src = 'blue-robot.png'; // this sprite sheet has 8 cells
>    this.targetMode = 'idle';
>    this.walk = function () {
>      this.targetMode = 'walk';
>    };
>    this.stop = function () {
>      this.targetMode = 'idle';
>    };
>    this.frameIndex = {
>      'idle': [0], // first cell is the idle frame
>      'walk': [1,2,3,4,5,6], // the walking animation is cells 1-6
>      'stop': [7], // last cell is the stopping animation
>    };
>    this.mode = 'idle';
>    this.frame = 0; // index into frameIndex
>    this.tick = function () {
>      // this advances the frame and the robot
>      // the return value is how many pixels the robot has moved
>      this.frame += 1;
>      if (this.frame >= this.frameIndex[this.mode].length) {
>        // we've reached the end of this animation cycle
>        this.frame = 0;
>        if (this.mode != this.targetMode) {
>          // switch to next cycle
>          if (this.mode == 'walk') {
>            // we need to stop walking before we decide what to do next
>            this.mode = 'stop';
>          } else if (this.mode == 'stop') {
>            if (this.targetMode == 'walk')
>              this.mode = 'walk';
>            else
>              this.mode = 'idle';
>          } else if (this.mode == 'idle') {
>            if (this.targetMode == 'walk')
>              this.mode = 'walk';
>          }
>        }
>      }
>      if (this.mode == 'walk')
>        return 8;
>      return 0;
>    },
>    this.paint = function (context, x, y) {
>      if (!this.sprites.complete) return;
>      // draw the right frame out of the sprite sheet onto the canvas
>      // we assume each frame is as high as the sprite sheet
>      // the x,y coordinates give the position of the bottom center of the sprite
>      context.drawImage(this.sprites,
>                        this.frameIndex[this.mode][this.frame] * this.sprites.height, 0, this.sprites.height, this.sprites.height,
>                        x-this.sprites.height/2, y-this.sprites.height, this.sprites.height, this.sprites.height);
>    };
>  };
> </script>
> <script>
>  var canvas = document.getElementsByTagName('canvas')[0];
>  var context = canvas.getContext('2d');
>  var landscape = new Landscape(context, canvas.width, canvas.height);
>  var blueRobot = new BlueRobot();
>  // paint when the browser wants us to, using requestAnimationFrame()
>  function paint() {
>    context.clearRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
>    landscape.paintBackground(context, canvas.width, canvas.height);
>    blueRobot.paint(context, canvas.width/2, landscape.horizon*1.1);
>    landscape.paintForeground(context, canvas.width, canvas.height);
>    requestAnimationFrame(paint);
>  }
>  paint();
>  // but tick every 100ms, so that we don't slow down when we don't paint
>  setInterval(function () {
>    var dx = blueRobot.tick();
>    landscape.advance(dx);
>  }, 100);
> </script>
> <p class="buttons">
>  <input type=button value="Walk" onclick="blueRobot.walk()">
>  <input type=button value="Stop" onclick="blueRobot.stop()">
> <footer>
>  <small> Blue Robot Player Sprite by <a href="https://johncolburn.deviantart.com/">JohnColburn</a>.
>  Licensed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution Share-Alike 3.0 Unported license.</small>
>  <small> This work is itself licensed under a <a rel="license" href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/">Creative
>  Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported License</a>.</small>
> </footer>
> 
> ```

##### 4.12.5.2 The [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) rendering context

###### 4.12.5.2.1 Introduction

[`ImageBitmapRenderingContext`](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) is a performance-oriented interface that provides a low overhead method for displaying the contents of [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) objects. It uses transfer semantics to reduce overall memory consumption. It also streamlines performance by avoiding intermediate compositing, unlike the [`drawImage()`](#4125115-drawing-images) method of [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context).

Using an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element as an intermediate for getting an image resource into a canvas, for example, would result in two copies of the decoded image existing in memory at the same time: the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's copy, and the one in the canvas's backing store. This memory cost can be prohibitive when dealing with extremely large images. This can be avoided by using [`ImageBitmapRenderingContext`](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface).

> [!example]
> Using [`ImageBitmapRenderingContext`](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface), here is how to transcode an image to the JPEG format in a memory- and CPU-efficient way:
> 
> ```javascript
> createImageBitmap(inputImageBlob).then(image => {
>   const canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
>   const context = canvas.getContext('bitmaprenderer');
>   context.transferFromImageBitmap(image);
> 
>   canvas.toBlob(outputJPEGBlob => {
>     // Do something with outputJPEGBlob.
>   }, 'image/jpeg');
> });
> ```

###### 4.12.5.2.2 The [`ImageBitmapRenderingContext`](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) interface

```webidl
[Exposed=(Window,Worker)]
interface ImageBitmapRenderingContext {
  readonly attribute (HTMLCanvasElement or OffscreenCanvas) canvas;
  undefined transferFromImageBitmap(ImageBitmap? bitmap);
};

dictionary ImageBitmapRenderingContextSettings {
  boolean alpha = true;
};
```

`context = canvas.getContext('bitmaprenderer' [, { [ alpha: false ] } ])`

Returns an [`ImageBitmapRenderingContext`](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) object that is permanently bound to a particular [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element.

If the [`alpha`](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) setting is provided and set to false, then the canvas is forced to always be opaque.

`context.canvas`

Returns the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element that the context is bound to.

`context.transferFromImageBitmap(imageBitmap)`

Transfers the underlying [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) from imageBitmap to context, and the bitmap becomes the contents of the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element to which context is bound.

`context.transferFromImageBitmap(null)`

Replaces contents of the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element to which context is bound with a [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black) bitmap whose size corresponds to the [`width`](#4125-the-canvas-element) and [`height`](#4125-the-canvas-element) content attributes of the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element.

The `canvas` attribute must return the value it was initialized to when the object was created.

An [`ImageBitmapRenderingContext`](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) object has an output bitmap, which is a reference to [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface).

An [`ImageBitmapRenderingContext`](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) object has a bitmap mode, which can be set to valid or blank. A value of [valid](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) indicates that the context's [output bitmap](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) refers to [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) that was acquired via [`transferFromImageBitmap()`](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface). A value [blank](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) indicates that the context's [output bitmap](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) is a default transparent bitmap.

An [`ImageBitmapRenderingContext`](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) object also has an alpha flag, which can be set to true or false. When an [`ImageBitmapRenderingContext`](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) object has its [alpha](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) flag set to false, the contents of the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element to which the context is bound are obtained by compositing the context's [output bitmap](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) onto an [opaque black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#opaque-black) bitmap of the same size using the [source-over](https://drafts.csswg.org/compositing/#porterduffcompositingoperators_srcover) compositing operator. If the [alpha](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) flag is set to true, then the [output bitmap](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) is used as the contents of the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element to which the context is bound. [\[COMPOSITE\]](#references)

> [!note]
> The step of compositing over an [opaque black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#opaque-black) bitmap ought to be elided whenever equivalent results can be obtained more efficiently by other means.

---

When a user agent is required to set an `ImageBitmapRenderingContext`'s output bitmap, with a context argument that is an [`ImageBitmapRenderingContext`](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) object and an optional argument bitmap that refers to [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface), it must run these steps:
1. If a bitmap argument was not provided:
   1. Set context's [bitmap mode](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) to [blank](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface).
   2. Let canvas be the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element to which context is bound.
   3. Set context's [output bitmap](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) to be [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black) with a [natural width](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-width) equal to [the numeric value](#4125-the-canvas-element) of canvas's [`width`](#4125-the-canvas-element) attribute and a [natural height](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-height) equal to [the numeric value](#4125-the-canvas-element) of canvas's [`height`](#4125-the-canvas-element) attribute, those values being interpreted in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px).
   4. Set the [output bitmap](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface)'s [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag to true.
2. If a bitmap argument was provided:
   1. Set context's [bitmap mode](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) to [valid](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface).
   2. Set context's [output bitmap](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) to refer to the same underlying bitmap data as bitmap, without making a copy.

      > [!note]
      > The [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag of bitmap is included in the bitmap data to be referenced by context's [output bitmap](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface).

---

The `ImageBitmapRenderingContext` creation algorithm, which is passed a target and options, consists of running these steps:
1. Let settings be the result of [converting](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-type-mapping) options to the dictionary type [`ImageBitmapRenderingContextSettings`](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface). (This can throw an exception.)
2. Let context be a new [`ImageBitmapRenderingContext`](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) object.
3. Initialize context's [`canvas`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) attribute to point to target.
4. Set context's [output bitmap](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) to the same bitmap as target's bitmap (so that they are shared).
5. Run the steps to [set an `ImageBitmapRenderingContext`'s output bitmap](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) with context.
6. Initialize context's [alpha](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) flag to true.
7. Process each of the members of settings as follows:

   `alpha`

   If false, then set context's [alpha](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) flag to false.

8. Return context.

---

The `transferFromImageBitmap(bitmap)` method, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. Let bitmapContext be the [`ImageBitmapRenderingContext`](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) object on which the [`transferFromImageBitmap()`](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) method was called.
2. If bitmap is null, then run the steps to [set an ImageBitmapRenderingContext's output bitmap](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface), with bitmapContext as the *context* argument and no *bitmap* argument, then return.
3. If the value of bitmap's [\[\[Detached\]\]](#272-transferable-objects) internal slot is set to true, then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
4. Run the steps to [set an `ImageBitmapRenderingContext`'s output bitmap](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface), with the *context* argument equal to bitmapContext, and the *bitmap* argument referring to bitmap's underlying [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface).
5. Set the value of bitmap's [\[\[Detached\]\]](#272-transferable-objects) internal slot to true.
6. Unset bitmap's [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface).

##### 4.12.5.3 The [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) interface

```webidl
typedef (OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D or ImageBitmapRenderingContext or WebGLRenderingContext or WebGL2RenderingContext or GPUCanvasContext) OffscreenRenderingContext;

dictionary ImageEncodeOptions {
  DOMString type = "image/png";
  unrestricted double quality;
};

enum OffscreenRenderingContextId { "2d", "bitmaprenderer", "webgl", "webgl2", "webgpu" };

[Exposed=(Window,Worker), Transferable]
interface OffscreenCanvas : EventTarget {
  constructor([EnforceRange] unsigned long long width, [EnforceRange] unsigned long long height);

  attribute [EnforceRange] unsigned long long width;
  attribute [EnforceRange] unsigned long long height;

  OffscreenRenderingContext? getContext(OffscreenRenderingContextId contextId, optional any options = null);
  ImageBitmap transferToImageBitmap();
  Promise<Blob> convertToBlob(optional ImageEncodeOptions options = {});

  attribute EventHandler oncontextlost;
  attribute EventHandler oncontextrestored;
};
```

> [!note]
> [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) is an [`EventTarget`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget), so both [`OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D`](#412531-the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context) and WebGL can fire events at it. [`OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D`](#412531-the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context) can fire [`contextlost`](#events) and [`contextrestored`](#events), and WebGL can fire `webglcontextlost` and `webglcontextrestored`. [\[WEBGL\]](#references)

[`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) objects are used to create rendering contexts, much like an [`HTMLCanvasElement`](#4125-the-canvas-element), but with no connection to the DOM. This makes it possible to use canvas rendering contexts in [workers](#10-web-workers).

An [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object may hold a weak reference to a placeholder `canvas` element, which is typically in the DOM, whose embedded content is provided by the [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object. The bitmap of the [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object is pushed to the [placeholder `canvas` element](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) as part of the [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface)'s [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [update the rendering](#8173-processing-model) steps.

`offscreenCanvas = new OffscreenCanvas(width,
   height)`

Returns a new [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object that is not linked to a [placeholder `canvas` element](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface), and whose bitmap's size is determined by the width and height arguments.

`context = offscreenCanvas.getContext(contextId [,
   options ])`

Returns an object that exposes an API for drawing on the [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object. contextId specifies the desired API: "[`2d`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface)", "[`bitmaprenderer`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface)", "[`webgl`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface)", "[`webgl2`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface)", or "[`webgpu`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface)". options is handled by that API.

This specification defines the "[`2d`](#4125-the-canvas-element)" context below, which is similar but distinct from the "[`2d`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface)" context that is created from a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element. The WebGL specifications define the "[`webgl`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface)" and "[`webgl2`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface)" contexts. WebGPU defines the "[`webgpu`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface)" context. [\[WEBGL\]](#references) [\[WEBGPU\]](#references)

Returns null if the canvas has already been initialized with another context type (e.g., trying to get a "[`2d`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface)" context after getting a "[`webgl`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface)" context).

An [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object has an internal bitmap that is initialized when the object is created. The width and height of the [bitmap](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) are equal to the values of the [`width`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) and [`height`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) attributes of the [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object. Initially, all the bitmap's pixels are [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black).

An [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object has an internal inherited language and inherited direction set when the [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) is created.

An [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object can have a rendering context bound to it. Initially, it does not have a bound rendering context. To keep track of whether it has a rendering context or not, and what kind of rendering context it is, an [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object also has a context mode, which is initially none but can be changed to either 2d, bitmaprenderer, webgl, webgl2, webgpu, or detached by algorithms defined in this specification.

The `new OffscreenCanvas(width,
  height)` constructor steps are:
1. Initialize the [bitmap](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) to a rectangular array of [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black) pixels of the dimensions specified by width and height.
2. Initialize the [`width`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) to width.
3. Initialize the [`height`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) to height.
4. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [inherited language](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) to [explicitly unknown](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes).
5. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [inherited direction](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) to "`ltr`".
6. Let global be the [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
7. If global is a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object:
   1. Let element be the [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) of global's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object).
   2. If element is not null:
      1. Set the [inherited language](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) to element's [language](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes).
      2. Set the [inherited direction](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) to element's [directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute).

[`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) objects are [transferable](#272-transferable-objects). Their [transfer steps](#272-transferable-objects), given value and dataHolder, are as follows:
1. If value's [context mode](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) is not equal to [none](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface), then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Set value's [context mode](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) to [detached](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface).
3. Let width and height be the dimensions of value's [bitmap](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface).
4. Let language and direction be the values of value's [inherited language](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) and [inherited direction](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface).
5. Unset value's [bitmap](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface).
6. Set dataHolder.\[\[Width\]\] to width and dataHolder.\[\[Height\]\] to height.
7. Set dataHolder.\[\[Language\]\] to language and dataHolder.\[\[Direction\]\] to direction.
8. Set dataHolder.\[\[PlaceholderCanvas\]\] to be a weak reference to value's [placeholder `canvas` element](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface), if value has one, or null if it does not.

Their [transfer-receiving steps](#272-transferable-objects), given dataHolder and value, are:
1. Initialize value's [bitmap](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) to a rectangular array of [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black) pixels with width given by dataHolder.\[\[Width\]\] and height given by dataHolder.\[\[Height\]\].
2. Set value's [inherited language](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) to dataHolder.\[\[Language\]\] and its [inherited direction](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) to dataHolder.\[\[Direction\]\].
3. If dataHolder.\[\[PlaceholderCanvas\]\] is not null, set value's [placeholder `canvas` element](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) to dataHolder.\[\[PlaceholderCanvas\]\] (while maintaining the weak reference semantics).

---

The `getContext(contextId,
  options)` method of an [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. If options is not an [object](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-object), then set options to null.
2. Set options to the result of [converting](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-type-mapping) options to a JavaScript value.
3. Run the steps in the cell of the following table whose column header matches this [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object's [context mode](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) and whose row header matches contextId:

   •

   Let context be the result of running the [offscreen 2D context creation algorithm](#412531-the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) and options.

   •

   Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [context mode](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) to [2d](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface).

   •

   Return context.

   •

   Let context be the result of running the [`ImageBitmapRenderingContext` creation algorithm](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) and options.

   •

   Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [context mode](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) to [bitmaprenderer](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface).

   •

   Return context.

   •

   Let context be the result of following the instructions given in the WebGL specifications' *Context Creation* sections. [\[WEBGL\]](#references)

   •

   If context is null, then return null; otherwise set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [context mode](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) to [webgl](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) or [webgl2](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface).

   •

   Return context.

   •

   Let context be the result of following the instructions given in WebGPU's [Canvas Rendering](https://gpuweb.github.io/gpuweb/#canvas-rendering) section. [\[WEBGPU\]](#references)

   •

   If context is null, then return null; otherwise set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [context mode](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) to [webgpu](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface).

   •

   Return context.

   |  | [none](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) | [2d](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) | [bitmaprenderer](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) | [webgl](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) or [webgl2](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) | [webgpu](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) | [detached](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
   | "`2d`" |  | Return the same object as was returned the last time the method was invoked with this same first argument. | Return null. | Return null. | Return null. | Throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException). |
   | "`bitmaprenderer`" |  | Return null. | Return the same object as was returned the last time the method was invoked with this same first argument. | Return null. | Return null. | Throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException). |
   | "`webgl`" or "`webgl2`" |  | Return null. | Return null. | Return the same value as was returned the last time the method was invoked with this same first argument. | Return null. | Throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException). |
   | "`webgpu`" |  | Return null. | Return null. | Return null. | Return the same value as was returned the last time the method was invoked with this same first argument. | Throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException). |

---

`offscreenCanvas.width [
   = value ]`

`offscreenCanvas.height [
   = value ]`

These attributes return the dimensions of the [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object's [bitmap](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface).

They can be set, to replace the [bitmap](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) with a new, [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black) bitmap of the specified dimensions (effectively resizing it).

If either the `width` or `height` attributes of an [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object are set (to a new value or to the same value as before) and the [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object's [context mode](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) is [2d](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface), then [reset the rendering context to its default state](#412513-the-canvas-state) and resize the [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object's [bitmap](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) to the new values of the [`width`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) and [`height`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) attributes.

The resizing behavior for "[`webgl`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface)" and "[`webgl2`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface)" contexts is defined in the WebGL specifications. [\[WEBGL\]](#references)

The resizing behavior for "[`webgpu`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface)" context is defined in WebGPU. [\[WEBGPU\]](#references)

> [!note]
> If an [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object whose dimensions were changed has a [placeholder `canvas` element](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface), then the [placeholder `canvas` element](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface)'s [natural size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions) will only be updated during the [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface)'s [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [update the rendering](#8173-processing-model) steps.

`promise = offscreenCanvas.convertToBlob([options])`

Returns a promise that will fulfill with a new [`Blob`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-Blob) object representing a file containing the image in the [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object.

The argument, if provided, is a dictionary that controls the encoding options of the image file to be created. The [`type`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) field specifies the file format and has a default value of "[`image/png`](#mime-types)"; that type is also used if the requested type isn't supported. If the image format supports variable quality (such as "[`image/jpeg`](#mime-types)"), then the [`quality`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) field is a number in the range 0.0 to 1.0 inclusive indicating the desired quality level for the resulting image.

`canvas.transferToImageBitmap()`

Returns a newly created [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) object with the image in the [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object. The image in the [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object is replaced with a new blank image.

The `convertToBlob(options)` method steps are:
1. If the value of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [\[\[Detached\]\]](#272-transferable-objects) internal slot is true, then return [a promise rejected with](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#a-promise-rejected-with) an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [context mode](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) is [2d](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) and the rendering context's [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings)'s [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag is set to false, then return [a promise rejected with](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#a-promise-rejected-with) a ["`SecurityError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
3. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [bitmap](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) has no pixels (i.e., either its horizontal dimension or its vertical dimension is zero), then return [a promise rejected with](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#a-promise-rejected-with) an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
4. Let bitmap be a copy of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [bitmap](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface).
5. Let result be a new promise object.
6. Let global be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant).
7. Run these steps [in parallel](#211-parallelism):
   1. Let file be [a serialization of bitmap as a file](#41255-serializing-bitmaps-to-a-file), with options's `type` and `quality` if present.
   2. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [canvas blob serialization task source](#4125-the-canvas-element) given global to run these steps:
      1. If file is null, then reject result with an ["`EncodingError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#encodingerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
      2. Otherwise, resolve result with a new [`Blob`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-Blob) object, created in global's [relevant realm](#81334-relevant), representing file. [\[FILEAPI\]](#references)
8. Return result.

The `transferToImageBitmap()` method, when invoked, must run the following steps:
1. If the value of this [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object's [\[\[Detached\]\]](#272-transferable-objects) internal slot is set to true, then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. If this [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object's [context mode](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) is set to [none](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface), then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
3. Let image be a newly created [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) object that references the same underlying bitmap data as this [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object's [bitmap](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface).
4. Set this [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object's [bitmap](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) to reference a newly created bitmap of the same dimensions and color space as the previous bitmap, and with its pixels initialized to [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black), or [opaque black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#opaque-black) if the rendering context's [alpha](#412512-the-canvas-settings) is false.

   > [!note]
   > This means that if the rendering context of this [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) is a [`WebGLRenderingContext`](https://www.khronos.org/registry/webgl/specs/latest/1.0/#WebGLRenderingContext), the value of [`preserveDrawingBuffer`](https://www.khronos.org/registry/webgl/specs/latest/1.0/#WebGLContextAttributes) will have no effect. [\[WEBGL\]](#references)

5. Return image.

The following are the [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers) (and their corresponding [event handler event types](#8181-event-handlers)) that must be supported, as [event handler IDL attributes](#8181-event-handlers), by all objects implementing the [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) interface:

| [Event handler](#8181-event-handlers) | [Event handler event type](#8181-event-handlers) |
| --- | --- |
| `oncontextlost` | [`contextlost`](#events) |
| `oncontextrestored` | [`contextrestored`](#events) |

###### 4.12.5.3.1 The offscreen 2D rendering context

```webidl
[Exposed=(Window,Worker)]
interface OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D {
  readonly attribute OffscreenCanvas canvas;
};

OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasSettings;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasState;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasTransform;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasCompositing;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasImageSmoothing;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasFillStrokeStyles;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasShadowStyles;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasFilters;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasRect;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasDrawPath;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasText;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasDrawImage;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasImageData;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasPathDrawingStyles;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasTextDrawingStyles;
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D includes CanvasPath;
```

The [`OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D`](#412531-the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context) object is a rendering context for drawing to the [bitmap](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) of an [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object. It is similar to the [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) object, with the following differences:
- there is no support for [user interface](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) features;
- its [`canvas`](#412531-the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context) attribute refers to an [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object rather than a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element;

An [`OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D`](#412531-the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context) object has an associated `OffscreenCanvas` object, which is the [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object from which the [`OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D`](#412531-the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context) object was created.

`offscreenCanvas = offscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D.canvas`

Returns the [associated `OffscreenCanvas` object](#412531-the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context).

The offscreen 2D context creation algorithm, which is passed a target (an [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) object) and optionally some arguments, consists of running the following steps:
1. If the algorithm was passed some arguments, let arg be the first such argument. Otherwise, let arg be undefined.
2. Let settings be the result of [converting](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-type-mapping) arg to the dictionary type [`CanvasRenderingContext2DSettings`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context). (This can throw an exception.)
3. Let context be a new [`OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D`](#412531-the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context) object.
4. Set context's [associated `OffscreenCanvas` object](#412531-the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context) to target.
5. Run the [canvas settings output bitmap initialization algorithm](#412512-the-canvas-settings), given context and settings.
6. Set context's [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings) to a newly created bitmap with the dimensions specified by the [`width`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) and [`height`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) attributes of target, and set target's bitmap to the same bitmap (so that they are shared).
7. If context's [alpha](#412512-the-canvas-settings) flag is set to true, initialize all the pixels of context's [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings) to [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black). Otherwise, initialize the pixels to [opaque black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#opaque-black).
8. Return context.

> [!note]
> Implementations are encouraged to short-circuit the graphics update steps of the [window event loop](#8171-definitions) for the purposes of updating the contents of a [placeholder `canvas` element](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) to the display. This could mean, for example, that the bitmap contents are copied directly to a graphics buffer that is mapped to the physical display location of the [placeholder `canvas` element](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface). This or similar short-circuiting approaches can significantly reduce display latency, especially in cases where the [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) is updated from a [worker event loop](#8171-definitions) and the [window event loop](#8171-definitions) of the [placeholder `canvas` element](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) is busy. However, such shortcuts cannot have any script-observable side-effects. This means that the committed bitmap still needs to be sent to the [placeholder `canvas` element](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface), in case the element is used as a [`CanvasImageSource`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context), as an [`ImageBitmapSource`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface), or in case [`toDataURL()`](#4125-the-canvas-element) or [`toBlob()`](#4125-the-canvas-element) are called on it.

The `canvas` attribute, on getting, must return this [`OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D`](#412531-the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context)'s [associated `OffscreenCanvas` object](#412531-the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context).

##### 4.12.5.4 Color spaces and color space conversion

```webidl
enum PredefinedColorSpace { "srgb", "srgb-linear", "display-p3", "display-p3-linear" };
```

The [`PredefinedColorSpace`](#41254-color-spaces-and-color-space-conversion) enumeration is used to specify the [color space](#412512-the-canvas-settings) of the canvas's backing store.

The "`srgb`" value indicates the ['srgb'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#valdef-color-srgb) color space.

The "`srgb-linear`" value indicates the ['srgb-linear'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#valdef-color-srgb-linear) color space.

The "`display-p3`" value indicates the ['display-p3'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#valdef-color-display-p3) color space.

The "`display-p3-linear`" value indicates the ['display-p3-linear'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#display-p3-linear-space) color space.

[Color space conversion](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#color-conversion) must be applied to the canvas's backing store when rendering the canvas to the output device.

> [!note]
> The algorithm for converting between color spaces can be found in the [Converting Colors](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#color-conversion) section of CSS Color. This color space conversion is identical to the color space conversion that would be applied to an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element with a color profile that specifies the same [color space](#412512-the-canvas-settings) as the canvas's backing store. [\[CSSCOLOR\]](#references)

##### 4.12.5.5 Serializing bitmaps to a file

When a user agent is to create a serialization of the bitmap as a file, given a type and an optional quality, it must create an image file in the format given by type. If an error occurs during the creation of the image file (e.g. an internal encoder error), then the result of the serialization is null. [\[PNG\]](#references)

The image file's pixel data must be the bitmap's pixel data scaled to one image pixel per coordinate space unit, and if the file format used supports encoding resolution metadata, the resolution must be given as 96dpi (one image pixel per [CSS pixel](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px)).

If type is supplied, then it must be interpreted as a [MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type) giving the format to use. If the type has any parameters, then it must be treated as not supported.

> [!example]
> For example, the value "[`image/png`](#mime-types)" would mean to generate a PNG image, the value "[`image/jpeg`](#mime-types)" would mean to generate a JPEG image, and the value "[`image/svg+xml`](#mime-types)" would mean to generate an SVG image (which would require that the user agent track how the bitmap was generated, an unlikely, though potentially awesome, feature).

User agents must support PNG ("[`image/png`](#mime-types)"). User agents may support other types. If the user agent does not support the requested type, then it must create the file using the PNG format. [\[PNG\]](#references)

User agents must [convert the provided type to ASCII lowercase](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) before establishing if they support that type.

For image types that do not support an alpha component, the serialized image must be the bitmap image composited onto an [opaque black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#opaque-black) background using the [source-over](https://drafts.csswg.org/compositing/#porterduffcompositingoperators_srcover) compositing operator.

For image types that support color profiles, the serialized image must include a color profile indicating the color space of the underlying bitmap. For image types that do not support color profiles, the serialized image must be [converted](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#color-conversion) to the ['srgb'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#valdef-color-srgb) color space using ['relative-colorimetric'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color-5/#valdef-color-profile-rendering-intent-relative-colorimetric) rendering intent.

> [!note]
> Thus, in the 2D context, calling the [`drawImage()`](#4125115-drawing-images) method to render the output of the [`toDataURL()`](#4125-the-canvas-element) or [`toBlob()`](#4125-the-canvas-element) method to the canvas, given the appropriate dimensions, has no visible effect beyond, at most, clipping colors of the canvas to a more narrow gamut.

For image types that support multiple bit depths, the serialized image must use the bit depth that best preserves content of the underlying bitmap.

> [!example]
> For example, when serializing a 2D context that has [color type](#412512-the-canvas-settings) of [float16](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) to type "[`image/png`](#mime-types)", the resulting image would have 16 bits per sample. This serialization will still lose significant detail (all values less than 0.5/65535 would be clamped to 0, and all values greater than 1 would be clamped to 1).

If type is an image format that supports variable quality (such as "[`image/jpeg`](#mime-types)"), quality is given, and type is not "[`image/png`](#mime-types)", then, if quality [is a Number](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ecmascript-language-types-number-type) in the range 0.0 to 1.0 inclusive, the user agent must treat quality as the desired quality level. Otherwise, the user agent must use its default quality value, as if the quality argument had not been given.

> [!note]
> The use of type-testing here, instead of simply declaring quality as a Web IDL `double`, is a historical artifact.

> [!note]
> Different implementations can have slightly different interpretations of "quality". When the quality is not specified, an implementation-specific default is used that represents a reasonable compromise between compression ratio, image quality, and encoding time.

##### 4.12.5.6 Security with [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) elements

*This section is non-normative.*

**Information leakage** can occur if scripts from one [origin](#711-origins) can access information (e.g. read pixels) from images from another origin (one that isn't the [same](#711-origins)).

To mitigate this, bitmaps used with [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) elements, [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) objects, and [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) objects are defined to have a flag indicating whether they are [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element). All bitmaps start with their [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) set to true. The flag is set to false when cross-origin images are used.

The [`toDataURL()`](#4125-the-canvas-element), [`toBlob()`](#4125-the-canvas-element), and [`getImageData()`](#4125116-pixel-manipulation) methods check the flag and will throw a ["`SecurityError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) rather than leak cross-origin data.

The value of the [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag is propagated from a source's bitmap to a new [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) object by [`createImageBitmap()`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface). Conversely, a destination [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element's bitmap will have its [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flags set to false by [`drawImage`](#4125115-drawing-images) if the source image is an [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) object whose bitmap has its [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag set to false.

The flag can be reset in certain situations; for example, when changing the value of the [`width`](#4125-the-canvas-element) or the [`height`](#4125-the-canvas-element) content attribute of the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element to which a [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) is bound, the bitmap is cleared and its [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag is reset.

When using an [`ImageBitmapRenderingContext`](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface), the value of the [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag is propagated from [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) objects when they are transferred to the [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) via [transferFromImageBitmap()](#412522-the-imagebitmaprenderingcontext-interface).

##### 4.12.5.7 Premultiplied alpha and the 2D rendering context

Premultiplied alpha refers to one way of representing transparency in an image, the other being non-premultiplied alpha.

Under non-premultiplied alpha, the red, green, and blue components of a pixel represent that pixel's color, and its alpha component represents that pixel's opacity.

Under premultiplied alpha, however, the red, green, and blue components of a pixel represent the amounts of color that the pixel adds to the image, and its alpha component represents the amount that the pixel obscures whatever is behind it.

> [!example]
> For instance, assuming the color components range from 0 (off) to 255 (full intensity), these example colors are represented in the following ways:
> 
> | CSS color representation | Premultiplied representation | Non-premultiplied representation | Description of color | Image of color blended above other content |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> | rgba(255, 127, 0, 1) | 255, 127, 0, 255 | 255, 127, 0, 255 | Completely-opaque orange | ![An opaque orange circle sits atop a background](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/premultiplied-example-1.png) |
> | rgba(255, 255, 0, 0.5) | 127, 127, 0, 127 | 255, 255, 0, 127 | Halfway-opaque yellow | ![A yellow circle, halfway transparent, sits atop a background](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/premultiplied-example-2.png) |
> | Unrepresentable | 255, 127, 0, 127 | Unrepresentable | Additive halfway-opaque orange | ![An orange circle somewhat brightens the background that it sits atop](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/premultiplied-example-3.png) |
> | Unrepresentable | 255, 127, 0, 0 | Unrepresentable | Additive fully-transparent orange | ![An orange circle completely brightens the background that it sits atop](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/premultiplied-example-4.png) |
> | rgba(255, 127, 0, 0) | 0, 0, 0, 0 | 255, 127, 0, 0 | Fully-transparent ("invisible") orange | ![An empty background with nothing atop it](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/premultiplied-example-5.png) |
> | rgba(0, 127, 255, 0) | 0, 0, 0, 0 | 255, 127, 0, 0 | Fully-transparent ("invisible") turquoise | ![An empty background with nothing atop it](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/premultiplied-example-5.png) |

Converting a color value from a non-premultiplied representation to a premultiplied one involves multiplying the color's red, green, and blue components by its alpha component (remapping the range of the alpha component such that "fully transparent" is 0, and "fully opaque" is 1).

Converting a color value from a premultiplied representation to a non-premultiplied one involves the inverse: dividing the color's red, green, and blue components by its alpha component.

As certain colors can only be represented under premultiplied alpha (for instance, additive colors), and others can only be represented under non-premultiplied alpha (for instance, "invisible" colors which hold certain red, green, and blue values even with no opacity); and division and multiplication using finite precision entails a loss of accuracy, converting between premultiplied and non-premultiplied alpha is a lossy operation on colors that are not fully opaque.

A [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context)'s [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings) and an [`OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D`](#412531-the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context)'s [output bitmap](#412512-the-canvas-settings) must use premultiplied alpha to represent transparent colors.

> [!note]
> It is important for canvas bitmaps to represent colors using premultiplied alpha because it affects the range of representable colors. While additive colors cannot currently be drawn onto canvases directly because CSS colors are non-premultiplied and cannot represent them, it is still possible to, for instance, draw additive colors onto a WebGL canvas and then draw that WebGL canvas onto a 2D canvas via [`drawImage()`](#4125115-drawing-images).

### 4.13 Custom elements

#### 4.13.1 Introduction

*This section is non-normative.*

[Custom elements](#4133-core-concepts) provide a way for authors to build their own fully-featured DOM elements. Although authors could always use non-standard elements in their documents, with application-specific behavior added after the fact by scripting or similar, such elements have historically been non-conforming and not very functional. By [defining](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) a custom element, authors can inform the parser how to properly construct an element and how elements of that class should react to changes.

Custom elements are part of a larger effort to "rationalise the platform", by explaining existing platform features (like the elements of HTML) in terms of lower-level author-exposed extensibility points (like custom element definition). Although today there are many limitations on the capabilities of custom elements—both functionally and semantically—that prevent them from fully explaining the behaviors of HTML's existing elements, we hope to shrink this gap over time.

##### 4.13.1.1 Creating an autonomous custom element

*This section is non-normative.*

For the purposes of illustrating how to create an [autonomous custom element](#4133-core-concepts), let's define a custom element that encapsulates rendering a small icon for a country flag. Our goal is to be able to use it like so:

```html
<flag-icon country="nl"></flag-icon>
```

To do this, we first declare a class for the custom element, extending [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom):

```javascript
class FlagIcon extends HTMLElement {
  constructor() {
    super();
    this._countryCode = null;
  }

  static observedAttributes = ["country"];

  attributeChangedCallback(name, oldValue, newValue) {
    // name will always be "country" due to observedAttributes
    this._countryCode = newValue;
    this._updateRendering();
  }
  connectedCallback() {
    this._updateRendering();
  }

  get country() {
    return this._countryCode;
  }
  set country(v) {
    this.setAttribute("country", v);
  }

  _updateRendering() {
    // Left as an exercise for the reader. But, you'll probably want to
    // check this.ownerDocument.defaultView to see if we've been
    // inserted into a document with a browsing context, and avoid
    // doing any work if not.
  }
}
```

We then need to use this class to define the element:

```javascript
customElements.define("flag-icon", FlagIcon);
```

At this point, our above code will work! The parser, whenever it sees the `flag-icon` tag, will construct a new instance of our `FlagIcon` class, and tell our code about its new `country` attribute, which we then use to set the element's internal state and update its rendering (when appropriate).

You can also create `flag-icon` elements using the DOM API:

```javascript
const flagIcon = document.createElement("flag-icon")
flagIcon.country = "jp"
document.body.appendChild(flagIcon)
```

Finally, we can also use the [custom element constructor](#4133-core-concepts) itself. That is, the above code is equivalent to:

```javascript
const flagIcon = new FlagIcon()
flagIcon.country = "jp"
document.body.appendChild(flagIcon)
```

##### 4.13.1.2 Creating a form-associated custom element

*This section is non-normative.*

Adding a static `formAssociated` property, with a true value, makes an [autonomous custom element](#4133-core-concepts) a [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts). The [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) interface helps you to implement functions and properties common to form control elements.

```javascript
class MyCheckbox extends HTMLElement {
  static formAssociated = true;
  static observedAttributes = ['checked'];

  constructor() {
    super();
    this._internals = this.attachInternals();
    this.addEventListener('click', this._onClick.bind(this));
  }

  get form() { return this._internals.form; }
  get name() { return this.getAttribute('name'); }
  get type() { return this.localName; }

  get checked() { return this.hasAttribute('checked'); }
  set checked(flag) { this.toggleAttribute('checked', Boolean(flag)); }

  attributeChangedCallback(name, oldValue, newValue) {
    // name will always be "checked" due to observedAttributes
    this._internals.setFormValue(this.checked ? 'on' : null);
  }

  _onClick(event) {
    this.checked = !this.checked;
  }
}
customElements.define('my-checkbox', MyCheckbox);
```

You can use the custom element `my-checkbox` like a built-in form-associated element. For example, putting it in [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) or [`label`](#4104-the-label-element) associates the `my-checkbox` element with them, and submitting the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) will send data provided by `my-checkbox` implementation.

```html
<form action="..." method="...">
  <label><my-checkbox name="agreed"></my-checkbox> I read the agreement.</label>
  <input type="submit">
</form>

```

##### 4.13.1.3 Creating a custom element with default accessible roles, states, and properties

*This section is non-normative.*

By using the appropriate properties of [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface), your custom element can have default accessibility semantics. The following code expands our form-associated checkbox from the previous section to properly set its default role and checkedness, as viewed by accessibility technology:

```javascript
class MyCheckbox extends HTMLElement {
  static formAssociated = true;
  static observedAttributes = ['checked'];

  constructor() {
    super();
    this._internals = this.attachInternals();
    this.addEventListener('click', this._onClick.bind(this));

    this._internals.role = 'checkbox';
    this._internals.ariaChecked = 'false';
  }

  get form() { return this._internals.form; }
  get name() { return this.getAttribute('name'); }
  get type() { return this.localName; }

  get checked() { return this.hasAttribute('checked'); }
  set checked(flag) { this.toggleAttribute('checked', Boolean(flag)); }

  attributeChangedCallback(name, oldValue, newValue) {
    // name will always be "checked" due to observedAttributes
    this._internals.setFormValue(this.checked ? 'on' : null);
    this._internals.ariaChecked = this.checked;
  }

  _onClick(event) {
    this.checked = !this.checked;
  }
}
customElements.define('my-checkbox', MyCheckbox);
```

Note that, like for built-in elements, these are only defaults, and can be overridden by the page author using the [`role`](#219-dependencies) and [`aria-*`](#219-dependencies) attributes:

```html
<!-- This markup is non-conforming -->
<input type="checkbox" checked role="button" aria-checked="false">
```

```html
<!-- This markup is probably not what the custom element author intended -->
<my-checkbox role="button" checked aria-checked="false">
```

Custom element authors are encouraged to state what aspects of their accessibility semantics are strong native semantics, i.e., should not be overridden by users of the custom element. In our example, the author of the `my-checkbox` element would state that its [role](https://w3c.github.io/aria/#dfn-role) and [`aria-checked`](https://w3c.github.io/aria/#aria-checked) values are strong native semantics, thus discouraging code such as the above.

##### 4.13.1.4 Creating a customized built-in element

*This section is non-normative.*

[Customized built-in elements](#4133-core-concepts) are a distinct kind of [custom element](#4133-core-concepts), which are defined slightly differently and used very differently compared to [autonomous custom elements](#4133-core-concepts). They exist to allow reuse of behaviors from the existing elements of HTML, by extending those elements with new custom functionality. This is important since many of the existing behaviors of HTML elements can unfortunately not be duplicated by using purely [autonomous custom elements](#4133-core-concepts). Instead, [customized built-in elements](#4133-core-concepts) allow the installation of custom construction behavior, lifecycle hooks, and prototype chain onto existing elements, essentially "mixing in" these capabilities on top of the already-existing element.

[Customized built-in elements](#4133-core-concepts) require a distinct syntax from [autonomous custom elements](#4133-core-concepts) because user agents and other software key off an element's local name in order to identify the element's semantics and behavior. That is, the concept of [customized built-in elements](#4133-core-concepts) building on top of existing behavior depends crucially on the extended elements retaining their original local name.

In this example, we'll be creating a [customized built-in element](#4133-core-concepts) named `plastic-button`, which behaves like a normal button but gets fancy animation effects added whenever you click on it. We start by defining a class, just like before, although this time we extend [`HTMLButtonElement`](#4106-the-button-element) instead of [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom):

```javascript
class PlasticButton extends HTMLButtonElement {
  constructor() {
    super();

    this.addEventListener("click", () => {
      // Draw some fancy animation effects!
    });
  }
}
```

When defining our custom element, we have to also specify the [`extends`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) option:

```javascript
customElements.define("plastic-button", PlasticButton, { extends: "button" });
```

In general, the name of the element being extended cannot be determined simply by looking at what element interface it extends, as many elements share the same interface (such as [`q`](#457-the-q-element) and [`blockquote`](#444-the-blockquote-element) both sharing [`HTMLQuoteElement`](#444-the-blockquote-element)).

To construct our [customized built-in element](#4133-core-concepts) from parsed HTML source text, we use the [`is`](#4133-core-concepts) attribute on a [`button`](#4106-the-button-element) element:

```html
<button is="plastic-button">Click Me!</button>
```

Trying to use a [customized built-in element](#4133-core-concepts) as an [autonomous custom element](#4133-core-concepts) will *not* work; that is, `<plastic-button>Click
  me?</plastic-button>` will simply create an [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom) with no special behavior.

If you need to create a customized built-in element programmatically, you can use the following form of [`createElement()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document):

```javascript
const plasticButton = document.createElement("button", { is: "plastic-button" });
plasticButton.textContent = "Click me!";
```

And as before, the constructor will also work:

```javascript
const plasticButton2 = new PlasticButton();
console.log(plasticButton2.localName);  // will output "button"
console.assert(plasticButton2 instanceof PlasticButton);
console.assert(plasticButton2 instanceof HTMLButtonElement);
```

Note that when creating a customized built-in element programmatically, the [`is`](#4133-core-concepts) attribute will not be present in the DOM, since it was not explicitly set. However, [it will be added to the output when serializing](#133-serializing-html-fragments):

```javascript
console.assert(!plasticButton.hasAttribute("is"));
console.log(plasticButton.outerHTML); // will output '<button is="plastic-button"></button>'
```

Regardless of how it is created, all of the ways in which [`button`](#4106-the-button-element) is special apply to such "plastic buttons" as well: their focus behavior, ability to participate in [form submission](#410223-form-submission-algorithm), the [`disabled`](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute) attribute, and so on.

[Customized built-in elements](#4133-core-concepts) are designed to allow extension of existing HTML elements that have useful user-agent supplied behavior or APIs. As such, they can only extend existing HTML elements defined in this specification, and cannot extend legacy elements such as [`bgsound`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`blink`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`isindex`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`keygen`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`multicol`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`nextid`](#162-non-conforming-features), or [`spacer`](#162-non-conforming-features) that have been defined to use [`HTMLUnknownElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom) as their [element interface](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

One reason for this requirement is future-compatibility: if a [customized built-in element](#4133-core-concepts) was defined that extended a currently-unknown element, for example `combobox`, this would prevent this specification from defining a `combobox` element in the future, as consumers of the derived [customized built-in element](#4133-core-concepts) would have come to depend on their base element having no interesting user-agent-supplied behavior.

##### 4.13.1.5 Drawbacks of autonomous custom elements

*This section is non-normative.*

As specified below, and alluded to above, simply defining and using an element called `taco-button` does not mean that such elements [represent](#322-elements-in-the-dom) buttons. That is, tools such as web browsers, search engines, or accessibility technology will not automatically treat the resulting element as a button just based on its defined name.

To convey the desired button semantics to a variety of users, while still using an [autonomous custom element](#4133-core-concepts), a number of techniques would need to be employed:
- The addition of the [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attribute would make the `taco-button` [focusable](#662-data-model). Note that if the `taco-button` were to become logically disabled, the [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attribute would need to be removed.
- The addition of an ARIA role and various ARIA states and properties helps convey semantics to accessibility technology. For example, setting the [role](https://w3c.github.io/aria/#dfn-role) to "[`button`](https://w3c.github.io/aria/#button)" will convey the semantics that this is a button, enabling users to successfully interact with the control using usual button-like interactions in their accessibility technology. Setting the [`aria-label`](https://w3c.github.io/aria/#aria-label) property is necessary to give the button an [accessible name](https://w3c.github.io/accname/#dfn-accessible-name), instead of having accessibility technology traverse its child text nodes and announce them. And setting the [`aria-disabled`](https://w3c.github.io/aria/#aria-disabled) state to "`true`" when the button is logically disabled conveys to accessibility technology the button's disabled state.
- The addition of event handlers to handle commonly-expected button behaviors helps convey the semantics of the button to web browser users. In this case, the most relevant event handler would be one that proxies appropriate [`keydown`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-keydown) events to become [`click`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click) events, so that you can activate the button both with keyboard and by clicking.
- In addition to any default visual styling provided for `taco-button` elements, the visual styling will also need to be updated to reflect changes in logical state, such as becoming disabled; that is, whatever style sheet has rules for `taco-button` will also need to have rules for `taco-button[disabled]`.

With these points in mind, a full-featured `taco-button` that took on the responsibility of conveying button semantics (including the ability to be disabled) might look something like this:

```javascript
class TacoButton extends HTMLElement {
  static observedAttributes = ["disabled"];

  constructor() {
    super();
    this._internals = this.attachInternals();
    this._internals.role = "button";

    this.addEventListener("keydown", e => {
      if (e.code === "Enter" || e.code === "Space") {
        this.dispatchEvent(new PointerEvent("click", {
          bubbles: true,
          cancelable: true
        }));
      }
    });

    this.addEventListener("click", e => {
      if (this.disabled) {
        e.preventDefault();
        e.stopImmediatePropagation();
      }
    });

    this._observer = new MutationObserver(() => {
      this._internals.ariaLabel = this.textContent;
    });
  }

  connectedCallback() {
    this.setAttribute("tabindex", "0");

    this._observer.observe(this, {
      childList: true,
      characterData: true,
      subtree: true
    });
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    this._observer.disconnect();
  }

  get disabled() {
    return this.hasAttribute("disabled");
  }
  set disabled(flag) {
    this.toggleAttribute("disabled", Boolean(flag));
  }

  attributeChangedCallback(name, oldValue, newValue) {
    // name will always be "disabled" due to observedAttributes
    if (this.disabled) {
      this.removeAttribute("tabindex");
      this._internals.ariaDisabled = "true";
    } else {
      this.setAttribute("tabindex", "0");
      this._internals.ariaDisabled = "false";
    }
  }
}
```

Even with this rather-complicated element definition, the element is not a pleasure to use for consumers: it will be continually "sprouting" [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attributes of its own volition, and its choice of `tabindex="0"` focusability behavior may not match the [`button`](#4106-the-button-element) behavior on the current platform.
