This is because as of now there is no way to specify default focus behavior for custom elements, forcing the use of the [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attribute to do so (even though it is usually reserved for allowing the consumer to override default behavior).

In contrast, a simple [customized built-in element](#4133-core-concepts), as shown in the previous section, would automatically inherit the semantics and behavior of the [`button`](#4106-the-button-element) element, with no need to implement these behaviors manually. In general, for any elements with nontrivial behavior and semantics that build on top of existing elements of HTML, [customized built-in elements](#4133-core-concepts) will be easier to develop, maintain, and consume.

##### 4.13.1.6 Upgrading elements after their creation

*This section is non-normative.*

Because [element definition](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) can occur at any time, a non-custom element could be [created](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), and then later become a [custom element](#4133-core-concepts) after an appropriate [definition](#4133-core-concepts) is registered. We call this process "upgrading" the element, from a normal element into a custom element.

[Upgrades](#4135-upgrades) enable scenarios where it may be preferable for [custom element definitions](#4133-core-concepts) to be registered after relevant elements have been initially created, such as by the parser. They allow progressive enhancement of the content in the custom element. For example, in the following HTML document the element definition for `img-viewer` is loaded asynchronously:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<title>Image viewer example</title>

<img-viewer filter="Kelvin">
  <img src="images/tree.jpg" alt="A beautiful tree towering over an empty savannah">
</img-viewer>

<script src="js/elements/img-viewer.js" async></script>
```

The definition for the `img-viewer` element here is loaded using a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element marked with the [`async`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute, placed after the `<img-viewer>` tag in the markup. While the script is loading, the `img-viewer` element will be treated as an undefined element, similar to a [`span`](#4526-the-span-element). Once the script loads, it will define the `img-viewer` element, and the existing `img-viewer` element on the page will be upgraded, applying the custom element's definition (which presumably includes applying an image filter identified by the string "Kelvin", enhancing the image's visual appearance).

---

Note that [upgrades](#4135-upgrades) only apply to elements in the document tree. (Formally, elements that are [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree).) An element that is not inserted into a document will stay un-upgraded. An example illustrates this point:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<title>Upgrade edge-cases example</title>

<example-element></example-element>

<script>
  "use strict";

  const inDocument = document.querySelector("example-element");
  const outOfDocument = document.createElement("example-element");

  // Before the element definition, both are HTMLElement:
  console.assert(inDocument instanceof HTMLElement);
  console.assert(outOfDocument instanceof HTMLElement);

  class ExampleElement extends HTMLElement {}
  customElements.define("example-element", ExampleElement);

  // After element definition, the in-document element was upgraded:
  console.assert(inDocument instanceof ExampleElement);
  console.assert(!(outOfDocument instanceof ExampleElement));

  document.body.appendChild(outOfDocument);

  // Now that we've moved the element into the document, it too was upgraded:
  console.assert(outOfDocument instanceof ExampleElement);
</script>
```

##### 4.13.1.7 Scoped custom element registries

To allow multiple libraries to co-exist without explicit coordination, [`CustomElementRegistry`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) can be used in a scoped fashion as well.

```javascript
const scoped = new CustomElementRegistry();
scoped.define("example-element", ExampleElement);

const element = document.createElement("example-element", { customElementRegistry: scoped });
```

A node with an associated scoped [`CustomElementRegistry`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) will use that registry for all its operations, such as when invoking [`setHTMLUnsafe()`](#852-html-parsing-methods).

##### 4.13.1.8 Exposing custom element states

Built-in elements provided by user agents have certain states that can change over time depending on user interaction and other factors, and are exposed to web authors through [pseudo-classes](https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#pseudo-class). For example, some form controls have the "invalid" state, which is exposed through the [`:invalid`](#4163-pseudo-classes) [pseudo-class](https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#pseudo-class).

Like built-in elements, [custom elements](#4133-core-concepts) can have various states to be in too, and [custom element](#4133-core-concepts) authors want to expose these states in a similar fashion as the built-in elements.

This is done via the [`:state()`](#4163-pseudo-classes) pseudo-class. A custom element author can use the [`states`](#41375-custom-state-pseudo-class) property of [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) to add and remove such custom states, which are then exposed as arguments to the [`:state()`](#4163-pseudo-classes) pseudo-class.

> [!example]
> The following shows how [`:state()`](#4163-pseudo-classes) can be used to style a custom checkbox element. Assume that `LabeledCheckbox` doesn't expose its "checked" state via a content attribute.
> 
> ```html
> <script>
> class LabeledCheckbox extends HTMLElement {
>   constructor() {
>     super();
>     this._internals = this.attachInternals();
>     this.addEventListener('click', this._onClick.bind(this));
> 
>     const shadowRoot = this.attachShadow({mode: 'closed'});
>     shadowRoot.innerHTML =
>       `<style>
>        :host::before {
>          content: '[ ]';
>          white-space: pre;
>          font-family: monospace;
>        }
>        :host(:state(checked))::before { content: '[x]' }
>        </style>
>        <slot>Label</slot>`;
>   }
> 
>   get checked() { return this._internals.states.has('checked'); }
> 
>   set checked(flag) {
>     if (flag)
>       this._internals.states.add('checked');
>     else
>       this._internals.states.delete('checked');
>   }
> 
>   _onClick(event) {
>     this.checked = !this.checked;
>   }
> }
> 
> customElements.define('labeled-checkbox', LabeledCheckbox);
> </script>
> 
> <style>
> labeled-checkbox { border: dashed red; }
> labeled-checkbox:state(checked) { border: solid; }
> </style>
> 
> <labeled-checkbox>You need to check this</labeled-checkbox>
> ```

> [!example]
> Custom pseudo-classes can even target shadow parts. An extension of the above example shows this:
> 
> ```html
> <script>
> class QuestionBox extends HTMLElement {
>   constructor() {
>     super();
>     const shadowRoot = this.attachShadow({mode: 'closed'});
>     shadowRoot.innerHTML =
>       `<div><slot>Question</slot></div>
>        <labeled-checkbox part='checkbox'>Yes</labeled-checkbox>`;
>   }
> }
> customElements.define('question-box', QuestionBox);
> </script>
> 
> <style>
> question-box::part(checkbox) { color: red; }
> question-box::part(checkbox):state(checked) { color: green; }
> </style>
> 
> <question-box>Continue?</question-box>
> ```

#### 4.13.2 Requirements for custom element constructors and reactions

When authoring [custom element constructors](#4133-core-concepts), authors are bound by the following conformance requirements:
- A parameter-less call to `super()` must be the first statement in the constructor body, to establish the correct prototype chain and **this** value before any further code is run.
- A `return` statement must not appear anywhere inside the constructor body, unless it is a simple early-return (`return` or `return
     this`).
- The constructor must not use the [`document.write()`](#843-documentwrite) or [`document.open()`](#841-opening-the-input-stream) methods.
- The element's attributes and children must not be inspected, as in the non-[upgrade](#4135-upgrades) case none will be present, and relying on upgrades makes the element less usable.
- The element must not gain any attributes or children, as this violates the expectations of consumers who use the [`createElement`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) or [`createElementNS`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) methods.
- In general, work should be deferred to `connectedCallback` as much as possible—especially work involving fetching resources or rendering. However, note that `connectedCallback` can be called more than once, so any initialization work that is truly one-time will need a guard to prevent it from running twice.
- In general, the constructor should be used to set up initial state and default values, and to set up event listeners and possibly a [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot).

Several of these requirements are checked during [element creation](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), either directly or indirectly, and failing to follow them will result in a custom element that cannot be instantiated by the parser or DOM APIs. This is true even if the work is done inside a constructor-initiated [microtask](#8171-definitions), as a [microtask checkpoint](#8173-processing-model) can occur immediately after construction.

When authoring [custom element reactions](#4136-custom-element-reactions), authors should avoid manipulating the node tree as this can lead to unexpected results.

> [!example]
> An element's `connectedCallback` can be queued before the element is disconnected, but as the callback queue is still processed, it results in a `connectedCallback` for an element that is no longer connected:
> 
> ```javascript
> class CParent extends HTMLElement {
>   connectedCallback() {
>     this.firstChild.remove();
>   }
> }
> customElements.define("c-parent", CParent);
> 
> class CChild extends HTMLElement {
>   connectedCallback() {
>     console.log("CChild connectedCallback: isConnected =", this.isConnected);
>   }
> }
> customElements.define("c-child", CChild);
> 
> const parent = new CParent(),
>       child = new CChild();
> parent.append(child);
> document.body.append(parent);
> 
> // Logs:
> // CChild connectedCallback: isConnected = false
> ```

##### 4.13.2.1 Preserving custom element state when moved

*This section is non-normative.*

When manipulating the DOM tree, an element can be [moved](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) in the tree while connected. This applies to custom elements as well. By default, the "`disconnectedCallback`" and "`connectedCallback`" would be called on the element, one after the other. This is done to maintain compatibility with existing custom elements that predate the [`moveBefore()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#426-mixin-parentnode) method. This means that by default, custom elements reset their state as if they were removed and re-inserted. In the example [above](#41315-drawbacks-of-autonomous-custom-elements), the impact would be that the observer would be disconnected and re-connected, and the tab index would be reset.

To opt in to a state-preserving behavior while [moving](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms), the author can implement a "`connectedMoveCallback`". The existence of this callback, even if empty, would supersede the default behavior of calling "`disconnectedCallback`" and "`connectedCallback`". "`connectedMoveCallback`" can also be an appropriate place to execute logic that depends on the element's ancestors. For example:

```javascript
class TacoButton extends HTMLElement {
  static observedAttributes = ["disabled"];

  constructor() {
    super();
    this._internals = this.attachInternals();
    this._internals.role = "button";

    this._observer = new MutationObserver(() => {
      this._internals.ariaLabel = this.textContent;
    });
  }

  _notifyMain() {
    if (this.parentElement.tagName === "MAIN") {
      // Execute logic that depends on ancestors.
    }
  }

  connectedCallback() {
    this.setAttribute("tabindex", "0");

    this._observer.observe(this, {
      childList: true,
      characterData: true,
      subtree: true
    });

    this._notifyMain();
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    this._observer.disconnect();
  }

  // Implementing this function would avoid resetting the tab index or re-registering the
  // mutation observer when this element is moved inside the DOM without being disconnected.
  connectedMoveCallback() {
    // The parent can change during a state-preserving move.
    this._notifyMain();
  }
}
```

#### 4.13.3 Core concepts

A custom element is an element that is [custom](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element). Informally, this means that its constructor and prototype are defined by the author, instead of by the user agent. This author-supplied constructor function is called the custom element constructor.

Two distinct types of [custom elements](#4133-core-concepts) can be defined:
- An autonomous custom element, which is defined with no [`extends`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) option. These types of custom elements have a local name equal to their [defined name](#4133-core-concepts).
- A customized built-in element, which is defined with an [`extends`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) option. These types of custom elements have a local name equal to the value passed in their [`extends`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) option, and their [defined name](#4133-core-concepts) is used as the value of the `is` attribute, which therefore must be a [valid custom element name](#4133-core-concepts).

After a [custom element](#4133-core-concepts) is [created](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), changing the value of the [`is`](#4133-core-concepts) attribute does not change the element's behavior, as it is saved on the element as its [`is` value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element).

[Autonomous custom elements](#4133-core-concepts) have the following element definition:

[Categories](#324-element-definitions):

[Flow content](#32522-flow-content).

[Phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content).

[Palpable content](#32528-palpable-content).

For [form-associated custom elements](#4133-core-concepts): [Listed](#4102-categories), [labelable](#4102-categories), [submittable](#4102-categories), and [resettable](#4102-categories) [form-associated element](#4102-categories).

[Contexts in which this element can be used](#324-element-definitions):

Where [phrasing content](#32525-phrasing-content) is expected.

[Content model](#324-element-definitions):

[Transparent](#3253-transparent-content-models).

[Content attributes](#324-element-definitions):

[Global attributes](#326-global-attributes), except the [`is`](#4133-core-concepts) attribute

[`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms), for [form-associated custom elements](#4133-core-concepts) — Associates the element with a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element

[`disabled`](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute), for [form-associated custom elements](#4133-core-concepts) — Whether the form control is disabled

[`readonly`](#4133-core-concepts), for [form-associated custom elements](#4133-core-concepts) — Affects [`willValidate`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api), plus any behavior added by the custom element author

[`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute), for [form-associated custom elements](#4133-core-concepts) — Name of the element to use for [form submission](#41022-form-submission) and in the [`form.elements`](#4103-the-form-element) API

Any other attribute that has no namespace (see prose).

[Accessibility considerations](#324-element-definitions):

For [form-associated custom elements](#4133-core-concepts): [for authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-form-associated-custom-element); [for implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-form-associated-custom-element).

Otherwise: [for authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-autonomous-custom-element); [for implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-autonomous-custom-element).

[Sanitization](#324-element-definitions):

[Uncategorized](#865-sanitization-constants).

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

Supplied by the element's author (inherits from [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom))

An [autonomous custom element](#4133-core-concepts) does not have any special meaning: it [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) its children. A [customized built-in element](#4133-core-concepts) inherits the semantics of the element that it extends.

Any namespace-less attribute that is relevant to the element's functioning, as determined by the element's author, may be specified on an [autonomous custom element](#4133-core-concepts), so long as the attribute name is a [valid attribute local name](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#14-name-validation) and contains no [ASCII upper alphas](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points). The exception is the [`is`](#4133-core-concepts) attribute, which must not be specified on an [autonomous custom element](#4133-core-concepts) (and which will have no effect if it is).

[Customized built-in elements](#4133-core-concepts) follow the normal requirements for attributes, based on the elements they extend. To add custom attribute-based behavior, use [`data-*`](#3266-embedding-custom-non-visible-data-with-the-data--attributes) attributes.

---

An [autonomous custom element](#4133-core-concepts) is called a form-associated custom element if the element is associated with a [custom element definition](#4133-core-concepts) whose [form-associated](#4133-core-concepts) field is set to true.

The [`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) attribute represents the [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts)'s name. The [`disabled`](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute) attribute is used to make the [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts) non-interactive and to prevent its [submission value](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements) from being submitted. The [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) attribute is used to explicitly associate the [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts) with its [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms).

The `readonly` attribute of [form-associated custom elements](#4133-core-concepts) specifies that the element is [barred from constraint validation](#410211-definitions). User agents don't provide any other behavior for the attribute, but custom element authors should, where possible, use its presence to make their control non-editable in some appropriate fashion, similar to the behavior for the [readonly](#410533-the-readonly-attribute) attribute on built-in form controls.

**Constraint validation**: If the [`readonly`](#4133-core-concepts) attribute is specified on a [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts), the element is [barred from constraint validation](#410211-definitions).

The [reset algorithm](#41023-resetting-a-form) for [form-associated custom elements](#4133-core-concepts) is to [enqueue a custom element callback reaction](#4136-custom-element-reactions) with the element, callback name "`formResetCallback`", and « ».

---

A string name is a valid custom element name if all of the following are true:
- name is a [valid element local name](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#14-name-validation);

  > [!note]
  > This ensures the custom element can be created with [`createElement()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

- name's 0th [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) is an [ASCII lower alpha](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points);

  > [!note]
  > This ensures the HTML parser will treat the name as a tag name instead of as text.

- name does not contain any [ASCII upper alphas](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points);

  > [!note]
  > This ensures the user agent can always treat HTML elements ASCII-case-insensitively.

- name contains a U+002D (-); and

  > [!note]
  > This is used for namespacing and to ensure forward compatibility (since no elements will be added to HTML, SVG, or MathML with hyphen-containing local names going forward).

- name is not one of the following:
  - "`annotation-xml`"
  - "`color-profile`"
  - "`font-face`"
  - "`font-face-src`"
  - "`font-face-uri`"
  - "`font-face-format`"
  - "`font-face-name`"
  - "`missing-glyph`"

  > [!note]
  > The list of names above is the summary of all hyphen-containing element names from the [applicable specifications](#2110-extensibility), namely SVG 2 and MathML. [\[SVG\]](#references) [\[MATHML\]](#references)

Apart from these restrictions, a large variety of names is allowed, to give maximum flexibility for use cases like `<math-α>` or `<emotion-😍>`.

---

A custom element definition describes a [custom element](#4133-core-concepts) and consists of:

A name

A [valid custom element name](#4133-core-concepts)

A local name

A local name

A constructor

A Web IDL [`CustomElementConstructor`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) callback function type value wrapping the [custom element constructor](#4133-core-concepts)

A list of observed attributes

A `sequence<DOMString>`

A collection of lifecycle callbacks

A map, whose keys are the strings "`connectedCallback`", "`disconnectedCallback`", "`connectedMoveCallback`", "`adoptedCallback`", "`attributeChangedCallback`", "`formAssociatedCallback`", "`formDisabledCallback`", "`formResetCallback`", and "`formStateRestoreCallback`". The corresponding values are either a Web IDL [`Function`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#common-Function) callback function type value, or null. By default the value of each entry is null.

A construction stack

A list, initially empty, that is manipulated by the [upgrade an element](#4135-upgrades) algorithm and the [HTML element constructors](#323-html-element-constructors). Each entry in the list will be either an element or an *already constructed* marker.

A form-associated boolean

If this is true, user agent treats elements associated to this [custom element definition](#4133-core-concepts) as [form-associated custom elements](#4133-core-concepts).

A disable internals boolean

Controls [`attachInternals()`](#4137-element-internals).

A disable shadow boolean

Controls [`attachShadow()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element).

To look up a custom element definition, given null or a [`CustomElementRegistry`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) object registry, string-or-null namespace, string localName, and string-or-null is, perform the following steps. They will return either a [custom element definition](#4133-core-concepts) or null:
1. If registry is null, then return null.
2. If namespace is not the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces), then return null.
3. If registry's [custom element definition set](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) an item with [name](#4133-core-concepts) and [local name](#4133-core-concepts) both equal to localName, then return that item.
4. If registry's [custom element definition set](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) an item with [name](#4133-core-concepts) equal to is and [local name](#4133-core-concepts) equal to localName, then return that item.
5. Return null.

#### 4.13.4 The [`CustomElementRegistry`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) interface

Each [similar-origin window agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism) has an associated active custom element constructor map, which is a [map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) of constructors to [`CustomElementRegistry`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) objects.

The [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) `customElements` getter steps are:
1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is a [`CustomElementRegistry`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) object.

   > [!note]
   > A [`Window`](#722-the-window-object)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object) is always created with a new [`CustomElementRegistry`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) object.

2. Return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface CustomElementRegistry {
  constructor();

  [CEReactions] undefined define(DOMString name, CustomElementConstructor constructor, optional ElementDefinitionOptions options = {});
  (CustomElementConstructor or undefined) get(DOMString name);
  DOMString? getName(CustomElementConstructor constructor);
  Promise<CustomElementConstructor> whenDefined(DOMString name);
  [CEReactions] undefined upgrade(Node root);
  [CEReactions] undefined initialize(Node root);
};

callback CustomElementConstructor = HTMLElement ();

dictionary ElementDefinitionOptions {
  DOMString extends;
};
```

Every [`CustomElementRegistry`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) has an is scoped, a boolean, initially false.

Every [`CustomElementRegistry`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) has a scoped document set, a [set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) of [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) objects, initially « ».

Every [`CustomElementRegistry`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) has a custom element definition set, a [set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) of [custom element definitions](#4133-core-concepts), initially « ». Lookup of items in this [set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) uses their [name](#4133-core-concepts), [local name](#4133-core-concepts), or [constructor](#4133-core-concepts).

Every [`CustomElementRegistry`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) also has an element definition is running boolean which is used to prevent reentrant invocations of [element definition](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface). It is initially false.

Every [`CustomElementRegistry`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) also has a when-defined promise map, a [map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) of [valid custom element names](#4133-core-concepts) to promises. It is used to implement the [`whenDefined()`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) method.

To look up a custom element registry, given a [`Node`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) object node:
1. If node is an [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) object, then return node's [custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element).
2. If node is a [`ShadowRoot`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) object, then return node's [custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot).
3. If node is a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object, then return node's [custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).
4. Return null.

`registry = window.customElements`

Returns the global's associated [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [`CustomElementRegistry`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) object.

`registry = new CustomElementRegistry()`

Constructs a new [`CustomElementRegistry`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) object, for scoped usage.

`registry.define(name,
   constructor)`

Defines a new [custom element](#4133-core-concepts), mapping the given name to the given constructor as an [autonomous custom element](#4133-core-concepts).

`registry.define(name, constructor,
   { extends: baseLocalName })`

Defines a new [custom element](#4133-core-concepts), mapping the given name to the given constructor as a [customized built-in element](#4133-core-concepts) for the [element type](#213-xml-compatibility) identified by the supplied baseLocalName. A ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) will be thrown upon trying to extend a [custom element](#4133-core-concepts) or an unknown element, or when registry is not a global [`CustomElementRegistry`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) object.

`registry.get(name)`

Retrieves the [custom element constructor](#4133-core-concepts) defined for the given [name](#4133-core-concepts). Returns undefined if there is no [custom element definition](#4133-core-concepts) with the given [name](#4133-core-concepts).

`registry.getName(constructor)`

Retrieves the given name for a [custom element](#4133-core-concepts) defined for the given [constructor](#4133-core-concepts). Returns null if there is no [custom element definition](#4133-core-concepts) with the given [constructor](#4133-core-concepts).

`registry.whenDefined(name)`

Returns a promise that will be fulfilled with the [custom element](#4133-core-concepts)'s constructor when a [custom element](#4133-core-concepts) becomes defined with the given name. (If such a [custom element](#4133-core-concepts) is already defined, the returned promise will be immediately fulfilled.) Returns a promise rejected with a ["`SyntaxError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if not given a [valid custom element name](#4133-core-concepts).

`registry.upgrade(root)`

[Tries to upgrade](#4135-upgrades) all [shadow-including inclusive descendant](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) elements of root, even if they are not [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree).

`registry.initialize(root)`

Each [inclusive descendant](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) of root with a null registry will have it updated to this [`CustomElementRegistry`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) object. A ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) will be thrown if this [`CustomElementRegistry`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) object is not for scoped usage and either root is a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) node or root's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is not this [`CustomElementRegistry`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) object.

The `new CustomElementRegistry()` constructor steps are to set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [is scoped](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) to true.

Element definition is a process of adding a [custom element definition](#4133-core-concepts) to the [`CustomElementRegistry`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface). This is accomplished by the [`define()`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) method.

The `define(name, constructor,
  options)` method steps are:
1. If [IsConstructor](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-isconstructor)(constructor) is false, then throw a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror).
2. If name is not a [valid custom element name](#4133-core-concepts), then throw a ["`SyntaxError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
3. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [custom element definition set](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) an item with [name](#4133-core-concepts) name, then throw a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
4. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [custom element definition set](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) an item with [constructor](#4133-core-concepts) constructor, then throw a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
5. Let localName be name.
6. Let extends be options\["[`extends`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface)"\] if it [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps); otherwise null.
7. If extends is not null:
   1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [is scoped](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) is true, then throw a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
   2. If extends is a [valid custom element name](#4133-core-concepts), then throw a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
   3. If the [element interface](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) for extends and the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) is [`HTMLUnknownElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom) (e.g., if extends does not indicate an element definition in this specification), then throw a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
   4. Set localName to extends.
8. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [element definition is running](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) is true, then throw a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
9. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [element definition is running](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) to true.
10. Let formAssociated be false.
11. Let disableInternals be false.
12. Let disableShadow be false.
13. Let observedAttributes be an empty `sequence<DOMString>`.
14. Run the following steps while catching any exceptions:
    1. Let prototype be ? [Get](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-get-o-p)(constructor, "prototype").
    2. If prototype [is not an Object](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-object-type), then throw a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) exception.
    3. Let lifecycleCallbacks be the [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) «\[ "`connectedCallback`" → null, "`disconnectedCallback`" → null, "`connectedMoveCallback`" → null, "`adoptedCallback`" → null, "`attributeChangedCallback`" → null \]».
    4. For each callbackName of [the keys](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) of lifecycleCallbacks:
       1. Let callbackValue be ? [Get](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-get-o-p)(prototype, callbackName).
       2. If callbackValue is not undefined, then [set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) lifecycleCallbacks\[callbackName\] to the result of [converting](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-type-mapping) callbackValue to the Web IDL [`Function`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#common-Function) callback type.
    5. If lifecycleCallbacks\["`attributeChangedCallback`"\] is not null:
       1. Let observedAttributesIterable be ? [Get](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-get-o-p)(constructor, "observedAttributes").
       2. If observedAttributesIterable is not undefined, then set observedAttributes to the result of [converting](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-type-mapping) observedAttributesIterable to a `sequence<DOMString>`. Rethrow any exceptions from the conversion.
    6. Let disabledFeatures be an empty `sequence<DOMString>`.
    7. Let disabledFeaturesIterable be ? [Get](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-get-o-p)(constructor, "disabledFeatures").
    8. If disabledFeaturesIterable is not undefined, then set disabledFeatures to the result of [converting](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-type-mapping) disabledFeaturesIterable to a `sequence<DOMString>`. Rethrow any exceptions from the conversion.
    9. If disabledFeatures [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) "`internals`", then set disableInternals to true.
    10. If disabledFeatures [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) "`shadow`", then set disableShadow to true.
    11. Let formAssociatedValue be ? [Get](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-get-o-p)( constructor, "formAssociated").
    12. Set formAssociated to the result of [converting](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-type-mapping) formAssociatedValue to a `boolean`.
    13. If formAssociated is true, then for each callbackName of « "`formAssociatedCallback`", "`formResetCallback`", "`formDisabledCallback`", "`formStateRestoreCallback`" »:
        1. Let callbackValue be ? [Get](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-get-o-p)(prototype, callbackName).
        2. If callbackValue is not undefined, then [set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) lifecycleCallbacks\[callbackName\] to the result of [converting](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-type-mapping) callbackValue to the Web IDL [`Function`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#common-Function) callback type.

    Then, regardless of whether the above steps threw an exception or not: set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [element definition is running](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) to false.

    Finally, if the steps threw an exception, rethrow that exception.

15. Let definition be a new [custom element definition](#4133-core-concepts) with [name](#4133-core-concepts) name, [local name](#4133-core-concepts) localName, [constructor](#4133-core-concepts) constructor, [observed attributes](#4133-core-concepts) observedAttributes, [lifecycle callbacks](#4133-core-concepts) lifecycleCallbacks, [form-associated](#4133-core-concepts) formAssociated, [disable internals](#4133-core-concepts) disableInternals, and [disable shadow](#4133-core-concepts) disableShadow.
16. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) definition to [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [custom element definition set](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface).
17. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [is scoped](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) is true, then for each document of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [scoped document set](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface): [upgrade particular elements within a document](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), document, definition, and localName.
18. Otherwise, [upgrade particular elements within a document](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object), definition, localName, and name.
19. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [when-defined promise map](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface)\[name\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps):
    1. Resolve [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [when-defined promise map](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface)\[name\] with constructor.
    2. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [when-defined promise map](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface)\[name\].

To upgrade particular elements within a document given a [`CustomElementRegistry`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) object registry, a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object document, a [custom element definition](#4133-core-concepts) definition, a string localName, and optionally a string name (default localName):
1. Let upgradeCandidates be all elements that are [shadow-including descendants](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) of document, whose [custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) is registry, whose namespace is the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces), and whose local name is localName, in [shadow-including tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot). Additionally, if name is not localName, only include elements whose [`is` value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) is equal to name.
2. For each element element of upgradeCandidates: [enqueue a custom element upgrade reaction](#4136-custom-element-reactions) given element and definition.

The `get(name)` method steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [custom element definition set](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) an item with [name](#4133-core-concepts) name, then return that item's [constructor](#4133-core-concepts).
2. Return undefined.

The `getName(constructor)` method steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [custom element definition set](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) an item with [constructor](#4133-core-concepts) constructor, then return that item's [name](#4133-core-concepts).
2. Return null.

The `whenDefined(name)` method steps are:
1. If name is not a [valid custom element name](#4133-core-concepts), then return [a promise rejected with](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#a-promise-rejected-with) a ["`SyntaxError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [custom element definition set](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) an item with [name](#4133-core-concepts) name, then return [a promise resolved with](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#a-promise-resolved-with) that item's [constructor](#4133-core-concepts).
3. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [when-defined promise map](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface)\[name\] does not [exist](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then [set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [when-defined promise map](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface)\[name\] to a new promise.
4. Return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [when-defined promise map](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface)\[name\].

> [!example]
> The [`whenDefined()`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) method can be used to avoid performing an action until all appropriate [custom elements](#4133-core-concepts) are [defined](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element). In this example, we combine it with the [`:defined`](#4163-pseudo-classes) pseudo-class to hide a dynamically-loaded article's contents until we're sure that all of the [autonomous custom elements](#4133-core-concepts) it uses are defined.
> 
> ```javascript
> articleContainer.hidden = true;
> 
> fetch(articleURL)
>   .then(response => response.text())
>   .then(text => {
>     articleContainer.innerHTML = text;
> 
>     return Promise.all(
>       [...articleContainer.querySelectorAll(":not(:defined)")]
>         .map(el => customElements.whenDefined(el.localName))
>     );
>   })
>   .then(() => {
>     articleContainer.hidden = false;
>   });
> ```

The `upgrade(root)` method steps are:
1. For each [shadow-including inclusive descendant](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) candidate of root, in [shadow-including tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot):
   1. If candidate is not an [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) node, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   2. If candidate's [custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) is not [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   3. [Try to upgrade](#4135-upgrades) candidate.

> [!example]
> The [`upgrade()`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) method allows upgrading of elements at will. Normally elements are automatically upgraded when they become [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree), but this method can be used if you need to upgrade before you're ready to connect the element.
> 
> ```javascript
> const el = document.createElement("spider-man");
> 
> class SpiderMan extends HTMLElement {}
> customElements.define("spider-man", SpiderMan);
> 
> console.assert(!(el instanceof SpiderMan)); // not yet upgraded
> 
> customElements.upgrade(el);
> console.assert(el instanceof SpiderMan);    // upgraded!
> ```

The `initialize(root)` method steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [is scoped](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) is false and either root is a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) node or root's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is not [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), then throw a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. If root is a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) node whose [custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is null, then set root's [custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) to [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
3. Otherwise, if root is a [`ShadowRoot`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) node whose [custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) is null, then set root's [custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) to [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
4. For each [inclusive descendant](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) inclusiveDescendant of root, in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees):
   1. If inclusiveDescendant is not an [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) node, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   2. If inclusiveDescendant's [custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) is null:
      1. Set inclusiveDescendant's [custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) to [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
      2. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [is scoped](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) is true, then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) inclusiveDescendant's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) to [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [scoped document set](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface).
   3. If inclusiveDescendant's [custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) is not [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   4. [Try to upgrade](#4135-upgrades) inclusiveDescendant.

> [!note]
> Once the custom element registry of a node is initialized to a [`CustomElementRegistry`](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) object, it intentionally cannot be changed any further. This simplifies reasoning about code and allows implementations to optimize.

#### 4.13.5 Upgrades

To upgrade an element, given as input a [custom element definition](#4133-core-concepts) definition and an element element, run the following steps:
1. If element's [custom element state](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) is not "`undefined`" or "`uncustomized`", then return.

   > [!example]
   > One scenario where this can occur due to reentrant invocation of this algorithm, as in the following example:
   > 
   > ```html
   > <!DOCTYPE html>
   > <x-foo id="a"></x-foo>
   > <x-foo id="b"></x-foo>
   > 
   > <script>
   > // Defining enqueues upgrade reactions for both "a" and "b"
   > customElements.define("x-foo", class extends HTMLElement {
   >   constructor() {
   >     super();
   > 
   >     const b = document.querySelector("#b");
   >     b.remove();
   > 
   >     // While this constructor is running for "a", "b" is still
   >     // undefined, and so inserting it into the document will enqueue a
   >     // second upgrade reaction for "b" in addition to the one enqueued
   >     // by defining x-foo.
   >     document.body.appendChild(b);
   >   }
   > })
   > </script>
   > ```
   > 
   > This step will thus bail out the algorithm early when [upgrade an element](#4135-upgrades) is invoked with "`b`" a second time.

2. Set element's [custom element definition](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) to definition.
3. Set element's [custom element state](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) to "`failed`".

   > [!note]
   > It will be set to "`custom`" [after the upgrade succeeds](#4135-upgrades). For now, we set it to "`failed`" so that any reentrant invocations will hit [the above early-exit step](#4135-upgrades).

4. For each attribute in element's [attribute list](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), in order, [enqueue a custom element callback reaction](#4136-custom-element-reactions) with element, callback name "`attributeChangedCallback`", and « attribute's local name, null, attribute's value, attribute's namespace ».
5. If element is [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree), then [enqueue a custom element callback reaction](#4136-custom-element-reactions) with element, callback name "`connectedCallback`", and « ».
6. Add element to the end of definition's [construction stack](#4133-core-concepts).
7. Let C be definition's [constructor](#4133-core-concepts).
8. Let previousRegistry be the [surrounding agent](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#surrounding-agent)'s [active custom element constructor map](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface)\[C\] [with default](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) null.
9. [Set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) the [surrounding agent](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#surrounding-agent)'s [active custom element constructor map](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface)\[C\] to element's [custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element).
10. Run the following steps while catching any exceptions:
    1. If definition's [disable shadow](#4133-core-concepts) is true and element's [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) is non-null, then throw a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

       > [!note]
       > This is needed as [`attachShadow()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) does not use [look up a custom element definition](#4133-core-concepts) while [`attachInternals()`](#4137-element-internals) does.

    2. Set element's [custom element state](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) to "`precustomized`".
    3. Let constructResult be the result of [constructing](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#construct-a-callback-function) C, with no arguments.

       > [!note]
       > If C [non-conformantly](#4132-requirements-for-custom-element-constructors-and-reactions) uses an API decorated with the [`[CEReactions]`](#4136-custom-element-reactions) extended attribute, then the reactions enqueued at the beginning of this algorithm will execute during this step, before C finishes and control returns to this algorithm. Otherwise, they will execute after C and the rest of the upgrade process finishes.

    4. If [SameValue](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-samevalue)(constructResult, element) is false, then throw a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror).

       > [!note]
       > This can occur if C constructs another instance of the same custom element before calling `super()`, or if C uses JavaScript's `return`-override feature to return an arbitrary [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom) object from the constructor.

    Then, perform the following steps, regardless of whether the above steps threw an exception or not:
    1. If previousRegistry is null, then [remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) the [surrounding agent](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#surrounding-agent)'s [active custom element constructor map](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface)\[C\].
    2. Otherwise, [set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) the [surrounding agent](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#surrounding-agent)'s [active custom element constructor map](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface)\[C\] to previousRegistry.
    3. Remove the last entry from the end of definition's [construction stack](#4133-core-concepts).

       > [!note]
       > Assuming C calls `super()` (as it will if it is [conformant](#4132-requirements-for-custom-element-constructors-and-reactions)), and that the call succeeds, this will be the [*already constructed* marker](#4133-core-concepts) that replaced the element we pushed at the beginning of this algorithm. (The [HTML element constructor](#323-html-element-constructors) carries out this replacement.)
       > 
       > If C does not call `super()` (i.e. it is not [conformant](#4132-requirements-for-custom-element-constructors-and-reactions)), or if any step in the [HTML element constructor](#323-html-element-constructors) throws, then this entry will still be element.

    Finally, if the above steps threw an exception:
    1. Set element's [custom element definition](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) to null.
    2. Empty element's [custom element reaction queue](#4136-custom-element-reactions).
    3. Rethrow the exception (thus terminating this algorithm).

    > [!note]
    > If the above steps threw an exception, then element's [custom element state](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) will remain "`failed`" or "`precustomized`".

11. If element is a [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts):
    1. [Reset the form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) of element. If element is associated with a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element, then [enqueue a custom element callback reaction](#4136-custom-element-reactions) with element, callback name "`formAssociatedCallback`", and « the associated [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) ».
    2. If element is [disabled](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute), then [enqueue a custom element callback reaction](#4136-custom-element-reactions) with element, callback name "`formDisabledCallback`", and « true ».
12. Set element's [custom element state](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) to "`custom`".

To try to upgrade an element given an element element:
1. Let definition be the result of [looking up a custom element definition](#4133-core-concepts) given element's [custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), element's [namespace](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), element's [local name](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), and element's [`is` value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element).
2. If definition is not null, then [enqueue a custom element upgrade reaction](#4136-custom-element-reactions) given element and definition.

#### 4.13.6 Custom element reactions

A [custom element](#4133-core-concepts) possesses the ability to respond to certain occurrences by running author code:
- When [upgraded](#4135-upgrades), its [constructor](#4133-core-concepts) is run, with no arguments.
- When it [becomes connected](#214-dom-trees), its `connectedCallback` is called, with no arguments.
- When it [becomes disconnected](#214-dom-trees), its `disconnectedCallback` is called, with no arguments.
- When it is [moved](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms), its `connectedMoveCallback` is called, with no arguments.
- When it is [adopted](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) into a new document, its `adoptedCallback` is called, given the old document and new document as arguments.
- When any of its attributes are [changed](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), [appended](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), [removed](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), or [replaced](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), its `attributeChangedCallback` is called, given the attribute's local name, old value, new value, and namespace as arguments. (An attribute's old or new value is considered to be null when the attribute is added or removed, respectively.)
- When the user agent [resets the form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) of a [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts) and doing so changes the form owner, its `formAssociatedCallback` is called, given the new form owner (or null if no owner) as an argument.
- When the form owner of a [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts) is [reset](#41023-resetting-a-form), its `formResetCallback` is called.
- When the [disabled](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute) state of a [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts) is changed, its `formDisabledCallback` is called, given the new state as an argument.
- When the user agent updates a [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts)'s value on behalf of a user or [as part of navigation](#7465-persisted-history-entry-state), its `formStateRestoreCallback` is called, given the new state and a string indicating a reason, "`autocomplete`" or "`restore`", as arguments.

We call these reactions collectively custom element reactions.

The way in which [custom element reactions](#4136-custom-element-reactions) are invoked is done with special care, to avoid running author code during the middle of delicate operations. Effectively, they are delayed until "just before returning to user script". This means that for most purposes they appear to execute synchronously, but in the case of complicated composite operations (like [cloning](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), or [range](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-interface-abstractrange) manipulation), they will instead be delayed until after all the relevant user agent processing steps have completed, and then run together as a batch.

Additionally, the precise ordering of these reactions is managed via a somewhat-complicated stack-of-queues system, described below. The intention behind this system is to guarantee that [custom element reactions](#4136-custom-element-reactions) always are invoked in the same order as their triggering actions, at least within the local context of a single [custom element](#4133-core-concepts). (Because [custom element reaction](#4136-custom-element-reactions) code can perform its own mutations, it is not possible to give a global ordering guarantee across multiple elements.)

---

Each [similar-origin window agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism) has a custom element reactions stack, which is initially empty. A [similar-origin window agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s current element queue is the [element queue](#4136-custom-element-reactions) at the top of its [custom element reactions stack](#4136-custom-element-reactions). Each item in the stack is an element queue, which is initially empty as well. Each item in an [element queue](#4136-custom-element-reactions) is an element. (The elements are not necessarily [custom](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) yet, since this queue is used for [upgrades](#4135-upgrades) as well.)

Each [custom element reactions stack](#4136-custom-element-reactions) has an associated backup element queue, which is an initially-empty [element queue](#4136-custom-element-reactions). Elements are pushed onto the [backup element queue](#4136-custom-element-reactions) during operations that affect the DOM without going through an API decorated with [`[CEReactions]`](#4136-custom-element-reactions), or through the parser's [create an element for the token](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) algorithm. An example of this is a user-initiated editing operation which modifies the descendants or attributes of an [editable](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable) element. To prevent reentrancy when processing the [backup element queue](#4136-custom-element-reactions), each [custom element reactions stack](#4136-custom-element-reactions) also has a processing the backup element queue flag, initially unset.

All elements have an associated custom element reaction queue, initially empty. Each item in the [custom element reaction queue](#4136-custom-element-reactions) is of one of two types:
- An upgrade reaction, which will [upgrade](#4135-upgrades) the custom element and contains a [custom element definition](#4133-core-concepts); or
- A callback reaction, which will call a lifecycle callback, and contains a callback function as well as a list of arguments.

This is all summarized in the following schematic diagram:

![A custom element reactions stack consists of a stack of element queues. Zooming in on a particular queue, we see that it contains a number of elements (in our example, <x-a>, then <x-b>, then <x-c>). Any particular element in the queue then has a custom element reaction queue. Zooming in on the custom element reaction queue, we see that it contains a variety of queued-up reactions (in our example, upgrade, then attribute changed, then another attribute changed, then connected).](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/custom-element-reactions.svg)

To enqueue an element on the appropriate element queue, given an element element, run the following steps:
1. Let reactionsStack be element's [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [custom element reactions stack](#4136-custom-element-reactions).
2. If reactionsStack is empty:
   1. Add element to reactionsStack's [backup element queue](#4136-custom-element-reactions).
   2. If reactionsStack's [processing the backup element queue](#4136-custom-element-reactions) flag is set, then return.
   3. Set reactionsStack's [processing the backup element queue](#4136-custom-element-reactions) flag.
   4. [Queue a microtask](#8172-queuing-tasks) to perform the following steps:
      1. [Invoke custom element reactions](#4136-custom-element-reactions) in reactionsStack's [backup element queue](#4136-custom-element-reactions).
      2. Unset reactionsStack's [processing the backup element queue](#4136-custom-element-reactions) flag.
3. Otherwise, add element to element's [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [current element queue](#4136-custom-element-reactions).

To enqueue a custom element callback reaction, given a [custom element](#4133-core-concepts) element, a callback name callbackName, and a list of arguments args, run the following steps:
1. Let definition be element's [custom element definition](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element).
2. Let callback be the value of the entry in definition's [lifecycle callbacks](#4133-core-concepts) with key callbackName.
3. If callbackName is "`connectedMoveCallback`" and callback is null:
   1. Let disconnectedCallback be the value of the entry in definition's [lifecycle callbacks](#4133-core-concepts) with key "`disconnectedCallback`".
   2. Let connectedCallback be the value of the entry in definition's [lifecycle callbacks](#4133-core-concepts) with key "`connectedCallback`".
   3. If connectedCallback and disconnectedCallback are null, then return.
   4. Set callback to the following steps:
      1. If disconnectedCallback is not null, then call disconnectedCallback with no arguments.
      2. If connectedCallback is not null, then call connectedCallback with no arguments.
4. If callback is null, then return.
5. If callbackName is "`attributeChangedCallback`":
   1. Let attributeName be the first element of args.
   2. If definition's [observed attributes](#4133-core-concepts) does not contain attributeName, then return.
6. Add a new [callback reaction](#4136-custom-element-reactions) to element's [custom element reaction queue](#4136-custom-element-reactions), with callback function callback and arguments args.
7. [Enqueue an element on the appropriate element queue](#4136-custom-element-reactions) given element.

To enqueue a custom element upgrade reaction, given an element element and [custom element definition](#4133-core-concepts) definition, run the following steps:
1. Add a new [upgrade reaction](#4136-custom-element-reactions) to element's [custom element reaction queue](#4136-custom-element-reactions), with [custom element definition](#4133-core-concepts) definition.
2. [Enqueue an element on the appropriate element queue](#4136-custom-element-reactions) given element.

To invoke custom element reactions in an [element queue](#4136-custom-element-reactions) queue, run the following steps:
1. While queue is not [empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists):
   1. Let element be the result of [dequeuing](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#512-queues) from queue.
   2. Let reactions be element's [custom element reaction queue](#4136-custom-element-reactions).
   3. Repeat until reactions is empty:
      1. Remove the first element of reactions, and let reaction be that element. Switch on reaction's type:

         [upgrade reaction](#4136-custom-element-reactions)

         [Upgrade](#4135-upgrades) element using reaction's [custom element definition](#4133-core-concepts).

         If this throws an exception, catch it, and [report](#8146-runtime-script-errors) it for reaction's [custom element definition](#4133-core-concepts)'s [constructor](#4133-core-concepts)'s corresponding JavaScript object's [associated realm](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-associated-realm)'s [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).

         [callback reaction](#4136-custom-element-reactions)

         [Invoke](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invoke-a-callback-function) reaction's callback function with reaction's arguments and "`report`", and *[callback this value](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-callback-this-value)* set to element.

---

To ensure [custom element reactions](#4136-custom-element-reactions) are triggered appropriately, we introduce the `[CEReactions]` IDL [extended attribute](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-extended-attribute). It indicates that the relevant algorithm is to be supplemented with additional steps in order to appropriately track and invoke [custom element reactions](#4136-custom-element-reactions).

The [`[CEReactions]`](#4136-custom-element-reactions) extended attribute must take no arguments, and must not appear on anything other than an operation, attribute, setter, or deleter. Additionally, it must not appear on readonly attributes.

Operations, attributes, setters, or deleters annotated with the [`[CEReactions]`](#4136-custom-element-reactions) extended attribute must run the following steps in place of the ones specified in their description:
1. [Push](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#511-stacks) a new [element queue](#4136-custom-element-reactions) onto this object's [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [custom element reactions stack](#4136-custom-element-reactions).
2. Run the originally-specified steps for this construct, catching any exceptions. If the steps return a value, let value be the returned value. If they throw an exception, let exception be the thrown exception.
3. Let queue be the result of [popping](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#511-stacks) from this object's [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [custom element reactions stack](#4136-custom-element-reactions).
4. [Invoke custom element reactions](#4136-custom-element-reactions) in queue.
5. If an exception exception was thrown by the original steps, rethrow exception.
6. If a value value was returned from the original steps, return value.

> [!note]
> The intent behind this extended attribute is somewhat subtle. One way of accomplishing its goals would be to say that every operation, attribute, setter, and deleter on the platform must have these steps inserted, and to allow implementers to optimize away unnecessary cases (where no DOM mutation is possible that could cause [custom element reactions](#4136-custom-element-reactions) to occur).
> 
> However, in practice this imprecision could lead to non-interoperable implementations of [custom element reactions](#4136-custom-element-reactions), as some implementations might forget to invoke these steps in some cases. Instead, we settled on the approach of explicitly annotating all relevant IDL constructs, as a way of ensuring interoperable behavior and helping implementations easily pinpoint all cases where these steps are necessary.

Any nonstandard APIs introduced by the user agent that could modify the DOM in such a way as to cause [enqueuing a custom element callback reaction](#4136-custom-element-reactions) or [enqueuing a custom element upgrade reaction](#4136-custom-element-reactions), for example by modifying any attributes or child elements, must also be decorated with the [`[CEReactions]`](#4136-custom-element-reactions) attribute.

> [!note]
> As of the time of this writing, the following nonstandard or not-yet-standardized APIs are known to fall into this category:
> - [`HTMLInputElement`](#4105-the-input-element)'s `webkitdirectory` and `incremental` IDL attributes
> - [`HTMLLinkElement`](#424-the-link-element)'s `scope` IDL attribute

#### 4.13.7 Element internals

Certain capabilities are meant to be available to a custom element author, but not to a custom element consumer. These are provided by the [`element.attachInternals()`](#4137-element-internals) method, which returns an instance of [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface). The properties and methods of [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) allow control over internal features which the user agent provides to all elements.

`element.attachInternals()`

Returns an [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) object targeting the [custom element](#4133-core-concepts) element. Throws an exception if element is not a [custom element](#4133-core-concepts), if the "`internals`" feature was disabled as part of the element definition, or if it is called twice on the same element.

Each [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom) has an attached internals (null or an [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) object), initially null.

The `attachInternals()` method steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`is` value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) is not null, then throw a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Let definition be the result of [looking up a custom element definition](#4133-core-concepts) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [namespace](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [local name](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), and null.
3. If definition is null, then throw a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
4. If definition's [disable internals](#4133-core-concepts) is true, then throw a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
5. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [attached internals](#4137-element-internals) is non-null, then throw a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
6. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [custom element state](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) is not "`precustomized`" or "`custom`", then throw a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
7. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [attached internals](#4137-element-internals) to a new [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) instance whose [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) is [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
8. Return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [attached internals](#4137-element-internals).

##### 4.13.7.1 The [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) interface

The IDL for the [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) interface is as follows, with the various operations and attributes defined in the following sections:

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface ElementInternals {
  // Shadow root access
  readonly attribute ShadowRoot? shadowRoot;

  // Form-associated custom elements
  undefined setFormValue((File or USVString or FormData)? value,
                         optional (File or USVString or FormData)? state);

  readonly attribute HTMLFormElement? form;

  undefined setValidity(optional ValidityStateFlags flags = {},
                        optional DOMString message,
                        optional HTMLElement anchor);
  readonly attribute boolean willValidate;
  readonly attribute ValidityState validity;
  readonly attribute DOMString validationMessage;
  boolean checkValidity();
  boolean reportValidity();

  readonly attribute NodeList labels;

  // Custom state pseudo-class
  [SameObject] readonly attribute CustomStateSet states;
};

// Accessibility semantics
ElementInternals includes ARIAMixin;

dictionary ValidityStateFlags {
  boolean valueMissing = false;
  boolean typeMismatch = false;
  boolean patternMismatch = false;
  boolean tooLong = false;
  boolean tooShort = false;
  boolean rangeUnderflow = false;
  boolean rangeOverflow = false;
  boolean stepMismatch = false;
  boolean badInput = false;
  boolean customError = false;
};
```

Each [`ElementInternals`](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) has a target element, which is a [custom element](#4133-core-concepts).

##### 4.13.7.2 Shadow root access

`internals.shadowRoot`

Returns the [`ShadowRoot`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) for internals's [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface), if the [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) is a [shadow host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), or null otherwise.

The `shadowRoot` getter steps are:
1. Let target be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface).
2. If target is not a [shadow host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), then return null.
3. Let shadow be target's [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element).
4. If shadow's [available to element internals](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) is false, then return null.
5. Return shadow.

##### 4.13.7.3 Form-associated custom elements

`internals.setFormValue(value)`

Sets both the [state](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements) and [submission value](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements) of internals's [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) to value.

If value is null, the element won't participate in form submission.

`internals.setFormValue(value,
   state)`

Sets the [submission value](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements) of internals's [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) to value, and its [state](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements) to state.

If value is null, the element won't participate in form submission.

`internals.form`

Returns the [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) of internals's [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface).

`internals.setValidity(flags,
   message [, anchor ])`

Marks internals's [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) as suffering from the constraints indicated by the flags argument, and sets the element's validation message to message. If anchor is specified, the user agent might use it to indicate problems with the constraints of internals's [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) when the [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) is validated interactively or [`reportValidity()`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) is called.

`internals.setValidity({})`

Marks internals's [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) as [satisfying its constraints](#410211-definitions).

`internals.willValidate`

Returns true if internals's [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) will be validated when the form is submitted; false otherwise.

`internals.validity`

Returns the [`ValidityState`](#410213-the-constraint-validation-api) object for internals's [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface).

`internals.validationMessage`

Returns the error message that would be shown to the user if internals's [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) was to be checked for validity.

`valid = internals.checkValidity()`

Returns true if internals's [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) has no validity problems; false otherwise. Fires an [`invalid`](#events) event at the element in the latter case.

`valid = internals.reportValidity()`

Returns true if internals's [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) has no validity problems; otherwise, returns false, fires an [`invalid`](#events) event at the element, and (if the event isn't canceled) reports the problem to the user.

`internals.labels`

Returns a [`NodeList`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42101-interface-nodelist) of all the [`label`](#4104-the-label-element) elements that internals's [target element](#41371-the-elementinternals-interface) is associated with.

Each [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts) has submission value. It is used to provide one or more [entries](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) on form submission. The initial value of [submission value](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements) is null, and [submission value](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements) can be null, a string, a [`File`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file), or a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [entries](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list).

Each [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts) has state. It is information with which the user agent can restore a user's input for the element. The initial value of [state](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements) is null, and [state](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements) can be null, a string, a [`File`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file), or a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [entries](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list).

The [`setFormValue()`](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements) method is used by the custom element author to set the element's [submission value](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements) and [state](#41373-form-associated-custom-elements), thus communicating these to the user agent.
