- If the item is a [typed item](#522-items): a defined property name allowed in this situation according to the specification that defines the [relevant types](#522-items) for the item, or
- A [valid URL string](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-url-string) that is an [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute) defined as an item property name allowed in this situation by a vocabulary specification, or
- A [valid URL string](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-url-string) that is an [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute), used as a proprietary item property name (i.e. one used by the author for private purposes, not defined in a public specification), or
- If the item is not a [typed item](#522-items): a string that contains no U+002E FULL STOP characters (.) and no U+003A COLON characters (:), used as a proprietary item property name (i.e. one used by the author for private purposes, not defined in a public specification).

Specifications that introduce [defined property names](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute) must ensure all such property names contain no U+002E FULL STOP characters (.), no U+003A COLON characters (:), and no [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).

> [!note]
> The rules above disallow U+003A COLON characters (:) in non-URL values because otherwise they could not be distinguished from URLs. Values with U+002E FULL STOP characters (.) are reserved for future extensions. [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) are disallowed because otherwise the values would be parsed as multiple tokens.

When an element with an [`itemprop`](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute [adds a property](#525-associating-names-with-items) to multiple [items](#522-items), the requirement above regarding the tokens applies for each [item](#522-items) individually.

The property names of an element are the tokens that the element's [`itemprop`](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute is found to contain when its value is [split on ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings), with the order preserved but with duplicates removed (leaving only the first occurrence of each name).

Within an [item](#522-items), the properties are unordered with respect to each other, except for properties with the same name, which are ordered in the order they are given by the algorithm that defines [the properties of an item](#525-associating-names-with-items).

> [!example]
> In the following example, the "a" property has the values "1" and "2", *in that order*, but whether the "a" property comes before the "b" property or not is not important:
> 
> ```html
> <div itemscope>
>  <p itemprop="a">1</p>
>  <p itemprop="a">2</p>
>  <p itemprop="b">test</p>
> </div>
> ```
> 
> Thus, the following is equivalent:
> 
> ```html
> <div itemscope>
>  <p itemprop="b">test</p>
>  <p itemprop="a">1</p>
>  <p itemprop="a">2</p>
> </div>
> ```
> 
> As is the following:
> 
> ```html
> <div itemscope>
>  <p itemprop="a">1</p>
>  <p itemprop="b">test</p>
>  <p itemprop="a">2</p>
> </div>
> ```
> 
> And the following:
> 
> ```html
> <div id="x">
>  <p itemprop="a">1</p>
> </div>
> <div itemscope itemref="x">
>  <p itemprop="b">test</p>
>  <p itemprop="a">2</p>
> </div>
> ```

#### 5.2.4 Values

The property value of a name-value pair added by an element with an [`itemprop`](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute is as given for the first matching case in the following list:

If the element also has an [`itemscope`](#522-items) attribute

The value is the [item](#522-items) created by the element.

If the element is a [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element

The value is the value of the element's [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute, if any, or the empty string if there is no such attribute.

If the element is an [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element), [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element), [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element), [`img`](#483-the-img-element), [`source`](#482-the-source-element), [`track`](#4810-the-track-element), or [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element

The value is the result of [encoding-parsing-and-serializing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given the element's `src` attribute's value, relative to the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), at the time the attribute is set, or the empty string if there is no such attribute or the result is failure.

If the element is an [`a`](#451-the-a-element), [`area`](#4813-the-area-element), or [`link`](#424-the-link-element) element

The value is the result of [encoding-parsing-and-serializing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given the element's `href` attribute's value, relative to the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), at the time the attribute is set, or the empty string if there is no such attribute or the result is failure.

If the element is an [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element

The value is the result of [encoding-parsing-and-serializing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given the element's `data` attribute's value, relative to the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), at the time the attribute is set, or the empty string if there is no such attribute or the result is failure.

If the element is a [`data`](#4513-the-data-element) element

The value is the value of the element's [`value`](#4513-the-data-element) attribute, if it has one, or the empty string otherwise.

If the element is a [`meter`](#41014-the-meter-element) element

The value is the value of the element's [`value`](#41014-the-meter-element) attribute, if it has one, or the empty string otherwise.

If the element is a [`time`](#4514-the-time-element) element

The value is the element's [datetime value](#4514-the-time-element).

Otherwise

The value is the element's [descendant text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text).

The URL property elements are the [`a`](#451-the-a-element), [`area`](#4813-the-area-element), [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element), [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element), [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element), [`img`](#483-the-img-element), [`link`](#424-the-link-element), [`object`](#487-the-object-element), [`source`](#482-the-source-element), [`track`](#4810-the-track-element), and [`video`](#488-the-video-element) elements.

If a property's [value](#524-values), as defined by the property's definition, is an [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute), the property must be specified using a [URL property element](#524-values).

> [!note]
> These requirements do not apply just because a property value happens to match the syntax for a URL. They only apply if the property is explicitly defined as taking such a value.

> [!example]
> For example, a book about the first moon landing could be called "mission:moon". A "title" property from a vocabulary that defines a title as being a string would not expect the title to be given in an [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element, even though it looks like a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url). On the other hand, if there was a (rather narrowly scoped!) vocabulary for "books whose titles look like URLs" which had a "title" property defined to take a URL, then the property *would* expect the title to be given in an [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element (or one of the other [URL property elements](#524-values)), because of the requirement above.

#### 5.2.5 Associating names with items

To find the properties of an item defined by the element root, the user agent must run the following steps. These steps are also used to flag [microdata errors](#525-associating-names-with-items).
1. Let results, memory, and pending be empty lists of elements.
2. Add the element root to memory.
3. Add the child elements of root, if any, to pending.
4. If root has an [`itemref`](#522-items) attribute, [split the value of that `itemref` attribute on ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings). For each resulting token ID, if there is an element in the [tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) of root with the [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) ID, then add the first such element to pending.
5. While pending is not empty:
   1. Remove an element from pending and let current be that element.
   2. If current is already in memory, there is a [microdata error](#525-associating-names-with-items); [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   3. Add current to memory.
   4. If current does not have an [`itemscope`](#522-items) attribute, then add all the child elements of current to pending.
   5. If current has an [`itemprop`](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute specified and has one or more [property names](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute), then add current to results.
6. Sort results in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
7. Return results.

A document must not contain any [items](#522-items) for which the algorithm to find [the properties of an item](#525-associating-names-with-items) finds any microdata errors.

An [item](#522-items) is a top-level microdata item if its element does not have an [`itemprop`](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute.

All [`itemref`](#522-items) attributes in a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) must be such that there are no cycles in the graph formed from representing each [item](#522-items) in the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) as a node in the graph and each [property](#525-associating-names-with-items) of an item whose [value](#524-values) is another item as an edge in the graph connecting those two items.

A document must not contain any elements that have an [`itemprop`](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute) attribute that would not be found to be a property of any of the [items](#522-items) in that document were their [properties](#525-associating-names-with-items) all to be determined.

> [!example]
> In this example, a single license statement is applied to two works, using [`itemref`](#522-items) from the items representing the works:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <html lang="en">
>  <head>
>   <title>Photo gallery</title>
>  </head>
>  <body>
>   <h1>My photos</h1>
>   <figure itemscope itemtype="http://n.whatwg.org/work" itemref="licenses">
>    <img itemprop="work" src="images/house.jpeg" alt="A white house, boarded up, sits in a forest.">
>    <figcaption itemprop="title">The house I found.</figcaption>
>   </figure>
>   <figure itemscope itemtype="http://n.whatwg.org/work" itemref="licenses">
>    <img itemprop="work" src="images/mailbox.jpeg" alt="Outside the house is a mailbox. It has a leaflet inside.">
>    <figcaption itemprop="title">The mailbox.</figcaption>
>   </figure>
>   <footer>
>    <p id="licenses">All images licensed under the <a itemprop="license"
>    href="http://www.opensource.org/licenses/mit-license.php">MIT
>    license</a>.</p>
>   </footer>
>  </body>
> </html>
> ```
> 
> The above results in two items with the type "`http://n.whatwg.org/work`", one with:
> 
> work
> 
> `images/house.jpeg`
> 
> title
> 
> The house I found.
> 
> license
> 
> `http://www.opensource.org/licenses/mit-license.php`
> 
> ...and one with:
> 
> work
> 
> `images/mailbox.jpeg`
> 
> title
> 
> The mailbox.
> 
> license
> 
> `http://www.opensource.org/licenses/mit-license.php`

#### 5.2.6 Microdata and other namespaces

Currently, the [`itemscope`](#522-items), [`itemprop`](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute), and other microdata attributes are only defined for [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility). This means that attributes with the literal names "`itemscope`", "`itemprop`", etc, do not cause microdata processing to occur on elements in other namespaces, such as SVG.

> [!example]
> Thus, in the following example there is only one item, not two.
> 
> ```html
> <p itemscope></p> <!-- this is an item (with no properties and no type) -->
> <svg itemscope></svg> <!-- this is not, it's just an SVG svg element with an invalid unknown attribute -->
> ```

### 5.3 Sample microdata vocabularies

The vocabularies in this section are primarily intended to demonstrate how a vocabulary is specified, though they are also usable in their own right.

#### 5.3.1 vCard

An item with the [item type](#522-items) `http://microformats.org/profile/hcard` represents a person's or organization's contact information.

This vocabulary does not [support global identifiers for items](#522-items).

The following are the type's [defined property names](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute). They are based on the vocabulary defined in vCard Format Specification (vCard) and its extensions, where more information on how to interpret the values can be found. [\[RFC6350\]](#references)

`kind`

Describes what kind of contact the item represents.

The [value](#524-values) must be text that is [identical to](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) one of the [kind strings](#531-vcard).

A single property with the name [`kind`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`fn`

Gives the formatted text corresponding to the name of the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

Exactly one property with the name [`fn`](#531-vcard) must be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`n`

Gives the structured name of the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be an [item](#522-items) with zero or more of each of the [`family-name`](#531-vcard), [`given-name`](#531-vcard), [`additional-name`](#531-vcard), [`honorific-prefix`](#531-vcard), and [`honorific-suffix`](#531-vcard) properties.

Exactly one property with the name [`n`](#531-vcard) must be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`family-name` (inside [`n`](#531-vcard))

Gives the family name of the person, or the full name of the organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

Any number of properties with the name [`family-name`](#531-vcard) may be present within the [item](#522-items) that forms the [value](#524-values) of the [`n`](#531-vcard) property of an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`given-name` (inside [`n`](#531-vcard))

Gives the given-name of the person.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

Any number of properties with the name [`given-name`](#531-vcard) may be present within the [item](#522-items) that forms the [value](#524-values) of the [`n`](#531-vcard) property of an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`additional-name` (inside [`n`](#531-vcard))

Gives the any additional names of the person.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

Any number of properties with the name [`additional-name`](#531-vcard) may be present within the [item](#522-items) that forms the [value](#524-values) of the [`n`](#531-vcard) property of an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`honorific-prefix` (inside [`n`](#531-vcard))

Gives the honorific prefix of the person.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

Any number of properties with the name [`honorific-prefix`](#531-vcard) may be present within the [item](#522-items) that forms the [value](#524-values) of the [`n`](#531-vcard) property of an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`honorific-suffix` (inside [`n`](#531-vcard))

Gives the honorific suffix of the person.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

Any number of properties with the name [`honorific-suffix`](#531-vcard) may be present within the [item](#522-items) that forms the [value](#524-values) of the [`n`](#531-vcard) property of an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`nickname`

Gives the nickname of the person or organization.

> [!note]
> The nickname is the descriptive name given instead of or in addition to the one belonging to a person, place, or thing. It can also be used to specify a familiar form of a proper name specified by the [`fn`](#531-vcard) or [`n`](#531-vcard) properties.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

Any number of properties with the name [`nickname`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`photo`

Gives a photograph of the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be an [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute).

Any number of properties with the name [`photo`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`bday`

Gives the birth date of the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be a [valid date string](#2352-dates).

A single property with the name [`bday`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`anniversary`

Gives the birth date of the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be a [valid date string](#2352-dates).

A single property with the name [`anniversary`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`sex`

Gives the biological sex of the person.

The [value](#524-values) must be one of `F`, meaning "female", `M`, meaning "male", `N`, meaning "none or not applicable", `O`, meaning "other", or `U`, meaning "unknown".

A single property with the name [`sex`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`gender-identity`

Gives the gender identity of the person.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

A single property with the name [`gender-identity`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`adr`

Gives the delivery address of the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be an [item](#522-items) with zero or more [`type`](#531-vcard), [`post-office-box`](#531-vcard), [`extended-address`](#531-vcard), and [`street-address`](#531-vcard) properties, and optionally a [`locality`](#531-vcard) property, optionally a [`region`](#531-vcard) property, optionally a [`postal-code`](#531-vcard) property, and optionally a [`country-name`](#531-vcard) property.

If no [`type`](#531-vcard) properties are present within an [item](#522-items) that forms the [value](#524-values) of an [`adr`](#531-vcard) property of an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard), then the [address type string](#531-vcard) [`work`](#531-vcard) is implied.

Any number of properties with the name [`adr`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`type` (inside [`adr`](#531-vcard))

Gives the type of delivery address.

The [value](#524-values) must be text that is [identical to](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) one of the [address type strings](#531-vcard).

Any number of properties with the name [`type`](#531-vcard) may be present within the [item](#522-items) that forms the [value](#524-values) of an [`adr`](#531-vcard) property of an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard), but within each such [`adr`](#531-vcard) property [item](#522-items) there must only be one [`type`](#531-vcard) property per distinct value.

`post-office-box` (inside [`adr`](#531-vcard))

Gives the post office box component of the delivery address of the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

Any number of properties with the name [`post-office-box`](#531-vcard) may be present within the [item](#522-items) that forms the [value](#524-values) of an [`adr`](#531-vcard) property of an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

> [!note]
> vCard urges authors not to use this field.

`extended-address` (inside [`adr`](#531-vcard))

Gives an additional component of the delivery address of the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

Any number of properties with the name [`extended-address`](#531-vcard) may be present within the [item](#522-items) that forms the [value](#524-values) of an [`adr`](#531-vcard) property of an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

> [!note]
> vCard urges authors not to use this field.

`street-address` (inside [`adr`](#531-vcard))

Gives the street address component of the delivery address of the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

Any number of properties with the name [`street-address`](#531-vcard) may be present within the [item](#522-items) that forms the [value](#524-values) of an [`adr`](#531-vcard) property of an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`locality` (inside [`adr`](#531-vcard))

Gives the locality component (e.g. city) of the delivery address of the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

A single property with the name [`locality`](#531-vcard) may be present within the [item](#522-items) that forms the [value](#524-values) of an [`adr`](#531-vcard) property of an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`region` (inside [`adr`](#531-vcard))

Gives the region component (e.g. state or province) of the delivery address of the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

A single property with the name [`region`](#531-vcard) may be present within the [item](#522-items) that forms the [value](#524-values) of an [`adr`](#531-vcard) property of an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`postal-code` (inside [`adr`](#531-vcard))

Gives the postal code component of the delivery address of the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

A single property with the name [`postal-code`](#531-vcard) may be present within the [item](#522-items) that forms the [value](#524-values) of an [`adr`](#531-vcard) property of an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`country-name` (inside [`adr`](#531-vcard))

Gives the country name component of the delivery address of the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

A single property with the name [`country-name`](#531-vcard) may be present within the [item](#522-items) that forms the [value](#524-values) of an [`adr`](#531-vcard) property of an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`tel`

Gives the telephone number of the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be either text that can be interpreted as a telephone number as defined in the CCITT specifications E.163 and X.121, or an [item](#522-items) with zero or more [`type`](#531-vcard) properties and exactly one [`value`](#531-vcard) property. [\[E163\]](#references) [\[X121\]](#references)

If no [`type`](#531-vcard) properties are present within an [item](#522-items) that forms the [value](#524-values) of a [`tel`](#531-vcard) property of an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard), or if the [value](#524-values) of such a [`tel`](#531-vcard) property is text, then the [telephone type string](#531-vcard) [`voice`](#531-vcard) is implied.

Any number of properties with the name [`tel`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`type` (inside [`tel`](#531-vcard))

Gives the type of telephone number.

The [value](#524-values) must be text that is [identical to](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) one of the [telephone type strings](#531-vcard).

Any number of properties with the name [`type`](#531-vcard) may be present within the [item](#522-items) that forms the [value](#524-values) of a [`tel`](#531-vcard) property of an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard), but within each such [`tel`](#531-vcard) property [item](#522-items) there must only be one [`type`](#531-vcard) property per distinct value.

`value` (inside [`tel`](#531-vcard))

Gives the actual telephone number of the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be text that can be interpreted as a telephone number as defined in the CCITT specifications E.163 and X.121. [\[E163\]](#references) [\[X121\]](#references)

Exactly one property with the name [`value`](#531-vcard) must be present within the [item](#522-items) that forms the [value](#524-values) of a [`tel`](#531-vcard) property of an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`email`

Gives the email address of the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

Any number of properties with the name [`email`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`impp`

Gives a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) for instant messaging and presence protocol communications with the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be an [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute).

Any number of properties with the name [`impp`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`lang`

Gives a language understood by the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be a valid BCP 47 language tag. [\[BCP47\]](#references)

Any number of properties with the name [`lang`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`tz`

Gives the time zone of the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be text and must match the following syntax:
1. Either a U+002B PLUS SIGN character (+) or a U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS character (-).
2. A [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers) that is exactly two digits long and that represents a number in the range 00..23.
3. A U+003A COLON character (:).
4. A [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers) that is exactly two digits long and that represents a number in the range 00..59.

Any number of properties with the name [`tz`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`geo`

Gives the geographical position of the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be text and must match the following syntax:
1. Optionally, either a U+002B PLUS SIGN character (+) or a U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS character (-).
2. One or more [ASCII digits](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).
3. Optionally\*, a U+002E FULL STOP character (.) followed by one or more [ASCII digits](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).
4. A U+003B SEMICOLON character (;).
5. Optionally, either a U+002B PLUS SIGN character (+) or a U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS character (-).
6. One or more [ASCII digits](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).
7. Optionally\*, a U+002E FULL STOP character (.) followed by one or more [ASCII digits](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).

The optional components marked with an asterisk (\*) should be included, and should have six digits each.

> [!note]
> The value specifies latitude and longitude, in that order (i.e., "LAT LON" ordering), in decimal degrees. The longitude represents the location east and west of the prime meridian as a positive or negative real number, respectively. The latitude represents the location north and south of the equator as a positive or negative real number, respectively.

Any number of properties with the name [`geo`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`title`

Gives the job title, functional position or function of the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

Any number of properties with the name [`title`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`role`

Gives the role, occupation, or business category of the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

Any number of properties with the name [`role`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`logo`

Gives the logo of the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be an [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute).

Any number of properties with the name [`logo`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`agent`

Gives the contact information of another person who will act on behalf of the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be either an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard), or an [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute), or text.

Any number of properties with the name [`agent`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`org`

Gives the name and units of the organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be either text or an [item](#522-items) with one [`organization-name`](#531-vcard) property and zero or more [`organization-unit`](#531-vcard) properties.

Any number of properties with the name [`org`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`organization-name` (inside [`org`](#531-vcard))

Gives the name of the organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

Exactly one property with the name [`organization-name`](#531-vcard) must be present within the [item](#522-items) that forms the [value](#524-values) of an [`org`](#531-vcard) property of an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`organization-unit` (inside [`org`](#531-vcard))

Gives the name of the organization unit.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

Any number of properties with the name [`organization-unit`](#531-vcard) may be present within the [item](#522-items) that forms the [value](#524-values) of the [`org`](#531-vcard) property of an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`member`

Gives a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) that represents a member of the group.

The [value](#524-values) must be an [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute).

Any number of properties with the name [`member`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard) if the [item](#522-items) also has a property with the name [`kind`](#531-vcard) whose value is "[`group`](#531-vcard)".

`related`

Gives a relationship to another entity.

The [value](#524-values) must be an [item](#522-items) with one [`url`](#531-vcard) property and one [`rel`](#531-vcard) properties.

Any number of properties with the name [`related`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`url` (inside [`related`](#531-vcard))

Gives the [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) for the related entity.

The [value](#524-values) must be an [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute).

Exactly one property with the name [`url`](#531-vcard) must be present within the [item](#522-items) that forms the [value](#524-values) of a [`related`](#531-vcard) property of an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`rel` (inside [`related`](#531-vcard))

Gives the relationship between the entity and the related entity.

The [value](#524-values) must be text that is [identical to](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) one of the [relationship strings](#531-vcard).

Exactly one property with the name [`rel`](#531-vcard) must be present within the [item](#522-items) that forms the [value](#524-values) of a [`related`](#531-vcard) property of an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`categories`

Gives the name of a category or tag that the person or organization could be classified as.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

Any number of properties with the name [`categories`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`note`

Gives supplemental information or a comment about the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

Any number of properties with the name [`note`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`rev`

Gives the revision date and time of the contact information.

The [value](#524-values) must be text that is a [valid global date and time string](#2357-global-dates-and-times).

> [!note]
> The value distinguishes the current revision of the information for other renditions of the information.

Any number of properties with the name [`rev`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`sound`

Gives a sound file relating to the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be an [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute).

Any number of properties with the name [`sound`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`uid`

Gives a globally unique identifier corresponding to the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

A single property with the name [`uid`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

`url`

Gives a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) relating to the person or organization.

The [value](#524-values) must be an [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute).

Any number of properties with the name [`url`](#531-vcard) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).

The kind strings are:

`individual`

Indicates a single entity (e.g. a person).

`group`

Indicates multiple entities (e.g. a mailing list).

`org`

Indicates a single entity that is not a person (e.g. a company).

`location`

Indicates a geographical place (e.g. an office building).

The address type strings are:

`home`

Indicates a delivery address for a residence.

`work`

Indicates a delivery address for a place of work.

The telephone type strings are:

`home`

Indicates a residential number.

`work`

Indicates a telephone number for a place of work.

`text`

Indicates that the telephone number supports text messages (SMS).

`voice`

Indicates a voice telephone number.

`fax`

Indicates a facsimile telephone number.

`cell`

Indicates a cellular telephone number.

`video`

Indicates a video conferencing telephone number.

`pager`

Indicates a paging device telephone number.

`textphone`

Indicates a telecommunication device for people with hearing or speech difficulties.

The relationship strings are:

`emergency`

An emergency contact.

`agent`

Another entity that acts on behalf of this entity.

##### 5.3.1.1 Conversion to vCard

Given a list of nodes nodes in a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), a user agent must run the following algorithm to extract any vCard data represented by those nodes (only the first vCard is returned):
1. If none of the nodes in nodes are [items](#522-items) with the [item type](#522-items) [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard), then there is no vCard. Abort the algorithm, returning nothing.
2. Let node be the first node in nodes that is an [item](#522-items) with the [item type](#522-items) [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard).
3. Let output be an empty string.
4. [Add a vCard line](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) with the type "`BEGIN`" and the value "`VCARD`" to output.
5. [Add a vCard line](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) with the type "`PROFILE`" and the value "`VCARD`" to output.
6. [Add a vCard line](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) with the type "`VERSION`" and the value "`4.0`" to output.
7. [Add a vCard line](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) with the type "`SOURCE`" and the result of [escaping the vCard text string](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) that is the document's [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) as the value to output.
8. If [the `title` element](#317-dom-tree-accessors) is not null, [add a vCard line](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) with the type "`NAME`" and with the result of [escaping the vCard text string](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) obtained from [the `title` element](#317-dom-tree-accessors)'s [descendant text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) as the value to output.
9. Let sex be the empty string.
10. Let gender-identity be the empty string.
11. For each element element that is [a property of the item](#525-associating-names-with-items) node: for each name name in element's [property names](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute), run the following substeps:
    1. Let parameters be an empty set of name-value pairs.
    2. Run the appropriate set of substeps from the following list. The steps will set a variable value, which is used in the next step.

       If the property's [value](#524-values) is an [item](#522-items) subitem and name is [`n`](#531-vcard)
       1. Let value be the empty string.
       2. Append to value the result of [collecting the first vCard subproperty](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) named [`family-name`](#531-vcard) in subitem.
       3. Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to value.
       4. Append to value the result of [collecting the first vCard subproperty](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) named [`given-name`](#531-vcard) in subitem.
       5. Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to value.
       6. Append to value the result of [collecting the first vCard subproperty](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) named [`additional-name`](#531-vcard) in subitem.
       7. Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to value.
       8. Append to value the result of [collecting the first vCard subproperty](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) named [`honorific-prefix`](#531-vcard) in subitem.
       9. Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to value.
       10. Append to value the result of [collecting the first vCard subproperty](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) named [`honorific-suffix`](#531-vcard) in subitem.

       If the property's [value](#524-values) is an [item](#522-items) subitem and name is [`adr`](#531-vcard)
       1. Let value be the empty string.
       2. Append to value the result of [collecting vCard subproperties](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) named [`post-office-box`](#531-vcard) in subitem.
       3. Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to value.
       4. Append to value the result of [collecting vCard subproperties](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) named [`extended-address`](#531-vcard) in subitem.
       5. Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to value.
       6. Append to value the result of [collecting vCard subproperties](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) named [`street-address`](#531-vcard) in subitem.
       7. Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to value.
       8. Append to value the result of [collecting the first vCard subproperty](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) named [`locality`](#531-vcard) in subitem.
       9. Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to value.
       10. Append to value the result of [collecting the first vCard subproperty](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) named [`region`](#531-vcard) in subitem.
       11. Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to value.
       12. Append to value the result of [collecting the first vCard subproperty](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) named [`postal-code`](#531-vcard) in subitem.
       13. Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to value.
       14. Append to value the result of [collecting the first vCard subproperty](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) named [`country-name`](#531-vcard) in subitem.
       15. If there is a property named [`type`](#531-vcard) in subitem, and the first such property has a [value](#524-values) that is not an [item](#522-items) and whose value consists only of [ASCII alphanumerics](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), then add a parameter named "`TYPE`" whose value is the [value](#524-values) of that property to parameters.

       If the property's [value](#524-values) is an [item](#522-items) subitem and name is [`org`](#531-vcard)
       1. Let value be the empty string.
       2. Append to value the result of [collecting the first vCard subproperty](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) named [`organization-name`](#531-vcard) in subitem.
       3. For each property named [`organization-unit`](#531-vcard) in subitem, run the following steps:
          1. If the [value](#524-values) of the property is an [item](#522-items), then skip this property.
          2. Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to value.
          3. Append the result of [escaping the vCard text string](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) given by the [value](#524-values) of the property to value.

       If the property's [value](#524-values) is an [item](#522-items) subitem with the [item type](#522-items) [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard) and name is [`related`](#531-vcard)
       1. Let value be the empty string.
       2. If there is a property named [`url`](#531-vcard) in subitem, and its element is a [URL property element](#524-values), then append the result of [escaping the vCard text string](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) given by the [value](#524-values) of the first such property to value, and add a parameter with the name "`VALUE`" and the value "`URI`" to parameters.
       3. If there is a property named [`rel`](#531-vcard) in subitem, and the first such property has a [value](#524-values) that is not an [item](#522-items) and whose value consists only of [ASCII alphanumerics](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), then add a parameter named "`RELATION`" whose value is the [value](#524-values) of that property to parameters.

       If the property's [value](#524-values) is an [item](#522-items) and name is none of the above
       1. Let value be the result of [collecting the first vCard subproperty](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) named `value` in subitem.
       2. If there is a property named `type` in subitem, and the first such property has a [value](#524-values) that is not an [item](#522-items) and whose value consists only of [ASCII alphanumerics](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), then add a parameter named "`TYPE`" whose value is the [value](#524-values) of that property to parameters.

       If the property's [value](#524-values) is not an [item](#522-items) and name is [`sex`](#531-vcard)

       If this is the first such property to be found, set sex to the property's [value](#524-values).

       If the property's [value](#524-values) is not an [item](#522-items) and name is [`gender-identity`](#531-vcard)

       If this is the first such property to be found, set gender-identity to the property's [value](#524-values).

       Otherwise (the property's [value](#524-values) is not an [item](#522-items))
       1. Let value be the property's [value](#524-values).
       2. If element is one of the [URL property elements](#524-values), add a parameter with the name "`VALUE`" and the value "`URI`" to parameters.
       3. Otherwise, if name is [`bday`](#531-vcard) or [`anniversary`](#531-vcard) and the value is a [valid date string](#2352-dates), add a parameter with the name "`VALUE`" and the value "`DATE`" to parameters.
       4. Otherwise, if name is [`rev`](#531-vcard) and the value is a [valid global date and time string](#2357-global-dates-and-times), add a parameter with the name "`VALUE`" and the value "`DATE-TIME`" to parameters.
       5. Prefix every U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\) in value with another U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\).
       6. Prefix every U+002C COMMA character (,) in value with a U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\).
       7. Unless name is [`geo`](#531-vcard), prefix every U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) in value with a U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\).
       8. Replace every U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN U+000A LINE FEED character pair (CRLF) in value with a U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\) followed by a U+006E LATIN SMALL LETTER N character (n).
       9. Replace every remaining U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) or U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character in value with a U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\) followed by a U+006E LATIN SMALL LETTER N character (n).

    3. [Add a vCard line](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) with the type name, the parameters parameters, and the value value to output.

12. If either sex or gender-identity has a value that is not the empty string, [add a vCard line](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) with the type "`GENDER`" and the value consisting of the concatenation of sex, a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;), and gender-identity to output.
13. [Add a vCard line](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) with the type "`END`" and the value "`VCARD`" to output.

When the above algorithm says that the user agent is to add a vCard line consisting of a type type, optionally some parameters, and a value value to a string output, it must run the following steps:
1. Let line be an empty string.
2. Append type, [converted to ASCII uppercase](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings), to line.
3. If there are any parameters, then for each parameter, in the order that they were added, run these substeps:
   1. Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to line.
   2. Append the parameter's name to line.
   3. Append a U+003D EQUALS SIGN character (=) to line.
   4. Append the parameter's value to line.
4. Append a U+003A COLON character (:) to line.
5. Append value to line.
6. Let maximum length be 75.
7. While line's [code point length](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) is greater than maximum length:
   1. Append the first maximum length code points of line to output.
   2. Remove the first maximum length code points from line.
   3. Append a U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN character (CR) to output.
   4. Append a U+000A LINE FEED character (LF) to output.
   5. Append a U+0020 SPACE character to output.
   6. Let maximum length be 74.
8. Append (what remains of) line to output.
9. Append a U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN character (CR) to output.
10. Append a U+000A LINE FEED character (LF) to output.

When the steps above require the user agent to obtain the result of collecting vCard subproperties named subname in subitem, the user agent must run the following steps:
1. Let value be the empty string.
2. For each property named subname in the item subitem, run the following substeps:
   1. If the [value](#524-values) of the property is itself an [item](#522-items), then skip this property.
   2. If this is not the first property named subname in subitem (ignoring any that were skipped by the previous step), then append a U+002C COMMA character (,) to value.
   3. Append the result of [escaping the vCard text string](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) given by the [value](#524-values) of the property to value.
3. Return value.

When the steps above require the user agent to obtain the result of collecting the first vCard subproperty named subname in subitem, the user agent must run the following steps:
1. If there are no properties named subname in subitem, then return the empty string.
2. If the [value](#524-values) of the first property named subname in subitem is an [item](#522-items), then return the empty string.
3. Return the result of [escaping the vCard text string](#5311-conversion-to-vcard) given by the [value](#524-values) of the first property named subname in subitem.

When the above algorithms say the user agent is to escape the vCard text string value, the user agent must use the following steps:
1. Prefix every U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\) in value with another U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\).
2. Prefix every U+002C COMMA character (,) in value with a U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\).
3. Prefix every U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) in value with a U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\).
4. Replace every U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN U+000A LINE FEED character pair (CRLF) in value with a U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\) followed by a U+006E LATIN SMALL LETTER N character (n).
5. Replace every remaining U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) or U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character in value with a U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\) followed by a U+006E LATIN SMALL LETTER N character (n).
6. Return the mutated value.

> [!note]
> This algorithm can generate invalid vCard output, if the input does not conform to the rules described for the [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard) [item type](#522-items) and [defined property names](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute).

##### 5.3.1.2 Examples

*This section is non-normative.*

> [!example]
> Here is a long example vCard for a fictional character called "Jack Bauer":
> 
> ```html
> <section id="jack" itemscope itemtype="http://microformats.org/profile/hcard">
>  <h1 itemprop="fn">
>   <span itemprop="n" itemscope>
>    <span itemprop="given-name">Jack</span>
>    <span itemprop="family-name">Bauer</span>
>   </span>
>  </h1>
>  <img itemprop="photo" alt="" src="jack-bauer.jpg">
>  <p itemprop="org" itemscope>
>   <span itemprop="organization-name">Counter-Terrorist Unit</span>
>   (<span itemprop="organization-unit">Los Angeles Division</span>)
>  </p>
>  <p>
>   <span itemprop="adr" itemscope>
>    <span itemprop="street-address">10201 W. Pico Blvd.</span><br>
>    <span itemprop="locality">Los Angeles</span>,
>    <span itemprop="region">CA</span>
>    <span itemprop="postal-code">90064</span><br>
>    <span itemprop="country-name">United States</span><br>
>   </span>
>   <span itemprop="geo">34.052339;-118.410623</span>
>  </p>
>  <h2>Assorted Contact Methods</h2>
>  <ul>
>   <li itemprop="tel" itemscope>
>    <span itemprop="value">+1 (310) 597 3781</span> <span itemprop="type">work</span>
>    <meta itemprop="type" content="voice">
>   </li>
>   <li><a itemprop="url" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Bauer">I'm on Wikipedia</a>
>   so you can leave a message on my user talk page.</li>
>   <li><a itemprop="url" href="http://www.jackbauerfacts.com/">Jack Bauer Facts</a></li>
>   <li itemprop="email"><a href="mailto:j.bauer@la.ctu.gov.invalid">j.bauer@la.ctu.gov.invalid</a></li>
>   <li itemprop="tel" itemscope>
>    <span itemprop="value">+1 (310) 555 3781</span> <span>
>    <meta itemprop="type" content="cell">mobile phone</span>
>   </li>
>  </ul>
>  <ins datetime="2008-07-20 21:00:00+01:00">
>   <meta itemprop="rev" content="2008-07-20 21:00:00+01:00">
>   <p itemprop="tel" itemscope><strong>Update!</strong>
>   My new <span itemprop="type">home</span> phone number is
>   <span itemprop="value">01632 960 123</span>.</p>
>  </ins>
> </section>
> ```
> 
> The odd line wrapping is needed because newlines are meaningful in microdata: newlines would be preserved in a conversion to, for example, the vCard format.

> [!example]
> This example shows a site's contact details (using the [`address`](#4310-the-address-element) element) containing an address with two street components:
> 
> ```html
> <address itemscope itemtype="http://microformats.org/profile/hcard">
>  <strong itemprop="fn"><span itemprop="n" itemscope><span itemprop="given-name">Alfred</span>
>  <span itemprop="family-name">Person</span></span></strong> <br>
>  <span itemprop="adr" itemscope>
>   <span itemprop="street-address">1600 Amphitheatre Parkway</span> <br>
>   <span itemprop="street-address">Building 43, Second Floor</span> <br>
>   <span itemprop="locality">Mountain View</span>,
>    <span itemprop="region">CA</span> <span itemprop="postal-code">94043</span>
>  </span>
> </address>
> ```

> [!example]
> The vCard vocabulary can be used to just mark up people's names:
> 
> ```html
> <span itemscope itemtype="http://microformats.org/profile/hcard"
> ><span itemprop=fn><span itemprop="n" itemscope><span itemprop="given-name"
> >George</span> <span itemprop="family-name">Washington</span></span
> ></span></span>
> ```
> 
> This creates a single item with a two name-value pairs, one with the name "fn" and the value "George Washington", and the other with the name "n" and a second item as its value, the second item having the two name-value pairs "given-name" and "family-name" with the values "George" and "Washington" respectively. This is defined to map to the following vCard:
> 
> ```
> BEGIN:VCARD
> PROFILE:VCARD
> VERSION:4.0
> SOURCE:document's address
> FN:George Washington
> N:Washington;George;;;
> END:VCARD
> ```

#### 5.3.2 vEvent

An item with the [item type](#522-items) `http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent` represents an event.

This vocabulary does not [support global identifiers for items](#522-items).

The following are the type's [defined property names](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute). They are based on the vocabulary defined in Internet Calendaring and Scheduling Core Object Specification (iCalendar), where more information on how to interpret the values can be found. [\[RFC5545\]](#references)

> [!note]
> Only the parts of the iCalendar vocabulary relating to events are used here; this vocabulary cannot express a complete iCalendar instance.

`attach`

Gives the address of an associated document for the event.

The [value](#524-values) must be an [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute).

Any number of properties with the name [`attach`](#532-vevent) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent).

`categories`

Gives the name of a category or tag that the event could be classified as.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

Any number of properties with the name [`categories`](#532-vevent) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent).

`class`

Gives the access classification of the information regarding the event.

The [value](#524-values) must be text with one of the following values:
- `public`
- `private`
- `confidential`

> [!warning]
> This is merely advisory and cannot be considered a confidentiality measure.

A single property with the name [`class`](#532-vevent) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent).

`comment`

Gives a comment regarding the event.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

Any number of properties with the name [`comment`](#532-vevent) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent).

`description`

Gives a detailed description of the event.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

A single property with the name [`description`](#532-vevent) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent).

`geo`

Gives the geographical position of the event.

The [value](#524-values) must be text and must match the following syntax:
1. Optionally, either a U+002B PLUS SIGN character (+) or a U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS character (-).
2. One or more [ASCII digits](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).
3. Optionally\*, a U+002E FULL STOP character (.) followed by one or more [ASCII digits](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).
4. A U+003B SEMICOLON character (;).
5. Optionally, either a U+002B PLUS SIGN character (+) or a U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS character (-).
6. One or more [ASCII digits](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).
7. Optionally\*, a U+002E FULL STOP character (.) followed by one or more [ASCII digits](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).

The optional components marked with an asterisk (\*) should be included, and should have six digits each.

> [!note]
> The value specifies latitude and longitude, in that order (i.e., "LAT LON" ordering), in decimal degrees. The longitude represents the location east and west of the prime meridian as a positive or negative real number, respectively. The latitude represents the location north and south of the equator as a positive or negative real number, respectively.

A single property with the name [`geo`](#532-vevent) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent).

`location`

Gives the location of the event.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

A single property with the name [`location`](#532-vevent) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent).

`resources`

Gives a resource that will be needed for the event.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

Any number of properties with the name [`resources`](#532-vevent) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent).

`status`

Gives the confirmation status of the event.

The [value](#524-values) must be text with one of the following values:
- `tentative`
- `confirmed`
- `canceled`

A single property with the name [`status`](#532-vevent) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent).

`summary`

Gives a short summary of the event.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

User agents should replace U+000A LINE FEED (LF) characters in the [value](#524-values) by U+0020 SPACE characters when using the value.

A single property with the name [`summary`](#532-vevent) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent).

`dtend`

Gives the date and time by which the event ends.

If the property with the name [`dtend`](#532-vevent) is present within an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent) that has a property with the name [`dtstart`](#532-vevent) whose value is a [valid date string](#2352-dates), then the [value](#524-values) of the property with the name [`dtend`](#532-vevent) must be text that is a [valid date string](#2352-dates) also. Otherwise, the [value](#524-values) of the property must be text that is a [valid global date and time string](#2357-global-dates-and-times).

In either case, the [value](#524-values) be later in time than the value of the [`dtstart`](#532-vevent) property of the same [item](#522-items).

> [!note]
> The time given by the [`dtend`](#532-vevent) property is not inclusive. For day-long events, therefore, the [`dtend`](#532-vevent) property's [value](#524-values) will be the day *after* the end of the event.

A single property with the name [`dtend`](#532-vevent) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent), so long as that [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent) does not have a property with the name [`duration`](#532-vevent).

`dtstart`

Gives the date and time at which the event starts.

The [value](#524-values) must be text that is either a [valid date string](#2352-dates) or a [valid global date and time string](#2357-global-dates-and-times).

Exactly one property with the name [`dtstart`](#532-vevent) must be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent).

`duration`

Gives the duration of the event.

The [value](#524-values) must be text that is a [valid vevent duration string](#532-vevent).

The duration represented is the sum of all the durations represented by integers in the value.

A single property with the name [`duration`](#532-vevent) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent), so long as that [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent) does not have a property with the name [`dtend`](#532-vevent).

`transp`

Gives whether the event is to be considered as consuming time on a calendar, for the purpose of free-busy time searches.

The [value](#524-values) must be text with one of the following values:
- `opaque`
- `transparent`

A single property with the name [`transp`](#532-vevent) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent).

`contact`

Gives the contact information for the event.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

Any number of properties with the name [`contact`](#532-vevent) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent).

`url`

Gives a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) for the event.

The [value](#524-values) must be an [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute).

A single property with the name [`url`](#532-vevent) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent).

`uid`

Gives a globally unique identifier corresponding to the event.

The [value](#524-values) must be text.

A single property with the name [`uid`](#532-vevent) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent).

`exdate`

Gives a date and time at which the event does not occur despite the recurrence rules.

The [value](#524-values) must be text that is either a [valid date string](#2352-dates) or a [valid global date and time string](#2357-global-dates-and-times).

Any number of properties with the name [`exdate`](#532-vevent) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent).

`rdate`

Gives a date and time at which the event recurs.

The [value](#524-values) must be text that is one of the following:
- A [valid date string](#2352-dates).
- A [valid global date and time string](#2357-global-dates-and-times).
- A [valid global date and time string](#2357-global-dates-and-times) followed by a U+002F SOLIDUS character (/) followed by a second [valid global date and time string](#2357-global-dates-and-times) representing a later time.
- A [valid global date and time string](#2357-global-dates-and-times) followed by a U+002F SOLIDUS character (/) followed by a [valid vevent duration string](#532-vevent).

Any number of properties with the name [`rdate`](#532-vevent) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent).

`rrule`

Gives a rule for finding dates and times at which the event occurs.

The [value](#524-values) must be text that matches the RECUR value type defined in iCalendar. [\[RFC5545\]](#references)

A single property with the name [`rrule`](#532-vevent) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent).

`created`

Gives the date and time at which the event information was first created in a calendaring system.

The [value](#524-values) must be text that is a [valid global date and time string](#2357-global-dates-and-times).

A single property with the name [`created`](#532-vevent) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent).

`last-modified`

Gives the date and time at which the event information was last modified in a calendaring system.

The [value](#524-values) must be text that is a [valid global date and time string](#2357-global-dates-and-times).

A single property with the name [`last-modified`](#532-vevent) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent).

`sequence`

Gives a revision number for the event information.

The [value](#524-values) must be text that is a [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers).

A single property with the name [`sequence`](#532-vevent) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent).

A string is a valid vevent duration string if it matches the following pattern:
1. A U+0050 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER P character (P).
2. One of the following:
   - A [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers) followed by a U+0057 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER W character (W). The integer represents a duration of that number of weeks.
   - At least one, and possible both in this order, of the following:
     1. A [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers) followed by a U+0044 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER D character (D). The integer represents a duration of that number of days.
     2. A U+0054 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER T character (T) followed by any one of the following, or the first and second of the following in that order, or the second and third of the following in that order, or all three of the following in this order:
        1. A [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers) followed by a U+0048 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER H character (H). The integer represents a duration of that number of hours.
        2. A [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers) followed by a U+004D LATIN CAPITAL LETTER M character (M). The integer represents a duration of that number of minutes.
        3. A [valid non-negative integer](#2342-non-negative-integers) followed by a U+0053 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER S character (S). The integer represents a duration of that number of seconds.

##### 5.3.2.1 Conversion to iCalendar

Given a list of nodes nodes in a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), a user agent must run the following algorithm to extract any vEvent data represented by those nodes:
1. If none of the nodes in nodes are [items](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent), then there is no vEvent data. Abort the algorithm, returning nothing.
2. Let output be an empty string.
3. [Add an iCalendar line](#5321-conversion-to-icalendar) with the type "`BEGIN`" and the value "`VCALENDAR`" to output.
4. [Add an iCalendar line](#5321-conversion-to-icalendar) with the type "`PRODID`" and the value equal to a user-agent-specific string representing the user agent to output.
5. [Add an iCalendar line](#5321-conversion-to-icalendar) with the type "`VERSION`" and the value "`2.0`" to output.
6. For each node node in nodes that is an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent), run the following steps:
   1. [Add an iCalendar line](#5321-conversion-to-icalendar) with the type "`BEGIN`" and the value "`VEVENT`" to output.
   2. [Add an iCalendar line](#5321-conversion-to-icalendar) with the type "`DTSTAMP`" and a value consisting of an iCalendar DATE-TIME string representing the current date and time, with the annotation "`VALUE=DATE-TIME`", to output. [\[RFC5545\]](#references)
   3. For each element element that is [a property of the item](#525-associating-names-with-items) node: for each name name in element's [property names](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute), run the appropriate set of substeps from the following list:

      If the property's [value](#524-values) is an [item](#522-items)

      Skip the property.

      If the property is [`dtend`](#532-vevent)

      If the property is [`dtstart`](#532-vevent)

      If the property is [`exdate`](#532-vevent)

      If the property is [`rdate`](#532-vevent)

      If the property is [`created`](#532-vevent)

      If the property is [`last-modified`](#532-vevent)

      Let value be the result of stripping all U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS (-) and U+003A COLON (:) characters from the property's [value](#524-values).

      If the property's [value](#524-values) is a [valid date string](#2352-dates), then [add an iCalendar line](#5321-conversion-to-icalendar) with the type name and the value value to output, with the annotation "`VALUE=DATE`".

      Otherwise, if the property's [value](#524-values) is a [valid global date and time string](#2357-global-dates-and-times), then [add an iCalendar line](#5321-conversion-to-icalendar) with the type name and the value value to output, with the annotation "`VALUE=DATE-TIME`".

      Otherwise, skip the property.

      Otherwise

      [Add an iCalendar line](#5321-conversion-to-icalendar) with the type name and the property's [value](#524-values) to output.

   4. [Add an iCalendar line](#5321-conversion-to-icalendar) with the type "`END`" and the value "`VEVENT`" to output.

7. [Add an iCalendar line](#5321-conversion-to-icalendar) with the type "`END`" and the value "`VCALENDAR`" to output.

When the above algorithm says that the user agent is to add an iCalendar line consisting of a type type, a value value, and optionally an annotation, to a string output, it must run the following steps:
1. Let line be an empty string.
2. Append type, [converted to ASCII uppercase](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings), to line.
3. If there is an annotation:
   1. Append a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) to line.
   2. Append the annotation to line.
4. Append a U+003A COLON character (:) to line.
5. Prefix every U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\) in value with another U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\).
6. Prefix every U+002C COMMA character (,) in value with a U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\).
7. Prefix every U+003B SEMICOLON character (;) in value with a U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\).
8. Replace every U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN U+000A LINE FEED character pair (CRLF) in value with a U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\) followed by a U+006E LATIN SMALL LETTER N character (n).
9. Replace every remaining U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) or U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character in value with a U+005C REVERSE SOLIDUS character (\\) followed by a U+006E LATIN SMALL LETTER N character (n).
10. Append value to line.
11. Let maximum length be 75.
12. While line's [code point length](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) is greater than maximum length:
    1. Append the first maximum length code points of line to output.
    2. Remove the first maximum length code points from line.
    3. Append a U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN character (CR) to output.
    4. Append a U+000A LINE FEED character (LF) to output.
    5. Append a U+0020 SPACE character to output.
    6. Let maximum length be 74.
13. Append (what remains of) line to output.
14. Append a U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN character (CR) to output.
15. Append a U+000A LINE FEED character (LF) to output.

> [!note]
> This algorithm can generate invalid iCalendar output, if the input does not conform to the rules described for the [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent`](#532-vevent) [item type](#522-items) and [defined property names](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute).

##### 5.3.2.2 Examples

*This section is non-normative.*

> [!example]
> Here is an example of a page that uses the vEvent vocabulary to mark up an event:
> 
> ```html
> <body itemscope itemtype="http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent">
>  ...
>  <h1 itemprop="summary">Bluesday Tuesday: Money Road</h1>
>  ...
>  <time itemprop="dtstart" datetime="2009-05-05T19:00:00Z">May 5th @ 7pm</time>
>  (until <time itemprop="dtend" datetime="2009-05-05T21:00:00Z">9pm</time>)
>  ...
>  <a href="http://livebrum.co.uk/2009/05/05/bluesday-tuesday-money-road"
>     rel="bookmark" itemprop="url">Link to this page</a>
>  ...
>  <p>Location: <span itemprop="location">The RoadHouse</span></p>
>  ...
>  <p><input type=button value="Add to Calendar"
>            onclick="location = getCalendar(this)"></p>
>  ...
>  <meta itemprop="description" content="via livebrum.co.uk">
> </body>
> ```
> 
> The `getCalendar()` function is left as an exercise for the reader.
> 
> The same page could offer some markup, such as the following, for copy-and-pasting into blogs:
> 
> ```html
> <div itemscope itemtype="http://microformats.org/profile/hcalendar#vevent">
>  <p>I'm going to
>  <strong itemprop="summary">Bluesday Tuesday: Money Road</strong>,
>  <time itemprop="dtstart" datetime="2009-05-05T19:00:00Z">May 5th at 7pm</time>
>  to <time itemprop="dtend" datetime="2009-05-05T21:00:00Z">9pm</time>,
>  at <span itemprop="location">The RoadHouse</span>!</p>
>  <p><a href="http://livebrum.co.uk/2009/05/05/bluesday-tuesday-money-road"
>        itemprop="url">See this event on livebrum.co.uk</a>.</p>
>  <meta itemprop="description" content="via livebrum.co.uk">
> </div>
> ```

#### 5.3.3 Licensing works

An item with the [item type](#522-items) `http://n.whatwg.org/work` represents a work (e.g. an article, an image, a video, a song, etc.). This type is primarily intended to allow authors to include licensing information for works.

The following are the type's [defined property names](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute).

`work`

Identifies the work being described.

The [value](#524-values) must be an [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute).

Exactly one property with the name [`work`](#533-licensing-works) must be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://n.whatwg.org/work`](#533-licensing-works).

`title`

Gives the name of the work.

A single property with the name [`title`](#533-licensing-works) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://n.whatwg.org/work`](#533-licensing-works).

`author`

Gives the name or contact information of one of the authors or creators of the work.

The [value](#524-values) must be either an [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://microformats.org/profile/hcard`](#531-vcard), or text.

Any number of properties with the name [`author`](#533-licensing-works) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://n.whatwg.org/work`](#533-licensing-works).

`license`

Identifies one of the licenses under which the work is available.

The [value](#524-values) must be an [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute).

Any number of properties with the name [`license`](#533-licensing-works) may be present within each [item](#522-items) with the type [`http://n.whatwg.org/work`](#533-licensing-works).

##### 5.3.3.1 Examples

*This section is non-normative.*

> [!example]
> This example shows an embedded image entitled My Pond, licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0 International License and the MIT license simultaneously.
> 
> ```html
> <figure itemscope itemtype="http://n.whatwg.org/work">
>  <img itemprop="work" src="mypond.jpeg">
>  <figcaption>
>   <p><cite itemprop="title">My Pond</cite></p>
>   <p><small>Licensed under the <a itemprop="license"
>   href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/">Creative
>   Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0 International License</a>
>   and the <a itemprop="license"
>   href="http://www.opensource.org/licenses/mit-license.php">MIT
>   license</a>.</small>
>  </figcaption>
> </figure>
> ```

### 5.4 Converting HTML to other formats

#### 5.4.1 JSON

Given a list of nodes nodes in a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), a user agent must run the following algorithm to extract the microdata from those nodes into a JSON form:
1. Let result be an empty object.
2. Let items be an empty array.
3. For each node in nodes, check if the element is a [top-level microdata item](#525-associating-names-with-items), and if it is then [get the object](#541-json) for that element and add it to items.
4. Add an entry to result called "`items`" whose value is the array items.
5. Return the result of serializing result to JSON in the shortest possible way (meaning no whitespace between tokens, no unnecessary zero digits in numbers, and only using Unicode escapes in strings for characters that do not have a dedicated escape sequence), and with a lowercase "`e`" used, when appropriate, in the representation of any numbers. [\[JSON\]](#references)

> [!note]
> This algorithm returns an object with a single property that is an array, instead of just returning an array, so that it is possible to extend the algorithm in the future if necessary.

When the user agent is to get the object for an item item, optionally with a list of elements memory, it must run the following substeps:
1. Let result be an empty object.
2. If no memory was passed to the algorithm, let memory be an empty list.
3. Add item to memory.
4. If the item has any [item types](#522-items), add an entry to result called "`type`" whose value is an array listing the [item types](#522-items) of item, in the order they were specified on the [`itemtype`](#522-items) attribute.
5. If the item has a [global identifier](#522-items), add an entry to result called "`id`" whose value is the [global identifier](#522-items) of item.
6. Let properties be an empty object.
7. For each element element that has one or more [property names](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute) and is one of [the properties of the item](#525-associating-names-with-items) item, in the order those elements are given by the algorithm that returns [the properties of an item](#525-associating-names-with-items), run the following substeps:
   1. Let value be the [property value](#524-values) of element.
   2. If value is an [item](#522-items), then: if value is in memory, then let value be the string "`ERROR`". Otherwise, [get the object](#541-json) for value, passing a copy of memory, and then replace value with the object returned from those steps.
   3. For each name name in element's [property names](#523-names-the-itemprop-attribute), run the following substeps:
      1. If there is no entry named name in properties, then add an entry named name to properties whose value is an empty array.
      2. Append value to the entry named name in properties.
8. Add an entry to result called "`properties`" whose value is the object properties.
9. Return result.

> [!example]
> For example, take this markup:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <html lang="en">
> <title>My Blog</title>
> <article itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/BlogPosting">
>  <header>
>   <h1 itemprop="headline">Progress report</h1>
>   <p><time itemprop="datePublished" datetime="2013-08-29">today</time></p>
>   <link itemprop="url" href="?comments=0">
>  </header>
>  <p>All in all, he's doing well with his swim lessons. The biggest thing was he had trouble
>  putting his head in, but we got it down.</p>
>  <section>
>   <h1>Comments</h1>
>   <article itemprop="comment" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/UserComments" id="c1">
>    <link itemprop="url" href="#c1">
>    <footer>
