>     <p>Posted by: <span itemprop="creator" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person">
>      <span itemprop="name">Greg</span>
>     </span></p>
>     <p><time itemprop="commentTime" datetime="2013-08-29">15 minutes ago</time></p>
>    </footer>
>    <p>Ha!</p>
>   </article>
>   <article itemprop="comment" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/UserComments" id="c2">
>    <link itemprop="url" href="#c2">
>    <footer>
>     <p>Posted by: <span itemprop="creator" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person">
>      <span itemprop="name">Charlotte</span>
>     </span></p>
>     <p><time itemprop="commentTime" datetime="2013-08-29">5 minutes ago</time></p>
>    </footer>
>    <p>When you say "we got it down"...</p>
>   </article>
>  </section>
> </article>
> ```
> 
> It would be turned into the following JSON by the algorithm above (supposing that the page's URL was `https://blog.example.com/progress-report`):
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "items": [
>     {
>       "type": [ "http://schema.org/BlogPosting" ],
>       "properties": {
>         "headline": [ "Progress report" ],
>         "datePublished": [ "2013-08-29" ],
>         "url": [ "https://blog.example.com/progress-report?comments=0" ],
>         "comment": [
>           {
>             "type": [ "http://schema.org/UserComments" ],
>             "properties": {
>               "url": [ "https://blog.example.com/progress-report#c1" ],
>               "creator": [
>                 {
>                   "type": [ "http://schema.org/Person" ],
>                   "properties": {
>                     "name": [ "Greg" ]
>                   }
>                 }
>               ],
>               "commentTime": [ "2013-08-29" ]
>             }
>           },
>           {
>             "type": [ "http://schema.org/UserComments" ],
>             "properties": {
>               "url": [ "https://blog.example.com/progress-report#c2" ],
>               "creator": [
>                 {
>                   "type": [ "http://schema.org/Person" ],
>                   "properties": {
>                     "name": [ "Charlotte" ]
>                   }
>                 }
>               ],
>               "commentTime": [ "2013-08-29" ]
>             }
>           }
>         ]
>       }
>     }
>   ]
> }
> ```

## 6 User interaction

### 6.1 The [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute

All [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) may have the `hidden` content attribute set. The [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hidden` | Hidden | Will not be rendered. |
| `until-found` | Hidden Until Found | Will not be rendered, but content inside will be accessible to [find-in-page](#691-introduction) and [fragment navigation](#74233-fragment-navigations). |

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* is the Not Hidden state, and its *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[empty value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the [Hidden](#61-the-hidden-attribute) state.

When an element has the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute in the [Hidden](#61-the-hidden-attribute) state, it indicates that the element is not yet, or is no longer, directly relevant to the page's current state, or that it is being used to declare content to be reused by other parts of the page as opposed to being directly accessed by the user. User agents should not render elements that are in the [Hidden](#61-the-hidden-attribute) state.

> [!note]
> The requirement for user agents not to render elements that are in the [Hidden](#61-the-hidden-attribute) state can be implemented indirectly through the style layer. For example, a web browser could implement these requirements [using the rules suggested in the Rendering section](#1531-hidden-elements).

When an element has the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute in the [Hidden Until Found](#61-the-hidden-attribute) state, it indicates that the element is hidden like the [Hidden](#61-the-hidden-attribute) state but the content inside the element will be accessible to [find-in-page](#691-introduction) and [fragment navigation](#74233-fragment-navigations). When these features attempt to scroll to a target which is in the element's subtree, the user agent will remove the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute in order to reveal the content before scrolling to it by running the [ancestor revealing algorithm](#61-the-hidden-attribute) on the target node.

> [!note]
> Web browsers will use 'content-visibility: hidden' instead of 'display: none' when the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute is in the [Hidden Until Found](#61-the-hidden-attribute) state, as specified in the [Rendering section](#1531-hidden-elements).

> [!note]
> Because this attribute is typically implemented using CSS, it's also possible to override it using CSS. For instance, a rule that applies 'display: block' to all elements will cancel the effects of the [Hidden](#61-the-hidden-attribute) state. Authors therefore have to take care when writing their style sheets to make sure that the attribute is still styled as expected. In addition, legacy user agents which don't support the [Hidden Until Found](#61-the-hidden-attribute) state will have 'display: none' instead of 'content-visibility: hidden', so authors are encouraged to make sure that their style sheets don't change the 'display' or 'content-visibility' properties of [Hidden Until Found](#61-the-hidden-attribute) elements.
> 
> Since elements with the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute in the [Hidden Until Found](#61-the-hidden-attribute) state use 'content-visibility: hidden' instead of 'display: none', there are two caveats of the [Hidden Until Found](#61-the-hidden-attribute) state that make it different from the [Hidden](#61-the-hidden-attribute) state:
> 1. The element needs to be affected by [layout containment](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-contain/#containment-layout) in order to be revealed by find-in-page. This means that if the element in the [Hidden Until Found](#61-the-hidden-attribute) state has a 'display' value of 'none', 'contents', or 'inline', then the element will not be revealed by find-in-page.
> 2. The element will still have a [generated box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#propdef-visibility) when in the [Hidden Until Found](#61-the-hidden-attribute) state, which means that borders, margin, and padding will still be rendered around the element.

> [!example]
> In the following skeletal example, the attribute is used to hide the web game's main screen until the user logs in:
> 
> ```html
>   <h1>The Example Game</h1>
>   <section id="login">
>    <h2>Login</h2>
>    <form>
>     ...
>     <!-- calls login() once the user's credentials have been checked -->
>    </form>
>    <script>
>     function login() {
>       // switch screens
>       document.getElementById('login').hidden = true;
>       document.getElementById('game').hidden = false;
>     }
>    </script>
>   </section>
>   <section id="game" hidden>
>    ...
>   </section>
> ```

The [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute must not be used to hide content that could legitimately be shown in another presentation. For example, it is incorrect to use [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) to hide panels in a tabbed dialog, because the tabbed interface is merely a kind of overflow presentation — one could equally well just show all the form controls in one big page with a scrollbar. It is similarly incorrect to use this attribute to hide content just from one presentation — if something is marked [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute), it is hidden from all presentations, including, for instance, screen readers.

Elements that are not themselves [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) must not [hyperlink](#461-introduction) to elements that are [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute). The `for` attributes of [`label`](#4104-the-label-element) and [`output`](#41012-the-output-element) elements that are not themselves [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) must similarly not refer to elements that are [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute). In both cases, such references would cause user confusion.

Elements and scripts may, however, refer to elements that are [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) in other contexts.

> [!example]
> For example, it would be incorrect to use the [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute to link to a section marked with the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute. If the content is not applicable or relevant, then there is no reason to link to it.
> 
> It would be fine, however, to use the ARIA [`aria-describedby`](https://w3c.github.io/aria/#aria-describedby) attribute to refer to descriptions that are themselves [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute). While hiding the descriptions implies that they are not useful alone, they could be written in such a way that they are useful in the specific context of being referenced from the elements that they describe.
> 
> Similarly, a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element with the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute could be used by a scripted graphics engine as an off-screen buffer, and a form control could refer to a hidden [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element using its [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) attribute.

Elements in a section hidden by the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute are still active, e.g. scripts and form controls in such sections still execute and submit respectively. Only their presentation to the user changes.

The `hidden` getter steps are:
1. If the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute is in the [Hidden Until Found](#61-the-hidden-attribute) state, then return "[`until-found`](#61-the-hidden-attribute)".
2. If the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute is set, then return true.
3. Return false.

The [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) setter steps are:
1. If the given value is a string that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for "[`until-found`](#61-the-hidden-attribute)", then set the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute to "[`until-found`](#61-the-hidden-attribute)".
2. Otherwise, if the given value is false, then remove the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute.
3. Otherwise, if the given value is the empty string, then remove the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute.
4. Otherwise, if the given value is null, then remove the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute.
5. Otherwise, if the given value is 0, then remove the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute.
6. Otherwise, if the given value is NaN, then remove the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute.
7. Otherwise, set the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute to the empty string.

An ancestor reveal pair is a [tuple](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#531-tuples) consisting of a node and a string.

The ancestor revealing algorithm given a node target is:
1. Let ancestorsToReveal be « ».
2. Let ancestor be target.
3. While ancestor has a parent node within the [flat tree](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scoping/#flat-tree):
   1. If ancestor has a [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute in the [Hidden Until Found](#61-the-hidden-attribute) state, then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) (ancestor, "`until-found`") to ancestorsToReveal.
   2. If ancestor is slotted into the second slot of a [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element which does not have an [`open`](#4111-the-details-element) attribute, then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) (ancestor's parent node, "`details`") to ancestorsToReveal.
   3. Set ancestor to the parent node of ancestor within the [flat tree](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scoping/#flat-tree).
4. For each (ancestorToReveal, revealType) of ancestorsToReveal:
   1. If ancestorToReveal is not [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree), then return.
   2. If revealType is "`until-found`":
      1. If ancestorToReveal's [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute is not in the [Hidden Until Found](#61-the-hidden-attribute) state, then return.
      2. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`beforematch`](#events) at ancestorToReveal with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true.
      3. If ancestorToReveal is not [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree), then return.
      4. If ancestorToReveal's [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute is not in the [Hidden Until Found](#61-the-hidden-attribute) state, then return.
      5. Remove the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute from ancestorToReveal.
   3. Otherwise:
      1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): revealType is "`details`".
      2. If ancestorToReveal has an [`open`](#4111-the-details-element) attribute, then return.
      3. Set ancestorToReveal's [`open`](#4111-the-details-element) attribute to the empty string.

### 6.2 Page visibility

A [traversable navigable](#7311-traversable-navigables)'s [system visibility state](#7311-traversable-navigables), including its initial value upon creation, is determined by the user agent. It represents, for example, whether the browser window is minimized, a browser tab is currently in the background, or a system element such as a task switcher obscures the page.

When a user agent determines that the [system visibility state](#7311-traversable-navigables) for [traversable navigable](#7311-traversable-navigables) traversable has changed to newState, it must run the following steps:
1. Let navigables be the [inclusive descendant navigables](#7315-related-navigable-collections) of traversable's [active document](#731-navigables).
2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) navigable of navigables in what order?:
   1. Let document be navigable's [active document](#731-navigables).
   2. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [user interaction task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given document's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) to [update the visibility state](#62-page-visibility) of document with newState.

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a visibility state, which is either "`hidden`" or "`visible`", initially set to "`hidden`".

The `visibilityState` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [visibility state](#62-page-visibility).

The `hidden` getter steps are to return true if [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [visibility state](#62-page-visibility) is "`hidden`", otherwise false.

To update the visibility state of [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document to visibilityState:
1. If document's [visibility state](#62-page-visibility) equals visibilityState, then return.
2. Set document's [visibility state](#62-page-visibility) to visibilityState.
3. [Queue](https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#queue-a-performanceentry) a new [`VisibilityStateEntry`](#621-the-visibilitystateentry-interface) whose [visibility state](#621-the-visibilitystateentry-interface) is visibilityState and whose [timestamp](#621-the-visibilitystateentry-interface) is the [current high resolution time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time) given document's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant).
4. Run the [screen orientation change steps](https://w3c.github.io/screen-orientation/#dfn-screen-orientation-change-steps) with document. [\[SCREENORIENTATION\]](#references)
5. Run the [view transition page visibility change steps](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-view-transitions/#view-transition-page-visibility-change-steps) with document.
6. Run any page visibility change steps which may be defined in other specifications, with [visibility state](#62-page-visibility) and document.

   > [!warning]
   > It would be better if specification authors sent a pull request to add calls from here into their specifications directly, instead of using the [page visibility change steps](#62-page-visibility) hook, to ensure well-defined cross-specification call order. As of the time of this writing the following specifications are known to have [page visibility change steps](#62-page-visibility), which will be run in an unspecified order: Device Posture API and Web NFC. [\[DEVICEPOSTURE\]](#references) [\[WEBNFC\]](#references)

7. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`visibilitychange`](#events) at document, with its [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true.

To set the initial visibility state of [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document to visibilityState:
1. Set document's [visibility state](#62-page-visibility) to visibilityState.
2. [Queue](https://w3c.github.io/performance-timeline/#queue-a-performanceentry) a new [`VisibilityStateEntry`](#621-the-visibilitystateentry-interface) whose [visibility state](#621-the-visibilitystateentry-interface) is document's [visibility state](#62-page-visibility) and whose [timestamp](#621-the-visibilitystateentry-interface) is 0.

#### 6.2.1 The [`VisibilityStateEntry`](#621-the-visibilitystateentry-interface) interface

The [`VisibilityStateEntry`](#621-the-visibilitystateentry-interface) interface exposes visibility changes to the document, from the moment the document becomes active.

> [!example]
> For example, this allows JavaScript code in the page to examine correlation between visibility changes and paint timing:
> 
> ```javascript
> function wasHiddenBeforeFirstContentfulPaint() {
>     const fcpEntry = performance.getEntriesByName("first-contentful-paint")[0];
>     const visibilityStateEntries = performance.getEntriesByType("visibility-state");
>     return visibilityStateEntries.some(e =>
>                                             e.startTime < fcpEntry.startTime &&
>                                             e.name === "hidden");
> }
> ```

> [!note]
> Since hiding a page can cause throttling of rendering and other user-agent operations, it is common to use visibility changes as an indication that such throttling has occurred. However, other things could also cause throttling in different browsers, such as long periods of inactivity.

```webidl
[Exposed=(Window)]
interface VisibilityStateEntry : PerformanceEntry {
  readonly attribute DOMString name;                 // shadows inherited name
  readonly attribute DOMString entryType;            // shadows inherited entryType
  readonly attribute DOMHighResTimeStamp startTime;  // shadows inherited startTime
  readonly attribute unsigned long duration;         // shadows inherited duration
};
```

The [`VisibilityStateEntry`](#621-the-visibilitystateentry-interface) has an associated [`DOMHighResTimeStamp`](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dom-domhighrestimestamp) timestamp.

The [`VisibilityStateEntry`](#621-the-visibilitystateentry-interface) has an associated "`visible`" or "`hidden`" visibility state.

The `name` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [visibility state](#621-the-visibilitystateentry-interface).

The `entryType` getter steps are to return "`visibility-state`".

The `startTime` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [timestamp](#621-the-visibilitystateentry-interface).

The `duration` getter steps are to return zero.

### 6.3 Inert subtrees

> [!note]
> See also [`inert`](#632-the-inert-attribute) for an explanation of the attribute of the same name.

A node (in particular elements and text nodes) can be inert. When a node is [inert](#63-inert-subtrees):
- Hit-testing must act as if the ['pointer-events'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui-4/#pointer-events-control) CSS property were set to 'none'.
- Text selection functionality must act as if the ['user-select'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui-4/#content-selection) CSS property were set to 'none'.
- If it is [editable](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable), the node behaves as if it were non-editable.
- The user agent should ignore the node for the purposes of [find-in-page](#691-introduction).

> [!note]
> Inert nodes generally cannot be focused, and user agents do not expose the inert nodes to accessibility APIs or assistive technologies. Inert nodes that are [commands](#41131-facets) will become inoperable to users, in the manner described above.

User agents may allow the user to override the restrictions on [find-in-page](#691-introduction) and text selection, however.

By default, a node is not [inert](#63-inert-subtrees).

#### 6.3.1 Modal dialogs and inert subtrees

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document is blocked by a modal dialog subject if subject is the topmost [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) element in document's [top layer](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position-4/#document-top-layer). While document is so blocked, every node that is [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree) to document, with the exception of the subject element and its [flat tree](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scoping/#flat-tree) descendants, must become [inert](#63-inert-subtrees).

subject can additionally become [inert](#63-inert-subtrees) via the [`inert`](#632-the-inert-attribute) attribute, but only if specified on subject itself (i.e., subject escapes inertness of ancestors); subject's [flat tree](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scoping/#flat-tree) descendants can become [inert](#63-inert-subtrees) in a similar fashion.

> [!note]
> The [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) element's [`showModal()`](#4114-the-dialog-element) method causes this mechanism to trigger, by [adding](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position-4/#add-an-element-to-the-top-layer) the [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) element to its [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [top layer](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position-4/#document-top-layer).

#### 6.3.2 The `inert` attribute

The [`inert`](#632-the-inert-attribute) attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes) that indicates, by its presence, that the element and all its [flat tree](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scoping/#flat-tree) descendants which don't otherwise escape inertness (such as modal dialogs) are to be made [inert](#63-inert-subtrees) by the user agent.

An inert subtree should not contain any content or controls which are critical to understanding or using aspects of the page which are not in the inert state. Content in an inert subtree will not be perceivable by all users, or interactive. Authors should not specify elements as inert unless the content they represent are also visually obscured in some way. In most cases, authors should not specify the [`inert`](#63-inert-subtrees) attribute on individual form controls. In these instances, the [`disabled`](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute) attribute is probably more appropriate.

> [!example]
> The following example shows how to mark partially loaded content, visually obscured by a "loading" message, as inert.
> 
> ```html
> <section aria-labelledby=s1>
>   <h3 id=s1>Population by City</h3>
>   <div class=container>
>     <div class=loading><p>Loading...</p></div>
>     <div inert>
>       <form>
>         <fieldset>
>           <legend>Date range</legend>
>           <div>
>             <label for=start>Start</label>
>             <input type=date id=start>
>           </div>
>           <div>
>             <label for=end>End</label>
>             <input type=date id=end>
>           </div>
>           <div>
>             <button>Apply</button>
>           </div>
>         </fieldset>
>       </form>
>       <table>
>         <caption>From 20-- to 20--</caption>
>         <thead>
>           <tr>
>             <th>City</th>
>             <th>State</th>
>             <th>20-- Population</th>
>             <th>20-- Population</th>
>             <th>Percentage change</th>
>           </tr>
>         </thead>
>         <tbody>
>           <!-- ... -->
>         </tbody>
>       </table>
>     </div>
>   </div>
> </section>
> ```
> 
> ![Screenshot of Population by City content with an overlaid loading message which visually obscures the form controls and data table which have not fully rendered, and thus are in the inert state.](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/inert-example-loading-section.png)
> 
> The "loading" overlay obscures the inert content, making it visually apparent that the inert content is not presently accessible. Notice that the heading and "loading" text are not descendants of the element with the [`inert`](#63-inert-subtrees) attribute. This will ensure this text is accessible to all users, while the inert content cannot be interacted with by anyone.

> [!note]
> By default, there is no persistent visual indication of an element or its subtree being inert. Appropriate visual styles for such content is often context-dependent. For instance, an inert off-screen navigation panel would not require a default style, as its off-screen position visually obscures the content. Similarly, a modal [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) element's backdrop will serve as the means to visually obscure the inert content of the web page, rather than styling the inert content specifically.
> 
> However, for many other situations authors are strongly encouraged to clearly mark what parts of their document are active and which are inert, to avoid user confusion. In particular, it is worth remembering that not all users can see all parts of a page at once; for example, users of screen readers, users on small devices or with magnifiers, and even users using particularly small windows might not be able to see the active part of a page and might get frustrated if inert sections are not obviously inert.

### 6.4 Tracking user activation

To prevent abuse of certain APIs that could be annoying to users (e.g., opening popups or vibrating phones), user agents allow these APIs only when the user is actively interacting with the web page or has interacted with the page at least once. This "active interaction" state is maintained through the mechanisms defined in this section.

#### 6.4.1 Data model

For the purpose of tracking user activation, each [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) W has two relevant values:
- A last activation timestamp, which is either a [`DOMHighResTimeStamp`](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dom-domhighrestimestamp), positive infinity (indicating that W has never been activated), or negative infinity (indicating that the activation has been [consumed](#642-processing-model)). Initially positive infinity.
- A last history-action activation timestamp, which is either a [`DOMHighResTimeStamp`](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dom-domhighrestimestamp) or positive infinity, initially positive infinity.

A user agent also defines a transient activation duration, which is a constant number indicating how long a user activation is available for certain [user activation-gated APIs](#643-apis-gated-by-user-activation) (e.g., for opening popups).

> [!note]
> The [transient activation duration](#641-data-model) is expected be at most a few seconds, so that the user can possibly perceive the link between an interaction with the page and the page calling the activation-gated API.

We then have the following boolean user activation states for W:

Sticky activation

When the [current high resolution time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time) given W is greater than or equal to the [last activation timestamp](#641-data-model) in W, W is said to have [sticky activation](#641-data-model).

This is W's historical activation state, indicating whether the user has ever interacted in W. It starts false, then changes to true (and never changes back to false) when W gets the very first [activation notification](#642-processing-model).

Transient activation

When the [current high resolution time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time) given W is greater than or equal to the [last activation timestamp](#641-data-model) in W, and less than the [last activation timestamp](#641-data-model) in W plus the [transient activation duration](#641-data-model), then W is said to have [transient activation](#641-data-model).

This is W's current activation state, indicating whether the user has interacted in W recently. This starts with a false value, and remains true for a limited time after every [activation notification](#642-processing-model) W gets.

The [transient activation](#641-data-model) state is considered expired if it becomes false because the [transient activation duration](#641-data-model) time has elapsed since the last user activation. Note that it can become false even before the expiry time through an [activation consumption](#642-processing-model).

History-action activation

When the [last history-action activation timestamp](#641-data-model) of W is not equal to the [last activation timestamp](#641-data-model) of W, then W is said to have [history-action activation](#641-data-model).

This is a special variant of user activation, used to allow access to certain session history APIs which, if used too frequently, would make it harder for the user to traverse back using [browser UI](#79-browser-user-interface-considerations). It starts with a false value, and becomes true whenever the user interacts with W, but is reset to false through [history-action activation consumption](#642-processing-model). This ensures such APIs cannot be used multiple times in a row without an intervening user activation. But unlike [transient activation](#641-data-model), there is no time limit within which such APIs must be used.

> [!note]
> The [last activation timestamp](#641-data-model) and [last history-action activation timestamp](#641-data-model) are retained even after the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) changes its [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents) status (e.g., after navigating away from a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), or navigating to a cached [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)). This means [sticky activation](#641-data-model) state spans multiple navigations as long as the same [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) gets reused. For the transient activation state, the original [expiry](#641-data-model) time remains unchanged (i.e., the state still expires within the [transient activation duration](#641-data-model) limit from the original [activation triggering input event](#642-processing-model)). It is important to consider this when deciding whether to base certain things off [sticky activation](#641-data-model) or [transient activation](#641-data-model).

#### 6.4.2 Processing model

When a user interaction causes firing of an [activation triggering input event](#642-processing-model) in a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document, the user agent must perform the following activation notification steps *before* [dispatching](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#29-dispatching-events) the event:
1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): document is [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents).
2. Let windows be « document's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) ».
3. [Extend](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) windows with the [active window](#731-navigables) of each of document's [ancestor navigables](#7315-related-navigable-collections).
4. [Extend](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) windows with the [active window](#731-navigables) of each of document's [descendant navigables](#7315-related-navigable-collections), filtered to include only those [navigables](#731-navigables) whose [active document](#731-navigables)'s [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is [same origin](#711-origins) with document's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).
5. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) window in windows:
   1. Set window's [last activation timestamp](#641-data-model) to the [current high resolution time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time).
   2. [Notify the close watcher manager about user activation](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) given window.

An activation triggering input event is any event whose [`isTrusted`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute is true and whose [`type`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) is one of:
- "[`keydown`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-keydown)", provided the key is neither the Esc key nor a shortcut key reserved by the user agent;
- "[`mousedown`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#mousedown)";
- "[`pointerdown`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#the-pointerdown-event)", provided the event's [`pointerType`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#dom-pointerevent-pointertype) is "`mouse`";
- "[`pointerup`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#the-pointerup-event)", provided the event's [`pointerType`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#dom-pointerevent-pointertype) is not "`mouse`"; or
- "[`touchend`](https://w3c.github.io/touch-events/#event-touchend)".

[Activation consuming APIs](#643-apis-gated-by-user-activation) defined in this and other specifications can consume user activation by performing the following steps, given a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) W:
1. If W's [navigable](#722-the-window-object) is null, then return.
2. Let top be W's [navigable](#722-the-window-object)'s [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables).
3. Let navigables be the [inclusive descendant navigables](#7315-related-navigable-collections) of top's [active document](#731-navigables).
4. Let windows be the list of [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) objects constructed by taking the [active window](#731-navigables) of each item in navigables.
5. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) window in windows, if window's [last activation timestamp](#641-data-model) is not positive infinity, then set window's [last activation timestamp](#641-data-model) to negative infinity.

[History-action activation-consuming APIs](#643-apis-gated-by-user-activation) can consume history-action user activation by performing the following steps, given a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) W:
1. If W's [navigable](#722-the-window-object) is null, then return.
2. Let top be W's [navigable](#722-the-window-object)'s [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables).
3. Let navigables be the [inclusive descendant navigables](#7315-related-navigable-collections) of top's [active document](#731-navigables).
4. Let windows be the list of [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) objects constructed by taking the [active window](#731-navigables) of each item in navigables.
5. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) window in windows, set window's [last history-action activation timestamp](#641-data-model) to window's [last activation timestamp](#641-data-model).

> [!note]
> Note the asymmetry in the sets of [browsing contexts](#732-browsing-contexts) in the page that are affected by an [activation notification](#642-processing-model) vs an [activation consumption](#642-processing-model): an activation consumption changes (to false) the [transient activation](#641-data-model) states for all browsing contexts in the page, but an activation notification changes (to true) the states for a subset of those browsing contexts. The exhaustive nature of consumption here is deliberate: it prevents malicious sites from making multiple calls to an [activation consuming API](#643-apis-gated-by-user-activation) from a single user activation (possibly by exploiting a deep hierarchy of [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element)s).

#### 6.4.3 APIs gated by user activation

APIs that are dependent on user activation are classified into different levels:

Sticky activation-gated APIs

These APIs require the [sticky activation](#641-data-model) state to be true, so they are blocked until the very first user activation.

Transient activation-gated APIs

These APIs require the [transient activation](#641-data-model) state to be true, but they don't [consume](#642-processing-model) it, so multiple calls are allowed per user activation until the transient state [expires](#641-data-model).

Transient activation-consuming APIs

These APIs require the [transient activation](#641-data-model) state to be true, and they [consume user activation](#642-processing-model) in each call to prevent multiple calls per user activation.

History-action activation-consuming APIs

These APIs require the [history-action activation](#641-data-model) state to be true, and they [consume history-action user activation](#642-processing-model) in each call to prevent multiple calls per user activation.

#### 6.4.4 The [`UserActivation`](#644-the-useractivation-interface) interface

Each [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) has an associated `UserActivation`, which is a [`UserActivation`](#644-the-useractivation-interface) object. Upon creation of the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object, its [associated `UserActivation`](#644-the-useractivation-interface) must be set to a [new](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#new) [`UserActivation`](#644-the-useractivation-interface) object created in the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object's [relevant realm](#81334-relevant).

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface UserActivation {
  readonly attribute boolean hasBeenActive;
  readonly attribute boolean isActive;
};

partial interface Navigator {
  [SameObject] readonly attribute UserActivation userActivation;
};
```

`navigator.userActivation.hasBeenActive`

Returns whether the window has [sticky activation](#641-data-model).

`navigator.userActivation.isActive`

Returns whether the window has [transient activation](#641-data-model).

The `userActivation` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant)'s [associated `UserActivation`](#644-the-useractivation-interface).

The `hasBeenActive` getter steps are to return true if [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) has [sticky activation](#641-data-model), and false otherwise.

The `isActive` getter steps are to return true if [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) has [transient activation](#641-data-model), and false otherwise.

#### 6.4.5 User agent automation

For the purposes of user-agent automation and application testing, this specification defines the following [extension command](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#dfn-extension-commands) for the Web Driver specification. It is optional for a user agent to support the following [extension command](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#dfn-extension-commands). [\[WEBDRIVER\]](#references)

| HTTP Method | URI Template |
| --- | --- |
| \``POST`\` | `/session/{session id}/window/consume-user-activation` |

The [remote end steps](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#dfn-remote-end-steps) are:
1. Let window be the [current browsing context](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#dfn-current-browsing-context)'s [active window](#732-browsing-contexts).
2. Let consume be true if window has [transient activation](#641-data-model); otherwise false.
3. If consume is true, then [consume user activation](#642-processing-model) of window.
4. Return [success](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver/#dfn-success) with data consume.

### 6.5 Activation behavior of elements

Certain elements in HTML have an [activation behavior](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget), which means that the user can activate them. This is always caused by a [`click`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click) event.

The user agent should allow the user to manually trigger elements that have an [activation behavior](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget), for instance using keyboard or voice input, or through mouse clicks. When the user triggers an element with a defined [activation behavior](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) in a manner other than clicking it, the default action of the interaction event must be to [fire a `click` event](#8183-event-firing) at the element.

`element.click()`

Acts as if the element was clicked.

Each element has an associated click in progress flag, which is initially unset.

The `click()` method must run the following steps:
1. If this element is a form control that is [disabled](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute), then return.
2. If this element's [click in progress flag](#65-activation-behavior-of-elements) is set, then return.
3. Set this element's [click in progress flag](#65-activation-behavior-of-elements).
4. [Fire a synthetic pointer event](#8183-event-firing) named [`click`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click) at this element, with the *not trusted flag* set.
5. Unset this element's [click in progress flag](#65-activation-behavior-of-elements).

#### 6.5.1 The [`ToggleEvent`](#651-the-toggleevent-interface) interface

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface ToggleEvent : Event {
  constructor(DOMString type, optional ToggleEventInit eventInitDict = {});
  readonly attribute DOMString oldState;
  readonly attribute DOMString newState;
  readonly attribute Element? source;
};

dictionary ToggleEventInit : EventInit {
  DOMString oldState = "";
  DOMString newState = "";
  Element? source = null;
};
```

`event.oldState`

Set to "`closed`" when transitioning from closed to open, or set to "`open`" when transitioning from open to closed.

`event.newState`

Set to "`open`" when transitioning from closed to open, or set to "`closed`" when transitioning from open to closed.

`event.source`

Set to the element which initiated the toggle, which can be set up with the [`popovertarget`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes) and [`commandfor`](#4106-the-button-element) attributes. If there is no source element, then it is set to null.

The `oldState` and `newState` attributes must return the values they are initialized to.

The `source` getter steps are to return the result of [retargeting](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) [`source`](#651-the-toggleevent-interface) against [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`currentTarget`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event).

> [!warning]
> [DOM standard issue #1328](https://github.com/whatwg/dom/issues/1328) tracks how to better standardize associated event data in a way which makes sense on Events. Currently an event attribute initialized to a value cannot also have a getter, and so an internal slot (or map of additional fields) is required to properly specify this.

A toggle task tracker is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) which has:

task

A [task](#8171-definitions) which fires a [`ToggleEvent`](#651-the-toggleevent-interface).

old state

A string which represents the [task](#651-the-toggleevent-interface)'s event's value for the [`oldState`](#651-the-toggleevent-interface) attribute.

#### 6.5.2 The [`CommandEvent`](#652-the-commandevent-interface) interface

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface CommandEvent : Event {
  constructor(DOMString type, optional CommandEventInit eventInitDict = {});
  readonly attribute Element? source;
  readonly attribute DOMString command;
};

dictionary CommandEventInit : EventInit {
  Element? source = null;
  DOMString command = "";
};
```

`event.command`

Returns what action the element can take.

`event.source`

Returns the [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) that was interacted with in order to cause this event.

The `command` attribute must return the value it was initialized to.

The `source` getter steps are to return the result of [retargeting](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) [`source`](#652-the-commandevent-interface) against [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`currentTarget`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event).

> [!warning]
> [DOM standard issue #1328](https://github.com/whatwg/dom/issues/1328) tracks how to better standardize associated event data in a way which makes sense on Events. Currently an event attribute initialized to a value cannot also have a getter, and so an internal slot (or map of additional fields) is required to properly specify this.

### 6.6 Focus

#### 6.6.1 Introduction

*This section is non-normative.*

An HTML user interface typically consists of multiple interactive widgets, such as form controls, scrollable regions, links, dialog boxes, browser tabs, and so forth. These widgets form a hierarchy, with some (e.g. browser tabs, dialog boxes) containing others (e.g. links, form controls).

When interacting with an interface using a keyboard, key input is channeled from the system, through the hierarchy of interactive widgets, to an active widget, which is said to be [focused](#662-data-model).

> [!example]
> Consider an HTML application running in a browser tab running in a graphical environment. Suppose this application had a page with some text controls and links, and was currently showing a modal dialog, which itself had a text control and a button.
> 
> The hierarchy of focusable widgets, in this scenario, would include the browser window, which would have, amongst its children, the browser tab containing the HTML application. The tab itself would have as its children the various links and text controls, as well as the dialog. The dialog itself would have as its children the text control and the button.
> 
> ![](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/focus-tree.png)
> 
> If the widget with [focus](#662-data-model) in this example was the text control in the dialog box, then key input would be channeled from the graphical system to ① the web browser, then to ② the tab, then to ③ the dialog, and finally to ④ the text control.

Keyboard *events* are always targeted at this [focused](#662-data-model) element.

#### 6.6.2 Data model

A [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables) has system focus when it can receive keyboard input channeled from the operating system, possibly targeted at one of its [active document](#731-navigables)'s [descendant navigables](#7315-related-navigable-collections).

A [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables) has user attention when its [system visibility state](#7311-traversable-navigables) is "`visible`", and it either has [system focus](#662-data-model) or user agent widgets directly related to it can receive keyboard input channeled from the operating system.

> [!note]
> User attention is lost when a browser window loses focus, whereas system focus might also be lost to other system widgets in the browser window such as a location bar.

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) d is a fully active descendant of a top-level traversable with user attention when d is [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents) and d's [node navigable](#731-navigables)'s [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables) has [user attention](#662-data-model).

The term focusable area is used to refer to regions of the interface that can further become the target of such keyboard input. Focusable areas can be elements, parts of elements, or other regions managed by the user agent.

Each [focusable area](#662-data-model) has a DOM anchor, which is a [`Node`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) object that represents the position of the [focusable area](#662-data-model) in the DOM. (When the [focusable area](#662-data-model) is itself a [`Node`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), it is its own [DOM anchor](#662-data-model).) The [DOM anchor](#662-data-model) is used in some APIs as a substitute for the [focusable area](#662-data-model) when there is no other DOM object to represent the [focusable area](#662-data-model).

The following table describes what objects can be [focusable areas](#662-data-model). The cells in the left column describe objects that can be [focusable areas](#662-data-model); the cells in the right column describe the [DOM anchors](#662-data-model) for those elements. (The cells that span both columns are non-normative examples.)

[`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element), [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element), [`<input type=text>`](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch), sometimes [`<a
     href="">`](#451-the-a-element) (depending on platform conventions).

In the following example, the [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element creates two shapes, one on each image. The [DOM anchor](#662-data-model) of the first shape is the first [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element, and the [DOM anchor](#662-data-model) of the second shape is the second [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element.

```html
<map id=wallmap><area alt="Enter Door" coords="10,10,100,200" href="door.html"></map>
...
<img src="images/innerwall.jpeg" alt="There is a white wall here, with a door." usemap="#wallmap">
...
<img src="images/outerwall.jpeg" alt="There is a red wall here, with a door." usemap="#wallmap">
```

The [controls in the user interface](#481113-user-interface) for a [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element, the up and down buttons in a spin-control version of [`<input type=number>`](#4105112-number-state-typenumber), the part of a [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element's rendering that enables the element to be opened or closed using keyboard input.

The CSS ['overflow'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-overflow/#propdef-overflow) property's 'scroll' value typically creates a scrollable region.

The contents of an [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element).

A user agent could make all list item bullets [sequentially focusable](#662-data-model), so that a user can more easily navigate lists.

Similarly, a user agent could make all elements with [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attributes [sequentially focusable](#662-data-model), so that their advisory information can be accessed.

| [Focusable area](#662-data-model) | [DOM anchor](#662-data-model) |
| --- | --- |
| Examples |
| Elements that meet all the following criteria:  • the element's [tabindex value](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) is non-null, or the element is determined by the user agent to be focusable; • the element is either not a [shadow host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), or has a [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) whose [delegates focus](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) is false; • the element is not [actually disabled](#415-disabled-elements); • the element is not [inert](#63-inert-subtrees); • the element is either [being rendered](#151-introduction), [delegating its rendering to its children](#151-introduction), or [being used as relevant canvas fallback content](#4125-the-canvas-element). | The element itself. |
|  |
| The shapes of [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements in an [image map](#48141-authoring) associated with an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element that is [being rendered](#151-introduction) and is not [inert](#63-inert-subtrees). | The [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element. |
|  |
| The user-agent provided subwidgets of elements that are [being rendered](#151-introduction) and are not [actually disabled](#415-disabled-elements) or [inert](#63-inert-subtrees). | The element for which the [focusable area](#662-data-model) is a subwidget. |
|  |
| The scrollable regions of elements that are [being rendered](#151-introduction) and are not [inert](#63-inert-subtrees). | The element for which the box that the scrollable region scrolls was created. |
|  |
| The [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) of a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) that has a non-null [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) and is not [inert](#63-inert-subtrees). | The [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) for which the [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) was created. |
|  |
| Any other element or part of an element determined by the user agent to be a focusable area, especially to aid with accessibility or to better match platform conventions. | The element. |
|  |

> [!note]
> A [navigable container](#7313-child-navigables) (e.g. an [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element)) is a [focusable area](#662-data-model), but key events routed to a [navigable container](#7313-child-navigables) get immediately routed to its [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables)'s [active document](#731-navigables). Similarly, in sequential focus navigation a [navigable container](#7313-child-navigables) essentially acts merely as a placeholder for its [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables)'s [active document](#731-navigables).

---

One [focusable area](#662-data-model) in each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is designated the focused area of the document. Which control is so designated changes over time, based on algorithms in this specification.

> [!note]
> Even if a document is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents) and not shown to the user, it can still have a [focused area of the document](#662-data-model). If a document's [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents) state changes, its [focused area of the document](#662-data-model) will stay the same.

The currently focused area of a top-level traversable traversable is the [focusable area](#662-data-model)-or-null returned by this algorithm:
1. If traversable does not have [system focus](#662-data-model), then return null.
2. Let candidate be traversable's [active document](#731-navigables).
3. While candidate's [focused area](#662-data-model) is a [navigable container](#7313-child-navigables) with a non-null [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables): set candidate to the [active document](#731-navigables) of that [navigable container](#7313-child-navigables)'s [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables).
4. If candidate's [focused area](#662-data-model) is non-null, set candidate to candidate's [focused area](#662-data-model).
5. Return candidate.

The current focus chain of a top-level traversable traversable is the [focus chain](#662-data-model) of the [currently focused area](#662-data-model) of traversable, if traversable is non-null, or an empty list otherwise.

An element that is the [DOM anchor](#662-data-model) of a [focusable area](#662-data-model) is said to gain focus when that [focusable area](#662-data-model) becomes the [currently focused area of a top-level traversable](#662-data-model). When an element is the [DOM anchor](#662-data-model) of a [focusable area](#662-data-model) of the [currently focused area of a top-level traversable](#662-data-model), it is focused.

The focus chain of a [focusable area](#662-data-model) subject is the ordered list constructed as follows:
1. Let output be an empty [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).
2. Let currentObject be subject.
3. While true:
   1. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) currentObject to output.
   2. If currentObject is an [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element's shape, then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) that [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element to output.

      Otherwise, if currentObject's [DOM anchor](#662-data-model) is an element that is not currentObject itself, then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) currentObject's [DOM anchor](#662-data-model) to output.

   3. If currentObject is a [focusable area](#662-data-model), then set currentObject to currentObject's [DOM anchor](#662-data-model)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).

      Otherwise, if currentObject is a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) whose [node navigable](#731-navigables)'s [parent](#731-navigables) is non-null, then set currentObject to currentObject's [node navigable](#731-navigables)'s [parent](#731-navigables).

      Otherwise, [break](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).

4. Return output.

   > [!note]
   > The chain starts with subject and (if subject is or can be the [currently focused area of a top-level traversable](#662-data-model)) continues up the focus hierarchy up to the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) of the [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables).

All elements that are [focusable areas](#662-data-model) are said to be focusable.

There are two special types of focusability for [focusable areas](#662-data-model):
- A [focusable area](#662-data-model) is said to be sequentially focusable if it is included in its [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [sequential focus navigation order](#665-sequential-focus-navigation) and the user agent determines that it is sequentially focusable.
- A [focusable area](#662-data-model) is said to be click focusable if the user agent determines that it is click focusable. User agents should consider focusable areas with non-null [tabindex values](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) to be click focusable.

> [!note]
> Elements which are not [focusable](#662-data-model) are not [focusable areas](#662-data-model), and thus not [sequentially focusable](#662-data-model) and not [click focusable](#662-data-model).

> [!note]
> Being [focusable](#662-data-model) is a statement about whether an element can be focused programmatically, e.g. via the [`focus()`](#666-focus-management-apis) method or [`autofocus`](#667-the-autofocus-attribute) attribute. In contrast, [sequentially focusable](#662-data-model) and [click focusable](#662-data-model) govern how the user agent responds to user interaction: respectively, to [sequential focus navigation](#665-sequential-focus-navigation) and as [activation behavior](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget).
> 
> The user agent might determine that an element is not [sequentially focusable](#662-data-model) even if it is [focusable](#662-data-model) and is included in its [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [sequential focus navigation order](#665-sequential-focus-navigation), according to user preferences. For example, macOS users can set the user agent to skip non-form control elements, or can skip links when doing [sequential focus navigation](#665-sequential-focus-navigation) with just the Tab key (as opposed to using both the Option and Tab keys).
> 
> Similarly, the user agent might determine that an element is not [click focusable](#662-data-model) even if it is [focusable](#662-data-model). For example, in some user agents, clicking on a non-editable form control does not focus it, i.e. the user agent has determined that such controls are not click focusable.
> 
> Thus, an element can be [focusable](#662-data-model), but neither [sequentially focusable](#662-data-model) nor [click focusable](#662-data-model). For example, in some user agents, a non-editable form-control with a negative-integer [tabindex value](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) would not be focusable via user interaction, only via programmatic APIs.

When a user [activates](#65-activation-behavior-of-elements) a [click focusable](#662-data-model) [focusable area](#662-data-model), the user agent must run the [focusing steps](#664-processing-model) on the [focusable area](#662-data-model) with *focus trigger* set to "`click`".

> [!note]
> Note that focusing is not an [activation behavior](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget), i.e. calling the [`click()`](#65-activation-behavior-of-elements) method on an element or dispatching a synthetic [`click`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click) event on it won't cause the element to get focused.

---

A node is a focus navigation scope owner if it is a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), a [shadow host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), a [slot](#4124-the-slot-element), or an element which is the [popover trigger](#612-the-popover-attribute) of an element in the [popover showing state](#612-the-popover-attribute).

Each [focus navigation scope owner](#662-data-model) has a focus navigation scope, which is a list of elements. Its contents are determined as follows:

Every element element has an associated focus navigation owner, which is either null or a [focus navigation scope owner](#662-data-model). It is determined by the following algorithm:
1. If element's parent is null, then return null.
2. If element's parent is a [shadow host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), then return element's [assigned slot](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#4222-slottables).
3. If element's parent is a [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot), then return the parent's [host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment).
4. If element's parent is the [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree), then return the parent's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
5. If element is in the [popover showing state](#612-the-popover-attribute) and has a [popover trigger](#612-the-popover-attribute) set, then return element's [popover trigger](#612-the-popover-attribute).
6. Return element's parent's [associated focus navigation owner](#662-data-model).

Then, the contents of a given [focus navigation scope owner](#662-data-model) owner's [focus navigation scope](#662-data-model) are all elements whose [associated focus navigation owner](#662-data-model) is owner.

> [!note]
> The order of elements within a [focus navigation scope](#662-data-model) does not impact any of the algorithms in this specification. Ordering only becomes important for the [tabindex-ordered focus navigation scope](#662-data-model) and [flattened tabindex-ordered focus navigation scope](#662-data-model) concepts defined below.

A tabindex-ordered focus navigation scope is a list of [focusable areas](#662-data-model) and [focus navigation scope owners](#662-data-model). Every [focus navigation scope owner](#662-data-model) owner has [tabindex-ordered focus navigation scope](#662-data-model), whose contents are determined as follows:
- It contains all elements in owner's [focus navigation scope](#662-data-model) that are themselves [focus navigation scope owners](#662-data-model), except the elements whose [tabindex value](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) is a negative integer.
- It contains all of the [focusable areas](#662-data-model) whose [DOM anchor](#662-data-model) is an element in owner's [focus navigation scope](#662-data-model), except the [focusable areas](#662-data-model) whose [tabindex value](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) is a negative integer.

The order within a [tabindex-ordered focus navigation scope](#662-data-model) is determined by each element's [tabindex value](#663-the-tabindex-attribute), as described in the section below.

> [!note]
> The rules there do not give a precise ordering, as they are composed mostly of "should" statements and relative orderings.

A flattened tabindex-ordered focus navigation scope is a list of [focusable areas](#662-data-model). Every [focus navigation scope owner](#662-data-model) owner owns a distinct [flattened tabindex-ordered focus navigation scope](#662-data-model), whose contents are determined by the following algorithm:
1. Let result be a [clone](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of owner's [tabindex-ordered focus navigation scope](#662-data-model).
2. For each item of result:
   1. If item is not a [focus navigation scope owner](#662-data-model), then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   2. If item is not a [focusable area](#662-data-model), then replace item with all of the items in item's [flattened tabindex-ordered focus navigation scope](#662-data-model).
   3. Otherwise, insert the contents of item's [flattened tabindex-ordered focus navigation scope](#662-data-model) after item.

#### 6.6.3 The [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attribute

The `tabindex` content attribute allows authors to make an element and regions that have the element as its [DOM anchor](#662-data-model) be [focusable areas](#662-data-model), allow or prevent them from being [sequentially focusable](#662-data-model), and determine their relative ordering for [sequential focus navigation](#665-sequential-focus-navigation).

The name "tab index" comes from the common use of the Tab key to navigate through the focusable elements. The term "tabbing" refers to moving forward through [sequentially focusable](#662-data-model) [focusable areas](#662-data-model).

The [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attribute, if specified, must have a value that is a [valid integer](#2341-signed-integers). Positive numbers specify the relative position of the element's [focusable areas](#662-data-model) in the [sequential focus navigation order](#665-sequential-focus-navigation), and negative numbers indicate that the control is not [sequentially focusable](#662-data-model).

Developers should use caution when using values other than 0 or −1 for their [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attributes as this is complicated to do correctly.

> [!note]
> The following provides a non-normative summary of the behaviors of the possible [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attribute values. The below processing model gives the more precise rules.
> 
> omitted (or non-integer values)
> 
> The user agent will decide whether the element is [focusable](#662-data-model), and if it is, whether it is [sequentially focusable](#662-data-model) or [click focusable](#662-data-model) (or both).
> 
> −1 (or other negative integer values)
> 
> Causes the element to be [focusable](#662-data-model), and indicates that the author would prefer the element to be [click focusable](#662-data-model) but not [sequentially focusable](#662-data-model). The user agent might ignore this preference for click and sequential focusability, e.g., for specific element types according to platform conventions, or for keyboard-only users.
> 
> 0
> 
> Causes the element to be [focusable](#662-data-model), and indicates that the author would prefer the element to be both [click focusable](#662-data-model) and [sequentially focusable](#662-data-model). The user agent might ignore this preference for click and sequential focusability.
> 
> positive integer values
> 
> Behaves the same as 0, but in addition creates a relative ordering within a [tabindex-ordered focus navigation scope](#662-data-model), so that elements with higher [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attribute value come later.
> 
> Note that the [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attribute cannot be used to make an element non-focusable. The only way a page author can do that is by [disabling](#415-disabled-elements) the element, or making it [inert](#63-inert-subtrees).

---

The tabindex value of an element is the value of its [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attribute, parsed using the [rules for parsing integers](#2341-signed-integers). If parsing fails or the attribute is not specified, then the [tabindex value](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) is null.

The [tabindex value](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) of a [focusable area](#662-data-model) is the [tabindex value](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) of its [DOM anchor](#662-data-model).

The [tabindex value](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) of an element must be interpreted as follows:

If the value is null

The user agent should follow platform conventions to determine if the element should be considered as a [focusable area](#662-data-model) and if so, whether the element and any [focusable areas](#662-data-model) that have the element as their [DOM anchor](#662-data-model) are [sequentially focusable](#662-data-model), and if so, what their relative position in their [tabindex-ordered focus navigation scope](#662-data-model) is to be. If the element is a [focus navigation scope owner](#662-data-model), it must be included in its [tabindex-ordered focus navigation scope](#662-data-model) even if it is not a [focusable area](#662-data-model).

The relative ordering within a [tabindex-ordered focus navigation scope](#662-data-model) for elements and [focusable areas](#662-data-model) that belong to the same [focus navigation scope](#662-data-model) and whose [tabindex value](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) is null should be in [shadow-including tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot).

Modulo platform conventions, it is suggested that the following elements should be considered as [focusable areas](#662-data-model) and be [sequentially focusable](#662-data-model):
- [`a`](#451-the-a-element) elements that have an [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute
- [`button`](#4106-the-button-element) elements
- [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute are not in the [Hidden](#410511-hidden-state-typehidden) state
- [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) elements
- [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements
- [`summary`](#4112-the-summary-element) elements that are the first [`summary`](#4112-the-summary-element) element child of a [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element
- Elements with a [`draggable`](#6117-the-draggable-attribute) attribute set, if that would enable the user agent to allow the user to begin drag operations for those elements without the use of a pointing device
- [Editing hosts](#684-editing-apis)
- [Navigable containers](#7313-child-navigables)

If the value is a negative integer

The user agent must consider the element as a [focusable area](#662-data-model), but should omit the element from any [tabindex-ordered focus navigation scope](#662-data-model).

> [!note]
> One valid reason to ignore the requirement that sequential focus navigation not allow the author to lead to the element would be if the user's only mechanism for moving the focus is sequential focus navigation. For instance, a keyboard-only user would be unable to click on a text control with a negative [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute), so that user's user agent would be well justified in allowing the user to tab to the control regardless.

If the value is a zero

The user agent must allow the element to be considered as a [focusable area](#662-data-model) and should allow the element and any [focusable areas](#662-data-model) that have the element as their [DOM anchor](#662-data-model) to be [sequentially focusable](#662-data-model).

The relative ordering within a [tabindex-ordered focus navigation scope](#662-data-model) for elements and [focusable areas](#662-data-model) that belong to the same [focus navigation scope](#662-data-model) and whose [tabindex value](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) is zero should be in [shadow-including tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot).

If the value is greater than zero

The user agent must allow the element to be considered as a [focusable area](#662-data-model) and should allow the element and any [focusable areas](#662-data-model) that have the element as their [DOM anchor](#662-data-model) to be [sequentially focusable](#662-data-model), and should place the element — referenced as candidate below — and the aforementioned [focusable areas](#662-data-model) in the [tabindex-ordered focus navigation scope](#662-data-model) where the element is a part of so that, relative to other elements and [focusable areas](#662-data-model) that belong to the same [focus navigation scope](#662-data-model), they are:
- before any [focusable area](#662-data-model) whose [DOM anchor](#662-data-model) is an element whose [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attribute has been omitted or whose value, when parsed, returns an error,
- before any [focusable area](#662-data-model) whose [DOM anchor](#662-data-model) is an element whose [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attribute has a value less than or equal to zero,
- after any [focusable area](#662-data-model) whose [DOM anchor](#662-data-model) is an element whose [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attribute has a value greater than zero but less than the value of the [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attribute on candidate,
- after any [focusable area](#662-data-model) whose [DOM anchor](#662-data-model) is an element whose [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attribute has a value equal to the value of the [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attribute on candidate but that is located earlier than candidate in [shadow-including tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot),
- before any [focusable area](#662-data-model) whose [DOM anchor](#662-data-model) is an element whose [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attribute has a value equal to the value of the [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attribute on candidate but that is located later than candidate in [shadow-including tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot), and
- before any [focusable area](#662-data-model) whose [DOM anchor](#662-data-model) is an element whose [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attribute has a value greater than the value of the [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attribute on candidate.

The `tabIndex` getter steps are:
1. Let attribute be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`tabindex`](#663-the-tabindex-attribute) attribute.
2. If attribute is not null:
   1. Let parsedValue be the result of [integer parsing](#2341-signed-integers) attribute's [value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#492-interface-attr).
   2. If parsedValue is not an error and is within the [`long`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-long) range, then return parsedValue.
3. Return 0 if [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) is an [`a`](#451-the-a-element), [`area`](#4813-the-area-element), [`button`](#4106-the-button-element), [`frame`](#1632-frames), [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element), [`input`](#4105-the-input-element), [`object`](#487-the-object-element), [`select`](#4107-the-select-element), [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element), or [SVG `a`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/linking.html#elementdef-a) element, or [MathML `a`](https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#dfn-a) element, or is a [`summary`](#4112-the-summary-element) element that is a [summary for its parent details](#4112-the-summary-element); otherwise −1.

> [!note]
> The varying default value based on element type is a historical artifact.

#### 6.6.4 Processing model

To get the focusable area for a focus target that is either an element that is not a [focusable area](#662-data-model), or is a [navigable](#731-navigables), given an optional string focus trigger (default "`other`"), run the first matching set of steps from the following list:

If focus target is an [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element with one or more shapes that are [focusable areas](#662-data-model)

Return the shape corresponding to the first [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) that uses the image map to which the [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element belongs.

If focus target is an element with one or more scrollable regions that are [focusable areas](#662-data-model)

Return the element's first scrollable region, according to a pre-order, depth-first traversal of the [flat tree](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scoping/#flat-tree). [\[CSSSCOPING\]](#references)

If focus target is the [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) of its [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)

Return the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport).

If focus target is a [navigable](#731-navigables)

Return the [navigable](#731-navigables)'s [active document](#731-navigables).

If focus target is a [navigable container](#7313-child-navigables) with a non-null [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables)

Return the [navigable container](#7313-child-navigables)'s [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables)'s [active document](#731-navigables).

If focus target is a [shadow host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) whose [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element)'s [delegates focus](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) is true
1. Let focusedElement be the [currently focused area of a top-level traversable](#662-data-model)'s [DOM anchor](#662-data-model).
2. If focus target is a [shadow-including inclusive ancestor](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) of focusedElement, then return focusedElement.
3. Return the [focus delegate](#664-processing-model) for focus target given focus trigger.

> [!note]
> For [sequential focusability](#662-data-model), the handling of [shadow hosts](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) and [delegates focus](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) is done when constructing the [sequential focus navigation order](#665-sequential-focus-navigation). That is, the [focusing steps](#664-processing-model) will never be called on such [shadow hosts](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) as part of sequential focus navigation.

Otherwise

Return null.

The focus delegate for a focusTarget, given an optional string focusTrigger (default "`other`"), is given by the following steps:
1. If focusTarget is a [shadow host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) and its [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element)'s [delegates focus](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) is false, then return null.
2. Let whereToLook be focusTarget.
3. If whereToLook is a [shadow host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), then set whereToLook to whereToLook's [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element).
4. Let autofocusDelegate be the [autofocus delegate](#664-processing-model) for whereToLook given focusTrigger.
5. If autofocusDelegate is not null, then return autofocusDelegate.
6. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) descendant of whereToLook's [descendants](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees):
   1. Let focusableArea be null.
   2. If focusTarget is a [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) element and descendant is [sequentially focusable](#662-data-model), then set focusableArea to descendant.
   3. Otherwise, if focusTarget is not a [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) and descendant is a [focusable area](#662-data-model), set focusableArea to descendant.
   4. Otherwise, set focusableArea to the result of [getting the focusable area](#664-processing-model) for descendant given focusTrigger.

      > [!note]
      > This step can end up recursing, i.e., the [get the focusable area](#664-processing-model) steps might return the [focus delegate](#664-processing-model) of descendant.

   5. If focusableArea is not null, then return focusableArea.

   > [!note]
   > It's important that we are *not* looking at the [shadow-including descendants](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) here, but instead only at the [descendants](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees). [Shadow hosts](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) are instead handled by the recursive case mentioned above.

7. Return null.

> [!note]
> The above algorithm essentially returns the first suitable [focusable area](#662-data-model) where the path between its [DOM anchor](#662-data-model) and focusTarget delegates focus at any shadow tree boundaries.

The autofocus delegate for a focus target given a focus trigger is given by the following steps:
1. For each [descendant](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) descendant of focus target, in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees):
