   1. If descendant does not have an [`autofocus`](#667-the-autofocus-attribute) content attribute, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   2. Let focusable area be descendant, if descendant is a [focusable area](#662-data-model); otherwise let focusable area be the result of [getting the focusable area](#664-processing-model) for descendant given focus trigger.
   3. If focusable area is null, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   4. If focusable area is not [click focusable](#662-data-model) and focus trigger is "`click`", then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   5. Return focusable area.
2. Return null.

The focusing steps for an object new focus target that is either a [focusable area](#662-data-model), or an element that is not a [focusable area](#662-data-model), or a [navigable](#731-navigables), are as follows. They can optionally be run with a fallback target and a string focus trigger.
1. If new focus target is not a [focusable area](#662-data-model), then set new focus target to the result of [getting the focusable area](#664-processing-model) for new focus target, given focus trigger if it was passed.
2. If new focus target is null:
   1. If no fallback target was specified, then return.
   2. Otherwise, set new focus target to the fallback target.
3. If new focus target is a [navigable container](#7313-child-navigables) with non-null [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables), then set new focus target to the [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables)'s [active document](#731-navigables).
4. If new focus target is a [focusable area](#662-data-model) and its [DOM anchor](#662-data-model) is [inert](#63-inert-subtrees), then return.
5. If new focus target is the [currently focused area of a top-level traversable](#662-data-model), then return.
6. Let old chain be the [current focus chain of the top-level traversable](#662-data-model) in which new focus target finds itself.
7. Let new chain be the [focus chain](#662-data-model) of new focus target.
8. Run the [focus update steps](#664-processing-model) with old chain, new chain, and new focus target respectively.

User agents must [immediately](#211-parallelism) run the [focusing steps](#664-processing-model) for a [focusable area](#662-data-model) or [navigable](#731-navigables) candidate whenever the user attempts to move the focus to candidate.

The unfocusing steps for an object old focus target that is either a [focusable area](#662-data-model) or an element that is not a [focusable area](#662-data-model) are as follows:
1. If old focus target is a [shadow host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) whose [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element)'s [delegates focus](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) is true, and old focus target's [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) is a [shadow-including inclusive ancestor](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) of the [currently focused area of a top-level traversable](#662-data-model)'s [DOM anchor](#662-data-model), then set old focus target to that [currently focused area of a top-level traversable](#662-data-model).
2. If old focus target is [inert](#63-inert-subtrees), then return.
3. If old focus target is an [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element and one of its shapes is the [currently focused area of a top-level traversable](#662-data-model), or, if old focus target is an element with one or more scrollable regions, and one of them is the [currently focused area of a top-level traversable](#662-data-model), then let old focus target be that [currently focused area of a top-level traversable](#662-data-model).
4. Let old chain be the [current focus chain of the top-level traversable](#662-data-model) in which old focus target finds itself.
5. If old focus target is not one of the entries in old chain, then return.
6. If old focus target is not a [focusable area](#662-data-model), then return.
7. Let topDocument be old chain's last entry.
8. If topDocument's [node navigable](#731-navigables) has [system focus](#662-data-model), then run the [focusing steps](#664-processing-model) for topDocument's [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport).

   Otherwise, apply any relevant platform-specific conventions for removing [system focus](#662-data-model) from topDocument's [node navigable](#731-navigables), and run the [focus update steps](#664-processing-model) given old chain, an empty list, and null.

> [!note]
> The [unfocusing steps](#664-processing-model) do not always result in the focus changing, even when applied to the [currently focused area of a top-level traversable](#662-data-model). For example, if the [currently focused area of a top-level traversable](#662-data-model) is a [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport), then it will usually keep its focus regardless until another [focusable area](#662-data-model) is explicitly focused with the [focusing steps](#664-processing-model).

---

The focus update steps, given an old chain, a new chain, and a new focus target respectively, are as follows:
1. If the last entry in old chain and the last entry in new chain are the same, pop the last entry from old chain and the last entry from new chain and redo this step.
2. For each entry entry in old chain, in order, run these substeps:
   1. If entry is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element, and the [`change`](#events) event [applies](#4105-the-input-element) to the element, and the element does not have a defined [activation behavior](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget), and the user has changed the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) or its list of [selected files](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) while the control was focused without committing that change (such that it is different to what it was when the control was first focused):
      1. Set entry's [user validity](#410181-a-form-controls-value) to true.
      2. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`change`](#events) at the element, with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true.
   2. If entry is an element, let blur event target be entry.

      If entry is a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object, let blur event target be that [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant).

      Otherwise, let blur event target be null.

   3. If entry is the last entry in old chain, and entry is an [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), and the last entry in new chain is also an [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), then let related blur target be the last entry in new chain. Otherwise, let related blur target be null.
   4. If blur event target is not null, [fire a focus event](#664-processing-model) named [`blur`](#events) at blur event target, with related blur target as the related target.

      > [!note]
      > In some cases, e.g., if entry is an [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element's shape, a scrollable region, or a [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport), no event is fired.

3. Apply any relevant platform-specific conventions for focusing new focus target. (For example, some platforms select the contents of a text control when that control is focused.)
4. For each entry entry in new chain, in reverse order, run these substeps:
   1. If entry is a [focusable area](#662-data-model), and the [focused area of the document](#662-data-model) is not entry:
      1. Set document's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant)'s [navigation API](#7262-the-navigation-interface)'s [focus changed during ongoing navigation](#7268-ongoing-navigation-tracking) to true.
      2. Designate entry as the [focused area of the document](#662-data-model).
   2. If entry is an element, let focus event target be entry.

      If entry is a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object, let focus event target be that [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant).

      Otherwise, let focus event target be null.

   3. If entry is the last entry in new chain, and entry is an [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), and the last entry in old chain is also an [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), then let related focus target be the last entry in old chain. Otherwise, let related focus target be null.
   4. If focus event target is not null, [fire a focus event](#664-processing-model) named [`focus`](#events) at focus event target, with related focus target as the related target.

      > [!note]
      > In some cases, e.g. if entry is an [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element's shape, a scrollable region, or a [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport), no event is fired.

To fire a focus event named e at an element or a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object target given a related target relatedTarget:
1. Let view be target if target is a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object; otherwise target's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant).
2. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named e at target, using [`FocusEvent`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#focusevent), with the [`relatedTarget`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#dom-focusevent-relatedtarget) attribute initialized to relatedTarget, the [`view`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#dom-uievent-view) attribute initialized to view, and the [composed flag](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) set.

---

When a key event is to be routed in a [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables), the user agent must run the following steps:
1. Let target area be the [currently focused area of the top-level traversable](#662-data-model).
2. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): target area is not null, since key events are only routed to [top-level traversables](#7312-top-level-traversables) that have [system focus](#662-data-model). Therefore, target area is a [focusable area](#662-data-model).
3. Let target node be target area's [DOM anchor](#662-data-model).
4. If target node is a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) that has a [body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors), then let target node be [the body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors) of that [`Document`](#311-the-document-object).

   Otherwise, if target node is a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object that has a non-null [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree), then let target node be that [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree).

5. If target node is not [inert](#63-inert-subtrees):
   1. Let canHandle be the result of [dispatching](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#29-dispatching-events) the key event at target node.
   2. If canHandle is true, then let target area handle the key event. This might include [firing a `click` event](#8183-event-firing) at target node.

---

The has focus steps, given a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object target, are as follows:
1. If target's [node navigable](#731-navigables)'s [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables) does not have [system focus](#662-data-model), then return false.
2. Let candidate be target's [node navigable](#731-navigables)'s [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables)'s [active document](#732-browsing-contexts).
3. While true:
   1. If candidate is target, then return true.
   2. If the [focused area](#662-data-model) of candidate is a [navigable container](#7313-child-navigables) with a non-null [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables), then set candidate to the [active document](#731-navigables) of that [navigable container](#7313-child-navigables)'s [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables).
   3. Otherwise, return false.

#### 6.6.5 Sequential focus navigation

Each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a sequential focus navigation order, which orders some or all of the [focusable areas](#662-data-model) in the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) relative to each other. Its contents and ordering are given by the [flattened tabindex-ordered focus navigation scope](#662-data-model) of the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object).

> [!note]
> Per the rules defining the [flattened tabindex-ordered focus navigation scope](#662-data-model), the ordering is not necessarily related to the [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) of the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object).

If a [focusable area](#662-data-model) is omitted from the [sequential focus navigation order](#665-sequential-focus-navigation) of its [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), then it is unreachable via [sequential focus navigation](#665-sequential-focus-navigation).

There can also be a sequential focus navigation starting point. It is initially unset. The user agent may set it when the user indicates that it should be moved.

> [!example]
> For example, the user agent could set it to the position of the user's click if the user clicks on the document contents.

> [!note]
> User agents are required to set the [sequential focus navigation starting point](#665-sequential-focus-navigation) to the [target element](#7464-scrolling-to-a-fragment) when [navigating to a fragment](#74233-fragment-navigations).

A sequential focus direction is one of two possible values: "`forward`", or "`backward`". They are used in the below algorithms to describe the direction in which sequential focus travels at the user's request.

A selection mechanism is one of two possible values: "`DOM`", or "`sequential`". They are used to describe how the [sequential navigation search algorithm](#665-sequential-focus-navigation) finds the [focusable area](#662-data-model) it returns.

When the user requests that focus move from the [currently focused area of a top-level traversable](#662-data-model) to the next or previous [focusable area](#662-data-model) (e.g., as the default action of pressing the tab key), or when the user requests that focus sequentially move to a [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables) in the first place (e.g., from the browser's location bar), the user agent must use the following algorithm:
1. Let starting point be the [currently focused area of a top-level traversable](#662-data-model), if the user requested to move focus sequentially from there, or else the [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables) itself, if the user instead requested to move focus from outside the [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables).
2. If there is a [sequential focus navigation starting point](#665-sequential-focus-navigation) defined and it is inside starting point, then let starting point be the [sequential focus navigation starting point](#665-sequential-focus-navigation) instead.
3. Let direction be "[`forward`](#665-sequential-focus-navigation)" if the user requested the next control, and "[`backward`](#665-sequential-focus-navigation)" if the user requested the previous control.

   > [!note]
   > Typically, pressing tab requests the next control, and pressing shift + tab requests the previous control.

4. *Loop*: Let selection mechanism be "[`sequential`](#665-sequential-focus-navigation)" if starting point is a [navigable](#731-navigables) or if starting point is in its [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [sequential focus navigation order](#665-sequential-focus-navigation).

   Otherwise, starting point is not in its [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [sequential focus navigation order](#665-sequential-focus-navigation); let selection mechanism be "[`DOM`](#665-sequential-focus-navigation)".

5. Let candidate be the result of running the [sequential navigation search algorithm](#665-sequential-focus-navigation) with starting point, direction, and selection mechanism.
6. If candidate is not null, then run the [focusing steps](#664-processing-model) for candidate and return.
7. Otherwise, unset the [sequential focus navigation starting point](#665-sequential-focus-navigation).
8. If starting point is a [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables), or a [focusable area](#662-data-model) in the [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables), the user agent should transfer focus to its own controls appropriately (if any), honouring direction, and then return.

   > [!example]
   > For example, if direction is *backward*, then the last [sequentially focusable](#662-data-model) control before the browser's rendering area would be the control to focus.

   If the user agent has no [sequentially focusable](#662-data-model) controls — a kiosk-mode browser, for instance — then the user agent may instead restart these steps with the starting point being the [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables) itself.

9. Otherwise, starting point is a [focusable area](#662-data-model) in a [child navigable](#7313-child-navigables). Set starting point to that [child navigable](#7313-child-navigables)'s [parent](#731-navigables) and return to the step labeled *loop*.

The sequential navigation search algorithm, given a [focusable area](#662-data-model) starting point, [sequential focus direction](#665-sequential-focus-navigation) direction, and [selection mechanism](#665-sequential-focus-navigation) selection mechanism, consists of the following steps. They return a [focusable area](#662-data-model)-or-null.
1. Pick the appropriate cell from the following table, and follow the instructions in that cell.

   The appropriate cell is the one that is from the column whose header describes direction and from the first row whose header describes starting point and selection mechanism.

   Let candidate be the [suitable sequentially focusable area](#665-sequential-focus-navigation), that appears nearest after starting point in starting point's [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), in [shadow-including tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot), if any; or else null.

   In this case, starting point does not necessarily belong to its [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [sequential focus navigation order](#665-sequential-focus-navigation), so we'll select the [suitable](#665-sequential-focus-navigation) [item](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) from that list that comes *after* starting point in [shadow-including tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot).

   |  | direction is "[`forward`](#665-sequential-focus-navigation)" | direction is "[`backward`](#665-sequential-focus-navigation)" |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | starting point is a [navigable](#731-navigables) | Let candidate be the first [suitable sequentially focusable area](#665-sequential-focus-navigation) in starting point's [active document](#731-navigables), if any; or else null. | Let candidate be the last [suitable sequentially focusable area](#665-sequential-focus-navigation) in starting point's [active document](#731-navigables), if any; or else null. |
   | selection mechanism is "[`DOM`](#665-sequential-focus-navigation)" |  | Let candidate be the [suitable sequentially focusable area](#665-sequential-focus-navigation), that appears nearest before starting point in starting point's [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), in [shadow-including tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot), if any; or else null. |
   | selection mechanism is "[`sequential`](#665-sequential-focus-navigation)" | Let candidate be the first [suitable sequentially focusable area](#665-sequential-focus-navigation) after starting point, in starting point's [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [sequential focus navigation order](#665-sequential-focus-navigation), if any; or else null. | Let candidate be the last [suitable sequentially focusable area](#665-sequential-focus-navigation) before starting point, in starting point's [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [sequential focus navigation order](#665-sequential-focus-navigation), if any; or else null. |

   A suitable sequentially focusable area is a [focusable area](#662-data-model) whose [DOM anchor](#662-data-model) is not [inert](#63-inert-subtrees) and is [sequentially focusable](#662-data-model).

2. If candidate is a [navigable container](#7313-child-navigables) with a non-null [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables):
   1. Let recursive candidate be the result of running the [sequential navigation search algorithm](#665-sequential-focus-navigation) with candidate's [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables), direction, and "[`sequential`](#665-sequential-focus-navigation)".
   2. If recursive candidate is null, then return the result of running the [sequential navigation search algorithm](#665-sequential-focus-navigation) with candidate, direction, and selection mechanism.
   3. Otherwise, set candidate to recursive candidate.
3. Return candidate.

#### 6.6.6 Focus management APIs

```webidl
dictionary FocusOptions {
  boolean preventScroll = false;
  boolean focusVisible;
};
```

`documentOrShadowRoot.activeElement`

Returns the deepest element in documentOrShadowRoot through which or to which key events are being routed. This is, roughly speaking, the focused element in the document.

For the purposes of this API, when a [child navigable](#7313-child-navigables) is focused, its [container](#7313-child-navigables) is [focused](#662-data-model) within its [parent](#731-navigables)'s [active document](#731-navigables). For example, if the user moves the focus to a text control in an [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element), the [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) is the element returned by the [`activeElement`](#666-focus-management-apis) API in the [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).

Similarly, when the focused element is in a different [node tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42-node-tree) than documentOrShadowRoot, the element returned will be the [host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) that's located in the same [node tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42-node-tree) as documentOrShadowRoot if documentOrShadowRoot is a [shadow-including inclusive ancestor](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) of the focused element, and null if not.

`document.hasFocus()`

Returns true if key events are being routed through or to document; otherwise, returns false. Roughly speaking, this corresponds to document, or a document nested inside document, being focused.

`window.focus()`

Moves the focus to window's [navigable](#722-the-window-object), if any.

`element.focus()`

`element.focus({ preventScroll, focusVisible })`

Moves the focus to element.

If element is a [navigable container](#7313-child-navigables), moves the focus to its [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables) instead.

By default, this method also scrolls element into view. Providing the [`preventScroll`](#666-focus-management-apis) option and setting it to true prevents this behavior.

By default, user agents use [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) heuristics to determine whether to [indicate focus](https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#indicate-focus) via a focus ring. Providing the [`focusVisible`](#666-focus-management-apis) option and setting it to true will ensure the focus ring is always visible.

`element.blur()`

Moves the focus to the [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport). Use of this method is discouraged; if you want to focus the [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport), call the [`focus()`](#666-focus-management-apis) method on the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree).

Do not use this method to hide the focus ring if you find the focus ring unsightly. Instead, use the [`:focus-visible`](https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#the-focus-visible-pseudo) pseudo-class to override the ['outline'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#outline) property, and provide a different way to show what element is focused. Be aware that if an alternative focusing style isn't made available, the page will be significantly less usable for people who primarily navigate pages using a keyboard, or those with reduced vision who use focus outlines to help them navigate the page.

> [!example]
> For example, to hide the outline from [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements and instead use a yellow background to indicate focus, you could use:
> 
> ```css
> textarea:focus-visible { outline: none; background: yellow; color: black; }
> ```

The [`DocumentOrShadowRoot`](#312-the-documentorshadowroot-interface) `activeElement` getter steps are:
1. Let candidate be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [focused area](#662-data-model)'s [DOM anchor](#662-data-model).
2. Set candidate to the result of [retargeting](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) candidate against [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
3. If candidate's [root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) is not [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), then return null.
4. If candidate is not a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object, then return candidate.
5. If candidate has a [body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors), then return that [body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors).
6. If candidate's [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) is non-null, then return that [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree).
7. Return null.

The [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) `hasFocus()` method steps are to return the result of running the [has focus steps](#664-processing-model) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).

---

The [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) `focus()` method steps are:
1. Let current be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [navigable](#722-the-window-object).
2. If current is null, then return.
3. If the [allow focus steps](#666-focus-management-apis) given current's [active document](#731-navigables) return false, then return.
4. Run the [focusing steps](#664-processing-model) with current.
5. If current is a [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables), user agents are encouraged to trigger some sort of notification to indicate to the user that the page is attempting to gain focus.

The [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) `blur()` method steps are to do nothing.

> [!note]
> Historically, the [`focus()`](#666-focus-management-apis) and [`blur()`](#666-focus-management-apis) methods actually affected the system-level focus of the system widget (e.g., tab or window) that contained the [navigable](#731-navigables), but hostile sites widely abuse this behavior to the user's detriment.

---

The [`HTMLOrSVGOrMathMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom) `focus(options)` method steps are:
1. If the [allow focus steps](#666-focus-management-apis) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) return false, then return.
2. Run the [focusing steps](#664-processing-model) for [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
3. If options\["`focusVisible`"\] is true, or does not [exist](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) but in an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) way the user agent determines it would be best to do so, then [indicate focus](https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#indicate-focus).
4. If options\["`preventScroll`"\] is false, then [scroll a target into view](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view/#scroll-a-target-into-view) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), "`auto`", "`center`", and "`center`".

The [`HTMLOrSVGOrMathMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom) `blur()` method steps are:
1. The user agent should run the [unfocusing steps](#664-processing-model) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).

   User agents may instead selectively or uniformly do nothing, for usability reasons.

> [!example]
> For example, if the [`blur()`](#666-focus-management-apis) method is unwisely being used to remove the focus ring for aesthetics reasons, the page would become unusable by keyboard users. Ignoring calls to this method would thus allow keyboard users to interact with the page.

---

The allow focus steps, given a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object target, are:
1. If target is [allowed to use](#485-the-iframe-element) the "[`focus-without-user-activation`](#22-policy-controlled-features)" feature, then return true.
2. If target's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) has [transient activation](#641-data-model), then return true.
3. Return false.

#### 6.6.7 The [`autofocus`](#667-the-autofocus-attribute) attribute

The `autofocus` content attribute allows the author to indicate that an element is to be focused as soon as the page is loaded, allowing the user to just start typing without having to manually focus the main element.

When the [`autofocus`](#667-the-autofocus-attribute) attribute is specified on an element inside [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) elements or [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) whose [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute is set, then it will be focused when the dialog or popover becomes shown.

The [`autofocus`](#667-the-autofocus-attribute) attribute is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes).

To find the nearest ancestor autofocus scoping root element given an [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) element:
1. If element is a [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) element, then return element.
2. If element's [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute is not in the [No Popover](#612-the-popover-attribute) state, then return element.
3. Let ancestor be element.
4. While ancestor has a [parent element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element):
   1. Set ancestor to ancestor's [parent element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element).
   2. If ancestor is a [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) element, then return ancestor.
   3. If ancestor's [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute is not in the [No Popover](#612-the-popover-attribute) state, then return ancestor.
5. Return ancestor.

There must not be two elements with the same [nearest ancestor autofocus scoping root element](#667-the-autofocus-attribute) that both have the [`autofocus`](#667-the-autofocus-attribute) attribute specified.

Each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has an autofocus candidates [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists), initially empty.

Each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has an autofocus processed flag boolean, initially false.

When an element with the [`autofocus`](#667-the-autofocus-attribute) attribute specified is [inserted into a document](#214-dom-trees), run the following steps:
1. If the user has indicated (for example, by starting to type in a form control) that they do not wish focus to be changed, then optionally return.
2. Let target be the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
3. If target is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents), then return.
4. If target's [active sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing) has the [sandboxed automatic features browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing), then return.
5. If the [allow focus steps](#666-focus-management-apis) given target return false, then return.
6. Let topDocument be target's [node navigable](#731-navigables)'s [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables)'s [active document](#731-navigables).
7. If topDocument's [autofocus processed flag](#667-the-autofocus-attribute) is false, then [remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) the element from topDocument's [autofocus candidates](#667-the-autofocus-attribute), and [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) the element to topDocument's [autofocus candidates](#667-the-autofocus-attribute).

> [!note]
> We do not check if an element is a [focusable area](#662-data-model) before storing it in the [autofocus candidates](#667-the-autofocus-attribute) list, because even if it is not a focusable area when it is inserted, it could become one by the time [flush autofocus candidates](#667-the-autofocus-attribute) sees it.

To flush autofocus candidates for a document topDocument, run these steps:
1. If topDocument's [autofocus processed flag](#667-the-autofocus-attribute) is true, then return.
2. Let candidates be topDocument's [autofocus candidates](#667-the-autofocus-attribute).
3. If candidates [is empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists), then return.
4. If topDocument's [focused area](#662-data-model) is not topDocument itself, or topDocument has non-null [target element](#7464-scrolling-to-a-fragment):
   1. [Empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) candidates.
   2. Set topDocument's [autofocus processed flag](#667-the-autofocus-attribute) to true.
   3. Return.
5. While candidates is not [empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists):
   1. Let element be candidates\[0\].
   2. Let doc be element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
   3. If doc is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents), then [remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) element from candidates, and [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   4. If doc's [node navigable](#731-navigables)'s [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables) is not the same as topDocument's [node navigable](#731-navigables), then [remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) element from candidates, and [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   5. If doc's [script-blocking style sheet set](#427-interactions-of-styling-and-scripting) is not [empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists), then return.

      > [!note]
      > In this case, element is the currently-best candidate, but doc is not ready for autofocusing. We'll try again next time [flush autofocus candidates](#667-the-autofocus-attribute) is called.

   6. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) element from candidates.
   7. Let inclusiveAncestorDocuments be a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) consisting of the [active document](#731-navigables) of doc's [inclusive ancestor navigables](#7315-related-navigable-collections).
   8. If any [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) in inclusiveAncestorDocuments has non-null [target element](#7464-scrolling-to-a-fragment), then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   9. Let target be element.
   10. If target is not a [focusable area](#662-data-model), then set target to the result of [getting the focusable area](#664-processing-model) for target.

       > [!note]
       > [Autofocus candidates](#667-the-autofocus-attribute) can [contain](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) elements which are not [focusable areas](#662-data-model). In addition to the special cases handled in the [get the focusable area](#664-processing-model) algorithm, this can happen because a non-[focusable area](#662-data-model) element with an [`autofocus`](#667-the-autofocus-attribute) attribute was [inserted into a document](#214-dom-trees) and it never became focusable, or because the element was focusable but its status changed while it was stored in [autofocus candidates](#667-the-autofocus-attribute).

   11. If target is not null:
       1. [Empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) candidates.
       2. Set topDocument's [autofocus processed flag](#667-the-autofocus-attribute) to true.
       3. Run the [focusing steps](#664-processing-model) for target.

> [!note]
> This handles the automatic focusing during document load. The [`show()`](#4114-the-dialog-element) and [`showModal()`](#4114-the-dialog-element) methods of [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) elements also processes the [`autofocus`](#667-the-autofocus-attribute) attribute.

> [!note]
> Focusing the element does not imply that the user agent has to focus the browser window if it has lost focus.

> [!example]
> In the following snippet, the text control would be focused when the document was loaded.
> 
> ```html
> <input maxlength="256" name="q" value="" autofocus>
> <input type="submit" value="Search">
> ```

> [!example]
> The [`autofocus`](#667-the-autofocus-attribute) attribute applies to all elements, not just to form controls. This allows examples such as the following:
> 
> ```html
> <div contenteditable autofocus>Edit <strong>me!</strong><div>
> ```

### 6.7 Assigning keyboard shortcuts

#### 6.7.1 Introduction

*This section is non-normative.*

Each element that can be activated or focused can be assigned a single key combination to activate it, using the [`accesskey`](#672-the-accesskey-attribute) attribute.

The exact shortcut is determined by the user agent, based on information about the user's keyboard, what keyboard shortcuts already exist on the platform, and what other shortcuts have been specified on the page, using the information provided in the [`accesskey`](#672-the-accesskey-attribute) attribute as a guide.

In order to ensure that a relevant keyboard shortcut is available on a wide variety of input devices, the author can provide a number of alternatives in the [`accesskey`](#672-the-accesskey-attribute) attribute.

Each alternative consists of a single character, such as a letter or digit.

User agents can provide users with a list of the keyboard shortcuts, but authors are encouraged to do so also. The [`accessKeyLabel`](#673-processing-model) IDL attribute returns a string representing the actual key combination assigned by the user agent.

> [!example]
> In this example, an author has provided a button that can be invoked using a shortcut key. To support full keyboards, the author has provided "C" as a possible key. To support devices equipped only with numeric keypads, the author has provided "1" as another possible key.
> 
> ```html
> <input type=button value=Collect onclick="collect()"
>        accesskey="C 1" id=c>
> ```

> [!example]
> To tell the user what the shortcut key is, the author has here opted to explicitly add the key combination to the button's label:
> 
> ```javascript
> function addShortcutKeyLabel(button) {
>   if (button.accessKeyLabel != '')
>     button.value += ' (' + button.accessKeyLabel + ')';
> }
> addShortcutKeyLabel(document.getElementById('c'));
> ```
> 
> Browsers on different platforms will show different labels, even for the same key combination, based on the convention prevalent on that platform. For example, if the key combination is the Control key, the Shift key, and the letter C, a Windows browser might display "Ctrl+Shift+C", whereas a Mac browser might display "^⇧C", while an Emacs browser might just display "C-C". Similarly, if the key combination is the Alt key and the Escape key, Windows might use "Alt+Esc", Mac might use "⌥⎋", and an Emacs browser might use "M-ESC" or "ESC ESC".
> 
> In general, therefore, it is unwise to attempt to parse the value returned from the [`accessKeyLabel`](#673-processing-model) IDL attribute.

#### 6.7.2 The `accesskey` attribute

All [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) may have the [`accesskey`](#672-the-accesskey-attribute) content attribute set. The [`accesskey`](#672-the-accesskey-attribute) attribute's value is used by the user agent as a guide for creating a keyboard shortcut that activates or focuses the element.

If specified, the value must be an [ordered set of unique space-separated tokens](#237-space-separated-tokens) none of which are [identical to](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) another token and each of which must be exactly one code point in length.

> [!example]
> In the following example, a variety of links are given with access keys so that keyboard users familiar with the site can more quickly navigate to the relevant pages:
> 
> ```html
> <nav>
>  <p>
>   <a title="Consortium Activities" accesskey="A" href="/Consortium/activities">Activities</a> |
>   <a title="Technical Reports and Recommendations" accesskey="T" href="/TR/">Technical Reports</a> |
>   <a title="Alphabetical Site Index" accesskey="S" href="/Consortium/siteindex">Site Index</a> |
>   <a title="About This Site" accesskey="B" href="/Consortium/">About Consortium</a> |
>   <a title="Contact Consortium" accesskey="C" href="/Consortium/contact">Contact</a>
>  </p>
> </nav>
> ```

> [!example]
> In the following example, the search field is given two possible access keys, "s" and "0" (in that order). A user agent on a device with a full keyboard might pick Ctrl + Alt + S as the shortcut key, while a user agent on a small device with just a numeric keypad might pick just the plain unadorned key 0:
> 
> ```html
> <form action="/search">
>  <label>Search: <input type="search" name="q" accesskey="s 0"></label>
>  <input type="submit">
> </form>
> ```

> [!example]
> In the following example, a button has possible access keys described. A script then tries to update the button's label to advertise the key combination the user agent selected.
> 
> ```html
> <input type=submit accesskey="N @ 1" value="Compose">
> ...
> <script>
>  function labelButton(button) {
>    if (button.accessKeyLabel)
>      button.value += ' (' + button.accessKeyLabel + ')';
>  }
>  var inputs = document.getElementsByTagName('input');
>  for (var i = 0; i < inputs.length; i += 1) {
>    if (inputs[i].type == "submit")
>      labelButton(inputs[i]);
>  }
> </script>
> ```
> 
> On one user agent, the button's label might become "Compose (⌘N)". On another, it might become "Compose (Alt+⇧+1)". If the user agent doesn't assign a key, it will be just "Compose". The exact string depends on what the [assigned access key](#673-processing-model) is, and on how the user agent represents that key combination.

#### 6.7.3 Processing model

An element's assigned access key is a key combination derived from the element's [`accesskey`](#672-the-accesskey-attribute) content attribute. Initially, an element must not have an [assigned access key](#673-processing-model).

Whenever an element's [`accesskey`](#672-the-accesskey-attribute) attribute is set, changed, or removed, the user agent must update the element's [assigned access key](#673-processing-model) by running the following steps:
1. If the element has no [`accesskey`](#672-the-accesskey-attribute) attribute, then skip to the *fallback* step below.
2. Otherwise, [split the attribute's value on ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings), and let keys be the resulting tokens.
3. For each value in keys in turn, in the order the tokens appeared in the attribute's value, run the following substeps:
   1. If the value is not a string exactly one code point in length, then skip the remainder of these steps for this value.
   2. If the value does not correspond to a key on the system's keyboard, then skip the remainder of these steps for this value.
   3. [![(This is a tracking vector.)](https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg)](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#24-privacy-concerns) If the user agent can find a mix of zero or more modifier keys that, combined with the key that corresponds to the value given in the attribute, can be used as the access key, then the user agent may assign that combination of keys as the element's [assigned access key](#673-processing-model) and return.
4. *Fallback*: Optionally, the user agent may assign a key combination of its choosing as the element's [assigned access key](#673-processing-model) and then return.
5. If this step is reached, the element has no [assigned access key](#673-processing-model).

Once a user agent has selected and assigned an access key for an element, the user agent should not change the element's [assigned access key](#673-processing-model) unless the [`accesskey`](#672-the-accesskey-attribute) content attribute is changed or the element is moved to another [`Document`](#311-the-document-object).

When the user presses the key combination corresponding to the [assigned access key](#673-processing-model) for an element, if the element [defines a command](#41131-facets), the command's [Hidden State](#41131-facets) facet is false (visible), the command's [Disabled State](#41131-facets) facet is also false (enabled), the element is [in a document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) that has a non-null [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts), and neither the element nor any of its ancestors has a [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute specified, then the user agent must trigger the [Action](#41131-facets) of the command.

> [!note]
> User agents [might expose](#41131-facets) elements that have an [`accesskey`](#672-the-accesskey-attribute) attribute in other ways as well, e.g. in a menu displayed in response to a specific key combination.

---

The `accessKeyLabel` IDL attribute must return a string that represents the element's [assigned access key](#673-processing-model), if any. If the element does not have one, then the IDL attribute must return the empty string.

### 6.8 Editing

#### 6.8.1 Making document regions editable: The [`contenteditable`](#681-making-document-regions-editable-the-contenteditable-content-attribute) content attribute

```webidl
interface mixin ElementContentEditable {
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString contentEditable;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString enterKeyHint;
  readonly attribute boolean isContentEditable;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString inputMode;
};
```

The `contenteditable` content attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `true` | True | The element is editable. |
| `false` | False | The element is not editable. |
| `plaintext-only` | Plaintext-Only | Only the element's raw text content is editable; rich formatting is disabled. |

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the Inherit state. The inherit state indicates that the element is editable (or not) based on the parent element's state. The attribute's *[empty value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* is the [True](#681-making-document-regions-editable-the-contenteditable-content-attribute) state.

> [!example]
> For example, consider a page that has a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) and a [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) to publish a new article, where the user is expected to write the article using HTML:
> 
> ```html
> <form method=POST>
>  <fieldset>
>   <legend>New article</legend>
>   <textarea name=article>&lt;p>Hello world.&lt;/p></textarea>
>  </fieldset>
>  <p><button>Publish</button></p>
> </form>
> ```
> 
> When scripting is enabled, the [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element could be replaced with a rich text control instead, using the [`contenteditable`](#681-making-document-regions-editable-the-contenteditable-content-attribute) attribute:
> 
> ```html
> <form method=POST>
>  <fieldset>
>   <legend>New article</legend>
>   <textarea id=textarea name=article>&lt;p>Hello world.&lt;/p></textarea>
>   <div id=div style="white-space: pre-wrap" hidden><p>Hello world.</p></div>
>   <script>
>    let textarea = document.getElementById("textarea");
>    let div = document.getElementById("div");
>    textarea.hidden = true;
>    div.hidden = false;
>    div.contentEditable = "true";
>    div.oninput = (e) => {
>      textarea.value = div.innerHTML;
>    };
>   </script>
>  </fieldset>
>  <p><button>Publish</button></p>
> </form>
> ```
> 
> Features to enable, e.g., inserting links, can be implemented using the [`document.execCommand()`](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#execcommand%28%29) API, or using [`Selection`](https://w3c.github.io/selection-api/#selection-interface) APIs and other DOM APIs. [\[EXECCOMMAND\]](#references) [\[SELECTION\]](#references) [\[DOM\]](#references)

> [!example]
> The [`contenteditable`](#681-making-document-regions-editable-the-contenteditable-content-attribute) attribute can also be used to great effect:
> 
> ```html
> <!doctype html>
> <html lang=en>
> <title>Live CSS editing!</title>
> <style style=white-space:pre contenteditable>
> html { margin:.2em; font-size:2em; color:lime; background:purple }
> head, title, style { display:block }
> body { display:none }
> </style>
> ```

`element.contentEditable [ = value ]`

Returns "`true`", "`plaintext-only`", "`false`", or "`inherit`", based on the state of the [`contenteditable`](#681-making-document-regions-editable-the-contenteditable-content-attribute) attribute.

Can be set, to change that state.

Throws a ["`SyntaxError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the new value isn't one of those strings.

`element.isContentEditable`

Returns true if the element is editable; otherwise, returns false.

The `contentEditable` IDL attribute, on getting, must return the string "`true`" if the content attribute is set to the [True](#681-making-document-regions-editable-the-contenteditable-content-attribute) state, "`plaintext-only`" if the content attribute is set to the [Plaintext-Only](#681-making-document-regions-editable-the-contenteditable-content-attribute) state, "`false`" if the content attribute is set to the [False](#681-making-document-regions-editable-the-contenteditable-content-attribute) state, and "`inherit`" otherwise. On setting, if the new value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`inherit`", then the content attribute must be removed, if the new value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`true`", then the content attribute must be set to the string "`true`", if the new value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`plaintext-only`", then the content attribute must be set to the string "`plaintext-only`", if the new value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`false`", then the content attribute must be set to the string "`false`", and otherwise the attribute setter must throw a ["`SyntaxError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

The `isContentEditable` IDL attribute, on getting, must return true if the element is either an [editing host](#684-editing-apis) or [editable](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable), and false otherwise.

#### 6.8.2 Making entire documents editable: the [`designMode`](#682-making-entire-documents-editable-the-designmode-getter-and-setter) getter and setter

`document.designMode [ = value ]`

Returns "`on`" if the document is editable, and "`off`" if it isn't.

Can be set, to change the document's current state. This focuses the document and resets the selection in that document.

[`Document`](#311-the-document-object) objects have an associated design mode enabled, which is a boolean. It is initially false.

The `designMode` getter steps are to return "`on`" if [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [design mode enabled](#682-making-entire-documents-editable-the-designmode-getter-and-setter) is true; otherwise "`off`".

The [`designMode`](#682-making-entire-documents-editable-the-designmode-getter-and-setter) setter steps are:
1. Let value be the given value, [converted to ASCII lowercase](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).
2. If value is "`on`" and [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [design mode enabled](#682-making-entire-documents-editable-the-designmode-getter-and-setter) is false:
   1. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [design mode enabled](#682-making-entire-documents-editable-the-designmode-getter-and-setter) to true.
   2. Reset [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [active range](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#active-range)'s start and end boundary points to be at the start of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
   3. Run the [focusing steps](#664-processing-model) for [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree), if non-null.
3. If value is "`off`", then set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [design mode enabled](#682-making-entire-documents-editable-the-designmode-getter-and-setter) to false.

#### 6.8.3 Best practices for in-page editors

Authors are encouraged to set the ['white-space'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#white-space-property) property on [editing hosts](#684-editing-apis) and on markup that was originally created through these editing mechanisms to the value 'pre-wrap'. Default HTML whitespace handling is not well suited to WYSIWYG editing, and line wrapping will not work correctly in some corner cases if ['white-space'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#white-space-property) is left at its default value.

> [!example]
> As an example of problems that occur if the default 'normal' value is used instead, consider the case of the user typing "yellow␣␣ball", with two spaces (here represented by "␣") between the words. With the editing rules in place for the default value of ['white-space'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#white-space-property) ('normal'), the resulting markup will either consist of "yellow&nbsp; ball" or "yellow &nbsp;ball"; i.e., there will be a non-breaking space between the two words in addition to the regular space. This is necessary because the 'normal' value for ['white-space'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#white-space-property) requires adjacent regular spaces to be collapsed together.
> 
> In the former case, "yellow⍽" might wrap to the next line ("⍽" being used here to represent a non-breaking space) even though "yellow" alone might fit at the end of the line; in the latter case, "⍽ball", if wrapped to the start of the line, would have visible indentation from the non-breaking space.
> 
> When ['white-space'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#white-space-property) is set to 'pre-wrap', however, the editing rules will instead simply put two regular spaces between the words, and should the two words be split at the end of a line, the spaces would be neatly removed from the rendering.

#### 6.8.4 Editing APIs

An editing host is either an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) with its [`contenteditable`](#681-making-document-regions-editable-the-contenteditable-content-attribute) attribute in the *true* state or *plaintext-only* state, or a [child](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) of a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) whose [design mode enabled](#682-making-entire-documents-editable-the-designmode-getter-and-setter) is true.

The definition of the terms [active range](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#active-range), [editing host of](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editing-host-of), and [editable](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable), the user interface requirements of elements that are [editing hosts](#684-editing-apis) or [editable](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable), the [`execCommand()`](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#execcommand%28%29), [`queryCommandEnabled()`](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#querycommandenabled%28%29), [`queryCommandIndeterm()`](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#querycommandindeterm%28%29), [`queryCommandState()`](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#querycommandstate%28%29), [`queryCommandSupported()`](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#querycommandsupported%28%29), and [`queryCommandValue()`](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#querycommandvalue%28%29) methods, text selections, and the [delete the selection](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#delete-the-selection) algorithm are defined in execCommand. [\[EXECCOMMAND\]](#references)

#### 6.8.5 Spelling and grammar checking

User agents can support the checking of spelling and grammar of editable text, either in form controls (such as the value of [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements), or in elements in an [editing host](#684-editing-apis) (e.g. using [`contenteditable`](#681-making-document-regions-editable-the-contenteditable-content-attribute)).

For each element, user agents must establish a default behavior, either through defaults or through preferences expressed by the user. There are three possible default behaviors for each element:

true-by-default

The element will be checked for spelling and grammar if its contents are editable and spellchecking is not explicitly disabled through the [`spellcheck`](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) attribute.

false-by-default

The element will never be checked for spelling and grammar unless spellchecking is explicitly enabled through the [`spellcheck`](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) attribute.

inherit-by-default

The element's default behavior is the same as its parent element's. Elements that have no parent element cannot have this as their default behavior.

---

The `spellcheck` attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `true` | True | Spelling and grammar will be checked. |
| `false` | False | Spelling and grammar will not be checked. |

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the Default state. The default state indicates that the element is to act according to a default behavior, possibly based on the parent element's own [`spellcheck`](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) state, as defined below. The attribute's *[empty value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* is the [True](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) state.

---

`element.spellcheck [ = value ]`

Returns true if the element is to have its spelling and grammar checked; otherwise, returns false.

Can be set, to override the default and set the [`spellcheck`](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) content attribute.

The `spellcheck` IDL attribute, on getting, must return true if the element's [`spellcheck`](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) content attribute is in the [True](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) state, or if the element's [`spellcheck`](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) content attribute is in the [Default](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) state and the element's [default behavior](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) is [true-by-default](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking), or if the element's [`spellcheck`](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) content attribute is in the [Default](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) state and the element's [default behavior](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) is [inherit-by-default](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) and the element's parent element's [`spellcheck`](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) IDL attribute would return true; otherwise, if none of those conditions applies, then the attribute must instead return false.

> [!note]
> The [`spellcheck`](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) IDL attribute is not affected by user preferences that override the [`spellcheck`](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) content attribute, and therefore might not reflect the actual spellchecking state.

On setting, if the new value is true, then the element's [`spellcheck`](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) content attribute must be set to "`true`", otherwise it must be set to "`false`".

---

User agents should only consider the following pieces of text as checkable for the purposes of this feature:
- The [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attributes are in the [Text](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch), [Search](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch), [URL](#410514-url-state-typeurl), or [Email](#410515-email-state-typeemail) states and that are [mutable](#410182-mutability) (i.e. that do not have the [`readonly`](#410533-the-readonly-attribute) attribute specified and that are not [disabled](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute)).
- The [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) of [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements that do not have a [`readonly`](#41011-the-textarea-element) attribute and that are not [disabled](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute).
- Text in [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) nodes that are children of [editing hosts](#684-editing-apis) or [editable](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable) elements.
- Text in attributes of [editable](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable) elements.

For text that is part of a [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node, the element with which the text is associated is the element that is the immediate parent of the first character of the word, sentence, or other piece of text. For text in attributes, it is the attribute's element. For the values of [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) and [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements, it is the element itself.

To determine if a word, sentence, or other piece of text in an applicable element (as defined above) is to have spelling- and grammar-checking enabled, the UA must use the following algorithm:
1. If the user has disabled the checking for this text, then the checking is disabled.
2. Otherwise, if the user has forced the checking for this text to always be enabled, then the checking is enabled.
3. Otherwise, if the element with which the text is associated has a [`spellcheck`](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) content attribute, then: if that attribute is in the [True](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) state, then checking is enabled; otherwise, if that attribute is in the [False](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) state, then checking is disabled.
4. Otherwise, if there is an ancestor element with a [`spellcheck`](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) content attribute that is not in the [Default](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) state, then: if the nearest such ancestor's [`spellcheck`](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) content attribute is in the [True](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) state, then checking is enabled; otherwise, checking is disabled.
5. Otherwise, if the element's [default behavior](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) is [true-by-default](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking), then checking is enabled.
6. Otherwise, if the element's [default behavior](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking) is [false-by-default](#685-spelling-and-grammar-checking), then checking is disabled.
7. Otherwise, if the element's parent element has *its* checking enabled, then checking is enabled.
8. Otherwise, checking is disabled.

If the checking is enabled for a word/sentence/text, the user agent should indicate spelling and grammar errors in that text. User agents should take into account the other semantics given in the document when suggesting spelling and grammar corrections. User agents may use the language of the element to determine what spelling and grammar rules to use, or may use the user's preferred language settings. UAs should use [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element attributes such as [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute) to ensure that the resulting value is valid, where possible.

If checking is disabled, the user agent should not indicate spelling or grammar errors for that text.

> [!example]
> The element with ID "a" in the following example would be the one used to determine if the word "Hello" is checked for spelling errors. In this example, it would not be.
> 
> ```html
> <div contenteditable="true">
>  <span spellcheck="false" id="a">Hell</span><em>o!</em>
> </div>
> ```
> 
> The element with ID "b" in the following example would have checking enabled (the leading space character in the attribute's value on the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element causes the attribute to be ignored, so the ancestor's value is used instead, regardless of the default).
> 
> ```html
> <p spellcheck="true">
>  <label>Name: <input spellcheck=" false" id="b"></label>
> </p>
> ```

> [!note]
> This specification does not define the user interface for spelling and grammar checkers. A user agent could offer on-demand checking, could perform continuous checking while the checking is enabled, or could use other interfaces.

#### 6.8.6 Writing suggestions

User agents offer writing suggestions as users type into editable regions, either in form controls (e.g., the [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element) or in elements in an [editing host](#684-editing-apis).

The `writingsuggestions` content attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `true` | True | Writing suggestions should be offered on this element. |
| `false` | False | Writing suggestions should not be offered on this element. |

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* is the Default state. The default state indicates that the element is to act according to a default behavior, possibly based on the parent element's own [`writingsuggestions`](#686-writing-suggestions) state, as defined below.

The attribute's *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[empty value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the [True](#686-writing-suggestions) state.

`element.writingSuggestions [ = value ]`

Returns "`true`" if the user agent is to offer writing suggestions under the scope of the element; otherwise, returns "`false`".

Can be set, to override the default and set the [`
    writingsuggestions`](#686-writing-suggestions) content attribute.

The computed writing suggestions value of a given element is determined by running the following steps:
1. If element's [`writingsuggestions`](#686-writing-suggestions) content attribute is in the [False](#686-writing-suggestions) state, return "`false`".
2. If element's [`writingsuggestions`](#686-writing-suggestions) content attribute is in the [Default](#686-writing-suggestions) state, element has a parent element, and the [computed writing suggestions value](#686-writing-suggestions) of element's parent element is "`false`", then return "`false`".
3. Return "`true`".

The `writingSuggestions` getter steps are:
1. Return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [computed writing suggestions value](#686-writing-suggestions).

> [!note]
> The [`writingSuggestions`](#686-writing-suggestions) IDL attribute is not affected by user preferences that override the [`writingsuggestions`](#686-writing-suggestions) content attribute, and therefore might not reflect the actual writing suggestions state.

---

User agents should only offer suggestions within an element's scope if the result of running the following algorithm given element returns true:
1. If the user has disabled writing suggestions, then return false.
2. If none of the following conditions are true:
   - element is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in either the [Text](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch), [Search](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch), [Telephone](#410513-telephone-state-typetel), [URL](#410514-url-state-typeurl), or [Email](#410515-email-state-typeemail) state and element is [mutable](#410182-mutability);
   - element is a [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element that is [mutable](#410182-mutability); or
   - element is an [editing host](#684-editing-apis) or is [editable](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable),

   then return false.

3. If element has an [inclusive ancestor](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) with a [`writingsuggestions`](#686-writing-suggestions) content attribute that's not in the [Default](#686-writing-suggestions) and the nearest such ancestor's [`writingsuggestions`](#686-writing-suggestions) content attribute is in the [False](#686-writing-suggestions) state, then return false.
4. Otherwise, return true.

> [!note]
> This specification does not define the user interface for writing suggestions. A user agent could offer on-demand suggestions, continuous suggestions as the user types, inline suggestions, autofill-like suggestions in a popup, or could use other interfaces.

#### 6.8.7 Autocapitalization

Some methods of entering text, for example virtual keyboards on mobile devices, and also voice input, often assist users by automatically capitalizing the first letter of sentences (when composing text in a language with this convention). A virtual keyboard that implements autocapitalization might automatically switch to showing uppercase letters (but allow the user to toggle it back to lowercase) when a letter that should be autocapitalized is about to be typed. Other types of input, for example voice input, may perform autocapitalization in a way that does not give users an option to intervene first. The [`autocapitalize`](#687-autocapitalization) attribute allows authors to control such behavior.

The [`autocapitalize`](#687-autocapitalization) attribute, as typically implemented, does not affect behavior when typing on a physical keyboard. (For this reason, as well as the ability for users to override the autocapitalization behavior in some cases or edit the text after initial input, the attribute must not be relied on for any sort of input validation.)

The [`autocapitalize`](#687-autocapitalization) attribute can be used on an [editing host](#684-editing-apis) to control autocapitalization behavior for the hosted editable region, on an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) or [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element to control the behavior for inputting text into that element, or on a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element to control the default behavior for all [autocapitalize-and-autocorrect inheriting elements](#4102-categories) associated with the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element.

The [`autocapitalize`](#687-autocapitalization) attribute never causes autocapitalization to be enabled for [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in one of the [URL](#410514-url-state-typeurl), [Email](#410515-email-state-typeemail), or [Password](#410516-password-state-typepassword) states. (This behavior is included in the [used autocapitalization hint](#687-autocapitalization) algorithm below.)

The autocapitalization processing model is based on selecting among five autocapitalization hints, defined as follows:

Default

The user agent and input method should make their own determination of whether or not to enable autocapitalization.

None

No autocapitalization should be applied (all letters should default to lowercase).

Sentences

The first letter of each sentence should default to a capital letter; all other letters should default to lowercase.

Words

The first letter of each word should default to a capital letter; all other letters should default to lowercase.

Characters

All letters should default to uppercase.

The `autocapitalize` attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) whose states are the possible [autocapitalization hints](#687-autocapitalization). The [autocapitalization hint](#687-autocapitalization) specified by the attribute's state combines with other considerations to form the [used autocapitalization hint](#687-autocapitalization), which informs the behavior of the user agent. The keywords for this attribute and their state mappings are as follows:

| Keyword | State |
| --- | --- |
| `off` | [None](#687-autocapitalization) |
| `none` |
| `on` | [Sentences](#687-autocapitalization) |
| `sentences` |
| `words` | [Words](#687-autocapitalization) |
| `characters` | [Characters](#687-autocapitalization) |

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* is the [Default](#687-autocapitalization) state, and its *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* is the [Sentences](#687-autocapitalization) state.

`element.autocapitalize [ = value ]`

Returns the current autocapitalization state for the element, or an empty string if it hasn't been set. Note that for [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) and [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements that inherit their state from a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element, this will return the autocapitalization state of the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element, but for an element in an editable region, this will not return the autocapitalization state of the editing host (unless this element is, in fact, the [editing host](#684-editing-apis)).

Can be set, to set the [`autocapitalize`](#687-autocapitalization) content attribute (and thereby change the autocapitalization behavior for the element).

To compute the own autocapitalization hint of an element element, run the following steps:
1. If the [`autocapitalize`](#687-autocapitalization) content attribute is present on element, and its value is not the empty string, return the state of the attribute.
2. If element is an [autocapitalize-and-autocorrect inheriting element](#4102-categories) and has a non-null [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms), return the [own autocapitalization hint](#687-autocapitalization) of element's [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms).
3. Return [Default](#687-autocapitalization).

The `autocapitalize` getter steps are to:
1. Let state be the [own autocapitalization hint](#687-autocapitalization) of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
2. If state is [Default](#687-autocapitalization), then return the empty string.
3. If state is [None](#687-autocapitalization), then return "[`none`](#687-autocapitalization)".
4. If state is [Sentences](#687-autocapitalization), then return "[`sentences`](#687-autocapitalization)".
5. Return the keyword value corresponding to state.

---

User agents that support customizable autocapitalization behavior for a text input method and wish to allow web developers to control this functionality should, during text input into an element, compute the used autocapitalization hint for the element. This will be an [autocapitalization hint](#687-autocapitalization) that describes the recommended autocapitalization behavior for text input into the element.

User agents or input methods may choose to ignore or override the [used autocapitalization hint](#687-autocapitalization) in certain circumstances.

The [used autocapitalization hint](#687-autocapitalization) for an element element is computed using the following algorithm:
1. If element is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in one of the [URL](#410514-url-state-typeurl), [Email](#410515-email-state-typeemail), or [Password](#410516-password-state-typepassword) states, then return [Default](#687-autocapitalization).
2. If element is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element or a [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element, then return element's [own autocapitalization hint](#687-autocapitalization).
3. If element is an [editing host](#684-editing-apis) or an [editable](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable) element, then return the [own autocapitalization hint](#687-autocapitalization) of the [editing host of](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editing-host-of) element.
4. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): this step is never reached, since text input only occurs in elements that meet one of the above criteria.

#### 6.8.8 Autocorrection

Some methods of entering text assist users by automatically correcting misspelled words while typing, a process also known as autocorrection. User agents can support autocorrection of editable text, either in form controls (such as the value of [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements), or in elements in an [editing host](#684-editing-apis) (e.g., using [`contenteditable`](#681-making-document-regions-editable-the-contenteditable-content-attribute)). Autocorrection may be accompanied by user interfaces indicating that text is about to be autocorrected or has been autocorrected, and is commonly performed when inserting punctuation characters, spaces, or new paragraphs after misspelled words. The [`autocorrect`](#688-autocorrection) attribute allows authors to control such behavior.

The [`autocorrect`](#688-autocorrection) attribute can be used on an editing host to control autocorrection behavior for the hosted editable region, on an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) or [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element to control the behavior when inserting text into that element, or on a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element to control the default behavior for all [autocapitalize-and-autocorrect inheriting elements](#4102-categories) associated with the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element.

The [`autocorrect`](#688-autocorrection) attribute never causes autocorrection to be enabled for [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in one of the [URL](#410514-url-state-typeurl), [Email](#410515-email-state-typeemail), or [Password](#410516-password-state-typepassword) states. (This behavior is included in the [used autocorrection state](#688-autocorrection) algorithm below.)

The `autocorrect` attribute is an enumerated attribute with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `on` | On | The user agent is permitted to automatically correct spelling errors while the user types. Whether spelling is automatically corrected while typing left is for the user agent to decide, and may depend on the element as well as the user's preferences. |
| `off` | Off | The user agent is not allowed to automatically correct spelling while the user types. |

The attribute's *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)*, *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)*, and *[empty value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are all the [On](#688-autocorrection) state.

The `autocorrect` getter steps are: return true if the element's [used autocorrection state](#688-autocorrection) is [On](#688-autocorrection) and false if the element's [used autocorrection state](#688-autocorrection) is [Off](#688-autocorrection). The setter steps are: if the given value is true, then the element's [`autocorrect`](#688-autocorrection) attribute must be set to "`on`"; otherwise it must be set to "`off`".

To compute the used autocorrection state of an element element, run these steps:
1. If element is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in one of the [URL](#410514-url-state-typeurl), [Email](#410515-email-state-typeemail), or [Password](#410516-password-state-typepassword) states, then return [Off](#688-autocorrection).
