2. If the [`autocorrect`](#688-autocorrection) content attribute is present on element, then return the state of the attribute.
3. If element is an [autocapitalize-and-autocorrect inheriting element](#4102-categories) and has a non-null [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms), then return the state of element's [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms)'s [`autocorrect`](#688-autocorrection) attribute.
4. Return [On](#688-autocorrection).

element . [`autocorrect`](#688-autocorrection)

Returns the autocorrection behavior of the element. Note that for [autocapitalize-and-autocorrect inheriting elements](#4102-categories) that inherit their state from a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element, this will return the autocorrection behavior of the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element, but for an element in an editable region, this will not return the autocorrection behavior of the [editing host](#684-editing-apis) (unless this element is, in fact, the [editing host](#684-editing-apis)).

element . [`autocorrect`](#688-autocorrection) = value

Updates the [`autocorrect`](#688-autocorrection) content attribute (and thereby changes the autocorrection behavior of the element).

> [!example]
> The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element in the following example would not allow autocorrection, since it does not have an [`autocorrect`](#688-autocorrection) content attribute and therefore inherits from the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element, which has an attribute of "[`off`](#688-autocorrection)". However, the [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element would allow autocorrection, since it has an [`autocorrect`](#688-autocorrection) content attribute with a value of "[`on`](#688-autocorrection)".
> 
> ```html
> <form autocorrect="off">
>  <input type="search">
>  <textarea autocorrect="on"></textarea>
> </form>
> ```

#### 6.8.9 Input modalities: the [`inputmode`](#689-input-modalities-the-inputmode-attribute) attribute

User agents can support the [`inputmode`](#689-input-modalities-the-inputmode-attribute) attribute on form controls (such as the value of [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements), or in elements in an [editing host](#684-editing-apis) (e.g., using [`contenteditable`](#681-making-document-regions-editable-the-contenteditable-content-attribute)).

The `inputmode` content attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) that specifies what kind of input mechanism would be most helpful for users entering content.

| Keyword | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `none` | The user agent should not display a virtual keyboard. This keyword is useful for content that renders its own keyboard control. |
| `text` | The user agent should display a virtual keyboard capable of text input in the user's locale. |
| `tel` | The user agent should display a virtual keyboard capable of telephone number input. This should including keys for the digits 0 to 9, the "#" character, and the "\*" character. In some locales, this can also include alphabetic mnemonic labels (e.g., in the US, the key labeled "2" is historically also labeled with the letters A, B, and C). |
| `url` | The user agent should display a virtual keyboard capable of text input in the user's locale, with keys for aiding in the input of [URLs](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url), such as that for the "/" and "." characters and for quick input of strings commonly found in domain names such as "www." or ".com". |
| `email` | The user agent should display a virtual keyboard capable of text input in the user's locale, with keys for aiding in the input of email addresses, such as that for the "@" character and the "." character. |
| `numeric` | The user agent should display a virtual keyboard capable of numeric input. This keyword is useful for PIN entry. |
| `decimal` | The user agent should display a virtual keyboard capable of fractional numeric input. Numeric keys and the format separator for the locale should be shown. |
| `search` | The user agent should display a virtual keyboard optimized for search. |

The `inputMode` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`inputmode`](#689-input-modalities-the-inputmode-attribute) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

When [`inputmode`](#689-input-modalities-the-inputmode-attribute) is unspecified (or is in a state not supported by the user agent), the user agent should determine the default virtual keyboard to be shown. Contextual information such as the input [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) or [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute) attributes should be used to determine which type of virtual keyboard should be presented to the user.

#### 6.8.10 Input modalities: the [`enterkeyhint`](#6810-input-modalities-the-enterkeyhint-attribute) attribute

User agents can support the [`enterkeyhint`](#6810-input-modalities-the-enterkeyhint-attribute) attribute on form controls (such as the value of [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements), or in elements in an [editing host](#684-editing-apis) (e.g., using [`contenteditable`](#681-making-document-regions-editable-the-contenteditable-content-attribute)).

The `enterkeyhint` content attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) that specifies what action label (or icon) to present for the enter key on virtual keyboards. This allows authors to customize the presentation of the enter key in order to make it more helpful for users.

| Keyword | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `enter` | The user agent should present a cue for the operation 'enter', typically inserting a new line. |
| `done` | The user agent should present a cue for the operation 'done', typically meaning there is nothing more to input and the input method editor (IME) will be closed. |
| `go` | The user agent should present a cue for the operation 'go', typically meaning to take the user to the target of the text they typed. |
| `next` | The user agent should present a cue for the operation 'next', typically taking the user to the next field that will accept text. |
| `previous` | The user agent should present a cue for the operation 'previous', typically taking the user to the previous field that will accept text. |
| `search` | The user agent should present a cue for the operation 'search', typically taking the user to the results of searching for the text they have typed. |
| `send` | The user agent should present a cue for the operation 'send', typically delivering the text to its target. |

The `enterKeyHint` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`enterkeyhint`](#6810-input-modalities-the-enterkeyhint-attribute) content attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

When [`enterkeyhint`](#6810-input-modalities-the-enterkeyhint-attribute) is unspecified (or is in a state not supported by the user agent), the user agent should determine the default action label (or icon) to present. Contextual information such as the [`inputmode`](#689-input-modalities-the-inputmode-attribute), [`type`](#4105-the-input-element), or [`pattern`](#410536-the-pattern-attribute) attributes should be used to determine which action label (or icon) to present on the virtual keyboard.

### 6.9 Find-in-page

#### 6.9.1 Introduction

This section defines find-in-page — a common user-agent mechanism which allows users to search through the contents of the page for particular information.

Access to the [find-in-page](#691-introduction) feature is provided via a find-in-page interface. This is a user-agent provided user interface, which allows the user to specify input and the parameters of the search. This interface can appear as a result of a shortcut or a menu selection.

A combination of text input and settings in the [find-in-page interface](#691-introduction) represents the user query. This typically includes the text that the user wants to search for, as well as optional settings (e.g., the ability to restrict the search to whole words only).

The user-agent processes page contents for a given [query](#691-introduction), and identifies zero or more matches, which are content ranges that satisfy the user [query](#691-introduction).

One of the [matches](#691-introduction) is identified to the user as the active match. It is highlighted and scrolled into view. The user can navigate through the [matches](#691-introduction) by advancing the [active match](#691-introduction) using the [find-in-page interface](#691-introduction).

> [!warning]
> [Issue #3539](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/3539) tracks standardizing how [find-in-page](#691-introduction) underlies the currently-unspecified `window.find()` API.

#### 6.9.2 Interaction with [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) and [`hidden=until-found`](#61-the-hidden-attribute)

When find-in-page begins searching for matches, all [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) elements in the page which do not have their [`open`](#4111-the-details-element) attribute set should have the [skipped contents](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-contain/#skips-its-contents) of their second slot become accessible, without modifying the [`open`](#4111-the-details-element) attribute, in order to make find-in-page able to search through it. Similarly, all HTML elements with the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute in the [Hidden Until Found](#61-the-hidden-attribute) state should have their [skipped contents](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-contain/#skips-its-contents) become accessible without modifying the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute in order to make find-in-page able to search through them. After find-in-page finishes searching for matches, the [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) elements and the elements with the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute in the [Hidden Until Found](#61-the-hidden-attribute) state should have their contents become skipped again. This entire process must happen synchronously (and so is not observable to users or to author code). [\[CSSCONTAIN\]](#references)

When find-in-page chooses a new [active match](#691-introduction), perform the following steps:
1. Let node be the first node in the [active match](#691-introduction).
2. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [user interaction task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given node's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) to run the [ancestor revealing algorithm](#61-the-hidden-attribute) on node.

> [!warning]
> [![(This is a tracking vector.)](https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg)](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#24-privacy-concerns) When find-in-page auto-expands a [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element like this, it will fire a [`toggle`](#events) event. As with the separate [`scroll`](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view/#eventdef-document-scroll) event that find-in-page fires, this event could be used by the page to discover what the user is typing into the find-in-page dialog. If the page creates a tiny scrollable area with the current search term and every possible next character the user could type separated by a gap, and observes which one the browser scrolls to, it can add that character to the search term and update the scrollable area to incrementally build the search term. By wrapping each possible next match in a closed [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element, the page could listen to [`toggle`](#events) events instead of [`scroll`](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view/#eventdef-document-scroll) events. This attack could be addressed for both events by not acting on every character the user types into the find-in-page dialog.

#### 6.9.3 Interaction with selection

The find-in-page process is invoked in the context of a document, and may have an effect on the [selection](https://w3c.github.io/selection-api/#dfn-selection) of that document. Specifically, the range that defines the [active match](#691-introduction) can dictate the current selection. These selection updates, however, can happen at different times during the find-in-page process (e.g. upon the [find-in-page interface](#691-introduction) dismissal or upon a change in the [active match](#691-introduction) range).

### 6.10 Close requests and close watchers

#### 6.10.1 Close requests

In an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) (and likely device-specific) manner, a user can send a close request to the user agent. This indicates that the user wishes to close something that is currently being shown on the screen, such as a popover, menu, dialog, picker, or display mode.

> [!example]
> Some example close requests are:
> - The Esc key on desktop platforms.
> - The back button or gesture on certain mobile platforms such as Android.
> - Any assistive technology's dismiss gesture, such as iOS VoiceOver's two-finger scrub "z" gesture.
> - A game controller's canonical "back" button, such as the circle button on a DualShock gamepad.

Whenever the user agent receives a potential close request targeted at a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document, it must [queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [user interaction task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given document's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) to perform the following close request steps:
1. If document's [fullscreen element](https://fullscreen.spec.whatwg.org/#fullscreen-element) is not null:
   1. [Fully exit fullscreen](https://fullscreen.spec.whatwg.org/#fully-exit-fullscreen) given document's [node navigable](#731-navigables)'s [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables)'s [active document](#731-navigables).
   2. Return.

   > [!note]
   > This does *not* fire any relevant event, such as [`keydown`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-keydown); it only causes [`fullscreenchange`](https://fullscreen.spec.whatwg.org/#eventdef-document-fullscreenchange) to be eventually fired.

2. Optionally, skip to the step labeled [alternative processing](#6101-close-requests).

   > [!note]
   > For example, if the user agent detects user frustration at repeated close request interception by the current web page, it might take this path.

3. Fire any relevant events, per UI Events or other relevant specifications. [\[UIEVENTS\]](#references)

   > [!example]
   > An example of a relevant event in the UI Events model would be the [`keydown`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-keydown) event that UI Events [suggests](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#events-keyboard-event-order) firing when the user presses the Esc key on their keyboard. On most platforms with keyboards, this is treated as a [close request](#6101-close-requests), and so would trigger these [close request steps](#6101-close-requests).

   > [!example]
   > An example of relevant events that are outside of the model given in UI Events would be assistive technology synthesizing an Esc [`keydown`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-keydown) event when the user sends a [close request](#6101-close-requests) by using a dismiss gesture.

4. Let event be null if no such events are fired, or the [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) object representing one of the fired events otherwise. If multiple events are fired, which one is chosen is [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology).
5. If event is not null, and its [canceled flag](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) is set, then return.
6. If document is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents), then return.

   > [!note]
   > This step is necessary because, if event is not null, then an event listener might have caused document to no longer be [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents).

7. Let closedSomething be the result of [processing close watchers](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) on document's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant).
8. If closedSomething is true, then return.
9. *Alternative processing*: Otherwise, there was nothing watching for a [close request](#6101-close-requests). The user agent may instead interpret this interaction as some other action, instead of interpreting it as a close request.

On platforms where pressing the Esc key is interpreted as a [close request](#6101-close-requests), the user agent must interpret the key being pressed *down* as the close request, instead of the key being released. Thus, in the above algorithm, the "relevant events" that are fired must be the single [`keydown`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-keydown) event.

> [!example]
> On platforms where Esc is the [close request](#6101-close-requests), the user agent will first fire an appropriately-initialized [`keydown`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-keydown) event. If the web developer cancels the event by calling [`preventDefault()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event), then nothing further happens. But if the event fires without being canceled, then the user agent proceeds to [process close watchers](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure).

> [!example]
> On platforms where a back button is a potential [close request](#6101-close-requests), no event is involved, so when the back button is pressed, the user agent proceeds directly to [process close watchers](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure). If there is an [active](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) [close watcher](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure), then that will get triggered. If there is not, then the user agent can interpret the back button press in another way, for example as a request to [traverse the history by a delta](#743-reloading-and-traversing) of −1.

#### 6.10.2 Close watcher infrastructure

Each [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) has a close watcher manager, which is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) with the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):
- Groups, a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [lists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [close watchers](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure), initially empty.
- Allowed number of groups, a number, initially 1.
- Next user interaction allows a new group, a boolean, initially true.

Most of the complexity of the [close watcher manager](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) comes from anti-abuse protections designed to prevent developers from disabling users' history traversal abilities, for platforms where a [close request](#6101-close-requests)'s [fallback action](#6101-close-requests) is the main mechanism of history traversal. In particular:

The grouping of [close watchers](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) is designed so that if multiple close watchers are created without [history-action activation](#641-data-model), they are grouped together, so that a user-triggered [close request](#6101-close-requests) will close all of the close watchers in a group. This ensures that web developers can't intercept an unlimited number of close requests by creating close watchers; instead they can create a number equal to at most 1 + the number of times the [user activates the page](#64-tracking-user-activation).

The [next user interaction allows a new group](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) boolean encourages web developers to create [close watchers](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) in a way that is tied to individual [user activations](#64-tracking-user-activation). Without it, each user activation would increase the [allowed number of groups](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure), even if the web developer isn't "using" those user activations to create close watchers. In short:
- Allowed: user interaction; create a close watcher in its own group; user interaction; create a close watcher in a second independent group.
- Disallowed: user interaction; user interaction; create a close watcher in its own group; create a close watcher in a second independent group.
- Allowed: user interaction; user interaction; create a close watcher in its own group; create a close watcher grouped with the previous one.

This protection is *not* important for upholding our desired invariant of creating at most (1 + the number of times the [user activates the page](#64-tracking-user-activation)) groups. A determined abuser will just create one close watcher per user interaction, "banking" them for future abuse. But this system causes more predictable behavior for the normal case, and encourages non-abusive developers to create close watchers directly in response to user interactions.

To notify the close watcher manager about user activation given a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) window:
1. Let manager be window's [close watcher manager](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure).
2. If manager's [next user interaction allows a new group](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) is true, then increment manager's [allowed number of groups](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure).
3. Set manager's [next user interaction allows a new group](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) to false.

---

A close watcher is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) with the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):
- A window, a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object).
- A cancel action, an algorithm accepting a boolean argument and returning a boolean. The argument indicates whether or not the cancel action algorithm can prevent the close request from proceeding via the algorithm's return value. If the boolean argument is true, then the algorithm can return either true to indicate that the caller will proceed to the [close action](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure), or false to indicate that the caller will bail out. If the argument is false, then the return value is always false. This algorithm can never throw an exception.
- A close action, an algorithm accepting no arguments and returning nothing. This algorithm can never throw an exception.
- An is running cancel action boolean.
- A get enabled state, an algorithm accepting no arguments and returning a boolean. This algorithm can never throw an exception.

A [close watcher](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) closeWatcher is active if closeWatcher's [window](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure)'s [close watcher manager](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) any list which [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) closeWatcher.

---

To establish a close watcher given a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) window, a list of steps cancelAction, a list of steps closeAction, and an algorithm that returns a boolean getEnabledState:
1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): window's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object) is [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents).
2. Let closeWatcher be a new [close watcher](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure), with

   [window](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure)

   window

   [cancel action](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure)

   cancelAction

   [close action](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure)

   closeAction

   [is running cancel action](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure)

   false

   [get enabled state](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure)

   getEnabledState

3. Let manager be window's [close watcher manager](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure).
4. If manager's [groups](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure)'s [size](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) is less than manager's [allowed number of groups](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure), then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) « closeWatcher » to manager's [groups](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure).
5. Otherwise:
   1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): manager's [groups](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure)'s [size](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) is at least 1 in this branch, since manager's [allowed number of groups](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) is always at least 1.
   2. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) closeWatcher to manager's [groups](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure)'s last [item](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).
6. Set manager's [next user interaction allows a new group](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) to true.
7. Return closeWatcher.

To request to close a [close watcher](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) closeWatcher with boolean requireHistoryActionActivation:
1. If closeWatcher [is not active](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure), then return true.
2. If the result of running closeWatcher's [get enabled state](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) is false, then return true.
3. If closeWatcher's [is running cancel action](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) is true, then return true.
4. Let window be closeWatcher's [window](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure).
5. If window's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object) is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents), then return true.
6. Let canPreventClose be true if requireHistoryActionActivation is false, or if window's [close watcher manager](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure)'s [groups](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure)'s [size](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) is less than window's [close watcher manager](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure)'s [allowed number of groups](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure), and window has [history-action activation](#641-data-model); otherwise false.
7. Set closeWatcher's [is running cancel action](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) to true.
8. Let shouldContinue be the result of running closeWatcher's [cancel action](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) given canPreventClose.
9. Set closeWatcher's [is running cancel action](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) to false.
10. If shouldContinue is false:
    1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): canPreventClose is true.
    2. [Consume history-action user activation](#642-processing-model) given window.
    3. Return false.

    > [!note]
    > Note that since these substeps [consume history-action user activation](#642-processing-model), [requesting to close](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) a [close watcher](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) twice without any intervening [user activation](#64-tracking-user-activation) will result in canPreventClose being false the second time.

11. [Close](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) closeWatcher.
12. Return true.

To close a [close watcher](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) closeWatcher:
1. If closeWatcher [is not active](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure), then return.
2. If the result of running closeWatcher's [get enabled state](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) is false, then return.
3. If closeWatcher's [window](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object) is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents), then return.
4. [Destroy](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) closeWatcher.
5. Run closeWatcher's [close action](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure).

To destroy a [close watcher](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) closeWatcher:
1. Let manager be closeWatcher's [window](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure)'s [close watcher manager](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure).
2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) group of manager's [groups](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure): [remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) closeWatcher from group.
3. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) any item from manager's [groups](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) that [is empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).

---

To process close watchers given a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) window:
1. Let processedACloseWatcher be false.
2. If window's [close watcher manager](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure)'s [groups](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) is not empty:
   1. Let group be the last [item](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) in window's [close watcher manager](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure)'s [groups](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure).
   2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) closeWatcher of group, in reverse order:
      1. If the result of running closeWatcher's [get enabled state](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) is true, set processedACloseWatcher to true.
      2. Let shouldProceed be the result of [requesting to close](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) closeWatcher with true.
      3. If shouldProceed is false, then [break](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
3. If window's [close watcher manager](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure)'s [allowed number of groups](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) is greater than 1, decrement it by 1.
4. Return processedACloseWatcher.

#### 6.10.3 The [`CloseWatcher`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) interface

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface CloseWatcher : EventTarget {
  constructor(optional CloseWatcherOptions options = {});

  undefined requestClose();
  undefined close();
  undefined destroy();

  attribute EventHandler oncancel;
  attribute EventHandler onclose;
};

dictionary CloseWatcherOptions {
  AbortSignal signal;
};
```

`watcher = new CloseWatcher()`

`watcher = new CloseWatcher({ signal })`

Creates a new [`CloseWatcher`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) instance.

If the [`signal`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) option is provided, then watcher can be destroyed (as if by [`watcher.destroy()`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface)) by aborting the given [`AbortSignal`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#32-interface-abortsignal).

If any [close watcher](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) is already active, and the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) does not have [history-action activation](#641-data-model), then the resulting [`CloseWatcher`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) will be closed together with that already-active [close watcher](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) in response to any [close request](#6101-close-requests). (This already-active [close watcher](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) does not necessarily have to be a [`CloseWatcher`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) object; it could be a modal [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) element, or a popover generated by an element with the [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute.)

`watcher.requestClose()`

Acts as if a [close request](#6101-close-requests) was sent targeting watcher, by first firing a [`cancel`](#events) event, and if that event is not canceled with [`preventDefault()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event), proceeding to fire a [`close`](#events) event before deactivating the close watcher as if [`watcher.destroy()`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) was called.

This is a helper utility that can be used to consolidate cancelation and closing logic into the [`cancel`](#events) and [`close`](#events) event handlers, by having all non-[close request](#6101-close-requests) closing affordances call this method.

`watcher.close()`

Immediately fires the [`close`](#events) event, and then deactivates the close watcher as if [`watcher.destroy()`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) was called.

This is a helper utility that can be used trigger the closing logic into the [`close`](#events) event handler, skipping any logic in the [`cancel`](#events) event handler.

`watcher.destroy()`

Deactivates watcher, so that it will no longer receive [`close`](#events) events and so that new independent [`CloseWatcher`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) instances can be constructed.

This is intended to be called if the relevant UI element is torn down in some other way than being closed.

Each [`CloseWatcher`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) instance has an internal close watcher, which is a [close watcher](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure).

The `new CloseWatcher(options)` constructor steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object) is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents), then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Let closeWatcher be the result of [establishing a close watcher](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant), with:
   - *[cancelAction](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure)* given canPreventClose being to return the result of [firing an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`cancel`](#events) at [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), with the [`cancelable`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to canPreventClose.
   - *[closeAction](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure)* being to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`close`](#events) at [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
   - *[getEnabledState](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure)* being to return true.
3. If options\["[`signal`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface)"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps):
   1. If options\["[`signal`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface)"\] is [aborted](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#32-interface-abortsignal), then [destroy](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) closeWatcher.
   2. [Add](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#32-interface-abortsignal) the following steps to options\["[`signal`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface)"\]:
      1. [Destroy](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) closeWatcher.
4. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [internal close watcher](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) to closeWatcher.

The `requestClose()` method steps are to [request to close](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [internal close watcher](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) with false.

The `close()` method steps are to [close](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [internal close watcher](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface).

The `destroy()` method steps are to [destroy](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [internal close watcher](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface).

The following are the [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers) (and their corresponding [event handler event types](#8181-event-handlers)) that must be supported, as [event handler IDL attributes](#8181-event-handlers), by all objects implementing the [`CloseWatcher`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) interface:

| [Event handler](#8181-event-handlers) | [Event handler event type](#8181-event-handlers) |
| --- | --- |
| `oncancel` | [`cancel`](#events) |
| `onclose` | [`close`](#events) |

> [!example]
> If one wanted to implement a custom picker control, which closed itself on a user-provided [close request](#6101-close-requests) as well as when a close button is pressed, the following code shows how one would use the [`CloseWatcher`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) API to process close requests:
> 
> ```javascript
> const watcher = new CloseWatcher();
> const picker = setUpAndShowPickerDOMElement();
> 
> let chosenValue = null;
> 
> watcher.onclose = () => {
>   chosenValue = picker.querySelector('input').value;
>   picker.remove();
> };
> 
> picker.querySelector('.close-button').onclick = () => watcher.requestClose();
> ```
> 
> Note how the logic to gather the chosen value is centralized in the [`CloseWatcher`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) object's [`close`](#events) event handler, with the [`click`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click) event handler for the close button delegating to that logic by calling [`requestClose()`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface).

> [!example]
> The [`cancel`](#events) event on [`CloseWatcher`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) objects can be used to prevent the [`close`](#events) event from firing, and the [`CloseWatcher`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) from being destroying. A typical use case is as follows:
> 
> ```javascript
> watcher.oncancel = async (e) => {
>   if (hasUnsavedData && e.cancelable) {
>     e.preventDefault();
> 
>     const userReallyWantsToClose = await askForConfirmation("Are you sure you want to close?");
>     if (userReallyWantsToClose) {
>       hasUnsavedData = false;
>       watcher.close();
>     }
>   }
> };
> ```
> 
> For abuse prevention purposes, this event is only [`cancelable`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) if the page has [history-action activation](#641-data-model), which will be lost after any given [close request](#6101-close-requests). This ensures that if the user sends a close request twice in a row without any intervening user activation, the request definitely succeeds; the second request ignores any [`cancel`](#events) event handler's attempt to call [`preventDefault()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) and proceeds to close the [`CloseWatcher`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface).

Combined, the above two examples show how [`requestClose()`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) and [`close()`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) differ. Because we used [`requestClose()`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) in the [`click`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click) event handler for the close button, clicking that button will trigger the [`CloseWatcher`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface)'s [`cancel`](#events) event, and thus potentially ask the user for confirmation if there is unsaved data. If we had used [`close()`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface), then this check would be skipped. Sometimes that is appropriate, but usually [`requestClose()`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) is the better option for user-triggered close requests.

> [!example]
> In addition to the [user activation](#64-tracking-user-activation) restrictions for [`cancel`](#events) events, there is a more subtle form of user activation gating for [`CloseWatcher`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) construction. If one creates more than one [`CloseWatcher`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) without user activation, then the newly-created one will get grouped together with the most-recently-created [close watcher](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure), so that a single [close request](#6101-close-requests) will close them both:
> 
> ```javascript
> window.onload = () => {
>   // This will work as normal: it is the first close watcher created without user activation.
>   (new CloseWatcher()).onclose = () => { /* ... */ };
> };
> 
> button1.onclick = () => {
>   // This will work as normal: the button click counts as user activation.
>   (new CloseWatcher()).onclose = () => { /* ... */ };
> };
> 
> button2.onclick = () => {
>   // These will be grouped together, and both will close in response to a single close request.
>   (new CloseWatcher()).onclose = () => { /* ... */ };
>   (new CloseWatcher()).onclose = () => { /* ... */ };
> };
> ```
> 
> This means that calling [`destroy()`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface), [`close()`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface), or [`requestClose()`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) properly is important. Doing so is the only way to get back the "free" ungrouped close watcher slot. Such close watchers created without user activation are useful for cases like session inactivity timeout dialogs or urgent notifications of server-triggered events, which are not generated in response to user activation.

### 6.11 Drag and drop

This section defines an event-based drag-and-drop mechanism.

This specification does not define exactly what a *drag-and-drop operation* actually is.

On a visual medium with a pointing device, a drag operation could be the default action of a [`mousedown`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#mousedown) event that is followed by a series of [`mousemove`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#mousemove) events, and the drop could be triggered by the mouse being released.

When using an input modality other than a pointing device, users would probably have to explicitly indicate their intention to perform a drag-and-drop operation, stating what they wish to drag and where they wish to drop it, respectively.

However it is implemented, drag-and-drop operations must have a starting point (e.g. where the mouse was clicked, or the start of the selection or element that was selected for the drag), may have any number of intermediate steps (elements that the mouse moves over during a drag, or elements that the user picks as possible drop points as they cycle through possibilities), and must either have an end point (the element above which the mouse button was released, or the element that was finally selected), or be canceled. The end point must be the last element selected as a possible drop point before the drop occurs (so if the operation is not canceled, there must be at least one element in the middle step).

#### 6.11.1 Introduction

*This section is non-normative.*

To make an element draggable, give the element a [`draggable`](#6117-the-draggable-attribute) attribute, and set an event listener for [`dragstart`](#6116-events-summary) that stores the data being dragged.

The event handler typically needs to check that it's not a text selection that is being dragged, and then needs to store data into the [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object and set the allowed effects (copy, move, link, or some combination).

For example:

```html
<p>What fruits do you like?</p>
<ol ondragstart="dragStartHandler(event)">
 <li draggable="true" data-value="fruit-apple">Apples</li>
 <li draggable="true" data-value="fruit-orange">Oranges</li>
 <li draggable="true" data-value="fruit-pear">Pears</li>
</ol>
<script>
  var internalDNDType = 'text/x-example'; // set this to something specific to your site
  function dragStartHandler(event) {
    if (event.target instanceof HTMLLIElement) {
      // use the element's data-value="" attribute as the value to be moving:
      event.dataTransfer.setData(internalDNDType, event.target.dataset.value);
      event.dataTransfer.effectAllowed = 'move'; // only allow moves
    } else {
      event.preventDefault(); // don't allow selection to be dragged
    }
  }
</script>
```

---

To accept a drop, the drop target has to listen to the following events:
1. The [`dragenter`](#6116-events-summary) event handler reports whether or not the drop target is potentially willing to accept the drop, by canceling the event.
2. The [`dragover`](#6116-events-summary) event handler specifies what feedback will be shown to the user, by setting the [`dropEffect`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) attribute of the [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) associated with the event. This event also needs to be canceled.
3. The [`drop`](#6116-events-summary) event handler has a final chance to accept or reject the drop. If the drop is accepted, the event handler must perform the drop operation on the target. This event needs to be canceled, so that the [`dropEffect`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) attribute's value can be used by the source. Otherwise, the drop operation is rejected.

For example:

```html
<p>Drop your favorite fruits below:</p>
<ol ondragenter="dragEnterHandler(event)" ondragover="dragOverHandler(event)"
    ondrop="dropHandler(event)">
</ol>
<script>
  var internalDNDType = 'text/x-example'; // set this to something specific to your site
  function dragEnterHandler(event) {
    var items = event.dataTransfer.items;
    for (var i = 0; i < items.length; ++i) {
      var item = items[i];
      if (item.kind == 'string' && item.type == internalDNDType) {
        event.preventDefault();
        return;
      }
    }
  }
  function dragOverHandler(event) {
    event.dataTransfer.dropEffect = 'move';
    event.preventDefault();
  }
  function dropHandler(event) {
    var li = document.createElement('li');
    var data = event.dataTransfer.getData(internalDNDType);
    if (data == 'fruit-apple') {
      li.textContent = 'Apples';
    } else if (data == 'fruit-orange') {
      li.textContent = 'Oranges';
    } else if (data == 'fruit-pear') {
      li.textContent = 'Pears';
    } else {
      li.textContent = 'Unknown Fruit';
    }
    event.target.appendChild(li);
  }
</script>
```

---

To remove the original element (the one that was dragged) from the display, the [`dragend`](#6116-events-summary) event can be used.

For our example here, that means updating the original markup to handle that event:

```html
<p>What fruits do you like?</p>
<ol ondragstart="dragStartHandler(event)" ondragend="dragEndHandler(event)">
 ...as before...
</ol>
<script>
  function dragStartHandler(event) {
    // ...as before...
  }
  function dragEndHandler(event) {
    if (event.dataTransfer.dropEffect == 'move') {
      // remove the dragged element
      event.target.parentNode.removeChild(event.target);
    }
  }
</script>
```

#### 6.11.2 The drag data store

The data that underlies a drag-and-drop operation, known as the drag data store, consists of the following information:
- A drag data store item list, which is a list of items representing the dragged data, each consisting of the following information:

  The drag data item kind

  The kind of data:

  *Text*

  Text.

  *File*

  Binary data with a filename.

  The drag data item type string

  A Unicode string giving the type or format of the data, generally given by a [MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type). Some values that are not [MIME types](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type) are special-cased for legacy reasons. The API does not enforce the use of [MIME types](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type); other values can be used as well. In all cases, however, the values are all [converted to ASCII lowercase](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) by the API.

  There is a limit of one *text* item per [item type string](#6112-the-drag-data-store).

  The actual data

  A Unicode or binary string, in some cases with a filename (itself a Unicode string), as per [the drag data item kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store).

  The [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is ordered in the order that the items were added to the list; most recently added last.

- The following information, used to generate the UI feedback during the drag:
  - User-agent-defined default feedback information, known as the drag data store default feedback.
  - Optionally, a bitmap image and the coordinate of a point within that image, known as the drag data store bitmap and drag data store hot spot coordinate.
- A drag data store mode, which is one of the following:

  Read/write mode

  For the [`dragstart`](#6116-events-summary) event. New data can be added to the [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store).

  Read-only mode

  For the [`drop`](#6116-events-summary) event. The list of items representing dragged data can be read, including the data. No new data can be added.

  Protected mode

  For all other events. The formats and kinds in the [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store) list of items representing dragged data can be enumerated, but the data itself is unavailable and no new data can be added.

- A drag data store allowed effects state, which is a string.

When a [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is created, it must be initialized such that its [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is empty, it has no [drag data store default feedback](#6112-the-drag-data-store), it has no [drag data store bitmap](#6112-the-drag-data-store) and [drag data store hot spot coordinate](#6112-the-drag-data-store), its [drag data store mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is [protected mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store), and its [drag data store allowed effects state](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is the string "[`uninitialized`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)".

#### 6.11.3 The [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) interface

[`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) objects are used to expose the [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store) that underlies a drag-and-drop operation.

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface DataTransfer {
  constructor();

  attribute DOMString dropEffect;
  attribute DOMString effectAllowed;

  [SameObject] readonly attribute DataTransferItemList items;

  undefined setDragImage(Element image, long x, long y);

  /* old interface */
  readonly attribute FrozenArray<DOMString> types;
  DOMString getData(DOMString format);
  undefined setData(DOMString format, DOMString data);
  undefined clearData(optional DOMString format);
  [SameObject] readonly attribute FileList files;
};
```

`dataTransfer = new DataTransfer()`

Creates a new [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object with an empty [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store).

`dataTransfer.dropEffect [ = value ]`

Returns the kind of operation that is currently selected. If the kind of operation isn't one of those that is allowed by the [`effectAllowed`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) attribute, then the operation will fail.

Can be set, to change the selected operation.

The possible values are "[`none`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", "[`copy`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", "[`link`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", and "[`move`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)".

`dataTransfer.effectAllowed [ = value ]`

Returns the kinds of operations that are to be allowed.

Can be set (during the [`dragstart`](#6116-events-summary) event), to change the allowed operations.

The possible values are "[`none`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", "[`copy`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", "[`copyLink`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", "[`copyMove`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", "[`link`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", "[`linkMove`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", "[`move`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", "[`all`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", and "[`uninitialized`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)",

`dataTransfer.items`

Returns a [`DataTransferItemList`](#61131-the-datatransferitemlist-interface) object, with the drag data.

`dataTransfer.setDragImage(element, x, y)`

Uses the given element to update the drag feedback, replacing any previously specified feedback.

`dataTransfer.types`

Returns a [frozen array](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-frozen-array-type) listing the formats that were set in the [`dragstart`](#6116-events-summary) event. In addition, if any files are being dragged, then one of the types will be the string "`Files`".

`data = dataTransfer.getData(format)`

Returns the specified data. If there is no such data, returns the empty string.

`dataTransfer.setData(format, data)`

Adds the specified data.

`dataTransfer.clearData([ format ])`

Removes the data of the specified formats. Removes all data if the argument is omitted.

`dataTransfer.files`

Returns a [`FileList`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#filelist-section) of the files being dragged, if any.

[`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) objects that are created as part of [drag-and-drop events](#6116-events-summary) are only valid while those events are being fired.

A [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object is associated with a [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store) while it is valid.

A [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object has an associated types array, which is a [`FrozenArray<DOMString>`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-frozen-array-type), initially empty. When the contents of the [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object's [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store) change, or when the [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object becomes no longer associated with a [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store), run the following steps:
1. Let L be an empty sequence.
2. If the [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object is still associated with a [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store):
   1. For each item in the [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object's [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store) whose [kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is *text*, add an entry to L consisting of the item's [type string](#6112-the-drag-data-store).
   2. If there are any items in the [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object's [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store) whose [kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is *File*, then add an entry to L consisting of the string "`Files`". (This value can be distinguished from the other values because it is not lowercase.)
3. Set the [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object's [types array](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) to the result of [creating a frozen array](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-create-frozen-array) from L.

The `DataTransfer()` constructor, when invoked, must return a newly created [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object initialized as follows:
1. Set the [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store)'s [item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store) to be an empty list.
2. Set the [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store)'s [mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store) to [read/write mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store).
3. Set the [`dropEffect`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) and [`effectAllowed`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) to "none".

The `dropEffect` attribute controls the drag-and-drop feedback that the user is given during a drag-and-drop operation. When the [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object is created, the [`dropEffect`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) attribute is set to a string value. On getting, it must return its current value. On setting, if the new value is one of "`none`", "`copy`", "`link`", or "`move`", then the attribute's current value must be set to the new value. Other values must be ignored.

The `effectAllowed` attribute is used in the drag-and-drop processing model to initialize the [`dropEffect`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) attribute during the [`dragenter`](#6116-events-summary) and [`dragover`](#6116-events-summary) events. When the [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object is created, the [`effectAllowed`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) attribute is set to a string value. On getting, it must return its current value. On setting, if the [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store)'s [mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is the [read/write mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store) and the new value is one of "`none`", "`copy`", "`copyLink`", "`copyMove`", "`link`", "`linkMove`", "`move`", "`all`", or "`uninitialized`", then the attribute's current value must be set to the new value. Otherwise, it must be left unchanged.

The `items` attribute must return a [`DataTransferItemList`](#61131-the-datatransferitemlist-interface) object associated with the [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object.

The `setDragImage(image, x,
  y)` method must run the following steps:
1. If the [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object is no longer associated with a [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store), return. Nothing happens.
2. If the [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store)'s [mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is not the [read/write mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store), return. Nothing happens.
3. If image is an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element, then set the [drag data store bitmap](#6112-the-drag-data-store) to the element's image (at its [natural size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions)); otherwise, set the [drag data store bitmap](#6112-the-drag-data-store) to an image generated from the given element (the exact mechanism for doing so is not currently specified).
4. Set the [drag data store hot spot coordinate](#6112-the-drag-data-store) to the given x, y coordinate.

The `types` attribute must return this [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object's [types array](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface).

The `getData(format)` method must run the following steps:
1. If the [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object is no longer associated with a [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store), then return the empty string.
2. If the [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store)'s [mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is the [protected mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store), then return the empty string.
3. Let format be the first argument, [converted to ASCII lowercase](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).
4. Let convert-to-URL be false.
5. If format equals "`text`", change it to "`text/plain`".
6. If format equals "`url`", change it to "`text/uri-list`" and set convert-to-URL to true.
7. If there is no item in the [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store) whose [kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is *text* and whose [type string](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is equal to format, return the empty string.
8. Let result be the data of the item in the [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store) whose [kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is *Plain Unicode string* and whose [type string](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is equal to format.
9. If convert-to-URL is true, then parse result as appropriate for `text/uri-list` data, and then set result to the first URL from the list, if any, or the empty string otherwise. [\[RFC2483\]](#references)
10. Return result.

The `setData(format, data)` method must run the following steps:
1. If the [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object is no longer associated with a [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store), return. Nothing happens.
2. If the [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store)'s [mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is not the [read/write mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store), return. Nothing happens.
3. Let format be the first argument, [converted to ASCII lowercase](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).
4. If format equals "`text`", change it to "`text/plain`".

   If format equals "`url`", change it to "`text/uri-list`".

5. Remove the item in the [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store) whose [kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is *text* and whose [type string](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is equal to format, if there is one.
6. Add an item to the [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store) whose [kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is *text*, whose [type string](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is equal to format, and whose data is the string given by the method's second argument.

The `clearData(format)` method must run the following steps:
1. If the [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object is no longer associated with a [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store), return. Nothing happens.
2. If the [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store)'s [mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is not the [read/write mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store), return. Nothing happens.
3. If the method was called with no arguments, remove each item in the [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store) whose [kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is *Plain Unicode string*, and return.
4. Set format to format, [converted to ASCII lowercase](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).
5. If format equals "`text`", change it to "`text/plain`".

   If format equals "`url`", change it to "`text/uri-list`".

6. Remove the item in the [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store) whose [kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is *text* and whose [type string](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is equal to format, if there is one.

> [!note]
> The [`clearData()`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) method does not affect whether any files were included in the drag, so the [`types`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) attribute's list might still not be empty after calling [`clearData()`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) (it would still contain the "`Files`" string if any files were included in the drag).

The `files` attribute must return a [live](#215-scripting) [`FileList`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#filelist-section) sequence consisting of [`File`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file) objects representing the files found by the following steps. Furthermore, for a given [`FileList`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#filelist-section) object and a given underlying file, the same [`File`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file) object must be used each time.
1. Start with an empty list L.
2. If the [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object is no longer associated with a [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store), the [`FileList`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#filelist-section) is empty. Return the empty list L.
3. If the [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store)'s [mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is the [protected mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store), return the empty list L.
4. For each item in the [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store) whose [kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is *File*, add the item's data (the file, in particular its name and contents, as well as its [type](#6112-the-drag-data-store)) to the list L.
5. The files found by these steps are those in the list L.

> [!note]
> This version of the API does not expose the types of the files during the drag.

##### 6.11.3.1 The [`DataTransferItemList`](#61131-the-datatransferitemlist-interface) interface

Each [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object is associated with a [`DataTransferItemList`](#61131-the-datatransferitemlist-interface) object.

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface DataTransferItemList {
  readonly attribute unsigned long length;
  getter DataTransferItem (unsigned long index);
  DataTransferItem? add(DOMString data, DOMString type);
  DataTransferItem? add(File data);
  undefined remove(unsigned long index);
  undefined clear();
};
```

`items.length`

Returns the number of items in the [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store).

`items[index]`

Returns the [`DataTransferItem`](#61132-the-datatransferitem-interface) object representing the indexth entry in the [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store).

`items.remove(index)`

Removes the indexth entry in the [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store).

`items.clear()`

Removes all the entries in the [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store).

`items.add(data)`

`items.add(data, type)`

Adds a new entry for the given data to the [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store). If the data is plain text then a type string has to be provided also.

While the [`DataTransferItemList`](#61131-the-datatransferitemlist-interface) object's [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object is associated with a [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store), the [`DataTransferItemList`](#61131-the-datatransferitemlist-interface) object's *mode* is the same as the [drag data store mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store). When the [`DataTransferItemList`](#61131-the-datatransferitemlist-interface) object's [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object is *not* associated with a [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store), the [`DataTransferItemList`](#61131-the-datatransferitemlist-interface) object's *mode* is the *disabled mode*. The [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store) referenced in this section (which is used only when the [`DataTransferItemList`](#61131-the-datatransferitemlist-interface) object is not in the *disabled mode*) is the [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store) with which the [`DataTransferItemList`](#61131-the-datatransferitemlist-interface) object's [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object is associated.

The `length` attribute must return zero if the object is in the *disabled mode*; otherwise it must return the number of items in the [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store).

When a [`DataTransferItemList`](#61131-the-datatransferitemlist-interface) object is not in the *disabled mode*, its [supported property indices](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-supported-property-indices) are the [indices](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of the [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store).

To [determine the value of an indexed property](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-determine-the-value-of-an-indexed-property) i of a [`DataTransferItemList`](#61131-the-datatransferitemlist-interface) object, the user agent must return a [`DataTransferItem`](#61132-the-datatransferitem-interface) object representing the ith item in the [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store). The same object must be returned each time a particular item is obtained from this [`DataTransferItemList`](#61131-the-datatransferitemlist-interface) object. The [`DataTransferItem`](#61132-the-datatransferitem-interface) object must be associated with the same [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object as the [`DataTransferItemList`](#61131-the-datatransferitemlist-interface) object when it is first created.

The `add()` method must run the following steps:
1. If the [`DataTransferItemList`](#61131-the-datatransferitemlist-interface) object is not in the *[read/write mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store)*, return null.
2. Jump to the appropriate set of steps from the following list:

   If the first argument to the method is a string

   If there is already an item in the [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store) whose [kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is *text* and whose [type string](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is equal to the value of the method's second argument, [converted to ASCII lowercase](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings), then throw a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

   Otherwise, add an item to the [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store) whose [kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is *text*, whose [type string](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is equal to the value of the method's second argument, [converted to ASCII lowercase](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings), and whose data is the string given by the method's first argument.

   If the first argument to the method is a [`File`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file)

   Add an item to the [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store) whose [kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is *File*, whose [type string](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is the [`type`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-type) of the [`File`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file), [converted to ASCII lowercase](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings), and whose data is the same as the [`File`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file)'s data.

3. [Determine the value of the indexed property](#61131-the-datatransferitemlist-interface) corresponding to the newly added item, and return that value (a newly created [`DataTransferItem`](#61132-the-datatransferitem-interface) object).

The `remove(index)` method must run these steps:
1. If the [`DataTransferItemList`](#61131-the-datatransferitemlist-interface) object is not in the *[read/write mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store)*, throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. If the [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store) does not contain an indexth item, then return.
3. Remove the indexth item from the [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store).

The `clear()` method, if the [`DataTransferItemList`](#61131-the-datatransferitemlist-interface) object is in the *[read/write mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store)*, must remove all the items from the [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store). Otherwise, it must do nothing.

##### 6.11.3.2 The [`DataTransferItem`](#61132-the-datatransferitem-interface) interface

Each [`DataTransferItem`](#61132-the-datatransferitem-interface) object is associated with a [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object.

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface DataTransferItem {
  readonly attribute DOMString kind;
  readonly attribute DOMString type;
  undefined getAsString(FunctionStringCallback? _callback);
  File? getAsFile();
};

callback FunctionStringCallback = undefined (DOMString data);
```

`item.kind`

Returns [the drag data item kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store), one of: "string", "file".

`item.type`

Returns [the drag data item type string](#6112-the-drag-data-store).

`item.getAsString(callback)`

Invokes the callback with the string data as the argument, if [the drag data item kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is *text*.

`file = item.getAsFile()`

Returns a [`File`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file) object, if [the drag data item kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is *File*.

While the [`DataTransferItem`](#61132-the-datatransferitem-interface) object's [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object is associated with a [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store) and that [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store)'s [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store) still contains the item that the [`DataTransferItem`](#61132-the-datatransferitem-interface) object represents, the [`DataTransferItem`](#61132-the-datatransferitem-interface) object's *mode* is the same as the [drag data store mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store). When the [`DataTransferItem`](#61132-the-datatransferitem-interface) object's [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object is *not* associated with a [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store), or if the item that the [`DataTransferItem`](#61132-the-datatransferitem-interface) object represents has been removed from the relevant [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store), the [`DataTransferItem`](#61132-the-datatransferitem-interface) object's *mode* is the *disabled mode*. The [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store) referenced in this section (which is used only when the [`DataTransferItem`](#61132-the-datatransferitem-interface) object is not in the *disabled mode*) is the [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store) with which the [`DataTransferItem`](#61132-the-datatransferitem-interface) object's [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object is associated.

The `kind` attribute must return the empty string if the [`DataTransferItem`](#61132-the-datatransferitem-interface) object is in the *disabled mode*; otherwise it must return the string given in the cell from the second column of the following table from the row whose cell in the first column contains [the drag data item kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store) of the item represented by the [`DataTransferItem`](#61132-the-datatransferitem-interface) object:

| Kind | String |
| --- | --- |
| *Text* | "`string`" |
| *File* | "`file`" |

The `type` attribute must return the empty string if the [`DataTransferItem`](#61132-the-datatransferitem-interface) object is in the *disabled mode*; otherwise it must return [the drag data item type string](#6112-the-drag-data-store) of the item represented by the [`DataTransferItem`](#61132-the-datatransferitem-interface) object.

The `getAsString(callback)` method must run the following steps:
1. If the callback is null, return.
2. If the [`DataTransferItem`](#61132-the-datatransferitem-interface) object is not in the *[read/write mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store)* or the *[read-only mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store)*, return. The callback is never invoked.
3. If [the drag data item kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is not *text*, then return. The callback is never invoked.
4. Otherwise, [queue a task](#8172-queuing-tasks) to invoke callback, passing the actual data of the item represented by the [`DataTransferItem`](#61132-the-datatransferitem-interface) object as the argument.

The `getAsFile()` method must run the following steps:
1. If the [`DataTransferItem`](#61132-the-datatransferitem-interface) object is not in the *[read/write mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store)* or the *[read-only mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store)*, then return null.
2. If [the drag data item kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store) is not *File*, then return null.
3. Return a new [`File`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-file) object representing the actual data of the item represented by the [`DataTransferItem`](#61132-the-datatransferitem-interface) object.

#### 6.11.4 The [`DragEvent`](#6114-the-dragevent-interface) interface

The drag-and-drop processing model involves several events. They all use the [`DragEvent`](#6114-the-dragevent-interface) interface.

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface DragEvent : MouseEvent {
  constructor(DOMString type, optional DragEventInit eventInitDict = {});

  readonly attribute DataTransfer? dataTransfer;
};

dictionary DragEventInit : MouseEventInit {
  DataTransfer? dataTransfer = null;
};
```

`event.dataTransfer`

Returns the [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object for the event.

> [!note]
> Although, for consistency with other event interfaces, the [`DragEvent`](#6114-the-dragevent-interface) interface has a constructor, it is not particularly useful. In particular, there's no way to create a useful [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object from script, as [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) objects have a processing and security model that is coordinated by the browser during drag-and-drops.

The `dataTransfer` attribute of the [`DragEvent`](#6114-the-dragevent-interface) interface must return the value it was initialized to. It represents the context information for the event.

When a user agent is required to fire a DND event named e at an element, using a particular [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store), and optionally with a specific related target, the user agent must run the following steps:
1. Let dataDragStoreWasChanged be false.
2. If no specific related target was provided, set related target to null.
3. Let window be the [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) of the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object of the specified target element.
4. If e is [`dragstart`](#6116-events-summary), then set the [drag data store mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store) to the [read/write mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store) and set dataDragStoreWasChanged to true.

   If e is [`drop`](#6116-events-summary), set the [drag data store mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store) to the [read-only mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store).

5. Let dataTransfer be a newly created [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object associated with the given [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store).
6. Set the [`effectAllowed`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) attribute to the [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store)'s [drag data store allowed effects state](#6112-the-drag-data-store).
7. Set the [`dropEffect`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) attribute to "[`none`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" if e is [`dragstart`](#6116-events-summary), [`drag`](#6116-events-summary), or [`dragleave`](#6116-events-summary); to the value corresponding to the [current drag operation](#6115-processing-model) if e is [`drop`](#6116-events-summary) or [`dragend`](#6116-events-summary); and to a value based on the [`effectAllowed`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) attribute's value and the drag-and-drop source, as given by the following table, otherwise (i.e. if e is [`dragenter`](#6116-events-summary) or [`dragover`](#6116-events-summary)):

   | [`effectAllowed`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) | [`dropEffect`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) |
   | --- | --- |
   | "[`none`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" | "[`none`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" |
   | "[`copy`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" | "[`copy`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" |
   | "[`copyLink`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" | "[`copy`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", or, [if appropriate](#6114-the-dragevent-interface), "[`link`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" |
   | "[`copyMove`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" | "[`copy`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", or, [if appropriate](#6114-the-dragevent-interface), "[`move`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" |
   | "[`all`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" | "[`copy`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", or, [if appropriate](#6114-the-dragevent-interface), either "[`link`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" or "[`move`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" |
   | "[`link`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" | "[`link`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" |
   | "[`linkMove`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" | "[`link`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", or, [if appropriate](#6114-the-dragevent-interface), "[`move`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" |
   | "[`move`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" | "[`move`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" |
   | "[`uninitialized`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" when what is being dragged is a selection from a text control | "[`move`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", or, [if appropriate](#6114-the-dragevent-interface), either "[`copy`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" or "[`link`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" |
   | "[`uninitialized`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" when what is being dragged is a selection | "[`copy`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", or, [if appropriate](#6114-the-dragevent-interface), either "[`link`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" or "[`move`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" |
   | "[`uninitialized`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" when what is being dragged is an [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element with an [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute | "[`link`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", or, [if appropriate](#6114-the-dragevent-interface), either "[`copy`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" or "[`move`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" |
   | Any other case | "[`copy`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", or, [if appropriate](#6114-the-dragevent-interface), either "[`link`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" or "[`move`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" |

   Where the table above provides possibly appropriate alternatives, user agents may instead use the listed alternative values if platform conventions dictate that the user has requested those alternate effects.

   > [!example]
   > For example, Windows platform conventions are such that dragging while holding the "alt" key indicates a preference for linking the data, rather than moving or copying it. Therefore, on a Windows system, if "[`link`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" is an option according to the table above while the "alt" key is depressed, the user agent could select that instead of "[`copy`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" or "[`move`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)".

8. Let event be the result of [creating an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#25-constructing-events) using [`DragEvent`](#6114-the-dragevent-interface).
9. Initialize event's [`type`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute to e, its [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute to true, its [`view`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#dom-uievent-view) attribute to window, its [`relatedTarget`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#dom-mouseevent-relatedtarget) attribute to related target, and its [`dataTransfer`](#6114-the-dragevent-interface) attribute to dataTransfer.
10. If e is not [`dragleave`](#6116-events-summary) or [`dragend`](#6116-events-summary), then initialize event's [`cancelable`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute to true.
11. Initialize event's mouse and key attributes according to the state of the input devices as they would be for user interaction events.
