    If there is no relevant pointing device, then initialize event's `screenX`, `screenY`, [`clientX`](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view/#dom-mouseevent-clientx), [`clientY`](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view/#dom-mouseevent-clienty), and `button` attributes to 0.

12. [Dispatch](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#29-dispatching-events) event at the specified target element.
13. Set the [drag data store allowed effects state](#6112-the-drag-data-store) to the current value of dataTransfer's [`effectAllowed`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) attribute. (It can only have changed value if e is [`dragstart`](#6116-events-summary).)
14. If dataDragStoreWasChanged is true, then set the [drag data store mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store) back to the [protected mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store).
15. Break the association between dataTransfer and the [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store).

#### 6.11.5 Processing model

When the user attempts to begin a drag operation, the user agent must run the following steps. User agents must act as if these steps were run even if the drag actually started in another document or application and the user agent was not aware that the drag was occurring until it intersected with a document under the user agent's purview.
1. Determine what is being dragged, as follows:

   If the drag operation was invoked on a selection, then it is the selection that is being dragged.

   Otherwise, if the drag operation was invoked on a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), it is the first element, going up the ancestor chain, starting at the node that the user tried to drag, that has the IDL attribute [`draggable`](#6117-the-draggable-attribute) set to true. If there is no such element, then nothing is being dragged; return, the drag-and-drop operation is never started.

   Otherwise, the drag operation was invoked outside the user agent's purview. What is being dragged is defined by the document or application where the drag was started.

   > [!note]
   > [`img`](#483-the-img-element) elements and [`a`](#451-the-a-element) elements with an [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute have their [`draggable`](#6117-the-draggable-attribute) attribute set to true by default.

2. [Create a drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store). All the DND events fired subsequently by the steps in this section must use this [drag data store](#6112-the-drag-data-store).
3. Establish which DOM node is the source node, as follows:

   If it is a selection that is being dragged, then the [source node](#6115-processing-model) is the [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node that the user started the drag on (typically the [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node that the user originally clicked). If the user did not specify a particular node, for example if the user just told the user agent to begin a drag of "the selection", then the [source node](#6115-processing-model) is the first [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node containing a part of the selection.

   Otherwise, if it is an element that is being dragged, then the [source node](#6115-processing-model) is the element that is being dragged.

   Otherwise, the [source node](#6115-processing-model) is part of another document or application. When this specification requires that an event be dispatched at the [source node](#6115-processing-model) in this case, the user agent must instead follow the platform-specific conventions relevant to that situation.

   > [!note]
   > Multiple events are fired on the [source node](#6115-processing-model) during the course of the drag-and-drop operation.

4. Determine the list of dragged nodes, as follows:

   If it is a selection that is being dragged, then the [list of dragged nodes](#6115-processing-model) contains, in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), every node that is partially or completely included in the selection (including all their ancestors).

   Otherwise, the [list of dragged nodes](#6115-processing-model) contains only the [source node](#6115-processing-model), if any.

5. If it is a selection that is being dragged, then add an item to the [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store), with its properties set as follows:

   [The drag data item type string](#6112-the-drag-data-store)

   "[`text/plain`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.1.3)"

   [The drag data item kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store)

   *Text*

   The actual data

   The text of the selection

   Otherwise, if any files are being dragged, then add one item per file to the [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store), with their properties set as follows:

   [The drag data item type string](#6112-the-drag-data-store)

   The MIME type of the file, if known, or "[`application/octet-stream`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.5.1)" otherwise.

   [The drag data item kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store)

   *File*

   The actual data

   The file's contents and name.

   > [!note]
   > Dragging files can currently only happen from outside a [navigable](#731-navigables), for example from a file system manager application.

   If the drag initiated outside of the application, the user agent must add items to the [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store) as appropriate for the data being dragged, honoring platform conventions where appropriate; however, if the platform conventions do not use [MIME types](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type) to label dragged data, the user agent must make a best-effort attempt to map the types to MIME types, and, in any case, all the [drag data item type strings](#6112-the-drag-data-store) must be [converted to ASCII lowercase](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).

   User agents may also add one or more items representing the selection or dragged element(s) in other forms, e.g. as HTML.

6. If the [list of dragged nodes](#6115-processing-model) is not empty, then [extract the microdata from those nodes into a JSON form](#541-json), and add one item to the [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store), with its properties set as follows:

   [The drag data item type string](#6112-the-drag-data-store)

   [`application/microdata+json`](#175-applicationmicrodatajson)

   [The drag data item kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store)

   *Text*

   The actual data

   The resulting JSON string.

7. Run the following substeps:
   1. Let urls be « ».
   2. For each node in the [list of dragged nodes](#6115-processing-model):

      If the node is an [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element with an [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute

      Add to urls the result of [encoding-parsing-and-serializing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given the element's [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) content attribute's value, relative to the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).

      If the node is an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element with a [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute

      Add to urls the result of [encoding-parsing-and-serializing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given the element's [`src`](#483-the-img-element) content attribute's value, relative to the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).

   3. If urls is still empty, then return.
   4. Let url string be the result of concatenating the strings in urls, in the order they were added, separated by a U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN U+000A LINE FEED character pair (CRLF).
   5. Add one item to the [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store), with its properties set as follows:

      [The drag data item type string](#6112-the-drag-data-store)

      [`text/uri-list`](#mime-types)

      [The drag data item kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store)

      *Text*

      The actual data

      url string

8. Update the [drag data store default feedback](#6112-the-drag-data-store) as appropriate for the user agent (if the user is dragging the selection, then the selection would likely be the basis for this feedback; if the user is dragging an element, then that element's rendering would be used; if the drag began outside the user agent, then the platform conventions for determining the drag feedback should be used).
9. [Fire a DND event](#6114-the-dragevent-interface) named [`dragstart`](#6116-events-summary) at the [source node](#6115-processing-model).

   If the event is canceled, then the drag-and-drop operation should not occur; return.

   > [!note]
   > Since events with no event listeners registered are, almost by definition, never canceled, drag-and-drop is always available to the user if the author does not specifically prevent it.

10. [Fire a pointer event](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#dfn-fire-a-pointer-event) at the [source node](#6115-processing-model) named [`pointercancel`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#the-pointercancel-event), and fire any other follow-up events as required by Pointer Events. [\[POINTEREVENTS\]](#references)
11. [Initiate the drag-and-drop operation](#6115-processing-model) in a manner consistent with platform conventions, and as described below.

    The drag-and-drop feedback must be generated from the first of the following sources that is available:
    1. The [drag data store bitmap](#6112-the-drag-data-store), if any. In this case, the [drag data store hot spot coordinate](#6112-the-drag-data-store) should be used as hints for where to put the cursor relative to the resulting image. The values are expressed as distances in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) from the left side and from the top side of the image respectively. [\[CSS\]](#references)
    2. The [drag data store default feedback](#6112-the-drag-data-store).

From the moment that the user agent is to initiate the drag-and-drop operation, until the end of the drag-and-drop operation, device input events (e.g. mouse and keyboard events) must be suppressed.

During the drag operation, the element directly indicated by the user as the drop target is called the immediate user selection. (Only elements can be selected by the user; other nodes must not be made available as drop targets.) However, the [immediate user selection](#6115-processing-model) is not necessarily the current target element, which is the element currently selected for the drop part of the drag-and-drop operation.

The [immediate user selection](#6115-processing-model) changes as the user selects different elements (either by pointing at them with a pointing device, or by selecting them in some other way). The [current target element](#6115-processing-model) changes when the [immediate user selection](#6115-processing-model) changes, based on the results of event listeners in the document, as described below.

Both the [current target element](#6115-processing-model) and the [immediate user selection](#6115-processing-model) can be null, which means no target element is selected. They can also both be elements in other (DOM-based) documents, or other (non-web) programs altogether. (For example, a user could drag text to a word-processor.) The [current target element](#6115-processing-model) is initially null.

In addition, there is also a current drag operation, which can take on the values "`none`", "`copy`", "`link`", and "`move`". Initially, it has the value "[`none`](#6115-processing-model)". It is updated by the user agent as described in the steps below.

User agents must, as soon as the drag operation is [initiated](#6115-processing-model) and every 350ms (±200ms) thereafter for as long as the drag operation is ongoing, [queue a task](#8172-queuing-tasks) to perform the following steps in sequence:
1. If the user agent is still performing the previous iteration of the sequence (if any) when the next iteration becomes due, return for this iteration (effectively "skipping missed frames" of the drag-and-drop operation).
2. [Fire a DND event](#6114-the-dragevent-interface) named [`drag`](#6116-events-summary) at the [source node](#6115-processing-model). If this event is canceled, the user agent must set the [current drag operation](#6115-processing-model) to "[`none`](#6115-processing-model)" (no drag operation).
3. If the [`drag`](#6116-events-summary) event was not canceled and the user has not ended the drag-and-drop operation, check the state of the drag-and-drop operation, as follows:
   1. If the user is indicating a different [immediate user selection](#6115-processing-model) than during the last iteration (or if this is the first iteration), and if this [immediate user selection](#6115-processing-model) is not the same as the [current target element](#6115-processing-model), then update the [current target element](#6115-processing-model) as follows:

      If the new [immediate user selection](#6115-processing-model) is null

      Set the [current target element](#6115-processing-model) to null also.

      If the new [immediate user selection](#6115-processing-model) is in a non-DOM document or application

      Set the [current target element](#6115-processing-model) to the [immediate user selection](#6115-processing-model).

      Otherwise

      [Fire a DND event](#6114-the-dragevent-interface) named [`dragenter`](#6116-events-summary) at the [immediate user selection](#6115-processing-model).

      If the event is canceled, then set the [current target element](#6115-processing-model) to the [immediate user selection](#6115-processing-model).

      Otherwise, run the appropriate step from the following list:

      If the [immediate user selection](#6115-processing-model) is a text control (e.g., [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element), or an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Text](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch) state) or an [editing host](#684-editing-apis) or [editable](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable) element, and the [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store) has an item with [the drag data item type string](#6112-the-drag-data-store) "[`text/plain`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.1.3)" and [the drag data item kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store) *text*

      Set the [current target element](#6115-processing-model) to the [immediate user selection](#6115-processing-model) anyway.

      If the [immediate user selection](#6115-processing-model) is [the body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors)

      Leave the [current target element](#6115-processing-model) unchanged.

      Otherwise

      [Fire a DND event](#6114-the-dragevent-interface) named [`dragenter`](#6116-events-summary) at [the body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors), if there is one, or at the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object, if not. Then, set the [current target element](#6115-processing-model) to [the body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors), regardless of whether that event was canceled or not.

   2. If the previous step caused the [current target element](#6115-processing-model) to change, and if the previous target element was not null or a part of a non-DOM document, then [fire a DND event](#6114-the-dragevent-interface) named [`dragleave`](#6116-events-summary) at the previous target element, with the new [current target element](#6115-processing-model) as the specific *related target*.
   3. If the [current target element](#6115-processing-model) is a DOM element, then [fire a DND event](#6114-the-dragevent-interface) named [`dragover`](#6116-events-summary) at this [current target element](#6115-processing-model).

      If the [`dragover`](#6116-events-summary) event is not canceled, run the appropriate step from the following list:

      If the [current target element](#6115-processing-model) is a text control (e.g., [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element), or an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Text](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch) state) or an [editing host](#684-editing-apis) or [editable](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable) element, and the [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store) has an item with [the drag data item type string](#6112-the-drag-data-store) "[`text/plain`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.1.3)" and [the drag data item kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store) *text*

      Set the [current drag operation](#6115-processing-model) to either "[`copy`](#6115-processing-model)" or "[`move`](#6115-processing-model)", as appropriate given the platform conventions.

      Otherwise

      Reset the [current drag operation](#6115-processing-model) to "[`none`](#6115-processing-model)".

      Otherwise (if the [`dragover`](#6116-events-summary) event *is* canceled), set the [current drag operation](#6115-processing-model) based on the values of the [`effectAllowed`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) and [`dropEffect`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) attributes of the [`DragEvent`](#6114-the-dragevent-interface) object's [`dataTransfer`](#6114-the-dragevent-interface) object as they stood after the event [dispatch](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#29-dispatching-events) finished, as per the following table:

      | [`effectAllowed`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) | [`dropEffect`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) | Drag operation |
      | --- | --- | --- |
      | "[`uninitialized`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", "[`copy`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", "[`copyLink`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", "[`copyMove`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", or "[`all`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" | "[`copy`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" | "[`copy`](#6115-processing-model)" |
      | "[`uninitialized`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", "[`link`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", "[`copyLink`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", "[`linkMove`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", or "[`all`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" | "[`link`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" | "[`link`](#6115-processing-model)" |
      | "[`uninitialized`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", "[`move`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", "[`copyMove`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", "[`linkMove`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)", or "[`all`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" | "[`move`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" | "[`move`](#6115-processing-model)" |
      | Any other case | "[`none`](#6115-processing-model)" |

   4. Otherwise, if the [current target element](#6115-processing-model) is not a DOM element, use platform-specific mechanisms to determine what drag operation is being performed (none, copy, link, or move), and set the [current drag operation](#6115-processing-model) accordingly.
   5. Update the drag feedback (e.g. the mouse cursor) to match the [current drag operation](#6115-processing-model), as follows:

      | Drag operation | Feedback |
      | --- | --- |
      | "[`copy`](#6115-processing-model)" | Data will be copied if dropped here. |
      | "[`link`](#6115-processing-model)" | Data will be linked if dropped here. |
      | "[`move`](#6115-processing-model)" | Data will be moved if dropped here. |
      | "[`none`](#6115-processing-model)" | No operation allowed, dropping here will cancel the drag-and-drop operation. |

4. Otherwise, if the user ended the drag-and-drop operation (e.g. by releasing the mouse button in a mouse-driven drag-and-drop interface), or if the [`drag`](#6116-events-summary) event was canceled, then this will be the last iteration. Run the following steps, then stop the drag-and-drop operation:
   1. If the [current drag operation](#6115-processing-model) is "[`none`](#6115-processing-model)" (no drag operation), or if the user ended the drag-and-drop operation by canceling it (e.g. by hitting the Escape key), or if the [current target element](#6115-processing-model) is null, then the drag operation failed. Run these substeps:
      1. Let dropped be false.
      2. If the [current target element](#6115-processing-model) is a DOM element, [fire a DND event](#6114-the-dragevent-interface) named [`dragleave`](#6116-events-summary) at it; otherwise, if it is not null, use platform-specific conventions for drag cancelation.
      3. Set the [current drag operation](#6115-processing-model) to "[`none`](#6115-processing-model)".

      Otherwise, the drag operation might be a success; run these substeps:
      1. Let dropped be true.
      2. If the [current target element](#6115-processing-model) is a DOM element, [fire a DND event](#6114-the-dragevent-interface) named [`drop`](#6116-events-summary) at it; otherwise, use platform-specific conventions for indicating a drop.
      3. If the event is canceled, set the [current drag operation](#6115-processing-model) to the value of the [`dropEffect`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) attribute of the [`DragEvent`](#6114-the-dragevent-interface) object's [`dataTransfer`](#6114-the-dragevent-interface) object as it stood after the event [dispatch](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#29-dispatching-events) finished.

         Otherwise, the event is not canceled; perform the event's default action, which depends on the exact target as follows:

         If the [current target element](#6115-processing-model) is a text control (e.g., [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element), or an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Text](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch) state) or an [editing host](#684-editing-apis) or [editable](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable) element, and the [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store) has an item with [the drag data item type string](#6112-the-drag-data-store) "[`text/plain`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.1.3)" and [the drag data item kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store) *text*

         Insert the actual data of the first item in the [drag data store item list](#6112-the-drag-data-store) to have [a drag data item type string](#6112-the-drag-data-store) of "[`text/plain`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.1.3)" and [a drag data item kind](#6112-the-drag-data-store) that is *text* into the text control or [editing host](#684-editing-apis) or [editable](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#editable) element in a manner consistent with platform-specific conventions (e.g. inserting it at the current mouse cursor position, or inserting it at the end of the field).

         Otherwise

         Reset the [current drag operation](#6115-processing-model) to "[`none`](#6115-processing-model)".

   2. [Fire a DND event](#6114-the-dragevent-interface) named [`dragend`](#6116-events-summary) at the [source node](#6115-processing-model).
   3. Run the appropriate steps from the following list as the default action of the [`dragend`](#6116-events-summary) event:

      If dropped is true, the [current target element](#6115-processing-model) is a *text control* (see below), the [current drag operation](#6115-processing-model) is "[`move`](#6115-processing-model)", and the source of the drag-and-drop operation is a selection in the DOM that is entirely contained within an [editing host](#684-editing-apis)

      [Delete the selection](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#delete-the-selection).

      If dropped is true, the [current target element](#6115-processing-model) is a *text control* (see below), the [current drag operation](#6115-processing-model) is "[`move`](#6115-processing-model)", and the source of the drag-and-drop operation is a selection in a text control

      The user agent should delete the dragged selection from the relevant text control.

      If dropped is false or if the [current drag operation](#6115-processing-model) is "[`none`](#6115-processing-model)"

      The drag was canceled. If the platform conventions dictate that this be represented to the user (e.g. by animating the dragged selection going back to the source of the drag-and-drop operation), then do so.

      Otherwise

      The event has no default action.

      For the purposes of this step, a *text control* is a [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element or an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in one of the [Text](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch), [Search](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch), [Tel](#410513-telephone-state-typetel), [URL](#410514-url-state-typeurl), [Email](#410515-email-state-typeemail), [Password](#410516-password-state-typepassword), or [Number](#4105112-number-state-typenumber) states.

> [!note]
> User agents are encouraged to consider how to react to drags near the edge of scrollable regions. For example, if a user drags a link to the bottom of the [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) on a long page, it might make sense to scroll the page so that the user can drop the link lower on the page.

> [!note]
> This model is independent of which [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object the nodes involved are from; the events are fired as described above and the rest of the processing model runs as described above, irrespective of how many documents are involved in the operation.

#### 6.11.6 Events summary

*This section is non-normative.*

The following events are involved in the drag-and-drop model.

| Event name | Target | Cancelable? | [Drag data store mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store) | [`dropEffect`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) | Default Action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dragstart` | [Source node](#6115-processing-model) | ✓ Cancelable | [Read/write mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store) | "[`none`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" | Initiate the drag-and-drop operation |
| `drag` | [Source node](#6115-processing-model) | ✓ Cancelable | [Protected mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store) | "[`none`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" | Continue the drag-and-drop operation |
| `dragenter` | [Immediate user selection](#6115-processing-model) or [the body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors) | ✓ Cancelable | [Protected mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store) | [Based on `effectAllowed` value](#6114-the-dragevent-interface) | Reject [immediate user selection](#6115-processing-model) as potential [target element](#6115-processing-model) |
| `dragleave` | [Previous target element](#6115-processing-model) | — | [Protected mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store) | "[`none`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" | None |
| `dragover` | [Current target element](#6115-processing-model) | ✓ Cancelable | [Protected mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store) | [Based on `effectAllowed` value](#6114-the-dragevent-interface) | Reset the [current drag operation](#6115-processing-model) to "none" |
| `drop` | [Current target element](#6115-processing-model) | ✓ Cancelable | [Read-only mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store) | [Current drag operation](#6115-processing-model) | Varies |
| `dragend` | [Source node](#6115-processing-model) | — | [Protected mode](#6112-the-drag-data-store) | [Current drag operation](#6115-processing-model) | Varies |

All of these events bubble, are composed, and the [`effectAllowed`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) attribute always has the value it had after the [`dragstart`](#6116-events-summary) event, defaulting to "[`uninitialized`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface)" in the [`dragstart`](#6116-events-summary) event.

#### 6.11.7 The [`draggable`](#6117-the-draggable-attribute) attribute

All [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) may have the `draggable` content attribute set. The [`draggable`](#6117-the-draggable-attribute) attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `true` | True | The element will be draggable. |
| `false` | False | The element will not be draggable. |

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the Auto state. The auto state uses the default behavior of the user agent.

An element with a [`draggable`](#6117-the-draggable-attribute) attribute should also have a [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute that names the element for the purpose of non-visual interactions.

`element.draggable [ = value ]`

Returns true if the element is draggable; otherwise, returns false.

Can be set, to override the default and set the [`draggable`](#6117-the-draggable-attribute) content attribute.

The `draggable` IDL attribute, whose value depends on the content attribute's in the way described below, controls whether or not the element is draggable. Generally, only text selections are draggable, but elements whose [`draggable`](#6117-the-draggable-attribute) IDL attribute is true become draggable as well.

If an element's [`draggable`](#6117-the-draggable-attribute) content attribute has the state [True](#6117-the-draggable-attribute), the [`draggable`](#6117-the-draggable-attribute) IDL attribute must return true.

Otherwise, if the element's [`draggable`](#6117-the-draggable-attribute) content attribute has the state [False](#6117-the-draggable-attribute), the [`draggable`](#6117-the-draggable-attribute) IDL attribute must return false.

Otherwise, the element's [`draggable`](#6117-the-draggable-attribute) content attribute has the state [Auto](#6117-the-draggable-attribute). If the element is an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element, an [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element that [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) an image, or an [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element with an [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) content attribute, the [`draggable`](#6117-the-draggable-attribute) IDL attribute must return true; otherwise, the [`draggable`](#6117-the-draggable-attribute) IDL attribute must return false.

If the [`draggable`](#6117-the-draggable-attribute) IDL attribute is set to the value false, the [`draggable`](#6117-the-draggable-attribute) content attribute must be set to the literal value "`false`". If the [`draggable`](#6117-the-draggable-attribute) IDL attribute is set to the value true, the [`draggable`](#6117-the-draggable-attribute) content attribute must be set to the literal value "`true`".

#### 6.11.8 Security risks in the drag-and-drop model

User agents must not make the data added to the [`DataTransfer`](#6113-the-datatransfer-interface) object during the [`dragstart`](#6116-events-summary) event available to scripts until the [`drop`](#6116-events-summary) event, because otherwise, if a user were to drag sensitive information from one document to a second document, crossing a hostile third document in the process, the hostile document could intercept the data.

For the same reason, user agents must consider a drop to be successful only if the user specifically ended the drag operation — if any scripts end the drag operation, it must be considered unsuccessful (canceled) and the [`drop`](#6116-events-summary) event must not be fired.

User agents should take care to not start drag-and-drop operations in response to script actions. For example, in a mouse-and-window environment, if a script moves a window while the user has their mouse button depressed, the UA would not consider that to start a drag. This is important because otherwise UAs could cause data to be dragged from sensitive sources and dropped into hostile documents without the user's consent.

User agents should filter potentially active (scripted) content (e.g. HTML) when it is dragged and when it is dropped, using a safelist of known-safe features. Similarly, [relative URLs](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-relative) should be turned into absolute URLs to avoid references changing in unexpected ways. This specification does not specify how this is performed.

> [!example]
> Consider a hostile page providing some content and getting the user to select and drag and drop (or indeed, copy and paste) that content to a victim page's [`contenteditable`](#681-making-document-regions-editable-the-contenteditable-content-attribute) region. If the browser does not ensure that only safe content is dragged, potentially unsafe content such as scripts and event handlers in the selection, once dropped (or pasted) into the victim site, get the privileges of the victim site. This would thus enable a cross-site scripting attack.

### 6.12 The [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute

All [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) may have the `popover` content attribute set. When specified, the element won't be rendered until it becomes shown, at which point it will be rendered on top of other page content.

> [!example]
> The [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute is a global attribute that allows authors flexibility to ensure popover functionality can be applied to elements with the most relevant semantics.
> 
> The following demonstrates how one might create a popover sub-navigation list of links, within the global navigation for a website.
> 
> ```html
> <ul>
>   <li>
>     <a href=...>All Products</a>
>     <button popovertarget=sub-nav>
>      <img src=down-arrow.png alt="Product pages">
>     </button>
>     <ul popover id=sub-nav>
>      <li><a href=...>Shirts</a>
>      <li><a href=...>Shoes</a>
>      <li><a href=...>Hats etc.</a>
>     </ul>
>   </li>
>   <!-- other list items and links here -->
> </ul>
> ```

When using [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) on elements without accessibility semantics, for instance the [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element, authors should use the appropriate ARIA attributes to ensure the popover is accessible.

> [!example]
> The following shows the baseline markup to create a custom menu popover, where the first menuitem will receive keyboard focus when the popover is invoked due to the use of the `autofocus` attribute. Navigating the menuitems with arrow keys and activation behaviors would still need author scripting. Additional requirements for building custom menus widgets are defined in the [WAI-ARIA specification](https://w3c.github.io/aria/#menu).
> 
> ```html
> <button popovertarget=m>Actions</button>
> <div role=menu id=m popover>
>   <button role=menuitem tabindex=-1 autofocus>Edit</button>
>   <button role=menuitem tabindex=-1>Hide</button>
>   <button role=menuitem tabindex=-1>Delete</button>
> </div>
> ```
> 
> A popover can be useful for rendering a status message, confirming the action performed by the user. The following demonstrates how one could reveal a popover in an [`output`](#41012-the-output-element) element.
> 
> ```html
> <button id=submit>Submit</button>
> <p><output><span popover=manual></span></output></p>
> 
> <script>
>  const sBtn = document.getElementById("submit");
>  const outSpan = document.querySelector("output [popover=manual]");
>  let successMessage;
>  let errorMessage;
> 
>  /* define logic for determining success of action
>   and determining the appropriate success or error
>   messages to use */
> 
>  sBtn.addEventListener("click", ()=> {
>   if ( success ) {
>    outSpan.textContent = successMessage;
>   }
>   else {
>    outSpan.textContent = errorMessage;
>   }
>   outSpan.showPopover();
> 
>   setTimeout(function () {
>    outSpan.hidePopover();
>   }, 10000);
>  });
> </script>
> ```

> [!note]
> Inserting a popover element into an [`output`](#41012-the-output-element) element will generally cause screen readers to announce the content when it becomes visible. Depending on the complexity or frequency of the content, this could be either useful or annoying to users of these assistive technologies. Keep this in mind when using the [`output`](#41012-the-output-element) element or other ARIA live regions to ensure the best user experience.

The [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auto` | Auto | Closes other popovers when opened; has [light dismiss](#6122-popover-light-dismiss) and responds to [close requests](#6101-close-requests). |
| `manual` | Manual | Does not close other popovers; does not [light dismiss](#6122-popover-light-dismiss) or respond to [close requests](#6101-close-requests). |
| `hint` | Hint | Closes other hint popovers when opened, but not other auto popovers; has [light dismiss](#6122-popover-light-dismiss) and responds to [close requests](#6101-close-requests). |

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* is the No Popover state, its *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* is the [Manual](#612-the-popover-attribute) state, and its *[empty value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* is the [Auto](#612-the-popover-attribute) state.

The `popover` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [popover](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

Every [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) has a popover visibility state, initially [hidden](#612-the-popover-attribute), with these potential values:
- hidden
- showing

Every [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a popover pointerdown target, which is an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) or null, initially null.

Every [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) has a popover trigger, which is an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) or null, initially set to null.

Every [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) has a popover hiding, which is a boolean, initially set to false.

Every [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) popover toggle task tracker, which is a [toggle task tracker](#651-the-toggleevent-interface) or null, initially null.

Every [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) has a popover close watcher, which is a [close watcher](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) or null, initially null.

Every [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) has an opened in popover mode, which is "`auto`", "`hint`", or null, initially null.

Every [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a hiding popover nesting count, which is a number, initially 0.

Every [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a showing popover, which is a boolean, initially false.

Every [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a hint stack parent, which is an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) or null, initially null.

> [!note]
> The [hint stack parent](#612-the-popover-attribute) tracks which item in the [showing auto popover list](#612-the-popover-attribute) is the 'parent' of the first item in the [showing hint popover list](#612-the-popover-attribute), or null if the first item in [showing hint popover list](#612-the-popover-attribute) is not 'child' to an item in the [showing auto popover list](#612-the-popover-attribute).
> 
> Therefore, when the [hint stack parent](#612-the-popover-attribute) is not null, it will have an [opened in popover mode](#612-the-popover-attribute) of "`auto`".

The following [attribute change steps](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), given element, localName, oldValue, value, and namespace, are used for all [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility):
1. If namespace is not null, then return.
2. If localName is not [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute), then return.
3. If element's [popover visibility state](#612-the-popover-attribute) is in the [showing state](#612-the-popover-attribute) and oldValue and value are in different [states](#612-the-popover-attribute), then run the [hide popover algorithm](#612-the-popover-attribute) given element, true, true, false, and null.

`element.showPopover()`

Shows the popover element by adding it to the top layer. If element's [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute is in the [Auto](#612-the-popover-attribute) state, then this will also close all other [Auto](#612-the-popover-attribute) popovers unless they are an ancestor of element according to the [topmost popover ancestor](#612-the-popover-attribute) algorithm.

`element.hidePopover()`

Hides the popover element by removing it from the top layer and applying `display: none` to it.

`element.togglePopover()`

If the popover element is not showing, then this method shows it. Otherwise, this method hides it. This method returns true if the popover is open after calling it, otherwise false.

The `showPopover(options)` method steps are:
1. Let source be options\["[`source`](#322-elements-in-the-dom)"\] if it [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps); otherwise, null.
2. Run [show popover](#612-the-popover-attribute) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), true, and source.

To show popover, given an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) element, a boolean throwExceptions, and an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) or null source:
1. Let document be element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
2. If document's [showing popover](#612-the-popover-attribute) is true, or document's [hiding popover nesting count](#612-the-popover-attribute) is not 0:
   1. If throwExceptions is true, then throw a ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
   2. Return.

   > [!note]
   > This prevents showing a popover during the show or hide of another popover.

3. Let validityResult be the result of running [check popover validity](#612-the-popover-attribute) given element, false, and null. If this throws an exception, catch it, and set validityResult to that exception.
4. If validityResult is not true:
   1. If throwExceptions is true and validityResult is a [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException), then throw validityResult.
   2. Return.
5. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): element's [popover trigger](#612-the-popover-attribute) is null.
6. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): element is not in document's [top layer](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position-4/#document-top-layer).
7. Set document's [showing popover](#612-the-popover-attribute) to true.
8. Let cleanupShowingSteps be the following steps:
   1. Set document's [showing popover](#612-the-popover-attribute) to false.
9. If the result of [firing an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`beforetoggle`](#events), using [`ToggleEvent`](#651-the-toggleevent-interface), with the [`cancelable`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true, the [`oldState`](#651-the-toggleevent-interface) attribute initialized to "`closed`", the [`newState`](#651-the-toggleevent-interface) attribute initialized to "`open`", and the [`source`](#651-the-toggleevent-interface) attribute initialized to source at element is false, then run cleanupShowingSteps and return.
10. Set validityResult to the result of running [check popover validity](#612-the-popover-attribute) given element, false, and document. If this throws an exception, catch it, and set validityResult to that exception.

    > [!note]
    > [Check popover validity](#612-the-popover-attribute) is called again because firing the [`beforetoggle`](#events) event could have disconnected this element or changed its [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute.

11. If validityResult is not true:
    1. Run cleanupShowingSteps.
    2. If throwExceptions is true and validityResult is a [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException), then throw validityResult.
    3. Return.
12. Let shouldRestoreFocus be false.
13. Let originalType be the current state of element's [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute.
14. Let effectiveType be originalType.
15. If originalType is [Auto](#612-the-popover-attribute) or [Hint](#612-the-popover-attribute):
    1. Let ancestor be the result of running the [topmost popover ancestor](#612-the-popover-attribute) algorithm given element, source, and true.
    2. If all of the following are true:
       - ancestor is not null;
       - ancestor's [opened in popover mode](#612-the-popover-attribute) is "`hint`"; and
       - effectiveType is the [Auto](#612-the-popover-attribute) state,

       then set effectiveType to the [Hint](#612-the-popover-attribute) state.

       > [!note]
       > [Hint](#612-the-popover-attribute) popovers are lower priority than [Auto](#612-the-popover-attribute) popovers, so an [Auto](#612-the-popover-attribute) popover cannot have a [Hint](#612-the-popover-attribute) popover as a 'parent'. To resolve this case, the effectiveType is 'downgraded' to [Hint](#612-the-popover-attribute).

    3. Run [hide popover stack until](#612-the-popover-attribute) given document, ancestor, [Hint](#612-the-popover-attribute), shouldRestoreFocus, and true.
    4. If effectiveType is the [Auto](#612-the-popover-attribute) state, then run [hide popover stack until](#612-the-popover-attribute) given document, ancestor, [Auto](#612-the-popover-attribute), shouldRestoreFocus, and true.
    5. If originalType is not equal to the value of element's [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute:
       1. Run cleanupShowingSteps.
       2. If throwExceptions is true, then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
       3. Return.
    6. Set validityResult to the result of running [check popover validity](#612-the-popover-attribute) given element, false, and document. If this throws an exception, catch it, and set validityResult to that exception.

       > [!note]
       > [Check popover validity](#612-the-popover-attribute) is called again because running [hide popover stack until](#612-the-popover-attribute) above could have fired the [`beforetoggle`](#events) event, and an event handler could have disconnected this element or changed its [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute.

    7. If validityResult is not true:
       1. Run cleanupShowingSteps.
       2. If throwExceptions is true and validityResult is a [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException), then throw validityResult.
       3. Return.
    8. If the result of running [topmost auto or hint popover](#612-the-popover-attribute) on document is null, then set shouldRestoreFocus to true.

       > [!note]
       > This ensures that focus is returned to the previously-focused element only for the first popover in a stack.

    9. If effectiveType is [Auto](#612-the-popover-attribute):
       1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): document's [showing auto popover list](#612-the-popover-attribute) does not contain element.
       2. Set element's [opened in popover mode](#612-the-popover-attribute) to "`auto`".

       Otherwise:
       1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): effectiveType is [Hint](#612-the-popover-attribute).
       2. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): document's [showing hint popover list](#612-the-popover-attribute) does not contain element.
       3. Set element's [opened in popover mode](#612-the-popover-attribute) to "`hint`".

    10. Set element's [popover close watcher](#612-the-popover-attribute) to the result of [establishing a close watcher](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) given element's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant), with:
        - *[cancelAction](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure)* being to return true.
        - *[closeAction](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure)* being to [hide a popover](#612-the-popover-attribute) given element, true, true, false, and null.
        - *[getEnabledState](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure)* being to return true.

16. Set element's [previously focused element](#4114-the-dialog-element) to null.
17. Let originallyFocusedElement be document's [focused area of the document](#662-data-model)'s [DOM anchor](#662-data-model).
18. [Add an element to the top layer](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position-4/#add-an-element-to-the-top-layer) given element.
19. If effectiveType is [Hint](#612-the-popover-attribute) and ancestor's [opened in popover mode](#612-the-popover-attribute) is "`auto`", then set document's [hint stack parent](#612-the-popover-attribute) to ancestor.
20. Set element's [popover visibility state](#612-the-popover-attribute) to [showing](#612-the-popover-attribute).
21. Set element's [popover trigger](#612-the-popover-attribute) to source.
22. Set element's [implicit anchor element](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-anchor-position/#implicit-anchor-element) to source.
23. Run the [popover focusing steps](#612-the-popover-attribute) given element.
24. If shouldRestoreFocus is true and element's [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute is not in the [No Popover](#612-the-popover-attribute) state, then set element's [previously focused element](#4114-the-dialog-element) to originallyFocusedElement.
25. Run cleanupShowingSteps.
26. [Queue a popover toggle event task](#612-the-popover-attribute) given element, "`closed`", "`open`", and source.

To queue a popover toggle event task given an element element, a string oldState, a string newState, and an [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) or null source:
1. If element's [popover toggle task tracker](#612-the-popover-attribute) is not null:
   1. Set oldState to element's [popover toggle task tracker](#612-the-popover-attribute)'s [old state](#651-the-toggleevent-interface).
   2. Remove element's [popover toggle task tracker](#612-the-popover-attribute)'s [task](#651-the-toggleevent-interface) from its [task queue](#8171-definitions).
   3. Set element's [popover toggle task tracker](#612-the-popover-attribute) to null.
2. [Queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) given the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) and element to run the following steps:
   1. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`toggle`](#events) at element, using [`ToggleEvent`](#651-the-toggleevent-interface), with the [`oldState`](#651-the-toggleevent-interface) attribute initialized to oldState, the [`newState`](#651-the-toggleevent-interface) attribute initialized to newState, and the [`source`](#651-the-toggleevent-interface) attribute initialized to source.
   2. Set element's [popover toggle task tracker](#612-the-popover-attribute) to null.
3. Set element's [popover toggle task tracker](#612-the-popover-attribute) to a struct with [task](#651-the-toggleevent-interface) set to the just-queued [task](#8171-definitions) and [old state](#651-the-toggleevent-interface) set to oldState.

The `hidePopover()` method steps are:
1. Run the [hide popover algorithm](#612-the-popover-attribute) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), true, true, true, and null.

To hide a popover given an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) element, a boolean focusPreviousElement, a boolean fireEvents, a boolean throwExceptions, and an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) or null source:
1. Let validityResult be the result of running [check popover validity](#612-the-popover-attribute) given element, true, and null. If this throws an exception, catch it, and let validityResult be that exception.
2. If validityResult is not true:
   1. If throwExceptions is true and validityResult is a [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException), then throw validityResult.
   2. Return.
3. Let document be element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
4. Let nestedHide be element's [popover hiding](#612-the-popover-attribute).
5. Set element's [popover hiding](#612-the-popover-attribute) to true.
6. If nestedHide is true, then set fireEvents to false.
7. Increment document's [hiding popover nesting count](#612-the-popover-attribute).
8. Let cleanupSteps be the following steps:
   1. If nestedHide is false, then set element's [popover hiding](#612-the-popover-attribute) to false.
   2. Decrement document's [hiding popover nesting count](#612-the-popover-attribute).
9. Let autoPopoverListContainsElement be true if document's [showing auto popover list](#612-the-popover-attribute) [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) element; otherwise false.
10. Let hintPopoverListContainsElement be true if document's [showing hint popover list](#612-the-popover-attribute) [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) element; otherwise false.
11. If element's [opened in popover mode](#612-the-popover-attribute) is "`auto`" or "`hint`":
    1. If hintPopoverListContainsElement is true, then run [hide popover stack until](#612-the-popover-attribute) given document, element, [Hint](#612-the-popover-attribute), focusPreviousElement, and fireEvents.
    2. If element is document's [hint stack parent](#612-the-popover-attribute), then run [hide popover stack until](#612-the-popover-attribute) given document, null, [Hint](#612-the-popover-attribute), focusPreviousElement, and fireEvents.

       > [!note]
       > If the document's [hint stack parent](#612-the-popover-attribute) is being hidden, then *all* hint popovers are hidden.

    3. If autoPopoverListContainsElement is true, then run [hide popover stack until](#612-the-popover-attribute) given document, element, [Auto](#612-the-popover-attribute), focusPreviousElement, and fireEvents.
    4. Set validityResult to the result of running [check popover validity](#612-the-popover-attribute) given element, true, and document. If this throws an exception, catch it, and set validityResult to that exception.

       > [!note]
       > [Check popover validity](#612-the-popover-attribute) is called again because running [hide popover stack until](#612-the-popover-attribute) could have disconnected element or changed its [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute.

    5. If validityResult is not true:
       1. Run cleanupSteps.
       2. If throwExceptions is true and validityResult is a [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException), then throw validityResult.
       3. Return.

12. If fireEvents is true:
    1. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`beforetoggle`](#events), using [`ToggleEvent`](#651-the-toggleevent-interface), with the [`oldState`](#651-the-toggleevent-interface) attribute initialized to "`open`", the [`newState`](#651-the-toggleevent-interface) attribute initialized to "`closed`", and the [`source`](#651-the-toggleevent-interface) attribute set to source at element.
    2. Set validityResult to the result of running [check popover validity](#612-the-popover-attribute) given element, true, and document. If this throws an exception, catch it, and set validityResult to that exception.

       > [!note]
       > [Check popover validity](#612-the-popover-attribute) is called again because firing the [`beforetoggle`](#events) event could have disconnected element or changed its [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute.

    3. If validityResult is not true:
       1. Run cleanupSteps.
       2. If throwExceptions is true and validityResult is a [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException), then throw validityResult.
       3. Return.
    4. [Request an element to be removed from the top layer](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position-4/#request-an-element-to-be-removed-from-the-top-layer) given element.
    5. Set element's [implicit anchor element](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-anchor-position/#implicit-anchor-element) to null.

13. Otherwise, [remove an element from the top layer immediately](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position-4/#remove-an-element-from-the-top-layer-immediately) given element.
14. Set element's [popover trigger](#612-the-popover-attribute) to null.
15. Set element's [opened in popover mode](#612-the-popover-attribute) to null.
16. Set element's [popover visibility state](#612-the-popover-attribute) to [hidden](#612-the-popover-attribute).
17. If element is document's [hint stack parent](#612-the-popover-attribute), or document's [showing hint popover list](#612-the-popover-attribute) is [empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists), then set document's [hint stack parent](#612-the-popover-attribute) to null.
18. If fireEvents is true, then [queue a popover toggle event task](#612-the-popover-attribute) given element, "`open`", "`closed`", and source.
19. Let previouslyFocusedElement be element's [previously focused element](#4114-the-dialog-element).
20. If previouslyFocusedElement is not null:
    1. Set element's [previously focused element](#4114-the-dialog-element) to null.
    2. If focusPreviousElement is true and document's [focused area of the document](#662-data-model)'s [DOM anchor](#662-data-model) is a [shadow-including inclusive descendant](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) of element, then run the [focusing steps](#664-processing-model) for previouslyFocusedElement; the viewport should not be scrolled by doing this step.
21. If element's [popover close watcher](#612-the-popover-attribute) is not null:
    1. [Destroy](#6102-close-watcher-infrastructure) element's [popover close watcher](#612-the-popover-attribute).
    2. Set element's [popover close watcher](#612-the-popover-attribute) to null.
22. Run cleanupSteps.

The `togglePopover(options)` method steps are:
1. Let force be null.
2. If options is a boolean, set force to options.
3. Otherwise, if options\["[`force`](#322-elements-in-the-dom)"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), set force to options\["[`force`](#322-elements-in-the-dom)"\].
4. Let source be options\["[`source`](#322-elements-in-the-dom)"\] if it [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps); otherwise, null.
5. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [popover visibility state](#612-the-popover-attribute) is [showing](#612-the-popover-attribute), and force is null or false, then run the [hide popover algorithm](#612-the-popover-attribute) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), true, true, true, and null.
6. Otherwise, if force is null or true, then run [show popover](#612-the-popover-attribute) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), true, and source.
7. Otherwise:
   1. Let expectedToBeShowing be true if [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [popover visibility state](#612-the-popover-attribute) is [showing](#612-the-popover-attribute); otherwise false.
   2. Run [check popover validity](#612-the-popover-attribute) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), expectedToBeShowing, and null.
8. Return true if [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [popover visibility state](#612-the-popover-attribute) is [showing](#612-the-popover-attribute); otherwise false.

To hide popovers until, given a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document, an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) or null endpoint, a boolean focusPreviousElement, and a boolean fireEvents:
1. Let endpointIsHint be true if document's [showing hint popover list](#612-the-popover-attribute) [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) endpoint; otherwise false.
2. Run [hide popover stack until](#612-the-popover-attribute) given document, endpoint, [Hint](#612-the-popover-attribute), focusPreviousElement, and fireEvents.
3. Let autoEndpoint be endpoint.
4. If endpointIsHint is true, then set autoEndpoint to document's [hint stack parent](#612-the-popover-attribute).

   > [!note]
   > This means, if endpoint is a hint popover, auto popovers are closed, except those that are parent to that hint popover.

5. Run [hide popover stack until](#612-the-popover-attribute) given document, autoEndpoint, [Auto](#612-the-popover-attribute), focusPreviousElement, and fireEvents.

To hide popover stack until, given a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document, an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) or null endpoint, an [Auto](#612-the-popover-attribute) or [Hint](#612-the-popover-attribute) stackType, a boolean focusPreviousElement, and a boolean fireEvents:
1. Let popoverList be document's [showing auto popover list](#612-the-popover-attribute) if stackType is [Auto](#612-the-popover-attribute); otherwise document's [showing hint popover list](#612-the-popover-attribute).
2. Let lastHideIndex be 0 if popoverList does not [contain](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) endpoint; otherwise the index of endpoint in popoverList plus 1.
3. Let toHide be a [slice](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of popoverList [from](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) lastHideIndex, in [reverse](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) order.
4. Let toRemain be a [slice](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of popoverList [from](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) 0 [to](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) lastHideIndex.
5. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) popover of toHide: run the [hide popover algorithm](#612-the-popover-attribute) given popover, focusPreviousElement, fireEvents, false, and null.
6. Let newPopoverList be document's [showing auto popover list](#612-the-popover-attribute) if stackType is [Auto](#612-the-popover-attribute); otherwise document's [showing hint popover list](#612-the-popover-attribute).
7. Let toCheck be newPopoverList in [reverse](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) order.
8. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) popover of toCheck:
   1. If toRemain [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) popover, then continue.
   2. Run the [hide popover algorithm](#612-the-popover-attribute) given popover, focusPreviousElement, false, false, and null.

      > [!note]
      > This happens if popovers are shown whilst hiding popovers. For example, in [`beforetoggle`](#events) events. This is usually a developer error, so user agents are encouraged to show a warning. In this additional hiding phase, fireEvents is ignored, and false is used instead.

> [!note]
> The [hide popover stack until](#612-the-popover-attribute) algorithm is used in several cases to hide all popovers that don't stay open when something happens. For example, during light-dismiss of a popover, this algorithm ensures that we close only the popovers that aren't related to the node clicked by the user.

To find the topmost popover ancestor, given a [`Node`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) newPopoverOrTopLayerElement, an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) or null source, and a boolean isPopover, perform the following steps. They return an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) or null.

> [!note]
> The [topmost popover ancestor](#612-the-popover-attribute) algorithm will return the topmost ancestor popover for the provided popover or top layer element. Popovers can be related to each other in several ways, creating a tree of popovers. There are two paths through which one popover (call it the "child" popover) can have a topmost ancestor popover (call it the "parent" popover):
> 1. The popovers are nested within each other in the node tree. In this case, the descendant popover is the "child" and its topmost ancestor popover is the "parent".
> 2. An element is the 'source' of the popover (e.g., a [`button`](#4106-the-button-element) with [`command`](#4106-the-button-element) in the [Show Popover](#4106-the-button-element) state). In this case, the popover is the "child", and the popover subtree the trigger element is in is the "parent". The trigger element has to be in a popover and reference an open popover.
> 
> In each of the relationships formed above, the parent popover has to be strictly earlier in the [showing auto popover list](#612-the-popover-attribute) or [showing hint popover list](#612-the-popover-attribute) than the child popover, or it does not form a valid ancestral relationship. This eliminates non-showing popovers and self-pointers (e.g., a popover containing an invoking element that points back to the containing popover), and it allows for the construction of a well-formed tree from the (possibly cyclic) graph of connections. Only [Auto](#612-the-popover-attribute) and [Hint](#612-the-popover-attribute) popovers are considered.
> 
> If the provided element is a top layer element such as a [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) which is not showing as a popover, then [topmost popover ancestor](#612-the-popover-attribute) will only look in the node tree to find the first popover.
1. If isPopover is true:
   1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): newPopoverOrTopLayerElement is an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility).
   2. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): newPopoverOrTopLayerElement's [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute is not in the [No Popover State](#612-the-popover-attribute) or the [Manual](#612-the-popover-attribute) state.
   3. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): newPopoverOrTopLayerElement's [popover visibility state](#612-the-popover-attribute) is not in the [popover showing state](#612-the-popover-attribute).
2. Otherwise:
   1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): source is null.
3. Let document be newPopoverOrTopLayerElement's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
4. Let combinedPopovers be document's [showing auto popover list](#612-the-popover-attribute) [extended](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) with document's [showing hint popover list](#612-the-popover-attribute).
5. Let popoverAncestorIndex be the index of the last [item](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) in combinedPopovers of which newPopoverOrTopLayerElement is a [flat tree](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scoping/#flat-tree) [descendant](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), otherwise -1.
6. Let sourceAncestorIndex be -1.
7. If source is not null, then set sourceAncestorIndex to the index of the last [item](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) in combinedPopovers of which source is a [flat tree](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scoping/#flat-tree) [descendant](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), otherwise -1.
8. Let ancestorIndex be the maximum of popoverAncestorIndex and sourceAncestorIndex.
9. If ancestorIndex is -1, then return null.
10. Return combinedPopovers\[ancestorIndex\].

To find the nearest inclusive open popover given a [`Node`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) node, perform the following steps. They return an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) or null.
1. Let currentNode be node.
2. While currentNode is not null:
   1. If currentNode's [opened in popover mode](#612-the-popover-attribute) is "`auto`" or "`hint`", and currentNode's [popover visibility state](#612-the-popover-attribute) is [showing](#612-the-popover-attribute), then return currentNode.
   2. Set currentNode to currentNode's parent in the [flat tree](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-scoping/#flat-tree).
3. Return null.

To find the topmost auto or hint popover given a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document, perform the following steps. They return an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) or null.
1. If document's [showing hint popover list](#612-the-popover-attribute) is not empty, then return document's [showing hint popover list](#612-the-popover-attribute)'s last element.
2. If document's [showing auto popover list](#612-the-popover-attribute) is not empty, then return document's [showing auto popover list](#612-the-popover-attribute)'s last element.
3. Return null.

To perform the popover focusing steps for an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) subject:
1. If the [allow focus steps](#666-focus-management-apis) given subject's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) return false, then return.
2. If subject is a [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) element, then run the [dialog focusing steps](#4114-the-dialog-element) given subject and return.
3. If subject has the [`autofocus`](#667-the-autofocus-attribute) attribute, then let control be subject.
4. Otherwise, let control be the [autofocus delegate](#664-processing-model) for subject given "`other`".
5. If control is null, then return.
6. Run the [focusing steps](#664-processing-model) given control.
7. Let topDocument be control's [node navigable](#731-navigables)'s [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables)'s [active document](#731-navigables).
8. If control's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is not the [same](#711-origins) as the [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) of topDocument, then return.
9. [Empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) topDocument's [autofocus candidates](#667-the-autofocus-attribute).
10. Set topDocument's [autofocus processed flag](#667-the-autofocus-attribute) to true.

To check popover validity for an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) element given a boolean expectedToBeShowing and a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) or null expectedDocument, perform the following steps. They throw an exception or return a boolean.
1. If element's [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute is in the [No Popover](#612-the-popover-attribute) state, then throw a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. If any of the following are true:
   - expectedToBeShowing is true and element's [popover visibility state](#612-the-popover-attribute) is not [showing](#612-the-popover-attribute); or
   - expectedToBeShowing is false and element's [popover visibility state](#612-the-popover-attribute) is not [hidden](#612-the-popover-attribute),

   then return false.

3. If any of the following are true:
   - expectedToBeShowing is false and element is not [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree);

     > [!note]
     > A popover can be [showing](#612-the-popover-attribute) while it is not [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree), as the [removing steps](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) run after the element has been removed from its parent. It can also be [showing](#612-the-popover-attribute) while its [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents), for example if the [navigable](#731-navigables) containing it navigated away. The [hide popover algorithm](#612-the-popover-attribute) needs to succeed in both cases.

   - expectedToBeShowing is false and element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents);
   - expectedDocument is not null and element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) is not expectedDocument;
   - element is a [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) element and its [is modal](#4114-the-dialog-element) is set to true; or
   - element's [fullscreen flag](https://fullscreen.spec.whatwg.org/#fullscreen-flag) is set,

   then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

4. Return true.

To get the showing auto popover list for a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document:
1. Let popovers be « ».
2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) element of document's [top layer](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position-4/#document-top-layer):
   1. If all of the following are true:
      - element is an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility);
      - element's [opened in popover mode](#612-the-popover-attribute) is "`auto`"; and
      - element's [popover visibility state](#612-the-popover-attribute) is [showing](#612-the-popover-attribute),

      then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) element to popovers.

3. Return popovers.

To get the showing hint popover list for a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document:
1. Let popovers be « ».
2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) element of document's [top layer](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position-4/#document-top-layer):
   1. If all of the following are true:
      - element is an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility);
      - element's [opened in popover mode](#612-the-popover-attribute) is "`hint`"; and
      - element's [popover visibility state](#612-the-popover-attribute) is [showing](#612-the-popover-attribute),

      then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) element to popovers.

3. Return popovers.

#### 6.12.1 The popover target attributes

[Buttons](#4102-categories) may have the following content attributes:
- `popovertarget`
- `popovertargetaction`

If specified, the [`popovertarget`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes) attribute value must be the [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) of an element with a [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute in the same [tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) as the [button](#4102-categories) with the [`popovertarget`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes) attribute.

The [`popovertargetaction`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes) attribute is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states:

| Keyword | State | Brief description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `toggle` | Toggle | Shows or hides the targeted popover element. |
| `show` | Show | Shows the targeted popover element. |
| `hide` | Hide | Hides the targeted popover element. |

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the [Toggle](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes) state.

> [!note]
> Whenever possible ensure the popover element is placed immediately after its triggering element in the DOM. Doing so will help ensure that the popover is exposed in a logical programmatic reading order for users of assistive technology, such as screen readers.

> [!example]
> The following shows how the [`popovertarget`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes) attribute in combination with the [`popovertargetaction`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes) attribute can be used to show and close a popover:
> 
> ```html
> <button popovertarget="foo" popovertargetaction="show">
>   Show a popover
> </button>
> 
> <article popover="auto" id="foo">
>   This is a popover article!
>   <button popovertarget="foo" popovertargetaction="hide">Close</button>
> </article>
> ```
> 
> If a [`popovertargetaction`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes) attribute is not specified, the default action will be to toggle the associated popover. The following shows how only specifying the [`popovertarget`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes) attribute on its invoking button can toggle a manual popover between its opened and closed states. A manual popover will not respond to [light dismiss](#6122-popover-light-dismiss) or [close requests](#6101-close-requests):
> 
> ```html
> <input type="button" popovertarget="foo" value="Toggle the popover">
> 
> <div popover=manual id="foo">
>   This is a popover!
> </div>
> ```

[DOM interface](#324-element-definitions):

```webidl
interface mixin PopoverTargetAttributes {
  [CEReactions, Reflect="popovertarget"] attribute Element? popoverTargetElement;
  [CEReactions] attribute DOMString popoverTargetAction;
};
```

The `popoverTargetAction` IDL attribute must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the [`popovertargetaction`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes) attribute, [limited to only known values](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).

To run the popover target attribute activation behavior given a [`Node`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) node and a [`Node`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) eventTarget:
1. Let popover be node's [popover target element](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes).
2. If popover is null, then return.
3. If eventTarget is a [shadow-including inclusive descendant](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) of popover and popover is a [shadow-including descendant](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) of node, then return.
4. If node's [`popovertargetaction`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes) attribute is in the [show](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes) state and popover's [popover visibility state](#612-the-popover-attribute) is [showing](#612-the-popover-attribute), then return.
5. If node's [`popovertargetaction`](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes) attribute is in the [hide](#6121-the-popover-target-attributes) state and popover's [popover visibility state](#612-the-popover-attribute) is [hidden](#612-the-popover-attribute), then return.
6. If popover's [popover visibility state](#612-the-popover-attribute) is [showing](#612-the-popover-attribute), then run the [hide popover algorithm](#612-the-popover-attribute) given popover, true, true, false, and node.
7. Otherwise:
   1. Let validity be the result of running [check popover validity](#612-the-popover-attribute) given popover, false, and null. If this throws an exception, catch it, and let validity be false.
   2. If validity is true, then run [show popover](#612-the-popover-attribute) given popover, false, and node.

To get the popover target element given a [`Node`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) node, perform the following steps. They return an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) or null.
1. If node is not a [button](#4102-categories), then return null.
2. If node is [disabled](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute), then return null.
3. If node has a [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) and node is a [submit button](#4102-categories), then return null.
4. Let popoverElement be the result of running node's [get the `popovertarget`-associated element](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes).
5. If popoverElement is null, then return null.
6. If popoverElement's [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute is in the [No Popover](#612-the-popover-attribute) state, then return null.
7. Return popoverElement.

#### 6.12.2 Popover light dismiss

> [!note]
> "Light dismiss" means that clicking outside of a popover whose [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute is in the [Auto](#612-the-popover-attribute) or [Hint](#612-the-popover-attribute) state will close the popover. This is in addition to how such popovers respond to [close requests](#6101-close-requests).

To light dismiss open popovers, given a [`PointerEvent`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#pointerevent-interface) event:
1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): event's [`isTrusted`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute is true.
2. Let target be event's [target](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event).
3. Let document be target's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
4. If the result of running [topmost auto or hint popover](#612-the-popover-attribute) given document is null, then return.
5. If event's [`type`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) is "[`pointerdown`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#the-pointerdown-event)": set document's [popover pointerdown target](#612-the-popover-attribute) to the result of running [topmost clicked popover](#6122-popover-light-dismiss) given target.
