1. Let serialized be the result of [serializing a response URL for reporting](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#serialize-a-response-url-for-reporting) with response.
2. Let body be a new object containing the following properties:

   | key | value |
   | --- | --- |
   | type | type |
   | blockedURL | serialized |
   | disposition | disposition |

3. [Queue](https://w3c.github.io/reporting/#queue-report) body as the ["`coep`" report type](#714-cross-origin-embedder-policies) for endpoint on settings.

#### 7.1.5 Sandboxing

A sandboxing flag set is a set of zero or more of the following flags, which are used to restrict the abilities that potentially untrusted resources have:

The sandboxed navigation browsing context flag

This flag [prevents content from navigating browsing contexts other than the sandboxed browsing context itself](#7422-beginning-navigation) (or browsing contexts further nested inside it), [auxiliary browsing contexts](#732-browsing-contexts) (which are protected by the [sandboxed auxiliary navigation browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing) defined next), and the [top-level browsing context](#7322-related-browsing-contexts) (which is protected by the [sandboxed top-level navigation without user activation browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing) and [sandboxed top-level navigation with user activation browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing) defined below).

If the [sandboxed auxiliary navigation browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing) is not set, then in certain cases the restrictions nonetheless allow popups (new [top-level browsing contexts](#7322-related-browsing-contexts)) to be opened. These [browsing contexts](#732-browsing-contexts) always have one permitted sandboxed navigator, set when the browsing context is created, which allows the [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) that created them to actually navigate them. (Otherwise, the [sandboxed navigation browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing) would prevent them from being navigated even if they were opened.)

The sandboxed auxiliary navigation browsing context flag

This flag [prevents content from creating new auxiliary browsing contexts](#7317-navigable-target-names), e.g. using the [`target`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute or the [`window.open()`](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows) method.

The sandboxed top-level navigation without user activation browsing context flag

This flag [prevents content from navigating their top-level browsing context](#7422-beginning-navigation) and [prevents content from closing their top-level browsing context](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows). It is consulted only when the sandboxed browsing context's [active window](#732-browsing-contexts) does not have [transient activation](#641-data-model).

When the [sandboxed top-level navigation without user activation browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing) is *not* set, content can navigate its [top-level browsing context](#7322-related-browsing-contexts), but other [browsing contexts](#732-browsing-contexts) are still protected by the [sandboxed navigation browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing) and possibly the [sandboxed auxiliary navigation browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing).

The sandboxed top-level navigation with user activation browsing context flag

This flag [prevents content from navigating their top-level browsing context](#7422-beginning-navigation) and [prevents content from closing their top-level browsing context](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows). It is consulted only when the sandboxed browsing context's [active window](#732-browsing-contexts) has [transient activation](#641-data-model).

As with the [sandboxed top-level navigation without user activation browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing), this flag only affects the [top-level browsing context](#7322-related-browsing-contexts); if it is not set, other [browsing contexts](#732-browsing-contexts) might still be protected by other flags.

The sandboxed origin browsing context flag

This flag [forces content into an opaque origin](#7321-creating-browsing-contexts), thus preventing it from accessing other content from the same [origin](#711-origins).

This flag also [prevents script from reading from or writing to the `document.cookie` IDL attribute](#314-resource-metadata-management), and blocks access to [`localStorage`](#1223-the-localstorage-getter).

The sandboxed forms browsing context flag

This flag [blocks form submission](#410223-form-submission-algorithm).

The sandboxed pointer lock browsing context flag

This flag disables the Pointer Lock API. [\[POINTERLOCK\]](#references)

The sandboxed scripts browsing context flag

This flag [blocks script execution](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting).

The sandboxed automatic features browsing context flag

This flag blocks features that trigger automatically, such as [automatically playing a video](#48117-ready-states) or [automatically focusing a form control](#667-the-autofocus-attribute).

The sandboxed `document.domain` browsing context flag

This flag prevents content from using the [`document.domain`](#7112-relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction) setter.

The sandbox propagates to auxiliary browsing contexts flag

This flag prevents content from escaping the sandbox by ensuring that any [auxiliary browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) it creates inherits the content's [active sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing).

The sandboxed modals flag

This flag prevents content from using any of the following features to produce modal dialogs:
- [`window.alert()`](#891-simple-dialogs)
- [`window.confirm()`](#891-simple-dialogs)
- [`window.print()`](#892-printing)
- [`window.prompt()`](#891-simple-dialogs)
- the [`beforeunload`](#events) event

The sandboxed orientation lock browsing context flag

This flag disables the ability to lock the screen orientation. [\[SCREENORIENTATION\]](#references)

The sandboxed presentation browsing context flag

This flag disables the Presentation API. [\[PRESENTATION\]](#references)

The sandboxed downloads browsing context flag

This flag prevents content from initiating or instantiating downloads, whether through [downloading hyperlinks](#466-downloading-resources) or through [navigation](#745-populating-a-session-history-entry) that gets [handled as a download](#466-downloading-resources).

The sandboxed custom protocols navigation browsing context flag

This flag prevents navigations toward non [fetch schemes](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-scheme) from being [handed off to external software](#74234-non-fetch-schemes-and-external-software).

When the user agent is to parse a sandboxing directive, given a string input and a [sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing) output, it must run the following steps:
1. [Split input on ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings), to obtain tokens.
2. Let output be empty.
3. Add the following flags to output:
   - The [sandboxed navigation browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing).
   - The [sandboxed auxiliary navigation browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing), unless tokens contains the `allow-popups` keyword.
   - The [sandboxed top-level navigation without user activation browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing), unless tokens contains the `allow-top-navigation` keyword.
   - The [sandboxed top-level navigation with user activation browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing), unless tokens contains either the `allow-top-navigation-by-user-activation` keyword or the [`allow-top-navigation`](#715-sandboxing) keyword.

     > [!note]
     > This means that if the [`allow-top-navigation`](#715-sandboxing) is present, the [`allow-top-navigation-by-user-activation`](#715-sandboxing) keyword will have no effect. For this reason, specifying both is a document conformance error.

   - The [sandboxed origin browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing), unless the tokens contains the `allow-same-origin` keyword.

     > [!note]
     > The [`allow-same-origin`](#715-sandboxing) keyword is intended for two cases.
     > 
     > First, it can be used to allow content from the same site to be sandboxed to disable scripting, while still allowing access to the DOM of the sandboxed content.
     > 
     > Second, it can be used to embed content from a third-party site, sandboxed to prevent that site from opening popups, etc, without preventing the embedded page from communicating back to its originating site, using the database APIs to store data, etc.

   - The [sandboxed forms browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing), unless tokens contains the `allow-forms` keyword.
   - The [sandboxed pointer lock browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing), unless tokens contains the `allow-pointer-lock` keyword.
   - The [sandboxed scripts browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing), unless tokens contains the `allow-scripts` keyword.
   - The [sandboxed automatic features browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing), unless tokens contains the [`allow-scripts`](#715-sandboxing) keyword (defined above).

     > [!note]
     > This flag is relaxed by the same keyword as scripts, because when scripts are enabled these features are trivially possible anyway, and it would be unfortunate to force authors to use script to do them when sandboxed rather than allowing them to use the declarative features.

   - The [sandboxed `document.domain` browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing).
   - The [sandbox propagates to auxiliary browsing contexts flag](#715-sandboxing), unless tokens contains the `allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox` keyword.
   - The [sandboxed modals flag](#715-sandboxing), unless tokens contains the `allow-modals` keyword.
   - The [sandboxed orientation lock browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing), unless tokens contains the `allow-orientation-lock` keyword.
   - The [sandboxed presentation browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing), unless tokens contains the `allow-presentation` keyword.
   - The [sandboxed downloads browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing), unless tokens contains the `allow-downloads` keyword.
   - The [sandboxed custom protocols navigation browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing), unless tokens contains either the `allow-top-navigation-to-custom-protocols` keyword, the [`allow-popups`](#715-sandboxing) keyword, or the [`allow-top-navigation`](#715-sandboxing) keyword.

---

Every [top-level browsing context](#7322-related-browsing-contexts) has a popup sandboxing flag set, which is a [sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing). When a [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) is created, its [popup sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing) must be empty. It is populated by [the rules for choosing a navigable](#7317-navigable-target-names) and the [obtain a browsing context to use for a navigation response](#7132-browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-opener-policy) algorithm.

Every [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) element has an `iframe` sandboxing flag set, which is a [sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing). Which flags in an [`iframe` sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing) are set at any particular time is determined by the [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) element's [`sandbox`](#485-the-iframe-element) attribute.

Every [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has an active sandboxing flag set, which is a [sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing). When the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is created, its [active sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing) must be empty. It is populated by the [navigation algorithm](#7422-beginning-navigation).

Every [CSP list](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#csp-list) cspList has CSP-derived sandboxing flags, which is a [sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing). It is the return value of the following algorithm:
1. Let directives be an empty [ordered set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets).
2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) policy in cspList:
   1. If policy's [disposition](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#policy-disposition) is not "`enforce`", then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   2. If policy's [directive set](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#policy-directive-set) [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) a [directive](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#directives) whose name is "[`sandbox`](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#sandbox)", then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) that directive to directives.
3. If directives is empty, then return an empty [sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing).
4. Let directive be directives\[directives's [size](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) − 1\].
5. Return the result of [parsing the sandboxing directive](#715-sandboxing) directive.

---

To determine the creation sandboxing flags for a [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) browsing context, given null or an element embedder, return the [union](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) of the flags that are present in the following [sandboxing flag sets](#715-sandboxing):
- If embedder is null, then the flags set on browsing context's [popup sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing).
- If embedder is an element, then the flags set on embedder's [`iframe` sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing).
- If embedder is an element, then the flags set on embedder's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [active sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing).

#### 7.1.6 [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) element referrer policy

To determine the `iframe` element referrer policy given an element-or-null embedder:
1. If embedder is an [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) element, then return embedder's [`referrerpolicy`](#485-the-iframe-element) attribute's state's corresponding keyword.
2. Return the empty string.

> [!note]
> This is used for allowing masking of some [origins](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) in the [internal ancestor origin objects list creation steps](#313-ancestor-origins).

#### 7.1.7 Policy containers

A policy container is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) containing policies that apply to a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), a [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface), or a [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope). It has the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):
- A CSP list, which is a [CSP list](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#csp-list). It is initially empty.
- An embedder policy, which is an [embedder policy](#714-cross-origin-embedder-policies). It is initially a new [embedder policy](#714-cross-origin-embedder-policies).
- A referrer policy, which is a [referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy). It is initially the [default referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#default-referrer-policy).
- An integrity policy, which is an [integrity policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-subresource-integrity/#integrity-policy), initially a new [integrity policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-subresource-integrity/#integrity-policy).
- A report-only integrity policy, which is an [integrity policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-subresource-integrity/#integrity-policy), initially a new [integrity policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-subresource-integrity/#integrity-policy).

> [!warning]
> Move other policies into the policy container.

To clone a policy container given a [policy container](#717-policy-containers) policyContainer:
1. Let clone be a new [policy container](#717-policy-containers).
2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) policy in policyContainer's [CSP list](#717-policy-containers), [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) a copy of policy into clone's [CSP list](#717-policy-containers).
3. Set clone's [embedder policy](#717-policy-containers) to a copy of policyContainer's [embedder policy](#717-policy-containers).
4. Set clone's [referrer policy](#717-policy-containers) to policyContainer's [referrer policy](#717-policy-containers).
5. Set clone's [integrity policy](#717-policy-containers) to a copy of policyContainer's [integrity policy](#717-policy-containers).
6. Return clone.

To determine whether a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) url requires storing the policy container in history:
1. If url's [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) is "`blob`", then return false.
2. If url [is local](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#is-local), then return true.
3. Return false.

To create a policy container from a fetch response given a [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response and an [environment](#8131-environments)-or-null environment:
1. If response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url)'s [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) is "`blob`", then return a [clone](#717-policy-containers) of response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url)'s [blob URL entry](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-blob-entry)'s [environment](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#blob-url-entry-environment)'s [policy container](#8132-environment-settings-objects).
2. Let result be a new [policy container](#717-policy-containers).
3. Set result's [CSP list](#717-policy-containers) to the result of [parsing a response's Content Security Policies](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#parse-response-csp) given response.
4. If environment is non-null, then set result's [embedder policy](#717-policy-containers) to the result of [obtaining an embedder policy](#7141-the-headers) given response and environment. Otherwise, set it to "[`unsafe-none`](#714-cross-origin-embedder-policies)".
5. Set result's [referrer policy](#717-policy-containers) to the result of [parsing the \``Referrer-Policy`\` header](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#parse-referrer-policy-from-header) given response. [\[REFERRERPOLICY\]](#references)
6. [Parse Integrity-Policy headers](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-subresource-integrity/#parse-integrity-policy-headers) with response and result.
7. Return result.

To determine navigation params policy container given a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) responseURL and four [policy container](#717-policy-containers)-or-nulls historyPolicyContainer, initiatorPolicyContainer, parentPolicyContainer, and responsePolicyContainer:
1. If historyPolicyContainer is not null:
   1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): responseURL [requires storing the policy container in history](#717-policy-containers).
   2. Return a [clone](#717-policy-containers) of historyPolicyContainer.
2. If responseURL is [`about:srcdoc`](#241-terminology):
   1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): parentPolicyContainer is not null.
   2. Return a [clone](#717-policy-containers) of parentPolicyContainer.
3. If responseURL [is local](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#is-local) and initiatorPolicyContainer is not null, then return a [clone](#717-policy-containers) of initiatorPolicyContainer.
4. If responsePolicyContainer is not null, then return responsePolicyContainer.
5. Return a new [policy container](#717-policy-containers).

To initialize a worker global scope's policy container given a [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) workerGlobalScope, a [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response, and an [environment](#8131-environments) environment:
1. If workerGlobalScope's [url](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) [is local](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#is-local) but its [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) is not "`blob`":
   1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): workerGlobalScope's [owner set](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface)'s [size](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) is 1.
   2. Set workerGlobalScope's [policy container](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) to a [clone](#717-policy-containers) of workerGlobalScope's [owner set](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface)\[0\]'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant)'s [policy container](#8132-environment-settings-objects).
2. Otherwise, set workerGlobalScope's [policy container](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) to the result of [creating a policy container from a fetch response](#717-policy-containers) given response and environment.

### 7.2 APIs related to navigation and session history

#### 7.2.1 Security infrastructure for [`Window`](#722-the-window-object), [`WindowProxy`](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object), and [`Location`](#724-the-location-interface) objects

Although typically objects cannot be accessed across [origins](#711-origins), the web platform would not be true to itself if it did not have some legacy exceptions to that rule that the web depends upon.

This section uses the terminology and typographic conventions from the JavaScript specification. [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#references)

##### 7.2.1.1 Integration with IDL

When [perform a security check](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-perform-a-security-check) is invoked, with a platformObject, identifier, and type, run these steps:
1. If platformObject is not a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) or [`Location`](#724-the-location-interface) object, then return.
2. For each e of [CrossOriginProperties](#72131-crossoriginproperties--o-)(platformObject):
   1. If [SameValue](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-samevalue)(e.\[\[Property\]\], identifier) is true:
      1. If type is "`method`" and e has neither \[\[NeedsGetter\]\] nor \[\[NeedsSetter\]\], then return.
      2. Otherwise, if type is "`getter`" and e.\[\[NeedsGetter\]\] is true, then return.
      3. Otherwise, if type is "`setter`" and e.\[\[NeedsSetter\]\] is true, then return.
3. If [IsPlatformObjectSameOrigin](#72133-isplatformobjectsameorigin--o-)(platformObject) is false, then throw a ["`SecurityError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

##### 7.2.1.2 Shared internal slot: \[\[CrossOriginPropertyDescriptorMap\]\]

[`Window`](#722-the-window-object) and [`Location`](#724-the-location-interface) objects both have a \[\[CrossOriginPropertyDescriptorMap\]\] internal slot, whose value is initially an empty map.

The [\[\[CrossOriginPropertyDescriptorMap\]\]](#7212-shared-internal-slot-crossoriginpropertydescriptormap) internal slot contains a map with entries whose keys are (currentGlobal, objectGlobal, propertyKey)-tuples and values are property descriptors, as a memoization of what is visible to scripts when currentGlobal inspects a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) or [`Location`](#724-the-location-interface) object from objectGlobal. It is filled lazily by [CrossOriginGetOwnPropertyHelper](#72134-crossorigingetownpropertyhelper--o-p-), which consults it on future lookups.

User agents should allow a value held in the map to be garbage collected along with its corresponding key when nothing holds a reference to any part of the value. That is, as long as garbage collection is not observable.

> [!example]
> For example, with `const href =
>   Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(crossOriginLocation, "href").set` the value and its corresponding key in the map cannot be garbage collected as that would be observable.

User agents may have an optimization whereby they remove key-value pairs from the map when [`document.domain`](#7112-relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction) is set. This is not observable as [`document.domain`](#7112-relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction) cannot revisit an earlier value.

> [!example]
> For example, setting [`document.domain`](#7112-relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction) to "`example.com`" on www.example.com means user agents can remove all key-value pairs from the map where part of the key is www.example.com, as that can never be part of the [origin](#711-origins) again and therefore the corresponding value could never be retrieved from the map.

##### 7.2.1.3 Shared abstract operations

###### 7.2.1.3.1 CrossOriginProperties ( O )
1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): O is a [`Location`](#724-the-location-interface) or [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object.
2. If O is a [`Location`](#724-the-location-interface) object, then return « { \[\[Property\]\]: "`href`", \[\[NeedsGetter\]\]: false, \[\[NeedsSetter\]\]: true }, { \[\[Property\]\]: "`replace`" } ».
3. Return « { \[\[Property\]\]: "`window`", \[\[NeedsGetter\]\]: true, \[\[NeedsSetter\]\]: false }, { \[\[Property\]\]: "`self`", \[\[NeedsGetter\]\]: true, \[\[NeedsSetter\]\]: false }, { \[\[Property\]\]: "`location`", \[\[NeedsGetter\]\]: true, \[\[NeedsSetter\]\]: true }, { \[\[Property\]\]: "`close`" }, { \[\[Property\]\]: "`closed`", \[\[NeedsGetter\]\]: true, \[\[NeedsSetter\]\]: false }, { \[\[Property\]\]: "`focus`" }, { \[\[Property\]\]: "`blur`" }, { \[\[Property\]\]: "`frames`", \[\[NeedsGetter\]\]: true, \[\[NeedsSetter\]\]: false }, { \[\[Property\]\]: "`length`", \[\[NeedsGetter\]\]: true, \[\[NeedsSetter\]\]: false }, { \[\[Property\]\]: "`top`", \[\[NeedsGetter\]\]: true, \[\[NeedsSetter\]\]: false }, { \[\[Property\]\]: "`opener`", \[\[NeedsGetter\]\]: true, \[\[NeedsSetter\]\]: false }, { \[\[Property\]\]: "`parent`", \[\[NeedsGetter\]\]: true, \[\[NeedsSetter\]\]: false }, { \[\[Property\]\]: "`postMessage`" } ».

> [!note]
> This abstract operation does not return a [Completion Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type).

> [!note]
> Indexed properties do not need to be safelisted in this algorithm, as they are handled directly by the [`WindowProxy`](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object) object.

A JavaScript property name P is a cross-origin accessible window property name if it is "`window`", "`self`", "`location`", "`close`", "`closed`", "`focus`", "`blur`", "`frames`", "`length`", "`top`", "`opener`", "`parent`", "`postMessage`", or an [array index property name](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-array-index-property-name).

###### 7.2.1.3.2 CrossOriginPropertyFallback ( P )
1. If P is "`then`", [%Symbol.toStringTag%](#219-dependencies), [%Symbol.hasInstance%](#219-dependencies), or [%Symbol.isConcatSpreadable%](#219-dependencies), then return [PropertyDescriptor](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-property-descriptor-specification-type) { \[\[Value\]\]: undefined, \[\[Writable\]\]: false, \[\[Enumerable\]\]: false, \[\[Configurable\]\]: true }.
2. Throw a ["`SecurityError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

###### 7.2.1.3.3 IsPlatformObjectSameOrigin ( O )
1. Return true if the [current settings object](#81333-current)'s [origin](#8132-environment-settings-objects) is [same origin-domain](#711-origins) with O's [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant)'s [origin](#8132-environment-settings-objects), and false otherwise.

> [!note]
> This abstract operation does not return a [Completion Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type).

> [!note]
> Here the [current settings object](#81333-current) roughly corresponds to the "caller", because this check occurs before the [execution context](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-execution-contexts) for the getter/setter/method in question makes its way onto the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack). For example, in the code `w.document`, this step is invoked before the [`document`](#722-the-window-object) getter is reached as part of the [\[\[Get\]\]](#7237-get--p-receiver-) algorithm for the [`WindowProxy`](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object) w.

###### 7.2.1.3.4 CrossOriginGetOwnPropertyHelper ( O, P )

> [!note]
> If this abstract operation returns undefined and there is no custom behavior, the caller needs to throw a ["`SecurityError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException). In practice this is handled by the caller calling [CrossOriginPropertyFallback](#72132-crossoriginpropertyfallback--p-).
1. Let crossOriginKey be a tuple consisting of the [current settings object](#81333-current), O's [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant), and P.
2. For each e of [CrossOriginProperties](#72131-crossoriginproperties--o-)(O):
   1. If [SameValue](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-samevalue)(e.\[\[Property\]\], P) is true:
      1. If the value of the [\[\[CrossOriginPropertyDescriptorMap\]\]](#7212-shared-internal-slot-crossoriginpropertydescriptormap) internal slot of O contains an entry whose key [equals](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#311-identity-and-equality) crossOriginKey, then return that entry's value.
      2. Let originalDesc be [OrdinaryGetOwnProperty](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ordinarygetownproperty)(O, P).
      3. Let crossOriginDesc be undefined.
      4. If e.\[\[NeedsGetter\]\] and e.\[\[NeedsSetter\]\] are absent:
         1. Let value be originalDesc.\[\[Value\]\].
         2. If [IsCallable](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-iscallable)(value) is true, then set value to an anonymous built-in function, created in the [current realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#current-realm), that performs the same steps as the IDL operation P on object O.
         3. Set crossOriginDesc to [PropertyDescriptor](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-property-descriptor-specification-type) { \[\[Value\]\]: value, \[\[Enumerable\]\]: false, \[\[Writable\]\]: false, \[\[Configurable\]\]: true }.
      5. Otherwise:
         1. Let crossOriginGetter be undefined.
         2. If e.\[\[NeedsGetter\]\] is true, then set crossOriginGetter to an anonymous built-in function, created in the [current realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#current-realm), that performs the same steps as the getter of the IDL attribute P on object O.
         3. Let crossOriginSetter be undefined.
         4. If e.\[\[NeedsSetter\]\] is true, then set crossOriginSetter to an anonymous built-in function, created in the [current realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#current-realm), that performs the same steps as the setter of the IDL attribute P on object O.
         5. Set crossOriginDesc to [PropertyDescriptor](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-property-descriptor-specification-type) { \[\[Getter\]\]: crossOriginGetter, \[\[Setter\]\]: crossOriginSetter, \[\[Enumerable\]\]: false, \[\[Configurable\]\]: true }.
      6. Create an entry in the value of the [\[\[CrossOriginPropertyDescriptorMap\]\]](#7212-shared-internal-slot-crossoriginpropertydescriptormap) internal slot of O with key crossOriginKey and value crossOriginDesc.
      7. Return crossOriginDesc.
3. Return undefined.

> [!note]
> This abstract operation does not return a [Completion Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type).

> [!note]
> The reason that the property descriptors produced here are configurable is to preserve the [invariants of the essential internal methods](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-invariants-of-the-essential-internal-methods) required by the JavaScript specification. In particular, since the value of the property can change as a consequence of navigation, it is required that the property be configurable. (However, see [tc39/ecma262 issue #672](https://github.com/tc39/ecma262/issues/672) and references to it elsewhere in this specification for cases where we are not able to preserve these invariants, for compatibility with existing web content.) [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#references)

> [!note]
> The reason the property descriptors are non-enumerable, despite this mismatching the same-origin behavior, is for compatibility with existing web content. See [issue #3183](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/3183) for details.

###### 7.2.1.3.5 CrossOriginGet ( O, P, Receiver )
1. Let desc be ? O.\[\[GetOwnProperty\]\](P).
2. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): desc is not undefined.
3. If [IsDataDescriptor](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-isdatadescriptor)(desc) is true, then return desc.\[\[Value\]\].
4. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): [IsAccessorDescriptor](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-isaccessordescriptor)(desc) is true.
5. Let getter be desc.\[\[Getter\]\].
6. If getter is undefined, then throw a ["`SecurityError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
7. Return ? [Call](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-call)(getter, Receiver).

###### 7.2.1.3.6 CrossOriginSet ( O, P, V, Receiver )
1. Let desc be ? O.\[\[GetOwnProperty\]\](P).
2. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): desc is not undefined.
3. If desc.\[\[Setter\]\] is present and its value is not undefined:
   1. Perform ? [Call](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-call)(desc.\[\[Setter\]\], Receiver, « V »).
   2. Return true.
4. Throw a ["`SecurityError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

###### 7.2.1.3.7 CrossOriginOwnPropertyKeys ( O )
1. Let keys be a new empty [List](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type).
2. For each e of [CrossOriginProperties](#72131-crossoriginproperties--o-)(O), [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) e.\[\[Property\]\] to keys.
3. Return the concatenation of keys and « "`then`", [%Symbol.toStringTag%](#219-dependencies), [%Symbol.hasInstance%](#219-dependencies), [%Symbol.isConcatSpreadable%](#219-dependencies) ».

> [!note]
> This abstract operation does not return a [Completion Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type).

#### 7.2.2 The [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object

```webidl
[Global=Window,
 Exposed=Window,
 LegacyUnenumerableNamedProperties]
interface Window : EventTarget {
  // the current browsing context
  [LegacyUnforgeable] readonly attribute WindowProxy window;
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute WindowProxy self;
  [LegacyUnforgeable] readonly attribute Document document;
  attribute DOMString name; 
  [PutForwards=href, LegacyUnforgeable] readonly attribute Location location;
  readonly attribute History history;
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute Navigation navigation;
  readonly attribute CustomElementRegistry customElements;
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute BarProp locationbar;
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute BarProp menubar;
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute BarProp personalbar;
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute BarProp scrollbars;
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute BarProp statusbar;
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute BarProp toolbar;
  attribute DOMString status;
  undefined close();
  readonly attribute boolean closed;
  undefined stop();
  undefined focus();
  undefined blur();

  // other browsing contexts
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute WindowProxy frames;
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute unsigned long length;
  [LegacyUnforgeable] readonly attribute WindowProxy? top;
  attribute any opener;
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute WindowProxy? parent;
  readonly attribute Element? frameElement;
  WindowProxy? open(optional USVString url = "", optional DOMString target = "_blank", optional [LegacyNullToEmptyString] DOMString features = "");

  // Since this is the global object, the IDL named getter adds a NamedPropertiesObject exotic
  // object on the prototype chain. Indeed, this does not make the global object an exotic object.
  // Indexed access is taken care of by the WindowProxy exotic object.
  getter object (DOMString name);

  // the user agent
  readonly attribute Navigator navigator;
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute Navigator clientInformation; // legacy alias of .navigator
  readonly attribute boolean originAgentCluster;

  // user prompts
  undefined alert();
  undefined alert(DOMString message);
  boolean confirm(optional DOMString message = "");
  DOMString? prompt(optional DOMString message = "", optional DOMString default = "");
  undefined print();

  undefined postMessage(any message, USVString targetOrigin, optional sequence<object> transfer = []);
  undefined postMessage(any message, optional WindowPostMessageOptions options = {});

  // also has obsolete members
};
Window includes GlobalEventHandlers;
Window includes WindowEventHandlers;

dictionary WindowPostMessageOptions : StructuredSerializeOptions {
  USVString targetOrigin = "/";
};
```

`window.window`

`window.frames`

`window.self`

These attributes all return window.

`window.document`

Returns the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) associated with window.

`document.defaultView`

Returns the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) associated with document, if there is one, or null otherwise.

The [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object has an associated `Document`, which is a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object. It is set when the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object is created, and only ever changed during [navigation](#7422-beginning-navigation) from the [initial `about:blank`](#311-the-document-object) [`Document`](#311-the-document-object).

A [`Window`](#722-the-window-object)'s browsing context is its [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts). It is either null or a [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts).

A [`Window`](#722-the-window-object)'s navigable is the [navigable](#731-navigables) whose [active document](#731-navigables) is the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s, or null if there is no such [navigable](#731-navigables).

The `window`, `frames`, and `self` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant realm](#81334-relevant).\[\[GlobalEnv\]\].\[\[GlobalThisValue\]\].

The `document` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object).

> [!note]
> The [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object associated with a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object can change in exactly one case: when the [navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation) algorithm [creates a new `Document` object](#751-shared-document-creation-infrastructure) for the first page loaded in a [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts). In that specific case, the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object of the [initial `about:blank`](#311-the-document-object) page is reused and gets a new [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object.

The `defaultView` getter steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) is null, then return null.
2. Return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts)'s [`WindowProxy`](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object) object.

---

For historical reasons, [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) objects must also have a writable, configurable, non-enumerable property named `HTMLDocument` whose value is the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) [interface object](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-interface-object).

##### 7.2.2.1 Opening and closing windows

`window = window.open([ url [, target [, features ] ] ])`

Opens a window to show url (defaults to "[`about:blank`](#219-dependencies)"), and returns it. target (defaults to "`_blank`") gives the name of the new window. If a window already exists with that name, it is reused. The features argument can contain a [set of comma-separated tokens](#238-comma-separated-tokens):

"`noopener`"

"`noreferrer`"

These behave equivalently to the [`noopener`](#46814-link-type-noopener) and [`noreferrer`](#46815-link-type-noreferrer) link types on [hyperlinks](#461-introduction).

"`popup`"

Encourages user agents to provide a minimal web browser user interface for the new window. (Impacts the [`visible`](#7225-historical-browser-interface-element-apis) getter on all [`BarProp`](#7225-historical-browser-interface-element-apis) objects as well.)

```javascript
globalThis.open("https://email.example/message/CAOOOkFcWW97r8yg=SsWg7GgCmp4suVX9o85y8BvNRqMjuc5PXg", undefined, "noopener,popup");
```

`window.name [ = value ]`

Returns the name of the window.

Can be set, to change the name.

`window.close()`

Closes the window.

`window.closed`

Returns true if the window has been closed, false otherwise.

`window.stop()`

Cancels the document load.

To get noopener for window open, given a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) sourceDocument, an [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) tokenizedFeatures, and a [URL record](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url)-or-null url, perform the following steps. They return a boolean.
1. If url is not null and url's [blob URL entry](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-blob-entry) is not null:
   1. Let blobOrigin be url's [blob URL entry](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-blob-entry)'s [environment](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#blob-url-entry-environment)'s [origin](#8132-environment-settings-objects).
   2. Let topLevelOrigin be sourceDocument's [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant)'s [top-level origin](#8131-environments).
   3. If blobOrigin is not [same site](#7111-sites) with topLevelOrigin, then return true.
2. Let noopener be false.
3. If tokenizedFeatures\["`noopener`"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then set noopener to the result of [parsing tokenizedFeatures\["`noopener`"\] as a boolean feature](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows).
4. Return noopener.

The window open steps, given a string url, a string target, and a string features, are as follows:
1. If the [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [termination nesting level](#759-unloading-documents) is nonzero, then return null.
2. Let sourceDocument be the [entry global object](#81331-entry)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object).
3. Let urlRecord be null.
4. If url is not the empty string:
   1. Set urlRecord to the result of [encoding-parsing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given url, relative to sourceDocument.
   2. If urlRecord is failure, then throw a ["`SyntaxError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
5. If target is the empty string, then set target to "`_blank`".
6. Let tokenizedFeatures be the result of [tokenizing](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows) features.
7. Let noreferrer be false.
8. If tokenizedFeatures\["`noreferrer`"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then set noreferrer to the result of [parsing tokenizedFeatures\["`noreferrer`"\] as a boolean feature](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows).
9. Let noopener be the result of [getting noopener for window open](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows) with sourceDocument, tokenizedFeatures, and urlRecord.
10. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) tokenizedFeatures\["`noopener`"\] and tokenizedFeatures\["`noreferrer`"\].
11. Let referrerPolicy be the empty string.
12. If noreferrer is true, then set noopener to true and set referrerPolicy to "`no-referrer`".
13. Let targetNavigable and windowType be the result of applying [the rules for choosing a navigable](#7317-navigable-target-names) given target, sourceDocument's [node navigable](#731-navigables), and noopener.

    > [!example]
    > If there is a user agent that supports control-clicking a link to open it in a new tab, and the user control-clicks on an element whose [`onclick`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects) handler uses the [`window.open()`](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows) API to open a page in an [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) element, the user agent could override the selection of the target browsing context to instead target a new tab.

14. If targetNavigable is null, then return null.
15. If windowType is either "`new and unrestricted`" or "`new with no opener`":
    1. Set targetNavigable's [active browsing context](#731-navigables)'s [is popup](#732-browsing-contexts) to the result of [checking if a popup window is requested](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows), given tokenizedFeatures.
    2. [Set up browsing context features](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view/#set-up-browsing-context-features) for targetNavigable's [active browsing context](#731-navigables) given tokenizedFeatures. [\[CSSOMVIEW\]](#references)
    3. If urlRecord is null, then set urlRecord to a [URL record](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) representing [`about:blank`](#219-dependencies).
    4. If urlRecord [matches `about:blank`](#241-terminology), then perform the [URL and history update steps](#744-non-fragment-synchronous-navigations) given targetNavigable's [active document](#731-navigables) and urlRecord.

       > [!note]
       > This is necessary in case url is something like `about:blank?foo`. If url is just plain `about:blank`, this will do nothing.

    5. Otherwise, [navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation) targetNavigable to urlRecord using sourceDocument, with *[referrerPolicy](#7422-beginning-navigation)* set to referrerPolicy and *[exceptionsEnabled](#7422-beginning-navigation)* set to true.

16. Otherwise:
    1. If urlRecord is not null, then [navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation) targetNavigable to urlRecord using sourceDocument, with *[referrerPolicy](#7422-beginning-navigation)* set to referrerPolicy and *[exceptionsEnabled](#7422-beginning-navigation)* set to true.
    2. If noopener is false, then set targetNavigable's [active browsing context](#731-navigables)'s [opener browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) to sourceDocument's [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts).
17. If windowType is "`new with no opener`", then return null.
18. If noopener is true and target is not an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for "`_self`", "`_parent`", or "`_top`", then return null.
19. Return targetNavigable's [active `WindowProxy`](#731-navigables).

The `open(url, target,
  features)` method steps are to run the [window open steps](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows) with url, target, and features.

> [!note]
> The method provides a mechanism for [navigating](#7422-beginning-navigation) an existing [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) or opening and navigating an [auxiliary browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts).

---

To tokenize the features argument:
1. Let tokenizedFeatures be a new [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps).
2. Let position point at the first code point of features.
3. [While](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration) position is not past the end of features:
   1. Let name be the empty string.
   2. Let value be the empty string.
   3. [Collect a sequence of code points](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) that are [feature separators](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows) from features given position. This skips past leading separators before the name.
   4. [Collect a sequence of code points](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) that are not [feature separators](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows) from features given position. Set name to the collected characters, [converted to ASCII lowercase](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).
   5. Set name to the result of [normalizing the feature name](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows) name.
   6. [While](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration) position is not past the end of features and the code point at position in features is not U+003D (=):
      1. If the code point at position in features is U+002C (,), or if it is not a [feature separator](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows), then [break](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
      2. Advance position by 1.

      > [!note]
      > This skips to the first U+003D (=) but does not skip past a U+002C (,) or a non-separator.

   7. If the code point at position in features is a [feature separator](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows):
      1. While position is not past the end of features and the code point at position in features is a [feature separator](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows):
         1. If the code point at position in features is U+002C (,), then [break](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
         2. Advance position by 1.

         > [!note]
         > This skips to the first non-separator but does not skip past a U+002C (,).

      2. [Collect a sequence of code points](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) that are not [feature separators](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows) code points from features given position. Set value to the collected code points, [converted to ASCII lowercase](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).

   8. If name is not the empty string, then set tokenizedFeatures\[name\] to value.

4. Return tokenizedFeatures.

To check if a window feature is set, given tokenizedFeatures, featureName, and defaultValue:
1. If tokenizedFeatures\[featureName\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then return the result of [parsing tokenizedFeatures\[featureName\] as a boolean feature](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows).
2. Return defaultValue.

To check if a popup window is requested, given tokenizedFeatures:
1. If tokenizedFeatures is [empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then return false.
2. If tokenizedFeatures\["`popup`"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then return the result of [parsing tokenizedFeatures\["`popup`"\] as a boolean feature](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows).
3. Let location be the result of [checking if a window feature is set](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows), given tokenizedFeatures, "`location`", and false.
4. Let toolbar be the result of [checking if a window feature is set](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows), given tokenizedFeatures, "`toolbar`", and false.
5. If location and toolbar are both false, then return true.
6. Let menubar be the result of [checking if a window feature is set](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows), given tokenizedFeatures, "`menubar`", and false.
7. If menubar is false, then return true.
8. Let resizable be the result of [checking if a window feature is set](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows), given tokenizedFeatures, "`resizable`", and true.
9. If resizable is false, then return true.
10. Let scrollbars be the result of [checking if a window feature is set](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows), given tokenizedFeatures, "`scrollbars`", and false.
11. If scrollbars is false, then return true.
12. Let status be the result of [checking if a window feature is set](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows), given tokenizedFeatures, "`status`", and false.
13. If status is false, then return true.
14. Return false.

A code point is a feature separator if it is [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), U+003D (=), or U+002C (,).

For legacy reasons, there are some aliases of some feature names. To normalize a feature name name, switch on name:

"`screenx`"

Return "`left`".

"`screeny`"

Return "`top`".

"`innerwidth`"

Return "`width`".

"`innerheight`"

Return "`height`".

Anything else

Return name.

To parse a boolean feature given a string value:
1. If value is the empty string, then return true.
2. If value [is](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) "`yes`", then return true.
3. If value [is](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) "`true`", then return true.
4. Let parsed be the result of [parsing value as an integer](#2341-signed-integers).
5. If parsed is an error, then set it to 0.
6. Return false if parsed is 0, and true otherwise.

---

The `name` getter steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [navigable](#722-the-window-object) is null, then return the empty string.
2. Return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [navigable](#722-the-window-object)'s [target name](#731-navigables).

The [`name`](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows) setter steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [navigable](#722-the-window-object) is null, then return.
2. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [navigable](#722-the-window-object)'s [active session history entry](#731-navigables)'s [document state](#7411-session-history-entries)'s [navigable target name](#7412-document-state) to the given value.

> [!note]
> The name [gets reset](#74231-the-usual-cross-document-navigation-case) when the navigable is [navigated](#7422-beginning-navigation) to another [origin](#711-origins).

---

The `close()` method steps are:
1. Let thisTraversable be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [navigable](#722-the-window-object).
2. If thisTraversable is not a [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables), then return.
3. If thisTraversable's [is closing](#731-navigables) is true, then return.
4. Let browsingContext be thisTraversable's [active browsing context](#731-navigables).
5. Let sourceSnapshotParams be the result of [snapshotting source snapshot params](#7421-supporting-concepts) given thisTraversable's [active document](#731-navigables).
6. If all the following are true:
   - thisTraversable is [script-closable](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows);
   - the [incumbent global object](#81332-incumbent)'s [browsing context](#722-the-window-object) is [familiar with](#7322-related-browsing-contexts) browsingContext; and
   - the [incumbent global object](#81332-incumbent)'s [navigable](#722-the-window-object) is [allowed by sandboxing to navigate](#7424-preventing-navigation) thisTraversable, given sourceSnapshotParams,

   then:
   1. Set thisTraversable's [is closing](#731-navigables) to true.
   2. [Queue a task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) to [definitely close](#7316-navigable-destruction) thisTraversable.

A [navigable](#731-navigables) is script-closable if it is a [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables), and any of the following are true:
- its [is created by web content](#7311-traversable-navigables) is true; or
- its [session history entries](#7311-traversable-navigables)'s [size](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) is 1.

The `closed` getter steps are to return true if [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [navigable](#722-the-window-object) is null or its [is closing](#731-navigables) is true; otherwise false.

The `stop()` method steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [navigable](#722-the-window-object) is null, then return.
2. [Stop loading](#7511-aborting-a-document-load) [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [navigable](#722-the-window-object).

##### 7.2.2.2 Indexed access on the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object

`window.length`

Returns the number of [document-tree child navigables](#7315-related-navigable-collections).

`window[index]`

Returns the [`WindowProxy`](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object) corresponding to the indicated [document-tree child navigables](#7315-related-navigable-collections).

The `length` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [document-tree child navigables](#7315-related-navigable-collections)'s [size](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).

> [!note]
> Indexed access to [document-tree child navigables](#7315-related-navigable-collections) is defined through the [\[\[GetOwnProperty\]\]](#7235-getownproperty--p-) internal method of the [`WindowProxy`](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object) object.

##### 7.2.2.3 Named access on the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object

`window[name]`

Returns the indicated element or collection of elements.

As a general rule, relying on this will lead to brittle code. Which IDs end up mapping to this API can vary over time, as new features are added to the web platform, for example. Instead of this, use `document.getElementById()` or `document.querySelector()`.

The document-tree child navigable target name property set of a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object window is the return value of running these steps:
1. Let children be the [document-tree child navigables](#7315-related-navigable-collections) of window's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object).
2. Let firstNamedChildren be an empty [ordered set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets).
3. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) navigable of children:
   1. Let name be navigable's [target name](#731-navigables).
   2. If name is the empty string, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   3. If firstNamedChildren [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) a [navigable](#731-navigables) whose [target name](#731-navigables) is name, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   4. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) navigable to firstNamedChildren.
4. Let names be an empty [ordered set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets).
5. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) navigable of firstNamedChildren:
   1. Let name be navigable's [target name](#731-navigables).
   2. If navigable's [active document](#731-navigables)'s [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is [same origin](#711-origins) with window's [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant)'s [origin](#8132-environment-settings-objects), then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) name to names.
6. Return names.

> [!example]
> The two separate iterations mean that in the following example, hosted on `https://example.org/`, assuming `https://elsewhere.example/` sets [`window.name`](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows) to "`spices`", evaluating `window.spices` after everything has loaded will yield undefined:
> 
> ```html
> <iframe src=https://elsewhere.example.com/></iframe>
> <iframe name=spices></iframe>
> ```

The [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object [supports named properties](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-support-named-properties). The [supported property names](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-supported-property-names) of a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object window at any moment consist of the following, in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) according to the element that contributed them, ignoring later duplicates:
- window's [document-tree child navigable target name property set](#7223-named-access-on-the-window-object);
- the value of the `name` content attribute for all [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element), [`form`](#4103-the-form-element), [`img`](#483-the-img-element), and [`object`](#487-the-object-element) elements that have a non-empty `name` content attribute and are [in a document tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) with window's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object) as their [root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees); and
- the [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) of all elements that have an [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) and are [in a document tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) with window's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object) as their [root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).

To [determine the value of a named property](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-determine-the-value-of-a-named-property) name in a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object window, the user agent must return the value obtained using the following steps:
1. Let objects be the list of [named objects](#7223-named-access-on-the-window-object) of window with the name name.

   > [!note]
   > There will be at least one such object, since the algorithm would otherwise not have been [invoked by Web IDL](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#named-properties-object-getownproperty).

2. If objects contains a [navigable](#731-navigables):
   1. Let container be the first [navigable container](#7313-child-navigables) in window's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [descendants](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) whose [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables) is in objects.
   2. Return container's [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables)'s [active `WindowProxy`](#731-navigables).
3. Otherwise, if objects has only one element, return that element.
4. Otherwise, return an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) rooted at window's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object), whose filter matches only [named objects](#7223-named-access-on-the-window-object) of window with the name name. (By definition, these will all be elements.)

Named objects of [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object window with the name name, for the purposes of the above algorithm, consist of the following:
- [document-tree child navigables](#7315-related-navigable-collections) of window's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object) whose [target name](#731-navigables) is name;
- [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element), [`form`](#4103-the-form-element), [`img`](#483-the-img-element), or [`object`](#487-the-object-element) elements that have a `name` content attribute whose value is name and are [in a document tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) with window's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object) as their [root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees); and
- elements whose [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) is name and that are [in a document tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) with window's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object) as their [root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).

> [!note]
> Since the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) interface has the [`[Global]`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#Global) extended attribute, its named properties follow the rules for [named properties objects](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-named-properties-object) rather than [legacy platform objects](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-legacy-platform-object).

##### 7.2.2.4 Accessing related windows

`window.top`

Returns the [`WindowProxy`](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object) for the [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables).

`window.opener [ = value ]`

Returns the [`WindowProxy`](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object) for the [opener browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts).

Returns null if there isn't one or if it has been set to null.

Can be set to null.

`window.parent`

Returns the [`WindowProxy`](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object) for the [parent navigable](#731-navigables).

`window.frameElement`

Returns the [navigable container](#7313-child-navigables) element.

Returns null if there isn't one, and in cross-origin situations.

The `top` getter steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [navigable](#722-the-window-object) is null, then return null.
2. Return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [navigable](#722-the-window-object)'s [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables)'s [active `WindowProxy`](#731-navigables).

The `opener` getter steps are:
1. Let current be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [browsing context](#722-the-window-object).
2. If current is null, then return null.
3. If current's [opener browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) is null, then return null.
4. Return current's [opener browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts)'s [`WindowProxy`](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object) object.

The [`opener`](#7224-accessing-related-windows) setter steps are:
1. If the given value is null and [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [browsing context](#722-the-window-object) is non-null, then set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [browsing context](#722-the-window-object)'s [opener browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) to null.
2. If the given value is non-null, then perform ? [DefinePropertyOrThrow](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-definepropertyorthrow)([this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), "`opener`", { \[\[Value\]\]: the given value, \[\[Writable\]\]: true, \[\[Enumerable\]\]: true, \[\[Configurable\]\]: true }).

> [!note]
> Setting [`window.opener`](#7224-accessing-related-windows) to null clears the [opener browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) reference. In practice, this prevents future scripts from accessing their [opener browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts)'s [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object.
> 
> By default, scripts can access their [opener browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts)'s [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object through the [`window.opener`](#7224-accessing-related-windows) getter. E.g., a script can set `window.opener.location`, causing the [opener browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) to navigate.

The `parent` getter steps are:
1. Let navigable be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [navigable](#722-the-window-object).
2. If navigable is null, then return null.
3. If navigable's [parent](#731-navigables) is not null, then set navigable to navigable's [parent](#731-navigables).
4. Return navigable's [active `WindowProxy`](#731-navigables).

The `frameElement` getter steps are:
1. Let current be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [node navigable](#731-navigables).
2. If current is null, then return null.
3. Let container be current's [container](#7313-child-navigables).
4. If container is null, then return null.
5. If container's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is not [same origin-domain](#711-origins) with the [current settings object](#81333-current)'s [origin](#8132-environment-settings-objects), then return null.
6. Return container.

> [!example]
> An example of when these properties can return null is as follows:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE html>
> <iframe></iframe>
> 
> <script>
> "use strict";
> const element = document.querySelector("iframe");
> const iframeWindow = element.contentWindow;
> element.remove();
> 
> console.assert(iframeWindow.top === null);
> console.assert(iframeWindow.parent === null);
> console.assert(iframeWindow.frameElement === null);
> </script>
> ```
> 
> Here the [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) corresponding to `iframeWindow` was [nulled out](#7510-destroying-documents) when `element` was removed from the document.

##### 7.2.2.5 Historical browser interface element APIs

For historical reasons, the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) interface had some properties that represented the visibility of certain web browser interface elements.

For privacy and interoperability reasons, those properties now return values that represent whether the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object)'s [browsing context](#722-the-window-object)'s [is popup](#732-browsing-contexts) property is true or false.

Each interface element is represented by a [`BarProp`](#7225-historical-browser-interface-element-apis) object:

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface BarProp {
  readonly attribute boolean visible;
};
```

`window.locationbar.visible`

`window.menubar.visible`

`window.personalbar.visible`

`window.scrollbars.visible`

`window.statusbar.visible`

`window.toolbar.visible`

Returns true if the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) is not a popup; otherwise, returns false.

The `visible` getter steps are:
1. Let browsingContext be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant)'s [browsing context](#722-the-window-object).
2. If browsingContext is null, then return true.
3. Return the negation of browsingContext's [top-level browsing context](#7322-related-browsing-contexts)'s [is popup](#732-browsing-contexts).

The following [`BarProp`](#7225-historical-browser-interface-element-apis) objects must exist for each [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object:

The location bar `BarProp` object

Historically represented the user interface element that contains a control that displays the browser's location bar.

The menu bar `BarProp` object

Historically represented the user interface element that contains a list of commands in menu form, or some similar interface concept.

The personal bar `BarProp` object

Historically represented the user interface element that contains links to the user's favorite pages, or some similar interface concept.

The scrollbar `BarProp` object

Historically represented the user interface element that contains a scrolling mechanism, or some similar interface concept.

The status bar `BarProp` object

Historically represented a user interface element found immediately below or after the document, as appropriate for the user's media, which typically provides information about ongoing network activity or information about elements that the user's pointing device is currently indicating.

The toolbar `BarProp` object

Historically represented the user interface element found immediately above or before the document, as appropriate for the user's media, which typically provides [session history traversal](#7461-updating-the-traversable) controls (back and forward buttons, reload buttons, etc.).

The `locationbar` attribute must return [the location bar `BarProp` object](#7225-historical-browser-interface-element-apis).

The `menubar` attribute must return [the menu bar `BarProp` object](#7225-historical-browser-interface-element-apis).

The `personalbar` attribute must return [the personal bar `BarProp` object](#7225-historical-browser-interface-element-apis).

The `scrollbars` attribute must return [the scrollbar `BarProp` object](#7225-historical-browser-interface-element-apis).

The `statusbar` attribute must return [the status bar `BarProp` object](#7225-historical-browser-interface-element-apis).

The `toolbar` attribute must return [the toolbar `BarProp` object](#7225-historical-browser-interface-element-apis).

---

For historical reasons, the `status` attribute on the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object must, on getting, return the last string it was set to, and on setting, must set itself to the new value. When the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object is created, the attribute must be set to the empty string. It does not do anything else.

##### 7.2.2.6 Script settings for [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) objects

To set up a window environment settings object, given a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) creationURL, a [JavaScript execution context](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-execution-contexts) execution context, null or an [environment](#8131-environments) reservedEnvironment, a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) topLevelCreationURL, and an [origin](#711-origins) topLevelOrigin, run these steps:
1. Let realm be the value of execution context's Realm component.
2. Let window be realm's [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
3. Let settings object be a new [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) whose algorithms are defined as follows:

   The [realm execution context](#8132-environment-settings-objects)

   Return execution context.

   The [module map](#8132-environment-settings-objects)

   Return the [module map](#311-the-document-object) of window's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object).

   The [API base URL](#8132-environment-settings-objects)

   Return the current [base URL](#243-document-base-urls) of window's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object).

   The [origin](#8132-environment-settings-objects)

   Return the [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) of window's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object).

   The [has cross-site ancestor](#8132-environment-settings-objects)
   1. If window's [navigable](#731-navigables)'s [parent](#731-navigables) is null, then return false.
   2. Let parentDocument be window's [navigable](#731-navigables)'s [parent](#731-navigables)'s [active document](#731-navigables).
   3. If parentDocument's [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant)'s [has cross-site ancestor](#8132-environment-settings-objects) is true, then return true.
   4. If parentDocument's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is not [same site](#7111-sites) with window's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), then return true.
   5. Return false.

   The [policy container](#8132-environment-settings-objects)

   Return the [policy container](#311-the-document-object) of window's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object).

   The [cross-origin isolated capability](#8132-environment-settings-objects)

   Return true if both of the following hold, and false otherwise:
   - realm's [agent cluster](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters)'s [cross-origin-isolation mode](#8122-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-cluster-formalism) is "[`concrete`](#7323-groupings-of-browsing-contexts)", and
   - window's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object) is [allowed to use](#485-the-iframe-element) the "[`cross-origin-isolated`](#22-policy-controlled-features)" feature.

   The [time origin](#8132-environment-settings-objects)

   Return window's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [load timing info](#315-reporting-document-loading-status)'s [navigation start time](#315-reporting-document-loading-status).

4. If reservedEnvironment is non-null:
   1. Set settings object's [id](#8131-environments) to reservedEnvironment's [id](#8131-environments), [target browsing context](#8131-environments) to reservedEnvironment's [target browsing context](#8131-environments), and [active service worker](#8131-environments) to reservedEnvironment's [active service worker](#8131-environments).
   2. Set reservedEnvironment's [id](#8131-environments) to the empty string.

      > [!note]
      > The identity of the reserved environment is considered to be fully transferred to the created [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects). The reserved environment is not searchable by the [environment](#8131-environments)’s [id](#8131-environments) from this point on.

5. Otherwise, set settings object's [id](#8131-environments) to a new unique opaque string, settings object's [target browsing context](#8131-environments) to null, and settings object's [active service worker](#8131-environments) to null.
6. Set settings object's [creation URL](#8131-environments) to creationURL, settings object's [top-level creation URL](#8131-environments) to topLevelCreationURL, and settings object's [top-level origin](#8131-environments) to topLevelOrigin.
7. Set realm's \[\[HostDefined\]\] field to settings object.

#### 7.2.3 The [`WindowProxy`](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object) exotic object

A `WindowProxy` is an exotic object that wraps a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) ordinary object, indirecting most operations through to the wrapped object. Each [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) has an associated [`WindowProxy`](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object) object. When the [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) is [navigated](#7422-beginning-navigation), the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object wrapped by the [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts)'s associated [`WindowProxy`](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object) object is changed.

The [`WindowProxy`](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object) exotic object must use the ordinary internal methods except where it is explicitly specified otherwise below.

There is no [`WindowProxy`](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object) [interface object](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-interface-object).

Every [`WindowProxy`](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object) object has a \[\[Window\]\] internal slot representing the wrapped [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object.

> [!note]
> Although [`WindowProxy`](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object) is named as a "proxy", it does not do polymorphic dispatch on its target's internal methods as a real proxy would, due to a desire to reuse machinery between [`WindowProxy`](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object) and [`Location`](#724-the-location-interface) objects. As long as the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object remains an ordinary object this is unobservable and can be implemented either way.

##### 7.2.3.1 \[\[GetPrototypeOf\]\] ( )
1. Let W be the value of the [\[\[Window\]\]](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object) internal slot of **this**.
2. If [IsPlatformObjectSameOrigin](#72133-isplatformobjectsameorigin--o-)(W) is true, then return ! [OrdinaryGetPrototypeOf](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ordinarygetprototypeof)(W).
3. Return null.

##### 7.2.3.2 \[\[SetPrototypeOf\]\] ( V )
1. Return ! [SetImmutablePrototype](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-set-immutable-prototype)(**this**, V).

##### 7.2.3.3 \[\[IsExtensible\]\] ( )
1. Return true.

##### 7.2.3.4 \[\[PreventExtensions\]\] ( )
1. Return false.

##### 7.2.3.5 \[\[GetOwnProperty\]\] ( P )
1. Let W be the value of the [\[\[Window\]\]](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object) internal slot of **this**.
2. If P is an [array index property name](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-array-index-property-name):
   1. Let index be ! [ToUint32](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-touint32)(P).
   2. Let children be the [document-tree child navigables](#7315-related-navigable-collections) of W's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object).
   3. Let value be undefined.
   4. If index is less than children's [size](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists):
      1. [Sort](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) children in ascending order, with navigableA being less than navigableB if navigableA's [container](#7313-child-navigables) was inserted into W's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object) earlier than navigableB's [container](#7313-child-navigables) was.
      2. Set value to children\[index\]'s [active `WindowProxy`](#731-navigables).
   5. If value is undefined:
      1. If [IsPlatformObjectSameOrigin](#72133-isplatformobjectsameorigin--o-)(W) is true, then return undefined.
      2. Throw a ["`SecurityError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
   6. Return [PropertyDescriptor](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-property-descriptor-specification-type) { \[\[Value\]\]: value, \[\[Writable\]\]: false, \[\[Enumerable\]\]: true, \[\[Configurable\]\]: true }.
3. If [IsPlatformObjectSameOrigin](#72133-isplatformobjectsameorigin--o-)(W) is true, then return ! [OrdinaryGetOwnProperty](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ordinarygetownproperty)(W, P).

   > [!note]
   > This is a [willful violation](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-compliance-with-other-specifications) of the JavaScript specification's [invariants of the essential internal methods](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-invariants-of-the-essential-internal-methods) to maintain compatibility with existing web content. See [tc39/ecma262 issue #672](https://github.com/tc39/ecma262/issues/672) for more information. [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#references)

4. Let property be [CrossOriginGetOwnPropertyHelper](#72134-crossorigingetownpropertyhelper--o-p-)(W, P).
5. If property is not undefined, then return property.
6. If property is undefined and P is in W's [document-tree child navigable target name property set](#7223-named-access-on-the-window-object):
   1. Let value be the [active `WindowProxy`](#731-navigables) of the [named object](#7223-named-access-on-the-window-object) of W with the name P.
   2. Return [PropertyDescriptor](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-property-descriptor-specification-type) { \[\[Value\]\]: value, \[\[Enumerable\]\]: false, \[\[Writable\]\]: false, \[\[Configurable\]\]: true }.

      > [!note]
      > The reason the property descriptors are non-enumerable, despite this mismatching the same-origin behavior, is for compatibility with existing web content. See [issue #3183](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/3183) for details.

7. Return ? [CrossOriginPropertyFallback](#72132-crossoriginpropertyfallback--p-)(P).

##### 7.2.3.6 \[\[DefineOwnProperty\]\] ( P, Desc )
1. Let W be the value of the [\[\[Window\]\]](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object) internal slot of **this**.
2. If [IsPlatformObjectSameOrigin](#72133-isplatformobjectsameorigin--o-)(W) is true:
