- The platform has accumulated various exciting navigation-related features that need special-casing, such as [`javascript:`](#74232-the-javascript-url-special-case) URLs, [`srcdoc`](#485-the-iframe-element) [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element)s, and the [`beforeunload`](#events) event.

In what follows, we have attempted to guide the reader through these complexities by appropriately cordoning them off into labeled sections and algorithms, and giving appropriate words of introduction where possible. Nevertheless, if you wish to truly understand navigation and session history, [the usual advice](#191-how-to-read-this-specification) will be invaluable.

#### 7.4.1 Session history

##### 7.4.1.1 Session history entries

A session history entry is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) with the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):
- step, a non-negative integer or "`pending`", initially "`pending`".
- URL, a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url)
- document state, a [document state](#7412-document-state).
- classic history API state, which is [serialized state](#7411-session-history-entries), initially [StructuredSerializeForStorage](#275-structuredserializeforstorage--value-)(null).
- navigation API state, which is a [serialized state](#7411-session-history-entries), initially [StructuredSerializeForStorage](#275-structuredserializeforstorage--value-)(undefined).
- navigation API key, which is a string, initially set to the result of [generating a random UUID](https://w3c.github.io/webcrypto/#dfn-generate-a-random-uuid).
- navigation API ID, which is a string, initially set to the result of [generating a random UUID](https://w3c.github.io/webcrypto/#dfn-generate-a-random-uuid).
- scroll restoration mode, a [scroll restoration mode](#7411-session-history-entries), initially "[`auto`](#7411-session-history-entries)".
- scroll position data, which is scroll position data for the [document](#7411-session-history-entries)'s [restorable scrollable regions](#7465-persisted-history-entry-state).
- persisted user state, which is [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology), initially null

  > [!example]
  > For example, some user agents might want to persist the values of form controls.

  > [!note]
  > User agents that persist the value of form controls are encouraged to also persist their directionality (the value of the element's [`dir`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) attribute). This prevents values from being displayed incorrectly after a history traversal when the user had originally entered the values with an explicit, non-default directionality.

To get a [session history entry](#7411-session-history-entries)'s document, return its [document state](#7411-session-history-entries)'s [document](#7412-document-state).

---

Serialized state is a serialization (via [StructuredSerializeForStorage](#275-structuredserializeforstorage--value-)) of an object representing a user interface state. We sometimes informally refer to "state objects", which are the objects representing user interface state supplied by the author, or alternately the objects created by deserializing (via [StructuredDeserialize](#276-structureddeserialize--serialized-targetrealm---memory--)) serialized state.

Pages can [add](#725-the-history-interface) [serialized state](#7411-session-history-entries) to the session history. These are then [deserialized](#276-structureddeserialize--serialized-targetrealm---memory--) and [returned to the script](#events) when the user (or script) goes back in the history, thus enabling authors to use the "navigation" metaphor even in one-page applications.

> [!note]
> [Serialized state](#7411-session-history-entries) is intended to be used for two main purposes: first, storing a preparsed description of the state in the [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) so that in the simple case an author doesn't have to do the parsing (though one would still need the parsing for handling [URLs](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) passed around by users, so it's only a minor optimization). Second, so that the author can store state that one wouldn't store in the URL because it only applies to the current [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) instance and it would have to be reconstructed if a new [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) were opened.
> 
> An example of the latter would be something like keeping track of the precise coordinate from which a popup [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) was made to animate, so that if the user goes back, it can be made to animate to the same location. Or alternatively, it could be used to keep a pointer into a cache of data that would be fetched from the server based on the information in the [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url), so that when going back and forward, the information doesn't have to be fetched again.

---

A scroll restoration mode indicates whether the user agent should restore the persisted scroll position (if any) when traversing to an [entry](#7411-session-history-entries). A scroll restoration mode is one of the following:

"`auto`"

The user agent is responsible for restoring the scroll position upon navigation.

"`manual`"

The page is responsible for restoring the scroll position and the user agent does not attempt to do so automatically

##### 7.4.1.2 Document state

Document state holds state inside a [session history entry](#7411-session-history-entries) regarding how to present and, if necessary, recreate, a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object). It has:
- A document, a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) or null, initially null.

  > [!note]
  > When a history entry is [active](#731-navigables), it has a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) in its [document state](#7411-session-history-entries). However, when a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents), it's possible for it to be [destroyed](#7510-destroying-documents) to free resources. In such cases, this [document](#7412-document-state) item will be nulled out. The [URL](#7411-session-history-entries) and other data in the [session history entry](#7411-session-history-entries) and [document state](#7411-session-history-entries) is then used to bring a new [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) into being to take the place of the original, in the case where the user agent finds itself having to traverse to the entry.
  > 
  > If the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is *not* [destroyed](#7510-destroying-documents), then during [history traversal](#743-reloading-and-traversing), it can be [reactivated](#7462-updating-the-document). The cache in which browsers store such [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)s is often called a *back-forward cache*, or *bfcache* (or perhaps ["blazingly fast"](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=274784) cache).

- A history policy container, a [policy container](#717-policy-containers) or null, initially null.
- A request referrer, which is "`no-referrer`", "`client`", or a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url), initially "`client`".
- A request referrer policy, which is a [referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy), initially the [default referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#default-referrer-policy).

  > [!note]
  > The [request referrer policy](#7412-document-state) is distinct from the [history policy container](#7412-document-state)'s [referrer policy](#717-policy-containers). The former is used for fetches *of* this document, whereas the latter controls fetches *by* this document.

- An initiator origin, which is an [origin](#711-origins) or null, initially null.
- An origin, which is an [origin](#711-origins) or null, initially null.

  > [!note]
  > This is the origin that we set "`about:`"-schemed [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)s' [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) to. We store it here because it is also used when restoring these [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)s during traversal, since they are reconstructed locally without visiting the network. It is also used to compare the origin before and after the [session history entry](#7411-session-history-entries) is [repopulated](#745-populating-a-session-history-entry). If the origins change, the [navigable target name](#7412-document-state) is cleared.

- An about base URL, which is a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) or null, initially null.

  > [!note]
  > This will be populated only for "`about:`"-schemed [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)s and will be the [fallback base URL](#243-document-base-urls) for those [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)s. It is a snapshot of the initiator [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [document base URL](#243-document-base-urls).

- Nested histories, a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [nested histories](#7412-document-state), initially an empty [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).
- A resource, a string, [POST resource](#7412-document-state) or null, initially null.

  > [!note]
  > A string is treated as HTML. It's used to store the source of an [`iframe` `srcdoc` document](#485-the-iframe-element).

- A reload pending boolean, initially false.
- An ever populated boolean, initially false.
- A navigable target name string, initially the empty string.
- A not restored reasons, a [not restored reasons](#728-the-notrestoredreasons-interface) or null, initially null.

User agents may [destroy a document and its descendants](#7510-destroying-documents) given the [documents](#7412-document-state) of [document states](#7412-document-state) with non-null [documents](#7412-document-state), as long as the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents).

Apart from that restriction, this standard does not specify when user agents should destroy the [document](#7412-document-state) stored in a [document state](#7412-document-state), versus keeping it cached.

---

A POST resource has:
- A request body, a [byte sequence](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-byte-sequences) or failure.

  This is only ever accessed [in parallel](#211-parallelism), so it doesn't need to be stored in memory. However, it must return the same [byte sequence](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-byte-sequences) each time. If this isn't possible due to resources changing on disk, or if resources can no longer be accessed, then this must be set to failure.

- A request content-type, which is \`[`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-urlencoded)\`, \`[`multipart/form-data`](#mime-types)\`, or \`[`text/plain`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.1.3)\`.

---

A nested history has:
- An id, a [unique internal value](#2311-unique-internal-values).

  > [!note]
  > This is used to associate the [nested history](#7412-document-state) with a [navigable](#731-navigables).

- Entries, a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [session history entries](#7411-session-history-entries).

> [!warning]
> This will later contain ways to identify a child navigable across reloads.

---

---

Several contiguous entries in a session history can share the same [document state](#7411-session-history-entries). This can occur when the initial entry is reached via normal [navigation](#7422-beginning-navigation), and the following entry is added via [`history.pushState()`](#725-the-history-interface). Or it can occur via [navigation to a fragment](#74233-fragment-navigations).

> [!note]
> All entries that share the same [document state](#7411-session-history-entries) (and that are therefore merely different states of one particular document) are contiguous by construction.

---

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a latest entry, a [session history entry](#7411-session-history-entries) or null.

> [!note]
> This is the entry that was most recently represented by a given [`Document`](#311-the-document-object). A single [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) can represent many [session history entries](#7411-session-history-entries) over time, as many contiguous [session history entries](#7411-session-history-entries) can share the same [document state](#7411-session-history-entries) as explained above.

##### 7.4.1.3 Centralized modifications of session history

To maintain a single source of truth, all modifications to a [traversable navigable](#7311-traversable-navigables)'s [session history entries](#7311-traversable-navigables) need to be synchronized. This is especially important due to how session history is influenced by all of the descendant [navigables](#731-navigables), and thus by multiple [event loops](#8171-definitions). To accomplish this, we use the [session history traversal parallel queue](#7413-centralized-modifications-of-session-history) structure.

A session history traversal parallel queue is very similar to a [parallel queue](#211-parallelism). It has an algorithm set, an [ordered set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets).

The [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) in a [session history traversal parallel queue](#7413-centralized-modifications-of-session-history)'s [algorithm set](#7413-centralized-modifications-of-session-history) are either algorithm steps, or synchronous navigation steps, which are a particular brand of algorithm steps involving a target navigable (a [navigable](#731-navigables)).

To append session history traversal steps to a [traversable navigable](#7311-traversable-navigables) traversable given algorithm steps steps, [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) steps to traversable's [session history traversal queue](#7311-traversable-navigables)'s [algorithm set](#7413-centralized-modifications-of-session-history).

To append session history synchronous navigation steps involving a [navigable](#731-navigables) targetNavigable to a [traversable navigable](#7311-traversable-navigables) traversable given algorithm steps steps, [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) steps as [synchronous navigation steps](#7413-centralized-modifications-of-session-history) targeting [target navigable](#7413-centralized-modifications-of-session-history) targetNavigable to traversable's [session history traversal queue](#7311-traversable-navigables)'s [algorithm set](#7413-centralized-modifications-of-session-history).

To start a new session history traversal parallel queue:
1. Let sessionHistoryTraversalQueue be a new [session history traversal parallel queue](#7413-centralized-modifications-of-session-history).
2. Run the following steps [in parallel](#211-parallelism):
   1. While true:
      1. If sessionHistoryTraversalQueue's [algorithm set](#7413-centralized-modifications-of-session-history) is empty, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
      2. Let steps be the result of [dequeuing](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#512-queues) from sessionHistoryTraversalQueue's [algorithm set](#7413-centralized-modifications-of-session-history).
      3. Run steps.
3. Return sessionHistoryTraversalQueue.

[Synchronous navigation steps](#7413-centralized-modifications-of-session-history) are tagged in the [algorithm set](#7413-centralized-modifications-of-session-history) to allow them to conditionally "jump the queue". This is handled [within apply the history step](#7461-updating-the-traversable).

> [!example]
> Imagine the joint session history depicted by this [Jake diagram](#7314-jake-diagrams):
> 
> |  | 0 | 1 |
> | --- | --- | --- |
> | `top` | /a | /b |
> 
> And the following code runs at the top level:
> 
> ```javascript
> history.back();
> location.href = '#foo';
> ```
> 
> The desired result is:
> 
> |  | 0 | 1 | 2 |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> | `top` | /a | /b | /b#foo |
> 
> This isn't straightforward, as the sync navigation wins the race in terms of being observable, whereas the traversal wins the race in terms of queuing steps on the [session history traversal parallel queue](#7413-centralized-modifications-of-session-history). To achieve this result, the following happens:
> 1. [`history.back()`](#725-the-history-interface) [appends steps](#7413-centralized-modifications-of-session-history) intended to traverse by a delta of −1.
> 2. [`location.href = '#foo'`](#724-the-location-interface) synchronously changes the [active session history entry](#731-navigables) entry to a newly-created one, with the URL `/b#foo`, and [appends synchronous steps](#7413-centralized-modifications-of-session-history) to notify the central source of truth about that new entry. Note that this does *not* yet update the [current session history entry](#731-navigables), [current session history step](#7311-traversable-navigables), or the [session history entries](#7311-traversable-navigables) list; those updates cannot be done synchronously, and instead must be done as part of the queued steps.
> 3. On the [session history traversal parallel queue](#7413-centralized-modifications-of-session-history), the steps queued by [`history.back()`](#725-the-history-interface) run:
>    1. The target history step is determined to be 0: the [current session history step](#7311-traversable-navigables) (i.e., 1) plus the intended delta of −1.
>    2. We enter the main [apply the history step](#7461-updating-the-traversable) algorithm.
> 
>       The entry at step 0, for the `/a` URL, has its [document](#7411-session-history-entries) [populated](#745-populating-a-session-history-entry).
> 
>       Meanwhile, the queue is checked for [synchronous navigation steps](#7413-centralized-modifications-of-session-history). The steps queued by the [`location.href`](#724-the-location-interface) setter now run, and block the traversal from performing effects beyond document population (such as, unloading documents and switching active history entries) until they are finished. Those steps cause the following to happen:
>       1. The entry with URL `/b#foo` is added, with its [step](#7411-session-history-entries) determined to be 2: the [current session history step](#7311-traversable-navigables) (i.e., 1) plus 1.
>       2. We fully switch to that newly added entry, including a nested call to [apply the history step](#7461-updating-the-traversable). This ultimately results in [updating the document](#7462-updating-the-document) by dispatching events like [`hashchange`](#events).
> 
>       Only once that is all complete, and the `/a` history entry has been fully populated with a [document](#7411-session-history-entries), do we move on with applying the history step given the target step of 0.
> 
>       At this point, the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) with URL `/b#foo` [unloads](#759-unloading-documents), and we finish moving to our target history step 0, which makes the entry with URL `/a` become the [active session history entry](#731-navigables) and 0 become the [current session history step](#7311-traversable-navigables).

> [!example]
> Here is another more complex example, involving races between populating two different [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element)s, and a synchronous navigation once one of those iframes loads. We start with this setup:
> 
> |  | 0 | 1 | 2 |
> | --- | --- | --- | --- |
> | `top` | /t |
> | `frames[0]` | /i-0-a | /i-0-b |
> | `frames[1]` | /i-1-a | /i-1-b |
> 
> and then call [`history.go(-2)`](#725-the-history-interface). The following then occurs:
> 1. [`history.go(-2)`](#725-the-history-interface) [appends steps](#7413-centralized-modifications-of-session-history) intended to traverse by a delta of −2. Once those steps run:
>    1. The target step is determined to be 2 + (−2) = 0.
>    2. In parallel, the fetches are made to [populate](#745-populating-a-session-history-entry) the two iframes, fetching `/i-0-a` and `/i-1-a` respectively.
> 
>       Meanwhile, the queue is checked for [synchronous navigation steps](#7413-centralized-modifications-of-session-history). There aren't any right now.
> 
>    3. In the fetch race, the fetch for `/i-0-a` wins. We proceed onward to finish all of [apply the history step](#7461-updating-the-traversable)'s work for how the traversal impacts the `frames[0]` [navigable](#731-navigables), including updating its [active session history entry](#731-navigables) to the entry with URL `/i-0-a`.
>    4. Before the fetch for `/i-1-a` finishes, we reach the point where [scripts may run for the newly-created document](#7462-updating-the-document) in the `frames[0]` [navigable](#731-navigables)'s [active document](#731-navigables). Some such script does run:
> 
>       ```javascript
>       location.href = '#foo'
>       ```
> 
>       This synchronously changes the `frames[0]` navigable's [active session history entry](#731-navigables) entry to a newly-created one, with the URL `/i-0-a#foo`, and [appends synchronous steps](#7413-centralized-modifications-of-session-history) to notify the central source of truth about that new entry.
> 
>       Unlike in the [previous example](#7413-centralized-modifications-of-session-history), these synchronous steps do *not* "jump the queue" and update the [traversable](#7311-traversable-navigables) before we finish the fetch for `/i-1-a`. This is because the navigable in question, `frames[0]`, has already been altered as part of the traversal, so we know that with the [current session history step](#7311-traversable-navigables) being 2, adding the new entry as a step 3 doesn't make sense.
> 
>    5. Once the fetch for `/i-1-a` finally finishes, we proceed to finish updating the `frames[1]` [navigable](#731-navigables) for the traversal, including updating its [active session history entry](#731-navigables) to the entry with URL `/i-1-a`.
>    6. Now that both navigables have finished processing the traversal, we update the [current session history step](#7311-traversable-navigables) to the target step of 0.
> 
> 2. Now we can process the steps that were queued for the synchronous navigation:
>    1. The `/i-0-a#foo` entry is added, with its [step](#7411-session-history-entries) determined to be 1: the [current session history step](#7311-traversable-navigables) (i.e., 0) plus 1. This also [clears existing forward history](#7414-low-level-operations-on-session-history).
>    2. We fully switch to that newly added entry, including calling [apply the history step](#7461-updating-the-traversable). This ultimately results in [updating the document](#7462-updating-the-document) by dispatching events like [`hashchange`](#events), as well as updating the [current session history step](#7311-traversable-navigables) to the target step of 1.
> 
> The end result is:
> 
> |  | 0 | 1 |
> | --- | --- | --- |
> | `top` | /t |
> | `frames[0]` | /i-0-a | /i-0-a#foo |
> | `frames[1]` | /i-1-a |

##### 7.4.1.4 Low-level operations on session history

This section contains a miscellaneous grab-bag of operations that we perform throughout the standard when manipulating session history. The best way to get a sense of what they do is to look at their call sites.

To get session history entries of a [navigable](#731-navigables) navigable:
1. Let traversable be navigable's [traversable navigable](#7311-traversable-navigables).
2. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): this is running within traversable's [session history traversal queue](#7311-traversable-navigables).
3. If navigable is traversable, return traversable's [session history entries](#7311-traversable-navigables).
4. Let docStates be an empty [ordered set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) of [document states](#7412-document-state).
5. For each entry of traversable's [session history entries](#7311-traversable-navigables), [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) entry's [document state](#7411-session-history-entries) to docStates.
6. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) docState of docStates:
   1. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) nestedHistory of docState's [nested histories](#7412-document-state):
      1. If nestedHistory's [id](#7412-document-state) equals navigable's [id](#731-navigables), return nestedHistory's [entries](#7412-document-state).
      2. For each entry of nestedHistory's [entries](#7412-document-state), [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) entry's [document state](#7411-session-history-entries) to docStates.
7. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): this step is not reached.

To get session history entries for the navigation API of a [navigable](#731-navigables) navigable given an integer targetStep:
1. Let rawEntries be the result of [getting session history entries](#7414-low-level-operations-on-session-history) for navigable.
2. Let entriesForNavigationAPI be a new empty [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).
3. Let startingIndex be the index of the [session history entry](#7411-session-history-entries) in rawEntries who has the greatest [step](#7411-session-history-entries) less than or equal to targetStep.

   > [!note]
   > See [this example](#7461-updating-the-traversable) to understand why it's the greatest step less than or equal to targetStep.

4. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) rawEntries\[startingIndex\] to entriesForNavigationAPI.
5. Let startingOrigin be rawEntries\[startingIndex\]'s [document state](#7411-session-history-entries)'s [origin](#7412-document-state).
6. Let i be startingIndex − 1.
7. While i > 0:
   1. If rawEntries\[i\]'s [document state](#7411-session-history-entries)'s [origin](#7412-document-state) is not [same origin](#711-origins) with startingOrigin, then [break](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   2. [Prepend](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) rawEntries\[i\] to entriesForNavigationAPI.
   3. Set i to i − 1.
8. Set i to startingIndex + 1.
9. While i < rawEntries's [size](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists):
   1. If rawEntries\[i\]'s [document state](#7411-session-history-entries)'s [origin](#7412-document-state) is not [same origin](#711-origins) with startingOrigin, then [break](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   2. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) rawEntries\[i\] to entriesForNavigationAPI.
   3. Set i to i + 1.
10. Return entriesForNavigationAPI.

To clear the forward session history of a [traversable navigable](#7311-traversable-navigables) navigable:
1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): this is running within navigable's [session history traversal queue](#7311-traversable-navigables).
2. Let step be the navigable's [current session history step](#7311-traversable-navigables).
3. Let entryLists be the [ordered set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) « navigable's [session history entries](#7311-traversable-navigables) ».
4. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) entryList of entryLists:
   1. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) every [session history entry](#7411-session-history-entries) from entryList that has a [step](#7411-session-history-entries) greater than step.
   2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) entry of entryList:
      1. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) nestedHistory of entry's [document state](#7411-session-history-entries)'s [nested histories](#7412-document-state), [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) nestedHistory's [entries list](#7412-document-state) to entryLists.

To get all used history steps that are part of [traversable navigable](#7311-traversable-navigables) traversable:
1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): this is running within traversable's [session history traversal queue](#7311-traversable-navigables).
2. Let steps be an empty [ordered set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) of non-negative integers.
3. Let entryLists be the [ordered set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) « traversable's [session history entries](#7311-traversable-navigables) ».
4. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) entryList of entryLists:
   1. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) entry of entryList:
      1. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) entry's [step](#7411-session-history-entries) to steps.
      2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) nestedHistory of entry's [document state](#7411-session-history-entries)'s [nested histories](#7412-document-state), [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) nestedHistory's [entries list](#7412-document-state) to entryLists.
5. Return steps, [sorted](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).

#### 7.4.2 Navigation

Certain actions cause a [navigable](#731-navigables) to *[navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation)* to a new resource.

> [!example]
> For example, [following a hyperlink](#465-following-hyperlinks), [form submission](#410223-form-submission-algorithm), and the [`window.open()`](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows) and [`location.assign()`](#724-the-location-interface) methods can all cause navigation.

> [!note]
> Although in this standard the word "navigation" refers specifically to the [navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation) algorithm, this doesn't always line up with web developer or user perceptions. For example:
> - The [URL and history update steps](#744-non-fragment-synchronous-navigations) are often used during so-called "single-page app navigations" or "same-document navigations", but they do not trigger the [navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation) algorithm.
> - [Reloads](#743-reloading-and-traversing) and [traversals](#743-reloading-and-traversing) are sometimes talked about as a type of navigation, since all three will often [attempt to populate the history entry's document](#745-populating-a-session-history-entry) and thus could perform navigational fetches. See, e.g., the APIs exposed Navigation Timing. But they have their own entry point algorithms, separate from the [navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation) algorithm. [\[NAVIGATIONTIMING\]](#references)
> - Although [fragment navigations](#74233-fragment-navigations) are always done through the [navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation) algorithm, a user might perceive them as more like jumping around a single page, than as a true navigation.

##### 7.4.2.1 Supporting concepts

Before we can jump into the [navigation algorithm](#7422-beginning-navigation) itself, we need to establish several important structures that it uses.

The source snapshot params [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) is used to capture data from a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) initiating a navigation. It is snapshotted at the beginning of a navigation and used throughout the navigation's lifetime. It has the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):

has transient activation

a boolean

sandboxing flags

a [sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing)

allows downloading

a boolean

fetch client

an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) or null, only to be used as a [request client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client)

source policy container

a [policy container](#717-policy-containers)

To snapshot source snapshot params given a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)-or-null sourceDocument:
1. If sourceDocument is null, then return a new [source snapshot params](#7421-supporting-concepts) with

   [has transient activation](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   true

   [sandboxing flags](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   an empty [sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing)

   [allows downloading](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   true

   [fetch client](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   null

   [source policy container](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   a new [policy container](#717-policy-containers)

   > [!note]
   > This [only occurs](#7422-beginning-navigation) in the case of a browser UI-initiated navigation.

2. Return a new [source snapshot params](#7421-supporting-concepts) with

   [has transient activation](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   true if sourceDocument's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) has [transient activation](#641-data-model); otherwise false

   [sandboxing flags](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   sourceDocument's [active sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing)

   [allows downloading](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   false if sourceDocument's [active sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing) has the [sandboxed downloads browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing) set; otherwise true

   [fetch client](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   sourceDocument's [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant)

   [source policy container](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   a [clone](#717-policy-containers) of sourceDocument's [policy container](#311-the-document-object)

---

The target snapshot params [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) is used to capture data from a [navigable](#731-navigables) being navigated. Like [source snapshot params](#7421-supporting-concepts), it is snapshotted at the beginning of a navigation and used throughout the navigation's lifetime. It has the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):

sandboxing flags

a [sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing)

`iframe` element referrer policy

a [referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy)

To snapshot target snapshot params given a [navigable](#731-navigables) targetNavigable, return a new [target snapshot params](#7421-supporting-concepts) with:

[sandboxing flags](#7421-supporting-concepts)

the result of [determining the creation sandboxing flags](#715-sandboxing) given targetNavigable's [active browsing context](#731-navigables) and targetNavigable's [container](#7313-child-navigables)

[`iframe` element referrer policy](#7421-supporting-concepts)

the result of [determining the `iframe` element referrer policy](#716-iframe-element-referrer-policy) given targetNavigable's [container](#7313-child-navigables)

---

Much of the navigation process is concerned with determining how to create a new [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), which ultimately happens in the [create and initialize a `Document` object](#751-shared-document-creation-infrastructure) algorithm. The parameters to that algorithm are tracked via a navigation params [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs), which has the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):

id

null or a [navigation ID](#7421-supporting-concepts)

navigable

the [navigable](#731-navigables) to be navigated

request

null or a [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) that started the navigation

response

a [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) that ultimately was navigated to (potentially a [network error](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-network-error))

fetch controller

null or a [fetch controller](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-controller)

commit early hints

null or an algorithm accepting a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), once it has been created

COOP enforcement result

an [opener policy enforcement result](#7132-browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-opener-policy), used for reporting and potentially for causing a [browsing context group switch](#7132-browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-opener-policy)

reserved environment

null or an [environment](#8131-environments) reserved for the new [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)

origin

an [origin](#711-origins) to use for the new [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)

policy container

a [policy container](#717-policy-containers) to use for the new [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)

final sandboxing flag set

a [sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing) to impose on the new [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)

`iframe` element referrer policy

a [referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy), used in the [internal ancestor origin objects list creation steps](#313-ancestor-origins)

opener policy

an [opener policy](#713-cross-origin-opener-policies) to use for the new [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)

navigation timing type

a [`NavigationTimingType`](https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-navigationtimingtype) used for [creating the navigation timing entry](https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dfn-create-the-navigation-timing-entry) for the new [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)

about base URL

a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) or null used to populate the new [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [about base URL](#311-the-document-object)

user involvement

a [user navigation involvement](#7421-supporting-concepts) used when [obtaining a browsing context](#7132-browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-opener-policy) for the new [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)

> [!note]
> Once a [navigation params](#7421-supporting-concepts) struct is created, this standard does not mutate any of its [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs). They are only passed onward to other algorithms.

---

A navigation ID is a UUID string generated during navigation. It is used to interface with the WebDriver BiDi specification as well as to track the [ongoing navigation](#7425-aborting-navigation). [\[WEBDRIVERBIDI\]](#references)

---

After [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) creation, the relevant [traversable navigable](#7311-traversable-navigables)'s [session history](#7311-traversable-navigables) gets updated. The [`NavigationHistoryBehavior`](#7262-the-navigation-interface) enumeration is used to indicate the desired type of session history update to the [navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation) algorithm. It is one of the following:

"`push`"

A regular navigation which adds a new [session history entry](#7411-session-history-entries), and will [clear the forward session history](#7414-low-level-operations-on-session-history).

"`replace`"

A navigation that will replace the [active session history entry](#731-navigables).

"`auto`"

The default value, which will be converted very early in the [navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation) algorithm into "[`push`](#7421-supporting-concepts)" or "[`replace`](#7421-supporting-concepts)". Usually it becomes "[`push`](#7421-supporting-concepts)", but under [certain circumstances](#7422-beginning-navigation) it becomes "[`replace`](#7421-supporting-concepts)" instead.

A history handling behavior is a [`NavigationHistoryBehavior`](#7262-the-navigation-interface) that is either "[`push`](#7421-supporting-concepts)" or "[`replace`](#7421-supporting-concepts)", i.e., that has been resolved away from any initial "[`auto`](#7421-supporting-concepts)" value.

The navigation must be a replace, given a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) url and a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document, if any of the following are true:
- url's [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) is "[`javascript`](#74232-the-javascript-url-special-case)"; or
- document's [is initial `about:blank`](#311-the-document-object) is true.

> [!note]
> Other cases that often, but not always, force a "[`replace`](#7421-supporting-concepts)" navigation are:
> - if the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is not [completely loaded](#758-finishing-the-loading-process); or
> - if the target [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) equals the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

---

Various parts of the platform track whether a user is involved in a navigation. A user navigation involvement is one of the following:

"`browser UI`"

The navigation was initiated by the user via browser UI mechanisms.

"`activation`"

The navigation was initiated by the user via the [activation behavior](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) of an element.

"`none`"

The navigation was not initiated by the user.

For convenience at certain call sites, the user navigation involvement for an [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) event is defined as follows:
1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): this algorithm is being called as part of an [activation behavior](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) definition.
2. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): event's [`type`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) is "[`click`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click)".
3. If event's [`isTrusted`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) is initialized to true, then return "[`activation`](#7421-supporting-concepts)".
4. Return "[`none`](#7421-supporting-concepts)".

##### 7.4.2.2 Beginning navigation

To navigate a [navigable](#731-navigables) navigable to a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) url using an optional [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)-or-null sourceDocument (default null), with an optional [POST resource](#7412-document-state), string, or null documentResource (default null), an optional [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response)-or-null response (default null), an optional boolean exceptionsEnabled (default false), an optional [`NavigationHistoryBehavior`](#7262-the-navigation-interface) historyHandling (default "[`auto`](#7421-supporting-concepts)"), an optional [serialized state](#7411-session-history-entries)-or-null navigationAPIState (default null), an optional [entry list](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) or null formDataEntryList (default null), an optional [referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy) referrerPolicy (default the empty string), an optional [user navigation involvement](#7421-supporting-concepts) userInvolvement (default "[`none`](#7421-supporting-concepts)"), an optional [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) sourceElement (default null), an optional boolean initialInsertion (default false), and an optional [navigation API method tracker](#7268-ongoing-navigation-tracking)-or-null apiMethodTracker (default null):
1. Let cspNavigationType be "`form-submission`" if formDataEntryList is non-null; otherwise "`other`".
2. Let sourceSnapshotParams be the result of [snapshotting source snapshot params](#7421-supporting-concepts) given sourceDocument.
3. Let initiatorOriginSnapshot be a new [opaque origin](#711-origins).
4. Let initiatorBaseURLSnapshot be [`about:blank`](#219-dependencies).
5. If sourceDocument is null:
   1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): userInvolvement is "[`browser UI`](#7421-supporting-concepts)".
   2. If url's [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) is "[`javascript`](#74232-the-javascript-url-special-case)", then set initiatorOriginSnapshot to navigable's [active document](#731-navigables)'s [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).
6. Otherwise:
   1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): userInvolvement is not "[`browser UI`](#7421-supporting-concepts)".
   2. If sourceDocument's [node navigable](#731-navigables) is not [allowed by sandboxing to navigate](#7424-preventing-navigation) navigable given sourceSnapshotParams:
      1. If exceptionsEnabled is true, then throw a ["`SecurityError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
      2. Return.
   3. Set initiatorOriginSnapshot to sourceDocument's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).
   4. Set initiatorBaseURLSnapshot to sourceDocument's [document base URL](#243-document-base-urls).
7. Let navigationId be the result of [generating a random UUID](https://w3c.github.io/webcrypto/#dfn-generate-a-random-uuid). [\[WEBCRYPTO\]](#references)
8. If the [surrounding agent](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#surrounding-agent) is equal to navigable's [active document](#731-navigables)'s [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism), then continue these steps. Otherwise, [queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [navigation and traversal task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given navigable's [active window](#731-navigables) to continue these steps.

   > [!note]
   > We do this because we are about to look at a lot of properties of navigable's [active document](#731-navigables), which are in theory only accessible over in the appropriate [event loop](#8171-definitions). (But, we do not want to unconditionally queue a task, since — for example — same-event-loop [fragment navigations](#74233-fragment-navigations) need to take effect synchronously.)
   > 
   > Another implementation strategy would be to replicate the relevant information across event loops, or into a canonical "browser process", so that it can be consulted without queueing a task. This could give different results than what we specify here in edge cases, where the relevant properties have changed over in the target event loop but not yet been replicated. Further testing is needed to determine which of these strategies best matches browser behavior, in such racy edge cases.

9. If navigable's [active document](#731-navigables)'s [unload counter](#759-unloading-documents) is greater than 0, then invoke [WebDriver BiDi navigation failed](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-navigation-failed) with navigable and a [WebDriver BiDi navigation status](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-navigation-status) whose [id](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-id) is navigationId, [status](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-status) is "[`canceled`](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-canceled)", and [url](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-url) is url, and return.
10. Let container be navigable's [container](#7313-child-navigables).
11. If container is an [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) element and [will lazy load element steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) given container returns true, then [stop intersection-observing a lazy loading element](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) container and set container's [lazy load resumption steps](#257-lazy-loading-attributes) to null.
12. If navigable's [allowed to perform a navigation or history update](#731-navigables) returns [blocked](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-singletons), then invoke [WebDriver BiDi navigation failed](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-navigation-failed) with navigable and a [WebDriver BiDi navigation status](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-navigation-status) whose [id](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-id) is navigationId, [status](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-status) is "[`canceled`](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-canceled)", and [url](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-url) is url, and return.
13. If historyHandling is "[`auto`](#7421-supporting-concepts)":
    1. If url [equals](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-equals) navigable's [active document](#731-navigables)'s [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), and either userInvolvement is "[`browser UI`](#7421-supporting-concepts)" or initiatorOriginSnapshot is [same origin](#711-origins) with navigable's [active document](#731-navigables)'s [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), then set historyHandling to "[`replace`](#7421-supporting-concepts)".
    2. Otherwise, set historyHandling to "[`push`](#7421-supporting-concepts)".
14. If [the navigation must be a replace](#7421-supporting-concepts) given url and navigable's [active document](#731-navigables), then set historyHandling to "[`replace`](#7421-supporting-concepts)".
15. If all of the following are true:
    - documentResource is null;
    - response is null;
    - url [equals](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-equals) navigable's [active session history entry](#731-navigables)'s [URL](#7411-session-history-entries) with [*exclude fragments*](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-equals-exclude-fragments) set to true; and
    - url's [fragment](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment) is non-null,

    then:
    1. [Navigate to a fragment](#74233-fragment-navigations) given navigable, url, historyHandling, userInvolvement, sourceElement, navigationAPIState, and navigationId.
    2. Return.

16. If navigable's [parent](#731-navigables) is non-null, then set navigable's [is delaying `load` events](#731-navigables) to true.
17. Let targetSnapshotParams be the result of [snapshotting target snapshot params](#7421-supporting-concepts) given navigable.
18. Invoke [WebDriver BiDi navigation started](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-navigation-started) with navigable and a new [WebDriver BiDi navigation status](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-navigation-status) whose [id](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-id) is navigationId, [status](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-status) is "[`pending`](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-pending)", and [url](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-url) is url.
19. If navigable's [ongoing navigation](#7425-aborting-navigation) is "`traversal`":
    1. Invoke [WebDriver BiDi navigation failed](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-navigation-failed) with navigable and a new [WebDriver BiDi navigation status](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-navigation-status) whose [id](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-id) is navigationId, [status](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-status) is "[`canceled`](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-canceled)", and [url](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-url) is url.
    2. Return.

    > [!note]
    > Any attempts to navigate a [navigable](#731-navigables) that is currently [traversing](#7461-updating-the-traversable) are ignored.

20. [Set the ongoing navigation](#7425-aborting-navigation) for navigable to navigationId.

    > [!note]
    > This will have the effect of aborting other ongoing navigations of navigable, since at certain points during navigation changes to the [ongoing navigation](#7425-aborting-navigation) will cause further work to be abandoned.

21. If url's [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) is "[`javascript`](#74232-the-javascript-url-special-case)":
    1. Let request be a new [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request), with

       [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url)

       url

       [client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client)

       sourceSnapshotParams's [fetch client](#7421-supporting-concepts)

       [policy container](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-policy-container)

       sourceSnapshotParams's [source policy container](#7421-supporting-concepts)

       > [!note]
       > This is a synthetic [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request), needed because the Content Security Policy check in [navigate to a `javascript:` URL](#74232-the-javascript-url-special-case) operates on a [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request). It will never hit the network.

    2. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [navigation and traversal task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given navigable's [active window](#731-navigables) to [navigate to a `javascript:` URL](#74232-the-javascript-url-special-case) given navigable, request, historyHandling, initiatorOriginSnapshot, userInvolvement, cspNavigationType, initialInsertion, and navigationId.
    3. Return.

22. If all of the following are true:
    - userInvolvement is not "[`browser
           UI`](#7421-supporting-concepts)";
    - navigable's [active document](#731-navigables)'s [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is [same origin-domain](#711-origins) with sourceDocument's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document);
    - navigable's [active document](#731-navigables)'s [is initial `about:blank`](#311-the-document-object) is false; and
    - url's [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) is a [fetch scheme](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-scheme),

    then:
    1. Let navigation be navigable's [active window](#731-navigables)'s [navigation API](#7262-the-navigation-interface).
    2. Let entryListForFiring be formDataEntryList if documentResource is a [POST resource](#7412-document-state); otherwise, null.
    3. Let navigationAPIStateForFiring be navigationAPIState if navigationAPIState is not null; otherwise, [StructuredSerializeForStorage](#275-structuredserializeforstorage--value-)(undefined).
    4. Let continue be the result of [firing a push/replace/reload `navigate` event](#726104-firing-the-event) at navigation with *[navigationType](#726104-firing-the-event)* set to historyHandling, *[isSameDocument](#726104-firing-the-event)* set to false, *[userInvolvement](#726104-firing-the-event)* set to userInvolvement, *[sourceElement](#726104-firing-the-event)* set to sourceElement, *[formDataEntryList](#726104-firing-the-event)* set to entryListForFiring, *[destinationURL](#726104-firing-the-event)* set to url, *[navigationAPIState](#726104-firing-the-event)* set to navigationAPIStateForFiring, and *[apiMethodTracker](#726104-firing-the-event)* set to apiMethodTracker.
    5. If continue is false, then return.

    > [!note]
    > It is possible for navigations with userInvolvement of "[`browser UI`](#7421-supporting-concepts)" or initiated by a [cross origin-domain](#711-origins) sourceDocument to fire [`navigate`](#events) events, if they go through the earlier [navigate to a fragment](#74233-fragment-navigations) path.

23. If sourceDocument is navigable's [container document](#7313-child-navigables), then [reserve deferred fetch quota](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#reserve-deferred-fetch-quota) for navigable's [container](#7313-child-navigables) given url's [origin](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-origin).
24. [In parallel](#211-parallelism), run these steps:
    1. Let unloadPromptCanceled be the result of [checking if unloading is canceled](#7424-preventing-navigation) for navigable's [active document](#731-navigables)'s [inclusive descendant navigables](#7315-related-navigable-collections).
    2. If unloadPromptCanceled is not "`continue`", or navigable's [ongoing navigation](#7425-aborting-navigation) is no longer navigationId:
       1. Invoke [WebDriver BiDi navigation failed](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-navigation-failed) with navigable and a new [WebDriver BiDi navigation status](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-navigation-status) whose [id](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-id) is navigationId, [status](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-status) is "[`canceled`](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-canceled)", and [url](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-url) is url.
       2. Abort these steps.
    3. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [navigation and traversal task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given navigable's [active window](#731-navigables) to [abort a document and its descendants](#7511-aborting-a-document-load) given navigable's [active document](#731-navigables).
    4. Let documentState be a new [document state](#7412-document-state) with

       [request referrer policy](#7412-document-state)

       referrerPolicy

       [initiator origin](#7412-document-state)

       initiatorOriginSnapshot

       [resource](#7412-document-state)

       documentResource

       [navigable target name](#7412-document-state)

       navigable's [target name](#731-navigables)

       > [!note]
       > The [navigable target name](#7412-document-state) can get cleared under various conditions later in the navigation process, before the document state is finalized.

    5. If url [matches `about:blank`](#241-terminology) or is [`about:srcdoc`](#241-terminology):
       1. Set documentState's [origin](#7412-document-state) to initiatorOriginSnapshot.
       2. Set documentState's [about base URL](#7412-document-state) to initiatorBaseURLSnapshot.
    6. Let historyEntry be a new [session history entry](#7411-session-history-entries), with its [URL](#7411-session-history-entries) set to url and its [document state](#7411-session-history-entries) set to documentState.
    7. Let navigationParams be null.
    8. If response is non-null:

       > [!note]
       > The [navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation) algorithm is only supplied with a [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) as part of the [`object`](#487-the-object-element) and [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element) processing models, or for processing parts of [`multipart/x-mixed-replace` responses](#755-loading-multipartx-mixed-replace-documents) after the initial response.
       1. Let sourcePolicyContainer be a [clone](#717-policy-containers) of the sourceDocument's [policy container](#311-the-document-object), if sourceDocument is not null; otherwise null.
       2. Let policyContainer be the result of [determining navigation params policy container](#717-policy-containers) given response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url), null, sourcePolicyContainer, navigable's [container document](#7313-child-navigables)'s [policy container](#311-the-document-object), and null.
       3. Let finalSandboxFlags be the [union](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) of targetSnapshotParams's [sandboxing flags](#7421-supporting-concepts) and policyContainer's [CSP list](#717-policy-containers)'s [CSP-derived sandboxing flags](#715-sandboxing).
       4. Let responseOrigin be the result of [determining the origin](#7321-creating-browsing-contexts) given response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url), finalSandboxFlags, and documentState's [initiator origin](#7412-document-state).
       5. Let coop be a new [opener policy](#713-cross-origin-opener-policies).
       6. Let coopEnforcementResult be a new [opener policy enforcement result](#7132-browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-opener-policy) with

          [url](#7132-browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-opener-policy)

          response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url)

          [origin](#7132-browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-opener-policy)

          responseOrigin

          [opener policy](#7132-browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-opener-policy)

          coop

       7. Set navigationParams to a new [navigation params](#7421-supporting-concepts), with

          [id](#7421-supporting-concepts)

          navigationId

          [navigable](#7421-supporting-concepts)

          navigable

          [request](#7421-supporting-concepts)

          null

          [response](#7421-supporting-concepts)

          response

          [fetch controller](#7421-supporting-concepts)

          null

          [commit early hints](#7421-supporting-concepts)

          null

          [COOP enforcement result](#7421-supporting-concepts)

          coopEnforcementResult

          [reserved environment](#7421-supporting-concepts)

          null

          [origin](#7421-supporting-concepts)

          responseOrigin

          [policy container](#7421-supporting-concepts)

          policyContainer

          [final sandboxing flag set](#7421-supporting-concepts)

          finalSandboxFlags

          [`iframe` element referrer policy](#7421-supporting-concepts)

          targetSnapshotParams's [`iframe` element referrer policy](#7421-supporting-concepts)

          [opener policy](#7421-supporting-concepts)

          coop

          [navigation timing type](#7421-supporting-concepts)

          "[`navigate`](https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-navigationtimingtype-navigate)"

          [about base URL](#7421-supporting-concepts)

          documentState's [about base URL](#7412-document-state)

          [user involvement](#7421-supporting-concepts)

          userInvolvement

    9. [Attempt to populate the history entry's document](#745-populating-a-session-history-entry) for historyEntry, given navigable, "[`navigate`](https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-navigationtimingtype-navigate)", sourceSnapshotParams, targetSnapshotParams, userInvolvement, navigationId, navigationParams, cspNavigationType, with *[allowPOST](#745-populating-a-session-history-entry)* set to true and *[completionSteps](#745-populating-a-session-history-entry)* set to the following step:
       1. [Append session history traversal steps](#7413-centralized-modifications-of-session-history) to navigable's [traversable navigable](#7311-traversable-navigables) to [finalize a cross-document navigation](#74231-the-usual-cross-document-navigation-case) given navigable, historyHandling, userInvolvement, and historyEntry.

##### 7.4.2.3 Ending navigation

Although the usual cross-document navigation case will first foray into [populating a session history entry](#745-populating-a-session-history-entry) with a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), all navigations that don't get aborted will ultimately end up calling into one of the below algorithms.

###### 7.4.2.3.1 The usual cross-document navigation case

To finalize a cross-document navigation given a [navigable](#731-navigables) navigable, a [history handling behavior](#7421-supporting-concepts) historyHandling, a [user navigation involvement](#7421-supporting-concepts) userInvolvement, and a [session history entry](#7411-session-history-entries) historyEntry:
1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): this is running on navigable's [traversable navigable](#7311-traversable-navigables)'s [session history traversal queue](#7311-traversable-navigables).
2. Set navigable's [is delaying `load` events](#731-navigables) to false.
3. If historyEntry's [document](#7411-session-history-entries) is null, then return.

   > [!note]
   > This means that [attempting to populate the history entry's document](#745-populating-a-session-history-entry) ended up not creating a document, as a result of e.g., the navigation being canceled by a subsequent navigation, a 204 No Content response, etc.

4. If all of the following are true:
   - navigable's [parent](#731-navigables) is null;
   - historyEntry's [document](#7411-session-history-entries)'s [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) is not an [auxiliary browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) whose [opener browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) is non-null; and
   - historyEntry's [document](#7411-session-history-entries)'s [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is not [same origin](#711-origins) with navigable's [active document](#731-navigables)'s [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document),

   then set historyEntry's [document state](#7411-session-history-entries)'s [navigable target name](#7412-document-state) to the empty string.

5. Let entryToReplace be navigable's [active session history entry](#731-navigables) if historyHandling is "[`replace`](#7421-supporting-concepts)", otherwise null.
6. Let traversable be navigable's [traversable navigable](#7311-traversable-navigables).
7. Let targetStep be null.
8. Let targetEntries be the result of [getting session history entries](#7414-low-level-operations-on-session-history) for navigable.
9. If entryToReplace is null:
   1. [Clear the forward session history](#7414-low-level-operations-on-session-history) of traversable.
   2. Set targetStep to traversable's [current session history step](#7311-traversable-navigables) + 1.
   3. Set historyEntry's [step](#7411-session-history-entries) to targetStep.
   4. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) historyEntry to targetEntries.

   Otherwise:
   1. [Replace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) entryToReplace with historyEntry in targetEntries.
   2. Set historyEntry's [step](#7411-session-history-entries) to entryToReplace's [step](#7411-session-history-entries).
   3. If historyEntry's [document state](#7411-session-history-entries)'s [origin](#7412-document-state) is [same origin](#711-origins) with entryToReplace's [document state](#7411-session-history-entries)'s [origin](#7412-document-state), then set historyEntry's [navigation API key](#7411-session-history-entries) to entryToReplace's [navigation API key](#7411-session-history-entries).
   4. Set targetStep to traversable's [current session history step](#7311-traversable-navigables).

10. [Apply the push/replace history step](#7461-updating-the-traversable) targetStep to traversable given historyHandling and userInvolvement.

###### 7.4.2.3.2 The `javascript:` URL special case

> [!warning]
> [`javascript:`](#74232-the-javascript-url-special-case) URLs have a [dedicated label](https://github.com/whatwg/html/labels/topic%3A%20javascript%3A%20URLs) on the issue tracker documenting various problems with their specification.

To navigate to a `javascript:` URL, given a [navigable](#731-navigables) targetNavigable, a [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) request, a [history handling behavior](#7421-supporting-concepts) historyHandling, an [origin](#711-origins) initiatorOrigin, a [user navigation involvement](#7421-supporting-concepts) userInvolvement, a string cspNavigationType, a boolean initialInsertion, and a [navigation ID](#7421-supporting-concepts) navigationId:
1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): historyHandling is "[`replace`](#7421-supporting-concepts)".
2. If targetNavigable's [ongoing navigation](#7425-aborting-navigation) is no longer navigationId, then return.
3. [Set the ongoing navigation](#7425-aborting-navigation) for targetNavigable to null.
4. If initiatorOrigin is not [same origin-domain](#711-origins) with targetNavigable's [active document](#731-navigables)'s [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), then return.
5. If the result of [should navigation request of type be blocked by Content Security Policy?](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#should-block-navigation-request) given request and cspNavigationType is "`Blocked`", then return. [\[CSP\]](#references)

   > [!note]
   > This can change request's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url), as the [`require-trusted-types-for` pre-navigation check](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#require-trusted-types-for-pre-navigation-check) passes the script source through the default policy. [\[TRUSTED-TYPES\]](#references)

6. Let newDocument be the result of [evaluating a `javascript:` URL](#74232-the-javascript-url-special-case) given targetNavigable, request's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url), initiatorOrigin, userInvolvement, and navigationId.
7. If newDocument is null:
   1. Let container be targetNavigable's [container](#7313-child-navigables).
   2. If initialInsertion is true, container is non-null, and targetNavigable's [active document](#731-navigables)'s [is initial `about:blank`](#311-the-document-object) is true:
      1. If container is an [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) element, then run the [iframe load event steps](#485-the-iframe-element) given container.
      2. Otherwise, [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`load`](#events) at container.

      > [!note]
      > container can be null if author code, such as the Trusted Types default policy or `javascript:frameElement.remove()`, removed it.

   3. Return.

   > [!note]
   > In this case, some JavaScript code was executed, but no new [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) was created, so we will not perform a navigation.

8. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): initiatorOrigin is newDocument's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).
9. Let entryToReplace be targetNavigable's [active session history entry](#731-navigables).
10. Let oldDocState be entryToReplace's [document state](#7411-session-history-entries).
11. Let documentState be a new [document state](#7412-document-state) with

    [document](#7412-document-state)

    newDocument

    [history policy container](#7412-document-state)

    a [clone](#717-policy-containers) of the oldDocState's [history policy container](#7412-document-state) if it is non-null; null otherwise

    [request referrer](#7412-document-state)

    oldDocState's [request referrer](#7412-document-state)

    [request referrer policy](#7412-document-state)

    oldDocState's [request referrer policy](#7412-document-state) or should this be the referrerPolicy that was passed to [navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation)?

    [initiator origin](#7412-document-state)

    initiatorOrigin

    [origin](#7412-document-state)

    initiatorOrigin

    [about base URL](#7412-document-state)

    oldDocState's [about base URL](#7412-document-state)

    [resource](#7412-document-state)

    null

    [ever populated](#7412-document-state)

    true

    [navigable target name](#7412-document-state)

    oldDocState's [navigable target name](#7412-document-state)

12. Let historyEntry be a new [session history entry](#7411-session-history-entries), with

    [URL](#7411-session-history-entries)

    entryToReplace's [URL](#7411-session-history-entries)

    [document state](#7411-session-history-entries)

    documentState

    > [!note]
    > For the [URL](#7411-session-history-entries), we do *not* use request's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url), i.e., the [`javascript:`](#74232-the-javascript-url-special-case) URL that was evaluated. This means [`javascript:`](#74232-the-javascript-url-special-case) URLs are never stored in session history, and so can never be traversed to.

13. [Append session history traversal steps](#7413-centralized-modifications-of-session-history) to targetNavigable's [traversable navigable](#7311-traversable-navigables) to [finalize a cross-document navigation](#74231-the-usual-cross-document-navigation-case) with targetNavigable, historyHandling, userInvolvement, and historyEntry.

To evaluate a `javascript:` URL given a [navigable](#731-navigables) targetNavigable, a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) url, an [origin](#711-origins) newDocumentOrigin, a [user navigation involvement](#7421-supporting-concepts) userInvolvement, and a [navigation ID](#7421-supporting-concepts) navigationId:
1. Let urlString be the result of running the [URL serializer](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer) on url.
2. Let encodedScriptSource be the result of removing the leading "`javascript:`" from urlString.
3. Let scriptSource be the [UTF-8 decoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8-decode) of the [percent-decoding](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#string-percent-decode) of encodedScriptSource.
4. Let settings be targetNavigable's [active document](#731-navigables)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant).
5. Let baseURL be settings's [API base URL](#8132-environment-settings-objects).
6. Let script be the result of [creating a classic script](#8143-creating-scripts) given scriptSource, settings, baseURL, and the [default script fetch options](#8142-fetching-scripts).
7. Let evaluationStatus be the result of [running the classic script](#8144-calling-scripts) script.
8. Let result be null.
9. If evaluationStatus is a normal completion, and evaluationStatus.\[\[Value\]\] is a String, then set result to evaluationStatus.\[\[Value\]\].
10. Otherwise, return null.
11. Let response be a new [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) with

    [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url)

    targetNavigable's [active document](#731-navigables)'s [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document)

    [header list](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-header-list)

    « (\`[`Content-Type`](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource)\`, \``text/html;charset=utf-8`\`) »

    [body](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-body)

    the [UTF-8 encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8-encode) of result, [as a body](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#byte-sequence-as-a-body)

    > [!note]
    > The encoding to UTF-8 means that unpaired [surrogates](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) will not roundtrip, once the HTML parser decodes the response body.

12. Let policyContainer be targetNavigable's [active document](#731-navigables)'s [policy container](#311-the-document-object).
13. Let finalSandboxFlags be policyContainer's [CSP list](#717-policy-containers)'s [CSP-derived sandboxing flags](#715-sandboxing).
14. Let coop be targetNavigable's [active document](#731-navigables)'s [opener policy](#311-the-document-object).
15. Let coopEnforcementResult be a new [opener policy enforcement result](#7132-browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-opener-policy) with

    [url](#7132-browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-opener-policy)

    url

    [origin](#7132-browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-opener-policy)

    newDocumentOrigin

    [opener policy](#7132-browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-opener-policy)

    coop

16. Let navigationParams be a new [navigation params](#7421-supporting-concepts), with

    [id](#7421-supporting-concepts)

    navigationId

    [navigable](#7421-supporting-concepts)

    targetNavigable

    [request](#7421-supporting-concepts)

    null this will cause the referrer of the resulting [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) to be null; is that correct?

    [response](#7421-supporting-concepts)

    response

    [fetch controller](#7421-supporting-concepts)

    null

    [commit early hints](#7421-supporting-concepts)

    null

    [COOP enforcement result](#7421-supporting-concepts)

    coopEnforcementResult

    [reserved environment](#7421-supporting-concepts)

    null

    [origin](#7421-supporting-concepts)

    newDocumentOrigin

    [policy container](#7421-supporting-concepts)

    policyContainer

    [final sandboxing flag set](#7421-supporting-concepts)

    finalSandboxFlags

    [`iframe` element referrer policy](#7421-supporting-concepts)

    targetSnapshotParams's [`iframe` element referrer policy](#7421-supporting-concepts)

    [opener policy](#7421-supporting-concepts)

    coop

    [navigation timing type](#7421-supporting-concepts)

    "[`navigate`](https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-navigationtimingtype-navigate)"

    [about base URL](#7421-supporting-concepts)

    targetNavigable's [active document](#731-navigables)'s [about base URL](#311-the-document-object)

    [user involvement](#7421-supporting-concepts)

    userInvolvement

17. Return the result of [loading an HTML document](#752-loading-html-documents) given navigationParams.

###### 7.4.2.3.3 Fragment navigations

To navigate to a fragment given a [navigable](#731-navigables) navigable, a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) url, a [history handling behavior](#7421-supporting-concepts) historyHandling, a [user navigation involvement](#7421-supporting-concepts) userInvolvement, an [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element)-or-null sourceElement, a [serialized state](#7411-session-history-entries)-or-null navigationAPIState, and a [navigation ID](#7421-supporting-concepts) navigationId:
1. Let navigation be navigable's [active window](#731-navigables)'s [navigation API](#7262-the-navigation-interface).
2. Let destinationNavigationAPIState be navigable's [active session history entry](#731-navigables)'s [navigation API state](#7411-session-history-entries).
3. If navigationAPIState is not null, then set destinationNavigationAPIState to navigationAPIState.
4. Let continue be the result of [firing a push/replace/reload `navigate` event](#726104-firing-the-event) at navigation with *[navigationType](#726104-firing-the-event)* set to historyHandling, *[isSameDocument](#726104-firing-the-event)* set to true, *[userInvolvement](#726104-firing-the-event)* set to userInvolvement, *[sourceElement](#726104-firing-the-event)* set to sourceElement, *[destinationURL](#726104-firing-the-event)* set to url, and *[navigationAPIState](#726104-firing-the-event)* set to destinationNavigationAPIState.
5. If continue is false:
   1. If navigation's [ongoing `navigate` event](#7268-ongoing-navigation-tracking) is not null, then [set the ongoing navigation](#7425-aborting-navigation) of navigable to navigationId.

      > [!note]
      > This makes intercepted hash navigations cancelable by browser UI or [`window.stop()`](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows).

   2. Return.

6. Let historyEntry be a new [session history entry](#7411-session-history-entries), with

   [URL](#7411-session-history-entries)

   url

   [document state](#7411-session-history-entries)

   navigable's [active session history entry](#731-navigables)'s [document state](#7411-session-history-entries)

   [navigation API state](#7411-session-history-entries)

   destinationNavigationAPIState

   [scroll restoration mode](#7411-session-history-entries)

   navigable's [active session history entry](#731-navigables)'s [scroll restoration mode](#7411-session-history-entries)

   > [!note]
   > For navigations performed with [`navigation.navigate()`](#7267-initiating-navigations), the value provided by the [`state`](#7262-the-navigation-interface) option is used for the new [navigation API state](#7411-session-history-entries). (This will set it to the serialization of undefined, if no value is provided for that option.) For other fragment navigations, including user-initiated ones, the [navigation API state](#7411-session-history-entries) is carried over from the previous entry.
   > 
   > The [classic history API state](#7411-session-history-entries) is never carried over.

7. Let entryToReplace be navigable's [active session history entry](#731-navigables) if historyHandling is "[`replace`](#7421-supporting-concepts)", otherwise null.
8. If entryToReplace is non-null, then set historyEntry's [navigation API key](#7411-session-history-entries) to entryToReplace's [navigation API key](#7411-session-history-entries).
9. Let history be navigable's [active document](#731-navigables)'s [history object](#725-the-history-interface).
10. Let scriptHistoryIndex be history's [index](#725-the-history-interface).
11. Let scriptHistoryLength be history's [length](#725-the-history-interface).
12. If historyHandling is "[`push`](#7421-supporting-concepts)":
    1. Set history's [state](#725-the-history-interface) to null.
    2. Increment scriptHistoryIndex.
    3. Set scriptHistoryLength to scriptHistoryIndex + 1.
13. Set navigable's [active document](#731-navigables)'s [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) to url.
14. Set navigable's [active session history entry](#731-navigables) to historyEntry.
15. [Update document for history step application](#7462-updating-the-document) given navigable's [active document](#731-navigables), historyEntry, true, scriptHistoryIndex, scriptHistoryLength, and historyHandling.

    > [!note]
    > This algorithm will be called twice as a result of a single fragment navigation: once synchronously, where best-guess values scriptHistoryIndex and scriptHistoryLength are set, [`history.state`](#725-the-history-interface) is nulled out, and various events are fired; and once asynchronously, where the final values for index and length are set, [`history.state`](#725-the-history-interface) remains untouched, and no events are fired.

16. [Scroll to the fragment](#7464-scrolling-to-a-fragment) given navigable's [active document](#731-navigables).

    > [!note]
