    1. Let fullTimingInfo be the result of [extracting the full timing info](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#extract-full-timing-info) from navigationParams's [fetch controller](#7421-supporting-concepts).
    2. Let redirectCount be 0.
    3. If navigationParams's [response](#7421-supporting-concepts)'s [redirect taint](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#response-redirect-taint) is "`same-origin`", or all of the following are true:
       - navigationParams's [request](#7421-supporting-concepts)'s [client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client) is null, or navigationParams's [request](#7421-supporting-concepts)'s [referrer](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-referrer) is not "`no-referrer`", and
       - [navigation TAO check](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#navigation-tao-check) given navigationParams's [response](#7421-supporting-concepts) and navigationParams's [origin](#7421-supporting-concepts) returns [success](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-singletons),

       then set redirectCount to navigationParams's [request](#7421-supporting-concepts)'s [redirect count](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-redirect-count).

    4. [Create the navigation timing entry](https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dfn-create-the-navigation-timing-entry) for document, given fullTimingInfo, redirectCount, navigationTimingType, navigationParams's [response](#7421-supporting-concepts)'s [service worker timing info](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#response-service-worker-timing-info), and navigationParams's [response](#7421-supporting-concepts)'s [body info](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-body-info).

16. [Create the navigation timing entry](https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dfn-create-the-navigation-timing-entry) for document, with navigationParams's [response](#7421-supporting-concepts)'s [timing info](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-timing-info), redirectCount, navigationParams's [navigation timing type](#7421-supporting-concepts), and navigationParams's [response](#7421-supporting-concepts)'s [service worker timing info](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#response-service-worker-timing-info).
17. If navigationParams's [response](#7421-supporting-concepts) has a \`[`Refresh`](#78-the-refresh-header)\` header:
    1. Let value be the [isomorphic decoding](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-byte-sequences) of the value of the header.
    2. Run the [shared declarative refresh steps](#4253-pragma-directives) with document and value.

    > [!warning]
    > We do not currently have a spec for how to handle multiple \`[`Refresh`](#78-the-refresh-header)\` headers. This is tracked as [issue #2900](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/2900).

18. If navigationParams's [commit early hints](#7421-supporting-concepts) is not null, then call navigationParams's [commit early hints](#7421-supporting-concepts) with document.
19. [Process link headers](#4244-processing-link-headers) given document, navigationParams's [response](#7421-supporting-concepts), and "`pre-media`".
20. If navigationParams's [navigable](#7421-supporting-concepts) is a [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables), then [process the \``Speculation-Rules`\` header](#763-the-speculation-rules-header) given document and navigationParams's [response](#7421-supporting-concepts).

    > [!note]
    > This is conditional because [speculative loads are only considered for top-level traversables](#7613-processing-model), so it would be wasteful to fetch these rules otherwise.

21. [Potentially free deferred fetch quota](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#potentially-free-deferred-fetch-quota) for document.
22. Return document.

> [!example]
> In this example, the child document is not allowed to use [`PaymentRequest`](https://w3c.github.io/payment-request/#dom-paymentrequest), despite being [same origin-domain](#711-origins) at the time the child document tries to use it. At the time the child document is initialized, only the parent document has set [`document.domain`](#7112-relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction), and the child document has not.
> 
> ```html
> <!-- https://foo.example.com/a.html -->
> <!doctype html>
> <script>
> document.domain = 'example.com';
> </script>
> <iframe src=b.html></iframe>
> ```
> 
> ```html
> <!-- https://bar.example.com/b.html -->
> <!doctype html>
> <script>
> document.domain = 'example.com'; // This happens after the document is initialized
> new PaymentRequest(…); // Not allowed to use
> </script>
> ```

> [!example]
> In this example, the child document *is* allowed to use [`PaymentRequest`](https://w3c.github.io/payment-request/#dom-paymentrequest), despite not being [same origin-domain](#711-origins) at the time the child document tries to use it. At the time the child document is initialized, none of the documents have set [`document.domain`](#7112-relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction) yet so [same origin-domain](#711-origins) falls back to a normal [same origin](#711-origins) check.
> 
> ```html
> <!-- https://example.com/a.html -->
> <!doctype html>
> <iframe src=b.html></iframe>
> <!-- The child document is now initialized, before the script below is run. -->
> <script>
> document.domain = 'example.com';
> </script>
> ```
> 
> ```html
> <!-- https://example.com/b.html -->
> <!doctype html>
> <script>
> new PaymentRequest(…); // Allowed to use
> </script>
> ```

To populate with `html`/`head`/`body` given a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document:
1. Let html be the result of [creating an element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) given document, "`html`", and the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces).
2. Let head be the result of [creating an element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) given document, "`head`", and the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces).
3. Let body be the result of [creating an element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) given document, "`body`", and the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces).
4. [Append](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) html to document.
5. [Append](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) head to html.
6. [Append](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) body to html.

#### 7.5.2 Loading HTML documents

To load an HTML document, given [navigation params](#7421-supporting-concepts) navigationParams:
1. Let document be the result of [creating and initializing a `Document` object](#751-shared-document-creation-infrastructure) given "`html`", "`text/html`", and navigationParams.
2. If document's [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is [`about:blank`](#219-dependencies), then [populate with `html`/`head`/`body`](#751-shared-document-creation-infrastructure) given document.

   > [!note]
   > This special case, where even non-[initial `about:blank`](#311-the-document-object) [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)s are synchronously given their element nodes, is necessary for compatibility with deployed content. In other words, it is not compatible to instead go down the "otherwise" branch and feed the empty [byte sequence](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-byte-sequences) into an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) to asynchronously populate document.

3. Otherwise, create an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) whose [allow declarative shadow roots](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) is true and associate it with document.

   Each [task](#8171-definitions) that the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) places on the [task queue](#8171-definitions) while fetching runs must then fill the parser's [input byte stream](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) with the fetched bytes and cause the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) to perform the appropriate processing of the input stream.

   The first [task](#8171-definitions) that the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) places on the [task queue](#8171-definitions) while fetching runs must [process link headers](#4244-processing-link-headers) given document, navigationParams's [response](#7421-supporting-concepts), and "`media`", after the task has been processed by the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents).

   Before any script execution occurs, the user agent must wait for [scripts may run for the newly-created document](#7462-updating-the-document) to be true for document.

   > [!note]
   > The [input byte stream](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) converts bytes into characters for use in the [tokenizer](#1325-tokenization). This process relies, in part, on character encoding information found in the real [Content-Type metadata](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource) of the resource; the computed type is not used for this purpose.

   When no more bytes are available, the user agent must [queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given document's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) to have the parser process the implied EOF character, which eventually causes a [`load`](#events) event to be fired.

4. Return document.

#### 7.5.3 Loading XML documents

When faced with displaying an XML file inline, provided [navigation params](#7421-supporting-concepts) navigationParams and a string type, user agents must follow the requirements defined in XML and Namespaces in XML, XML Media Types, DOM, and other relevant specifications to [create and initialize a `Document` object](#751-shared-document-creation-infrastructure) document, given "`xml`", type, and navigationParams, and return that [`Document`](#311-the-document-object). They must also create a corresponding [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents). [\[XML\]](#references) [\[XMLNS\]](#references) [\[RFC7303\]](#references) [\[DOM\]](#references)

> [!note]
> At the time of writing, the XML specification community had not actually yet specified how XML and the DOM interact.

The first [task](#8171-definitions) that the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) places on the [task queue](#8171-definitions) while fetching runs must [process link headers](#4244-processing-link-headers) given document, navigationParams's [response](#7421-supporting-concepts), and "`media`", after the task has been processed by the [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents).

The actual HTTP headers and other metadata, not the headers as mutated or implied by the algorithms given in this specification, are the ones that must be used when determining the character encoding according to the rules given in the above specifications. Once the character encoding is established, the [document's character encoding](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) must be set to that character encoding.

Before any script execution occurs, the user agent must wait for [scripts may run for the newly-created document](#7462-updating-the-document) to be true for the newly-created [`Document`](#311-the-document-object).

Once parsing is complete, the user agent must set document's [during-loading navigation ID for WebDriver BiDi](#311-the-document-object) to null.

> [!note]
> For HTML documents this is reset when parsing is complete, after firing the load event.

Error messages from the parse process (e.g., XML namespace well-formedness errors) may be reported inline by mutating the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object).

#### 7.5.4 Loading text documents

To load a text document, given a [navigation params](#7421-supporting-concepts) navigationParams and a string type:
1. Let document be the result of [creating and initializing a `Document` object](#751-shared-document-creation-infrastructure) given "`html`", type, and navigationParams.
2. Set document's [parser cannot change the mode flag](#132641-the-initial-insertion-mode) to true.
3. Set document's [mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) to "`no-quirks`".
4. Create an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) and associate it with the document. Act as if the tokenizer had emitted a start tag token with the tag name "pre" followed by a single U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character, and switch the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents)'s tokenizer to the [PLAINTEXT state](#13255-plaintext-state). Each [task](#8171-definitions) that the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) places on the [task queue](#8171-definitions) while fetching runs must then fill the parser's [input byte stream](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) with the fetched bytes and cause the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) to perform the appropriate processing of the input stream.

   document's [encoding](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) must be set to the character encoding used to decode the document during parsing.

   The first [task](#8171-definitions) that the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) places on the [task queue](#8171-definitions) while fetching runs must [process link headers](#4244-processing-link-headers) given document, navigationParams's [response](#7421-supporting-concepts), and "`media`", after the task has been processed by the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents).

   Before any script execution occurs, the user agent must wait for [scripts may run for the newly-created document](#7462-updating-the-document) to be true for document.

   When no more bytes are available, the user agent must [queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given document's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) to have the parser process the implied EOF character, which eventually causes a [`load`](#events) event to be fired.

5. User agents may add content to the [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element of document, e.g., linking to a style sheet, providing script, or giving the document a [`title`](#422-the-title-element).

   > [!note]
   > In particular, if the user agent supports the `Format=Flowed` feature of RFC 3676 then the user agent would need to apply extra styling to cause the text to wrap correctly and to handle the quoting feature. This could be performed using, e.g., a CSS extension.

6. Return document.

The rules for how to convert the bytes of the plain text document into actual characters, and the rules for actually rendering the text to the user, are defined by the specifications for the [computed MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#computed-mime-type) of the resource (i.e., type).

#### 7.5.5 Loading [`multipart/x-mixed-replace`](#172-multipartx-mixed-replace) documents

To load a `multipart/x-mixed-replace` document, given [navigation params](#7421-supporting-concepts) navigationParams, [source snapshot params](#7421-supporting-concepts) sourceSnapshotParams, and [origin](#711-origins) initiatorOrigin:
1. Parse navigationParams's [response](#7421-supporting-concepts)'s [body](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-body) using the rules for multipart types. [\[RFC2046\]](#references)
2. Let firstPartNavigationParams be a copy of navigationParams.
3. Set firstPartNavigationParams's [response](#7421-supporting-concepts) to a new [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) representing the first part of navigationParams's [response](#7421-supporting-concepts)'s [body](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-body)'s multipart stream.
4. Let document be the result of [loading a document](#745-populating-a-session-history-entry) given firstPartNavigationParams, sourceSnapshotParams, and initiatorOrigin.

   For each additional body part obtained from navigationParams's [response](#7421-supporting-concepts), the user agent must [navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation) document's [node navigable](#731-navigables) to navigationParams's [request](#7421-supporting-concepts)'s [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url), using document, with *[response](#7422-beginning-navigation)* set to navigationParams's [response](#7421-supporting-concepts) and *[historyHandling](#7422-beginning-navigation)* set to "[`replace`](#7421-supporting-concepts)".

5. Return document.

For the purposes of algorithms processing these body parts as if they were complete stand-alone resources, the user agent must act as if there were no more bytes for those resources whenever the boundary following the body part is reached.

> [!note]
> Thus, [`load`](#events) events (and for that matter [`unload`](#events) events) do fire for each body part loaded.

#### 7.5.6 Loading media documents

To load a media document, given navigationParams and a string type:
1. Let document be the result of [creating and initializing a `Document` object](#751-shared-document-creation-infrastructure) given "`html`", type, and navigationParams.
2. Set document's [mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) to "`no-quirks`".
3. [Populate with `html`/`head`/`body`](#751-shared-document-creation-infrastructure) given document.
4. Append an element host element for the media, as described below, to the [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element.
5. Set the appropriate attribute of the element host element, as described below, to the address of the image, video, or audio resource.
6. User agents may add content to the [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element of document, or attributes to host element, e.g., to link to a style sheet, to provide a script, to give the document a [`title`](#422-the-title-element), or to make the media [autoplay](#48117-ready-states).
7. [Process link headers](#4244-processing-link-headers) given document, navigationParams's [response](#7421-supporting-concepts), and "`media`".
8. Act as if the user agent had [stopped parsing](#1327-the-end) document.
9. Return document.

The element host element to create for the media is the element given in the table below in the second cell of the row whose first cell describes the media. The appropriate attribute to set is the one given by the third cell in that same row.

| Type of media | Element for the media | Appropriate attribute |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Image | [`img`](#483-the-img-element) | [`src`](#483-the-img-element) |
| Video | [`video`](#488-the-video-element) | [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) |
| Audio | [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) | [`src`](#48112-location-of-the-media-resource) |

Before any script execution occurs, the user agent must wait for [scripts may run for the newly-created document](#7462-updating-the-document) to be true for the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object).

#### 7.5.7 Loading a document for inline content that doesn't have a DOM

When the user agent is to create a document to display a user agent page or PDF viewer inline, provided a [navigable](#731-navigables) navigable, a [navigation ID](#7421-supporting-concepts) navigationId, a [`NavigationTimingType`](https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dom-navigationtimingtype) navTimingType, and a [user navigation involvement](#7421-supporting-concepts) userInvolvement, the user agent should:
1. Let origin be a new [opaque origin](#711-origins).
2. Let coop be a new [opener policy](#713-cross-origin-opener-policies).
3. Let coopEnforcementResult be a new [opener policy enforcement result](#7132-browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-opener-policy) with

   [url](#7132-browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-opener-policy)

   response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url)

   [origin](#7132-browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-opener-policy)

   origin

   [opener policy](#7132-browsing-context-group-switches-due-to-opener-policy)

   coop

4. Let navigationParams be a new [navigation params](#7421-supporting-concepts) with

   [id](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   navigationId

   [navigable](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   navigable

   [request](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   null

   [response](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   a new [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response)

   [origin](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   origin

   [fetch controller](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   null

   [commit early hints](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   null

   [COOP enforcement result](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   coopEnforcementResult

   [reserved environment](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   null

   [policy container](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   a new [policy container](#717-policy-containers)

   [final sandboxing flag set](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   an empty set

   [`iframe` element referrer policy](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   the empty string

   [opener policy](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   coop

   [navigation timing type](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   navTimingType

   [about base URL](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   null

   [user involvement](#7421-supporting-concepts)

   userInvolvement

5. Let document be the result of [creating and initializing a `Document` object](#751-shared-document-creation-infrastructure) given "`html`", "`text/html`", and navigationParams.
6. Either associate document with a custom rendering that is not rendered using the normal [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) rendering rules, or mutate document until it represents the content the user agent wants to render.
7. Act as if the user agent had [stopped parsing](#1327-the-end) document.

   > [!note]
   > This is done to avoid leaking information to the parent page about whether a navigation has been blocked by CSP, or if the response was a [network error](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-network-error). In the case where the container is an [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) element, [stopping parsing](#1327-the-end) causes the [iframe load event steps](#485-the-iframe-element) to run.

8. Return document.

> [!note]
> Because we ensure the resulting [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is [opaque](#711-origins), and the resulting [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) cannot run script with access to the DOM, the existence and properties of this [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) are not observable to web developer code. This means that most of the above values, e.g., the [`text/html`](#171-texthtml) [type](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), do not matter. Similarly, most of the items in navigationParams don't have any observable effect, besides preventing the [`Document`-creation algorithm](#751-shared-document-creation-infrastructure) from getting confused, and so are set to default values.

#### 7.5.8 Finishing the loading process

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a completely loaded time (a time or null), which is initially null.

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is considered completely loaded if its [completely loaded time](#758-finishing-the-loading-process) is non-null.

To completely finish loading a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document:
1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): document's [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) is non-null.
2. Set document's [completely loaded time](#758-finishing-the-loading-process) to the current time.
3. Let container be document's [node navigable](#731-navigables)'s [container](#7313-child-navigables).

   > [!note]
   > This will be null in the case where document is the [initial `about:blank`](#311-the-document-object) [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) in a [`frame`](#1632-frames) or [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element), since at the point of [browsing context creation](#7321-creating-browsing-contexts) which calls this algorithm, the container relationship has not yet been established. (That happens in a subsequent step of [create a new child navigable](#7313-child-navigables).)
   > 
   > The consequence of this is that the following steps do nothing, i.e., we do not fire an asynchronous [`load`](#events) event on the container element for such cases. Instead, a synchronous [`load`](#events) event is fired in a special initial-insertion case when [processing the `iframe` attributes](#485-the-iframe-element).

4. If container is an [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) element, then [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given container to run the [iframe load event steps](#485-the-iframe-element) given container.
5. Otherwise, if container is non-null, then [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given container to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`load`](#events) at container.

#### 7.5.9 Unloading documents

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a *salvageable* state, which must initially be true, and a page showing boolean, which is initially false. The [page showing](#759-unloading-documents) boolean is used to ensure that scripts receive [`pageshow`](#events) and [`pagehide`](#events) events in a consistent manner (e.g., that they never receive two [`pagehide`](#events) events in a row without an intervening [`pageshow`](#events), or vice versa).

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a [`DOMHighResTimeStamp`](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dom-domhighrestimestamp) suspension time, initially 0.

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of suspended timer handles, initially empty.

[Event loops](#8171-definitions) have a termination nesting level counter, which must initially be 0.

[`Document`](#311-the-document-object) objects have an unload counter, which is used to ignore certain operations while the below algorithms run. Initially, the counter must be set to zero.

To unload a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) oldDocument, given an optional [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) newDocument:
1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): this is running as part of a [task](#8171-definitions) queued on oldDocument's [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [event loop](#8171-definitions).
2. Let unloadTimingInfo be a new [document unload timing info](#315-reporting-document-loading-status).
3. If newDocument is not given, then set unloadTimingInfo to null.

   > [!note]
   > In this case there is no new document that needs to know about how long it took oldDocument to unload.

4. Otherwise, if newDocument's [event loop](#8171-definitions) is not oldDocument's [event loop](#8171-definitions), then the user agent may be [unloading](#759-unloading-documents) oldDocument [in parallel](#211-parallelism). In that case, the user agent should set unloadTimingInfo to null.

   > [!note]
   > In this case newDocument's loading is not impacted by how long it takes to unload oldDocument, so it would be meaningless to communicate that timing info.

5. Let intendToKeepInBfcache be true if the user agent intends to keep oldDocument alive in a [session history entry](#7411-session-history-entries), such that it can later be [used for history traversal](#7412-document-state).

   This must be false if oldDocument is not *[salvageable](#759-unloading-documents)*, or if there are any descendants of oldDocument which the user agent does not intend to keep alive in the same way (including due to their lack of *[salvageability](#759-unloading-documents)*).

6. Let eventLoop be oldDocument's [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [event loop](#8171-definitions).
7. Increase eventLoop's [termination nesting level](#759-unloading-documents) by 1.
8. Increase oldDocument's [unload counter](#759-unloading-documents) by 1.
9. If intendToKeepInBfcache is false, then set oldDocument's *[salvageable](#759-unloading-documents)* state to false.
10. If oldDocument's [page showing](#759-unloading-documents) is true:
    1. Set oldDocument's [page showing](#759-unloading-documents) to false.
    2. [Fire a page transition event](#7276-the-pagetransitionevent-interface) named [`pagehide`](#events) at oldDocument's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) with oldDocument's *[salvageable](#759-unloading-documents)* state.
    3. [Update the visibility state](#62-page-visibility) of oldDocument to "`hidden`".
11. If unloadTimingInfo is not null, then set unloadTimingInfo's [unload event start time](#315-reporting-document-loading-status) to the [current high resolution time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time) given newDocument's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant), [coarsened](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-coarsen-time) given oldDocument's [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant)'s [cross-origin isolated capability](#8132-environment-settings-objects).
12. If oldDocument's *[salvageable](#759-unloading-documents)* state is false, then [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`unload`](#events) at oldDocument's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant), with *legacy target override flag* set.
13. If unloadTimingInfo is not null, then set unloadTimingInfo's [unload event end time](#315-reporting-document-loading-status) to the [current high resolution time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time) given newDocument's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant), [coarsened](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-coarsen-time) given oldDocument's [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant)'s [cross-origin isolated capability](#8132-environment-settings-objects).
14. Decrease eventLoop's [termination nesting level](#759-unloading-documents) by 1.
15. Set oldDocument's [suspension time](#759-unloading-documents) to the [current high resolution time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time) given document's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant).
16. Set oldDocument's [suspended timer handles](#759-unloading-documents) to the result of [getting the keys](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) for the [map of active timers](#87-timers).
17. Set oldDocument's [has been scrolled by the user](#7465-persisted-history-entry-state) to false.
18. Run any [unloading document cleanup steps](#759-unloading-documents) for oldDocument that are defined by this specification and [other applicable specifications](#2110-extensibility).
19. If oldDocument's [node navigable](#731-navigables) is a [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables), [build not restored reasons for a top-level traversable and its descendants](#7462-updating-the-document) given oldDocument's [node navigable](#731-navigables).
20. If oldDocument's *[salvageable](#759-unloading-documents)* state is false, then [destroy](#7510-destroying-documents) oldDocument.
21. Decrease oldDocument's [unload counter](#759-unloading-documents) by 1.
22. If newDocument is given, newDocument's [was created via cross-origin redirects](#315-reporting-document-loading-status) is false, and newDocument's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is the [same](#711-origins) as oldDocument's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), then set newDocument's [previous document unload timing](#315-reporting-document-loading-status) to unloadTimingInfo.

To unload a document and its descendants, given a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document, an optional [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)-or-null newDocument (default null), an optional set of steps afterAllUnloads, and an optional set of steps firePageSwapSteps:
1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): this is running within document's [node navigable](#731-navigables)'s [traversable navigable](#7311-traversable-navigables)'s [session history traversal queue](#7311-traversable-navigables).
2. Let childNavigables be document's [child navigables](#7313-child-navigables).
3. Let numberUnloaded be 0.
4. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) childNavigable of childNavigables in what order?, [queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [navigation and traversal task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given childNavigable's [active window](#731-navigables) to perform the following steps:
   1. Let incrementUnloaded be an algorithm step which increments numberUnloaded.
   2. [Unload a document and its descendants](#759-unloading-documents) given childNavigable's [active document](#731-navigables), null, and incrementUnloaded.
5. Wait until numberUnloaded equals childNavigable's [size](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).
6. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [navigation and traversal task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given document's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) to perform the following steps:
   1. If firePageSwapSteps is given, then run firePageSwapSteps.
   2. [Unload](#759-unloading-documents) document, passing along newDocument if it is not null.
   3. If afterAllUnloads was given, then run it.

This specification defines the following unloading document cleanup steps. Other specifications can define more. Given a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document:
1. Let window be document's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant).
2. For each [`WebSocket`](https://websockets.spec.whatwg.org/#websocket) object webSocket whose [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) is window, [make disappear](https://websockets.spec.whatwg.org/#make-disappear) webSocket.

   If this affected any [`WebSocket`](https://websockets.spec.whatwg.org/#websocket) objects, then [make document unsalvageable](#7462-updating-the-document) given document and "[`websocket`](#728-the-notrestoredreasons-interface)".

3. For each [`WebTransport`](https://w3c.github.io/webtransport/#webtransport) object transport whose [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) is window, run the [context cleanup steps](https://w3c.github.io/webtransport/#context-cleanup-steps) given transport.
4. If document's *[salvageable](#759-unloading-documents)* state is false:
   1. For each [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object eventSource whose [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) is equal to window, [forcibly close](#929-garbage-collection) eventSource.
   2. [Clear](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) window's [map of active timers](#87-timers).

> [!warning]
> It would be better if specification authors sent a pull request to add calls from here into their specifications directly, instead of using the [unloading document cleanup steps](#759-unloading-documents) hook, to ensure well-defined cross-specification call order. As of the time of this writing the following specifications are known to have [unloading document cleanup steps](#759-unloading-documents), which will be run in an unspecified order: Fullscreen API, Web NFC, WebDriver BiDi, Compute Pressure, File API, Media Capture and Streams, Picture-in-Picture, Screen Orientation, Service Workers, WebLocks API, WebAudio API, WebRTC. [\[FULLSCREEN\]](#references) [\[WEBNFC\]](#references) [\[WEBDRIVERBIDI\]](#references) [\[COMPUTEPRESSURE\]](#references) [\[FILEAPI\]](#references) [\[MEDIASTREAM\]](#references) [\[PICTUREINPICTURE\]](#references) [\[SCREENORIENTATION\]](#references) [\[SW\]](#references) [\[WEBLOCKS\]](#references) [\[WEBAUDIO\]](#references) [\[WEBRTC\]](#references)
> 
> [Issue #8906](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/8906) tracks the work to make the order of these steps clear.

#### 7.5.10 Destroying documents

To destroy a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document:
1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): this is running as part of a [task](#8171-definitions) queued on document's [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [event loop](#8171-definitions).
2. [Abort](#7511-aborting-a-document-load) document.
3. Set document's *[salvageable](#759-unloading-documents)* state to false.
4. Run any [unloading document cleanup steps](#759-unloading-documents) for document that are defined by this specification and [other applicable specifications](#2110-extensibility).
5. Remove any [tasks](#8171-definitions) whose [document](#8171-definitions) is document from any [task queue](#8171-definitions) (without running those tasks).
6. Set document's [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) to null.
7. Set document's [node navigable](#731-navigables)'s [active session history entry](#731-navigables)'s [document state](#7411-session-history-entries)'s [document](#7412-document-state) to null.
8. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) document from the [owner set](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) of each [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) object whose set [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) document.
9. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) workletGlobalScope in document's [worklet global scopes](#1133-the-worklets-lifetime), [terminate](#11312-creation-and-termination) workletGlobalScope.

> [!note]
> Even after destruction, the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object itself might still be accessible to script, in the case where we are [destroying a child navigable](#7316-navigable-destruction).

To destroy a document and its descendants given a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document and an optional set of steps afterAllDestruction, perform the following steps [in parallel](#211-parallelism):
1. If document is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents):
   1. Let reason be a string from [user-agent specific blocking reasons](#728-the-notrestoredreasons-interface). If none apply, then let reason be "[`masked`](#728-the-notrestoredreasons-interface)".
   2. [Make document unsalvageable](#7462-updating-the-document) given document and reason.
   3. If document's [node navigable](#731-navigables) is a [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables), [build not restored reasons for a top-level traversable and its descendants](#7462-updating-the-document) given document's [node navigable](#731-navigables).
2. Let childNavigables be document's [child navigables](#7313-child-navigables).
3. Let numberDestroyed be 0.
4. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) childNavigable of childNavigables in what order?, [queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [navigation and traversal task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given childNavigable's [active window](#731-navigables) to perform the following steps:
   1. Let incrementDestroyed be an algorithm step which increments numberDestroyed.
   2. [Destroy a document and its descendants](#7510-destroying-documents) given childNavigable's [active document](#731-navigables) and incrementDestroyed.
5. Wait until numberDestroyed equals childNavigable's [size](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).
6. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [navigation and traversal task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given document's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) to perform the following steps:
   1. [Destroy](#7510-destroying-documents) document.
   2. If afterAllDestruction was given, then run it.

#### 7.5.11 Aborting a document load

To abort a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document:
1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): this is running as part of a [task](#8171-definitions) queued on document's [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [event loop](#8171-definitions).
2. Cancel any instances of the [fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) algorithm in the context of document, discarding any [tasks](#8171-definitions) [queued](#8172-queuing-tasks) for them, and discarding any further data received from the network for them. If this resulted in any instances of the [fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) algorithm being canceled or any [queued](#8172-queuing-tasks) [tasks](#8171-definitions) or any network data getting discarded, then [make document unsalvageable](#7462-updating-the-document) given document and "[`fetch`](#728-the-notrestoredreasons-interface)".
3. If document's [during-loading navigation ID for WebDriver BiDi](#311-the-document-object) is non-null:
   1. Invoke [WebDriver BiDi navigation aborted](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-navigation-aborted) with document's [node navigable](#731-navigables) and a new [WebDriver BiDi navigation status](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-navigation-status) whose [id](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-id) is document's [during-loading navigation ID for WebDriver BiDi](#311-the-document-object), [status](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-status) is "[`canceled`](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-canceled)", and [url](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-url) is document's [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).
   2. Set document's [during-loading navigation ID for WebDriver BiDi](#311-the-document-object) to null.
4. If document has an [active parser](#315-reporting-document-loading-status):
   1. Set document's [active parser was aborted](#841-opening-the-input-stream) to true.
   2. [Abort that parser](#1327-the-end).
   3. [Make document unsalvageable](#7462-updating-the-document) given document and "[`parser-aborted`](#728-the-notrestoredreasons-interface)".

To abort a document and its descendants given a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document:
1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): this is running as part of a [task](#8171-definitions) queued on document's [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [event loop](#8171-definitions).
2. Let descendantNavigables be document's [descendant navigables](#7315-related-navigable-collections).
3. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) descendantNavigable of descendantNavigables in what order?, [queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [navigation and traversal task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given descendantNavigable's [active window](#731-navigables) to perform the following steps:
   1. [Abort](#7511-aborting-a-document-load) descendantNavigable's [active document](#731-navigables).
   2. If descendantNavigable's [active document](#731-navigables)'s *[salvageable](#759-unloading-documents)* is false, then set document's *[salvageable](#759-unloading-documents)* to false.
4. [Abort](#7511-aborting-a-document-load) document.

To stop loading a [navigable](#731-navigables) navigable:
1. Let document be navigable's [active document](#731-navigables).
2. If document's [unload counter](#759-unloading-documents) is 0, and navigable's [ongoing navigation](#7425-aborting-navigation) is a [navigation ID](#7421-supporting-concepts), then [set the ongoing navigation](#7425-aborting-navigation) for navigable to null.

   > [!note]
   > This will have the effect of aborting any ongoing navigations of navigable, since at certain points during navigation, changes to the [ongoing navigation](#7425-aborting-navigation) will cause further work to be abandoned.

3. [Abort a document and its descendants](#7511-aborting-a-document-load) given document.

> [!warning]
> Through their [user interface](#79-browser-user-interface-considerations), user agents also allow stopping traversals, i.e. cases where the [ongoing navigation](#7425-aborting-navigation) is "`traversal`". The above algorithm does not account for this. (On the other hand, user agents do not allow [`window.stop()`](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows) to stop traversals, so the above algorithm is correct for that caller.) See [issue #6905](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/6905).

### 7.6 Speculative loading

Speculative loading is the practice of performing navigation actions, such as prefetching, ahead of navigation starting. This makes subsequent navigations faster.

Developers can initiate speculative loads by using [speculation rules](#7611-data-model). User agents might also perform speculative loads in certain [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) scenarios, such as typing into the address bar.

#### 7.6.1 Speculation rules

[Speculation rules](#7611-data-model) are how developers instruct the browser about speculative loading operations that the developer believes will be beneficial. They are delivered as JSON documents, via either:
- inline [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements with their [`type`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute set to "`speculationrules`"; or
- resources fetched from a URL specified in the \`[`Speculation-Rules`](#763-the-speculation-rules-header)\` HTTP response header.

> [!example]
> The following JSON document is parsed into a [speculation rule set](#7611-data-model) specifying a number of desired conditions for the user agent to [start a referrer-initiated navigational prefetch](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#start-a-referrer-initiated-navigational-prefetch):
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "prefetch": [
>     {
>       "urls": ["/chapters/5"]
>     },
>     {
>       "eagerness": "moderate",
>       "where": {
>         "and": [
>           { "href_matches": "/*" },
>           { "not": { "selector_matches": ".no-prefetch" } }
>         ]
>       }
>     }
>   ]
> }
> ```

A JSON document representing a [speculation rule set](#7611-data-model) must meet the following speculation rule set authoring requirements:
- It must be valid JSON. [\[JSON\]](#references)
- The JSON must represent a JSON object, with at most three keys "`tag`", "`prefetch`" and "`prerender`".

  > [!note]
  > In this standard, "`prerender`" is optionally converted to "`prefetch`" [at parse time](#7612-parsing). Some implementations might implement different behavior for prerender, as specified in Prerendering Revamped. [\[PRERENDERING-REVAMPED\]](#references)

- The value corresponding to the "`tag`" key, if present, must be a [speculation rule tag](#7611-data-model).
- The values corresponding to the "`prefetch`" and "`prerender`" keys, if present, must be arrays of [valid speculation rules](#761-speculation-rules).

A valid speculation rule is a JSON object that meets the following requirements:
- It must have at most the following keys: "`source`", "`urls`", "`where`", "`relative_to`", "`eagerness`", "`referrer_policy`", "`tag`", "`requires`", "`expects_no_vary_search`", or "`target_hint`".

  > [!note]
  > In this standard, ["`target_hint`" is ignored](#7612-parsing).

- The value corresponding to the "`source`" key, if present, must be either "`list`" or "`document`".
- If the value corresponding to the "`source`" key is "`list`", then the "`urls`" key must be present, and the "`where`" key must be absent.
- If the value corresponding to the "`source`" key is "`document`", then the "`urls`" key must be absent.
- The "`urls`" and "`where`" keys must not both be present.
- If the value corresponding to the "`source`" key is "`document`" or the "`where`" key is present, then the "`relative_to`" key must be absent.
- The value corresponding to the "`urls`" key, if present, must be an array of [valid URL strings](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-url-string).
- The value corresponding to the "`where`" key, if present, must be a [valid document rule predicate](#761-speculation-rules).
- The value corresponding to the "`relative_to`" key, if present, must be either "`ruleset`" or "`document`".
- The value corresponding to the "`eagerness`" key, if present, must be a [speculation rule eagerness](#7611-data-model).
- The value corresponding to the "`referrer_policy`" key, if present, must be a [referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy).
- The value corresponding to the "`tag`" key, if present, must be a [speculation rule tag](#7611-data-model).
- The value corresponding to the "`requires`" key, if present, must be an array of [speculation rule requirements](#7611-data-model).
- The value corresponding to the "`expects_no_vary_search`" key, if present, must be a [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) that is [parseable](https://httpwg.org/http-extensions/draft-ietf-httpbis-no-vary-search.html#parse-a-url-search-variance) as a \`[`No-Vary-Search`](https://httpwg.org/http-extensions/draft-ietf-httpbis-no-vary-search.html#name-http-header-field-definitio)\` header value.

A valid document rule predicate is a JSON object that meets the following requirements:
- It must contain exactly one of the keys "`and`", "`or`", "`not`", "`href_matches`", or "`selector_matches`".
- It must not contain any keys apart from the above or "`relative_to`".
- If it contains the key "`relative_to`", then it must also contain the key "`href_matches`".
- The value corresponding to the "`relative_to`" key, if present, must be either "`ruleset`" or "`document`".
- The value corresponding to the "`and`" or "`or`" keys, if present, must be arrays of [valid document rule predicates](#761-speculation-rules).
- The value corresponding to the "`not`" key, if present, must be a [valid document rule predicate](#761-speculation-rules).
- The value corresponding to the "`href_matches`" key, if present, must be either a [valid URL pattern input](#761-speculation-rules) or an array of [valid URL pattern inputs](#761-speculation-rules).
- The value corresponding to the "`selector_matches`" key, if present, must be either a [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) matching [`<selector-list>`](https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#typedef-selector-list) or an array of [strings](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) that match [`<selector-list>`](https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#typedef-selector-list).

A valid URL pattern input is either:
- a [scalar value string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) that can be successfully [parsed](https://urlpattern.spec.whatwg.org/#parse-a-constructor-string) as a URL pattern constructor string, or;
- a JSON object whose keys are drawn from the members of the [`URLPatternInit`](https://urlpattern.spec.whatwg.org/#dictdef-urlpatterninit) dictionary and whose values are [scalar value strings](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).

##### 7.6.1.1 Data model

A speculation rule set is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) with the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):
- prefetch rules, a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [speculation rules](#7611-data-model), initially empty

> [!note]
> In the future, other rules will be possible, e.g., prerender rules. See Prerendering Revamped for such not-yet-accepted extensions. [\[PRERENDERING-REVAMPED\]](#references)

A speculation rule is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) with the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):
- URLs, an [ordered set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) of [URLs](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url)
- predicate, a [document rule predicate](#7611-data-model) or null
- eagerness, a [speculation rule eagerness](#7611-data-model)
- referrer policy, a [referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy)
- tags, an [ordered set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) of [speculation rule tags](#7611-data-model)
- requirements, an [ordered set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) of [speculation rule requirements](#7611-data-model)
- No-Vary-Search hint, a [URL search variance](https://httpwg.org/http-extensions/draft-ietf-httpbis-no-vary-search.html#name-data-model)

---

A document rule predicate is one of the following:
- a [document rule conjunction](#7611-data-model);
- a [document rule disjunction](#7611-data-model);
- a [document rule negation](#7611-data-model);
- a [document rule URL pattern predicate](#7611-data-model); or
- a [document rule selector predicate](#7611-data-model).

A document rule conjunction is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) with the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):
- clauses, a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [document rule predicates](#7611-data-model)

A document rule disjunction is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) with the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):
- clauses, a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [document rule predicates](#7611-data-model)

A document rule negation is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) with the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):
- clause, a [document rule predicate](#7611-data-model)

A document rule URL pattern predicate is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) with the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):
- patterns, a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [URL patterns](https://urlpattern.spec.whatwg.org/#url-pattern)

A document rule selector predicate is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) with the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):
- selectors, a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [selectors](https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#selector)

---

A speculation rule eagerness is one of the following [strings](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings):

"`immediate`"

The developer believes that performing the associated speculative loads is very likely to be worthwhile, and they might also expect that load to require significant lead time to complete. User agents should usually enact the speculative load candidate as soon as practical, subject only to considerations such as user preferences, device conditions, and resource limits.

"`eager`"

User agents should enact the speculative load candidate on even a slight suggestion that the user may navigate to this URL in the future. For instance, the user might have moved the cursor toward a link or hovered it, even momentarily, or paused scrolling when the link is one of the more prominent ones in the viewport. The author is seeking to capture as many navigations as possible, as early as possible.

"`moderate`"

User agents should enact the candidate if user behavior suggests the user may navigate to this URL in the near future. For instance, the user might have scrolled a link into the viewport and shown signs of being likely to click it, e.g., by moving the cursor over it for some time. The developer is seeking a balance between "[`eager`](#7611-data-model)" and "[`conservative`](#7611-data-model)".

"`conservative`"

User agents should enact the candidate only when the user is very likely to navigate to this URL at any moment. For instance, the user might have begun to interact with a link. The developer is seeking to capture some of the benefits of speculative loading with a fairly small tradeoff of resources.

A [speculation rule eagerness](#7611-data-model) A is less eager than another [speculation rule eagerness](#7611-data-model) B if A follows B in the above list.

A [speculation rule eagerness](#7611-data-model) A is at least as eager as another [speculation rule eagerness](#7611-data-model) B if A is not [less eager](#7611-data-model) than B.

---

A speculation rule tag is either an [ASCII string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) whose [code points](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) are all in the range U+0020 to U+007E inclusive, or null.

> [!note]
> This code point range restriction ensures the value can be sent in an HTTP header with no escaping or modification.

---

A speculation rule requirement is the string "`anonymous-client-ip-when-cross-origin`".

> [!note]
> In the future, more possible requirements might be defined.

##### 7.6.1.2 Parsing

> [!note]
> Since speculative loading is a progressive enhancement, this standard is fairly conservative in its parsing behavior. In particular, unknown keys or invalid values usually cause parsing failure, since it is safer to do nothing than to possibly misinterpret a speculation rule.
> 
> That said, parsing failure for a single speculation rule still allows other speculation rules to be processed. It is only in the case of top-level misconfiguration that the entire speculation rule set is discarded.

To parse a speculation rule set string given a [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) input, a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document, and a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) baseURL:
1. Let parsed be the result of [parsing a JSON string to an Infra value](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#6-json) given input.
2. If parsed is not a [map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then throw a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) indicating that the top-level value needs to be a JSON object.
3. Let result be a new [speculation rule set](#7611-data-model).
4. Let tag be null.
5. If parsed\["`tag`"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps):
   1. If parsed\["`tag`"\] is not a [speculation rule tag](#7611-data-model), then throw a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) indicating that the speculation rule tag is invalid.
   2. Set tag to parsed\["`tag`"\].
6. Let typesToTreatAsPrefetch be « "`prefetch`" ».
7. The user agent may [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) "`prerender`" to typesToTreatAsPrefetch.

   > [!note]
   > Since this specification only includes prefetching, this allows user agents to treat requests for prerendering as requests for prefetching. User agents which implement prerendering, per the Prerendering Revamped specification, will instead interpret these as prerender requests. [\[PRERENDERING-REVAMPED\]](#references)

8. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) type of typesToTreatAsPrefetch:
   1. If parsed\[type\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps):
      1. If parsed\[type\] is a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists), then [for each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) rule of parsed\[type\]:
         1. Let rule be the result of [parsing a speculation rule](#7612-parsing) given rule, tag, document, and baseURL.
         2. If rule is null, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
         3. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) rule to result's [prefetch rules](#7611-data-model).
      2. Otherwise, the user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the rules list for type needs to be a JSON array.
9. Return result.

To parse a speculation rule given a [map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) input, a [speculation rule tag](#7611-data-model) rulesetLevelTag, a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document, and a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) baseURL:
1. If input is not a [map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps):
   1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the rule needs to be a JSON object.
   2. Return null.
2. If input has any [key](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) other than "`source`", "`urls`", "`where`", "`relative_to`", "`eagerness`", "`referrer_policy`", "`tag`", "`requires`", "`expects_no_vary_search`", or "`target_hint`":
   1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the rule has unrecognized keys.
   2. Return null.

   > [!note]
   > "`target_hint`" has no impact on the processing model in this standard. However, implementations of Prerendering Revamped can use it for prerendering rules, and so requiring user agents to fail parsing such rules would be counterproductive. [\[PRERENDERING-REVAMPED\]](#references).

3. Let source be null.
4. If input\["`source`"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then set source to input\["`source`"\].
5. Otherwise, if input\["`urls`"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) and input\["`where`"\] does not [exist](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then set source to "`list`".
6. Otherwise, if input\["`where`"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) and input\["`urls`"\] does not [exist](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then set source to "`document`".
7. If source is neither "`list`" nor "`document`":
   1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that a source could not be inferred or an invalid source was specified.
   2. Return null.
8. Let urls be an empty [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).
9. Let predicate be null.
10. If source is "`list`":
    1. If input\["`where`"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps):
       1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that there were conflicting sources for this rule.
       2. Return null.
    2. If input\["`relative_to`"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps):
       1. If input\["`relative_to`"\] is neither "`ruleset`" nor "`document`":
          1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the supplied relative-to value was invalid.
          2. Return null.
       2. If input\["`relative_to`"\] is "`document`", then set baseURL to document's [document base URL](#243-document-base-urls).
    3. If input\["`urls`"\] does not [exist](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) or is not a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists):
       1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the supplied URL list was invalid.
       2. Return null.
    4. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) urlString of input\["`urls`"\]:
       1. If urlString is not a string:
          1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the supplied URL must be a string.
          2. Return null.
       2. Let parsedURL be the result of [URL parsing](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser) urlString with baseURL.
       3. If parsedURL is failure, or parsedURL's [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) is not an [HTTP(S) scheme](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#http-scheme):
          1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the supplied URL string was unparseable.
          2. [Continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
       4. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) parsedURL to urls.
11. If source is "`document`":
    1. If input\["`urls`"\] or input\["`relative_to`"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps):
       1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that there were conflicting sources for this rule.
       2. Return null.
    2. If input\["`where`"\] does not [exist](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then set predicate to a [document rule conjunction](#7611-data-model) whose [clauses](#7611-data-model) is an empty [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).

       > [!note]
       > Such a predicate will match all links.

    3. Otherwise, set predicate to the result of [parsing a document rule predicate](#7612-parsing) given input\["`where`"\], document, and baseURL.
    4. If predicate is null, then return null.

12. Let eagerness be "[`immediate`](#7611-data-model)" if source is "`list`"; otherwise, "[`conservative`](#7611-data-model)".
13. If input\["`eagerness`"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps):
    1. If input\["`eagerness`"\] is not a [speculation rule eagerness](#7611-data-model):
       1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the eagerness was invalid.
       2. Return null.
    2. Set eagerness to input\["`eagerness`"\].
14. Let referrerPolicy be the empty string.
15. If input\["`referrer_policy`"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps):
    1. If input\["`referrer_policy`"\] is not a [referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy):
       1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the referrer policy was invalid.
       2. Return null.
    2. Set referrerPolicy to input\["`referrer_policy`"\].
16. Let tags be an empty [ordered set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets).
17. If rulesetLevelTag is not null, then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) rulesetLevelTag to tags.
18. If input\["`tag`"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps):
    1. If input\["`tag`"\] is not a [speculation rule tag](#7611-data-model):
       1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the tag was invalid.
       2. Return null.
    2. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) input\["`tag`"\] to tags.
19. If tags [is empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists), then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) null to tags.
20. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): tags's [size](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) is either 1 or 2.
21. Let requirements be an empty [ordered set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets).
22. If input\["`requires`"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps):
    1. If input\["`requires`"\] is not a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists):
       1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the requirements were not understood.
       2. Return null.
    2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) requirement of input\["`requires`"\]:
       1. If requirement is not a [speculation rule requirement](#7611-data-model):
          1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the requirement was not understood.
          2. Return null.
       2. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) requirement to requirements.
23. Let noVarySearchHint be the [default URL search variance](https://httpwg.org/http-extensions/draft-ietf-httpbis-no-vary-search.html#name-data-model).
24. If input\["`expects_no_vary_search`"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps):
    1. If input\["`expects_no_vary_search`"\] is not a [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings):
       1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the \`[`No-Vary-Search`](https://httpwg.org/http-extensions/draft-ietf-httpbis-no-vary-search.html#name-http-header-field-definitio)\` hint was invalid.
       2. Return null.
    2. Set noVarySearchHint to the result of [parsing a URL search variance](https://httpwg.org/http-extensions/draft-ietf-httpbis-no-vary-search.html#parse-a-url-search-variance) given input\["`expects_no_vary_search`"\].
25. Return a [speculation rule](#7611-data-model) with:

    [URLs](#7611-data-model)

    urls

    [predicate](#7611-data-model)

    predicate

    [eagerness](#7611-data-model)

    eagerness

    [referrer policy](#7611-data-model)

    referrerPolicy

    [tags](#7611-data-model)

    tags

    [requirements](#7611-data-model)

    requirements

    [No-Vary-Search hint](#7611-data-model)

    noVarySearchHint

To parse a document rule predicate given a value input, a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document, and a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) baseURL:
1. If input is not a [map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps):
   1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the document rule predicate was invalid.
   2. Return null.
2. If input does not [contain](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) exactly one of "`and`", "`or`", "`not`", "`href_matches`", or "`selector_matches`":
   1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the document rule predicate was empty or ambiguous.
   2. Return null.
3. Let predicateType be the single key found in the previous step.
4. If predicateType is "`and`" or "`or`":
   1. If input has any [key](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) other than predicateType:
      1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the document rule predicate had unexpected extra options.
      2. Return null.
   2. If input\[predicateType\] is not a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists):
      1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the document rule predicate had an invalid clause list.
      2. Return null.
   3. Let clauses be an empty [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).
   4. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) rawClause of input\[predicateType\]:
      1. Let clause be the result of [parsing a document rule predicate](#7612-parsing) given rawClause, document, and baseURL.
      2. If clause is null, then return null.
      3. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) clause to clauses.
   5. If predicateType is "`and`", then return a [document rule conjunction](#7611-data-model) whose [clauses](#7611-data-model) is clauses.
   6. Return a [document rule disjunction](#7611-data-model) whose [clauses](#7611-data-model) is clauses.
5. If predicateType is "`not`":
   1. If input has any [key](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) other than "`not`":
      1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the document rule predicate had unexpected extra options.
      2. Return null.
   2. Let clause be the result of [parsing a document rule predicate](#7612-parsing) given input\[predicateType\], document, and baseURL.
   3. If clause is null, then return null.
   4. Return a [document rule negation](#7611-data-model) whose [clause](#7611-data-model) is clause.
6. If predicateType is "`href_matches`":
   1. If input has any [key](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) other than "`href_matches`" or "`relative_to`":
      1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the document rule predicate had unexpected extra options.
      2. Return null.
   2. If input\["`relative_to`"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps):
      1. If input\["`relative_to`"\] is neither "`ruleset`" nor "`document`":
         1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the supplied relative-to value was invalid.
         2. Return null.
      2. If input\["`relative_to`"\] is "`document`", then set baseURL to document's [document base URL](#243-document-base-urls).
   3. Let rawPatterns be input\["`href_matches`"\].
   4. If rawPatterns is not a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists), then set rawPatterns to « rawPatterns ».
   5. Let patterns be an empty [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).
   6. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) rawPattern of rawPatterns:
      1. Let pattern be the result of [building a URL pattern from an Infra value](https://urlpattern.spec.whatwg.org/#build-a-url-pattern-from-an-infra-value) given rawPattern and baseURL. If this step throws an exception, catch the exception and set pattern to null.
      2. If pattern is null:
         1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the supplied URL pattern was invalid.
         2. Return null.
      3. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) pattern to patterns.
   7. Return a [document rule URL pattern predicate](#7611-data-model) whose [patterns](#7611-data-model) is patterns.
7. If predicateType is "`selector_matches`":
   1. If input has any [key](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) other than "`selector_matches`":
      1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the document rule predicate had unexpected extra options.
      2. Return null.
   2. Let rawSelectors be input\["`selector_matches`"\].
   3. If rawSelectors is not a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists), then set rawSelectors to « rawSelectors ».
   4. Let selectors be an empty [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).
   5. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) rawSelector of rawSelectors:
      1. Let parsedSelectorList be failure.
      2. If rawSelector is a string, then set parsedSelectorList to the result of [parsing a selector](https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#parse-a-selector) given rawSelector.
      3. If parsedSelectorList is failure:
         1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the supplied selector list was invalid.
         2. Return null.
      4. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) selector of parsedSelectorList, [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) selector to selectors.
   6. Return a [document rule selector predicate](#7611-data-model) whose [selectors](#7611-data-model) is selectors.
8. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): this step is never reached, as one of the previous branches was taken.

##### 7.6.1.3 Processing model

A speculative load candidate is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) with the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):
- URL, a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url)
- No-Vary-Search hint, a [URL search variance](https://httpwg.org/http-extensions/draft-ietf-httpbis-no-vary-search.html#name-data-model)
- eagerness, a [speculation rule eagerness](#7611-data-model)
- referrer policy, a [referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy)
- tags, an [ordered set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) of [speculation rule tags](#7611-data-model)

A prefetch candidate is a [speculative load candidate](#7613-processing-model) with the following additional [item](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):
- anonymization policy, a [prefetch IP anonymization policy](#7613-processing-model)

A prefetch IP anonymization policy is either null or a [cross-origin prefetch IP anonymization policy](#7613-processing-model).

A cross-origin prefetch IP anonymization policy is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) whose single [item](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) is its origin, an [origin](#711-origins).

---

A [speculative load candidate](#7613-processing-model) candidateA is redundant with another [speculative load candidate](#7613-processing-model) candidateB if the following steps return true:
1. If candidateA's [No-Vary-Search hint](#7613-processing-model) is not equal to candidateB's [No-Vary-Search hint](#7613-processing-model), then return false.
2. If candidateA's [URL](#7613-processing-model) is not [equivalent modulo search variance](https://httpwg.org/http-extensions/draft-ietf-httpbis-no-vary-search.html#name-comparing) to candidateB's [URL](#7613-processing-model) given candidateA's [No-Vary-Search hint](#7613-processing-model), then return false.
3. Return true.

> [!note]
> The requirement that the [No-Vary-Search hints](#7613-processing-model) be equivalent is somewhat strict. It means that some cases which could theoretically be treated as matching, are not treated as such. Thus, redundant speculative loads could happen.
> 
> However, allowing more lenient matching makes the check no longer an equivalence relation, and producing such matches would require an implementation strategy that does a full comparison, instead of a simpler one using normalized URL keys. This is in line with the best practices for server operators, and attendant HTTP cache implementation notes, in [No Vary Search § 6 Comparing](https://httpwg.org/http-extensions/draft-ietf-httpbis-no-vary-search.html#section-6).
> 
> In practice, we do not expect this to cause redundant speculative loads, since server operators and the corresponding speculation rules-writing web developers will follow best practices and use static \`[`No-Vary-Search`](https://httpwg.org/http-extensions/draft-ietf-httpbis-no-vary-search.html#name-http-header-field-definitio)\` header values/speculation rule hints.

> [!example]
> Consider three [speculative load candidates](#7613-processing-model):
> 1. A has a [URL](#7613-processing-model) of `https://example.com?a=1&b=1` and a [No-Vary-Search hint](#7613-processing-model) parsed from `params=("a")`.
> 2. B has a [URL](#7613-processing-model) of `https://example.com?a=2&b=1` and a [No-Vary-Search hint](#7613-processing-model) parsed from `params=("b")`.
> 3. C has a [URL](#7613-processing-model) of `https://example.com?a=2&b=2` and a [No-Vary-Search hint](#7613-processing-model) parsed from `params=("a")`.
> 
> With the current definition of [redundant with](#7613-processing-model), none of these candidates are redundant with each other. A [speculation rule set](#7611-data-model) which contained all three could cause three separate speculative loads.
> 
> A definition which did not require equivalent [No-Vary-Search hints](#7613-processing-model) could consider A and B to match (using A's [No-Vary-Search hint](#7613-processing-model)), and B and C to match (using B's [No-Vary-Search hint](#7613-processing-model)). But it could not consider A and C to match, so it would not be transitive, and thus not an equivalence relation.

---

Every [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has speculation rule sets, a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [speculation rule sets](#7611-data-model), initially empty.

Every [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a consider speculative loads microtask queued, a boolean, initially false.

To consider speculative loads for a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document:
1. If document's [node navigable](#731-navigables) is not a [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables), then return.

   > [!note]
   > Supporting speculative loads into [child navigables](#7313-child-navigables) has some complexities and is not currently defined. It might be possible to define it in the future.

2. If document's [consider speculative loads microtask queued](#7613-processing-model) is true, then return.
3. Set document's [consider speculative loads microtask queued](#7613-processing-model) to true.
4. [Queue a microtask](#8172-queuing-tasks) given document to run the following steps:
   1. Set document's [consider speculative loads microtask queued](#7613-processing-model) to false.
   2. Run the [inner consider speculative loads steps](#7613-processing-model) for document.

In addition to the call sites explicitly given in this standard:
- When style recalculation would cause selector matching results to change, the user agent must [consider speculative loads](#7613-processing-model) for the relevant [`Document`](#311-the-document-object).
- When the user indicates interest in [hyperlinks](#461-introduction), in one of the [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) ways that the user agent uses to implement the [speculation rule eagerness](#7611-data-model) heuristics, the user agent may [consider speculative loads](#7613-processing-model) for the hyperlink's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).

  > [!example]
