  > For example, a user agent which implements "[`conservative`](#7611-data-model)" eagerness by watching for [`pointerdown`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#the-pointerdown-event) events would want to [consider speculative loads](#7613-processing-model) as part of reacting to such events.

> [!note]
> In this standard, every call to [consider speculative loads](#7613-processing-model) is given just a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), and the algorithm re-computes all possible candidates in a stateless way. A real implementation would likely cache previous computations, and pass along information from the call site to make updates more efficient. For example, if an [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element's [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute is changed, that specific element could be passed along in order to update only the related [speculative load candidate](#7613-processing-model).
> 
> Note that because of how [consider speculative loads](#7613-processing-model) queues a microtask, by the time the [inner consider speculative loads steps](#7613-processing-model) are run, multiple updates (or [cancelations](#7613-processing-model)) might be processed together.

The inner consider speculative loads steps for a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document are:
1. If document is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents), then return.
2. Let prefetchCandidates be an empty [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).
3. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) ruleSet of document's [speculation rule sets](#7613-processing-model):
   1. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) rule of ruleSet's [prefetch rules](#7611-data-model):
      1. Let anonymizationPolicy be null.
      2. If rule's [requirements](#7611-data-model) [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) "`anonymous-client-ip-when-cross-origin`", then set anonymizationPolicy to a [cross-origin prefetch IP anonymization policy](#7613-processing-model) whose [origin](#7613-processing-model) is document's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).
      3. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) url of rule's [URLs](#7611-data-model):
         1. Let referrerPolicy be the result of [computing a speculative load referrer policy](#7613-processing-model) given rule and null.
         2. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) a new [prefetch candidate](#7613-processing-model) with

            [URL](#7613-processing-model)

            url

            [No-Vary-Search hint](#7613-processing-model)

            rule's [No-Vary-Search hint](#7611-data-model)

            [eagerness](#7613-processing-model)

            rule's [eagerness](#7611-data-model)

            [referrer policy](#7613-processing-model)

            referrerPolicy

            [tags](#7613-processing-model)

            rule's [tags](#7611-data-model)

            [anonymization policy](#7613-processing-model)

            anonymizationPolicy

            to prefetchCandidates.

      4. If rule's [predicate](#7611-data-model) is not null:
         1. Let links be the result of [finding matching links](#7613-processing-model) given document and rule's [predicate](#7611-data-model).
         2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) link of links:
            1. Let referrerPolicy be the result of [computing a speculative load referrer policy](#7613-processing-model) given rule and link.
            2. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) a new [prefetch candidate](#7613-processing-model) with

               [URL](#7613-processing-model)

               link's [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements)

               [No-Vary-Search hint](#7613-processing-model)

               rule's [No-Vary-Search hint](#7611-data-model)

               [eagerness](#7613-processing-model)

               rule's [eagerness](#7611-data-model)

               [referrer policy](#7613-processing-model)

               referrerPolicy

               [tags](#7613-processing-model)

               rule's [tags](#7611-data-model)

               [anonymization policy](#7613-processing-model)

               anonymizationPolicy

               to prefetchCandidates.

4. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) prefetchRecord of document's [prefetch records](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#document-prefetch-records):
   1. If prefetchRecord's [source](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#prefetch-record-source) is not "`speculation rules`", then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   2. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): prefetchRecord's [state](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#prefetch-record-state) is not "`canceled`".
   3. If prefetchRecord is not [still being speculated](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#prefetch-record-still-being-speculated) given prefetchCandidates, then [cancel and discard](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#prefetch-record-cancel-and-discard) prefetchRecord given document.
5. Let prefetchCandidateGroups be an empty [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).
6. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) candidate of prefetchCandidates:
   1. Let group be « candidate ».
   2. [Extend](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) group with all [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) in prefetchCandidates, apart from candidate itself, which are [redundant with](#7613-processing-model) candidate and whose [eagerness](#7613-processing-model) is [at least as eager](#7611-data-model) as candidate's [eagerness](#7613-processing-model).
   3. If prefetchCandidateGroups [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) another group whose [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) are the same as group, ignoring order, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   4. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) group to prefetchCandidateGroups.

   > [!example]
   > The following speculation rules generate two [redundant](#7613-processing-model) [prefetch candidates](#7613-processing-model):
   > 
   > ```json
   > {
   >   "prefetch": [
   >     {
   >       "tag": "a",
   >       "urls": ["next.html"]
   >     },
   >     {
   >       "tag": "b",
   >       "urls": ["next.html"],
   >       "referrer_policy": "no-referrer"
   >     }
   >   ]
   > }
   > ```
   > 
   > This step will create a single group containing them both, in the given order. (The second pass through will not create a group, since its contents would be the same as the first group, just in a different order.) This means that if the user agent chooses to execute the "may" step below to enact the group, it will enact the first candidate, and ignore the second. Thus, the request will be made with the [default referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#default-referrer-policy), instead of using "[`no-referrer`](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy-no-referrer)".
   > 
   > However, the [collect tags from speculative load candidates](#7613-processing-model) algorithm will collect tags from both candidates in the group, so the \`[`Sec-Speculation-Tags`](#764-the-sec-speculation-tags-header)\` header value will be \``"a", "b"`\`. This indicates to server operators that either rule could have caused the speculative load.

7. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) group of prefetchCandidateGroups:
   1. The user agent may run the following steps:
      1. Let prefetchCandidate be group\[0\].
      2. Let tagsToSend be the result of [collecting tags from speculative load candidates](#7613-processing-model) given group.
      3. Let prefetchRecord be a new [prefetch record](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#prefetch-record) with

         [source](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#prefetch-record-source)

         "`speculation rules`"

         [URL](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#prefetch-record-url)

         prefetchCandidate's [URL](#7613-processing-model)

         [No-Vary-Search hint](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#prefetch-record-no-vary-search-hint)

         prefetchCandidate's [No-Vary-Search hint](#7613-processing-model)

         [referrer policy](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#prefetch-record-referrer-policy)

         prefetchCandidate's [referrer policy](#7613-processing-model)

         [anonymization policy](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#prefetch-record-anonymization-policy)

         prefetchCandidate's [anonymization policy](#7613-processing-model)

         [tags](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#prefetch-record-tags)

         tagsToSend

      4. [Start a referrer-initiated navigational prefetch](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#start-a-referrer-initiated-navigational-prefetch) given document and prefetchRecord.

      When deciding whether to execute this "may" step, user agents should consider prefetchCandidate's [eagerness](#7613-processing-model), in accordance to the current behavior of the user and the definitions of [speculation rule eagerness](#7611-data-model).

      prefetchCandidate's [No-Vary-Search hint](#7613-processing-model) can also be useful in implementing the heuristics defined for the [speculation rule eagerness](#7611-data-model) values. For example, a user hovering of a link whose [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) is [equivalent modulo search variance](https://httpwg.org/http-extensions/draft-ietf-httpbis-no-vary-search.html#name-comparing) to prefetchCandidate's [URL](#7613-processing-model) given prefetchCandidate's [No-Vary-Search hint](#7613-processing-model) could indicate to the user agent that performing this step would be useful.

      When deciding whether to execute this "may" step, user agents should prioritize user preferences (express or implied, such as data-saver or battery-saver modes) over the eagerness supplied by the web developer.

To compute a speculative load referrer policy given a [speculation rule](#7611-data-model) rule and an [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element, [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element, or null link:
1. If rule's [referrer policy](#7611-data-model) is not the empty string, then return rule's [referrer policy](#7611-data-model).
2. If link is null, then return the empty string.
3. Return link's [hyperlink referrer policy](#465-following-hyperlinks).

To collect tags from speculative load candidates given a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [speculative load candidates](#7613-processing-model) candidates:
1. Let tags be an empty [ordered set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets).
2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) candidate of candidates:
   1. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) tag of candidate's [tags](#7613-processing-model): [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) tag to tags.
3. [Sort in ascending order](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) tags, with tagA being less than tagB if tagA is null, or if tagA is [code unit less than](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) tagB.
4. Return tags.

---

To find matching links given a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document and a [document rule predicate](#7611-data-model) predicate:
1. Let links be an empty [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).
2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) [shadow-including descendant](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) descendant of document, in [shadow-including tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot):
   1. If descendant is not an [`a`](#451-the-a-element) or [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element with an [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   2. If descendant is not [being rendered](#151-introduction) or is part of [skipped contents](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-contain/#skips-its-contents), then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).

      > [!note]
      > Such links, though present in document, aren't available for the user to interact with, and thus are unlikely to be good candidates. In addition, they might not have their style or layout computed, which might make selector matching less efficient in user agents which skip some or all of that work for these elements.

   3. If descendant's [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) is null, or its [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) is not an [HTTP(S) scheme](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#http-scheme), then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   4. If predicate [matches](#7613-processing-model) descendant, then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) descendant to links.

3. Return links.

A [document rule predicate](#7611-data-model) predicate matches an [`a`](#451-the-a-element) or [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element el if the following steps return true, switching on predicate's type:

[document rule conjunction](#7611-data-model)
1. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) clause of predicate's [clauses](#7611-data-model):
   1. If clause does not [match](#7613-processing-model) el, then return false.
2. Return true.

[document rule disjunction](#7611-data-model)
1. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) clause of predicate's [clauses](#7611-data-model):
   1. If clause [matches](#7613-processing-model) el, then return true.
2. Return false.

[document rule negation](#7611-data-model)
1. If predicate's [clause](#7611-data-model) [matches](#7613-processing-model) el, then return false.
2. Return true.

[document rule URL pattern predicate](#7611-data-model)
1. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) pattern of predicate's [patterns](#7611-data-model):
   1. If performing a [match](https://urlpattern.spec.whatwg.org/#url-pattern-match) given pattern and el's [url](#463-api-for-hyperlink-elements) gives a non-null value, then return true.
2. Return false.

[document rule selector predicate](#7611-data-model)
1. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) selector of predicate's [selectors](#7611-data-model):
   1. If performing a [match](https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#match-a-selector-against-an-element) given selector and el with the [scoping root](https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#scoping-root) set to el's [root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) returns success, then return true.
2. Return false.

---

Speculation rules features use the speculation rules task source, which is a [task source](#8171-definitions).

> [!note]
> Because speculative loading is generally less important than processing tasks for the purpose of the current document, implementations might give [tasks](#8171-definitions) enqueued here an especially low priority.

#### 7.6.2 Navigational prefetching

For now, the navigational prefetching process is defined in the Prefetch specification. Moving it into this standard is tracked in [issue #11123](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11123). [\[PREFETCH\]](#references)

This standard refers to the following concepts defined there:
- [prefetch record](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#prefetch-record), and its items [source](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#prefetch-record-source), [URL](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#prefetch-record-url), [No-Vary-Search hint](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#prefetch-record-no-vary-search-hint), [referrer policy](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#prefetch-record-referrer-policy), [anonymization policy](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#prefetch-record-anonymization-policy), [tags](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#prefetch-record-tags), and [state](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#prefetch-record-state)
- [cancel and discard](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#prefetch-record-cancel-and-discard)
- [still being speculated](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#prefetch-record-still-being-speculated)
- [prefetch records](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#document-prefetch-records)
- [start a referrer-initiated navigational prefetch](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#start-a-referrer-initiated-navigational-prefetch)

#### 7.6.3 The \`[`Speculation-Rules`](#763-the-speculation-rules-header)\` header

The \``Speculation-Rules`\` HTTP response header allows the developer to request that the user agent fetch and apply a given [speculation rule set](#7611-data-model) to the current [`Document`](#311-the-document-object). It is a [structured header](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8941.html) whose value must be a [list](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8941.html#list) of [strings](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8941.html#string) that are all [valid URL strings](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-url-string).

To process the \``Speculation-Rules`\` header given a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document and a [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response:
1. Let parsedList be the result of [getting a structured field value](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-header-list-get-structured-header) given \`[`Speculation-Rules`](#763-the-speculation-rules-header)\` and "`list`" from response's [header list](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-header-list).
2. If parsedList is null, then return.
3. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) item of parsedList:
   1. If item is not a [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings), then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   2. Let url be the result of [URL parsing](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser) item with document's [document base URL](#243-document-base-urls).
   3. If url is failure, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   4. [In parallel](#211-parallelism):
      1. Optionally, wait for an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) amount of time.

         > [!note]
         > This allows the implementation to prioritize other work ahead of loading speculation rules, as especially during [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) creation and header processing, there are often many more important things going on.

      2. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [speculation rules task source](#7613-processing-model) given document's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) to perform the following steps:
         1. Let request be a new [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) whose [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url) is url, [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) is "`speculationrules`", and [mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-mode) is "`cors`".
         2. [Fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request with the following *[processResponseConsumeBody](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#process-response-end-of-body)* steps given [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response and null, failure, or a [byte sequence](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-byte-sequences) bodyBytes:
            1. If bodyBytes is null or failure, then abort these steps.
            2. If response's [status](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-status) is not an [ok status](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#ok-status), then abort these steps.
            3. If the result of [extracting a MIME type](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-header-extract-mime-type) from response's [header list](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-header-list) does not have an [essence](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type-essence) of "[`application/speculationrules+json`](#176-applicationspeculationrulesjson)", then abort these steps.
            4. Let bodyText be the result of [UTF-8 decoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8-decode) bodyBytes.
            5. Let ruleSet be the result of [parsing a speculation rule set string](#7612-parsing) given bodyText, document, and response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url). If this throws an exception, then abort these steps.
            6. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) ruleSet to document's [speculation rule sets](#7613-processing-model).
            7. [Consider speculative loads](#7613-processing-model) for document.

#### 7.6.4 The \`[`Sec-Speculation-Tags`](#764-the-sec-speculation-tags-header)\` header

The \``Sec-Speculation-Tags`\` HTTP request header specifies the web developer-provided tags associated with the speculative navigation request. It can also be used to distinguish speculative navigation requests from speculative subresource requests, since \`[`Sec-Purpose`](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#sec-purpose-header)\` can be sent by both categories of requests.

The header is a [structured header](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8941.html) whose value must be a [list](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8941.html#list). The list can contain either [token](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8941.html#token) or [string](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc8941.html#string) values. String values represent developer-provided tags, whereas token values represent predefined tags. As of now, the only predefined tag is `null`, which indicates a speculative navigation request with no developer-defined tag.

#### 7.6.5 Security considerations

##### 7.6.5.1 Cross-site requests

Speculative loads can be initiated by web pages to cross-site destinations. However, because such cross-site speculative loads are always done without [credentials](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#credentials), as explained [below](#7662-state-partitioning), ambient authority is limited to requests that are already possible via other mechanisms on the platform.

The \`[`Speculation-Rules`](#763-the-speculation-rules-header)\` header can also be used to issue requests, for JSON documents whose body will be [parsed as a speculation rule set string](#7612-parsing). However, they use the "`same-origin`" [credentials mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode), the "`cors`" [mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-mode), and responses which do not use the [`application/speculationrules+json`](#176-applicationspeculationrulesjson) [MIME type essence](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type-essence) are ignored, so they are not useful in mounting attacks.

##### 7.6.5.2 Injected content

Because links in a document can be selected for speculative loading via [document rule predicates](#7611-data-model), developers need to be cautious if such links might contain user-generated markup. For example, if the [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) of a link can be entered by one user and displayed to all other users, a malicious user might choose a value like "`/logout`", causing other users' browsers to automatically log out of the site when that link is speculatively loaded. Using a [document rule selector predicate](#7611-data-model) to exclude such potentially-dangerous links, or using a [document rule URL pattern predicate](#7611-data-model) to allowlist known-safe links, are useful techniques in this regard.

As with all uses of the [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element, developers need to be cautious about inserting user-provided content into `<script type=speculationrules>`'s [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text). In particular, the insertion of an unescaped closing `</script>` tag could be used to break out of the [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element context and inject attacker-controlled markup.

The `<script type=speculationrules>` feature causes activity in response to content found in the document, so it is worth considering the options open to an attacker able to inject unescaped HTML. Such an attacker is already able to inject JavaScript or [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) elements. Speculative loads are generally less dangerous than arbitrary script execution. However, the use of [document rule predicates](#7611-data-model) could be used to speculatively load links in the document, and the existence of those loads could provide a vector for exfiltrating information about those links. Defense-in-depth against this possibility is provided by Content Security Policy. In particular, the `script-src` directive can be used to restrict the parsing of speculation rules [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements, and the `default-src` directive applies to navigational prefetch requests arising from such speculation rules. Additional defense is provided by the requirement that speculative loads are only performed to [potentially-trustworthy URLs](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-secure-contexts/#potentially-trustworthy-url), so an on-path attacker would only have access to metadata and traffic analysis, and could not see the URLs directly. [\[CSP\]](#references)

It's generally not expected that user-generated content will be added as arbitrary response headers: server operators are already going to encounter significant trouble if this is possible. It is therefore unlikely that the \`[`Speculation-Rules`](#763-the-speculation-rules-header)\` header meaningfully expands the XSS attack surface. For this reason, Content Security Policy does not apply to the loading of rule sets via that header.

##### 7.6.5.3 IP anonymization

This standard allows developers to request that navigational prefetches are performed using IP anonymization technology provided by the user agent. The details of this anonymization are not specified, but some general security principles apply.

To the extent IP anonymization is implemented using a proxy service, it is advisable to minimize the information available to the service operator and other entities on the network path. This likely involves, at a minimum, the use of TLS for the connection.

Site operators need to be aware that, similar to virtual private network (VPN) technology, the client IP address seen by the HTTP server might not exactly correspond to the user's actual network provider or location, and a traffic for multiple distinct subscribers could originate from a single client IP address. This can affect site operators' security and abuse prevention measures. IP anonymization measures might make an effort to use an egress IP address which has a similar geolocation or is located in the same jurisdiction as the user, but any such behavior is particular to the user agent and not guaranteed.

#### 7.6.6 Privacy considerations

##### 7.6.6.1 Heuristics and optionality

The [consider speculative loads](#7613-processing-model) algorithm contains a crucial "may" step, which encourages user agents to [start referrer-initiated navigational prefetches](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#start-a-referrer-initiated-navigational-prefetch) based on a combination of the [speculation rule eagerness](#7611-data-model) and other features of the user's environment. Because it can be observable to the document whether speculative loads are performed, user agents must take care to protect privacy when making such decisions—for instance by only using information which is already available to the origin. If these heuristics depend on any persistent state, that state must be erased whenever the user erases other site data. If the user agent automatically clears other site data from time to time, it must erase such persistent state at the same time.

> [!note]
> The use of [origin](#711-origins) instead of [site](#7111-sites) here is intentional. Although same-site origins are generally allowed to coordinate if they wish, the web's security model is premised on preventing origins from accessing the data of other origins, even same-site ones. Thus, the user agent needs to be sure not to leak such data unintentionally across origins, not just across sites.

Examples of inputs which would be already known to the document:
- author-supplied [eagerness](#7611-data-model)
- order of appearance in the document
- whether a link is in the viewport
- whether the cursor is near a link
- rendered size of a link

Examples of persistent data related to the origin (which the origin could have gathered itself) but which must be erased according to user intent:
- whether the user has clicked this or similar links on this document or other documents on the same origin

Examples of device information which might be valuable in deciding whether speculative loading is appropriate, but which needs to be considered as part of the user agent's overall privacy posture because it can make the user more identifiable across origins:
- coarse device class (CPU, memory)
- coarse battery level
- whether the network connection is known to be metered
- any user-toggleable settings, such as a speculative loading toggle, a battery-saver toggle, or a data-saver toggle

##### 7.6.6.2 State partitioning

The [start a referrer-initiated navigational prefetch](https://wicg.github.io/nav-speculation/prefetch.html#start-a-referrer-initiated-navigational-prefetch) algorithm is designed to ensure that the HTTP requests that it issues behave consistently with how user agents partition [credentials](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#credentials) according to [storage keys](https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-key). This property is maintained even for cross-partition prefetches, as follows.

If a future navigation using a prefetched response would load a document in the same partition, then at prefetch time, the partitioned credentials can be sent, as they can with subresource requests and scripted fetches. If such a future navigation would instead load a document in another partition, it would be inconsistent with the partitioning scheme to use partitioned credentials for the destination partition (since this would cross the boundary between partitions without a top-level navigation) and also inconsistent to use partitioned credentials within the originating partition (since this would result in the user seeing a document with different state than a non-prefetched navigation). Instead, a third, initially empty, partition is used for such requests. These requests therefore send along no credentials from either partition. However, the resulting prefetched response body constructed using this initially-empty partition can only be used if, at activation time, the destination partition contains no credentials.

This is somewhat similar to the behavior of only sending such prefetch requests if the destination partition is known ahead of time to not contain credentials. However, to avoid such behavior being used a way of probing for the presence of credentials, instead such prefetch requests are always completed, and in the case of conflicting credentials, their results are not used.

Redirects are possible between these two types of requests. A redirect from a same- to cross-partition URL could contain information derived from partitioned credentials in the originating partition; however, this is equivalent to the originating document fetching the same-partition URL itself and then issuing a request for the cross-partition URL. A redirect from a cross- to same-origin URL could carry credentials from the isolated partition, but since this partition has no prior state this does not enable tracking based on the user's prior browsing activity on that site, and the document could construct the same state by issuing uncredentialed requests itself.

##### 7.6.6.3 Identity joining

Speculative loads provide a mechanism through which HTTP requests for later top-level navigation can be made without a user gesture. It is natural to ask whether it is possible for two coordinating sites to connect user identities.

Since existing [credentials](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#credentials) for the destination site are not sent (as explained in the previous section), that site is limited in its ability to identify the user before navigation in a similar way to if the referrer site had simply used [`fetch()`](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-global-fetch) to make an uncredentialed request. Upon navigation, this becomes similar to ordinary navigation (e.g., by clicking a link that was not speculatively loaded).

To the extent that user agents attempt to mitigate identity joining for ordinary fetches and navigations, they can apply similar mitigations to speculatively-loaded navigations.

### 7.7 The \`[`X-Frame-Options`](#77-the-x-frame-options-header)\` header

The \``X-Frame-Options`\` HTTP response header is a way of controlling whether and how a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) may be loaded inside of a [child navigable](#7313-child-navigables). For sites using CSP, the [`frame-ancestors`](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#frame-ancestors) directive provides more granular control over the same situations. It was originally defined in HTTP Header Field X-Frame-Options, but the definition and processing model here supersedes that document. [\[CSP\]](#references) [\[RFC7034\]](#references)

> [!note]
> In particular, HTTP Header Field X-Frame-Options specified an \``ALLOW-FROM`\` variant of the header, but that is not to be implemented.

> [!note]
> Per the below processing model, if both a CSP [`frame-ancestors`](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#frame-ancestors) directive and an \`[`X-Frame-Options`](#77-the-x-frame-options-header)\` header are used in the same [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response), then \`[`X-Frame-Options`](#77-the-x-frame-options-header)\` is ignored.

For web developers and conformance checkers, its value [ABNF](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#abnf) is:

```abnf
X-Frame-Options = "DENY" / "SAMEORIGIN"
```

To check a navigation response's adherence to \``X-Frame-Options`\`, given a [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response, a [navigable](#731-navigables) navigable, a [CSP list](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#csp-list) cspList, and an [origin](#711-origins) destinationOrigin:
1. If navigable is not a [child navigable](#7313-child-navigables), then return true.
2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) policy of cspList:
   1. If policy's [disposition](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#policy-disposition) is not "`enforce`", then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   2. If policy's [directive set](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#policy-directive-set) [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) a [`frame-ancestors`](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#frame-ancestors) directive, then return true.
3. Let rawXFrameOptions be the result of [getting, decoding, and splitting](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-header-list-get-decode-split) \`[`X-Frame-Options`](#77-the-x-frame-options-header)\` from response's [header list](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-header-list).
4. Let xFrameOptions be a new [set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets).
5. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) value of rawXFrameOptions, [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) value, [converted to ASCII lowercase](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings), to xFrameOptions.
6. If xFrameOptions's [size](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) is greater than 1, and xFrameOptions [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) any of "`deny`", "`allowall`", or "`sameorigin`", then return false.

   > [!note]
   > The intention here is to block any attempts at applying \`[`X-Frame-Options`](#77-the-x-frame-options-header)\` which were trying to do something valid, but appear confused.

   > [!note]
   > This is the only impact of the legacy \``ALLOWALL`\` value on the processing model.

7. If xFrameOptions's [size](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) is greater than 1, then return true.

   > [!note]
   > This means it contains multiple invalid values, which we treat the same way as if the header was omitted entirely.

8. If xFrameOptions\[0\] is "`deny`", then return false.
9. If xFrameOptions\[0\] is "`sameorigin`":
   1. Let containerDocument be navigable's [container document](#7313-child-navigables).
   2. [While](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration) containerDocument is not null:
      1. If containerDocument's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is not [same origin](#711-origins) with destinationOrigin, then return false.
      2. Set containerDocument to containerDocument's [container document](#7313-child-navigables).
10. Return true.

    > [!note]
    > If we've reached this point then we have a lone invalid value (which could potentially be one the legacy \``ALLOWALL`\` or \``ALLOW-FROM`\` forms). These are treated as if the header were omitted entirely.

---

> [!example]
> The following table illustrates the processing of various values for the header, including non-conformant ones:
> 
> | \`[`X-Frame-Options`](#77-the-x-frame-options-header)\` | Valid | Result |
> | --- | --- | --- |
> | \``DENY`\` | ✅ | embedding disallowed |
> | \``SAMEORIGIN`\` | ✅ | same-origin embedding allowed |
> | \``INVALID`\` | ❌ | embedding allowed |
> | \``ALLOWALL`\` | ❌ | embedding allowed |
> | \``ALLOW-FROM=https://example.com/`\` | ❌ | embedding allowed (from anywhere) |

> [!example]
> The following table illustrates how various non-conformant cases involving multiple values are processed:
> 
> | \`[`X-Frame-Options`](#77-the-x-frame-options-header)\` | Result |
> | --- | --- |
> | \``SAMEORIGIN, SAMEORIGIN`\` | same-origin embedding allowed |
> | \``SAMEORIGIN, DENY`\` | embedding disallowed |
> | \``SAMEORIGIN,`\` | embedding disallowed |
> | \``SAMEORIGIN, ALLOWALL`\` | embedding disallowed |
> | \``SAMEORIGIN, INVALID`\` | embedding disallowed |
> | \``ALLOWALL, INVALID`\` | embedding disallowed |
> | \``ALLOWALL,`\` | embedding disallowed |
> | \``INVALID, INVALID`\` | embedding allowed |
> 
> The same results are obtained whether the values are delivered in a single header whose value is comma-delimited, or in multiple headers.

### 7.8 The \`[`Refresh`](#78-the-refresh-header)\` header

The \``Refresh`\` HTTP response header is the HTTP-equivalent to a [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element with an [`http-equiv`](#4253-pragma-directives) attribute in the [Refresh state](#4253-pragma-directives). It takes [the same value](#4253-pragma-directives) and works largely the same. Its processing model is detailed in [create and initialize a `Document` object](#751-shared-document-creation-infrastructure).

### 7.9 Browser user interface considerations

Browser user agents should provide the ability to [navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation), [reload](#743-reloading-and-traversing), and [stop loading](#7511-aborting-a-document-load) any [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables) in their [top-level traversable set](#7312-top-level-traversables).

> [!example]
> For example, via a location bar and reload/stop button UI.

Browser user agents should provide the ability to [traverse by a delta](#743-reloading-and-traversing) any [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables) in their [top-level traversable set](#7312-top-level-traversables).

> [!example]
> For example, via back and forward buttons, possibly including long-press abilities to change the delta.

It is suggested that such user agents allow traversal by deltas greater than one, to avoid letting a page "trap" the user by stuffing the session history with spurious entries. (For example, via repeated calls to [`history.pushState()`](#725-the-history-interface) or [fragment navigations](#74233-fragment-navigations).)

> [!note]
> Some user agents have heuristics for translating a single "back" or "forward" button press into a larger delta, specifically to overcome such abuses. We are contemplating specifying these heuristics in [issue #7832](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/7832).

Browser user agents should offer users the ability to [create a fresh top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables), given a user-provided or user agent-determined initial [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url).

> [!example]
> For example, via a "new tab" or "new window" button.

Browser user agents should offer users the ability to arbitrarily [close](#7316-navigable-destruction) any [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables) in their [top-level traversable set](#7312-top-level-traversables).

> [!example]
> For example, by clicking a "close tab" button.

---

Browser user agents may provide ways for the user to explicitly cause any [navigable](#731-navigables) (not just a [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables)) to [navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation), [reload](#743-reloading-and-traversing), or [stop loading](#7511-aborting-a-document-load).

> [!example]
> For example, via a context menu.

Browser user agents may provide the ability for users to [destroy a top-level traversable](#7316-navigable-destruction).

> [!example]
> For example, by force-closing a window containing one or more such [top-level traversables](#7312-top-level-traversables).

---

When a user requests a [reload](#743-reloading-and-traversing) of a [navigable](#731-navigables) whose [active session history entry](#731-navigables)'s [document state](#7411-session-history-entries)'s [resource](#7412-document-state) is a [POST resource](#7412-document-state), the user agent should prompt the user to confirm the operation first, since otherwise transactions (e.g., purchases or database modifications) could be repeated.

When a user requests a [reload](#743-reloading-and-traversing) of a [navigable](#731-navigables), user agents may provide a mechanism for ignoring any caches when reloading.

---

All calls to [navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation) initiated by the mechanisms mentioned above must have the *[userInvolvement](#7422-beginning-navigation)* argument set to "[`browser UI`](#7421-supporting-concepts)".

All calls to [reload](#743-reloading-and-traversing) initiated by the mechanisms mentioned above must have the *[userInvolvement](#743-reloading-and-traversing)* argument set to "[`browser UI`](#7421-supporting-concepts)".

All calls to [traverse the history by a delta](#743-reloading-and-traversing) initiated by the mechanisms mentioned above must not pass a value for the *[sourceDocument](#743-reloading-and-traversing)* argument.

---

The above recommendations, and the data structures in this specification, are not meant to place restrictions on how user agents represent the session history to the user.

For example, although a [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables)'s [session history entries](#7311-traversable-navigables) are stored and maintained as a list, and the user agent is recommended to give an interface for [traversing that list by a delta](#743-reloading-and-traversing), a novel user agent could instead or in addition present a tree-like view, with each page having multiple "forward" pages that the user can choose between.

Similarly, although session history for all descendant [navigables](#731-navigables) is stored in their [traversable navigable](#7311-traversable-navigables), user agents could present the user with a more nuanced per-[navigable](#731-navigables) view of the session history.

---

Browser user agents may use a [top-level browsing context](#7322-related-browsing-contexts)'s [is popup](#732-browsing-contexts) boolean for the following purposes:
- Deciding whether or not to provide a minimal web browser user interface for the corresponding [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables).
- Performing the optional steps in [set up browsing context features](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view/#set-up-browsing-context-features).

In both cases user agents might additionally incorporate user preferences, or present a choice as to whether to go down the popup route.

User agents that provide a minimal user interface for such popups are encouraged to not hide the browser's location bar.

## 8 Web application APIs

### 8.1 Scripting

#### 8.1.1 Introduction

Various mechanisms can cause author-provided executable code to run in the context of a document. These mechanisms include, but are probably not limited to:
- Processing of [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements.
- Navigating to [`javascript:` URLs](#74232-the-javascript-url-special-case).
- Event handlers, whether registered through the DOM using `addEventListener()`, by explicit [event handler content attributes](#8181-event-handlers), by [event handler IDL attributes](#8181-event-handlers), or otherwise.
- Processing of technologies like SVG that have their own scripting features.

#### 8.1.2 Agents and agent clusters

##### 8.1.2.1 Integration with the JavaScript agent formalism

JavaScript defines the concept of an [agent](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agents). This section gives the mapping of that language-level concept on to the web platform.

> [!note]
> Conceptually, the [agent](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agents) concept is an architecture-independent, idealized "thread" in which JavaScript code runs. Such code can involve multiple globals/[realms](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) that can synchronously access each other, and thus needs to run in a single execution thread.
> 
> Two [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) objects having the same [agent](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agents) does not indicate they can directly access all objects created in each other's realms. They would have to be [same origin-domain](#711-origins); see [IsPlatformObjectSameOrigin](#72133-isplatformobjectsameorigin--o-).

The following types of agents exist on the web platform:

Similar-origin window agent

Contains various [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) objects which can potentially reach each other, either directly or by using [`document.domain`](#7112-relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction).

If the encompassing [agent cluster](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters)'s [is origin-keyed](#8122-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-cluster-formalism) is true, then all the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) objects will be [same origin](#711-origins), can reach each other directly, and [`document.domain`](#7112-relaxing-the-same-origin-restriction) will no-op.

> [!note]
> Two [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) objects that are [same origin](#711-origins) can be in different [similar-origin window agents](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism), for instance if they are each in their own [browsing context group](#7323-groupings-of-browsing-contexts).

Dedicated worker agent

Contains a single [`DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10212-dedicated-workers-and-the-dedicatedworkerglobalscope-interface).

Shared worker agent

Contains a single [`SharedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface).

Service worker agent

Contains a single [`ServiceWorkerGlobalScope`](https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#serviceworkerglobalscope).

Worklet agent

Contains a single [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope) object.

> [!note]
> Although a given worklet can have multiple realms, each such realm needs its own agent, as each realm can be executing code independently and at the same time as the others.

Only [shared](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism) and [dedicated worker agents](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism) allow the use of JavaScript [`Atomics`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-atomics-object) APIs to potentially [block](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-forward-progress).

To create an agent, given a boolean canBlock:
1. Let signifier be a new unique internal value.
2. Let candidateExecution be a new [candidate execution](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-candidate-executions).
3. Let agent be a new [agent](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agents) whose \[\[CanBlock\]\] is canBlock, \[\[Signifier\]\] is signifier, \[\[CandidateExecution\]\] is candidateExecution, and \[\[IsLockFree1\]\], \[\[IsLockFree2\]\], and \[\[LittleEndian\]\] are set at the implementation's discretion.
4. Set agent's [event loop](#8171-definitions) to a new [event loop](#8171-definitions).
5. Return agent.

For a [realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms) realm, the [agent](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agents) whose \[\[Signifier\]\] is realm.\[\[AgentSignifier\]\] is the realm's agent.

The relevant agent for a [platform object](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object) platformObject is platformObject's [relevant realm](#81334-relevant)'s [agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism).

> [!note]
> The agent equivalent of the [current realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#current-realm) is the [surrounding agent](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#surrounding-agent).

##### 8.1.2.2 Integration with the JavaScript agent cluster formalism

JavaScript also defines the concept of an [agent cluster](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters), which this standard maps to the web platform by placing agents appropriately when they are created using the [obtain a similar-origin window agent](#8122-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-cluster-formalism) or [obtain a worker/worklet agent](#8122-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-cluster-formalism) algorithms.

The [agent cluster](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters) concept is crucial for defining the JavaScript memory model, and in particular among which [agents](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agents) the backing data of [`SharedArrayBuffer`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-sharedarraybuffer-objects) objects can be shared.

> [!note]
> Conceptually, the [agent cluster](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters) concept is an architecture-independent, idealized "process boundary" that groups together multiple "threads" ([agents](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agents)). The [agent clusters](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters) defined by the specification are generally more restrictive than the actual process boundaries implemented in user agents. By enforcing these idealized divisions at the specification level, we ensure that web developers see interoperable behavior with regard to shared memory, even in the face of varying and changing user agent process models.

An [agent cluster](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters) has an associated cross-origin isolation mode, which is a [cross-origin isolation mode](#7323-groupings-of-browsing-contexts). It is initially "[`none`](#7323-groupings-of-browsing-contexts)".

An [agent cluster](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters) has an associated is origin-keyed (a boolean), which is initially false.

---

The following defines the allocation of the [agent clusters](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters) of [similar-origin window agents](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism).

An agent cluster key is a [site](#7111-sites) or [tuple origin](#711-origins). Without web developer action to achieve [origin-keyed agent clusters](#712-origin-keyed-agent-clusters), it will be a [site](#7111-sites).

> [!note]
> An equivalent formulation is that an [agent cluster key](#8122-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-cluster-formalism) can be a [scheme-and-host](#7111-sites) or an [origin](#711-origins).

To obtain a similar-origin window agent, given an [origin](#711-origins) origin, a [browsing context group](#7323-groupings-of-browsing-contexts) group, and a boolean requestsOAC, run these steps:
1. Let site be the result of [obtaining a site](#7111-sites) with origin.
2. Let key be site.
3. If group's [cross-origin isolation mode](#7323-groupings-of-browsing-contexts) is not "[`none`](#7323-groupings-of-browsing-contexts)", then set key to origin.
4. Otherwise, if group's [historical agent cluster key map](#7323-groupings-of-browsing-contexts)\[origin\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then set key to group's [historical agent cluster key map](#7323-groupings-of-browsing-contexts)\[origin\].
5. Otherwise:
   1. If requestsOAC is true, then set key to origin.
   2. Set group's [historical agent cluster key map](#7323-groupings-of-browsing-contexts)\[origin\] to key.
6. If group's [agent cluster map](#7323-groupings-of-browsing-contexts)\[key\] [does not exist](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps):
   1. Let agentCluster be a new [agent cluster](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters).
   2. Set agentCluster's [cross-origin isolation mode](#8122-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-cluster-formalism) to group's [cross-origin isolation mode](#7323-groupings-of-browsing-contexts).
   3. If key is an [origin](#711-origins):
      1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): key is origin.
      2. Set agentCluster's [is origin-keyed](#8122-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-cluster-formalism) to true.
   4. Add the result of [creating an agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism), given false, to agentCluster.
   5. Set group's [agent cluster map](#7323-groupings-of-browsing-contexts)\[key\] to agentCluster.
7. Return the single [similar-origin window agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism) contained in group's [agent cluster map](#7323-groupings-of-browsing-contexts)\[key\].

> [!note]
> This means that there is only one [similar-origin window agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism) per browsing context agent cluster. (However, [dedicated worker](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism) and [worklet agents](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism) might be in the same cluster.)

---

The following defines the allocation of the [agent clusters](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters) of all other types of agents.

To obtain a worker/worklet agent, given an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) or null outside settings, a boolean isTopLevel, and a boolean canBlock, run these steps:
1. Let agentCluster be null.
2. If isTopLevel is true:
   1. Set agentCluster to a new [agent cluster](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters).
   2. Set agentCluster's [is origin-keyed](#8122-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-cluster-formalism) to true.

      > [!note]
      > These workers can be considered to be origin-keyed. However, this is not exposed through any APIs (in the way that [`originAgentCluster`](#712-origin-keyed-agent-clusters) exposes the origin-keyedness for windows).

3. Otherwise:
   1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): outside settings is not null.
   2. Let ownerAgent be outside settings's [realm](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects)'s [agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism).
   3. Set agentCluster to the agent cluster which contains ownerAgent.
4. Let agent be the result of [creating an agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism) given canBlock.
5. Add agent to agentCluster.
6. Return agent.

To obtain a dedicated/shared worker agent, given an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) outside settings and a boolean isShared, return the result of [obtaining a worker/worklet agent](#8122-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-cluster-formalism) given outside settings, isShared, and true.

To obtain a worklet agent, given an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) outside settings, return the result of [obtaining a worker/worklet agent](#8122-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-cluster-formalism) given outside settings, false, and false.

To obtain a service worker agent, return the result of [obtaining a worker/worklet agent](#8122-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-cluster-formalism) given null, true, and false.

---

> [!example]
> The following pairs of global objects are each within the same [agent cluster](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters), and thus can use [`SharedArrayBuffer`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-sharedarraybuffer-objects) instances to share memory with each other:
> - A [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object and a dedicated worker that it created.
> - A worker (of any type) and a dedicated worker it created.
> - A [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object A and the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object of an [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) element that A created that could be [same origin-domain](#711-origins) with A.
> - A [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object and a [same origin-domain](#711-origins) [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object that opened it.
> - A [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object and a worklet that it created.
> 
> The following pairs of global objects are *not* within the same [agent cluster](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters), and thus cannot share memory:
> - A [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object and a shared worker it created.
> - A worker (of any type) and a shared worker it created.
> - A [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object and a service worker it created.
> - A [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object A and the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object of an [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) element that A created that cannot be [same origin-domain](#711-origins) with A.
> - Any two [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) objects with no opener or ancestor relationship. This holds even if the two [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) objects are [same origin](#711-origins).

#### 8.1.3 Realms and their counterparts

The JavaScript specification introduces the [realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms) concept, representing a global environment in which script is run. Each realm comes with an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects); much of this specification is devoted to defining that global object and its properties.

For web specifications, it is often useful to associate values or algorithms with a realm/global object pair. When the values are specific to a particular type of realm, they are associated directly with the global object in question, e.g., in the definition of the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) or [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) interfaces. When the values have utility across multiple realms, we use the [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) concept.

Finally, in some cases it is necessary to track associated values before a realm/global object/environment settings object even comes into existence (for example, during [navigation](#7422-beginning-navigation)). These values are tracked in the [environment](#8131-environments) concept.

##### 8.1.3.1 Environments

An environment is an object that identifies the settings of a current or potential execution environment (i.e., a [navigation params](#7421-supporting-concepts)'s [reserved environment](#7421-supporting-concepts) or a [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request)'s [reserved client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-reserved-client)). An [environment](#8131-environments) has the following fields:

An id

An opaque string that uniquely identifies this [environment](#8131-environments).

A creation URL

A [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) that represents the location of the resource with which this [environment](#8131-environments) is associated.

> [!note]
> In the case of a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects), this URL might be distinct from its [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), due to mechanisms such as [`history.pushState()`](#725-the-history-interface) which modify the latter.

A top-level creation URL

Null or a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) that represents the [creation URL](#8131-environments) of the "top-level" [environment](#8131-environments). It is null for workers and worklets.

A top-level origin

A for now [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) value, null, or an [origin](#711-origins). For a "top-level" potential execution environment it is null (i.e., when there is no response yet); otherwise it is the "top-level" [environment](#8131-environments)'s [origin](#8132-environment-settings-objects). For a dedicated worker or worklet it is the [top-level origin](#8131-environments) of its creator. For a shared or service worker it is an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) value.

> [!note]
> This is distinct from the [top-level creation URL](#8131-environments)'s [origin](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-origin) when sandboxing, workers, and worklets are involved.

A target browsing context

Null or a target [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) for a [navigation request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#navigation-request).

An active service worker

Null or a [service worker](https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#dfn-service-worker) that [controls](https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#dfn-control) the [environment](#8131-environments).

An execution ready flag

A flag that indicates whether the environment setup is done. It is initially unset.

Specifications may define environment discarding steps for environments. The steps take an [environment](#8131-environments) as input.

> [!note]
> The [environment discarding steps](#8131-environments) are run for only a select few environments: the ones that will never become execution ready because, for example, they failed to load.

##### 8.1.3.2 Environment settings objects

An environment settings object is an [environment](#8131-environments) that additionally specifies algorithms for:

A realm execution context

A [JavaScript execution context](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-execution-contexts) shared by all [scripts](#4121-the-script-element) that use this settings object, i.e., all scripts in a given [realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms). When we [run a classic script](#8144-calling-scripts) or [run a module script](#8144-calling-scripts), this execution context becomes the top of the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack), on top of which another execution context specific to the script in question is pushed. (This setup ensures [Source Text Module Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-source-text-module-records)'s [Evaluate](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-moduleevaluation) knows which realm to use.)

A module map

A [module map](#8167-module-related-host-hooks) that is used when importing JavaScript modules.

An API base URL

A [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) used by APIs called by scripts that use this [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) to [parse URLs](#242-parsing-urls).

An origin

An [origin](#711-origins) used in security checks.

A has cross-site ancestor

A boolean used in security checks.

A policy container

A [policy container](#717-policy-containers) containing policies used for security checks.

A cross-origin isolated capability

A boolean representing whether scripts that use this [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) are allowed to use APIs that require cross-origin isolation.

A time origin

A number used as the baseline for performance-related timestamps. [\[HRT\]](#references)

An [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects)'s responsible event loop is its [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects)'s [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [event loop](#8171-definitions).

##### 8.1.3.3 Realms, settings objects, and global objects

A global object is a JavaScript object that is the \[\[GlobalObject\]\] field of a [realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms).

> [!note]
> In this specification, all [realms](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms) are [created](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) with [global objects](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) that are either [`Window`](#722-the-window-object), [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface), or [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope) objects.

A [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) has an in error reporting mode boolean, which is initially false.

A [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) has an outstanding rejected promises weak set, a [set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) of [`Promise`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-promise) objects, initially empty. This set must not create strong references to any of its members, and implementations are free to limit its size in an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) manner, e.g., by removing old entries from it when new ones are added.

A [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) has an about-to-be-notified rejected promises list, a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [`Promise`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-promise) objects, initially empty.

A [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) has an import map, initially an [empty import map](#8153-import-map-processing-model).

> [!note]
> For now, only [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) [global objects](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) have their [import map](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) modified from the initial empty one. The [import map](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) is only accessed for the resolution of a root [module script](#8141-scripts).

A [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) has a resolved module set, a [set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) of [specifier resolution records](#8153-import-map-processing-model), initially empty.

> [!note]
> The [resolved module set](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) ensures that module specifier resolution returns the same result when called multiple times with the same (referrer, specifier) pair. It does that by ensuring that [import map](#8153-import-map-processing-model) rules that impact the specifier in its referrer's scope cannot be defined after its initial resolution. For now, only [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) [global objects](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) have their module set data structures modified from the initial empty one.

---

There is always a 1-to-1-to-1 mapping between [realms](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms), [global objects](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects), and [environment settings objects](#8132-environment-settings-objects):
- A [realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms) has a \[\[HostDefined\]\] field, which contains the realm's settings object.
- A [realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms) has a \[\[GlobalObject\]\] field, which contains the realm's global object.
- Each [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) in this specification is created during the [creation](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) of a corresponding [realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms), known as the global object's realm.
- Each [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) in this specification is created alongside a corresponding [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects), known as its [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant).
- An [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects)'s [realm execution context](#8132-environment-settings-objects)'s Realm component is the environment settings object's realm.
- An [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects)'s [realm](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) then has a \[\[GlobalObject\]\] field, which contains the environment settings object's global object.

To create a new realm in an [agent](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agents) agent, optionally with instructions to create a global object or a global **this** binding (or both), the following steps are taken:
1. Perform [InitializeHostDefinedRealm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-initializehostdefinedrealm)() with the provided customizations for creating the global object and the global **this** binding.
2. Let realm execution context be the [running JavaScript execution context](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#running-execution-context).

   > [!note]
   > This is the [JavaScript execution context](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-execution-contexts) created in the previous step.

3. Remove realm execution context from the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack).
4. Let realm be realm execution context's Realm component.
5. If agent's [agent cluster](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters)'s [cross-origin isolation mode](#8122-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-cluster-formalism) is "[`none`](#7323-groupings-of-browsing-contexts)":
   1. Let global be realm's [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
   2. Let status be ! global.\[\[Delete\]\]("`SharedArrayBuffer`").
   3. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): status is true.

   > [!note]
   > This is done for compatibility with web content and there is some hope that this can be removed in the future. Web developers can still get at the constructor through `new WebAssembly.Memory({ shared:true, initial:0, maximum:0
   >     }).buffer.constructor`.

6. Return realm execution context.

---

When defining algorithm steps throughout this specification, it is often important to indicate what [realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms) is to be used—or, equivalently, what [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) or [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) is to be used. In general, there are at least four possibilities:

Entry

This corresponds to the script that initiated the currently running script action: i.e., the function or script that the user agent called into when it called into author code.

Incumbent

This corresponds to the most-recently-entered author function or script on the stack, or the author function or script that originally scheduled the currently-running callback.

Current

This corresponds to the currently-running function object, including built-in user-agent functions which might not be implemented as JavaScript. (It is derived from the [current realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#current-realm).)

Relevant

Every [platform object](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object) has a [relevant realm](#81334-relevant), which is roughly the [realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms) in which it was created. When writing algorithms, the most prominent [platform object](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object) whose [relevant realm](#81334-relevant) might be important is the **this** value of the currently-running function object. In some cases, there can be other important [relevant realms](#81334-relevant), such as those of any arguments.

Note how the [entry](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects), [incumbent](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects), and [current](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) concepts are usable without qualification, whereas the [relevant](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) concept must be applied to a particular [platform object](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object).

> [!warning]
> The [incumbent](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) and [entry](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) concepts should not be used by new specifications, as they are excessively complicated and unintuitive to work with. We are working to remove almost all existing uses from the platform: see [issue #1430](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/1430) for [incumbent](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects), and [issue #1431](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/1431) for [entry](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).

In general, web platform specifications should use the [relevant](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) concept, applied to the object being operated on (usually the **this** value of the current method). This mismatches the JavaScript specification, where [current](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) is generally used as the default (e.g., in determining the [realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms) whose `Array` constructor should be used to construct the result in `Array.prototype.map`). But this inconsistency is so embedded in the platform that we have to accept it going forward.

> [!example]
> Consider the following pages, with `a.html` being loaded in a browser window, `b.html` being loaded in an [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) as shown, and `c.html` and `d.html` omitted (they can simply be empty documents):
> 
> ```html
> <!-- a.html -->
> <!DOCTYPE html>
> <html lang="en">
> <title>Entry page</title>
> 
> <iframe src="b.html"></iframe>
> <button onclick="frames[0].hello()">Hello</button>
> 
> <!--b.html -->
> <!DOCTYPE html>
> <html lang="en">
> <title>Incumbent page</title>
> 
> <iframe src="c.html" id="c"></iframe>
> <iframe src="d.html" id="d"></iframe>
> 
> <script>
>   const c = document.querySelector("#c").contentWindow;
>   const d = document.querySelector("#d").contentWindow;
> 
>   window.hello = () => {
>     c.print.call(d);
>   };
> </script>
> ```
> 
> Each page has its own [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts), and thus its own [realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms), [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects), and [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects).
> 
> When the [`print()`](#892-printing) method is called in response to pressing the button in `a.html`:
> - The [entry realm](#81331-entry) is that of `a.html`.
> - The [incumbent realm](#81332-incumbent) is that of `b.html`.
> - The [current realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#current-realm) is that of `c.html` (since it is the [`print()`](#892-printing) method from `c.html` whose code is running).
> - The [relevant realm](#81334-relevant) of the object on which the [`print()`](#892-printing) method is being called is that of `d.html`.

> [!example]
> One reason why the [relevant](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) concept is generally a better default choice than the [current](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) concept is that it is more suitable for creating an object that is to be persisted and returned multiple times. For example, the [`navigator.getBattery()`](https://w3c.github.io/battery/#dom-navigator-getbattery) method creates promises in the [relevant realm](#81334-relevant) for the [`Navigator`](#8101-the-navigator-object) object on which it is invoked. This has the following impact: [\[BATTERY\]](#references)
> 
> ```html
> <!-- outer.html -->
> <!DOCTYPE html>
> <html lang="en">
> <title>Relevant realm demo: outer page</title>
> <script>
>   function doTest() {
>     const promise = navigator.getBattery.call(frames[0].navigator);
> 
>     console.log(promise instanceof Promise);           // logs false
>     console.log(promise instanceof frames[0].Promise); // logs true
> 
>     frames[0].hello();
>   }
> </script>
> <iframe src="inner.html" onload="doTest()"></iframe>
> 
> <!-- inner.html -->
> <!DOCTYPE html>
> <html lang="en">
> <title>Relevant realm demo: inner page</title>
> <script>
>   function hello() {
>     const promise = navigator.getBattery();
> 
>     console.log(promise instanceof Promise);        // logs true
>     console.log(promise instanceof parent.Promise); // logs false
>   }
> </script>
> ```
> 
> If the algorithm for the [`getBattery()`](https://w3c.github.io/battery/#dom-navigator-getbattery) method had instead used the [current realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#current-realm), all the results would be reversed. That is, after the first call to [`getBattery()`](https://w3c.github.io/battery/#dom-navigator-getbattery) in `outer.html`, the [`Navigator`](#8101-the-navigator-object) object in `inner.html` would be permanently storing a `Promise` object created in `outer.html`'s [realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms), and calls like that inside the `hello()` function would thus return a promise from the "wrong" realm. Since this is undesirable, the algorithm instead uses the [relevant realm](#81334-relevant), giving the sensible results indicated in the comments above.

---

The rest of this section deals with formally defining the [entry](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects), [incumbent](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects), [current](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects), and [relevant](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) concepts.

###### 8.1.3.3.1 Entry

The process of [calling scripts](#8144-calling-scripts) will push or pop [realm execution contexts](#8132-environment-settings-objects) onto the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack), interspersed with other [execution contexts](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-execution-contexts).

With this in hand, we define the entry execution context to be the most recently pushed item in the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack) that is a [realm execution context](#8132-environment-settings-objects). The entry realm is the [entry execution context](#81331-entry)'s Realm component.

Then, the entry settings object is the [environment settings object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) of the [entry realm](#81331-entry).

Similarly, the entry global object is the [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) of the [entry realm](#81331-entry).

###### 8.1.3.3.2 Incumbent

All [JavaScript execution contexts](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-execution-contexts) must contain, as part of their code evaluation state, a skip-when-determining-incumbent counter value, which is initially zero. In the process of [preparing to run a callback](#81332-incumbent) and [cleaning up after running a callback](#81332-incumbent), this value will be incremented and decremented.

Every [event loop](#8171-definitions) has an associated backup incumbent settings object stack, initially empty. Roughly speaking, it is used to determine the [incumbent settings object](#81332-incumbent) when no author code is on the stack, but author code is responsible for the current algorithm having been run in some way. The process of [preparing to run a callback](#81332-incumbent) and [cleaning up after running a callback](#81332-incumbent) manipulate this stack. [\[WEBIDL\]](#references)

When Web IDL is used to [invoke](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invoke-a-callback-function) author code, or when [HostEnqueuePromiseJob](#81664-hostenqueuepromisejobjob-realm) invokes a promise job, they use the following algorithms to track relevant data for determining the [incumbent settings object](#81332-incumbent):

To prepare to run a callback with an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settings:
1. Push settings onto the [backup incumbent settings object stack](#81332-incumbent).
