2. Let context be the [topmost script-having execution context](#81332-incumbent).
3. If context is not null, increment context's [skip-when-determining-incumbent counter](#81332-incumbent).

To clean up after running a callback with an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settings:
1. Let context be the [topmost script-having execution context](#81332-incumbent).

   > [!note]
   > This will be the same as the [topmost script-having execution context](#81332-incumbent) inside the corresponding invocation of [prepare to run a callback](#81332-incumbent).

2. If context is not null, decrement context's [skip-when-determining-incumbent counter](#81332-incumbent).
3. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): the topmost entry of the [backup incumbent settings object stack](#81332-incumbent) is settings.
4. Remove settings from the [backup incumbent settings object stack](#81332-incumbent).

Here, the topmost script-having execution context is the topmost entry of the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack) that has a non-null ScriptOrModule component, or null if there is no such entry in the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack).

With all this in place, the incumbent settings object is determined as follows:
1. Let context be the [topmost script-having execution context](#81332-incumbent).
2. If context is null, or if context's [skip-when-determining-incumbent counter](#81332-incumbent) is greater than zero:
   1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): the [backup incumbent settings object stack](#81332-incumbent) is not empty.

      > [!note]
      > This assert would fail if you try to obtain the [incumbent settings object](#81332-incumbent) from inside an algorithm that was triggered neither by [calling scripts](#8144-calling-scripts) nor by Web IDL [invoking](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invoke-a-callback-function) a callback. For example, it would trigger if you tried to obtain the [incumbent settings object](#81332-incumbent) inside an algorithm that ran periodically as part of the [event loop](#8171-definitions), with no involvement of author code. In such cases the [incumbent](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) concept cannot be used.

   2. Return the topmost entry of the [backup incumbent settings object stack](#81332-incumbent).

3. Return context's Realm component's [settings object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).

Then, the incumbent realm is the [realm](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) of the [incumbent settings object](#81332-incumbent).

Similarly, the incumbent global object is the [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) of the [incumbent settings object](#81332-incumbent).

---

The following series of examples is intended to make it clear how all of the different mechanisms contribute to the definition of the [incumbent](#81332-incumbent) concept:

> [!example]
> Consider the following starter example:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE html>
> <iframe></iframe>
> <script>
>   frames[0].postMessage("some data", "*");
> </script>
> ```
> 
> There are two interesting [environment settings objects](#8132-environment-settings-objects) here: that of `window`, and that of `frames[0]`. Our concern is: what is the [incumbent settings object](#81332-incumbent) at the time that the algorithm for [`postMessage()`](#933-posting-messages) executes?
> 
> It should be that of `window`, to capture the intuitive notion that the author script responsible for causing the algorithm to happen is executing in `window`, not `frames[0]`. This makes sense: the [window post message steps](#933-posting-messages) use the [incumbent settings object](#81332-incumbent) to determine the [`source`](#91-the-messageevent-interface) property of the resulting [`MessageEvent`](#91-the-messageevent-interface), and in this case `window` is definitely the source of the message.
> 
> Let us now explain how the steps given above give us our intuitively-desired result of `window`'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant).
> 
> When the [window post message steps](#933-posting-messages) look up the [incumbent settings object](#81332-incumbent), the [topmost script-having execution context](#81332-incumbent) will be that corresponding to the [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element: it was pushed onto the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack) as part of [ScriptEvaluation](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-runtime-semantics-scriptevaluation) during the [run a classic script](#8144-calling-scripts) algorithm. Since there are no Web IDL callback invocations involved, the context's [skip-when-determining-incumbent counter](#81332-incumbent) is zero, so it is used to determine the [incumbent settings object](#81332-incumbent); the result is the [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) of `window`.
> 
> (Note how the [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) of `frames[0]` is the [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant) of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) at the time the [`postMessage()`](#933-posting-messages) method is called, and thus is involved in determining the *target* of the message. Whereas the incumbent is used to determine the *source*.)

> [!example]
> Consider the following more complicated example:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE html>
> <iframe></iframe>
> <script>
>   const bound = frames[0].postMessage.bind(frames[0], "some data", "*");
>   window.setTimeout(bound);
> </script>
> ```
> 
> This example is very similar to the previous one, but with an extra indirection through `Function.prototype.bind` as well as [`setTimeout()`](#87-timers). But, the answer should be the same: invoking algorithms asynchronously should not change the [incumbent](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) concept.
> 
> This time, the result involves more complicated mechanisms:
> 
> When `bound` is [converted](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-type-mapping) to a Web IDL callback type, the [incumbent settings object](#81332-incumbent) is that corresponding to `window` (in the same manner as in our starter example above). Web IDL stores this as the resulting callback value's [callback context](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-callback-context).
> 
> When the [task](#8171-definitions) posted by [`setTimeout()`](#87-timers) executes, the algorithm for that task uses Web IDL to [invoke](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invoke-a-callback-function) the stored callback value. Web IDL in turn calls the above [prepare to run a callback](#81332-incumbent) algorithm. This pushes the stored [callback context](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-callback-context) onto the [backup incumbent settings object stack](#81332-incumbent). At this time (inside the timer task) there is no author code on the stack, so the [topmost script-having execution context](#81332-incumbent) is null, and nothing gets its [skip-when-determining-incumbent counter](#81332-incumbent) incremented.
> 
> Invoking the callback then calls `bound`, which in turn calls the [`postMessage()`](#933-posting-messages) method of `frames[0]`. When the [`postMessage()`](#933-posting-messages) algorithm looks up the [incumbent settings object](#81332-incumbent), there is still no author code on the stack, since the bound function just directly calls the built-in method. So the [topmost script-having execution context](#81332-incumbent) will be null: the [JavaScript execution context](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-execution-contexts) stack only contains an execution context corresponding to [`postMessage()`](#933-posting-messages), with no [ScriptEvaluation](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-runtime-semantics-scriptevaluation) context or similar below it.
> 
> This is where we fall back to the [backup incumbent settings object stack](#81332-incumbent). As noted above, it will contain as its topmost entry the [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant) of `window`. So that is what is used as the [incumbent settings object](#81332-incumbent) while executing the [`postMessage()`](#933-posting-messages) algorithm.

> [!example]
> Consider this final, even more convoluted example:
> 
> ```html
> <!-- a.html -->
> <!DOCTYPE html>
> <button>click me</button>
> <iframe></iframe>
> <script>
> const bound = frames[0].location.assign.bind(frames[0].location, "https://example.com/");
> document.querySelector("button").addEventListener("click", bound);
> </script>
> ```
> 
> ```html
> <!-- b.html -->
> <!DOCTYPE html>
> <iframe src="a.html"></iframe>
> <script>
>   const iframe = document.querySelector("iframe");
>   iframe.onload = function onLoad() {
>     iframe.contentWindow.document.querySelector("button").click();
>   };
> </script>
> ```
> 
> Again there are two interesting [environment settings objects](#8132-environment-settings-objects) in play: that of `a.html`, and that of `b.html`. When the [`location.assign()`](#724-the-location-interface) method triggers the [`Location`-object navigate](#724-the-location-interface) algorithm, what will be the [incumbent settings object](#81332-incumbent)? As before, it should intuitively be that of `a.html`: the [`click`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click) listener was originally scheduled by `a.html`, so even if something involving `b.html` causes the listener to fire, the [incumbent](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) responsible is that of `a.html`.
> 
> The callback setup is similar to the previous example: when `bound` is [converted](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-type-mapping) to a Web IDL callback type, the [incumbent settings object](#81332-incumbent) is that corresponding to `a.html`, which is stored as the callback's [callback context](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-callback-context).
> 
> When the [`click()`](#65-activation-behavior-of-elements) method is called inside `b.html`, it [dispatches](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#29-dispatching-events) a [`click`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click) event on the button that is inside `a.html`. This time, when the [prepare to run a callback](#81332-incumbent) algorithm executes as part of event dispatch, there *is* author code on the stack; the [topmost script-having execution context](#81332-incumbent) is that of the `onLoad` function, whose [skip-when-determining-incumbent counter](#81332-incumbent) gets incremented. Additionally, `a.html`'s [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) (stored as the [`EventHandler`](#8181-event-handlers)'s [callback context](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-callback-context)) is pushed onto the [backup incumbent settings object stack](#81332-incumbent).
> 
> Now, when the [`Location`-object navigate](#724-the-location-interface) algorithm looks up the [incumbent settings object](#81332-incumbent), the [topmost script-having execution context](#81332-incumbent) is still that of the `onLoad` function (due to the fact we are using a bound function as the callback). Its [skip-when-determining-incumbent counter](#81332-incumbent) value is one, however, so we fall back to the [backup incumbent settings object stack](#81332-incumbent). This gives us the [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) of `a.html`, as expected.
> 
> Note that this means that even though it is the [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) inside `a.html` that navigates, it is `a.html` itself that is used as the source [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), which determines among other things the [request client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client). This is [perhaps the only justifiable use of the incumbent concept on the web platform](https://www.w3.org/Bugs/Public/show_bug.cgi?id=26603#c36); in all other cases the consequences of using it are simply confusing and we hope to one day switch them to use [current](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) or [relevant](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) as appropriate.

###### 8.1.3.3.3 Current

The JavaScript specification defines the [current realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#current-realm), also known as the "current Realm Record". [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#references)

Then, the current settings object is the [environment settings object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) of the [current realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#current-realm).

Similarly, the current global object is the [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) of the [current realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#current-realm).

###### 8.1.3.3.4 Relevant

The relevant realm for a [platform object](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object) is the value of [its \[\[Realm\]\] field](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-platform-objects).

Then, the relevant settings object for a [platform object](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object) o is the [environment settings object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) of the [relevant realm](#81334-relevant) for o.

Similarly, the relevant global object for a [platform object](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object) o is the [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) of the [relevant realm](#81334-relevant) for o.

##### 8.1.3.4 Enabling and disabling scripting

Scripting is enabled for an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settings when all of the following conditions are true:
- The user agent supports scripting.
- [![(This is a tracking vector.)](https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg)](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#24-privacy-concerns) The user has not disabled scripting for settings at this time. (User agents may provide users with the option to disable scripting globally, or in a finer-grained manner, e.g., on a per-origin basis, down to the level of individual [environment settings objects](#8132-environment-settings-objects).)
- Either settings's [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) is not a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object, or settings's [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [active sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing) does not have its [sandboxed scripts browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing) set.
- The result of [WebDriver BiDi scripting is enabled](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-scripting-is-enabled) with settings is true.

Scripting is disabled for an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) when scripting is not [enabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting) for it, i.e., when any of the above conditions are false.

---

Scripting is disabled for a [platform object](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object) object if any of the following are true:
- [Scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting) for object's [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant).
- The object implements [`Node`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), and object's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) is null.
- The object implements [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) and object's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) is null.

Scripting is enabled for a [platform object](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-platform-object) object, when object's scripting is not [disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting).

##### 8.1.3.5 Secure contexts

An [environment](#8131-environments) environment is a secure context if the following algorithm returns true:
1. If environment is an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects):
   1. Let global be environment's [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
   2. If global is a [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface):
      1. If global's [owner set](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface)\[0\]'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant) is a [secure context](#8135-secure-contexts), then return true.

         > [!note]
         > We only need to check the 0th item since they will necessarily all be consistent.

      2. Return false.

   3. If global is a [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope), then return true.

      > [!note]
      > Worklets can only be created in secure contexts.

2. If the result of [Is url potentially trustworthy?](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-secure-contexts/#potentially-trustworthy-url) given environment's [top-level creation URL](#8131-environments) is "`Potentially
      Trustworthy`", then return true.
3. Return false.

An [environment](#8131-environments) is a non-secure context if it is not a [secure context](#8135-secure-contexts).

#### 8.1.4 Script processing model

##### 8.1.4.1 Scripts

A script is one of two possible [structs](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) (namely, a [classic script](#8141-scripts) or a [module script](#8141-scripts)). All scripts have:

A settings object

An [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects), containing various settings that are shared with other [scripts](#8141-scripts) in the same context.

A record

One of the following:
- a [script record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-script-records), for [classic scripts](#8141-scripts);
- a [Source Text Module Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-source-text-module-records), for [JavaScript module scripts](#8141-scripts);
- a [Synthetic Module Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-synthetic-module-records), for [CSS module scripts](#8141-scripts), [JSON module scripts](#8141-scripts), and [text module scripts](#8141-scripts);
- a [WebAssembly Module Record](https://webassembly.github.io/esm-integration/js-api/index.html#webassembly-module-record), for [WebAssembly module scripts](#8141-scripts); or
- null, representing a parsing failure.

A parse error

A JavaScript value, which has meaning only if the [record](#8141-scripts) is null, indicating that the corresponding script source text could not be parsed.

> [!note]
> This value is used for internal tracking of immediate parse errors when [creating scripts](#8143-creating-scripts), and is not to be used directly. Instead, consult the [error to rethrow](#8141-scripts) when determining "what went wrong" for this script.

An error to rethrow

A JavaScript value representing an error that will prevent evaluation from succeeding. It will be re-thrown by any attempts to [run](#8144-calling-scripts) the script.

> [!note]
> This could be the script's [parse error](#8141-scripts), but in the case of a [module script](#8141-scripts) it could instead be the [parse error](#8141-scripts) from one of its dependencies, or an error from [resolve a module specifier](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm).

> [!note]
> Since this exception value is provided by the JavaScript specification, we know that it is never null, so we use null to signal that no error has occurred.

Fetch options

Null or a [script fetch options](#8142-fetching-scripts), containing various options related to fetching this script or [module scripts](#8141-scripts) that it imports.

A base URL

Null or a base [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) used for [resolving module specifiers](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm). When non-null, this will either be the URL from which the script was obtained, for external scripts, or the [document base URL](#243-document-base-urls) of the containing document, for inline scripts.

A classic script is a type of [script](#8141-scripts) that has the following additional [item](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):

A muted errors boolean

A boolean which, if true, means that error information will not be provided for errors in this script. This is used to mute errors for cross-origin scripts, since that can leak private information.

A module script is another type of [script](#8141-scripts). It has no additional [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs).

[Module scripts](#8141-scripts) can be classified into five types:
- A [module script](#8141-scripts) is a JavaScript module script if its [record](#8141-scripts) is a [Source Text Module Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-source-text-module-records).
- A [module script](#8141-scripts) is a CSS module script if its [record](#8141-scripts) is a [Synthetic Module Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-synthetic-module-records), and it was created via the [create a CSS module script](#8143-creating-scripts) algorithm. CSS module scripts represent a parsed CSS style sheet.
- A [module script](#8141-scripts) is a JSON module script if its [record](#8141-scripts) is a [Synthetic Module Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-synthetic-module-records), and it was created via the [create a JSON module script](#8143-creating-scripts) algorithm. JSON module scripts represent a parsed JSON document.
- A [module script](#8141-scripts) is a text module script if its [record](#8141-scripts) is a [Synthetic Module Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-synthetic-module-records), and it was created via the [create a text module script](#8143-creating-scripts) algorithm. Text module scripts represent textual data encoded as UTF-8.
- A [module script](#8141-scripts) is a WebAssembly module script if its [record](#8141-scripts) is a [WebAssembly Module Record](https://webassembly.github.io/esm-integration/js-api/index.html#webassembly-module-record).

> [!note]
> As CSS style sheets, JSON documents, and text do not import dependent modules, and do not throw exceptions on evaluation, the [fetch options](#8141-scripts) and [base URL](#8141-scripts) of [CSS module scripts](#8141-scripts), [JSON module scripts](#8141-scripts), and [text module scripts](#8141-scripts) are always null.

The active script is determined by the following algorithm:
1. Let record be [GetActiveScriptOrModule](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-getactivescriptormodule)().
2. If record is null, return null.
3. Return record.\[\[HostDefined\]\].

> [!note]
> The [active script](#8141-scripts) concept is so far only used by the [`import()`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-import-calls) feature, to determine the [base URL](#8141-scripts) to use for resolving relative module specifiers.

##### 8.1.4.2 Fetching scripts

This section introduces a number of algorithms for fetching scripts, taking various necessary inputs and resulting in [classic](#8141-scripts) or [module scripts](#8141-scripts).

---

Script fetch options is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) with the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):

cryptographic nonce

The [cryptographic nonce metadata](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-nonce-metadata) used for the initial fetch and for fetching any imported modules

integrity metadata

The [integrity metadata](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-integrity-metadata) used for the initial fetch

parser metadata

The [parser metadata](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-parser-metadata) used for the initial fetch and for fetching any imported modules

credentials mode

The [credentials mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode) used for the initial fetch (for [module scripts](#8141-scripts)) and for fetching any imported modules (for both [module scripts](#8141-scripts) and [classic scripts](#8141-scripts))

referrer policy

The [referrer policy](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-referrer-policy) used for the initial fetch and for fetching any imported modules

> [!note]
> This policy can mutate after a [module script](#8141-scripts)'s [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) is received, to be the [referrer policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#referrer-policy) [parsed](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#parse-referrer-policy-from-header) from the [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response), and used when fetching any module dependencies.

render-blocking

The boolean value of [render-blocking](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-render-blocking) used for the initial fetch and for fetching any imported modules. Unless otherwise stated, its value is false.

fetch priority

The [priority](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-priority) used for the initial fetch

> [!note]
> Recall that via the [`import()`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-import-calls) feature, [classic scripts](#8141-scripts) can import [module scripts](#8141-scripts).

The default script fetch options are a [script fetch options](#8142-fetching-scripts) whose [cryptographic nonce](#8142-fetching-scripts) is the empty string, [integrity metadata](#8142-fetching-scripts) is the empty string, [parser metadata](#8142-fetching-scripts) is "`not-parser-inserted`", [credentials mode](#8142-fetching-scripts) is "`same-origin`", [referrer policy](#8142-fetching-scripts) is the empty string, and [fetch priority](#8142-fetching-scripts) is "`auto`".

To set up the classic script request, given a [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) request and a [script fetch options](#8142-fetching-scripts) options, set request's [cryptographic nonce metadata](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-nonce-metadata) to options's [cryptographic nonce](#8142-fetching-scripts), its [integrity metadata](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-integrity-metadata) to options's [integrity metadata](#8142-fetching-scripts), its [parser metadata](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-parser-metadata) to options's [parser metadata](#8142-fetching-scripts), its [referrer policy](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-referrer-policy) to options's [referrer policy](#8142-fetching-scripts), its [render-blocking](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-render-blocking) to options's [render-blocking](#8142-fetching-scripts), and its [priority](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-priority) to options's [fetch priority](#8142-fetching-scripts).

To set up the module script request, given a [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) request and a [script fetch options](#8142-fetching-scripts) options, set request's [cryptographic nonce metadata](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-nonce-metadata) to options's [cryptographic nonce](#8142-fetching-scripts), its [integrity metadata](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-integrity-metadata) to options's [integrity metadata](#8142-fetching-scripts), its [parser metadata](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-parser-metadata) to options's [parser metadata](#8142-fetching-scripts), its [credentials mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode) to options's [credentials mode](#8142-fetching-scripts), its [referrer policy](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-referrer-policy) to options's [referrer policy](#8142-fetching-scripts), its [render-blocking](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-render-blocking) to options's [render-blocking](#8142-fetching-scripts), and its [priority](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-priority) to options's [fetch priority](#8142-fetching-scripts).

To get the descendant script fetch options given a [script fetch options](#8142-fetching-scripts) originalOptions, a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) url, and an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settingsObject:
1. Let newOptions be a copy of originalOptions.
2. Let integrity be the result of [resolving a module integrity metadata](#8142-fetching-scripts) with url and settingsObject.
3. Set newOptions's [integrity metadata](#8142-fetching-scripts) to integrity.
4. Set newOptions's [fetch priority](#8142-fetching-scripts) to "`auto`".
5. Return newOptions.

To resolve a module integrity metadata, given a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) url and an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settingsObject:
1. Let map be settingsObject's [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects)'s [import map](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
2. If map's [integrity](#8153-import-map-processing-model)\[url\] does not [exist](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then return the empty string.
3. Return map's [integrity](#8153-import-map-processing-model)\[url\].

---

Several of the below algorithms can be customized with a perform the fetch hook algorithm, which takes a [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request), a boolean [isTopLevel](#8142-fetching-scripts), and a processCustomFetchResponse algorithm. It runs [processCustomFetchResponse](#8142-fetching-scripts) with a [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) and either null (on failure) or a [byte sequence](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-byte-sequences) containing the response body. isTopLevel will be true for all [classic script](#8141-scripts) fetches, and for the initial fetch when [fetching an external module script graph](#8142-fetching-scripts) or [fetching a module worker script graph](#8142-fetching-scripts), but false for the fetches resulting from `import` statements encountered throughout the graph or from `import()` expressions.

By default, not supplying a [perform the fetch hook](#8142-fetching-scripts) will cause the below algorithms to simply [fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) the given [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request), with algorithm-specific customizations to the [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) and validations of the resulting [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response).

To layer your own customizations on top of these algorithm-specific ones, supply a [perform the fetch hook](#8142-fetching-scripts) that modifies the given [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request), [fetches](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) it, and then performs specific validations of the resulting [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) (completing with a [network error](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-network-error) if the validations fail).

The hook can also be used to perform more subtle customizations, such as keeping a cache of [responses](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) and avoiding performing a [fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) at all.

> [!note]
> Service Workers is an example of a specification that runs these algorithms with its own options for the hook. [\[SW\]](#references)

---

Now for the algorithms themselves.

To fetch a classic script given a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) url, an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settingsObject, a [script fetch options](#8142-fetching-scripts) options, a [CORS settings attribute state](#254-cors-settings-attributes) corsSetting, an [encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#encoding) encoding, and an algorithm onComplete, run these steps. onComplete must be an algorithm accepting null (on failure) or a [classic script](#8141-scripts) (on success).
1. Let request be the result of [creating a potential-CORS request](#251-terminology) given url, "`script`", and corsSetting.
2. Set request's [client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client) to settingsObject.
3. Set request's [initiator type](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-initiator-type) to "`script`".
4. [Set up the classic script request](#8142-fetching-scripts) given request and options.
5. [Fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request with the following *[processResponseConsumeBody](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#process-response-end-of-body)* steps given [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response and null, failure, or a [byte sequence](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-byte-sequences) bodyBytes:

   > [!note]
   > response can be either [CORS-same-origin](#251-terminology) or [CORS-cross-origin](#251-terminology). This only affects how error reporting happens.
   1. Set response to response's [unsafe response](#251-terminology).
   2. If any of the following are true:
      - bodyBytes is null or failure; or
      - response's [status](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-status) is not an [ok status](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#ok-status),

      then run onComplete given null, and abort these steps.

      > [!note]
      > For historical reasons, this algorithm does not include MIME type checking, unlike the other script-fetching algorithms in this section.

   3. Let potentialMIMETypeForEncoding be the result of [extracting a MIME type](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-header-extract-mime-type) given response's [header list](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-header-list).
   4. Set encoding to the result of [legacy extracting an encoding](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#legacy-extract-an-encoding) given potentialMIMETypeForEncoding and encoding.

      > [!note]
      > This intentionally ignores the [MIME type essence](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type-essence).

   5. Let sourceText be the result of [decoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#decode) bodyBytes to Unicode, using encoding as the fallback encoding.

      > [!note]
      > The [decode](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#decode) algorithm overrides encoding if the file contains a BOM.

   6. Let mutedErrors be true if response was [CORS-cross-origin](#251-terminology), and false otherwise.
   7. Let script be the result of [creating a classic script](#8143-creating-scripts) given sourceText, settingsObject, response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url), options, mutedErrors, and url.
   8. Run onComplete given script.

To fetch a classic worker script given a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) url, an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) fetchClient, a [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) destination, an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settingsObject, an algorithm onComplete, and an optional [perform the fetch hook](#8142-fetching-scripts) performFetch, run these steps. onComplete must be an algorithm accepting null (on failure) or a [classic script](#8141-scripts) (on success).
1. Let request be a new [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) whose [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url) is url, [client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client) is fetchClient, [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) is destination, [initiator type](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-initiator-type) is "`other`", [mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-mode) is "`same-origin`", [credentials mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode) is "`same-origin`", [parser metadata](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-parser-metadata) is "`not parser-inserted`", and whose [use-URL-credentials flag](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-use-url-credentials-flag) is set.
2. If performFetch was given, run performFetch with request, true, and with processResponseConsumeBody as defined below.

   Otherwise, [fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request with *[processResponseConsumeBody](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#process-response-end-of-body)* set to processResponseConsumeBody as defined below.

   In both cases, let processResponseConsumeBody given [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response and null, failure, or a [byte sequence](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-byte-sequences) bodyBytes be the following algorithm:
   1. Set response to response's [unsafe response](#251-terminology).
   2. If any of the following are true:
      - bodyBytes is null or failure; or
      - response's [status](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-status) is not an [ok status](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#ok-status),

      then run onComplete given null, and abort these steps.

   3. If all of the following are true:
      - response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url)'s [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) is an [HTTP(S) scheme](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#http-scheme); and
      - the result of [extracting a MIME type](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-header-extract-mime-type) from response's [header list](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-header-list) is not a [JavaScript MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type),

      then run onComplete given null, and abort these steps.

      > [!note]
      > Other [fetch schemes](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-scheme) are exempted from MIME type checking for historical web-compatibility reasons. We might be able to tighten this in the future; see [issue #3255](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/3255).

   4. Let sourceText be the result of [UTF-8 decoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8-decode) bodyBytes.
   5. Let script be the result of [creating a classic script](#8143-creating-scripts) using sourceText, settingsObject, response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url), and the [default script fetch options](#8142-fetching-scripts).
   6. Run onComplete given script.

To fetch a classic worker-imported script given a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) url, an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settingsObject, and an optional [perform the fetch hook](#8142-fetching-scripts) performFetch, run these steps. The algorithm will return a [classic script](#8141-scripts) on success, or throw an exception on failure.
1. Let response be null.
2. Let bodyBytes be null.
3. Let request be a new [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) whose [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url) is url, [client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client) is settingsObject, [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) is "`script`", [initiator type](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-initiator-type) is "`other`", [parser metadata](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-parser-metadata) is "`not parser-inserted`", and whose [use-URL-credentials flag](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-use-url-credentials-flag) is set.
4. If performFetch was given, run performFetch with request, isTopLevel, and with processResponseConsumeBody as defined below.

   Otherwise, [fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request with *[processResponseConsumeBody](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#process-response-end-of-body)* set to processResponseConsumeBody as defined below.

   In both cases, let processResponseConsumeBody given [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) res and null, failure, or a [byte sequence](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-byte-sequences) bb be the following algorithm:
   1. Set bodyBytes to bb.
   2. Set response to res.

5. [Pause](#8173-processing-model) until response is not null.

   > [!note]
   > Unlike other algorithms in this section, the fetching process is synchronous here.

6. Set response to response's [unsafe response](#251-terminology).
7. If any of the following are true:
   - bodyBytes is null or failure;
   - response's [status](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-status) is not an [ok status](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#ok-status); or
   - the result of [extracting a MIME type](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-header-extract-mime-type) from response's [header list](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-header-list) is not a [JavaScript MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type),

   then throw a ["`NetworkError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#networkerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

8. Let sourceText be the result of [UTF-8 decoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8-decode) bodyBytes.
9. Let mutedErrors be true if response was [CORS-cross-origin](#251-terminology), and false otherwise.
10. Let script be the result of [creating a classic script](#8143-creating-scripts) given sourceText, settingsObject, response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url), the [default script fetch options](#8142-fetching-scripts), and mutedErrors.
11. Return script.

To fetch an external module script graph given a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) url, an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settingsObject, a [script fetch options](#8142-fetching-scripts) options, and an algorithm onComplete, run these steps. onComplete must be an algorithm accepting null (on failure) or a [module script](#8141-scripts) (on success).
1. [Fetch a single module script](#8142-fetching-scripts) given url, settingsObject, "`script`", options, settingsObject, "`client`", true, and with the following steps given result:
   1. If result is null, run onComplete given null, and abort these steps.
   2. [Fetch the descendants of and link](#8142-fetching-scripts) result given settingsObject, "`script`", and onComplete.

To fetch a modulepreload module script graph given a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) url, a [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) destination, an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settingsObject, a [script fetch options](#8142-fetching-scripts) options, and an algorithm onComplete, run these steps. onComplete must be an algorithm accepting null (on failure) or a [module script](#8141-scripts) (on success).
1. [Fetch a single module script](#8142-fetching-scripts) given url, settingsObject, destination, options, settingsObject, "`client`", true, and with the following steps given result:
   1. Run onComplete given result.
   2. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): settingsObject's [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) implements [`Window`](#722-the-window-object).
   3. If result is not null, optionally [fetch the descendants of and link](#8142-fetching-scripts) result given settingsObject, destination, and an empty algorithm.

      > [!note]
      > Generally, performing this step will be beneficial for performance, as it allows pre-loading the modules that will invariably be requested later, via algorithms such as [fetch an external module script graph](#8142-fetching-scripts) that fetch the entire graph. However, user agents might wish to skip them in bandwidth-constrained situations, or situations where the relevant fetches are already in flight.

To fetch an inline module script graph given a [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) sourceText, a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) baseURL, an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settingsObject, a [script fetch options](#8142-fetching-scripts) options, and an algorithm onComplete, run these steps. onComplete must be an algorithm accepting null (on failure) or a [module script](#8141-scripts) (on success).
1. Let script be the result of [creating a JavaScript module script](#8143-creating-scripts) using sourceText, settingsObject, baseURL, and options.
2. [Fetch the descendants of and link](#8142-fetching-scripts) script, given settingsObject, "`script`", and onComplete.

To fetch a module worker script graph given a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) url, an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) fetchClient, a [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) destination, a [credentials mode](#8142-fetching-scripts) credentialsMode, an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settingsObject, and an algorithm onComplete, [fetch a worklet/module worker script graph](#8142-fetching-scripts) given url, fetchClient, destination, credentialsMode, settingsObject, and onComplete.

To fetch a worklet script graph given a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) url, an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) fetchClient, a [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) destination, a [credentials mode](#8142-fetching-scripts) credentialsMode, an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settingsObject, a [module responses map](#1132-the-worklet-class) moduleResponsesMap, and an algorithm onComplete, [fetch a worklet/module worker script graph](#8142-fetching-scripts) given url, fetchClient, destination, credentialsMode, settingsObject, onComplete, and the following [perform the fetch hook](#8142-fetching-scripts) given request and [processCustomFetchResponse](#8142-fetching-scripts):
1. Let requestURL be request's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url).
2. If moduleResponsesMap\[requestURL\] is "`fetching`", wait [in parallel](#211-parallelism) until that entry's value changes, then [queue a task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) to proceed with running the following steps.
3. If moduleResponsesMap\[requestURL\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps):
   1. Let cached be moduleResponsesMap\[requestURL\].
   2. Run processCustomFetchResponse with cached\[0\] and cached\[1\].
   3. Return.
4. [Set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) moduleResponsesMap\[requestURL\] to "`fetching`".
5. [Fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request, with *[processResponseConsumeBody](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#process-response-end-of-body)* set to the following steps given [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response and null, failure, or a [byte sequence](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-byte-sequences) bodyBytes:
   1. Set moduleResponsesMap\[requestURL\] to (response, bodyBytes).
   2. Run processCustomFetchResponse with response and bodyBytes.

---

The following algorithms are meant for internal use by this specification only as part of [fetching an external module script graph](#8142-fetching-scripts) or other similar concepts above, and should not be used directly by other specifications.

This diagram illustrates how these algorithms relate to the ones above, as well as to each other:

To fetch a worklet/module worker script graph given a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) url, an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) fetchClient, a [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) destination, a [credentials mode](#8142-fetching-scripts) credentialsMode, an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settingsObject, an algorithm onComplete, and an optional [perform the fetch hook](#8142-fetching-scripts) performFetch, run these steps. onComplete must be an algorithm accepting null (on failure) or a [module script](#8141-scripts) (on success).
1. Let options be a [script fetch options](#8142-fetching-scripts) whose [cryptographic nonce](#8142-fetching-scripts) is the empty string, [integrity metadata](#8142-fetching-scripts) is the empty string, [parser metadata](#8142-fetching-scripts) is "`not-parser-inserted`", [credentials mode](#8142-fetching-scripts) is credentialsMode, [referrer policy](#8142-fetching-scripts) is the empty string, and [fetch priority](#8142-fetching-scripts) is "`auto`".
2. [Fetch a single module script](#8142-fetching-scripts) given url, fetchClient, destination, options, settingsObject, "`client`", true, and onSingleFetchComplete as defined below. If performFetch was given, pass it along as well.

   onSingleFetchComplete given result is the following algorithm:
   1. If result is null, run onComplete given null, and abort these steps.
   2. [Fetch the descendants of and link](#8142-fetching-scripts) result given fetchClient, destination, and onComplete. If performFetch was given, pass it along as well.

To fetch the descendants of and link a [module script](#8141-scripts) moduleScript, given an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) fetchClient, a [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) destination, an algorithm onComplete, and an optional [perform the fetch hook](#8142-fetching-scripts) performFetch, run these steps. onComplete must be an algorithm accepting null (on failure) or a [module script](#8141-scripts) (on success).
1. Let record be moduleScript's [record](#8141-scripts).
2. If record is null:
   1. Set moduleScript's [error to rethrow](#8141-scripts) to moduleScript's [parse error](#1322-parse-errors).
   2. Run onComplete given moduleScript.
   3. Return.
3. Let state be [Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type) { \[\[ErrorToRethrow\]\]: null, \[\[Destination\]\]: destination, \[\[PerformFetch\]\]: null, \[\[FetchClient\]\]: fetchClient }.
4. If performFetch was given, set state.\[\[PerformFetch\]\] to performFetch.
5. Let loadingPromise be record.[LoadRequestedModules](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-LoadRequestedModules)(state).

   > [!note]
   > This step will recursively load all the module transitive dependencies.

6. [Upon fulfillment](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#upon-fulfillment) of loadingPromise, run the following steps:
   1. Perform record.[Link](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-moduledeclarationlinking)().

      > [!note]
      > This step will recursively call [Link](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-moduledeclarationlinking) on all of the module's unlinked dependencies.

      If this throws an exception, catch it, and set moduleScript's [error to rethrow](#8141-scripts) to that exception.

   2. Run onComplete given moduleScript.

7. [Upon rejection](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#upon-rejection) of loadingPromise, run the following steps:
   1. If state.\[\[ErrorToRethrow\]\] is not null, set moduleScript's [error to rethrow](#8141-scripts) to state.\[\[ErrorToRethrow\]\] and run onComplete given moduleScript.
   2. Otherwise, run onComplete given null.

      > [!note]
      > state.\[\[ErrorToRethrow\]\] is null when loadingPromise is rejected due to a loading error.

To fetch a single module script, given a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) url, an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) fetchClient, a [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) destination, a [script fetch options](#8142-fetching-scripts) options, an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settingsObject, a [referrer](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-referrer) referrer, an optional [ModuleRequest Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#modulerequest-record) moduleRequest, a boolean [isTopLevel](#8142-fetching-scripts), an algorithm onComplete, and an optional [perform the fetch hook](#8142-fetching-scripts) performFetch, run these steps. onComplete must be an algorithm accepting null (on failure) or a [module script](#8141-scripts) (on success).
1. Let moduleType be "`javascript-or-wasm`".
2. If moduleRequest was given, then set moduleType to the result of running the [module type from module request](#8143-creating-scripts) steps given moduleRequest.
3. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): the result of running the [module type allowed](#8143-creating-scripts) steps given moduleType and settingsObject is true. Otherwise, we would not have reached this point because a failure would have been raised when inspecting moduleRequest.\[\[Attributes\]\] in [HostLoadImportedModule](#81673-hostloadimportedmodulereferrer-modulerequest-loadstate-payload) or [fetch a single imported module script](#8142-fetching-scripts).
4. Let moduleMap be settingsObject's [module map](#8132-environment-settings-objects).
5. If moduleMap\[(url, moduleType)\] is a [module script](#8141-scripts), run onComplete given moduleMap\[(url, moduleType)\], and return.
6. If moduleMap\[(url, moduleType)\] is a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists), [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) onComplete to moduleMap\[(url, moduleType)\], and return.
7. [Set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) moduleMap\[(url, moduleType)\] to « onComplete ».
8. Let request be a new [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request) whose [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url) is url, [mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-mode) is "`cors`", [referrer](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-referrer) is referrer, and [client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client) is fetchClient.
9. Set request's [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) to the result of running the [fetch destination from module type](#8143-creating-scripts) steps given destination and moduleType.
10. If destination is "`worker`", "`sharedworker`", or "`serviceworker`", and isTopLevel is true, then set request's [mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-mode) to "`same-origin`".
11. Set request's [initiator type](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-initiator-type) to "`script`".
12. [Set up the module script request](#8142-fetching-scripts) given request and options.
13. If performFetch was given, run performFetch with request, isTopLevel, and with processResponseConsumeBody as defined below.

    Otherwise, [fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request with *[processResponseConsumeBody](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#process-response-end-of-body)* set to processResponseConsumeBody as defined below.

    In both cases, let processResponseConsumeBody given [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response and null, failure, or a [byte sequence](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-byte-sequences) bodyBytes be the following algorithm:

    > [!note]
    > response is always [CORS-same-origin](#251-terminology).
    1. If any of the following are true:
       - bodyBytes is null or failure; or
       - response's [status](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-status) is not an [ok status](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#ok-status),

       then:
       1. Let callbacks be moduleMap\[(url, moduleType)\].
       2. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) moduleMap\[(url, moduleType)\].
       3. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) callback of callbacks: run callback given null.
       4. Return.

    2. Let mimeType be the result of [extracting a MIME type](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-header-extract-mime-type) from response's [header list](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-header-list).
    3. Let moduleScript be null.
    4. Let referrerPolicy be the result of [parsing the \``Referrer-Policy`\` header](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-referrer-policy/#parse-referrer-policy-from-header) given response. [\[REFERRERPOLICY\]](#references)
    5. If referrerPolicy is not the empty string, set options's [referrer policy](#8142-fetching-scripts) to referrerPolicy.
    6. If mimeType's [essence](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type-essence) is "[`application/wasm`](#mime-types)" and moduleType is "`javascript-or-wasm`", then set moduleScript to the result of [creating a WebAssembly module script](#8143-creating-scripts) given bodyBytes, settingsObject, response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url), and options.
    7. Otherwise:
       1. Let sourceText be the result of [UTF-8 decoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8-decode) bodyBytes.
       2. If moduleType is "`text`", then set moduleScript to the result of [creating a text module script](#8143-creating-scripts) given sourceText and settingsObject.
       3. If mimeType is a [JavaScript MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type) and moduleType is "`javascript-or-wasm`", then set moduleScript to the result of [creating a JavaScript module script](#8143-creating-scripts) given sourceText, settingsObject, response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url), and options.
       4. If the [MIME type essence](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type-essence) of mimeType is "[`text/css`](#mime-types)" and moduleType is "`css`", then set moduleScript to the result of [creating a CSS module script](#8143-creating-scripts) given sourceText and settingsObject.
       5. If mimeType is a [JSON MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#json-mime-type) and moduleType is "`json`", then set moduleScript to the result of [creating a JSON module script](#8143-creating-scripts) given sourceText and settingsObject.
    8. Let callbacks be moduleMap\[(url, moduleType)\].
    9. If moduleScript is null, then [remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) moduleMap\[(url, moduleType)\]; otherwise [set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) moduleMap\[(url, moduleType)\] to moduleScript.

       > [!note]
       > It is intentional that the [module map](#8167-module-related-host-hooks) is keyed by the [request URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url), whereas the [base URL](#8141-scripts) for the [module script](#8141-scripts) is set to the [response URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url). The former is used to deduplicate fetches, while the latter is used for URL resolution.

    10. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) callback of callbacks: run callback given moduleScript.

To fetch a single imported module script, given a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) url, an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) fetchClient, a [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) destination, a [script fetch options](#8142-fetching-scripts) options, [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settingsObject, a [referrer](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-referrer) referrer, a [ModuleRequest Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#modulerequest-record) moduleRequest, an algorithm onComplete, and an optional [perform the fetch hook](#8142-fetching-scripts) performFetch, run these steps. onComplete must be an algorithm accepting null (on failure) or a [module script](#8141-scripts) (on success).
1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): moduleRequest.\[\[Attributes\]\] does not contain any [Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type) entry such that entry.\[\[Key\]\] is not "`type`", because we only asked for "`type`" attributes in [HostGetSupportedImportAttributes](#81672-hostgetsupportedimportattributes).
2. Let moduleType be the result of running the [module type from module request](#8143-creating-scripts) steps given moduleRequest.
3. If the result of running the [module type allowed](#8143-creating-scripts) steps given moduleType and settingsObject is false, then run onComplete given null, and return.
4. [Fetch a single module script](#8142-fetching-scripts) given url, fetchClient, destination, options, settingsObject, referrer, moduleRequest, false, and onComplete. If performFetch was given, pass it along as well.

##### 8.1.4.3 Creating scripts

This standard refers to the following concepts defined there:
- [WebDriver BiDi command "script.evaluate"](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-script-evaluate)

To create a classic script, given a [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) source, an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settings, a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) baseURL, a [script fetch options](#8142-fetching-scripts) options, an optional boolean mutedErrors (default false), an optional [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url)-or-null sourceURLForWindowScripts (default null), and an optional boolean bypassDisabledScripting (default false):

> [!note]
> The bypassDisabledScripting parameter is intended to be used for running scripts even if [scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting). This is required for some automation scenarios, e.g. for WebDriver BiDi command ["script.evaluate"](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#commands-scriptevaluate).

> [!note]
> The bypassDisabledScripting parameter is intended to be used for running scripts even if scripting is disabled. This is required for some automation scenarios, e.g. for [WebDriver BiDi command "script.evaluate"](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-script-evaluate). When the scripting process (e.g., executing a script via a WebDriver BiDi command) is invoked with bypassDisabledScripting set to true, the event loop is allowed to run to resolve thenables (from promises) and weakmap finalizations created by that script, even if [scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting). This is necessary to ensure the proper functioning of testing scripts, which often rely on asynchronous operations.
1. If mutedErrors is true, then set baseURL to [`about:blank`](#219-dependencies).

   > [!note]
   > When mutedErrors is true, baseURL is the script's [CORS-cross-origin](#251-terminology) [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response)'s [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url), which shouldn't be exposed to JavaScript. Therefore, baseURL is sanitized here.

2. If [scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting) for settings and bypassDisabledScripting is false, then set source to the empty string.
3. Let script be a new [classic script](#8141-scripts) that this algorithm will subsequently initialize.
4. Set script's [settings object](#8141-scripts) to settings.
5. Set script's [base URL](#8141-scripts) to baseURL.
6. Set script's [fetch options](#8141-scripts) to options.
7. Set script's [muted errors](#8141-scripts) to mutedErrors.
8. Set script's [parse error](#8141-scripts) and [error to rethrow](#8141-scripts) to null.
9. [Record classic script creation time](https://w3c.github.io/long-animation-frames/#record-classic-script-creation-time) given script and sourceURLForWindowScripts.
10. Let result be [ParseScript](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-parse-script)(source, settings's [realm](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects), script).

    > [!note]
    > Passing script as the last parameter here ensures result.\[\[HostDefined\]\] will be script.

11. If result is a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of errors:
    1. Set script's [parse error](#8141-scripts) and its [error to rethrow](#8141-scripts) to result\[0\].
    2. Return script.
12. Set script's [record](#8141-scripts) to result.
13. Return script.

To create a JavaScript module script, given a [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) source, an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settings, a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) baseURL, and a [script fetch options](#8142-fetching-scripts) options:
1. If [scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting) for settings, then set source to the empty string.
2. Let script be a new [module script](#8141-scripts) that this algorithm will subsequently initialize.
3. Set script's [settings object](#8141-scripts) to settings.
4. Set script's [base URL](#8141-scripts) to baseURL.
5. Set script's [fetch options](#8141-scripts) to options.
6. Set script's [parse error](#8141-scripts) and [error to rethrow](#8141-scripts) to null.
7. Let result be [ParseModule](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-parsemodule)(source, settings's [realm](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects), script).

   > [!note]
   > Passing script as the last parameter here ensures result.\[\[HostDefined\]\] will be script.

8. If result is a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of errors:
   1. Set script's [parse error](#8141-scripts) to result\[0\].
   2. Return script.
9. Set script's [record](#8141-scripts) to result.
10. Return script.

To create a WebAssembly module script, given a [byte sequence](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-byte-sequences) bodyBytes, an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settings, a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) baseURL, and a [script fetch options](#8142-fetching-scripts) options:
1. If [scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting) for settings, then set bodyBytes to the byte sequence 0x00 0x61 0x73 0x6D 0x01 0x00 0x00 0x00.

   > [!note]
   > This byte sequence corresponds to an empty WebAssembly module with only the magic bytes and version number provided.

2. Let script be a new [module script](#8141-scripts) that this algorithm will subsequently initialize.
3. Set script's [settings object](#8141-scripts) to settings.
4. Set script's [base URL](#8141-scripts) to baseURL.
5. Set script's [fetch options](#8141-scripts) to options.
6. Set script's [parse error](#8141-scripts) and [error to rethrow](#8141-scripts) to null.
7. Let result be the result of [parsing a WebAssembly module](https://webassembly.github.io/esm-integration/js-api/index.html#parse-a-webassembly-module) given bodyBytes, settings's [realm](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects), and script.

   > [!note]
   > Passing script as the last parameter here ensures result.\[\[HostDefined\]\] will be script.

8. If the previous step threw an error error:
   1. Set script's [parse error](#8141-scripts) to error.
   2. Return script.
9. Set script's [record](#8141-scripts) to result.
10. Return script.

> [!note]
> WebAssembly JavaScript Interface: ESM Integration specifies the hooks for the WebAssembly integration with ECMA-262 module loading. This includes support both for direct dependency imports, as well as for source phase imports, which support virtualization and multi-instantiation. [\[WASMESM\]](#references)

To create a CSS module script, given a string source and an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settings:
1. Let script be a new [module script](#8141-scripts) that this algorithm will subsequently initialize.
2. Set script's [settings object](#8141-scripts) to settings.
3. Set script's [base URL](#8141-scripts) and [fetch options](#8141-scripts) to null.
4. Set script's [parse error](#8141-scripts) and [error to rethrow](#8141-scripts) to null.
5. Let sheet be the result of running the steps to [create a constructed `CSSStyleSheet`](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#create-a-constructed-cssstylesheet) with an empty dictionary as the argument.
6. Run the steps to [synchronously replace the rules of a `CSSStyleSheet`](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#synchronously-replace-the-rules-of-a-cssstylesheet) on sheet given source.

   If this throws an exception, catch it, and set script's [parse error](#8141-scripts) to that exception, and return script.

   > [!note]
   > The steps to [synchronously replace the rules of a `CSSStyleSheet`](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#synchronously-replace-the-rules-of-a-cssstylesheet) will throw if source contains any `@import` rules. This is by-design for now because there is not yet an agreement on how to handle these for CSS module scripts; therefore they are blocked altogether until a consensus is reached.

7. Set script's [record](#8141-scripts) to the result of [CreateDefaultExportSyntheticModule](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-create-default-export-synthetic-module)(sheet).
8. Return script.

To create a JSON module script, given a string source and an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settings:
1. Let script be a new [module script](#8141-scripts) that this algorithm will subsequently initialize.
2. Set script's [settings object](#8141-scripts) to settings.
3. Set script's [base URL](#8141-scripts) and [fetch options](#8141-scripts) to null.
4. Set script's [parse error](#8141-scripts) and [error to rethrow](#8141-scripts) to null.
5. Let result be [ParseJSONModule](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-parse-json-module)(source).

   If this throws an exception, catch it, and set script's [parse error](#8141-scripts) to that exception, and return script.

6. Set script's [record](#8141-scripts) to result.
7. Return script.

To create a text module script, given a string text and an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settings:
1. Let script be a new [module script](#8141-scripts) that this algorithm will subsequently initialize.
2. Set script's [settings object](#8141-scripts) to settings.
3. Set script's [base URL](#8141-scripts) and [fetch options](#8141-scripts) to null.
4. Set script's [parse error](#8141-scripts) and [error to rethrow](#8141-scripts) to null.
5. Let result be [CreateTextModule](https://tc39.es/proposal-import-text/#sec-create-text-module)(text).
6. Set script's [record](#8141-scripts) to result.
7. Return script.

The module type from module request steps, given a [ModuleRequest Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#modulerequest-record) moduleRequest, are as follows:
1. Let moduleType be "`javascript-or-wasm`".
2. If moduleRequest.\[\[Attributes\]\] has a [Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type) entry such that entry.\[\[Key\]\] is "`type`":
   1. If entry.\[\[Value\]\] is "`javascript-or-wasm`", then set moduleType to null.

      > [!note]
      > This specification uses the "`javascript-or-wasm`" module type internally for [JavaScript module scripts](#8141-scripts) or [WebAssembly module scripts](#8141-scripts), so this step is needed to prevent modules from being imported using a "`javascript-or-wasm`" type attribute (a null moduleType will cause the [module type allowed](#8143-creating-scripts) check to fail).

   2. Otherwise, set moduleType to entry.\[\[Value\]\].

3. Return moduleType.

The module type allowed steps, given a [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) moduleType and an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settings, are as follows:
1. If moduleType is not "`javascript-or-wasm`", "`css`", "`json`", or "`text`", then return false.
2. If moduleType is "`css`" and the [`CSSStyleSheet`](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom/#the-cssstylesheet-interface) interface is not [exposed](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-exposed) in settings's [realm](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects), then return false.
3. Return true.

The fetch destination from module type steps, given a [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) defaultDestination and a [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) moduleType, are as follows:
1. If moduleType is "`json`", then return "`json`".
2. If moduleType is "`css`", then return "`style`".
3. If moduleType is "`text`", then return "`text`".
4. Return defaultDestination.

##### 8.1.4.4 Calling scripts

To run a classic script given a [classic script](#8141-scripts) script and an optional boolean rethrow errors (default false):
1. Let settings be the [settings object](#8141-scripts) of script.
2. [Check if we can run script](#8144-calling-scripts) with settings. If this returns "do not run", then return [NormalCompletion](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-normalcompletion)(empty).
3. [Record classic script execution start time](https://w3c.github.io/long-animation-frames/#record-classic-script-execution-start-time) given script.
4. [Prepare to run script](#8144-calling-scripts) given settings.
5. Let evaluationStatus be null.
6. If script's [error to rethrow](#8141-scripts) is not null, then set evaluationStatus to [ThrowCompletion](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-throwcompletion)(script's [error to rethrow](#8141-scripts)).
7. Otherwise, set evaluationStatus to [ScriptEvaluation](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-runtime-semantics-scriptevaluation)(script's [record](#8141-scripts)).

   If [ScriptEvaluation](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-runtime-semantics-scriptevaluation) does not complete because the user agent has [aborted the running script](#8145-killing-scripts), leave evaluationStatus as null.

8. If evaluationStatus is an [abrupt completion](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type):
   1. If rethrow errors is true and script's [muted errors](#8141-scripts) is false:
      1. [Clean up after running script](#8144-calling-scripts) with settings.
      2. Rethrow evaluationStatus.\[\[Value\]\].
   2. If rethrow errors is true and script's [muted errors](#8141-scripts) is true:
      1. [Clean up after running script](#8144-calling-scripts) with settings.
      2. Throw a ["`NetworkError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#networkerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
   3. Otherwise, rethrow errors is false. Perform the following steps:
      1. [Report an exception](#8146-runtime-script-errors) given by evaluationStatus.\[\[Value\]\] for script's [settings object](#8141-scripts)'s [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
      2. [Clean up after running script](#8144-calling-scripts) with settings.
      3. Return evaluationStatus.
9. [Clean up after running script](#8144-calling-scripts) with settings.
10. If evaluationStatus is a normal completion, then return evaluationStatus.
11. If we've reached this point, evaluationStatus was left as null because the script was [aborted prematurely](#8145-killing-scripts) during evaluation. Return [ThrowCompletion](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-throwcompletion)(a new [`QuotaExceededError`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#quotaexceedederror)).

To run a module script given a [module script](#8141-scripts) script and an optional boolean preventErrorReporting (default false):
1. Let settings be the [settings object](#8141-scripts) of script.
2. [Check if we can run script](#8144-calling-scripts) with settings. If this returns "do not run", then return [a promise resolved with](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#a-promise-resolved-with) undefined.
3. [Record module script execution start time](https://w3c.github.io/long-animation-frames/#record-module-script-execution-start-time) given script.
4. [Prepare to run script](#8144-calling-scripts) given settings.
5. Let evaluationPromise be null.
6. If script's [error to rethrow](#8141-scripts) is not null, then set evaluationPromise to [a promise rejected with](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#a-promise-rejected-with) script's [error to rethrow](#8141-scripts).
7. Otherwise:
   1. Let record be script's [record](#8141-scripts).
   2. Set evaluationPromise to record.[Evaluate](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-moduleevaluation)().

      > [!note]
      > This step will recursively evaluate all of the module's dependencies.

      If [Evaluate](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-moduleevaluation) fails to complete as a result of the user agent [aborting the running script](#8145-killing-scripts), then set evaluationPromise to [a promise rejected with](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#a-promise-rejected-with) a new [`QuotaExceededError`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#quotaexceedederror).

8. If preventErrorReporting is false, then [upon rejection](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#upon-rejection) of evaluationPromise with reason, [report an exception](#8146-runtime-script-errors) given by reason for script's [settings object](#8141-scripts)'s [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
9. [Clean up after running script](#8144-calling-scripts) with settings.
10. Return evaluationPromise.

The steps to check if we can run script with an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settings are as follows. They return either "run" or "do not run".
1. If the [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) specified by settings is a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object whose [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents), then return "do not run".
2. If [scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting) for settings, then return "do not run".
3. Return "run".

The steps to prepare to run script with an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settings are as follows:
1. Push settings's [realm execution context](#8132-environment-settings-objects) onto the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack); it is now the [running JavaScript execution context](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#running-execution-context).
2. Add settings to the [surrounding agent](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#surrounding-agent)'s [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [currently running task](#8171-definitions)'s [script evaluation environment settings object set](#8171-definitions).

The steps to clean up after running script with an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settings are as follows:
1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): settings's [realm execution context](#8132-environment-settings-objects) is the [running JavaScript execution context](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#running-execution-context).
2. Remove settings's [realm execution context](#8132-environment-settings-objects) from the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack).
3. If the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack) is now empty, [perform a microtask checkpoint](#8173-processing-model). (If this runs scripts, these algorithms will be invoked reentrantly.)

> [!note]
> These algorithms are not invoked by one script directly calling another, but they can be invoked reentrantly in an indirect manner, e.g. if a script dispatches an event which has event listeners registered.

The running script is the [script](#8141-scripts) in the \[\[HostDefined\]\] field in the ScriptOrModule component of the [running JavaScript execution context](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#running-execution-context).

##### 8.1.4.5 Killing scripts

Although the JavaScript specification does not account for this possibility, it's sometimes necessary to abort a running script. This causes any [ScriptEvaluation](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-runtime-semantics-scriptevaluation) or [Source Text Module Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-source-text-module-records) [Evaluate](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-moduleevaluation) invocations to cease immediately, emptying the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack) without triggering any of the normal mechanisms like `finally` blocks. [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#references)

User agents may impose resource limitations on scripts, for example CPU quotas, memory limits, total execution time limits, or bandwidth limitations. When a script exceeds a limit, the user agent may either throw a [`QuotaExceededError`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#quotaexceedederror), [abort the script](#8145-killing-scripts) without an exception, prompt the user, or throttle script execution.

> [!example]
> For example, the following script never terminates. A user agent could, after waiting for a few seconds, prompt the user to either terminate the script or let it continue.
> 
> ```html
> <script>
>  while (true) { /* loop */ }
> </script>
> ```

User agents are encouraged to allow users to disable scripting whenever the user is prompted either by a script (e.g. using the [`window.alert()`](#891-simple-dialogs) API) or because of a script's actions (e.g. because it has exceeded a time limit).
