If scripting is disabled while a script is executing, the script should be terminated immediately.

User agents may allow users to specifically disable scripts just for the purposes of closing a [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts).

> [!example]
> For example, the prompt mentioned in the example above could also offer the user with a mechanism to just close the page entirely, without running any [`unload`](#events) event handlers.

##### 8.1.4.6 Runtime script errors

`self.reportError(e)`

Dispatches an [`error`](#events) event at the global object for the given value e, in the same fashion as an unhandled exception.

To extract error information from a JavaScript value exception:
1. Let attributes be an empty [map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) keyed by IDL attributes.
2. Set attributes\[[`error`](#8146-runtime-script-errors)\] to exception.
3. [![(This is a tracking vector.)](https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg)](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#24-privacy-concerns) Set attributes\[[`message`](#8146-runtime-script-errors)\], attributes\[[`filename`](#8146-runtime-script-errors)\], attributes\[[`lineno`](#8146-runtime-script-errors)\], and attributes\[[`colno`](#8146-runtime-script-errors)\] to [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) values derived from exception.

   > [!note]
   > Browsers implement behavior not specified here or in the JavaScript specification to gather values which are helpful, including in unusual cases (e.g., `eval`). In the future, this might be specified in greater detail.

4. Return attributes.

To report an exception exception which is a JavaScript value, for a particular [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) global and optional boolean omitError (default false):
1. Let notHandled be true.
2. Let errorInfo be the result of [extracting error information](#8146-runtime-script-errors) from exception.
3. Let script be a [script](#8141-scripts) found in an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) way, or null. This should usually be the [running script](#8144-calling-scripts) (most notably during [run a classic script](#8144-calling-scripts)).

   > [!note]
   > Implementations have not yet settled on interoperable behavior for which script is used to determine whether errors are muted in less common cases.

4. If script is a [classic script](#8141-scripts) and script's [muted errors](#8141-scripts) is true, then set errorInfo\[[`error`](#8146-runtime-script-errors)\] to null, errorInfo\[[`message`](#8146-runtime-script-errors)\] to "`Script error.`", errorInfo\[[`filename`](#8146-runtime-script-errors)\] to the empty string, errorInfo\[[`lineno`](#8146-runtime-script-errors)\] to 0, and errorInfo\[[`colno`](#8146-runtime-script-errors)\] to 0.
5. If omitError is true, then set errorInfo\[[`error`](#8146-runtime-script-errors)\] to null.
6. If global is not [in error reporting mode](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects):
   1. Set global's [in error reporting mode](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) to true.
   2. If global implements [`EventTarget`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget), then set notHandled to the result of [firing an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) at global, using [`ErrorEvent`](#8146-runtime-script-errors), with the [`cancelable`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true, and additional attributes initialized according to errorInfo.

      > [!note]
      > Returning true in an event handler cancels the event per [the event handler processing algorithm](#8181-event-handlers).

   3. Set global's [in error reporting mode](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) to false.

7. If notHandled is true:
   1. Set errorInfo\[[`error`](#8146-runtime-script-errors)\] to null.
   2. If global implements [`DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10212-dedicated-workers-and-the-dedicatedworkerglobalscope-interface), [queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) with the global's associated [`Worker`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) to run these steps:
      1. Let workerObject be the [`Worker`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) object associated with global.
      2. Set notHandled to the result of [firing an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) at workerObject, using [`ErrorEvent`](#8146-runtime-script-errors), with the [`cancelable`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true, and additional attributes initialized according to errorInfo.
      3. If notHandled is true, then [report](#8146-runtime-script-errors) exception for workerObject's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) with [omitError](#8146-runtime-script-errors) set to true.

         > [!note]
         > The actual exception value will not be available in the owner realm, but the user agent still carries through enough information to set the message, filename, and other attributes, as well as potentially report to a developer console.

   3. Otherwise, the user agent may report exception to a developer console.

If the implicit port connecting a worker to its [`Worker`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) object has been disentangled (i.e. if the parent worker has been terminated), then the user agent must act as if the [`Worker`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) object had no [`error`](#events) event handler and as if that worker's [`onerror`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) attribute was null, but must otherwise act as described above.

> [!note]
> Thus, error reports propagate up to the chain of dedicated workers up to the original [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), even if some of the workers along this chain have been terminated and garbage collected.

Previous revisions of this standard defined an algorithm to report the exception. As part of [issue #958](https://github.com/whatwg/html), this has been superseded by [report an exception](#8146-runtime-script-errors) which behaves differently and takes different inputs. [Issue #10516](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10516) tracks updating the specification ecosystem.

---

The `reportError(e)` method steps are to [report an exception](#8146-runtime-script-errors) e for [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).

> [!warning]
> It is unclear whether [muting](#8141-scripts) is applicable here. In Chrome and Safari it is muted, but in Firefox it is not. See also [issue #958](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/958).

---

The [`ErrorEvent`](#8146-runtime-script-errors) interface is defined as follows:

```webidl
[Exposed=*]
interface ErrorEvent : Event {
  constructor(DOMString type, optional ErrorEventInit eventInitDict = {});

  readonly attribute DOMString message;
  readonly attribute USVString filename;
  readonly attribute unsigned long lineno;
  readonly attribute unsigned long colno;
  readonly attribute any error;
};

dictionary ErrorEventInit : EventInit {
  DOMString message = "";
  USVString filename = "";
  unsigned long lineno = 0;
  unsigned long colno = 0;
  any error;
};
```

The `message` attribute must return the value it was initialized to. It represents the error message.

The `filename` attribute must return the value it was initialized to. It represents the [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) of the script in which the error originally occurred.

The `lineno` attribute must return the value it was initialized to. It represents the line number where the error occurred in the script.

The `colno` attribute must return the value it was initialized to. It represents the column number where the error occurred in the script.

The `error` attribute must return the value it was initialized to. It must initially be initialized to undefined. Where appropriate, it is set to the object representing the error (e.g., the exception object in the case of an uncaught exception).

##### 8.1.4.7 Unhandled promise rejections

In addition to synchronous [runtime script errors](#8146-runtime-script-errors), scripts may experience asynchronous promise rejections, tracked via the [`unhandledrejection`](#events) and [`rejectionhandled`](#events) events. Tracking these rejections is done via the [HostPromiseRejectionTracker](#8164-hostpromiserejectiontrackerpromise-operation) abstract operation, but reporting them is defined here.

To notify about rejected promises given a [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) global:
1. Let list be a [clone](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of global's [about-to-be-notified rejected promises list](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
2. If list [is empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists), then return.
3. [Empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) global's [about-to-be-notified rejected promises list](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
4. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given global to run the following step:
   1. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) promise p of list:
      1. If p.\[\[PromiseIsHandled\]\] is true, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
      2. Let notCanceled be the result of [firing an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`unhandledrejection`](#events) at global, using [`PromiseRejectionEvent`](#8147-unhandled-promise-rejections), with the [`cancelable`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true, the [`promise`](#8147-unhandled-promise-rejections) attribute initialized to p, and the [`reason`](#8147-unhandled-promise-rejections) attribute initialized to p.\[\[PromiseResult\]\].
      3. If notCanceled is true, then the user agent may report p.\[\[PromiseResult\]\] to a developer console.
      4. If p.\[\[PromiseIsHandled\]\] is false, then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) p to global's [outstanding rejected promises weak set](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).

The [`PromiseRejectionEvent`](#8147-unhandled-promise-rejections) interface is defined as follows:

```webidl
[Exposed=*]
interface PromiseRejectionEvent : Event {
  constructor(DOMString type, PromiseRejectionEventInit eventInitDict);

  readonly attribute object promise;
  readonly attribute any reason;
};

dictionary PromiseRejectionEventInit : EventInit {
  required object promise;
  any reason;
};
```

The `promise` attribute must return the value it was initialized to. It represents the promise which this notification is about.

> [!note]
> Because of how Web IDL conversion rules for `Promise<T>` types always wrap the input into a new promise, the [`promise`](#8147-unhandled-promise-rejections) attribute is of type [`object`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-object) instead, which is more appropriate for representing an opaque handle to the original promise object.

The `reason` attribute must return the value it was initialized to. It represents the rejection reason for the promise.

##### 8.1.4.8 Import map parse results

An import map parse result is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) that is similar to a [script](#8141-scripts), and also can be stored in a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element's [result](#41211-processing-model), but is not counted as a [script](#8141-scripts) for other purposes. It has the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):

An import map

An [import map](#8153-import-map-processing-model) or null.

An error to rethrow

A JavaScript value representing an error that will prevent using this import map, when non-null.

To create an import map parse result given a [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) input and a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) baseURL:
1. Let result be an [import map parse result](#8148-import-map-parse-results) whose [import map](#8148-import-map-parse-results) is null and whose [error to rethrow](#8148-import-map-parse-results) is null.
2. [Parse an import map string](#8153-import-map-processing-model) given input and baseURL, catching any exceptions. If this threw an exception, then set result's [error to rethrow](#8148-import-map-parse-results) to that exception. Otherwise, set result's [import map](#8148-import-map-parse-results) to the return value.
3. Return result.

To register an import map given a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) global and an [import map parse result](#8148-import-map-parse-results) result:
1. If result's [error to rethrow](#8148-import-map-parse-results) is not null, then [report an exception](#8146-runtime-script-errors) given by result's [error to rethrow](#8148-import-map-parse-results) for global and return.
2. [Merge existing and new import maps](#8153-import-map-processing-model), given global and result's [import map](#8148-import-map-parse-results).

##### 8.1.4.9 Speculation rules parse results

A speculation rules parse result is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) that is similar to a [script](#8141-scripts), and also can be stored in a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element's [result](#41211-processing-model), but is not counted as a [script](#8141-scripts) for other purposes. It has the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):

A speculation rule set

A [speculation rule set](#7611-data-model) or null.

An error to rethrow

A JavaScript value representing an error that will prevent using these speculation rules, when non-null.

To create a speculation rules parse result given a [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) input and a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document:
1. Let result be a [speculation rules parse result](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results) whose [speculation rule set](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results) is null and whose [error to rethrow](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results) is null.
2. [Parse a speculation rule set string](#7612-parsing) given input, document, and document's [document base URL](#243-document-base-urls), catching any exceptions. If this threw an exception, then set result's [error to rethrow](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results) to that exception. Otherwise, set result's [speculation rule set](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results) to the return value.
3. Return result.

To register speculation rules given a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) global, a [speculation rules parse result](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results) result, and an optional boolean queueErrors (default false):
1. If result's [error to rethrow](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results) is not null:
   1. If queueErrors is true, then [queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given global to perform the following step:
      1. [Report an exception](#8146-runtime-script-errors) given by result's [error to rethrow](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results) for global.
   2. Otherwise, [report an exception](#8146-runtime-script-errors) given by result's [error to rethrow](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results) for global.
   3. Return.
2. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) result's [speculation rule set](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results) to global's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [speculation rule sets](#7613-processing-model).
3. [Consider speculative loads](#7613-processing-model) for global's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object).

To unregister speculation rules given a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) global and a [speculation rules parse result](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results) result:
1. If result's [error to rethrow](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results) is not null, then return.
2. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) result's [speculation rule set](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results) from global's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [speculation rule sets](#7613-processing-model).
3. [Consider speculative loads](#7613-processing-model) for global's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object).

To update speculation rules given a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) global, a [speculation rules parse result](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results) oldResult, and a [speculation rules parse result](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results) newResult:
1. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) oldResult's [speculation rule set](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results) from global's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [speculation rule sets](#7613-processing-model).
2. [Register speculation rules](#8149-speculation-rules-parse-results) given global, newResult, and true.

   > [!note]
   > When updating speculation rules, as opposed to registering them for the first time, we ensure that any [`error`](#events) events are queued as tasks, instead of synchronously fired. Although synchronously executing [`error`](#events) event handlers is OK when inserting [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements, it's best if other modifications do not cause such synchronous script execution.

#### 8.1.5 Module specifier resolution

##### 8.1.5.1 The resolution algorithm

The [resolve a module specifier](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm) algorithm is the primary entry point for converting module specifier strings into [URLs](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url). When no [import maps](#8153-import-map-processing-model) are involved, it is relatively straightforward, and reduces to [resolving a URL-like module specifier](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm).

When there is a non-empty [import map](#8153-import-map-processing-model) present, the behavior is more complex. It checks candidate entries from all applicable [module specifier maps](#8153-import-map-processing-model), from most-specific to least-specific [scopes](#8153-import-map-processing-model) (falling back to the top-level unscoped [imports](#8153-import-map-processing-model)), and from most-specific to least-specific prefixes. For each candidate, the [resolve an imports match](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm) algorithm will give one of the following results:
- Successful resolution of the specifier to a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url). Then the [resolve a module specifier](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm) algorithm will return that URL.
- Throwing an exception. Then the [resolve a module specifier](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm) algorithm will rethrow that exception, without any further fallbacks.
- Failing to resolve, without an error. In this case the outer [resolve a module specifier](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm) algorithm will move on to the next candidate.

In the end, if no successful resolution is found via any of the candidate [module specifier maps](#8153-import-map-processing-model), [resolve a module specifier](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm) will throw an exception. Thus the result is always either a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) or a thrown exception.

To resolve a module specifier given a [script](#4121-the-script-element)-or-null referringScript and a [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) specifier:
1. Let settingsObject and baseURL be null.
2. If referringScript is not null:
   1. Set settingsObject to referringScript's [settings object](#8141-scripts).
   2. Set baseURL to referringScript's [base URL](#8141-scripts).
3. Otherwise:
   1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): there is a [current settings object](#81333-current).
   2. Set settingsObject to the [current settings object](#81333-current).
   3. Set baseURL to settingsObject's [API base URL](#8132-environment-settings-objects).
4. Let importMap be an [empty import map](#8153-import-map-processing-model).
5. If settingsObject's [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) implements [`Window`](#722-the-window-object), then set importMap to settingsObject's [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects)'s [import map](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
6. Let serializedBaseURL be baseURL, [serialized](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer).
7. Let asURL be the result of [resolving a URL-like module specifier](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm) given specifier and baseURL.
8. Let normalizedSpecifier be the [serialization](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer) of asURL, if asURL is non-null; otherwise, specifier.
9. Let result be a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url)-or-null, initially null.
10. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) scopePrefix → scopeImports of importMap's [scopes](#8153-import-map-processing-model):
    1. If scopePrefix is serializedBaseURL, or if scopePrefix ends with U+002F (/) and scopePrefix is a [code unit prefix](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) of serializedBaseURL:
       1. Let scopeImportsMatch be the result of [resolving an imports match](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm) given normalizedSpecifier, asURL, and scopeImports.
       2. If scopeImportsMatch is not null, then set result to scopeImportsMatch, and [break](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
11. If result is null, set result to the result of [resolving an imports match](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm) given normalizedSpecifier, asURL, and importMap's [imports](#8153-import-map-processing-model).
12. If result is null, set it to asURL.

    > [!note]
    > By this point, if result was null, specifier wasn't remapped to anything by importMap, but it might have been able to be turned into a URL.

13. If result is not null:
    1. [Add module to resolved module set](#8153-import-map-processing-model) given settingsObject, serializedBaseURL, normalizedSpecifier, and asURL.
    2. Return result.
14. Throw a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) indicating that specifier was a bare specifier, but was not remapped to anything by importMap.

To resolve an imports match, given a [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) normalizedSpecifier, a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url)-or-null asURL, and a [module specifier map](#8153-import-map-processing-model) specifierMap:
1. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) specifierKey → resolutionResult of specifierMap:
   1. If specifierKey is normalizedSpecifier:
      1. If resolutionResult is null, then throw a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) indicating that resolution of specifierKey was blocked by a null entry.

         > [!note]
         > This will terminate the entire [resolve a module specifier](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm) algorithm, without any further fallbacks.

      2. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): resolutionResult is a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url).
      3. Return resolutionResult.

   2. If all of the following are true:
      - specifierKey ends with U+002F (/);
      - specifierKey is a [code unit prefix](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) of normalizedSpecifier; and
      - either asURL is null, or asURL [is special](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#is-special),

      then:
      1. If resolutionResult is null, then throw a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) indicating that the resolution of specifierKey was blocked by a null entry.

         > [!note]
         > This will terminate the entire [resolve a module specifier](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm) algorithm, without any further fallbacks.

      2. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): resolutionResult is a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url).
      3. Let afterPrefix be the portion of normalizedSpecifier after the initial specifierKey prefix.
      4. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): resolutionResult, [serialized](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer), ends with U+002F (/), as enforced during [parsing](#8153-import-map-processing-model).
      5. Let url be the result of [URL parsing](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser) afterPrefix with resolutionResult.
      6. If url is failure, then throw a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) indicating that resolution of normalizedSpecifier was blocked since the afterPrefix portion could not be URL-parsed relative to the resolutionResult mapped to by the specifierKey prefix.

         > [!note]
         > This will terminate the entire [resolve a module specifier](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm) algorithm, without any further fallbacks.

      7. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): url is a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url).
      8. If the [serialization](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer) of resolutionResult is not a [code unit prefix](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) of the [serialization](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer) of url, then throw a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) indicating that the resolution of normalizedSpecifier was blocked due to it backtracking above its prefix specifierKey.

         > [!note]
         > This will terminate the entire [resolve a module specifier](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm) algorithm, without any further fallbacks.

      9. Return url.

2. Return null.

   > [!note]
   > The [resolve a module specifier](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm) algorithm will fall back to a less-specific scope, or to "`imports`", if possible.

To resolve a URL-like module specifier, given a [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) specifier and a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) baseURL:
1. If specifier [starts with](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) "`/`", "`./`", or "`../`":
   1. Let url be the result of [URL parsing](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser) specifier with baseURL.
   2. If url is failure, then return null.

      > [!example]
      > One way this could happen is if specifier is "`../foo`" and baseURL is a [`data:`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2397#section-2) URL.

   3. Return url.

   > [!note]
   > This includes cases where specifier [starts with](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) "`//`", i.e., scheme-relative URLs. Thus, url might end up with a different [host](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-host) than baseURL.

2. Let url be the result of [URL parsing](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser) specifier (with no base URL).
3. If url is failure, then return null.
4. Return url.

##### 8.1.5.2 Import maps

An [import map](#8153-import-map-processing-model) allows control over module specifier resolution. Import maps are delivered via inline [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements with their [`type`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute set to "`importmap`", and with their [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) containing a JSON representation of the import map.

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) can have multiple import maps processed, which can happen either before or after any modules have been imported, e.g., via [`import()`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-import-calls) expressions or [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements with their [`type`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute set to "`module`". The [merge existing and new import maps](#8153-import-map-processing-model) algorithm ensures that new import maps cannot define the module resolution for modules that were already defined by past import maps, or for ones that were already resolved.

> [!example]
> The simplest use of import maps is to globally remap a bare module specifier:
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "imports": {
>     "moment": "/node_modules/moment/src/moment.js"
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> This enables statements like `import moment from "moment";` to work, fetching and evaluating the JavaScript module at the `/node_modules/moment/src/moment.js` URL.

> [!example]
> An import map can remap a class of module specifiers into a class of URLs by using trailing slashes, like so:
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "imports": {
>     "moment/": "/node_modules/moment/src/"
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> This enables statements like `import localeData from
>    "moment/locale/zh-cn.js";` to work, fetching and evaluating the JavaScript module at the `/node_modules/moment/src/locale/zh-cn.js` URL. Such trailing-slash mappings are often combined with bare-specifier mappings, e.g.
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "imports": {
>     "moment": "/node_modules/moment/src/moment.js",
>     "moment/": "/node_modules/moment/src/"
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> so that both the "main module" specified by "`moment`" and the "submodules" specified by paths such as "`moment/locale/zh-cn.js`" are available.

> [!example]
> Bare specifiers are not the only type of module specifiers which import maps can remap. "URL-like" specifiers, i.e., those that are either parseable as absolute URLs or start with "`/`", "`./`", or "`../`", can be remapped as well:
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "imports": {
>     "https://cdn.example.com/vue/dist/vue.runtime.esm.js": "/node_modules/vue/dist/vue.runtime.esm.js",
>     "/js/app.mjs": "/js/app-8e0d62a03.mjs",
>     "../helpers/": "https://cdn.example/helpers/"
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> Note how the URL to be remapped, as well as the URL being mapped to, can be specified either as absolute URLs, or as relative URLs starting with "`/`", "`./`", or "`../`". (They cannot be specified as relative URLs without those starting sigils, as those help distinguish from bare module specifiers.) Also note how the [trailing slash mapping](#8152-import-maps) works in this context as well.
> 
> Such remappings operate on the post-canonicalization URL, and do not require a match between the literal strings supplied in the import map key and the imported module specifier. So for example, if this import map was included on `https://example.com/app.html`, then not only would `import "/js/app.mjs"` be remapped, but so would `import "./js/app.mjs"` and `import "./foo/../js/app.mjs"`.

> [!example]
> All previous examples have globally remapped module specifiers, by using the top-level "`imports`" key in the import map. The top-level "`scopes`" key can be used to provide localized remappings, which only apply when the referring module matches a specific URL prefix. For example:
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "scopes": {
>     "/a/" : {
>       "moment": "/node_modules/moment/src/moment.js"
>     },
>     "/b/" : {
>       "moment": "https://cdn.example.com/moment/src/moment.js"
>     }
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> With this import map, the statement `import "moment"` will have different meanings depending on which referrer script contains the statement:
> - Inside scripts located under `/a/`, this will import `/node_modules/moment/src/moment.js`.
> - Inside scripts located under `/b/`, this will import `https://cdn.example.com/moment/src/moment.js`.
> - Inside scripts located under `/c/`, this will fail to resolve and thus throw an exception.
> 
> A typical usage of scopes is to allow multiple versions of the "same" module to exist in a web application, with some parts of the module graph importing one version, and other parts importing another version.

> [!example]
> Scopes can overlap each other, and overlap the global "`imports`" specifier map. At resolution time, scopes are consulted in order of most- to least-specific, where specificity is measured by sorting the scopes using the [code unit less than](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) operation. So, for example, "`/scope2/scope3/`" is treated as more specific than "`/scope2/`", which is treated as more specific than the top-level (unscoped) mappings.
> 
> The following import map illustrates this:
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "imports": {
>     "a": "/a-1.mjs",
>     "b": "/b-1.mjs",
>     "c": "/c-1.mjs"
>   },
>   "scopes": {
>     "/scope2/": {
>       "a": "/a-2.mjs"
>     },
>     "/scope2/scope3/": {
>       "b": "/b-3.mjs"
>     }
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> This results in the following resolutions (using relative URLs for brevity):
> 
> |  | Specifier |
> | --- | --- |
> | "`a`" | "`b`" | "`c`" |
> | Referrer | `/scope1/r.mjs` | `/a-1.mjs` | `/b-1.mjs` | `/c-1.mjs` |
> | `/scope2/r.mjs` | `/a-2.mjs` | `/b-1.mjs` | `/c-1.mjs` |
> | `/scope2/scope3/r.mjs` | `/a-2.mjs` | `/b-3.mjs` | `/c-1.mjs` |

> [!example]
> Import maps can also be used to provide modules with integrity metadata to be used in Subresource Integrity checks. [\[SRI\]](#references)
> 
> The following import map illustrates this:
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "imports": {
>     "a": "/a-1.mjs",
>     "b": "/b-1.mjs",
>     "c": "/c-1.mjs"
>   },
>   "integrity": {
>     "/a-1.mjs": "sha384-Li9vy3DqF8tnTXuiaAJuML3ky+er10rcgNR/VqsVpcw+ThHmYcwiB1pbOxEbzJr7",
>     "/d-1.mjs": "sha384-MBO5IDfYaE6c6Aao94oZrIOiC6CGiSN2n4QUbHNPhzk5Xhm0djZLQqTpL0HzTUxk"
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> The above example provides integrity metadata to be enforced on the modules `/a-1.mjs` and `/d-1.mjs`, even if the latter is not defined as an import in the map.

---

The [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) of a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element representing an [import map](#8153-import-map-processing-model) must match the following import map authoring requirements:
- It must be valid JSON. [\[JSON\]](#references)
- The JSON must represent a JSON object, with at most the three keys "`imports`", "`scopes`", and "`integrity`".
- The values corresponding to the "`imports`", "`scopes`", and "`integrity`" keys, if present, must themselves be JSON objects.
- The value corresponding to the "`imports`" key, if present, must be a [valid module specifier map](#8152-import-maps).
- The value corresponding to the "`scopes`" key, if present, must be a JSON object, whose keys are [valid URL strings](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-url-string) and whose values are [valid module specifier maps](#8152-import-maps).
- The value corresponding to the "`integrity`" key, if present, must be a JSON object, whose keys are [valid URL strings](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-url-string) and whose values fit [the requirements of the integrity attribute](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-subresource-integrity/#the-integrity-attribute).

A valid module specifier map is a JSON object that meets the following requirements:
- All of its keys must be nonempty.
- All of its values must be strings.
- Each value must be either a [valid absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute) or a [valid URL string](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-url-string) that [starts with](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) "`/`", "`./`", or "`../`".
- If a given key [ends with](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) "`/`", then the corresponding value must also.

##### 8.1.5.3 Import map processing model

Formally, an import map is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) with three [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):
- imports, a [module specifier map](#8153-import-map-processing-model);
- scopes, an [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) of [URLs](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) to [module specifier maps](#8153-import-map-processing-model); and
- integrity, a [module integrity map](#8153-import-map-processing-model).

A module specifier map is an [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) whose [keys](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) are [strings](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) and whose [values](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) are either [URLs](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) or nulls.

A module integrity map is an [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) whose [keys](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) are [URLs](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) and whose [values](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) are [strings](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) that will be used as [integrity metadata](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-integrity-metadata).

An empty import map is an [import map](#8153-import-map-processing-model) with its [imports](#8153-import-map-processing-model) and [scopes](#8153-import-map-processing-model) both being empty maps.

---

A specifier resolution record is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs). It has the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):

A serialized base URL

A [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings)-or-null that represents the base URL of the specifier, when one exists.

A specifier

A [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) representing the specifier.

A specifier as a URL

A [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url)-or-null that represents the URL in case of a URL-like module specifier.

> [!note]
> Implementations can replace [specifier as a URL](#8153-import-map-processing-model) with a boolean that indicates that the specifier is either bare or URL-like that [is special](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#is-special).

To add module to resolved module set given an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settingsObject, a [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) serializedBaseURL, a [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) normalizedSpecifier, and a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url)-or-null asURL:
1. Let global be settingsObject's [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
2. If global does not implement [`Window`](#722-the-window-object), then return.
3. Let record be a new [specifier resolution record](#8153-import-map-processing-model), with [serialized base URL](#8153-import-map-processing-model) set to serializedBaseURL, [specifier](#8153-import-map-processing-model) set to normalizedSpecifier, and [specifier as a URL](#8153-import-map-processing-model) set to asURL.
4. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) record to global's [resolved module set](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).

---

To parse an import map string, given a [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) input and a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) baseURL:
1. Let parsed be the result of [parsing a JSON string to an Infra value](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#6-json) given input.
2. If parsed is not an [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then throw a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) indicating that the top-level value needs to be a JSON object.
3. Let sortedAndNormalizedImports be an empty [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps).
4. If parsed\["`imports`"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps):
   1. If parsed\["`imports`"\] is not an [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then throw a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) indicating that the value for the "`imports`" top-level key needs to be a JSON object.
   2. Set sortedAndNormalizedImports to the result of [sorting and normalizing a module specifier map](#8153-import-map-processing-model) given parsed\["`imports`"\] and baseURL.
5. Let sortedAndNormalizedScopes be an empty [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps).
6. If parsed\["`scopes`"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps):
   1. If parsed\["`scopes`"\] is not an [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then throw a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) indicating that the value for the "`scopes`" top-level key needs to be a JSON object.
   2. Set sortedAndNormalizedScopes to the result of [sorting and normalizing scopes](#8153-import-map-processing-model) given parsed\["`scopes`"\] and baseURL.
7. Let normalizedIntegrity be an empty [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps).
8. If parsed\["`integrity`"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps):
   1. If parsed\["`integrity`"\] is not an [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then throw a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) indicating that the value for the "`integrity`" top-level key needs to be a JSON object.
   2. Set normalizedIntegrity to the result of [normalizing a module integrity map](#8153-import-map-processing-model) given parsed\["`integrity`"\] and baseURL.
9. If parsed's [keys](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) any items besides "`imports`", "`scopes`", or "`integrity`", then the user agent should [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that an invalid top-level key was present in the import map.

   > [!note]
   > This can help detect typos. It is not an error, because that would prevent any future extensions from being added backward-compatibly.

10. Return an [import map](#8153-import-map-processing-model) whose [imports](#8153-import-map-processing-model) are sortedAndNormalizedImports, whose [scopes](#8153-import-map-processing-model) are sortedAndNormalizedScopes, and whose [integrity](#8153-import-map-processing-model) are normalizedIntegrity.

> [!example]
> The [import map](#8153-import-map-processing-model) that results from this parsing algorithm is highly normalized. For example, given a base URL of `https://example.com/base/page.html`, the input
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "imports": {
>     "/app/helper": "node_modules/helper/index.mjs",
>     "lodash": "/node_modules/lodash-es/lodash.js"
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> will generate an [import map](#8153-import-map-processing-model) with [imports](#8153-import-map-processing-model) of
> 
> ```
> «[
>   "https://example.com/app/helper" → https://example.com/base/node_modules/helper/index.mjs
>   "lodash" → https://example.com/node_modules/lodash-es/lodash.js
> ]»
> ```
> 
> and (despite nothing being present in the input string) an empty [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) for its [scopes](#8153-import-map-processing-model).

---

To merge module specifier maps, given a [module specifier map](#8153-import-map-processing-model) newMap and a [module specifier map](#8153-import-map-processing-model) oldMap:
1. Let mergedMap be a deep copy of oldMap.
2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) specifier → url of newMap:
   1. If specifier [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) in oldMap:
      1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating the ignored rule. They may choose to avoid reporting if the rule is identical to an existing one.
      2. [Continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   2. Set mergedMap\[specifier\] to url.
3. Return mergedMap.

To merge existing and new import maps, given a [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) global and an [import map](#8153-import-map-processing-model) newImportMap:
1. Let newImportMapScopes be a deep copy of newImportMap's [scopes](#8153-import-map-processing-model).

   > [!note]
   > We're mutating these copies and removing items from them when they are used to ignore scope-specific rules. This is true for newImportMapScopes, as well as to newImportMapImports below.

2. Let oldImportMap be global's [import map](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
3. Let newImportMapImports be a deep copy of newImportMap's [imports](#8153-import-map-processing-model).
4. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) scopePrefix → scopeImports of newImportMapScopes:
   1. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) record of global's [resolved module set](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects):
      1. If scopePrefix is record's [serialized base URL](#8153-import-map-processing-model), or if scopePrefix ends with U+002F (/) and scopePrefix is a [code unit prefix](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) of record's [serialized base URL](#8153-import-map-processing-model):
         1. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) specifierKey → resolutionResult of scopeImports:
            1. If specifierKey is record's [specifier](#8153-import-map-processing-model), or if all of the following conditions are true:
               - specifierKey ends with U+002F (/);
               - specifierKey is a [code unit prefix](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) of record's [specifier](#8153-import-map-processing-model);
               - either record's [specifier as a URL](#8153-import-map-processing-model) is null or [is special](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#is-special),

               then:
               1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating the ignored rule. They may choose to avoid reporting if the rule is identical to an existing one.
               2. Remove scopeImports\[specifierKey\].

      > [!note]
      > Implementers are encouraged to implement a more efficient matching algorithm when working with the [resolved module set](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects). As guidance, the number of resolved/mapped modules in a large application can be on the order of thousands.

   2. If scopePrefix [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) in oldImportMap's [scopes](#8153-import-map-processing-model), then set oldImportMap's [scopes](#8153-import-map-processing-model)\[scopePrefix\] to the result of [merging module specifier maps](#8153-import-map-processing-model), given scopeImports and oldImportMap's [scopes](#8153-import-map-processing-model)\[scopePrefix\].
   3. Otherwise, set oldImportMap's [scopes](#8153-import-map-processing-model)\[scopePrefix\] to scopeImports.

5. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) url → integrity of newImportMap's [integrity](#8153-import-map-processing-model):
   1. If url [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) in oldImportMap's [integrity](#8153-import-map-processing-model):
      1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating the ignored rule. They may choose to avoid reporting if the rule is identical to an existing one.
      2. [Continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   2. Set oldImportMap's [integrity](#8153-import-map-processing-model)\[url\] to integrity.
6. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) record of global's [resolved module set](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects):
   1. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) specifier → url of newImportMapImports:
      1. If specifier [starts with](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) record's [specifier](#8153-import-map-processing-model):
         1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating the ignored rule. They may choose to avoid reporting if the rule is identical to an existing one.
         2. Remove newImportMapImports\[specifier\].
7. Set oldImportMap's [imports](#8153-import-map-processing-model) to the result of [merge module specifier maps](#8153-import-map-processing-model), given newImportMapImports and oldImportMap's [imports](#8153-import-map-processing-model).

The above algorithm merges a new import map into the given [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects)'s [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects)'s [import map](#8153-import-map-processing-model). Let's examine a few examples:

> [!example]
> There are two cases when rules of the new import map don't get merged into the existing one.
> 1. The new import map rule has the exact same scope and specifier as a rule in the existing import map. We'll call that "conflicting rule".
> 2. The new import map rule may impact the resolution of an already resolved module. We'll call that "impacted already resolved module".
> 
> When the new import map has no conflicting rules, and there are no impacted resolved modules, the resulting map would be a combination of the new and existing maps. Rules that would have individually impacted similar modules (e.g. "/app/" and "/app/helper") but are not an exact match are not conflicting, and all make it to the merged map.
> 
> So, the following existing and new import maps:
> 
> ```json
> {
>    "imports": {
>     "/app/": "./original-app/",
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "imports": {
>     "/app/helper": "./helper/index.mjs"
>   },
>   "scopes": {
>     "/js": {
>       "/app/": "./js-app/"
>     }
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> Would be equivalent to the following single import map:
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "imports": {
>     "/app/": "./original-app/",
>     "/app/helper": "./helper/index.mjs"
>   },
>   "scopes": {
>     "/js": {
>       "/app/": "./js-app/"
>     }
>   }
> }
> ```

> [!example]
> When the new import map impacts an already resolved module, that rule gets dropped from the import map.
> 
> So, if the [resolved module set](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) already contains the "`/app/helper`", the following new import map:
> 
> ```json
> {
>    "imports": {
>     "/app/helper": "./helper/index.mjs",
>     "lodash": "/node_modules/lodash-es/lodash.js"
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> Would be equivalent to the following one:
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "imports": {
>     "lodash": "/node_modules/lodash-es/lodash.js"
>   }
> }
> ```

> [!example]
> The same is true for rules that impact already resolved modules defined in specific scopes. If we already resolved "`/app/helper`" from "`/app/main.mjs`" the following new import map:
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "scopes": {
>     "/app/": {
>       "/app/helper": "./helper/index.mjs"
>     }
>   },
>    "imports": {
>     "lodash": "/node_modules/lodash-es/lodash.js"
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> Would similarly be equivalent to:
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "imports": {
>     "lodash": "/node_modules/lodash-es/lodash.js"
>   }
> }
> ```

> [!example]
> We could also have cases where a single already-resolved module specifier has multiple rules for its resolution, depending on the referring script. In such cases, only the relevant rules would not be added to the map.
> 
> For example, if we already resolved "`/app/helper`" from "`/app/vendor/main.mjs`", the following new import map:
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "scopes": {
>     "/app/": {
>       "/app/helper": "./helper/index.mjs"
>     },
>     "/app/vendor/": {
>       "/app/": "./vendor_helper/"
>     },
>     "/vendor/": {
>       "/app/helper": "./helper/vendor_index.mjs"
>     }
>   },
>    "imports": {
>     "lodash": "/node_modules/lodash-es/lodash.js"
>     "/app/": "./general_app_path/"
>     "/app/helper": "./other_path/helper/index.mjs"
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> Would be equivalent to:
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "scopes": {
>     "/vendor/": {
>       "/app/helper": "./helper/vendor_index.mjs"
>     }
>   },
>   "imports": {
>     "lodash": "/node_modules/lodash-es/lodash.js"
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> This is achieved by the fact that the merge algorithm tracks already resolved modules and removes rules affecting them from new import maps before they are merged into the existing one.

> [!example]
> When the new import map has conflicting rules to the existing import map, with no impacted already resolved modules, the existing import map rules persist.
> 
> For example, the following existing and new import maps:
> 
> ```json
> {
>    "imports": {
>     "/app/helper": "./helper/index.mjs",
>     "lodash": "/node_modules/lodash-es/lodash.js"
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "imports": {
>     "/app/helper": "./main/helper/index.mjs"
>   }
> }
> ```
> 
> Would be equivalent to the following single import map:
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "imports": {
>     "/app/helper": "./helper/index.mjs",
>     "lodash": "/node_modules/lodash-es/lodash.js",
>   }
> }
> ```

To sort and normalize a module specifier map, given an [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) originalMap and a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) baseURL:
1. Let normalized be an empty [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps).
2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) specifierKey → value of originalMap:
   1. Let normalizedSpecifierKey be the result of [normalizing a specifier key](#8153-import-map-processing-model) given specifierKey and baseURL.
   2. If normalizedSpecifierKey is null, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   3. If value is not a [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings):
      1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that addresses need to be strings.
      2. Set normalized\[normalizedSpecifierKey\] to null.
      3. [Continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   4. Let addressURL be the result of [resolving a URL-like module specifier](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm) given value and baseURL.
   5. If addressURL is null:
      1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the address was invalid.
      2. Set normalized\[normalizedSpecifierKey\] to null.
      3. [Continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   6. If specifierKey ends with U+002F (/), and the [serialization](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer) of addressURL does not end with U+002F (/):
      1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that an invalid address was given for the specifier key specifierKey; since specifierKey ends with a slash, the address needs to as well.
      2. Set normalized\[normalizedSpecifierKey\] to null.
      3. [Continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   7. Set normalized\[normalizedSpecifierKey\] to addressURL.
3. Return the result of [sorting in descending order](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) normalized, with an entry a being less than an entry b if a's [key](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) is [code unit less than](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) b's [key](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps).

To sort and normalize scopes, given an [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) originalMap and a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) baseURL:
1. Let normalized be an empty [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps).
2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) scopePrefix → potentialSpecifierMap of originalMap:
   1. If potentialSpecifierMap is not an [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then throw a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) indicating that the value of the scope with prefix scopePrefix needs to be a JSON object.
   2. Let scopePrefixURL be the result of [URL parsing](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser) scopePrefix with baseURL.
   3. If scopePrefixURL is failure:
      1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) that the scope prefix URL was not parseable.
      2. [Continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   4. Let normalizedScopePrefix be the [serialization](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer) of scopePrefixURL.
   5. Set normalized\[normalizedScopePrefix\] to the result of [sorting and normalizing a module specifier map](#8153-import-map-processing-model) given potentialSpecifierMap and baseURL.
3. Return the result of [sorting in descending order](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) normalized, with an entry a being less than an entry b if a's [key](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) is [code unit less than](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) b's [key](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps).

> [!note]
> In the above two algorithms, sorting keys and scopes in descending order has the effect of putting "`foo/bar/`" before "`foo/`". This in turn gives "`foo/bar/`" a higher priority than "`foo/`" during [module specifier resolution](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm).

To normalize a module integrity map, given an [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) originalMap:
1. Let normalized be an empty [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps).
2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) key → value of originalMap:
   1. Let resolvedURL be the result of [resolving a URL-like module specifier](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm) given key and baseURL.

      > [!note]
      > Unlike "`imports`", keys of the integrity map are treated as URLs, not module specifiers. However, we use the [resolve a URL-like module specifier](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm) algorithm to prohibit "bare" relative URLs like `foo`, which could be mistaken for module specifiers.

   2. If resolvedURL is null:
      1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that the key failed to resolve.
      2. [Continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   3. If value is not a [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings):
      1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that [integrity metadata](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-integrity-metadata) values need to be [strings](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings).
      2. [Continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
   4. Set normalized\[resolvedURL\] to value.

3. Return normalized.

To normalize a specifier key, given a [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) specifierKey and a [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) baseURL:
1. If specifierKey is the empty string:
   1. The user agent may [report a warning to the console](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#report-a-warning-to-the-console) indicating that specifier keys may not be the empty string.
   2. Return null.
2. Let url be the result of [resolving a URL-like module specifier](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm), given specifierKey and baseURL.
3. If url is not null, then return the [serialization](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer) of url.
4. Return specifierKey.

#### 8.1.6 JavaScript specification host hooks

The JavaScript specification contains a number of [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) abstract operations, that vary depending on the host environment. This section defines them for user agent hosts.

##### 8.1.6.1 HostEnsureCanAddPrivateElement(O)

JavaScript contains an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) [HostEnsureCanAddPrivateElement](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-hostensurecanaddprivateelement)(O) abstract operation. User agents must use the following implementation: [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#references)
1. If O is a [`WindowProxy`](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object) object, or [implements](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#implements) [`Location`](#724-the-location-interface), then return [ThrowCompletion](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-throwcompletion)(a new [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror)).
2. Return [NormalCompletion](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-normalcompletion)(unused).

> [!note]
> JavaScript private fields can be applied to arbitrary objects. Since this can dramatically complicate implementation for particularly-exotic host objects, the JavaScript language specification provides this hook to allow hosts to reject private fields on objects meeting a host-defined criteria. In the case of HTML, [`WindowProxy`](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object) and [`Location`](#724-the-location-interface) have complicated semantics — particularly around navigation and security — that make implementation of private field semantics challenging, so our implementation simply rejects those objects.

##### 8.1.6.2 HostEnsureCanCompileStrings(realm, parameterStrings, bodyString, codeString, compilationType, parameterArgs, bodyArg)

JavaScript contains an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) [HostEnsureCanCompileStrings](https://tc39.es/proposal-dynamic-code-brand-checks/#sec-hostensurecancompilestrings) abstract operation, redefined by the Dynamic Code Brand Checks proposal. User agents must use the following implementation: [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#references) [\[JSDYNAMICCODEBRANDCHECKS\]](#references)
1. Perform ? [EnsureCSPDoesNotBlockStringCompilation](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#can-compile-strings)(realm, parameterStrings, bodyString, codeString, compilationType, parameterArgs, bodyArg). [\[CSP\]](#references)

##### 8.1.6.3 HostGetCodeForEval(argument)

The Dynamic Code Brand Checks proposal contains an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) [HostGetCodeForEval](https://tc39.es/proposal-dynamic-code-brand-checks/#sec-hostgetcodeforeval)(argument) abstract operation. User agents must use the following implementation: [\[JSDYNAMICCODEBRANDCHECKS\]](#references)
1. If argument is a [`TrustedScript`](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trustedscript) object, then return argument's [data](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trustedscript-data).
2. Otherwise, return no-code.

##### 8.1.6.4 HostPromiseRejectionTracker(promise, operation)

JavaScript contains an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) [HostPromiseRejectionTracker](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-host-promise-rejection-tracker)(promise, operation) abstract operation. User agents must use the following implementation: [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#references)
1. Let script be the [running script](#8144-calling-scripts).
2. If script is a [classic script](#8141-scripts) and script's [muted errors](#8141-scripts) is true, then return.
3. Let settingsObject be the [current settings object](#81333-current).
4. If script is not null, then set settingsObject to script's [settings object](#8141-scripts).
5. Let global be settingsObject's [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
6. If operation is "`reject`":
   1. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) promise to global's [about-to-be-notified rejected promises list](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
7. If operation is "`handle`":
   1. If global's [about-to-be-notified rejected promises list](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) promise, then [remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) promise from that list and return.
   2. If global's [outstanding rejected promises weak set](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) does not [contain](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) promise, then return.
   3. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) promise from global's [outstanding rejected promises weak set](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
   4. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given global to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`rejectionhandled`](#events) at global, using [`PromiseRejectionEvent`](#8147-unhandled-promise-rejections), with the [`promise`](#8147-unhandled-promise-rejections) attribute initialized to promise, and the [`reason`](#8147-unhandled-promise-rejections) attribute initialized to promise.\[\[PromiseResult\]\].

##### 8.1.6.5 HostSystemUTCEpochNanoseconds(global)

The Temporal proposal contains an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) [HostSystemUTCEpochNanoseconds](https://tc39.es/proposal-temporal/#sec-hostsystemutcepochnanoseconds) abstract operation. User agents must use the following implementation: [\[JSTEMPORAL\]](#references)
1. Let settingsObject be global's [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant).
2. Let time be settingsObject's [current wall time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-wall-time).
3. Let ns be the number of nanoseconds from the [Unix epoch](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-unix-epoch) to time, rounded to the nearest integer.
4. Return the result of [clamping](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#clamping) ns between [nsMinInstant](https://tc39.es/proposal-temporal/#eqn-nsMinInstant) and [nsMaxInstant](https://tc39.es/proposal-temporal/#eqn-nsMaxInstant).

##### 8.1.6.6 Job-related host hooks

The JavaScript specification defines Jobs to be scheduled and run later by the host, as well as [JobCallback Records](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-jobcallback-records) which encapsulate JavaScript functions that are called as part of jobs. The JavaScript specification contains a number of [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) abstract operations that lets the host define how jobs are scheduled and how JobCallbacks are handled. HTML uses these abstract operations to track the [incumbent settings object](#81332-incumbent) in promises and [`FinalizationRegistry`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-finalization-registry-objects) callbacks by saving and restoring the [incumbent settings object](#81332-incumbent) and a [JavaScript execution context](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-execution-contexts) for the [active script](#8141-scripts) in JobCallbacks. This section defines them for user agent hosts.

###### 8.1.6.6.1 HostCallJobCallback(callback, V, argumentsList)

JavaScript contains an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) [HostCallJobCallback](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-hostcalljobcallback)(callback, V, argumentsList) abstract operation to let hosts restore state when invoking JavaScript callbacks from inside tasks. User agents must use the following implementation: [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#references)
1. Let incumbent settings be callback.\[\[HostDefined\]\].\[\[IncumbentSettings\]\].
2. Let script execution context be callback.\[\[HostDefined\]\].\[\[ActiveScriptContext\]\].
3. [Prepare to run a callback](#81332-incumbent) with incumbent settings.

   > [!note]
   > This affects the [incumbent](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) concept while the callback runs.

4. If script execution context is not null, then [push](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#511-stacks) script execution context onto the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack).

   > [!note]
   > This affects the [active script](#8141-scripts) while the callback runs.

5. Let result be [Call](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-call)(callback.\[\[Callback\]\], V, argumentsList).
6. If script execution context is not null, then [pop](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#511-stacks) script execution context from the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack).
7. [Clean up after running a callback](#81332-incumbent) with incumbent settings.
8. Return result.

###### 8.1.6.6.2 HostEnqueueFinalizationRegistryCleanupJob(finalizationRegistry)

JavaScript has the ability to register objects with [`FinalizationRegistry`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-finalization-registry-objects) objects, in order to schedule a cleanup action if they are found to be garbage collected. The JavaScript specification contains an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) [HostEnqueueFinalizationRegistryCleanupJob](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-host-cleanup-finalization-registry)(finalizationRegistry) abstract operation to schedule the cleanup action.

> [!note]
> The timing and occurrence of cleanup work is [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) in the JavaScript specification. User agents might differ in when and whether an object is garbage collected, affecting both whether the return value of the [`WeakRef.prototype.deref()`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-weak-ref.prototype.deref) method is undefined, and whether [`FinalizationRegistry`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-finalization-registry-objects) cleanup callbacks occur. There are well-known cases in popular web browsers where objects are not accessible to JavaScript, but they remain retained by the garbage collector indefinitely. HTML clears kept-alive [`WeakRef`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-weak-ref-objects) objects in the [perform a microtask checkpoint](#8173-processing-model) algorithm. Authors would be best off not depending on the timing details of garbage collection implementations.

Cleanup actions do not take place interspersed with synchronous JavaScript execution, but rather happen in queued [tasks](#8171-definitions). User agents must use the following implementation: [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#references)
1. Let global be finalizationRegistry.\[\[Realm\]\]'s [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
2. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the JavaScript engine task source given global to perform the following steps:
   1. Let entry be finalizationRegistry.\[\[CleanupCallback\]\].\[\[Callback\]\].\[\[Realm\]\]'s [environment settings object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
   2. [Prepare to run script](#8144-calling-scripts) with entry.

      > [!note]
      > This affects the [entry](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) concept while the cleanup callback runs.

   3. Let result be the result of performing [CleanupFinalizationRegistry](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-cleanup-finalization-registry)(finalizationRegistry).
   4. [Clean up after running script](#8144-calling-scripts) with entry.
   5. If result is an [abrupt completion](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type), then [report an exception](#8146-runtime-script-errors) given by result.\[\[Value\]\] for global.

###### 8.1.6.6.3 HostEnqueueGenericJob(job, realm)

JavaScript contains an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) [HostEnqueueGenericJob](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-hostenqueuegenericjob)(job, realm) abstract operation to perform generic jobs in a particular realm (e.g., resolve promises resulting from [`Atomics.waitAsync`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-atomics.waitasync)). User agents must use the following implementation: [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#references)
1. Let global be realm's [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
2. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [JavaScript engine task source](#81662-hostenqueuefinalizationregistrycleanupjobfinalizationregistry) given global to perform job().

###### 8.1.6.6.4 HostEnqueuePromiseJob(job, realm)

JavaScript contains an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) [HostEnqueuePromiseJob](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-hostenqueuepromisejob)(job, realm) abstract operation to schedule Promise-related operations. HTML schedules these operations in the microtask queue. User agents must use the following implementation: [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#references)
1. If realm is not null, then let job settings be the [settings object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) for realm. Otherwise, let job settings be null.

   > [!note]
   > If realm is not null, it is the [realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms) of the author code that will run. When job is returned by [NewPromiseReactionJob](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-newpromisereactionjob), it is the realm of the promise's handler function. When job is returned by [NewPromiseResolveThenableJob](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-newpromiseresolvethenablejob), it is the realm of the `then` function.
   > 
   > If realm is null, either no author code will run or author code is guaranteed to throw. For the former, the author may not have passed in code to run, such as in `promise.then(null, null)`. For the latter, it is because a revoked Proxy was passed. In both cases, all the steps below that would otherwise use job settings get skipped.
   > 
   > > [!warning]
   > > [NewPromiseResolveThenableJob](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-newpromiseresolvethenablejob) and [NewPromiseReactionJob](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-newpromisereactionjob) both seem to provide non-null realms (the current Realm Record) in the case of a revoked proxy. The previous text could be updated to reflect that.

2. [Queue a microtask](#8172-queuing-tasks) to perform the following steps:
   1. If job settings is not null, then [prepare to run script](#8144-calling-scripts) with job settings.

      > [!note]
      > This affects the [entry](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) concept while the job runs.

   2. Let result be job().

      > [!note]
      > job is an [abstract closure](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-abstract-closure) returned by [NewPromiseReactionJob](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-newpromisereactionjob) or [NewPromiseResolveThenableJob](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-newpromiseresolvethenablejob). The promise's handler function when job is returned by [NewPromiseReactionJob](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-newpromisereactionjob), and the `then` function when job is returned by [NewPromiseResolveThenableJob](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-newpromiseresolvethenablejob), are wrapped in [JobCallback Records](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-jobcallback-records). HTML saves the [incumbent settings object](#81332-incumbent) and a [JavaScript execution context](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-execution-contexts) for to the [active script](#8141-scripts) in [HostMakeJobCallback](#81666-hostmakejobcallbackcallable) and restores them in [HostCallJobCallback](#81661-hostcalljobcallbackcallback-v-argumentslist).

   3. If job settings is not null, then [clean up after running script](#8144-calling-scripts) with job settings.
   4. If result is an [abrupt completion](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-completion-record-specification-type), then [report an exception](#8146-runtime-script-errors) given by result.\[\[Value\]\] for realm's [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).

      > [!warning]
      > There is a very gnarly case where HostEnqueuePromiseJob is called with a null realm (e.g., because Promise.prototype.then was called with null handlers) but also the job returns abruptly (because the promise capability's resolve or reject handler threw, possibly because this is a subclass of Promise that takes the supplied functions and wraps them in throwing functions before passing them on to the function passed to the Promise superclass constructor). Which global is to be used then, considering that the current realm could be different at each of those steps, by using a Promise constructor or Promise.prototype.then from another realm? See [issue #10526](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10526).

###### 8.1.6.6.5 HostEnqueueTimeoutJob(job, realm, milliseconds)

JavaScript contains an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) [HostEnqueueTimeoutJob](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-hostenqueuetimeoutjob)(job, milliseconds) abstract operation to schedule an operation to be performed after a timeout. HTML schedules these operations using [run steps after a timeout](#87-timers). User agents must use the following implementation: [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#references)
1. Let global be realm's [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
2. Let timeoutStep be an algorithm step which [queues a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [JavaScript engine task source](#81662-hostenqueuefinalizationregistrycleanupjobfinalizationregistry) given global to perform job().
3. [Run steps after a timeout](#87-timers) given global, "`JavaScript`", milliseconds, and timeoutStep.

###### 8.1.6.6.6 HostMakeJobCallback(callable)

JavaScript contains an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) [HostMakeJobCallback](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-hostmakejobcallback)(callable) abstract operation to let hosts attach state to JavaScript callbacks that are called from inside [task](#8171-definitions)s. User agents must use the following implementation: [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#references)
1. Let incumbent settings be the [incumbent settings object](#81332-incumbent).
2. Let active script be the [active script](#8141-scripts).
3. Let script execution context be null.
4. If active script is not null, set script execution context to a new [JavaScript execution context](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-execution-contexts), with its Function field set to null, its Realm field set to active script's [settings object](#8141-scripts)'s [realm](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects), and its ScriptOrModule set to active script's [record](#8141-scripts).

   > [!note]
   > As seen below, this is used in order to propagate the current [active script](#8141-scripts) forward to the time when the job callback is invoked.

   > [!example]
   > A case where active script is non-null, and saving it in this way is useful, is the following:
   > 
   > ```javascript
   > Promise.resolve('import(`./example.mjs`)').then(eval);
   > ```
   > 
   > Without this step (and the steps that use it in [HostCallJobCallback](#81661-hostcalljobcallbackcallback-v-argumentslist)), there would be no [active script](#8141-scripts) when the [`import()`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-import-calls) expression is evaluated, since [`eval()`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-eval-x) is a built-in function that does not originate from any particular [script](#8141-scripts).
   > 
   > With this step in place, the active script is propagated from the above code into the job, allowing [`import()`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-import-calls) to use the original script's [base URL](#8141-scripts) appropriately.

   > [!example]
   > active script can be null if the user clicks on the following button:
   > 
   > ```html
   > <button onclick="Promise.resolve('import(`./example.mjs`)').then(eval)">Click me</button>
   > ```
   > 
   > In this case, the JavaScript function for the [event handler](#8181-event-handlers) will be created by the [get the current value of the event handler](#8181-event-handlers) algorithm, which creates a function with null \[\[ScriptOrModule\]\] value. Thus, when the promise machinery calls [HostMakeJobCallback](#81666-hostmakejobcallbackcallable), there will be no [active script](#8141-scripts) to pass along.
   > 
   > As a consequence, this means that when the [`import()`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-import-calls) expression is evaluated, there will still be no [active script](#8141-scripts). Fortunately that is handled by our implementation of [HostLoadImportedModule](#81673-hostloadimportedmodulereferrer-modulerequest-loadstate-payload) by falling back to using the [current settings object](#81333-current)'s [API base URL](#8132-environment-settings-objects).

5. Return the [JobCallback Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-jobcallback-records) { \[\[Callback\]\]: callable, \[\[HostDefined\]\]: { \[\[IncumbentSettings\]\]: incumbent settings, \[\[ActiveScriptContext\]\]: script execution context } }.

##### 8.1.6.7 Module-related host hooks

The JavaScript specification defines a syntax for modules, as well as some host-agnostic parts of their processing model. This specification defines the rest of their processing model: how the module system is bootstrapped, via the [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element with [`type`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute set to "`module`", and how modules are fetched, resolved, and executed. [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#references)

> [!note]
