> Although the JavaScript specification speaks in terms of "scripts" versus "modules", in general this specification speaks in terms of [classic scripts](#8141-scripts) versus [module scripts](#8141-scripts), since both of them use the [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element.

`modulePromise = import(specifier)`

Returns a promise for the module namespace object for the [module script](#8141-scripts) identified by specifier. This allows dynamic importing of module scripts at runtime, instead of statically using the `import` statement form. The specifier will be [resolved](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm) relative to the [active script](#8141-scripts).

The returned promise will be rejected if an invalid specifier is given, or if a failure is encountered while [fetching](#81673-hostloadimportedmodulereferrer-modulerequest-loadstate-payload) or evaluating the resulting module graph.

This syntax can be used inside both [classic](#8141-scripts) and [module scripts](#8141-scripts). It thus provides a bridge into the module-script world, from the classic-script world.

`url = import.meta.url`

Returns the [active module script](#8141-scripts)'s [base URL](#8141-scripts).

This syntax can only be used inside [module scripts](#8141-scripts).

`url = import.meta.resolve(specifier)`

Returns specifier, [resolved](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm) relative to the [active script](#8141-scripts). That is, this returns the URL that would be imported by using [`import(specifier)`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-import-calls).

Throws a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) exception if an invalid specifier is given.

This syntax can only be used inside [module scripts](#8141-scripts).

A module map is a [map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) keyed by [tuples](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#531-tuples) consisting of a [URL record](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) and a [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings). The [URL record](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) is the [request URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-url) at which the module was fetched, and the [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) indicates the type of the module (e.g. "`javascript-or-wasm`"). The [module map](#8167-module-related-host-hooks)'s values are either a [module script](#8141-scripts) or a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of algorithms (that are waiting for the fetch to complete). [Module maps](#8167-module-related-host-hooks) are used to ensure that imported module scripts are only fetched, parsed, and evaluated once per [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) or [worker](#10-web-workers).

> [!example]
> Since [module maps](#8167-module-related-host-hooks) are keyed by (URL, module type), the following code will create three separate entries in the [module map](#8167-module-related-host-hooks), since it results in three different (URL, module type) [tuples](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#531-tuples) (all with "`javascript-or-wasm`" type):
> 
> ```javascript
> import "https://example.com/module.mjs";
> import "https://example.com/module.mjs#map-buster";
> import "https://example.com/module.mjs?debug=true";
> ```
> 
> That is, URL [queries](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-query) and [fragments](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment) can be varied to create distinct entries in the [module map](#8167-module-related-host-hooks); they are not ignored. Thus, three separate fetches and three separate module evaluations will be performed.
> 
> In contrast, the following code would only create a single entry in the [module map](#8167-module-related-host-hooks), since after applying the [URL parser](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-parser) to these inputs, the resulting [URL records](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) are equal:
> 
> ```javascript
> import "https://example.com/module2.mjs";
> import "https:example.com/module2.mjs";
> import "https://///example.com\\module2.mjs";
> import "https://example.com/foo/../module2.mjs";
> ```
> 
> So in this second example, only one fetch and one module evaluation will occur.
> 
> Note that this behavior is the same as how [shared workers](#10264-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface) are keyed by their parsed [constructor URL](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface).

> [!example]
> Since module type is also part of the [module map](#8167-module-related-host-hooks) key, the following code will create two separate entries in the [module map](#8167-module-related-host-hooks) (the type is "`javascript-or-wasm`" for the first, and "`css`" for the second):
> 
> ```html
> <script type=module>
>   import "https://example.com/module";
> </script>
> <script type=module>
>   import "https://example.com/module" with { type: "css" };
> </script>
> ```
> 
> This can result in two separate fetches and two separate module evaluations being performed.
> 
> > [!warning]
> > In practice, due to the as-yet-unspecified memory cache (see issue [#6110](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/6110)) the resource may only be fetched once in WebKit and Blink-based browsers. Additionally, as long as all module types are mutually exclusive, the module type check in [fetch a single module script](#8142-fetching-scripts) will fail for at least one of the imports, so at most one module evaluation will occur.
> 
> The purpose of including the type in the [module map](#8167-module-related-host-hooks) key is so that an import with the wrong type attribute does not prevent a different import of the same specifier but with the correct type from succeeding.

> [!example]
> JavaScript module scripts are the default import type when importing from another JavaScript module; that is, when an `import` statement lacks a `type` import attribute the imported module script's type will be JavaScript. Attempting to import a JavaScript resource using an `import` statement with a `type` import attribute will fail:
> 
> ```html
> <script type="module">
>     // All of the following will fail, assuming that the imported .mjs files are served with a
>     // JavaScript MIME type. JavaScript module scripts are the default and cannot be imported with
>     // any import type attribute.
>     import foo from "./foo.mjs" with { type: "javascript" };
>     import foo2 from "./foo2.mjs" with { type: "js" };
>     import foo3 from "./foo3.mjs" with { type: "" };
>     await import("./foo4.mjs", { with: { type: null } });
>     await import("./foo5.mjs", { with: { type: undefined } });
> </script>
> ```

###### 8.1.6.7.1 HostGetImportMetaProperties(moduleRecord)

JavaScript contains an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) [HostGetImportMetaProperties](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-hostgetimportmetaproperties) abstract operation. User agents must use the following implementation: [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#references)
1. Let moduleScript be moduleRecord.\[\[HostDefined\]\].
2. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): moduleScript's [base URL](#8141-scripts) is not null, as moduleScript is a [JavaScript module script](#8141-scripts).
3. Let urlString be moduleScript's [base URL](#8141-scripts), [serialized](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer).
4. Let steps be the following steps, given the argument specifier:
   1. Set specifier to ? [ToString](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-tostring)(specifier).
   2. Let url be the result of [resolving a module specifier](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm) given moduleScript and specifier.
   3. Return the [serialization](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer) of url.
5. Let resolveFunction be ! [CreateBuiltinFunction](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-createbuiltinfunction)(steps, 1, "`resolve`", « »).
6. Return « [Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type) { \[\[Key\]\]: "`url`", \[\[Value\]\]: urlString }, [Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type) { \[\[Key\]\]: "`resolve`", \[\[Value\]\]: resolveFunction } ».

###### 8.1.6.7.2 HostGetSupportedImportAttributes()

JavaScript contains an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) [HostGetSupportedImportAttributes](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-hostgetsupportedimportattributes) abstract operation. User agents must use the following implementation: [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#references)
1. Return « "`type`" ».

###### 8.1.6.7.3 HostLoadImportedModule(referrer, moduleRequest, loadState, payload)

JavaScript contains an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) [HostLoadImportedModule](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-HostLoadImportedModule) abstract operation. User agents must use the following implementation: [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#references)
1. Let settingsObject be the [current settings object](#81333-current).
2. If settingsObject's [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) implements [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope) or [`ServiceWorkerGlobalScope`](https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#serviceworkerglobalscope) and loadState is undefined:

   > [!note]
   > loadState is undefined when the current fetching process has been initiated by a dynamic [`import()`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-import-calls) call, either directly or when loading the transitive dependencies of the dynamically imported module.
   1. Perform [FinishLoadingImportedModule](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-FinishLoadingImportedModule)(referrer, moduleRequest, payload, [ThrowCompletion](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-throwcompletion)(a new [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror))).
   2. Return.

3. Let referencingScript be null.
4. Let originalFetchOptions be the [default script fetch options](#8142-fetching-scripts).
5. Let fetchReferrer be "`client`".
6. If referrer is a [Script Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-script-records) or a [Cyclic Module Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-cyclic-module-records):
   1. Set referencingScript to referrer.\[\[HostDefined\]\].
   2. Set settingsObject to referencingScript's [settings object](#8141-scripts).
   3. Set fetchReferrer to referencingScript's [base URL](#8141-scripts).
   4. Set originalFetchOptions to referencingScript's [fetch options](#8141-scripts).

   > [!example]
   > referrer is usually a [Script Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-script-records) or a [Cyclic Module Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-cyclic-module-records), but it will not be so for event handlers per the [get the current value of the event handler](#8181-event-handlers) algorithm. For example, given:
   > 
   > ```html
   > <button onclick="import('./foo.mjs')">Click me</button>
   > ```
   > 
   > If a [`click`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click) event occurs, then at the time the [`import()`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-import-calls) expression runs, [GetActiveScriptOrModule](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-getactivescriptormodule) will return null, and this operation will receive the [current realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#current-realm) as a fallback referrer.

7. If referrer is a [Cyclic Module Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-cyclic-module-records) and moduleRequest is equal to the first element of referrer.\[\[RequestedModules\]\]:
   1. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) [ModuleRequest record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#modulerequest-record) requested of referrer.\[\[RequestedModules\]\]:
      1. If requested.\[\[Attributes\]\] contains a [Record](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-list-and-record-specification-type) entry such that entry.\[\[Key\]\] is not "`type`":
         1. Let error be a new [`SyntaxError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-syntaxerror) exception.
         2. If loadState is not undefined and loadState.\[\[ErrorToRethrow\]\] is null, set loadState.\[\[ErrorToRethrow\]\] to error.
         3. Perform [FinishLoadingImportedModule](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-FinishLoadingImportedModule)(referrer, moduleRequest, payload, [ThrowCompletion](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-throwcompletion)(error)).
         4. Return.

         > [!note]
         > The JavaScript specification re-performs this validation but it is duplicated here to avoid unnecessarily loading any of the dependencies on validation failure.

      2. [Resolve a module specifier](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm) given referencingScript and requested.\[\[Specifier\]\], catching any exceptions. If they throw an exception, let resolutionError be the thrown exception.
      3. If the previous step threw an exception:
         1. If loadState is not undefined and loadState.\[\[ErrorToRethrow\]\] is null, set loadState.\[\[ErrorToRethrow\]\] to resolutionError.
         2. Perform [FinishLoadingImportedModule](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-FinishLoadingImportedModule)(referrer, moduleRequest, payload, [ThrowCompletion](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-throwcompletion)(resolutionError)).
         3. Return.
      4. Let moduleType be the result of running the [module type from module request](#8143-creating-scripts) steps given requested.
      5. If the result of running the [module type allowed](#8143-creating-scripts) steps given moduleType and settingsObject is false:
         1. Let error be a new [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) exception.
         2. If loadState is not undefined and loadState.\[\[ErrorToRethrow\]\] is null, set loadState.\[\[ErrorToRethrow\]\] to error.
         3. Perform [FinishLoadingImportedModule](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-FinishLoadingImportedModule)(referrer, moduleRequest, payload, [ThrowCompletion](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-throwcompletion)(error)).
         4. Return.

      > [!note]
      > This step is essentially validating all of the requested module specifiers and type attributes when the first call to [HostLoadImportedModule](#81673-hostloadimportedmodulereferrer-modulerequest-loadstate-payload) for a static module dependency list is made, to avoid further loading operations in the case any one of the dependencies has a static error. We treat a module with unresolvable module specifiers or unsupported type attributes the same as one that cannot be parsed; in both cases, a syntactic issue makes it impossible to ever contemplate linking the module later.

8. Let url be the result of [resolving a module specifier](#8151-the-resolution-algorithm) given referencingScript and moduleRequest.\[\[Specifier\]\], catching any exceptions. If they throw an exception, let resolutionError be the thrown exception.
9. If the previous step threw an exception:
   1. If loadState is not undefined and loadState.\[\[ErrorToRethrow\]\] is null, set loadState.\[\[ErrorToRethrow\]\] to resolutionError.
   2. Perform [FinishLoadingImportedModule](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-FinishLoadingImportedModule)(referrer, moduleRequest, payload, [ThrowCompletion](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-throwcompletion)(resolutionError)).
   3. Return.
10. Let fetchOptions be the result of [getting the descendant script fetch options](#8142-fetching-scripts) given originalFetchOptions, url, and settingsObject.
11. Let destination be `"script"`.
12. Let fetchClient be settingsObject.
13. If loadState is not undefined:
    1. Set destination to loadState.\[\[Destination\]\].
    2. Set fetchClient to loadState.\[\[FetchClient\]\].
14. [Fetch a single imported module script](#8142-fetching-scripts) given url, fetchClient, destination, fetchOptions, settingsObject, fetchReferrer, moduleRequest, and onSingleFetchComplete as defined below. If loadState is not undefined and loadState.\[\[PerformFetch\]\] is not null, pass loadState.\[\[PerformFetch\]\] along as well.

    onSingleFetchComplete given moduleScript is the following algorithm:
    1. Let completion be null.
    2. If moduleScript is null, then set completion to [ThrowCompletion](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-throwcompletion)(a new [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror)).
    3. Otherwise, if moduleScript's [parse error](#8141-scripts) is not null:
       1. Let parseError be moduleScript's [parse error](#8141-scripts).
       2. Set completion to [ThrowCompletion](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-throwcompletion)(parseError).
       3. If loadState is not undefined and loadState.\[\[ErrorToRethrow\]\] is null, set loadState.\[\[ErrorToRethrow\]\] to parseError.
    4. Otherwise, set completion to [NormalCompletion](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-normalcompletion)(moduleScript's [record](#8141-scripts)).
    5. Perform [FinishLoadingImportedModule](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-FinishLoadingImportedModule)(referrer, moduleRequest, payload, completion).

#### 8.1.7 Event loops

##### 8.1.7.1 Definitions

To coordinate events, user interaction, scripts, rendering, networking, and so forth, user agents must use event loops as described in this section. Each [agent](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agents) has an associated event loop, which is unique to that agent.

The [event loop](#8171-definitions) of a [similar-origin window agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism) is known as a window event loop. The [event loop](#8171-definitions) of a [dedicated worker agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism), [shared worker agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism), or [service worker agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism) is known as a worker event loop. And the [event loop](#8171-definitions) of a [worklet agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism) is known as a worklet event loop.

> [!note]
> [Event loops](#8171-definitions) do not necessarily correspond to implementation threads. For example, multiple [window event loops](#8171-definitions) could be cooperatively scheduled in a single thread.
> 
> However, for the various worker [agents](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agents) that are allocated with \[\[CanBlock\]\] set to true, the JavaScript specification does place requirements on them regarding [forward progress](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-forward-progress), which effectively amount to requiring dedicated per-agent threads in those cases.

---

An [event loop](#8171-definitions) has one or more task queues. A [task queue](#8171-definitions) is a [set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) of [tasks](#8171-definitions).

> [!note]
> [Task queues](#8171-definitions) are [sets](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets), not [queues](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#512-queues), because the [event loop processing model](#8173-processing-model) grabs the first [*runnable*](#8171-definitions) [task](#8171-definitions) from the chosen queue, instead of [dequeuing](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#512-queues) the first task.

> [!note]
> The [microtask queue](#8171-definitions) is not a [task queue](#8171-definitions).

Tasks encapsulate algorithms that are responsible for such work as:

Events

Dispatching an [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) object at a particular [`EventTarget`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) object is often done by a dedicated task.

> [!note]
> Not all events are dispatched using the [task queue](#8171-definitions); many are dispatched during other tasks.

Parsing

The [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) tokenizing one or more bytes, and then processing any resulting tokens, is typically a task.

Callbacks

Calling a callback is often done by a dedicated task.

Using a resource

When an algorithm [fetches](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) a resource, if the fetching occurs in a non-blocking fashion then the processing of the resource once some or all of the resource is available is performed by a task.

Reacting to DOM manipulation

Some elements have tasks that trigger in response to DOM manipulation, e.g. when that element is [inserted into the document](#214-dom-trees).

Formally, a task is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) which has:

Steps

A series of steps specifying the work to be done by the task.

A source

One of the [task sources](#8171-definitions), used to group and serialize related tasks.

A document

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) associated with the task, or null for tasks that are not in a [window event loop](#8171-definitions).

A script evaluation environment settings object set

A [set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) of [environment settings objects](#8132-environment-settings-objects) used for tracking script evaluation during the task.

A [task](#8171-definitions) is runnable if its [document](#8171-definitions) is either null or [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents).

Per its [source](#8171-definitions) field, each [task](#8171-definitions) is defined as coming from a specific task source. For each [event loop](#8171-definitions), every [task source](#8171-definitions) must be associated with a specific [task queue](#8171-definitions).

> [!note]
> Essentially, [task sources](#8171-definitions) are used within standards to separate logically-different types of tasks, which a user agent might wish to distinguish between. [Task queues](#8171-definitions) are used by user agents to coalesce task sources within a given [event loop](#8171-definitions).

> [!example]
> For example, a user agent could have one [task queue](#8171-definitions) for mouse and key events (to which the [user interaction task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) is associated), and another to which all other [task sources](#8171-definitions) are associated. Then, using the freedom granted in the initial step of the [event loop processing model](#8173-processing-model), it could give keyboard and mouse events preference over other tasks three-quarters of the time, keeping the interface responsive but not starving other task queues. Note that in this setup, the processing model still enforces that the user agent would never process events from any one [task source](#8171-definitions) out of order.

---

Each [event loop](#8171-definitions) has a currently running task, which is either a [task](#8171-definitions) or null. Initially, this is null. It is used to handle reentrancy.

Each [event loop](#8171-definitions) has a microtask queue, which is a [queue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#512-queues) of [microtasks](#8171-definitions), initially empty. A microtask is a colloquial way of referring to a [task](#8171-definitions) that was created via the [queue a microtask](#8172-queuing-tasks) algorithm.

Each [event loop](#8171-definitions) has a performing a microtask checkpoint boolean, which is initially false. It is used to prevent reentrant invocation of the [perform a microtask checkpoint](#8173-processing-model) algorithm.

Each [window event loop](#8171-definitions) has a [`DOMHighResTimeStamp`](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dom-domhighrestimestamp) last render opportunity time, initially set to zero.

Each [window event loop](#8171-definitions) has a [`DOMHighResTimeStamp`](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dom-domhighrestimestamp) last idle period start time, initially set to zero.

To get the same-loop windows for a [window event loop](#8171-definitions) loop, return all [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) objects whose [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [event loop](#8171-definitions) is loop.

##### 8.1.7.2 Queuing tasks

To queue a task on a [task source](#8171-definitions) source, which performs a series of steps steps, optionally given an event loop event loop and a document document:
1. If event loop was not given, set event loop to the [implied event loop](#8172-queuing-tasks).
2. If document was not given, set document to the [implied document](#8172-queuing-tasks).
3. Let task be a new [task](#8171-definitions).
4. Set task's [steps](#8171-definitions) to steps.
5. Set task's [source](#8171-definitions) to source.
6. Set task's [document](#8171-definitions) to the document.
7. Set task's [script evaluation environment settings object set](#8171-definitions) to an empty [set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets).
8. Let queue be the [task queue](#8171-definitions) to which source is associated on event loop.
9. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) task to queue.

> [!warning]
> Failing to pass an event loop and document to [queue a task](#8172-queuing-tasks) means relying on the ambiguous and poorly-specified [implied event loop](#8172-queuing-tasks) and [implied document](#8172-queuing-tasks) concepts. Specification authors should either always pass these values, or use the wrapper algorithms [queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) or [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) instead. Using the wrapper algorithms is recommended.

To queue a global task on a [task source](#8171-definitions) source, with a [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) global and a series of steps steps:
1. Let event loop be global's [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [event loop](#8171-definitions).
2. Let document be global's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object), if global is a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object; otherwise null.
3. [Queue a task](#8172-queuing-tasks) given source, event loop, document, and steps.

To queue an element task on a [task source](#8171-definitions) source, with an element element and a series of steps steps:
1. Let global be element's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant).
2. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) given source, global, and steps.

To queue a microtask which performs a series of steps steps, optionally given a document document:
1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): there is a [surrounding agent](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#surrounding-agent). I.e., this algorithm is not called while [in parallel](#211-parallelism).
2. Let eventLoop be the [surrounding agent](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#surrounding-agent)'s [event loop](#8171-definitions).
3. If document was not given, set document to the [implied document](#8172-queuing-tasks).
4. Let microtask be a new [task](#8171-definitions).
5. Set microtask's [steps](#8171-definitions) to steps.
6. Set microtask's [source](#8171-definitions) to the microtask task source.
7. Set microtask's [document](#8171-definitions) to document.
8. Set microtask's [script evaluation environment settings object set](#8171-definitions) to an empty [set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets).
9. [Enqueue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#512-queues) microtask on eventLoop's [microtask queue](#8171-definitions).

> [!note]
> It is possible for a [microtask](#8171-definitions) to be moved to a regular [task queue](#8171-definitions), if, during its initial execution, it [spins the event loop](#8173-processing-model). This is the only case in which the [source](#8171-definitions), [document](#8171-definitions), and [script evaluation environment settings object set](#8171-definitions) of the microtask are consulted; they are ignored by the [perform a microtask checkpoint](#8173-processing-model) algorithm.

The implied event loop when queuing a task is the one that can deduced from the context of the calling algorithm. This is generally unambiguous, as most specification algorithms only ever involve a single [agent](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agents) (and thus a single [event loop](#8171-definitions)). The exception is algorithms involving or specifying cross-agent communication (e.g., between a window and a worker); for those cases, the [implied event loop](#8172-queuing-tasks) concept must not be relied upon and specifications must explicitly provide an [event loop](#8171-definitions) when [queuing a task](#8172-queuing-tasks).

The implied document when queuing a task on an [event loop](#8171-definitions) event loop is determined as follows:
1. If event loop is not a [window event loop](#8171-definitions), then return null.
2. If the task is being queued in the context of an element, then return the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
3. If the task is being queued in the context of a [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts), then return the browsing context's [active document](#732-browsing-contexts).
4. If the task is being queued by or for a [script](#8141-scripts), then return the script's [settings object](#8141-scripts)'s [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object).
5. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): this step is never reached, because one of the previous conditions is true. Really?

> [!warning]
> Both [implied event loop](#8172-queuing-tasks) and [implied document](#8172-queuing-tasks) are vaguely-defined and have a lot of action-at-a-distance. The hope is to remove these, especially [implied document](#8172-queuing-tasks). See [issue #4980](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/4980).

##### 8.1.7.3 Processing model

An [event loop](#8171-definitions) must continually run through the following steps for as long as it exists:
1. Let oldestTask and taskStartTime be null.
2. If the [event loop](#8171-definitions) has a [task queue](#8171-definitions) with at least one [runnable](#8171-definitions) [task](#8171-definitions):
   1. Let taskQueue be one such [task queue](#8171-definitions), chosen in an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) manner.

      > [!note]
      > Remember that the [microtask queue](#8171-definitions) is not a [task queue](#8171-definitions), so it will not be chosen in this step. However, a [task queue](#8171-definitions) to which the [microtask task source](#8172-queuing-tasks) is associated might be chosen in this step. In that case, the [task](#8171-definitions) chosen in the next step was originally a [microtask](#8171-definitions), but it got moved as part of [spinning the event loop](#8173-processing-model).

   2. Set taskStartTime to the [unsafe shared current time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-unsafe-shared-current-time).
   3. Set oldestTask to the first [runnable](#8171-definitions) [task](#8171-definitions) in taskQueue, and [remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) it from taskQueue.
   4. If oldestTask's [document](#8171-definitions) is not null, then [record task start time](https://w3c.github.io/long-animation-frames/#record-task-start-time) given taskStartTime and oldestTask's [document](#8171-definitions).
   5. Set the [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [currently running task](#8171-definitions) to oldestTask.
   6. Perform oldestTask's [steps](#8171-definitions).
   7. Set the [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [currently running task](#8171-definitions) back to null.
   8. [Perform a microtask checkpoint](#8173-processing-model).

3. Let taskEndTime be the [unsafe shared current time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-unsafe-shared-current-time). [\[HRT\]](#references)
4. If oldestTask is not null:
   1. Let top-level browsing contexts be an empty [set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets).
   2. For each [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settings of oldestTask's [script evaluation environment settings object set](#8171-definitions):
      1. Let global be settings's [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
      2. If global is not a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
      3. If global's [browsing context](#722-the-window-object) is null, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
      4. Let tlbc be global's [browsing context](#722-the-window-object)'s [top-level browsing context](#7322-related-browsing-contexts).
      5. If tlbc is not null, then [append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) it to top-level browsing contexts.
   3. [Report long tasks](https://w3c.github.io/longtasks/#report-long-tasks), passing in taskStartTime, taskEndTime, top-level browsing contexts, and oldestTask.
   4. If oldestTask's [document](#8171-definitions) is not null, then [record task end time](https://w3c.github.io/long-animation-frames/#record-task-end-time) given taskEndTime and oldestTask's [document](#8171-definitions).
5. If this is a [window event loop](#8171-definitions) that has no [*runnable*](#8171-definitions) [task](#8171-definitions) in this [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [task queues](#8171-definitions):
   1. Set this [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [last idle period start time](#8171-definitions) to the [unsafe shared current time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-unsafe-shared-current-time).
   2. Let computeDeadline be the following steps:
      1. Let deadline be this [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [last idle period start time](#8171-definitions) plus 50.

         > [!note]
         > The cap of 50ms in the future is to ensure responsiveness to new user input within the threshold of human perception.

      2. Let hasPendingRenders be false.
      3. For each windowInSameLoop of the [same-loop windows](#8171-definitions) for this [event loop](#8171-definitions):
         1. If windowInSameLoop's [map of animation frame callbacks](#812-animation-frames) is not [empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), or if the user agent believes that the windowInSameLoop might have pending rendering updates, set hasPendingRenders to true.
         2. Let timerCallbackEstimates be the result of [getting the values](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) of windowInSameLoop's [map of active timers](#87-timers).
         3. For each timeoutDeadline of timerCallbackEstimates, if timeoutDeadline is less than deadline, set deadline to timeoutDeadline.
      4. If hasPendingRenders is true:
         1. Let nextRenderDeadline be this [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [last render opportunity time](#8171-definitions) plus (1000 divided by the current refresh rate).

            The refresh rate can be hardware- or implementation-specific. For a refresh rate of 60Hz, the nextRenderDeadline would be about 16.67ms after the [last render opportunity time](#8171-definitions).

         2. If nextRenderDeadline is less than deadline, then return nextRenderDeadline.

      5. Return deadline.

   3. For each win of the [same-loop windows](#8171-definitions) for this [event loop](#8171-definitions), perform the [start an idle period algorithm](https://w3c.github.io/requestidlecallback/#start-an-idle-period-algorithm) for win with the following step: return the result of calling computeDeadline, [coarsened](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-coarsen-time) given win's [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant)'s [cross-origin isolated capability](#8132-environment-settings-objects). [\[REQUESTIDLECALLBACK\]](#references)

6. If this is a [worker event loop](#8171-definitions):
   1. If this [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [agent](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agents)'s single [realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms)'s [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) is a [supported](#812-animation-frames) [`DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10212-dedicated-workers-and-the-dedicatedworkerglobalscope-interface) and the user agent believes that it would benefit from having its rendering updated at this time:
      1. Let now be the [current high resolution time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time) given the [`DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10212-dedicated-workers-and-the-dedicatedworkerglobalscope-interface). [\[HRT\]](#references)
      2. [Run the animation frame callbacks](#812-animation-frames) for that [`DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10212-dedicated-workers-and-the-dedicatedworkerglobalscope-interface), passing in now as the timestamp.
      3. Update the rendering of that dedicated worker to reflect the current state.

      > [!note]
      > Similar to the notes for [updating the rendering](#8173-processing-model) in a [window event loop](#8171-definitions), a user agent can determine the rate of rendering in the dedicated worker.

   2. If there are no [tasks](#8171-definitions) in the [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [task queues](#8171-definitions) and the [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) object's [closing](#1022-the-event-loop) flag is true, then destroy the [event loop](#8171-definitions), aborting these steps, resuming the [run a worker](#1024-processing-model) steps described in the [Web workers](#10-web-workers) section below.

A [window event loop](#8171-definitions) eventLoop must also run the following [in parallel](#211-parallelism), as long as it exists:
1. Wait until at least one [navigable](#731-navigables) whose [active document](#731-navigables)'s [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [event loop](#8171-definitions) is eventLoop might have a [rendering opportunity](#8173-processing-model).
2. Set eventLoop's [last render opportunity time](#8171-definitions) to the [unsafe shared current time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-unsafe-shared-current-time).
3. For each navigable that has a [rendering opportunity](#8173-processing-model), [queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [rendering task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given navigable's [active window](#731-navigables) to update the rendering:

   > [!note]
   > This might cause redundant calls to [update the rendering](#8173-processing-model). However, these calls would have no observable effect because there will be no rendering necessary, as per the *Unnecessary rendering* step. Implementations can introduce further optimizations such as only queuing this task when it is not already queued. However, note that the document associated with the task might become inactive before the task is processed.
   1. Let frameTimestamp be eventLoop's [last render opportunity time](#8171-definitions).
   2. Let docs be all [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents) [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) objects whose [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [event loop](#8171-definitions) is eventLoop, sorted arbitrarily except that the following conditions must be met:
      - Any [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) B whose [container document](#7313-child-navigables) is A must be listed after A in the list.
      - If there are two documents A and B that both have the same non-null [container document](#7313-child-navigables) C, then the order of A and B in the list must match the [shadow-including tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) of their respective [navigable containers](#7313-child-navigables) in C's [node tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42-node-tree).

      In the steps below that iterate over docs, each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) must be processed in the order it is found in the list.

   3. *Filter non-renderable documents*: Remove from docs any [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object doc for which any of the following are true:
      - doc is [render-blocked](#316-render-blocking-mechanism);
      - doc's [visibility state](#62-page-visibility) is "`hidden`";
      - doc's rendering is [suppressed for view transitions](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-view-transitions/#document-rendering-suppression-for-view-transitions); or
      - doc's [node navigable](#731-navigables) doesn't currently have a [rendering opportunity](#8173-processing-model).

      > [!note]
      > We have to check for rendering opportunities here, in addition to checking that in the [in parallel](#211-parallelism) steps, as some documents that share the same [event loop](#8171-definitions) might not have a [rendering opportunity](#8173-processing-model) at the same time.

   4. *Unnecessary rendering*: Remove from docs any [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object doc for which all of the following are true:
      - the user agent believes that updating the rendering of doc's [node navigable](#731-navigables) would have no visible effect; and
      - doc's [map of animation frame callbacks](#812-animation-frames) is empty.
   5. Remove from docs all [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) objects for which the user agent believes that it's preferable to skip updating the rendering for other reasons.

      > [!note]
      > The step labeled *Filter non-renderable documents* prevents the user agent from updating the rendering when it is unable to present new content to the user.
      > 
      > The step labeled *Unnecessary rendering* prevents the user agent from updating the rendering when there's no new content to draw.
      > 
      > This step enables the user agent to prevent the steps below from running for other reasons, for example, to ensure certain [tasks](#8171-definitions) are executed immediately after each other, with only [microtask checkpoints](#8173-processing-model) interleaved (and without, e.g., [animation frame callbacks](#812-animation-frames) interleaved). Concretely, a user agent might wish to coalesce timer callbacks together, with no intermediate rendering updates.

   6. For each doc of docs, [reveal](#7463-revealing-the-document) doc.
   7. For each doc of docs, [flush autofocus candidates](#667-the-autofocus-attribute) for doc if its [node navigable](#731-navigables) is a [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables).
   8. For each doc of docs, [run the resize steps](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view/#document-run-the-resize-steps) for doc. [\[CSSOMVIEW\]](#references)
   9. For each doc of docs, [run the scroll steps](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view/#document-run-the-scroll-steps) for doc. [\[CSSOMVIEW\]](#references)
   10. For each doc of docs, [evaluate media queries and report changes](https://drafts.csswg.org/cssom-view/#evaluate-media-queries-and-report-changes) for doc. [\[CSSOMVIEW\]](#references)
   11. For each doc of docs, [update animations and send events](https://drafts.csswg.org/web-animations-1/#update-animations-and-send-events) for doc, passing in [relative high resolution time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-relative-high-resolution-time) given frameTimestamp and doc's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) as the timestamp. [\[WEBANIMATIONS\]](#references)
   12. For each doc of docs, [run the fullscreen steps](https://fullscreen.spec.whatwg.org/#run-the-fullscreen-steps) for doc. [\[FULLSCREEN\]](#references)
   13. For each doc of docs, if the user agent detects that the backing storage associated with a [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) or an [`OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D`](#412531-the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context), context, has been lost, then it must run the context lost steps for each such context:
       1. Let canvas be the value of context's [`canvas`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) attribute, if context is a [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context), or the [associated `OffscreenCanvas` object](#412531-the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context) for context otherwise.
       2. Set context's [context lost](#412513-the-canvas-state) to true.
       3. [Reset the rendering context to its default state](#412513-the-canvas-state) given context.
       4. Let shouldRestore be the result of [firing an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`contextlost`](#events) at canvas, with the [`cancelable`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true.
       5. If shouldRestore is false, then abort these steps.
       6. Attempt to restore context by creating a backing storage using context's attributes and associating them with context. If this fails, then abort these steps.
       7. Set context's [context lost](#412513-the-canvas-state) to false.
       8. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`contextrestored`](#events) at canvas.
   14. For each doc of docs, [run the animation frame callbacks](#812-animation-frames) for doc, passing in the [relative high resolution time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-relative-high-resolution-time) given frameTimestamp and doc's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) as the timestamp.
   15. Let unsafeStyleAndLayoutStartTime be the [unsafe shared current time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-unsafe-shared-current-time).
   16. For each doc of docs:
       1. Let resizeObserverDepth be 0.
       2. While true:
          1. Recalculate styles and update layout for doc.
          2. Let hadInitialVisibleContentVisibilityDetermination be false.
          3. For each element element with ['auto'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-contain/#propdef-content-visibility) used value of ['content-visibility'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-contain/#content-visibility):
             1. Let checkForInitialDetermination be true if element's [proximity to the viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-contain/#proximity-to-the-viewport) is not determined and it is not [relevant to the user](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-contain/#relevant-to-the-user). Otherwise, let checkForInitialDetermination be false.
             2. Determine [proximity to the viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-contain/#proximity-to-the-viewport) for element.
             3. If checkForInitialDetermination is true and element is now [relevant to the user](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-contain/#relevant-to-the-user), then set hadInitialVisibleContentVisibilityDetermination to true.
          4. If hadInitialVisibleContentVisibilityDetermination is true, then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).

             > [!note]
             > The intent of this step is for the initial viewport proximity determination, which takes effect immediately, to be reflected in the style and layout calculation which is carried out in a previous step of this loop. Proximity determinations other than the initial one take effect at the next [rendering opportunity](#8173-processing-model). [\[CSSCONTAIN\]](#references)

          5. [Gather active resize observations at depth](https://drafts.csswg.org/resize-observer-1/#gather-active-observations-h) resizeObserverDepth for doc.
          6. If doc [has active resize observations](https://drafts.csswg.org/resize-observer-1/#has-active-observations-h):
             1. Set resizeObserverDepth to the result of [broadcasting active resize observations](https://drafts.csswg.org/resize-observer-1/#broadcast-resize-notifications-h) given doc.
             2. [Continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).
          7. Otherwise, [break](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).

       3. If doc [has skipped resize observations](https://drafts.csswg.org/resize-observer-1/#has-skipped-observations-h), then [deliver resize loop error](https://drafts.csswg.org/resize-observer-1/#deliver-resize-error) given doc.

   17. For each doc of docs, if the [focused area](#662-data-model) of doc is not a [focusable area](#662-data-model), then run the [focusing steps](#664-processing-model) for doc's [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport), and set doc's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant)'s [navigation API](#7262-the-navigation-interface)'s [focus changed during ongoing navigation](#7268-ongoing-navigation-tracking) to false.

       > [!example]
       > For example, this might happen because an element has the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute added, causing it to stop [being rendered](#151-introduction). It might also happen to an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element when the element gets [disabled](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute).

       > [!note]
       > This will [usually](#664-processing-model) fire [`blur`](#events) events, and possibly [`change`](#events) events.

       > [!note]
       > In addition to this asynchronous fixup, if the [focused area of the document](#662-data-model) is removed, there is a [synchronous fixup](#214-dom-trees). That one will *not* fire [`blur`](#events) or [`change`](#events) events.

   18. For each doc of docs, [perform pending transition operations](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-view-transitions/#perform-pending-transition-operations) for doc. [\[CSSVIEWTRANSITIONS\]](#references)
   19. For each doc of docs, [run the update intersection observations steps](https://w3c.github.io/IntersectionObserver/#run-the-update-intersection-observations-steps) for doc, passing in the [relative high resolution time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-relative-high-resolution-time) given now and doc's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) as the timestamp. [\[INTERSECTIONOBSERVER\]](#references)
   20. For each doc of docs, [record rendering time](https://w3c.github.io/long-animation-frames/#record-rendering-time) for doc given unsafeStyleAndLayoutStartTime.
   21. For each doc of docs, [mark paint timing](https://w3c.github.io/paint-timing/#mark-paint-timing) for doc.
   22. For each doc of docs, update the rendering or user interface of doc and its [node navigable](#731-navigables) to reflect the current state.
   23. For each doc of docs, [process top layer removals](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position-4/#process-top-layer-removals) given doc.

A [navigable](#731-navigables) has a rendering opportunity if the user agent is currently able to present the contents of the [navigable](#731-navigables) to the user, accounting for hardware refresh rate constraints and user agent throttling for performance reasons, but considering content presentable even if it's outside the viewport.

A [navigable](#731-navigables)'s [rendering opportunities](#8173-processing-model) are determined based on hardware constraints such as display refresh rates and other factors such as page performance or whether its [active document](#731-navigables)'s [visibility state](#62-page-visibility) is "`visible`". Rendering opportunities typically occur at regular intervals.

> [!note]
> This specification does not mandate any particular model for selecting rendering opportunities. But for example, if the browser is attempting to achieve a 60Hz refresh rate, then rendering opportunities occur at a maximum of every 60th of a second (about 16.7ms). If the browser finds that a [navigable](#731-navigables) is not able to sustain this rate, it might drop to a more sustainable 30 rendering opportunities per second for that [navigable](#731-navigables), rather than occasionally dropping frames. Similarly, if a [navigable](#731-navigables) is not visible, the user agent might decide to drop that page to a much slower 4 rendering opportunities per second, or even less.

---

When a user agent is to perform a microtask checkpoint:
1. If the [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [performing a microtask checkpoint](#8171-definitions) is true, then return.
2. Set the [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [performing a microtask checkpoint](#8171-definitions) to true.
3. While the [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [microtask queue](#8171-definitions) is not [empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists):
   1. Let oldestMicrotask be the result of [dequeuing](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#512-queues) from the [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [microtask queue](#8171-definitions).
   2. Set the [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [currently running task](#8171-definitions) to oldestMicrotask.
   3. Run oldestMicrotask.

      > [!note]
      > This might involve invoking scripted callbacks, which eventually calls the [clean up after running script](#8144-calling-scripts) steps, which call this [perform a microtask checkpoint](#8173-processing-model) algorithm again, which is why we use the [performing a microtask checkpoint](#8171-definitions) flag to avoid reentrancy.

   4. Set the [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [currently running task](#8171-definitions) back to null.

4. For each [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) settingsObject whose [responsible event loop](#8132-environment-settings-objects) is this [event loop](#8171-definitions), [notify about rejected promises](#8147-unhandled-promise-rejections) given settingsObject's [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
5. [Cleanup Indexed Database transactions](https://w3c.github.io/IndexedDB/#cleanup-indexed-database-transactions).
6. Perform [ClearKeptObjects](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-clear-kept-objects)().

   > [!note]
   > When [`WeakRef.prototype.deref()`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-weak-ref.prototype.deref) returns an object, that object is kept alive until the next invocation of [ClearKeptObjects](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-clear-kept-objects)(), after which it is again subject to garbage collection.

7. Set the [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [performing a microtask checkpoint](#8171-definitions) to false.
8. [Record timing info for microtask checkpoint](https://w3c.github.io/long-animation-frames/#record-timing-info-for-microtask-checkpoint).

---

When an algorithm running [in parallel](#211-parallelism) is to await a stable state, the user agent must [queue a microtask](#8172-queuing-tasks) that runs the following steps, and must then stop executing (execution of the algorithm resumes when the microtask is run, as described in the following steps):
1. Run the algorithm's synchronous section.
2. Resume execution of the algorithm [in parallel](#211-parallelism), if appropriate, as described in the algorithm's steps.

> [!note]
> Steps in [synchronous sections](#8173-processing-model) are marked with ⌛.

---

Algorithm steps that say to spin the event loop until a condition goal is met are equivalent to substituting in the following algorithm steps:
1. Let task be the [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [currently running task](#8171-definitions).

   > [!note]
   > task could be a [microtask](#8171-definitions).

2. Let task source be task's [source](#8171-definitions).
3. Let old stack be a copy of the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack).
4. Empty the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack).
5. [Perform a microtask checkpoint](#8173-processing-model).

   > [!note]
   > If task is a [microtask](#8171-definitions) this step will be a no-op due to [performing a microtask checkpoint](#8171-definitions) being true.

6. [In parallel](#211-parallelism):
   1. Wait until the condition goal is met.
   2. [Queue a task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on task source to:
      1. Replace the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack) with old stack.
      2. Perform any steps that appear after this [spin the event loop](#8173-processing-model) instance in the original algorithm.

         > [!note]
         > This resumes task.

7. Stop task, allowing whatever algorithm that invoked it to resume.

   > [!note]
   > This causes the [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s main set of steps or the [perform a microtask checkpoint](#8173-processing-model) algorithm to continue.

> [!note]
> Unlike other algorithms in this and other specifications, which behave similar to programming-language function calls, [spin the event loop](#8173-processing-model) is more like a macro, which saves typing and indentation at the usage site by expanding into a series of steps and operations.

> [!example]
> An algorithm whose steps are:
> 1. Do something.
> 2. [Spin the event loop](#8173-processing-model) until awesomeness happens.
> 3. Do something else.
> 
> is a shorthand which, after "macro expansion", becomes
> 1. Do something.
> 2. Let old stack be a copy of the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack).
> 3. Empty the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack).
> 4. [Perform a microtask checkpoint](#8173-processing-model).
> 5. [In parallel](#211-parallelism):
>    1. Wait until awesomeness happens.
>    2. [Queue a task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the task source in which "do something" was done to:
>       1. Replace the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack) with old stack.
>       2. Do something else.

> [!example]
> Here is a more full example of the substitution, where the event loop is spun from inside a task that is queued from work in parallel. The version using [spin the event loop](#8173-processing-model):
> 1. [In parallel](#211-parallelism):
>    1. Do parallel thing 1.
>    2. [Queue a task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) to:
>       1. Do task thing 1.
>       2. [Spin the event loop](#8173-processing-model) until awesomeness happens.
>       3. Do task thing 2.
>    3. Do parallel thing 2.
> 
> The fully expanded version:
> 1. [In parallel](#211-parallelism):
>    1. Do parallel thing 1.
>    2. Let old stack be null.
>    3. [Queue a task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) to:
>       1. Do task thing 1.
>       2. Set old stack to a copy of the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack).
>       3. Empty the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack).
>       4. [Perform a microtask checkpoint](#8173-processing-model).
>    4. Wait until awesomeness happens.
>    5. [Queue a task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) to:
>       1. Replace the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack) with old stack.
>       2. Do task thing 2.
>    6. Do parallel thing 2.

---

Some of the algorithms in this specification, for historical reasons, require the user agent to pause while running a [task](#8171-definitions) until a condition goal is met. This means running the following steps:
1. Let global be the [current global object](#81333-current).
2. Let timeBeforePause be the [current high resolution time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time) given global.
3. If necessary, update the rendering or user interface of any [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) or [navigable](#731-navigables) to reflect the current state.
4. Wait until the condition goal is met. While a user agent has a paused [task](#8171-definitions), the corresponding [event loop](#8171-definitions) must not run further [tasks](#8171-definitions), and any script in the currently running [task](#8171-definitions) must block. User agents should remain responsive to user input while paused, however, albeit in a reduced capacity since the [event loop](#8171-definitions) will not be doing anything.
5. [Record pause duration](https://w3c.github.io/long-animation-frames/#record-pause-duration) given the [duration from](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-duration-from) timeBeforePause to the [current high resolution time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time) given global.

> [!warning]
> [Pausing](#8173-processing-model) is highly detrimental to the user experience, especially in scenarios where a single [event loop](#8171-definitions) is shared among multiple documents. User agents are encouraged to experiment with alternatives to [pausing](#8173-processing-model), such as [spinning the event loop](#8173-processing-model) or even simply proceeding without any kind of suspended execution at all, insofar as it is possible to do so while preserving compatibility with existing content. This specification will happily change if a less-drastic alternative is discovered to be web-compatible.
> 
> In the interim, implementers should be aware that the variety of alternatives that user agents might experiment with can change subtle aspects of [event loop](#8171-definitions) behavior, including [task](#8171-definitions) and [microtask](#8171-definitions) timing. Implementations should continue experimenting even if doing so causes them to violate the exact semantics implied by the [pause](#8173-processing-model) operation.

##### 8.1.7.4 Generic task sources

The following [task sources](#8171-definitions) are used by a number of mostly unrelated features in this and other specifications.

The DOM manipulation task source

This [task source](#8171-definitions) is used for features that react to DOM manipulations, such as things that happen in a non-blocking fashion when an element is [inserted into the document](#214-dom-trees).

The user interaction task source

This [task source](#8171-definitions) is used for features that react to user interaction, for example keyboard or mouse input.

Events sent in response to user input (e.g., [`click`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click) events) must be fired using [tasks](#8171-definitions) [queued](#8172-queuing-tasks) with the [user interaction task source](#8174-generic-task-sources). [\[UIEVENTS\]](#references)

The networking task source

This [task source](#8171-definitions) is used for features that trigger in response to network activity.

The navigation and traversal task source

This [task source](#8171-definitions) is used to queue tasks involved in [navigation](#7422-beginning-navigation) and [history traversal](#7461-updating-the-traversable).

The rendering task source

This [task source](#8171-definitions) is used solely to [update the rendering](#8173-processing-model).

##### 8.1.7.5 Dealing with the event loop from other specifications

Writing specifications that correctly interact with the [event loop](#8171-definitions) can be tricky. This is compounded by how this specification uses concurrency-model-independent terminology, so we say things like "[event loop](#8171-definitions)" and "[in parallel](#211-parallelism)" instead of using more familiar model-specific terms like "main thread" or "on a background thread".

By default, specification text generally runs on the [event loop](#8171-definitions). This falls out from the formal [event loop processing model](#8173-processing-model), in that you can eventually trace most algorithms back to a [task](#8171-definitions) [queued](#8172-queuing-tasks) there.

> [!example]
> The algorithm steps for any JavaScript method will be invoked by author code calling that method. And author code can only be run via queued tasks, usually originating somewhere in the [`script` processing model](#41211-processing-model).

From this starting point, the overriding guideline is that any work a specification needs to perform that would otherwise block the [event loop](#8171-definitions) must instead be performed [in parallel](#211-parallelism) with it. This includes (but is not limited to):
- performing heavy computation;
- displaying a user-facing prompt;
- performing operations which could require involving outside systems (i.e. "going out of process").

The next complication is that, in algorithm sections that are [in parallel](#211-parallelism), you must not create or manipulate objects associated to a specific [realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms), [global](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects), or [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects). (Stated in more familiar terms, you must not directly access main-thread artifacts from a background thread.) Doing so would create data races observable to JavaScript code, since after all, your algorithm steps are running *[in parallel](#211-parallelism)* to the JavaScript code.

By extension, you cannot access Web IDL's [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) value from steps running [in parallel](#211-parallelism), even if those steps were activated by an algorithm that *does* have access to the [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) value.

You can, however, manipulate specification-level data structures and values from Infra, as those are realm-agnostic. They are never directly exposed to JavaScript without a specific conversion taking place (often [via Web IDL](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-type-mapping)). [\[INFRA\]](#references) [\[WEBIDL\]](#references)

To affect the world of observable JavaScript objects, then, you must [queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) to perform any such manipulations. This ensures your steps are properly interleaved with respect to other things happening on the [event loop](#8171-definitions). Furthermore, you must choose a [task source](#8171-definitions) when [queuing a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks); this governs the relative order of your steps versus others. If you are unsure which [task source](#8171-definitions) to use, pick one of the [generic task sources](#8174-generic-task-sources) that sounds most applicable. Finally, you must indicate which [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) your queued task is associated with; this ensures that if that global object is inactive, the task does not run.

> [!note]
> The base primitive, on which [queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) builds, is the [queue a task](#8172-queuing-tasks) algorithm. In general, [queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) is better because it automatically picks the right [event loop](#8171-definitions) and, where appropriate, [document](#8171-definitions). Older specifications often use [queue a task](#8172-queuing-tasks) combined with the [implied event loop](#8172-queuing-tasks) and [implied document](#8172-queuing-tasks) concepts, but this is discouraged.

Putting this all together, we can provide a template for a typical algorithm that needs to do work asynchronously:
1. Do any synchronous setup work, while still on the [event loop](#8171-definitions). This may include converting [realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms)-specific JavaScript values into realm-agnostic specification-level values.
2. Perform a set of potentially-expensive steps [in parallel](#211-parallelism), operating entirely on realm-agnostic values, and producing a realm-agnostic result.
3. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks), on a specified [task source](#8171-definitions) and given an appropriate [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects), to convert the realm-agnostic result back into observable effects on the observable world of JavaScript objects on the [event loop](#8171-definitions).

> [!example]
> The following is an algorithm that "encrypts" a passed-in [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [scalar value strings](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) input, after parsing them as URLs:
> 1. Let urls be an empty [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).
> 2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) string of input:
>    1. Let parsed be the result of [encoding-parsing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given string, relative to the [current settings object](#81333-current).
>    2. If parsed is failure, then return [a promise rejected with](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#a-promise-rejected-with) a ["`SyntaxError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
>    3. Let serialized be the result of applying the [URL serializer](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer) to parsed.
>    4. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) serialized to urls.
> 3. Let realm be the [current realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#current-realm).
> 4. Let p be a new promise.
> 5. Run the following steps [in parallel](#211-parallelism):
>    1. Let encryptedURLs be an empty [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).
>    2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) url of urls:
>       1. Wait 100 milliseconds, so that people think we're doing heavy-duty encryption.
>       2. Let encrypted be a new [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) derived from url, whose nth [code unit](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) is equal to url's nth [code unit](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) plus 13.
>       3. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) encrypted to encryptedURLs.
>    3. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources), given realm's [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects), to perform the following steps:
>       1. Let array be the result of [converting](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-type-mapping) encryptedURLs to a JavaScript array, in realm.
>       2. Resolve p with array.
> 6. Return p.
> 
> Here are several things to notice about this algorithm:
> - It does its URL parsing up front, on the [event loop](#8171-definitions), before going to the [in parallel](#211-parallelism) steps. This is necessary, since parsing depends on the [current settings object](#81333-current), which would no longer be current after going [in parallel](#211-parallelism).
> - Alternately, it could have saved a reference to the [current settings object](#81333-current)'s [API base URL](#8132-environment-settings-objects) and used it during the [in parallel](#211-parallelism) steps; that would have been equivalent. However, we recommend instead doing as much work as possible up front, as this example does. Attempting to save the correct values can be error prone; for example, if we'd saved just the [current settings object](#81333-current), instead of its [API base URL](#8132-environment-settings-objects), there would have been a potential race.
> - It implicitly passes a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [strings](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) from the initial steps to the [in parallel](#211-parallelism) steps. This is OK, as both [lists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) and [strings](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) are [realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms)-agnostic.
> - It performs "expensive computation" (waiting for 100 milliseconds per input URL) during the [in parallel](#211-parallelism) steps, thus not blocking the main [event loop](#8171-definitions).
> - Promises, as observable JavaScript objects, are never created and manipulated during the [in parallel](#211-parallelism) steps. p is created before entering those steps, and then is manipulated during a [task](#8171-definitions) that is [queued](#8172-queuing-tasks) specifically for that purpose.
> - The creation of a JavaScript array object also happens during the queued task, and is careful to specify which realm it creates the array in since that is no longer obvious from context.
> 
> (On these last two points, see also [whatwg/webidl issue #135](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/issues/135) and [whatwg/webidl issue #371](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/issues/371), where we are still mulling over the subtleties of the above promise-resolution pattern.)
> 
> Another thing to note is that, in the event this algorithm was called from a Web IDL-specified operation taking a `sequence`<[`USVString`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-USVString)>, there was an automatic conversion from [realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms)-specific JavaScript objects provided by the author as input, into the realm-agnostic `sequence`<[`USVString`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-USVString)> Web IDL type, which we then treat as a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [scalar value strings](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings). So depending on how your specification is structured, there may be other implicit steps happening on the main [event loop](#8171-definitions) that play a part in this whole process of getting you ready to go [in parallel](#211-parallelism).

#### 8.1.8 Events

##### 8.1.8.1 Event handlers

Many objects can have event handlers specified. These act as non-capture [event listeners](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) for the object on which they are specified. [\[DOM\]](#references)

An [event handler](#8181-event-handlers) is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) with two [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):
- a value, which is either null, a callback object, or an [internal raw uncompiled handler](#8181-event-handlers). The [`EventHandler`](#8181-event-handlers) callback function type describes how this is exposed to scripts. Initially, an [event handler](#8181-event-handlers)'s [value](#8181-event-handlers) must be set to null.
- a listener, which is either null or an [event listener](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) responsible for running [the event handler processing algorithm](#8181-event-handlers). Initially, an [event handler](#8181-event-handlers)'s [listener](#8181-event-handlers) must be set to null.

Event handlers are exposed in two ways.

The first way, common to all event handlers, is as an [event handler IDL attribute](#8181-event-handlers).

The second way is as an [event handler content attribute](#8181-event-handlers). Event handlers on [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) and some of the event handlers on [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) objects are exposed in this way.

For both of these two ways, the [event handler](#8181-event-handlers) is exposed through a name, which is a string that always starts with "`on`" and is followed by the name of the event for which the handler is intended.

---

Most of the time, the object that exposes an [event handler](#8181-event-handlers) is the same as the object on which the corresponding [event listener](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) is added. However, the [`body`](#431-the-body-element) and [`frameset`](#1632-frames) elements expose several [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers) that act upon the element's [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object, if one exists. In either case, we call the object an [event handler](#8181-event-handlers) acts upon the target of that [event handler](#8181-event-handlers).

To determine the target of an event handler, given an [`EventTarget`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) object eventTarget on which the [event handler](#8181-event-handlers) is exposed, and an [event handler name](#8181-event-handlers) name, the following steps are taken:
1. If eventTarget is not a [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element or a [`frameset`](#1632-frames) element, then return eventTarget.
2. If name is not the name of an attribute member of the [`WindowEventHandlers`](#81821-idl-definitions) interface mixin and the [`Window`-reflecting body element event handler set](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects) does not [contain](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) name, then return eventTarget.
3. If eventTarget's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) is not an [active document](#732-browsing-contexts), then return null.

   > [!note]
   > This could happen if this object is a [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element without a corresponding [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object, for example.

   > [!note]
   > This check does not necessarily prevent [`body`](#431-the-body-element) and [`frameset`](#1632-frames) elements that are not [the body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors) of their [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) from reaching the next step. In particular, a [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element created in an [active document](#732-browsing-contexts) (perhaps with [`document.createElement()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document)) but not [connected](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree) will also have its corresponding [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object as the [target](#8181-event-handlers) of several [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers) exposed through it.

4. Return eventTarget's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant).

---

Each [`EventTarget`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) object that has one or more [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers) specified has an associated event handler map, which is a [map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) of strings representing [names](#8181-event-handlers) of [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers) to [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers).

When an [`EventTarget`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) object that has one or more [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers) specified is created, its [event handler map](#8181-event-handlers) must be initialized such that it contains an [entry](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) for each [event handler](#8181-event-handlers) that has that object as [target](#8181-event-handlers), with [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) in those [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers) set to their initial values.

> [!note]
> The order of the [entries](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) of [event handler map](#8181-event-handlers) could be arbitrary. It is not observable through any algorithms that operate on the map.

> [!note]
> [Entries](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) are not created in the [event handler map](#8181-event-handlers) of an object for [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers) that are merely exposed on that object, but have some other object as their [targets](#8181-event-handlers).

---

An event handler IDL attribute is an IDL attribute for a specific [event handler](#8181-event-handlers). The name of the IDL attribute is the same as the [name](#8181-event-handlers) of the [event handler](#8181-event-handlers).

The getter of an [event handler IDL attribute](#8181-event-handlers) with name name, when called, must run these steps:
1. Let eventTarget be the result of [determining the target of an event handler](#8181-event-handlers) given this object and name.
2. If eventTarget is null, then return null.
3. Return the result of [getting the current value of the event handler](#8181-event-handlers) given eventTarget and name.

The setter of an [event handler IDL attribute](#8181-event-handlers) with name name, when called, must run these steps:
1. Let eventTarget be the result of [determining the target of an event handler](#8181-event-handlers) given this object and name.
2. If eventTarget is null, then return.
3. If the given value is null, then [deactivate an event handler](#8181-event-handlers) given eventTarget and name.
4. Otherwise:
   1. Let handlerMap be eventTarget's [event handler map](#8181-event-handlers).
   2. Let eventHandler be handlerMap\[name\].
   3. Set eventHandler's [value](#8181-event-handlers) to the given value.
   4. [Activate an event handler](#8181-event-handlers) given eventTarget and name.

> [!note]
> Certain [event handler IDL attributes](#8181-event-handlers) have additional requirements, in particular the [`onmessage`](#943-the-messageeventtarget-mixin) attribute of [`MessagePort`](#944-message-ports) objects.

---

An event handler content attribute is a content attribute for a specific [event handler](#8181-event-handlers). The name of the content attribute is the same as the [name](#8181-event-handlers) of the [event handler](#8181-event-handlers).

[Event handler content attributes](#8181-event-handlers), when specified, must contain valid JavaScript code which, when parsed, would match the *[FunctionBody](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#prod-FunctionBody)* production after [automatic semicolon insertion](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-automatic-semicolon-insertion).

The following [attribute change steps](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) are used to synchronize between [event handler content attributes](#8181-event-handlers) and [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers): [\[DOM\]](#references)
1. If namespace is not null, or localName is not the name of an [event handler content attribute](#8181-event-handlers) on element, then return.
