2. Let eventTarget be the result of [determining the target of an event handler](#8181-event-handlers) given element and localName.
3. If eventTarget is null, then return.
4. If value is null, then [deactivate an event handler](#8181-event-handlers) given eventTarget and localName.
5. Otherwise:
   1. If the [Should element's inline behavior be blocked by Content Security Policy?](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#should-block-inline) algorithm returns "`Blocked`" when executed upon element, "`script attribute`", and value, then return. [\[CSP\]](#references)
   2. Let handlerMap be eventTarget's [event handler map](#8181-event-handlers).
   3. Let eventHandler be handlerMap\[localName\].
   4. Let location be the script location that triggered the execution of these steps.
   5. Set eventHandler's [value](#8181-event-handlers) to the [internal raw uncompiled handler](#8181-event-handlers) value/location.
   6. [Activate an event handler](#8181-event-handlers) given eventTarget and localName.

> [!note]
> Per the DOM Standard, these steps are run even if oldValue and value are identical (setting an attribute to its current value), but *not* if oldValue and value are both null (removing an attribute that doesn't currently exist). [\[DOM\]](#references)

---

To deactivate an event handler given an [`EventTarget`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) object eventTarget and a string name that is the [name](#8181-event-handlers) of an [event handler](#8181-event-handlers), run these steps:
1. Let handlerMap be eventTarget's [event handler map](#8181-event-handlers).
2. Let eventHandler be handlerMap\[name\].
3. Set eventHandler's [value](#8181-event-handlers) to null.
4. Let listener be eventHandler's [listener](#8181-event-handlers).
5. If listener is not null, then [remove an event listener](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) with eventTarget and listener.
6. Set eventHandler's [listener](#8181-event-handlers) to null.

To erase all event listeners and handlers given an [`EventTarget`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) object eventTarget, run these steps:
1. If eventTarget has an associated [event handler map](#8181-event-handlers), then for each name → eventHandler of eventTarget's associated [event handler map](#8181-event-handlers), [deactivate an event handler](#8181-event-handlers) given eventTarget and name.
2. [Remove all event listeners](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) given eventTarget.

> [!note]
> This algorithm is used to define [`document.open()`](#841-opening-the-input-stream).

To activate an event handler given an [`EventTarget`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) object eventTarget and a string name that is the [name](#8181-event-handlers) of an [event handler](#8181-event-handlers), run these steps:
1. Let handlerMap be eventTarget's [event handler map](#8181-event-handlers).
2. Let eventHandler be handlerMap\[name\].
3. If eventHandler's [listener](#8181-event-handlers) is not null, then return.
4. Let callback be the result of creating a Web IDL [`EventListener`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) instance representing a reference to a function of one argument that executes the steps of [the event handler processing algorithm](#8181-event-handlers), given eventTarget, name, and its argument.

   The [`EventListener`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget)'s [callback context](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-callback-context) can be arbitrary; it does not impact the steps of [the event handler processing algorithm](#8181-event-handlers). [\[DOM\]](#references)

   > [!note]
   > The callback is emphatically *not* the [event handler](#8181-event-handlers) itself. Every event handler ends up registering the same callback, the algorithm defined below, which takes care of invoking the right code, and processing the code's return value.

5. Let listener be a new [event listener](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) whose [type](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) is the event handler event type corresponding to eventHandler and [callback](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) is callback.

   > [!note]
   > To be clear, an [event listener](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) is different from an [`EventListener`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget).

6. [Add an event listener](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) with eventTarget and listener.
7. Set eventHandler's [listener](#8181-event-handlers) to listener.

> [!note]
> The event listener registration happens only if the [event handler](#8181-event-handlers)'s [value](#8181-event-handlers) is being set to non-null, and the [event handler](#8181-event-handlers) is not already activated. Since listeners are called in the order they were registered, assuming no [deactivation](#8181-event-handlers) occurred, the order of event listeners for a particular event type will always be:
> 1. the event listeners registered with [`addEventListener()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) before the first time the [event handler](#8181-event-handlers)'s [value](#8181-event-handlers) was set to non-null
> 2. then the callback to which it is currently set, if any
> 3. and finally the event listeners registered with [`addEventListener()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) *after* the first time the [event handler](#8181-event-handlers)'s [value](#8181-event-handlers) was set to non-null.

> [!example]
> This example demonstrates the order in which event listeners are invoked. If the button in this example is clicked by the user, the page will show four alerts, with the text "ONE", "TWO", "THREE", and "FOUR" respectively.
> 
> ```html
> <button id="test">Start Demo</button>
> <script>
>  var button = document.getElementById('test');
>  button.addEventListener('click', function () { alert('ONE') }, false);
>  button.setAttribute('onclick', "alert('NOT CALLED')"); // event handler listener is registered here
>  button.addEventListener('click', function () { alert('THREE') }, false);
>  button.onclick = function () { alert('TWO'); };
>  button.addEventListener('click', function () { alert('FOUR') }, false);
> </script>
> ```
> 
> However, in the following example, the event handler is [deactivated](#8181-event-handlers) after its initial activation (and its event listener is removed), before being reactivated at a later time. The page will show five alerts with "ONE", "TWO", "THREE", "FOUR", and "FIVE" respectively, in order.
> 
> ```html
> <button id="test">Start Demo</button>
> <script>
>  var button = document.getElementById('test');
>  button.addEventListener('click', function () { alert('ONE') }, false);
>  button.setAttribute('onclick', "alert('NOT CALLED')"); // event handler is activated here
>  button.addEventListener('click', function () { alert('TWO') }, false);
>  button.onclick = null;                                 // but deactivated here
>  button.addEventListener('click', function () { alert('THREE') }, false);
>  button.onclick = function () { alert('FOUR'); };       // and re-activated here
>  button.addEventListener('click', function () { alert('FIVE') }, false);
> </script>
> ```

> [!note]
> The interfaces implemented by the event object do not influence whether an [event handler](#8181-event-handlers) is triggered or not.

The event handler processing algorithm for an [`EventTarget`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) object eventTarget, a string name representing the [name](#8181-event-handlers) of an [event handler](#8181-event-handlers), and an [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) object event is as follows:
1. If the result of [WebDriver BiDi scripting is enabled](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-scripting-is-enabled) with eventTarget's [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant) is false, then return.
2. Let callback be the result of [getting the current value of the event handler](#8181-event-handlers) given eventTarget and name.
3. If callback is null, then return.
4. If callback's [associated realm](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-associated-realm)'s [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) is a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object whose [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object) is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents), then return.
5. Let special error event handling be true if event is an [`ErrorEvent`](#8146-runtime-script-errors) object, event's [`type`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) is "[`error`](#events)", and event's [`currentTarget`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) implements the [`WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope`](#82-the-windoworworkerglobalscope-mixin) mixin. Otherwise, let special error event handling be false.
6. Process the [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) object event as follows:

   If special error event handling is true

   Let return value be the result of [invoking](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invoke-a-callback-function) callback with « event's [`message`](#8146-runtime-script-errors), event's [`filename`](#8146-runtime-script-errors), event's [`lineno`](#8146-runtime-script-errors), event's [`colno`](#8146-runtime-script-errors), event's [`error`](#8146-runtime-script-errors) », "`rethrow`", and with *[callback this value](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-callback-this-value)* set to event's [`currentTarget`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event).

   Otherwise

   Let return value be the result of [invoking](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invoke-a-callback-function) callback with « event », "`rethrow`", and with *[callback this value](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-callback-this-value)* set to event's [`currentTarget`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event).

   > [!note]
   > If an exception gets thrown by the callback, it will be rethrown, ending these steps. The exception will propagate to the [DOM event dispatch logic](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#29-dispatching-events), which will then [report](#8146-runtime-script-errors) it.

7. Process return value as follows:

   If event is a [`BeforeUnloadEvent`](#7277-the-beforeunloadevent-interface) object and event's [`type`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) is "[`beforeunload`](#events)"

   > [!note]
   > In this case, the [event handler IDL attribute](#8181-event-handlers)'s type will be [`OnBeforeUnloadEventHandler`](#8181-event-handlers), so return value will have been coerced into either null or a [`DOMString`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-DOMString).

   If return value is not null:
   1. Set event's [canceled flag](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event).
   2. If event's [`returnValue`](#7277-the-beforeunloadevent-interface) attribute's value is the empty string, then set event's [`returnValue`](#7277-the-beforeunloadevent-interface) attribute's value to return value.

   If special error event handling is true

   If return value is true, then set event's [canceled flag](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event).

   Otherwise

   If return value is false, then set event's [canceled flag](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event).

   > [!note]
   > If we've gotten to this "Otherwise" clause because event's [`type`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) is "[`beforeunload`](#events)" but event is *not* a [`BeforeUnloadEvent`](#7277-the-beforeunloadevent-interface) object, then return value will never be false, since in such cases return value will have been coerced into either null or a [`DOMString`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-DOMString).

---

The [`EventHandler`](#8181-event-handlers) callback function type represents a callback used for event handlers. It is represented in Web IDL as follows:

```webidl
[LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull]
callback EventHandlerNonNull = any (Event event);
typedef EventHandlerNonNull? EventHandler;
```

> [!note]
> In JavaScript, any [`Function`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#common-Function) object implements this interface.

> [!example]
> For example, the following document fragment:
> 
> ```html
> <body onload="alert(this)" onclick="alert(this)">
> ```
> 
> ...leads to an alert saying "`[object Window]`" when the document is loaded, and an alert saying "`[object HTMLBodyElement]`" whenever the user clicks something in the page.

> [!note]
> The return value of the function affects whether the event is canceled or not: as described above, if the return value is false, the event is canceled.
> 
> There are two exceptions in the platform, for historical reasons:
> - The [`onerror`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects) handlers on global objects, where returning *true* cancels the event.
> - The [`onbeforeunload`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects) handler, where returning any non-null and non-undefined value will cancel the event.

For historical reasons, the [`onerror`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects) handler has different arguments:

```webidl
[LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull]
callback OnErrorEventHandlerNonNull = any ((Event or DOMString) event, optional DOMString source, optional unsigned long lineno, optional unsigned long colno, optional any error);
typedef OnErrorEventHandlerNonNull? OnErrorEventHandler;
```

> [!example]
> ```javascript
> window.onerror = (message, source, lineno, colno, error) => { … };
> ```

Similarly, the [`onbeforeunload`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects) handler has a different return value:

```webidl
[LegacyTreatNonObjectAsNull]
callback OnBeforeUnloadEventHandlerNonNull = DOMString? (Event event);
typedef OnBeforeUnloadEventHandlerNonNull? OnBeforeUnloadEventHandler;
```

---

An internal raw uncompiled handler is a tuple with the following information:
- An uncompiled script body
- A location where the script body originated, in case an error needs to be reported

When the user agent is to get the current value of the event handler given an [`EventTarget`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) object eventTarget and a string name that is the [name](#8181-event-handlers) of an [event handler](#8181-event-handlers), it must run these steps:
1. Let handlerMap be eventTarget's [event handler map](#8181-event-handlers).
2. Let eventHandler be handlerMap\[name\].
3. If eventHandler's [value](#8181-event-handlers) is an [internal raw uncompiled handler](#8181-event-handlers):
   1. If eventTarget is an element, then let element be eventTarget, and document be element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node). Otherwise, eventTarget is a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object, let element be null, and document be eventTarget's [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object).
   2. If document's [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) is null, or document's [active sandboxing flag set](#715-sandboxing) has its [sandboxed scripts browsing context flag](#715-sandboxing) set, then return null.
   3. Let body be the uncompiled script body in eventHandler's [value](#8181-event-handlers).
   4. Let location be the location where the script body originated, as given by eventHandler's [value](#8181-event-handlers).
   5. If element is not null and element has a [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms), let form owner be that [form owner](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms). Otherwise, let form owner be null.
   6. Let settings object be the [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant) of document.
   7. If body is not parsable as *[FunctionBody](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#prod-FunctionBody)* or if parsing detects an [early error](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#early-error-rule), then follow these substeps:
      1. Set eventHandler's [value](#8181-event-handlers) to null.

         > [!note]
         > This does not [deactivate](#8181-event-handlers) the event handler, which additionally [removes](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) the event handler's [listener](#8181-event-handlers) (if present).

      2. Let syntaxError be a new [`SyntaxError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-syntaxerror) exception associated with settings object's [realm](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) which describes the error while parsing. It should be based on location, where the script body originated.
      3. [Report an exception](#8146-runtime-script-errors) with syntaxError for settings object's [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
      4. Return null.

   8. Push settings object's [realm execution context](#8132-environment-settings-objects) onto the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack); it is now the [running JavaScript execution context](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#running-execution-context).

      > [!note]
      > This is necessary so the subsequent invocation of [OrdinaryFunctionCreate](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ordinaryfunctioncreate) takes place in the correct [realm](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-code-realms).

   9. Let function be the result of calling [OrdinaryFunctionCreate](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-ordinaryfunctioncreate), with arguments:

      *functionPrototype*

      [%Function.prototype%](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-properties-of-the-function-prototype-object)

      *sourceText*

      If name is [`onerror`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects) and eventTarget is a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object

      The string formed by concatenating "`function `", name, "`(event, source, lineno, colno, error) {`", U+000A LF, body, U+000A LF, and "`}`".

      Otherwise

      The string formed by concatenating "`function `", name, "`(event) {`", U+000A LF, body, U+000A LF, and "`}`".

      *ParameterList*

      If name is [`onerror`](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects) and eventTarget is a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object

      Let the function have five arguments, named `event`, `source`, `lineno`, `colno`, and `error`.

      Otherwise

      Let the function have a single argument called `event`.

      *body*

      The result of parsing body above.

      *thisMode*

      non-lexical-this

      *scope*
      1. Let realm be settings object's [realm](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
      2. Let scope be realm.\[\[GlobalEnv\]\].
      3. If eventHandler is an element's [event handler](#8181-event-handlers), then set scope to [NewObjectEnvironment](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-newobjectenvironment)(document, true, scope).

         (Otherwise, eventHandler is a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object's [event handler](#8181-event-handlers).)

      4. If form owner is not null, then set scope to [NewObjectEnvironment](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-newobjectenvironment)(form owner, true, scope).
      5. If element is not null, then set scope to [NewObjectEnvironment](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-newobjectenvironment)(element, true, scope).
      6. Return scope.

   10. Remove settings object's [realm execution context](#8132-environment-settings-objects) from the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack).
   11. Set function.\[\[ScriptOrModule\]\] to null.

       > [!note]
       > This is done because the default behavior, of associating the created function with the nearest [script](#8141-scripts) on the stack, can lead to path-dependent results. For example, an event handler which is first invoked by user interaction would end up with null \[\[ScriptOrModule\]\] (since then this algorithm would be first invoked when the [active script](#8141-scripts) is null), whereas one that is first invoked by dispatching an event from script would have its \[\[ScriptOrModule\]\] set to that script.
       > 
       > Instead, we just always set \[\[ScriptOrModule\]\] to null. This is more intuitive anyway; the idea that the first script which dispatches an event is somehow responsible for the event handler code is dubious.
       > 
       > In practice, this only affects the resolution of relative URLs via [`import()`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-import-calls), which consult the [base URL](#8141-scripts) of the associated script. Nulling out \[\[ScriptOrModule\]\] means that [HostLoadImportedModule](#81673-hostloadimportedmodulereferrer-modulerequest-loadstate-payload) will fall back to the [current settings object](#81333-current)'s [API base URL](#8132-environment-settings-objects).

   12. Set eventHandler's [value](#8181-event-handlers) to the result of creating a Web IDL [`EventHandler`](#8181-event-handlers) callback function object whose object reference is function and whose [callback context](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-callback-context) is settings object.

4. Return eventHandler's [value](#8181-event-handlers).

##### 8.1.8.2 Event handlers on elements, [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) objects, and [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) objects

The following are the [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers) (and their corresponding [event handler event types](#8181-event-handlers)) that must be supported by all [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility), as both [event handler content attributes](#8181-event-handlers) and [event handler IDL attributes](#8181-event-handlers); and that must be supported by all [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) and [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) objects, as [event handler IDL attributes](#8181-event-handlers):

| [Event handler](#8181-event-handlers) | [Event handler event type](#8181-event-handlers) |
| --- | --- |
| `onabort` | `abort` |
| `onauxclick` | [`auxclick`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#auxclick) |
| `onbeforeinput` | [`beforeinput`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-beforeinput) |
| `onbeforematch` | [`beforematch`](#events) |
| `onbeforetoggle` | [`beforetoggle`](#events) |
| `oncancel` | [`cancel`](#events) |
| `oncanplay` | [`canplay`](#481116-events-summary) |
| `oncanplaythrough` | [`canplaythrough`](#481116-events-summary) |
| `onchange` | [`change`](#events) |
| `onclick` | [`click`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click) |
| `onclose` | [`close`](#events) |
| `oncommand` | [`command`](#events) |
| `oncontextlost` | [`contextlost`](#events) |
| `oncontextmenu` | [`contextmenu`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-contextmenu) |

##### 8.1.8.3 Event firing

Certain operations and methods are defined as firing events on elements. For example, the [`click()`](#65-activation-behavior-of-elements) method on the [`HTMLElement`](#322-elements-in-the-dom) interface is defined as firing a [`click`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click) event on the element. [\[POINTEREVENTS\]](#references)

Firing a synthetic pointer event named e at target, with an optional not trusted flag, means running these steps:
1. Let event be the result of [creating an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#25-constructing-events) using [`PointerEvent`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#pointerevent-interface).
2. Initialize event's [`type`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute to e.
3. Initialize event's [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) and [`cancelable`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attributes to true.
4. Set event's [composed flag](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event).
5. If the not trusted flag is set, initialize event's [`isTrusted`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute to false.
6. Initialize event's `ctrlKey`, `shiftKey`, `altKey`, and `metaKey` attributes according to the current state of the key input device, if any (false for any keys that are not available).
7. Initialize event's [`view`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#dom-uievent-view) attribute to target's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object, if any, and null otherwise.
8. event's `getModifierState()` method is to return values appropriately describing the current state of the key input device.
9. Return the result of [dispatching](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#29-dispatching-events) event at target.

Firing a `click` event at target means [firing a synthetic pointer event named `click`](#8183-event-firing) at target.

### 8.2 The [`WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope`](#82-the-windoworworkerglobalscope-mixin) mixin

The [`WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope`](#82-the-windoworworkerglobalscope-mixin) mixin is for use of APIs that are to be exposed on [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) and [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) objects.

> [!note]
> Other standards are encouraged to further extend it using `partial
>   interface mixin WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope { … };` along with an appropriate reference.

```webidl
typedef (DOMString or Function or TrustedScript) TimerHandler;

interface mixin WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope {
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute USVString origin;
  readonly attribute boolean isSecureContext;
  readonly attribute boolean crossOriginIsolated;

  undefined reportError(any e);

  // base64 utility methods
  DOMString btoa(DOMString data);
  ByteString atob(DOMString data);

  // timers
  long setTimeout(TimerHandler handler, optional long timeout = 0, any... arguments);
  undefined clearTimeout(optional long id = 0);
  long setInterval(TimerHandler handler, optional long timeout = 0, any... arguments);
  undefined clearInterval(optional long id = 0);

  // microtask queuing
  undefined queueMicrotask(VoidFunction callback);

  // ImageBitmap
  Promise<ImageBitmap> createImageBitmap(ImageBitmapSource image, optional ImageBitmapOptions options = {});
  Promise<ImageBitmap> createImageBitmap(ImageBitmapSource image, long sx, long sy, long sw, long sh, optional ImageBitmapOptions options = {});

  // structured cloning
  any structuredClone(any value, optional StructuredSerializeOptions options = {});
};
Window includes WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope;
WorkerGlobalScope includes WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope;
```

`self.isSecureContext`

Returns whether or not this global object represents a [secure context](#8135-secure-contexts). [\[SECURE-CONTEXTS\]](#references)

`self.origin`

Returns the global object's [origin](#711-origins), serialized as string.

`self.crossOriginIsolated`

Returns whether scripts running in this global are allowed to use APIs that require cross-origin isolation. This depends on the \`[`Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy`](#7131-the-headers)\` and \`[`Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy`](#7141-the-headers)\` HTTP response headers and the "[`cross-origin-isolated`](#22-policy-controlled-features)" feature.

> [!example]
> Developers are strongly encouraged to use `self.origin` over `location.origin`. The former returns the [origin](#711-origins) of the environment, the latter of the URL of the environment. Imagine the following script executing in a document on `https://stargate.example/`:
> 
> ```javascript
> var frame = document.createElement("iframe")
> frame.onload = function() {
>   var frameWin = frame.contentWindow
>   console.log(frameWin.location.origin) // "null"
>   console.log(frameWin.origin) // "https://stargate.example"
> }
> document.body.appendChild(frame)
> ```
> 
> `self.origin` is a more reliable security indicator.

The `isSecureContext` getter steps are to return true if [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant) is a [secure context](#8135-secure-contexts), or false otherwise.

The `origin` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant)'s [origin](#8132-environment-settings-objects), [serialized](#711-origins).

The `crossOriginIsolated` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant)'s [cross-origin isolated capability](#8132-environment-settings-objects).

An element implementing the [`WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope`](#82-the-windoworworkerglobalscope-mixin) mixin has the following [extract an origin](#7113-the-origin-interface) steps:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant)'s [origin](#8132-environment-settings-objects) is not [same origin-domain](#711-origins) with the [entry settings object](#81331-entry)'s [origin](#8132-environment-settings-objects), then return null.
2. Return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant)'s [origin](#8132-environment-settings-objects).

> [!note]
> Since these objects are potentially accessible cross-origin (e.g., through [`WindowProxy`](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object)), we need a security check here before granting access to the origin.

### 8.3 Base64 utility methods

The [`atob()`](#83-base64-utility-methods) and [`btoa()`](#83-base64-utility-methods) methods allow developers to transform content to and from the base64 encoding.

> [!note]
> In these APIs, for mnemonic purposes, the "b" can be considered to stand for "binary", and the "a" for "ASCII". In practice, though, for primarily historical reasons, both the input and output of these functions are Unicode strings.

`result = self.btoa(data)`

Takes the input data, in the form of a Unicode string containing only characters in the range U+0000 to U+00FF, each representing a binary byte with values 0x00 to 0xFF respectively, and converts it to its base64 representation, which it returns.

Throws an ["`InvalidCharacterError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidcharactererror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the input string contains any out-of-range characters.

`result = self.atob(data)`

Takes the input data, in the form of a Unicode string containing base64-encoded binary data, decodes it, and returns a string consisting of characters in the range U+0000 to U+00FF, each representing a binary byte with values 0x00 to 0xFF respectively, corresponding to that binary data.

Throws an ["`InvalidCharacterError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidcharactererror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the input string is not valid base64 data.

The `btoa(data)` method must throw an ["`InvalidCharacterError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidcharactererror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if data contains any character whose code point is greater than U+00FF. Otherwise, the user agent must convert data to a byte sequence whose nth byte is the eight-bit representation of the nth code point of data, and then must apply [forgiving-base64 encode](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#7-forgiving-base64) to that byte sequence and return the result.

The `atob(data)` method steps are:
1. Let decodedData be the result of running [forgiving-base64 decode](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#7-forgiving-base64) on data.
2. If decodedData is failure, then throw an ["`InvalidCharacterError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidcharactererror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
3. Return decodedData.

### 8.4 Dynamic markup insertion

> [!note]
> APIs for dynamically inserting markup into the document interact with the parser, and thus their behavior varies depending on whether they are used with [HTML documents](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) (and the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents)) or [XML documents](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) (and the [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents)).

[`Document`](#311-the-document-object) objects have a throw-on-dynamic-markup-insertion counter, which is used in conjunction with the [create an element for the token](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) algorithm to prevent [custom element constructors](#4133-core-concepts) from being able to use [`document.open()`](#841-opening-the-input-stream), [`document.close()`](#842-closing-the-input-stream), and [`document.write()`](#843-documentwrite) when they are invoked by the parser. Initially, the counter must be set to zero.

#### 8.4.1 Opening the input stream

`document = document.open()`

Causes the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) to be replaced in-place, as if it was a new [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object, but reusing the previous object, which is then returned.

The resulting [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has an HTML parser associated with it, which can be given data to parse using [`document.write()`](#843-documentwrite).

The method has no effect if the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is still being parsed.

Throws an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is an [XML document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

Throws an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the parser is currently executing a [custom element constructor](#4133-core-concepts).

`window = document.open(url, name, features)`

Works like the [`window.open()`](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows) method.

[`Document`](#311-the-document-object) objects have an active parser was aborted boolean, which is used to prevent scripts from invoking the [`document.open()`](#841-opening-the-input-stream) and [`document.write()`](#843-documentwrite) methods (directly or indirectly) after the document's [active parser](#315-reporting-document-loading-status) has been aborted. It is initially false.

The document open steps, given a document, are as follows:
1. If document is an [XML document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. If document's [throw-on-dynamic-markup-insertion counter](#84-dynamic-markup-insertion) is greater than 0, then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
3. Let entryDocument be the [entry global object](#81331-entry)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object).
4. If document's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is not [same origin](#711-origins) to entryDocument's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), then throw a ["`SecurityError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
5. If document has an [active parser](#315-reporting-document-loading-status) whose [script nesting level](#1321-overview-of-the-parsing-model) is greater than 0, then return document.

   > [!note]
   > This basically causes [`document.open()`](#841-opening-the-input-stream) to be ignored when it's called in an inline script found during parsing, while still letting it have an effect when called from a non-parser task such as a timer callback or event handler.

6. Similarly, if document's [unload counter](#759-unloading-documents) is greater than 0, then return document.

   > [!note]
   > This basically causes [`document.open()`](#841-opening-the-input-stream) to be ignored when it's called from a [`beforeunload`](#events), [`pagehide`](#events), or [`unload`](#events) event handler while the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is being unloaded.

7. If document's [active parser was aborted](#841-opening-the-input-stream) is true, then return document.

   > [!note]
   > This notably causes [`document.open()`](#841-opening-the-input-stream) to be ignored if it is called after a [navigation](#7422-beginning-navigation) has started, but only during the initial parse. See [issue #4723](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/4723) for more background.

8. If document's [node navigable](#731-navigables) is non-null and document's [node navigable](#731-navigables)'s [ongoing navigation](#7425-aborting-navigation) is a [navigation ID](#7421-supporting-concepts), then [stop loading](#7511-aborting-a-document-load) document's [node navigable](#731-navigables).
9. For each [shadow-including inclusive descendant](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) node of document, [erase all event listeners and handlers](#8181-event-handlers) given node.
10. If document is the [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object) of document's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant), then [erase all event listeners and handlers](#8181-event-handlers) given document's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant).
11. [Replace all](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) with null within document.
12. If document is [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents):
    1. Let newURL be a copy of entryDocument's [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).
    2. If entryDocument is not document, then set newURL's [fragment](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment) to null.
    3. Run the [URL and history update steps](#744-non-fragment-synchronous-navigations) with document and newURL.
13. Set document's [is initial `about:blank`](#311-the-document-object) to false.
14. If document's [iframe load in progress](#485-the-iframe-element) flag is set, then set document's [mute iframe load](#485-the-iframe-element) flag.
15. Set document to [no-quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).
16. Create an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) whose [allow declarative shadow roots](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) is document's [allow declarative shadow roots](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md), and associate it with document. This is a script-created parser (meaning that it can be closed by the [`document.open()`](#841-opening-the-input-stream) and [`document.close()`](#842-closing-the-input-stream) methods, and that the tokenizer will wait for an explicit call to [`document.close()`](#842-closing-the-input-stream) before emitting an end-of-file token). The encoding [confidence](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) is *irrelevant*.
17. Set the [insertion point](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) to point at just before the end of the [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) (which at this point will be empty).
18. [Update the current document readiness](#315-reporting-document-loading-status) of document to "`loading`".

    > [!note]
    > This causes a [`readystatechange`](#events) event to fire, but the event is actually unobservable to author code, because of the previous step which [erased all event listeners and handlers](#8181-event-handlers) that could observe it.

19. Return document.

> [!note]
> The [document open steps](#841-opening-the-input-stream) do not affect whether a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is [ready for post-load tasks](#1327-the-end) or [completely loaded](#758-finishing-the-loading-process).

The `open(unused1,
  unused2)` method must return the result of running the [document open steps](#841-opening-the-input-stream) with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).

> [!note]
> The unused1 and unused2 arguments are ignored, but kept in the IDL to allow code that calls the function with one or two arguments to continue working. They are necessary due to Web IDL [overload resolution algorithm](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-overload-resolution-algorithm) rules, which would throw a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) exception for such calls had the arguments not been there. [whatwg/webidl issue #581](https://github.com/whatwg/webidl/issues/581) investigates changing the algorithm to allow for their removal. [\[WEBIDL\]](#references)

The `open(url,
  name, features)` method must run these steps:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents), then throw an ["`InvalidAccessError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidaccesserror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Return the result of running the [window open steps](#7221-opening-and-closing-windows) with url, name, and features.

#### 8.4.2 Closing the input stream

`document.close()`

Closes the input stream that was opened by the [`document.open()`](#841-opening-the-input-stream) method.

Throws an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is an [XML document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

Throws an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the parser is currently executing a [custom element constructor](#4133-core-concepts).

The `close()` method must run the following steps:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) is an [XML document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [throw-on-dynamic-markup-insertion counter](#84-dynamic-markup-insertion) is greater than zero, then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
3. If there is no [script-created parser](#841-opening-the-input-stream) associated with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), then return.
4. Insert an [explicit "EOF" character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) at the end of the parser's [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream).
5. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [pending parsing-blocking script](#41211-processing-model) is not null, then return.
6. Run the tokenizer, processing resulting tokens as they are emitted, and stopping when the tokenizer reaches the [explicit "EOF" character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) or [spins the event loop](#8173-processing-model).

#### 8.4.3 [`document.write()`](#843-documentwrite)

`document.write(...text)`

In general, adds the given string(s) to the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s input stream.

> [!warning]
> This method has very idiosyncratic behavior. In some cases, this method can affect the state of the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) while the parser is running, resulting in a DOM that does not correspond to the source of the document (e.g. if the string written is the string "`<plaintext>`" or "`<!--`"). In other cases, the call can clear the current page first, as if [`document.open()`](#841-opening-the-input-stream) had been called. In yet more cases, the method is simply ignored, or throws an exception. User agents are [explicitly allowed to avoid executing `script` elements inserted via this method](#132644-the-in-head-insertion-mode). And to make matters even worse, the exact behavior of this method can in some cases be dependent on network latency, which can lead to failures that are very hard to debug. **For all these reasons, use of this method is strongly discouraged.**

Throws an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) when invoked on [XML documents](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

Throws an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the parser is currently executing a [custom element constructor](#4133-core-concepts).

> [!warning]
> This method performs no sanitization to remove potentially-dangerous elements and attributes like [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) or [event handler content attributes](#8181-event-handlers).

[`Document`](#311-the-document-object) objects have an ignore-destructive-writes counter, which is used in conjunction with the processing of [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements to prevent external scripts from being able to use [`document.write()`](#843-documentwrite) to blow away the document by implicitly calling [`document.open()`](#841-opening-the-input-stream). Initially, the counter must be set to zero.

The document write steps, given a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object document, a list text, a boolean lineFeed, and a string sink, are as follows:
1. Let string be the empty string.
2. Let isTrusted be false if text [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) a string; otherwise true.
3. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) value of text:
   1. If value is a [`TrustedHTML`](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trustedhtml) object, then append value's associated [data](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trustedhtml-data) to string.
   2. Otherwise, append value to string.
4. If isTrusted is false, set string to the result of invoking the [get trusted type compliant string](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#get-trusted-type-compliant-string) algorithm with [`TrustedHTML`](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trustedhtml), [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant), string, sink, and "`script`".
5. If lineFeed is true, append U+000A LINE FEED to string.
6. If document is an [XML document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
7. If document's [throw-on-dynamic-markup-insertion counter](#84-dynamic-markup-insertion) is greater than 0, then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
8. If document's [active parser was aborted](#841-opening-the-input-stream) is true, then return.
9. If the [insertion point](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) is undefined:
   1. If document's [unload counter](#759-unloading-documents) is greater than 0 or document's [ignore-destructive-writes counter](#843-documentwrite) is greater than 0, then return.
   2. Run the [document open steps](#841-opening-the-input-stream) with document.
10. Insert string into the [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) just before the [insertion point](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream).
11. If document's [pending parsing-blocking script](#41211-processing-model) is null, then have the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) process string, one code point at a time, processing resulting tokens as they are emitted, and stopping when the tokenizer reaches the insertion point or when the processing of the tokenizer is aborted by the tree construction stage (this can happen if a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) end tag token is emitted by the tokenizer).

    > [!note]
    > If the [`document.write()`](#843-documentwrite) method was called from script executing inline (i.e. executing because the parser parsed a set of [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) tags), then this is a [reentrant invocation of the parser](#1321-overview-of-the-parsing-model). If the [parser pause flag](#1321-overview-of-the-parsing-model) is set, the tokenizer will abort immediately and no HTML will be parsed, per the tokenizer's [parser pause flag check](#1325-tokenization).

The `document.write(...text)` method steps are to run the [document write steps](#843-documentwrite) with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), text, false, and "`Document write`".

#### 8.4.4 [`document.writeln()`](#844-documentwriteln)

`document.writeln(...text)`

Adds the given string(s) to the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s input stream, followed by a newline character. If necessary, calls the [`open()`](#841-opening-the-input-stream) method implicitly first.

> [!warning]
> This method has very idiosyncratic behavior. **Use of this method is strongly discouraged, for the same reasons as [`document.write()`](#843-documentwrite).**

Throws an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) when invoked on [XML documents](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

Throws an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the parser is currently executing a [custom element constructor](#4133-core-concepts).

> [!warning]
> This method performs no sanitization to remove potentially-dangerous elements and attributes like [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) or [event handler content attributes](#8181-event-handlers).

The `document.writeln(...text)` method steps are to run the [document write steps](#843-documentwrite) with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), text, true, and "`Document writeln`".

### 8.5 DOM parsing and serialization APIs

```webidl
partial interface Element {
  [CEReactions] undefined setHTML(DOMString html, optional SetHTMLOptions options = {});
  [CEReactions] undefined setHTMLUnsafe((TrustedHTML or DOMString) html, optional (SetHTMLUnsafeOptions or TrustedHTMLParserOptions) options = {});
  DOMString getHTML(optional GetHTMLOptions options = {});

  [CEReactions] attribute (TrustedHTML or [LegacyNullToEmptyString] DOMString) innerHTML;
  [CEReactions] attribute (TrustedHTML or [LegacyNullToEmptyString] DOMString) outerHTML;
  [CEReactions] undefined insertAdjacentHTML(DOMString position, (TrustedHTML or DOMString) string);
};

partial interface ShadowRoot {
  [CEReactions] undefined setHTML(DOMString html, optional SetHTMLOptions options = {});
  [CEReactions] undefined setHTMLUnsafe((TrustedHTML or DOMString) html, optional (SetHTMLUnsafeOptions or TrustedHTMLParserOptions) options = {});
  DOMString getHTML(optional GetHTMLOptions options = {});

  [CEReactions] attribute (TrustedHTML or [LegacyNullToEmptyString] DOMString) innerHTML;
};

enum SanitizerPresets { "default" };
dictionary SetHTMLOptions {
  (Sanitizer or SanitizerConfig or SanitizerPresets) sanitizer = "default";
};
dictionary SetHTMLUnsafeOptions {
  (Sanitizer or SanitizerConfig or SanitizerPresets) sanitizer;
  boolean runScripts = false;
};
dictionary ParseHTMLUnsafeOptions {
  (Sanitizer or SanitizerConfig or SanitizerPresets) sanitizer;
};

dictionary GetHTMLOptions {
  boolean serializableShadowRoots = false;
  sequence<ShadowRoot> shadowRoots = [];
};
```

#### 8.5.1 The [`DOMParser`](#851-the-domparser-interface) interface

The [`DOMParser`](#851-the-domparser-interface) interface allows authors to create new [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) objects by parsing strings, as either HTML or XML.

`parser = new DOMParser()`

Constructs a new [`DOMParser`](#851-the-domparser-interface) object.

`document = parser.parseFromString(string, type)`

Parses string using either the HTML or XML parser, according to type, and returns the resulting [`Document`](#311-the-document-object). type can be "[`text/html`](#171-texthtml)" (which will invoke the HTML parser), or any of "[`text/xml`](#mime-types)", "[`application/xml`](#mime-types)", "[`application/xhtml+xml`](#173-applicationxhtmlxml)", or "[`image/svg+xml`](#mime-types)" (which will invoke the XML parser).

For the XML parser, if string cannot be parsed, then the returned [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) will contain elements describing the resulting error.

Note that [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements are not evaluated during parsing, and the resulting document's [encoding](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) will always be [UTF-8](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8). The document's [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) will be inherited from parser's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant).

Values other than the above for type will cause a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) exception to be thrown.

> [!note]
> The design of [`DOMParser`](#851-the-domparser-interface), as a class that needs to be constructed and then have its [`parseFromString()`](#851-the-domparser-interface) method called, is an unfortunate historical artifact. If we were designing this functionality today it would be a standalone function. For parsing HTML, the modern alternative is [`Document.parseHTMLUnsafe()`](#852-html-parsing-methods).

> [!warning]
> This method performs no sanitization to remove potentially-dangerous elements and attributes like [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) or [event handler content attributes](#8181-event-handlers).

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface DOMParser {
  constructor();

  [NewObject] Document parseFromString((TrustedHTML or DOMString) string, DOMParserSupportedType type);
};

enum DOMParserSupportedType {
  "text/html",
  "text/xml",
  "application/xml",
  "application/xhtml+xml",
  "image/svg+xml"
};
```

The `new DOMParser()` constructor steps are to do nothing.

The `parseFromString(string,
  type)` method steps are:
1. Let compliantString be the result of invoking the [get trusted type compliant string](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#get-trusted-type-compliant-string) algorithm with [`TrustedHTML`](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trustedhtml), [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant), string, "`DOMParser parseFromString`", and "`script`".
2. Let relevantDocument be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object).
3. Let document be a new [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), whose [content type](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is type, [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is relevantDocument's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), and [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is relevantDocument's [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

   > [!note]
   > The document's [encoding](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) will be left as its default, of [UTF-8](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8). In particular, any XML declarations or [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) elements found while parsing compliantString will have no effect.

4. Switch on type:

   "`text/html`"
   1. [Parse HTML from a string](#851-the-domparser-interface) given document and compliantString.

   > [!note]
   > Since document does not have a [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts), [scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting).

   Otherwise
   1. Create an [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents) parser, associated with document, and with [XML scripting support disabled](#142-parsing-xml-documents).
   2. Parse compliantString using parser.
   3. If the previous step resulted in an XML well-formedness or XML namespace well-formedness error:
      1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): document has no child nodes.
      2. Let root be the result of [creating an element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) given document, "`parsererror`", and "`http://www.mozilla.org/newlayout/xml/parsererror.xml`".
      3. Optionally, add attributes or children to root to describe the nature of the parsing error.
      4. [Append](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) root to document.

5. Return document.

To parse HTML from a string, given a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) document and a [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) html:
1. Set document's [type](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) to "`html`".
2. Let parser be a new [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) whose [allow declarative shadow roots](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) is document's [allow declarative shadow roots](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md), associated with document.
3. Place html into the [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) for parser. The encoding [confidence](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) is *irrelevant*.
4. Start parser and let it run until it has consumed all the characters just inserted into the input stream.

   > [!note]
   > This might mutate the document's [mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

#### 8.5.2 HTML parsing methods

`element.setHTML(html, options)`

Parses html using the HTML parser with options options, and replaces the children of element with the result. element provides context for the HTML parser. The parsed fragment is [sanitized](#864-sanitization-algorithms) based on options's [`sanitizer`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis) member, and [unsafe content is removed](#862-the-sanitizer-interface).

`shadowRoot.setHTML(html, options)`

Parses html using the HTML parser with options options, and replaces the children of shadowRoot with the result. shadowRoot's [host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) provides context for the HTML parser. The parsed fragment is [sanitized](#864-sanitization-algorithms) based on options's [`sanitizer`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis) member, and [unsafe content is removed](#862-the-sanitizer-interface).

`element.setHTMLUnsafe(html, options)`

Parses html using the HTML parser with options options, and replaces the children of element with the result. element provides context for the HTML parser. If options is a [`SetHTMLUnsafeOptions`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis) dictionary containing a [`sanitizer`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis) member or a [`TrustedHTMLParserOptions`](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trusted-html-parser-options) object with a non-null sanitizer configuration, it is used to [sanitize](#864-sanitization-algorithms) the parsed fragment before it is inserted into element. If options's [`runScripts`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis) is true, scripts contained in html will be executed immediately after the node tree is updated (unless altered by a Trusted Types default policy). If Trusted Types are enforced and options is not a [`TrustedHTMLParserOptions`](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trusted-html-parser-options) object, throws a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) if a default policy's `createParserOptions` returns null or undefined, or if no default policy defines `createParserOptions` and either options enables [`runScripts`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis) or specifies a non-empty [`sanitizer`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis), or html is not a [`TrustedHTML`](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trustedhtml) object (unless a default policy's `createHTML` returns one). Exceptions thrown by a default policy are rethrown.

`shadowRoot.setHTMLUnsafe(html, options)`

Parses html using the HTML parser with options options, and replaces the children of shadowRoot with the result. shadowRoot's [host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) provides context for the HTML parser. If options is a [`SetHTMLUnsafeOptions`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis) dictionary containing a [`sanitizer`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis) member or a [`TrustedHTMLParserOptions`](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trusted-html-parser-options) object with a non-null sanitizer configuration, it is used to [sanitize](#864-sanitization-algorithms) the parsed fragment before it is inserted into shadowRoot. If options's [`runScripts`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis) is true, scripts contained in html will be executed immediately after the node tree is updated (unless altered by a Trusted Types default policy). If Trusted Types are enforced and options is not a [`TrustedHTMLParserOptions`](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trusted-html-parser-options) object, throws a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) if a default policy's `createParserOptions` returns null or undefined, or if no default policy defines `createParserOptions` and either options enables [`runScripts`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis) or specifies a non-empty [`sanitizer`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis), or html is not a [`TrustedHTML`](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trustedhtml) object (unless a default policy's `createHTML` returns one). Exceptions thrown by a default policy are rethrown.

`doc = Document.parseHTML(html, options)`

Parses html using the HTML parser with options options, and returns a new [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) containing the result. The resulting document is [sanitized](#864-sanitization-algorithms) based on options's [`sanitizer`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis) member, and [unsafe content is removed](#862-the-sanitizer-interface).

`doc = Document.parseHTMLUnsafe(html, options)`

Parses html using the HTML parser with options options, and returns the resulting [`Document`](#311-the-document-object).

Note that [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements are not evaluated during parsing, and the resulting document's [encoding](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) will always be [UTF-8](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8). The document's [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) will be [`about:blank`](#219-dependencies). If options is a [`ParseHTMLUnsafeOptions`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis) dictionary containing a [`sanitizer`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis) member or a [`TrustedHTMLParserOptions`](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trusted-html-parser-options) object with a non-null sanitizer configuration, it is used to [sanitize](#864-sanitization-algorithms) the resulting DOM. If Trusted Types are enforced and options is not a [`TrustedHTMLParserOptions`](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trusted-html-parser-options) object, throws a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) if a default policy's `createParserOptions` returns null or undefined, or if no default policy defines `createParserOptions` and either options specifies a non-empty [`sanitizer`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis) or html is not a [`TrustedHTML`](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trustedhtml) object (unless a default policy's `createHTML` returns one). Exceptions thrown by a default policy are rethrown.

> [!warning]
> By default, the methods with an `Unsafe` suffix perform no sanitization to remove potentially-dangerous elements and attributes like [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) or [event handler content attributes](#8181-event-handlers).

[`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element)'s `setHTML(html, options)` method steps are:
1. Let target be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [template contents](#4123-the-template-element) if [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) is a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element; otherwise [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
2. [Set and filter HTML](#854-the-innerhtml-property) given target, html, options, and [Safe](#854-the-innerhtml-property).

[`ShadowRoot`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot)'s `setHTML(html, options)` method steps are:
1. [Set and filter HTML](#854-the-innerhtml-property) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), html, options, and [Safe](#854-the-innerhtml-property).

[`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element)'s `setHTMLUnsafe(html, options)` method steps are:
1. Let (compliantHTML, compliantOptions) be the result of invoking the [get trusted type compliant input](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#get-trusted-type-compliant-input) algorithm with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant), html, options, and "`Element setHTMLUnsafe`".
2. Let target be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [template contents](#4123-the-template-element) if [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) is a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element; otherwise [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
3. [Set and filter HTML](#854-the-innerhtml-property) given target, compliantHTML, compliantOptions, and [Unsafe](#854-the-innerhtml-property).

[`ShadowRoot`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot)'s `setHTMLUnsafe(html,
  options)` method steps are:
1. Let (compliantHTML, compliantOptions) be the result of invoking the [get trusted type compliant input](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#get-trusted-type-compliant-input) algorithm with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant), html, options, and "`ShadowRoot setHTMLUnsafe`".
2. [Set and filter HTML](#854-the-innerhtml-property) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), compliantHTML, compliantOptions, and [Unsafe](#854-the-innerhtml-property).

---

The static `parseHTML(html,
  options)` method steps are:
1. Let document be a new [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), whose [content type](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is "`text/html`" and [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

   > [!note]
   > Since document does not have a [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts), [scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting).

2. Set document's [allow declarative shadow roots](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md) to true.
3. [Parse HTML from a string](#851-the-domparser-interface) given document and html.
4. Let sanitizer be the result of [getting a sanitizer instance from options](#864-sanitization-algorithms) given options and true.
5. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): sanitizer is non-null.

   > [!note]
   > The [`sanitizer`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis) member of [`SetHTMLOptions`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis) defaults to "[`default`](#8631-configuration-invariants)".

6. [Sanitize](#864-sanitization-algorithms) document with sanitizer and true.
7. Return document.

The static `parseHTMLUnsafe(html, options)` method steps are:
1. Let (compliantHTML, compliantOptions) be the result of invoking the [get trusted type compliant input](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#get-trusted-type-compliant-input) algorithm with the [current global object](#81333-current), html, options, and "`Document parseHTMLUnsafe`".
2. Let document be a new [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), whose [content type](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is "`text/html`" and [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

   > [!note]
   > Since document does not have a [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts), [scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting).

3. Set document's [allow declarative shadow roots](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md) to true.
4. [Parse HTML from a string](#851-the-domparser-interface) given document and compliantHTML.
5. Let sanitizer be the result of [getting a sanitizer instance from options](#864-sanitization-algorithms) given compliantOptions and false.
6. If sanitizer is not null, then [sanitize](#864-sanitization-algorithms) document with sanitizer and false.
7. Return document.

#### 8.5.3 HTML serialization methods

`html = element.getHTML({ serializableShadowRoots, shadowRoots })`

Returns the result of serializing element to HTML. [Shadow roots](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) within element are serialized according to the provided options:
- If [`serializableShadowRoots`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis) is true, then all shadow roots marked as [serializable](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) are serialized.
- If the [`shadowRoots`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis) array is provided, then all shadow roots specified in the array are serialized, regardless of whether or not they are marked as serializable.

If neither option is provided, then no shadow roots are serialized.

`html = shadowRoot.getHTML({ serializableShadowRoots, shadowRoots })`

Returns the result of serializing shadowRoot to HTML, using its [shadow host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) as the context element. [Shadow roots](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) within shadowRoot are serialized according to the provided options, as above.

[`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element)'s `getHTML(options)` method steps are to return the result of [HTML fragment serialization algorithm](#133-serializing-html-fragments) with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), options\["[`serializableShadowRoots`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis)"\], and options\["[`shadowRoots`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis)"\].

[`ShadowRoot`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot)'s `getHTML(options)` method steps are to return the result of [HTML fragment serialization algorithm](#133-serializing-html-fragments) with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), options\["[`serializableShadowRoots`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis)"\], and options\["[`shadowRoots`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis)"\].

#### 8.5.4 The [`innerHTML`](#854-the-innerhtml-property) property

> [!warning]
> The [`innerHTML`](#854-the-innerhtml-property) property has a number of outstanding issues in the DOM Parsing and Serialization [issue tracker](https://github.com/w3c/DOM-Parsing/issues), documenting various problems with its specification.

`element.innerHTML`

Returns a fragment of HTML or XML that represents the element's contents.

In the case of an XML document, throws an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the element cannot be serialized to XML.

`element.innerHTML = value`

Replaces the contents of the element with nodes parsed from the given string.

In the case of an XML document, throws a ["`SyntaxError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the given string is not well-formed.

> [!note]
> Setting [`innerHTML`](#854-the-innerhtml-property) on a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element will replace all the nodes in its [template contents](#4123-the-template-element) rather than its [children](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).

`shadowRoot.innerHTML`

Returns a fragment of HTML that represents the shadow roots's contents.

`shadowRoot.innerHTML = value`

Replaces the contents of the shadow root with nodes parsed from the given string.

> [!warning]
> By default, these properties' setters perform no sanitization to remove potentially-dangerous elements and attributes like [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) or [event handler content attributes](#8181-event-handlers).

The fragment serializing algorithm steps, given an [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), or [`DocumentFragment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) node and a boolean require well-formed, are:
1. Let context document be node's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
2. If context document is an [HTML document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), then return the result of [HTML fragment serialization algorithm](#133-serializing-html-fragments) with node, false, and « ».
3. Return the [XML serialization](https://w3c.github.io/DOM-Parsing/#dfn-xml-serialization) of node given require well-formed.

A fragment parser mode is one of the following:

Safe

[Unsafe](#865-sanitization-constants) elements and attributes are removed, and [allow declarative shadow roots](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) is true. The [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) is used regardless of the type of document.

Unsafe

[Unsafe](#865-sanitization-constants) elements and attributes are not removed unless a sanitizer is supplied, and [allow declarative shadow roots](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) is true. The [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) is used regardless of the type of document.

Legacy

[Unsafe](#865-sanitization-constants) elements and attributes are not removed unless a sanitizer is supplied, and [allow declarative shadow roots](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) is false. In [XML documents](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), the [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents) is used.

To set and filter HTML, given an [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) or [`DocumentFragment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) target, a string html, a [`SetHTMLOptions`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis) or [`SetHTMLUnsafeOptions`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis) dictionary, or a [`TrustedHTMLParserOptions`](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trusted-html-parser-options) object options, and a [fragment parser mode](#854-the-innerhtml-property) mode:
1. If mode is [Safe](#854-the-innerhtml-property):
   1. Let context be target if target is an [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element); otherwise target's [host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment).
   2. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): context is non-null.
   3. If all of the following are true:
      - context's [local name](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) is "[`script`](#4121-the-script-element)"; and
      - context's [namespace](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) is the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) or the [SVG namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces),

      then return.

2. Let fragment be the result of invoking the [fragment parsing algorithm steps](#854-the-innerhtml-property) given target, html, options, and mode.
3. [Replace all](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) with fragment within target.

The fragment parsing algorithm steps, given an [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) or [`DocumentFragment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) target, a string markup, a [`SetHTMLOptions`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis) or [`SetHTMLUnsafeOptions`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis) dictionary, or a [`TrustedHTMLParserOptions`](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trusted-html-parser-options) object options, and a [fragment parser mode](#854-the-innerhtml-property) mode, are:
1. If mode is [Legacy](#854-the-innerhtml-property) and target's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) is an [XML document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), then return the result of invoking the [XML fragment parsing algorithm](#144-parsing-xml-fragments) given target and markup.

   > [!note]
   > Sanitization is not supported for [XML documents](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

2. Let safe be true if mode is [Safe](#854-the-innerhtml-property); otherwise false.
3. Let sanitizer be the result of [getting a sanitizer instance from options](#864-sanitization-algorithms) given options and safe.
4. Let scriptingMode be [Inert](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags).
5. Let runScripts be options's [runScripts](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trustedhtmlparseroptions-runscripts) if options is a [`TrustedHTMLParserOptions`](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trusted-html-parser-options); otherwise options\["[`runScripts`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis)"\] [with default](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) false.
6. If runScripts is true:
   1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): mode is not [Safe](#854-the-innerhtml-property).
   2. Set scriptingMode to [Fragment](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags).
7. Let allowDeclarativeShadowRoots be false if mode is [Legacy](#854-the-innerhtml-property); otherwise true.
8. Let fragment be the result of the [HTML fragment parsing algorithm](#134-parsing-html-fragments) given target, markup, allowDeclarativeShadowRoots, and scriptingMode.

   > [!note]
   > Scripts in fragment will only execute once they are inserted into a document, and only if scriptingMode is [Fragment](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags).

9. If sanitizer is not null, then [sanitize](#864-sanitization-algorithms) fragment with sanitizer and safe.
10. Return fragment.

[`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element)'s `innerHTML` getter steps are to return the result of running [fragment serializing algorithm steps](#854-the-innerhtml-property) with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) and true.

[`ShadowRoot`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot)'s `innerHTML` getter steps are to return the result of running [fragment serializing algorithm steps](#854-the-innerhtml-property) with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) and true.

[`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element)'s [`innerHTML`](#854-the-innerhtml-property) setter steps are:
1. Let (compliantString, compliantOptions) be the result of invoking the [get trusted type compliant input](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#get-trusted-type-compliant-input) algorithm with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant), the given value, a new [`SetHTMLUnsafeOptions`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis) dictionary, "`Element innerHTML`", [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [type](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), and false.
2. Let target be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [template contents](#4123-the-template-element) if [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) is a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element; otherwise [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
3. [Set and filter HTML](#854-the-innerhtml-property) given target, compliantString, compliantOptions, and [Legacy](#854-the-innerhtml-property).

[`ShadowRoot`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot)'s [`innerHTML`](#854-the-innerhtml-property) setter steps are:
1. Let (compliantString, compliantOptions) be the result of invoking the [get trusted type compliant input](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#get-trusted-type-compliant-input) algorithm with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant), the given value, a new [`SetHTMLUnsafeOptions`](#85-dom-parsing-and-serialization-apis) dictionary, "`ShadowRoot innerHTML`", [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [type](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), and false.
2. [Set and filter HTML](#854-the-innerhtml-property) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this), compliantString, compliantOptions, and [Legacy](#854-the-innerhtml-property).

#### 8.5.5 The [`outerHTML`](#855-the-outerhtml-property) property

> [!warning]
