```webidl
[Exposed=(Window,Worker),
 Serializable]
interface ImageData {
  constructor(unsigned long sw, unsigned long sh, optional ImageDataSettings settings = {});
  constructor(ImageDataArray data, unsigned long sw, optional unsigned long sh, optional ImageDataSettings settings = {});

  readonly attribute unsigned long width;
  readonly attribute unsigned long height;
  readonly attribute ImageDataArray data;
  readonly attribute ImageDataPixelFormat pixelFormat;
  readonly attribute PredefinedColorSpace colorSpace;
};

```

An [`ImageData`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) object represents a rectanglar bitmap with width equal to the [`
  width`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute and height equal to the [`height`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute. The pixel values of this bitmap are stored in the [`
  data`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute in left-to-right order, row by row from top to bottom, starting with 0 for the top left pixel, with the order and numerical representation of the color components of each pixel determined by the [`pixelFormat`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute. The color space of the pixel values of the bitmap is determined by the [`colorSpace`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute.

`imageData = new ImageData(sw, sh [, settings])`

Returns an [`ImageData`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) object with the given dimensions and the color space indicated by settings. All the pixels in the returned object are [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black).

Throws an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if either of the width or height arguments are zero.

`imageData = new ImageData(data, sw [, sh [, settings ] ])`

Returns an [`ImageData`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) object using the data provided in the [`ImageDataArray`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) argument, interpreted using the given dimensions and the color space indicated by settings.

The byte length of the data needs to be a multiple of the number of bytes per pixel times the given width. If the height is provided as well, then the length needs to be exactly the number of bytes per pixel times the width times the height.

Throws an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the given data and dimensions can't be interpreted consistently, or if either dimension is zero.

`imageData.width`

`imageData.height`

Returns the actual dimensions of the data in the [`ImageData`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) object, in pixels.

`imageData.data`

Returns the one-dimensional array containing the data in RGBA order, as integers in the range 0 to 255.

`imageData.colorSpace`

Returns the color space of the pixels.

The `new ImageData(sw,
  sh, settings)` constructor steps are:
1. If one or both of sw and sh are zero, then throw an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. [Initialize](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) given sw, sh, and settings.
3. Initialize the image data of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) to [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black).

The `new
  ImageData(data, sw, sh, settings)` constructor steps are:
1. Let bytesPerPixel be 4 if settings\["[`pixelFormat`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface)"\] is "[rgba-unorm8](#8111-the-imagedata-interface)"; otherwise 8.
2. Let length be the [buffer source byte length](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#buffersource-byte-length) of data.
3. If length is not a nonzero integral multiple of bytesPerPixel, then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
4. Let length be length divided by bytesPerPixel.
5. If length is not an integral multiple of sw, then throw an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

   > [!note]
   > At this step, the length is guaranteed to be greater than zero (otherwise the second step above would have aborted the steps), so if sw is zero, this step will throw the exception and return.

6. Let height be length divided by sw.
7. If sh was given and its value is not equal to height, then throw an ["`IndexSizeError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#indexsizeerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
8. [Initialize](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) given sw, sh, settings, and *[source](#8111-the-imagedata-interface)* set to data.

   > [!note]
   > This step does not set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s data to a copy of data. It sets it to the actual [`ImageDataArray`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) object passed as data.

To initialize an `ImageData` object imageData, given a positive integer number of pixels per row pixelsPerRow, a positive integer number of rows rows, an [`ImageDataSettings`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) settings, an optional [`ImageDataArray`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) source, and an optional [`PredefinedColorSpace`](#41254-color-spaces-and-color-space-conversion) defaultColorSpace:
1. If source was given:
   1. If settings\["[`pixelFormat`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface)"\] equals "[rgba-unorm8](#8111-the-imagedata-interface)" and source is not a [`Uint8ClampedArray`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-Uint8ClampedArray), then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
   2. If settings\["[`pixelFormat`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface)"\] is "[rgba-float16](#8111-the-imagedata-interface)" and source is not a [`Float16Array`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-Float16Array), then throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
   3. Initialize the `data` attribute of imageData to source.
2. Otherwise (source was not given):
   1. If settings\["[`pixelFormat`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface)"\] is "[rgba-unorm8](#8111-the-imagedata-interface)", then initialize the [`data`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute of imageData to a new [`Uint8ClampedArray`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-Uint8ClampedArray) object. The [`Uint8ClampedArray`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-Uint8ClampedArray) object must use a new [`ArrayBuffer`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-ArrayBuffer) for its storage, and must have a zero byte offset and byte length equal to the length of its storage, in bytes. The storage [`ArrayBuffer`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-ArrayBuffer) must have a length of 4 × rows × pixelsPerRow bytes.
   2. Otherwise, if settings\["[`pixelFormat`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface)"\] is "[rgba-float16](#8111-the-imagedata-interface)", then initialize the [`data`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute of imageData to a new [`Float16Array`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-Float16Array) object. The [`Float16Array`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-Float16Array) object must use a new [`ArrayBuffer`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-ArrayBuffer) for its storage, and must have a zero byte offset and byte length equal to the length of its storage, in bytes. The storage [`ArrayBuffer`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-ArrayBuffer) must have a length of 8 × rows × pixelsPerRow bytes.
   3. If the storage [`ArrayBuffer`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-ArrayBuffer) could not be allocated, then rethrow the [`RangeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-rangeerror) thrown by JavaScript, and return.
3. Initialize the `width` attribute of imageData to pixelsPerRow.
4. Initialize the `height` attribute of imageData to rows.
5. Initialize the `pixelFormat` attribute of imageData to settings\["`pixelFormat`"\].
6. If settings\["[`colorSpace`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface)"\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then initialize the `colorSpace` attribute of imageData to settings\["`colorSpace`"\].
7. Otherwise, if defaultColorSpace was given, then initialize the [`colorSpace`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute of imageData to defaultColorSpace.
8. Otherwise, initialize the [`colorSpace`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute of imageData to "[srgb](#41254-color-spaces-and-color-space-conversion)".

[`ImageData`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) objects are [serializable objects](#271-serializable-objects). Their [serialization steps](#271-serializable-objects), given value and serialized, are:
1. Set serialized.\[\[Data\]\] to the [sub-serialization](#273-structuredserializeinternal--value-forstorage---memory--) of the value of value's [`data`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute.
2. Set serialized.\[\[Width\]\] to the value of value's [`width`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute.
3. Set serialized.\[\[Height\]\] to the value of value's [`height`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute.
4. Set serialized.\[\[ColorSpace\]\] to the value of value's [`colorSpace`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute.
5. Set serialized.\[\[PixelFormat\]\] to the value of value's [`pixelFormat`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute.

Their [deserialization steps](#271-serializable-objects), given serialized, value, and targetRealm, are:
1. Initialize value's [`data`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute to the [sub-deserialization](#276-structureddeserialize--serialized-targetrealm---memory--) of serialized.\[\[Data\]\].
2. Initialize value's [`width`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute to serialized.\[\[Width\]\].
3. Initialize value's [`height`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute to serialized.\[\[Height\]\].
4. Initialize value's [`colorSpace`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute to serialized.\[\[ColorSpace\]\].
5. Initialize value's [`pixelFormat`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute to serialized.\[\[PixelFormat\]\].

The [`ImageDataPixelFormat`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) enumeration is used to specify type of the [`data`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute of an [`ImageData`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) and the arrangement and numerical representation of the color components for each pixel.

The "`rgba-unorm8`" value indicates that the [`data`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute of an [`ImageData`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) must be of type [Uint8ClampedArray](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-Uint8ClampedArray). The color components of each pixel must be stored in four sequential elements in the order of red, green, blue, and then alpha. Each element represents the 8-bit unsigned normalized value for that component.

The "`rgba-float16`" value indicates that the [`data`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute of an [`ImageData`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) must be of type [Float16Array](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-Float16Array). The color components of each pixel must be stored in four sequential elements in the order of red, green, blue, and then alpha. Each element represents the value for that component.

#### 8.11.2 The [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) interface

```webidl
[Exposed=(Window,Worker), Serializable, Transferable]
interface ImageBitmap {
  readonly attribute unsigned long width;
  readonly attribute unsigned long height;
  undefined close();
};

typedef (CanvasImageSource or
         Blob or
         ImageData) ImageBitmapSource;

enum ImageOrientation { "from-image", "flipY" };
enum PremultiplyAlpha { "none", "premultiply", "default" };
enum ColorSpaceConversion { "none", "default" };
enum ResizeQuality { "pixelated", "low", "medium", "high" };

dictionary ImageBitmapOptions {
  ImageOrientation imageOrientation = "from-image";
  PremultiplyAlpha premultiplyAlpha = "default";
  ColorSpaceConversion colorSpaceConversion = "default";
  [EnforceRange] unsigned long resizeWidth;
  [EnforceRange] unsigned long resizeHeight;
  ResizeQuality resizeQuality = "low";
};
```

An [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) object represents a bitmap image that can be painted to a canvas without undue latency.

> [!note]
> The exact judgement of what is undue latency of this is left up to the implementer, but in general if making use of the bitmap requires network I/O, or even local disk I/O, then the latency is probably undue; whereas if it only requires a blocking read from a GPU or system RAM, the latency is probably acceptable.

`promise = self.createImageBitmap(image [, options ])`

`promise = self.createImageBitmap(image, sx, sy, sw, sh [, options ])`

Takes image, which can be an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element, an [SVG `image`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/embedded.html#elementdef-image) element, a [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element, a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element, a [`Blob`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-Blob) object, an [`ImageData`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) object, or another [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) object, and returns a promise that is resolved when a new [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) is created.

If no [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) object can be constructed, for example because the provided image data is not actually an image, then the promise is rejected instead.

If sx, sy, sw, and sh arguments are provided, the source image is cropped to the given pixels, with any pixels missing in the original replaced by [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black). These coordinates are in the source image's pixel coordinate space, *not* in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px).

If options is provided, the [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) object's bitmap data is modified according to options. For example, if the [`premultiplyAlpha`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) option is set to "[`premultiply`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface)", the [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface)'s non-alpha color components are [premultiplied by the alpha component](#41257-premultiplied-alpha-and-the-2d-rendering-context).

Rejects the promise with an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the source image is not in a valid state (e.g., an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element that hasn't loaded successfully, an [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) object whose [\[\[Detached\]\]](#272-transferable-objects) internal slot value is true, an [`ImageData`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) object whose [`data`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute value's \[\[ViewedArrayBuffer\]\] internal slot is detached, or a [`Blob`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-Blob) whose data cannot be interpreted as a bitmap image).

`imageBitmap.close()`

Releases imageBitmap's underlying [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface).

`imageBitmap.width`

Returns the [natural width](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-width) of the image, in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px).

`imageBitmap.height`

Returns the [natural height](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-height) of the image, in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px).

An [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) object whose [\[\[Detached\]\]](#272-transferable-objects) internal slot value is false always has associated bitmap data, with a width and a height. However, it is possible for this data to be corrupted. If an [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) object's media data can be decoded without errors, it is said to be fully decodable.

An [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) object's bitmap has an [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag, which indicates whether the bitmap is tainted by content from a different [origin](#711-origins). The flag is initially set to true and may be changed to false by the steps of [`createImageBitmap()`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface).

---

[`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) objects are [serializable objects](#271-serializable-objects) and [transferable objects](#272-transferable-objects).

Their [serialization steps](#271-serializable-objects), given value and serialized, are:
1. If value's [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag is not set, then throw a ["`DataCloneError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Set serialized.\[\[BitmapData\]\] to a copy of value's [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface).

Their [deserialization steps](#271-serializable-objects), given serialized, value, and targetRealm, are:
1. Set value's [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) to serialized.\[\[BitmapData\]\].

Their [transfer steps](#272-transferable-objects), given value and dataHolder, are:
1. If value's [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag is not set, then throw a ["`DataCloneError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#datacloneerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Set dataHolder.\[\[BitmapData\]\] to value's [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface).
3. Unset value's [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface).

Their [transfer-receiving steps](#272-transferable-objects), given dataHolder and value, are:
1. Set value's [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) to dataHolder.\[\[BitmapData\]\].

---

The [createImageBitmap](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) method uses the bitmap task source to settle its returned Promise.

The `createImageBitmap(image,
  options)` and `createImageBitmap(image,
  sx, sy, sw, sh, options)` methods, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. If either sw or sh is given and is 0, then return [a promise rejected with](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#a-promise-rejected-with) a [`RangeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-rangeerror).
2. If either options's `resizeWidth` or options's `resizeHeight` is present and is 0, then return [a promise rejected with](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#a-promise-rejected-with) an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
3. [Check the usability of the image argument](#412519-image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts). If this throws an exception or returns *bad*, then return [a promise rejected with](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#a-promise-rejected-with) an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
4. Let promise be a new promise.
5. Let imageBitmap be a new [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) object.
6. Switch on image:

   [`img`](#483-the-img-element)

   [SVG `image`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/embedded.html#elementdef-image)
   1. If image's media data has no [natural dimensions](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions) (e.g., it's a vector graphic with no specified content size) and either options's [`resizeWidth`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) or options's [`resizeHeight`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) is not present, then return [a promise rejected with](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#a-promise-rejected-with) an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
   2. If image's media data has no [natural dimensions](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions) (e.g., it's a vector graphic with no specified content size), it should be rendered to a bitmap of the size specified by the [`resizeWidth`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) and the [`resizeHeight`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) options.
   3. Set imageBitmap's [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) to a copy of image's media data, [cropped to the source rectangle with formatting](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface). If this is an animated image, imageBitmap's [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) must only be taken from the default image of the animation (the one that the format defines is to be used when animation is not supported or is disabled), or, if there is no such image, the first frame of the animation.
   4. If image [is not origin-clean](#412519-image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts), then set the [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag of imageBitmap's bitmap to false.
   5. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks), using the [bitmap task source](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface), to resolve promise with imageBitmap.

   [`video`](#488-the-video-element)
   1. If image's [`networkState`](#48114-network-states) attribute is [`NETWORK_EMPTY`](#48114-network-states), then return [a promise rejected with](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#a-promise-rejected-with) an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
   2. Set imageBitmap's [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) to a copy of the frame at the [current playback position](#48116-offsets-into-the-media-resource), at the [media resource](#4811-media-elements)'s [natural width](#488-the-video-element) and [natural height](#488-the-video-element) (i.e., after any aspect-ratio correction has been applied), [cropped to the source rectangle with formatting](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface).
   3. If image [is not origin-clean](#412519-image-sources-for-2d-rendering-contexts), then set the [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag of imageBitmap's bitmap to false.
   4. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks), using the [bitmap task source](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface), to resolve promise with imageBitmap.

   [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element)
   1. Set imageBitmap's [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) to a copy of image's [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface), [cropped to the source rectangle with formatting](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface).
   2. Set the [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag of the imageBitmap's bitmap to the same value as the [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag of image's bitmap.
   3. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks), using the [bitmap task source](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface), to resolve promise with imageBitmap.

   [`Blob`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-Blob)

   Run these steps [in parallel](#211-parallelism):
   1. Let imageData be the result of reading image's data. If an [error occurs during reading of the object](#219-dependencies), then [queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks), using the [bitmap task source](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface), to reject promise with an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) and abort these steps.
   2. Apply the [image sniffing rules](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#rules-for-sniffing-images-specifically) to determine the file format of imageData, with MIME type of image (as given by image's [`type`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-type) attribute) giving the official type.
   3. If imageData is not in a supported image file format (e.g., it's not an image at all), or if imageData is corrupted in some fatal way such that the image dimensions cannot be obtained (e.g., a vector graphic with no natural size), then [queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks), using the [bitmap task source](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface), to reject promise with an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) and abort these steps.
   4. Set imageBitmap's [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) to imageData, [cropped to the source rectangle with formatting](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface). If this is an animated image, imageBitmap's [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) must only be taken from the default image of the animation (the one that the format defines is to be used when animation is not supported or is disabled), or, if there is no such image, the first frame of the animation.
   5. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks), using the [bitmap task source](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface), to resolve promise with imageBitmap.

   [`ImageData`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface)
   1. Let buffer be image's [`data`](#8111-the-imagedata-interface) attribute value's \[\[ViewedArrayBuffer\]\] internal slot.
   2. If [IsDetachedBuffer](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-isdetachedbuffer)(buffer) is true, then return [a promise rejected with](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#a-promise-rejected-with) an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
   3. Set imageBitmap's [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) to image's image data, [cropped to the source rectangle with formatting](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface).
   4. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks), using the [bitmap task source](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface), to resolve promise with imageBitmap.

   [`ImageBitmap`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface)
   1. Set imageBitmap's [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) to a copy of image's [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface), [cropped to the source rectangle with formatting](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface).
   2. Set the [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag of imageBitmap's bitmap to the same value as the [origin-clean](#4125-the-canvas-element) flag of image's bitmap.
   3. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks), using the [bitmap task source](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface), to resolve promise with imageBitmap.

   [`VideoFrame`](https://w3c.github.io/webcodecs/#videoframe-interface)
   1. Set imageBitmap's [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) to a copy of image's visible pixel data, [cropped to the source rectangle with formatting](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface).
   2. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks), using the [bitmap task source](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface), to resolve promise with imageBitmap.

7. Return promise.

When the steps above require that the user agent crop bitmap data to the source rectangle with formatting, the user agent must run the following steps:
1. Let input be the [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) being transformed.
2. If sx, sy, sw and sh are specified, let sourceRectangle be a rectangle whose corners are the four points (sx, sy), (sx+sw, sy), (sx+sw, sy+sh), (sx, sy+sh). Otherwise, let sourceRectangle be a rectangle whose corners are the four points (0, 0), (width of input, 0), (width of input, height of input), (0, height of input).

   > [!note]
   > If either sw or sh are negative, then the top-left corner of this rectangle will be to the left or above the (sx, sy) point.

3. Let outputWidth be determined as follows:

   If the [`resizeWidth`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) member of options is specified

   the value of the [`resizeWidth`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) member of options

   If the [`resizeWidth`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) member of options is not specified, but the [`resizeHeight`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) member is specified

   the width of sourceRectangle, times the value of the [`resizeHeight`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) member of options, divided by the height of sourceRectangle, rounded up to the nearest integer

   If neither [`resizeWidth`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) nor [`resizeHeight`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) are specified

   the width of sourceRectangle

4. Let outputHeight be determined as follows:

   If the [`resizeHeight`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) member of options is specified

   the value of the [`resizeHeight`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) member of options

   If the [`resizeHeight`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) member of options is not specified, but the [`resizeWidth`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) member is specified

   the height of sourceRectangle, times the value of the [`resizeWidth`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) member of options, divided by the width of sourceRectangle, rounded up to the nearest integer

   If neither [`resizeWidth`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) nor [`resizeHeight`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) are specified

   the height of sourceRectangle

5. Place input on an infinite [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black) grid plane, positioned so that its top left corner is at the origin of the plane, with the x-coordinate increasing to the right, and the y-coordinate increasing down, and with each pixel in the input image data occupying a cell on the plane's grid.
6. Let output be the rectangle on the plane denoted by sourceRectangle.
7. Scale output to the size specified by outputWidth and outputHeight. The user agent should use the value of the `resizeQuality` option to guide the choice of scaling algorithm.
8. If the value of the `imageOrientation` member of options is "`flipY`", output must be flipped vertically, disregarding any image orientation metadata of the source (such as EXIF metadata), if any. [\[EXIF\]](#references)

   > [!note]
   > If the value is "`from-image`", no extra step is needed.

   > [!note]
   > There used to be a "`none`" enum value. It was renamed to "[`from-image`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface)". In the future, "[`none`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface)" will be added back with a different meaning.

9. If image is an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element or a [`Blob`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-Blob) object, let val be the value of the `colorSpaceConversion` member of options, and then run these substeps:
   1. If val is "`default`", the color space conversion behavior is implementation-specific, and should be chosen according to the default color space that the implementation uses for drawing images onto the canvas.
   2. If val is "`none`", output must be decoded without performing any color space conversions. This means that the image decoding algorithm must ignore color profile metadata embedded in the source data as well as the display device color profile.
10. Let val be the value of `premultiplyAlpha` member of options, and then run these substeps:
    1. If val is "`default`", the alpha premultiplication behavior is implementation-specific, and should be chosen according to implementation deems optimal for drawing images onto the canvas.
    2. If val is "`premultiply`", the output that is not premultiplied by alpha must have its color components [multiplied by alpha](#41257-premultiplied-alpha-and-the-2d-rendering-context) and that is premultiplied by alpha must be left untouched.
    3. If val is "`none`", the output that is not premultiplied by alpha must be left untouched and that is premultiplied by alpha must have its color components [divided by alpha](#41257-premultiplied-alpha-and-the-2d-rendering-context).
11. Return output.

The `close()` method steps are:
1. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [\[\[Detached\]\]](#272-transferable-objects) internal slot value to true.
2. Unset [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [bitmap data](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface).

The `width` getter steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [\[\[Detached\]\]](#272-transferable-objects) internal slot's value is true, then return 0.
2. Return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s width, in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px).

The `height` getter steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [\[\[Detached\]\]](#272-transferable-objects) internal slot's value is true, then return 0.
2. Return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s height, in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px).

The [`ResizeQuality`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface) enumeration is used to express a preference for the interpolation quality to use when scaling images.

The "`pixelated`" value indicates a preference for scaling the image to preserve the pixelation of the original as much as possible, with minor smoothing as necessary to avoid distorting the image when the target size is not a clean multiple of the original.

To implement "[`pixelated`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface)", for each axis independently, first determine the integer multiple of its natural size that puts it closest to the target size and is greater than zero. Scale it to this integer-multiple-size using nearest neighbor, then scale it the rest of the way to the target size using bilinear interpolation.

The "`low`" value indicates a preference for a low level of image interpolation quality. Low-quality image interpolation may be more computationally efficient than higher settings.

The "`medium`" value indicates a preference for a medium level of image interpolation quality.

The "`high`" value indicates a preference for a high level of image interpolation quality. High-quality image interpolation may be more computationally expensive than lower settings.

> [!note]
> Bilinear scaling is an example of a relatively fast, lower-quality image-smoothing algorithm. Bicubic or Lanczos scaling are examples of image-scaling algorithms that produce higher-quality output. This specification does not mandate that specific interpolation algorithms be used, except for "[`pixelated`](#8112-the-imagebitmap-interface)" as described above.

> [!example]
> Using this API, a sprite sheet can be precut and prepared:
> 
> ```javascript
> var sprites = {};
> function loadMySprites() {
>   var image = new Image();
>   image.src = 'mysprites.png';
>   var resolver;
>   var promise = new Promise(function (arg) { resolver = arg });
>   image.onload = function () {
>     resolver(Promise.all([
>       createImageBitmap(image,  0,  0, 40, 40).then(function (image) { sprites.person = image }),
>       createImageBitmap(image, 40,  0, 40, 40).then(function (image) { sprites.grass  = image }),
>       createImageBitmap(image, 80,  0, 40, 40).then(function (image) { sprites.tree   = image }),
>       createImageBitmap(image,  0, 40, 40, 40).then(function (image) { sprites.hut    = image }),
>       createImageBitmap(image, 40, 40, 40, 40).then(function (image) { sprites.apple  = image }),
>       createImageBitmap(image, 80, 40, 40, 40).then(function (image) { sprites.snake  = image })
>     ]));
>   };
>   return promise;
> }
> 
> function runDemo() {
>   var canvas = document.querySelector('canvas#demo');
>   var context = canvas.getContext('2d');
>   context.drawImage(sprites.tree, 30, 10);
>   context.drawImage(sprites.snake, 70, 10);
> }
> 
> loadMySprites().then(runDemo);
> ```

### 8.12 Animation frames

Some objects include the [`AnimationFrameProvider`](#812-animation-frames) interface mixin.

```webidl
callback FrameRequestCallback = undefined (DOMHighResTimeStamp time);

interface mixin AnimationFrameProvider {
  unsigned long requestAnimationFrame(FrameRequestCallback callback);
  undefined cancelAnimationFrame(unsigned long handle);
};
Window includes AnimationFrameProvider;
DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope includes AnimationFrameProvider;
```

Each [`AnimationFrameProvider`](#812-animation-frames) object also has a target object that stores the provider's internal state. It is defined as follows:

If the [`AnimationFrameProvider`](#812-animation-frames) is a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object)

The [`Window`](#722-the-window-object)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)

If the [`AnimationFrameProvider`](#812-animation-frames) is a [`DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10212-dedicated-workers-and-the-dedicatedworkerglobalscope-interface)

The [`DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10212-dedicated-workers-and-the-dedicatedworkerglobalscope-interface)

Each [target object](#812-animation-frames) has a map of animation frame callbacks, which is an [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) that must be initially empty, and an animation frame callback identifier, which is a number that must initially be zero.

An [`AnimationFrameProvider`](#812-animation-frames) provider is considered supported if any of the following are true:
- provider is a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object).
- provider's [owner set](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) [contains](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object.
- Any of the [`DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10212-dedicated-workers-and-the-dedicatedworkerglobalscope-interface) objects in provider's [owner set](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) are [supported](#812-animation-frames).

---

The `requestAnimationFrame(callback)` method steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) is not [supported](#812-animation-frames), then throw a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Let target be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [target object](#812-animation-frames).
3. Increment target's [animation frame callback identifier](#812-animation-frames) by one, and let handle be the result.
4. Let callbacks be target's [map of animation frame callbacks](#812-animation-frames).
5. [Set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) callbacks\[handle\] to callback.
6. Return handle.

The `cancelAnimationFrame(handle)` method steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) is not [supported](#812-animation-frames), then throw a ["`NotSupportedError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#notsupportederror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
2. Let callbacks be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [target object](#812-animation-frames)'s [map of animation frame callbacks](#812-animation-frames).
3. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) callbacks\[handle\].

To run the animation frame callbacks for a [target object](#812-animation-frames) target with a timestamp now:
1. Let callbacks be target's [map of animation frame callbacks](#812-animation-frames).
2. Let callbackHandles be the result of [getting the keys](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) of callbacks.
3. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) handle in callbackHandles, if handle [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) in callbacks:
   1. Let callback be callbacks\[handle\].
   2. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) callbacks\[handle\].
   3. [Invoke](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invoke-a-callback-function) callback with « now » and "`report`".

> [!example]
> Inside workers, [`requestAnimationFrame()`](#812-animation-frames) can be used together with an [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) transferred from a [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element. First, in the document, transfer control to the worker:
> 
> ```javascript
> const offscreenCanvas = document.getElementById("c").transferControlToOffscreen();
> worker.postMessage(offscreenCanvas, [offscreenCanvas]);
> ```
> 
> Then, in the worker, the following code will draw a rectangle moving from left to right:
> 
> ```javascript
> let ctx, pos = 0;
> function draw(dt) {
>   ctx.clearRect(0, 0, 100, 100);
>   ctx.fillRect(pos, 0, 10, 10);
>   pos += 10 * dt;
>   requestAnimationFrame(draw);
> }
> 
> self.onmessage = function(ev) {
>   const transferredCanvas = ev.data;
>   ctx = transferredCanvas.getContext("2d");
>   draw();
> };
> ```

## 9 Communication

> [!note]
> The [`WebSocket`](https://websockets.spec.whatwg.org/#websocket) interface used to be defined here. It is now defined in WebSockets. [\[WEBSOCKETS\]](#references)

### 9.1 The [`MessageEvent`](#91-the-messageevent-interface) interface

Messages in [server-sent events](#92-server-sent-events), [cross-document messaging](#93-cross-document-messaging), [channel messaging](#94-channel-messaging), [broadcast channels](#95-broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts), and WebSockets use the [`MessageEvent`](#91-the-messageevent-interface) interface for their [`message`](#events) events: [\[WEBSOCKETS\]](#references)

```webidl
[Exposed=(Window,Worker,AudioWorklet)]
interface MessageEvent : Event {
  constructor(DOMString type, optional MessageEventInit eventInitDict = {});

  readonly attribute any data;
  readonly attribute USVString origin;
  readonly attribute DOMString lastEventId;
  readonly attribute MessageEventSource? source;
  readonly attribute FrozenArray<MessagePort> ports;

  undefined initMessageEvent(DOMString type, optional boolean bubbles = false, optional boolean cancelable = false, optional any data = null, optional USVString origin = "", optional DOMString lastEventId = "", optional MessageEventSource? source = null, optional sequence<MessagePort> ports = []);
};

dictionary MessageEventInit : EventInit {
  any data = null;
  USVString origin = "";
  DOMString lastEventId = "";
  MessageEventSource? source = null;
  sequence<MessagePort> ports = [];
};

typedef (WindowProxy or MessagePort or ServiceWorker) MessageEventSource;
```

Each [`MessageEvent`](#91-the-messageevent-interface) has an origin (an [origin](#711-origins), a string, or null), initially null.

`event.data`

Returns the data of the message.

`event.origin`

Returns the origin of the message, for [server-sent events](#92-server-sent-events) and [cross-document messaging](#93-cross-document-messaging).

`event.lastEventId`

Returns the [last event ID string](#922-the-eventsource-interface), for [server-sent events](#92-server-sent-events).

`event.source`

Returns the [`WindowProxy`](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object) of the source window, for [cross-document messaging](#93-cross-document-messaging), and the [`MessagePort`](#944-message-ports) being attached, in the [`connect`](#events) event fired at [`SharedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface) objects.

`event.ports`

Returns the [`MessagePort`](#944-message-ports) array sent with the message, for [cross-document messaging](#93-cross-document-messaging) and [channel messaging](#94-channel-messaging).

The `data` attribute must return the value it was initialized to. It represents the message being sent.

The `origin` attribute represents, in [server-sent events](#92-server-sent-events) and [cross-document messaging](#93-cross-document-messaging), the [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) of the document that sent the message (typically the scheme, hostname, and port of the document, but not its path or [fragment](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment)).

The [`origin`](#91-the-messageevent-interface) getter steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [origin](#91-the-messageevent-interface) is an [origin](#711-origins), then return the [serialization](#711-origins) of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [origin](#91-the-messageevent-interface).
2. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [origin](#91-the-messageevent-interface) is null, then return the empty string.
3. Return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [origin](#91-the-messageevent-interface).

When the [`origin`](#91-the-messageevent-interface) attribute is "initialized" (during [`MessageEvent`](#91-the-messageevent-interface)'s [constructor](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#25-constructing-events), for example), the initialization value is placed into the object's [origin](#91-the-messageevent-interface).

Objects implementing the [`MessageEvent`](#91-the-messageevent-interface) interface's [extract an origin](#7113-the-origin-interface) steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [origin](#91-the-messageevent-interface) if it is an [origin](#711-origins); otherwise null.

The `lastEventId` attribute must return the value it was initialized to. It represents, in [server-sent events](#92-server-sent-events), the [last event ID string](#922-the-eventsource-interface) of the event source.

The `source` attribute must return the value it was initialized to. It represents, in [cross-document messaging](#93-cross-document-messaging), the [`WindowProxy`](#723-the-windowproxy-exotic-object) of the [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) of the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object from which the message came; and in the [`connect`](#events) events used by [shared workers](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface), the newly connecting [`MessagePort`](#944-message-ports).

The `ports` attribute must return the value it was initialized to. It represents, in [cross-document messaging](#93-cross-document-messaging) and [channel messaging](#94-channel-messaging), the [`MessagePort`](#944-message-ports) array being sent.

The `initMessageEvent(type, bubbles,
  cancelable, data, origin, lastEventId,
  source, ports)` method must initialize the event in a manner analogous to the similarly-named [`initEvent()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) method. [\[DOM\]](#references)

> [!note]
> Various APIs (e.g., [`WebSocket`](https://websockets.spec.whatwg.org/#websocket), [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface)) use the [`MessageEvent`](#91-the-messageevent-interface) interface for their [`message`](#events) event without using the [`MessagePort`](#944-message-ports) API.

### 9.2 Server-sent events

#### 9.2.1 Introduction

*This section is non-normative.*

To enable servers to push data to web pages over HTTP or using dedicated server-push protocols, this specification introduces the [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) interface.

Using this API consists of creating an [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object and registering an event listener.

```javascript
var source = new EventSource('updates.cgi');
source.onmessage = function (event) {
  alert(event.data);
};
```

On the server-side, the script ("`updates.cgi`" in this case) sends messages in the following form, with the [`text/event-stream`](#177-textevent-stream) MIME type:

```
data: This is the first message.

data: This is the second message, it
data: has two lines.

data: This is the third message.
```

---

Authors can separate events by using different event types. Here is a stream that has two event types, "add" and "remove":

```
event: add
data: 73857293

event: remove
data: 2153

event: add
data: 113411
```

The script to handle such a stream would look like this (where `addHandler` and `removeHandler` are functions that take one argument, the event):

```javascript
var source = new EventSource('updates.cgi');
source.addEventListener('add', addHandler, false);
source.addEventListener('remove', removeHandler, false);
```

The default event type is "message".

Event streams are always decoded as UTF-8. There is no way to specify another character encoding.

---

Event stream requests can be redirected using HTTP 301 and 307 redirects as with normal HTTP requests. Clients will reconnect if the connection is closed; a client can be told to stop reconnecting using the HTTP 204 No Content response code.

Using this API rather than emulating it using [`XMLHttpRequest`](https://xhr.spec.whatwg.org/#xmlhttprequest) or an [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) allows the user agent to make better use of network resources in cases where the user agent implementer and the network operator are able to coordinate in advance. Amongst other benefits, this can result in significant savings in battery life on portable devices. This is discussed further in the section below on [connectionless push](#928-connectionless-push-and-other-features).

#### 9.2.2 The [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) interface

```webidl
[Exposed=(Window,Worker)]
interface EventSource : EventTarget {
  constructor(USVString url, optional EventSourceInit eventSourceInitDict = {});

  readonly attribute USVString url;
  readonly attribute boolean withCredentials;

  // ready state
  const unsigned short CONNECTING = 0;
  const unsigned short OPEN = 1;
  const unsigned short CLOSED = 2;
  readonly attribute unsigned short readyState;

  // networking
  attribute EventHandler onopen;
  attribute EventHandler onmessage;
  attribute EventHandler onerror;
  undefined close();
};

dictionary EventSourceInit {
  boolean withCredentials = false;
};
```

Each [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object has the following associated with it:
- A url (a [URL record](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url)). Set during construction.
- A request. This must initially be null.
- A reconnection time, in milliseconds. This must initially be an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) value, probably in the region of a few seconds.
- A last event ID string. This must initially be the empty string.

Apart from [url](#922-the-eventsource-interface) these are not currently exposed on the [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object.

`source = new EventSource(
   url [, { withCredentials:
   true } ])`

Creates a new [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object.

url is a string giving the [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) that will provide the event stream.

Setting [`withCredentials`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) to true will set the [credentials mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode) for connection requests to url to "`include`".

`source.close()`

Aborts any instances of the [fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) algorithm started for this [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object, and sets the [`readyState`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) attribute to [`CLOSED`](#922-the-eventsource-interface).

`source.url`

Returns the [URL providing the event stream](#922-the-eventsource-interface).

`source.withCredentials`

Returns true if the [credentials mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode) for connection requests to the [URL providing the event stream](#922-the-eventsource-interface) is set to "`include`", and false otherwise.

`source.readyState`

Returns the state of this [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object's connection. It can have the values described below.

The `EventSource(url, eventSourceInitDict)` constructor, when invoked, must run these steps:
1. Let ev be a new [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object.
2. Let settings be ev's [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant).
3. Let urlRecord be the result of [encoding-parsing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given url, relative to settings.
4. If urlRecord is failure, then throw a ["`SyntaxError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
5. Set ev's [url](#922-the-eventsource-interface) to urlRecord.
6. Let corsAttributeState be [Anonymous](#254-cors-settings-attributes).
7. If the value of eventSourceInitDict's [`withCredentials`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) member is true, then set corsAttributeState to [Use Credentials](#254-cors-settings-attributes) and set ev's [`withCredentials`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) attribute to true.
8. Let request be the result of [creating a potential-CORS request](#251-terminology) given urlRecord, the empty string, and corsAttributeState.
9. Set request's [client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-client) to settings.
10. User agents may [set](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-header-list-set) (\`[`Accept`](https://httpwg.org/specs/rfc7231.html#header.accept)\`, \`[`text/event-stream`](#177-textevent-stream)\`) in request's [header list](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-header-list).
11. Set request's [cache mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-cache-mode) to "`no-store`".
12. Set request's [initiator type](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#request-initiator-type) to "`other`".
13. Set ev's [request](#922-the-eventsource-interface) to request.
14. Let processEventSourceEndOfBody given [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) res be the following step: if res is not a [network error](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-network-error), then [reestablish the connection](#923-processing-model).
15. [Fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request, with *[processResponseEndOfBody](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#fetch-processresponseendofbody)* set to processEventSourceEndOfBody and *[processResponse](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#process-response)* set to the following steps given [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) res:
    1. If res is an [aborted network error](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-aborted-network-error), then [fail the connection](#923-processing-model).
    2. Otherwise, if res is a [network error](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-network-error), then [reestablish the connection](#923-processing-model), unless the user agent knows that to be futile, in which case the user agent may [fail the connection](#923-processing-model).
    3. Otherwise, if res's [status](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-status) is not 200, or if res's \`[`Content-Type`](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource)\` is not \`[`text/event-stream`](#177-textevent-stream)\`, then [fail the connection](#923-processing-model).
    4. Otherwise, [announce the connection](#923-processing-model) and [interpret](#926-interpreting-an-event-stream) res's [body](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-body) line by line.
16. Return ev.

---

The `url` attribute's getter must return the [serialization](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer) of this [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object's [url](#922-the-eventsource-interface).

The `withCredentials` attribute must return the value to which it was last initialized. When the object is created, it must be initialized to false.

The `readyState` attribute represents the state of the connection. It can have the following values:

`CONNECTING` (numeric value 0)

The connection has not yet been established, or it was closed and the user agent is reconnecting.

`OPEN` (numeric value 1)

The user agent has an open connection and is dispatching events as it receives them.

`CLOSED` (numeric value 2)

The connection is not open, and the user agent is not trying to reconnect. Either there was a fatal error or the [`close()`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) method was invoked.

When the object is created, its [`readyState`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) must be set to [`CONNECTING`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) (0). The rules given below for handling the connection define when the value changes.

The `close()` method must abort any instances of the [fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) algorithm started for this [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object, and must set the [`readyState`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) attribute to [`CLOSED`](#922-the-eventsource-interface).

The following are the [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers) (and their corresponding [event handler event types](#8181-event-handlers)) that must be supported, as [event handler IDL attributes](#8181-event-handlers), by all objects implementing the [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) interface:

| [Event handler](#8181-event-handlers) | [Event handler event type](#8181-event-handlers) |
| --- | --- |
| `onopen` | [`open`](#events) |
| `onmessage` | [`message`](#events) |
| `onerror` | [`error`](#events) |

---

#### 9.2.3 Processing model

When a user agent is to announce the connection, the user agent must [queue a task](#8172-queuing-tasks) which, if the [`readyState`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) attribute is set to a value other than [`CLOSED`](#922-the-eventsource-interface), sets the [`readyState`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) attribute to [`OPEN`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) and [fires an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`open`](#events) at the [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object.

When a user agent is to reestablish the connection, the user agent must run the following steps. These steps are run [in parallel](#211-parallelism), not as part of a [task](#8171-definitions). (The tasks that it queues, of course, are run like normal tasks and not themselves [in parallel](#211-parallelism).)
1. [Queue a task](#8172-queuing-tasks) to run the following steps:
   1. If the [`readyState`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) attribute is set to [`CLOSED`](#922-the-eventsource-interface), abort the task.
   2. Set the [`readyState`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) attribute to [`CONNECTING`](#922-the-eventsource-interface).
   3. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) at the [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object.
2. Wait a delay equal to the reconnection time of the event source.
3. Optionally, wait some more. In particular, if the previous attempt failed, then user agents might introduce an exponential backoff delay to avoid overloading a potentially already overloaded server. Alternatively, if the operating system has reported that there is no network connectivity, user agents might wait for the operating system to announce that the network connection has returned before retrying.
4. Wait until the aforementioned task has run, if it has not yet run.
5. [Queue a task](#8172-queuing-tasks) to run the following steps:
   1. If the [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object's [`readyState`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) attribute is not set to [`CONNECTING`](#922-the-eventsource-interface), then return.
   2. Let request be the [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object's [request](#922-the-eventsource-interface).
   3. If the [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object's [last event ID string](#922-the-eventsource-interface) is not the empty string:
      1. Let lastEventIDValue be the [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object's [last event ID string](#922-the-eventsource-interface), [encoded as UTF-8](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8-encode).
      2. [Set](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-header-list-set) (\`[`Last-Event-ID`](#924-the-last-event-id-header)\`, lastEventIDValue) in request's [header list](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-header-list).
   4. [Fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request and process the response obtained in this fashion, if any, as described earlier in this section.

When a user agent is to fail the connection, the user agent must [queue a task](#8172-queuing-tasks) which, if the [`readyState`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) attribute is set to a value other than [`CLOSED`](#922-the-eventsource-interface), sets the [`readyState`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) attribute to [`CLOSED`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) and [fires an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) at the [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object. **Once the user agent has [failed the connection](#923-processing-model), it does *not* attempt to reconnect.**

---

The [task source](#8171-definitions) for any [tasks](#8171-definitions) that are [queued](#8172-queuing-tasks) by [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) objects is the remote event task source.

#### 9.2.4 The \`[`Last-Event-ID`](#924-the-last-event-id-header)\` header

The `Last-Event-ID`\` HTTP request header reports an [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object's [last event ID string](#922-the-eventsource-interface) to the server when the user agent is to [reestablish the connection](#923-processing-model).

> [!warning]
> See [whatwg/html issue #7363](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/7363) to define the value space better. It is essentially any UTF-8 encoded string, that does not contain U+0000 NULL, U+000A LF, or U+000D CR.

#### 9.2.5 Parsing an event stream

This event stream format's [MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type) is [`text/event-stream`](#177-textevent-stream).

The event stream format is as described by the `stream` production of the following ABNF, the character set for which is Unicode. [\[ABNF\]](#references)

```abnf
stream        = [ bom ] *event
event         = *( comment / field ) end-of-line
comment       = colon *any-char end-of-line
field         = 1*name-char [ colon [ space ] *any-char ] end-of-line
end-of-line   = ( cr lf / cr / lf )

; characters
lf            = %x000A ; U+000A LINE FEED (LF)
cr            = %x000D ; U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR)
space         = %x0020 ; U+0020 SPACE
colon         = %x003A ; U+003A COLON (:)
bom           = %xFEFF ; U+FEFF BYTE ORDER MARK
name-char     = %x0000-0009 / %x000B-000C / %x000E-0039 / %x003B-10FFFF
                ; a scalar value other than U+000A LINE FEED (LF), U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR), or U+003A COLON (:)
any-char      = %x0000-0009 / %x000B-000C / %x000E-10FFFF
                ; a scalar value other than U+000A LINE FEED (LF) or U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR)
```

Event streams in this format must always be encoded as UTF-8. [\[ENCODING\]](#references)

Lines must be separated by either a U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN U+000A LINE FEED (CRLF) character pair, a single U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character, or a single U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) character.

Since connections established to remote servers for such resources are expected to be long-lived, UAs should ensure that appropriate buffering is used. In particular, while line buffering with lines are defined to end with a single U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character is safe, block buffering or line buffering with different expected line endings can cause delays in event dispatch.

#### 9.2.6 Interpreting an event stream

Streams must be decoded using the [UTF-8 decode](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8-decode) algorithm.

> [!note]
> The [UTF-8 decode](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8-decode) algorithm strips one leading UTF-8 Byte Order Mark (BOM), if any.

The stream must then be parsed by reading everything line by line, with a U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN U+000A LINE FEED (CRLF) character pair, a single U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character not preceded by a U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) character, and a single U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) character not followed by a U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character being the ways in which a line can end.

When a stream is parsed, a data buffer, an event type buffer, and a last event ID buffer must be associated with it. They must be initialized to the empty string.

Lines must be processed, in the order they are received, as follows:

If the line is empty (a blank line)

[Dispatch the event](#926-interpreting-an-event-stream), as defined below.

If the line starts with a U+003A COLON character (:)

Ignore the line.

If the line contains a U+003A COLON character (:)

Collect the characters on the line before the first U+003A COLON character (:), and let field be that string.

Collect the characters on the line after the first U+003A COLON character (:), and let value be that string. If value starts with a U+0020 SPACE character, remove it from value.

[Process the field](#926-interpreting-an-event-stream) using the steps described below, using field as the field name and value as the field value.

Otherwise, the string is not empty but does not contain a U+003A COLON character (:)

[Process the field](#926-interpreting-an-event-stream) using the steps described below, using the whole line as the field name, and the empty string as the field value.

Once the end of the file is reached, any pending data must be discarded. (If the file ends in the middle of an event, before the final empty line, the incomplete event is not dispatched.)

---

The steps to process the field given a field name and a field value depend on the field name, as given in the following list. Field names must be compared literally, with no case folding performed.

If the field name is "event"

Set the event type buffer to the field value.

If the field name is "data"

Append the field value to the data buffer, then append a single U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character to the data buffer.

If the field name is "id"

If the field value does not contain U+0000 NULL, then set the last event ID buffer to the field value. Otherwise, ignore the field.

If the field name is "retry"

If the field value consists of only [ASCII digits](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), then interpret the field value as an integer in base ten, and set the event stream's [reconnection time](#922-the-eventsource-interface) to that integer. Otherwise, ignore the field.

Otherwise

The field is ignored.

When the user agent is required to dispatch the event, the user agent must process the data buffer, the event type buffer, and the last event ID buffer using steps appropriate for the user agent.

For web browsers, the appropriate steps to [dispatch the event](#926-interpreting-an-event-stream) are as follows:
1. Set the [last event ID string](#922-the-eventsource-interface) of the event source to the value of the last event ID buffer. The buffer does not get reset, so the [last event ID string](#922-the-eventsource-interface) of the event source remains set to this value until the next time it is set by the server.
2. If the data buffer is an empty string, set the data buffer and the event type buffer to the empty string and return.
3. If the data buffer's last character is a U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character, then remove the last character from the data buffer.
4. Let event be the result of [creating an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#25-constructing-events) using [`MessageEvent`](#91-the-messageevent-interface), in the [relevant realm](#81334-relevant) of the [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object.
5. Initialize event's [`type`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute to "[`message`](#events)", its [`data`](#91-the-messageevent-interface) attribute to data, its [origin](#91-the-messageevent-interface) to the [origin](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-origin) of the event stream's final URL (i.e., the URL after redirects), and its [`lastEventId`](#91-the-messageevent-interface) attribute to the [last event ID string](#922-the-eventsource-interface) of the event source.
6. If the event type buffer has a value other than the empty string, change the [type](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) of the newly created event to equal the value of the event type buffer.
7. Set the data buffer and the event type buffer to the empty string.
8. [Queue a task](#8172-queuing-tasks) which, if the [`readyState`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) attribute is set to a value other than [`CLOSED`](#922-the-eventsource-interface), [dispatches](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#29-dispatching-events) the newly created event at the [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object.

> [!note]
> If an event doesn't have an "id" field, but an earlier event did set the event source's [last event ID string](#922-the-eventsource-interface), then the event's [`lastEventId`](#91-the-messageevent-interface) field will be set to the value of whatever the last seen "id" field was.

For other user agents, the appropriate steps to [dispatch the event](#926-interpreting-an-event-stream) are implementation dependent, but at a minimum they must set the data and event type buffers to the empty string before returning.

> [!example]
> The following event stream, once followed by a blank line:
> 
> ```
> data: YHOO
> data: +2
> data: 10
> ```
> 
> ...would cause an event [`message`](#events) with the interface [`MessageEvent`](#91-the-messageevent-interface) to be dispatched on the [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object. The event's [`data`](#91-the-messageevent-interface) attribute would contain the string "`YHOO\n+2\n10`" (where "`\n`" represents a newline).
> 
> This could be used as follows:
> 
> ```javascript
> var stocks = new EventSource("https://stocks.example.com/ticker.php");
> stocks.onmessage = function (event) {
>   var data = event.data.split('\n');
>   updateStocks(data[0], data[1], data[2]);
> };
> ```
> 
> ...where `updateStocks()` is a function defined as:
> 
> ```javascript
> function updateStocks(symbol, delta, value) { ... }
> ```
> 
> ...or some such.

> [!example]
> The following stream contains four blocks. The first block has just a comment, and will fire nothing. The second block has two fields with names "data" and "id" respectively; an event will be fired for this block, with the data "first event", and will then set the last event ID to "1" so that if the connection died between this block and the next, the server would be sent a \`[`Last-Event-ID`](#924-the-last-event-id-header)\` header with the value \``1`\`. The third block fires an event with data "second event", and also has an "id" field, this time with no value, which resets the last event ID to the empty string (meaning no \`[`Last-Event-ID`](#924-the-last-event-id-header)\` header will now be sent in the event of a reconnection being attempted). Finally, the last block just fires an event with the data " third event" (with a single leading space character). Note that the last still has to end with a blank line, the end of the stream is not enough to trigger the dispatch of the last event.
> 
> ```
> : test stream
> 
> data: first event
> id: 1
> 
> data:second event
> id
> 
> data:  third event
> 
> ```

> [!example]
> The following stream fires two events:
> 
> ```
> data
> 
> data
> data
> 
> data:
> ```
> 
> The first block fires events with the data set to the empty string, as would the last block if it was followed by a blank line. The middle block fires an event with the data set to a single newline character. The last block is discarded because it is not followed by a blank line.

> [!example]
> The following stream fires two identical events:
> 
> ```
> data:test
> 
> data: test
> 
> ```
> 
> This is because the space after the colon is ignored if present.

#### 9.2.7 Authoring notes

Legacy proxy servers are known to, in certain cases, drop HTTP connections after a short timeout. To protect against such proxy servers, authors can include a comment line (one starting with a ':' character) every 15 seconds or so.

Authors wishing to relate event source connections to each other or to specific documents previously served might find that relying on IP addresses doesn't work, as individual clients can have multiple IP addresses (due to having multiple proxy servers) and individual IP addresses can have multiple clients (due to sharing a proxy server). It is better to include a unique identifier in the document when it is served and then pass that identifier as part of the URL when the connection is established.

Authors are also cautioned that HTTP chunking can have unexpected negative effects on the reliability of this protocol, in particular if the chunking is done by a different layer unaware of the timing requirements. If this is a problem, chunking can be disabled for serving event streams.

Clients that support HTTP's per-server connection limitation might run into trouble when opening multiple pages from a site if each page has an [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) to the same domain. Authors can avoid this using the relatively complex mechanism of using unique domain names per connection, or by allowing the user to enable or disable the [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) functionality on a per-page basis, or by sharing a single [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object using a [shared worker](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface).

#### 9.2.8 Connectionless push and other features

User agents running in controlled environments, e.g. browsers on mobile handsets tied to specific carriers, may offload the management of the connection to a proxy on the network. In such a situation, the user agent for the purposes of conformance is considered to include both the handset software and the network proxy.

> [!example]
> For example, a browser on a mobile device, after having established a connection, might detect that it is on a supporting network and request that a proxy server on the network take over the management of the connection. The timeline for such a situation might be as follows:
> 1. Browser connects to a remote HTTP server and requests the resource specified by the author in the [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) constructor.
> 2. The server sends occasional messages.
> 3. In between two messages, the browser detects that it is idle except for the network activity involved in keeping the TCP connection alive, and decides to switch to sleep mode to save power.
> 4. The browser disconnects from the server.
> 5. The browser contacts a service on the network, and requests that the service, a "push proxy", maintain the connection instead.
> 6. The "push proxy" service contacts the remote HTTP server and requests the resource specified by the author in the [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) constructor (possibly including a \`[`Last-Event-ID`](#924-the-last-event-id-header)\` HTTP header, etc.).
> 7. The browser allows the mobile device to go to sleep.
> 8. The server sends another message.
> 9. The "push proxy" service uses a technology such as OMA push to convey the event to the mobile device, which wakes only enough to process the event and then returns to sleep.

This can reduce the total data usage, and can therefore result in considerable power savings.

As well as implementing the existing API and [`text/event-stream`](#177-textevent-stream) wire format as defined by this specification and in more distributed ways as described above, formats of event framing defined by [other applicable specifications](#2110-extensibility) may be supported. This specification does not define how they are to be parsed or processed.

#### 9.2.9 Garbage collection

While an [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object's [`readyState`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) is [`CONNECTING`](#922-the-eventsource-interface), and the object has one or more event listeners registered for [`open`](#events), [`message`](#events), or [`error`](#events) events, there must be a strong reference from the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) or [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) object that the [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object's constructor was invoked from to the [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object itself.

While an [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object's [`readyState`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) is [`OPEN`](#922-the-eventsource-interface), and the object has one or more event listeners registered for [`message`](#events) or [`error`](#events) events, there must be a strong reference from the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) or [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) object that the [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object's constructor was invoked from to the [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object itself.

While there is a task queued by an [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object on the [remote event task source](#923-processing-model), there must be a strong reference from the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) or [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) object that the [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object's constructor was invoked from to that [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object.

If a user agent is to forcibly close an [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object (this happens when a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object goes away permanently), the user agent must abort any instances of the [fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) algorithm started for this [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object, and must set the [`readyState`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) attribute to [`CLOSED`](#922-the-eventsource-interface).

If an [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) object is garbage collected while its connection is still open, the user agent must abort any instance of the [fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) algorithm opened by this [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface).

#### 9.2.10 Implementation advice

*This section is non-normative.*

User agents are strongly urged to provide detailed diagnostic information about [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) objects and their related network connections in their development consoles, to aid authors in debugging code using this API.

For example, a user agent could have a panel displaying all the [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) objects a page has created, each listing the constructor's arguments, whether there was a network error, what the CORS status of the connection is and what headers were sent by the client and received from the server to lead to that status, the messages that were received and how they were parsed, and so forth.

Implementations are especially encouraged to report detailed information to their development consoles whenever an [`error`](#events) event is fired, since little to no information can be made available in the events themselves.

### 9.3 Cross-document messaging

Web browsers, for security and privacy reasons, prevent documents in different domains from affecting each other; that is, cross-site scripting is disallowed.

While this is an important security feature, it prevents pages from different domains from communicating even when those pages are not hostile. This section introduces a messaging system that allows documents to communicate with each other regardless of their source domain, in a way designed to not enable cross-site scripting attacks.

> [!note]
> [![(This is a tracking vector.)](https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg)](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#24-privacy-concerns) The [`postMessage()`](#933-posting-messages) API can be used as a [tracking vector](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#24-privacy-concerns).

#### 9.3.1 Introduction

*This section is non-normative.*

> [!example]
> For example, if document A contains an [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) element that contains document B, and script in document A calls [`postMessage()`](#933-posting-messages) on the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object of document B, then a message event will be fired on that object, marked as originating from the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) of document A. The script in document A might look like:
> 
> ```javascript
> var o = document.getElementsByTagName('iframe')[0];
> o.contentWindow.postMessage('Hello world', 'https://b.example.org/');
> ```
> 
> To register an event handler for incoming events, the script would use `addEventListener()` (or similar mechanisms). For example, the script in document B might look like:
> 
> ```javascript
> window.addEventListener('message', receiver, false);
> function receiver(e) {
>   if (e.origin == 'https://example.com') {
