A [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) object has an associated embedder policy (an [embedder policy](#714-cross-origin-embedder-policies)).

A [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) object has an associated module map. It is a [module map](#8167-module-related-host-hooks), initially empty.

A [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) object has an associated cross-origin isolated capability boolean. It is initially false.

`workerGlobal.self`

Returns workerGlobal.

`workerGlobal.location`

Returns workerGlobal's [`WorkerLocation`](#1033-the-workerlocation-interface) object.

`workerGlobal.navigator`

Returns workerGlobal's [`WorkerNavigator`](#1032-the-workernavigator-interface) object.

`workerGlobal.importScripts(...urls)`

Fetches each [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) in urls, executes them one-by-one in the order they are passed, and then returns (or throws if something went amiss).

The `self` attribute must return the [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) object itself.

The `location` attribute must return the [`WorkerLocation`](#1033-the-workerlocation-interface) object whose associated [`WorkerGlobalScope` object](#1033-the-workerlocation-interface) is the [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) object.

> [!note]
> While the [`WorkerLocation`](#1033-the-workerlocation-interface) object is created after the [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) object, this is not problematic as it cannot be observed from script.

---

The following are the [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers) (and their corresponding [event handler event types](#8181-event-handlers)) that must be supported, as [event handler IDL attributes](#8181-event-handlers), by objects implementing the [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) interface:

| [Event handler](#8181-event-handlers) | [Event handler event type](#8181-event-handlers) |
| --- | --- |
| `onerror` | [`error`](#events) |
| `onlanguagechange` | [`languagechange`](#events) |
| `onoffline` | [`offline`](#events) |
| `ononline` | [`online`](#events) |
| `onrejectionhandled` | [`rejectionhandled`](#events) |
| `onunhandledrejection` | [`unhandledrejection`](#events) |

##### 10.2.1.2 Dedicated workers and the [`DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10212-dedicated-workers-and-the-dedicatedworkerglobalscope-interface) interface

```webidl
[Global=(Worker,DedicatedWorker),Exposed=DedicatedWorker]
interface DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope : WorkerGlobalScope {
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute DOMString name;

  undefined postMessage(any message, sequence<object> transfer);
  undefined postMessage(any message, optional StructuredSerializeOptions options = {});

  undefined close();
};

DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope includes MessageEventTarget;
```

[`DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10212-dedicated-workers-and-the-dedicatedworkerglobalscope-interface) objects have an associated inside port (a [`MessagePort`](#944-message-ports)). This port is part of a channel that is set up when the worker is created, but it is not exposed. This object must never be garbage collected before the [`DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10212-dedicated-workers-and-the-dedicatedworkerglobalscope-interface) object.

`dedicatedWorkerGlobal.name`

Returns dedicatedWorkerGlobal's [name](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface), i.e. the value given to the [`Worker`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) constructor. Primarily useful for debugging.

`dedicatedWorkerGlobal.postMessage(message [, transfer ])`

`dedicatedWorkerGlobal.postMessage(message [, { transfer } ])`

Clones message and transmits it to the [`Worker`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) object associated with dedicatedWorkerGlobal. transfer can be passed as a list of objects that are to be transferred rather than cloned.

`dedicatedWorkerGlobal.close()`

Aborts dedicatedWorkerGlobal.

The `name` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [name](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface). Its value represents the name given to the worker using the [`Worker`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) constructor, used primarily for debugging purposes.

The `postMessage(message,
  transfer)` and `postMessage(message,
  options)` methods on [`DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10212-dedicated-workers-and-the-dedicatedworkerglobalscope-interface) objects act as if, when invoked, it immediately invoked the respective [`postMessage(message, transfer)`](#944-message-ports) and [`postMessage(message,
  options)`](#944-message-ports) on the port, with the same arguments, and returned the same return value.

To close a worker, given a workerGlobal, run these steps:
1. Discard any [tasks](#8171-definitions) that have been added to workerGlobal's [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [task queues](#8171-definitions).
2. Set workerGlobal's [closing](#1022-the-event-loop) flag to true. (This prevents any further tasks from being queued.)

The `close()` method steps are to [close a worker](#10212-dedicated-workers-and-the-dedicatedworkerglobalscope-interface) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).

---

##### 10.2.1.3 Shared workers and the [`SharedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface) interface

```webidl
[Global=(Worker,SharedWorker),Exposed=SharedWorker]
interface SharedWorkerGlobalScope : WorkerGlobalScope {
  [Replaceable] readonly attribute DOMString name;

  undefined close();

  attribute EventHandler onconnect;
};
```

A [`SharedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface) object has associated constructor storage key (a [storage key](https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-key)), constructor URL (a [URL record](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url)), and credentials (a [credentials mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode)), and extended lifetime (a boolean). They are initialized when the [`SharedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface) object is created, in the [run a worker](#1024-processing-model) algorithm.

Shared workers receive message ports through [`connect`](#events) events on their [`SharedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface) object for each connection.

`sharedWorkerGlobal.name`

Returns sharedWorkerGlobal's [name](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface), i.e. the value given to the [`SharedWorker`](#10264-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface) constructor. Multiple [`SharedWorker`](#10264-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface) objects can correspond to the same shared worker (and [`SharedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface)), by reusing the same name.

`sharedWorkerGlobal.close()`

Aborts sharedWorkerGlobal.

The `name` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [name](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface). Its value represents the name that can be used to obtain a reference to the worker using the [`SharedWorker`](#10264-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface) constructor.

The `close()` method steps are to [close a worker](#10212-dedicated-workers-and-the-dedicatedworkerglobalscope-interface) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).

---

The following are the [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers) (and their corresponding [event handler event types](#8181-event-handlers)) that must be supported, as [event handler IDL attributes](#8181-event-handlers), by objects implementing the [`SharedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface) interface:

| [Event handler](#8181-event-handlers) | [Event handler event type](#8181-event-handlers) |
| --- | --- |
| `onconnect` | [`connect`](#events) |

#### 10.2.2 The event loop

A [worker event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [task queues](#8171-definitions) only have events, callbacks, and networking activity as [tasks](#8171-definitions). These [worker event loops](#8171-definitions) are created by the [run a worker](#1024-processing-model) algorithm.

Each [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) object has a closing flag, which must be initially false, but which can get set to true by the algorithms in the processing model section below.

Once the [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface)'s [closing](#1022-the-event-loop) flag is set to true, the [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [task queues](#8171-definitions) must discard any further [tasks](#8171-definitions) that would be added to them (tasks already on the queue are unaffected except where otherwise specified). Effectively, once the [closing](#1022-the-event-loop) flag is true, timers stop firing, notifications for all pending background operations are dropped, etc.

#### 10.2.3 The worker's lifetime

Workers communicate with other workers and with [`Window`](#722-the-window-object)s through [message channels](#94-channel-messaging) and their [`MessagePort`](#944-message-ports) objects.

Each [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) object worker global scope has a list of the worker's ports, which consists of all the [`MessagePort`](#944-message-ports) objects that are entangled with another port and that have one (but only one) port owned by worker global scope. This list includes the implicit [`MessagePort`](#944-message-ports) in the case of [dedicated workers](#10212-dedicated-workers-and-the-dedicatedworkerglobalscope-interface).

Given an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) o when creating or obtaining a worker, the relevant owner to add depends on the type of [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) specified by o. If o's [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) is a [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) object (i.e., if we are creating a nested dedicated worker), then the relevant owner is that global object. Otherwise, o's [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) is a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object, and the relevant owner is that [`Window`](#722-the-window-object)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object).

---

A user agent has an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) value, the between-loads shared worker timeout, which is some small amount of time. This represents how long the user agent allows shared workers to survive while a page is loading, in case that page is going to contact the shared worker again. Setting this value to greater than zero lets user agents avoid the cost of restarting a shared worker used by a site when the user is navigating from page to page within that site.

> [!note]
> A typical value for the [between-loads shared worker timeout](#1023-the-workers-lifetime) might be 5 seconds.

A user agent has an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) value, the extended lifetime shared worker timeout, which is some amount of time. This represents how long the user agent allows shared workers which the web developer has requested be given an extended lifetime, to survive and perform work after all of their [owners](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) have disappeared. User agents should choose a value that is equal to the longest lifetime that a service worker can stay alive without any [clients](https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#dfn-service-worker-client), and must not choose a value that is longer than that amount of time.

> [!note]
> A typical value for the [extended lifetime shared worker timeout](#1023-the-workers-lifetime) could be anywhere from 10 seconds to 5 minutes, depending on the implementation's individual policies regarding background work being performed by an origin without a user-visible representation.

---

A [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) global is in extended lifetime if the following algorithm returns true:
1. If global is not a [`SharedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface), then return false.
2. If global's [extended lifetime](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface) is false, then return false.
3. If global's [owner set](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) [is empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists), but has been empty for less than the user agent's [extended lifetime shared worker timeout](#1023-the-workers-lifetime), then return true.
4. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) owner of global's [owner set](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface):
   1. If owner is a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) that is [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents), then return false.

      > [!note]
      > In this case global will be [actively needed](#1023-the-workers-lifetime), but it's not in extended lifetime.

5. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) owner of global's [owner set](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface):
   1. If owner is a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) and the amount of time that owner has been non-[fully active](#733-fully-active-documents) is less than the user agent's [extended lifetime shared worker timeout](#1023-the-workers-lifetime), then return true.
   2. If owner is a [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) that is [in extended lifetime](#1023-the-workers-lifetime), then return true.
6. Return false.

A [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) global is actively needed if the following algorithm returns true:
1. If global is [in extended lifetime](#1023-the-workers-lifetime), then return true.
2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) owner of global's [owner set](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface):
   1. If owner is a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), and owner is [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents), then return true.
   2. If owner is a [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) that is [actively needed](#1023-the-workers-lifetime), then return true.
3. Return false.

A [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) global is protected if the following algorithm returns true:
1. If global is not [actively needed](#1023-the-workers-lifetime), then return false.
2. If global is [in extended lifetime](#1023-the-workers-lifetime), then return true.
3. If global is a [`SharedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface), then return true.
4. If global's [the worker's ports](#1023-the-workers-lifetime) is not [empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists), then return true.
5. If global has outstanding timers, database transactions, or network connections, then return true.
6. Return false.

A [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) global is permissible if the following algorithm returns true:
1. If global's [owner set](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) is not [empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists), then return true.
2. If global is [in extended lifetime](#1023-the-workers-lifetime), then return true.
3. If all of the following are true:
   - global is a [`SharedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface);
   - global's [owner set](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) has been [empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) for no more than the user agent's [between-loads shared worker timeout](#1023-the-workers-lifetime); and
   - the user agent has a [navigable](#731-navigables) whose [active document](#731-navigables) is not [completely loaded](#758-finishing-the-loading-process),

   then return true.

4. Return false.

> [!note]
> The following relationships hold between these terms:
> - Every [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) that is [in extended lifetime](#1023-the-workers-lifetime) is [actively needed](#1023-the-workers-lifetime), [protected](#1023-the-workers-lifetime), and [permissible](#1023-the-workers-lifetime).
> - Every [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) that is [actively needed](#1023-the-workers-lifetime) or [protected](#1023-the-workers-lifetime) is [permissible](#1023-the-workers-lifetime).
> - Every [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) that is [protected](#1023-the-workers-lifetime) is [actively needed](#1023-the-workers-lifetime).
> 
> However, the converses do not always hold:
> - A [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) can be [actively needed](#1023-the-workers-lifetime) but not [protected](#1023-the-workers-lifetime), if it's a dedicated worker with no outstanding async work that is still performing computation on behalf of a fully active owner, but whose corresponding [`Worker`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) object has been garbage collected. [Because of the garbage collection](#946-ports-and-garbage-collection), the [ports](#1023-the-workers-lifetime) collection is empty, so it is no longer protected. However, its event loop has not yet yielded to [empty its owner set](#1024-processing-model), so it is still actively needed.
> - A [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) can be [permissible](#1023-the-workers-lifetime) but not [protected](#1023-the-workers-lifetime) or [actively needed](#1023-the-workers-lifetime), if all the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)s in its transitive set of owners are in [bfcache](#7412-document-state), or if it's a [`SharedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface) with no current owners being kept alive for the duration of the [between-loads shared worker timeout](#1023-the-workers-lifetime).

> [!note]
> The [between-loads shared worker timeout](#1023-the-workers-lifetime) only influences the definition of [permissible](#1023-the-workers-lifetime), not [protected](#1023-the-workers-lifetime), and so implementations are not required to keep shared workers alive for that duration. Rather, they are required to close shared workers after the timeout is reached.
> 
> In contrast, the [extended lifetime shared worker timeout](#1023-the-workers-lifetime) does influence the definition of [protected](#1023-the-workers-lifetime), so implementations are required to keep shared workers alive (and not suspended) for that duration.

A [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) global is suspendable if the following algorithm returns true:
1. If global is [actively needed](#1023-the-workers-lifetime), then return false.
2. If global is [permissible](#1023-the-workers-lifetime), then return true.
3. Return false.

> [!note]
> These concepts are used elsewhere in the specification's normative requirements as follows:
> - Workers get [closed as orphans](#1024-processing-model) between when they stop being [protected](#1023-the-workers-lifetime) and when they stop being [permissible](#1023-the-workers-lifetime).
> - Workers that have been closed, but keep executing, [can be terminated](#1024-processing-model) at the user agent's discretion, once they stop being [actively needed](#1023-the-workers-lifetime).
> - Workers get [suspended or un-suspended](#1024-processing-model) based on whether they are [suspendable](#1023-the-workers-lifetime).

#### 10.2.4 Processing model

When a user agent is to run a worker for a script with [`Worker`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) or [`SharedWorker`](#10264-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface) object worker, [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) url, [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) outside settings, [`MessagePort`](#944-message-ports) outside port, and a [`WorkerOptions`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) dictionary options, it must run the following steps:
1. Let is shared be true if worker is a [`SharedWorker`](#10264-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface) object, and false otherwise.
2. Let owner be the [relevant owner to add](#1023-the-workers-lifetime) given outside settings.
3. Let unsafeWorkerCreationTime be the [unsafe shared current time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-unsafe-shared-current-time).
4. Let agent be the result of [obtaining a dedicated/shared worker agent](#8122-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-cluster-formalism) given outside settings and is shared. Run the rest of these steps in that agent.
5. Let realm execution context be the result of [creating a new realm](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) given agent and the following customizations:
   - For the global object, if is shared is true, create a new [`SharedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface) object. Otherwise, create a new [`DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10212-dedicated-workers-and-the-dedicatedworkerglobalscope-interface) object.
6. Let worker global scope be the [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) of realm execution context's Realm component.

   > [!note]
   > This is the [`DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10212-dedicated-workers-and-the-dedicatedworkerglobalscope-interface) or [`SharedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface) object created in the previous step.

7. [Set up a worker environment settings object](#10262-script-settings-for-workers) with realm execution context, outside settings, and unsafeWorkerCreationTime, and let inside settings be the result.
8. Set worker global scope's [name](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) to options\["[`name`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface)"\].
9. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) owner to worker global scope's [owner set](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface).
10. If is shared is true:
    1. Set worker global scope's [constructor storage key](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface) to the result of running [obtain a storage key for non-storage purposes](https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#obtain-a-storage-key-for-non-storage-purposes) given outside settings.
    2. Set worker global scope's [constructor URL](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface) to url.
    3. Set worker global scope's [type](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) to options\["[`type`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface)"\].
    4. Set worker global scope's [credentials](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface) to options\["[`credentials`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface)"\].
    5. Set worker global scope's [extended lifetime](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface) to options\["[`extendedLifetime`](#10264-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface)"\].
11. Let destination be "`sharedworker`" if is shared is true, and "`worker`" otherwise.
12. Obtain script by switching on options\["[`type`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface)"\]:

    "`classic`"

    [Fetch a classic worker script](#8142-fetching-scripts) given url, outside settings, destination, inside settings, and with onComplete and performFetch as defined below.

    "`module`"

    [Fetch a module worker script graph](#8142-fetching-scripts) given url, outside settings, destination, the value of the `credentials` member of options, inside settings, and with onComplete and performFetch as defined below.

    In both cases, let performFetch be the following [perform the fetch hook](#8142-fetching-scripts) given request, [isTopLevel](#8142-fetching-scripts), and [processCustomFetchResponse](#8142-fetching-scripts):
    1. If isTopLevel is false, [fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request with *[processResponseConsumeBody](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#process-response-end-of-body)* set to processCustomFetchResponse, and abort these steps.
    2. Set request's [reserved client](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-reserved-client) to inside settings.
    3. [Fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) request with *[processResponseConsumeBody](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#process-response-end-of-body)* set to the following steps given [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) response and null, failure, or a [byte sequence](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-byte-sequences) bodyBytes:
       1. Set worker global scope's [url](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) to response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url).
       2. Set inside settings's [creation URL](#8131-environments) to response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url).
       3. [Initialize worker global scope's policy container](#717-policy-containers) given worker global scope, response, and inside settings.
       4. If the [Run CSP initialization for a global object](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#run-global-object-csp-initialization) algorithm returns "`Blocked`" when executed upon worker global scope, set response to a [network error](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-network-error). [\[CSP\]](#references)
       5. If worker global scope's [embedder policy](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface)'s [value](#714-cross-origin-embedder-policies) is [compatible with cross-origin isolation](#714-cross-origin-embedder-policies) and is shared is true, then set agent's [agent cluster](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters)'s [cross-origin isolation mode](#8122-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-cluster-formalism) to "[`logical`](#7323-groupings-of-browsing-contexts)" or "[`concrete`](#7323-groupings-of-browsing-contexts)". The one chosen is [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology).

          > [!warning]
          > This really ought to be set when the agent cluster is created, which requires a redesign of this section.

       6. If the result of [checking a global object's embedder policy](#7142-embedder-policy-checks) with worker global scope, outside settings, and response is false, then set response to a [network error](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-network-error).
       7. Set worker global scope's [cross-origin isolated capability](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) to true if agent's [agent cluster](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-agent-clusters)'s [cross-origin isolation mode](#8122-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-cluster-formalism) is "[`concrete`](#7323-groupings-of-browsing-contexts)".
       8. If is shared is false and owner's [cross-origin isolated capability](#8132-environment-settings-objects) is false, then set worker global scope's [cross-origin isolated capability](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) to false.
       9. If is shared is false and response's [URL](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response-url)'s [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) is "`data`", then set worker global scope's [cross-origin isolated capability](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) to false.

          > [!note]
          > This is a conservative default for now, while we figure out how workers in general, and [`data:`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2397#section-2) URL workers in particular (which are cross-origin from their owner), will be treated in the context of permissions policies. See [w3c/webappsec-permissions-policy issue #207](https://github.com/w3c/webappsec-permissions-policy/issues/207) for more details.

       10. Run processCustomFetchResponse with response and bodyBytes.

    In both cases, let onComplete given script be the following steps:
    1. If script is null or if script's [error to rethrow](#8141-scripts) is non-null:
       1. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given worker's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) at worker.
       2. Run the [environment discarding steps](#8131-environments) for inside settings.
       3. Abort these steps.
    2. Associate worker with worker global scope.
    3. Let inside port be a [new](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#new) [`MessagePort`](#944-message-ports) object in inside settings's [realm](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
    4. If is shared is false:
       1. Set inside port's [message event target](#944-message-ports) to worker global scope.
       2. Set worker global scope's [inside port](#10212-dedicated-workers-and-the-dedicatedworkerglobalscope-interface) to inside port.
    5. [Entangle](#944-message-ports) outside port and inside port.
    6. Create a new [`WorkerLocation`](#1033-the-workerlocation-interface) object and associate it with worker global scope.
    7. *Closing orphan workers*: Start monitoring worker global scope such that no sooner than it stops being [protected](#1023-the-workers-lifetime), and no later than it stops being [permissible](#1023-the-workers-lifetime), worker global scope's [closing](#1022-the-event-loop) flag is set to true.
    8. *Suspending workers*: Start monitoring worker global scope, such that whenever worker global scope's [closing](#1022-the-event-loop) flag is false and it is [suspendable](#1023-the-workers-lifetime), the user agent suspends execution of script in worker global scope until such time as either the [closing](#1022-the-event-loop) flag switches to true or worker global scope stops being [suspendable](#1023-the-workers-lifetime).
    9. Set inside settings's [execution ready flag](#8131-environments).
    10. If script is a [classic script](#8141-scripts), then [run the classic script](#8144-calling-scripts) script. Otherwise, it is a [module script](#8141-scripts); [run the module script](#8144-calling-scripts) script.

        > [!note]
        > In addition to the usual possibilities of returning a value or failing due to an exception, this could be [prematurely aborted](#8145-killing-scripts) by the [terminate a worker](#1024-processing-model) algorithm defined below.

    11. Enable outside port's [port message queue](#944-message-ports).
    12. If is shared is false, enable the [port message queue](#944-message-ports) of the worker's implicit port.
    13. If is shared is true, then [queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given worker global scope to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`connect`](#events) at worker global scope, using [`MessageEvent`](#91-the-messageevent-interface), with the [`data`](#91-the-messageevent-interface) attribute initialized to the empty string, the [`ports`](#91-the-messageevent-interface) attribute initialized to a new [frozen array](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-frozen-array-type) containing inside port, and the [`source`](#91-the-messageevent-interface) attribute initialized to inside port.
    14. Enable the [client message queue](https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#dfn-client-message-queue) of the [`ServiceWorkerContainer`](https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#serviceworkercontainer) object whose associated [service worker client](https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#serviceworkercontainer-service-worker-client) is worker global scope's [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant).
    15. *Event loop*: Run the [responsible event loop](#8132-environment-settings-objects) specified by inside settings until it is destroyed.

        > [!note]
        > The handling of events or the execution of callbacks by [tasks](#8171-definitions) run by the [event loop](#8171-definitions) might get [prematurely aborted](#8145-killing-scripts) by the [terminate a worker](#1024-processing-model) algorithm defined below.

        > [!note]
        > The worker processing model remains on this step until the event loop is destroyed, which happens after the [closing](#1022-the-event-loop) flag is set to true, as described in the [event loop](#8171-definitions) processing model.

    16. [Clear](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) the worker global scope's [map of active timers](#87-timers).
    17. Disentangle all the ports in the list of [the worker's ports](#1023-the-workers-lifetime).
    18. [Empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) worker global scope's [owner set](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface).

---

When a user agent is to terminate a worker, it must run the following steps [in parallel](#211-parallelism) with the worker's main loop (the "[run a worker](#1024-processing-model)" processing model defined above):
1. Set the worker's [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) object's [closing](#1022-the-event-loop) flag to true.
2. If there are any [tasks](#8171-definitions) queued in the [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) object's [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [event loop](#8171-definitions)'s [task queues](#8171-definitions), discard them without processing them.
3. [Abort the script](#8145-killing-scripts) currently running in the worker.
4. If the worker's [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) object is actually a [`DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10212-dedicated-workers-and-the-dedicatedworkerglobalscope-interface) object (i.e. the worker is a dedicated worker), then empty the [port message queue](#944-message-ports) of the port that the worker's implicit port is entangled with.

User agents may invoke the [terminate a worker](#1024-processing-model) algorithm when a worker stops being [actively needed](#1023-the-workers-lifetime) and the worker continues executing even after its [closing](#1022-the-event-loop) flag was set to true.

#### 10.2.5 Runtime script errors

Whenever an uncaught runtime script error occurs in one of the worker's scripts, if the error did not occur while handling a previous script error, the user agent will [report](#8146-runtime-script-errors) it for the worker's [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) object.

#### 10.2.6 Creating workers

##### 10.2.6.1 The [`AbstractWorker`](#10261-the-abstractworker-mixin) mixin

```webidl
interface mixin AbstractWorker {
  attribute EventHandler onerror;
};
```

The following are the [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers) (and their corresponding [event handler event types](#8181-event-handlers)) that must be supported, as [event handler IDL attributes](#8181-event-handlers), by objects implementing the [`AbstractWorker`](#10261-the-abstractworker-mixin) interface:

| [Event handler](#8181-event-handlers) | [Event handler event type](#8181-event-handlers) |
| --- | --- |
| `onerror` | [`error`](#events) |

##### 10.2.6.2 Script settings for workers

To set up a worker environment settings object, given a [JavaScript execution context](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-execution-contexts) execution context, an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) outside settings, and a number unsafeWorkerCreationTime:
1. Let realm be the value of execution context's Realm component.
2. Let worker global scope be realm's [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
3. Let origin be a unique [opaque origin](#711-origins) if worker global scope's [url](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface)'s [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) is "`data`"; otherwise outside settings's [origin](#8132-environment-settings-objects).
4. Let settings object be a new [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) whose algorithms are defined as follows:

   The [realm execution context](#8132-environment-settings-objects)

   Return execution context.

   The [module map](#8132-environment-settings-objects)

   Return worker global scope's [module map](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface).

   The [API base URL](#8132-environment-settings-objects)

   Return worker global scope's [url](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface).

   The [origin](#8132-environment-settings-objects)

   Return origin.

   The [has cross-site ancestor](#8132-environment-settings-objects)
   1. If outside settings's [has cross-site ancestor](#8132-environment-settings-objects) is true, then return true.
   2. If worker global scope's [url](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface)'s [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme) is "`data`", then return true.
   3. Return false.

   The [policy container](#8132-environment-settings-objects)

   Return worker global scope's [policy container](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface).

   The [cross-origin isolated capability](#8132-environment-settings-objects)

   Return worker global scope's [cross-origin isolated capability](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface).

   The [time origin](#8132-environment-settings-objects)

   Return the result of [coarsening](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-coarsen-time) unsafeWorkerCreationTime with worker global scope's [cross-origin isolated capability](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface).

5. Set settings object's [id](#8131-environments) to a new unique opaque string, [creation URL](#8131-environments) to worker global scope's [url](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface), [top-level creation URL](#8131-environments) to null, [target browsing context](#8131-environments) to null, and [active service worker](#8131-environments) to null.
6. If worker global scope is a [`DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10212-dedicated-workers-and-the-dedicatedworkerglobalscope-interface) object, then set settings object's [top-level origin](#8131-environments) to outside settings's [top-level origin](#8131-environments).
7. Otherwise, set settings object's [top-level origin](#8131-environments) to an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) value.

   > [!warning]
   > See [Client-Side Storage Partitioning](https://privacycg.github.io/storage-partitioning/) for the latest on properly defining this.

8. Set realm's \[\[HostDefined\]\] field to settings object.
9. Return settings object.

##### 10.2.6.3 Dedicated workers and the [`Worker`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) interface

```webidl
[Exposed=(Window,DedicatedWorker,SharedWorker)]
interface Worker : EventTarget {
  constructor((TrustedScriptURL or USVString) scriptURL, optional WorkerOptions options = {});

  undefined terminate();

  undefined postMessage(any message, sequence<object> transfer);
  undefined postMessage(any message, optional StructuredSerializeOptions options = {});
};

dictionary WorkerOptions {
  DOMString name = "";
  WorkerType type = "classic";
  RequestCredentials credentials = "same-origin"; // credentials is only used if type is "module"
};

enum WorkerType { "classic", "module" };

Worker includes AbstractWorker;
Worker includes MessageEventTarget;
```

`worker = new Worker(scriptURL [, options ])`

Returns a new [`Worker`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) object. scriptURL will be fetched and executed in the background, creating a new global environment for which worker represents the communication channel.

options can contain the following values:
- [`name`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) can be used to define the [name](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) of that global environment, primarily for debugging purposes.
- [`type`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) can be used to load the new global environment from scriptURL as a JavaScript module, by setting it to the value "`module`".
- [`credentials`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) can be used to specify how scriptURL is fetched, but only if [`type`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) is set to "`module`".

`worker.terminate()`

Aborts worker's associated global environment.

`worker.postMessage(message [, transfer ])`

`worker.postMessage(message [, { transfer } ])`

Clones message and transmits it to worker's global environment. transfer can be passed as a list of objects that are to be transferred rather than cloned.

Each [`Worker`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) object has an associated outside port (a [`MessagePort`](#944-message-ports)). This port is part of a channel that is set up when the worker is created, but it is not exposed. This object must never be garbage collected before the [`Worker`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) object.

The `terminate()` method steps are to [terminate a worker](#1024-processing-model) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s worker.

The `postMessage(message, transfer)` and `postMessage(message,
  options)` methods on [`Worker`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) objects act as if, when invoked, they immediately invoked the respective [`postMessage(message, transfer)`](#944-message-ports) and [`postMessage(message,
  options)`](#944-message-ports) on [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [outside port](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface), with the same arguments, and returned the same return value.

> [!example]
> The [`postMessage()`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) method's first argument can be structured data:
> 
> ```javascript
> worker.postMessage({opcode: 'activate', device: 1938, parameters: [23, 102]});
> ```

---

The `new Worker(scriptURL,
  options)` constructor steps are:
1. Let compliantScriptURL be the result of invoking the [get trusted type compliant string](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#get-trusted-type-compliant-string) algorithm with [`TrustedScriptURL`](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trustedscripturl), [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant), scriptURL, "`Worker constructor`", and "`script`".
2. Let outsideSettings be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant).
3. Let workerURL be the result of [encoding-parsing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given compliantScriptURL, relative to outsideSettings.

   > [!note]
   > Any [same-origin](#711-origins) URL (including [`blob:`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#blob-url) URLs) can be used. [`data:`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2397#section-2) URLs can also be used, but they create a worker with an [opaque origin](#711-origins).

4. If workerURL is failure, then throw a ["`SyntaxError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
5. Let outsidePort be a [new](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#new) [`MessagePort`](#944-message-ports) in outsideSettings's [realm](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
6. Set outsidePort's [message event target](#944-message-ports) to [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
7. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [outside port](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) to outsidePort.
8. Let worker be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
9. Run this step [in parallel](#211-parallelism):
   1. [Run a worker](#1024-processing-model) given worker, workerURL, outsideSettings, outsidePort, and options.

##### 10.2.6.4 Shared workers and the [`SharedWorker`](#10264-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface) interface

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface SharedWorker : EventTarget {
  constructor((TrustedScriptURL or USVString) scriptURL, optional (DOMString or SharedWorkerOptions) options = {});

  readonly attribute MessagePort port;
};
SharedWorker includes AbstractWorker;

dictionary SharedWorkerOptions : WorkerOptions {
  boolean extendedLifetime = false;
};
```

`sharedWorker = new SharedWorker(scriptURL [, name ])`

Returns a new [`SharedWorker`](#10264-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface) object. scriptURL will be fetched and executed in the background, creating a new global environment for which sharedWorker represents the communication channel. name can be used to define the [name](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) of that global environment.

`sharedWorker = new SharedWorker(scriptURL [, options ])`

Returns a new [`SharedWorker`](#10264-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface) object. scriptURL will be fetched and executed in the background, creating a new global environment for which sharedWorker represents the communication channel.

options can contain the following values:
- [`name`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) can be used to define the [name](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) of that global environment.
- [`type`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) can be used to load the new global environment from scriptURL as a JavaScript module, by setting it to the value "`module`".
- [`credentials`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) can be used to specify how scriptURL is fetched, but only if [`type`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) is set to "`module`".
- [`extendedLifetime`](#10264-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface) can be set to request that the newly-created global environment be given extra time to perform its operations even after all of its [owners](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) have disappeared. This can be useful, for example, for performing asynchronous work after page unload.

> [!warning]
> Note that attempting to construct a shared worker with options whose [`type`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface), [`credentials`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface), or [`extendedLifetime`](#10264-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface) values mismatch those of an existing shared worker with the same [constructor URL](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface) and [name](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface), will cause the returned sharedWorker to fire an [`error`](#events) event and not connect to the existing shared worker.

`sharedWorker.port`

Returns sharedWorker's [`MessagePort`](#944-message-ports) object which can be used to communicate with the global environment.

A user agent has an associated shared worker manager which is the result of [starting a new parallel queue](#211-parallelism).

> [!note]
> Each user agent has a single [shared worker manager](#10264-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface) for simplicity. Implementations could use one per [origin](#711-origins); that would not be observably different and enables more concurrency.

---

Each [`SharedWorker`](#10264-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface) has a port, a [`MessagePort`](#944-message-ports) set when the object is created.

The `port` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [port](#10264-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface).

The `new
  SharedWorker(scriptURL, options)` constructor steps are:
1. Let compliantScriptURL be the result of invoking the [get trusted type compliant string](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#get-trusted-type-compliant-string) algorithm with [`TrustedScriptURL`](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trustedscripturl), [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant), scriptURL, "`SharedWorker constructor`", and "`script`".
2. If options is a [`DOMString`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#idl-DOMString), set options to a new [`WorkerOptions`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) dictionary whose [`name`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) member is set to the value of options and whose other members are set to their default values.
3. Let outsideSettings be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant).
4. Let urlRecord be the result of [encoding-parsing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given compliantScriptURL, relative to outsideSettings.

   > [!note]
   > Any [same-origin](#711-origins) URL (including [`blob:`](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#blob-url) URLs) can be used. [`data:`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2397#section-2) URLs can also be used, but they create a worker with an [opaque origin](#711-origins).

5. If urlRecord is failure, then throw a ["`SyntaxError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
6. Let outsidePort be a [new](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#new) [`MessagePort`](#944-message-ports) in outsideSettings's [realm](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
7. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [port](#10264-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface) to outsidePort.
8. Let callerIsSecureContext be true if outsideSettings is a [secure context](#8135-secure-contexts); otherwise, false.
9. Let outsideStorageKey be the result of running [obtain a storage key for non-storage purposes](https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#obtain-a-storage-key-for-non-storage-purposes) given outsideSettings.
10. Let worker be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
11. [Enqueue the following steps](#211-parallelism) to the [shared worker manager](#10264-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface):
    1. Let workerGlobalScope be null.
    2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) scope in the list of all [`SharedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface) objects:
       1. If all of the following are true:
          - scope's [constructor storage key](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface) [equals](https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-key-equal) outsideStorageKey;
          - scope's [closing](#1022-the-event-loop) flag is false;
          - scope's [constructor URL](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface) [equals](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-equals) urlRecord; and
          - scope's [name](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) equals options\["[`name`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface)"\],

          then:
          1. Set workerGlobalScope to scope.
          2. [Break](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration).

       > [!note]
       > [`data:`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2397#section-2) URLs create a worker with an [opaque origin](#711-origins), which would prevent such a worker from ever being matched if its own [storage key](https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-key) were used. Instead, the [constructor storage key](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface) (derived from the creating environment) and [constructor URL](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface) are compared, so the same [`data:`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2397#section-2) URL can be used within a [storage key](https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-key) to get to the same [`SharedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface) object, but cannot be used to bypass the [storage key](https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-key) restriction.

    3. If workerGlobalScope is not null, but the user agent has been configured to disallow communication between the worker represented by the workerGlobalScope and the [scripts](#8141-scripts) whose [settings object](#8141-scripts) is outsideSettings, then set workerGlobalScope to null.

       > [!note]
       > For example, a user agent could have a development mode that isolates a particular [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables) from all other pages, and scripts in that development mode could be blocked from connecting to shared workers running in the normal browser mode.

    4. If workerGlobalScope is not null, and any of the following are true:
       - workerGlobalScope's [type](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) is not equal to options\["[`type`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface)"\];
       - workerGlobalScope's [credentials](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface) is not equal to options\["[`credentials`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface)"\]; or
       - workerGlobalScope's [extended lifetime](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface) is not equal to options\["[`extendedLifetime`](#10264-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworker-interface)"\],

       then:
       1. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given worker's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) at worker.
       2. Abort these steps.

    5. If workerGlobalScope is not null:
       1. Let insideSettings be workerGlobalScope's [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant).
       2. Let workerIsSecureContext be true if insideSettings is a [secure context](#8135-secure-contexts); otherwise, false.
       3. If workerIsSecureContext is not callerIsSecureContext:
          1. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given worker's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`error`](#events) at worker.
          2. Abort these steps.
       4. Associate worker with workerGlobalScope.
       5. Let insidePort be a [new](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#new) [`MessagePort`](#944-message-ports) in insideSettings's [realm](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
       6. [Entangle](#944-message-ports) outsidePort and insidePort.
       7. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given workerGlobalScope to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`connect`](#events) at workerGlobalScope, using [`MessageEvent`](#91-the-messageevent-interface), with the [`data`](#91-the-messageevent-interface) attribute initialized to the empty string, the [`ports`](#91-the-messageevent-interface) attribute initialized to a new [frozen array](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-frozen-array-type) containing only insidePort, and the [`source`](#91-the-messageevent-interface) attribute initialized to insidePort.
       8. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) the [relevant owner to add](#1023-the-workers-lifetime) given outsideSettings to workerGlobalScope's [owner set](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface).
    6. Otherwise, [in parallel](#211-parallelism), [run a worker](#1024-processing-model) given worker, urlRecord, outsideSettings, outsidePort, and options.

#### 10.2.7 Concurrent hardware capabilities

```webidl
interface mixin NavigatorConcurrentHardware {
  readonly attribute unsigned long long hardwareConcurrency;
};
```

`self.navigator.hardwareConcurrency`

Returns the number of logical processors potentially available to the user agent.

[![(This is a tracking vector.)](https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg)](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#24-privacy-concerns) The `navigator.hardwareConcurrency` attribute's getter must return a number between 1 and the number of logical processors potentially available to the user agent. If this cannot be determined, the getter must return 1.

User agents should err toward exposing the number of logical processors available, using lower values only in cases where there are user-agent specific limits in place (such as a limitation on the number of [workers](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) that can be created) or when the user agent desires to limit fingerprinting possibilities.

### 10.3 APIs available to workers

#### 10.3.1 Importing scripts and libraries

The `importScripts(...urls)` method steps are:
1. Let urlStrings be « ».
2. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) url of urls:
   1. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) the result of invoking the [get trusted type compliant string](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#get-trusted-type-compliant-string) algorithm with [`TrustedScriptURL`](https://w3c.github.io/trusted-types/dist/spec/#trustedscripturl), [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant), url, "`WorkerGlobalScope importScripts`", and "`script`" to urlStrings.
3. [Import scripts into worker global scope](#1031-importing-scripts-and-libraries) given [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) and urlStrings.

To import scripts into worker global scope, given a [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) object worker global scope, a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [scalar value strings](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) urls, and an optional [perform the fetch hook](#8142-fetching-scripts) performFetch:
1. If worker global scope's [type](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) is "`module`", throw a [`TypeError`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-native-error-types-used-in-this-standard-typeerror) exception.
2. Let settings object be the [current settings object](#81333-current).
3. If urls is empty, return.
4. Let urlRecords be « ».
5. For each url of urls:
   1. Let urlRecord be the result of [encoding-parsing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given url, relative to settings object.
   2. If urlRecord is failure, then throw a ["`SyntaxError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
   3. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) urlRecord to urlRecords.
6. For each urlRecord of urlRecords:
   1. [Fetch a classic worker-imported script](#8142-fetching-scripts) given urlRecord and settings object, passing along performFetch if provided. If this succeeds, let script be the result. Otherwise, rethrow the exception.
   2. [Run the classic script](#8144-calling-scripts) script, with *rethrow errors* set to true.

      > [!note]
      > script will run until it either returns, fails to parse, fails to catch an exception, or gets [prematurely aborted](#8145-killing-scripts) by the [terminate a worker](#1024-processing-model) algorithm defined above.

      If an exception was thrown or if the script was [prematurely aborted](#8145-killing-scripts), then abort all these steps, letting the exception or aborting continue to be processed by the calling [script](#8141-scripts).

> [!note]
> Service Workers is an example of a specification that runs this algorithm with its own [perform the fetch hook](#8142-fetching-scripts). [\[SW\]](#references)

#### 10.3.2 The [`WorkerNavigator`](#1032-the-workernavigator-interface) interface

The `navigator` attribute of the [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) interface must return an instance of the [`WorkerNavigator`](#1032-the-workernavigator-interface) interface, which represents the identity and state of the user agent (the client):

```webidl
[Exposed=Worker]
interface WorkerNavigator {};
WorkerNavigator includes NavigatorID;
WorkerNavigator includes NavigatorLanguage;
WorkerNavigator includes NavigatorOnLine;
WorkerNavigator includes NavigatorConcurrentHardware;
```

#### 10.3.3 The [`WorkerLocation`](#1033-the-workerlocation-interface) interface

```webidl
[Exposed=Worker]
interface WorkerLocation {
  stringifier readonly attribute USVString href;
  readonly attribute USVString origin;
  readonly attribute USVString protocol;
  readonly attribute USVString host;
  readonly attribute USVString hostname;
  readonly attribute USVString port;
  readonly attribute USVString pathname;
  readonly attribute USVString search;
  readonly attribute USVString hash;
};
```

A [`WorkerLocation`](#1033-the-workerlocation-interface) object has an associated `WorkerGlobalScope` object (a [`WorkerGlobalScope`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) object).

The `href` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`WorkerGlobalScope` object](#1033-the-workerlocation-interface)'s [url](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface), [serialized](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer).

The `origin` getter steps are to return the [serialization](#711-origins) of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`WorkerGlobalScope` object](#1033-the-workerlocation-interface)'s [url](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface)'s [origin](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-origin).

The `protocol` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`WorkerGlobalScope` object](#1033-the-workerlocation-interface)'s [url](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface)'s [scheme](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-scheme), followed by "`:`".

The `host` getter steps are:
1. Let url be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`WorkerGlobalScope` object](#1033-the-workerlocation-interface)'s [url](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface).
2. If url's [host](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-host) is null, return the empty string.
3. If url's [port](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-port) is null, return url's [host](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-host), [serialized](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-host-serializer).
4. Return url's [host](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-host), [serialized](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-host-serializer), followed by "`:`" and url's [port](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-port), [serialized](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#serialize-an-integer).

The `hostname` getter steps are:
1. Let host be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`WorkerGlobalScope` object](#1033-the-workerlocation-interface)'s [url](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface)'s [host](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-host).
2. If host is null, return the empty string.
3. Return host, [serialized](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-host-serializer).

The `port` getter steps are:
1. Let port be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`WorkerGlobalScope` object](#1033-the-workerlocation-interface)'s [url](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface)'s [port](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-port).
2. If port is null, return the empty string.
3. Return port, [serialized](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#serialize-an-integer).

The `pathname` getter steps are to return the result of [URL path serializing](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-path-serializer) [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`WorkerGlobalScope` object](#1033-the-workerlocation-interface)'s [url](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface).

The `search` getter steps are:
1. Let query be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`WorkerGlobalScope` object](#1033-the-workerlocation-interface)'s [url](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface)'s [query](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-query).
2. If query is either null or the empty string, return the empty string.
3. Return "`?`", followed by query.

The `hash` getter steps are:
1. Let fragment be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [`WorkerGlobalScope` object](#1033-the-workerlocation-interface)'s [url](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface)'s [fragment](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment).
2. If fragment is either null or the empty string, return the empty string.
3. Return "`#`", followed by fragment.

## 11 Worklets

### 11.1 Introduction

*This section is non-normative.*

Worklets are a piece of specification infrastructure which can be used for running scripts independent of the main JavaScript execution environment, while not requiring any particular implementation model.

The worklet infrastructure specified here cannot be used directly by web developers. Instead, other specifications build upon it to create directly-usable worklet types, specialized for running in particular parts of the browser implementation pipeline.

#### 11.1.1 Motivations

*This section is non-normative.*

Allowing extension points to rendering, or other sensitive parts of the implementation pipeline such as audio output, is difficult. If extension points were done with full access to the APIs available on [`Window`](#722-the-window-object), engines would need to abandon previously-held assumptions for what could happen in the middle of those phases. For example, during the layout phase, rendering engines assume that no DOM will be modified.

Additionally, defining extension points in the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) environment would restrict user agents to performing work in the same thread as the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object. (Unless implementations added complex, high-overhead infrastructure to allow thread-safe APIs, as well as thread-joining guarantees.)

Worklets are designed to allow extension points, while keeping guarantees that user agents currently rely on. This is done through new global environments, based on subclasses of [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope).

Worklets are similar to web workers. However, they:
- Are thread-agnostic. That is, they are not designed to run on a dedicated separate thread, like each worker is. Implementations can run worklets wherever they choose (including on the main thread).
- Are able to have multiple duplicate instances of the global scope created, for the purpose of parallelism.
- Do not use an event-based API. Instead, classes are registered on the global scope, whose methods are invoked by the user agent.
- Have a reduced API surface on the global scope.
- Have a lifetime for their [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) which is defined by other specifications, often in an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) manner.

As worklets have relatively high overhead, they are best used sparingly. Due to this, a given [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope) is expected to be shared between multiple separate scripts. (This is similar to how a single [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) is shared between multiple separate scripts.)

Worklets are a general technology that serve different use cases. Some worklets, such as those defined in CSS Painting API, provide extension points intended for stateless, idempotent, and short-running computations, which have special considerations as described in the next couple of sections. Others, such as those defined in Web Audio API, are used for stateful, long-running operations. [\[CSSPAINT\]](#references) [\[WEBAUDIO\]](#references)

#### 11.1.2 Code idempotence

Some specifications which use worklets are intended to allow user agents to parallelize work over multiple threads, or to move work between threads as required. In these specifications, user agents might invoke methods on a web-developer-provided class in an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) order.

As a result of this, to prevent interoperability issues, authors who register classes on such [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope)s should make their code idempotent. That is, a method or set of methods on the class should produce the same output given a particular input.

This specification uses the following techniques in order to encourage authors to write code in an idempotent way:
- No reference to the global object is available (i.e., there is no counterpart to [`self`](#10211-the-workerglobalscope-common-interface) on [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope)).

  > [!warning]
  > Although this was the intention when worklets were first specified, the introduction of `globalThis` has made it no longer true. See [issue #6059](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/6059) for more discussion.

- Code is loaded as a [module script](#8141-scripts), which results in the code being executed in strict mode and with no shared `this` referencing the global proxy.

Together, these restrictions help prevent two different scripts from sharing state using properties of the [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).

Additionally, specifications which use worklets and intend to allow [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) behavior must obey the following:
- They must require user agents to always have at least two [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope) instances per [`Worklet`](#1132-the-worklet-class), and randomly assign a method or set of methods on a class to a particular [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope) instance. These specifications may provide an opt-out under memory constraints.
- These specifications must allow user agents to create and destroy instances of their [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope) subclasses at any time.

#### 11.1.3 Speculative evaluation

Some specifications which use worklets can invoke methods on a web-developer-provided class based on the state of the user agent. To increase concurrency between threads, a user agent may invoke a method speculatively, based on potential future states.

In these specifications, user agents might invoke such methods at any time, and with any arguments, not just ones corresponding to the current state of the user agent. The results of such speculative evaluations are not displayed immediately, but can be cached for use if the user agent state matches the speculated state. This can increase the concurrency between the user agent and worklet threads.

As a result of this, to prevent interoperability risks between user agents, authors who register classes on such [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope)s should make their code stateless. That is, the only effect of invoking a method should be its result, and not any side effects such as updating mutable state.

The same techniques which encourage [code idempotence](#1112-code-idempotence) also encourage authors to write stateless code.

### 11.2 Examples

*This section is non-normative.*

For these examples, we'll use a fake worklet. The [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object provides two [`Worklet`](#1132-the-worklet-class) instances, which each run code in their own collection of [`FakeWorkletGlobalScope`](#112-examples)s:

```webidl
partial interface Window {
  [SameObject, SecureContext] readonly attribute Worklet fakeWorklet1;
  [SameObject, SecureContext] readonly attribute Worklet fakeWorklet2;
};
```

Each [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) has two [`Worklet`](#1132-the-worklet-class) instances, fake worklet 1 and fake worklet 2. Both of these have their [worklet global scope type](#1132-the-worklet-class) set to [`FakeWorkletGlobalScope`](#112-examples), and their [worklet destination type](#1132-the-worklet-class) set to "`fakeworklet`". User agents should create at least two [`FakeWorkletGlobalScope`](#112-examples) instances per worklet.

> [!note]
> "`fakeworklet`" is not actually a valid [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination) per Fetch. But this illustrates how real worklets would generally have their own worklet-type-specific destination. [\[FETCH\]](#references)

The `fakeWorklet1` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [fake worklet 1](#112-examples).

The `fakeWorklet2` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [fake worklet 2](#112-examples).

---

```webidl
[Global=(Worklet,FakeWorklet),
 Exposed=FakeWorklet,
 SecureContext]
interface FakeWorkletGlobalScope : WorkletGlobalScope {
  undefined registerFake(DOMString type, Function classConstructor);
};
```

Each [`FakeWorkletGlobalScope`](#112-examples) has a registered class constructors map, which is an [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), initially empty.

The `registerFake(type, classConstructor)` method steps are to set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [registered class constructors map](#112-examples)\[type\] to classConstructor.

#### 11.2.1 Loading scripts

*This section is non-normative.*

To load scripts into [fake worklet 1](#112-examples), a web developer would write:

```javascript
window.fakeWorklet1.addModule('script1.mjs');
window.fakeWorklet1.addModule('script2.mjs');
```

Note that which script finishes fetching and runs first is dependent on network timing: it could be either `script1.mjs` or `script2.mjs`. This generally won't matter for well-written scripts intended to be loaded in worklets, if they follow the suggestions about preparing for [speculative evaluation](#1113-speculative-evaluation).

If a web developer wants to perform a task only after the scripts have successfully run and loaded into some worklets, they could write:

```javascript
Promise.all([
    window.fakeWorklet1.addModule('script1.mjs'),
    window.fakeWorklet2.addModule('script2.mjs')
]).then(() => {
    // Do something which relies on those scripts being loaded.
});
```

---

Another important point about script-loading is that loaded scripts can be run in multiple [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope)s per [`Worklet`](#1132-the-worklet-class), as discussed in the section on [code idempotence](#1112-code-idempotence). In particular, the specification above for [fake worklet 1](#112-examples) and [fake worklet 2](#112-examples) require this. So, consider a scenario such as the following:

```javascript
// script.mjs
console.log("Hello from a FakeWorkletGlobalScope!");
```

```javascript
// app.mjs
window.fakeWorklet1.addModule("script.mjs");
```

This could result in output such as the following from a user agent's console:

```
[fakeWorklet1#1] Hello from a FakeWorkletGlobalScope!
[fakeWorklet1#4] Hello from a FakeWorkletGlobalScope!
[fakeWorklet1#2] Hello from a FakeWorkletGlobalScope!
[fakeWorklet1#3] Hello from a FakeWorkletGlobalScope!
```

If the user agent at some point decided to kill and restart the third instance of [`FakeWorkletGlobalScope`](#112-examples), the console would again print `[fakeWorklet1#3] Hello from a FakeWorkletGlobalScope!` when this occurs.

#### 11.2.2 Registering a class and invoking its methods

*This section is non-normative.*

Let's say that one of the intended usages of our fake worklet by web developers is to allow them to customize the highly-complex process of boolean negation. They might register their customization as follows:

```javascript
// script.mjs
registerFake('negation-processor', class {
  process(arg) {
    return !arg;
  }
});
```

```javascript
// app.mjs
window.fakeWorklet1.addModule("script.mjs");
```

To make use of such registered classes, the specification for fake worklets could define a find the opposite of true algorithm, given a [`Worklet`](#1132-the-worklet-class) worklet:
1. Optionally, [create a worklet global scope](#11312-creation-and-termination) for worklet.
2. Let workletGlobalScope be one of worklet's [global scopes](#1132-the-worklet-class), chosen in an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) manner.
3. Let classConstructor be workletGlobalScope's [registered class constructors map](#112-examples)\["`negation-processor`"\].
4. Let classInstance be the result of [constructing](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#construct-a-callback-function) classConstructor, with no arguments.
5. Let function be [Get](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-get-o-p)(classInstance, "`process`"). Rethrow any exceptions.
6. Let callback be the result of [converting](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#es-type-mapping) function to a Web IDL [`Function`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#common-Function) instance.
7. Return the result of [invoking](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invoke-a-callback-function) callback with « true » and "`rethrow`", and with *[callback this value](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-callback-this-value)* set to classInstance.

> [!note]
> Another, perhaps better, specification architecture would be to extract the "`process`" property and convert it into a [`Function`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#common-Function) at registration time, as part of the [`registerFake()`](#112-examples) method steps.

### 11.3 Infrastructure

#### 11.3.1 The global scope

Subclasses of [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope) are used to create [global objects](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) wherein code loaded into a particular [`Worklet`](#1132-the-worklet-class) can execute.

```webidl
[Exposed=Worklet, SecureContext]
interface WorkletGlobalScope {};
```

> [!note]
> Other specifications are intended to subclass [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope), adding APIs to register a class, as well as other APIs specific for their worklet type.

Each [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope) has an associated module map. It is a [module map](#8167-module-related-host-hooks), initially empty.

##### 11.3.1.1 Agents and event loops

*This section is non-normative.*

Each [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope) is contained in its own [worklet agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism), which has its corresponding [event loop](#8171-definitions). However, in practice, implementation of these agents and event loops is expected to be different from most others.

A [worklet agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism) exists for each [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope) since, in theory, an implementation could use a separate thread for each [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope) instance, and allowing this level of parallelism is best done using agents. However, because their \[\[CanBlock\]\] value is false, there is no requirement that agents and threads are one-to-one. This allows implementations the freedom to execute scripts loaded into a worklet on any thread, including one running code from other agents with \[\[CanBlock\]\] of false, such as the thread of a [similar-origin window agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism) ("the main thread"). Contrast this with [dedicated worker agents](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism), whose true value for \[\[CanBlock\]\] effectively requires them to get a dedicated operating system thread.

Worklet [event loops](#8171-definitions) are also somewhat special. They are only used for [tasks](#8171-definitions) associated with [`addModule()`](#1132-the-worklet-class), tasks wherein the user agent invokes author-defined methods, and [microtasks](#8171-definitions). Thus, even though the [event loop processing model](#8173-processing-model) specifies that all event loops run continuously, implementations can achieve observably-equivalent results using a simpler strategy, which just [invokes](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invoke-a-callback-function) author-provided methods and then relies on that process to [perform a microtask checkpoint](#8173-processing-model).

##### 11.3.1.2 Creation and termination

To create a worklet global scope for a [`Worklet`](#1132-the-worklet-class) worklet:
1. Let outsideSettings be worklet's [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant).
