2. Let agent be the result of [obtaining a worklet agent](#8122-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-cluster-formalism) given outsideSettings. Run the rest of these steps in that agent.
3. Let realmExecutionContext be the result of [creating a new realm](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) given agent and the following customizations:
   - For the global object, create a new object of the type given by worklet's [worklet global scope type](#1132-the-worklet-class).
4. Let workletGlobalScope be the [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) of realmExecutionContext's Realm component.
5. Let insideSettings be the result of [setting up a worklet environment settings object](#11313-script-settings-for-worklets) given realmExecutionContext and outsideSettings.
6. Let pendingAddedModules be a [clone](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of worklet's [added modules list](#1132-the-worklet-class).
7. Let runNextAddedModule be the following steps:
   1. If pendingAddedModules [is not empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists):
      1. Let moduleURL be the result of [dequeuing](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#512-queues) from pendingAddedModules.
      2. [Fetch a worklet script graph](#8142-fetching-scripts) given moduleURL, insideSettings, worklet's [worklet destination type](#1132-the-worklet-class), what credentials mode?, insideSettings, worklet's [module responses map](#1132-the-worklet-class), and with the following steps given script:

         > [!note]
         > This will not actually perform a network request, as it will just reuse [responses](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) from worklet's [module responses map](#1132-the-worklet-class). The main purpose of this step is to create a new workletGlobalScope-specific [module script](#8141-scripts) from the [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response).
         1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): script is not null, since the fetch succeeded and the source text was successfully parsed when worklet's [module responses map](#1132-the-worklet-class) was initially populated with moduleURL.
         2. [Run a module script](#8144-calling-scripts) given script.
         3. Run runNextAddedModule.

      3. Abort these steps.

   2. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) workletGlobalScope to outsideSettings's [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [worklet global scopes](#1133-the-worklets-lifetime).
   3. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) workletGlobalScope to worklet's [global scopes](#1132-the-worklet-class).
   4. Run the [responsible event loop](#8132-environment-settings-objects) specified by insideSettings.

8. Run runNextAddedModule.

To terminate a worklet global scope given a [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope) workletGlobalScope:
1. Let eventLoop be workletGlobalScope's [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [event loop](#8171-definitions).
2. If there are any [tasks](#8171-definitions) queued in eventLoop's [task queues](#8171-definitions), discard them without processing them.
3. Wait for eventLoop to complete the [currently running task](#8171-definitions).
4. If the previous step doesn't complete within an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) period of time, then [abort the script](#8145-killing-scripts) currently running in the worklet.
5. Destroy eventLoop.
6. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) workletGlobalScope from the [global scopes](#1132-the-worklet-class) of the [`Worklet`](#1132-the-worklet-class) whose [global scopes](#1132-the-worklet-class) contains workletGlobalScope.
7. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) workletGlobalScope from the [worklet global scopes](#1133-the-worklets-lifetime) of the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) whose [worklet global scopes](#1133-the-worklets-lifetime) contains workletGlobalScope.

##### 11.3.1.3 Script settings for worklets

To set up a worklet environment settings object, given a [JavaScript execution context](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-execution-contexts) executionContext and an [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) outsideSettings:
1. Let origin be a unique [opaque origin](#711-origins).
2. Let inheritedAPIBaseURL be outsideSettings's [API base URL](#8132-environment-settings-objects).
3. Let inheritedPolicyContainer be a [clone](#717-policy-containers) of outsideSettings's [policy container](#8132-environment-settings-objects).
4. Let realm be the value of executionContext's Realm component.
5. Let workletGlobalScope be realm's [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects).
6. Let settingsObject be a new [environment settings object](#8132-environment-settings-objects) whose algorithms are defined as follows:

   The [realm execution context](#8132-environment-settings-objects)

   Return executionContext.

   The [module map](#8132-environment-settings-objects)

   Return workletGlobalScope's [module map](#1131-the-global-scope).

   The [API base URL](#8132-environment-settings-objects)

   Return inheritedAPIBaseURL.

   > [!note]
   > Unlike workers or other globals derived from a single resource, worklets have no primary resource; instead, multiple scripts, each with their own URL, are loaded into the global scope via [`worklet.addModule()`](#1132-the-worklet-class). So this [API base URL](#8132-environment-settings-objects) is rather unlike that of other globals. However, so far this doesn't matter, as no APIs available to worklet code make use of the [API base URL](#8132-environment-settings-objects).

   The [origin](#8132-environment-settings-objects)

   Return origin.

   The [has cross-site ancestor](#8132-environment-settings-objects)

   Return true.

   The [policy container](#8132-environment-settings-objects)

   Return inheritedPolicyContainer.

   The [cross-origin isolated capability](#8132-environment-settings-objects)

   Return outsideSettings's [cross-origin isolated capability](#8132-environment-settings-objects).

   The [time origin](#8132-environment-settings-objects)

   Return outsideSettings's [time origin](#8132-environment-settings-objects).

7. Set settingsObject's [id](#8131-environments) to a new unique opaque string, [creation URL](#8131-environments) to inheritedAPIBaseURL, [top-level creation URL](#8131-environments) to null, [top-level origin](#8131-environments) to outsideSettings's [top-level origin](#8131-environments), [target browsing context](#8131-environments) to null, and [active service worker](#8131-environments) to null.
8. Set realm's \[\[HostDefined\]\] field to settingsObject.
9. Return settingsObject.

#### 11.3.2 The [`Worklet`](#1132-the-worklet-class) class

The [`Worklet`](#1132-the-worklet-class) class provides the capability to add module scripts into its associated [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope)s. The user agent can then create classes registered on the [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope)s and invoke their methods.

```webidl
[Exposed=Window, SecureContext]
interface Worklet {
  [NewObject] Promise<undefined> addModule(USVString moduleURL, optional WorkletOptions options = {});
};

dictionary WorkletOptions {
  RequestCredentials credentials = "same-origin";
};
```

Specifications that create [`Worklet`](#1132-the-worklet-class) instances must specify the following for a given instance:
- its worklet global scope type, which must be a Web IDL type that [inherits](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-inherit) from [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope); and
- its worklet destination type, which must be a [destination](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-destination), and is used when fetching scripts.

`await worklet.addModule(moduleURL[, { credentials }])`

Loads and executes the [module script](#8141-scripts) given by moduleURL into all of worklet's [global scopes](#1132-the-worklet-class). It can also create additional global scopes as part of this process, depending on the worklet type. The returned promise will fulfill once the script has been successfully loaded and run in all global scopes.

The [`credentials`](#1132-the-worklet-class) option can be set to a [credentials mode](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-credentials-mode) to modify the script-fetching process. It defaults to "`same-origin`".

Any failures in [fetching](#8142-fetching-scripts) the script or its dependencies will cause the returned promise to be rejected with an ["`AbortError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#aborterror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException). Any errors in parsing the script or its dependencies will cause the returned promise to be rejected with the exception generated during parsing.

A [`Worklet`](#1132-the-worklet-class) has a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of global scopes, which contains instances of the [`Worklet`](#1132-the-worklet-class)'s [worklet global scope type](#1132-the-worklet-class). It is initially empty.

A [`Worklet`](#1132-the-worklet-class) has an added modules list, which is a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [URLs](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url), initially empty. Access to this list should be thread-safe.

A [`Worklet`](#1132-the-worklet-class) has a module responses map, which is an [ordered map](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) from [URLs](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) to either "`fetching`" or [tuples](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#531-tuples) consisting of a [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) and either null, failure, or a [byte sequence](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-byte-sequences) representing the response body. This map is initially empty, and access to it should be thread-safe.

> [!note]
> The [added modules list](#1132-the-worklet-class) and [module responses map](#1132-the-worklet-class) exist to ensure that [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope)s created at different times get equivalent [module scripts](#8141-scripts) run in them, based on the same source text. This allows the creation of additional [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope)s to be transparent to the author.
> 
> In practice, user agents are not expected to implement these data structures, and the algorithms that consult them, using thread-safe programming techniques. Instead, when [`addModule()`](#1132-the-worklet-class) is called, user agents can fetch the module graph on the main thread, and send the fetched source text (i.e., the important data contained in the [module responses map](#1132-the-worklet-class)) to each thread which has a [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope).
> 
> Then, when a user agent [creates](#11312-creation-and-termination) a new [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope) for a given [`Worklet`](#1132-the-worklet-class), it can simply send the map of fetched source text and the list of entry points from the main thread to the thread containing the new [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope).

The `addModule(moduleURL,
  options)` method steps are:
1. Let outsideSettings be the [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant) of [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
2. Let moduleURLRecord be the result of [encoding-parsing a URL](#242-parsing-urls) given moduleURL, relative to outsideSettings.
3. If moduleURLRecord is failure, then return [a promise rejected with](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#a-promise-rejected-with) a ["`SyntaxError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
4. Let promise be a new promise.
5. Let workletInstance be [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
6. Run the following steps [in parallel](#211-parallelism):
   1. If workletInstance's [global scopes](#1132-the-worklet-class) [is empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists):
      1. [Create a worklet global scope](#11312-creation-and-termination) given workletInstance.
      2. Optionally, [create](#11312-creation-and-termination) additional global scope instances given workletInstance, depending on the specific worklet in question and its specification.
      3. Wait for all steps of the [creation](#11312-creation-and-termination) process(es) — including those taking place within the [worklet agents](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism) — to complete, before moving on.
   2. Let pendingTasks be workletInstance's [global scopes](#1132-the-worklet-class)'s [size](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).
   3. Let addedSuccessfully be false.
   4. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) workletGlobalScope of workletInstance's [global scopes](#1132-the-worklet-class), [queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given workletGlobalScope to [fetch a worklet script graph](#8142-fetching-scripts) given moduleURLRecord, outsideSettings, workletInstance's [worklet destination type](#1132-the-worklet-class), options\["[`credentials`](#1132-the-worklet-class)"\], workletGlobalScope's [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant), workletInstance's [module responses map](#1132-the-worklet-class), and the following steps given script:

      > [!note]
      > Only the first of these fetches will actually perform a network request; the ones for other [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope)s will reuse [responses](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) from workletInstance's [module responses map](#1132-the-worklet-class).
      1. If script is null:
         1. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given workletInstance's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) to perform the following steps:
            1. If pendingTasks is not −1:
               1. Set pendingTasks to −1.
               2. Reject promise with an ["`AbortError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#aborterror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
         2. Abort these steps.
      2. If script's [error to rethrow](#8141-scripts) is not null:
         1. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given workletInstance's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) to perform the following steps:
            1. If pendingTasks is not −1:
               1. Set pendingTasks to −1.
               2. Reject promise with script's [error to rethrow](#8141-scripts).
         2. Abort these steps.
      3. If addedSuccessfully is false:
         1. [Append](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) moduleURLRecord to workletInstance's [added modules list](#1132-the-worklet-class).
         2. Set addedSuccessfully to true.
      4. [Run a module script](#8144-calling-scripts) given script.
      5. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [networking task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given workletInstance's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) to perform the following steps:
         1. If pendingTasks is not −1:
            1. Set pendingTasks to pendingTasks − 1.
            2. If pendingTasks is 0, then resolve promise.

7. Return promise.

#### 11.3.3 The worklet's lifetime

The lifetime of a [`Worklet`](#1132-the-worklet-class) has no special considerations; it is tied to the object it belongs to, such as the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object).

Each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a worklet global scopes, which is a [set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#513-sets) of [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope)s, initially empty.

The lifetime of a [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope) is, at a minimum, tied to the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) whose [worklet global scopes](#1133-the-worklets-lifetime) contain it. In particular, [destroying](#7510-destroying-documents) the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) will [terminate](#11312-creation-and-termination) the corresponding [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope) and allow it to be garbage-collected.

Additionally, user agents may, at any time, [terminate](#11312-creation-and-termination) a given [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope), unless the specification defining the corresponding worklet type says otherwise. For example, they might terminate them if the [worklet agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [event loop](#8171-definitions) has no [tasks](#8171-definitions) queued, or if the user agent has no pending operations planning to make use of the worklet, or if the user agent detects abnormal operations such as infinite loops or callbacks exceeding imposed time limits.

Finally, specifications for specific worklet types can give more specific details on when to [create](#11312-creation-and-termination) [`WorkletGlobalScope`](#1131-the-global-scope)s for a given worklet type. For example, they might create them during specific processes that call upon worklet code, as in the [example](#1122-registering-a-class-and-invoking-its-methods).

## 12 Web storage

### 12.1 Introduction

*This section is non-normative.*

This specification introduces two related mechanisms, similar to HTTP session cookies, for storing name-value pairs on the client side. [\[COOKIES\]](#references)

The first is designed for scenarios where the user is carrying out a single transaction, but could be carrying out multiple transactions in different windows at the same time.

Cookies don't really handle this case well. For example, a user could be buying plane tickets in two different windows, using the same site. If the site used cookies to keep track of which ticket the user was buying, then as the user clicked from page to page in both windows, the ticket currently being purchased would "leak" from one window to the other, potentially causing the user to buy two tickets for the same flight without noticing.

To address this, this specification introduces the [`sessionStorage`](#1222-the-sessionstorage-getter) getter. Sites can add data to the session storage, and it will be accessible to any page from the same site opened in that window.

> [!example]
> For example, a page could have a checkbox that the user ticks to indicate that they want insurance:
> 
> ```html
> <label>
>  <input type="checkbox" onchange="sessionStorage.insurance = checked ? 'true' : ''">
>   I want insurance on this trip.
> </label>
> ```
> 
> A later page could then check, from script, whether the user had checked the checkbox or not:
> 
> ```javascript
> if (sessionStorage.insurance) { ... }
> ```
> 
> If the user had multiple windows opened on the site, each one would have its own individual copy of the session storage object.

The second storage mechanism is designed for storage that spans multiple windows, and lasts beyond the current session. In particular, web applications might wish to store megabytes of user data, such as entire user-authored documents or a user's mailbox, on the client side for performance reasons.

Again, cookies do not handle this case well, because they are transmitted with every request.

The [`localStorage`](#1223-the-localstorage-getter) getter is used to access a page's local storage area.

> [!example]
> The site at example.com can display a count of how many times the user has loaded its page by putting the following at the bottom of its page:
> 
> ```html
> <p>
>   You have viewed this page
>   <span id="count">an untold number of</span>
>   time(s).
> </p>
> <script>
>   if (!localStorage.pageLoadCount)
>     localStorage.pageLoadCount = 0;
>   localStorage.pageLoadCount = parseInt(localStorage.pageLoadCount) + 1;
>   document.getElementById('count').textContent = localStorage.pageLoadCount;
> </script>
> ```

Each site has its own separate storage area.

> [!warning]
> The [`localStorage`](#1223-the-localstorage-getter) getter provides access to shared state. This specification does not define the interaction with other agent clusters in a multiprocess user agent, and authors are encouraged to assume that there is no locking mechanism. A site could, for instance, try to read the value of a key, increment its value, then write it back out, using the new value as a unique identifier for the session; if the site does this twice in two different browser windows at the same time, it might end up using the same "unique" identifier for both sessions, with potentially disastrous effects.

### 12.2 The API

#### 12.2.1 The [`Storage`](#1221-the-storage-interface) interface

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface Storage {
  readonly attribute unsigned long length;
  DOMString? key(unsigned long index);
  getter DOMString? getItem(DOMString key);
  setter undefined setItem(DOMString key, DOMString value);
  deleter undefined removeItem(DOMString key);
  undefined clear();
};
```

`storage.length`

Returns the number of key/value pairs.

`storage.key (n)`

Returns the name of the nth key, or null if n is greater than or equal to the number of key/value pairs.

`value = storage.getItem (key)`

Returns the current value associated with the given key, or null if the given key does not exist.

`value = storage[key]`

Returns the current value associated with the given key, or undefined if the given key does not exist.

`storage.setItem (key, value)`

`storage[key] = value`

Sets the value of the pair identified by key to value, creating a new key/value pair if none existed for key previously.

Throws a [`QuotaExceededError`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#quotaexceedederror) if the new value couldn't be set. (Setting could fail if, e.g., the user has disabled storage for the site, or if the quota has been exceeded.)

Dispatches a [`storage`](#events) event on [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) objects holding an equivalent [`Storage`](#1221-the-storage-interface) object.

`storage.removeItem (key)`

[`delete`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-delete-operator) storage\[key\]

Removes the key/value pair with the given key, if a key/value pair with the given key exists.

Dispatches a [`storage`](#events) event on [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) objects holding an equivalent [`Storage`](#1221-the-storage-interface) object.

`storage.clear()`

Removes all key/value pairs, if there are any.

Dispatches a [`storage`](#events) event on [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) objects holding an equivalent [`Storage`](#1221-the-storage-interface) object.

A [`Storage`](#1221-the-storage-interface) object has an associated:

map

A [storage proxy map](https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#storage-proxy-map).

type

"`local`" or "`session`".

To reorder a [`Storage`](#1221-the-storage-interface) object storage, reorder storage's [map](#1221-the-storage-interface)'s [entries](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) in an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) manner.

> [!note]
> Unfortunate as it is, iteration order is not defined and can change upon most mutations.

To broadcast a [`Storage`](#1221-the-storage-interface) object storage, given a key, oldValue, and newValue, run these steps:
1. Let thisDocument be storage's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object).
2. Let url be the [serialization](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-serializer) of thisDocument's [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).
3. Let remoteStorages be all [`Storage`](#1221-the-storage-interface) objects excluding storage whose:
   - [type](#1221-the-storage-interface) is storage's [type](#1221-the-storage-interface)
   - [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant)'s [origin](#711-origins) is [same origin](#711-origins) with storage's [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant)'s [origin](#711-origins)

   and, if [type](#1221-the-storage-interface) is "`session`", whose [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [node navigable](#731-navigables)'s [traversable navigable](#7311-traversable-navigables) is thisDocument's [node navigable](#731-navigables)'s [traversable navigable](#7311-traversable-navigables).

4. [For each](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) remoteStorage of remoteStorages: [queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given remoteStorage's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`storage`](#events) at remoteStorage's [relevant global object](#81334-relevant), using [`StorageEvent`](#1224-the-storageevent-interface), with [`key`](#1224-the-storageevent-interface) initialized to key, [`oldValue`](#1224-the-storageevent-interface) initialized to oldValue, [`newValue`](#1224-the-storageevent-interface) initialized to newValue, [`url`](#1224-the-storageevent-interface) initialized to url, and [`storageArea`](#1224-the-storageevent-interface) initialized to remoteStorage.

   > [!note]
   > The [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object associated with the resulting [task](#8171-definitions) is not necessarily [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents), but events fired on such objects are ignored by the [event loop](#8171-definitions) until the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) becomes [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents) again.

---

The `length` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [map](#1221-the-storage-interface)'s [size](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps).

The `key(index)` method steps are:
1. If index is greater than or equal to [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [map](#1221-the-storage-interface)'s [size](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then return null.
2. Let keys be the result of running [get the keys](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) on [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [map](#1221-the-storage-interface).
3. Return keys\[index\].

The [supported property names](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-supported-property-names) on a [`Storage`](#1221-the-storage-interface) object storage are the result of running [get the keys](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) on storage's [map](#1221-the-storage-interface).

The `getItem(key)` method steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [map](#1221-the-storage-interface)\[key\] does not [exist](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then return null.
2. Return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [map](#1221-the-storage-interface)\[key\].

The `setItem(key,
  value)` method steps are:
1. Let oldValue be null.
2. Let reorder be true.
3. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [map](#1221-the-storage-interface)\[key\] [exists](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps):
   1. Set oldValue to [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [map](#1221-the-storage-interface)\[key\].
   2. If oldValue [is](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) value, then return.
   3. Set reorder to false.
4. If value cannot be stored, then throw a [`QuotaExceededError`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#quotaexceedederror).
5. [Set](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [map](#1221-the-storage-interface)\[key\] to value.
6. If reorder is true, then [reorder](#1221-the-storage-interface) [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
7. [Broadcast](#1221-the-storage-interface) [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) with key, oldValue, and value.

The `removeItem(key)` method steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [map](#1221-the-storage-interface)\[key\] does not [exist](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then return.
2. Set oldValue to [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [map](#1221-the-storage-interface)\[key\].
3. [Remove](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [map](#1221-the-storage-interface)\[key\].
4. [Reorder](#1221-the-storage-interface) [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this).
5. [Broadcast](#1221-the-storage-interface) [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) with key, oldValue, and null.

The `clear()` method steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [map](#1221-the-storage-interface) is [empty](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps), then return.
2. [Clear](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#52-maps) [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [map](#1221-the-storage-interface).
3. [Broadcast](#1221-the-storage-interface) [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this) with null, null, and null.

#### 12.2.2 The [`sessionStorage`](#1222-the-sessionstorage-getter) getter

```webidl
interface mixin WindowSessionStorage {
  readonly attribute Storage sessionStorage;
};
Window includes WindowSessionStorage;
```

`window.sessionStorage`

Returns the [`Storage`](#1221-the-storage-interface) object associated with that window's origin's session storage area.

Throws a ["`SecurityError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is an [opaque origin](#711-origins) or if the request violates a policy decision (e.g., if the user agent is configured to not allow the page to persist data).

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object has an associated session storage holder, which is null or a [`Storage`](#1221-the-storage-interface) object. It is initially null.

[![(This is a tracking vector.)](https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg)](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#24-privacy-concerns) The `sessionStorage` getter steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [session storage holder](#1222-the-sessionstorage-getter) is non-null, then return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [session storage holder](#1222-the-sessionstorage-getter).
2. Let map be the result of running [obtain a session storage bottle map](https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#obtain-a-session-storage-bottle-map) with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant) and "`sessionStorage`".
3. If map is failure, then throw a ["`SecurityError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
4. Let storage be a new [`Storage`](#1221-the-storage-interface) object whose [map](#1221-the-storage-interface) is map.
5. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [session storage holder](#1222-the-sessionstorage-getter) to storage.
6. Return storage.

> [!note]
> After [creating a new auxiliary browsing context and document](#7321-creating-browsing-contexts), the session storage [is copied](#7312-top-level-traversables) over.

#### 12.2.3 The [`localStorage`](#1223-the-localstorage-getter) getter

```webidl
interface mixin WindowLocalStorage {
  readonly attribute Storage localStorage;
};
Window includes WindowLocalStorage;
```

`window.localStorage`

Returns the [`Storage`](#1221-the-storage-interface) object associated with window's origin's local storage area.

Throws a ["`SecurityError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) if the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is an [opaque origin](#711-origins) or if the request violates a policy decision (e.g., if the user agent is configured to not allow the page to persist data).

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object has an associated local storage holder, which is null or a [`Storage`](#1221-the-storage-interface) object. It is initially null.

[![(This is a tracking vector.)](https://resources.whatwg.org/tracking-vector.svg)](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#24-privacy-concerns) The `localStorage` getter steps are:
1. If [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [local storage holder](#1223-the-localstorage-getter) is non-null, then return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [local storage holder](#1223-the-localstorage-getter).
2. Let map be the result of running [obtain a local storage bottle map](https://storage.spec.whatwg.org/#obtain-a-local-storage-bottle-map) with [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant) and "`localStorage`".
3. If map is failure, then throw a ["`SecurityError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#securityerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
4. Let storage be a new [`Storage`](#1221-the-storage-interface) object whose [map](#1221-the-storage-interface) is map.
5. Set [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object)'s [local storage holder](#1223-the-localstorage-getter) to storage.
6. Return storage.

#### 12.2.4 The [`StorageEvent`](#1224-the-storageevent-interface) interface

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface StorageEvent : Event {
  constructor(DOMString type, optional StorageEventInit eventInitDict = {});

  readonly attribute DOMString? key;
  readonly attribute DOMString? oldValue;
  readonly attribute DOMString? newValue;
  readonly attribute USVString url;
  readonly attribute Storage? storageArea;

  undefined initStorageEvent(DOMString type, optional boolean bubbles = false, optional boolean cancelable = false, optional DOMString? key = null, optional DOMString? oldValue = null, optional DOMString? newValue = null, optional USVString url = "", optional Storage? storageArea = null);
};

dictionary StorageEventInit : EventInit {
  DOMString? key = null;
  DOMString? oldValue = null;
  DOMString? newValue = null;
  USVString url = "";
  Storage? storageArea = null;
};
```

`event.key`

Returns the key of the storage item being changed.

`event.oldValue`

Returns the old value of the key of the storage item whose value is being changed.

`event.newValue`

Returns the new value of the key of the storage item whose value is being changed.

`event.url`

Returns the [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) of the document whose storage item changed.

`event.storageArea`

Returns the [`Storage`](#1221-the-storage-interface) object that was affected.

The `key`, `oldValue`, `newValue`, `url`, and `storageArea` attributes must return the values they were initialized to.

The `initStorageEvent(type, bubbles,
  cancelable, key, oldValue, newValue, url,
  storageArea)` method must initialize the event in a manner analogous to the similarly-named [`initEvent()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) method. [\[DOM\]](#references)

### 12.3 Privacy

#### 12.3.1 User tracking

A third-party advertiser (or any entity capable of getting content distributed to multiple sites) could use a unique identifier stored in its local storage area to track a user across multiple sessions, building a profile of the user's interests to allow for highly targeted advertising. In conjunction with a site that is aware of the user's real identity (for example an e-commerce site that requires authenticated credentials), this could allow oppressive groups to target individuals with greater accuracy than in a world with purely anonymous web usage.

There are a number of techniques that can be used to mitigate the risk of user tracking:

Blocking third-party storage

User agents may restrict access to the [`localStorage`](#1223-the-localstorage-getter) objects to scripts originating at the domain of the [active document](#731-navigables) of the [top-level traversable](#7312-top-level-traversables), for instance denying access to the API for pages from other domains running in [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element)s.

Expiring stored data

User agents may, possibly in a manner configured by the user, automatically delete stored data after a period of time.

For example, a user agent could be configured to treat third-party local storage areas as session-only storage, deleting the data once the user had closed all the [navigables](#731-navigables) that could access it.

This can restrict the ability of a site to track a user, as the site would then only be able to track the user across multiple sessions when they authenticate with the site itself (e.g. by making a purchase or logging in to a service).

However, this also reduces the usefulness of the API as a long-term storage mechanism. It can also put the user's data at risk, if the user does not fully understand the implications of data expiration.

Treating persistent storage as cookies

If users attempt to protect their privacy by clearing cookies without also clearing data stored in the local storage area, sites can defeat those attempts by using the two features as redundant backup for each other. User agents should present the interfaces for clearing these in a way that helps users to understand this possibility and enables them to delete data in all persistent storage features simultaneously. [\[COOKIES\]](#references)

Site-specific safelisting of access to local storage areas

User agents may allow sites to access session storage areas in an unrestricted manner, but require the user to authorize access to local storage areas.

Origin-tracking of stored data

User agents may record the [origins](#711-origins) of sites that contained content from third-party origins that caused data to be stored.

If this information is then used to present the view of data currently in persistent storage, it would allow the user to make informed decisions about which parts of the persistent storage to prune. Combined with a blocklist ("delete this data and prevent this domain from ever storing data again"), the user can restrict the use of persistent storage to sites that they trust.

Shared blocklists

User agents may allow users to share their persistent storage domain blocklists.

This would allow communities to act together to protect their privacy.

While these suggestions prevent trivial use of this API for user tracking, they do not block it altogether. Within a single domain, a site can continue to track the user during a session, and can then pass all this information to the third party along with any identifying information (names, credit card numbers, addresses) obtained by the site. If a third party cooperates with multiple sites to obtain such information, a profile can still be created.

However, user tracking is to some extent possible even with no cooperation from the user agent whatsoever, for instance by using session identifiers in URLs, a technique already commonly used for innocuous purposes but easily repurposed for user tracking (even retroactively). This information can then be shared with other sites, using visitors' IP addresses and other user-specific data (e.g. user-agent headers and configuration settings) to combine separate sessions into coherent user profiles.

#### 12.3.2 Sensitivity of data

User agents should treat persistently stored data as potentially sensitive; it's quite possible for emails, calendar appointments, health records, or other confidential documents to be stored in this mechanism.

To this end, user agents should ensure that when deleting data, it is promptly deleted from the underlying storage.

### 12.4 Security

#### 12.4.1 DNS spoofing attacks

Because of the potential for DNS spoofing attacks, one cannot guarantee that a host claiming to be in a certain domain really is from that domain. To mitigate this, pages can use TLS. Pages using TLS can be sure that only the user, software working on behalf of the user, and other pages using TLS that have certificates identifying them as being from the same domain, can access their storage areas.

#### 12.4.2 Cross-directory attacks

Different authors sharing one host name, for example users hosting content on the now defunct `geocities.com`, all share one local storage object. There is no feature to restrict the access by pathname. Authors on shared hosts are therefore urged to avoid using these features, as it would be trivial for other authors to read the data and overwrite it.

> [!note]
> Even if a path-restriction feature was made available, the usual DOM scripting security model would make it trivial to bypass this protection and access the data from any path.

#### 12.4.3 Implementation risks

The two primary risks when implementing these persistent storage features are letting hostile sites read information from other domains, and letting hostile sites write information that is then read from other domains.

Letting third-party sites read data that is not supposed to be read from their domain causes *information leakage*. For example, a user's shopping wishlist on one domain could be used by another domain for targeted advertising; or a user's work-in-progress confidential documents stored by a word-processing site could be examined by the site of a competing company.

Letting third-party sites write data to the persistent storage of other domains can result in *information spoofing*, which is equally dangerous. For example, a hostile site could add items to a user's wishlist; or a hostile site could set a user's session identifier to a known ID that the hostile site can then use to track the user's actions on the victim site.

Thus, strictly following the [origin](#711-origins) model described in this specification is important for user security.

## 13 The HTML syntax

> [!note]
> This section only describes the rules for resources labeled with an [HTML MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#html-mime-type). Rules for XML resources are discussed in the section below entitled "[The XML syntax](#14-the-xml-syntax)".

### 13.1 Writing HTML documents

*This section only applies to documents, authoring tools, and markup generators. In particular, it does not apply to conformance checkers; conformance checkers must use the requirements given in the next section ("parsing HTML documents").*

Documents must consist of the following parts, in the given order:
1. Optionally, a single U+FEFF BYTE ORDER MARK (BOM) character.
2. Any number of [comments](#1316-comments) and [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).
3. A [DOCTYPE](#1311-the-doctype).
4. Any number of [comments](#1316-comments) and [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).
5. The [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree), in the form of an [`html`](#411-the-html-element) [element](#1312-elements).
6. Any number of [comments](#1316-comments) and [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).

The various types of content mentioned above are described in the next few sections.

In addition, there are some restrictions on how [character encoding declarations](#4254-specifying-the-documents-character-encoding) are to be serialized, as discussed in the section on that topic.

> [!note]
> [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) before the [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element, at the start of the [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element and before the [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element, will be dropped when the document is parsed; [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) *after* the [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element will be parsed as if it were at the end of the [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element. Thus, [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) around the [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) does not roundtrip.
> 
> It is suggested that newlines be inserted after the DOCTYPE, after any comments that are before the document element, after the [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element's start tag (if it is not [omitted](#13124-optional-tags)), and after any comments that are inside the [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element but before the [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element.

Many strings in the HTML syntax (e.g. the names of elements and their attributes) are case-insensitive, but only for [ASCII upper alphas](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) and [ASCII lower alphas](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points). For convenience, in this section this is just referred to as "case-insensitive".

#### 13.1.1 The DOCTYPE

A DOCTYPE is a required preamble.

> [!note]
> DOCTYPEs are required for legacy reasons. When omitted, browsers tend to use a different rendering mode that is incompatible with some specifications. Including the DOCTYPE in a document ensures that the browser makes a best-effort attempt at following the relevant specifications.

A DOCTYPE must consist of the following components, in this order:
1. A string that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`<!DOCTYPE`".
2. One or more [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).
3. A string that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`html`".
4. Optionally, a [DOCTYPE legacy string](#1311-the-doctype).
5. Zero or more [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).
6. A U+003E GREATER-THAN SIGN character (>).

> [!note]
> In other words, `<!DOCTYPE html>`, case-insensitively.

---

For the purposes of HTML generators that cannot output HTML markup with the short DOCTYPE "`<!DOCTYPE html>`", a DOCTYPE legacy string may be inserted into the DOCTYPE (in the position defined above). This string must consist of:
1. One or more [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).
2. A string that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`SYSTEM`".
3. One or more [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).
4. A U+0022 QUOTATION MARK or U+0027 APOSTROPHE character (the *quote mark*).
5. The literal string "[`about:legacy-compat`](#241-terminology)".
6. A matching U+0022 QUOTATION MARK or U+0027 APOSTROPHE character (i.e. the same character as in the earlier step labeled *quote mark*).

> [!note]
> In other words, `<!DOCTYPE html SYSTEM "about:legacy-compat">` or `<!DOCTYPE html SYSTEM 'about:legacy-compat'>`, case-insensitively except for the part in single or double quotes.

The [DOCTYPE legacy string](#1311-the-doctype) should not be used unless the document is generated from a system that cannot output the shorter string.

#### 13.1.2 Elements

There are six different kinds of elements: [void elements](#1312-elements), [the `template` element](#1312-elements), [raw text elements](#1312-elements), [escapable raw text elements](#1312-elements), [foreign elements](#1312-elements), and [normal elements](#1312-elements).

Void elements

[`area`](#4813-the-area-element), [`base`](#423-the-base-element), [`br`](#4527-the-br-element), [`col`](#494-the-col-element), [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element), [`hr`](#442-the-hr-element), [`img`](#483-the-img-element), [`input`](#4105-the-input-element), [`link`](#424-the-link-element), [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element), [`source`](#482-the-source-element), [`track`](#4810-the-track-element), [`wbr`](#4528-the-wbr-element)

The `template` element

[`template`](#4123-the-template-element)

Raw text elements

[`script`](#4121-the-script-element), [`style`](#426-the-style-element)

Escapable raw text elements

[`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element), [`title`](#422-the-title-element)

Foreign elements

Elements from the [MathML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) and the [SVG namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces).

Normal elements

All other allowed [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) are normal elements.

Tags are used to delimit the start and end of elements in the markup. [Raw text](#1312-elements), [escapable raw text](#1312-elements), and [normal](#1312-elements) elements have a [start tag](#13121-start-tags) to indicate where they begin, and an [end tag](#13122-end-tags) to indicate where they end. The start and end tags of certain [normal elements](#1312-elements) can be [omitted](#13124-optional-tags), as described below in the section on [optional tags](#13124-optional-tags). Those that cannot be omitted must not be omitted. [Void elements](#1312-elements) only have a start tag; end tags must not be specified for [void elements](#1312-elements). [Foreign elements](#1312-elements) must either have a start tag and an end tag, or a start tag that is marked as self-closing, in which case they must not have an end tag.

The [contents](#325-content-models) of the element must be placed between just after the start tag (which [might be implied, in certain cases](#13124-optional-tags)) and just before the end tag (which again, [might be implied in certain cases](#13124-optional-tags)). The exact allowed contents of each individual element depend on the [content model](#325-content-models) of that element, as described earlier in this specification. Elements must not contain content that their content model disallows. In addition to the restrictions placed on the contents by those content models, however, the five types of elements have additional *syntactic* requirements.

[Void elements](#1312-elements) can't have any contents (since there's no end tag, no content can be put between the start tag and the end tag).

[The `template` element](#1312-elements) can have [template contents](#4123-the-template-element), but such [template contents](#4123-the-template-element) are not children of the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element itself. Instead, they are stored in a [`DocumentFragment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) associated with a different [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) — without a [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) — so as to avoid the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) contents interfering with the main [`Document`](#311-the-document-object). The markup for the [template contents](#4123-the-template-element) of a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element is placed just after the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element's start tag and just before [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element's end tag (as with other elements), and may consist of any [text](#1313-text), [character references](#1314-character-references), [elements](#1312-elements), and [comments](#1316-comments), but the text must not contain the character U+003C LESS-THAN SIGN (<) or an [ambiguous ampersand](#1314-character-references).

[Raw text elements](#1312-elements) can have [text](#1313-text), though it has [restrictions](#13126-restrictions-on-the-contents-of-raw-text-and-escapable-raw-text-elements) described below.

[Escapable raw text elements](#1312-elements) can have [text](#1313-text) and [character references](#1314-character-references), but the text must not contain an [ambiguous ampersand](#1314-character-references). There are also [further restrictions](#13126-restrictions-on-the-contents-of-raw-text-and-escapable-raw-text-elements) described below.

[Foreign elements](#1312-elements) whose start tag is marked as self-closing can't have any contents (since, again, as there's no end tag, no content can be put between the start tag and the end tag). [Foreign elements](#1312-elements) whose start tag is *not* marked as self-closing can have [text](#1313-text), [character references](#1314-character-references), [CDATA sections](#1315-cdata-sections), other [elements](#1312-elements), and [comments](#1316-comments), but the text must not contain the character U+003C LESS-THAN SIGN (<) or an [ambiguous ampersand](#1314-character-references).

> [!note]
> The HTML syntax does not support namespace declarations, even in [foreign elements](#1312-elements).
> 
> For instance, consider the following HTML fragment:
> 
> ```html
> <p>
>  <svg>
>   <metadata>
>    <!-- this is invalid -->
>    <cdr:license xmlns:cdr="https://www.example.com/cdr/metadata" name="MIT"/>
>   </metadata>
>  </svg>
> </p>
> ```
> 
> The innermost element, `cdr:license`, is actually in the SVG namespace, as the "`xmlns:cdr`" attribute has no effect (unlike in XML). In fact, as the comment in the fragment above says, the fragment is actually non-conforming. This is because SVG 2 does not define any elements called "`cdr:license`" in the SVG namespace.

[Normal elements](#1312-elements) can have [text](#1313-text), [character references](#1314-character-references), other [elements](#1312-elements), and [comments](#1316-comments), but the text must not contain the character U+003C LESS-THAN SIGN (<) or an [ambiguous ampersand](#1314-character-references). Some [normal elements](#1312-elements) also have [yet more restrictions](#13125-restrictions-on-content-models) on what content they are allowed to hold, beyond the restrictions imposed by the content model and those described in this paragraph. Those restrictions are described below.

Tags contain a tag name, giving the element's name. HTML elements all have names that only use [ASCII alphanumerics](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points). In the HTML syntax, tag names, even those for [foreign elements](#1312-elements), may be written with any mix of lower- and uppercase letters that, when converted to all-lowercase, matches the element's tag name; tag names are case-insensitive.

##### 13.1.2.1 Start tags

Start tags must have the following format:
1. The first character of a start tag must be a U+003C LESS-THAN SIGN character (<).
2. The next few characters of a start tag must be the element's [tag name](#1312-elements).
3. If there are to be any attributes in the next step, there must first be one or more [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).
4. Then, the start tag may have a number of attributes, the [syntax for which](#13123-attributes) is described below. Attributes must be separated from each other by one or more [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).
5. After the attributes, or after the [tag name](#1312-elements) if there are no attributes, there may be one or more [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points). (Some attributes are required to be followed by a space. See the [attributes section](#13123-attributes) below.)
6. Then, if the element is one of the [void elements](#1312-elements), or if the element is a [foreign element](#1312-elements), then there may be a single U+002F SOLIDUS character (/), which on [foreign elements](#1312-elements) marks the start tag as self-closing. On [void elements](#1312-elements), it does not mark the start tag as self-closing but instead is unnecessary and has no effect of any kind. For such void elements, it should be used only with caution — especially since, if directly preceded by an [unquoted attribute value](#13123-attributes), it becomes part of the attribute value rather than being discarded by the parser.
7. Finally, start tags must be closed by a U+003E GREATER-THAN SIGN character (>).

##### 13.1.2.2 End tags

End tags must have the following format:
1. The first character of an end tag must be a U+003C LESS-THAN SIGN character (<).
2. The second character of an end tag must be a U+002F SOLIDUS character (/).
3. The next few characters of an end tag must be the element's [tag name](#1312-elements).
4. After the tag name, there may be one or more [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).
5. Finally, end tags must be closed by a U+003E GREATER-THAN SIGN character (>).

##### 13.1.2.3 Attributes

Attributes for an element are expressed inside the element's start tag.

Attributes have a name and a value. Attribute names must consist of one or more characters other than [controls](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), U+0020 SPACE, U+0022 ("), U+0027 ('), U+003E (>), U+002F (/), U+003D (=), and [noncharacters](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points). In the HTML syntax, attribute names, even those for [foreign elements](#1312-elements), may be written with any mix of [ASCII lower](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) and [ASCII upper alphas](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).

Attribute values are a mixture of [text](#1313-text) and [character references](#1314-character-references), except with the additional restriction that the text cannot contain an [ambiguous ampersand](#1314-character-references).

Attributes can be specified in four different ways:

Empty attribute syntax

Just the [attribute name](#13123-attributes). The value is implicitly the empty string.

> [!example]
> In the following example, the [`disabled`](#410195-enabling-and-disabling-form-controls-the-disabled-attribute) attribute is given with the empty attribute syntax:
> 
> ```html
> <input disabled>
> ```

If an attribute using the empty attribute syntax is to be followed by another attribute, then there must be [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) separating the two.

Unquoted attribute value syntax

The [attribute name](#13123-attributes), followed by zero or more [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), followed by a single U+003D EQUALS SIGN character, followed by zero or more [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), followed by the [attribute value](#13123-attributes), which, in addition to the requirements given above for attribute values, must not contain any literal [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), any U+0022 QUOTATION MARK characters ("), U+0027 APOSTROPHE characters ('), U+003D EQUALS SIGN characters (=), U+003C LESS-THAN SIGN characters (<), U+003E GREATER-THAN SIGN characters (>), or U+0060 GRAVE ACCENT characters (\`), and must not be the empty string.

> [!example]
> In the following example, the [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is given with the unquoted attribute value syntax:
> 
> ```html
> <input value=yes>
> ```

If an attribute using the unquoted attribute syntax is to be followed by another attribute or by the optional U+002F SOLIDUS character (/) allowed in step 6 of the [start tag](#13121-start-tags) syntax above, then there must be [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) separating the two.

Single-quoted attribute value syntax

The [attribute name](#13123-attributes), followed by zero or more [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), followed by a single U+003D EQUALS SIGN character, followed by zero or more [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), followed by a single U+0027 APOSTROPHE character ('), followed by the [attribute value](#13123-attributes), which, in addition to the requirements given above for attribute values, must not contain any literal U+0027 APOSTROPHE characters ('), and finally followed by a second single U+0027 APOSTROPHE character (').

> [!example]
> In the following example, the [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is given with the single-quoted attribute value syntax:
> 
> ```html
> <input type='checkbox'>
> ```

If an attribute using the single-quoted attribute syntax is to be followed by another attribute, then there must be [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) separating the two.

Double-quoted attribute value syntax

The [attribute name](#13123-attributes), followed by zero or more [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), followed by a single U+003D EQUALS SIGN character, followed by zero or more [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), followed by a single U+0022 QUOTATION MARK character ("), followed by the [attribute value](#13123-attributes), which, in addition to the requirements given above for attribute values, must not contain any literal U+0022 QUOTATION MARK characters ("), and finally followed by a second single U+0022 QUOTATION MARK character (").

> [!example]
> In the following example, the [`name`](#410191-naming-form-controls-the-name-attribute) attribute is given with the double-quoted attribute value syntax:
> 
> ```html
> <input name="be evil">
> ```

If an attribute using the double-quoted attribute syntax is to be followed by another attribute, then there must be [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) separating the two.

There must never be two or more attributes on the same start tag whose names are an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for each other.

---

When a [foreign element](#1312-elements) has one of the namespaced attributes given by the local name and namespace of the first and second cells of a row from the following table, it must be written using the name given by the third cell from the same row.

| Local name | Namespace | Attribute name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `actuate` | [XLink namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) | `xlink:actuate` |
| `arcrole` | [XLink namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) | `xlink:arcrole` |
| `href` | [XLink namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) | `xlink:href` |
| `role` | [XLink namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) | `xlink:role` |
| `show` | [XLink namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) | `xlink:show` |
| `title` | [XLink namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) | `xlink:title` |
| `type` | [XLink namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) | `xlink:type` |
| `lang` | [XML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) | `xml:lang` |
| `space` | [XML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) | `xml:space` |
| `xmlns` | [XMLNS namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) | `xmlns` |
| `xlink` | [XMLNS namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) | `xmlns:xlink` |

No other namespaced attribute can be expressed in [the HTML syntax](#13-the-html-syntax).

> [!note]
> Whether the attributes in the table above are conforming or not is defined by other specifications (e.g. SVG 2 and MathML); this section only describes the syntax rules if the attributes are serialized using the HTML syntax.

##### 13.1.2.4 Optional tags

Certain tags can be omitted.

> [!note]
> Omitting an element's [start tag](#13121-start-tags) in the situations described below does not mean the element is not present; it is implied, but it is still there. For example, an HTML document always has a root [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element, even if the string `<html>` doesn't appear anywhere in the markup.

An [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element's [start tag](#13121-start-tags) may be omitted if the first thing inside the [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element is not a [comment](#1316-comments).

> [!example]
> For example, in the following case it's ok to remove the "`<html>`" tag:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <html>
>   <head>
>     <title>Hello</title>
>   </head>
>   <body>
>     <p>Welcome to this example.</p>
>   </body>
> </html>
> ```
> 
> Doing so would make the document look like this:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> 
>   <head>
>     <title>Hello</title>
>   </head>
>   <body>
>     <p>Welcome to this example.</p>
>   </body>
> </html>
> ```
> 
> This has the exact same DOM. In particular, note that whitespace around the [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) is ignored by the parser. The following example would also have the exact same DOM:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML><head>
>     <title>Hello</title>
>   </head>
>   <body>
>     <p>Welcome to this example.</p>
>   </body>
> </html>
> ```
> 
> However, in the following example, removing the start tag moves the comment to before the [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <html>
>   <!-- where is this comment in the DOM? -->
>   <head>
>     <title>Hello</title>
>   </head>
>   <body>
>     <p>Welcome to this example.</p>
>   </body>
> </html>
> ```
> 
> With the tag removed, the document actually turns into the same as this:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <!-- where is this comment in the DOM? -->
> <html>
>   <head>
>     <title>Hello</title>
>   </head>
>   <body>
>     <p>Welcome to this example.</p>
>   </body>
> </html>
> ```
> 
> This is why the tag can only be removed if it is not followed by a comment: removing the tag when there is a comment there changes the document's resulting parse tree. Of course, if the position of the comment does not matter, then the tag can be omitted, as if the comment had been moved to before the start tag in the first place.

An [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) may be omitted if the [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element is not immediately followed by a [comment](#1316-comments).

A [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element's [start tag](#13121-start-tags) may be omitted if the element is empty, or if the first thing inside the [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element is an element.

A [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) may be omitted if the [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element is not immediately followed by [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) or a [comment](#1316-comments).

A [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element's [start tag](#13121-start-tags) may be omitted if the element is empty, or if the first thing inside the [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element is not [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) or a [comment](#1316-comments), except if the first thing inside the [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element is a [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element), [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element), [`link`](#424-the-link-element), [`script`](#4121-the-script-element), [`style`](#426-the-style-element), or [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element.

A [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) may be omitted if the [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element is not immediately followed by a [comment](#1316-comments).

> [!example]
> Note that in the example above, the [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element start and end tags, and the [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element start tag, can't be omitted, because they are surrounded by whitespace:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <html>
>   <head>
>     <title>Hello</title>
>   </head>
>   <body>
>     <p>Welcome to this example.</p>
>   </body>
> </html>
> ```
> 
> (The [`body`](#431-the-body-element) and [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element end tags could be omitted without trouble; any spaces after those get parsed into the [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element anyway.)
> 
> Usually, however, whitespace isn't an issue. If we first remove the whitespace we don't care about:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML><html><head><title>Hello</title></head><body><p>Welcome to this example.</p></body></html>
> ```
> 
> Then we can omit a number of tags without affecting the DOM:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML><title>Hello</title><p>Welcome to this example.</p>
> ```
> 
> At that point, we can also add some whitespace back:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <title>Hello</title>
> <p>Welcome to this example.</p>
> ```
> 
> This would be equivalent to this document, with the omitted tags shown in their parser-implied positions; the only whitespace text node that results from this is the newline at the end of the [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML>
> <html><head><title>Hello</title>
> </head><body><p>Welcome to this example.</p></body></html>
> ```

An [`li`](#448-the-li-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) may be omitted if the [`li`](#448-the-li-element) element is immediately followed by another [`li`](#448-the-li-element) element or if there is no more content in the parent element.

A [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) may be omitted if the [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) element is immediately followed by another [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) element or a [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) element.

A [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) may be omitted if the [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) element is immediately followed by another [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) element or a [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

A [`p`](#441-the-p-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) may be omitted if the [`p`](#441-the-p-element) element is immediately followed by an [`address`](#4310-the-address-element), [`article`](#432-the-article-element), [`aside`](#435-the-aside-element), [`blockquote`](#444-the-blockquote-element), [`details`](#4111-the-details-element), [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element), [`div`](#4416-the-div-element), [`dl`](#449-the-dl-element), [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element), [`figcaption`](#4413-the-figcaption-element), [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element), [`footer`](#439-the-footer-element), [`form`](#4103-the-form-element), [`h1`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements), [`h2`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements), [`h3`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements), [`h4`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements), [`h5`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements), [`h6`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements), [`header`](#438-the-header-element), [`hgroup`](#437-the-hgroup-element), [`hr`](#442-the-hr-element), [`main`](#4414-the-main-element), [`menu`](#447-the-menu-element), [`nav`](#434-the-nav-element), [`ol`](#445-the-ol-element), [`p`](#441-the-p-element), [`pre`](#443-the-pre-element), [`search`](#4415-the-search-element), [`section`](#433-the-section-element), [`table`](#491-the-table-element), or [`ul`](#446-the-ul-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element and the parent element is an [HTML element](#213-xml-compatibility) that is not an [`a`](#451-the-a-element), [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element), [`del`](#472-the-del-element), [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element), [`map`](#4812-the-map-element), [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element), or [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element, or an [autonomous custom element](#4133-core-concepts).

> [!example]
> We can thus simplify the earlier example further:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML><title>Hello</title><p>Welcome to this example.
> ```

An [`rt`](#4511-the-rt-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) may be omitted if the [`rt`](#4511-the-rt-element) element is immediately followed by an [`rt`](#4511-the-rt-element) or [`rp`](#4512-the-rp-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

An [`rp`](#4512-the-rp-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) may be omitted if the [`rp`](#4512-the-rp-element) element is immediately followed by an [`rt`](#4511-the-rt-element) or [`rp`](#4512-the-rp-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

An [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) may be omitted if the [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element is immediately followed by another [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element, if it is immediately followed by an [`hr`](#442-the-hr-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

An [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) may be omitted if the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element is immediately followed by another [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element, if it is immediately followed by an [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element, if it is immediately followed by an [`hr`](#442-the-hr-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

A [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element's [start tag](#13121-start-tags) may be omitted if the first thing inside the [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element is a [`col`](#494-the-col-element) element, and if the element is not immediately preceded by another [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element whose [end tag](#13122-end-tags) has been omitted. (It can't be omitted if the element is empty.)

A [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) may be omitted if the [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element is not immediately followed by [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) or a [comment](#1316-comments).

A [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) may be omitted if the [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element) element is not immediately followed by [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) or a [comment](#1316-comments).

A [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) may be omitted if the [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) element is immediately followed by a [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) or [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element.

A [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) element's [start tag](#13121-start-tags) may be omitted if the first thing inside the [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) element is a [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element, and if the element is not immediately preceded by a [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element), [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element), or [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element whose [end tag](#13122-end-tags) has been omitted. (It can't be omitted if the element is empty.)

A [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) may be omitted if the [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) element is immediately followed by a [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) or [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

A [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) may be omitted if there is no more content in the parent element.

A [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) may be omitted if the [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element is immediately followed by another [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

A [`td`](#499-the-td-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) may be omitted if the [`td`](#499-the-td-element) element is immediately followed by a [`td`](#499-the-td-element) or [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

A [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element's [end tag](#13122-end-tags) may be omitted if the [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element is immediately followed by a [`td`](#499-the-td-element) or [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element, or if there is no more content in the parent element.

> [!example]
> The ability to omit all these table-related tags makes table markup much terser.
> 
> Take this example:
> 
> ```html
> <table>
>  <caption>37547 TEE Electric Powered Rail Car Train Functions (Abbreviated)</caption>
>  <colgroup><col><col><col></colgroup>
>  <thead>
>   <tr>
>    <th>Function</th>
>    <th>Control Unit</th>
>    <th>Central Station</th>
>   </tr>
>  </thead>
>  <tbody>
>   <tr>
>    <td>Headlights</td>
>    <td>✔</td>
>    <td>✔</td>
>   </tr>
>   <tr>
>    <td>Interior Lights</td>
>    <td>✔</td>
>    <td>✔</td>
>   </tr>
>   <tr>
>    <td>Electric locomotive operating sounds</td>
>    <td>✔</td>
>    <td>✔</td>
>   </tr>
>   <tr>
>    <td>Engineer's cab lighting</td>
>    <td></td>
>    <td>✔</td>
>   </tr>
>   <tr>
>    <td>Station Announcements - Swiss</td>
>    <td></td>
>    <td>✔</td>
>   </tr>
>  </tbody>
> </table>
> ```
> 
> The exact same table, modulo some whitespace differences, could be marked up as follows:
> 
> ```html
> <table>
>  <caption>37547 TEE Electric Powered Rail Car Train Functions (Abbreviated)
>  <colgroup><col><col><col>
>  <thead>
>   <tr>
>    <th>Function
>    <th>Control Unit
>    <th>Central Station
>  <tbody>
>   <tr>
>    <td>Headlights
>    <td>✔
>    <td>✔
>   <tr>
>    <td>Interior Lights
>    <td>✔
>    <td>✔
>   <tr>
>    <td>Electric locomotive operating sounds
>    <td>✔
>    <td>✔
>   <tr>
>    <td>Engineer's cab lighting
>    <td>
>    <td>✔
>   <tr>
>    <td>Station Announcements - Swiss
>    <td>
>    <td>✔
> </table>
> ```
> 
> Since the cells take up much less room this way, this can be made even terser by having each row on one line:
> 
> ```html
> <table>
>  <caption>37547 TEE Electric Powered Rail Car Train Functions (Abbreviated)
>  <colgroup><col><col><col>
>  <thead>
>   <tr> <th>Function                              <th>Control Unit     <th>Central Station
>  <tbody>
>   <tr> <td>Headlights                            <td>✔                <td>✔
>   <tr> <td>Interior Lights                       <td>✔                <td>✔
>   <tr> <td>Electric locomotive operating sounds  <td>✔                <td>✔
>   <tr> <td>Engineer's cab lighting               <td>                 <td>✔
>   <tr> <td>Station Announcements - Swiss         <td>                 <td>✔
> </table>
> ```
> 
> The only differences between these tables, at the DOM level, is with the precise position of the (in any case semantically-neutral) whitespace.

**However**, a [start tag](#13121-start-tags) must never be omitted if it has any attributes.

> [!example]
> Returning to the earlier example with all the whitespace removed and then all the optional tags removed:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML><title>Hello</title><p>Welcome to this example.
> ```
> 
> If the [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element in this example had to have a [`class`](#326-global-attributes) attribute and the [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element had to have a [`lang`](#3262-the-lang-and-xmllang-attributes) attribute, the markup would have to become:
> 
> ```html
> <!DOCTYPE HTML><html lang="en"><title>Hello</title><body class="demo"><p>Welcome to this example.
> ```

> [!note]
> This section assumes that the document is conforming, in particular, that there are no [content model](#325-content-models) violations. Omitting tags in the fashion described in this section in a document that does not conform to the [content models](#325-content-models) described in this specification is likely to result in unexpected DOM differences (this is, in part, what the content models are designed to avoid).

##### 13.1.2.5 Restrictions on content models

For historical reasons, certain elements have extra restrictions beyond even the restrictions given by their content model.

A [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element must not contain [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) elements, even though these elements are technically allowed inside [`table`](#491-the-table-element) elements according to the content models described in this specification. (If a [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element is put inside a [`table`](#491-the-table-element) in the markup, it will in fact imply a [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) start tag before it.)

A single [newline](#13131-newlines) may be placed immediately after the [start tag](#13121-start-tags) of [`pre`](#443-the-pre-element) and [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements. This does not affect the processing of the element. The otherwise optional [newline](#13131-newlines) *must* be included if the element's contents themselves start with a [newline](#13131-newlines) (because otherwise the leading newline in the contents would be treated like the optional newline, and ignored).

> [!example]
> The following two [`pre`](#443-the-pre-element) blocks are equivalent:
> 
> ```html
> <pre>Hello</pre>
> ```
> 
> ```html
> <pre>Hello</pre>
> ```

##### 13.1.2.6 Restrictions on the contents of raw text and escapable raw text elements
