The text in [raw text](#1312-elements) and [escapable raw text elements](#1312-elements) must not contain any occurrences of the string "`</`" (U+003C LESS-THAN SIGN, U+002F SOLIDUS) followed by characters that case-insensitively match the tag name of the element followed by one of U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION (tab), U+000A LINE FEED (LF), U+000C FORM FEED (FF), U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR), U+0020 SPACE, U+003E GREATER-THAN SIGN (>), or U+002F SOLIDUS (/).

#### 13.1.3 Text

Text is allowed inside elements, attribute values, and comments. Extra constraints are placed on what is and what is not allowed in text based on where the text is to be put, as described in the other sections.

##### 13.1.3.1 Newlines

Newlines in HTML may be represented either as U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) characters, U+000A LINE FEED (LF) characters, or pairs of U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR), U+000A LINE FEED (LF) characters in that order.

Where [character references](#1314-character-references) are allowed, a character reference of a U+000A LINE FEED (LF) character (but not a U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR) character) also represents a [newline](#13131-newlines).

#### 13.1.4 Character references

In certain cases described in other sections, [text](#1313-text) may be mixed with character references. These can be used to escape characters that couldn't otherwise legally be included in [text](#1313-text).

Character references must start with a U+0026 AMPERSAND character (&). Following this, there are three possible kinds of character references:

Named character references

The ampersand must be followed by one of the names given in the [named character references](#135-named-character-references) section, using the same case. The name must be one that is terminated by a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;).

Decimal numeric character reference

The ampersand must be followed by a U+0023 NUMBER SIGN character (#), followed by one or more [ASCII digits](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), representing a base-ten integer that corresponds to a code point that is allowed according to the definition below. The digits must then be followed by a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;).

Hexadecimal numeric character reference

The ampersand must be followed by a U+0023 NUMBER SIGN character (#), which must be followed by either a U+0078 LATIN SMALL LETTER X character (x) or a U+0058 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER X character (X), which must then be followed by one or more [ASCII hex digits](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), representing a hexadecimal integer that corresponds to a code point that is allowed according to the definition below. The digits must then be followed by a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;).

The numeric character reference forms described above are allowed to reference any code point excluding U+000D CR, [noncharacters](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), and [controls](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) other than [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).

An ambiguous ampersand is a U+0026 AMPERSAND character (&) that is followed by one or more [ASCII alphanumerics](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), followed by a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;), where these characters do not match any of the names given in the [named character references](#135-named-character-references) section.

#### 13.1.5 CDATA sections

CDATA sections must consist of the following components, in this order:
1. The string "`<![CDATA[`".
2. Optionally, [text](#1313-text), with the additional restriction that the text must not contain the string "`]]>`".
3. The string "`]]>`".

> [!example]
> CDATA sections can only be used in foreign content (MathML or SVG). In this example, a CDATA section is used to escape the contents of a [MathML `ms`](https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#string-literal-ms) element:
> 
> ```html
> <p>You can add a string to a number, but this stringifies the number:</p>
> <math>
>  <ms><![CDATA[x<y]]></ms>
>  <mo>+</mo>
>  <mn>3</mn>
>  <mo>=</mo>
>  <ms><![CDATA[x<y3]]></ms>
> </math>
> ```

#### 13.1.6 Comments

Comments must have the following format:
1. The string "`<!--`".
2. Optionally, [text](#1313-text), with the additional restriction that the text must not start with the string "`>`", nor start with the string "`->`", nor contain the strings "`<!--`", "`-->`", or "`--!>`", nor end with the string "`<!-`".
3. The string "`-->`".

> [!note]
> The [text](#1313-text) is allowed to end with the string "`<!`", as in `<!--My favorite operators are > and
>   <!-->`.

#### 13.1.7 Processing instructions

A processing instruction marks a location in a document for further processing.

Processing instructions must have the following format:
1. "`<?`".
2. A [target](#1317-processing-instructions).
3. Either of the following two options:
   - Zero or more [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).
   - One or more [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), followed by [data](#1317-processing-instructions).
4. Optionally, a U+003F (?).
5. A U+003E (>).

The target consists of [ASCII alphanumeric](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), U+002D (-), and U+005F (\_) code points. It must start with an [ASCII alpha](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) or U+005F (\_) and must not be an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for "`xml`" or "`xml-stylesheet`".

The data is [text](#1313-text), with the additional restriction that the text must not contain U+003E (>), nor end with U+003F (?).

> [!note]
> Processing instructions in the HTML syntax have some notable differences to [processing instructions in XML](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-pi): [\[XML\]](#references)
> - In HTML, a processing instruction can end with "`>`" or "`?>`", while in XML it can only end with "`?>`".
> - In HTML, "`<?xml ...?>`" and "`<?xml-stylesheet ...?>`" specifically are not parsed as processing instructions but instead treated as [bogus comments](#132541-bogus-comment-state). This is for compatibility with existing HTML content, where such syntax is relatively common.
> - HTML does not support the full [Name](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#NT-Name) production for [processing instruction targets](#1317-processing-instructions). A much more limited subset is allowed, as noted above. [\[XML\]](#references)

### 13.2 Parsing HTML documents

*This section only applies to user agents, data mining tools, and conformance checkers.*

> [!note]
> The rules for parsing XML documents into DOM trees are covered by the next section, entitled "[The XML syntax](#14-the-xml-syntax)".

User agents must use the parsing rules described in this section to generate the DOM trees from [`text/html`](#171-texthtml) resources. Together, these rules define what is referred to as the HTML parser.

> [!note]
> While the HTML syntax described in this specification bears a close resemblance to SGML and XML, it is a separate language with its own parsing rules.
> 
> Some earlier versions of HTML (in particular from HTML2 to HTML4) were based on SGML and used SGML parsing rules. However, few (if any) web browsers ever implemented true SGML parsing for HTML documents; the only user agents to strictly handle HTML as an SGML application have historically been validators. The resulting confusion — with validators claiming documents to have one representation while widely deployed web browsers interoperably implemented a different representation — has wasted decades of productivity. This version of HTML thus returns to a non-SGML basis.

For the purposes of conformance checkers, if a resource is determined to be in [the HTML syntax](#13-the-html-syntax), then it is an [HTML document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

> [!note]
> As stated [in the terminology section](#213-xml-compatibility), references to [element types](#213-xml-compatibility) that do not explicitly specify a namespace always refer to elements in the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces). For example, if the spec talks about "a [`menu`](#447-the-menu-element) element", then that is an element with the local name "`menu`", the namespace "`http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml`", and the interface [`HTMLMenuElement`](#447-the-menu-element). Where possible, references to such elements are hyperlinked to their definition.

#### 13.2.1 Overview of the parsing model

![](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/parsing-model-overview.svg)

The input to the HTML parsing process consists of a stream of [code points](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), which is passed through a [tokenization](#1325-tokenization) stage followed by a [tree construction](#1326-tree-construction) stage. The output is a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object.

> [!note]
> Implementations that [do not support scripting](#218-conformance-classes) do not have to actually create a DOM [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object, but the DOM tree in such cases is still used as the model for the rest of the specification.

In the common case, the data handled by the tokenization stage comes from the network, but [it can also come from script](#84-dynamic-markup-insertion) running in the user agent, e.g. using the [`document.write()`](#843-documentwrite) API.

There is only one set of states for the tokenizer stage and the tree construction stage, but the tree construction stage is reentrant, meaning that while the tree construction stage is handling one token, the tokenizer might be resumed, causing further tokens to be emitted and processed before the first token's processing is complete.

> [!example]
> In the following example, the tree construction stage will be called upon to handle a "p" start tag token while handling the "script" end tag token:
> 
> ```html
> ...
> <script>
>  document.write('<p>');
> </script>
> ...
> ```

To handle these cases, parsers have a script nesting level, which must be initially set to zero, and a parser pause flag, which must be initially set to false.

#### 13.2.2 Parse errors

This specification defines the parsing rules for HTML documents, whether they are syntactically correct or not. Certain points in the parsing algorithm are said to be [parse errors](#1322-parse-errors). The error handling for parse errors is well-defined (that's the processing rules described throughout this specification), but user agents, while parsing an HTML document, may [abort the parser](#1327-the-end) at the first [parse error](#1322-parse-errors) that they encounter for which they do not wish to apply the rules described in this specification.

Conformance checkers must report at least one parse error condition to the user if one or more parse error conditions exist in the document and must not report parse error conditions if none exist in the document. Conformance checkers may report more than one parse error condition if more than one parse error condition exists in the document.

> [!note]
> Parse errors are only errors with the *syntax* of HTML. In addition to checking for parse errors, conformance checkers will also verify that the document obeys all the other conformance requirements described in this specification.

Some parse errors have dedicated codes outlined in the table below that should be used by conformance checkers in reports.

*Error descriptions in the table below are non-normative.*

This error occurs if the parser encounters an empty [comment](#1316-comments) that is abruptly closed by a U+003E (>) [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) (i.e., `<!-->` or `<!--->`). The parser behaves as if the comment is closed correctly.

This error occurs if the parser encounters a U+003E (>) [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) in the [DOCTYPE](#1311-the-doctype) public identifier (e.g., `<!DOCTYPE html PUBLIC "foo>`). In such a case, if the DOCTYPE is correctly placed as a document preamble, the parser sets the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) to [quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

This error occurs if the parser encounters a U+003E (>) [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) in the [DOCTYPE](#1311-the-doctype) system identifier (e.g., `<!DOCTYPE html PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.01//EN" "foo>`). In such a case, if the DOCTYPE is correctly placed as a document preamble, the parser sets the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) to [quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

This error occurs if the parser encounters a numeric [character reference](#1314-character-references) that doesn't contain any digits (e.g., `&#qux;`). In this case the parser doesn't resolve the character reference.

This error occurs if the parser encounters a [CDATA section](#1315-cdata-sections) outside of foreign content (SVG or MathML). The parser treats such CDATA sections (including leading "`[CDATA[`" and trailing "`]]`") as comments.

This error occurs if the parser encounters a numeric [character reference](#1314-character-references) that references a [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) that is greater than the valid Unicode range. The parser resolves such a character reference to a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER.

This error occurs if the [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) contains a [control](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) that is not [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) or U+0000 NULL. Such code points are parsed as-is and usually, where parsing rules don't apply any additional restrictions, make their way into the DOM.

This error occurs if the parser encounters a numeric [character reference](#1314-character-references) that references a [control](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) that is not [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) or is a U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN. The parser resolves such character references as-is except C1 control references that are replaced according to the [numeric character reference end state](#132584-numeric-character-reference-end-state).

This error occurs if the parser encounters a [processing instruction target](#1317-processing-instructions) that is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for "`xml`" or "`xml-stylesheet`". The preceding U+003F (?) and all content that follows up to a U+003E (>) (if present) or to the end of the [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) is treated as a comment.

This error occurs if the parser encounters an [attribute](#13123-attributes) in a tag that already has an attribute with the same name. The parser ignores all such duplicate occurrences of the attribute.

This error occurs if the parser encounters an [end tag](#13122-end-tags) with [attributes](#13123-attributes). Attributes in end tags are ignored and do not make their way into the DOM.

This error occurs if the parser encounters an [end tag](#13122-end-tags) that has a U+002F (/) [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) right before the closing U+003E (>) code point (e.g., `</div/>`). Such a tag is treated as a regular end tag.

This error occurs if the parser encounters the end of the [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) where a tag name is expected. In this case the parser treats the beginning of a [start tag](#13121-start-tags) (i.e., `<`) or an [end tag](#13122-end-tags) (i.e., `</`) as text content.

This error occurs if the parser encounters the end of the [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) in a [CDATA section](#1315-cdata-sections). The parser treats such CDATA sections as if they are closed immediately before the end of the input stream.

This error occurs if the parser encounters the end of the [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) in a [comment](#1316-comments). The parser treats such comments as if they are closed immediately before the end of the input stream.

This error occurs if the parser encounters the end of the input stream in a [DOCTYPE](#1311-the-doctype). In such a case, if the DOCTYPE is correctly placed as a document preamble, the parser sets the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) to [quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

This error occurs if the parser encounters the end of the [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) in a [processing instruction](#1317-processing-instructions) (e.g., `<?` or `<?marker name=`). Such processing instructions are ignored.

This error occurs if the parser encounters the end of the [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) in text that resembles an [HTML comment](#1316-comments) inside [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element content (e.g., `<script><!-- foo`).

Syntactic structures that resemble HTML comments in [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements are parsed as text content. They can be a part of a scripting language-specific syntactic structure or be treated as an HTML-like comment, if the scripting language supports them (e.g., parsing rules for HTML-like comments can be found in Annex B of the JavaScript specification). The common reason for this error is a violation of the [restrictions for contents of `script` elements](#41213-restrictions-for-contents-of-script-elements). [\[JAVASCRIPT\]](#references)

This error occurs if the parser encounters the end of the [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) in a [start tag](#13121-start-tags) or an [end tag](#13122-end-tags) (e.g., `<div id=`). Such a tag is ignored.

This error occurs if the parser encounters a [comment](#1316-comments) that is closed by the "`--!>`" [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) sequence. The parser treats such comments as if they are correctly closed by the "`-->`" code point sequence.

This error occurs if the parser encounters the "`<!`" [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) sequence that is not immediately followed by two U+002D (-) code points and that is not the start of a [DOCTYPE](#1311-the-doctype) or a [CDATA section](#1315-cdata-sections). All content that follows the "`<!`" code point sequence up to a U+003E (>) code point (if present) or to the end of the [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) is treated as a comment.

One possible cause of this error is using an XML markup declaration (e.g., `<!ELEMENT br EMPTY>`) in HTML.

This error occurs if the parser encounters any [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) sequence other than "`PUBLIC`" and "`SYSTEM`" keywords after a [DOCTYPE](#1311-the-doctype) name. In such a case, the parser ignores any following public or system identifiers, and if the DOCTYPE is correctly placed as a document preamble, and if the [parser cannot change the mode flag](#132641-the-initial-insertion-mode) is false, sets the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) to [quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

This error occurs if the parser encounters a [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) that is not an [ASCII alpha](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) or U+005F (\_) where the first code point of a [processing instruction target](#1317-processing-instructions) is expected. The preceding U+003F (?) and all content that follows up to a U+003E (>) (if present) or to the end of the [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) is treated as a comment.

This error occurs if the parser encounters a [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) that is not an [ASCII alpha](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) where the first code point of a [start tag](#13121-start-tags) name or an [end tag](#13122-end-tags) name is expected. If a start tag was expected such code point and a preceding U+003C (<) is treated as text content, and all content that follows is treated as markup. Whereas, if an end tag was expected, such code point and all content that follows up to a U+003E (>) code point (if present) or to the end of the [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) is treated as a comment.

For example, consider the following markup:

```html
<42></42>
```

This will be parsed into:

• [`html`](#411-the-html-element) • [`head`](#421-the-head-element) • [`body`](#431-the-body-element) • [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): <42> • [`#comment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#414-interface-comment): 42

While the first code point of a tag name is limited to an [ASCII alpha](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), a wide range of code points (including [ASCII digits](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points)) is allowed in subsequent positions.

This error occurs if the parser encounters a [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) that is not an [ASCII alphanumeric](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), U+002D (-), or U+005F (\_) where a [processing instruction target](#1317-processing-instructions) is expected. The preceding U+003F (?) and all content that follows up to a U+003E (>) (if present) or to the end of the [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) is treated as a comment.

This error occurs if the parser encounters a U+003E (>) [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) where an [attribute](#13123-attributes) value is expected (e.g., `<div id=>`). The parser treats the attribute as having an empty value.

This error occurs if the parser encounters a [DOCTYPE](#1311-the-doctype) that is missing a name (e.g., `<!DOCTYPE>`). In such a case, if the DOCTYPE is correctly placed as a document preamble, the parser sets the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) to [quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

This error occurs if the parser encounters a U+003E (>) [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) where start of the [DOCTYPE](#1311-the-doctype) public identifier is expected (e.g., `<!DOCTYPE html PUBLIC >`). In such a case, if the DOCTYPE is correctly placed as a document preamble, the parser sets the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) to [quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

This error occurs if the parser encounters a U+003E (>) [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) where start of the [DOCTYPE](#1311-the-doctype) system identifier is expected (e.g., `<!DOCTYPE html SYSTEM >`). In such a case, if the DOCTYPE is correctly placed as a document preamble, the parser sets the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) to [quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

This error occurs if the parser encounters a U+003E (>) [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) where an [end tag](#13122-end-tags) name is expected, i.e., `</>`. The parser ignores the whole "`</>`" code point sequence.

This error occurs if the parser encounters the [DOCTYPE](#1311-the-doctype) public identifier that is not preceded by a quote (e.g., `<!DOCTYPE html PUBLIC -//W3C//DTD HTML 4.01//EN">`). In such a case, the parser ignores the public identifier, and if the DOCTYPE is correctly placed as a document preamble, sets the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) to [quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

This error occurs if the parser encounters the [DOCTYPE](#1311-the-doctype) system identifier that is not preceded by a quote (e.g., `<!DOCTYPE html SYSTEM
     http://www.w3.org/TR/xhtml1/DTD/xhtml1-transitional.dtd">`). In such a case, the parser ignores the system identifier, and if the DOCTYPE is correctly placed as a document preamble, sets the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) to [quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

This error occurs if the parser encounters a [character reference](#1314-character-references) that is not terminated by a U+003B (;) [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points). The parser behaves the same as if the character reference is terminated by the U+003B (;) code point.

Most [named character references](#135-named-character-references) require a terminating U+003B (;) [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points). Those that don't might get resolved as a longer named [character reference](#1314-character-references) in certain ambiguous scenarios.

For example, `&notin` will be parsed as "`¬in`", i.e., the same as if the input were `&not;in`, whereas `&notin;` will be parsed as "`∉`".

This error occurs if the parser encounters a [DOCTYPE](#1311-the-doctype) whose "`PUBLIC`" keyword and public identifier are not separated by [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points). In this case the parser behaves as if ASCII whitespace is present.

This error occurs if the parser encounters a [DOCTYPE](#1311-the-doctype) whose "`SYSTEM`" keyword and system identifier are not separated by [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points). In this case the parser behaves as if ASCII whitespace is present.

This error occurs if the parser encounters a [DOCTYPE](#1311-the-doctype) whose "`DOCTYPE`" keyword and name are not separated by [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points). In this case the parser behaves as if ASCII whitespace is present.

This error occurs if the parser encounters [attributes](#13123-attributes) that are not separated by [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) (e.g., `<div id="foo"class="bar">`). In this case the parser behaves as if ASCII whitespace is present.

This error occurs if the parser encounters a [DOCTYPE](#1311-the-doctype) whose public and system identifiers are not separated by [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points). In this case the parser behaves as if ASCII whitespace is present.

This error occurs if the parser encounters a nested [comment](#1316-comments) (e.g., `<!-- <!-- nested -->
     -->`). Such a comment will be closed by the first occurring "`-->`" [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) sequence and everything that follows will be treated as markup.

This error occurs if the parser encounters a numeric [character reference](#1314-character-references) that references a [noncharacter](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points). The parser resolves such character references as-is.

This error occurs if the [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) contains a [noncharacter](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points). Such [code points](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) are parsed as-is and usually, where parsing rules don't apply any additional restrictions, make their way into the DOM.

This error occurs if the parser encounters a [start tag](#13121-start-tags) for an element that is not in the list of [void elements](#1312-elements) or is not a part of foreign content (i.e., not an SVG or MathML element) that has a U+002F (/) [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) right before the closing U+003E (>) code point. The parser behaves as if the U+002F (/) is not present.

For example, consider the following markup:

```html
<div/><span></span><span></span>
```

This will be parsed into:

• [`html`](#411-the-html-element) • [`head`](#421-the-head-element) • [`body`](#431-the-body-element) • [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) • [`span`](#4526-the-span-element) • [`span`](#4526-the-span-element)

The trailing U+002F (/) in a start tag name can be used only in foreign content to specify self-closing tags. (Self-closing tags don't exist in HTML.) It is also allowed for void elements, but doesn't have any effect in this case.

This error occurs if the parser encounters a numeric [character reference](#1314-character-references) that references a U+0000 NULL [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points). The parser resolves such character references to a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER.

This error occurs if the parser encounters a numeric [character reference](#1314-character-references) that references a [surrogate](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points). The parser resolves such character references to a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER.

This error occurs if the [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) contains a [surrogate](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points). Such [code points](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) are parsed as-is and usually, where parsing rules don't apply any additional restrictions, make their way into the DOM.

Surrogates can only find their way into the input stream via script APIs such as [`document.write()`](#843-documentwrite).

This error occurs if the parser encounters any [code points](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) other than [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) or closing U+003E (>) after the [DOCTYPE](#1311-the-doctype) system identifier. The parser ignores these code points.

This error occurs if the parser encounters a U+0022 ("), U+0027 ('), or U+003C (<) [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) in an [attribute name](#13123-attributes). The parser includes such code points in the attribute name.

Code points that trigger this error are usually a part of another syntactic construct and can be a sign of a typo around the attribute name.

For example, consider the following markup:

```html
<div foo<div>
```

Due to a forgotten U+003E (>) code point after `foo` the parser treats this markup as a single [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element with a "`foo<div`" attribute.

As another example of this error, consider the following markup:

```html
<div id'bar'>
```

Due to a forgotten U+003D (=) code point between an attribute name and value the parser treats this markup as a [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element with the attribute "`id'bar'`" that has an empty value.

This error occurs if the parser encounters a U+0022 ("), U+0027 ('), U+003C (<), U+003D (=), or U+0060 (\`) [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) in an unquoted [attribute value](#13123-attributes). The parser includes such code points in the attribute value.

Code points that trigger this error are usually a part of another syntactic construct and can be a sign of a typo around the attribute value.

U+0060 (\`) is in the list of code points that trigger this error because certain legacy user agents treat it as a quote.

For example, consider the following markup:

```html
<div foo=b'ar'>
```

Due to a misplaced U+0027 (') code point the parser sets the value of the "`foo`" attribute to "`b'ar'`".

This error occurs if the parser encounters a U+003D (=) [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) before an attribute name. In this case the parser treats U+003D (=) as the first code point of the attribute name.

The common reason for this error is a forgotten attribute name.

For example, consider the following markup:

```html
<div foo="bar" ="baz">
```

Due to a forgotten attribute name the parser treats this markup as a [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element with two attributes: a "`foo`" attribute with a "`bar`" value and a "`="baz"`" attribute with an empty value.

This error occurs if the parser encounters a U+0000 NULL [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) in the [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) in certain positions. In general, such code points are either ignored or, for security reasons, replaced with a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER.

This error occurs if the parser encounters a U+002F (/) [code point](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) that is not a part of a quoted [attribute](#13123-attributes) value and not immediately followed by a U+003E (>) code point in a tag (e.g., `<div /
     id="foo">`). In this case the parser behaves as if it encountered [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points).

This error occurs if the parser encounters an [ambiguous ampersand](#1314-character-references). In this case the parser doesn't resolve the [character reference](#1314-character-references).

#### 13.2.3 The input byte stream

The stream of code points that comprises the input to the tokenization stage will be initially seen by the user agent as a stream of bytes (typically coming over the network or from the local file system). The bytes encode the actual characters according to a particular *character encoding*, which the user agent uses to decode the bytes into characters.

> [!note]
> For XML documents, the algorithm user agents are required to use to determine the character encoding is given by XML. This section does not apply to XML documents. [\[XML\]](#references)

Usually, the [encoding sniffing algorithm](#13232-determining-the-character-encoding) defined below is used to determine the character encoding.

Given a character encoding, the bytes in the [input byte stream](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) must be converted to characters for the tokenizer's [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream), by passing the [input byte stream](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) and character encoding to [decode](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#decode).

> [!note]
> A leading Byte Order Mark (BOM) causes the character encoding argument to be ignored and will itself be skipped.

> [!note]
> Bytes or sequences of bytes in the original byte stream that did not conform to the Encoding standard (e.g. invalid UTF-8 byte sequences in a UTF-8 input byte stream) are errors that conformance checkers are expected to report. [\[ENCODING\]](#references)

> [!warning]
> The decoder algorithms describe how to handle invalid input; for security reasons, it is imperative that those rules be followed precisely. Differences in how invalid byte sequences are handled can result in, amongst other problems, script injection vulnerabilities ("XSS").

When the HTML parser is decoding an input byte stream, it uses a character encoding and a confidence. The confidence is either *tentative*, *certain*, or *irrelevant*. The encoding used, and whether the confidence in that encoding is *tentative* or *certain*, is [used during the parsing](#132644-the-in-head-insertion-mode) to determine whether to [change the encoding](#13234-changing-the-encoding-while-parsing). If no encoding is necessary, e.g. because the parser is operating on a Unicode stream and doesn't have to use a character encoding at all, then the [confidence](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) is *irrelevant*.

> [!note]
> Some algorithms feed the parser by directly adding characters to the [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) rather than adding bytes to the [input byte stream](#1323-the-input-byte-stream).

##### 13.2.3.1 Parsing with a known character encoding

When the HTML parser is to operate on an input byte stream that has a known definite encoding, then the character encoding is that encoding and the [confidence](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) is *certain*.

##### 13.2.3.2 Determining the character encoding

In some cases, it might be impractical to unambiguously determine the encoding before parsing the document. Because of this, this specification provides for a two-pass mechanism with an optional pre-scan. Implementations are allowed, as described below, to apply a simplified parsing algorithm to whatever bytes they have available before beginning to parse the document. Then, the real parser is started, using a tentative encoding derived from this pre-parse and other out-of-band metadata. If, while the document is being loaded, the user agent discovers a character encoding declaration that conflicts with this information, then the parser can get reinvoked to perform a parse of the document with the real encoding.

User agents must use the following algorithm, called the encoding sniffing algorithm, to determine the character encoding to use when decoding a document in the first pass. This algorithm takes as input any out-of-band metadata available to the user agent (e.g. the [Content-Type metadata](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource) of the document) and all the bytes available so far, and returns a character encoding and a [confidence](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) that is either *tentative* or *certain*.
1. If the result of [BOM sniffing](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#bom-sniff) is an encoding, return that encoding with [confidence](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) *certain*.

   > [!note]
   > Although the [decode](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#decode) algorithm will itself change the encoding to use based on the presence of a byte order mark, this algorithm sniffs the BOM as well in order to set the correct [document's character encoding](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) and [confidence](#1323-the-input-byte-stream).

2. If the user has explicitly instructed the user agent to override the document's character encoding with a specific encoding, optionally return that encoding with the [confidence](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) *certain*.

   > [!note]
   > Typically, user agents remember such user requests across sessions, and in some cases apply them to documents in [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element)s as well.

3. The user agent may wait for more bytes of the resource to be available, either in this step or at any later step in this algorithm. For instance, a user agent might wait 500ms or 1024 bytes, whichever came first. In general preparsing the source to find the encoding improves performance, as it reduces the need to throw away the data structures used when parsing upon finding the encoding information. However, if the user agent delays too long to obtain data to determine the encoding, then the cost of the delay could outweigh any performance improvements from the preparse.

   > [!note]
   > The authoring conformance requirements for character encoding declarations limit them to only appearing [in the first 1024 bytes](#4254-specifying-the-documents-character-encoding). User agents are therefore encouraged to use the prescan algorithm below (as invoked by these steps) on the first 1024 bytes, but not to stall beyond that.

4. If the transport layer specifies a character encoding, and it is supported, return that encoding with the [confidence](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) *certain*.
5. Optionally, [prescan the byte stream to determine its encoding](#13232-determining-the-character-encoding), with the *[end condition](#13232-determining-the-character-encoding)* being when the user agent decides that scanning further bytes would not be efficient. User agents are encouraged to only prescan the first 1024 bytes. User agents may decide that scanning *any* bytes is not efficient, in which case these substeps are entirely skipped.

   The aforementioned algorithm returns either a character encoding or failure. If it returns a character encoding, then return the same encoding, with [confidence](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) *tentative*.

6. If the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) for which this algorithm is being run is associated with a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) d whose [container document](#7313-child-navigables) is non-null:
   1. Let parentDocument be d's [container document](#7313-child-navigables).
   2. If parentDocument's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is [same origin](#711-origins) with d's [origin](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) and parentDocument's [character encoding](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is not [UTF-16BE/LE](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-16be-le), then return parentDocument's [character encoding](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), with the [confidence](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) *tentative*.
7. Otherwise, if the user agent has information on the likely encoding for this page, e.g. based on the encoding of the page when it was last visited, then return that encoding, with the [confidence](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) *tentative*.
8. The user agent may attempt to autodetect the character encoding from applying frequency analysis or other algorithms to the data stream. Such algorithms may use information about the resource other than the resource's contents, including the address of the resource. If autodetection succeeds in determining a character encoding, and that encoding is a supported encoding, then return that encoding, with the [confidence](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) *tentative*. [\[UNIVCHARDET\]](#references)

   > [!note]
   > User agents are generally discouraged from attempting to autodetect encodings for resources obtained over the network, since doing so involves inherently non-interoperable heuristics. Attempting to detect encodings based on an HTML document's preamble is especially tricky since HTML markup typically uses only ASCII characters, and HTML documents tend to begin with a lot of markup rather than with text content.

   > [!note]
   > The UTF-8 encoding has a highly detectable bit pattern. Files from the local file system that contain bytes with values greater than 0x7F which match the UTF-8 pattern are very likely to be UTF-8, while documents with byte sequences that do not match it are very likely not. When a user agent can examine the whole file, rather than just the preamble, detecting for UTF-8 specifically can be especially effective. [\[PPUTF8\]](#references) [\[UTF8DET\]](#references)

9. Otherwise, return an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) or user-specified default character encoding, with the [confidence](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) *tentative*.

   In controlled environments or in environments where the encoding of documents can be prescribed (for example, for user agents intended for dedicated use in new networks), the comprehensive `UTF-8` encoding is suggested.

   In other environments, the default encoding is typically dependent on the user's locale (an approximation of the languages, and thus often encodings, of the pages that the user is likely to frequent). The following table gives suggested defaults based on the user's locale, for compatibility with legacy content. Locales are identified by BCP 47 language tags. [\[BCP47\]](#references) [\[ENCODING\]](#references)

   | zh-Hant, zh-HK, zh-MO, zh-TW | Chinese, Traditional | [Big5](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#big5) |

   The contents of this table are derived from the intersection of Windows, Chrome, and Firefox defaults.

The [document's character encoding](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) must immediately be set to the value returned from this algorithm, at the same time as the user agent uses the returned value to select the decoder to use for the input byte stream.

---

When an algorithm requires a user agent to prescan a byte stream to determine its encoding, given some defined end condition, then it must run the following steps. If at any point during these steps (including during instances of the [get an attribute](#13232-determining-the-character-encoding) algorithm invoked by this one) the user agent either runs out of bytes (meaning the position pointer created in the first step below goes beyond the end of the byte stream obtained so far) or reaches its end condition, then abort the [prescan a byte stream to determine its encoding](#13232-determining-the-character-encoding) algorithm and return the result [get an XML encoding](#13232-determining-the-character-encoding) applied to the same bytes that the [prescan a byte stream to determine its encoding](#13232-determining-the-character-encoding) algorithm was applied to. Otherwise, these steps will return a character encoding.
1. Let position be a pointer to a byte in the input byte stream, initially pointing at the first byte.
2. Prescan for UTF-16 XML declarations: If position points to:

   A sequence of bytes starting with: 0x3C, 0x0, 0x3F, 0x0, 0x78, 0x0 (case-sensitive UTF-16 little-endian '<?x')

   Return [UTF-16LE](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-16le).

   A sequence of bytes starting with: 0x0, 0x3C, 0x0, 0x3F, 0x0, 0x78 (case-sensitive UTF-16 big-endian '<?x')

   Return [UTF-16BE](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-16be).

   > [!note]
   > For historical reasons, the prefix is two bytes longer than in [Appendix F](https://www.w3.org/TR/REC-xml/#sec-guessing) of XML and the encoding name is not checked.

3. *Loop*: If position points to:

   A sequence of bytes starting with: 0x3C 0x21 0x2D 0x2D (\``<!--`\`)

   Advance the position pointer so that it points at the first 0x3E byte which is preceded by two 0x2D bytes (i.e. at the end of an ASCII '-->' sequence) and comes after the 0x3C byte that was found. (The two 0x2D bytes can be the same as those in the '<!--' sequence.)

   A sequence of bytes starting with: 0x3C, 0x4D or 0x6D, 0x45 or 0x65, 0x54 or 0x74, 0x41 or 0x61, and one of 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0C, 0x0D, 0x20, 0x2F (case-insensitive ASCII '<meta' followed by a space or slash)
   1. Advance the position pointer so that it points at the next 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0C, 0x0D, 0x20, or 0x2F byte (the one in sequence of characters matched above).
   2. Let attribute list be an empty list of strings.
   3. Let got pragma be false.
   4. Let need pragma be null.
   5. Let charset be the null value (which, for the purposes of this algorithm, is distinct from an unrecognized encoding or the empty string).
   6. *Attributes*: [Get an attribute](#13232-determining-the-character-encoding) and its value. If no attribute was sniffed, then jump to the *processing* step below.
   7. If the attribute's name is already in attribute list, then return to the step labeled *attributes*.
   8. Add the attribute's name to attribute list.
   9. Run the appropriate step from the following list, if one applies:

      If the attribute's name is "`http-equiv`"

      If the attribute's value is "`content-type`", then set got pragma to true.

      If the attribute's name is "`content`"

      Apply the [algorithm for extracting a character encoding from a `meta` element](#253-extracting-character-encodings-from-meta-elements), giving the attribute's value as the string to parse. If a character encoding is returned, and if charset is still set to null, let charset be the encoding returned, and set need pragma to true.

      If the attribute's name is "`charset`"

      Let charset be the result of [getting an encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-encoding-get) from the attribute's value, and set need pragma to false.

   10. Return to the step labeled *attributes*.
   11. *Processing*: If need pragma is null, then jump to the step below labeled *next byte*.
   12. If need pragma is true but got pragma is false, then jump to the step below labeled *next byte*.
   13. If charset is failure, then jump to the step below labeled *next byte*.
   14. If charset is [UTF-16BE/LE](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-16be-le), then set charset to [UTF-8](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8).
   15. If charset is [x-user-defined](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#x-user-defined), then set charset to [windows-1252](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#windows-1252).
   16. Return charset.

   A sequence of bytes starting with a 0x3C byte (<), optionally a 0x2F byte (/), and finally a byte in the range 0x41-0x5A or 0x61-0x7A (A-Z or a-z)
   1. Advance the position pointer so that it points at the next 0x09 (HT), 0x0A (LF), 0x0C (FF), 0x0D (CR), 0x20 (SP), or 0x3E (>) byte.
   2. Repeatedly [get an attribute](#13232-determining-the-character-encoding) until no further attributes can be found, then jump to the step below labeled *next byte*.

   A sequence of bytes starting with: 0x3C 0x21 (\``<!`\`)

   A sequence of bytes starting with: 0x3C 0x2F (\``</`\`)

   A sequence of bytes starting with: 0x3C 0x3F (\``<?`\`)

   Advance the position pointer so that it points at the first 0x3E byte (>) that comes after the 0x3C byte that was found.

   Any other byte

   Do nothing with that byte.

4. *Next byte*: Move position so it points at the next byte in the input byte stream, and return to the step above labeled *loop*.

When the [prescan a byte stream to determine its encoding](#13232-determining-the-character-encoding) algorithm says to get an attribute, it means doing this:
1. If the byte at position is one of 0x09 (HT), 0x0A (LF), 0x0C (FF), 0x0D (CR), 0x20 (SP), or 0x2F (/), then advance position to the next byte and redo this step.
2. If the byte at position is 0x3E (>), then abort the [get an attribute](#13232-determining-the-character-encoding) algorithm. There isn't one.
3. Otherwise, the byte at position is the start of the attribute name. Let attribute name and attribute value be the empty string.
4. Process the byte at position as follows:

   If it is 0x3D (=), and the attribute name is longer than the empty string

   Advance position to the next byte and jump to the step below labeled *value*.

   If it is 0x09 (HT), 0x0A (LF), 0x0C (FF), 0x0D (CR), or 0x20 (SP)

   Jump to the step below labeled *spaces*.

   If it is 0x2F (/) or 0x3E (>)

   Abort the [get an attribute](#13232-determining-the-character-encoding) algorithm. The attribute's name is the value of attribute name, its value is the empty string.

   If it is in the range 0x41 (A) to 0x5A (Z)

   Append the code point b+0x20 to attribute name (where b is the value of the byte at position). (This converts the input to lowercase.)

   Anything else

   Append the code point with the same value as the byte at position to attribute name. (It doesn't actually matter how bytes outside the ASCII range are handled here, since only ASCII bytes can contribute to the detection of a character encoding.)

5. Advance position to the next byte and return to the previous step.
6. *Spaces*: If the byte at position is one of 0x09 (HT), 0x0A (LF), 0x0C (FF), 0x0D (CR), or 0x20 (SP), then advance position to the next byte, then, repeat this step.
7. If the byte at position is *not* 0x3D (=), abort the [get an attribute](#13232-determining-the-character-encoding) algorithm. The attribute's name is the value of attribute name, its value is the empty string.
8. Advance position past the 0x3D (=) byte.
9. *Value*: If the byte at position is one of 0x09 (HT), 0x0A (LF), 0x0C (FF), 0x0D (CR), or 0x20 (SP), then advance position to the next byte, then, repeat this step.
10. Process the byte at position as follows:

    If it is 0x22 (") or 0x27 (')
    1. Let b be the value of the byte at position.
    2. *Quote loop*: Advance position to the next byte.
    3. If the value of the byte at position is the value of b, then advance position to the next byte and abort the "get an attribute" algorithm. The attribute's name is the value of attribute name, and its value is the value of attribute value.
    4. Otherwise, if the value of the byte at position is in the range 0x41 (A) to 0x5A (Z), then append a code point to attribute value whose value is 0x20 more than the value of the byte at position.
    5. Otherwise, append a code point to attribute value whose value is the same as the value of the byte at position.
    6. Return to the step above labeled *quote loop*.

    If it is 0x3E (>)

    Abort the [get an attribute](#13232-determining-the-character-encoding) algorithm. The attribute's name is the value of attribute name, its value is the empty string.

    If it is in the range 0x41 (A) to 0x5A (Z)

    Append a code point b+0x20 to attribute value (where b is the value of the byte at position). Advance position to the next byte.

    Anything else

    Append a code point with the same value as the byte at position to attribute value. Advance position to the next byte.

11. Process the byte at position as follows:

    If it is 0x09 (HT), 0x0A (LF), 0x0C (FF), 0x0D (CR), 0x20 (SP), or 0x3E (>)

    Abort the [get an attribute](#13232-determining-the-character-encoding) algorithm. The attribute's name is the value of attribute name and its value is the value of attribute value.

    If it is in the range 0x41 (A) to 0x5A (Z)

    Append a code point b+0x20 to attribute value (where b is the value of the byte at position).

    Anything else

    Append a code point with the same value as the byte at position to attribute value.

12. Advance position to the next byte and return to the previous step.

When the [prescan a byte stream to determine its encoding](#13232-determining-the-character-encoding) algorithm is aborted without returning an encoding, get an XML encoding means doing this.

> [!note]
> Looking for syntax resembling an XML declaration, even in [`text/html`](#171-texthtml), is necessary for compatibility with existing content.
1. Let encodingPosition be a pointer to the start of the stream.
2. If encodingPosition does not point to the start of a byte sequence 0x3C, 0x3F, 0x78, 0x6D, 0x6C (\``<?xml`\`), then return failure.
3. Let xmlDeclarationEnd be a pointer to the next byte in the input byte stream which is 0x3E (>). If there is no such byte, then return failure.
4. Set encodingPosition to the position of the first occurrence of the subsequence of bytes 0x65, 0x6E, 0x63, 0x6F, 0x64, 0x69, 0x6E, 0x67 (\``encoding`\`) at or after the current encodingPosition and before xmlDeclarationEnd. If there is no such sequence, then return failure.
5. Advance encodingPosition past the 0x67 (g) byte.
6. While the byte at encodingPosition is less than or equal to 0x20 (i.e., it is either an ASCII space or control character), advance encodingPosition to the next byte.
7. If the byte at encodingPosition is not 0x3D (=), then return failure.
8. Advance encodingPosition to the next byte.
9. While the byte at encodingPosition is less than or equal to 0x20 (i.e., it is either an ASCII space or control character), advance encodingPosition to the next byte.
10. Let quoteMark be the byte at encodingPosition.
11. If quoteMark is not either 0x22 (") or 0x27 ('), then return failure.
12. Advance encodingPosition to the next byte.
13. Let encodingEndPosition be the position of the next occurrence of quoteMark at or after encodingPosition. If quoteMark does not occur again, then return failure.
14. Let potentialEncoding be the sequence of the bytes between encodingPosition (inclusive) and encodingEndPosition (exclusive).
15. If potentialEncoding contains one or more bytes whose byte value is 0x20 or below, then return failure.
16. Let encoding be the result of [getting an encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-encoding-get) given potentialEncoding [isomorphic decoded](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-byte-sequences).
17. If the encoding is [UTF-16BE/LE](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-16be-le), then change it to [UTF-8](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8).
18. Return encoding.

For the sake of interoperability, user agents should not use a pre-scan algorithm that returns different results than the one described above. (But, if you do, please at least let us know, so that we can improve this algorithm and benefit everyone...)

##### 13.2.3.3 Character encodings

User agents must support the encodings defined in Encoding, including, but not limited to, [UTF-8](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8), [ISO-8859-2](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#iso-8859-2), [ISO-8859-7](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#iso-8859-7), [ISO-8859-8](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#iso-8859-8), [windows-874](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#windows-874), [windows-1250](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#windows-1250), [windows-1251](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#windows-1251), [windows-1252](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#windows-1252), [windows-1254](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#windows-1254), [windows-1255](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#windows-1255), [windows-1256](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#windows-1256), [windows-1257](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#windows-1257), [windows-1258](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#windows-1258), [GBK](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#gbk), [Big5](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#big5), [ISO-2022-JP](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#iso-2022-jp), [Shift\_JIS](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#shift_jis), [EUC-KR](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#euc-kr), [UTF-16BE](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-16be), [UTF-16LE](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-16le), [UTF-16BE/LE](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-16be-le), and [x-user-defined](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#x-user-defined). User agents must not support other encodings.

> [!note]
> The above prohibits supporting, for example, CESU-8, UTF-7, BOCU-1, SCSU, EBCDIC, and UTF-32. This specification does not make any attempt to support prohibited encodings in its algorithms; support and use of prohibited encodings would thus lead to unexpected behavior. [\[CESU8\]](#references) [\[UTF7\]](#references) [\[BOCU1\]](#references) [\[SCSU\]](#references)

##### 13.2.3.4 Changing the encoding while parsing

When the parser requires the user agent to change the encoding, it must run the following steps. This might happen if the [encoding sniffing algorithm](#13232-determining-the-character-encoding) described above failed to find a character encoding, or if it found a character encoding that was not the actual encoding of the file.
1. If the encoding that is already being used to interpret the input stream is [UTF-16BE/LE](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-16be-le), then set the [confidence](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) to *certain* and return. The new encoding is ignored; if it was anything but the same encoding, then it would be clearly incorrect.
2. If the new encoding is [UTF-16BE/LE](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-16be-le), then change it to [UTF-8](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8).
3. If the new encoding is [x-user-defined](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#x-user-defined), then change it to [windows-1252](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#windows-1252).
4. If the new encoding is identical or equivalent to the encoding that is already being used to interpret the input stream, then set the [confidence](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) to *certain* and return. This happens when the encoding information found in the file matches what the [encoding sniffing algorithm](#13232-determining-the-character-encoding) determined to be the encoding, and in the second pass through the parser if the first pass found that the encoding sniffing algorithm described in the earlier section failed to find the right encoding.
5. If all the bytes up to the last byte converted by the current decoder have the same Unicode interpretations in both the current encoding and the new encoding, and if the user agent supports changing the converter on the fly, then the user agent may change to the new converter for the encoding on the fly. Set the [document's character encoding](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) and the encoding used to convert the input stream to the new encoding, set the [confidence](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) to *certain*, and return.
6. Otherwise, restart the [navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation) algorithm, with *[historyHandling](#7422-beginning-navigation)* set to "[`replace`](#7421-supporting-concepts)" and other inputs kept the same, but this time skip the [encoding sniffing algorithm](#13232-determining-the-character-encoding) and instead just set the encoding to the new encoding and the [confidence](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) to *certain*. Whenever possible, this should be done without actually contacting the network layer (the bytes should be re-parsed from memory), even if, e.g., the document is marked as not being cacheable. If this is not possible and contacting the network layer would involve repeating a request that uses a method other than \``GET`\`, then instead set the [confidence](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) to *certain* and ignore the new encoding. The resource will be misinterpreted. User agents may notify the user of the situation, to aid in application development.

> [!note]
> This algorithm is only invoked when a new encoding is found declared on a [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element.

##### 13.2.3.5 Preprocessing the input stream

The input stream consists of the characters pushed into it as the [input byte stream](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) is decoded or from the various APIs that directly manipulate the input stream.

Any occurrences of [surrogates](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) are [surrogate-in-input-stream](#1322-parse-errors) [parse errors](#1322-parse-errors). Any occurrences of [noncharacters](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) are [noncharacter-in-input-stream](#1322-parse-errors) [parse errors](#1322-parse-errors) and any occurrences of [controls](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) other than [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) and U+0000 NULL characters are [control-character-in-input-stream](#1322-parse-errors) [parse errors](#1322-parse-errors).

> [!note]
> The handling of U+0000 NULL characters varies based on where the characters are found and happens at the later stages of the parsing. They are either ignored or, for security reasons, replaced with a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER. This handling is, by necessity, spread across both the tokenization stage and the tree construction stage.

Before the [tokenization](#1325-tokenization) stage, the input stream must be preprocessed by [normalizing newlines](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings). Thus, newlines in HTML DOMs are represented by U+000A LF characters, and there are never any U+000D CR characters in the input to the [tokenization](#1325-tokenization) stage.

The next input character is the first character in the [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) that has not yet been consumed or explicitly ignored by the requirements in this section. Initially, the *[next input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream)* is the first character in the input. The current input character is the last character to have been *consumed*.

The insertion point is the position (just before a character or just before the end of the input stream) where content inserted using [`document.write()`](#843-documentwrite) is actually inserted. The insertion point is relative to the position of the character immediately after it, it is not an absolute offset into the input stream. Initially, the insertion point is undefined.

The "EOF" character in the tables below is a conceptual character representing the end of the [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream). If the parser is a [script-created parser](#841-opening-the-input-stream), then the end of the [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) is reached when an explicit "EOF" character (inserted by the [`document.close()`](#842-closing-the-input-stream) method) is consumed. Otherwise, the "EOF" character is not a real character in the stream, but rather the lack of any further characters.

#### 13.2.4 Parse state

##### 13.2.4.1 The insertion mode

The insertion mode is a state variable that controls the primary operation of the tree construction stage.

> [!note]
> The rules for parsing tokens [in foreign content](#13265-the-rules-for-parsing-tokens-in-foreign-content) are not an [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode). The [tree construction dispatcher](#1326-tree-construction) selects them independently of the current [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode), which is left unchanged while they are in use.

Initially, the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) is "[initial](#132641-the-initial-insertion-mode)". It can change to "[before html](#132642-the-before-html-insertion-mode)", "[before head](#132643-the-before-head-insertion-mode)", "[in head](#132644-the-in-head-insertion-mode)", "[in head noscript](#132645-the-in-head-noscript-insertion-mode)", "[after head](#132646-the-after-head-insertion-mode)", "[in body](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)", "[text](#132648-the-text-insertion-mode)", "[in table](#132649-the-in-table-insertion-mode)", "[in table text](#1326410-the-in-table-text-insertion-mode)", "[in caption](#1326411-the-in-caption-insertion-mode)", "[in column group](#1326412-the-in-column-group-insertion-mode)", "[in table body](#1326413-the-in-table-body-insertion-mode)", "[in row](#1326414-the-in-row-insertion-mode)", "[in cell](#1326415-the-in-cell-insertion-mode)", "[in template](#1326416-the-in-template-insertion-mode)", "[after body](#1326417-the-after-body-insertion-mode)", "[in frameset](#1326418-the-in-frameset-insertion-mode)", "[after frameset](#1326419-the-after-frameset-insertion-mode)", "[after after body](#1326420-the-after-after-body-insertion-mode)", and "[after after frameset](#1326421-the-after-after-frameset-insertion-mode)" during the course of the parsing, as described in the [tree construction](#1326-tree-construction) stage. The insertion mode affects how tokens are processed.

Several of these modes, namely "[in head](#132644-the-in-head-insertion-mode)", "[in body](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)", and "[in table](#132649-the-in-table-insertion-mode)", are special, in that the other modes defer to them at various times. When the algorithm below says that the user agent is to do something "using the rules for the m insertion mode", where m is one of these modes, the user agent must use the rules described under the m [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode)'s section, but must leave the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) unchanged unless the rules in m themselves switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to a new value.

When the insertion mode is switched to "[text](#132648-the-text-insertion-mode)" or "[in table text](#1326410-the-in-table-text-insertion-mode)", the original insertion mode is also set. This is the insertion mode to which the tree construction stage will return.

Similarly, to parse nested [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) elements, a stack of template insertion modes is used. It is initially empty. The current template insertion mode is the insertion mode that was most recently added to the [stack of template insertion modes](#13241-the-insertion-mode). The algorithms in the sections below will *push* insertion modes onto this stack, meaning that the specified insertion mode is to be added to the stack, and *pop* insertion modes from the stack, which means that the most recently added insertion mode must be removed from the stack.

---

When the steps below require the UA to reset the insertion mode appropriately, it means the UA must follow these steps:
1. Let last be false.
2. Let node be the last node in the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).
3. *Loop*: If node is the first node in the stack of open elements, then set last to true, and, if the parser's [fragment context element](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) is non-null, then set node to that element ([fragment case](#134-parsing-html-fragments)).
4. If node is a [`td`](#499-the-td-element) or [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element and last is false, then switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[in cell](#1326415-the-in-cell-insertion-mode)" and return.
5. If node is a [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element, then switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[in row](#1326414-the-in-row-insertion-mode)" and return.
6. If node is a [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element), [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element), or [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element, then switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[in table body](#1326413-the-in-table-body-insertion-mode)" and return.
7. If node is a [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element) element, then switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[in caption](#1326411-the-in-caption-insertion-mode)" and return.
8. If node is a [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element, then switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[in column group](#1326412-the-in-column-group-insertion-mode)" and return.
9. If node is a [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element, then switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[in table](#132649-the-in-table-insertion-mode)" and return.
10. If node is a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element, then switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to the [current template insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) and return.
11. If node is a [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element and last is false, then switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[in head](#132644-the-in-head-insertion-mode)" and return.
12. If node is a [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element, then switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[in body](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)" and return.
13. If node is a [`frameset`](#1632-frames) element, then switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[in frameset](#1326418-the-in-frameset-insertion-mode)" and return. ([fragment case](#134-parsing-html-fragments))
14. If node is an [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element, run these substeps:
    1. If the [`head` element pointer](#13244-the-element-pointers) is null, switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[before head](#132643-the-before-head-insertion-mode)" and return. ([fragment case](#134-parsing-html-fragments))
    2. Otherwise, the [`head` element pointer](#13244-the-element-pointers) is not null, switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[after head](#132646-the-after-head-insertion-mode)" and return.
15. If last is true, then switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[in body](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)" and return. ([fragment case](#134-parsing-html-fragments))
16. Let node now be the node before node in the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).
17. Return to the step labeled *loop*.

##### 13.2.4.2 The stack of open elements

Initially, the stack of open elements is empty. The stack grows downwards; the topmost node on the stack is the first one added to the stack, and the bottommost node of the stack is the most recently added node in the stack (notwithstanding when the stack is manipulated in a random access fashion as part of [the handling for misnested tags](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)).

> [!note]
> The "[before html](#132642-the-before-html-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) creates the [`html`](#411-the-html-element) [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree), which is then added to the stack.

> [!note]
> In the [fragment case](#134-parsing-html-fragments), the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) is initialized to contain an [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element that is created as part of [that algorithm](#134-parsing-html-fragments). (The [fragment case](#134-parsing-html-fragments) skips the "[before html](#132642-the-before-html-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode).)

The [`html`](#411-the-html-element) node, however it is created, is the topmost node of the stack. It only gets popped off the stack when the parser [finishes](#1327-the-end).

The current node is the bottommost node in this [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).

The adjusted current node is the parser's [fragment context element](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) if that element is non-null and the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) has only one element in it ([fragment case](#134-parsing-html-fragments)); otherwise, the [adjusted current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) is the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).

When the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) is removed from the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements), [process internal resource links](#4686-link-type-expect) given the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).

Elements in the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) fall into the following categories:

Special

The following elements have varying levels of special parsing rules: HTML's [`address`](#4310-the-address-element), [`applet`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`area`](#4813-the-area-element), [`article`](#432-the-article-element), [`aside`](#435-the-aside-element), [`base`](#423-the-base-element), [`basefont`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`bgsound`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`blockquote`](#444-the-blockquote-element), [`body`](#431-the-body-element), [`br`](#4527-the-br-element), [`button`](#4106-the-button-element), [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element), [`center`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`col`](#494-the-col-element), [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element), [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element), [`details`](#4111-the-details-element), [`dir`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`div`](#4416-the-div-element), [`dl`](#449-the-dl-element), [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element), [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element), [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element), [`figcaption`](#4413-the-figcaption-element), [`figure`](#4412-the-figure-element), [`footer`](#439-the-footer-element), [`form`](#4103-the-form-element), [`frame`](#1632-frames), [`frameset`](#1632-frames), [`h1`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements), [`h2`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements), [`h3`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements), [`h4`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements), [`h5`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements), [`h6`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements), [`head`](#421-the-head-element),
