##### 13.2.5.69 CDATA section state

Consume the [next input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream):

U+005D RIGHT SQUARE BRACKET (\])

Switch to the [CDATA section bracket state](#132570-cdata-section-bracket-state).

EOF

This is an [eof-in-cdata](#1322-parse-errors) [parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Emit an end-of-file token.

Anything else

Emit the [current input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) as a character token.

> [!note]
> U+0000 NULL characters are handled in the tree construction stage, as part of the rules for parsing tokens [in foreign content](#13265-the-rules-for-parsing-tokens-in-foreign-content), which is the only place where CDATA sections can appear.

##### 13.2.5.70 CDATA section bracket state

Consume the [next input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream):

U+005D RIGHT SQUARE BRACKET (\])

Switch to the [CDATA section end state](#132571-cdata-section-end-state).

Anything else

Emit a U+005D RIGHT SQUARE BRACKET character token. [Reconsume](#1325-tokenization) in the [CDATA section state](#132569-cdata-section-state).

##### 13.2.5.71 CDATA section end state

Consume the [next input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream):

U+005D RIGHT SQUARE BRACKET (\])

Emit a U+005D RIGHT SQUARE BRACKET character token.

U+003E GREATER-THAN SIGN (>)

Switch to the [data state](#13251-data-state).

Anything else

Emit two U+005D RIGHT SQUARE BRACKET character tokens. [Reconsume](#1325-tokenization) in the [CDATA section state](#132569-cdata-section-state).

##### 13.2.5.72 Processing instruction open state

Consume the [next input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream):

[ASCII alpha](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points)

U+005F LOW LINE (\_)

[Reconsume](#1325-tokenization) in the [processing instruction target state](#132573-processing-instruction-target-state).

EOF

This is an [eof-in-processing-instruction](#1322-parse-errors) [parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Emit an end-of-file token.

Anything else

This is an [invalid-first-character-of-processing-instruction-target](#1322-parse-errors) [parse error](#1322-parse-errors). [Convert the temporary buffer to a comment](#1325-tokenization). [Reconsume](#1325-tokenization) in the [bogus comment state](#132541-bogus-comment-state).

##### 13.2.5.73 Processing instruction target state

Consume the [next input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream):

U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION (tab)

U+000A LINE FEED (LF)

U+000C FORM FEED (FF)

U+0020 SPACE

U+003F QUESTION MARK (?)

U+003E GREATER-THAN SIGN (>)

Let target be the concatenation of the [code points](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) in the [temporary buffer](#1325-tokenization), in the order they were added to the buffer.

If target is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for "`xml`" or "`xml-stylesheet`":
1. This is a [disallowed-processing-instruction-target](#1322-parse-errors) [parse error](#1322-parse-errors).
2. [Convert the temporary buffer to a comment](#1325-tokenization).
3. [Reconsume](#1325-tokenization) in the [bogus comment state](#132541-bogus-comment-state).

Otherwise:
1. Create a processing instruction token whose target is target and data is the empty string.
2. [Reconsume](#1325-tokenization) in the [after processing instruction target state](#132574-after-processing-instruction-target-state).

[ASCII alphanumeric](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points)

U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS (-)

U+005F LOW LINE (\_)

Append the [current input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) to the [temporary buffer](#1325-tokenization).

EOF

This is an [eof-in-processing-instruction](#1322-parse-errors) [parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Emit an end-of-file token.

Anything else

This is an [invalid-processing-instruction-target](#1322-parse-errors) [parse error](#1322-parse-errors). [Convert the temporary buffer to a comment](#1325-tokenization). [Reconsume](#1325-tokenization) in the [bogus comment state](#132541-bogus-comment-state).

##### 13.2.5.74 After processing instruction target state

Consume the [next input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream):

U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION (tab)

U+000A LINE FEED (LF)

U+000C FORM FEED (FF)

U+0020 SPACE

Ignore the character.

Anything else

[Reconsume](#1325-tokenization) in the [processing instruction data state](#132575-processing-instruction-data-state).

##### 13.2.5.75 Processing instruction data state

Consume the [next input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream):

U+003F QUESTION MARK (?)

Switch to the [processing instruction questionable state](#132576-processing-instruction-questionable-state).

U+003E GREATER-THAN SIGN (>)

Switch to the [data state](#13251-data-state). Emit the current processing instruction token.

EOF

This is an [eof-in-processing-instruction](#1322-parse-errors) [parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Emit an end-of-file token.

Anything else

Append the [current input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) to the current processing instruction token's data.

##### 13.2.5.76 Processing instruction questionable state

Consume the [next input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream):

U+003E GREATER-THAN SIGN (>)

Switch to the [data state](#13251-data-state). Emit the current processing instruction token.

EOF

This is an [eof-in-processing-instruction](#1322-parse-errors) [parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Emit an end-of-file token.

Anything else

Append U+003F (?) to the current processing instruction token's data. [Reconsume](#1325-tokenization) in the [processing instruction data state](#132575-processing-instruction-data-state).

##### 13.2.5.77 Character reference state

Set the [temporary buffer](#1325-tokenization) to the empty string. Append a U+0026 AMPERSAND (&) character to the [temporary buffer](#1325-tokenization). Consume the [next input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream):

[ASCII alphanumeric](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points)

[Reconsume](#1325-tokenization) in the [named character reference state](#132578-named-character-reference-state).

U+0023 NUMBER SIGN (#)

Append the [current input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) to the [temporary buffer](#1325-tokenization). Switch to the [numeric character reference state](#132580-numeric-character-reference-state).

Anything else

[Flush code points consumed as a character reference](#1325-tokenization). [Reconsume](#1325-tokenization) in the [return state](#1325-tokenization).

##### 13.2.5.78 Named character reference state

Consume the maximum number of characters possible, where the consumed characters are one of the identifiers in the first column of the [named character references](#135-named-character-references) table. Append each character to the [temporary buffer](#1325-tokenization) when it's consumed.

If there is a match

If the character reference was [consumed as part of an attribute](#1325-tokenization), and the last character matched is not a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;), and the [next input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) is either a U+003D EQUALS SIGN character (=) or an [ASCII alphanumeric](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), then, for historical reasons, [flush code points consumed as a character reference](#1325-tokenization) and switch to the [return state](#1325-tokenization).

Otherwise:
1. If the last character matched is not a U+003B SEMICOLON character (;), then this is a [missing-semicolon-after-character-reference](#1322-parse-errors) [parse error](#1322-parse-errors).
2. Set the [temporary buffer](#1325-tokenization) to the empty string. Append one or two characters corresponding to the character reference name (as given by the second column of the [named character references](#135-named-character-references) table) to the [temporary buffer](#1325-tokenization).
3. [Flush code points consumed as a character reference](#1325-tokenization). Switch to the [return state](#1325-tokenization).

Otherwise

[Flush code points consumed as a character reference](#1325-tokenization). Switch to the [ambiguous ampersand state](#132579-ambiguous-ampersand-state).

> [!example]
> If the markup contains (not in an attribute) the string `I'm &notit; I
>     tell you`, the character reference is parsed as "not", as in, `I'm ¬it;
>     I tell you` (and this is a parse error). But if the markup was `I'm
>     &notin; I tell you`, the character reference would be parsed as "notin;", resulting in `I'm ∉ I tell you` (and no parse error).
> 
> However, if the markup contains the string `I'm &notit; I tell you` in an attribute, no character reference is parsed and string remains intact (and there is no parse error).

##### 13.2.5.79 Ambiguous ampersand state

Consume the [next input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream):

[ASCII alphanumeric](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points)

If the character reference was [consumed as part of an attribute](#1325-tokenization), then append the [current input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) to the current attribute's value. Otherwise, emit the [current input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) as a character token.

U+003B SEMICOLON (;)

This is an [unknown-named-character-reference](#1322-parse-errors) [parse error](#1322-parse-errors). [Reconsume](#1325-tokenization) in the [return state](#1325-tokenization).

Anything else

[Reconsume](#1325-tokenization) in the [return state](#1325-tokenization).

##### 13.2.5.80 Numeric character reference state

Set the character reference code to zero (0).

Consume the [next input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream):

U+0078 LATIN SMALL LETTER X

U+0058 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER X

Append the [current input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) to the [temporary buffer](#1325-tokenization). Switch to the [hexadecimal character reference start state](#132581-hexadecimal-character-reference-start-state).

[ASCII digit](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points)

[Reconsume](#1325-tokenization) in the [decimal character reference state](#132583-decimal-character-reference-state).

Anything else

This is an [absence-of-digits-in-numeric-character-reference](#1322-parse-errors) [parse error](#1322-parse-errors). [Flush code points consumed as a character reference](#1325-tokenization). [Reconsume](#1325-tokenization) in the [return state](#1325-tokenization).

##### 13.2.5.81 Hexadecimal character reference start state

Consume the [next input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream):

[ASCII hex digit](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points)

[Reconsume](#1325-tokenization) in the [hexadecimal character reference state](#132582-hexadecimal-character-reference-state).

Anything else

This is an [absence-of-digits-in-numeric-character-reference](#1322-parse-errors) [parse error](#1322-parse-errors). [Flush code points consumed as a character reference](#1325-tokenization). [Reconsume](#1325-tokenization) in the [return state](#1325-tokenization).

##### 13.2.5.82 Hexadecimal character reference state

Consume the [next input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream):

[ASCII digit](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points)

Multiply the [character reference code](#132580-numeric-character-reference-state) by 16. Add a numeric version of the [current input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) (subtract 0x0030 from the character's code point) to the [character reference code](#132580-numeric-character-reference-state).

[ASCII upper hex digit](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points)

Multiply the [character reference code](#132580-numeric-character-reference-state) by 16. Add a numeric version of the [current input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) as a hexadecimal digit (subtract 0x0037 from the character's code point) to the [character reference code](#132580-numeric-character-reference-state).

[ASCII lower hex digit](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points)

Multiply the [character reference code](#132580-numeric-character-reference-state) by 16. Add a numeric version of the [current input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) as a hexadecimal digit (subtract 0x0057 from the character's code point) to the [character reference code](#132580-numeric-character-reference-state).

U+003B SEMICOLON (;)

Switch to the [numeric character reference end state](#132584-numeric-character-reference-end-state).

Anything else

This is a [missing-semicolon-after-character-reference](#1322-parse-errors) [parse error](#1322-parse-errors). [Reconsume](#1325-tokenization) in the [numeric character reference end state](#132584-numeric-character-reference-end-state).

##### 13.2.5.83 Decimal character reference state

Consume the [next input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream):

[ASCII digit](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points)

Multiply the [character reference code](#132580-numeric-character-reference-state) by 10. Add a numeric version of the [current input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) (subtract 0x0030 from the character's code point) to the [character reference code](#132580-numeric-character-reference-state).

U+003B SEMICOLON (;)

Switch to the [numeric character reference end state](#132584-numeric-character-reference-end-state).

Anything else

This is a [missing-semicolon-after-character-reference](#1322-parse-errors) [parse error](#1322-parse-errors). [Reconsume](#1325-tokenization) in the [numeric character reference end state](#132584-numeric-character-reference-end-state).

##### 13.2.5.84 Numeric character reference end state

Check the [character reference code](#132580-numeric-character-reference-state):
- If the number is 0x00, then this is a [null-character-reference](#1322-parse-errors) [parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Set the [character reference code](#132580-numeric-character-reference-state) to 0xFFFD.
- If the number is greater than 0x10FFFF, then this is a [character-reference-outside-unicode-range](#1322-parse-errors) [parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Set the [character reference code](#132580-numeric-character-reference-state) to 0xFFFD.
- If the number is a [surrogate](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), then this is a [surrogate-character-reference](#1322-parse-errors) [parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Set the [character reference code](#132580-numeric-character-reference-state) to 0xFFFD.
- If the number is a [noncharacter](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), then this is a [noncharacter-character-reference](#1322-parse-errors) [parse error](#1322-parse-errors).
- If the number is 0x0D, or a [control](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) that's not [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points), then this is a [control-character-reference](#1322-parse-errors) [parse error](#1322-parse-errors). If the number is one of the numbers in the first column of the following table, then find the row with that number in the first column, and set the [character reference code](#132580-numeric-character-reference-state) to the number in the second column of that row.

  | Number | Code point |
  | --- | --- |
  | 0x80 | 0x20AC | EURO SIGN (€) |
  | 0x82 | 0x201A | SINGLE LOW-9 QUOTATION MARK (‚) |
  | 0x83 | 0x0192 | LATIN SMALL LETTER F WITH HOOK (ƒ) |
  | 0x84 | 0x201E | DOUBLE LOW-9 QUOTATION MARK („) |
  | 0x85 | 0x2026 | HORIZONTAL ELLIPSIS (…) |
  | 0x86 | 0x2020 | DAGGER (†) |
  | 0x87 | 0x2021 | DOUBLE DAGGER (‡) |
  | 0x88 | 0x02C6 | MODIFIER LETTER CIRCUMFLEX ACCENT (ˆ) |
  | 0x89 | 0x2030 | PER MILLE SIGN (‰) |
  | 0x8A | 0x0160 | LATIN CAPITAL LETTER S WITH CARON (Š) |
  | 0x8B | 0x2039 | SINGLE LEFT-POINTING ANGLE QUOTATION MARK (‹) |
  | 0x8C | 0x0152 | LATIN CAPITAL LIGATURE OE (Œ) |
  | 0x8E | 0x017D | LATIN CAPITAL LETTER Z WITH CARON (Ž) |
  | 0x91 | 0x2018 | LEFT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK (‘) |
  | 0x92 | 0x2019 | RIGHT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK (’) |
  | 0x93 | 0x201C | LEFT DOUBLE QUOTATION MARK (“) |
  | 0x94 | 0x201D | RIGHT DOUBLE QUOTATION MARK (”) |
  | 0x95 | 0x2022 | BULLET (•) |
  | 0x96 | 0x2013 | EN DASH (–) |
  | 0x97 | 0x2014 | EM DASH (—) |
  | 0x98 | 0x02DC | SMALL TILDE (˜) |
  | 0x99 | 0x2122 | TRADE MARK SIGN (™) |
  | 0x9A | 0x0161 | LATIN SMALL LETTER S WITH CARON (š) |
  | 0x9B | 0x203A | SINGLE RIGHT-POINTING ANGLE QUOTATION MARK (›) |
  | 0x9C | 0x0153 | LATIN SMALL LIGATURE OE (œ) |
  | 0x9E | 0x017E | LATIN SMALL LETTER Z WITH CARON (ž) |
  | 0x9F | 0x0178 | LATIN CAPITAL LETTER Y WITH DIAERESIS (Ÿ) |

Set the [temporary buffer](#1325-tokenization) to the empty string. Append a code point equal to the [character reference code](#132580-numeric-character-reference-state) to the [temporary buffer](#1325-tokenization). [Flush code points consumed as a character reference](#1325-tokenization). Switch to the [return state](#1325-tokenization).

#### 13.2.6 Tree construction

The input to the tree construction stage is a sequence of tokens from the [tokenization](#1325-tokenization) stage. The tree construction stage is associated with a DOM [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object when a parser is created. The "output" of this stage consists of dynamically modifying or extending that document's DOM tree.

This specification does not define when an interactive user agent has to render the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) so that it is available to the user, or when it has to begin accepting user input.

---

As each token is emitted from the tokenizer, the user agent must follow the appropriate steps from the following list, known as the tree construction dispatcher:

If the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) is empty

If the [adjusted current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) is an element in the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces)

If the [adjusted current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) is a [MathML text integration point](#1326-tree-construction) and the token is a start tag whose tag name is neither "mglyph" nor "malignmark"

If the [adjusted current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) is a [MathML text integration point](#1326-tree-construction) and the token is a character token

If the [adjusted current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) is a [MathML `annotation-xml`](https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#dfn-annotation-xml) element and the token is a start tag whose tag name is "svg"

If the [adjusted current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) is an [HTML integration point](#1326-tree-construction) and the token is a start tag

If the [adjusted current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) is an [HTML integration point](#1326-tree-construction) and the token is a character token

If the token is an end-of-file token

Process the token according to the rules given in the section corresponding to the current [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) in HTML content.

Otherwise

Process the token according to the rules given in the section for parsing tokens [in foreign content](#13265-the-rules-for-parsing-tokens-in-foreign-content).

The next token is the token that is about to be processed by the [tree construction dispatcher](#1326-tree-construction) (even if the token is subsequently just ignored).

A node is a MathML text integration point if it is one of the following elements:
- A [MathML `mi`](https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#the-mi-element) element
- A [MathML `mo`](https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#operator-fence-separator-or-accent-mo) element
- A [MathML `mn`](https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#number-mn) element
- A [MathML `ms`](https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#string-literal-ms) element
- A [MathML `mtext`](https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#text-mtext) element

A node is an HTML integration point if it is one of the following elements:
- A [MathML `annotation-xml`](https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#dfn-annotation-xml) element whose start tag token had an attribute with the name "encoding" whose value was an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for "`text/html`"
- A [MathML `annotation-xml`](https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#dfn-annotation-xml) element whose start tag token had an attribute with the name "encoding" whose value was an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for "`application/xhtml+xml`"
- An [SVG `foreignObject`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/embedded.html#elementdef-foreignObject) element
- An [SVG `desc`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/struct.html#elementdef-desc) element
- An [SVG `title`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/struct.html#elementdef-title) element

> [!note]
> If the node in question is the parser's [fragment context element](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags), then the start tag token for that element is the "fake" token created by the [HTML fragment parsing algorithm](#134-parsing-html-fragments).

---

> [!note]
> Not all of the tag names mentioned below are conformant tag names in this specification; many are included to handle legacy content. They still form part of the algorithm that implementations are required to implement to claim conformance.

> [!note]
> The algorithm described below places no limit on the depth of the DOM tree generated, or on the length of tag names, attribute names, attribute values, [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) nodes, etc. While implementers are encouraged to [avoid arbitrary limits](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#32-avoid-limits-on-algorithm-inputs), it is recognized that practical concerns will likely force user agents to impose nesting depth constraints.

##### 13.2.6.1 Creating and inserting nodes

An insertion location is a [tuple](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#531-tuples) consisting of a target parent (a [`Node`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)) and a reference child (a [`Node`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) or null).

While the parser is processing a token, it can enable or disable foster parenting. This affects the following algorithm.

To find the appropriate place for inserting a node, given an optional [`Node`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) overrideTarget (default null), perform the following steps. They return an [insertion location](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).
1. Let targetParent be overrideTarget if it is not null; otherwise the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).
2. Let referenceChild be null.
3. If [foster parenting](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) is enabled and targetParent is a [`table`](#491-the-table-element), [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element), [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element), [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element), or [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element:

   > [!note]
   > Foster parenting happens when content is misnested in tables.
   1. Let lastTemplateOrTable be the last [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) or [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element in the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) if there is one; otherwise null.
   2. If lastTemplateOrTable is null, then return (the first element in the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) (the [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element), null). ([fragment case](#134-parsing-html-fragments))
   3. If lastTemplateOrTable is a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element, then set targetParent to lastTemplateOrTable.
   4. Otherwise, if lastTemplateOrTable's [parent](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) is not null, then set targetParent to lastTemplateOrTable's [parent](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) and set referenceChild to lastTemplateOrTable.
   5. Otherwise, set targetParent to the element immediately above lastTemplateOrTable in the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).

   > [!note]
   > These steps are involved in part because it's possible for elements, the [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element in this case in particular, to have been moved by a script around in the DOM, or indeed removed from the DOM entirely, after the element was inserted by the parser.

4. If targetParent is not a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element, then return (targetParent, referenceChild).
5. Let patchInsertionTarget be targetParent's [insertion target](#4123-the-template-element).
6. If patchInsertionTarget is null, then return (targetParent's [template contents](#4123-the-template-element), null).
7. If targetParent's [insertion end marker](#4123-the-template-element) is not null and its [parent](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) is patchInsertionTarget, then return (patchInsertionTarget, targetParent's [insertion end marker](#4123-the-template-element)).

   > [!note]
   > If the end marker has been removed or moved to another node, nodes are instead appended to patchInsertionTarget in the following step.

8. Return (patchInsertionTarget, null).

---

To create an element for a token, given a token token, a string namespace, a [`Node`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) object intendedParent, and an optional string-or-null prefix (default null):
1. If the [active speculative HTML parser](#1328-speculative-html-parsing) is not null, then return the result of [creating a speculative mock element](#1328-speculative-html-parsing) given namespace, token's tag name, and token's attributes.
2. Otherwise, optionally [create a speculative mock element](#1328-speculative-html-parsing) given namespace, token's tag name, and token's attributes.

   > [!note]
   > The result is not used. This step allows for a [speculative fetch](#1328-speculative-html-parsing) to be initiated from non-speculative parsing. The fetch is still speculative at this point, because, for example, by the time the element is inserted, intendedParent might have been removed from the document.

3. Let document be intendedParent's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
4. Let localName be token's tag name.
5. Let is be the value of the "[`is`](#4133-core-concepts)" attribute in token, if such an attribute exists; otherwise null.
6. Let registry be the result of [looking up a custom element registry](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) given intendedParent.
7. Let definition be the result of [looking up a custom element definition](#4133-core-concepts) given registry, namespace, localName, and is.
8. Let willExecuteScript be true if definition is non-null and the parser's [fragment context element](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) is null; otherwise false.
9. If willExecuteScript is true:
   1. Increment document's [throw-on-dynamic-markup-insertion counter](#84-dynamic-markup-insertion).
   2. If the [JavaScript execution context stack](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#execution-context-stack) is empty, then [perform a microtask checkpoint](#8173-processing-model).
   3. Push a new [element queue](#4136-custom-element-reactions) onto document's [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [custom element reactions stack](#4136-custom-element-reactions).
10. Let element be the result of [creating an element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) given document, localName, namespace, prefix, is, willExecuteScript, and registry.

    > [!note]
    > This will cause [custom element constructors](#4133-core-concepts) to run, if willExecuteScript is true. However, since we incremented the [throw-on-dynamic-markup-insertion counter](#84-dynamic-markup-insertion), this cannot cause [new characters to be inserted into the tokenizer](#843-documentwrite), or [the document to be blown away](#841-opening-the-input-stream).

11. [Append](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) each attribute in the given token to element.

    > [!note]
    > This can [enqueue a custom element callback reaction](#4136-custom-element-reactions) for the `attributeChangedCallback`, which might run immediately (in the next step).

    > [!note]
    > Even though the [`is`](#4133-core-concepts) attribute governs the [creation](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) of a [customized built-in element](#4133-core-concepts), it is not present during the execution of the relevant [custom element constructor](#4133-core-concepts); it is appended in this step, along with all other attributes.

12. If willExecuteScript is true:
    1. Let queue be the result of popping from document's [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [custom element reactions stack](#4136-custom-element-reactions). (This will be the same [element queue](#4136-custom-element-reactions) as was pushed above.)
    2. [Invoke custom element reactions](#4136-custom-element-reactions) in queue.
    3. Decrement document's [throw-on-dynamic-markup-insertion counter](#84-dynamic-markup-insertion).
13. If element has an `xmlns` attribute *in the [XMLNS namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces)* whose value is not exactly the same as the element's namespace, that is a [parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Similarly, if element has an `xmlns:xlink` attribute in the [XMLNS namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) whose value is not the [XLink Namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces), that is a [parse error](#1322-parse-errors).
14. If element is a [resettable element](#4102-categories) and not a [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts), then invoke its [reset algorithm](#41023-resetting-a-form). (This initializes the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) and [checkedness](#410181-a-form-controls-value) based on the element's attributes.)
15. If element is a [form-associated element](#4102-categories) and not a [form-associated custom element](#4133-core-concepts), the [`form` element pointer](#13244-the-element-pointers) is not null, the parser is not [parsing template contents](#13244-the-element-pointers), the parser's [fragment context element](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) is null, element is either not [listed](#4102-categories) or doesn't have a [`form`](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) attribute, and the intendedParent is in the same [tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) as the element pointed to by the [`form` element pointer](#13244-the-element-pointers), then [associate](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms) element with the [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element pointed to by the [`form` element pointer](#13244-the-element-pointers) and set element's [parser inserted flag](#410183-association-of-controls-and-forms).
16. Return element.

To compute the adjusted insertion location with an optional [insertion location](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) insertionLocation (default null):
1. Let overrideTarget be null if insertionLocation is null; otherwise insertionLocation's [target parent](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).
2. Let adjustedInsertionLocation be the [appropriate place for inserting a node](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) given overrideTarget.
3. If adjustedInsertionLocation's [target parent](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) is the first element in the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) and the parser's [root insertion target](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) is non-null, then set adjustedInsertionLocation to (the parser's [root insertion target](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags), null).
4. Return adjustedInsertionLocation.

---

To insert an element at the adjusted insertion location with an element element and an optional [insertion location](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) insertionLocation (default null):
1. Let (targetParent, referenceChild) be the [adjusted insertion location](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) given insertionLocation.
2. If any of the following are true:
   - element's [parent](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) is non-null;
   - element is a [host-including inclusive ancestor](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) of targetParent; or
   - targetParent is a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) node that already has an element child,

   then return.

3. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): [ensure pre-insert validity](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) given element, targetParent, referenceChild, and « » does not throw.
4. If the parser's [fragment context element](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) is null, then push a new [element queue](#4136-custom-element-reactions) onto element's [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [custom element reactions stack](#4136-custom-element-reactions).
5. [Insert](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) element into targetParent before referenceChild.
6. If the parser's [fragment context element](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) is null, then pop the [element queue](#4136-custom-element-reactions) from element's [relevant agent](#8121-integration-with-the-javascript-agent-formalism)'s [custom element reactions stack](#4136-custom-element-reactions), and [invoke custom element reactions](#4136-custom-element-reactions) in that queue.

To insert a foreign element, given a token token, a string namespace, and a boolean onlyAddToElementStack:
1. Let adjustedInsertionLocation be the [appropriate place for inserting a node](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).
2. Let element be the result of [creating an element for the token](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) given token, namespace, and adjustedInsertionLocation's [target parent](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).
3. If onlyAddToElementStack is false, then run [insert an element at the adjusted insertion location](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) with element.
4. Push element onto the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) so that it is the new [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).
5. Return element.

To insert an HTML element given a token token: [insert a foreign element](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) given token, the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces), and false.

---

When the steps below require the user agent to insert a character while processing a token, the user agent must run the following steps:
1. Let data be the characters passed to the algorithm, or, if no characters were explicitly specified, the character of the character token being processed.
2. Let (targetParent, referenceChild) be the [adjusted insertion location](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).
3. If targetParent is a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) node, then return.

   > [!note]
   > The DOM will not let [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) nodes have [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node children, so they are dropped on the floor.

4. Let previousSibling be referenceChild's [previous sibling](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) if referenceChild is non-null; otherwise targetParent's [last child](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
5. If previousSibling is a [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node, then append data to previousSibling's [data](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#410-interface-characterdata).

   Otherwise, let text be the result of [creating a text node](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) given targetParent's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) and data, and [insert](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) text into targetParent before referenceChild.

> [!example]
> Here are some sample inputs to the parser and the corresponding number of [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) nodes that they result in, assuming a user agent that executes scripts.
> 
> ```html
> A<script>
> var script = document.getElementsByTagName('script')[0];
> document.body.removeChild(script);
> </script>B
> ```
> 
> ```html
> A<script>
> var text = document.createTextNode('B');
> document.body.appendChild(text);
> </script>C
> ```
> 
> ```html
> A<script>
> var text = document.getElementsByTagName('script')[0].firstChild;
> text.data = 'B';
> document.body.appendChild(text);
> </script>C
> ```
> 
> ```html
> A<table>B<tr>C</tr>D</table>
> ```
> 
> ```html
> A<table><tr> B</tr> C</table>
> ```
> 
> ```html
> A<table><tr> B</tr> </em>C</table>
> ```
> 
> | Input | Number of [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) nodes |
> | --- | --- |
> |  | One [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node in the document, containing "AB". |
> |  | Three [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) nodes; "A" before the script, the script's contents, and "BC" after the script (the parser appends to the [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node created by the script). |
> |  | Two adjacent [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) nodes in the document, containing "A" and "BC". |
> |  | One [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node before the table, containing "ABCD". (This is caused by [foster parenting](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).) |
> |  | One [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node before the table, containing "A B C" (A-space-B-space-C). (This is caused by [foster parenting](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).) |
> |  | One [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node before the table, containing "A BC" (A-space-B-C), and one [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node inside the table (as a child of a [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element)) with a single space character. (Space characters separated from non-space characters by non-character tokens are not affected by [foster parenting](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes), even if those other tokens then get ignored.) |

---

When the steps below require the user agent to insert a comment while processing a comment token, with an optional [insertion location](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) insertionLocation (default null), the user agent must run the following steps:
1. Let data be the data given in the comment token being processed.
2. Let (targetParent, referenceChild) be the [adjusted insertion location](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) given insertionLocation.
3. Let comment be the result of [creating a comment node](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#414-interface-comment) given targetParent's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) and data.
4. [Insert](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) comment into targetParent before referenceChild.

When the steps below require the user agent to insert a processing instruction while processing a processing instruction token, with an optional [insertion location](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) insertionLocation (default null), the user agent must run the following steps:
1. Let piTarget be the target given in the processing instruction token being processed.
2. Let data be the data given in the processing instruction token being processed.
3. Let (targetParent, referenceChild) be the [adjusted insertion location](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) given insertionLocation.
4. Let pi be the result of [creating a processing instruction node](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#413-interface-processinginstruction) given targetParent's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), piTarget, and data.
5. [Insert](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) pi into targetParent before referenceChild.

##### 13.2.6.2 Parsing elements that contain only text

The generic raw text element parsing algorithm and the generic RCDATA element parsing algorithm consist of the following steps. These algorithms are always invoked in response to a start tag token.
1. [Insert an HTML element](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) for the token.
2. If the algorithm that was invoked is the [generic raw text element parsing algorithm](#13262-parsing-elements-that-contain-only-text), switch the tokenizer to the [RAWTEXT state](#13253-rawtext-state); otherwise the algorithm invoked was the [generic RCDATA element parsing algorithm](#13262-parsing-elements-that-contain-only-text), switch the tokenizer to the [RCDATA state](#13252-rcdata-state).
3. Set the [original insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to the current [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode).
4. Then, switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[text](#132648-the-text-insertion-mode)".

##### 13.2.6.3 Closing elements that have implied end tags

When the steps below require the UA to generate implied end tags, then, while the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) is a [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) element, a [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) element, an [`li`](#448-the-li-element) element, an [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element, an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element, a [`p`](#441-the-p-element) element, an [`rb`](#162-non-conforming-features) element, an [`rp`](#4512-the-rp-element) element, an [`rt`](#4511-the-rt-element) element, or an [`rtc`](#162-non-conforming-features) element, the UA must pop the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) off the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).

If a step requires the UA to generate implied end tags but lists an element to exclude from the process, then the UA must perform the above steps as if that element was not in the above list.

When the steps below require the UA to generate all implied end tags thoroughly, then, while the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) is a [`caption`](#492-the-caption-element) element, a [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element, a [`dd`](#4411-the-dd-element) element, a [`dt`](#4410-the-dt-element) element, an [`li`](#448-the-li-element) element, an [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element, an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element, a [`p`](#441-the-p-element) element, an [`rb`](#162-non-conforming-features) element, an [`rp`](#4512-the-rp-element) element, an [`rt`](#4511-the-rt-element) element, an [`rtc`](#162-non-conforming-features) element, a [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) element, a [`td`](#499-the-td-element) element, a [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) element, a [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element, a [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element) element, or a [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element, the UA must pop the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) off the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).

##### 13.2.6.4 The rules for parsing tokens in HTML content

###### 13.2.6.4.1 The "initial" insertion mode

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object has an associated parser cannot change the mode flag (a boolean). It is initially false.

When the user agent is to apply the rules for the "[initial](#132641-the-initial-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode), the user agent must handle the token as follows:

A character token that is one of U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION, U+000A LINE FEED (LF), U+000C FORM FEED (FF), U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR), or U+0020 SPACE

Ignore the token.

A comment token

[Insert a comment](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) given (the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object, null).

A processing instruction token

[Insert a processing instruction](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) given (the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object, null).

A DOCTYPE token

If the DOCTYPE token's name is not "`html`", or the token's public identifier is not missing, or the token's system identifier is neither missing nor "[`about:legacy-compat`](#241-terminology)", then there is a [parse error](#1322-parse-errors).

Let doctype be the result of [creating a doctype](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-interface-documenttype) given the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) node, the name given in the DOCTYPE token (or the empty string if the name was missing), the public identifier given in the DOCTYPE token (or the empty string if the public identifier was missing), and the system identifier given in the DOCTYPE token (or the empty string if the system identifier was missing). Then, if the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) node has neither a [`DocumentType`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-interface-documenttype) child nor an element child, append doctype to the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) node.

> [!note]
> This also ensures that the [`DocumentType`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-interface-documenttype) node is returned as the value of the [`doctype`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) attribute of the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object.

Then, if the document is *not* [an `iframe` `srcdoc` document](#485-the-iframe-element), and the [parser cannot change the mode flag](#132641-the-initial-insertion-mode) is false, and the DOCTYPE token matches one of the conditions in the following list, then set the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) to [quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document):
- The *[force-quirks flag](#1325-tokenization)* is set to *on*.
- The name is not "`html`".
- The public identifier is set to: "`-//W3O//DTD W3 HTML Strict 3.0//EN//`"
- The public identifier is set to: "`-/W3C/DTD HTML 4.0 Transitional/EN`"
- The public identifier is set to: "`HTML`"
- The system identifier is set to: "`http://www.ibm.com/data/dtd/v11/ibmxhtml1-transitional.dtd`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`+//Silmaril//dtd html Pro v0r11 19970101//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//AS//DTD HTML 3.0 asWedit + extensions//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//AdvaSoft Ltd//DTD HTML 3.0 asWedit + extensions//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//IETF//DTD HTML 2.0 Level 1//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//IETF//DTD HTML 2.0 Level 2//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//IETF//DTD HTML 2.0 Strict Level 1//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//IETF//DTD HTML 2.0 Strict Level 2//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//IETF//DTD HTML 2.0 Strict//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//IETF//DTD HTML 2.0//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//IETF//DTD HTML 2.1E//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//IETF//DTD HTML 3.0//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//IETF//DTD HTML 3.2 Final//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//IETF//DTD HTML 3.2//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//IETF//DTD HTML 3//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//IETF//DTD HTML Level 0//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//IETF//DTD HTML Level 1//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//IETF//DTD HTML Level 2//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//IETF//DTD HTML Level 3//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//IETF//DTD HTML Strict Level 0//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//IETF//DTD HTML Strict Level 1//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//IETF//DTD HTML Strict Level 2//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//IETF//DTD HTML Strict Level 3//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//IETF//DTD HTML Strict//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//IETF//DTD HTML//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//Metrius//DTD Metrius Presentational//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//Microsoft//DTD Internet Explorer 2.0 HTML Strict//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//Microsoft//DTD Internet Explorer 2.0 HTML//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//Microsoft//DTD Internet Explorer 2.0 Tables//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//Microsoft//DTD Internet Explorer 3.0 HTML Strict//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//Microsoft//DTD Internet Explorer 3.0 HTML//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//Microsoft//DTD Internet Explorer 3.0 Tables//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//Netscape Comm. Corp.//DTD HTML//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//Netscape Comm. Corp.//DTD Strict HTML//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//O'Reilly and Associates//DTD HTML 2.0//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//O'Reilly and Associates//DTD HTML Extended 1.0//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//O'Reilly and Associates//DTD HTML Extended Relaxed 1.0//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//SQ//DTD HTML 2.0 HoTMetaL + extensions//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//SoftQuad Software//DTD HoTMetaL PRO 6.0::19990601::extensions to HTML 4.0//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//SoftQuad//DTD HoTMetaL PRO 4.0::19971010::extensions to HTML 4.0//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//Spyglass//DTD HTML 2.0 Extended//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//Sun Microsystems Corp.//DTD HotJava HTML//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//Sun Microsystems Corp.//DTD HotJava Strict HTML//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//W3C//DTD HTML 3 1995-03-24//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2 Draft//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2 Final//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//W3C//DTD HTML 3.2S Draft//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.0 Frameset//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.0 Transitional//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//W3C//DTD HTML Experimental 19960712//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//W3C//DTD HTML Experimental 970421//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//W3C//DTD W3 HTML//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//W3O//DTD W3 HTML 3.0//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//WebTechs//DTD Mozilla HTML 2.0//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//WebTechs//DTD Mozilla HTML//`"
- The system identifier is missing or the empty string, and the public identifier starts with: "`-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.01 Frameset//`"
- The system identifier is missing or the empty string, and the public identifier starts with: "`-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.01 Transitional//`"

Otherwise, if the document is *not* [an `iframe` `srcdoc` document](#485-the-iframe-element), and the [parser cannot change the mode flag](#132641-the-initial-insertion-mode) is false, and the DOCTYPE token matches one of the conditions in the following list, then set the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) to [limited-quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document):
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Frameset//`"
- The public identifier starts with: "`-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Transitional//`"
- The system identifier is neither missing nor the empty string, and the public identifier starts with: "`-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.01 Frameset//`"
- The system identifier is neither missing nor the empty string, and the public identifier starts with: "`-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.01 Transitional//`"

The system identifier and public identifier strings must be compared to the values given in the lists above in an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) manner. A system identifier whose value is the empty string is not considered missing for the purposes of the conditions above.

Then, switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[before html](#132642-the-before-html-insertion-mode)".

Anything else

If the document is *not* [an `iframe` `srcdoc` document](#485-the-iframe-element), then this is a [parse error](#1322-parse-errors); if the [parser cannot change the mode flag](#132641-the-initial-insertion-mode) is false, set the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) to [quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

In any case, switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[before html](#132642-the-before-html-insertion-mode)", then reprocess the token.

###### 13.2.6.4.2 The "before html" insertion mode

When the user agent is to apply the rules for the "[before html](#132642-the-before-html-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode), the user agent must handle the token as follows:

A DOCTYPE token

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Ignore the token.

A comment token

[Insert a comment](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) given (the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object, null).

A processing instruction token

[Insert a processing instruction](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) given (the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object, null).

A character token that is one of U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION, U+000A LINE FEED (LF), U+000C FORM FEED (FF), U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR), or U+0020 SPACE

Ignore the token.

A start tag whose tag name is "html"

[Create an element for the token](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) in the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces), with the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) as the intended parent. [Insert an element at the adjusted insertion location](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) with that element and (the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), null). Put this element in the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).

Switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[before head](#132643-the-before-head-insertion-mode)".

An end tag whose tag name is one of: "head", "body", "html", "br"

Act as described in the "anything else" entry below.

Any other end tag

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Ignore the token.

Anything else

Create an [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element whose [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) is the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object. Append it to the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object. Put this element in the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).

Switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[before head](#132643-the-before-head-insertion-mode)", then reprocess the token.

The [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) can end up being removed from the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object, e.g. by scripts; nothing in particular happens in such cases, content continues being appended to the nodes as described in the next section.

###### 13.2.6.4.3 The "before head" insertion mode

When the user agent is to apply the rules for the "[before head](#132643-the-before-head-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode), the user agent must handle the token as follows:

A character token that is one of U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION, U+000A LINE FEED (LF), U+000C FORM FEED (FF), U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR), or U+0020 SPACE

Ignore the token.

A comment token

[Insert a comment](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

A processing instruction token

[Insert a processing instruction](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

A DOCTYPE token

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Ignore the token.

A start tag whose tag name is "html"

Process the token [using the rules for](#13241-the-insertion-mode) the "[in body](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode).

A start tag whose tag name is "head"

[Insert an HTML element](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) for the token.

Set the [`head` element pointer](#13244-the-element-pointers) to the newly created [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element.

Switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[in head](#132644-the-in-head-insertion-mode)".

An end tag whose tag name is one of: "head", "body", "html", "br"

Act as described in the "anything else" entry below.

Any other end tag

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Ignore the token.

Anything else

[Insert an HTML element](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) for a "head" start tag token with no attributes.

Set the [`head` element pointer](#13244-the-element-pointers) to the newly created [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element.

Switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[in head](#132644-the-in-head-insertion-mode)".

Reprocess the current token.

###### 13.2.6.4.4 The "in head" insertion mode

When the user agent is to apply the rules for the "[in head](#132644-the-in-head-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode), the user agent must handle the token as follows:

A character token that is one of U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION, U+000A LINE FEED (LF), U+000C FORM FEED (FF), U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR), or U+0020 SPACE

[Insert the character](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

A comment token

[Insert a comment](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

A processing instruction token

[Insert a processing instruction](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

A DOCTYPE token

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Ignore the token.

A start tag whose tag name is "html"

Process the token [using the rules for](#13241-the-insertion-mode) the "[in body](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode).

A start tag whose tag name is one of: "base", "basefont", "bgsound", "link"

[Insert an HTML element](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) for the token. Immediately pop the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) off the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).

[Acknowledge the token's *self-closing flag*](#1325-tokenization), if it is set.

A start tag whose tag name is "meta"

[Insert an HTML element](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) for the token. Immediately pop the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) off the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).

[Acknowledge the token's *self-closing flag*](#1325-tokenization), if it is set.

If the [active speculative HTML parser](#1328-speculative-html-parsing) is null:
1. If the element has a [`charset`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute, and [getting an encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-encoding-get) from its value results in an [encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#encoding), and the [confidence](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) is currently *tentative*, then [change the encoding](#13234-changing-the-encoding-while-parsing) to the resulting encoding.
2. Otherwise, if the element has an [`http-equiv`](#4253-pragma-directives) attribute whose value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for "`Content-Type`", and the element has a [`content`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute, and applying the [algorithm for extracting a character encoding from a `meta` element](#253-extracting-character-encodings-from-meta-elements) to that attribute's value returns an [encoding](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#encoding), and the [confidence](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) is currently *tentative*, then [change the encoding](#13234-changing-the-encoding-while-parsing) to the extracted encoding.

> [!note]
> The [speculative HTML parser](#1328-speculative-html-parsing) doesn't speculatively apply character encoding declarations in order to reduce implementation complexity.

A start tag whose tag name is "title"

Follow the [generic RCDATA element parsing algorithm](#13262-parsing-elements-that-contain-only-text).

A start tag whose tag name is "noscript", if [scripting mode](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) is not [Disabled](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags)

A start tag whose tag name is one of: "noframes", "style"

Follow the [generic raw text element parsing algorithm](#13262-parsing-elements-that-contain-only-text).

A start tag whose tag name is "noscript", if [scripting mode](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) is [Disabled](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags)

[Insert an HTML element](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) for the token.

Switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[in head noscript](#132645-the-in-head-noscript-insertion-mode)".

A start tag whose tag name is "script"

Run these steps:
1. Let adjustedInsertionLocation be the [appropriate place for inserting a node](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).
2. [Create an element for the token](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) in the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces), with the intended parent being the node in which the adjustedInsertionLocation finds itself.
3. If the [scripting mode](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) is not [Fragment](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags), then set the element's [parser document](#41211-processing-model) to the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object).

   > [!note]
   > The [Fragment](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) [scripting mode](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) treats [parser-inserted](#41211-processing-model) scripts as if they were not parser-inserted, allowing, for example, executing scripts when applying a fragment created by [`createContextualFragment()`](#857-the-createcontextualfragment-method).

4. Set the element's [force async](#41211-processing-model) to false.

   > [!note]
   > This ensures that, if the script is external, any [`document.write()`](#843-documentwrite) calls in the script will execute in-line, instead of blowing the document away, as would happen in most other cases. It also prevents the script from executing until the end tag is seen.

5. If the parser's [scripting mode](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) is [Inert](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags), then set the [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element's [already started](#41211-processing-model) to true. ([fragment case](#134-parsing-html-fragments))
6. If the parser was invoked via the [`document.write()`](#843-documentwrite) or [`document.writeln()`](#844-documentwriteln) methods, then optionally set the [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element's [already started](#41211-processing-model) to true. (For example, the user agent might use this clause to prevent execution of [cross-origin](#711-origins) scripts inserted via [`document.write()`](#843-documentwrite) under slow network conditions, or when the page has already taken a long time to load.)
7. [Insert an element at the adjusted insertion location](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) with the newly created element and adjustedInsertionLocation.
8. Push the element onto the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) so that it is the new [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).
9. Switch the tokenizer to the [script data state](#13254-script-data-state).
10. Set the [original insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to the current [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode).
11. Switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[text](#132648-the-text-insertion-mode)".

An end tag whose tag name is "head"

Pop the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) (which will be the [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element) off the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).

Switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[after head](#132646-the-after-head-insertion-mode)".

An end tag whose tag name is one of: "body", "html", "br"

Act as described in the "anything else" entry below.

A start tag whose tag name is "template"

Run these steps:
1. Let templateStartTag be the start tag.
2. Insert a [marker](#13243-the-list-of-active-formatting-elements) at the end of the [list of active formatting elements](#13243-the-list-of-active-formatting-elements).
3. Set the [frameset-ok flag](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) to "not ok".
4. Switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[in template](#1326416-the-in-template-insertion-mode)".
5. Push "[in template](#1326416-the-in-template-insertion-mode)" onto the [stack of template insertion modes](#13241-the-insertion-mode) so that it is the new [current template insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode).
6. Let adjustedInsertionLocation be the [appropriate place for inserting a node](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).
7. If templateStartTag's [`shadowrootmode`](#4123-the-template-element) is not in the [None](#4123-the-template-element) state:
   1. If the parser's [allow declarative shadow roots](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) is false, or the [adjusted current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) is the topmost element in the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements), then [insert an HTML element](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) for the token and return.
   2. Let declarativeShadowHostElement be the [adjusted current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).
   3. Let template be the result of [insert a foreign element](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) for templateStartTag, with [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) and true.
   4. Let mode be templateStartTag's [`shadowrootmode`](#4123-the-template-element) attribute's value.
   5. Let delegatesFocus be true if templateStartTag has a [`shadowrootdelegatesfocus`](#4123-the-template-element) attribute; otherwise false.
   6. Let serializable be true if templateStartTag has a [`shadowrootserializable`](#4123-the-template-element) attribute; otherwise false.
   7. Let slotAssignment be "`named`".
   8. If templateStartTag's [`shadowrootslotassignment`](#4123-the-template-element) attribute is in the [Manual](#4123-the-template-element) state, then set slotAssignment to "`manual`".
   9. Let clonable be true if templateStartTag has a [`shadowrootclonable`](#4123-the-template-element) attribute; otherwise false.
   10. If declarativeShadowHostElement is a [shadow host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), then [insert an element at the adjusted insertion location](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) with template and adjustedInsertionLocation.
   11. Otherwise:
       1. Let registry be null if templateStartTag has a [`shadowrootcustomelementregistry`](#4123-the-template-element) attribute; otherwise declarativeShadowHostElement's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element).
       2. [Attach a shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) with declarativeShadowHostElement, mode, delegatesFocus, serializable, slotAssignment, clonable, and registry.

          If an exception is thrown, then catch it and:
          1. [Insert an element at the adjusted insertion location](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) with template and adjustedInsertionLocation.
          2. The user agent may report an error to the developer console.
          3. Return.

       3. Let shadow be declarativeShadowHostElement's [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element).
       4. Set shadow's [available to element internals](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) to true.
       5. Set shadow's [declarative](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) to true.
       6. Set template's [template contents](#4123-the-template-element) to shadow.
       7. If templateStartTag has a [`shadowrootcustomelementregistry`](#4123-the-template-element) attribute, then set shadow's [keep custom element registry null](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) to true.

8. Otherwise, if templateStartTag's [`for`](#4123-the-template-element) attribute is specified:
   1. Let scope be the node that contains the [adjusted insertion location](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

      > [!note]
      > In the [fragment case](#134-parsing-html-fragments), scope can be the [`DocumentFragment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) into which nodes are being inserted.

   2. If scope is a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element, then set scope to scope's [template contents](#4123-the-template-element).

      > [!note]
      > This is to support patching inside plain [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) elements or those using [`shadowrootmode`](#4123-the-template-element). Nested patching is not supported, since in this case the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element's [template contents](#4123-the-template-element) will have no children and [prepare content patching](#4123-the-template-element) will fail.

   3. Otherwise, if scope is [the body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors) of its [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), then set scope to its [parent](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).

      > [!note]
      > This is to support patching [`head`](#421-the-head-element) with a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) inside [`body`](#431-the-body-element).

   4. Let template be the result of [insert a foreign element](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) for templateStartTag, with [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) and true.
   5. Let success be the result of [prepare content patching](#4123-the-template-element) given scope and template.
   6. If success is false:
      1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): template is the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).
      2. Pop the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) off the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).
      3. [Insert an element at the adjusted insertion location](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) with template.
      4. Push template onto the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).

         > [!note]
         > The above steps undo the effect of the *onlyAddToElementStack* argument from the [insert a foreign element](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) call that created template, inserting it where it would have been inserted otherwise. This is to signal an error.

9. Otherwise, [insert an HTML element](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) for templateStartTag.

An end tag whose tag name is "template"

If there is no [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element on the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements), then this is a [parse error](#1322-parse-errors); ignore the token.

Otherwise, run these steps:
1. [Generate all implied end tags thoroughly](#13263-closing-elements-that-have-implied-end-tags).
2. If the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) is not a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element, then this is a [parse error](#1322-parse-errors).
3. Let template be the last [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element in the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).

   > [!note]
   > This is the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element that will be popped from the stack below. It is not necessarily the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements), as the content of a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element with a [`for`](#4123-the-template-element) attribute might have left an element open.

4. If template's [insertion target](#4123-the-template-element) is not null:
   1. Let start be template's [insertion start marker](#4123-the-template-element).
   2. Let end be template's [insertion end marker](#4123-the-template-element).
   3. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): start is not null.
   4. If start's [parent](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) is not null, then [remove](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) start.
   5. If end is not null and end's [parent](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) is not null, then [remove](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) end.
   6. Set template's [insertion target](#4123-the-template-element) to null.
   7. Set template's [insertion start marker](#4123-the-template-element) to null.
   8. Set template's [insertion end marker](#4123-the-template-element) to null.
5. Pop elements from the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) until a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element has been popped from the stack.
6. [Clear the list of active formatting elements up to the last marker](#13243-the-list-of-active-formatting-elements).
7. Pop the [current template insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) off the [stack of template insertion modes](#13241-the-insertion-mode).
8. [Reset the insertion mode appropriately](#13241-the-insertion-mode).

A start tag whose tag name is "head"

Any other end tag

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Ignore the token.

Anything else

Pop the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) (which will be the [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element) off the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).

Switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[after head](#132646-the-after-head-insertion-mode)".

Reprocess the token.

###### 13.2.6.4.5 The "in head noscript" insertion mode

When the user agent is to apply the rules for the "[in head noscript](#132645-the-in-head-noscript-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode), the user agent must handle the token as follows:

A DOCTYPE token

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Ignore the token.

A start tag whose tag name is "html"

Process the token [using the rules for](#13241-the-insertion-mode) the "[in body](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode).

An end tag whose tag name is "noscript"

Pop the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) (which will be a [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element) from the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements); the new [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) will be a [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element.

Switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[in head](#132644-the-in-head-insertion-mode)".

A character token that is one of U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION, U+000A LINE FEED (LF), U+000C FORM FEED (FF), U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR), or U+0020 SPACE

A comment token

A processing instruction token

A start tag whose tag name is one of: "basefont", "bgsound", "link", "meta", "noframes", "style"

Process the token [using the rules for](#13241-the-insertion-mode) the "[in head](#132644-the-in-head-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode).

An end tag whose tag name is "br"

Act as described in the "anything else" entry below.

A start tag whose tag name is one of: "head", "noscript"

Any other end tag

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Ignore the token.

Anything else

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors).

Pop the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) (which will be a [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element) from the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements); the new [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) will be a [`head`](#421-the-head-element) element.

Switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[in head](#132644-the-in-head-insertion-mode)".

Reprocess the token.

###### 13.2.6.4.6 The "after head" insertion mode

When the user agent is to apply the rules for the "[after head](#132646-the-after-head-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode), the user agent must handle the token as follows:

A character token that is one of U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION, U+000A LINE FEED (LF), U+000C FORM FEED (FF), U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR), or U+0020 SPACE

[Insert the character](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

A comment token

[Insert a comment](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

A processing instruction token

[Insert a processing instruction](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

A DOCTYPE token

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Ignore the token.

A start tag whose tag name is "html"

Process the token [using the rules for](#13241-the-insertion-mode) the "[in body](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode).

A start tag whose tag name is "body"

[Insert an HTML element](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) for the token.

Set the [frameset-ok flag](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) to "not ok".

Switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[in body](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)".

A start tag whose tag name is "frameset"

[Insert an HTML element](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) for the token.

Switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[in frameset](#1326418-the-in-frameset-insertion-mode)".

A start tag whose tag name is one of: "base", "basefont", "bgsound", "link", "meta", "noframes", "script", "style", "template", "title"

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors).

Push the node pointed to by the [`head` element pointer](#13244-the-element-pointers) onto the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).

Process the token [using the rules for](#13241-the-insertion-mode) the "[in head](#132644-the-in-head-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode).

Remove the node pointed to by the [`head` element pointer](#13244-the-element-pointers) from the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements). (It might not be the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) at this point.)

> [!note]
> The [`head` element pointer](#13244-the-element-pointers) cannot be null at this point.

An end tag whose tag name is "template"

Process the token [using the rules for](#13241-the-insertion-mode) the "[in head](#132644-the-in-head-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode).

An end tag whose tag name is one of: "body", "html", "br"

Act as described in the "anything else" entry below.

A start tag whose tag name is "head"

Any other end tag

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Ignore the token.

Anything else

[Insert an HTML element](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) for a "body" start tag token with no attributes.

Set the [frameset-ok flag](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) to "ok".

Switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[in body](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)".

Reprocess the current token.

###### 13.2.6.4.7 The "in body" insertion mode

When the user agent is to apply the rules for the "[in body](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode), the user agent must handle the token as follows:

A character token that is U+0000 NULL

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Ignore the token.

A character token that is one of U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION, U+000A LINE FEED (LF), U+000C FORM FEED (FF), U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR), or U+0020 SPACE

[Reconstruct the active formatting elements](#13243-the-list-of-active-formatting-elements), if any.

[Insert the token's character](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

Any other character token

[Reconstruct the active formatting elements](#13243-the-list-of-active-formatting-elements), if any.

[Insert the token's character](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

Set the [frameset-ok flag](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) to "not ok".

A comment token

[Insert a comment](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

A processing instruction token

[Insert a processing instruction](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

A DOCTYPE token

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Ignore the token.

A start tag whose tag name is "html"

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors).

If there is a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element on the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements), then ignore the token.

Otherwise, for each attribute on the token, check to see if the attribute is already present on the top element of the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements). If it is not, add the attribute and its corresponding value to that element.

A start tag whose tag name is one of: "base", "basefont", "bgsound", "link", "meta", "noframes", "script", "style", "template", "title"

An end tag whose tag name is "template"

Process the token [using the rules for](#13241-the-insertion-mode) the "[in head](#132644-the-in-head-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode).

A start tag whose tag name is "body"

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors).
