Push "[in row](#1326414-the-in-row-insertion-mode)" onto the [stack of template insertion modes](#13241-the-insertion-mode) so that it is the new [current template insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode).

Switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[in row](#1326414-the-in-row-insertion-mode)", and reprocess the token.

Any other start tag

Pop the [current template insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) off the [stack of template insertion modes](#13241-the-insertion-mode).

Push "[in body](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)" onto the [stack of template insertion modes](#13241-the-insertion-mode) so that it is the new [current template insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode).

Switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[in body](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)", and reprocess the token.

Any other end tag

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Ignore the token.

An end-of-file token

If there is no [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element on the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements), then [stop parsing](#1327-the-end). ([fragment case](#134-parsing-html-fragments))

Otherwise, this is a [parse error](#1322-parse-errors).

Pop elements from the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) until a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element has been popped from the stack.

[Clear the list of active formatting elements up to the last marker](#13243-the-list-of-active-formatting-elements).

Pop the [current template insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) off the [stack of template insertion modes](#13241-the-insertion-mode).

[Reset the insertion mode appropriately](#13241-the-insertion-mode).

Reprocess the token.

###### 13.2.6.4.17 The "after body" insertion mode

When the user agent is to apply the rules for the "[after body](#1326417-the-after-body-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode), the user agent must handle the token as follows:

A character token that is one of U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION, U+000A LINE FEED (LF), U+000C FORM FEED (FF), U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR), or U+0020 SPACE

Process the token [using the rules for](#13241-the-insertion-mode) the "[in body](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode).

A comment token

[Insert a comment](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) given (the first element in the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) (the [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element), null).

A processing instruction token

[Insert a processing instruction](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) given (the first element in the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) (the [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element), null).

A DOCTYPE token

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Ignore the token.

A start tag whose tag name is "html"

Process the token [using the rules for](#13241-the-insertion-mode) the "[in body](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode).

An end tag whose tag name is "html"

If the parser's [fragment context element](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) is non-null, this is a [parse error](#1322-parse-errors); ignore the token. ([fragment case](#134-parsing-html-fragments))

Otherwise, switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[after after body](#1326420-the-after-after-body-insertion-mode)".

An end-of-file token

[Stop parsing](#1327-the-end).

Anything else

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[in body](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)" and reprocess the token.

###### 13.2.6.4.18 The "in frameset" insertion mode

When the user agent is to apply the rules for the "[in frameset](#1326418-the-in-frameset-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode), the user agent must handle the token as follows:

A character token that is one of U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION, U+000A LINE FEED (LF), U+000C FORM FEED (FF), U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR), or U+0020 SPACE

[Insert the character](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

A comment token

[Insert a comment](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

A processing instruction token

[Insert a processing instruction](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

A DOCTYPE token

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Ignore the token.

A start tag whose tag name is "html"

Process the token [using the rules for](#13241-the-insertion-mode) the "[in body](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode).

A start tag whose tag name is "frameset"

[Insert an HTML element](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) for the token.

An end tag whose tag name is "frameset"

If the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) is the root [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element, then this is a [parse error](#1322-parse-errors); ignore the token. ([fragment case](#134-parsing-html-fragments))

Otherwise, pop the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) from the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).

If the parser's [fragment context element](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) is null and the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) is no longer a [`frameset`](#1632-frames) element, then switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[after frameset](#1326419-the-after-frameset-insertion-mode)".

A start tag whose tag name is "frame"

[Insert an HTML element](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) for the token. Immediately pop the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) off the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).

[Acknowledge the token's *self-closing flag*](#1325-tokenization), if it is set.

A start tag whose tag name is "noframes"

Process the token [using the rules for](#13241-the-insertion-mode) the "[in head](#132644-the-in-head-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode).

An end-of-file token

If the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) is not the root [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element, then this is a [parse error](#1322-parse-errors).

> [!note]
> The [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) can only be the root [`html`](#411-the-html-element) element in the [fragment case](#134-parsing-html-fragments).

[Stop parsing](#1327-the-end).

Anything else

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Ignore the token.

###### 13.2.6.4.19 The "after frameset" insertion mode

When the user agent is to apply the rules for the "[after frameset](#1326419-the-after-frameset-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode), the user agent must handle the token as follows:

A character token that is one of U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION, U+000A LINE FEED (LF), U+000C FORM FEED (FF), U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR), or U+0020 SPACE

[Insert the character](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

A comment token

[Insert a comment](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

A processing instruction token

[Insert a processing instruction](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

A DOCTYPE token

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Ignore the token.

A start tag whose tag name is "html"

Process the token [using the rules for](#13241-the-insertion-mode) the "[in body](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode).

An end tag whose tag name is "html"

Switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[after after frameset](#1326421-the-after-after-frameset-insertion-mode)".

A start tag whose tag name is "noframes"

Process the token [using the rules for](#13241-the-insertion-mode) the "[in head](#132644-the-in-head-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode).

An end-of-file token

[Stop parsing](#1327-the-end).

Anything else

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Ignore the token.

###### 13.2.6.4.20 The "after after body" insertion mode

When the user agent is to apply the rules for the "[after after body](#1326420-the-after-after-body-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode), the user agent must handle the token as follows:

A comment token

[Insert a comment](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) given (the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object, null).

A processing instruction token

[Insert a processing instruction](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) given (the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object, null).

A DOCTYPE token

A character token that is one of U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION, U+000A LINE FEED (LF), U+000C FORM FEED (FF), U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR), or U+0020 SPACE

A start tag whose tag name is "html"

Process the token [using the rules for](#13241-the-insertion-mode) the "[in body](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode).

An end-of-file token

[Stop parsing](#1327-the-end).

Anything else

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Switch the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) to "[in body](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)" and reprocess the token.

###### 13.2.6.4.21 The "after after frameset" insertion mode

When the user agent is to apply the rules for the "[after after frameset](#1326421-the-after-after-frameset-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode), the user agent must handle the token as follows:

A comment token

[Insert a comment](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) given (the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object, null).

A processing instruction token

[Insert a processing instruction](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) given (the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object, null).

A DOCTYPE token

A character token that is one of U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION, U+000A LINE FEED (LF), U+000C FORM FEED (FF), U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR), or U+0020 SPACE

A start tag whose tag name is "html"

Process the token [using the rules for](#13241-the-insertion-mode) the "[in body](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode).

An end-of-file token

[Stop parsing](#1327-the-end).

A start tag whose tag name is "noframes"

Process the token [using the rules for](#13241-the-insertion-mode) the "[in head](#132644-the-in-head-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode).

Anything else

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Ignore the token.

##### 13.2.6.5 The rules for parsing tokens in foreign content

When the user agent is to apply the rules for parsing tokens in foreign content, the user agent must handle the token as follows:

A character token that is U+0000 NULL

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors). [Insert a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER character](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

A character token that is one of U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION, U+000A LINE FEED (LF), U+000C FORM FEED (FF), U+000D CARRIAGE RETURN (CR), or U+0020 SPACE

[Insert the token's character](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

Any other character token

[Insert the token's character](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

Set the [frameset-ok flag](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) to "not ok".

A comment token

[Insert a comment](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

A processing instruction token

[Insert a processing instruction](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

A DOCTYPE token

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors). Ignore the token.

A start tag whose tag name is one of: "b", "big", "blockquote", "body", "br", "center", "code", "dd", "div", "dl", "dt", "em", "embed", "h1", "h2", "h3", "h4", "h5", "h6", "head", "hr", "i", "img", "li", "listing", "menu", "meta", "nobr", "ol", "p", "pre", "ruby", "s", "small", "span", "strong", "strike", "sub", "sup", "table", "tt", "u", "ul", "var"

A start tag whose tag name is "font", if the token has any attributes named "color", "face", or "size"

An end tag whose tag name is "br", "p"

[Parse error](#1322-parse-errors).

While the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) is not a [MathML text integration point](#1326-tree-construction), an [HTML integration point](#1326-tree-construction), or an element in the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces), pop elements from the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).

Reprocess the token according to the rules given in the section corresponding to the current [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) in HTML content.

Any other start tag

If the [adjusted current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) is an element in the [MathML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces), [adjust MathML attributes](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) for the token. (This fixes the case of MathML attributes that are not all lowercase.)

If the [adjusted current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) is an element in the [SVG namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces), and the token's tag name is one of the ones in the first column of the following table, change the tag name to the name given in the corresponding cell in the second column. (This fixes the case of SVG elements that are not all lowercase.)

| Tag name | Element name |
| --- | --- |
| `altglyph` | `altGlyph` |
| `altglyphdef` | `altGlyphDef` |
| `altglyphitem` | `altGlyphItem` |
| `animatecolor` | `animateColor` |
| `animatemotion` | `animateMotion` |
| `animatetransform` | `animateTransform` |
| `clippath` | `clipPath` |
| `feblend` | `feBlend` |
| `fecolormatrix` | `feColorMatrix` |
| `fecomponenttransfer` | `feComponentTransfer` |
| `fecomposite` | `feComposite` |
| `feconvolvematrix` | `feConvolveMatrix` |
| `fediffuselighting` | `feDiffuseLighting` |
| `fedisplacementmap` | `feDisplacementMap` |
| `fedistantlight` | `feDistantLight` |
| `fedropshadow` | `feDropShadow` |
| `feflood` | `feFlood` |
| `fefunca` | `feFuncA` |
| `fefuncb` | `feFuncB` |
| `fefuncg` | `feFuncG` |
| `fefuncr` | `feFuncR` |
| `fegaussianblur` | `feGaussianBlur` |
| `feimage` | `feImage` |
| `femerge` | `feMerge` |
| `femergenode` | `feMergeNode` |
| `femorphology` | `feMorphology` |
| `feoffset` | `feOffset` |
| `fepointlight` | `fePointLight` |
| `fespecularlighting` | `feSpecularLighting` |
| `fespotlight` | `feSpotLight` |
| `fetile` | `feTile` |
| `feturbulence` | `feTurbulence` |
| `foreignobject` | `foreignObject` |
| `glyphref` | `glyphRef` |
| `lineargradient` | `linearGradient` |
| `radialgradient` | `radialGradient` |
| `textpath` | `textPath` |

If the [adjusted current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) is an element in the [SVG namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces), [adjust SVG attributes](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) for the token. (This fixes the case of SVG attributes that are not all lowercase.)

[Adjust foreign attributes](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) for the token. (This fixes the use of namespaced attributes, in particular XLink in SVG.)

[Insert a foreign element](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) for the token, with the [adjusted current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements)'s namespace and false.

If the token has its *[self-closing flag](#1325-tokenization)* set, then run the appropriate steps from the following list:

If the token's tag name is "script", and the new [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) is in the [SVG namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces)

[Acknowledge the token's *self-closing flag*](#1325-tokenization), and then act as described in the steps for a "script" end tag below.

Otherwise

Pop the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) off the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) and [acknowledge the token's *self-closing flag*](#1325-tokenization).

An end tag whose tag name is "script", if the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) is an [SVG `script`](https://w3c.github.io/svgwg/svg2-draft/interact.html#elementdef-script) element

Pop the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) off the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).

Let the old insertion point have the same value as the current [insertion point](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream). Let the [insertion point](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) be just before the [next input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream).

Increment the parser's [script nesting level](#1321-overview-of-the-parsing-model) by one. Set the [parser pause flag](#1321-overview-of-the-parsing-model) to true.

If the [active speculative HTML parser](#1328-speculative-html-parsing) is null and the user agent supports SVG, then [Process the SVG `script` element](https://www.w3.org/TR/SVGMobile12/script.html#ScriptContentProcessing) according to the SVG rules. [\[SVG\]](#references)

> [!note]
> Even if this causes [new characters to be inserted into the tokenizer](#843-documentwrite), the parser will not be executed reentrantly, since the [parser pause flag](#1321-overview-of-the-parsing-model) is true.

Decrement the parser's [script nesting level](#1321-overview-of-the-parsing-model) by one. If the parser's [script nesting level](#1321-overview-of-the-parsing-model) is zero, then set the [parser pause flag](#1321-overview-of-the-parsing-model) to false.

Let the [insertion point](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) have the value of the old insertion point. (In other words, restore the [insertion point](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) to its previous value. This value might be the "undefined" value.)

Any other end tag

Run these steps:
1. Initialize node to be the [current node](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) (the bottommost node of the stack).
2. If node's tag name, [converted to ASCII lowercase](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings), is not the same as the tag name of the token, then this is a [parse error](#1322-parse-errors).
3. *Loop*: If node is the topmost element in the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements), then return. ([fragment case](#134-parsing-html-fragments))
4. If node's tag name, [converted to ASCII lowercase](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings), is the same as the tag name of the token, pop elements from the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) until node has been popped from the stack, and then return.
5. Set node to the previous entry in the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).
6. If node is not an element in the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces), return to the step labeled *loop*.
7. Otherwise, process the token according to the rules given in the section corresponding to the current [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) in HTML content.

#### 13.2.7 The end

Once the user agent stops parsing the document, the user agent must run the following steps:
1. If the [active speculative HTML parser](#1328-speculative-html-parsing) is not null, then [stop the speculative HTML parser](#1328-speculative-html-parsing) and return.
2. Set the [insertion point](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) to undefined.
3. [Update the current document readiness](#315-reporting-document-loading-status) to "`interactive`".
4. Pop *all* the nodes off the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).
5. While the [list of scripts that will execute when the document has finished parsing](#41211-processing-model) is not empty:
   1. [Spin the event loop](#8173-processing-model) until the first [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) in the [list of scripts that will execute when the document has finished parsing](#41211-processing-model) has its [ready to be parser-executed](#41211-processing-model) set to true *and* the parser's [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) [has no style sheet that is blocking scripts](#427-interactions-of-styling-and-scripting).
   2. [Execute the script element](#41211-processing-model) given by the first [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) in the [list of scripts that will execute when the document has finished parsing](#41211-processing-model).
   3. Remove the first [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element from the [list of scripts that will execute when the document has finished parsing](#41211-processing-model) (i.e. shift out the first entry in the list).
6. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) to run the following substeps:
   1. Set the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [load timing info](#315-reporting-document-loading-status)'s [DOM content loaded event start time](#315-reporting-document-loading-status) to the [current high resolution time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time) given the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant).
   2. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`DOMContentLoaded`](#events) at the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object, with its [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true.
   3. Set the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [load timing info](#315-reporting-document-loading-status)'s [DOM content loaded event end time](#315-reporting-document-loading-status) to the [current high resolution time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time) given the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant).
   4. Enable the [client message queue](https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#dfn-client-message-queue) of the [`ServiceWorkerContainer`](https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#serviceworkercontainer) object whose associated [service worker client](https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#serviceworkercontainer-service-worker-client) is the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object's [relevant settings object](#81334-relevant).
   5. Invoke [WebDriver BiDi DOM content loaded](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-dom-content-loaded) with the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts), and a new [WebDriver BiDi navigation status](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-navigation-status) whose [id](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-id) is the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object's [during-loading navigation ID for WebDriver BiDi](#311-the-document-object), [status](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-status) is "[`pending`](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-pending)", and [url](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-url) is the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object's [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).
7. [Spin the event loop](#8173-processing-model) until the [set of scripts that will execute as soon as possible](#41211-processing-model) and the [list of scripts that will execute in order as soon as possible](#41211-processing-model) are empty.
8. [Spin the event loop](#8173-processing-model) until there is nothing that delays the load event in the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object).
9. [Queue a global task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [DOM manipulation task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant) to run the following steps:
   1. [Update the current document readiness](#315-reporting-document-loading-status) to "`complete`".
   2. If the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object's [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) is null, then abort these steps.
   3. Let window be the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [relevant global object](#81334-relevant).
   4. Set the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [load timing info](#315-reporting-document-loading-status)'s [load event start time](#315-reporting-document-loading-status) to the [current high resolution time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time) given window.
   5. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`load`](#events) at window, with *legacy target override flag* set.
   6. Invoke [WebDriver BiDi load complete](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-load-complete) with the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts), and a new [WebDriver BiDi navigation status](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#webdriver-bidi-navigation-status) whose [id](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-id) is the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object's [during-loading navigation ID for WebDriver BiDi](#311-the-document-object), [status](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-status) is "[`complete`](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-complete)", and [url](https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#navigation-status-url) is the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object's [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).
   7. Set the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object's [during-loading navigation ID for WebDriver BiDi](#311-the-document-object) to null.
   8. Set the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [load timing info](#315-reporting-document-loading-status)'s [load event end time](#315-reporting-document-loading-status) to the [current high resolution time](https://w3c.github.io/hr-time/#dfn-current-high-resolution-time) given window.
   9. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [page showing](#759-unloading-documents) is false.
   10. Set the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [page showing](#759-unloading-documents) to true.
   11. [Fire a page transition event](#7276-the-pagetransitionevent-interface) named [`pageshow`](#events) at window with false.
   12. [Completely finish loading](#758-finishing-the-loading-process) the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object).
   13. [Queue the navigation timing entry](https://w3c.github.io/navigation-timing/#dfn-queue-the-navigation-timing-entry) for the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object).
10. If the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [print when loaded](#892-printing) flag is set, then run the [printing steps](#892-printing).
11. The [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is now ready for post-load tasks.

When the user agent is to abort a parser, it must run the following steps:
1. Throw away any pending content in the [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream), and discard any future content that would have been added to it.
2. [Stop the speculative HTML parser](#1328-speculative-html-parsing) for this HTML parser.
3. [Update the current document readiness](#315-reporting-document-loading-status) to "`interactive`".
4. Pop *all* the nodes off the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).
5. [Update the current document readiness](#315-reporting-document-loading-status) to "`complete`".

#### 13.2.8 Speculative HTML parsing

User agents may implement an optimization, as described in this section, to speculatively fetch resources that are declared in the HTML markup while the HTML parser is waiting for a [pending parsing-blocking script](#41211-processing-model) to be fetched and executed, or during normal parsing, at the time [an element is created for a token](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes). While this optimization is not defined in precise detail, there are some rules to consider for interoperability.

Each [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) can have an active speculative HTML parser. It is initially null.

The speculative HTML parser must act like the normal HTML parser (e.g., the tree builder rules apply), with some exceptions:
- The state of the normal HTML parser and the document itself must not be affected.

  > [!example]
  > For example, the [next input character](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) or the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) for the normal HTML parser is not affected by the [speculative HTML parser](#1328-speculative-html-parsing).

- Bytes pushed into the HTML parser's [input byte stream](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) must also be pushed into the speculative HTML parser's [input byte stream](#1323-the-input-byte-stream). Bytes read from the streams must be independent.
- The result of the speculative parsing is primarily a series of [speculative fetches](#1328-speculative-html-parsing). Which kinds of resources to speculatively fetch is [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology), but user agents must not speculatively fetch resources that would not be fetched with the normal HTML parser, under the assumption that the script that is blocking the HTML parser does nothing.

  > [!note]
  > It is possible that the same markup is seen multiple times from the [speculative HTML parser](#1328-speculative-html-parsing) and then the normal HTML parser. It is expected that duplicated fetches will be prevented by caching rules, which are not yet fully specified.

A speculative fetch for a [speculative mock element](#1328-speculative-html-parsing) element must follow these rules:

> [!warning]
> Should some of these things be applied to the document "for real", even though they are found speculatively?
- If the [speculative HTML parser](#1328-speculative-html-parsing) encounters one of the following elements, then act as if that element is processed for the purpose of its effect of subsequent speculative fetches.
  - A [`base`](#423-the-base-element) element.
  - A [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element whose [`http-equiv`](#4253-pragma-directives) attribute is in the [Content security policy](#4253-pragma-directives) state.
  - A [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element whose [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for "[`referrer`](#4251-standard-metadata-names)".
  - A [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element whose [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for "`viewport`". (This can affect whether a media query list [matches the environment](#2310-media-queries).) [\[CSSDEVICEADAPT\]](#references)
- Let url be the [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) that element would fetch if it was processed normally. If there is no such [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) or if it is the empty string, then do nothing. Otherwise, if url is already in the [list of speculative fetch URLs](#1328-speculative-html-parsing), then do nothing. Otherwise, fetch url as if the element was processed normally, and add url to the [list of speculative fetch URLs](#1328-speculative-html-parsing).

Each [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has a list of speculative fetch URLs, which is a [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) of [URLs](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url), initially empty.

To start the speculative HTML parser for an instance of an HTML parser parser:
1. Optionally, return.

   > [!note]
   > This step allows user agents to opt out of speculative HTML parsing.

2. If parser's [active speculative HTML parser](#1328-speculative-html-parsing) is not null, then [stop the speculative HTML parser](#1328-speculative-html-parsing) for parser.

   > [!note]
   > This can happen when [`document.write()`](#843-documentwrite) writes another parser-blocking script. For simplicity, this specification always restarts speculative parsing, but user agents can implement a more efficient strategy, so long as the end result is equivalent.

3. Let speculativeParser be a new [speculative HTML parser](#1328-speculative-html-parsing), with the same state as parser.
4. Let speculativeDoc be a new isomorphic representation of parser's [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), where all elements are instead [speculative mock elements](#1328-speculative-html-parsing). Let speculativeParser parse into speculativeDoc.
5. Set parser's [active speculative HTML parser](#1328-speculative-html-parsing) to speculativeParser.
6. [In parallel](#211-parallelism), run speculativeParser until it is stopped or until it reaches the end of its [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream).

To stop the speculative HTML parser for an instance of an HTML parser parser:
1. Let speculativeParser be parser's [active speculative HTML parser](#1328-speculative-html-parsing).
2. If speculativeParser is null, then return.
3. Throw away any pending content in speculativeParser's [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream), and discard any future content that would have been added to it.
4. Set parser's [active speculative HTML parser](#1328-speculative-html-parsing) to null.

The [speculative HTML parser](#1328-speculative-html-parsing) will create [speculative mock elements](#1328-speculative-html-parsing) instead of normal elements. DOM operations that the tree builder normally does on elements are expected to work appropriately on speculative mock elements.

A speculative mock element is a [struct](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs) with the following [items](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#53-structs):
- A [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) namespace, corresponding to an element's [namespace](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element).
- A [string](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) local name, corresponding to an element's [local name](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element).
- A [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) attribute list, corresponding to an element's [attribute list](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element).
- A [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists) children, corresponding to an element's [children](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).

To create a speculative mock element given a namespace, tagName, and attributes:
1. Let element be a new [speculative mock element](#1328-speculative-html-parsing).
2. Set element's [namespace](#1328-speculative-html-parsing) to namespace.
3. Set element's [local name](#1328-speculative-html-parsing) to tagName.
4. Set element's [attribute list](#1328-speculative-html-parsing) to attributes.
5. Set element's [children](#1328-speculative-html-parsing) to a new empty [list](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#51-lists).
6. Optionally, perform a [speculative fetch](#1328-speculative-html-parsing) for element.
7. Return element.

When the tree builder says to insert an element into a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element's [template contents](#4123-the-template-element), if that is a [speculative mock element](#1328-speculative-html-parsing), and the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element's [template contents](#4123-the-template-element) is not a [`ShadowRoot`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) node, instead do nothing. URLs found speculatively inside non-declarative-shadow-root [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) elements might themselves be templates, and must not be speculatively fetched.

#### 13.2.9 Coercing an HTML DOM into an infoset

When an application uses an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) in conjunction with an XML pipeline, it is possible that the constructed DOM is not compatible with the XML tool chain in certain subtle ways. For example, an XML toolchain might not be able to represent attributes with the name `xmlns`, since they conflict with the Namespaces in XML syntax. There is also some data that the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) generates that isn't included in the DOM itself. This section specifies some rules for handling these issues.

If the XML API being used doesn't support DOCTYPEs, the tool may drop DOCTYPEs altogether.

If the XML API doesn't support attributes in no namespace that are named "`xmlns`", attributes whose names start with "`xmlns:`", or attributes in the [XMLNS namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces), then the tool may drop such attributes.

The tool may annotate the output with any namespace declarations required for proper operation.

If the XML API being used restricts the allowable characters in the local names of elements and attributes, then the tool may map all element and attribute local names that the API wouldn't support to a set of names that *are* allowed, by replacing any character that isn't supported with the uppercase letter U and the six digits of the character's code point when expressed in hexadecimal, using digits 0-9 and capital letters A-F as the symbols, in increasing numeric order.

> [!example]
> For example, the element name `foo<bar`, which can be output by the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents), though it is neither a legal HTML element name nor a well-formed XML element name, would be converted into `fooU00003Cbar`, which *is* a well-formed XML element name (though it's still not legal in HTML by any means).

> [!example]
> As another example, consider the attribute `xlink:href`. Used on a MathML element, it becomes, after being [adjusted](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes), an attribute with a prefix "`xlink`" and a local name "`href`". However, used on an HTML element, it becomes an attribute with no prefix and the local name "`xlink:href`", which is not a valid NCName, and thus might not be accepted by an XML API. It could thus get converted, becoming "`xlinkU00003Ahref`".

> [!note]
> The resulting names from this conversion conveniently can't clash with any attribute generated by the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents), since those are all either lowercase or those listed in the [adjust foreign attributes](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes) algorithm's table.

If the XML API restricts comments from having two consecutive U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS characters (--), the tool may insert a single U+0020 SPACE character between any such offending characters.

If the XML API restricts comments from ending in a U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS character (-), the tool may insert a single U+0020 SPACE character at the end of such comments.

If the XML API restricts allowed characters in character data, attribute values, or comments, the tool may replace any U+000C FORM FEED (FF) character with a U+0020 SPACE character, and any other literal non-XML character with a U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER.

If the tool has no way to convey out-of-band information, then the tool may drop the following information:
- Whether the document is set to *[no-quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document)*, *[limited-quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document)*, or *[quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document)*
- The association between form controls and forms that aren't their nearest [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element ancestor (use of the [`form` element pointer](#13244-the-element-pointers) in the parser)
- The [template contents](#4123-the-template-element) of any [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) elements.

> [!note]
> The mutations allowed by this section apply *after* the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents)'s rules have been applied. For example, a `<a::>` start tag will be closed by a `</a::>` end tag, and never by a `</aU00003AU00003A>` end tag, even if the user agent is using the rules above to then generate an actual element in the DOM with the name `aU00003AU00003A` for that start tag.

#### 13.2.10 An introduction to error handling and strange cases in the parser

*This section is non-normative.*

This section examines some erroneous markup and discusses how the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) handles these cases.

##### 13.2.10.1 Misnested tags: <b><i></b></i>

*This section is non-normative.*

The most-often discussed example of erroneous markup is as follows:

```html
<p>1<b>2<i>3</b>4</i>5</p>
```

The parsing of this markup is straightforward up to the "3". At this point, the DOM looks like this:
- [`html`](#411-the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#421-the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#431-the-body-element)
    - [`p`](#441-the-p-element)
      - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): 1
      - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
        - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): 2
        - [`i`](#4520-the-i-element)
          - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): 3

Here, the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) has five elements on it: [`html`](#411-the-html-element), [`body`](#431-the-body-element), [`p`](#441-the-p-element), [`b`](#4521-the-b-element), and [`i`](#4520-the-i-element). The [list of active formatting elements](#13243-the-list-of-active-formatting-elements) just has two: [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) and [`i`](#4520-the-i-element). The [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) is "[in body](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)".

Upon receiving the end tag token with the tag name "b", the "[adoption agency algorithm](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)" is invoked. This is a simple case, in that the formattingElement is the [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) element, and there is no furthest block. Thus, the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) ends up with just three elements: [`html`](#411-the-html-element), [`body`](#431-the-body-element), and [`p`](#441-the-p-element), while the [list of active formatting elements](#13243-the-list-of-active-formatting-elements) has just one: [`i`](#4520-the-i-element). The DOM tree is unmodified at this point.

The next token is a character ("4"), triggers the [reconstruction of the active formatting elements](#13243-the-list-of-active-formatting-elements), in this case just the [`i`](#4520-the-i-element) element. A new [`i`](#4520-the-i-element) element is thus created for the "4" [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node. After the end tag token for the "i" is also received, and the "5" [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node is inserted, the DOM looks as follows:
- [`html`](#411-the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#421-the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#431-the-body-element)
    - [`p`](#441-the-p-element)
      - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): 1
      - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
        - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): 2
        - [`i`](#4520-the-i-element)
          - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): 3
      - [`i`](#4520-the-i-element)
        - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): 4
      - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): 5

##### 13.2.10.2 Misnested tags: <b><p></b></p>

*This section is non-normative.*

A case similar to the previous one is the following:

```html
<b>1<p>2</b>3</p>
```

Up to the "2" the parsing here is straightforward:
- [`html`](#411-the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#421-the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#431-the-body-element)
    - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
      - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): 1
      - [`p`](#441-the-p-element)
        - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): 2

The interesting part is when the end tag token with the tag name "b" is parsed.

Before that token is seen, the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) has four elements on it: [`html`](#411-the-html-element), [`body`](#431-the-body-element), [`b`](#4521-the-b-element), and [`p`](#441-the-p-element). The [list of active formatting elements](#13243-the-list-of-active-formatting-elements) just has the one: [`b`](#4521-the-b-element). The [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) is "[in body](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)".

Upon receiving the end tag token with the tag name "b", the "[adoption agency algorithm](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)" is invoked, as in the previous example. However, in this case, there *is* a furthest block, namely the [`p`](#441-the-p-element) element. Thus, this time the adoption agency algorithm isn't skipped over.

The common ancestor is the [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element. A conceptual "bookmark" marks the position of the [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) in the [list of active formatting elements](#13243-the-list-of-active-formatting-elements), but since that list has only one element in it, the bookmark won't have much effect.

As the algorithm progresses, node ends up set to the formatting element ([`b`](#4521-the-b-element)), and last node ends up set to the furthest block ([`p`](#441-the-p-element)).

The last node gets appended (moved) to the common ancestor, so that the DOM looks like:
- [`html`](#411-the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#421-the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#431-the-body-element)
    - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
      - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): 1
    - [`p`](#441-the-p-element)
      - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): 2

A new [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) element is created, and the children of the [`p`](#441-the-p-element) element are moved to it:
- [`html`](#411-the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#421-the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#431-the-body-element)
    - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
      - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): 1
    - [`p`](#441-the-p-element)
- [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
  - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): 2

Finally, the new [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) element is appended to the [`p`](#441-the-p-element) element, so that the DOM looks like:
- [`html`](#411-the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#421-the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#431-the-body-element)
    - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
      - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): 1
    - [`p`](#441-the-p-element)
      - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
        - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): 2

The [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) element is removed from the [list of active formatting elements](#13243-the-list-of-active-formatting-elements) and the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements), so that when the "3" is parsed, it is appended to the [`p`](#441-the-p-element) element:
- [`html`](#411-the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#421-the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#431-the-body-element)
    - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
      - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): 1
    - [`p`](#441-the-p-element)
      - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
        - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): 2
      - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): 3

##### 13.2.10.3 Unexpected markup in tables

*This section is non-normative.*

Error handling in tables is, for historical reasons, especially strange. For example, consider the following markup:

```html
<table><b><tr><td>aaa</td></tr>bbb</table>ccc
```

The highlighted [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) element start tag is not allowed directly inside a table like that, and the parser handles this case by placing the element *before* the table. (This is called *[foster parenting](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes)*.) This can be seen by examining the DOM tree as it stands just after the [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element's start tag has been seen:
- [`html`](#411-the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#421-the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#431-the-body-element)
    - [`table`](#491-the-table-element)

...and then immediately after the [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) element start tag has been seen:
- [`html`](#411-the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#421-the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#431-the-body-element)
    - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
    - [`table`](#491-the-table-element)

At this point, the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) has on it the elements [`html`](#411-the-html-element), [`body`](#431-the-body-element), [`table`](#491-the-table-element), and [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) (in that order, despite the resulting DOM tree); the [list of active formatting elements](#13243-the-list-of-active-formatting-elements) just has the [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) element in it; and the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) is "[in table](#132649-the-in-table-insertion-mode)".

The [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) start tag causes the [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) element to be popped off the stack and a [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) start tag to be implied; the [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) and [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) elements are then handled in a rather straight-forward manner, taking the parser through the "[in table body](#1326413-the-in-table-body-insertion-mode)" and "[in row](#1326414-the-in-row-insertion-mode)" insertion modes, after which the DOM looks as follows:
- [`html`](#411-the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#421-the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#431-the-body-element)
    - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
    - [`table`](#491-the-table-element)
      - [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element)
        - [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element)

Here, the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) has on it the elements [`html`](#411-the-html-element), [`body`](#431-the-body-element), [`table`](#491-the-table-element), [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element), and [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element); the [list of active formatting elements](#13243-the-list-of-active-formatting-elements) still has the [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) element in it; and the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) is "[in row](#1326414-the-in-row-insertion-mode)".

The [`td`](#499-the-td-element) element start tag token, after putting a [`td`](#499-the-td-element) element on the tree, puts a [marker](#13243-the-list-of-active-formatting-elements) on the [list of active formatting elements](#13243-the-list-of-active-formatting-elements) (it also switches to the "[in cell](#1326415-the-in-cell-insertion-mode)" [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode)).
- [`html`](#411-the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#421-the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#431-the-body-element)
    - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
    - [`table`](#491-the-table-element)
      - [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element)
        - [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element)
          - [`td`](#499-the-td-element)

The [marker](#13243-the-list-of-active-formatting-elements) means that when the "aaa" character tokens are seen, no [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) element is created to hold the resulting [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node:
- [`html`](#411-the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#421-the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#431-the-body-element)
    - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
    - [`table`](#491-the-table-element)
      - [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element)
        - [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element)
          - [`td`](#499-the-td-element)
            - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): aaa

The end tags are handled in a straight-forward manner; after handling them, the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) has on it the elements [`html`](#411-the-html-element), [`body`](#431-the-body-element), [`table`](#491-the-table-element), and [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element); the [list of active formatting elements](#13243-the-list-of-active-formatting-elements) still has the [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) element in it (the [marker](#13243-the-list-of-active-formatting-elements) having been removed by the "td" end tag token); and the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) is "[in table body](#1326413-the-in-table-body-insertion-mode)".

Thus it is that the "bbb" character tokens are found. These trigger the "[in table text](#1326410-the-in-table-text-insertion-mode)" insertion mode to be used (with the [original insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) set to "[in table body](#1326413-the-in-table-body-insertion-mode)"). The character tokens are collected, and when the next token (the [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element end tag) is seen, they are processed as a group. Since they are not all spaces, they are handled as per the "anything else" rules in the "[in table](#132649-the-in-table-insertion-mode)" insertion mode, which defer to the "[in body](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode)" insertion mode but with [foster parenting](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes).

When [the active formatting elements are reconstructed](#13243-the-list-of-active-formatting-elements), a [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) element is created and [foster parented](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes), and then the "bbb" [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node is appended to it:
- [`html`](#411-the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#421-the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#431-the-body-element)
    - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
    - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
      - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): bbb
    - [`table`](#491-the-table-element)
      - [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element)
        - [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element)
          - [`td`](#499-the-td-element)
            - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): aaa

The [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) has on it the elements [`html`](#411-the-html-element), [`body`](#431-the-body-element), [`table`](#491-the-table-element), [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element), and the new [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) (again, note that this doesn't match the resulting tree!); the [list of active formatting elements](#13243-the-list-of-active-formatting-elements) has the new [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) element in it; and the [insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode) is still "[in table body](#1326413-the-in-table-body-insertion-mode)".

Had the character tokens been only [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) instead of "bbb", then that [ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) would just be appended to the [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element) element.

Finally, the [`table`](#491-the-table-element) is closed by a "table" end tag. This pops all the nodes from the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) up to and including the [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element, but it doesn't affect the [list of active formatting elements](#13243-the-list-of-active-formatting-elements), so the "ccc" character tokens after the table result in yet another [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) element being created, this time after the table:
- [`html`](#411-the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#421-the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#431-the-body-element)
    - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
    - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
      - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): bbb
    - [`table`](#491-the-table-element)
      - [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element)
        - [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element)
          - [`td`](#499-the-td-element)
            - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): aaa
    - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
      - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): ccc

##### 13.2.10.4 Scripts that modify the page as it is being parsed

*This section is non-normative.*

Consider the following markup, which for this example we will assume is the document with [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) `https://example.com/inner`, being rendered as the content of an [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) in another document with the [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) `https://example.com/outer`:

```html
<div id=a>
 <script>
  var div = document.getElementById('a');
  parent.document.body.appendChild(div);
 </script>
 <script>
  alert(document.URL);
 </script>
</div>
<script>
 alert(document.URL);
</script>
```

Up to the first "script" end tag, before the script is parsed, the result is relatively straightforward:
- [`html`](#411-the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#421-the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#431-the-body-element)
    - [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) [`id`](#326-global-attributes)="`a`"
      - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text):
      - [`script`](#4121-the-script-element)
        - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): var div = document.getElementById('a'); ⏎ parent.document.body.appendChild(div);

After the script is parsed, though, the [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element and its child [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element are gone:
- [`html`](#411-the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#421-the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#431-the-body-element)

They are, at this point, in the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) of the aforementioned outer [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts). However, the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) *still contains the [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element*.

Thus, when the second [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element is parsed, it is inserted *into the outer [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object*.

Those parsed into different [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)s than the one the parser was created for do not execute, so the first alert does not show.

Once the [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element's end tag is parsed, the [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element is popped off the stack, and so the next [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element is in the inner [`Document`](#311-the-document-object):
- [`html`](#411-the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#421-the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#431-the-body-element)
    - [`script`](#4121-the-script-element)
      - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): alert(document.URL);

This script does execute, resulting in an alert that says "https://example.com/inner".

##### 13.2.10.5 The execution of scripts that are moving across multiple documents

*This section is non-normative.*

Elaborating on the example in the previous section, consider the case where the second [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element is an external script (i.e. one with a [`src`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute). Since the element was not in the parser's [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) when it was created, that external script is not even downloaded.

In a case where a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element with a [`src`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute is parsed normally into its parser's [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), but while the external script is being downloaded, the element is moved to another document, the script continues to download, but does not execute.

> [!note]
> In general, moving [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements between [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)s is considered a bad practice.

##### 13.2.10.6 Unclosed formatting elements

*This section is non-normative.*

The following markup shows how nested formatting elements (such as [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)) get collected and continue to be applied even as the elements they are contained in are closed, but that excessive duplicates are thrown away.

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<p><b class=x><b class=x><b><b class=x><b class=x><b>X
<p>X
<p><b><b class=x><b>X
<p></b></b></b></b></b></b>X
```

The resulting DOM tree is as follows:
- DOCTYPE: `html`
- [`html`](#411-the-html-element)
  - [`head`](#421-the-head-element)
  - [`body`](#431-the-body-element)
    - [`p`](#441-the-p-element)
      - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) [`class`](#326-global-attributes)="`x`"
        - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) [`class`](#326-global-attributes)="`x`"
          - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
            - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) [`class`](#326-global-attributes)="`x`"
              - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) [`class`](#326-global-attributes)="`x`"
                - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
                  - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): X⏎
    - [`p`](#441-the-p-element)
      - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) [`class`](#326-global-attributes)="`x`"
        - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
          - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) [`class`](#326-global-attributes)="`x`"
            - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) [`class`](#326-global-attributes)="`x`"
              - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
                - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): X⏎
    - [`p`](#441-the-p-element)
      - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) [`class`](#326-global-attributes)="`x`"
        - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
          - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) [`class`](#326-global-attributes)="`x`"
            - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) [`class`](#326-global-attributes)="`x`"
              - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
                - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
                  - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) [`class`](#326-global-attributes)="`x`"
                    - [`b`](#4521-the-b-element)
                      - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): X⏎
    - [`p`](#441-the-p-element)
      - [`#text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text): X⏎

Note how the second [`p`](#441-the-p-element) element in the markup has no explicit [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) elements, but in the resulting DOM, up to three of each kind of formatting element (in this case three [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) elements with the class attribute, and two unadorned [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) elements) get reconstructed before the element's "X".

Also note how this means that in the final paragraph only six [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) end tags are needed to completely clear the [list of active formatting elements](#13243-the-list-of-active-formatting-elements), even though nine [`b`](#4521-the-b-element) start tags have been seen up to this point.

### 13.3 Serializing HTML fragments

For the purposes of the following algorithm, an element serializes as void if its element type is one of the [void elements](#1312-elements), or is [`basefont`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`bgsound`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`frame`](#1632-frames), [`keygen`](#162-non-conforming-features), or [`param`](#162-non-conforming-features).

The following steps form the HTML fragment serialization algorithm. The algorithm takes as input a DOM [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), or [`DocumentFragment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) referred to as the node, a boolean serializableShadowRoots, and a `sequence<ShadowRoot>` shadowRoots, and returns a string.

> [!note]
> This algorithm serializes the *children* of the node being serialized, not the node itself.
1. If the node [serializes as void](#133-serializing-html-fragments), then return the empty string.
2. Let s be a string, and initialize it to the empty string.
3. If the node is a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element, then let the node instead be the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element's [template contents](#4123-the-template-element) (a [`DocumentFragment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) node).
4. If current node is a [shadow host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element):
   1. Let shadow be current node's [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element).
   2. If one of the following is true:
      - serializableShadowRoots is true and shadow's [serializable](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) is true; or
      - shadowRoots contains shadow,

      then:
      1. Append "`<template shadowrootmode="`".
      2. If shadow's [mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) is "`open`", then append "`open`". Otherwise, append "`closed`".
      3. Append U+0022 (").
      4. If shadow's [delegates focus](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) is set, then append "` shadowrootdelegatesfocus=""`".
      5. If shadow's [serializable](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) is set, then append "` shadowrootserializable=""`".
      6. If shadow's [slot assignment](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) is "`manual`", then append "` shadowrootslotassignment="manual"`".
      7. If shadow's [clonable](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) is set, then append "` shadowrootclonable=""`".
      8. Let shouldAppendRegistryAttribute be the result of running these steps:
         1. Let documentRegistry be shadow's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).
         2. Let shadowRegistry be shadow's [custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot).
         3. If documentRegistry is null and shadowRegistry is null, then return false.
         4. If documentRegistry [is a global custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) and shadowRegistry [is a global custom element registry](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), then return false.
         5. Return true.
      9. If shouldAppendRegistryAttribute is true, then append "` shadowrootcustomelementregistry=""`".
      10. Append U+003E (>).
      11. Append the value of running the [HTML fragment serialization algorithm](#133-serializing-html-fragments) with shadow, serializableShadowRoots, and shadowRoots (thus recursing into this algorithm for that element).
      12. Append "`</template>`".

5. For each child node of the node, in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), run the following steps:
   1. Let current node be the child node being processed.
   2. Append the appropriate string from the following list to s:

      If current node is an [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element)

      If current node is an element in the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces), the [MathML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces), or the [SVG namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces), then let tagname be current node's local name. Otherwise, let tagname be current node's qualified name.

      Append U+003C (<), followed by tagname.

      > [!note]
      > For [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) created by the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) or [`createElement()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), tagname will be lowercase.

      If current node's [`is` value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) is not null, and the element does not have an [`is`](#4133-core-concepts) attribute in its attribute list, then append "` is="`", followed by current node's [`is` value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) [escaped as described below](#133-serializing-html-fragments) in *attribute mode*, and U+0022 (").

      For each attribute that the element has, append U+0020 SPACE, the [attribute's serialized name as described below](#133-serializing-html-fragments), "`="`", the attribute's value, [escaped as described below](#133-serializing-html-fragments) in *attribute mode*, and U+0022 (").

      An attribute's serialized name for the purposes of the previous paragraph must be determined as follows:

      If the attribute has no namespace

      The attribute's serialized name is the attribute's local name.

      > [!note]
      > For attributes on [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility) set by the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) or by [`setAttribute()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), the local name will be lowercase.

      If the attribute is in the [XML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces)

      The attribute's serialized name is "`xml:`" followed by the attribute's local name.

      If the attribute is in the [XMLNS namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) and the attribute's local name is `xmlns`

      The attribute's serialized name is "`xmlns`".

      If the attribute is in the [XMLNS namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces) and the attribute's local name is not `xmlns`

      The attribute's serialized name is "`xmlns:`" followed by the attribute's local name.

      If the attribute is in the [XLink namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces)

      The attribute's serialized name is "`xlink:`" followed by the attribute's local name.

      If the attribute is in some other namespace

      The attribute's serialized name is the attribute's qualified name.

      While the exact order of attributes is [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology), and may depend on factors such as the order that the attributes were given in the original markup, the sort order must be stable, such that consecutive invocations of this algorithm serialize an element's attributes in the same order.

      Append U+003E (>).

      If current node [serializes as void](#133-serializing-html-fragments), then [continue](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#39-iteration) on to the next child node at this point.

      Append the value of running the [HTML fragment serialization algorithm](#133-serializing-html-fragments) with current node, serializableShadowRoots, and shadowRoots (thus recursing into this algorithm for that node), followed by "`</`", tagname, and U+003E (>).

      If current node is a [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node

      If the parent of current node is a [`style`](#426-the-style-element), [`script`](#4121-the-script-element), [`xmp`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element), [`noembed`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`noframes`](#162-non-conforming-features), or [`plaintext`](#162-non-conforming-features) element, or if the parent of current node is a [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element) element and [scripting is enabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting) for the node, then append the value of current node's [data](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#410-interface-characterdata) literally.

      Otherwise, append the value of current node's [data](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#410-interface-characterdata), [escaped as described below](#133-serializing-html-fragments).

      If current node is a [`Comment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#414-interface-comment)

      Append "`<!--`", followed by the value of current node's [data](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#410-interface-characterdata), and "`-->`".

      If current node is a [`ProcessingInstruction`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#413-interface-processinginstruction)

      Append "`<?`", followed by the value of current node's [target](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#413-interface-processinginstruction), U+0020 SPACE, the value of current node's [data](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#410-interface-characterdata), and "`?>`".

      If current node is a [`DocumentType`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-interface-documenttype)

      Append "`<!DOCTYPE `", followed by the value of current node's [name](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-interface-documenttype) and U+003E (>).

6. Return s.

> [!warning]
> It is possible that the output of this algorithm, if parsed with an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents), will not return the original tree structure. Tree structures that do not roundtrip a serialize and reparse step can also be produced by the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) itself, although such cases are typically non-conforming.

> [!example]
> For instance, if a [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element to which a `Comment` node has been appended is serialized and the output is then reparsed, the comment will end up being displayed in the text control. Similarly, if, as a result of DOM manipulation, an element contains a comment that contains "`-->`", then when the result of serializing the element is parsed, the comment will be truncated at that point and the rest of the comment will be interpreted as markup. More examples would be making a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element contain a [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node with the text string "`</script>`", or having a [`p`](#441-the-p-element) element that contains a [`ul`](#446-the-ul-element) element (as the [`ul`](#446-the-ul-element) element's [start tag](#13121-start-tags) would imply the end tag for the [`p`](#441-the-p-element)).
> 
> This can enable cross-site scripting attacks. An example of this would be a page that lets the user enter some font family names that are then inserted into a CSS [`style`](#426-the-style-element) block via the DOM and which then uses the [`innerHTML`](#854-the-innerhtml-property) IDL attribute to get the HTML serialization of that [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element: if the user enters "`</style><script>attack</script>`" as a font family name, [`innerHTML`](#854-the-innerhtml-property) will return markup that, if parsed in a different context, would contain a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) node, even though no [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) node existed in the original DOM.

> [!example]
> For example, consider the following markup:
> 
> ```html
> <form id="outer"><div></form><form id="inner"><input>
> ```
> 
> This will be parsed into:
> - [`html`](#411-the-html-element)
>   - [`head`](#421-the-head-element)
>   - [`body`](#431-the-body-element)
>     - [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) [`id`](#326-global-attributes)="`outer`"
>       - [`div`](#4416-the-div-element)
>         - [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) [`id`](#326-global-attributes)="`inner`"
>           - [`input`](#4105-the-input-element)
> 
> The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element will be associated with the inner [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element. Now, if this tree structure is serialized and reparsed, the `<form
>    id="inner">` start tag will be ignored, and so the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element will be associated with the outer [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element instead.
> 
> ```html
> <html><head></head><body><form id="outer"><div><form id="inner"><input></form></div></form></body></html>
> ```
> - [`html`](#411-the-html-element)
>   - [`head`](#421-the-head-element)
>   - [`body`](#431-the-body-element)
>     - [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) [`id`](#326-global-attributes)="`outer`"
>       - [`div`](#4416-the-div-element)
>         - [`input`](#4105-the-input-element)

> [!example]
> As another example, consider the following markup:
> 
> ```html
> <a><table><a>
> ```
> 
> This will be parsed into:
> - [`html`](#411-the-html-element)
>   - [`head`](#421-the-head-element)
>   - [`body`](#431-the-body-element)
>     - [`a`](#451-the-a-element)
>       - [`a`](#451-the-a-element)
>       - [`table`](#491-the-table-element)
> 
> That is, the [`a`](#451-the-a-element) elements are nested, because the second [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element is [foster parented](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes). After a serialize-reparse roundtrip, the [`a`](#451-the-a-element) elements and the [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element would all be siblings, because the second `<a>` start tag implicitly closes the first [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element.
> 
> ```html
> <html><head></head><body><a><a></a><table></table></a></body></html>
> ```
> - [`html`](#411-the-html-element)
>   - [`head`](#421-the-head-element)
>   - [`body`](#431-the-body-element)
>     - [`a`](#451-the-a-element)
>     - [`a`](#451-the-a-element)
>     - [`table`](#491-the-table-element)

For historical reasons, this algorithm does not roundtrip an initial U+000A (LF) character in [`pre`](#443-the-pre-element), [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element), or [`listing`](#162-non-conforming-features) elements, even though (in the first two cases) the markup being roundtripped can be conforming. The [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) will drop such a character during parsing, but this algorithm does *not* serialize an extra U+000A (LF) character.

> [!example]
> For example, consider the following markup:
> 
> ```html
> <pre>
> 
> Hello.</pre>
> ```
> 
> When this document is first parsed, the [`pre`](#443-the-pre-element) element's [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) starts with a single newline character. After a serialize-reparse roundtrip, the [`pre`](#443-the-pre-element) element's [child text content](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) is simply "`Hello.`".

Because of the special role of the [`is`](#4133-core-concepts) attribute in signaling the creation of [customized built-in elements](#4133-core-concepts), in that it provides a mechanism for parsed HTML to set the element's [`is` value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), we special-case its handling during serialization. This ensures that an element's [`is` value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) is preserved through serialize-parse roundtrips.

> [!example]
> When creating a [customized built-in element](#4133-core-concepts) via the parser, a developer uses the [`is`](#4133-core-concepts) attribute directly; in such cases serialize-parse roundtrips work fine.
> 
> ```html
> <script>
> window.SuperP = class extends HTMLParagraphElement {};
> customElements.define("super-p", SuperP, { extends: "p" });
> </script>
> 
> <div id="container"><p is="super-p">Superb!</p></div>
> 
> <script>
> console.log(container.innerHTML); // <p is="super-p">
> container.innerHTML = container.innerHTML;
> console.log(container.innerHTML); // <p is="super-p">
> console.assert(container.firstChild instanceof SuperP);
> </script>
> ```
> 
> But when creating a customized built-in element via its [constructor](#4133-core-concepts) or via [`createElement()`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), the [`is`](#4133-core-concepts) attribute is not added. Instead, the [`is` value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) (which is what the custom elements machinery uses) is set without intermediating through an attribute.
> 
> ```html
> <script>
> container.innerHTML = "";
> const p = document.createElement("p", { is: "super-p" });
> container.appendChild(p);
> 
> // The is attribute is not present in the DOM:
> console.assert(!p.hasAttribute("is"));
> 
> // But the element is still a super-p:
> console.assert(p instanceof SuperP);
> </script>
> ```
> 
> To ensure that serialize-parse roundtrips still work, the serialization process explicitly writes out the element's [`is` value](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) as an [`is`](#4133-core-concepts) attribute:
> 
> ```html
> <script>
> console.log(container.innerHTML); // <p is="super-p">
> container.innerHTML = container.innerHTML;
> console.log(container.innerHTML); // <p is="super-p">
> console.assert(container.firstChild instanceof SuperP);
> </script>
> ```

Escaping a string (for the purposes of the algorithm above) consists of running the following steps:
1. Replace any occurrence of "`&`" character by "`&amp;`".
2. Replace any occurrences of the U+00A0 NO-BREAK SPACE character by "`&nbsp;`".
3. Replace any occurrences of the "`<`" character by "`&lt;`".
4. Replace any occurrences of the "`>`" character by "`&gt;`".
5. If the algorithm was invoked in the *attribute mode*, then replace any occurrences of the "`"`" character by "`&quot;`".

### 13.4 Parsing HTML fragments

The HTML fragment parsing algorithm, given an [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) or [`DocumentFragment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) target, a string input, an optional boolean allowDeclarativeShadowRoots (default false), and an optional [parser scripting mode](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) scriptingMode (default [Inert](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags)), is the following steps. They return a [`DocumentFragment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment).

> [!note]
> Parts marked fragment case in algorithms in the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) section are parts that only occur if the parser's [fragment context element](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) is non-null. The algorithms have been annotated with such markings for informational purposes only; such markings have no normative weight. If it is possible for a condition described as a [fragment case](#134-parsing-html-fragments) to occur even when the parser's [fragment context element](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) is null, then that is an error in the specification.
