1. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): scriptingMode is either [Inert](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) or [Fragment](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags).
2. Let context be target if target is an [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element); otherwise target's [host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment).
3. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): [context](#134-parsing-html-fragments) is non-null.
4. Let document be a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) node whose [type](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) is "`html`".
5. Let contextDocument be [context](#134-parsing-html-fragments)'s [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
6. If contextDocument is in [quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), then set document's [mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) to "`quirks`".
7. Otherwise, if contextDocument is in [limited-quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), then set document's [mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) to "`limited-quirks`".
8. Create a new [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) whose [allow declarative shadow roots](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) is allowDeclarativeShadowRoots, and associate it with document.
9. Set the parser's [fragment context element](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) to [context](#134-parsing-html-fragments).
10. If contextDocument's [scripting is disabled](#8134-enabling-and-disabling-scripting), then set scriptingMode to [Disabled](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags).
11. Set the parser's [scripting mode](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) to scriptingMode.
12. Set the state of the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents)'s [tokenization](#1325-tokenization) stage as follows, switching on [context](#134-parsing-html-fragments):

    [`title`](#422-the-title-element)

    [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element)

    Switch the tokenizer to the [RCDATA state](#13252-rcdata-state).

    [`style`](#426-the-style-element)

    [`xmp`](#162-non-conforming-features)

    [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element)

    [`noembed`](#162-non-conforming-features)

    [`noframes`](#162-non-conforming-features)

    Switch the tokenizer to the [RAWTEXT state](#13253-rawtext-state).

    [`script`](#4121-the-script-element)

    Switch the tokenizer to the [script data state](#13254-script-data-state).

    [`noscript`](#4122-the-noscript-element)

    If [scripting mode](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) is not [Disabled](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags), switch the tokenizer to the [RAWTEXT state](#13253-rawtext-state). Otherwise, leave the tokenizer in the [data state](#13251-data-state).

    [`plaintext`](#162-non-conforming-features)

    Switch the tokenizer to the [PLAINTEXT state](#13255-plaintext-state).

    Any other element

    Leave the tokenizer in the [data state](#13251-data-state).

    > [!note]
    > For performance reasons, an implementation that does not report errors and that uses the actual state machine described in this specification directly could use the PLAINTEXT state instead of the RAWTEXT and script data states where those are mentioned in the list above. Except for rules regarding parse errors, they are equivalent, since there is no [appropriate end tag token](#1325-tokenization) in the fragment case, yet they involve far fewer state transitions.

13. Let root be the result of [creating an element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) given document, "`html`", the [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces), null, null, false, and the result of [looking up a custom element registry](#4134-the-customelementregistry-interface) given target.
14. [Append](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) root to document.
15. Set up the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents)'s [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements) so that it contains just the single element root.
16. Let fragment be the result of [creating a document fragment](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) given target's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
17. Set the parser's [root insertion target](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) to fragment.
18. If [context](#134-parsing-html-fragments) is a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element, then push "[in template](#1326416-the-in-template-insertion-mode)" onto the [stack of template insertion modes](#13241-the-insertion-mode) so that it is the new [current template insertion mode](#13241-the-insertion-mode).
19. Create a start tag token whose name is the local name of [context](#134-parsing-html-fragments) and whose attributes are the attributes of [context](#134-parsing-html-fragments).

    Let this start tag token be the start tag token of [context](#134-parsing-html-fragments); e.g. for the purposes of determining if it is an [HTML integration point](#1326-tree-construction).

20. [Reset the parser's insertion mode appropriately](#13241-the-insertion-mode).

    > [!note]
    > The parser will reference its [fragment context element](#13245-other-parsing-state-flags) as part of that algorithm.

21. Set the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents)'s [`form` element pointer](#13244-the-element-pointers) to the nearest node to [context](#134-parsing-html-fragments) that is a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element (going straight up the ancestor chain, and including the element itself, if it is a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element), if any. (If there is no such [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element, the [`form` element pointer](#13244-the-element-pointers) keeps its initial value, null.)
22. Place the input into the [input stream](#13235-preprocessing-the-input-stream) for the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) just created. The encoding [confidence](#1323-the-input-byte-stream) is *irrelevant*.
23. Start the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) and let it run until it has consumed all the characters just inserted into the input stream.
24. Return fragment.

## 14 The XML syntax

> [!note]
> This section only describes the rules for XML resources. Rules for [`text/html`](#171-texthtml) resources are discussed in the section above entitled "[The HTML syntax](#13-the-html-syntax)".

> [!warning]
> Using the XML syntax is not recommended, for reasons which include the fact that there is no specification which defines the rules for how an XML parser must map a string of bytes or characters into a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object, as well as the fact that the XML syntax is essentially unmaintained — in that, it’s not expected that any further features will ever be added to the XML syntax (even when such features have been added to the [HTML syntax](#13-the-html-syntax)).

### 14.1 Writing documents in the XML syntax

> [!note]
> The XML syntax for HTML was formerly referred to as "XHTML", but this specification does not use that term (among other reasons, because no such term is used for the HTML syntaxes of MathML and SVG).

The syntax for XML is defined in XML and Namespaces in XML. [\[XML\]](#references) [\[XMLNS\]](#references)

This specification does not define any syntax-level requirements beyond those defined for XML proper.

XML documents may contain a `DOCTYPE` if desired, but this is not required to conform to this specification. This specification does not define a public or system identifier, nor provide a formal DTD.

> [!note]
> According to XML, XML processors are not guaranteed to process the external DTD subset referenced in the DOCTYPE. This means, for example, that using [entity references](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#dt-entref) for characters in XML documents is unsafe if they are defined in an external file (except for `&lt;`, `&gt;`, `&amp;`, `&quot;`, and `&apos;`).

### 14.2 Parsing XML documents

This section describes the relationship between XML and the DOM, with a particular emphasis on how this interacts with HTML.

An XML parser, for the purposes of this specification, is a construct that follows the rules given in XML to map a string of bytes or characters into a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object.

> [!note]
> At the time of writing, no such rules actually exist.

An [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents) is either associated with a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object when it is created, or creates one implicitly.

This [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) must then be populated with DOM nodes that represent the tree structure of the input passed to the parser, as defined by XML, Namespaces in XML, and DOM. These nodes must be created using the following algorithms:
- For elements, [create an element for a token](#13261-creating-and-inserting-nodes), given the element's prefix, to ensure the proper [element interfaces](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) are created and that [custom elements](#4133-core-concepts) are set up correctly.
- For [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) nodes, [create a text node](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text).
- For [`CDATASection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#412-interface-cdatasection) nodes, [create a CDATA section node](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#412-interface-cdatasection).
- For [`Comment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#414-interface-comment) nodes, [create a comment node](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#414-interface-comment).
- For [`ProcessingInstruction`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#413-interface-processinginstruction) nodes, [create a processing instruction node](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#413-interface-processinginstruction).
- For [`DocumentType`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-interface-documenttype) nodes, [create a doctype](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-interface-documenttype).

For the operations that the [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents) performs on the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s tree, the user agent must act as if elements and attributes were individually appended and set respectively so as to trigger rules in this specification regarding what happens when an element is inserted into a document or has its attributes set, and DOM's requirements regarding [mutation observers](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#43-mutation-observers) mean that mutation observers *are* fired. [\[XML\]](#references) [\[XMLNS\]](#references) [\[DOM\]](#references) [\[UIEVENTS\]](#references)

Between the time an element's start tag is parsed and the time either the element's end tag is parsed or the parser detects a well-formedness error, the user agent must act as if the element was in a [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).

> [!note]
> This is used by various elements to only start certain processes once they are popped off of the [stack of open elements](#13242-the-stack-of-open-elements).

[\[XML\]](#references)
- `-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Transitional//EN`
- `-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.1//EN`
- `-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Strict//EN`

Furthermore, user agents should attempt to retrieve the above external entity's content when one of the above public identifiers is used, and should not attempt to retrieve any other external entity's content.

> [!note]
> This is not strictly a [violation](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-compliance-with-other-specifications) of XML, but it does contradict the spirit of XML's requirements. This is motivated by a desire for user agents to all handle entities in an interoperable fashion without requiring any network access for handling external subsets. [\[XML\]](#references)

XML parsers can be invoked with XML scripting support enabled or XML scripting support disabled. Except where otherwise specified, XML parsers are invoked with [XML scripting support enabled](#142-parsing-xml-documents).

When an [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents) with [XML scripting support enabled](#142-parsing-xml-documents) creates a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element, it must have its [parser document](#41211-processing-model) set and its [force async](#41211-processing-model) set to false. If the parser was created as part of the [XML fragment parsing algorithm](#144-parsing-xml-fragments), then the element's [already started](#41211-processing-model) must be set to true. When the element's end tag is subsequently parsed, the user agent must [perform a microtask checkpoint](#8173-processing-model), and then [prepare](#41211-processing-model) the [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element. If this causes there to be a [pending parsing-blocking script](#41211-processing-model), then the user agent must run the following steps:
1. Block this instance of the [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents), such that the [event loop](#8171-definitions) will not run [tasks](#8171-definitions) that invoke it.
2. [Spin the event loop](#8173-processing-model) until the parser's [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) [has no style sheet that is blocking scripts](#427-interactions-of-styling-and-scripting) and the [pending parsing-blocking script](#41211-processing-model)'s [ready to be parser-executed](#41211-processing-model) is true.
3. Unblock this instance of the [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents), such that [tasks](#8171-definitions) that invoke it can again be run.
4. [Execute the script element](#41211-processing-model) given by the [pending parsing-blocking script](#41211-processing-model).
5. Set the [pending parsing-blocking script](#41211-processing-model) to null.

> [!note]
> Since the [`document.write()`](#843-documentwrite) API is not available for [XML documents](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), much of the complexity in the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents) is not needed in the [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents).

> [!note]
> When the [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents) has [XML scripting support disabled](#142-parsing-xml-documents), none of this happens.

When an [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents) would append a node to a [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element, it must instead append it to the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element's [template contents](#4123-the-template-element) (a [`DocumentFragment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) node).

> [!note]
> This is a [willful violation](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-compliance-with-other-specifications) of XML; unfortunately, XML is not formally extensible in the manner that is needed for [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) processing. [\[XML\]](#references)

When an [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents) creates a [`Node`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) object, its [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) must be set to the [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) of the node into which the newly created node is to be inserted.

Certain algorithms in this specification spoon-feed the parser characters one at a time. In such cases, the [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents) must act as it would have if faced with a single string consisting of the concatenation of all those characters.

When an [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents) reaches the end of its input, it must [stop parsing](#1327-the-end), following the same rules as the [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents). An [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents) can also be [aborted](#1327-the-end), which must again be done in the same way as for an [HTML parser](#132-parsing-html-documents).

For the purposes of conformance checkers, if a resource is determined to be in [the XML syntax](#14-the-xml-syntax), then it is an [XML document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document).

### 14.3 Serializing XML fragments

The XML fragment serialization algorithm for a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) or [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) node either returns a fragment of XML that represents that node or throws an exception.

For [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)s, the algorithm must return a string in the form of a [document entity](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-well-formed), if none of the error cases below apply.

For [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element)s, the algorithm must return a string in the form of an [internal general parsed entity](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#wf-entities), if none of the error cases below apply.

In both cases, the string returned must be XML namespace-well-formed and must be an isomorphic serialization of all of that node's [relevant child nodes](#143-serializing-xml-fragments), in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees). User agents may adjust prefixes and namespace declarations in the serialization (and indeed might be forced to do so in some cases to obtain namespace-well-formed XML). User agents may use a combination of regular text and character references to represent [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) nodes in the DOM.

A node's relevant child nodes are those that apply given the following rules:

For [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) elements

The [relevant child nodes](#143-serializing-xml-fragments) are the child nodes of the [`template`](#4123-the-template-element) element's [template contents](#4123-the-template-element), if any.

For all other nodes

The [relevant child nodes](#143-serializing-xml-fragments) are the child nodes of node itself, if any.

For [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element)s, if any of the elements in the serialization are in no namespace, the default namespace in scope for those elements must be explicitly declared as the empty string. (This doesn't apply in the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) case.) [\[XML\]](#references) [\[XMLNS\]](#references)

For the purposes of this section, an internal general parsed entity is considered XML namespace-well-formed if a document consisting of an element with no namespace declarations whose contents are the internal general parsed entity would itself be XML namespace-well-formed.

If any of the following error cases are found in the DOM subtree being serialized, then the algorithm must throw an ["`InvalidStateError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#invalidstateerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException) instead of returning a string:
- A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) node with no child element nodes.
- A [`DocumentType`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-interface-documenttype) node that has an external subset public identifier that contains characters that are not matched by the XML `PubidChar` production. [\[XML\]](#references)
- A [`DocumentType`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-interface-documenttype) node that has an external subset system identifier that contains both a U+0022 QUOTATION MARK (") and a U+0027 APOSTROPHE (') or that contains characters that are not matched by the XML `Char` production. [\[XML\]](#references)
- A node with a local name containing a U+003A COLON (:).
- A node with a local name that does not match the XML [`Name`](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#NT-Name) production. [\[XML\]](#references)
- An [`Attr`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#492-interface-attr) node with no namespace whose local name is the lowercase string "`xmlns`". [\[XMLNS\]](#references)
- An [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) node with two or more attributes with the same local name and namespace.
- An [`Attr`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#492-interface-attr) node, [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node, [`Comment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#414-interface-comment) node, or [`ProcessingInstruction`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#413-interface-processinginstruction) node whose data contains characters that are not matched by the XML `Char` production. [\[XML\]](#references)
- A [`Comment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#414-interface-comment) node whose data contains two adjacent U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS characters (-) or ends with such a character.
- A [`ProcessingInstruction`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#413-interface-processinginstruction) node whose target name is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`xml`".
- A [`ProcessingInstruction`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#413-interface-processinginstruction) node whose target name contains a U+003A COLON (:).
- A [`ProcessingInstruction`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#413-interface-processinginstruction) node whose data contains the string "`?>`".

> [!note]
> These are the only ways to make a DOM unserialisable. The DOM enforces all the other XML constraints; for example, trying to append two elements to a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) node will throw a ["`HierarchyRequestError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#hierarchyrequesterror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).

### 14.4 Parsing XML fragments

The XML fragment parsing algorithm given an [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) or [`DocumentFragment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) node target and a string input, runs the following steps. They return a [`DocumentFragment`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment).
1. Let [context](#134-parsing-html-fragments) be target if target is an [`Element`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element); otherwise target's [host](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment).
2. [Assert](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#310-assertions): [context](#134-parsing-html-fragments) is non-null.
3. Create a new [XML parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents).
4. [Feed the parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents) just created the string corresponding to the start tag of [context](#134-parsing-html-fragments), declaring all the namespace prefixes that are in scope on that element in the DOM, as well as declaring the default namespace (if any) that is in scope on that element in the DOM.

   A namespace prefix is in scope if the DOM `lookupNamespaceURI()` method on the element would return a non-null value for that prefix.

   The default namespace is the namespace for which the DOM `isDefaultNamespace()` method on the element would return true.

   > [!note]
   > No `DOCTYPE` is passed to the parser, and therefore no external subset is referenced, and therefore no entities will be recognized.

5. [Feed the parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents) just created the string input.
6. [Feed the parser](#142-parsing-xml-documents) just created the string corresponding to the end tag of [context](#134-parsing-html-fragments).
7. If there is an XML well-formedness or XML namespace well-formedness error, then throw a ["`SyntaxError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
8. If the [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree) of the resulting [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has any sibling nodes, then throw a ["`SyntaxError`"](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#syntaxerror) [`DOMException`](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-DOMException).
9. Let newChildren be the resulting [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) node's [document element](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#421-document-tree)'s [children](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees), in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees).
10. Let fragment be the result of [creating a document fragment](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-interface-documentfragment) given context's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node).
11. For each node of newChildren, in [tree order](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees): [append](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#423-mutation-algorithms) node to fragment.
12. Return fragment.

## 15 Rendering

*User agents are not required to present HTML documents in any particular way. However, this section provides a set of suggestions for rendering HTML documents that, if followed, are likely to lead to a user experience that closely resembles the experience intended by the documents' authors. So as to avoid confusion regarding the normativity of this section, "must" has not been used. Instead, the term "expected" is used to indicate behavior that will lead to this experience. For the purposes of conformance for user agents designated as [supporting the suggested default rendering](#218-conformance-classes), the term "expected" in this section has the same conformance implications as "must".*

### 15.1 Introduction

The suggestions in this section are generally expressed in CSS terms. User agents are [expected](#15-rendering) to either support CSS, or translate from the CSS rules given in this section to approximations for other presentation mechanisms.

In the absence of style-layer rules to the contrary (e.g. author style sheets), user agents are [expected](#15-rendering) to render an element so that it conveys to the user the meaning that the element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom), as described by this specification.

The suggestions in this section generally assume a visual output medium with a resolution of 96dpi or greater, but HTML is intended to apply to multiple media (it is a *media-independent* language). User agent implementers are encouraged to adapt the suggestions in this section to their target media.

---

An element is being rendered if it has any associated CSS layout boxes, SVG layout boxes, or some equivalent in other styling languages.

> [!note]
> Just being off-screen does not mean the element is not [being rendered](#151-introduction). The presence of the [`hidden`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute normally means the element is not [being rendered](#151-introduction), though this might be overridden by the style sheets.

> [!note]
> The [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents) state does not affect whether an element is [being rendered](#151-introduction) or not. Even if a document is not [fully active](#733-fully-active-documents) and not shown at all to the user, elements within it can still qualify as "being rendered".

An element is said to intersect the viewport when it is [being rendered](#151-introduction) and its associated CSS layout box intersects the [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport).

> [!note]
> Similar to the [being rendered](#151-introduction) state, elements in non-[fully active](#733-fully-active-documents) documents can still [intersect the viewport](#151-introduction). The [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) is not shared between documents and might not always be shown to the user, so an element in a non-[fully active](#733-fully-active-documents) document can still intersect the [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) associated with its document.

> [!note]
> This specification does not define the precise timing for when the intersection is tested, but it is suggested that the timing match that of the Intersection Observer API. [\[INTERSECTIONOBSERVER\]](#references)

An element is delegating its rendering to its children if it is not [being rendered](#151-introduction) but its children (if any) could [be rendered](#151-introduction), as a result of CSS 'display: contents', or some equivalent in other styling languages. [\[CSSDISPLAY\]](#references)

---

User agents that do not honor author-level CSS style sheets are nonetheless [expected](#15-rendering) to act as if they applied the CSS rules given in these sections in a manner consistent with this specification and the relevant CSS and Unicode specifications. [\[CSS\]](#references) [\[UNICODE\]](#references) [\[BIDI\]](#references)

> [!note]
> This is especially important for issues relating to the ['display'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop), ['unicode-bidi'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#unicode-bidi), and ['direction'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#direction) properties.

### 15.2 The CSS user agent style sheet and presentational hints

The CSS rules given in these subsections are, except where otherwise specified, [expected](#15-rendering) to be used as part of the user-agent level style sheet defaults for all documents that contain [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility).

Some rules are intended for the author-level zero-specificity presentational hints part of the CSS cascade; these are explicitly called out as presentational hints.

---

When the text below says that an attribute attribute on an element element maps to the pixel length property (or properties) properties, it means that if element has an attribute attribute set, and parsing that attribute's value using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers) doesn't generate an error, then the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to use the parsed value as a pixel length for a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) for properties.

When the text below says that an attribute attribute on an element element maps to the dimension property (or properties) properties, it means that if element has an attribute attribute set, and parsing that attribute's value using the [rules for parsing dimension values](#2344-percentages-and-lengths) doesn't generate an error, then the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to use the parsed dimension as the value for a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) for properties, with the value given as a pixel length if the dimension was a length, and with the value given as a percentage if the dimension was a percentage.

When the text below says that an attribute attribute on an element element maps to the dimension property (ignoring zero) (or properties) properties, it means that if element has an attribute attribute set, and parsing that attribute's value using the [rules for parsing nonzero dimension values](#2345-nonzero-percentages-and-lengths) doesn't generate an error, then the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to use the parsed dimension as the value for a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) for properties, with the value given as a pixel length if the dimension was a length, and with the value given as a percentage if the dimension was a percentage.

When the text below says that a pair of attributes w and h on an element element map to the aspect-ratio property, it means that if element has both attributes w and h, and parsing those attributes' values using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers) doesn't generate an error for either, then the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to use the parsed integers as a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) for the ['aspect-ratio'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing-4/#aspect-ratio) property of the form `auto w /
  h`.

When the text below says that a pair of attributes w and h on an element element map to the aspect-ratio property (using dimension rules), it means that if element has both attributes w and h, and parsing those attributes' values using the [rules for parsing dimension values](#2344-percentages-and-lengths) doesn't generate an error or return a percentage for either, then the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to use the parsed dimensions as a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) for the ['aspect-ratio'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing-4/#aspect-ratio) property of the form `auto w /
  h`.

When a user agent is to align descendants of a node, the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to align only those descendants that have both their ['margin-inline-start'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-margin-inline-start) and ['margin-inline-end'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-margin-inline-end) properties computing to a value other than 'auto', that are over-constrained and that have one of those two margins with a [used value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#used-value) forced to a greater value, and that do not themselves have an applicable `align` attribute. When multiple elements are to [align](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) a particular descendant, the most deeply nested such element is [expected](#15-rendering) to override the others. Aligned elements are [expected](#15-rendering) to be aligned by having the [used values](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#used-value) of their margins on the [line-left](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#line-left) and [line-right](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#line-right) sides be set accordingly. [\[CSSLOGICAL\]](#references) [\[CSSWM\]](#references)

### 15.3 Non-replaced elements

#### 15.3.1 Hidden elements

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

area, base, basefont, datalist, head, link, meta, noembed,
noframes, param, rp, script, style, template, title {
  display: none;
}

[hidden]:not([hidden=until-found i]):not(embed) {
  display: none;
}

[hidden=until-found i]:not(embed) {
  content-visibility: hidden;
}

embed[hidden] { display: inline; height: 0; width: 0; } 

input[type=hidden i] { display: none !important; }

@media (scripting) {
  noscript { display: none !important; }
}
```

#### 15.3.2 The page

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

html, body { display: block; }
```

For each property in the table below, given a [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element, the first attribute that exists [maps to the pixel length property](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) on the [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element. If none of the attributes for a property are found, or if the value of the attribute that was found cannot be parsed successfully, then a default value of 8px is [expected](#15-rendering) to be used for that property instead.

| Property | Source |
| --- | --- |
| ['margin-top'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-margin-top), ['margin-bottom'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-margin-bottom) | The [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element's [`marginheight`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute |
| The [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element's [`topmargin`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute |
| The [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element's [container frame element](#1532-the-page)'s [`marginheight`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute |
| ['margin-left'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-margin-left), ['margin-right'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-margin-right) | The [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element's [`marginwidth`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute |
| The [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element's [`leftmargin`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute |
| The [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element's [container frame element](#1532-the-page)'s [`marginwidth`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute |

If the [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [node navigable](#731-navigables) is a [child navigable](#7313-child-navigables), and the [container](#7313-child-navigables) of that [navigable](#731-navigables) is a [`frame`](#1632-frames) or [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) element, then the container frame element of the [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element is that [`frame`](#1632-frames) or [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) element. Otherwise, there is no [container frame element](#1532-the-page).

> [!warning]
> The above requirements imply that a page can change the margins of another page (including one from another [origin](#711-origins)) using, for example, an [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element). This is potentially a security risk, as it might in some cases allow an attack to contrive a situation in which a page is rendered not as the author intended, possibly for the purposes of phishing or otherwise misleading the user.

---

If a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [node navigable](#731-navigables) is a [child navigable](#7313-child-navigables), then it is [expected](#15-rendering) to be positioned and sized to fit inside the [content box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#content-box) of the [container](#7313-child-navigables) of that [navigable](#731-navigables). If the [container](#7313-child-navigables) is not [being rendered](#151-introduction), the [navigable](#731-navigables) is [expected](#15-rendering) to have a [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) with zero width and zero height.

If a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [node navigable](#731-navigables) is a [child navigable](#7313-child-navigables), the [container](#7313-child-navigables) of that [navigable](#731-navigables) is a [`frame`](#1632-frames) or [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) element, that element has a `scrolling` attribute, and that attribute's value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`off`", "`noscroll`", or "`no`", then the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to prevent any scrollbars from being shown for the [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) of the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object)'s [node navigable](#731-navigables), regardless of the ['overflow'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-overflow/#propdef-overflow) property that applies to that [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport).

---

When a [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element has a [`background`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute set to a non-empty value, the new value is [expected](#15-rendering) to be [encoding-parsed-and-serialized](#242-parsing-urls) relative to the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), and if that does not return failure, the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) setting the element's ['background-image'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-background-image) property to the return value.

When a [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element has a [`bgcolor`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute set, the new value is [expected](#15-rendering) to be parsed using the [rules for parsing a legacy color value](#236-legacy-colors), and if that does not return failure, the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) setting the element's ['background-color'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-background-color) property to the resulting color.

When a [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element has a [`text`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute, its value is [expected](#15-rendering) to be parsed using the [rules for parsing a legacy color value](#236-legacy-colors), and if that does not return failure, the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) setting the element's ['color'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#the-color-property) property to the resulting color.

When a [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element has a [`link`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute, its value is [expected](#15-rendering) to be parsed using the [rules for parsing a legacy color value](#236-legacy-colors), and if that does not return failure, the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) setting the ['color'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#the-color-property) property of any element in the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) matching the [`:link`](#4163-pseudo-classes) [pseudo-class](https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#pseudo-class) to the resulting color.

When a [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element has a [`vlink`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute, its value is [expected](#15-rendering) to be parsed using the [rules for parsing a legacy color value](#236-legacy-colors), and if that does not return failure, the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) setting the ['color'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#the-color-property) property of any element in the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) matching the [`:visited`](#4163-pseudo-classes) [pseudo-class](https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#pseudo-class) to the resulting color.

When a [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element has an [`alink`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute, its value is [expected](#15-rendering) to be parsed using the [rules for parsing a legacy color value](#236-legacy-colors), and if that does not return failure, the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) setting the ['color'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#the-color-property) property of any element in the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) matching the [`:active`](#4163-pseudo-classes) [pseudo-class](https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#pseudo-class) and either the [`:link`](#4163-pseudo-classes) [pseudo-class](https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#pseudo-class) or the [`:visited`](#4163-pseudo-classes) [pseudo-class](https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#pseudo-class) to the resulting color.

#### 15.3.3 Flow content

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

address, blockquote, center, dialog, div, figure, figcaption, footer, form,
header, hr, legend, listing, main, p, plaintext, pre, search, xmp {
  display: block;
}

blockquote, figure, listing, p, plaintext, pre, xmp {
  margin-block: 1em;
}

blockquote, figure { margin-inline: 40px; }

address { font-style: italic; }
listing, plaintext, pre, xmp {
  font-family: monospace; white-space: pre;
}

dialog:not([open]) { display: none; }
dialog {
  position: absolute;
  inset-inline-start: 0; inset-inline-end: 0;
  width: fit-content;
  height: fit-content;
  margin: auto;
  border: solid;
  padding: 1em;
  background-color: Canvas;
  color: CanvasText;
}
dialog:modal {
  position: fixed;
  overflow: auto;
  inset-block: 0;
  max-width: calc(100% - 6px - 2em);
  max-height: calc(100% - 6px - 2em);
}
dialog::backdrop {
  background: rgba(0,0,0,0.1);
}

[popover]:not(:popover-open):not(dialog[open]) {
  display:none;
}

dialog:popover-open {
  display:block;
}

[popover] {
  position: fixed;
  inset: 0;
  width: fit-content;
  height: fit-content;
  margin: auto;
  border: solid;
  padding: 0.25em;
  overflow: auto;
  color: CanvasText;
  background-color: Canvas;
}

:popover-open::backdrop {
  position: fixed;
  inset: 0;
  pointer-events: none !important;
  background-color: transparent;
}

slot {
  display: contents;
}
```

The following rules are also [expected](#15-rendering) to apply, as [presentational hints](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints):

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

pre[wrap] { white-space: pre-wrap; }
```

In [quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), the following rules are also [expected](#15-rendering) to apply:

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

form { margin-block-end: 1em; }
```

---

The [`center`](#162-non-conforming-features) element, and the [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element when it has an [`align`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute whose value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for either the string "`center`" or the string "`middle`", are [expected](#15-rendering) to center text within themselves, as if they had their ['text-align'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#text-align-property) property set to 'center' in a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints), and to [align descendants](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) to the center.

The [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element, when it has an [`align`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute whose value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`left`", is [expected](#15-rendering) to left-align text within itself, as if it had its ['text-align'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#text-align-property) property set to 'left' in a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints), and to [align descendants](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) to the left.

The [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element, when it has an [`align`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute whose value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`right`", is [expected](#15-rendering) to right-align text within itself, as if it had its ['text-align'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#text-align-property) property set to 'right' in a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints), and to [align descendants](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) to the right.

The [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element, when it has an [`align`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute whose value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`justify`", is [expected](#15-rendering) to full-justify text within itself, as if it had its ['text-align'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#text-align-property) property set to 'justify' in a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints), and to [align descendants](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) to the left.

#### 15.3.4 Phrasing content

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

cite, dfn, em, i, var { font-style: italic; }
b, strong { font-weight: bolder; }
code, kbd, samp, tt { font-family: monospace; }
big { font-size: larger; }
small { font-size: smaller; }

sub { vertical-align: sub; }
sup { vertical-align: super; }
sub, sup { line-height: normal; font-size: smaller; }

ruby { display: ruby; }
rt { display: ruby-text; }

:link { color: #0000EE; }
:visited { color: #551A8B; }
:link:active, :visited:active { color: #FF0000; }
:link, :visited { text-decoration: underline; cursor: pointer; }

:focus-visible { outline: auto; }

mark { background: yellow; color: black; } /* this color is just a suggestion and can be changed based on implementation feedback */

abbr[title], acronym[title] { text-decoration: dotted underline; }
ins, u { text-decoration: underline; }
del, s, strike { text-decoration: line-through; }

q::before { content: open-quote; }
q::after { content: close-quote; }

br { display-outside: newline; } /* this also has bidi implications */
nobr { white-space: nowrap; }
wbr { display-outside: break-opportunity; } /* this also has bidi implications */
nobr wbr { white-space: normal; }
```

The following rules are also [expected](#15-rendering) to apply, as [presentational hints](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints):

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

br[clear=left i] { clear: left; }
br[clear=right i] { clear: right; }
br[clear=all i], br[clear=both i] { clear: both; }
```

For the purposes of the CSS ruby model, runs of children of [`ruby`](#4510-the-ruby-element) elements that are not [`rt`](#4511-the-rt-element) or [`rp`](#4512-the-rp-element) elements are [expected](#15-rendering) to be wrapped in anonymous boxes whose ['display'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop) property has the value ['ruby-base'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ruby/#valdef-display-ruby-base). [\[CSSRUBY\]](#references)

When a particular part of a ruby has more than one annotation, the annotations should be distributed on both sides of the base text so as to minimize the stacking of ruby annotations on one side.

> [!note]
> When it becomes possible to do so, the preceding requirement will be updated to be expressed in terms of CSS ruby. (Currently, CSS ruby does not handle nested [`ruby`](#4510-the-ruby-element) elements or multiple sequential [`rt`](#4511-the-rt-element) elements, which is how this semantic is expressed.)

User agents that do not support correct ruby rendering are [expected](#15-rendering) to render parentheses around the text of [`rt`](#4511-the-rt-element) elements in the absence of [`rp`](#4512-the-rp-element) elements.

---

User agents are [expected](#15-rendering) to support the ['clear'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#flow-control) property on inline elements (in order to render [`br`](#4527-the-br-element) elements with [`clear`](#162-non-conforming-features) attributes) in the manner described in the non-normative note to this effect in CSS.

The initial value for the ['color'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#the-color-property) property is [expected](#15-rendering) to be black. The initial value for the ['background-color'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-background-color) property is [expected](#15-rendering) to be 'transparent'. The canvas's background is [expected](#15-rendering) to be white.

---

When a [`font`](#162-non-conforming-features) element has a `color` attribute, its value is [expected](#15-rendering) to be parsed using the [rules for parsing a legacy color value](#236-legacy-colors), and if that does not return failure, the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) setting the element's ['color'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#the-color-property) property to the resulting color.

When a [`font`](#162-non-conforming-features) element has a `face` attribute, the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) setting the element's ['font-family'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-family-prop) property to the attribute's value.

When a [`font`](#162-non-conforming-features) element has a `size` attribute, the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to use the following steps, known as the rules for parsing a legacy font size, to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) setting the element's ['font-size'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-size-prop) property:
1. Let input be the attribute's value.
2. Let position be a pointer into input, initially pointing at the start of the string.
3. [Skip ASCII whitespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) within input given position.
4. If position is past the end of input, there is no [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints). Return.
5. If the character at position is a U+002B PLUS SIGN character (+), then let mode be *relative-plus*, and advance position to the next character. Otherwise, if the character at position is a U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS character (-), then let mode be *relative-minus*, and advance position to the next character. Otherwise, let mode be *absolute*.
6. [Collect a sequence of code points](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) that are [ASCII digits](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#46-code-points) from input given position, and let digits be the resulting sequence.
7. If digits is the empty string, there is no [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints). Return.
8. Interpret digits as a base-ten integer. Let value be the resulting number.
9. If mode is *relative-plus*, then increment value by 3. If mode is *relative-minus*, then let value be the result of subtracting value from 3.
10. If value is greater than 7, let it be 7.
11. If value is less than 1, let it be 1.
12. Set the ['font-size'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-size-prop) property to the keyword corresponding to the value of value according to the following table:

    | value | ['font-size'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-size-prop) keyword |
    | --- | --- |
    | 1 | 'x-small' |
    | 2 | 'small' |
    | 3 | 'medium' |
    | 4 | 'large' |
    | 5 | 'x-large' |
    | 6 | 'xx-large' |
    | 7 | 'xxx-large' |

#### 15.3.5 Bidirectional text

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

[dir]:dir(ltr), bdi:dir(ltr), input[type=tel i]:dir(ltr) { direction: ltr; }
[dir]:dir(rtl), bdi:dir(rtl) { direction: rtl; }

address, blockquote, center, div, figure, figcaption, footer, form, header, hr,
legend, listing, main, p, plaintext, pre, summary, xmp, article, aside,
:heading, hgroup, nav, search, section, table, caption, colgroup, col, thead,
tbody, tfoot, tr, td, th, dir, dd, dl, dt, menu, ol, ul, li, bdi, output,
[dir=ltr i], [dir=rtl i], [dir=auto i] {
  unicode-bidi: isolate; 
}

bdo, bdo[dir] { unicode-bidi: isolate-override; } 

input[dir=auto i]:is([type=search i], [type=tel i], [type=url i],
[type=email i]), textarea[dir=auto i], pre[dir=auto i] {
  unicode-bidi: plaintext;
}
/* see prose for input elements whose type attribute is in the Text state */

/* the rules setting the 'content' property on br and wbr elements also has bidi implications */
```

When an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element's [`dir`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) attribute is in the [auto](#3264-the-dir-attribute) state and its [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Text](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch) state, then the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to act as if it had a user-agent-level style sheet rule setting the ['unicode-bidi'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#unicode-bidi) property to 'plaintext'.

Input fields (i.e. [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements, and [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements when their [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Text](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch), [Search](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch), [Telephone](#410513-telephone-state-typetel), [URL](#410514-url-state-typeurl), or [Email](#410515-email-state-typeemail) state) are [expected](#15-rendering) to present an editing user interface with a directionality that matches the element's ['direction'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#direction) property.

When the document's character encoding is [ISO-8859-8](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#iso-8859-8), the following rules are additionally [expected](#15-rendering) to apply, following those above: [\[ENCODING\]](#references)

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

address, blockquote, center, div, figure, figcaption, footer, form, header, hr,
legend, listing, main, p, plaintext, pre, summary, xmp, article, aside,
:heading, hgroup, nav, search, section, table, caption, colgroup, col, thead,
tbody, tfoot, tr, td, th, dir, dd, dl, dt, menu, ol, ul, li, [dir=ltr i],
[dir=rtl i], [dir=auto i], *|* {
  unicode-bidi: bidi-override;
}
input:not([type=submit i]):not([type=reset i]):not([type=button i]),
textarea {
  unicode-bidi: normal;
}
```

#### 15.3.6 Sections and headings

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

article, aside, :heading, hgroup, nav, section {
  display: block;
}

:heading { font-weight: bold; }

:heading(1) { margin-block: 0.67em; font-size: 2.00em; }
:heading(2) { margin-block: 0.83em; font-size: 1.50em; }
:heading(3) { margin-block: 1.00em; font-size: 1.17em; }
:heading(4) { margin-block: 1.33em; font-size: 1.00em; }
:heading(5) { margin-block: 1.67em; font-size: 0.83em; }
:heading(6, 7, 8, 9) {
  font-size: 0.67em;
  margin-block: 2.33em;
}

```

#### 15.3.7 Lists

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

dir, dd, dl, dt, menu, ol, ul { display: block; }
li { display: list-item; text-align: match-parent; }

dir, dl, menu, ol, ul { margin-block: 1em; }

:is(dir, dl, menu, ol, ul) :is(dir, dl, menu, ol, ul) {
  margin-block: 0;
}

dd { margin-inline-start: 40px; }
dir, menu, ol, ul { padding-inline-start: 40px; }

ol, ul, menu { counter-reset: list-item; }
ol { list-style-type: decimal; }

dir, menu, ul {
  list-style-type: disc;
}
:is(dir, menu, ol, ul) :is(dir, menu, ul) {
  list-style-type: circle;
}
:is(dir, menu, ol, ul) :is(dir, menu, ol, ul) :is(dir, menu, ul) {
  list-style-type: square;
}
```

The following rules are also [expected](#15-rendering) to apply, as [presentational hints](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints):

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

ol[type="1"], li[type="1"] { list-style-type: decimal; }
ol[type=a s], li[type=a s] { list-style-type: lower-alpha; }
ol[type=A s], li[type=A s] { list-style-type: upper-alpha; }
ol[type=i s], li[type=i s] { list-style-type: lower-roman; }
ol[type=I s], li[type=I s] { list-style-type: upper-roman; }
ul[type=none i], li[type=none i] { list-style-type: none; }
ul[type=disc i], li[type=disc i] { list-style-type: disc; }
ul[type=circle i], li[type=circle i] { list-style-type: circle; }
ul[type=square i], li[type=square i] { list-style-type: square; }
```

In [quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), the following rules are also [expected](#15-rendering) to apply:

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

li { list-style-position: inside; }
li :is(dir, menu, ol, ul) { list-style-position: outside; }
:is(dir, menu, ol, ul) :is(dir, menu, ol, ul, li) { list-style-position: unset; }
```

When rendering [`li`](#448-the-li-element) elements, non-CSS user agents are [expected](#15-rendering) to use the [ordinal value](#448-the-li-element) of the [`li`](#448-the-li-element) element to render the counter in the list item marker.

For CSS user agents, some aspects of rendering [list items](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-lists/#list-item) are defined by the CSS Lists specification. Additionally, the following attribute mappings are [expected](#15-rendering) to apply: [\[CSSLISTS\]](#references)

When an [`li`](#448-the-li-element) element has a [`value`](#448-the-li-element) attribute, and parsing that attribute's value using the [rules for parsing integers](#2341-signed-integers) doesn't generate an error, the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to use the parsed value value as a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) for the ['counter-set'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-lists/#propdef-counter-set) property of the form `list-item value`.

When an [`ol`](#445-the-ol-element) element has a [`start`](#445-the-ol-element) attribute or a [`reversed`](#445-the-ol-element) attribute, or both, the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to use the following steps to treat the attributes as a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) for the ['counter-reset'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-lists/#propdef-counter-reset) property:
1. Let value be null.
2. If the element has a [`start`](#445-the-ol-element) attribute, then set value to the result of parsing the attribute's value using the [rules for parsing integers](#2341-signed-integers).
3. If the element has a [`reversed`](#445-the-ol-element) attribute:
   1. If value is an integer, then increment value by 1 and return `reversed(list-item) value`.
   2. Otherwise, return `reversed(list-item)`.

      > [!note]
      > Either the [`start`](#445-the-ol-element) attribute was absent, or parsing its value resulted in an error.

4. Otherwise:
   1. If value is an integer, then decrement value by 1 and return `list-item value`.
   2. Otherwise, there is no [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints).

```css
table[rules=rows i] > tr, table[rules=rows i] > thead > tr,
table[rules=rows i] > tbody > tr, table[rules=rows i] > tfoot > tr {
  border-block-width: 1px;
  border-block-style: solid;
}
```

In [quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), the following rules are also [expected](#15-rendering) to apply:

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

table {
  font-weight: initial;
  font-style: initial;
  font-variant: initial;
  font-size: initial;
  line-height: initial;
  white-space: initial;
  text-align: initial;
}
```

---

For the purposes of the CSS table model, the [`col`](#494-the-col-element) element is [expected](#15-rendering) to be treated as if it was present as many times as its [`span`](#494-the-col-element) attribute [specifies](#2342-non-negative-integers).

For the purposes of the CSS table model, the [`colgroup`](#493-the-colgroup-element) element, if it contains no [`col`](#494-the-col-element) element, is [expected](#15-rendering) to be treated as if it had as many such children as its [`span`](#493-the-colgroup-element) attribute [specifies](#2342-non-negative-integers).

For the purposes of the CSS table model, the [`colspan`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements) and [`rowspan`](#4911-attributes-common-to-td-and-th-elements) attributes on [`td`](#499-the-td-element) and [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) elements are [expected](#15-rendering) to [provide](#2342-non-negative-integers) the *special knowledge* regarding cells spanning rows and columns.

In [HTML documents](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), the following rules are also [expected](#15-rendering) to apply:

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

:is(table, thead, tbody, tfoot, tr) > form { display: none !important; }
```

---

The [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element's [`cellspacing`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute [maps to the pixel length property](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) ['border-spacing'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-tables/#propdef-border-spacing) on the element.

The [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element's [`cellpadding`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute [maps to the pixel length properties](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) ['padding-top'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-padding-top), ['padding-right'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-padding-right), ['padding-bottom'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-padding-bottom), and ['padding-left'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-padding-left) of any [`td`](#499-the-td-element) and [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) elements that have corresponding [cells](#4912-processing-model) in the [table](#4912-processing-model) corresponding to the [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element.

The [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element's [`height`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute [maps to the dimension property](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) ['height'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-height-property) on the [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element.

The [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element's [`width`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute [maps to the dimension property (ignoring zero)](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) ['width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-width-property) on the [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element.

The [`col`](#494-the-col-element) element's [`width`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute [maps to the dimension property](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) ['width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-width-property) on the [`col`](#494-the-col-element) element.

The [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element), [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element), and [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element) elements' [`height`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute [maps to the dimension property](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) ['height'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-height-property) on the element.

The [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element's [`height`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute [maps to the dimension property](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) ['height'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-height-property) on the [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element) element.

The [`td`](#499-the-td-element) and [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) elements' [`height`](#162-non-conforming-features) attributes [map to the dimension property (ignoring zero)](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) ['height'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-height-property) on the element.

The [`td`](#499-the-td-element) and [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) elements' [`width`](#162-non-conforming-features) attributes [map to the dimension property (ignoring zero)](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) ['width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-width-property) on the element.

---

The [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element), [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element), [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element), [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element), [`td`](#499-the-td-element), and [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) elements, when they have an `align` attribute whose value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for either the string "`center`" or the string "`middle`", are [expected](#15-rendering) to center text within themselves, as if they had their ['text-align'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#text-align-property) property set to 'center' in a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints), and to [align descendants](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) to the center.

The [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element), [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element), [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element), [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element), [`td`](#499-the-td-element), and [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) elements, when they have an `align` attribute whose value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`left`", are [expected](#15-rendering) to left-align text within themselves, as if they had their ['text-align'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#text-align-property) property set to 'left' in a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints), and to [align descendants](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) to the left.

The [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element), [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element), [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element), [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element), [`td`](#499-the-td-element), and [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) elements, when they have an `align` attribute whose value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`right`", are [expected](#15-rendering) to right-align text within themselves, as if they had their ['text-align'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#text-align-property) property set to 'right' in a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints), and to [align descendants](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) to the right.

The [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element), [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element), [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element), [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element), [`td`](#499-the-td-element), and [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) elements, when they have an `align` attribute whose value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`justify`", are [expected](#15-rendering) to full-justify text within themselves, as if they had their ['text-align'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#text-align-property) property set to 'justify' in a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints), and to [align descendants](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) to the left.

User agents are [expected](#15-rendering) to have a rule in their user agent style sheet that matches [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) elements that have a parent node whose [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) for the ['text-align'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#text-align-property) property is its initial value, whose declaration block consists of just a single declaration that sets the ['text-align'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#text-align-property) property to the value 'center'.

---

When a [`table`](#491-the-table-element), [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element), [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element), [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element), [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element), [`td`](#499-the-td-element), or [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element has a [`background`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute set to a non-empty value, the new value is [expected](#15-rendering) to be [encoding-parsed-and-serialized](#242-parsing-urls) relative to the element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node), and if that does not return failure, the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) setting the element's ['background-image'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-background-image) property to the return value.

When a [`table`](#491-the-table-element), [`thead`](#496-the-thead-element), [`tbody`](#495-the-tbody-element), [`tfoot`](#497-the-tfoot-element), [`tr`](#498-the-tr-element), [`td`](#499-the-td-element), or [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element has a `bgcolor` attribute set, the new value is [expected](#15-rendering) to be parsed using the [rules for parsing a legacy color value](#236-legacy-colors), and if that does not return failure, the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) setting the element's ['background-color'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-background-color) property to the resulting color.

When a [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element has a [`bordercolor`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute, its value is [expected](#15-rendering) to be parsed using the [rules for parsing a legacy color value](#236-legacy-colors), and if that does not return failure, the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) setting the element's ['border-top-color'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-top-color), ['border-right-color'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-right-color), ['border-bottom-color'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-bottom-color), and ['border-left-color'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-left-color) properties to the resulting color.

---

The [`table`](#491-the-table-element) element's [`border`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute [maps to the pixel length properties](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) ['border-top-width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-top-width), ['border-right-width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-right-width), ['border-bottom-width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-bottom-width), ['border-left-width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-left-width) on the element. If the attribute is present but parsing the attribute's value using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers) generates an error, a default value of 1px is [expected](#15-rendering) to be used for that property instead.

Rules marked "only if border is not equivalent to zero" in the CSS block above is [expected](#15-rendering) to only be applied if the [`border`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute mentioned in the selectors for the rule is not only present but, when parsed using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers), is also found to have a value other than zero or to generate an error.

---

In [quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), a [`td`](#499-the-td-element) element or a [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element that has a [`nowrap`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute but also has a [`width`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute whose value, when parsed using the [rules for parsing nonzero dimension values](#2345-nonzero-percentages-and-lengths), is found to be a length (not an error or a number classified as a percentage), is [expected](#15-rendering) to have a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) setting the element's ['white-space'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#white-space-property) property to 'normal', overriding the rule in the CSS block above that sets it to 'nowrap'.

#### 15.3.9 Margin collapsing quirks

A node is substantial if it is a text node that is not [inter-element whitespace](#325-content-models), or if it is an element node.

A node is blank if it is an element that contains no [substantial](#1539-margin-collapsing-quirks) nodes.

The elements with default margins are the following elements: [`blockquote`](#444-the-blockquote-element), [`dir`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`dl`](#449-the-dl-element), [`h1`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements), [`h2`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements), [`h3`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements), [`h4`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements), [`h5`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements), [`h6`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements), [`listing`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`menu`](#447-the-menu-element), [`ol`](#445-the-ol-element), [`p`](#441-the-p-element), [`plaintext`](#162-non-conforming-features), [`pre`](#443-the-pre-element), [`ul`](#446-the-ul-element), [`xmp`](#162-non-conforming-features).

In [quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), any [element with default margins](#1539-margin-collapsing-quirks) that is the [child](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) of a [`body`](#431-the-body-element), [`td`](#499-the-td-element), or [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element and has no [substantial](#1539-margin-collapsing-quirks) previous siblings is [expected](#15-rendering) to have a user-agent level style sheet rule that sets its ['margin-block-start'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-margin-block-start) property to zero.

In [quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), any [element with default margins](#1539-margin-collapsing-quirks) that is the [child](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) of a [`body`](#431-the-body-element), [`td`](#499-the-td-element), or [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element, has no [substantial](#1539-margin-collapsing-quirks) previous siblings, and is [blank](#1539-margin-collapsing-quirks), is [expected](#15-rendering) to have a user-agent level style sheet rule that sets its ['margin-block-end'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-margin-block-end) property to zero also.

In [quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), any [element with default margins](#1539-margin-collapsing-quirks) that is the [child](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) of a [`td`](#499-the-td-element) or [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element, has no [substantial](#1539-margin-collapsing-quirks) following siblings, and is [blank](#1539-margin-collapsing-quirks), is [expected](#15-rendering) to have a user-agent level style sheet rule that sets its ['margin-block-start'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-margin-block-start) property to zero.

In [quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), any [`p`](#441-the-p-element) element that is the [child](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) of a [`td`](#499-the-td-element) or [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element and has no [substantial](#1539-margin-collapsing-quirks) following siblings, is [expected](#15-rendering) to have a user-agent level style sheet rule that sets its ['margin-block-end'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-margin-block-end) property to zero.

#### 15.3.10 Form controls

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

input, button, textarea {
  letter-spacing: initial;
  word-spacing: initial;
  line-height: initial;
}

input, select, button, textarea {
  text-transform: initial;
  text-indent: initial;
  text-shadow: initial;
  appearance: auto;
}

input:not([type=range i], [type=checkbox i], [type=radio i]) {
  overflow: clip !important;
  overflow-clip-margin: 0 !important;
}

input[type=image i] {
  overflow-clip-margin: content-box !important;
}

input, select, textarea {
  text-align: initial;
}

:autofill {
  field-sizing: fixed !important;
}

input:is([type=reset i], [type=button i], [type=submit i]), button {
  text-align: center;
}

input, button {
  display: inline-block;
}

input[type=hidden i], input[type=file i], input[type=image i] {
  appearance: none;
}

input:is([type=radio i], [type=checkbox i], [type=reset i], [type=button i],
[type=submit i], [type=color i], [type=search i]), select, button {
  box-sizing: border-box;
}

textarea { white-space: pre-wrap; }

input:not([type=file i], [type=range i], [type=checkbox i], [type=radio i]) {
  align-content: unsafe center;
}

button,
::file-selector-button,
input:is([type=color i], [type=reset i], [type=button i], [type=submit i]) {
  align-content: center;
}

```

In [quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), the following rules are also [expected](#15-rendering) to apply:

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

input:not([type=image i]), textarea { box-sizing: border-box; }
```

Each kind of form control is also described in the [Widgets](#155-widgets) section, which describes the look and feel of the control.

For [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements where the [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is not in the [Hidden](#410511-hidden-state-typehidden) state or the [Image Button](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) state, and that are [being rendered](#151-introduction), are [expected](#15-rendering) to act as follows:
- The [inner display type](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#inner-display-type) is always 'flow-root'.

#### 15.3.11 The [`hr`](#442-the-hr-element) element

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

hr {
  color: gray;
  border-style: inset;
  border-width: 1px;
  margin-block: 0.5em;
  margin-inline: auto;
  overflow: hidden;
}
```

The following rules are also [expected](#15-rendering) to apply, as [presentational hints](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints):

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

hr[align=left i] { margin-left: 0; margin-right: auto; }
hr[align=right i] { margin-left: auto; margin-right: 0; }
hr[align=center i] { margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto; }
hr[color], hr[noshade] { border-style: solid; }
```

If an [`hr`](#442-the-hr-element) element has either a [`color`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute or a [`noshade`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute, and furthermore also has a [`size`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute, and parsing that attribute's value using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers) doesn't generate an error, then the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to use the parsed value divided by two as a pixel length for [presentational hints](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) for the properties ['border-top-width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-top-width), ['border-right-width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-right-width), ['border-bottom-width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-bottom-width), and ['border-left-width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-left-width) on the element.
