Otherwise, if an [`hr`](#442-the-hr-element) element has neither a [`color`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute nor a [`noshade`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute, but does have a [`size`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute, and parsing that attribute's value using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers) doesn't generate an error, then: if the parsed value is one, then the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to use the attribute as a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) setting the element's ['border-bottom-width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-bottom-width) to 0; otherwise, if the parsed value is greater than one, then the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to use the parsed value minus two as a pixel length for [presentational hints](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) for the ['height'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-height-property) property on the element.

The [`width`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute on an [`hr`](#442-the-hr-element) element [maps to the dimension property](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) ['width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-width-property) on the element.

When an [`hr`](#442-the-hr-element) element has a [`color`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute, its value is [expected](#15-rendering) to be parsed using the [rules for parsing a legacy color value](#236-legacy-colors), and if that does not return failure, the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) setting the element's ['color'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#the-color-property) property to the resulting color.

#### 15.3.12 The [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) and [`legend`](#41016-the-legend-element) elements

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

fieldset {
  display: block;
  margin-inline: 2px;
  border: groove 2px ThreeDFace;
  padding-block: 0.35em 0.625em;
  padding-inline: 0.75em;
  min-inline-size: min-content;
}

legend {
  padding-inline: 2px;
}

legend[align=left i] {
  justify-self: left;
}

legend[align=center i] {
  justify-self: center;
}

legend[align=right i] {
  justify-self: right;
}
```

The [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element, when it generates a [CSS box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#css-box), is [expected](#15-rendering) to act as follows:
- The element is [expected](#15-rendering) to establish a new [block formatting context](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#block-formatting-context).
- The ['display'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop) property is [expected](#15-rendering) to act as follows:
  - If the computed value of ['display'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop) is a value such that the [outer display type](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#outer-display-type) is 'inline', then behave as 'inline-block'.
  - Otherwise, behave as 'flow-root'.

  > [!note]
  > This does not change the computed value.

- If the element's box has a child box that matches the conditions in the list below, then the first such child box is the 'fieldset' element's rendered legend:
  - The child is a [`legend`](#41016-the-legend-element) element.
  - The child's used value of ['float'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#float-position) is 'none'.
  - The child's used value of ['position'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position/#position-property) is not 'absolute' or 'fixed'.
- If the element has a [rendered legend](#15312-the-fieldset-and-legend-elements), then the border is [expected](#15-rendering) to not be painted behind the rectangle defined as follows, using the writing mode of the fieldset:
  1. The block-start edge of the rectangle is the smaller of the block-start edge of the [rendered legend](#15312-the-fieldset-and-legend-elements)'s margin rectangle at its static position (ignoring transforms), and the block-start outer edge of the [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element)'s border.
  2. The block-end edge of the rectangle is the larger of the block-end edge of the [rendered legend](#15312-the-fieldset-and-legend-elements)'s margin rectangle at its static position (ignoring transforms), and the block-end outer edge of the [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element)'s border.
  3. The inline-start edge of the rectangle is the smaller of the inline-start edge of the [rendered legend](#15312-the-fieldset-and-legend-elements)'s border rectangle at its static position (ignoring transforms), and the inline-start outer edge of the [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element)'s border.
  4. The inline-end edge of the rectangle is the larger of the inline-end edge of the [rendered legend](#15312-the-fieldset-and-legend-elements)'s border rectangle at its static position (ignoring transforms), and the inline-end outer edge of the [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element)'s border.
- The space allocated for the element's border on the block-start side is [expected](#15-rendering) to be the element's ['border-block-start-width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-border-block-start-width) or the [rendered legend](#15312-the-fieldset-and-legend-elements)'s margin box size in the [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element)'s block-flow direction, whichever is greater.
- For the purpose of calculating the used ['block-size'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-block-size), if the computed ['block-size'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-block-size) is not 'auto', the space allocated for the [rendered legend](#15312-the-fieldset-and-legend-elements)'s margin box that spills out past the border, if any, is [expected](#15-rendering) to be subtracted from the ['block-size'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-block-size). If the content box's block-size would be negative, then let the content box's block-size be 0 instead.
- If the element has a [rendered legend](#15312-the-fieldset-and-legend-elements), then that element is [expected](#15-rendering) to be the first child box.
- The [anonymous fieldset content box](#15312-the-fieldset-and-legend-elements) is [expected](#15-rendering) to appear after the [rendered legend](#15312-the-fieldset-and-legend-elements) and is [expected](#15-rendering) to contain the content (including the '::before' and '::after' pseudo-elements) of the [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element except for the [rendered legend](#15312-the-fieldset-and-legend-elements), if there is one.
- The used value of the ['padding-top'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-padding-top), ['padding-right'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-padding-right), ['padding-bottom'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-padding-bottom), and ['padding-left'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-padding-left) properties are [expected](#15-rendering) to be zero.
- For the purpose of calculating the min-content inline size, use the greater of the min-content inline size of the [rendered legend](#15312-the-fieldset-and-legend-elements) and the min-content inline size of the [anonymous fieldset content box](#15312-the-fieldset-and-legend-elements).
- For the purpose of calculating the max-content inline size, use the greater of the max-content inline size of the [rendered legend](#15312-the-fieldset-and-legend-elements) and the max-content inline size of the [anonymous fieldset content box](#15312-the-fieldset-and-legend-elements).

A [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element's [rendered legend](#15312-the-fieldset-and-legend-elements), if any, is [expected](#15-rendering) to act as follows:
- The element is [expected](#15-rendering) to establish a new [formatting context](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#formatting-context) for its contents. The type of this [formatting context](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#formatting-context) is determined by its ['display'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop) value, as usual.
- The ['display'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop) property is [expected](#15-rendering) to behave as if its computed value was blockified.

  > [!note]
  > This does not change the computed value.

- If the [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of ['inline-size'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-inline-size) is 'auto', then the [used value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#used-value) is the [fit-content inline size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#fit-content-inline-size).
- The element is [expected](#15-rendering) to be positioned in the inline direction as is normal for blocks (e.g., taking into account margins and the ['justify-self'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-align/#propdef-justify-self) property).
- The element's box is [expected](#15-rendering) to be constrained in the inline direction by the inline content size of the [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) as if it had used its computed inline padding.

  > [!example]
  > For example, if the [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) has a specified padding of 50px, then the [rendered legend](#15312-the-fieldset-and-legend-elements) will be positioned 50px in from the [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element)'s border. The padding will further apply to the [anonymous fieldset content box](#15312-the-fieldset-and-legend-elements) instead of the [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element itself.

- The element is [expected](#15-rendering) to be positioned in the block-flow direction such that its border box is centered over the border on the block-start side of the [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element.

A [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element's anonymous fieldset content box is [expected](#15-rendering) to act as follows:
- The ['display'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop) property is [expected](#15-rendering) to act as follows:
  - If the computed value of ['display'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop) on the [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element is 'grid' or 'inline-grid', then set the used value to 'grid'.
  - If the computed value of ['display'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop) on the [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element is 'flex' or 'inline-flex', then set the used value to 'flex'.
  - Otherwise, set the used value to 'flow-root'.
- The following properties are [expected](#15-rendering) to inherit from the [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element:
  - ['align-content'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-align/#propdef-align-content)
  - ['align-items'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-align/#propdef-align-items)
  - ['border-radius'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-radius)
  - ['column-count'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-multicol/#propdef-column-count)
  - ['column-fill'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-multicol/#propdef-column-fill)
  - ['column-width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-multicol/#propdef-column-width)
  - ['flex-direction'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-flexbox/#propdef-flex-direction)
  - ['flex-wrap'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-flexbox/#propdef-flex-wrap)
  - ['gap'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-gaps/#propdef-gap)
  - ['grid-auto-columns'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid/#propdef-grid-auto-columns)
  - ['grid-auto-flow'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid/#propdef-grid-auto-flow)
  - ['grid-auto-rows'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid/#propdef-grid-auto-rows)
  - ['grid-template-areas'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid/#propdef-grid-template-areas)
  - ['grid-template-columns'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid/#propdef-grid-template-columns)
  - ['grid-template-rows'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-grid/#propdef-grid-template-rows)
  - ['justify-content'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-align/#propdef-justify-content)
  - ['justify-items'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-align/#propdef-justify-items)
  - ['overflow'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-overflow/#propdef-overflow)
  - ['padding-bottom'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-padding-bottom)
  - ['padding-left'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-padding-left)
  - ['padding-right'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-padding-right)
  - ['padding-top'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-padding-top)
  - ['rule'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-gaps/#propdef-rule)
  - ['rule-break'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-gaps/#propdef-rule-break)
  - ['rule-inset'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-gaps/#propdef-rule-inset)
  - ['rule-overlap'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-gaps/#propdef-rule-overlap)
  - ['rule-visibility-items'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-gaps/#propdef-rule-visibility-items)
  - ['text-overflow'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-overflow/#propdef-text-overflow)
  - ['unicode-bidi'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#unicode-bidi)
- The ['block-size'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-block-size) property is [expected](#15-rendering) to be set to '100%'.
- For the purpose of calculating percentage padding, act as if the padding was calculated for the [`fieldset`](#41015-the-fieldset-element) element.

> [!note]
> The legend is rendered over the top border, and the top border area reserves vertical space for the legend. The fieldset's top margin starts at the top margin edge of the legend. The legend's horizontal margins, or the ['justify-self'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-align/#propdef-justify-self) property, gives its horizontal position. The [anonymous fieldset content box](#15312-the-fieldset-and-legend-elements) appears below the legend.

### 15.4 Replaced elements

> [!note]
> The following elements can be [replaced elements](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#replaced-element): [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element), [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element), [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element), [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element), [`img`](#483-the-img-element), [`input`](#4105-the-input-element), [`object`](#487-the-object-element), and [`video`](#488-the-video-element).

#### 15.4.1 Embedded content

The [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element), [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element), and [`video`](#488-the-video-element) elements are [expected](#15-rendering) to be treated as [replaced elements](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#replaced-element).

A [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) element that [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) [embedded content](#32526-embedded-content) is [expected](#15-rendering) to be treated as a [replaced element](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#replaced-element); the contents of such elements are the element's bitmap, if any, or else a [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black) bitmap with the same [natural dimensions](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions) as the element. Other [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) elements are [expected](#15-rendering) to be treated as ordinary elements in the rendering model.

An [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element that [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) an image, plugin, or its [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables) is [expected](#15-rendering) to be treated as a [replaced element](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#replaced-element). Other [`object`](#487-the-object-element) elements are [expected](#15-rendering) to be treated as ordinary elements in the rendering model.

The [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) element, when it is [exposing a user interface](#481113-user-interface), is [expected](#15-rendering) to be treated as a [replaced element](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#replaced-element) about one line high, as wide as is necessary to expose the user agent's user interface features. When an [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) element is not [exposing a user interface](#481113-user-interface), the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to force its ['display'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop) property to compute to 'none', irrespective of CSS rules.

Whether a [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element is [exposing a user interface](#481113-user-interface) is not [expected](#15-rendering) to affect the size of the rendering; controls are [expected](#15-rendering) to be overlaid above the page content without causing any layout changes, and are [expected](#15-rendering) to disappear when the user does not need them.

When a [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element represents a poster frame or frame of video, the poster frame or frame of video is [expected](#15-rendering) to be rendered at the largest size that maintains the aspect ratio of that poster frame or frame of video without being taller or wider than the [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element itself, and is [expected](#15-rendering) to be centered in the [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element.

Any subtitles or captions are [expected](#15-rendering) to be overlaid directly on top of their [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element, as defined by the relevant rendering rules; for WebVTT, those are the [rules for updating the display of WebVTT text tracks](https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#rules-for-updating-the-display-of-webvtt-text-tracks). [\[WEBVTT\]](#references)

When the user agent starts [exposing a user interface](#481113-user-interface) for a [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element, the user agent should run the [rules for updating the text track rendering](#4811111-text-track-model) of each of the [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) in the [`video`](#488-the-video-element) element's [list of text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) that are [showing](#4811111-text-track-model) and whose [text track kind](#4811111-text-track-model) is one of [`subtitles`](#4811111-text-track-model) or [`captions`](#4811111-text-track-model) (e.g., for [text tracks](#4811111-text-track-model) based on WebVTT, the [rules for updating the display of WebVTT text tracks](https://w3c.github.io/webvtt/#rules-for-updating-the-display-of-webvtt-text-tracks)). [\[WEBVTT\]](#references)

> [!note]
> Resizing [`video`](#488-the-video-element) and [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) elements does not interrupt video playback or clear the canvas.

---

The following CSS rules are [expected](#15-rendering) to apply:

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

iframe { border: 2px inset; }
video { object-fit: contain; }
```

#### 15.4.2 Images

User agents are [expected](#15-rendering) to render [`img`](#483-the-img-element) elements and [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attributes are in the [Image Button](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) state, according to the first applicable rules from the following list:

If the element [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) an image

The user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to treat the element as a [replaced element](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#replaced-element) and render the image according to the rules for doing so defined in CSS.

If the element does not [represent](#322-elements-in-the-dom) an image and either:
- the user agent has reason to believe that the image will become *[available](#4843-processing-model)* and be rendered in due course, or
- the element has no `alt` attribute, or
- the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is in [quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), and the element already has [natural dimensions](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions) (e.g., from the [dimension attributes](#4817-dimension-attributes) or CSS rules)

The user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to treat the element as a [replaced element](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#replaced-element) whose content is the text that the element represents, if any, optionally alongside an icon indicating that the image is being obtained (if applicable). For [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements, the element is [expected](#15-rendering) to appear button-like to indicate that the element is a [button](#4102-categories).

If the element is an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element that [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) some text and the user agent does not expect this to change

The user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to treat the element as a non-replaced phrasing element whose content is the text, optionally with an icon indicating that an image is missing, so that the user can request the image be displayed or investigate why it is not rendering. In non-graphical contexts, such an icon should be omitted.

If the element is an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element that [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) nothing and the user agent does not expect this to change

The user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to treat the element as a [replaced element](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#replaced-element) whose [natural dimensions](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions) are 0. (In the absence of further styles, this will cause the element to essentially not be rendered.)

If the element is an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element that does not [represent](#322-elements-in-the-dom) an image and the user agent does not expect this to change

The user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to treat the element as a [replaced element](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#replaced-element) consisting of a button whose content is the element's alternative text. The [natural dimensions](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-dimensions) of the button are [expected](#15-rendering) to be about one line in height and whatever width is necessary to render the text on one line.

The icons mentioned above are [expected](#15-rendering) to be relatively small so as not to disrupt most text but be easily clickable. In a visual environment, for instance, icons could be 16 pixels by 16 pixels square, or 1em by 1em if the images are scalable. In an audio environment, the icon could be a short bleep. The icons are intended to indicate to the user that they can be used to get to whatever options the UA provides for images, and, where appropriate, are [expected](#15-rendering) to provide access to the context menu that would have come up if the user interacted with the actual image.

---

All animated images with the same [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute) and the same image data are [expected](#15-rendering) to be rendered synchronized to the same timeline as a group, with the timeline starting at the time of the least recent addition to the group.

> [!note]
> In other words, when a second image with the same [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute) and animated image data is inserted into a document, it jumps to the point in the animation cycle that is currently being displayed by the first image.

When a user agent is to restart the animation for an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element showing an animated image, all animated images with the same [absolute URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#syntax-url-absolute) and the same image data in that [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node) are [expected](#15-rendering) to restart their animation from the beginning.

---

The following CSS rules are [expected](#15-rendering) to apply:

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

img:is([sizes="auto" i], [sizes^="auto," i]) {
  contain: size !important;
  contain-intrinsic-size: 300px 150px;
}
```

The following CSS rules are [expected](#15-rendering) to apply when the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is in [quirks mode](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document):

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

img[align=left i] { margin-right: 3px; }
img[align=right i] { margin-left: 3px; }
```

#### 15.4.3 Attributes for embedded content and images

The following CSS rules are [expected](#15-rendering) to apply as [presentational hints](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints):

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

embed[align=left i], iframe[align=left i], img[align=left i],
input[type=image i][align=left i], object[align=left i] {
  float: left;
}

embed[align=right i], iframe[align=right i], img[align=right i],
input[type=image i][align=right i], object[align=right i] {
  float: right;
}

embed[align=top i], iframe[align=top i], img[align=top i],
input[type=image i][align=top i], object[align=top i] {
  vertical-align: top;
}

embed[align=baseline i], iframe[align=baseline i], img[align=baseline i],
input[type=image i][align=baseline i], object[align=baseline i] {
  vertical-align: baseline;
}

embed[align=texttop i], iframe[align=texttop i], img[align=texttop i],
input[type=image i][align=texttop i], object[align=texttop i] {
  vertical-align: text-top;
}

embed[align=absmiddle i], iframe[align=absmiddle i], img[align=absmiddle i],
input[type=image i][align=absmiddle i], object[align=absmiddle i],
embed[align=abscenter i], iframe[align=abscenter i], img[align=abscenter i],
input[type=image i][align=abscenter i], object[align=abscenter i] {
  vertical-align: middle;
}

embed[align=bottom i], iframe[align=bottom i], img[align=bottom i],
input[type=image i][align=bottom i], object[align=bottom i] {
  vertical-align: bottom;
}
```

When an [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element), [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element), [`img`](#483-the-img-element), or [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element, or an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Image Button](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) state, has an `align` attribute whose value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`center`" or the string "`middle`", the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to act as if the element's ['vertical-align'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#propdef-vertical-align) property was set to a value that aligns the vertical middle of the element with the parent element's baseline.

The `hspace` attribute of [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element), [`img`](#483-the-img-element), or [`object`](#487-the-object-element) elements, and [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements with a [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute in the [Image Button](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) state, [maps to the dimension properties](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) ['margin-left'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-margin-left) and ['margin-right'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-margin-right) on the element.

The `vspace` attribute of [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element), [`img`](#483-the-img-element), or [`object`](#487-the-object-element) elements, and [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements with a [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute in the [Image Button](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) state, [maps to the dimension properties](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) ['margin-top'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-margin-top) and ['margin-bottom'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-margin-bottom) on the element.

When an [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) element has a [`frameborder`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute whose value, when parsed using the [rules for parsing integers](#2341-signed-integers), is zero or an error, the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to have [presentational hints](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) setting the element's ['border-top-width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-top-width), ['border-right-width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-right-width), ['border-bottom-width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-bottom-width), and ['border-left-width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-left-width) properties to zero.

When an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element, [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element, or [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element with a [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute in the [Image Button](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) state has a `border` attribute whose value, when parsed using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers), is found to be a number greater than zero, the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to use the parsed value for eight [presentational hints](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints): four setting the parsed value as a pixel length for the element's ['border-top-width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-top-width), ['border-right-width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-right-width), ['border-bottom-width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-bottom-width), and ['border-left-width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-left-width) properties, and four setting the element's ['border-top-style'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-top-style), ['border-right-style'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-right-style), ['border-bottom-style'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-bottom-style), and ['border-left-style'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-border-left-style) properties to the value 'solid'.

The [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes) and [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes) attributes on an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element's [dimension attribute source](#483-the-img-element) [map to the dimension properties](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) ['width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-width-property) and ['height'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-height-property) on the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element respectively. They similarly [map to the aspect-ratio property (using dimension rules)](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) of the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element.

The [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes) and [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes) attributes on [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element), [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element), [`object`](#487-the-object-element), and [`video`](#488-the-video-element) elements, and [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements with a [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute in the [Image Button](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) state and that either represents an image or that the user expects will eventually represent an image, [map to the dimension properties](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) ['width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-width-property) and ['height'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-height-property) on the element respectively.

The [`width`](#4817-dimension-attributes) and [`height`](#4817-dimension-attributes) attributes [map to the aspect-ratio property (using dimension rules)](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) on [`img`](#483-the-img-element) and [`video`](#488-the-video-element) elements, and [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements with a [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute in the [Image Button](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) state.

The [`width`](#4125-the-canvas-element) and [`height`](#4125-the-canvas-element) attributes [map to the aspect-ratio property](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) on [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) elements.

#### 15.4.4 Image maps

Shapes on an [image map](#48141-authoring) are [expected](#15-rendering) to act, for the purpose of the CSS cascade, as elements independent of the original [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element that happen to match the same style rules but inherit from the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) or [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element.

For the purposes of the rendering, only the ['cursor'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#cursor) property is [expected](#15-rendering) to have any effect on the shape.

> [!example]
> Thus, for example, if an [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element has a [`style`](#3265-the-style-attribute) attribute that sets the ['cursor'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#cursor) property to 'help', then when the user designates that shape, the cursor would change to a Help cursor.

> [!example]
> Similarly, if an [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element had a CSS rule that set its ['cursor'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#cursor) property to 'inherit' (or if no rule setting the ['cursor'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#cursor) property matched the element at all), the shape's cursor would be inherited from the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) or [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element of the [image map](#48141-authoring), not from the parent of the [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) element.

### 15.5 Widgets

#### 15.5.1 Native appearance

The CSS Basic User Interface specification calls elements that can have a [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance) [widgets](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#widget), and defines whether to use that [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance) depending on the ['appearance'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#appearance-switching) property. That logic, in turn, depends on whether each the element is classified as a [devolvable widget](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable) or [non-devolvable widget](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#non-devolvable). This section defines which elements match these concepts for HTML, what their [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance) is, and any particularity of their [devolved](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolved) state or [primitive appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance). [\[CSSUI\]](#references)

The following elements can have a [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance) for the purpose of the CSS ['appearance'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#appearance-switching) property.
- [`button`](#4106-the-button-element)
- [`input`](#4105-the-input-element)
- [`meter`](#41014-the-meter-element)
- [`progress`](#41013-the-progress-element)
- [`select`](#4107-the-select-element)
- [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element)

#### 15.5.2 Writing mode

Several widgets have their rendering controlled by the ['writing-mode'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#propdef-writing-mode) CSS property. For the purposes of those widgets, we have the following definitions.

A horizontal writing mode is when resolving the ['writing-mode'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#propdef-writing-mode) property of the control results in a computed value of 'horizontal-tb'.

A vertical writing mode is when resolving the ['writing-mode'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#propdef-writing-mode) property of the control results in a computed value of either 'vertical-rl', 'vertical-lr', 'sideways-rl' or 'sideways-lr'.

#### 15.5.3 Button layout

When an element uses [button layout](#1553-button-layout), it is a [devolvable widget](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable), and its [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance) is that of a button.

Button layout is as follows:
- If the element is a [`button`](#4106-the-button-element) element, then the ['display'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop) property is [expected](#15-rendering) to act as follows:
  - If the computed value of ['display'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop) is 'inline-grid', 'grid', 'inline-flex', 'flex', 'none', or 'contents', then behave as the computed value.
  - Otherwise, if the computed value of ['display'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop) is a value such that the [outer display type](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#outer-display-type) is 'inline', then behave as 'inline-block'.
  - Otherwise, behave as 'flow-root'.
- The element is [expected](#15-rendering) to establish a new [formatting context](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#formatting-context) for its contents. The type of this formatting context is determined by its ['display'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#display-prop) value, as usual.
- If the element is [absolutely-positioned](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position/#absolute-position), then for the purpose of the [CSS visual formatting model](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#visuren), act as if the element is a [replaced element](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#replaced-element). [\[CSS\]](#references)
- If the [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of ['inline-size'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-inline-size) is 'auto', then the [used value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#used-value) is the [fit-content inline size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#fit-content-inline-size).
- For the purpose of the 'normal' keyword of the ['align-self'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-align/#propdef-align-self) property, act as if the element is a replaced element.

> [!warning]
> Need to define the [primitive appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance).

#### 15.5.4 The [`button`](#4106-the-button-element) element

The [`button`](#4106-the-button-element) element, when it generates a [CSS box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#css-box), is [expected](#15-rendering) to depict a button and to use [button layout](#1553-button-layout).

#### 15.5.5 The [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) and [`summary`](#4112-the-summary-element) elements

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

details, summary {
  display: block;
}
details > summary:first-of-type {
  display: list-item;
  counter-increment: list-item 0;
  list-style: disclosure-closed inside;
}
details[open] > summary:first-of-type {
  list-style-type: disclosure-open;
}
```

The [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element is [expected](#15-rendering) to have an internal [shadow tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree) with three child elements:
1. The first child element is a [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element) that is [expected](#15-rendering) to take the [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element's first [`summary`](#4112-the-summary-element) element child, if any. This element has a single child [`summary`](#4112-the-summary-element) element called the default summary which has text content that is [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) (and probably locale-specific).

   The [`summary`](#4112-the-summary-element) element that this slot [represents](#322-elements-in-the-dom) is [expected](#15-rendering) to allow the user to request the details be shown or hidden.

2. The second child element is a [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element) that is [expected](#15-rendering) to take the [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element's remaining descendants, if any. This element has no contents.

   This element is [expected](#15-rendering) to match the ['::details-content'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-pseudo/#details-content-pseudo) pseudo-element.

   This element is [expected](#15-rendering) to have its [`style`](#3265-the-style-attribute) attribute set to "`display: block; content-visibility: hidden;`" when the [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element does not have an [`open`](#4111-the-details-element) attribute. When it does have the [`open`](#4111-the-details-element) attribute, the [`style`](#3265-the-style-attribute) attribute is [expected](#15-rendering) to be set to "`display: block;`".

   > [!note]
   > Because the slots are hidden inside a shadow tree, this [`style`](#3265-the-style-attribute) attribute is not directly visible to author code. Its impacts, however, are visible. Notably, the choice of `content-visibility: hidden` instead of, e.g., `display: none`, impacts the results of various APIs that query layout information.

3. The third child element is either a [`link`](#424-the-link-element) or [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element with the following styles for the [default summary](#1555-the-details-and-summary-elements):

   ```css
   :host summary {
     display: list-item;
     counter-increment: list-item 0;
     list-style: disclosure-closed inside;
   }
   :host([open]) summary {
     list-style-type: disclosure-open;
   }
   ```

   > [!note]
   > The position of this child element relative to the other two is not observable. This means that implementations might have it in a different order relative to its siblings. Implementations might even associate the style with the shadow tree using a mechanism that is not an element.

> [!note]
> The structure of this shadow tree is observable through the ways that the children of the [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) element and the ['::details-content'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-pseudo/#details-content-pseudo) pseudo-element respond to CSS styles.

#### 15.5.6 The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element as a text entry widget

An [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Text](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch), [Telephone](#410513-telephone-state-typetel), [URL](#410514-url-state-typeurl), or [Email](#410515-email-state-typeemail) state, is a [devolvable widget](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable). Its [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance) is [expected](#15-rendering) to render as an ['inline-block'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block) box depicting a one-line text control.

An [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Search](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch) state is a [devolvable widget](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable). Its [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance) is [expected](#15-rendering) to render as an ['inline-block'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block) box depicting a one-line text control. If the [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of the element's ['appearance'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#appearance-switching) property is not [`'textfield'`](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#valdef-appearance-textfield), it may have a distinct style indicating that it is a search field.

An [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Password](#410516-password-state-typepassword) state is a [devolvable widget](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable). Its [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance) is [expected](#15-rendering) to render as an ['inline-block'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block) box depicting a one-line text control that obscures data entry.

For [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in one of the above states, the [used value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#used-value) of the ['line-height'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#propdef-line-height) property must be a length value that is no smaller than what the [used value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#used-value) would be for 'line-height: normal'.

> [!note]
> The [used value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#used-value) will not be the actual keyword 'normal'. Also, this rule does not affect the [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value).

If these text controls provide a text selection, then, when the user changes the current selection, the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [user interaction task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`select`](#events) at the element, with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true.

An [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in one of the above states is an [element with default preferred size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-forms/#element-with-default-preferred-size), and user agents are [expected](#15-rendering) to apply the ['field-sizing'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#field-sizing) CSS property to the element. User agents are [expected](#15-rendering) to determine the [inline size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#inline-size) of its [intrinsic size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#intrinsic-size) by the following steps:
1. If the ['field-sizing'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#field-sizing) property on the element has a [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of ['content'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#valdef-field-sizing-content), the [inline size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#inline-size) is determined by the text which the element shows. The text is either a [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value) or a short hint specified by the [`placeholder`](#4105310-the-placeholder-attribute) attribute. User agents may take the text caret size into account in the [inline size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#inline-size).
2. If the element has a [`size`](#410532-the-size-attribute) attribute, and parsing that attribute's value using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers) doesn't generate an error, return the value obtained from applying the [converting a character width to pixels](#1556-the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget) algorithm to the value of the attribute.
3. Otherwise, return the value obtained from applying the [converting a character width to pixels](#1556-the-input-element-as-a-text-entry-widget) algorithm to the number 20.

The converting a character width to pixels algorithm returns (size-1)×avg + max, where size is the character width to convert, avg is the average character width of the primary font for the element for which the algorithm is being run, in pixels, and max is the maximum character width of that same font, also in pixels. (The element's ['letter-spacing'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#letter-spacing-property) property does not affect the result.)

These text controls are [expected](#15-rendering) to be [scroll containers](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-overflow/#scroll-container) and support scrolling in the [inline axis](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#inline-axis), but not the [block axis](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#block-axis).

> [!warning]
> Need to detail the [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance) and [primitive appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance).

#### 15.5.7 The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element as domain-specific widgets

An [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Date](#410517-date-state-typedate) state is a [devolvable widget](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable) [expected](#15-rendering) to render as an ['inline-block'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block) box depicting a date control.

An [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Month](#410518-month-state-typemonth) state is a [devolvable widget](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable) [expected](#15-rendering) to render as an ['inline-block'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block) box depicting a month control.

An [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Week](#410519-week-state-typeweek) state is a [devolvable widget](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable) [expected](#15-rendering) to render as an ['inline-block'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block) box depicting a week control.

An [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Time](#4105110-time-state-typetime) state is a [devolvable widget](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable) [expected](#15-rendering) to render as an ['inline-block'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block) box depicting a time control.

An [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Local Date and Time](#4105111-local-date-and-time-state-typedatetime-local) state is a [devolvable widget](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable) [expected](#15-rendering) to render as an ['inline-block'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block) box depicting a local date and time control.

An [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Number](#4105112-number-state-typenumber) state is a [devolvable widget](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable) [expected](#15-rendering) to render as an ['inline-block'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block) box depicting a number control.

An [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Number](#4105112-number-state-typenumber) state is an [element with default preferred size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-forms/#element-with-default-preferred-size), and user agents are [expected](#15-rendering) to apply the ['field-sizing'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#field-sizing) CSS property to the element. The [block size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#block-size) of the [intrinsic size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#intrinsic-size) is about one line high. If the ['field-sizing'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#field-sizing) property on the element has a [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of ['content'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#valdef-field-sizing-content), the [inline size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#inline-size) of the [intrinsic size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#intrinsic-size) is [expected](#15-rendering) to be about as wide as necessary to show the current [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value). Otherwise, the [inline size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#inline-size) of the [intrinsic size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#intrinsic-size) is [expected](#15-rendering) to be about as wide as necessary to show the widest possible value.

An [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Date](#410517-date-state-typedate), [Month](#410518-month-state-typemonth), [Week](#410519-week-state-typeweek), [Time](#4105110-time-state-typetime), or [Local Date and Time](#4105111-local-date-and-time-state-typedatetime-local) state, is [expected](#15-rendering) to be about one line high, and about as wide as necessary to show the widest possible value.

> [!warning]
> Need to detail the [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance) and [primitive appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance).

#### 15.5.8 The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element as a range control

An [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Range](#4105113-range-state-typerange) state is a [non-devolvable widget](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#non-devolvable). Its [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance) is [expected](#15-rendering) to render as an ['inline-block'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block) box depicting a slider control.

When this control has a [horizontal writing mode](#1552-writing-mode), the control is [expected](#15-rendering) to be a horizontal slider. Its lowest value is on the right if the ['direction'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#direction) property has a [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of 'rtl', and on the left otherwise. When this control has a [vertical writing mode](#1552-writing-mode), it is [expected](#15-rendering) to be a vertical slider. Its lowest value is on the bottom if the ['direction'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#direction) property has a [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of 'rtl', and on the top otherwise.

Predefined suggested values (provided by the [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute) attribute) are [expected](#15-rendering) to be shown as tick marks on the slider, which the slider can snap to.

> [!warning]
> Need to detail the [primitive appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance).

#### 15.5.9 The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element as a color well

An [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Color](#4105114-color-state-typecolor) state is [expected](#15-rendering) to depict a color well, which, when activated, provides the user with a color picker (e.g. a color wheel or color palette) from which the color can be changed. The element, when it generates a [CSS box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#css-box), is [expected](#15-rendering) to use [button layout](#1553-button-layout), that has a single [block-level](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#block-level) [block container](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#block-container) child box, which is [expected](#15-rendering) to have a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) setting the ['background-color'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-background-color) property to the element's [value](#410181-a-form-controls-value).

Predefined suggested values (provided by the [`list`](#410539-the-list-attribute) attribute) are [expected](#15-rendering) to be shown in the color picker interface, not on the color well itself.

> [!warning]
> Need to detail the [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance) and [primitive appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance).

#### 15.5.10 The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element as a checkbox and radio button widgets

An [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Checkbox](#4105115-checkbox-state-typecheckbox) state is a [non-devolvable widget](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#non-devolvable) [expected](#15-rendering) to render as an ['inline-block'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block) box containing a single checkbox control, with no label.

> [!warning]
> Need to detail the [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance) and [primitive appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance).

An [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Radio Button](#4105116-radio-button-state-typeradio) state is a [non-devolvable widget](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#non-devolvable) [expected](#15-rendering) to render as an ['inline-block'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block) box containing a single radio button control, with no label.

> [!warning]
> Need to detail the [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance) and [primitive appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance).

#### 15.5.11 The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element as a file upload control

An [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [File Upload](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) state, when it generates a [CSS box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#css-box), is [expected](#15-rendering) to render as an ['inline-block'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block) box containing a span of text giving the filename(s) of the [selected files](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile), if any, followed by a button that, when activated, provides the user with a file picker from which the selection can be changed. The button is [expected](#15-rendering) to use [button layout](#1553-button-layout) and match the ['::file-selector-button'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-pseudo/#file-selector-button-pseudo) pseudo-element. Its contents are [expected](#15-rendering) to be [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) (and possibly locale-specific) text, for example "Choose file".

User agents may handle an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [File Upload](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) state as an [element with default preferred size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-forms/#element-with-default-preferred-size), and user agents may apply the ['field-sizing'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#field-sizing) CSS property to the element. If the ['field-sizing'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#field-sizing) property on the element has a [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of ['content'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#valdef-field-sizing-content), the [intrinsic size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#intrinsic-size) of the element is [expected](#15-rendering) to depend on its content such as the ['::file-selector-button'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-pseudo/#file-selector-button-pseudo) pseudo-element and chosen file names.

#### 15.5.12 The [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element as a button

An [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Submit Button](#4105118-submit-button-state-typesubmit), [Reset Button](#4105120-reset-button-state-typereset), or [Button](#4105121-button-state-typebutton) state, when it generates a [CSS box](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#css-box), is [expected](#15-rendering) to depict a button and use [button layout](#1553-button-layout) and its contents are [expected](#15-rendering) to be the text of the element's [`value`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute, if any, or text derived from the element's [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute in an [implementation-defined](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#23-terminology) (and probably locale-specific) fashion, if not.

#### 15.5.13 The [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element) element

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

marquee {
  display: inline-block;
  text-align: initial;
  overflow: hidden !important;
}
```

The [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element) element, while [turned on](#1631-the-marquee-element), is [expected](#15-rendering) to render in an animated fashion according to its attributes as follows:

If the element's [`behavior`](#1631-the-marquee-element) attribute is in the [scroll](#1631-the-marquee-element) state

Slide the contents of the element in the direction described by the [`direction`](#1631-the-marquee-element) attribute as defined below, such that it begins off the start side of the [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element), and ends flush with the inner end side.

> [!example]
> For example, if the [`direction`](#1631-the-marquee-element) attribute is [left](#1631-the-marquee-element) (the default), then the contents would start such that their left edge are off the side of the right edge of the [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element)'s [content area](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#content-area), and the contents would then slide up to the point where the left edge of the contents are flush with the left inner edge of the [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element)'s [content area](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#content-area).

Once the animation has ended, the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to [increment the marquee current loop index](#1631-the-marquee-element). If the element is still [turned on](#1631-the-marquee-element) after this, then the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to restart the animation.

If the element's [`behavior`](#1631-the-marquee-element) attribute is in the [slide](#1631-the-marquee-element) state

Slide the contents of the element in the direction described by the [`direction`](#1631-the-marquee-element) attribute as defined below, such that it begins off the start side of the [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element), and ends off the end side of the [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element).

> [!example]
> For example, if the [`direction`](#1631-the-marquee-element) attribute is [left](#1631-the-marquee-element) (the default), then the contents would start such that their left edge are off the side of the right edge of the [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element)'s [content area](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#content-area), and the contents would then slide up to the point where the *right* edge of the contents are flush with the left inner edge of the [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element)'s [content area](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#content-area).

Once the animation has ended, the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to [increment the marquee current loop index](#1631-the-marquee-element). If the element is still [turned on](#1631-the-marquee-element) after this, then the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to restart the animation.

If the element's [`behavior`](#1631-the-marquee-element) attribute is in the [alternate](#1631-the-marquee-element) state

When the [marquee current loop index](#1631-the-marquee-element) is even (or zero), slide the contents of the element in the direction described by the [`direction`](#1631-the-marquee-element) attribute as defined below, such that it begins flush with the start side of the [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element), and ends flush with the end side of the [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element).

When the [marquee current loop index](#1631-the-marquee-element) is odd, slide the contents of the element in the opposite direction than that described by the [`direction`](#1631-the-marquee-element) attribute as defined below, such that it begins flush with the end side of the [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element), and ends flush with the start side of the [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element).

> [!example]
> For example, if the [`direction`](#1631-the-marquee-element) attribute is [left](#1631-the-marquee-element) (the default), then the contents would with their right edge flush with the right inner edge of the [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element)'s [content area](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#content-area), and the contents would then slide up to the point where the *left* edge of the contents are flush with the left inner edge of the [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element)'s [content area](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#content-area).

Once the animation has ended, the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to [increment the marquee current loop index](#1631-the-marquee-element). If the element is still [turned on](#1631-the-marquee-element) after this, then the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to continue the animation.

The [`direction`](#1631-the-marquee-element) attribute has the meanings described in the following table:

| [`direction`](#1631-the-marquee-element) attribute state | Direction of animation | Start edge | End edge | Opposite direction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [left](#1631-the-marquee-element) | ← Right to left | Right | Left | → Left to Right |
| [right](#1631-the-marquee-element) | → Left to Right | Left | Right | ← Right to left |
| [up](#1631-the-marquee-element) | ↑ Up (Bottom to Top) | Bottom | Top | ↓ Down (Top to Bottom) |
| [down](#1631-the-marquee-element) | ↓ Down (Top to Bottom) | Top | Bottom | ↑ Up (Bottom to Top) |

In any case, the animation should proceed such that there is a delay given by the [marquee scroll interval](#1631-the-marquee-element) between each frame, and such that the content moves at most the distance given by the [marquee scroll distance](#1631-the-marquee-element) with each frame.

When a [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element) element has a `bgcolor` attribute set, the value is [expected](#15-rendering) to be parsed using the [rules for parsing a legacy color value](#236-legacy-colors), and if that does not return failure, the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) setting the element's ['background-color'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-background-color) property to the resulting color.

The `width` and `height` attributes on a [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element) element [map to the dimension properties](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) ['width'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-width-property) and ['height'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#the-height-property) on the element respectively.

The [natural height](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-images/#natural-height) of a [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element) element with its [`direction`](#1631-the-marquee-element) attribute in the [up](#1631-the-marquee-element) or [down](#1631-the-marquee-element) states is 200 [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px).

The `vspace` attribute of a [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element) element [maps to the dimension properties](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) ['margin-top'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-margin-top) and ['margin-bottom'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-margin-bottom) on the element. The `hspace` attribute of a [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element) element [maps to the dimension properties](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) ['margin-left'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-margin-left) and ['margin-right'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-box/#propdef-margin-right) on the element.

#### 15.5.14 The [`meter`](#41014-the-meter-element) element

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

meter { appearance: auto; }
```

The [`meter`](#41014-the-meter-element) element is a [devolvable widget](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable). Its [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance) is [expected](#15-rendering) to render as an ['inline-block'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block) box with a ['block-size'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-block-size) of '1em' and an ['inline-size'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-inline-size) of '5em', a ['vertical-align'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#propdef-vertical-align) of '-0.2em', and with its contents depicting a gauge.

When this element has a [horizontal writing mode](#1552-writing-mode), the depiction is [expected](#15-rendering) to be of a horizontal gauge. Its minimum value is on the right if the ['direction'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#direction) property has a [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of 'rtl', and on the left otherwise. When this element has a [vertical writing mode](#1552-writing-mode), it is [expected](#15-rendering) to depict a vertical gauge. Its minimum value is on the bottom if the ['direction'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#direction) property has a [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of 'rtl', and on the top otherwise.

User agents are [expected](#15-rendering) to use a presentation consistent with platform conventions for gauges, if any.

> [!note]
> Requirements for what must be depicted in the gauge are included in the definition of the [`meter`](#41014-the-meter-element) element.

> [!warning]
> Need to detail the [primitive appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance).

#### 15.5.15 The [`progress`](#41013-the-progress-element) element

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

progress { appearance: auto; }
```

The [`progress`](#41013-the-progress-element) element is a [devolvable widget](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable). Its [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance) is [expected](#15-rendering) to render as an ['inline-block'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block) box with a ['block-size'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-block-size) of '1em' and an ['inline-size'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-logical/#propdef-inline-size) of '10em', and a ['vertical-align'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#propdef-vertical-align) of '-0.2em'.

![](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/sample-progress.png) When this element has a [horizontal writing mode](#1552-writing-mode), the element is [expected](#15-rendering) to be depicted as a horizontal progress bar. The start is on the right and the end is on the left if the ['direction'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#direction) property on this element has a [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of 'rtl', and with the start on the left and the end on the right otherwise. When this element has a [vertical writing mode](#1552-writing-mode), it is [expected](#15-rendering) to be depicted as a vertical progress bar. The start is on the bottom and the end is on the top if the ['direction'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#direction) property on this element has a [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of 'rtl', and with the start on the top and the end on the bottom otherwise.

User agents are [expected](#15-rendering) to use a presentation consistent with platform conventions for progress bars. In particular, user agents are [expected](#15-rendering) to use different presentations for determinate and indeterminate progress bars. User agents are also [expected](#15-rendering) to vary the presentation based on the dimensions of the element.

> [!note]
> Requirements for how to determine if the progress bar is determinate or indeterminate, and what progress a determinate progress bar is to show, are included in the definition of the [`progress`](#41013-the-progress-element) element.

> [!warning]
> Need to detail the [primitive appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance).

#### 15.5.16 The [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element

The [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element is an [element with default preferred size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-forms/#element-with-default-preferred-size), and user agents are [expected](#15-rendering) to apply the ['field-sizing'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#field-sizing) CSS property to [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) elements.

A [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element is either a list box or a drop-down box, depending on its attributes.

A [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element whose [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute is present is [expected](#15-rendering) to render as a multi-select [list box](#15516-the-select-element) if its [display size](#4107-the-select-element) is greater than 1. If the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element has the [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute and a [display size](#4107-the-select-element) of 1, then it may render as a multi-select [drop-down box](#15516-the-select-element) if the platform supports it; otherwise as a multi-select [list box](#15516-the-select-element).

A [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element whose [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute is absent is [expected](#15-rendering) to render as a single-select [drop-down box](#15516-the-select-element) if its [display size](#4107-the-select-element) is 1, or as a single-select [list box](#15516-the-select-element) if its [display size](#4107-the-select-element) is greater than 1.

When the element renders as a [list box](#15516-the-select-element), it is a [devolvable widget](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable) [expected](#15-rendering) to render as an ['inline-block'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block) box. The [inline size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#inline-size) of its [intrinsic size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#intrinsic-size) is the [width of the `select`'s labels](#15516-the-select-element) plus the width of a scrollbar. The [block size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#block-size) of its [intrinsic size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#intrinsic-size) is determined by the following steps:
1. If the ['field-sizing'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#field-sizing) property on the element has a [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of ['content'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#valdef-field-sizing-content), return the height necessary to contain all rows for items.
2. If the [`size`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute is absent or it has no valid value, return the height necessary to contain four rows.
3. Otherwise, return the height necessary to contain as many rows for items as given by the element's [display size](#4107-the-select-element).

A [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element which is being rendered as a [drop-down box](#15516-the-select-element) is [expected](#15-rendering) to render as an ['inline-block'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block) box. The [inline size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#inline-size) of its [intrinsic size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#intrinsic-size) is the [width of the `select`'s labels](#15516-the-select-element). If the ['field-sizing'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#field-sizing) property on the element has a [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of ['content'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#valdef-field-sizing-content), the [inline size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-writing-modes/#inline-size) of the [intrinsic size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#intrinsic-size) depends on the shown text. The shown text is typically the label of an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) of which [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) is set to true.

When the element renders as a [drop-down box](#15516-the-select-element), it is a [devolvable widget](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable). Its appearance in the devolved state, as well as its appearance when the [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of the element's ['appearance'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#appearance-switching) property is [`'menulist-button'`](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#valdef-appearance-menulist-button), is that of a drop-down box, including a "drop-down button", but not necessarily rendered using a native control of the host operating system. In such a state, CSS properties such as ['color'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#the-color-property), ['background-color'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-backgrounds/#propdef-background-color), and 'border' should not be disregarded (as is generally permissible when rendering an element according to its [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance)).

In either case ([list box](#15516-the-select-element) or [drop-down box](#15516-the-select-element)), the element's items are [expected](#15-rendering) to be the element's [list of options](#4107-the-select-element), with the element's [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element [children](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) providing headers for groups of options where applicable.

[`select`](#4107-the-select-element) elements which render as a [drop-down box](#15516-the-select-element) support a [base appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance) in addition to [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance) and [primitive appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance).

[`select`](#4107-the-select-element) elements which render as a [drop-down box](#15516-the-select-element) without the [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute or as a [list box](#15516-the-select-element) support a [base appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance) in addition to [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance) and [primitive appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance).

The [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element's [select popover](#15516-the-select-element) supports a [base appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance) and a [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance). The [select popover](#15516-the-select-element) can only be rendered with [base appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance) if its associated [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) is being rendered with [base appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance).

When a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) is being rendered as a [drop-down box](#15516-the-select-element) with [base appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance), it is [expected](#15-rendering) to render with a [shadow tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree) that contains the following elements:
1. A select button slot, which is a [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element) element. It is appended to the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element)'s [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) as the first child. It is [expected](#15-rendering) to take the first child element of the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) if the first child element is a [`button`](#4106-the-button-element).
2. A select fallback button text, which is a [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element. It is appended to the [select button slot](#15516-the-select-element).
3. A select popover, which is a [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element. It is appended to the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element)'s [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) as the second child, after the [select button slot](#15516-the-select-element). The [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element's ['::picker'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-forms/#picker-pseudo) pseudo-element is the [select popover](#15516-the-select-element) if the [provided argument](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-forms/#typedef-picker-form-control-identifier) is `select`.
4. A select popover slot, which is a [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element) element. It is appended to the [select popover](#15516-the-select-element). It is [expected](#15-rendering) to take all child nodes of the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) except for the first child [`button`](#4106-the-button-element), which is taken by the [select button slot](#15516-the-select-element).

> [!note]
> Since [base appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance) is determined by computing style, it isn't possible to swap this DOM structure when switching appearance. Implementations can always include the DOM structure for [base appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance) when the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) is rendered as a [drop-down box](#15516-the-select-element) and then choose to include or exclude it from the layout tree in order to control whether it gets rendered or not.

> [!note]
