> The [select popover](#15516-the-select-element) is only rendered when it is opted in to [base appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance) separately from the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element. Otherwise, a native picker is used.

When a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) is being rendered as a [list box](#15516-the-select-element) with [base appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance), it is expected to render with a [shadow tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree) that contains a select list box slot, which is a [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element) element. The [select list box slot](#15516-the-select-element) is appended to the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element)'s [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) as the first child. The [select list box slot](#15516-the-select-element) is expected to take all children of the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element.

The [select popover](#15516-the-select-element)'s [implicit anchor element](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-anchor-position/#implicit-anchor-element) is its associated [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element.

When a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element is being rendered with [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance) or [primitive appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance), or the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element is being rendered as a [list box](#15516-the-select-element), the ['::picker'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-forms/#picker-pseudo) pseudo-element and the ['::picker-icon'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-forms/#selectordef-picker-icon) pseudo-element do not apply.

The ['::picker'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-forms/#picker-pseudo) pseudo-element is not rendered when it has [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance) or [primitive appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance).

The ['::checkmark'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-forms/#checkmark) pseudo-element only applies to [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements which are [being rendered with base appearance](#15516-the-select-element).

An [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element has an internal [shadow tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree) with at least one [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element) element.

An [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element is rendered with base appearance if it has a [nearest ancestor `select`](#41010-the-option-element) whose [contents are being rendered with base appearance](#15516-the-select-element).

If an [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element is not being [rendered with base appearance](#15516-the-select-element), then it is [expected](#15-rendering) to be rendered by displaying the element's [label](#4109-the-optgroup-element) and children.

If an [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element is being [rendered with base appearance](#15516-the-select-element), then it is [expected](#15-rendering) to render with a [shadow tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree) that contains the following elements:
1. An optgroup legend slot, which is a [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element) element. It is appended to the [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element)'s [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) as the first child. It is [expected](#15-rendering) to take the first child element of the [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) if the first child element is a [`legend`](#41016-the-legend-element) element.
2. An optgroup label element, which is a [`div`](#4416-the-div-element) element. It is appended to the [optgroup legend slot](#15516-the-select-element). It is [expected](#15-rendering) to contain a [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node whose [data](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#410-interface-characterdata) is the result of [getting an `optgroup` element's label](#4109-the-optgroup-element) given the [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element.
3. An optgroup contents slot, which is a [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element) element. It is appended to the [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element)'s [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) after the [optgroup legend slot](#15516-the-select-element). It is [expected](#15-rendering) to take all remaining child nodes of the [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element) element.

To determine if a `select`'s contents are being rendered with base appearance, given a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element select:
1. If select is being rendered as a [list box](#15516-the-select-element) with [base appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance), then return true.
2. If select is being rendered as a [drop-down box](#15516-the-select-element) with [base appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance), and its [select popover](#15516-the-select-element) is being rendered with [base appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance), and select does not have the [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute set, then return true.
3. Return false.

An [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element has an internal [shadow tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree) with a [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element) element.

An [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element is rendered with base appearance if it has a [nearest ancestor `select`](#41010-the-option-element) and the [`select`'s contents are being rendered with base appearance](#15516-the-select-element).

If an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) does not have a [nearest ancestor `select`](#41010-the-option-element), then it is [expected](#15-rendering) to render its children.

Otherwise, if an [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element is not being [rendered with base appearance](#15516-the-select-element), then it is [expected](#15-rendering) to be rendered by displaying the result of [getting an `option` element's label](#41010-the-option-element) given the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) and true.

Otherwise, it is [expected](#15-rendering) to render with a [shadow tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#422-shadow-tree) that contains the following elements:
1. An option contents slot, which is a [`slot`](#4124-the-slot-element) element. It is appended to the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element)'s [shadow root](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#48-interface-shadowroot) as the first child. If the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element has a [`label`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute whose value is not the empty string, then the [option contents slot](#15516-the-select-element) is [expected](#15-rendering) to not take any nodes. Otherwise, it is [expected](#15-rendering) to take all child nodes of the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element.

   > [!note]
   > When the [option contents slot](#15516-the-select-element) does not take any elements, the [option label element](#15516-the-select-element) is rendered as fallback content.

2. An option label element, which is a [`span`](#4526-the-span-element) element. It is appended to the [option contents slot](#15516-the-select-element). It is [expected](#15-rendering) to contain a [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) node whose [data](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#410-interface-characterdata) is the value of the [`option`](#41010-the-option-element)'s [`label`](#41010-the-option-element) attribute.

Each sequence of one or more child [`hr`](#442-the-hr-element) element siblings may be rendered as a single separator.

The width of the `select`'s labels is the wider of the width necessary to render the widest [`optgroup`](#4109-the-optgroup-element), and the width necessary to render the widest [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) element in the element's [list of options](#4107-the-select-element) (including its indent, if any). If the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) has the [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) attribute and is being rendered as a [drop-down box](#15516-the-select-element), then the width should also be wide enough to accomodate the text rendered in the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) with any combination of [`option`](#41010-the-option-element)s selected.

> [!note]
> The [width of the `select`'s labels](#15516-the-select-element) has an accomodation for [`multiple`](#4107-the-select-element) because some implementations use special text to represent multiple options being selected, such as "2 selected." In this case, the select needs to be wide enough to render "2 selected" in addition to the individual [`option`](#41010-the-option-element)s.

If a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element contains a [placeholder label option](#4107-the-select-element), the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to render that [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) in a manner that conveys that it is a label, rather than a valid option of the control. This can include preventing the [placeholder label option](#4107-the-select-element) from being explicitly selected by the user. When the [placeholder label option](#4107-the-select-element)'s [selectedness](#41010-the-option-element) is true, the control is [expected](#15-rendering) to be displayed in a fashion that indicates that no valid option is currently selected.

User agents are [expected](#15-rendering) to render the labels in a [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) in such a manner that any alignment remains consistent whether the label is being displayed as part of the page or in a menu control.

> [!warning]
> Need to detail the [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance) and [primitive appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance).

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

option {
  display: block;
}

optgroup {
  display: block;
  font-weight: bolder;
}
```

The following styles are [expected](#15-rendering) to apply to [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) elements when they are being rendered as a [drop-down box](#15516-the-select-element):

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

select {
  align-content: center;
}
```

The following styles are [expected](#15-rendering) to apply to [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) elements when they are being rendered with [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance) or [primitive appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance):

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

select {
  letter-spacing: initial;
  word-spacing: initial;
  line-height: initial;
}
```

The following styles are [expected](#15-rendering) to apply to [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) elements when they are being rendered as a [drop-down box](#15516-the-select-element) with [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance) or [primitive appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance):

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

select {
  display: inline-block;
}
```

The following styles are [expected](#15-rendering) to apply to [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) elements when they are being rendered with [base appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance):

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

select {
  background-color: transparent;
  border: 1px solid currentColor;
  user-select: none;
  box-sizing: border-box;
}

select option:enabled:hover {
  background-color: color-mix(currentColor 10%, transparent);
}
select option:enabled:active {
  background-color: color-mix(currentColor 20%, transparent);
}
select option:disabled {
  color: color-mix(currentColor 50%, transparent);
}

select option {
  min-inline-size: 24px;
  min-block-size: max(24px, 1lh);
  padding-inline: 0.5em;
  padding-block-end: 0;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 0.5em;
  white-space: nowrap;
}

select option::checkmark {
  content: '\2713' / '';
}
select option:not(:checked)::checkmark {
  visibility: hidden;
}

select optgroup {
  display: block;
  font-weight: bolder;
}

select optgroup option {
  font-weight: normal;
}

select optgroup legend {
  padding-inline: 0.5em;
  min-block-size: 1lh;
}
```

The following styles are [expected](#15-rendering) to apply to [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) elements when they are being rendered as a [drop-down box](#15516-the-select-element) with [base appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance):

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

select {
  border-radius: 0.5em;
  padding-block: 0.25em;
  padding-inline: 0.5em;
  min-block-size: calc-size(auto, max(size, 24px, 1lh));
  min-inline-size: calc-size(auto, max(size, 24px));
  display: inline-flex;
  gap: 0.5em;
  border-radius: 0.5em;
  field-sizing: content !important;
}

select > button:first-child {
  all: unset;
  display: contents;
}

select:enabled:hover {
  background-color: color-mix(currentColor 10%, transparent);
}
select:enabled:active {
  background-color: color-mix(currentColor 20%, transparent);
}
select:disabled {
  color: color-mix(currentColor 50%, transparent);
}

::picker(select) {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  border: 1px solid;
  padding: 0;
  color: CanvasText;
  background-color: Canvas;
  margin: 0;
  inset: auto;
  min-inline-size: anchor-size(self-inline);
  max-block-size: stretch;
  overflow: auto;
  position-area: self-block-end span-self-inline-end;
  position-try-order: most-block-size;
  position-try-fallbacks:
    self-block-start span-self-inline-end,
    self-block-end span-self-inline-start,
    self-block-start span-self-inline-start;
}

select::picker-icon {
  content: counter(fake-counter-name, disclosure-open);
  display: block;
  margin-inline-start: auto;
}
```

The following styles are [expected](#15-rendering) to apply to [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) elements when they are being rendered as a [list box](#15516-the-select-element) with [base appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#base-appearance):

```css
@namespace "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml";

select {
  overflow: auto;
  display: inline-block;
  block-size: calc(max(24px, 1lh) * attr(size type(<integer>), 4));
}
```

The following styles are [expected](#15-rendering) to apply to the [optgroup label element](#15516-the-select-element):
- `padding-inline: 0.5em`
- `min-block-size: 1lh`

#### 15.5.17 The [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element

The [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element is a [devolvable widget](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#devolvable) [expected](#15-rendering) to render as an ['inline-block'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#value-def-inline-block) box depicting a multiline text control. If this multiline text control provides a selection, then, when the user changes the current selection, the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to [queue an element task](#8172-queuing-tasks) on the [user interaction task source](#8174-generic-task-sources) given the [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element to [fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`select`](#events) at the element, with the [`bubbles`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) attribute initialized to true.

The [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element is an [element with default preferred size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-forms/#element-with-default-preferred-size), and user agents are [expected](#15-rendering) to apply the ['field-sizing'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#field-sizing) CSS property to [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements.

If the ['field-sizing'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#field-sizing) property on the element has a [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of ['content'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#valdef-field-sizing-content), the [intrinsic size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#intrinsic-size) is determined from the text which the element shows. The text is either a [raw value](#41011-the-textarea-element) or a short hint specified by the [`placeholder`](#41011-the-textarea-element) attribute. User agents may take the text caret size into account in the [intrinsic size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#intrinsic-size). Otherwise, its [intrinsic size](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-sizing/#intrinsic-size) is computed from [textarea effective width](#15517-the-textarea-element) and [textarea effective height](#15517-the-textarea-element) (as defined below).

The textarea effective width of a [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element is size×avg + sbw, where size is the element's [character width](#41011-the-textarea-element), avg is the average character width of the primary font of the element, in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px), and sbw is the width of a scrollbar, in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px). (The element's ['letter-spacing'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#letter-spacing-property) property does not affect the result.)

The textarea effective height of a [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) element is the height in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) of the number of lines given by the element's [character height](#41011-the-textarea-element), plus the height of a scrollbar in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px).

User agents are [expected](#15-rendering) to apply the ['white-space'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#white-space-property) CSS property to [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements. For historical reasons, if the element has a [`wrap`](#41011-the-textarea-element) attribute whose value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`off`", then the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to treat the attribute as a [presentational hint](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints) setting the element's ['white-space'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-text/#white-space-property) property to 'pre'.

> [!warning]
> Need to detail the [native appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#native-appearance) and [primitive appearance](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-ui/#primitive-appearance).

### 15.6 Frames and framesets

User agents are [expected](#15-rendering) to render [`frameset`](#1632-frames) elements as a box with the height and width of the [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport), with a surface rendered according to the following layout algorithm:
1. The cols and rows variables are lists of zero or more pairs consisting of a number and a unit, the unit being one of *percentage*, *relative*, and *absolute*.

   Use the [rules for parsing a list of dimensions](#2347-lists-of-dimensions) to parse the value of the element's `cols` attribute, if there is one. Let cols be the result, or an empty list if there is no such attribute.

   Use the [rules for parsing a list of dimensions](#2347-lists-of-dimensions) to parse the value of the element's `rows` attribute, if there is one. Let rows be the result, or an empty list if there is no such attribute.

2. For any of the entries in cols or rows that have the number zero and the unit *relative*, change the entry's number to one.
3. If cols has no entries, then add a single entry consisting of the value 1 and the unit *relative* to cols.

   If rows has no entries, then add a single entry consisting of the value 1 and the unit *relative* to rows.

4. Invoke the algorithm defined below to [convert a list of dimensions to a list of pixel values](#156-frames-and-framesets) using cols as the input list, and the width of the surface that the [`frameset`](#1632-frames) is being rendered into, in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px), as the input dimension. Let sized cols be the resulting list.

   Invoke the algorithm defined below to [convert a list of dimensions to a list of pixel values](#156-frames-and-framesets) using rows as the input list, and the height of the surface that the [`frameset`](#1632-frames) is being rendered into, in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px), as the input dimension. Let sized rows be the resulting list.

5. Split the surface into a grid of w×h rectangles, where w is the number of entries in sized cols and h is the number of entries in sized rows.

   Size the columns so that each column in the grid is as many [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) wide as the corresponding entry in the sized cols list.

   Size the rows so that each row in the grid is as many [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px) high as the corresponding entry in the sized rows list.

6. Let children be the list of [`frame`](#1632-frames) and [`frameset`](#1632-frames) elements that are [children](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) of the [`frameset`](#1632-frames) element for which the algorithm was invoked.
7. For each row of the grid of rectangles created in the previous step, from top to bottom, run these substeps:
   1. For each rectangle in the row, from left to right, run these substeps:
      1. If there are any elements left in children, take the first element in the list, and assign it to the rectangle.

         If this is a [`frameset`](#1632-frames) element, then recurse the entire [`frameset`](#1632-frames) layout algorithm for that [`frameset`](#1632-frames) element, with the rectangle as the surface.

         Otherwise, it is a [`frame`](#1632-frames) element; render its [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables), positioned and sized to fit the rectangle.

      2. If there are any elements left in children, remove the first element from children.

8. If the [`frameset`](#1632-frames) element [has a border](#156-frames-and-framesets), draw an outer set of borders around the rectangles, using the element's [frame border color](#156-frames-and-framesets).

   For each rectangle, if there is an element assigned to that rectangle, and that element [has a border](#156-frames-and-framesets), draw an inner set of borders around that rectangle, using the element's [frame border color](#156-frames-and-framesets).

   For each (visible) border that does not abut a rectangle that is assigned a [`frame`](#1632-frames) element with a `noresize` attribute (including rectangles in further nested [`frameset`](#1632-frames) elements), the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to allow the user to move the border, resizing the rectangles within, keeping the proportions of any nested [`frameset`](#1632-frames) grids.

   A [`frameset`](#1632-frames) or [`frame`](#1632-frames) element has a border if the following algorithm returns true:
   1. If the element has a `frameborder` attribute whose value is not the empty string and whose first character is either a U+0031 DIGIT ONE (1) character, a U+0079 LATIN SMALL LETTER Y character (y), or a U+0059 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER Y character (Y), then return true.
   2. Otherwise, if the element has a `frameborder` attribute, return false.
   3. Otherwise, if the element has a parent element that is a [`frameset`](#1632-frames) element, then return true if *that* element [has a border](#156-frames-and-framesets), and false if it does not.
   4. Otherwise, return true.

   The frame border color of a [`frameset`](#1632-frames) or [`frame`](#1632-frames) element is the color obtained from the following algorithm:
   1. If the element has a `bordercolor` attribute, and applying the [rules for parsing a legacy color value](#236-legacy-colors) to that attribute's value does not return failure, then return the color so obtained.
   2. Otherwise, if the element has a parent element that is a [`frameset`](#1632-frames) element, then return the [frame border color](#156-frames-and-framesets) of that element.
   3. Otherwise, return gray.

The algorithm to convert a list of dimensions to a list of pixel values consists of the following steps:
1. Let input list be the list of numbers and units passed to the algorithm.

   Let output list be a list of numbers the same length as input list, all zero.

   Entries in output list correspond to the entries in input list that have the same position.

2. Let input dimension be the size passed to the algorithm.
3. Let total percentage be the sum of all the numbers in input list whose unit is *percentage*.

   Let total relative be the sum of all the numbers in input list whose unit is *relative*.

   Let total absolute be the sum of all the numbers in input list whose unit is *absolute*.

   Let remaining space be the value of input dimension.

4. If total absolute is greater than remaining space, then for each entry in input list whose unit is *absolute*, set the corresponding value in output list to the number of the entry in input list multiplied by remaining space and divided by total absolute. Then, set remaining space to zero.

   Otherwise, for each entry in input list whose unit is *absolute*, set the corresponding value in output list to the number of the entry in input list. Then, decrement remaining space by total absolute.

5. If total percentage multiplied by the input dimension and divided by 100 is greater than remaining space, then for each entry in input list whose unit is *percentage*, set the corresponding value in output list to the number of the entry in input list multiplied by remaining space and divided by total percentage. Then, set remaining space to zero.

   Otherwise, for each entry in input list whose unit is *percentage*, set the corresponding value in output list to the number of the entry in input list multiplied by the input dimension and divided by 100. Then, decrement remaining space by total percentage multiplied by the input dimension and divided by 100.

6. For each entry in input list whose unit is *relative*, set the corresponding value in output list to the number of the entry in input list multiplied by remaining space and divided by total relative.
7. Return output list.

User agents working with integer values for frame widths (as opposed to user agents that can lay frames out with subpixel accuracy) are [expected](#15-rendering) to distribute the remainder first to the last entry whose unit is *relative*, then equally (not proportionally) to each entry whose unit is *percentage*, then equally (not proportionally) to each entry whose unit is *absolute*, and finally, failing all else, to the last entry.

---

The contents of a [`frame`](#1632-frames) element that does not have a [`frameset`](#1632-frames) parent are [expected](#15-rendering) to be rendered as [transparent black](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#transparent-black); the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to not render its [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables) in this case, and its [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables) is [expected](#15-rendering) to have a [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport) with zero width and zero height.

### 15.7 Interactive media

#### 15.7.1 Links, forms, and navigation

User agents are [expected](#15-rendering) to allow the user to control aspects of [hyperlink](#461-introduction) activation and [form submission](#41022-form-submission), such as which [navigable](#731-navigables) is to be used for the subsequent [navigation](#7422-beginning-navigation).

User agents are [expected](#15-rendering) to allow users to discover the destination of [hyperlinks](#461-introduction) and of [forms](#4103-the-form-element) before triggering their [navigation](#7422-beginning-navigation).

User agents are [expected](#15-rendering) to inform the user of whether a [hyperlink](#461-introduction) includes [hyperlink auditing](#467-hyperlink-auditing), and to let them know at a minimum which domains will be contacted as part of such auditing.

User agents may allow users to [navigate](#7422-beginning-navigation) [navigables](#731-navigables) to the URLs [indicated](#242-parsing-urls) by the `cite` attributes on [`q`](#457-the-q-element), [`blockquote`](#444-the-blockquote-element), [`ins`](#471-the-ins-element), and [`del`](#472-the-del-element) elements.

User agents may surface [hyperlinks](#461-introduction) created by [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements in their user interface, as discussed [previously](#4246-providing-users-with-a-means-to-follow-hyperlinks-created-using-the-link-element).

#### 15.7.2 The [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute

User agents are [expected](#15-rendering) to expose the [advisory information](#3261-the-title-attribute) of elements upon user request, and to make the user aware of the presence of such information.

On interactive graphical systems where the user can use a pointing device, this could take the form of a tooltip. When the user is unable to use a pointing device, then the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to make the content available in some other fashion, e.g. by making the element a [focusable area](#662-data-model) and always displaying the [advisory information](#3261-the-title-attribute) of the currently [focused](#662-data-model) element, or by showing the [advisory information](#3261-the-title-attribute) of the elements under the user's finger on a touch device as the user pans around the screen.

U+000A LINE FEED (LF) characters are [expected](#15-rendering) to cause line breaks in the tooltip; U+0009 CHARACTER TABULATION (tab) characters are [expected](#15-rendering) to render as a nonzero horizontal shift that lines up the next glyph with the next tab stop, with tab stops occurring at points that are multiples of 8 times the width of a U+0020 SPACE character.

> [!example]
> For example, a visual user agent could make elements with a [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute [focusable](#662-data-model), and could make any [focused](#662-data-model) element with a [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute show its tooltip under the element while the element has focus. This would allow a user to tab around the document to find all the advisory text.

> [!example]
> As another example, a screen reader could provide an audio cue when reading an element with a tooltip, with an associated key to read the last tooltip for which a cue was played.

#### 15.7.3 Editing hosts

The current text editing caret (i.e. the [active range](https://w3c.github.io/editing/docs/execCommand/#active-range), if it is empty and in an [editing host](#684-editing-apis)), if any, is [expected](#15-rendering) to act like an inline [replaced element](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-display/#replaced-element) with the vertical dimensions of the caret and with zero width for the purposes of the CSS rendering model.

> [!note]
> This means that even an empty block can have the caret inside it, and that when the caret is in such an element, it prevents [margins from collapsing](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#collapsing-margins) through the element.

#### 15.7.4 Text rendered in native user interfaces

User agents are [expected](#15-rendering) to honor the Unicode semantics of text that is exposed in user interfaces, for example supporting the bidirectional algorithm in text shown in dialogs, title bars, popup menus, and tooltips. Text from the contents of elements is [expected](#15-rendering) to be rendered in a manner that honors [the directionality](#3264-the-dir-attribute) of the element from which the text was obtained. Text from attributes is [expected](#15-rendering) to be rendered in a manner that honours the [directionality of the attribute](#3264-the-dir-attribute).

> [!example]
> Consider the following markup, which has Hebrew text asking for a programming language, the languages being text for which a left-to-right direction is important given the punctuation in some of their names:
> 
> ```html
> <p dir="rtl" lang="he">
>  <label>
>   בחר שפת תכנות:
>   <select>
>    <option dir="ltr">C++</option>
>    <option dir="ltr">C#</option>
>    <option dir="ltr">FreePascal</option>
>    <option dir="ltr">F#</option>
>   </select>
>  </label>
> </p>
> ```
> 
> If the [`select`](#4107-the-select-element) element was rendered as a drop down box, a correct rendering would ensure that the punctuation was the same both in the drop down, and in the box showing the current selection.
> 
> ![](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/bidiselect.png)

> [!example]
> The directionality of attributes depends on the attribute and on the element's [`dir`](#3264-the-dir-attribute) attribute, as the following example demonstrates. Consider this markup:
> 
> ```html
> <table>
>  <tr>
>   <th abbr="(א" dir=ltr>A
>   <th abbr="(א" dir=rtl>A
>   <th abbr="(א" dir=auto>A
> </table>
> ```
> 
> If the [`abbr`](#4910-the-th-element) attributes are rendered, e.g. in a tooltip or other user interface, the first will have a left parenthesis (because the direction is 'ltr'), the second will have a right parenthesis (because the direction is 'rtl'), and the third will have a right parenthesis (because the direction is determined *from the attribute value* to be 'rtl').
> 
> However, if instead the attribute was not a [directionality-capable attribute](#3264-the-dir-attribute), the results would be different:
> 
> ```html
> <table>
>  <tr>
>   <th data-abbr="(א" dir=ltr>A
>   <th data-abbr="(א" dir=rtl>A
>   <th data-abbr="(א" dir=auto>A
> </table>
> ```
> 
> In this case, if the user agent were to expose the `data-abbr` attribute in the user interface (e.g. in a debugging environment), the last case would be rendered with a *left* parenthesis, because the direction would be determined from the element's contents.

A string provided by a script (e.g. the argument to [`window.alert()`](#891-simple-dialogs)) is [expected](#15-rendering) to be treated as an independent set of one or more bidirectional algorithm paragraphs when displayed, as defined by the bidirectional algorithm, including, for instance, supporting the paragraph-breaking behavior of U+000A LINE FEED (LF) characters. For the purposes of determining the paragraph level of such text in the bidirectional algorithm, this specification does *not* provide a higher-level override of rules P2 and P3. [\[BIDI\]](#references)

When necessary, authors can enforce a particular direction for a given paragraph by starting it with the Unicode U+200E LEFT-TO-RIGHT MARK or U+200F RIGHT-TO-LEFT MARK characters.

> [!example]
> Thus, the following script:
> 
> ```javascript
> alert('\u05DC\u05DE\u05D3 HTML \u05D4\u05D9\u05D5\u05DD!')
> ```
> 
> ...would always result in a message reading "למד LMTH היום!" (not "דמל HTML םויה!"), regardless of the language of the user agent interface or the direction of the page or any of its elements.

> [!example]
> For a more complex example, consider the following script:
> 
> ```javascript
> /* Warning: this script does not handle right-to-left scripts correctly */
> var s;
> if (s = prompt('What is your name?')) {
>   alert(s + '! Ok, Fred, ' + s + ', and Wilma will get the car.');
> }
> ```
> 
> When the user enters "Kitty", the user agent would alert "Kitty! Ok, Fred, Kitty, and Wilma will get the car.". However, if the user enters "لا أفهم", then the bidirectional algorithm will determine that the direction of the paragraph is right-to-left, and so the output will be the following unintended mess: "لا أفهم! derF ,kO, لا أفهم, rac eht teg lliw amliW dna."
> 
> To force an alert that starts with user-provided text (or other text of unknown directionality) to render left-to-right, the string can be prefixed with a U+200E LEFT-TO-RIGHT MARK character:
> 
> ```javascript
> var s;
> if (s = prompt('What is your name?')) {
>   alert('\u200E' + s + '! Ok, Fred, ' + s + ', and Wilma will get the car.');
> }
> ```

### 15.8 Print media

User agents are [expected](#15-rendering) to allow the user to request the opportunity to obtain a physical form (or a representation of a physical form) of a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object). For example, selecting the option to print a page or convert it to PDF format. [\[PDF\]](#references)

When the user actually [obtains a physical form](#158-print-media) (or a representation of a physical form) of a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to create a new rendering of the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) for the print media.

### 15.9 Unstyled XML documents

HTML user agents may, in certain circumstances, find themselves rendering non-HTML documents that use vocabularies for which they lack any built-in knowledge. This section provides for a way for user agents to handle such documents in a somewhat useful manner.

While a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is an [unstyled document](#159-unstyled-xml-documents), the user agent is [expected](#15-rendering) to render [an unstyled document view](#159-unstyled-xml-documents).

A [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) is an unstyled document while it matches the following conditions:
- The [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has no author style sheets (whether referenced by HTTP headers, processing instructions, elements like [`link`](#424-the-link-element), inline elements like [`style`](#426-the-style-element), or any other mechanism).
- None of the elements in the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) have any [presentational hints](#152-the-css-user-agent-style-sheet-and-presentational-hints).
- None of the elements in the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) have any [style attributes](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-style-attr/#style-attribute).
- None of the elements in the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) are in any of the following namespaces: [HTML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces), [SVG namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces), [MathML namespace](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#8-namespaces).
- The [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has no [focusable area](#662-data-model) (e.g. from XLink) other than the [viewport](https://drafts.csswg.org/css2/#viewport).
- The [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) has no [hyperlinks](#461-introduction) (e.g. from XLink).
- There exists no [script](#8141-scripts) whose [settings object](#8141-scripts)'s [global object](#8133-realms-settings-objects-and-global-objects) is a [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object with this [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) as its [associated `Document`](#722-the-window-object).
- None of the elements in the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) have any registered event listeners.

An unstyled document view is one where the DOM is not rendered according to CSS (which would, since there are no applicable styles in this context, just result in a wall of text), but is instead rendered in a manner that is useful for a developer. This could consist of just showing the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object's source, maybe with syntax highlighting, or it could consist of displaying just the DOM tree, or simply a message saying that the page is not a styled document.

> [!note]
> If a [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) stops being an [unstyled document](#159-unstyled-xml-documents), then the conditions above stop applying, and thus a user agent following these requirements will switch to using the regular CSS rendering.

## 16 Obsolete features

### 16.1 Obsolete but conforming features

Features listed in this section will trigger warnings in conformance checkers.

Authors should not specify a [`border`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute on an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element. If the attribute is present, its value must be the string "`0`". CSS should be used instead.

Authors should not specify a [`charset`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute on a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element. If the attribute is present, its value must be an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for "`utf-8`". (This has no effect in a document that conforms to the requirements elsewhere in this standard of being encoded as [UTF-8](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8).)

Authors should not specify a [`language`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute on a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element. If the attribute is present, its value must be an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`JavaScript`" and either the [`type`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute must be omitted or its value must be an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`text/javascript`". The attribute should be entirely omitted instead (with the value "`JavaScript`", it has no effect), or replaced with use of the [`type`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute.

Authors should not specify a value for the [`type`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute on [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements that is the empty string or a [JavaScript MIME type essence match](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type-essence-match). Instead, they should omit the attribute, which has the same effect.

Authors should not specify a [`type`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute on a [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element. If the attribute is present, its value must be an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for "[`text/css`](#mime-types)".

Authors should not specify the [`name`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute on [`a`](#451-the-a-element) elements. If the attribute is present, its value must not be the empty string and must neither be equal to the value of any of the [IDs](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element) in the element's [tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees) other than the element's own [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), if any, nor be equal to the value of any of the other [`name`](#162-non-conforming-features) attributes on [`a`](#451-the-a-element) elements in the element's [tree](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#11-trees). If this attribute is present and the element has an [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element), then the attribute's value must be equal to the element's [ID](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#49-interface-element). In earlier versions of the language, this attribute was intended as a way to specify possible targets for [fragments](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment) in [URLs](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url). The [`id`](#326-global-attributes) attribute should be used instead.

Authors should not, but may despite requirements to the contrary elsewhere in this specification, specify the [`maxlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes) and [`size`](#410532-the-size-attribute) attributes on [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attributes are in the [Number](#4105112-number-state-typenumber) state. One valid reason for using these attributes regardless is to help legacy user agents that do not support [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements with `type="number"` to still render the text control with a useful width.

#### 16.1.1 Warnings for obsolete but conforming features

To ease the transition from HTML4 Transitional documents to the language defined in *this* specification, and to discourage certain features that are only allowed in very few circumstances, conformance checkers must warn the user when the following features are used in a document. These are generally old obsolete features that have no effect, and are allowed only to distinguish between likely mistakes (regular conformance errors) and mere vestigial markup or unusual and discouraged practices (these warnings).

The following features must be categorized as described above:
- The presence of a [`border`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute on an [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element if its value is the string "`0`".
- The presence of a [`charset`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute on a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element if its value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for "`utf-8`".
- The presence of a [`language`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute on a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element if its value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`JavaScript`" and if there is no [`type`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute or there is and its value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`text/javascript`".
- The presence of a [`type`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute on a [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element if its value is a [JavaScript MIME type essence match](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-mime-type-essence-match).
- The presence of a [`type`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute on a [`style`](#426-the-style-element) element if its value is an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for "[`text/css`](#mime-types)".
- The presence of a [`name`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute on an [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element, if its value is not the empty string.
- The presence of a [`maxlength`](#410531-the-maxlength-and-minlength-attributes) attribute on an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Number](#4105112-number-state-typenumber) state.
- The presence of a [`size`](#410532-the-size-attribute) attribute on an [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) element whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [Number](#4105112-number-state-typenumber) state.

Conformance checkers must distinguish between pages that have no conformance errors and have none of these obsolete features, and pages that have no conformance errors but do have some of these obsolete features.

> [!example]
> For example, a validator could report some pages as "Valid HTML" and others as "Valid HTML with warnings".

### 16.2 Non-conforming features

Elements in the following list are entirely obsolete, and must not be used by authors:

`applet`

Use [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element) or [`object`](#487-the-object-element) instead.

`acronym`

Use [`abbr`](#459-the-abbr-element) instead.

`bgsound`

Use [`audio`](#489-the-audio-element) instead.

`dir`

Use [`ul`](#446-the-ul-element) instead.

[`frame`](#1632-frames)

[`frameset`](#1632-frames)

`noframes`

Either use [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) and CSS instead, or use server-side includes to generate complete pages with the various invariant parts merged in.

`isindex`

Use an explicit [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) and [text control](#410512-text-typetext-state-and-search-state-typesearch) combination instead.

`keygen`

For enterprise device management use cases, use native on-device management capabilities.

For certificate enrollment use cases, use the Web Cryptography API to generate a keypair for the certificate, and then export the certificate and key to allow the user to install them manually. [\[WEBCRYPTO\]](#references)

`listing`

Use [`pre`](#443-the-pre-element) and [`code`](#4515-the-code-element) instead.

`menuitem`

To implement a custom context menu, use script to handle the [`contextmenu`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-contextmenu) event.

`nextid`

Use GUIDs instead.

`noembed`

Use [`object`](#487-the-object-element) instead of [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element) when fallback is necessary.

`param`

Use the [`data`](#487-the-object-element) attribute of the [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element to set the URL of the external resource.

`plaintext`

Use the "[`text/plain`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2046#section-4.1.3)" [MIME type](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#mime-type) instead.

`rb`

`rtc`

Providing the ruby base directly inside the [`ruby`](#4510-the-ruby-element) element or using nested [`ruby`](#4510-the-ruby-element) elements is sufficient.

`strike`

Use [`del`](#472-the-del-element) instead if the element is marking an edit, otherwise use [`s`](#455-the-s-element) instead.

`xmp`

Use [`pre`](#443-the-pre-element) and [`code`](#4515-the-code-element) instead, and escape "`<`" and "`&`" characters as "`&lt;`" and "`&amp;`" respectively.

`basefont`

`big`

`blink`

`center`

`font`

[`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element)

`multicol`

`nobr`

`spacer`

`tt`

Use appropriate elements or CSS instead.

Where the [`tt`](#162-non-conforming-features) element would have been used for marking up keyboard input, consider the [`kbd`](#4518-the-kbd-element) element; for variables, consider the [`var`](#4516-the-var-element) element; for computer code, consider the [`code`](#4515-the-code-element) element; and for computer output, consider the [`samp`](#4517-the-samp-element) element.

Similarly, if the [`big`](#162-non-conforming-features) element is being used to denote a heading, consider using the [`h1`](#436-the-h1-h2-h3-h4-h5-and-h6-elements) element; if it is being used for marking up important passages, consider the [`strong`](#453-the-strong-element) element; and if it is being used for highlighting text for reference purposes, consider the [`mark`](#4523-the-mark-element) element.

See also the [text-level semantics usage summary](#4529-usage-summary) for more suggestions with examples.

---

The following attributes are obsolete (though the elements are still part of the language), and must not be used by authors:

`charset` on [`a`](#451-the-a-element) elements

`charset` on [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements

Use an HTTP \`[`Content-Type`](#252-determining-the-type-of-a-resource)\` header on the linked resource instead.

`charset` on [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements (except as noted in the previous section)

Omit the attribute. Both documents and scripts are required to use [UTF-8](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-8), so it is redundant to specify it on the [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) element since it inherits from the document.

`coords` on [`a`](#451-the-a-element) elements

`shape` on [`a`](#451-the-a-element) elements

Use [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) instead of [`a`](#451-the-a-element) for image maps.

`methods` on [`a`](#451-the-a-element) elements

`methods` on [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements

Use the HTTP OPTIONS feature instead.

`name` on [`a`](#451-the-a-element) elements (except as noted in the previous section)

`name` on [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element) elements

`name` on [`img`](#483-the-img-element) elements

`name` on [`option`](#41010-the-option-element) elements

Use the [`id`](#326-global-attributes) attribute instead.

`rev` on [`a`](#451-the-a-element) elements

`rev` on [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements

Use the [`rel`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute instead, with an opposite term. (For example, instead of `rev="made"`, use `rel="author"`.)

`urn` on [`a`](#451-the-a-element) elements

`urn` on [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements

Specify the preferred persistent identifier using the [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute instead.

`accept` on [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements

Use the [`accept`](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) attribute directly on the [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements instead.

`hreflang` on [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements

`type` on [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements

These attributes do not do anything useful, and for historical reasons there are no corresponding IDL attributes on [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements. Omit them altogether.

`nohref` on [`area`](#4813-the-area-element) elements

Omitting the [`href`](#462-links-created-by-a-and-area-elements) attribute is sufficient; the [`nohref`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute is unnecessary. Omit it altogether.

`profile` on [`head`](#421-the-head-element) elements

Unnecessary. Omit it altogether.

`manifest` on [`html`](#411-the-html-element) elements

Use service workers instead. [\[SW\]](#references)

`version` on [`html`](#411-the-html-element) elements

Unnecessary. Omit it altogether.

`ismap` on [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements

Unnecessary. Omit it altogether. All [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements with a [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute in the [Image Button](#4105119-image-button-state-typeimage) state are processed as server-side image maps.

`usemap` on [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements

`usemap` on [`object`](#487-the-object-element) elements

Use the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element for image maps.

`longdesc` on [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) elements

`longdesc` on [`img`](#483-the-img-element) elements

Use a regular [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element to link to the description, or (in the case of images) use an [image map](#48141-authoring) to provide a link from the image to the image's description.

`lowsrc` on [`img`](#483-the-img-element) elements

Use a progressive JPEG image (given in the [`src`](#483-the-img-element) attribute), instead of using two separate images.

`target` on [`link`](#424-the-link-element) elements

Unnecessary. Omit it altogether.

`type` on [`menu`](#447-the-menu-element) elements

To implement a custom context menu, use script to handle the [`contextmenu`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-contextmenu) event. For toolbar menus, omit the attribute.

`label` on [`menu`](#447-the-menu-element) elements

`contextmenu` on all elements

`onshow` on all elements

To implement a custom context menu, use script to handle the [`contextmenu`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-contextmenu) event.

`scheme` on [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) elements

Use only one scheme per field, or make the scheme declaration part of the value.

`archive` on [`object`](#487-the-object-element) elements

`classid` on [`object`](#487-the-object-element) elements

`code` on [`object`](#487-the-object-element) elements

`codebase` on [`object`](#487-the-object-element) elements

`codetype` on [`object`](#487-the-object-element) elements

Use the [`data`](#487-the-object-element) and [`type`](#487-the-object-element) attributes to invoke [plugins](#216-plugins).

`declare` on [`object`](#487-the-object-element) elements

Repeat the [`object`](#487-the-object-element) element completely each time the resource is to be reused.

`standby` on [`object`](#487-the-object-element) elements

Optimize the linked resource so that it loads quickly or, at least, incrementally.

`typemustmatch` on [`object`](#487-the-object-element) elements

Avoid using [`object`](#487-the-object-element) elements with untrusted resources.

`language` on [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements (except as noted in the previous section)

Omit the attribute for JavaScript; for [data blocks](#4121-the-script-element), use the [`type`](#4121-the-script-element) attribute instead.

`event` on [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements

`for` on [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) elements

Use DOM events mechanisms to register event listeners. [\[DOM\]](#references)

`type` on [`style`](#426-the-style-element) elements (except as noted in the previous section)

Omit the attribute for CSS; for [data blocks](#4121-the-script-element), use [`script`](#4121-the-script-element) as the container instead of [`style`](#426-the-style-element).

`datapagesize` on [`table`](#491-the-table-element) elements

Unnecessary. Omit it altogether.

`summary` on [`table`](#491-the-table-element) elements

Use one of the [techniques for describing tables](#4911-techniques-for-describing-tables) given in the [`table`](#491-the-table-element) section instead.

`abbr` on [`td`](#499-the-td-element) elements

Use text that begins in an unambiguous and terse manner, and include any more elaborate text after that. The [`title`](#3261-the-title-attribute) attribute can also be useful in including more detailed text, so that the cell's contents can be made terse. If it's a heading, use [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) (which has an [`abbr`](#4910-the-th-element) attribute).

`axis` on [`td`](#499-the-td-element) and [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) elements

Use the [`scope`](#4910-the-th-element) attribute on the relevant [`th`](#4910-the-th-element).

`scope` on [`td`](#499-the-td-element) elements

Use [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) elements for heading cells.

`datasrc` on [`a`](#451-the-a-element), [`button`](#4106-the-button-element), [`div`](#4416-the-div-element), [`frame`](#1632-frames), [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element), [`img`](#483-the-img-element), [`input`](#4105-the-input-element), [`label`](#4104-the-label-element), [`legend`](#41016-the-legend-element), [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element), [`object`](#487-the-object-element), [`option`](#41010-the-option-element), [`select`](#4107-the-select-element), [`span`](#4526-the-span-element), [`table`](#491-the-table-element), and [`textarea`](#41011-the-textarea-element) elements

### 16.3 Requirements for implementations

#### 16.3.1 The `marquee` element

The [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element) element is a presentational element that animates content. CSS transitions and animations are a more appropriate mechanism. [\[CSSANIMATIONS\]](#references) [\[CSSTRANSITIONS\]](#references)

The [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element) element must implement the [`HTMLMarqueeElement`](#1631-the-marquee-element) interface.

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLMarqueeElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString behavior;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString bgColor;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString direction;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString height;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute unsigned long hspace;
  [CEReactions] attribute long loop;
  [CEReactions, Reflect, ReflectDefault=6] attribute unsigned long scrollAmount;
  [CEReactions, Reflect, ReflectDefault=85] attribute unsigned long scrollDelay;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean trueSpeed;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute unsigned long vspace;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString width;

  undefined start();
  undefined stop();
};
```

A [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element) element can be turned on or turned off. When it is created, it is [turned on](#1631-the-marquee-element).

When the `start()` method is called, the [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element) element must be [turned on](#1631-the-marquee-element).

When the `stop()` method is called, the [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element) element must be [turned off](#1631-the-marquee-element).

---

The `behavior` content attribute on [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element) elements is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states (all non-conforming):

| Keyword | State |
| --- | --- |
| `scroll` | scroll |
| `slide` | slide |
| `alternate` | alternate |

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the [scroll](#1631-the-marquee-element) state.

---

The `direction` content attribute on [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element) elements is an [enumerated attribute](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes) with the following keywords and states (all non-conforming):

| Keyword | State |
| --- | --- |
| `left` | left |
| `right` | right |
| `up` | up |
| `down` | down |

The attribute's *[missing value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* and *[invalid value default](#233-keywords-and-enumerated-attributes)* are both the [left](#1631-the-marquee-element) state.

---

The `truespeed` content attribute on [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element) elements is a [boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes).

---

A [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element) element has a marquee scroll interval, which is obtained as follows:
1. If the element has a `scrolldelay` attribute, and parsing its value using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers) does not return an error, then let delay be the parsed value. Otherwise, let delay be 85.
2. If the element does not have a [`truespeed`](#1631-the-marquee-element) attribute, and the delay value is less than 60, then let delay be 60 instead.
3. The [marquee scroll interval](#1631-the-marquee-element) is delay, interpreted in milliseconds.

---

A [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element) element has a marquee scroll distance, which, if the element has a `scrollamount` attribute, and parsing its value using the [rules for parsing non-negative integers](#2342-non-negative-integers) does not return an error, is the parsed value interpreted in [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px), and otherwise is 6 [CSS pixels](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#px).

---

A [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element) element has a marquee loop count, which, if the element has a `loop` attribute, and parsing its value using the [rules for parsing integers](#2341-signed-integers) does not return an error or a number less than 1, is the parsed value, and otherwise is −1.

The `loop` IDL attribute, on getting, must return the element's [marquee loop count](#1631-the-marquee-element); and on setting, if the new value is different than the element's [marquee loop count](#1631-the-marquee-element) and either greater than zero or equal to −1, must set the element's [`loop`](#1631-the-marquee-element) content attribute (adding it if necessary) to the [valid integer](#2341-signed-integers) that represents the new value. (Other values are ignored.)

A [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element) element also has a marquee current loop index, which is zero when the element is created.

The rendering layer will occasionally increment the marquee current loop index, which must cause the following steps to be run:
1. If the [marquee loop count](#1631-the-marquee-element) is −1, then return.
2. Increment the [marquee current loop index](#1631-the-marquee-element) by one.
3. If the [marquee current loop index](#1631-the-marquee-element) is now greater than or equal to the element's [marquee loop count](#1631-the-marquee-element), [turn off](#1631-the-marquee-element) the [`marquee`](#1631-the-marquee-element) element.

---

#### 16.3.2 Frames

The `frameset` element acts as [the body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors) in documents that use frames.

The [`frameset`](#1632-frames) element must implement the [`HTMLFrameSetElement`](#1632-frames) interface.

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLFrameSetElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString cols;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString rows;
};
HTMLFrameSetElement includes WindowEventHandlers;
```

The [`frameset`](#1632-frames) element exposes as [event handler content attributes](#8181-event-handlers) a number of the [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers) of the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object. It also mirrors their [event handler IDL attributes](#8181-event-handlers).

The [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers) of the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object named by the [`Window`-reflecting body element event handler set](#8182-event-handlers-on-elements-document-objects-and-window-objects), exposed on the [`frameset`](#1632-frames) element, replace the generic [event handlers](#8181-event-handlers) with the same names normally supported by [HTML elements](#213-xml-compatibility).

---

The `frame` element has a [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables) similar to the [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) element, but rendered within a [`frameset`](#1632-frames) element.

The [`frame`](#1632-frames) [HTML element post-connection steps](#214-dom-trees), given insertedNode, are:
1. If insertedNode's [node document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#44-interface-node)'s [browsing context](#732-browsing-contexts) is null, then return.
2. [Create a new child navigable](#7313-child-navigables) for insertedNode.
3. [Process the `frame` attributes](#1632-frames) for insertedNode, with *[initialInsertion](#1632-frames)* set to true.

The [`frame`](#1632-frames) [HTML element removing steps](#214-dom-trees), given removedNode, are to [destroy a child navigable](#7316-navigable-destruction) given removedNode.

Whenever a [`frame`](#1632-frames) element with a non-null [content navigable](#7313-child-navigables) has its `src` attribute set, changed, or removed, the user agent must [process the `frame` attributes](#1632-frames).

To process the `frame` attributes for an element element, with an optional boolean initialInsertion (default false):
1. Let url be the result of running the [shared attribute processing steps for `iframe` and `frame` elements](#485-the-iframe-element) given element and initialInsertion.
2. If url is null, then return.
3. If url [matches `about:blank`](#241-terminology) and initialInsertion is true:
   1. [Fire an event](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#210-firing-events) named [`load`](#events) at element.
   2. Return.
4. [Navigate an `iframe` or `frame`](#485-the-iframe-element) given element, url, the empty string, null, and initialInsertion.

The [`frame`](#1632-frames) element [potentially delays the load event](#485-the-iframe-element).

The [`frame`](#1632-frames) element must implement the [`HTMLFrameElement`](#1632-frames) interface.

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLFrameElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString name;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString scrolling;
  [CEReactions, ReflectURL] attribute USVString src;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute DOMString frameBorder;
  [CEReactions, ReflectURL] attribute USVString longDesc;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean noResize;
  readonly attribute Document? contentDocument;
  readonly attribute WindowProxy? contentWindow;

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute [LegacyNullToEmptyString] DOMString marginHeight;
  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute [LegacyNullToEmptyString] DOMString marginWidth;
};
```

The `contentDocument` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [content document](#7313-child-navigables).

The `contentWindow` getter steps are to return [this](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#this)'s [content window](#7313-child-navigables).

User agents may treat the [`scheme`](#162-non-conforming-features) content attribute on the [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element as an extension of the element's [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) content attribute when processing a [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) element with a [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute whose value is one that the user agent recognizes as supporting the [`scheme`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute.

User agents are encouraged to ignore the [`scheme`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute and instead process the value given to the metadata name as if it had been specified for each expected value of the [`scheme`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute.

> [!example]
> For example, if the user agent acts on [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) elements with [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) attributes having the value "eGMS.subject.keyword", and knows that the [`scheme`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute is used with this metadata name, then it could take the [`scheme`](#162-non-conforming-features) attribute into account, acting as if it was an extension of the [`name`](#425-the-meta-element) attribute. Thus the following two [`meta`](#425-the-meta-element) elements could be treated as two elements giving values for two different metadata names, one consisting of a combination of "eGMS.subject.keyword" and "LGCL", and the other consisting of a combination of "eGMS.subject.keyword" and "ORLY":
> 
> ```html
> <!-- this markup is invalid -->
> <meta name="eGMS.subject.keyword" scheme="LGCL" content="Abandoned vehicles">
> <meta name="eGMS.subject.keyword" scheme="ORLY" content="Mah car: kthxbye">
> ```
> 
> The suggested processing of this markup, however, would be equivalent to the following:
> 
> ```html
> <meta name="eGMS.subject.keyword" content="Abandoned vehicles">

```webidl
partial interface Document {
  [CEReactions] attribute [LegacyNullToEmptyString] DOMString fgColor;
  [CEReactions] attribute [LegacyNullToEmptyString] DOMString linkColor;
  [CEReactions] attribute [LegacyNullToEmptyString] DOMString vlinkColor;
  [CEReactions] attribute [LegacyNullToEmptyString] DOMString alinkColor;
  [CEReactions] attribute [LegacyNullToEmptyString] DOMString bgColor;

  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection anchors;
  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLCollection applets;

  undefined clear();
  undefined captureEvents();
  undefined releaseEvents();

  [SameObject] readonly attribute HTMLAllCollection all;
};
```

The attributes of the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object listed in the first column of the following table must [reflect](#261-reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes) the content attribute on [the body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors) with the name given in the corresponding cell in the second column on the same row, if [the body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors) is a [`body`](#431-the-body-element) element (as opposed to a [`frameset`](#1632-frames) element). When there is no [body element](#317-dom-tree-accessors) or if it is a [`frameset`](#1632-frames) element, the attributes must instead return the empty string on getting and do nothing on setting.

| IDL attribute | Content attribute |
| --- | --- |
| `fgColor` | [`text`](#162-non-conforming-features) |
| `linkColor` | [`link`](#162-non-conforming-features) |
| `vlinkColor` | [`vlink`](#162-non-conforming-features) |
| `alinkColor` | [`alink`](#162-non-conforming-features) |
| `bgColor` | [`bgcolor`](#162-non-conforming-features) |

---

The `anchors` attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) rooted at the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) node, whose filter matches only [`a`](#451-the-a-element) elements with [`name`](#162-non-conforming-features) attributes.

The `applets` attribute must return an [`HTMLCollection`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#42102-interface-htmlcollection) rooted at the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) node, whose filter matches nothing. (It exists for historical reasons.)

The `clear()`, `captureEvents()`, and `releaseEvents()` methods must do nothing.

---

The `all` attribute must return an [`HTMLAllCollection`](#2641-the-htmlallcollection-interface) rooted at the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) node, whose filter matches all elements.

---

```webidl
partial interface Window {
  undefined captureEvents();
  undefined releaseEvents();

  [Replaceable, SameObject] readonly attribute External external;
};
```

The `captureEvents()` and `releaseEvents()` methods must do nothing.

The `external` attribute of the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) interface must return an instance of the [`External`](#1633-other-elements-attributes-and-apis) interface:

```webidl
[Exposed=Window]
interface External {
  undefined AddSearchProvider();
  undefined IsSearchProviderInstalled();
};
```

The `AddSearchProvider()` and `IsSearchProviderInstalled()` methods must do nothing.

## 17 IANA considerations

### 17.1 `text/html`

This registration is for community review and will be submitted to the IESG for review, approval, and registration with IANA.

Type name:

text

Subtype name:

html

Required parameters:

No required parameters

Optional parameters:

`charset`

The `charset` parameter may be provided to specify the [document's character encoding](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document), overriding any [character encoding declarations](#4254-specifying-the-documents-character-encoding) in the document other than a Byte Order Mark (BOM). The parameter's value must be an [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for the string "`utf-8`". [\[ENCODING\]](#references)

Encoding considerations:

8bit (see the section on [character encoding declarations](#4254-specifying-the-documents-character-encoding))

Security considerations:

Entire novels have been written about the security considerations that apply to HTML documents. Many are listed in this document, to which the reader is referred for more details. Some general concerns bear mentioning here, however:

HTML is scripted language, and has a large number of APIs (some of which are described in this document). Script can expose the user to potential risks of information leakage, credential leakage, cross-site scripting attacks, cross-site request forgeries, and a host of other problems. While the designs in this specification are intended to be safe if implemented correctly, a full implementation is a massive undertaking and, as with any software, user agents are likely to have security bugs.

Even without scripting, there are specific features in HTML which, for historical reasons, are required for broad compatibility with legacy content but that expose the user to unfortunate security problems. In particular, the [`img`](#483-the-img-element) element can be used in conjunction with some other features as a way to effect a port scan from the user's location on the Internet. This can expose local network topologies that the attacker would otherwise not be able to determine.

HTML relies on a compartmentalization scheme sometimes known as the *same-origin policy*. An [origin](#711-origins) in most cases consists of all the pages served from the same host, on the same port, using the same protocol.

It is critical, therefore, to ensure that any untrusted content that forms part of a site be hosted on a different [origin](#711-origins) than any sensitive content on that site. Untrusted content can easily spoof any other page on the same origin, read data from that origin, cause scripts in that origin to execute, submit forms to and from that origin even if they are protected from cross-site request forgery attacks by unique tokens, and make use of any third-party resources exposed to or rights granted to that origin.

Interoperability considerations:

Rules for processing both conforming and non-conforming content are defined in this specification.

Published specification:

This document is the relevant specification. Labeling a resource with the [`text/html`](#171-texthtml) type asserts that the resource is an [HTML document](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) using [the HTML syntax](#13-the-html-syntax).

Applications that use this media type:

Web browsers, tools for processing web content, HTML authoring tools, search engines, validators.

Additional information:

Magic number(s):

No sequence of bytes can uniquely identify an HTML document. More information on detecting HTML documents is available in MIME Sniffing. [\[MIMESNIFF\]](#references)

File extension(s):

"`html`" and "`htm`" are commonly, but certainly not exclusively, used as the extension for HTML documents.

Macintosh file type code(s):

`TEXT`

Person & email address to contact for further information:

Ian Hickson <ian@hixie.ch>

Intended usage:

Common

Restrictions on usage:

No restrictions apply.

Author:

Ian Hickson <ian@hixie.ch>

Change controller:

W3C

[Fragments](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment) used with [`text/html`](#171-texthtml) resources either refer to the [indicated part](#7464-scrolling-to-a-fragment) of the corresponding [`Document`](#311-the-document-object), or provide state information for in-page scripts.

### 17.5 `application/microdata+json`

This registration is for community review and will be submitted to the IESG for review, approval, and registration with IANA.

Type name:

application

Subtype name:

microdata+json

Required parameters:

Same as for [`application/json`](#mime-types) [\[JSON\]](#references)

Optional parameters:

Encoding considerations:

8bit (always UTF-8)

Security considerations:

Same as for [`application/json`](#mime-types) [\[JSON\]](#references)

Interoperability considerations:

Same as for [`application/json`](#mime-types) [\[JSON\]](#references)

Published specification:

Labeling a resource with the [`application/microdata+json`](#175-applicationmicrodatajson) type asserts that the resource is a JSON text that consists of an object with a single entry called "`items`" consisting of an array of entries, each of which consists of an object with an entry called "`id`" whose value is a string, an entry called "`type`" whose value is another string, and an entry called "`properties`" whose value is an object whose entries each have a value consisting of an array of either objects or strings, the objects being of the same form as the objects in the aforementioned "`items`" entry. Thus, the relevant specifications are JSON and this specification. [\[JSON\]](#references)

Applications that use this media type:

Applications that transfer data intended for use with HTML's microdata feature, especially in the context of drag-and-drop, are the primary application class for this type.

Same as for [`application/json`](#mime-types) [\[JSON\]](#references)
