### 17.7 `text/event-stream`

This registration is for community review and will be submitted to the IESG for review, approval, and registration with IANA.

Type name:

text

Subtype name:

event-stream

Required parameters:

No parameters

Optional parameters:

`charset`

The `charset` parameter may be provided. The parameter's value must be "`utf-8`". This parameter serves no purpose; it is only allowed for compatibility with legacy servers.

Encoding considerations:

8bit (always UTF-8)

Security considerations:

An event stream from an origin distinct from the origin of the content consuming the event stream can result in information leakage. To avoid this, user agents are required to apply CORS semantics. [\[FETCH\]](#references)

Event streams can overwhelm a user agent; a user agent is expected to apply suitable restrictions to avoid depleting local resources because of an overabundance of information from an event stream.

Servers can be overwhelmed if a situation develops in which the server is causing clients to reconnect rapidly. Servers should use a 5xx status code to indicate capacity problems, as this will prevent conforming clients from reconnecting automatically.

Interoperability considerations:

Rules for processing both conforming and non-conforming content are defined in this specification.

Published specification:

This document is the relevant specification.

Applications that use this media type:

Web browsers and tools using web services.

Additional information:

Magic number(s):

No sequence of bytes can uniquely identify an event stream.

File extension(s):

No specific file extensions are recommended for this type.

Macintosh file type code(s):

No specific Macintosh file type codes are recommended for this type.

Person & email address to contact for further information:

Ian Hickson <ian@hixie.ch>

Intended usage:

Common

Restrictions on usage:

This format is only expected to be used by dynamic open-ended streams served using HTTP or a similar protocol. Finite resources are not expected to be labeled with this type.

Author:

Ian Hickson <ian@hixie.ch>

Change controller:

W3C

[Fragments](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment) have no meaning with [`text/event-stream`](#177-textevent-stream) resources.

### 17.8 `web+` scheme prefix

This section describes a convention for use with the IANA URI scheme registry. It does not itself register a specific scheme. [\[RFC7595\]](#references)

Scheme name:

Schemes starting with the four characters "`web+`" followed by one or more letters in the range `a`-`z`.

Status:

Permanent

Scheme syntax:

Scheme-specific.

Scheme semantics:

Scheme-specific.

Encoding considerations:

All "`web+`" schemes should use UTF-8 encodings where relevant.

Applications/protocols that use this scheme name:

Scheme-specific.

Interoperability considerations:

The scheme is expected to be used in the context of web applications.

Security considerations:

Any web page is able to register a handler for all "`web+`" schemes. As such, these schemes must not be used for features intended to be core platform features (e.g., HTTP). Similarly, such schemes must not store confidential information in their URLs, such as usernames, passwords, personal information, or confidential project names.

Contact:

Ian Hickson <ian@hixie.ch>

Change controller:

Ian Hickson <ian@hixie.ch>

References:

Custom scheme handlers, HTML Living Standard: [https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#custom-handlers](#81014-custom-scheme-handlers-the-registerprotocolhandler-method)

An asterisk (\*) in a cell indicates that the actual rules are more complicated than indicated in the table above.

† Categories in the "Parents" column refer to parents that list the given categories in their content model, not to elements that themselves are in those categories. For example, the [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element's "Parents" column says "phrasing", so any element whose content model contains the "phrasing" category could be a parent of an [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element. Since the "flow" category includes all the "phrasing" elements, that means the [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) element could be a parent to an [`a`](#451-the-a-element) element.

### Attributes

*This section is non-normative.*

List of attributes (excluding event handler content attributes)

| Attribute | Element(s) | Description | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `abbr` | [`th`](#4910-the-th-element) | Alternative label to use for the header cell when referencing the cell in other contexts | [Text](#3241-attributes)\* |
| `accept` | [`input`](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) | Hint for expected file type in [file upload controls](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) | [Set of comma-separated tokens](#238-comma-separated-tokens)\* consisting of [valid MIME type strings with no parameters](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-mime-type-with-no-parameters) or `audio/*`, `video/*`, or `image/*` |
| `accept-charset` | [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) | Character encodings to use for [form submission](#41022-form-submission) | [ASCII case-insensitive](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) match for "`UTF-8`" |
| `accesskey` | [HTML elements](#672-the-accesskey-attribute) | Keyboard shortcut to activate or focus element | [Ordered set of unique space-separated tokens](#237-space-separated-tokens), none of which are [identical to](infra-spec-whatwg-org.md#47-strings) another, each consisting of one code point in length |
| `action` | [`form`](#410196-form-submission-attributes) | [URL](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url) to use for [form submission](#41022-form-submission) | [Valid non-empty URL potentially surrounded by spaces](#241-terminology) |
| `allow` | [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) | [Permissions policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-feature-policy/#permissions-policy) to be applied to the [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element)'s contents | [Serialized permissions policy](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-feature-policy/#serialized-permissions-policy) |
| `allowfullscreen` | [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element) | Whether to allow the [`iframe`](#485-the-iframe-element)'s contents to use [`requestFullscreen()`](https://fullscreen.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-element-requestfullscreen) | [Boolean attribute](#232-boolean-attributes) |

### Events

*This section is non-normative.*

The following table lists events fired by this document, excluding those already defined in [media element events](#481116-events-summary) and [drag-and-drop events](#6116-events-summary).

List of events

| Event | Interface | Interesting targets | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `DOMContentLoaded` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) | Fired at the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) once the parser has finished |
| `afterprint` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) | Fired at the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) after printing |
| `beforeprint` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) | Fired at the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) before printing |
| `beforematch` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | Elements | Fired on elements with the [`hidden=until-found`](#61-the-hidden-attribute) attribute before they are revealed. |
| `beforetoggle` | [`ToggleEvent`](#651-the-toggleevent-interface) | Elements | Fired on elements with the [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute when they are transitioning between showing and hidden |
| `beforeunload` | [`BeforeUnloadEvent`](#7277-the-beforeunloadevent-interface) | [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) | Fired at the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) when the page is about to be unloaded, in case the page would like to show a warning prompt |
| `blur` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | [`Window`](#722-the-window-object), elements | Fired at nodes when they stop being [focused](#662-data-model) |
| `cancel` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | [`CloseWatcher`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface), [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) elements, [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements | Fired at [`CloseWatcher`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) objects or [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) elements when they receive a [close request](#6101-close-requests), or at [`input`](#4105-the-input-element) elements whose [`type`](#4105-the-input-element) attribute is in the [File](#4105117-file-upload-state-typefile) state when the user does not change their selection |
| `change` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | Form controls | Fired at controls when the user commits a value change (see also the [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) event) |
| [`click`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click) | [`PointerEvent`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#pointerevent-interface) | Elements | Normally a mouse event; also synthetically fired at an element before its [activation behavior](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#27-interface-eventtarget) is run, when an element is activated from a non-pointer input device (e.g. a keyboard) |
| `close` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | [`CloseWatcher`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface), [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) elements | Fired at [`CloseWatcher`](#6103-the-closewatcher-interface) objects or [`dialog`](#4114-the-dialog-element) elements when they are closed via a [close request](#6101-close-requests) or via web developer code |
| `command` | [`CommandEvent`](#652-the-commandevent-interface) | Elements | Fired at elements when they handle a user invocation, via a [`commandfor`](#4106-the-button-element) attribute. |
| `connect` | [`MessageEvent`](#91-the-messageevent-interface) | [`SharedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10213-shared-workers-and-the-sharedworkerglobalscope-interface) | Fired at a shared worker's global scope when a new client connects |
| `contextlost` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) elements, [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) objects | Fired when the corresponding [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) or [`OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D`](#412531-the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context) is lost |
| `contextrestored` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) elements, [`OffscreenCanvas`](#41253-the-offscreencanvas-interface) objects | Fired when the corresponding [`CanvasRenderingContext2D`](#41251-the-2d-rendering-context) or [`OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D`](#412531-the-offscreen-2d-rendering-context) is restored after being lost |
| `currententrychange` | [`NavigationCurrentEntryChangeEvent`](#7271-the-navigationcurrententrychangeevent-interface) | [`Navigation`](#7262-the-navigation-interface) | Fired when [`navigation.currentEntry`](#7266-the-history-entry-list) changes |
| `dispose` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | [`NavigationHistoryEntry`](#7265-the-navigationhistoryentry-interface) | Fired when the [session history entry](#7411-session-history-entries) corresponding to the [`NavigationHistoryEntry`](#7265-the-navigationhistoryentry-interface) has been permanently evicted from session history and can no longer be traversed to |
| `error` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) or [`ErrorEvent`](#8146-runtime-script-errors) | Global scope objects, [`Worker`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface) objects, elements, networking-related objects | Fired when unexpected errors occur (e.g. networking errors, script errors, decoding errors) |
| `focus` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | [`Window`](#722-the-window-object), elements | Fired at nodes [gaining focus](#662-data-model) |
| `formdata` | [`FormDataEvent`](#4102211-the-formdataevent-interface) | [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements | Fired at a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element when it is [constructing the entry list](#410224-constructing-the-entry-list) |
| `hashchange` | [`HashChangeEvent`](#7273-the-hashchangeevent-interface) | [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) | Fired at the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) when the [fragment](https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-url-fragment) part of the document's [URL](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#45-interface-document) changes |
| [`input`](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-input) | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | Elements | Fired when the user changes the [`contenteditable`](#681-making-document-regions-editable-the-contenteditable-content-attribute) element's content, or the form control's value. See also the [`change`](#events) event for form controls. |
| `invalid` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | Form controls | Fired at controls during form validation if they do not satisfy their constraints |
| `languagechange` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | Global scope objects | Fired at the global scope object when the user's preferred languages change |
| `load` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | [`Window`](#722-the-window-object), elements | Fired at the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) when the document has finished loading; fired at an element containing a resource (e.g. [`img`](#483-the-img-element), [`embed`](#486-the-embed-element)) when its resource has finished loading |
| `message` | [`MessageEvent`](#91-the-messageevent-interface) | [`Window`](#722-the-window-object), [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface), [`MessagePort`](#944-message-ports), [`BroadcastChannel`](#95-broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts), [`DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10212-dedicated-workers-and-the-dedicatedworkerglobalscope-interface), [`Worker`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface), [`ServiceWorkerContainer`](https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#serviceworkercontainer) | Fired at an object when it receives a message |
| `messageerror` | [`MessageEvent`](#91-the-messageevent-interface) | [`Window`](#722-the-window-object), [`MessagePort`](#944-message-ports), [`BroadcastChannel`](#95-broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts), [`DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope`](#10212-dedicated-workers-and-the-dedicatedworkerglobalscope-interface), [`Worker`](#10263-dedicated-workers-and-the-worker-interface), [`ServiceWorkerContainer`](https://w3c.github.io/ServiceWorker/#serviceworkercontainer) | Fired at an object when it receives a message that cannot be deserialized |
| `navigate` | [`NavigateEvent`](#726101-the-navigateevent-interface) | [`Navigation`](#7262-the-navigation-interface) | Fired before the [navigable](#731-navigables) [navigates](#7422-beginning-navigation), [reloads](#743-reloading-and-traversing), [traverses](#743-reloading-and-traversing), or [otherwise](#725-the-history-interface) changes its URL |
| `navigateerror` | [`ErrorEvent`](#8146-runtime-script-errors) | [`Navigation`](#7262-the-navigation-interface) | Fired when a navigation does not complete successfully |
| `navigatesuccess` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | [`Navigation`](#7262-the-navigation-interface) | Fired when a navigation completes successfully |
| `offline` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | Global scope objects | Fired at the global scope object when the network connections fails |
| `online` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | Global scope objects | Fired at the global scope object when the network connections returns |
| `open` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) | Fired at [`EventSource`](#922-the-eventsource-interface) objects when a connection is established |
| `pageswap` | [`PageSwapEvent`](#7274-the-pageswapevent-interface) | [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) | Fired at the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) right before a document is [unloaded](#759-unloading-documents) as a result of a navigation. |
| `pagehide` | [`PageTransitionEvent`](#7276-the-pagetransitionevent-interface) | [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) | Fired at the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) when the page's [session history entry](#7411-session-history-entries) stops being the [active entry](#731-navigables) |
| `pagereveal` | [`PageRevealEvent`](#7275-the-pagerevealevent-interface) | [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) | Fired at the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) when the page begins to render for the first time after it has been initialized or [reactivated](#7462-updating-the-document) |
| `pageshow` | [`PageTransitionEvent`](#7276-the-pagetransitionevent-interface) | [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) | Fired at the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) when the page's [session history entry](#7411-session-history-entries) becomes the [active entry](#731-navigables) |
| [`pointercancel`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#the-pointercancel-event) | [`PointerEvent`](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#pointerevent-interface) | Elements and [`Text`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#411-interface-text) nodes | Fired at the [source node](#6115-processing-model) when the user attempts to initiate a drag-and-drop operation |
| `popstate` | [`PopStateEvent`](#7272-the-popstateevent-interface) | [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) | Fired at the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) when in some cases of [session history traversal](#743-reloading-and-traversing) |
| `readystatechange` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) | Fired at the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) when it finishes parsing and again when all its subresources have finished loading |
| `rejectionhandled` | [`PromiseRejectionEvent`](#8147-unhandled-promise-rejections) | Global scope objects | Fired at global scope objects when a previously-unhandled promise rejection becomes handled |
| `reset` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements | Fired at a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element when it is [reset](#41023-resetting-a-form) |
| `select` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | Form controls | Fired at form controls when their text selection is adjusted (whether by an API or by the user) |
| `storage` | [`StorageEvent`](#1224-the-storageevent-interface) | [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) | Fired at [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) event when the corresponding [`localStorage`](#1223-the-localstorage-getter) or [`sessionStorage`](#1222-the-sessionstorage-getter) storage areas change |
| `submit` | [`SubmitEvent`](#4102210-the-submitevent-interface) | [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) elements | Fired at a [`form`](#4103-the-form-element) element when it is [submitted](#410223-form-submission-algorithm) |
| `toggle` | [`ToggleEvent`](#651-the-toggleevent-interface) | [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) and [popover](#612-the-popover-attribute) elements | Fired at [`details`](#4111-the-details-element) elements when they open or close; fired on elements with the [`popover`](#612-the-popover-attribute) attribute when they are transitioning between showing and hidden |
| `unhandledrejection` | [`PromiseRejectionEvent`](#8147-unhandled-promise-rejections) | Global scope objects | Fired at global scope objects when a promise rejection goes unhandled |
| `unload` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) | Fired at the [`Window`](#722-the-window-object) object when the page is going away |
| `visibilitychange` | [`Event`](dom-spec-whatwg-org.md#22-interface-event) | [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) | Fired at the [`Document`](#311-the-document-object) object when the page becomes visible or hidden to the user |

Thanks also to everyone who has ever posted about HTML to their blogs, public mailing lists, or forums, including all the contributors to the [various W3C HTML WG lists](https://www.w3.org/html/wg/lists/) and the [various WHATWG lists](https://whatwg.org/mailing-list).

Special thanks to Richard Williamson for creating the first implementation of [`canvas`](#4125-the-canvas-element) in Safari, from which the canvas feature was designed.

Special thanks also to the Microsoft employees who first implemented the event-based drag-and-drop mechanism, [`contenteditable`](#681-making-document-regions-editable-the-contenteditable-content-attribute), and other features first widely deployed by the Windows Internet Explorer browser.

Special thanks and $10,000 to David Hyatt who came up with a broken implementation of the [adoption agency algorithm](#132647-the-in-body-insertion-mode) that the editor had to reverse engineer and fix before using it in the parsing section.

Thanks to the participants of the microdata usability study for allowing us to use their mistakes as a guide for designing the microdata feature.

Thanks to the many sources that provided inspiration for the examples used in the specification.

Thanks also to the Microsoft blogging community for some ideas, to the attendees of the W3C Workshop on Web Applications and Compound Documents for inspiration, to the #mrt crew, the #mrt.no crew, and the #whatwg crew, and to Pillar and Hedral for their ideas and support.

Thanks to Igor Zhbanov for generating PDF versions of the specification.

Special thanks to the [RICG](https://www.w3.org/community/respimg/) for developing the [`picture`](#481-the-picture-element) element and related features; in particular thanks to Adrian Bateman, Bruce Lawson, David Newton, Ilya Grigorik, John Schoenick, Leon de Rijke, Mat Marquis, Marcos Cáceres, Tab Atkins, Theresa O'Connor, and Yoav Weiss for their contributions.

Special thanks to the [WPWG](https://www.w3.org/WebPlatform/WG/) for incubating the [custom elements](#413-custom-elements) feature. In particular, thanks to David Hyatt and Ian Hickson for their influence through the XBL specifications, Dimitri Glazkov for the first draft of the custom elements specification, and to Alex Komoroske, Alex Russell, Andres Rios, Boris Zbarsky, Brian Kardell, Daniel Buchner, Dominic Cooney, Erik Arvidsson, Elliott Sprehn, Hajime Morrita, Hayato Ito, Jan Miksovsky, Jonas Sicking, Olli Pettay, Rafael Weinstein, Roland Steiner, Ryosuke Niwa, Scott Miles, Steve Faulkner, Steve Orvell, Tab Atkins, Theresa O'Connor, Tim Perry, and William Chen for their contributions.

Special thanks to the [CSSWG](https://www.w3.org/Style/CSS/members) for developing the [worklets](#11-worklets). In particular, thanks to Ian Kilpatrick for his work as editor of the original worklets specification.

Special thanks to the [WICG](https://wicg.io/) for incubating the [speculative loading](#76-speculative-loading) feature. In particular, thanks to Jeremy Roman for his work as editor of the original speculation rules and prefetch specifications.

Special thanks to the [WICG](https://wicg.io/) for incubating the [Sanitizer API](#86-html-sanitization). In particular, thanks to Frederik Braun, Mario Heiderich, Daniel Vogelheim, and Tom Schuster for their work as editors of the original Sanitizer API specification.

For about ten years starting in 2003, this standard was almost entirely written by Ian Hickson ([Google](https://www.google.com/), [ian@hixie.ch](mailto:ian@hixie.ch)).

Starting in 2015, the editor group expanded. It is currently maintained by [Anne van Kesteren](https://annevankesteren.nl/) ([Apple](https://www.apple.com/), [annevk@annevk.nl](mailto:annevk@annevk.nl)), [Domenic Denicola](https://domenic.me/) ([Google](https://www.google.com/), [d@domenic.me](mailto:d@domenic.me)) [Dominic Farolino](https://domfarolino.com) ([Google](https://www.google.com/), [domfarolino@gmail.com](mailto:domfarolino@gmail.com)), [Philip Jägenstedt](https://foolip.org/) ([Google](https://www.google.com/), [philip@foolip.org](mailto:philip@foolip.org)), and Simon Pieters ([Mozilla](https://www.mozilla.org/), [zcorpan@gmail.com](mailto:zcorpan@gmail.com)).
